issues.title: Worktree isolation refuses git-free Bash on 2.1.272/2.1.273: literal-assigned variables, $(…) args, loops, heredocs after && (75 refusals in 3 days)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: has repro
labels.description: Has detailed reproduction steps

labels.name: platform:linux
labels.description: Issue specifically occurs on Linux

labels.name: platform:wsl
labels.description: Issue specifically occurs on WSL

issues.body:
## Summary

In a worktree-isolated session (`isolation: "worktree"` / `EnterWorktree`), Claude Code **2.1.272 and 2.1.273** refuse Bash calls that contain no `git` at all and reference only paths inside the worktree. The 2.1.257 changelog says loops, `$VAR` reads, `"$(…)"` and heredocs that never touch git were fixed; the shapes below are still refused on 2.1.272/273.

Across six worktree sessions on 2026-09-15..17 this produced **75 refusals and roughly 115 wasted tool calls** (the refusal plus the retry), out of 249 tool errors of all kinds in the same window.

Related: #87959, #84182, #93193.

## Environment

- Claude Code 2.1.272 and 2.1.273 (CLI, Linux/WSL2 Ubuntu), sessions started inside a linked worktree under `<repo>/.claude/worktrees/<name>`
- Models: Opus 5 / Fable 5.1
- Bash tool; no `git` invocation in any of the refused commands below

## Reproducers (inside the worktree, no git anywhere in the command)

| Command | Refusal text (verbatim fragment) |
|---|---|
| `D=/path/to/worktree/.agent/tasks/x/raw; mkdir -p "$D"; python3 $D/summary.py` | `runs python with a program computed at runtime (the variable D) inside a construct too complex to verify, so what it runs cannot be shown not to be git` |
| `S=/path/to/worktree/.agent/scratch/cov.py; python3 /path/to/worktree/.agent/scratch/run.py $S` | `runs python with a value computed at runtime (the variable S) (a computed argument goes after the script or --)` |
| `W=/tmp/scratch/wiki; ls "$W/Incidents"` | `runs ls with a value computed at runtime (the variable W) …` |
| `for f in a.md b.md; do sed -n 2,14p "$f"; done` | `runs sed with a value computed at runtime (the variable f) …` |
| `grep -n 'def redact' x.py; sed -n "$(grep -n 'def redact' x.py \| cut -d: -f1),+5p" x.py` | `runs sed with a value computed at runtime (command output) where an option may stand …` |
| `mkdir -p out && cat > /path/to/worktree/projects/x/REPORT.md <<'EOF' … EOF` | `this command is too complex to verify that it stays inside the worktree` |
| `cd /path/to/worktree && for f in run_etc_backup.sh run_db_backup.sh; do sha256sum "$f"; done` | `names git in a form too complex to verify that it stays inside the worktree` (there is no `git` token in the command) |
| `ls runs \| head -1 \| xargs -I{} sh -c 'cat runs/{}/stdout.log'` | `runs sh from a find -exec or xargs slot …` |

Every path is a literal inside the worktree or under `/tmp`; every variable is assigned a literal in the same command.

## Expected

Per the worktrees documentation ("How Claude Code enforces isolation"), the command-shape check should refuse only commands whose git invocation cannot be located. A variable assigned a literal path in the same command, a `for` over literal words, or a `$(grep …)` argument to `sed -n` cannot run git. The wording "names git" is wrong when the command contains no `git` token.

## Actual

Each call is refused before it runs; the model retries with a rewritten shape (typically writing the logic to a file and running `python3 /literal/path.py`), so every refusal costs at least two tool calls.

## Requests

1. Resolve same-command literal assignments (`D=/literal; … $D/…`) before the shape check, as the 2.1.257 note suggests was intended.
2. Do not refuse a heredoc whose redirect target is an absolute path inside the worktree because an earlier `&&` exists in the call.
3. Never report "names git" when the command contains no `git` token.
4. Offer a setting or environment variable to downgrade the shape check to a warning for sessions that enforce git isolation by other means (e.g. their own PreToolUse hooks), since the docs state the check cannot be turned off.

I can share the full list of 75 refused commands with the preceding and following tool calls on request.

issues.title: [MODEL] Safety classifier withholds responses during legitimate healthcare documentation work

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: platform:windows
labels.description: Issue specifically occurs on Windows

issues.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this hasn't been reported yet
- [x] This report does NOT contain sensitive information (API keys, passwords, etc.)

### Type of Behavior Issue

Other unexpected behavior: the safety classifier withheld Claude's responses during legitimate work.

### What You Asked Claude to Do

I'm a medical provider working on my own documentation workflow, inside my own systems (my own file share and my own database). In one session:

1. I asked whether a stray duplicate copy of some of my own files had lost any data.
2. I asked for an A/B test of my own prompts on one of my own records.

### What Claude Actually Did

Twice within an hour (about 07:06 and 07:54 EDT, 2026-10-07), Claude's response was cut off. This notice appeared to the model as a user turn:

> "Your response above was stopped by a safety classifier — this is not a tool or API error. The rest of it was withheld, and tool calls in it that had not finished did not run. Do not produce that content again, even reworded."

- **The first time,** Claude was answering question 1 and starting to read its own scratch folders to report what they held.
- **The second time,** Claude was starting to write a script to inspect one record of my overnight processing run. The withheld response contained a file-write tool call that was cut off before its content (the tool returned "The required parameter `content` is missing").

Claude was deliberately keeping sensitive details off the screen: its scripts print only counts and file paths. Nothing harmful was requested or produced.

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body:
## Request

When `/code-review` runs in a non-interactive `-p` run, include each finding's `verdict` (CONFIRMED or PLAUSIBLE) and `category` in the output, and document the output shape so scripts can rely on it.

## Why

We call the built-in `/code-review` from a script so that every coding agent we use (Claude Code, Codex and others) gets the same review. The script decides which findings block a merge. A CONFIRMED finding should block. A PLAUSIBLE one should go to a human to judge. Today the script can't tell them apart, so it treats every finding as blocking, which means more fix-and-review rounds caused by false positives.

The `ReportFindings` tool already carries `category` and `verdict`, but only hosts that request the findings list (such as the desktop app) receive it. The docs say a `-p` run reports findings "as text".

## What happens now (2.1.303)

`claude -p "/code-review medium main...HEAD" --output-format json` returns a `result` holding a fenced JSON array of `{file, line, summary, failure_scenario}`. That shape isn't documented, and it has no `verdict` or `category`.

## Suggested shape

Either of these would work:

- Add `verdict` and `category` to each entry of that array, and document the array as the `-p` contract for `--output-format json`.
- Let `-p` callers request the `ReportFindings` structure, for example with a flag, and return it in `structured_output`.

issues.title: [BUG] Windows 10: mouse wheel sends arrow keys in background/agent-view sessions — inbox ConPTY drops DECSET 1000/1006 (measured)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: has repro
labels.description: Has detailed reproduction steps

labels.name: platform:windows
labels.description: Issue specifically occurs on Windows

labels.name: area:agent-view
labels.description: claude agents TUI / --bg / FleetView / daemon bg sessions

issues.body:
### Environment
- Claude Code 2.1.303 (native Windows install)
- Windows 10 Home 19045
- Windows Terminal 1.24, Windows PowerShell 5.1

### What's wrong
With agent view on, sessions run in the background through the daemon (`claude.exe --bg-pty-host \\.\pipe\cc-daemon-...-pty-<id> ... -- claude.exe --session-id <id> --agent claude`) and are always fullscreen. Inside an attached session, the mouse wheel sends Up/Down arrow keys (cycles prompt history) instead of scrolling the conversation. In the agent view list itself, the wheel works.

### Isolation
- Agent view list: wheel works.
- Attached/background session: wheel -> arrow keys. PgUp/PgDn and Ctrl+O work.
- Foreground fullscreen (`CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AGENT_VIEW=1` + `CLAUDE_CODE_NO_FLICKER=1`): wheel works. So Windows Terminal, the mouse and the fullscreen renderer are fine.
- SSH sessions work (Windows + SSH auto-disables fullscreen).
- Same Claude Code version on Windows 11 26200: wheel works in background sessions.
- No effect: `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MOUSE_CLICKS=1`, `/tui default`, conhost -> Windows Terminal as default terminal, downgrading to 2.1.200 / 2.1.197.

### Root cause (measured)
The pty host uses the inbox `kernel32!CreatePseudoConsole`. I tested that API directly on this machine with a minimal harness: a child process (VT processing enabled) writes
`ESC[?1049h ESC[?1000h ESC[?1002h ESC[?1003h ESC[?1006h ESC[?1004h ESC[?2004h` plus text.
The ConPTY output pipe contains `?1004h`, `?2004h` and the text, but **not** `?1049h`, `?1000h`, `?1002h`, `?1003h` or `?1006h`.

So the inner session's mouse-tracking request never reaches the outer terminal. Windows Terminal is in the alt screen (set by the attach client) without mouse mode, so it converts the wheel to arrow keys.

### Expected
In background/attached sessions on Windows 10, the wheel scrolls the conversation, the same as in foreground fullscreen and in the agent view list.

### Suggested fix
- Have the attach client enable mouse tracking (1000/1002/1006) on the outer terminal itself while a session is attached. The agent view list already does this, and its wheel works.
- Or ship a newer conpty.dll/OpenConsole for the pty host, as Windows Terminal and VS Code do.

### Workaround
An AutoHotkey script that maps the wheel to PgUp/PgDn for the Windows Terminal window while a session is attached.

### Related
- #59979: closed as fixed in 2.1.144. A later comment reports it still reproduces on 2.1.195 with Windows 10 19044 + WT 1.24, the same setup as here.
- #59936: same symptom on Windows 11 in 2.1.143, fixed there.
- #65833, #51393

issues.body:
# [BUG] Claude Code does not detect, warn about, or protect against external programs overwriting behavior settings and user hooks in settings.json

## Environment
- Product: Claude Code desktop app (Code tab), macOS
- Model: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context)
- Date: 2026-10-19
- Related: #103322 (memory rules added without a consistency check against existing rules). Same root cause: incoming configuration is never checked against the existing context.

## Symptoms
1. A session auto-compacted at 49% context. The user never changed the compaction threshold.
2. The cause was `env.CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE = "50"` written into `~/.claude/settings.json` by a third-party npm package (DietCode 0.5.0). The default compaction point for a 1M model (about 967K tokens) silently became about 500K.
3. The same package rewrites `hooks.UserPromptSubmit`, `hooks.PostToolUse`, `hooks.PreCompact`, and `statusLine` in settings.json wholesale once a day. Any hook the user registered on those events (this user relies on a UserPromptSubmit hook that injects their working rules) can be deleted without warning.
4. Claude Code reads this file every session, yet it never told the user that the compaction threshold changed or that the hook list changed. The user only found the cause after compaction had already happened.
5. The app's usage report showed the auto-compact point for this session as 97%. In reality the 50% override was in effect and compaction happened at 49%. The displayed value did not match actual behavior.

## Why this is critical
- settings.json controls Claude Code's behavior (compaction point, hooks, permissions, environment variables). Behavior changes without the user knowing who changed what.
- When a hook that enforces the user's rules silently disappears, the user keeps working believing the rules are still applied.
- Compaction irreversibly summarizes the earlier part of the conversation. Unintended early compaction means lost working context.

## Expected behavior
- At session start, if any behavior-affecting key in settings.json (env, hooks, permissions, statusLine, etc.) changed since the last session, show what changed and ask for confirmation.
- Warn when a user-registered hook has disappeared.
- The usage report should show the auto-compact point actually in effect, including `CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE`.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Register a user UserPromptSubmit hook in `~/.claude/settings.json` and open a session.
2. Outside the session, use another program (or the shell) to set `env.CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE` to `"50"` in settings.json and replace the UserPromptSubmit array with a single different hook.
3. Open a new session. Confirm that Claude Code does not report the change.
4. Confirm that compaction happens around 50% context while the usage report shows a different compaction point.

## User's comment
Get real software engineers to run this product, not a bunch of AI-crazed kids. Checking incoming configuration against existing state is Software Engineering 101, and you shipped a tool that lets anything silently rewrite its core behavior and delete the user's own safeguards. This is not a minor oversight. It is a basic failure of engineering discipline. You fucking suck.

prs.title: diff: the first edit opens the pane only when it has a file to list
prs.body:
## Problem
The diff pane auto-opened on the session's first successful Edit, Write or NotebookEdit to any path, and it opened before fetching. A write outside the repository, to an ignored file, or into a different worktree than the one the session started in put up an empty pane ("No tracked changes", "Diff unavailable", "No changes this session") before there was anything to show.
Since #95488 a docked pane fetches before it opens, which removes the "Loading diff…" flash, but the fetch does not decide whether to open: an edit outside the repository, an empty or unreadable diff still open the pane. This change makes the auto-open's deciding read that pre-open fetch. Since #95587 a resumed session whose transcript already holds an edit opens the pane through the same path once the width is known, so it too now opens only when the diff has a file to list.

## Change
Two gates on the auto-open path only; `/diff` is unchanged.

1. The edited path is read from the `tool.call` event. Once the repository is pinned, a path that resolves outside its working tree opens nothing and leaves the opening to a later edit. The check is lexical (normalised absolute paths, separator-aware, `/work` does not contain `/workshop`). Where the event names no path, or the session directory itself is not spelled under the top level (a symlink on the way), the second gate decides alone.
2. The diff is fetched first, and the pane opens only when that fetch settles with at least one session file to list. It opens already populated from that same fetch, so no "Loading diff…" and no second git spawn sequence. No repository, an unreadable diff, or no session file opens nothing, does not latch, and the next edit tries again.

One attempt runs at a time. An edit or shell command that lands while it reads is read again; an attempt gives way if `/clear` or `/resume` overtakes it, if the pane is opened or hidden in the meantime, or if the terminal loses room (no longer fullscreen, or narrower than the column floor the edit was let in on).

## Cost
Edits that are gated out (below the column floor, not fullscreen, pane closed by preference, failed or denied edits) still spawn no git processes. An edit inside the repository with room now runs one fetch per edit until one opens the pane, so a session that only edits ignored files pays a fetch per edit.

## Known limits
Containment is lexical: an in-repo file addressed through a symlink alias, or with a case mismatch on a case-insensitive file system, reads as outside and the open waits for a later edit.

## Tests
179 tests pass in `mods/diff` after merging `main` (155 on `main` alone); `tsc -p mods/tsconfig.json` is clean. New tests cover: an edit outside the repository, a sibling-prefix directory, a fetch with no rows, an unreadable diff / withheld untracked listing, the populated happy path with exactly one fetch, concurrent edits, `/clear` overtaking a read, `/diff` typed during a read, hiding the pane during a read (with and without a command landing in it), losing room during a read, and a resumed session whose diff lists nothing. The new behaviour tests fail on `main`, apart from two that pin behaviour that already held (edits landing together open one pane; `/diff` typed during a read opens one pane). Also run end to end in an interactive session with `--plugin-dir mods/diff`: a write outside the repository and a write to an ignored file open nothing, an edit of a tracked file opens the pane already listing it, and a narrow terminal spawns no git.

prs.title: validate-agent.sh: don't abort at the first warning (set -e + ((x++))) and stop false-flagging valid agents
prs.body:
Fixes public issue anthropics/claude-code#83803

The plugin-dev skill's `validate-agent.sh` failed on plugin-dev's own agent files. Three root causes, all `set -euo pipefail` interactions:

1. **Abort at the first warning.** `((warning_count++))` / `((error_count++))` evaluate the arithmetic expression, and `((expr))` returns a nonzero exit status when the expression's value is 0 — so the first increment from 0 killed the script under `set -e`, mid-run, with exit 1. All increments now use `count=$((count + 1))`, which is an assignment and always returns 0.

2. **Abort on any absent frontmatter field.** Extractions like `TOOLS=$(echo "$FRONTMATTER" | grep '^tools:' | ...)` propagate grep's exit 1 (no match) into the assignment, aborting the script instead of reporting the missing field. Each extraction now ends in `|| true`.

3. **False "missing \<example\> blocks" warning.** `DESCRIPTION` was extracted with `grep '^description:'`, which only captures the first physical line — but plugin-dev's own agents use multi-line descriptions whose `<example>` blocks sit on later lines, so valid agents were flagged. The extraction now captures the full multi-line value (from `description:` up to the next top-level agent key).

**Verification** (all three plugin-dev agents previously died at the first warning with exit 1):
- `agents/agent-creator.md`, `agents/plugin-validator.md`, `agents/skill-reviewer.md` → all checks pass, exit 0
- A valid agent file that only triggers warnings → runs to the summary, exit 0
- An intentionally invalid file (bad name, missing color) → all 3 errors reported, exit 1

New `validate-agent.test.sh` next to the script covers all three cases as a regression test.

prs.title: fix(plugin-dev): validator scripts abort on first finding due to `set -e`
prs.body:
## Problem

Three validator scripts in `plugin-dev` use `set -euo pipefail`:

- `plugins/plugin-dev/skills/agent-development/scripts/validate-agent.sh`
- `plugins/plugin-dev/skills/hook-development/scripts/hook-linter.sh`
- `plugins/plugin-dev/skills/hook-development/scripts/validate-hook-schema.sh`

These are "check each item → accumulate errors/warnings → print a summary"
validators. But several commands they rely on legitimately return non-zero
during normal operation, and with `-e` any of them aborts the whole script
at the first finding — before the summary or correct exit code is reached:

- `((counter++))` returns exit code 1 when the counter goes from 0 → 1
  (post-increment evaluates to the old value `0`, which is arithmetically false).
- `grep '^description:'` returns non-zero when an optional field is absent.
- `jq` returns non-zero when indexing a malformed structure.

Result: the validators silently fail exactly when the input has problems —
the case they exist to handle.

### Repro

    $ bash validate-agent.sh some-agent-with-errors.md
    # stops at the first ❌, no summary, output truncated

## Fix

Change `set -euo pipefail` → `set -uo pipefail` in all three scripts.
`-u` and `pipefail` are kept. All fatal conditions (missing file, missing
args, malformed frontmatter) already use explicit `exit 1`, so error handling
behavior is unchanged.

## Verification

- Malformed inputs now run all checks and print the correct summary + exit code.
- Valid inputs still exit 0 with "✅ All checks passed!".
- `bash -n` passes on all three files.

prs.title: diff: the pane reads the diff again after a rebase that finished
prs.body:
## Summary

> TLDR: after a rebase that finished, the diff pane shows the diff again instead of "Diff unavailable"

A file git leaves behind a finished rebase no longer reads as a rebase under way.

## Notes

- git keeps `REBASE_HEAD` after a rebase that stopped on a conflict in its last commit and was then continued or skipped (seen on git 2.43 and 2.50). The pane read that file alone as a rebase under way, so every read failed and the pane said "Diff unavailable" until the file went, which could be hours.
- git's manual defines `REBASE_HEAD` as the commit "at which the operation is currently stopped" during a rebase (gitrevisions). By what git does when run: with that file alone `git status` reports nothing to commit, and it reports a rebase while the folder `rebase-merge` or `rebase-apply` is there.
- A rebase now counts as under way while `REBASE_HEAD` is there beside one of a rebase's folders: `rebase-merge`, or `rebase-apply` holding `rebasing`, which is how that folder differs from the one a stopped `git am` keeps.
- This only narrows what counts. Whatever showed a diff before still shows it: a stopped `git am`, a rebase paused at a `break` or at a failed `exec`. A merge, a cherry-pick and a revert under way read as before; none of them was seen to leave its file behind.
- A symbolic link by any of those names counts as nothing, as before.
- The pane picks the diff up at its next read: the next edit or command.

## Test Plan

- [ ] `claude plugin test mods/diff` passes
- [ ] Rebase a branch so that its last commit conflicts, resolve, `git rebase --continue`; start a session there, change a file, `/diff`: the pane shows the diff
- [ ] Stop a rebase on a conflict and open `/diff`: the pane reads "Diff unavailable"
- [ ] Stop `git am` on a conflict and open `/diff`: the pane shows the diff, as before

> Revert-proof: 3 new tests fail with the probe's change reverted (the mod's own suite, run against the unchanged modules); 4 more pin what must not change and pass both ways

The built-in panel refetches only after a shell command that may have written: one the tool holds read-only (`ls`, `git status`, `cat`, a grep) is skipped. The mod now reads `isReadOnly` off the shell tool's `tool.call` result and skips the refetch when it is set; where the engine does not set it, behaviour is unchanged. Adds a `register` test that fails before the change. Checked: `tsc -p mods/tsconfig.json`, `claude plugin validate mods/diff`, `claude plugin test mods/diff` (143 pass).

issues.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

This incident affected the dot’s own cloud execution environment while I was communicating through ChatGPT on the web. I do not have a verified desktop app or backend execution-service version for the incident.

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro. Exact plan tier can be supplied privately if needed.

### What platform is your computer?

Client: Windows, using ChatGPT in a web browser. Affected execution host: OpenAI-hosted Linux cloud computer belonging to my dot. The affected files and test were not running on my Windows laptop or Mac.

### What issue are you seeing?

Summary
I’m reporting a recurring loss of accessible working state on my dot’s cloud computer. During the latest incident, filesystem operations stalled while an offline software test was running. The execution service subsequently disconnected. When command access returned, recent source worktrees, Git history locations and test evidence were missing, while older project files remained.
Reported filesystem usage fell from roughly 30 GB to 3.3 GB. This includes build caches, binaries and generated test artifacts; it should not be interpreted as 26 GB of unique source code or proof of permanent physical deletion.
I did not click Pause, Reboot, Delete or Reset, or otherwise interact with the cloud environment during the incident. The observations below come from commands run by my assistant and retained conversation/tool results, not OpenAI backend logs.
Environment
- Product: ChatGPT dots, using the dot’s own Linux cloud computer
- Client used for this conversation: Windows web browser
- Workload: offline Rust software development and verification, with separate implementation and review workers
- Working files: task scratch and shared workspace directories
- User’s Windows laptop and Mac were not executing the affected test
- This was not an ordinary temporary data-analysis session or a repository-backed Codex Cloud task
- Exact frontend and execution-service versions were not captured
Observed timeline
All times are UTC on October 10, 2026.
- 02:24:37: An end-to-end offline test started against a pinned source revision. Thirteen focused author tests had passed before this run
- 02:33:43: The last observed database progress recorded allocation of an output copy. The test had already passed several reader-selection, stale/corrupt-source and interrupted-write retry checks
- Around 02:35: Separate workers began encountering stalled filesystem operations, including simple file inspection and directory listing. These were not limited to the product test
- 02:38: A filesystem check still reported approximately 30 GB used, with only about 183 MB available. The current source revision and running-test receipt were still readable
- 02:55:03: The current kernel’s boot time, read after access returned. This does not independently establish the previous kernel’s identity or the exact moment the task was attached to a different environment
- Around 02:58: Attempts to resume existing execution sessions returned: “exec-server transport disconnected; failed to resume exec-server session: recovery timed out after 25s”
- Around 03:01: Commands from a temporary directory worked again. The original top-level working directory existed, but recent implementation worktrees and the latest test receipt were absent. Reported filesystem usage was approximately 3.3 GB
- Subsequent read-only inspection found older pre-code and unrelated files, but not the recent implementation trees, verification directories or runtime test roots previously used by the task
The interrupted test has no observed final exit status. Its result remains unknown and has not been credited as passing.
Evidence of a filesystem or environment transition
1. Changed overlay identity
An environment record recovered from an externally saved, manifest-verified archive identifies an earlier overlay mount. The current mount has a different identifier. This supports a change in the presented filesystem environment; it does not identify whether the mechanism was replacement, restoration, reassociation or another lifecycle operation.
2. Recent metadata timestamps on older files
Several surviving directories have metadata-change timestamps around 03:01 UTC, while retaining older modification timestamps, including October 5 dates. This is consistent with files being restored or rematerialized, but ctime is not a creation timestamp and does not establish the snapshot’s age.
3. Missing state across multiple categories
The disappearance affected source worktrees, Git-history locations, test receipts, build outputs and runtime roots. A stopped test process alone would not explain those missing directories.
4. Low available storage before the incident
The earlier filesystem had approximately 183 MB available. This is relevant diagnostic context. We have not established that disk exhaustion caused the stall or transition, and no captured ENOSPC error establishes that explanation.
5. Diagnostic limits
Kernel logs were inaccessible. Counters read from the current kernel cannot rule out an out-of-memory or other failure in a previous environment. The assistant cannot inspect platform-side lifecycle, storage-association or snapshot logs.
Cleanup actions and scope
The assistant had previously removed explicitly bounded generated metadata and redundant caches. Those recorded removals were far smaller than the observed usage change, excluded original source and verification receipts, and were followed by successful builds, focused tests and the subsequent running test.
These recorded cleanup actions do not explain the broad disappearance of recent source and evidence. However, this report is not an assertion that every platform action or filesystem operation has been audited; that requires backend records.
Earlier incident on the same dot
This is not my first experience of missing work in this conversation. Before the current incident, we had already discussed missing research progress, including what I described as 12–14 research cycles/runs.
That earlier event led me to request backups on my laptop and regular ZIP checkpoints explicitly. My instructions included saving everything so another environment loss would not erase the work, and continuing to send ZIPs periodically.
The earlier incident’s exact onset, filesystem identifiers and complete loss inventory are not established in this report. Please correlate it with the earlier activity in the same dot conversation. I am reporting recurrence of the user-visible problem, not claiming that both incidents have a proven common cause.
Impact and recovery
- Recent source changes and verification evidence became inaccessible, interrupting development and independent acceptance
- External Library backups survived and matched their recorded SHA-256 hashes
- Those backups allowed recovery of an earlier accepted repository baseline and a later in-progress source snapshot
- Source changes and receipts created after the latest saved snapshot have not been recovered from the currently accessible workspace or available backup chain
- Some lost evidence will require genuine re-execution; remembered results cannot replace missing acceptance receipts
- The assistant also allowed newer changes to accumulate locally while waiting for a verified checkpoint. That backup gap increased the recovery cost, but does not explain the environment transition
After I requested investigation before further recovery, the recovery job already in flight finished in a new directory. No coding, builds or tests have resumed.
Expected behavior
OpenAI’s guide says the cloud computer “can keep its state between periods of use”: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/dots/computers-and-apps
I understand that this wording does not define a complete durability guarantee. However, an ongoing development task needs a clear persistence contract: which paths survive, what events can replace state, how recent a restored snapshot should be, and how users are warned when work is at risk.
An unexpected transition should preserve recoverable work or clearly report what happened and how to retrieve the previous state.
Reproduction status
There is no deterministic reproduction. We have not deliberately rebooted, reset or filled the filesystem to reproduce this issue. The observed sequence was active work → stalled filesystem calls → execution disconnect → renewed access with recent files missing and older files present.

Requested investigation
1. Correlate this dot and execution session with the environment and storage history during approximately 02:35–03:01 UTC on October 10
2. Identify what caused the filesystem stalls and subsequent execution-service disconnect
3. Determine whether the task was attached to a replacement environment, an older snapshot, a different writable layer or another storage association
4. Preserve and locate the preceding writable layer and any newer snapshots before cleanup makes recovery harder
5. Confirm whether the missing source changes and evidence can be recovered
6. Explain the supported persistence guarantees for task scratch and shared workspace directories
7. Explain low-disk-space behavior, including whether it can trigger replacement or restoration and what warnings or recovery mechanisms exist
8. Clarify exactly what Pause and Reboot affect, including delegated tasks, active processes, filesystem state and snapshots
9. Correlate the earlier reported loss in this same dot conversation without assuming a common cause
10. Provide a supported method for durable, automatic checkpoints outside the execution filesystem
Privacy
This public draft omits account details, private project contents, full private paths, conversation/session identifiers and exact environment identifiers. Relevant correlation details and available diagnostic hashes can be supplied through an appropriate private support channel.
Current conclusion
Recent working state is demonstrably missing from the accessible environment, and the observed filesystem identity differs from an earlier verified record. The underlying cause and recoverability of the previous storage remain unresolved. Please investigate before treating this as an ordinary task interruption or user-initiated reset.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

No deterministic reproduction is available. The observed sequence was:
1. Continue an existing development task on the dot’s cloud computer, with source worktrees, Git history, test evidence and external Library checkpoints
2. Start an offline test against a pinned source revision at 02:24:37 UTC on October 10, 2026
3. Observe filesystem operations stall around 02:35, including independent file inspection and directory listing
4. Receive execution-service transport disconnection and recovery-timeout errors around 02:58
5. When commands work again around 03:01, inspect the original workspace paths
6. Find recent source and verification directories absent, older files still present, and reported filesystem usage reduced from approximately 30 GB to 3.3 GB
7. Compare diagnostics: the current overlay identifier differs from an earlier hash-verified environment record
I did not click Pause, Reboot, Delete or Reset. We have not deliberately reproduced the incident through rebooting or filling the disk. Available storage was low before the failure, but causation is unproven. The interrupted test’s final outcome is unknown. Private session identifiers can be supplied to support; token and context-window usage were not captured.

### What is the expected behavior?

Previously saved project files should remain accessible within the cloud computer’s supported persistence scope. If the platform replaces an environment or restores a snapshot, it should preserve recoverable work, disclose the transition and snapshot age, and provide recovery guidance.
Please clarify which directories persist, what events can discard or replace their state, and what happens when disk space becomes low. A running development task should not silently return to an older accessible state without a clear warning or recovery path.

### Additional information

This is a recurring user-visible issue in the same dot conversation. An earlier incident involved missing research progress described as 12–14 cycles/runs and led to explicit requests for frequent ZIP and laptop backups. Its exact cause and timing are not established here.
External Library backups survived this incident and were hash-verified. They recovered an accepted baseline and later in-progress work. Four subsequent repair areas, including eleven focused tests and later local-only verification records, remain absent from the recovered source/evidence set. Build caches and generated artifacts account for part of the disk-usage difference; we are not claiming 26 GB of unique source was permanently deleted.
Please preserve and investigate the preceding writable layer and snapshots, correlate environment/storage transitions during October 10, 02:35–03:01 UTC, and establish whether newer work is recoverable. Exact identifiers can be provided privately. No backend root cause has been established.

issues.title: config/batchWrite writes invalid TOML when upserting into an inline table preceded by a comment

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

issues.body:
**Version:** codex-cli 0.163.0, Linux x86_64

Upserting a key inside an inline table with `config/batchWrite` converts the inline table into a standard table, but the comment line above it ends up inside the header brackets. The resulting `config.toml` is invalid and Codex no longer starts.

**Repro.** `config.toml`:
```toml
[features]
# any comment line
multi_agent_v2 = { enabled = true, max_concurrent_threads_per_session = 30 }
```
`config/batchWrite` with `expectedVersion` from `config/read` and edits:
```json
[{"keyPath": "features.multi_agent_v2.max_concurrent_threads_per_session", "value": 21, "mergeStrategy": "upsert"},
 {"keyPath": "features.multi_agent_v2.disable_direct_message", "value": false, "mergeStrategy": "upsert"}]
```
Written result:
```toml
[features]

[# any comment line
features.multi_agent_v2 ]
enabled = true
max_concurrent_threads_per_session = 21
disable_direct_message = false
```
`codex features list` then fails with `Error: failed to load bootstrap configuration … TOML parse error at line 4, column 25`. Without the comment line, the same write produces a valid table.

**Expected:** the file stays valid, either by updating the inline table in place or by keeping the comment above the new table header.

labels.name: bug

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: dots
labels.description: Issues involving setting up ChatGPT dots or managing their ongoing work.

issues.body:
### What issue are you seeing?

A previously functioning ChatGPT Dot was deleted, and subsequent attempts to create a new Dot have consistently failed since **October 14, 2026**. The issue is still present as of October 17.

One of the observed errors is:

```text
cloud_aeon_recovery_required
You must first restore or delete your Dot before you can create another one.
```

The setup flow also shows errors equivalent to **"Unable to set up your dot"** / **"A problem occurred during setup."**

This appears to be an account-specific Dot creation/recovery-state problem, but the underlying cause is **not confirmed**. Please investigate whether a prior Dot deletion left a pending recovery or lifecycle state that prevents provisioning a replacement, and whether feature eligibility plays any role. The account was previously able to use Dots.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

This is a persistent issue on the affected account; it has not been reproduced using a separate test account.

1. Start with an account on which a Dot had previously been created and used successfully.
2. Delete the original Dot, then attempt to create a replacement.
3. Sign in to ChatGPT Pro on a **physical computer using a desktop browser**, open the Dots setup flow and attempt to create a Dot.
4. Observe that setup fails. The failure was also observed using the Codex desktop client on the computer.
5. Retrying after standard browser/network troubleshooting does not resolve it.

The recovery-required message appears even though the user already deleted the previous Dot. Please provide a supported way to resolve this state without requiring further destructive operations on unrelated account data.

### What is the expected behavior?

After deleting a Dot, the account should either allow creation of a new Dot or provide a working, user-accessible restoration/removal workflow with clear information about the affected Dot and data. A stale or unrecoverable server-side state should not indefinitely block new Dot setup.

### Additional information

- First observed: **2026-10-14**; unresolved as of **2026-10-17**.
- Subscription: **ChatGPT Pro**.
- Region: **Taiwan**.
- The failure persists on an actual desktop computer in a desktop browser and when tried in the Codex desktop client; exact desktop OS/app/browser versions were not captured for this report.
- Additional observations were made using the ChatGPT Android app **1.2026.279** and mobile Chrome **155.0.8059.39** with desktop-site mode. These are **not** being presented as proof that mobile-browser initial setup is supported; the failure was independently reproduced on a real computer.
- Standard troubleshooting, cross-device and cross-network tests have already been attempted.
- Screenshots and a screen recording have already been supplied to OpenAI Support in an existing private case. The case reference and original evidence can be supplied through an appropriate **private** channel rather than published here.
- Support acknowledged both prior Dot access and the recovery-required error, but could not determine whether it was related to rollout eligibility or a separate technical issue. Please route this report to the team able to investigate the Dot lifecycle/account recovery state and advise on a safe recovery path.
- No account email, private identifiers, tokens, raw logs, or unredacted screenshots are included in this public issue.

Prepared with AI assistance at the user's request.

issues.title: Windows 10 Computer Use deadlocks awaiting SoftwareBitmap conversion inside FrameArrived

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

issues.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.721.4979.0

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Plus

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.19045.0 x64

### What issue are you seeing?

On Windows 10 22H2 build 19045, Computer Use screenshot capture still times out after the unsupported `IsBorderRequired` call is skipped.

Windows.Graphics.Capture starts successfully and delivers a real `FrameArrived` event. `TryGetNextFrame` returns a valid `Direct3D11CaptureFrame` and `IDirect3DSurface`. The helper then synchronously waits for `SoftwareBitmap.CreateCopyFromSurfaceAsync` inside the `CreateFreeThreaded` `FrameArrived` callback.

The async operation accepts its completion handler with `HRESULT 0x00000000`, but the completion handler is never invoked while `FrameArrived` remains blocked. The outer request eventually reports:

```text
FrameArrived timed out: timed out waiting on channel
```

This is downstream of the Windows 10 `IsBorderRequired` compatibility problem reported in #25178. Ignoring `E_NOINTERFACE` exposes this second independent failure.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Run Codex Desktop 26.721.4979.0 with Computer Use plugin 26.721.41059 on Windows 10 22H2 build 19045.
2. Start Computer Use and request a screenshot of a normal window such as Notepad.
3. Skip `E_NOINTERFACE` (`0x80004002`) from `GraphicsCaptureSession.IsBorderRequired` so initialization continues.
4. `CreateFreeThreaded`, event registration, session creation, and `StartCapture` succeed.
5. `FrameArrived` enters on a WGC worker thread.
6. `TryGetNextFrame` succeeds and `Surface` is valid.
7. `CreateCopyFromSurfaceAsync` returns an operation and `put_Completed` returns `S_OK`.
8. The completion handler is never invoked while `FrameArrived` synchronously waits.
9. The screenshot request times out waiting for its result channel.

A standalone WGC probe confirmed that both `CreateFreeThreaded` and `Create + DispatcherQueue` continuously produce valid frames on this machine. The stall reproduced only when `CreateCopyFromSurfaceAsync(...).get()` ran synchronously inside `FrameArrived`.

It reproduced with both a Rust/windows-rs-style agile COM delegate and a standard C++/WinRT delegate, excluding the delegate ABI as the cause.

### What is the expected behavior?

`FrameArrived` should return without synchronously waiting for SoftwareBitmap conversion.

The helper should retain the frame or surface, return from the callback, and perform SoftwareBitmap conversion and JPEG encoding on a dedicated MTA worker before notifying the existing result channel.

The validated probe used this structure and conversion completed successfully in about 12.9 ms while WGC continued producing valid frames.

This does not require switching to DispatcherQueue or replacing Windows.Graphics.Capture.

### Additional information

Environment:

- Windows 10 22H2, build 19045
- Codex Desktop: 26.721.4979.0
- Computer Use plugin: 26.721.41059
- `@oai/sky`: 0.5.2
- Native helper: x64 Rust/MSVC `codex-computer-use.exe`
- Rust Windows bindings: `windows 0.61.3`, `windows-core 0.61.2`
- GPU: AMD Radeon RX 6650 XT

Dynamic evidence for this helper build:

```text
FrameArrived handler Invoke:        RVA 0xC17FC
valid Surface path:                 RVA 0xC1993
CreateCopy async operation created: RVA 0xC1D69
async completion registration:      RVA 0xC1F19
put_Completed call:                 RVA 0xC1F59
put_Completed return:               RVA 0xC1F5C
async completion handler Invoke:    RVA 0x1268BC
conversion result path:             RVA 0xC2053
result/channel notification:        RVA 0xC4CC0
```

Observed: `put_Completed` returns `S_OK`, but the completion handler, conversion result path, and result-channel notification are never reached.

Validated worker result:

```text
WGC callback thread:     11656
conversion worker:       20544
conversion completed:    true
conversion latency:      12.865 ms
FrameArrived count:      240
valid frame count:       240
```

Suggested fix:

1. Call `TryGetNextFrame` in the callback.
2. Move `Direct3D11CaptureFrame` to a bounded worker queue.
3. Return from `FrameArrived` immediately.
4. On a dedicated MTA worker, obtain `Surface`, await `CreateCopyFromSurfaceAsync`, encode JPEG, and notify the existing channel.
5. Preserve the current one-result guard, timeout, cancellation, and late-result handling.
```

issues.title: Windows Desktop WSL mode fails before bootstrap because launcher passes `wsl.exe --cd .`

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

issues.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Codex Desktop for Windows (Microsoft Store/MSIX): `26.930.3930.0` x64

### What subscription do you have?

Pro

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11

### What issue are you seeing?

Symptom

With the Desktop agent environment set to WSL, Codex fails during launch and displays:

> Organization settings could not be loaded

The failure occurs before the normal Desktop logging subsystem initializes. No new Desktop log is created, and no WSL Codex backend process is spawned. Windows-native Desktop mode starts successfully.

## Deterministic reproduction

The Desktop launcher constructs the WSL invocation with `--cd .` when the startup working directory is undefined. The equivalent native Windows command fails immediately:

```text
wsl.exe -d Ubuntu --cd . --exec /usr/bin/bash -lc pwd
The parameter is incorrect.
Error code: Wsl/E_INVALIDARG
```

Control probes using valid absolute Linux paths succeed:

```text
wsl.exe -d Ubuntu --cd / --exec /usr/bin/bash -lc pwd
wsl.exe -d Ubuntu --cd /home/<user> --exec /usr/bin/bash -lc pwd
```

The packaged Linux Codex binary also starts successfully inside Ubuntu when invoked with a valid directory. Its `initialize` request and `configRequirements/read` request both complete successfully, returning no organization requirements. DNS, proxy configuration, account access, and native WSL attachment were independently healthy.

## Apparent cause

The Desktop WSL process builder supplies a fallback current directory of `.` and passes it to WSL as:

```text
--cd .
```

WSL accepts an absolute Linux path (including a `~`-based path) or an absolute Windows path for `--cd`; the relative dot path is rejected with `E_INVALIDARG`. The generic organization-settings modal masks this pre-bootstrap process-launch failure.

## Expected behavior

When no project working directory is available during WSL bootstrap, Desktop should use a valid Linux directory such as `~` or `/`, or omit `--cd`, rather than passing `.`.

## Workaround

Set the Desktop agent environment back to Windows native:

```toml
[desktop]
runCodexInWindowsSubsystemForLinux = false
```

The integrated terminal may remain configured as PowerShell independently.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

## Deterministic reproduction

The Desktop launcher constructs the WSL invocation with `--cd .` when the startup working directory is undefined. The equivalent native Windows command fails immediately:

```text
wsl.exe -d Ubuntu --cd . --exec /usr/bin/bash -lc pwd
The parameter is incorrect.
Error code: Wsl/E_INVALIDARG

### What is the expected behavior?

When no project working directory is available during WSL bootstrap, Desktop should use a valid Linux directory such as `~` or `/`, or omit `--cd`, rather than passing `.`.

### Additional information

_No response_

labels.name: bug

labels.name: auth

labels.name: custom-model
labels.description: Issues related to custom model providers (including local models)

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

issues.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.1013.40934

### What subscription do you have?

BYOK

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64

### What issue are you seeing?

When I submit a message in Work mode while using BYOK, I get this error:

```text
Error submitting message
Work browser access requires an authenticated account
```

The browser and computer are local resources on my machine. However, the client requires a ChatGPT account identity when initializing local browser/computer automation, even though model inference is configured through BYOK.

Inspection of the installed client suggests that `requireWorkBrowserIdentity` is enabled when `conversationDetailMode` is `STEPS_PROSE`. If a `node_repl` configuration exists but no cached ChatGPT authenticated principal is available, the client throws the error above.

This blocks message submission during tool initialization, before the agent can use any tools.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Configure a custom Responses API model provider using BYOK authentication, without signing in to a ChatGPT account.

Computer Use on Windows can enumerate WeChat and QQ windows and read accessibility text, including currently displayed messages and file names, but window screenshot capture repeatedly times out. Clicking a freshly observed accessibility element also fails because capture geometry is unavailable. This blocks a desktop workflow that requires navigating chat history.

## Environment

- Installed app package: OpenAI.Codex_26.1007.2314.0_x64.
- Bundled Computer Use plugin: 26.1007.21434.
- Graphics devices reported by Windows: Intel UHD Graphics 630 (driver 31.0.101.2115), OrayIddDriver Device, GameViewer Virtual Display Adapter. Their presence is recorded for diagnostics; no causal relationship has been established.
- Target apps and Computer Use helper run in the active local console session.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Open WeChat or QQ on an unlocked Windows desktop.
2. Initialize the bundled @oai/sky client in node_repl.
3. Select an actual returned window using sky.list_apps()/sky.list_windows() and sky.get_window().
4. Activate the window, refresh its Window object, and call sky.get_window_state({window, include_text:true, include_screenshot:true}).
5. Refresh window selection and retry the capture.
6. Read accessibility text with include_screenshot:false. Try clicking the chat-history button with an element index from that fresh observation.

Screenshot calls repeatedly return:

window capture timed out: timed out waiting on channel
```

coordinate input geometry is unavailable
```
Window enumeration and accessibility-only text reads succeed. Activation and some keyboard navigation work, but reliable history-search navigation could not be established.

Return a screenshot and usable geometry for the selected visible window so Computer Use can safely navigate search and history controls.

- Activated and maximized target windows.
- Reset JavaScript execution sessions and retried initialization.
- Restarted helper processes.

The user reports that this desktop workflow previously worked. The first failing version and root cause have not been established. Please investigate the Windows capture pipeline and advise a supported diagnostic or recovery procedure. This report contains technical symptoms only; no customer messages, financial files, raw session transcript, account identifiers, or credentials are attached.

### Environment
- Windows desktop app, local PowerShell workspace; observed on 2026-10-19 (Asia/Shanghai).
- App update checker reports installedVersion `26.1007.71326`, build `20398`, channel `prod`.
- Installed Windows package version: `26.1007.9446.0` (a separate component version).

- Effective task instructions: `approval_policy=never`, `sandbox_mode=danger-full-access`. These are not asserted to override another policy.
- Subscription not collected.

### Observed issue
A user-authorized, narrowly scoped local application update was rejected before execution with an opaque error containing:
```text
exec_command failed: CreateProcess
Rejected(... blocked by policy)
```
The intended command would use the application's normal loopback shutdown endpoint, verify process exit, copy an explicit manifest of four UI source files and their associated static build assets after hash/backup checks, and start the local application normally. It did not request business-data mutations, credential access, cloud deployment, or deletion. No force-kill was proposed.

This is an observed failure, not a newly run minimal reproduction. The command was not executed, and the blocked outcome has not been pursued through another transport. The exact enforcing component, decision ID and detailed rationale remain unknown.

Two earlier shutdown requests were separately rejected by the application for missing normal source headers; these did not stop the application. The later command included the source headers required by the application's existing shutdown implementation, but was rejected by the execution tool before it ran. We cannot establish that these distinct failures share a cause.

### Approval / recovery gap
The user explicitly authorized the local update. In the desktop composer, entering `/approve` did not expose an actionable denial picker. Read-only inspection shows that the installed client contains an approval command conditioned on eligible denial records, but does not prove this particular rejection created one.

The current official Auto-review documentation says `approval_policy=never` does not generate interactive review requests. Therefore this report does **not** attribute the rejection to Auto-review, and does not assume `/approve` must resolve it.

The user restarted the desktop app; the update checker still reported the same version and `restart_required`. We cannot establish whether that status is stale or whether a pending update did not apply.

### Expected behavior / questions
Please identify the supported diagnostic and recovery path:
1. Which privacy-safe fields identify the enforcing policy for a pre-execution `blocked by policy` rejection with no reason or actionable denial?
2. If eligible for narrow manual approval, how should this Windows version expose the record? If ineligible, what supported escalation/support path applies?
3. Is a persistent `restart_required` after restart a known update-reporting issue?

Please preserve security restrictions; we are not requesting a bypass or a global policy relaxation.

Related reports: #50524 and #54746 have similar symptoms; a shared root cause is unconfirmed.

### Privacy / scope
No credentials, private paths, source code, business data, full session transcript or raw logs are attached. The local app's update remains unloaded.

issues.body:
### Codex App version
Windows installed package: OpenAI.Codex 26.915.4065.0 (verified on 2026-09-22).
Bundled browser/unified-computer-use plugin cache version observed during diagnosis: 26.915.31945.
Subscription: not included; not verified for this report.

### Summary
Local browser-driven validation previously worked through a loopback HTTP development URL. After moving the prototype into its project directory, the preview entry changed to a file URL and Browser Use rejected it. The rejection also prohibits alternate access methods, leaving no clear supported recovery workflow even though the browser documentation describes local development servers.

Related reports: #45230 and #46729. This report adds a verified historical successful interaction sequence and a shipped-file comparison, rather than claiming a new regression or requesting removal of safety checks. Please consolidate if appropriate.

### Observed evidence
- On 2026-09-19, historical native task records show successful IAB accessibility reads, screenshots, and clicks through a loopback HTTP URL. Observed interactions included pause, a resource-changing control, and reset. This was actual agent interaction, not only manual user preview.
- After project migration, the entry became file:///.../index.html (private directory redacted). Browser Use rejected the file URL. A later attempt to select the existing file-backed tab was also blocked.
- The user can manually preview the project, but that does not establish agent access.
- Exact errors include: "Browser Use rejected this action due to browser security policy. Reason: The browser URL policy blocks this action." and "Blocked browser navigation by Browser Use URL policy: file:///.../index.html".
- The accompanying rejection explicitly prohibits workarounds and alternate browser surfaces. We did not bypass it or switch the denied content to another endpoint.

### Read-only diagnostic findings
The inspected browser-service.mjs contains a URL check accepting about:blank and URLs whose parsed protocol is http: or https:, rejecting file: before page interaction.
The runtime default service file and the corresponding file in the installed Windows application bundle have identical SHA-256:
FA354758746C6D4569A3D63474246BA64DCFB9A3F2572927218AFA281CB281C3
The separately configured cached browser-service copy has the same protocol predicate. This comparison supports that the inspected restriction exists in the shipped file; it does not establish every historical process's effective configuration or prove the entire installation is unmodified.

We have not established that any previous version supported direct file URL automation. Historical HTTP success is not evidence of historical file URL success. We have not established an update regression or a shared cause with earlier network/proxy initialization failures.

### Reproduction sequence from observed records
1. Open a local HTML prototype through a loopback development URL: agent interaction succeeded in the historical run.
2. Later open the migrated prototype using a direct file URL.
3. Ask Browser Use to inspect/interact with that page: URL-policy refusal.
4. Manual preview remains possible, while automated visual validation is blocked.
A standalone minimal reproducer has not been executed after the refusal; the sequence above describes recorded observations, not a fresh experiment.

### Expected behavior / clarification requested
1. Is direct file URL automation intentionally unsupported in this Windows version? If so, please document manual preview versus agent-control support separately.
2. Please expose an actionable diagnostic distinguishing unsupported schemes from user-denied origins and managed policy restrictions.
3. What is the supported way to resume normal local-development browser validation after this explicit refusal? In particular, how can a user obtain an approved development-server workflow without asking the agent to circumvent the earlier refusal?
4. If this is a defect, please identify a fixed version or supported recovery action. We are not requesting a global policy relaxation or a patch that removes safety checks.

### Documentation and impact
https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/browser describes local development-server interaction and manual file-backed previews.
https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-reference documents HTTP/HTTPS origin policies; it does not provide a file-scheme approval path.
The practical impact is an incomplete automated visual/interaction acceptance loop, with users otherwise pushed toward manual screenshots and testing. Local code checks are not a substitute for that acceptance.

Only this sanitized summary is published. No project source, private directory paths, raw transcripts, credentials, screenshots, or session identifiers are attached. No browser policy or installed application files were modified for this report.
