Two follow-ups to #55646 on `beta`.

**Traffic light spacing.** With the vertical tabs sidebar collapsed on macOS, the floating toggle started exactly at the 68px base width of the traffic lights. Newer macOS draws them wider (about 74px), so the toggle sat right against the green light. The collapsed toggle now lays out as if the traffic lights were the header's first control: it starts 16px past them, which is where the horizontal titlebar puts its first control. The header contents shift with it through `CollapsedSidebarToggleSpace`.

**Beta-only setting, off by default.** Sidebar toggling now sits behind **Settings → Experimental → Sidebar toggle**:

- The row appears (and is searchable) in every build except `prod`, which hides it and ignores any stored value.

- `tsc -b` and `src/settings` unit tests pass.
- I haven't checked the macOS pixel spacing in the native app. The offset change comes from the numbers above.

prs.title: fix(tui): keep Home and End in the session prompt
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #56890

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

On the start screen, `Home` and `End` move the prompt cursor. After submitting a prompt, they moved the transcript instead: to the first and last message. The cursor stayed where it was, so typing `hello world`, `Home`, `x`, `End`, `y` produced `hello worldxy` inside a session and `xhello worldy` on the start screen.

The cause is the default binding table. `session.first` included `home` and `session.last` included `end`, and the session route registers those two commands in a keymap layer that stays active while the prompt has focus. Any transcript binding registered later wins over the textarea's own `buffer-home` / `buffer-end`, so the key never reached the prompt.

The change drops `home` from `session.first` and `end` from `session.last`. Both commands keep their remaining keys (`ctrl+g` and `alt+home`, `ctrl+alt+g`), so jumping to the first or last message still works from the focused prompt; `Home` and `End` now reach the focused textarea everywhere, the same way they already did on the start screen. I did not change the textarea layer, its bindings, or the layer ordering: the conflict is only in the two default key strings.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New `packages/tui/test/session-prompt-home-end.test.tsx` mounts the real app on a session and checks both halves: with the prompt focused, typing `hello world`, `Home`, `x`, `End`, `y` leaves `xhello worldy` and the transcript does not scroll, and `ctrl+g` / `ctrl+alt+g` still jump to the first and last message. The first test fails on the unmodified tree and passes with the change.
- `packages/tui/test/session-home.test.tsx` drives transcript navigation, so its presses now use the remaining jump keys instead of `Home` / `End`.
- `cd packages/tui && bun test` — 1488 pass, 6 fail; the same 6 fail without this change (`node:*` reload cases and four plugin keymap layer cases, all timing out on frame predicates).
- `bun run typecheck`, `oxlint` and `prettier --check` pass on the touched files.

### Screenshots / recordings

Not a layout change, so no screenshot: the visible difference is which key moves the cursor, covered by the new test above.

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: fix(tui): bind keypad mirrors for navigation keybinds
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #55533

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Terminals that speak the kitty keyboard protocol report NumPad navigation keys as distinct keypad codes: Windows Terminal sends `CSI 57424 u` for NumPad End, `CSI 57423 u` for NumPad Home, and so on. OpenTUI decodes these correctly into keystroke names (`kpend`, `kphome`, `kpup`, `kpdown`, `kppageup`, `kppagedown`, `kpleft`, `kpright`), but the TUI's default keybindings only ever named the bare navigation keys (`end`, `home`, `up`, ...). No binding claimed the keypad names, so every NumPad keystroke was silently discarded — NumPad End does nothing while regular End scrolls to the last message.

This change adds the keypad mirror to every default binding that names a bare navigation key (33 defaults across diff, session, prompt, composer, and list navigation), establishing the invariant: **a default that binds a bare navigation key also binds its keypad counterpart.**

Two deliberate exceptions, both recording the same rule — Home and End belong to the focused prompt inside a session:

- `session.first` and `session.last` get no keypad mirror. #56910 removes plain `home` and `end` from those two transcript jumps so the caret keys reach the composer; mirroring Home and End onto the numpad there would hand the transcript back the keys on a numpad. They are exempt from the invariant, and the test says so with the reason.
- `input.line.home` stays `ctrl+a` only — regular Home in a text buffer means line-start, and mirroring Home there would make NumPad Home jump to the line start. `input.buffer.home` / `input.buffer.end` remain `none`.

The keypad names are already first-class in the stack: `@opentui/core` maps code points 57417–57426 to `kpleft`…`kpdelete`, and `@opentui/keymap` recognizes them as named single-stroke keys. This PR only extends the default definitions, so users who override any of these keybinds in config are unaffected, and keypad names were already valid in custom configurations.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New invariant test (`packages/tui/test/keybind.test.ts`): walks every default definition and asserts each bare navigation token is accompanied by its `kp*` mirror. Verified to fail with 34 violations against the pre-fix definitions and pass after.
- New end-to-end test (`packages/tui/test/keymap.test.tsx`): renders the real `Keymap.Provider` under `testRender`, feeds the raw byte sequences `\^[[57424u` and `\^[[57423u` through the renderer stdin (the exact sequences Windows Terminal sends for NumPad End and Home), and asserts the commands bound to `end,kpend` and `home,kphome` fire — using `diff.last` and `diff.first`, and asserting the transcript jumps stay silent.
- Updated the two existing assertions that pin exact default strings (`config-v2.test.tsx` defaults table, `mini/runtime.boot.test.ts` fallback expectations) to the new values.
- `tsc -b` clean; `oxlint` and `prettier --check` clean on the changed files; `bun test` over the touched suites (`config`, `config-v2`, `keybind`, `keymap`, `session-home`, `mini/runtime.boot`) is 62 pass / 0 fail.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: feat(ui): open images from their place in the message
prs.body: ## Why Clicking an image in a session makes the preview appear at full size in one frame, with no link to the thumbnail you clicked, and closing makes it vanish. Claude's desktop app instead grows the image out of its spot in the message while the page dims, and shrinks it back on close, which keeps you oriented and feels much better. ## What Changes The image now flies between its place on the page and the preview, in both directions. | Moment | Behavior | | --- | --- | | Open | The image grows from exactly where it sits (position, size, crop and corner radius) to the fitted preview. The page dims in step, and the preview panel and its zoom controls fade in as the image lands. | | While open | The inline image stays hidden, so there are never two copies on screen. | | Close (Esc, the close button, or a backdrop click) | The image shrinks back into its spot, re-measured at that moment. If you are zoomed in, it flies from the zoomed, cropped view on screen rather than snapping to fit first. The panel clears early in the flight. | | Close during the open | The flight turns around where it is and keeps its velocity, so the image slows, reverses and heads home rather than restarting a curve. | | Thumbnail gone or scrolled off screen | Plain fade instead of a flight. | | Reduced motion | 150 ms fade, no travel. | Clicking the open image doesn't close it: Claude doesn't either (its click toggles zoom). Double-click zoom, pinch, ⌘ + scroll, pan and the zoom controls from #56685 are unchanged. ### Timing, measured from Claude I measured the image rect frame by frame in a 60 fps screen recording of Claude's desktop preview, then fitted curves to it (progress 0 to 1, RMS error over every frame): | | Claude measured | Cubic-bezier fit | Spring from rest | **Spring with launch velocity (used)** | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Open | 285 → 651 px, no crop or overshoot; 25% after 1 frame, 61% after 3, 91% after 7, settled ≈250 ms | `(.2,.8,.2,1)` 285 ms: 0.0094 | 0.155 s: 0.0318 | 0.2 s, bounce 0, launched at 14 × distance/s: **0.0093** | | Close | 39% after 1 frame, 81% after 3, settled ≈170 ms | same curve 180 ms: 0.0105 | 0.10 s: 0.0401 | 0.2 s, bounce 0, launched at 32.5 × distance/s: **0.0075** | | Backdrop | dims in parallel, gentler start | `ease` ≈300 / ≈190 ms: 0.045 / 0.059 | **0.34 s / 0.2 s: 0.037 / 0.049 (used)** | | A spring that starts from rest can't match Claude, because Claude's image starts fast. The same spring launched with an initial velocity fits as well as the best bezier on open and better on close, and one spring (0.2 s, bounce 0) covers both directions; only the launch differs. Claude starts moving ≈150 ms after the click; this branch starts as soon as the full image has decoded, 15 to 45 ms after the click in the recordings. The image stays sharp mid-flight because the flight uses the full-resolution image. ## Shared-Element Flight A stand-in `` with the same `src` is laid out once at the preview image's fitted rect and moved with transform and `clip-path` only. A flight frame, in viewport pixels, is where the whole image would be drawn (always its own aspect ratio), which part of it shows, and the visible corner radius. Translate plus uniform scale moves the image and an inset clip crops it, so an `object-fit: cover` thumbnail (message and composer attachments) flies without squashing. Each of those nine numbers rides its own `Spring` on the shared `frameLoop`, and one job per preview writes the transform, clip and opacities straight to the DOM; no CSS transitions or WAAPI drive the flight. Because every edge moves on screen, corners and crops stay even mid-flight. Opening or closing retargets the springs and adds the launch velocity to whatever velocity they already have, which is what makes the mid-open reversal continuous. Once every edge is within a quarter pixel and the backdrop has settled, the real image takes over on the same pixels; on close, the thumbnail reappears under the stand-in when it lands. Callers pass the element the preview opens from as `origin`: markdown and tool output images, message attachments and composer attachments all do. Two supporting changes make the close visible: - The dialog stack disposes a closing dialog after a fixed 100 ms. `useDialogLayer()` gains `setExitDuration(ms)`, which the preview sets to 320 ms. - Kobalte unmounts closed content immediately unless a CSS animation runs, so the content holds a no-op exit animation for the same time. The preview draws its own scrim, in step with the flight, and makes the stack's overlay transparent; the overlay still handles backdrop clicks. ## Motion Library This PR also vendors Kit's spring library (from #56917, which this replaces; authorship kept on its own commit) as `@opencode/ui/motion` and `@opencode/ui/motion/solid`, unchanged: `Spring` with SwiftUI's duration and bounce mapping, retargeting that keeps velocity, the shared `frameLoop` with measured read and write phases, `springStyle`, `keyedPresence`, `steppedSlider`, reduced-motion helpers, tests and a README. From #56917's measurements: integrating 1,000 retargeted springs takes 0.015–0.042 ms per frame, and in headless Chromium `springStyle` costs about a third of `motion`'s `useSpring` script time and a quarter of its allocation. The image flight (`image-flight.ts`, `image-preview.tsx`) is its first user. The zoom ease still uses `motion`'s `animate()`. ## Demo Left: `beta`. Right: this branch. Headless Chromium on the new `UI/ImagePreview/FromMessage` story (a fictional poster drawn on a canvas), with real Playwright input: click the inline image, ⌘ + scroll zoom, Esc; click a cropped 58×46 thumbnail, click the backdrop; Esc 120 ms into an open; a plain open and close. Each action is synced on its click or key press. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/459cc829-7b59-4a67-bd1f-16b9e4127484 The same moments at 0.25×. The right side is recorded with the page clock slowed to 0.25, so every frame is real; `beta` has no animation, so its 1× recording is stretched. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/64ca4a97-34a8-4731-bb01-da4104b7c53e ## Scope Desktop and web image preview only. The open waits for the full image to load and decode before anything appears; it uses the same URL as the thumbnail, so it's normally cached. ## Verification ```sh cd packages/ui bun test src/components/image-flight.test.ts src/components/image-zoom.test.ts src/motion bun typecheck cd ../app bun test --conditions=browser --isolate --preload ./happydom.ts ./test-browser/motion-dom.test.ts bun typecheck cd ../session-ui && bun typecheck cd ../.. && bun run lint:changed origin/beta ``` - `image-flight.test.ts` covers `object-fit` cover and contain geometry, the transform and clip onto uncropped and cropped thumbnails, a zoomed view clipped to the viewport, the spring flight following Claude's measured open (25%, 61% and 91% after 1, 3 and 7 frames, no overshoot), and a mid-flight turn-around that starts exactly where the image is and carries its outward velocity. The zoom tests and the library's own tests (39 pure and 17 DOM) pass. - Typecheck passes in `ui`, `session-ui` and `app`, and `lint:changed` reports 0 problems. - Per-frame traces from the recordings (flight rect, clip, scrim and panel opacity, inline image visibility) show no frame with two images, no jump at the hand-off between the stand-in and the real image in either direction (under 0.3% brightness change at the open hand-off), a continuous turn-around when Esc lands mid-open, and a fade with no travel under reduced motion. - Not run inside the Electron desktop app.

prs.title: feat(core): edit saved permissions
prs.body:
## Problem

Saved permissions ("Always allow" answers) can be listed and removed through the API, but not changed. To narrow a broad approval, such as a saved `shell: *`, a client has to delete it, and there is no way to recreate a narrower one. This blocks a UI for reviewing saved approvals (#50600).

## Change

Adds `PATCH /api/permission/saved/:id` (`permission.saved.update`), which changes a saved permission's `action` and/or `resource`. The project can't change, and the rule stays an `allow`.

```diff
 /api/permission/saved
   GET     permission.saved.list
+  PATCH   permission.saved.update   { action?, resource? } → { data: PermissionSaved.Info }
   DELETE  permission.saved.remove
```

```text
PermissionSaved.update({ id, action?, resource? })
  row = find id                        → NotFoundError  (404 PermissionSavedNotFoundError)
  update row with action/resource replaced
    unique index rejects a duplicate   → ConflictError  (409 ConflictError)
  return updated row
```

The unique index on (project, action, resource) decides conflicts, so there is no separate duplicate query and no gap between check and write. Bun and Node report the violation with a SQLite code (`UniqueViolation`). Durable Object SQLite throws a plain `Error` without codes, so the check also matches `SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_UNIQUE` in the message; this was verified against the error a local workerd Durable Object throws.

The edit applies to the next permission check, like any saved permission. Requests already waiting are not re-checked, the same as `remove`.

- `packages/core/src/permission/saved.ts`: `update`, plus `NotFoundError` and `ConflictError`
- `packages/protocol`: the endpoint and a new `PermissionSavedNotFoundError` (the existing `PermissionNotFoundError` is for pending requests)
- `packages/server/src/handlers/permission.ts`: maps the core errors to 404 and 409
- `packages/client`: regenerated

## Out of scope

- An endpoint to add saved permissions directly.
- Change events for saved permissions, so other clients refresh live. `add` and `remove` don't publish one either.
- How saved permissions rank against a configured `ask` (today a saved `allow` wins; see #48456).
- A UI for listing and editing saved permissions.

## Verification

- `packages/core/test/permission.test.ts`: editing narrows what a saved permission allows (the edited resource is allowed, the old pattern prompts again), and conflict and not-found errors. `bun run script/test.ts test/permission.test.ts --rerun-each 5`: 530 pass.
- `packages/server/test/permission-saved.test.ts`: creates two saved permissions through the real request and "always" reply flow, then checks PATCH returns the updated entry, the list reflects it, a duplicate returns 409, and an unknown ID returns 404. `bun test test/permission-saved.test.ts --rerun-each 10`: 10 pass.
- `bun run check`: 34 of 34 tasks pass.

prs.title: fix(session-ui): wrap execute calls and show code mode output
prs.body:
## Problem

- Long Code Mode call rows (`mesh.exec [target=…, script=…]`) ran past the tool and the timeline edge instead of truncating.
- A successful Execute showed its calls but never its result. The output was only visible in the View code dialog.

## Fix

- **Wrapping:** Tools with an action (View code) lay out as a wrapping flex row. The content item kept `min-width: auto`, so its unbreakable `nowrap` call text set its width. Adding `min-width: 0` lets the rows truncate, as they were designed to.

```css
/* basic-tool.css */
[data-component="collapsible"].tool-collapsible[data-has-action="true"] > [data-slot="collapsible-content"] {
  flex-basis: 100%;
  min-width: 0;
}
```

- **Output:** When the script succeeds with output, a collapsed `› Output  N lines` row appears below the calls. Expanding it shows the result in the same card as the shell result, `ConsoleOutput` + `bash-result`. The card has a copy button and a 240px scroll area. A runtime error stays on the failing call row, as before.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  E[Execute expanded] --> C[call rows]
  E -->|error| R[error under failing call]
  E -->|output, no error| O["› Output N lines (collapsed)"]
  O -->|click| S[shell-style result card]
```

- **Test:** A story fixture with a long `mesh.exec` call and a component test check that the calls stay inside the tool, the output starts collapsed, and the result shows when expanded. Without the wrapping fix, the calls overflow by 518px.

Every channel has the same package name, so all of them shared one directory: | | Before | After | |---|---|---| | OpenCode | `Programs\@opencodedesktop` | `Programs\ai.opencode.desktop` | | OpenCode Beta | `Programs\@opencodedesktop` | `Programs\ai.opencode.desktop.beta` | | OpenCode Dev | `Programs\@opencodedesktop` | `Programs\ai.opencode.desktop.dev` | ```js // app-builder-lib/out/targets/targetUtil.js — oneClick && !perMachine passes false return isTryToUseProductName && /^[-_+0-9a-zA-Z .]+$/.test(appInfo.productFilename) ? appInfo.productFilename : appInfo.sanitizedName // "@opencode/desktop" → "@opencodedesktop" ``` The channels share the app code in `resources\app.asar`, so one channel's installer breaks the others: - **Installing one channel replaces another's app code.** For example, installing Dev made `OpenCode Beta.exe` run the Dev app. - **The running-app check closes every channel.** It stops every process under `$INSTDIR`, so updating one channel also closes the others. - **Uninstall deletes every channel.** Uninstalling one channel, or updating it (which runs the old uninstaller with `--updated`), runs `RMDir /r $INSTDIR` on the shared directory. ## How ```mermaid flowchart TD init["customInit (after initMultiUser)"] --> q{"$INSTDIR is ...\@opencodedesktop?"} q -- no --> keep["keep $INSTDIR"] q -- yes --> new["$INSTDIR = ...\Programs\APP_ID"] new --> e{"this channel's exe in the shared dir?"} e -- yes --> skip["clear UninstallString,
so uninstallOldVersion skips
the old uninstaller"] skip --> install["install into the new dir
(the template writes a new uninstall entry)"] install --> leave["leaveSharedInstall: delete this channel's exe + uninstaller,
its staged updates, and the shared dir
once no 'Uninstall *.exe' is left"] ``` - **`customInit`:** Computes the new directory from the parent of the template's choice, so a moved `UserProgramFiles` folder still works. An install in any other location stays where it is. - **`customCheckAppRunning`:** Also stops this channel's own executable in the shared directory, and leaves the other channels' apps running. - **Staged updates (`preInit --stage`):** Unpack beside the new directory, so the first update after this change still renames the staged copy into place. - **Taskbar pin:** Pointed at the new executable (`$QUICKLAUNCH\User Pinned\TaskBar\.lnk`). The template recreates the Start menu and desktop shortcuts itself. - **Data directory, staged CLI and `opencode://` registration:** Do not depend on the install directory.

prs.title: feat(desktop): ship the CLI as opencode and put it on the Windows PATH
prs.body:
- The bundled CLI is now `opencode` / `opencode.exe` (was `opencode-cli`) on every platform. That covers resources, staging, the version file, mac signing entitlements, dev builds and the Windows signature check in `publish.yml`. - On Windows, typing `opencode` in any new terminal now runs the desktop's CLI. ## Why a link directory Each version stages its CLI in its own folder (`\cli\-\`), because Windows cannot replace an exe that is still running. Putting that folder on PATH would mean editing PATH on every update. Instead, PATH gets one fixed folder that holds a hard link to the current stage: ```mermaid flowchart LR PATH["User PATH
%APPDATA%\ai.opencode.desktop\bin"] --> link["bin\opencode.exe
(hard link)"] link --> stage["cli\2.1.0-x64\opencode.exe"] old["cli\2.0.20-x64\opencode.exe"] -. "cleanStages" .-> gone((removed)) ``` - **PATH is edited once.** It is edited only on the launch that creates `bin\`. If the user removes the entry, it stays removed. - **No extra disk use.** The hard link uses no space, and an update only moves the link. If a hard link is not possible, the app copies the exe instead. - **Safe while the CLI runs.** If a terminal is still running the old link, the app renames it to `*.old` (Windows allows renaming a running exe) and deletes it on a later launch. - **Outside `$INSTDIR`.** The installer stops every process that runs from the install directory. A link there would kill open TUI sessions on every update. - **Existing installs win.** The entry goes at the end of the user PATH, so a curl, npm or winget `opencode` that is already on PATH keeps priority. ## PATH editing `cli-path.ts` makes a one-time call to Windows PowerShell off the startup path. It reads the raw registry value so `%USERPROFILE%` entries stay unexpanded and `REG_EXPAND_SZ` is kept. Then it broadcasts `WM_SETTINGCHANGE` so Explorer picks up the change: ```powershell $key = [Microsoft.Win32.Registry]::CurrentUser.CreateSubKey('Environment') $entries = @(([string]$key.GetValue('Path', '', 'DoNotExpandEnvironmentNames')) -split ';' | Where-Object { $_ }) if ($entries -contains $directory) { exit 0 } $key.SetValue('Path', (($entries + $directory) -join ';'), 'ExpandString') [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('OPENCODE_PATH_REFRESH', $null, 'User') # broadcasts WM_SETTINGCHANGE ``` - This avoids `setx`, which cuts PATH at 1024 characters, and `[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('Path', …)`, which rewrites PATH as `REG_SZ`. - A real uninstall (not an update) removes the PATH entry and `bin\` in `customUnInstall`. A reinstall then adds them again.

prs.title: fix(acp): forward session title updates to ACP clients via session_info_update
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #21013

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

The ACP protocol defines `session_info_update` as a valid `SessionUpdate` notification with `title` and `updatedAt` fields, but the OpenCode ACP agent never emitted it.

`Session.setTitle()` (called from `session/prompt.ts` after the first assistant turn generates a title) fires a `session.updated` bus event via `SyncEvent.run(Event.Updated, { sessionID, info: { title } })`. The `handleEvent` switch in `acp/agent.ts` only handled three event types — `permission.asked`, `message.part.updated`, and `message.part.delta` — so the title update was silently dropped and ACP clients never learned the session title had changed.

The fix adds a `case "session.updated"` that:
1. Looks up the session via `sessionManager.tryGet(props.sessionID)` — skips events for sessions not owned by this ACP connection
2. Guards on `props.info.title` being non-empty — avoids spamming clients on unrelated session patches (e.g. `time.updated` touches)
3. Calls `connection.sessionUpdate({ sessionId, update: { sessionUpdate: "session_info_update", title, updatedAt } })`

### How did you verify your code works?

- `cd packages/opencode && bun run typecheck` passes with no errors
- Traced the event path: `Session.setTitle()` → `patch()` → `SyncEvent.run(Event.Updated, ...)` → `handleEvent("session.updated")` → `connection.sessionUpdate(session_info_update)`
- `SessionInfoUpdate` and the `"session_info_update"` literal are both present in `@agentclientprotocol/sdk@0.16.1`

prs.title: fix(app): keep app shortcuts working inside the browser pane
prs.body:
## Why

When a web page in the built-in browser pane has keyboard focus, app shortcuts stop working. ⌘⇧R (toggle review), ⌘K (palette), ⌘1–9, ⌘W and custom keybinds all go to the page. The page is its own Electron `WebContentsView`. Its `before-input-event` handler only claimed F5, Escape while inspecting, ⌘⇧C, ⌘L and the zoom keys, and only the main window's renderer runs the command system.

Claiming every registered app keybind synchronously in `before-input-event` would steal shortcuts that web apps inside the browser pane handle themselves — for example, Google Docs, Notion, Linear, or a dev-server app using `⌘K`, `⌘P`, `⌘/`, or `⌘B` via `event.preventDefault()`.

## What Changes

Shortcuts in a focused browser page now follow a **page first, app second** model (matching VS Code's webview shortcut handling), while keeping browser-reserved tab/window chords synchronous in main:

1. **Reserved chords in main (`before-input-event`)**: The existing pane chords (`F5`, `Escape` while inspecting, `⌘⇧C`, `⌘L`, zoom) plus browser-reserved tab and window chords (`⌘T`, `⌘W`, `⌘N`, `⌘1–9`, `⌘⌥←/→`, and `Ctrl+Tab` / `Ctrl+Shift+Tab`, when registered as active app keybinds) are intercepted synchronously in `before-input-event` with `event.preventDefault()` and forwarded immediately to the app renderer. The page never sees them.
2. **Page-first app chords**: Every other active app keybind that is not page-owned is recorded as a pending shortcut in `before-input-event` and delivered to the page normally. An in-page `keydown` listener running in an isolated world (`Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument` + `Runtime.addBinding` on `opencode-browser-shortcuts`, attached to the main frame and every attached `iframe` target) appends a `{ once: true }` bubble listener on `window` plus a `setTimeout(..., 0)` fallback for pages that call `stopPropagation()`. After the page's handlers finish, it reports `event.defaultPrevented` back to main. If `defaultPrevented` is `false` and the report matches the pending `before-input-event` `keyDown` within 1s, main focuses the app window and forwards the shortcut to `#browser-panel`.
3. **Page-owned chords**: Clipboard (`⌘C`, `⌘X`, `⌘V`, `⌘⇧V`), select all (`⌘A`), undo/redo (`⌘Z`, `⌘⇧Z`, `Ctrl+Y` off macOS), find (`⌘F`, `⌘G`, `⌘⇧G`), reload (`⌘R`), history (`⌘[`, `⌘]`), text caret movement/deletion (`⌘/Ctrl` + arrows, `Backspace`, `Delete`, `Home`, `End`), and macOS Emacs bindings (`Ctrl+A`, `Ctrl+B`, `Ctrl+E`, …) are never forwarded, even if a page does not call `preventDefault()`.

| Chord while a page has focus (⌘ = Ctrl on Windows/Linux) | Owner |
| --- | --- |
| `⌘T`, `⌘W`, `⌘N`, `⌘1–9`, `⌘⌥←/→`, `Ctrl+Tab`, `Ctrl+Shift+Tab` | **App (reserved in main)** while registered: intercepted in `before-input-event`; `⌘W` closes the browser tab (`browser.close`), not the session |
| `⌘⇧R`, `⌘K`, `⌘P`, `⌘⇧P`, `⌘\`, `⌘,`, `Ctrl+\``, any other custom keybind | **Page first, App second**: page receives the key first; if it does not call `preventDefault()`, main forwards it to the app |
| `⌘C` `⌘X` `⌘V` `⌘⇧V` `⌘A` `⌘Z` `⌘⇧Z` (and `Ctrl+Y` off macOS) | **Page** (never forwarded) |
| `⌘F` `⌘G` `⌘⇧G`, `⌘R`, `⌘[` `⌘]` | **Page** (never forwarded) |
| `⌘L`, `⌘⇧C`, `F5`, `Escape` (inspecting), `⌘=` / `⌘+` / `⌘-` / `⌘0` | **Pane** (unchanged, synchronous in main) |
| `⌘/Ctrl` + arrows, `Backspace`, `Delete`, `Home`, `End` | **Page** (caret movement and selection) |
| `Control` + letter on macOS (`Ctrl+B`, `Ctrl+E`, …) | **Page** (Cocoa/Emacs text bindings, even though `Ctrl+B` is a default app keybind) |
| Plain typing, `Shift`, `Alt/Option` chords, `Tab` | **Page** |

## Shortcut Hand-off

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant R as App renderer
  participant M as Main (browser pane)
  participant P as Page WebContentsView (isolated world)
  R->>M: browser.pane.shortcuts({ chords }) whenever keybinds change
  alt Reserved chord (⌘W, ⌘T, ⌘N, ⌘1–9, ⌘⌥←/→, Ctrl+Tab)
    P->>M: before-input-event keyDown
    M->>P: event.preventDefault()
    M->>R: focus app, event { type: "shortcut", ... }
    R->>R: dispatch keydown on #browser-panel → command registry
  else Page-first app chord (⌘K, ⌘⇧R, ⌘P, ...)
    P->>M: before-input-event keyDown (records pendingShortcut)
    M->>P: allow keyDown into page
    P->>P: page capture & bubble listeners run
    P->>M: Runtime.bindingCalled({ ..., defaultPrevented })
    M->>M: pageShortcut(): !defaultPrevented && matches pending <= 1s
    opt Unhandled by page
      M->>R: focus app, event { type: "shortcut", ... }
      R->>R: dispatch keydown on #browser-panel → command registry
    end
  end
```

- The SDK's `ctx.keybinds` gets `chords()`: the palette's chord plus every enabled command's effective chord, already resolved (`mod` → `⌘` or `Ctrl`). It is empty while the app has keybinds suspended.
- `appShortcut()` (`gui-extensions/src/browser/shortcuts.ts`) classifies a chord into `"reserved"`, `"page"`, or `undefined`.
- `listenPageShortcuts()` runs inside each frame's isolated world (`opencode-browser-shortcuts`) so page scripts cannot call the binding directly or spoof shortcuts, and `pageShortcut()` in main consumes the single `pendingShortcut` recorded by `before-input-event` (within 1s) so a page cannot double-dispatch or synthesize shortcuts.
- Forwarded shortcuts dispatch a `keydown` on `<aside id="browser-panel">`, so scoped commands (`⌘W` → close browser tab) and `editable` commands work as if pressed in the pane.

## Scope

This only affects the browser pane's `WebContentsView`; the main window's keyboard handling is unchanged. A forwarded shortcut moves keyboard focus to the app when the page leaves it unhandled (or when it is a reserved browser chord).

## Verification

```sh
cd packages/gui-extensions && bun test src/browser/shortcuts.test.ts src/browser/connection.test.ts
cd packages/app && bun test --conditions=solid --isolate --preload ./happydom.ts src/shell/commands/
cd packages/gui-extensions && bun typecheck
cd packages/app && bun typecheck
cd packages/desktop && bun typecheck
bun script/sdk-docs.ts
bun run lint:changed origin/beta
cd packages/app && PLAYWRIGHT_STORYBOOK_PORT=6226 bun run test:components -- component-tests/browser-pane-restore.spec.ts -g "lets a focused page handle" --repeat-each=3
```

- `shortcuts.test.ts` covers `"reserved"`, `"page"`, and `undefined` (page-owned) classification across macOS and Windows/Linux, plus `pageShortcut()` validation (`defaultPrevented: false` forwards, `defaultPrevented: true` stays with the page, mismatched chord or `>1s` stale keyDown is rejected).
- Component story in `browser-pane-restore.spec.ts`: `"lets a focused page handle ⌘K first and hands unhandled and reserved shortcuts to the pane"` wires an embedded `<iframe>` page with `before-input-event` + `listenPageShortcuts` + `pageShortcut`, verifies that an input calling `preventDefault()` on `⌘K` keeps it without opening the command palette, a plain input leaving `⌘K` unhandled triggers the app command palette, and reserved `⌘W` is claimed before the page sees it and closes the browser tab rather than the session.
- **To try in the next beta build:** open a page with its own `⌘K` handler (e.g. a docs site or web app with a command menu) in the browser pane and press `⌘K` to confirm the page's menu opens instead of the app's; open a plain page or focus a plain input and press `⌘K` or `⌘⇧R` to confirm the app's command palette / review toggle runs; press `⌘W` inside any page to confirm the browser tab closes while the session stays open; and check that `⌘C`/`⌘V`/`⌘A`/`⌘Z`, `Ctrl+A`/`Ctrl+E`, and `⌥`/`⌘`+arrows still edit text in page inputs.

prs.title: feat(browser-extension): add OpenCode Browser, an extension agents control over MCP
prs.body:
## What this is

OpenCode Browser is a Chromium extension (Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera, Vivaldi, Chromium, Helium, Arc) that lets AI agents use the user's real browser through the `browse` MCP tools: open and drive tabs with Playwright, take screenshots, capture network traffic, record, and hand off to the user for logins, 2FA, and payments. It has no chat UI; agents control it.

```
agent ── browse MCP (stdio) ── relay (127.0.0.1:19988) ── WebSocket ── extension ── chrome.debugger ── tabs
```

- `packages/browser-extension` – the extension: relay link, agent tab groups (collapsed, at the start of the tab strip), idle agent tabs closing after 10 minutes, a toolbar button that lets agents use the current tab (or stops them), an in-page handoff banner, and a status page (also the options page).
- `packages/browser-extension/cli` – the npm package `opencode-browser-cli` (own lockfile, outside the workspace): the relay, the `browse` MCP server, the `opencode-browser` CLI, and setup. It is Browser Control (anomalyco/browser-control 8c80ac2, MIT) ported in: renamed, on port 19988, accepting only OpenCode Browser's extension IDs.
- `execute` uses `patchright-core` (Playwright's API without enabling CDP's `Runtime` domain, which pages can detect), and agent input is human-like by default (curved mouse paths, paced keys, gliding scroll).
- Releasing is manual for now (`npm publish` in `cli/`, `bun run package` for the store zip); see the package README.

## Install, and why there's no pairing

```sh
npx opencode-browser-cli install
```

This installs the CLI, adds the `browse` MCP server to opencode's global config, and copies the extension. If an unpacked build is already connected and older, it reloads it and checks the reload took effect. It then reports which browsers and profiles have the extension, and opens the Chrome Web Store listing when none does.

There's nothing to pair: the extension connects to the local relay, which only accepts OpenCode Browser's extension IDs (store `mfnicocicmmlkpjnaffgihfjhdgjkdjg`, unpacked `afeafocngkodbmaipcngoamamfmekgfo`).

## How to test

1. `cd packages/browser-extension/cli && bun install && bun run build && node dist/cli.mjs install`
2. Load `packages/browser-extension/dist` unpacked (Developer mode → Load unpacked), or let `install` reload an already loaded copy. Its status page says Connected once an agent uses the tools.
3. From an opencode session (restart it so it picks up the `browse` MCP server):
   - `session_new`
   - `execute` with `await page.goto("https://news.ycombinator.com"); return page.title()`
   - `execute` with `return (await page.screenshot()).length`
   - `session_list`

   A new agent tab group appears at the top of the tab strip.
4. Click the toolbar button on one of your own tabs; the badge shows ON. `status` lists it as `owner=user` with its `tab=` id, for `session_adopt({ tabId })`. Click again to take the tab back.
5. `opencode-browser status` shows the relay, the extension (with its build and origin), and every tab agents can use. `~/.local/share/opencode-browser/logs/relay.log` has the details.

## What was removed, and why

Earlier revisions of this PR also had a side panel:
- a chat client for the opencode server, with a session picker;
- multi-server pairing (a connect page redeeming `opencode pair` codes);
- a per-prompt "browser context" message and a "share tab" strip;
- site scripts, browsing-history and tab-request tools, which needed approval prompts in the panel.

All of that is gone. The extension is now only the piece agents control over MCP, which keeps it small (the built extension is about 90 KB, with no UI framework) and its permissions minimal.

Removed with it:
- the `sidePanel`, `userScripts`, `contextMenus`, `activeTab`, `nativeMessaging`, `downloads` and `webNavigation` permissions, and the optional history/bookmarks/topSites/sessions permissions;
- the keyboard shortcut, the native messaging host and the opencode plugin;
- the `@opencode/ui`, `@opencode/session-ui`, `@opencode/client`, Solid and Tailwind dependencies;
- the tag-triggered publish workflow.

`install` cleans up what earlier versions set up.

## Fixed: relay crash on oversized messages

Reported with Browser Control (CLI 0.8.3, extension 0.0.25): the relay crashed with `unhandled RangeError: Max payload size exceeded (WS_ERR_UNSUPPORTED_MESSAGE_LENGTH)` and kept crashing until the extension was reloaded.

Cause: `ws` reports an oversized frame as an `error` event on the socket. The relay had no listener for it, so Node killed the process.

Fix:
- The relay accepts messages up to 256 MiB, as Playwright does.
- It logs socket and HTTP server errors instead of crashing.
- The extension fails a single command whose result is too large, instead of sending it.

Checked on an isolated relay: a 240 MB CDP result passes, and a 260 MB client message gets a 1009 close while the relay stays up.

Also fixed while stripping it down: tab-capture recordings stopped after the first chunk, because the worker never answered the recording page's chunk messages.

## Verification

- Typecheck (extension and CLI), lint and build pass.
- Clean headless Chrome: the extension loads, the status page connects, the worker logs no errors, and the payload tests above pass.
- In Helium:
  - `install`: detection, reload with the build check, and an idempotent second run.
  - Through the `browse` MCP tools: `session_new`, `execute` (navigation, locators), a screenshot, `session_list`, a CDP recording and `session_delete`.
- Not exercised end to end: a tab-capture recording, which needs a real toolbar click on the tab.

### Issue for this PR

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement

### What does this PR do?

When the service registers as `http://0.0.0.0:<port>` (or IPv6 `::`), CLI clients probed that URL verbatim. With an HTTP proxy set and the wildcard not in `no_proxy`, the proxy answered 502 and the service looked unhealthy.

This change adds shared `loopbackURL()` and uses it for Effect/Promise probes, `baseUrl`, PTY handoff, and desktop connect so local clients hit `127.0.0.1` / `::1`. Registration can still advertise the wildcard for LAN/`opencode pair`.

prs.title: refactor(ai): type each protocol's provider metadata round-trip
prs.body:
## Why the change

Each protocol wrote its own provider metadata onto stream events through an untyped `Record<string, unknown>` and later read it back with `isRecord(x) && typeof x.signature === "string"`, so a typo on either side was invisible until a signature silently failed to round-trip; now one schema per protocol makes writer and reader agree at compile time.

## Special things to note

- **No behaviour change.** Every reader was traced and probed against `v2`: `undefined`/`null`/array/string metadata → `undefined`, `{}` → `{}`, unknown keys ignored, malformed fields dropped one at a time. Per-field leniency was already the behaviour (each `typeof` check was independent), so fields use `lenient` rather than `Schema.optional`.
- Bedrock declares its own two-field struct rather than importing Anthropic's — no protocol imports another protocol's internals today, and Anthropic's struct carries three fields Bedrock never writes.
- Raw `{ [key]: usage }` passthroughs stay raw: they forward each provider's usage object for consumers and are never read back. Modelling them would duplicate every provider's usage schema or change the wire shape.

## Change outline

One factory in `shared.ts` replaces the identical one-liner in three protocols and the ad hoc readers in five:

```ts
ProviderShared.providerMetadata(schema) → {
  write: (key, value: Type) => ({ [key]: value })                  // typo → TS2561
  read:  (metadata, key) => Type | undefined                       // decodeUnknownOption, sync
}
```

Each protocol declares the slice it publishes under its `providerMetadataKey`:

```diff
 packages/ai/src/protocols/
 ├── shared.ts
+│     providerMetadata(schema)                    # write / read pair
 ├── anthropic-messages.ts
-│     providerMetadata(key, Record<string, unknown>)
-│     signatureFromMetadata(), redactedDataFromMetadata()      # isRecord + typeof
+│     AnthropicProviderMetadata = providerMetadata(Struct({ signature, redactedData, blockType, result, stopSequence }))
 ├── bedrock-converse.ts
-│     providerMetadata(), reasoningSignature(), reasoningRedactedData()   # copy of Anthropic's
+│     BedrockProviderMetadata = providerMetadata(Struct({ signature, redactedData }))
 ├── gemini.ts
-│     providerMetadata(), thoughtSignature() narrowing
+│     GeminiProviderMetadata = providerMetadata(Struct({ thoughtSignature, promptFeedback }))
 ├── open-responses.ts
-│     providerMetadata(state, Record<string, unknown>)
-│     itemID() narrowing
+│     export providerMetadata = providerMetadata(Struct({ itemId, phase, reasoningEncryptedContent, responseId, serviceTier }))
 ├── openai-chat.ts
-│     reasoningField(), reasoningDetails() reading providerMetadata?.[key]?.x
+│     OpenAIChatProviderMetadata = providerMetadata(Struct({ reasoningField, reasoningDetails }))
 └── utils/responses-compaction.ts
-      { [key]: { itemId, reasoningEncryptedContent } }          # raw literal
+      OpenResponses.providerMetadata.write(key, { itemId, reasoningEncryptedContent })
```

Readers decode each part once and read typed fields:

```diff
 lowerMessages → reasoning part
-  signature    = part.encrypted ?? signatureFromMetadata(part.providerMetadata, key)
-  redactedData = redactedDataFromMetadata(part.providerMetadata, key)
+  metadata     = AnthropicProviderMetadata.read(part.providerMetadata, key)
+  signature    = part.encrypted ?? metadata?.signature
+  redactedData = metadata?.redactedData
```

`openai-chat` and `open-responses` previously read the same part several times per lowering pass (free property reads); they now decode once and derive from the result, so the decode runs once per part (~0.3 µs).

### Tests

Existing round-trips cover the change: thinking signatures, redacted thinking, Bedrock redacted, Gemini thought signatures, Responses replay / `itemId` / encrypted reasoning, OpenAI `reasoningField` / `reasoningDetails`. `packages/ai`: 1400 pass, `bun typecheck` clean. `packages/core`: `bun typecheck` clean. `bun run check`: 35/35.

### Follow-up

`open-responses.ts` has a strict message-level `MessageMetadata` decode (rejects with `InvalidRequest`) alongside the new lenient part-level struct, both under the same key with overlapping `itemId`/`phase`. Different policies on purpose; worth a comment or reconciliation in a separate change.

issues.title: Make the connect timeout configurable and expose request-level transport diagnostics

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Two small additions to the HTTP transport:

1. **Make the connect-phase timeout configurable.** `configureHttpDispatcher()` passes `autoSelectFamilyAttemptTimeout` to undici's `connect` but not `timeout`, so a stalled TCP+TLS connect is aborted at undici's 10s default. `httpIdleTimeoutMs` and `retry.provider.timeoutMs` only cover headers/body. A `net.connectTimeoutMs` setting (default 30s) would leave fast networks unchanged.
2. **Expose request-level transport diagnostics.** A connect timeout, a TLS stall, a proxy CONNECT failure and a provider timeout all surface as the same `Request timed out.`, with no phase or error code. An `http_request` extension event (host, status, connect/TLS/TTFB timings, error code) — or at least the phase and duration in the error — would make this diagnosable from an extension.

### Why?

On 1.3.0 (Linux x86_64), `deepseek/deepseek-flash` behind a local proxy fails every request with `Request timed out.` after ~10.5s and retries 3x (~56s total). Direct connectivity is fine: `NO_PROXY=api.deepseek.com` succeeds in ~1.2s, and `curl --noproxy '*'` has ~0.2s TTFB. #11106 described the same root cause; that report was later retracted as a firewall issue, but the missing `connect.timeout` is still there. I am not asking to change the default for everyone — only to make the connect phase configurable.

The exact reproduction and timings are in the fold below.

<details>
<summary>Minimal reproduction (proxy stub, commands, timings)</summary>

A proxy that accepts TCP, answers `CONNECT` with `200`, then stalls the TLS handshake. Save as `stall-tls-proxy.js`:

```js
const net = require("node:net");
net.createServer((socket) => {
  let connected = false;
  socket.on("data", (chunk) => {
    if (!connected && chunk.toString("latin1").startsWith("CONNECT")) {
      connected = true;
      socket.write("HTTP/1.1 200 Connection established\r\n\r\n"); // then never forward
    }
  });
  socket.on("error", () => {});
}).listen(7897, "127.0.0.1");
```

Then:

```bash
node stall-tls-proxy.js &

# 1) connect phase stalls: 4 attempts x ~10.5s + backoff, ~56s total
HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:7897 HTTP_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:7897 \
  pi -ne -p --no-session --model deepseek/deepseek-flash "Reply with OK"

# 2) same proxy, direct for the API host: ~1.2s
HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:7897 HTTP_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:7897 \
  NO_PROXY=api.deepseek.com \
  pi -ne -p --no-session --model deepseek/deepseek-flash "Reply with OK"
```

Observed on 1.3.0, Linux x86_64:

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| (1) | `Request timed out.` x4; 10460–10499 ms per attempt; ~56.2 s total |
| (2) | `OK` in ~1.25 s |
| `HTTPS_PROXY=http://192.0.2.1:7899` (blackhole TCP) | same ~56.2 s as (1) |

`pi -ne` disables every extension, so this is core. Any model works here; the request fails before the provider is reached. `NO_PROXY=api.deepseek.com` and `curl --noproxy '*'` both work, which points at the connect phase, not the provider.

</details>

### How?

- `connect: { ..., timeout: connectTimeoutMs ?? 30_000 }` in `configureHttpDispatcher()`, plus a setting.
- Emit `http_request`, or add timings/error to `after_provider_response`, and a `net.logLevel`.
- `NO_PROXY` already works (#8737), so no separate `noProxy` setting is needed on my side.

Happy to implement this if the shape is acceptable. Version 1.3.0, Linux x86_64.

---

_(Drafted with an AI assistant from my own reproduction notes; I verified the reproduction and timings myself. Happy to rewrite or adjust anything.)_

issues.title: coding-agent: final-settlement hook receives no cancellation signal
issues.body:
### What happened?

My verification extension runs before a completed turn settles. In Pi 1.2.0, `ctx.signal` exists in `agent_end` but is undefined in `agent_before_settle`. A hook that passes this signal to a cancellable wait cannot respond to `session.abort()`: abort waits for the entire hook. This prevents cancelling long verification commands at the final boundary.

### Steps to reproduce

Run the standalone SDK fixture in the next comment with no discovered extensions, skills, context files, themes, tools or live provider. Its only extension returns a synthetic final answer, then awaits `setTimeout(5000, undefined, { signal: ctx.signal })` in `agent_before_settle`. Call `session.abort()` as soon as the hook starts.

Observed on Windows, Node 24.15.0: signal present in `agent_end`, absent in `agent_before_settle`; abort took 5007 ms. No Tesota code is loaded. Related #6234 concerns a hook that ignores cancellation; this hook attempts to respect it but receives no signal.

### Expected behavior

The final boundary exposes a signal that `session.abort()` aborts, so a cooperative verification hook can stop its work before settling.

### Version

@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent 1.2.0 (npm latest checked 2026-10-14).

issues.title: Public tool-presentation API or built-in one-line tool mode
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Either:
- A public, display-only API so an extension can control the presentation of **all** tool rows, including built-ins, MCP, codemode, and custom extension tools.
- A built-in one-line mode showing the tool name, a short call summary, and running/success/error status, with full details available on demand.

For the API option, I want to build an extension with a shortcut that cycles between full output, a compact preview, and a one-line view. It should work for live calls and resumed history without replacing tool execution or patching Pi internals.

### Why?

Even with Ctrl+O collapsed, commands, diffs, and tool-result previews take up most of my screen and push the conversation out of view. The minimal-mode example helps with built-ins, but does not cover every MCP or custom tool.

This is only a display preference. Tool execution, model context, and stored results should stay unchanged.

### How? (optional)

A global tool-presentation hook would let extensions handle this without adding UI preferences to the core. A built-in one-line mode would also solve my problem.

Related: #5137, #9638, and #10011. I know these requests overlap; is either approach something maintainers would support?

issues.title: Enable the PowerShell tool by default on Windows

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
On Windows, the `powershell` tool is native and is the better default shell. The default `bash` tool needs Git Bash or another `bash.exe`, and it often breaks in ways that are hard to fix from inside the session (paths, quoting, encodings, WSL vs Git Bash mismatches). Today the `powershell` tool is opt-in, so most Windows users get `bash` unless they change `defaultTools`.

Proposed: on Windows, enable `powershell` by default. `bash` stays enabled as a fallback. Together with #11049 (prefer PowerShell when both are enabled), the model would use PowerShell by default and only fall back to bash when needed.

On macOS and Linux nothing changes, since the `powershell` tool is Windows-only and is not enabled there.

Workarounds that work today (thanks to @davidbrai on #11049): set `"defaultTools": ["-bash", "+powershell"]` in `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`, or add "Prefer the powershell tool over bash for shell commands on this machine." to `~/.pi/agent/APPEND_SYSTEM.md`. The goal of this issue is different: change the defaults for everyone, so Windows users get the setup that fits Pi's values without opting in.

Co-Authored-By: pi (anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5 via openrouter) <noreply@pi.dev>

When both `bash` and `powershell` are enabled on Windows, the model often picks `bash`. On Windows, the default `bash` tool runs Git Bash (or another `bash.exe` on PATH), which is not native to Windows and causes frequent problems (quoting, paths, encodings, missing tools). I then have to remind the model to use PowerShell.

Current prompt (`packages/coding-agent/src/core/system-prompt.ts`) when both are selected:

> Use bash or PowerShell for file operations like listing, searching, and finding files

This is neutral, so the model has no reason to prefer PowerShell.

Proposed: when both are enabled, prefer PowerShell. Users can still disable the tool or override the prompt, but the default should avoid the problem for everyone on Windows.

issues.title: waitForIdle() resolves during settled-handler compaction before deferred continuation
issues.body:
### What happened?

In SDK 1.1.0, `waitForIdle()` registered during an active request resolves while an awaited `agent_settled` extension is still finishing `ctx.compact()`, before its deferred continuation runs. The outer `prompt()` correctly waits for both requests. An SDK host using the idle promise can therefore report completion too soon.

### Steps to reproduce

Run the standalone local HTTP reproduction in the comment below with `node http-repro.mjs idle`. It loads only one inline extension (`noExtensions: true`) and uses Pi's real OpenAI-compatible streaming provider against localhost.

1. Register `waitForIdle()` during request 1.
2. In a one-time `agent_settled` handler, await `ctx.compact()` with an extension-provided summary, then `pi.sendMessage(..., { triggerTurn: true })`.
3. Observe: `request:1 → idle-resolved → compact-complete → continuation-queued → request:2 → prompt-resolved`.

Without compaction, the waiter correctly resolves after request 2. Both cases reproduced 5/5 times.

### Expected behavior

A waiter already registered during the run should remain pending through its awaited settlement handler and deferred continuation.

Related: #5886. Unlike #10388, this concerns an existing idle waiter; no nested `prompt()` promise is awaited.

### Version

`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@1.1.0`, fresh npm install; Node 26.5.0, macOS.

## What happened?

The built-in `powershell` tool (pi 0.84.3, Windows) always falls back to Windows PowerShell 5.1 in **interactive** mode, even though PowerShell 7 (`pwsh.exe`) is installed and on PATH. The same tool correctly uses `pwsh` in `-p` (print) mode.

Also tested: removing the local extension dir, bisecting npm packages, and `pi -ne` do not change the interactive result; the `-p` result (pwsh) is stable across all variants.

## Expected behavior

Per `docs/windows.md`, the tool "runs commands through pwsh.exe when available" — i.e., `pwsh` should be used in interactive mode too.

issues.title: Let prepareArguments see (and repair) tool-call arguments that failed to parse

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
**Version:** pi 1.3.0

Claude Sonnet 5 sometimes writes `"oldText">` instead of `"oldText": "` in `edit` calls:

```
{"path": "…/logic.ts", "edits": [{"oldText">export function stagePaths(entries: readonly DirtyEntry[]): string[] {
```

pi turns this into `arguments: {}` plus `argumentsError`, and the model gets `Invalid arguments for tool "edit": Expected ':' after property name in JSON at position 120`. In my session logs, 31 `edit` calls failed on malformed arguments between 4 and 18 Oct (17 of them on 18 Oct), 14 with exactly this shape. Once it starts in a session it tends to repeat, and every retry re-sends the whole `oldText`.

I wanted to handle it in an extension, but there is no point to hook in:
- `prepareArguments` receives only `{}`. The raw text exists only inside the `argumentsError` string, and `prepareToolCallArguments` keeps `argumentsError`, so `validateToolArguments` throws whatever `prepareArguments` returns.
- The failure becomes an `immediate` result, so no `tool_call` / `tool_result` handler runs, not even to add a hint.

What would help, in my order of preference:
1. Pass the raw text and the parse error to `prepareArguments` (e.g. `prepareArguments(args, { rawArguments, argumentsError })`), and let a non-`undefined` return clear the error.
2. Or emit an event on validation failure, so an extension can append a hint.
3. Or have pi's own error text name the `"key">` shape.

I'm not asking for `repairJson` to fix `"key">` blindly: the value after `>` is unquoted, so where it ends is a guess.

Related: https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/7607 (validation runs before any hook), https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11095 (another parse-path shape in 1.3.0).

The log analysis was done with my coding agent; its details are in the first comment, labeled as AI-written.

issues.title: Transcript never renders user-attached images (clipboard paste) — attachments reach the model, no inline preview; tool-result images do render

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## Summary

Images attached via clipboard paste (`Ctrl+V` → temp file path inserted by `handleClipboardPaste`) are correctly attached and sent to the model, but **the transcript never renders them inline** — the user only sees the `/tmp/pi-clipboard-<uuid>.jpg` path as plain text. Meanwhile, images returned by **tool results** render inline correctly in the same session/environment, so the Kitty rendering pipeline itself works.

Looking at the code, `UserMessageComponent` has no image handling at all, so pasted/attached user images are never drawn — it looks like an unimplemented feature rather than a broken pipeline.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Copy an image to the clipboard on Wayland/KDE (e.g. screenshot, or `wl-copy < file.jpg` — clipboard holds `image/png` or `image/jpeg` only).
2. In the interactive TUI, press `Ctrl+V` (`app.clipboard.pasteImage`) → the editor shows `/tmp/pi-clipboard-<uuid>.jpg` (attachment registered by the paste handler).
3. Press Enter to send.

**Expected:** the sent message renders the attached image inline (respecting `terminal.showImages`, Kitty-graphics terminals).

**Actual:** the transcript shows only the plain-text temp path; no image is drawn, before or after send.

## Evidence

- Session `.jsonl` shows the attachment actually reached the model: the user message contains `{"type":"image","data":"/9j/…"}` (full JPEG base64) and the model reacted to it.
- Raw TTY capture (`script -q`) of the same session: **no image APC is emitted for the user message**, while in the same session a `read` tool over an image file produced a tool result with content `['text','image']` and **did** emit a Kitty APC (`f=100` with PNG payload — the Photon transcoder converting JPEG → PNG works fine).
- `dist/modes/interactive/components/user-message.js` has zero image handling; only `ToolExecutionComponent` renders images (`result.content.filter(c => c.type === "image")`).

## Environment

- pi-coding-agent 1.2.0 (bundled by gentle-shell 4.3.0)
- Terminal: Ghostty 1.3.1 (Kitty graphics confirmed working)
- Multiplexer: herdr 0.9.5 with kitty graphics passthrough enabled (validated by rendering a raw Kitty APC in a pane)
- Wayland / KDE, Linux (Arch)
- Settings: `terminal.showImages` default (true, no overrides); detection correctly resolves `images: "kitty"` via `TERM_PROGRAM`.

## Request

Render user-message image attachments inline in the transcript (same path/tooling as tool-result images), or at minimum show a proper inline attachment indicator instead of the raw temp path. Happy to provide more captures if useful.

### What happened?

In Pi Durable, reading an image through codemode loses the image:

```js
const result = await tools.read({ path: "pixel.png" });
text({ type: typeof result, value: result });
// {"type":"string","value":""}
```

2. Put a valid PNG in the environment's working directory.
3. Execute the script above through codemode, then try `image(await tools.read({ path: "pixel.png" }))`.
4. Compare with a direct `read` of the same file.

Verified with the published SDK and a scripted faux provider in a network-disabled container, without application code, user-authored extensions, or credentials. Direct image reads, nested text-file reads, and `image(validImageBlock)` work.

### Expected behavior

A supported way to pass a local image from `tools.read()` to `image()`, as in the coding-agent fix for #10251. I'm not asking to change the general text-only behavior of schema-less tools.

### Version

@earendil-works/pi-durable and pi-codemode 1.3.0; Node.js 24.22.0; Linux. Relevant source also inspected at main commit 4954d760.

issues.title: openai-completions: a mid-stream drop reported as "The operation was aborted" is not retried

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## Summary

With pi 1.3.0 in print mode, an `openai-completions` stream through OpenRouter (`google/gemini-3.8-flash`) sometimes ends 12 to 28 s into a response with:

```
stopReason: "error"
errorMessage: "The operation was aborted"
```

pi does not retry this. `isRetryableAssistantError` (pi-ai `utils/retry.js`) returns `false` for that text, but `true` for the same class of transport fault when it is worded `terminated`, `fetch failed` or `socket hang up`. So one dropped stream ends the whole agent turn.

## Evidence

- 4 of about 70 requests in one session hit it (Brain and worker sessions alike). Durations at failure: 12.6 s, 13.5 s, 13.8 s, 15.1 s, 28.0 s.
- The caller did not abort anything. A `--require` preload patched `AbortController.prototype.abort` to log every call with its stack. No abort fired before the error. The first abort logged is the OpenAI SDK stream's own cleanup (`_Stream.iterator` → `messages.return`) after the loop in `openai-completions` had already thrown.
- `options.signal.aborted` was false (the message has `stopReason: "error"`, not `"aborted"`).

## Expected

A stream that ends with this error, when the request signal was not aborted, is a transient transport fault and is retried under `settings.retry`, like `terminated`.

## Possible fix

In `isRetryableAssistantError`, or where `openai-completions` maps the error, treat an AbortError-shaped message as retryable when the caller's signal is not aborted.

## Environment

pi 1.3.0 (npm global), Node 25.8.1, macOS 15 (Darwin 24.6), provider `openrouter`, api `openai-completions`.

issues.title: DeepSeek: every request times out at ~10.5s on Linux while curl succeeds (undici 10s connect.timeout not configurable)

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## What happened?

On Linux (remote server, user in `/home/zhj`), Pi 1.3.0 calling DeepSeek (`deepseek` provider, `openai-completions`) fails on **every** request with `Request timed out.` after a constant ~10.5 s (JSON log: 10526 / 10496 / 10497 / 10496 ms), then auto-retries 3× with 2/4/8 s backoff (~56 s total). It worked before and broke suddenly.

The same endpoint works fine from the same machine with curl:

- `curl --http1.1` to `api.deepseek.com`: TTFB 0.22 s, full stream ~1.02 s, HTTP 200, `[DONE]` received.
- `strace` shows Pi connecting to `119.36.225.121:443` / `112.84.131.227:443` with `getsockopt(...SO_ERROR...)=0` → **TCP connect succeeds**.
- DNS, API key (`ready`), and a Python HTTPS probe (HTTP 401 as expected) are all fine.

Ruled out: thinking on/off, tools on/off, simplified system prompt, `models.json` (none), proxy env vars (none).

## Root cause

The ~10.5 s constant is undici's default **connect timeout**. In `dist/core/http-dispatcher.js`, `configureHttpDispatcher()` builds an `undici.EnvHttpProxyAgent` with `headersTimeout`/`bodyTimeout` taken from `httpIdleTimeoutMs`, but the `connect` option only sets `autoSelectFamilyAttemptTimeout: 2000` and never sets `connect.timeout`. undici's `buildConnector` (`lib/core/connect.js`) then falls back to:

```js
timeout = timeout == null ? 10e3 : timeout   // 10 s
```

That 10 s cap covers the whole TCP+TLS connect phase, so a stalled **TLS handshake** (TCP already established, per `SO_ERROR=0`) is aborted at ~10 s. undici's error (`connect ... timeout: 10000ms`) matches the SDK's `/timed? ?out/i` classifier and surfaces as `Request timed out.`. `httpIdleTimeoutMs`/`retry.provider.timeoutMs` only govern header/body waits, so they can't affect this. curl (libcurl/OpenSSL) succeeding while Pi's TLS stack stalls points to a TLS-implementation-specific handshake stall against DeepSeek's endpoint.

## Steps to reproduce

1. On Linux, run Pi 1.3.0 with a DeepSeek key (`/login deepseek`).
2. Send any prompt with `deepseek/deepseek-flash`.
3. Every request errors with `Request timed out.` at ~10.5 s and retries 3×.
4. In parallel, `curl --http1.1 https://api.deepseek.com/...` returns in ~1 s.

## Expected behavior

Either connect successfully (like curl) or fail fast with the real error (connect vs TLS vs headers vs body). The connect-phase timeout should be configurable (e.g. via `httpIdleTimeoutMs` or a dedicated setting) instead of silently inheriting undici's 10 s default.

## Version

1.3.0 (Linux x86_64, binary at `/home/zhj/.pi/agent/bin/pi`)

issues.title: `transformMessages` + `isSameModel === false` thinking block normalization interacts poorly with `requiresReasoningContentOnAssistantMessages` compat flag

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What happened?

When the user switches models, `transformMessages` will normalize non-redacted/plain-text thinking content [by inlining it in to the assistant message content](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/927e98068cda276bf9188f4774fb927c89823388/packages/ai/src/api/transform-messages.ts#L98-L114), with no delimiters or control tokens, in an attempt to be provider agnostic.

But this strips the reasoning content from the assistant message block before it arrives at the checks around `requiresReasoningContentOnAssistantMessages`. This means that if you switch from any previous reasoning model to a reasoning model with `requiresReasoningContentOnAssistantMessages: true`, the historical message prefill is a little wonky. Specifically, [the actual attached reasoning content ends up being an empty string](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/927e98068cda276bf9188f4774fb927c89823388/packages/ai/src/api/openai-completions.ts#L1000-L1004). This doesn't fundamentally *break* anything, but in my experience, it *does* make the model a wee bit confused about what's going on (or at least it makes `glm-5.2-fp8` via vLLM a little confused).

### Steps to reproduce

- Use a reasoning model with thinking enabled
- Do some work
- Switch to another model/provider with reasoning enabled and `requiresReasoningContentOnAssistantMessages: true` in its compat configs
- Enable reasoning
- Send a prompt
- Observe the outbound REST messages

### Expected behavior

In the case that reasoning context is available as plaintext, the cross-provider normalization should probably try to remain aware of the destination model's `requiresReasoningContentOnAssistantMessages` configs and adhere to that when possible.

### Version

0.80.2

issues.title: Expose provider retries through an onRetry callback in retryProviderRequest

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Add an optional `onRetry` callback to `retryProviderRequest` in `packages/ai/src/utils/provider-retry.ts`. It fires before each backoff sleep, with the attempt number, the delay, and the error that caused the retry.

### Why?

Provider retries are invisible to callers. A request that succeeded on its third attempt looks the same as one that was simply slow, so I cannot tell whether a 17s turn was one slow call or three failures plus their backoff. I hit this building a run timeline on top of pi, where turn latency was unattributable.

`retryAssistantCall` already exposes this through `RetryCallbacks`, and the harness wires it for compaction and branch summarisation. The provider request path, which is every model turn, has no equivalent.

### How? (optional)

An optional field on `ProviderRetryOptions`, so nothing changes when it is unset. The callback runs inside a try/catch, because an observer that throws would otherwise turn a recoverable provider error into a failed request.

I have it implemented with 5 tests added to `packages/ai/test/provider-retry.test.ts`, and `npm run check` passes. I opened #7647 before reading CONTRIBUTING.md and it was auto-closed. That was my mistake. Happy to reopen it if you approve.

issues.title: coding-agent: make pending setModel safe across session-tree navigation

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?
In Pi 1.3.0, an extension can start `pi.setModel()` and session-tree navigation on the same `AgentSession` concurrently. `setModel()` awaits its authentication check before mutating that session's `sessionManager`; navigation can change the leaf during that await, so the pending model-change entry can be written on the newly selected branch instead of the branch intended when the selection began. The `setModel` closure is bound to its original `AgentSession`; this is a same-session branch race, not a rebind to a replacement session.

### Steps to reproduce
1. From an extension, call `pi.setModel(target)` with an auth check that remains pending.
2. Before auth completes, navigate to another branch in the same session.
3. Let auth complete and inspect the model-change entry / selected model on the resulting branch.

### Expected behavior
A pending model mutation should either complete against the session branch it was intended for or cancel without modifying another navigation state. A lifecycle/synchronization mechanism should make that guarantee observable to extensions.

### Version
Pi 1.3.0

issues.title: cacheWarming "idle" stops silently once an extension handles turn_end and the context holds a custom or compaction message
issues.body:
**What happened?**
With `cacheWarming: "idle"`, the idle warm never fires in our sessions: 507 `cache_warming_decision` events since September, all at `continuationProbability: 1`, none at 0.15. `/session` shows `Inactive (conversation context changed)` right after the run settles.

Cause: `cacheContextIsCurrent` (`core/sdk.js:214-222`) checks each captured message by object identity. When any extension has a `turn_end` handler, `_dispatchTurnEndBoundary` goes on to `_commitBoundaryDrafts`, which calls `_refreshFinalizedContext()` even with no drafts (`core/agent-session.js:492`, `:636`). `sessionEntryToContextMessages` (`core/session-manager.js:179-188`) builds new objects for `custom_message`, `branch_summary` and `compaction` entries on every projection. So `validateRun()` stops the warmer before any decision is emitted. Without a `turn_end` handler, idle warming works.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. `note.ts`: `pi.registerCommand("note", { handler: async () => pi.sendMessage({ customType: "n", content: "x", display: true }) })` plus `pi.on("turn_end", () => {})`.
2. `pi -ne -e note.ts` on an Anthropic model, `cacheWarming: "idle"`. Run `/note`, send one prompt, wait for it to settle.
3. `/session` → `Cache Warming … Inactive (conversation context changed)`.
4. Remove the `turn_end` line → `Decision in 4m …`, and the idle decision fires.

**Expected behavior**
The idle phase compares the prefix the provider saw: compare entry ids, or memoise the projected message per entry (entries don't change after append).

**Version**
1.2.0, Linux. Same symptom as https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10700; related to https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10515.

issues.title: Expose a prompt-composition breakdown in contextUsage (system / tools / messages)

labels.name: last-read
labels.description: A marker label for triaging

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Add an optional prompt-composition breakdown to `contextUsage`.

`get_session_stats` (docs/rpc-commands.md) returns `contextUsage: {tokens, contextWindow, percent}`, and `ctx.getContextUsage()` returns the same three fields. Nothing tells a client how much of that total is the system prompt, the tool schemas, and the messages.

Suggested shape (additive, optional):

```
breakdown?: { system: number; tools: number; messages: number }
```

Values would be estimates from the estimator the footer already uses (`estimateTokens`); `tokens` keeps its current "usage-based when valid" meaning, and `messages` is `tokens - system - tools` so the three add up.

### Why?

I work on PiDeck (Electron workbench that drives pi over RPC); its context panel shows a system / tools / conversation split. Sessions on the DSH runtime get that split from the host (dsh token-meter projects systemTokens / toolsTokens / messageTokens), but pi sessions have nothing to read, so PiDeck currently replays the prompt loadout out of the session file itself (system message `sections`, `toolsAdded` / `toolsRemoved`, compaction `systemMessage`). That re-implements pi's session-format knowledge inside a client and breaks silently when the format changes.

(#6247 asked for a TUI `/context` diagnostics command and was auto-closed; this is the narrower RPC/SDK side of the same need.)

### How? (optional)

`estimateTokens(message)` in `src/core/compaction/compaction.ts` already estimates messages per role, and the projection used by `estimateProjectedContextTokens()` already holds the current system message and the tool declarations, so the three numbers can be derived next to `getContextUsage()` without new estimation logic.

Happy to test against the client, and to send a patch if you like the shape.

---

Drafted with an AI agent (pi running inside PiDeck) at my request.

issues.title: Custom smaller contextWindow + thinking: max_tokens clamped to 1 mid-run, empty response poisons compaction anchor — session stuck in permanent loop

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
## Summary

When a user configures a `contextWindow` smaller than the model's real window (a supported customization — the maintainer position in #6206 is that the configured window is authoritative), a session can enter a **permanent failure loop** with no error and no recovery:

1. `clampMaxTokensToContext()` silently sends `max_tokens: 1` once the estimated input crosses the configured window,
2. the model returns a 1-token empty response whose reported usage **excludes historical thinking tokens** (the thinking budget is forced to 0 on that request) — far below the real context size,
3. `_checkCompaction()` only runs at run boundaries and only reads the *last* assistant message's usage — it sees the artificially low number and never compacts,
4. every subsequent run repeats the cycle: the first request is healthy (clamped against the low anchor), the second request is clamped to 1 again, another empty response, another low anchor. The session is stuck indefinitely.

We hit this in production: **12+ consecutive failed turns** on one session before manual intervention.

## New mechanism: thinking-excluded usage poisons the anchor *downward*

#6340 documented stale usage anchoring the estimate too *high* after compaction. We found the opposite direction, which has worse consequences. Exact numbers from the stuck session (anthropic-messages API, thinking=max):

- Last healthy response (mid-run, `stopReason: toolUse`): `usage.totalTokens = 507,871` (input 402, cacheRead 506,880)
- Next request (context now ~507,994 estimated) → `max_tokens` clamped to 1 → response: `stopReason: stop`, **empty text, output 1 token**, `usage.totalTokens = 364,853` (input 364,852, cacheRead 0)

The 143k delta is the historical thinking content, which the provider no longer bills/counts on a request whose thinking budget is 0. The recorded 364,853 is then used as the estimate anchor for everything that follows — including compaction checks. Since the compaction threshold is `500,000 − 16,384 = 483,616`, every boundary check concludes the context is healthy, while the real context stays at ~508k.

## Why boundary-only checks can't catch it

The real peak (507,871) only ever appears on **mid-run** `toolUse` messages; `_checkCompaction()` never evaluates those (also #6339). Additionally, the gap between the compaction threshold (`contextWindow − 16384`) and the `max_tokens = 1` point (`contextWindow − 4097`) is fixed at **12,287 tokens** — a single tool result can jump over it in one round, so even honest usage may arrive too late for a boundary check.

## Production evidence

- Session A: 12 consecutive empty-response turns across user re-activations; client-side instrumentation logged "run crossed threshold without SDK compaction event" 25 times (observed run max 506,001–507,871 vs threshold 483,616).
- Session B (different user): 4 identical deaths, then spontaneous recovery when one run happened to *end* on a full response whose honest usage finally triggered compaction — confirming recovery is currently a matter of luck.

## Why this is not a duplicate of #6206

#6206 established "the configured window is authoritative" — accepted, and this issue does not re-argue it. The point here is that *within* that philosophy, the mechanisms that should protect the configured window are defeated: (a) the clamp sends `max_tokens: 1` instead of failing, (b) usage under-reporting on thinking-disabled responses hides the real context size, and (c) checks only run at run boundaries against the last message. The user gets no error, no compaction, and no escape.

## Suggested fixes

1. **Floor**: never silently dispatch `max_tokens: 1` (or below a sane minimum). Treat hitting the clamp floor as an overflow condition — surface an error or trigger compaction (same conclusion as #6340).
2. **Anchor**: `estimateContextTokens()` / compaction checks should not trust usage from responses generated with a forced-zero thinking budget (or more generally, usage inconsistent with actual content size).
3. **Timing**: evaluate compaction mid-run between tool rounds, or have run-end checks consider the run's max observed usage (#6339).

## Environment

`pi-ai` / `pi-coding-agent` 0.82.1 (we embed these packages; pi CLI shares the same code path). Model: kimi-coding `k3` (anthropic-messages API), configured `contextWindow` 500,000 (vendor advertises 1,048,576), `maxTokens` 131,072, thinking=max.

Prior art: #6340, #6339, #6265, #6206, #6963.
