issues.title: Anthropic tool calls: corrupted non-ASCII edit arguments are silently accepted (dropped `u` in `\uXXXX` → `\b`/`\f` control chars)
issues.body:
### What happened?

With Claude models, `edit` calls on files containing Korean text fail very often, and occasionally corrupt a file. I have been tracking this for about three weeks. It keeps coming back and costs a lot of retries.

There are two symptoms, usually in the same sessions:

1. **Control characters instead of Korean.** The arguments contain C0 control characters where Korean characters were intended.
2. **Garbage calls.** An `edit` whose `oldText` is a few meaningless characters that exist nowhere in the file. Several in a row can occur.

Both usually fail safely as "Could not find ... oldText". Once, a corrupted `newText` was written to a file and had to be repaired by hand.

### The pattern behind symptom 1

It points to a `\uXXXX` escape whose `u` is missing in the tool-input JSON. When the next hex digit happens to be `b` or `f`, the result is still **valid JSON**: `\b` / `\f` followed by the remaining three hex digits. `JSON.parse` accepts it, so the tool runs with wrong strings instead of returning an error.

Illustration (synthetic): intended `\ub0b4` → emitted `\b0b4` → parsed as U+0008 + `0b4`.

### Evidence

Automated scan of my local session logs (edit arguments only, no file contents):

| Model | edit calls | errors | error rate | args with C0 control chars |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| openai-codex/gpt-6-astra | 398 | 9 | 2.3% | 0 |
| openai-codex/gpt-6-sol | 82 | 5 | 6.1% | 0 |
| xai/grok-4.7 | 27 | 3 | 11% | 0 |
| anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 | 212 | 86 | 40.6% | 15 |
| anthropic/claude-opus-5 | 34 | 20 | 58.8% | 8 |
| anthropic/claude-fable-5-1 | 20 | 8 | 40% | 2 |

- All control characters found in Claude edit arguments are U+0008 (`\b`) or U+000C (`\f`). 848 of 873 are followed by exactly three hex digits.
- An earlier manual classification over 20 days: 52 of 68 failed Opus 5.5 edits had lost their Korean text. GPT, Grok and DeepSeek had none.
- I found no case where `repairJson` turned an invalid escape into a literal backslash, so I don't think the repair path causes this. The corrupted cases are already valid JSON before any repair.

### What I ruled out

- **`eager_input_streaming`:** on vs off, 21 attempts each. One corrupted call in each group.
- **Session length:** I forked an affected session and ran four edits each with the default `edit`, a hash-anchored edit extension, and all extensions loaded. All 12 succeeded. On the same day, the original window failed 3 of 4.
- **Edit tool format:** the hash-anchored edit tool made no difference.
- **Encoding in general:** in the same failing window, shell edits, `write`, and a Node script inside the shell all wrote Korean correctly.

### A context effect

The failures cluster after corrupted strings have been visible in the context. In the original window, the broken calls closely resembled an example string that had just been displayed during analysis. Later, a fresh session reproduced it twice in a row right after reading notes that contained such an example. I also hit the garbage-call symptom about six times today in a long session, after the raw examples had already been removed from those notes, so removing them does not prevent it.

So this looks like a model-side tendency that feeds on its own output. I can't prove where the `u` goes missing from the client side.

### Why report it here

Even if the root cause is the model, the pi-side problem is that corruption is silent. A cheap guard would make it a normal retryable validation error:

- For `edit` / `write` (or any string tool args), reject C0 control characters other than `\t`, `\n`, `\r`, with a message like "argument contains control character U+0008; possible malformed \u escape".
- Or, in the Anthropic provider, flag `\b`/`\f` followed by hex digits in the raw `partialJson` before parsing.

If the context effect is real, the error should not echo the corrupted string back to the model. Naming the code point is probably enough.

I can write this guard as a local extension (a `tool_call` handler returning `{ block, reason }`). It seems worth handling in core, though, because every non-ASCII user on Claude is exposed to silent file corruption.

Related: #6278 (Claude tool-call schema errors, closed as model behavior). This case is narrower: non-ASCII content only, and it can corrupt files without any validation error.

### Steps to reproduce

Not deterministic. Using a Claude model, ask for several `edit` calls that replace Korean text in a UTF-8 file. It is much more likely once a corrupted string has appeared in the conversation. Failures show up as oldText mismatches whose arguments contain U+0008/U+000C, or as very short oldText values.

I can share the log-scanning script (counts only) if helpful.

### Version / environment

- pi 0.87.1 (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`), Windows, PowerShell 7
- Provider `anthropic`, Claude subscription login through the third-party `@gotgenes/pi-anthropic-auth` 3.3.2 extension. It only handles authentication, but I have not tested with an API key.

issues.title: Add a cacheRetention setting instead of only PI_CACHE_RETENTION

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Add a `cacheRetention` setting (`"short" | "long" | "none"`), with per-model overrides like `modelThinkingLevels`. Pi would pass it as `cacheRetention` in the request options.

### Why?

Right now there are only two ways to turn on 1h retention:

- `PI_CACHE_RETENTION=long`. This applies to the whole process, so it also changes other providers, e.g. openai-completions endpoints start sending `prompt_cache_key` + `prompt_cache_retention: "24h"`.
- A credential `env` in auth.json. The request then gets `ttl: "1h"`, but the cache warmer still plans for the short (5m) tier. `cacheWarmer.start()` gets the request options before `prepareRequest()` merges the credential env ([sdk.ts#L428](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/482c1381a00d8d00bc81697e4a980c593db6803e/packages/coding-agent/src/core/sdk.ts#L428), [model-runtime.ts#L683](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/482c1381a00d8d00bc81697e4a980c593db6803e/packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-runtime.ts#L683)). The miss notice's idle label also uses a fixed 5-minute `CACHE_TTL_MS` ([cache-stats.ts#L8](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/482c1381a00d8d00bc81697e4a980c593db6803e/packages/coding-agent/src/core/cache-stats.ts#L8)).

Why it matters: I run Opus behind Bedrock/Vertex gateways. A 6-minute pause made one session re-write a 136k-token prefix. In probes on both gateways, a 330 s idle missed with the default retention and was a full hit with 1h.

### How? (optional)

Resolve the value once in `buildRequestOptions()` and set `options.cacheRetention`. The provider and the warmer would then read the same value, and the miss notice could use the model's `promptCache` tier instead of a fixed 5 minutes.

issues.title: opencode-go provider returns HTTP 500 when using OpenCode API key

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## Description

Using an OpenCode API key (obtained via `opencode auth login` in OpenCode v1) with the `opencode-go` provider in Pi results in an HTTP 500 Internal Server Error when sending inference requests. The model list loads fine and models can be selected, but actual inference fails.

## Error

```
Error: 500 status code (no body)
```

## Reproduction Steps

1. Obtain an OpenCode API key via `opencode auth login` in OpenCode v1
2. Set the key in Pi: `export OPENCODE_API_KEY=your-key`
3. Start Pi and select a model from the `opencode-go` provider via `/model`
4. Send any message → HTTP 500 error

## Analysis

Looking at the source code:

- **Pi's opencode-go provider** calls: `https://opencode.ai/inference/go` (OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible protocol)
- **OpenCode v2** now uses: `https://opencode.ai/inference/systemone/v1` (TypeSafe System One protocol)

It appears that OpenCode v2 has migrated to a new API protocol (TypeSafe System One), and the old OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible inference endpoints may have been deprecated or are returning 500 errors.

## Questions

1. Has OpenCode deprecated the `/inference/go` and `/inference` endpoints that Pi relies on?
2. Is there a way to use the OpenCode API key with Pi going forward, or does Pi need to be updated to support the new TypeSafe System One protocol?
3. Are there plans to support the new OpenCode inference protocol in Pi?

## Environment

- Pi version: latest
- OS: macOS

issues.title: Sessions wedge permanently at the context ceiling on reasoning models
issues.body:
### What happened?

Sessions on reasoning models wedge permanently at the context ceiling. Every request comes back `stopReason: "length"` with `usage.output: 16`, and auto-compaction reports `Truncated response recovery failed after one compact-and-retry attempt.` In the session I hit this on (gpt-6-astra, 272k window) the last 9 turns spanning 44 minutes and 2 prompts all stopped on `length`, and not one compaction entry was written.

Three things compound:

**1. `estimateTokens()` cannot see reasoning.** In `packages/coding-agent/src/core/compaction/compaction.ts` a thinking block is scored as `block.thinking.length`. Reasoning models return an empty `thinking` and carry the reasoning in `thinkingSignature`, which is replayed to the provider and billed as input. Over the failing span, 1,524,314 chars of signature and 148,316 tokens of assistant `usage.output` scored at roughly zero: 268,261 real tokens estimated at 24,445, a 0.091 ratio. `findCutPoint()` walks that estimate backwards until it hits `keepRecentTokens`, so it keeps nearly the whole context and compaction cannot get the session under threshold.

**2. `isContextOverflow()` misclassifies it.** `clampMaxTokensToContext` collapses the output budget to free window space and `openai-responses` floors it at `OPENAI_RESPONSES_MIN_OUTPUT_TOKENS` (16). The model is asked for 16 tokens and answers `length` having emitted nothing. Case 3 needs `output === 0` (it is 16) and ratio >= 0.99 (268,535/272,000 = 0.987), so real exhaustion is treated as recoverable truncation.

**3. `_overflowRecoveryAttempted` dead-ends the turn.** It clears only on a user message or an assistant stop that is not error/length — impossible once wedged, so each new prompt buys one doomed attempt. The overflow branch also returns before the ordinary threshold-compaction path, so that never runs either.

### Steps to reproduce

Needs a genuinely large reasoning session, so the practical repro is the observable state rather than a script:

1. Run a long tool-heavy session on a reasoning model (gpt-6-astra, 272k window) until context is ~98% full.
2. Send any prompt. The response stops on `length` with `usage.output: 16` and `input + cacheRead` ~= 0.987 of the window.
3. The session emits `Truncated response recovery failed after one compact-and-retry attempt.` and never compacts again, on that prompt or any later one.

I pinned it deterministically instead: a regression test drives that exact usage shape through `_checkCompaction` and reproduces the dead end without a real 268k session.

### Expected behavior

Compaction accounts for reasoning tokens and actually shrinks the session, and a starved 16-token `length` stop is recognised as context overflow rather than recoverable truncation.

### Version

0.85.1

---

I have a fix with regression tests and would like to submit it: https://github.com/Sager611/pi/tree/fix/auto-compaction-wedged-at-context-ceiling — `npm run check` and `./test.sh` both pass. Happy to wait for approval per CONTRIBUTING.md before opening a PR.

issues.title: Mouse wheel scrolls prompt history instead of transcript in fullscreen on Windows + Zellij

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What happened?

Mouse wheel in fullscreen mode scrolls through the editor's prompt history instead of the conversation transcript when running inside Zellij on native Windows (Windows → Alacritty → Zellij → Pi).

Direct terminal (no multiplexer) works correctly. Linux with tmux also works correctly.

**Root cause:** `TuiAltScreen.beforeTerminalStart()` writes mouse DECSET sequences (`?1000h`, `?1002h`, `?1006h`) before `ProcessTerminal.start()` calls `process.stdin.setRawMode(true)`. Windows ConPTY silently consumes these sequences while stdin is in cooked mode, so the multiplexer's inner pane never enables mouse tracking. Zellij then falls back to emitting `ESC[A`/`ESC[B` arrow keys for wheel events on alternate-screen panes, which the editor interprets as history navigation. I made a PR #9655 already, please review.

**Fix:** Move the alt-screen entry and mouse DECSET writes from `beforeTerminalStart()` to `afterTerminalStart()`, after raw mode is active. I'd like to submit a PR for this.

**Environment:** Pi 0.85.1, Zellij 0.45.1, Alacritty 0.17.0, Windows 11 25H2 (build 26200), Node 22.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/82f73340-89d6-490d-9f55-534e6efee08b

### Steps to reproduce

Mouse wheel in fullscreen mode scrolls through the editor's prompt history instead of the conversation transcript when running inside Zellij on native Windows (Windows → Alacritty → Zellij → Pi).

### Expected behavior

_No response_

issues.title: powershell tool falls back to Windows PowerShell 5.1 when pwsh 7 is the Microsoft Store build
issues.body:
### What happened?

With PowerShell 7 installed from the Microsoft Store (7.6.7, no MSI), the built-in `powershell` tool runs Windows PowerShell 5.1.

`getPowerShellConfig` in `utils/shell.js` finds pwsh with `where pwsh.exe` and checks the first hit with `fs.existsSync`. The Store build puts an app-execution alias on PATH (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WindowsApps\pwsh.exe`, a zero-length reparse point). On that alias `existsSync` is false and `statSync` throws EACCES, while `lstatSync`, `accessSync`, and spawning it all work. So the check rejects a working pwsh and silently falls back to `powershell.exe`.

Windows 11 Pro 26300, Node 26.8.1, managed install. The resolver is identical in 1.0.0 and 1.2.0.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Only the Store PowerShell 7 installed (`Get-AppxPackage Microsoft.PowerShell`), no `C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7`.
2. `pi -ne -p -t +powershell,-bash "Use the powershell tool to run: $PSVersionTable.PSEdition"` → `Desktop`.
3. Resolver directly:
   ```
   node -e "import('@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/utils/shell.js').then(m=>console.log(m.getPowerShellConfig().shell))"
   ```
   → `C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe`
4. `where pwsh.exe` → the WindowsApps alias. On that path: `fs.existsSync` → `false`, `fs.statSync` → EACCES, `fs.lstatSync` → 85-byte reparse point, `spawnSync` → prints `Core`.

### Expected behavior

pwsh 7 is used, as `docs/windows.md` says ("runs commands through pwsh.exe when available"). Microsoft is steering users to the Store/MSIX build and retiring the MSI, so more Windows users will hit this.

Fix is small: in the Windows branch of `findExecutableOnPath`, verify the `where` hit with `fs.lstatSync` or `fs.accessSync` instead of `existsSync`, or trust `where` the way the Unix branch trusts `which`. Workaround I use today: `$env:Path = "$PSHOME;$env:Path"` before starting pi, so the real package folder comes first (a user-PATH entry alone is not enough from pwsh, because the Store build prepends its alias folder to PATH at startup). Happy to send a PR if you want one.

Related: #8582 has the same symptom from a different cause (a `where` timeout under load); this one is deterministic on an idle machine.

### Version

1.2.0

prs.title: fix(durable): builtin read resolves images to programs as image blocks in codemode
prs.body:
## Root cause

A code-mode program that nested `read` on an image got an empty string. `read` declared no structured
output schema, so the codemode harness projected the tool result to its text (`textOf()`) — an image
has no text, so the block was dropped.

## Fix

Give `read` a union structured-output schema and return that value:

- text files resolve with their text (unchanged behaviour);
- images resolve with `{ type: "image", data, mimeType }` — the same block codemode's `image()` accepts.

The shape follows the coding-agent precedent `021eae60`, minus `note`: durable's `ImageContent`
(`packages/ai/src/types.ts:430`) has no `note` field, so copying it would invent a field that does not
exist in this package.

`withStructuredOutput()` short-circuits on `result.isError === true`, so a failed read still rejects in
the program instead of being mistaken for `ok: true` (covered by a 24bpp BMP case).

## Reproduction matrix

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| direct `read` → one image | unchanged (existing `image()` path) |
| nested `read` → image block | resolves with the block itself |
| `image(nested read)` | one image, `data` identical to the source |
| nested `read` of a text file | resolves with its text |

## Tests

`npx vitest --run test/tools.test.ts test/codemode.test.ts test/tools-read-differential.test.ts` →
**83 passed, 1 skipped** (3 files).

Full durable suite: 1249 passed / 4 skipped / 10 failed. All ten are 60 s load timeouts (not assertion
failures); the codemode/tools-image cases pass in isolation, and the two harness-ownership/scheduler
files fail **more** on a clean `origin/main` worktree, so none are regressions from this change.

Fixes #11015

Prepared with AI assistance under human review.

This is our first contribution here — could a maintainer grant `lgtm` on the linked issue so future
PRs stay open? Happy to adjust anything.

prs.title: fix(tui): keep the leading tilde in fullscreen double-click word selection
prs.body:
## Root cause

In fullscreen mode the TUI owns mouse selection (regular mode delegates double-click to the terminal
emulator), and `getWordSelection()` decides which characters stay joined in a word.
`TERMINAL_WORD_SELECTION_JOINERS` contained `/` and `-` but not `~`, so double-clicking
`~/Downloads/archive.zip` copied `/Downloads/archive.zip` — the leading home marker was dropped.

That set has a single consumer: the fullscreen selection path
(`packages/tui/src/tui-alt-screen.ts:85` → `getWordSelection()` at L1176, joiner check at L1182). The
delegated regular-mode path is untouched.

## Fix

One line: add `~` to `TERMINAL_WORD_SELECTION_JOINERS`.

## Tests

- New case in `packages/tui/test/tui-alt-screen.test.ts` drives a real mouse double-click escape
  sequence and asserts the **whole** copied string is `~/Downloads/archive.zip`; the existing
  kebab-case (`earendil-works/pi-tui`) and plain-word controls still assert their original behaviour,
  guarding against the #7746 class of regression.
- Mutation check: reverting the joiner set to `["/", "-"]` makes the new case fail with
  `'/Downloads/archive.zip'`, so the test is not vacuous.
- `node --test test/tui-alt-screen.test.ts` → **67/67 passed**.

Fixes #10980

This is our first contribution here — could a maintainer grant `lgtm` on the linked issue so future
PRs stay open? Happy to adjust anything.

prs.title: durable: add task-scoped model access for hosts
prs.body:
## Summary

Add an optional `HarnessOptions.taskModels(scope, models)` callback. It lets a host return model access bound to the task that is asking for it.

`scope` contains the task ID, conversation ID, task kind and invocation abort signal. The scheduler supplies these values. The callback runs on each `TaskRuntime.models` access and receives the current host model configuration.

## Why

We need to check host permissions before a durable task calls a model. Generation hooks provide task identity, but a compaction resumed from its summary checkpoint does not run `beforeCompact` again. A shared `Models` object cannot identify that task by itself.

We currently have a temporary registry-reader adapter that captures task scope around phase execution. This callback would let us remove that adapter and use a supported SDK API.

## Scope

- Works independently of the conversation's selected extensions.
- Runs when a recovered task accesses models, as well as during normal execution.
- Leaves behaviour unchanged when the callback is absent.
- Does not add a database table or change task records.
- Does not provide a provider-request ID, atomic dispatch, billing settlement or exactly-once execution. Hosts still need those checks separately.

This is a small draft proposal. Feedback on the API name and placement is welcome. A recovery/compaction-specific integration test should be added before merge; the current test covers exact task scope across checkpoint phases and live model replacement.

## Validation

- 37 tests passed: the new task-model scope test and existing harness task tests.
- Biome passed for changed TypeScript files.
- `npm run check` could not finish in this environment: `node` resolves to Bun, and the runtime-dependency checker uses TypeScript's synchronous RPC API, which fails on `stdout._handle.fd`.
- A separate whole-repository typecheck was killed by the environment. Full checks are therefore not claimed as passing.

No release, dependency change or deployment is included.

---
AI-assisted contribution, prepared with OpenAI Codex. Human request: “send a PR to earendil asking for this, simplified technical english”, following a request for a temporary shim that can later be submitted to the SDK.

prs.title: docs: move documentation to the repository root
prs.body:
The docs now cover more than the coding agent (pi-ai, pi-durable, ...), so they move from `packages/coding-agent/docs` to `docs/` at the repository root.

## Bundling

npm can only pack files inside a package, so the coding-agent build copies `docs/` into `packages/coding-agent/docs/` (generated, gitignored) via `scripts/copy-docs.mjs`. Every release path packs after the build (npm tarballs, release binaries via `build-binaries.sh`, Nix, the evals image), so releases keep shipping `<package>/docs` with no changes to `files`, `build-binaries.sh` or the Dockerfile. The generated copy is byte-identical to the docs the package shipped before this change.

`copy-docs.mjs` is the place to filter what gets bundled later, since `docs/` will include pages unrelated to the coding agent.

## Links

Docs link to coding-agent files through the repository layout, e.g. `../packages/coding-agent/examples/sdk/`, so links work in the repository and on GitHub. `copy-docs.mjs` rewrites links that point into the package back to package-relative paths (`../examples/sdk/`) in the bundled copy. Links to other repository files are left unchanged.

## Runtime

- `getDocsPath()` returns the repository `docs/` in source checkouts and `<package>/docs` in npm installs and the binary.
- Compact rendering of `read` calls recognizes pages under `getDocsPath()`, which is outside the package root in source checkouts.

## Other references

Root README, coding-agent README (`../../docs/...`), the extensions URL in `migrations.ts`, the documentation test, the documentation audit eval, `.pi/prompts/pr.md`, `.pi/skills/add-llm-provider.md`.

## Before merging

pi.dev fetches docs from `packages/coding-agent/docs` on `main` and resolves `../` links against the package path. It needs to read `docs/` (with a fallback to the old path for older refs) and resolve `../` links against the repository root before this lands.

## Verification

- `npm run check`
- `test/documentation.test.ts`, `test/tool-execution-component.test.ts`, `test/config.test.ts`, `test/system-prompt.test.ts`, `test/changelog.test.ts`
- `npm pack --dry-run` includes all 46 docs files

prs.title: DRAFT: fix(coding-agent): run availability passes one at a time with a timeout
prs.body:
Parking this here for now.
I want to see whether it makes sense to go back to the one-at-a-time refresh we had before #7301 but with a timeout.

----
An awaited refresh could resolve before its availability pass saved. Passes ran concurrently, and only the most recently started pass could save its result; a superseded pass returned without saving and refresh() still resolved. At startup, the awaited refresh could lose to a fire-and-forget refresh started by an extension provider registration, so initial model selection read a snapshot without that provider and fell back to another provider's default. A login also cancelled any full pass that was running.

Availability passes now run one at a time. A request made while a pass is waiting to start joins it, so a caller always gets a pass that saw its changes. Each pass has a 10 s timeout, so a hung auth check or credential store no longer blocks the caller forever (#7301). A failed or timed-out provider check keeps that provider's previous state and is reported in getError().

The snapshot drops configuredProviders and all; hasConfiguredAuth reads the auth map.

Refs #8810, #9884

- providers/compat-schema.ts: serverSideCompaction compat flag (Responses API; off by default, not set on the generated catalog).
- api/openai-responses.ts: emit context_management when the model opts in via compat and a threshold is set; buildParams returns the per-group input item counts for adoption bookkeeping.
- api/openai-responses-shared.ts: ResponsesItemCounts per-group item counts in convertResponsesMessages; capture the compaction output item from output_item events and (authoritatively) the terminal response output, create no content slot for it, and invoke onServerCompaction with the request's item counts.
- api/simple-options.ts, index.ts: forward onServerCompaction/ contextManagement; export convertResponsesMessages/ResponsesItemCounts.
- test: openai-responses-server-compaction.test.ts (stream capture with and without adoption metadata, terminal-response fallback, context_management emission gating).

agent: forward onServerCompaction and contextManagement into loop configs.

coding-agent (agent-session):
- _setServerCompactionRequestState: per request, set compactThreshold = contextWindow - reserveTokens and capture the request-time projection snapshot; clear both for non-opting-in or virtual models.
- _adoptServerCompaction: rebuild the request transcript from the snapshot (transformContext + the agent's convertToLlm + the adapter's conversion), walk the per-group item counts to the first retained message, keep the whole entry containing it, and append a normal compaction entry (details.source = 'server'), emitting compaction_end. Auto-adoption requires the provider's items_compacted metadata; any mapping mismatch aborts silently and client-side compaction remains the fallback.
- defer pre-request client compaction while server compaction is active.
- docs: compaction.md server-side section; regenerate models-configuration reference and models.schema.json.

Related: the upstream feature requests in #7317, #6676, #6492, #9392 were closed without implementation; this is a self-contained opt-in version.

issues.title: /forget deletes an entire memory file with CRLF line endings instead of removing one entry

labels.name: priority/P1
labels.description: High priority issue

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working as expected

labels.name: category/core
labels.description: Core engine and logic

labels.name: scope/memory
labels.description: Memory and context management

issues.body:
## What happens

When a managed auto-memory file uses CRLF line endings (for example a project memory file that git checked out on Windows with `core.autocrlf`), `/forget <text>` deletes the whole file, including every entry that did not match the request.

## What should happen

Only the selected entry is removed and the remaining entries stay in the file, the same as for an LF file.

## Minimal repro

A memory file with two legacy entries, saved with CRLF line endings:

```js
const content = [
  '---', 'title: Project memory', '---', '',
  '# Project Memory', '',
  '- Keep this entry', '  - Why: unrelated',
  '- Forget this entry', '  - Why: requested', '',
].join('\r\n');
await fs.writeFile(filePath, content, 'utf-8');
```

Call `forgetManagedAutoMemoryMatches(projectRoot, [{ topic: 'project', summary: 'Forget this entry', filePath, entryIndex: 1 }])`.

Result on main: the file no longer exists. Expected: the file still contains `Keep this entry`.

## Root cause

The scanner (`parseAutoMemoryTopicDocument` in `packages/core/src/memory/structured-scan.ts`) normalizes `\r\n` to `\n` before matching the frontmatter, so CRLF files are indexed and their entries become forget candidates. `forgetManagedAutoMemoryMatches` in `packages/core/src/memory/forget.ts` reads the same file raw and matches it against `/^---\n([\s\S]*?)\n---\n?([\s\S]*)$/`. With CRLF the match fails, and the code takes the "No frontmatter, delete the whole file" branch, which unlinks the file.

I have a fix with a regression test ready and can open a PR if you assign this to me.

prs.title: feat(managed-agent): add a read-only --check preflight
prs.body:
## What this PR does

The server artifact now accepts `--check` and runs a read-only deployment preflight instead of starting Spring. It binds the same configuration sources the server would load, prints one row per input as `PASS`, `WARN`, `FAIL` or `SKIP`, and exits 1 when any row fails. It covers the JDK, the external configuration and its permissions, the credential key ring, the auth/bind combination, Harness reachability, the Workspace tool path, broker credentials and directories, the Workspace working directory, the server and broker ports, and MySQL connectivity, the `performance_schema` grant and the Flyway version against the release manifest.

The configuration-template base has merged, so this PR now targets `main`. The preflight documentation and the environment-only configuration warning refer to the bundled template that landed with it.

## Why it's needed

The reference deployment states its prerequisites in prose, but the server evaluated them one at a time at startup or on the first Turn. A missing `performance_schema` grant, an empty key ring, `auth mode=auto` on a non-loopback bind, an unreachable Harness, an undersized credential key, an unwritable state directory and an occupied port each surfaced as a separate failure, and some appeared only after a Session existed. Operators now get the whole picture in one run.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the packaged artifact with `--check` and no database. It must print the table, report the connection failure, and exit 1. Point the Harness base URL at a local HTTP server that answers `/capabilities` with 200 and enable the Harness; the harness row must become `PASS`. Set a non-loopback bind with `auth mode=auto`; the auth row must become `FAIL`. Set an undersized credential key; the broker row must become `FAIL`. The unit suite covers the validators, configuration-location precedence, auth verdicts, the Harness probe against a local HTTP server, broker checks and the tool-path cross-settings.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A (non-UI change). A local run without MySQL produces:

```
Managed Agent preflight
STATUS CHECK          DETAIL
PASS   java           21.0.11+10-LTS
WARN   config         no external configuration; environment only
SKIP   key-ring       no Runtime credential key configured
PASS   auth           address=127.0.0.1 mode=auto
SKIP   harness        disabled
SKIP   tool-path      Workspace files disabled
SKIP   broker         disabled
SKIP   workspace      no Workspace cwd configured
PASS   server-port    127.0.0.1:8080 is free
FAIL   database       jdbc:mysql://127.0.0.1:3306/qwen_managed_agent: Communications link failure
10 check(s), 1 warning(s), 1 failure(s)
```

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   N/A  |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

JDK 21, packaged artifact run locally; unit suite through Maven.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the port rows bind the configured addresses, so they report a false failure while the service is running. This is documented in the preflight section.
- Not validated / out of scope: the Harness capability digest is only observable on an authenticated Session, and native Workspace storage registration is outside the command.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. `--check` is a new argument; the normal startup path is unchanged.

prs.title: fix(ci): repair Java gates and report failures on PRs
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Repairs the observed Java acceptance failures and makes future Java failures visible on the associated PR. A close refused with `hosted_lifecycle_recovery_required` remains recoverable across its retry budget; MariaDB numeric Boolean CHECK expressions validate equivalently without accepting constraint drift. The fixture repairs retain ownership, durable-terminal and schema assertions.

Failed Java PR runs receive one updated summary with tested commit, job links, steps and test names. Main and merged-PR regressions enter the existing deduplicated issue queue; open PR failures receive a comment. Exact-head and destination-repository matching cover empty associations and fork approval runs. A prepared summary survives issue-lookup failure, and the privileged writers execute no PR code.

This consolidates the reporting branch from #14493 and the runtime/fixture repairs into this existing PR. No separate PR is needed for the individual failures.

## Why it's needed

Daemon recovery refusals could stop close recovery, and fresh MariaDB initialization rejected an equivalent CHECK expression. Remote acceptance also exposed fixture races and a destructive schema test that removed a shared CHECK. Independently, manual-main and approval-triggered Java failures could finish without a PR summary or tracking issue.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- Close remains pending and recoverable while the daemon settles a previous prompt, including direct and transport-wrapped refusals before/after the retry budget; it completes only after recovery clears.
- Real MySQL/MariaDB initialization accepts equivalent Boolean constraints and refuses changed values, thresholds, operators, quoted literals and missing constraints. Destructive schema probes preserve other tests' shared data and CHECKs.
- Replacement-writer, heartbeat, broker-outage and Hosted fault scenarios retain actual ownership, fencing, drain and durable-completion assertions.
- A failed Java PR run produces one summary with direct failure links; a rerun updates it. A main or already-merged regression also creates/updates the deduplicated issue. Superseded heads and repository mismatches receive no report.
- Infrastructure dispatch and issue-lookup failures preserve the applicable prepared summary. Publication jobs never execute contributor-controlled code or expose privileged tokens.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Current consolidated head: `876e9a1f05`. [Standard CI](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/39137488112) and [fast Java/SDK](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/39137488157) are the current acceptance runs. Further verification uses the existing ECS lanes; the temporary hosted manual run was cancelled at the user's request. No new local Mac build/test is being run. These current checks remain pending.

Retained source-scoped evidence: actual MariaDB/MySQL Boolean regressions passed23 cases each onb788; populated-schema isolation passed18 each onc12, preserving real shared snapshot rows and CHECKs, with an old-source failure control. Complete Hosted acceptance on898 passed84 main cases,44 Broker,2 admission and56 O4 cases, with2 expected Linux skips. Earlier SDK390 and CLI42778 passed on their documented heads. The reporting branch's388 focused tests and previous8b full CI passed. Subsequent production/reporting logic is preserved in this merge; historical runs are not claimed as current-head full acceptance.

A bounded remote invocation reproduced none of the four inherited CLI failures on either parent source; each ran4/4 with retries disabled, and the runtime HTTP contract ran115/115. Its complete jobs failed only because a temporary metadata guard counted filtered `skipped` entries; artifact inspection retained actual test results without another build. This does not establish the original full-suite failure causes. [Detailed evidence and current dispositions](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14522#issuecomment-6245542341).



The previous be9 head became conflicted with advancing main, and its live contract status failed because main also declared1.65.0. e2 merges main46bf, preserves both branches' repairs, and advances the contract to1.66.0. Independent exact-commit review found no Critical; only four informational/version JSON paths differ from main, and the SDK keepalive/typed-idle contract is retained. Current ECS checks cover this merged head. The previous cancelled runs are not passes.

Cancelled pull-request runs previously kept an always-running summary job queued for ECS, blocking the next head in workflow concurrency. The final job now skips cancelled non-full PR runs, including cancellation before tier selection; full/review/main/merge-group cancellation handling is retained. The two-file change has passed independent static review; the added regression cases await the current ECS script suite.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :--- | :--- |
| Linux | Current ECS acceptance pending; prior scoped remote proofs retained |
| macOS / Windows | Prior remote SDK matrix passed on its recorded head; current merged main changes are covered by the pending ECS run |

### Environment (optional)

Node22 and Java21; database proofs use MariaDB10.11/MySQL8.4. Further acceptance is on self-hosted ECS.

## Risk & Scope

Longer bounded host-lock waits avoid premature queue-timeout failures; they do not accelerate execution. Shared Maven cache/hardlink usage prevents assuming the lock can safely be removed. The authenticated diagnostic head probe adds an awaited request budget and can itself refuse an expired writer; its result is evidence, not an atomic store verdict. Authorization and production lease defaults remain unchanged.

Reporting activates after merge; live delivery and token permissions need a qualifying post-merge event. Cancelled/superseded runs are not passes. Review arrangements remain with the user.

## Linked Issues

Refs #14392, #14492 and #14406. Supersedes #14493.

prs.title: feat(serve): batch workspace session live-state snapshots
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds one read-only request for complete live-session snapshots from 1–20 explicitly selected registered workspaces. Each workspace keeps its own canonical identity, catalog version, and independent success or error result. The new request shares the existing single-workspace snapshot and catalog-cache reconciliation logic. A distinct capability and TypeScript SDK method let clients opt in with cancellation and timeout support.

## Why it's needed

Clients showing several workspaces currently make one live-state HTTP request per workspace on every refresh. The recently added batch session catalog can read persisted history, so it is not a suitable high-frequency execution-state endpoint. This API lets clients fetch the same authoritative in-memory state in one request, while preserving the existing single-workspace route and per-session SSE.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Start a local daemon with a primary workspace, register a trusted secondary workspace, then send one batch request containing both IDs and an unknown selector. Expect two full snapshots and one explicit `workspace_not_found` member in input order, with `Cache-Control: no-store`. Confirm malformed bodies fail with HTTP 400, an untrusted or transitioning workspace fails only its own member, and the capability is advertised. Change a live session between running, waiting, and idle without advancing its catalog version; every batch snapshot should still reflect the current state. Confirm the SDK makes one authenticated native REST request and preserves abort and timeout behavior. Older daemons should continue to use the single-workspace route after callers preflight capabilities.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A (HTTP and SDK change; no TUI change). The local daemon returned two workspace snapshots and one explicit unknown-workspace error in a single POST.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ Build, typecheck, bundle, focused tests, and local HTTP E2E passed; the large server test file showed unrelated intermittent failures |
| 🪟 Windows | Not tested locally |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ `dev` x86_64: frozen install/build/bundle, typecheck, focused tests, and daemon HTTP E2E passed |

### Environment (optional)

Node 22.23.1 on macOS arm64 and `dev` Linux x86_64, each with an isolated daemon on a dynamically assigned loopback port. The global `qwen` binary was unavailable for the pre-change CLI dry-run; the absence of this route was confirmed in the current base source.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: A batch is not atomic across workspaces. Each successful member is capped at 512 KiB and an oversized member gets an explicit error.
- Not validated / out of scope: Web Shell still polls workspaces separately until a client migration adopts the new capability; no model-driven live session was created in the HTTP E2E. Windows was not tested locally.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: None. Clients preflight `workspace_session_live_state_batch` and retain the existing single-workspace path for older daemons.

Design: [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/batch-workspace-live-state/docs/design/daemon-batch-session-live-state.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/batch-workspace-live-state/docs/design/daemon-batch-session-live-state.zh-CN.md)

## Linked Issues

Closes #12511

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 的改动

新增一个只读请求，一次获取 1–20 个显式选定、已注册 workspace 的完整会话运行状态快照。每个 workspace 独立返回规范化身份、目录版本及成功或错误结果。新请求与单 workspace 接口共用快照生成和目录缓存校准逻辑。独立 capability 和 TypeScript SDK 方法支持客户端按能力接入，并支持取消与超时。

## 为什么需要

同时展示多个 workspace 的客户端目前每次刷新都要逐 workspace 发起运行状态 HTTP 请求。近期增加的批量会话目录可能读取持久历史，不适合高频查询执行状态。新接口让客户端通过一次请求获取同样的权威内存状态，保留原单 workspace 路由和逐会话 SSE。

## 评审验证计划

### 如何验证

启动包含 primary workspace 的本地 daemon，注册可信的 secondary workspace，再用一次批量请求查询两个 ID 和一个未知 selector。预期按输入顺序得到两个完整快照和一个明确的 `workspace_not_found` 成员，响应包含 `Cache-Control: no-store`。确认无效请求体返回 HTTP 400，不可信或过渡中的 workspace 只影响自身成员，且 capability 已公布。在目录版本不变时使会话在运行、等待和空闲之间切换，每次快照都应反映当前状态。确认 SDK 只发送一次带鉴权的原生 REST 请求，并保留取消与超时行为。旧 daemon 的调用方应预检能力，继续使用单 workspace 路由。

### 前后证据

不适用（HTTP 与 SDK 改动，无 TUI 变化）。本地 daemon 实测一次 POST 返回两个 workspace 快照及一个未知 workspace 的明确错误。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ 构建、类型检查、打包、聚焦测试和本地 HTTP E2E 通过；大型 server 测试文件出现无关的间歇性失败 |
| 🪟 Windows | 本地未测试 |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ `dev` x86_64：锁文件安装/构建/打包、类型检查、聚焦测试与 daemon HTTP E2E 均通过 |

### 环境

在 macOS arm64 和 `dev` Linux x86_64 上使用 Node 22.23.1，各自启动使用动态 loopback 端口的隔离 daemon。全局 `qwen` 命令不可用，无法进行改动前 CLI dry-run；已从当前基线源码确认该路由不存在。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：批量结果不保证跨 workspace 原子性；每个成功成员上限为 512 KiB，超限会返回明确错误。
- 未验证或范围外：Web Shell 在后续客户端迁移前仍逐 workspace 轮询；HTTP E2E 未创建由模型驱动的运行会话；未在本地运行 Windows 测试。
- 破坏性变更或迁移说明：无。客户端预检 `workspace_session_live_state_batch`，旧 daemon 保留现有单 workspace 路径。

设计文档：[English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/batch-workspace-live-state/docs/design/daemon-batch-session-live-state.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/batch-workspace-live-state/docs/design/daemon-batch-session-live-state.zh-CN.md)

## 关联 Issue

Closes #12511

</details>

prs.title: fix(cli): resolve the /auth strings at render time, not at import time
prs.body:
## What this PR does

`/auth` no longer paints a half-translated dialog. Every string the auth dialogs render is now resolved when it is painted rather than while the module graph is being imported.

The eager module-scope constants in both parity implementations (`MAIN_ITEMS`, `PROTOCOL_ITEMS`, and the two navigation hints) become small thunks that call `t()` on demand. `VIEW_TITLES` is converted the same way so the two constant classes agree, but that half is a behaviour-preserving refactor: at this PR's merge base it was already a `Record<string, () => string>` invoked during render, so it carried no user-visible defect. That is the same shape `providerToItem` and `getStepLabel` in the same files already use.

## Why it's needed

Module-scope `t()` calls run at import time, and `initializeI18n()` is awaited later in the entry module. Whatever dictionary happens to be loaded when the module is first imported is what those constants keep forever. A zh-locale user opening `/auth` therefore saw the provider sub-menu titles translated (those call `t()` at render time) while the main view title and the navigation hints stayed in the import-time locale — half the dialog in Chinese, half in English, with no way to correct it short of a restart.

This is the remaining leg of the class the stacked credential PR closed for one constant; the sub-menu *items* were already translated before it because `providerToItem` calls `t()` per render.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the two suites that own these dialogs:

```
npx vitest run packages/cli/src/ui/auth/AuthDialog.test.tsx
npx vitest run packages/cli/src/ui/opentui/dialogs-auth.test.tsx
```

A reviewer can also confirm by hand: set the locale to Chinese, open `/auth`, and check that the main view title reads `连接服务商` rather than `Connect a Provider`. Before the change the title stayed English even though the sub-menu title one keystroke away was already Chinese.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Two new pins were added to `AuthDialog.test.tsx`. They are deliberately **keystroke-free and ungated**, because the keystroke assertions elsewhere in that file sit behind `itWhenTuiInputReliable`, which skips under `CI=true` — a gated pin would never run where it matters.

`AuthDialog locale resolution > resolves the main view title at render time, not at import time` renders the dialog in English, then switches the locale to Chinese and renders again without remounting the module, asserting the title follows the locale in force at render time.

Mutation check: freezing the titles at import time (`const __FROZEN = getViewTitles()` used by the render path) makes both new pins fail with `expected '┌────…' to contain '连接服务商'`; restoring the thunk makes them pass. The pins therefore track the fix, not the refactor.

```
✓ src/ui/auth/AuthDialog.test.tsx (29 tests | 20 skipped) 351ms
    Tests  9 passed | 20 skipped (29)
✓ src/ui/opentui/dialogs-auth.test.tsx (46 tests) 510ms
    Tests  46 passed (46)
npx eslint <the three files>            → clean
npx prettier --check <the three files>  → clean
```

The OpenTUI suite is version-sensitive (it fakes the renderer hooks), so the transformation was additionally verified for behaviour preservation on the baseline tree: applying the identical textual transformation to the pre-change `dialogs-auth.tsx` keeps all 46 OpenTUI tests green, i.e. the change only moves *when* `t()` runs.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  N/A   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ✅   |
|  🐧 Linux  |  N/A   |

Both suites above plus `eslint` and `prettier` were run on Windows. The change is locale resolution and render-time evaluation only; it contains no platform-specific code.

### Environment (optional)

N/A — unit tests only, no dev server or sandbox runtime involved.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the constants are now re-created per render instead of once per module load. They are three small array/object literals and two strings, and `providerToItem` already rebuilt a similar object per item per render, so the cost is negligible; the benefit is that a locale change is picked up without a restart.
- Not validated / out of scope: `MODELS_*` in `dialogs-auth.tsx` is intentionally left eager. Its keys have no zh entry today, and that region is hoisted specifically so the region budget measures the same strings the step paints; converting it would need a size-budget pass of its own.
- Not validated / out of scope: the OpenTUI suite could not be run against the post-change file in the environment used for this change (its fakes lag the current source); behaviour preservation was established on the baseline tree instead, as described above.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Refs #14328 — this closes the actionable set described there (`MAIN_ITEMS` labels/descriptions plus the two navigation hints). `VIEW_TITLES` is converted here as well, but only as a consistency refactor: it was already invoked at render time at this PR's merge base, so it was not a user-visible defect and this PR does not claim to fix one. It deliberately does not use a closing keyword: `MODELS_*` and the `itWhenTuiInputReliable` gating question raised in the same issue are out of scope here.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

`/auth` 不再渲染出「半翻译」的对话框。认证对话框渲染的每一个字符串，现在都在**绘制时**解析，而不是在模块被导入时解析。

两个对等实现里模块级的常量（`MAIN_ITEMS`、`PROTOCOL_ITEMS`，以及两条导航提示）改成按需调用 `t()` 的小函数（thunk）。`VIEW_TITLES` 也一并改成同样写法，让两类常量统一，但这一半属于行为等价的重构：在本 PR 的 merge base 上它已经是 `Record<string, () => string>`、在渲染期调用，并不携带用户可见缺陷。这与同文件里 `providerToItem`、`getStepLabel` 已有的写法一致。

## 为什么需要

模块级的 `t()` 调用发生在导入期，而 `initializeI18n()` 在入口模块里是更晚才被 await 的。模块第一次被导入时恰好加载了哪份字典，这些常量就会永远保留哪份。因此中文用户在打开 `/auth` 时会看到：服务商子菜单标题是中文（那些在渲染时调用 `t()`），而主视图标题和导航提示仍是导入时的语言——半个对话框中文、半个英文，且只能靠重启修正。

这是堆叠凭据 PR 只修掉其中一个常量的那一类问题里剩下的部分；子菜单**条目**在此之前就已经是翻译好的，因为 `providerToItem` 每次渲染都会调用 `t()`。

## 评审验证方式

运行拥有这两个对话框的两套测试：

```
npx vitest run packages/cli/src/ui/auth/AuthDialog.test.tsx
npx vitest run packages/cli/src/ui/opentui/dialogs-auth.test.tsx
```

也可以手工确认：把语言设为中文，打开 `/auth`，主视图标题应显示 `连接服务商` 而不是 `Connect a Provider`。改动前，即使相隔一次按键的子菜单标题已是中文，该标题仍保持英文。

## 证据（改动前 / 改动后）

在 `AuthDialog.test.tsx` 中新增了两条断言。它们刻意**不需要按键、也不被门控**，因为该文件里其他依赖按键的断言位于 `itWhenTuiInputReliable` 之后，在 `CI=true` 下会被跳过——被门控的断言在最需要它的地方根本不会运行。

`AuthDialog locale resolution > resolves the main view title at render time, not at import time` 先用英文渲染对话框，再切换语言为中文并重新渲染（不重新加载模块），断言标题跟随渲染时生效的语言。

变异校验：把标题在导入期冻结（渲染路径改用 `const __FROZEN = getViewTitles()`）会让两条新断言都以 `expected '┌────…' to contain '连接服务商'` 失败；恢复成 thunk 后通过。也就是说这两条断言锁定的是修复本身，而不是重构。

```
✓ src/ui/auth/AuthDialog.test.tsx (29 tests | 20 skipped) 351ms
    Tests  9 passed | 20 skipped (29)
✓ src/ui/opentui/dialogs-auth.test.tsx (46 tests) 510ms
    Tests  46 passed (46)
npx eslint <三个文件>            → 干净
npx prettier --check <三个文件>  → 干净
```

OpenTUI 那套测试对版本敏感（它伪造了渲染器 hook），所以另外在基线树上验证了变换的行为保持性：把完全相同的文本变换应用到改动前的 `dialogs-auth.tsx`，46 条 OpenTUI 测试全绿——说明本次改动只是改变了 `t()` 执行的**时机**。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：常量现在每次渲染重新构造，而不是每次模块加载构造一次。它们是三个小的数组/对象字面量和两个字符串，而 `providerToItem` 本来每次渲染、每个条目都会重建一个类似对象，开销可忽略；换来的是切换语言无需重启即可生效。
- 未验证 / 超出范围：`dialogs-auth.tsx` 里的 `MODELS_*` 有意保持模块级求值。它的键目前没有中文条目，而且该区域被特意提升出来，是为了让「区域预算」度量与步骤绘制的字符串一致；改动它需要单独做一次尺寸预算评估。
- 未验证 / 超出范围：在当前环境里无法对改动后的文件运行 OpenTUI 那套测试（它的伪造 hook 落后于当前源码）；因此改为在基线树上证明行为保持性，如上所述。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。

## 关联 Issue

prs.title: feat(web-shell): add approval mode allowlist
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds an optional approval-mode allowlist through `ui.allowedApprovalModes` in settings.json and the host `allowedApprovalModes` Prop. An explicit Prop overrides settings, including `[]`; leaving both unset preserves all four choices. The dropdown, approval dialog, custom composer footer and Shift+Tab cycle use the same normalized list, including split and side-task composers.

Each workspace session reads its own workspace settings. Unknown values, duplicates and `plan` are filtered out while retaining the built-in order. An empty list disables execution-mode selection and cycling; a singleton avoids redundant requests. A hidden current mode is still displayed accurately and is never changed automatically. Plan remains independent.

## Why it's needed

Embedded hosts and workspace owners currently cannot hide individual approval choices. Filtering only the main dropdown would leave other entry points inconsistent, and reading primary-workspace settings for a secondary session would produce different choices between main and split views.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Without configuration, confirm all four execution modes remain visible and Shift+Tab cycles through them.
2. Set `ui.allowedApprovalModes` to `["default", "auto"]`: the dropdown and `/approval-mode` dialog should offer exactly those modes, and Shift+Tab should alternate between them.
3. Supply host `allowedApprovalModes` as `["default", "yolo"]`, then `[]`: the host list should override settings in the main composer, split panes and side-task panel. The empty list should disable the picker and make cycling a no-op.
4. Use different primary and secondary workspace lists, then open the same secondary session in main and split views: both should use the secondary list. Change settings or host Props and confirm choices update consistently.
5. Restore a session whose current mode is excluded: its actual mode should remain displayed until an allowed mode is selected. Plan entry/exit should continue to work independently.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: all four choices were always offered; hosts and settings could not filter them. After: the browser-rendered dropdown and dialog below both show only `default` and `auto` supplied by host Props.

![Allowlisted dropdown](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ytahdn/qwen-code/3acfb7837db7d01cd2df8e6436f9805fe6b9bc3f/approval-mode-allowlist/menu.png)

![Allowlisted approval dialog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ytahdn/qwen-code/3acfb7837db7d01cd2df8e6436f9805fe6b9bc3f/approval-mode-allowlist/dialog.png)

The built standalone UI also shows only secondary-workspace `auto` in the split pane when primary allows only `default`:

![Secondary workspace split picker](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ytahdn/qwen-code/3acfb7837db7d01cd2df8e6436f9805fe6b9bc3f/approval-mode-allowlist/split-workspace.png)

All screenshots were captured through browser E2E and visually inspected. Daemon API/SSE responses are simulated; the split screenshot uses actual bundled HTML/assets served by `node dist/cli.js`. Separate real-daemon checks confirmed settings.json values through both settings endpoints. Screenshots do not establish real backend session operations or authorization enforcement. Images are stored on an independent fork asset branch and pinned to a fixed commit, outside the implementation branch.

Validation passed at `153fcc9535` after merging main `a8eb74fdf5`: frozen-lockfile dependency installation and patches; root build, typecheck and bundle; 1,226 App tests; 605 component/Managed/StreamingStatus tests; three source Chromium cases and two built-artifact cases. The allowlist and upstream Tokens/second setting coexist. Screenshots above were recaptured and visually inspected. Original feature verification also covered the default cycle, empty/singleton lists, Plan, side tasks and real settings.json projection, as detailed in the separate E2E reports. GitHub reports no merge conflict; the new CI run is pending.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ✅ tested |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested locally |
|  🐧 Linux  | ⚠️ not tested locally |

### Environment (optional)

macOS local worktree; Vitest and Chromium/Playwright; isolated built CLI daemon for settings checks and static serving; simulated daemon transport for browser interaction; no model requests.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: settings load asynchronously; until available, the UI uses the default four-mode list. Existing backend permission rules remain authoritative.
- Not validated / out of scope: backend permission enforcement, real multi-workspace session/tool operations, and local Windows/Linux execution.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none; all four choices remain the default. This is presentation customization rather than a security policy.

Design: [English](https://github.com/ytahdn/qwen-code/blob/153fcc9535c9b24f208428969064db5bee7f4c0c/docs/design/web-shell-approval-mode-allowlist.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/ytahdn/qwen-code/blob/153fcc9535c9b24f208428969064db5bee7f4c0c/docs/design/web-shell-approval-mode-allowlist.zh-CN.md). Both versions are complete and synchronized.

## Linked Issues

None.

prs.title: feat(managed-agent): support local and SSH workspace file references
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Enable Reference file and the @ file picker in new and existing managed conversations bound to a registered local or SSH Workspace. Browsing and filename search use the selected Workspace; selecting a UTF-8 file captures its complete bytes and digest as an attachment snapshot. Source edits, draft refreshes and an uncertain admission retry preserve that snapshot. Loading a selection blocks premature text-only submission, and accepted submissions clear saved references.

File access requires an authenticated tenant and actor, current Workspace OPERATOR/OWNER access, an ACTIVE Workspace and valid storage registration. Authorization and scope are checked before and after I/O. Storage-specific dispatch leaves a boundary for a future Kubernetes adapter; unsupported storage remains unavailable without falling back to the primary daemon. Single-file reads are limited to 24 KiB, and the existing 48 KiB encoded input and separate 64 KiB transport limits remain intact.

## Why it's needed

Managed conversations currently disable Reference file even when their local or SSH Workspace can execute file tools. Users must upload a separate copy or manually describe a path, and a typed path does not capture the selected content. This change makes Workspace files selectable while keeping the chosen bytes stable through refresh and retry and preserving existing grant, storage and input limits.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. With Workspace files enabled, an updated CLI and a registered local or SSH Workspace, open a new or existing managed conversation as a permitted operator. Reference file should be enabled and browse/search only the selected Workspace. Ordinary typed paths should remain plain text.
2. Select small UTF-8 files through Reference file and the @ picker, including two files with the same basename. Change the source files and refresh the unsent draft. Both references should retain their original complete bytes and distinguish their relative paths.
3. Delay a file read: sending should stay blocked until the snapshot is ready. Change the Workspace/cwd or revoke access during selection: the stale result should be rejected rather than submitted in the new scope. Binary, empty, oversized, traversing and symlink paths should be refused.
4. Drop an accepted admission response, refresh and retry. The stored input and idempotency key should produce the same Turn without rereading source files. Acceptance should clear reference metadata, including the remounted pending-replay path; rejection should preserve the draft.
5. Restore a draft containing inline file references into the mobile composer and add another reference. Both snapshots should survive its top-tag fallback. Normal composers should retain their existing plain-text draft and text-only clearing behavior.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: the managed Add menu showed Reference file as unavailable for both local and SSH Workspaces. After: the deployed browser enables Reference file, lists the selected directory and returns `qwen-code/AGENTS.md` for a filename search. Local query/read return 200 and the returned 18,371 bytes match the original file exactly; the deployed Java SSH query also returns 200 (the selected remote directory is empty, so this does not establish an SSH read).

Against the integrated main branch, build/typecheck/bundle passed. The latest regression run passed 2,374 Web tests across 22 suites, including the managed file/Skills picker, the approval-mode allowlist, the shared composer and App consumers; five CLI settings/reference/entry suites passed 465 tests. The prior integration also passed 500 Hosted Skill/model/Workspace/entry tests and affected Java verification with 323 tests and one skip, plus Checkstyle and SpotBugs; all Java/SDK sources are unchanged by the latest import-only conflict resolution. Before integration, the feature commit passed 760 Web tests, 102 focused CLI tests, 315 affected Java tests with one skip, API/surface checks with 23 tests and one skip, and the disposable MySQL profile's six new integration plus eight related unit tests with no skips. The file-access production implementation is unchanged by integration. Independent review, two clean self-audit passes and route/schema union checks found no blocking issue. Detailed artifact boundaries remain in the separate E2E comment.

**Full-suite Java validation remains incomplete:** the original feature commit's complete run of 4,667 tests had one H2 recovery error and 18 skips. Focused feature-source and exact-baseline diagnostic runs passed, but that error's cause remains unresolved. The integrated head has focused Java verification; its complete suite was not rerun. These controls do not establish that the earlier error is unrelated to this change.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :---: | :--- |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ Build/typecheck/bundle, focused tests, isolated MySQL/Harness/browser E2E and local deployment |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ Not tested |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ Limited real SSH CLI coverage on an earlier artifact; final deployed CLI capability and Java SSH directory query checked |

### Environment (optional)

Node.js 22+, JDK 21 and Maven 3.9.16 on macOS arm64; disposable MySQL 8.4.11, the packaged Hosted Harness, a native worker and a controlled loopback model. SSH checks used the existing authenticated transport. Deployment verification used read-only file access and did not send a prompt or execute a Runtime tool in a user Session.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: selecting a file stores its complete bounded content in the managed draft and pending input. Scope checks, atomic draft persistence, immutable retry input and synchronous acceptance cleanup protect against stale or lost references. The filesystem trust model assumes a trusted host/account and does not claim hostile same-UID isolation.
- Not validated / out of scope: the unresolved full-suite H2 error; a Kubernetes/CSI adapter; broad Hosted/fault profiles; Windows; real upstream models; broad Plan/upload/image browser regression coverage. The 52-case real SSH suite used an earlier artifact, and the six-scenario real browser run preceded the final shared-composer fixes; current-source DOM regressions cover those later fixes. Final deployment checks establish capability negotiation, local read/browse/search and SSH query, not a rerun of those complete suites.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: no schema migration, new model tool or attachment wire extension. Deploy the updated Java service, WebShell and file-access CLI on the local/SSH target. A CLI without the versioned help capability is refused before file I/O, leaving Reference file unavailable. Unsupported storage never falls back to the local daemon.

Design: [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/managed-file-references/docs/design/2026-10-19-managed-workspace-file-references.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/managed-file-references/docs/design/2026-10-19-managed-workspace-file-references.zh-CN.md). Both versions contain synchronized decisions, constraints, acceptance criteria and remaining work.

## Linked Issues

None.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 此 PR 的改动

为绑定已登记本机或 SSH Workspace 的新建及已有 Managed 会话启用 Reference file 和 @ 文件选择器。文件浏览和文件名搜索限定在所选 Workspace；选择 UTF-8 文件时，将完整字节及摘要保存为附件快照。源文件修改、草稿刷新和准入响应不确定后的重试均保留该快照。读取尚未完成时禁止提前提交纯文本输入，提交接受后清理已保存的文件引用。

文件访问要求可信租户和操作者身份、当前 Workspace OPERATOR/OWNER 权限、ACTIVE Workspace 及有效存储登记，并在 I/O 前后复核授权和范围。按存储类型分发的边界允许未来接入 Kubernetes 适配器；不支持的存储明确不可用，不回退到主 daemon。单文件最多 24 KiB，保留既有整体编码输入 48 KiB 及独立传输 64 KiB 限制。

## 为什么需要

目前即使本机或 SSH Workspace 已能执行文件工具，Managed 会话仍禁用 Reference file。用户只能另外上传副本或手动描述路径，而手输路径不会捕获所选文件内容。本次改动补上 Workspace 文件选择，并在刷新及重试期间保持所选字节不变，保留既有授权、存储和输入限制。

## 评审者测试计划

### 如何验证

1. 开启 Workspace files，使用更新后的 CLI 及已登记的本机或 SSH Workspace，以有权限的操作者打开新建或已有 Managed 会话。Reference file 应可用，浏览和搜索只访问所选 Workspace。普通手输路径仍应是纯文本。
2. 分别通过 Reference file 和 @ 选择较小 UTF-8 文件，包含不同目录下的同名文件。修改源文件并刷新尚未提交的草稿。两个引用都应保留原始完整字节，并能区分相对路径。
3. 延迟文件读取：快照就绪前不能发送。选择期间切换 Workspace/cwd 或撤销权限：过期结果应被拒绝，不能在新范围提交。二进制、空文件、超限、目录穿越和符号链接路径应被拒绝。
4. 丢弃一次已接受准入的响应，刷新后重试。应以相同已保存输入和幂等键得到同一 Turn，不重新读取源文件。接受后应清理引用元数据，包括刷新后的 pending 重放路径；拒绝时应保留草稿。
5. 在移动端输入框恢复含内联文件引用的草稿，再新增引用。两份快照都应经顶部标签回退路径保留。普通输入框应保留既有纯文本草稿及仅清文本的语义。

### 前后证据

改动前：本机和 SSH Workspace 的 Managed 添加菜单都将 Reference file 显示为不可用。改动后：实际部署的浏览器中已启用 Reference file，可以列出所选目录，文件名搜索返回 `qwen-code/AGENTS.md`。本机 query/read 均为 200，返回的 18,371 字节与原文件完全一致；经已部署 Java SSH 路径的 query 也返回 200（所选远程目录为空，因此不据此宣称 SSH read 已通过）。

整合主干后，build/typecheck/bundle 通过。最新回归为 Web 22 套、2,374 项通过，包含 Managed 文件/Skills 选择器、审批模式白名单、共享输入框和 App 消费者；CLI settings/reference/entry 五套、465 项通过。前一次整合还通过 Hosted Skill/model/Workspace/entry 相关 500 项及 Java 定向 verify 323 项（1 项跳过），Checkstyle、SpotBugs 通过；最后一轮仅解决导入冲突，没有改变任何 Java/SDK 源码。整合前，功能提交通过 Web 760 项、CLI 定向 102 项、Java 相关 315 项（1 项跳过）、API/surface 23 项（1 项跳过），以及隔离 MySQL profile 的六项新增集成与八项相关单测（无跳过）。整合没有改动文件访问生产实现；独立审查、两次 clean 自审及路由/schema 并集检查未发现阻塞问题。详细产物覆盖边界继续保留在单独 E2E 评论中。

**完整 Java 验证仍未完成：**整合前功能提交的完整运行包含 4,667 项测试、一项 H2 recovery error、18 项跳过。功能源码及精确基线的定向诊断通过，但该错误根因仍未定位；整合后的 head 进行了 Java 定向验证，没有重新运行完整套件。这些对照不能证明早先错误与本次改动无关。

### 测试平台

| OS | 状态 |
| :---: | :--- |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ build/typecheck/bundle、定向测试、隔离 MySQL/Harness/浏览器 E2E 及本地部署 |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ 未测试 |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ 早先产物的有限真实 SSH CLI 覆盖；已检查最终部署 CLI 能力及 Java SSH 目录查询 |

### 环境（可选）

macOS arm64，Node.js 22+、JDK 21、Maven 3.9.16；隔离 MySQL 8.4.11、打包 Hosted Harness、native worker 及受控本机模型。SSH 检查使用既有认证传输。本次部署验收只读文件，没有向用户 Session 发送提示或执行 Runtime 工具。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：选择文件会将完整且有界的内容保存到 Managed 草稿和 pending 输入。通过范围复核、原子草稿持久化、不可变重试输入和接受后的同步清理，防止引用过期或丢失。文件系统信任模型假设主机及账户可信，不声称能隔离恶意同 UID 进程。
- 未验证或范围外：完整套件中未定位的 H2 错误、Kubernetes/CSI 适配器、广泛 Hosted/fault profiles、Windows、真实上游模型及 Plan/普通上传/图片的广泛浏览器回归。真实 SSH 52 项使用早先产物，真实浏览器六场景运行于最后共享输入框修复前；后续修复由当前源码 DOM 回归覆盖。最终部署检查证明能力协商、本机读取/浏览/搜索及 SSH 查询正常，不等于完整重跑上述套件。
- 兼容及迁移：无 schema migration、新模型工具或附件 wire 扩展。需要部署更新后的 Java 服务、WebShell 和本机/SSH 目标上的文件访问 CLI。缺少版本化 help 能力的 CLI 在文件 I/O 前被拒绝，Reference file 保持不可用。不支持的存储不会回退到本机 daemon。

设计：[English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/managed-file-references/docs/design/2026-10-19-managed-workspace-file-references.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/managed-file-references/docs/design/2026-10-19-managed-workspace-file-references.zh-CN.md)。两版的决策、约束、验收标准及剩余工作保持同步。

## 关联 Issue

prs.title: fix(core): report speculation files that could not be applied
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Report real speculation copy failures with the failed paths and first I/O cause. Keep successfully applied files and their count; if any edit reached disk, report the partial result without resubmitting the same turn. Missing overlay entries and directory placeholders are skipped.

## Why it's needed

Swallowing a copy error lets the UI and model history claim an edit landed. Retrying after a partial copy can apply the edits twice. Both paths need an explicit failure result.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

From `packages/core`: `pnpm exec vitest run src/followup/overlayFs.test.ts src/followup/accept-speculation.test.ts`. From `packages/cli`: `pnpm exec vitest run src/ui/AppContainer.test.tsx`.

### Evidence (Before & After)

At `0e462ea31a` (merged main `18f80f5666`): core 26 passed; AppContainer 208 passed. Tests cover real copy failures, applied/failed counts and cause, missing/directory entries, failed telemetry, and no resubmit after partial writes. Earlier parent-directory red/green evidence remains in the review thread.

Core build/typecheck, full workspace build, CLI typecheck, and scoped ESLint/Prettier passed. The diff remains the original five files.

### Tested on

macOS. Windows and Linux were not tested locally.

### Environment (optional)

Frozen pnpm dependencies and the repository's Ink patch. Unit tests use local temporary files or test doubles; no live speculation E2E run.

## Risk & Scope

Successful copies remain on disk: this does not make writes atomic. With zero applied files, normal submission remains the fallback. Aggregating all causes remains a separate suggestion. Full preflight and live E2E were not run. No API migration.

## Linked Issues

Related follow-up: #13062.

prs.body:
## What this PR does

The preflight's Workspace tool-path row now mirrors the startup rules it claims to represent. It requires session isolation and a configured Workspace mount, creation root or SSH node before it reports a pass, and it reports other provisioners as not evaluated instead of passing them. The deployment documentation and the preflight design table describe the expanded scope.

This PR is stacked on the credential-bootstrap branch. That base must merge first because it is the fourth slice of the same deployment-usability chain and the preflight documentation is already carried by the earlier slices.

## Why it's needed

`--check` previously reported a pass for Workspace files whenever the Harness, Session Store and Broker were enabled. Startup additionally requires session isolation and a configured mount, creation root or SSH node, so a deployment that omitted the Workspace mount configuration passed the preflight and failed at boot. A capability profile that left the mount out would have produced the same false green.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the preflight with Workspace files enabled and no mount, creation root or SSH node; the tool-path row must fail and point at the missing mount configuration. Add a creation root to the same configuration; the row must pass. Switch the provisioner away from the local process path; the row must report that it was not evaluated rather than passing. The unit suite covers all three verdicts.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A (non-UI change). The focused suite reports 18 tests, 0 failures; the full module verify reports zero Checkstyle violations in both executions and zero SpotBugs findings.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   N/A  |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

JDK 21, Maven 3.9.11.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: deployments using a provisioner other than the local process path now see a warning instead of a pass; this is intentional because the resident path has additional startup rules the preflight does not evaluate.
- Not validated / out of scope: the native Workspace storage registration and mount identity are still outside the command.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. A configuration that already supplied a mount, creation root or SSH node keeps passing.
