prs.title: feat(web-shell): delete selected message groups from session history
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds grouped message deletion to Web Shell. The message action row keeps Copy and an overflow menu; Delete selects the current prompt and its complete reply group, with linked checkboxes and optional non-contiguous groups before or after the entry. The entry determines only the initial selection; during selection its Delete messages menu item remains visible but disabled. Reply selection stays beside the Processed header when present, including after expanding thoughts or tools.

Deletion removes the selected original records from JSONL and retained raw compression context, refreshes live model context and connected clients, and preserves every existing summary unchanged. Slash-command display groups can be removed without undoing command effects or files; frontend-only commands retain their position and identity across reloads and recovery.

## Why it's needed

Web Shell cannot currently remove arbitrary conversation groups. Rewind removes a suffix and retains abandoned history, so it does not satisfy physical deletion of selected turns. Users also need consistent behavior when deleting the only group, working around compression checkpoints, or recovering from stale snapshots and partially completed requests.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. In an idle local daemon session, open a user message's overflow menu and choose Delete messages. The current prompt/reply group should be selected; toggling either checkbox must toggle the group. Enter from a middle group and select groups before or after it; during selection Delete messages must remain visible but disabled and must not restart selection. Confirm a non-contiguous selection and verify only the chosen groups disappear after reload and in other connected clients.
2. Expand thoughts/tools and verify a reply group still has one checkbox beside Processed, or beside its first reply when no status header exists. Run a local display command between turns; deleting another group must preserve the command's order and identity. Repeat at narrow viewport width and with keyboard/touch menu interaction.
3. Delete the only/all groups and continue the same session. Inspect persisted history and reopen the session: selected originals and paired tool records must remain absent, while files and command effects remain unchanged.
4. Compress a conversation, then delete groups before and after compression. Existing summaries must remain identical; only selected retained raw context should change later model input. A full compression followed by fast compression must retain the summary boundary and allow safe deletion.
5. Change history from another client while a selection is open. A conflict must clear stale selection and explain re-selection without automatically resubmitting deletion. A busy session must refuse deletion. If persistence succeeds but context installation fails, deleted identities must still reach the originator, its UI must reconcile, and further prompts must explicitly require reopening. Failed reloads must retain unselected saved messages and local commands and explain that deletion succeeded but refresh failed. Reopening must recover context without repeating deletion, and lifecycle close must remain available. Historical transcript pages must not offer deletion.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: there is no grouped physical-deletion action. After: the current captures show the overflow menu, selection extending after the middle entry with a visible disabled Delete messages item, a retained middle turn from non-contiguous deletion, and surviving rows after deletion succeeds but history reload fails.

**Captured with Playwright Chromium and simulated daemon HTTP/SSE responses; all four images were visually inspected. These screenshots establish UI states only. Earlier real-daemon/ACP/JSONL/model evidence remains in the PR discussion; the current recovery fixes additionally have independent fault-injection probes.** Images live only in an independent fork asset branch, pinned to commit `7995424fb171c6904a94833091c7ed25cc7e0c2d`.

![Overflow menu while composer focus is retained (simulated daemon)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ytahdn/qwen-code/7995424fb171c6904a94833091c7ed25cc7e0c2d/menu.png)

### Environment (optional)

Local worktree development and bundled runtime; Chromium Playwright with simulated daemon responses for UI/error recovery, and isolated real daemon/ACP/JSONL with a deterministic local OpenAI-compatible model for persistence and model-context checks. The latest deletion browser suite passed 26/26 cases, including the review regressions. A separate E2E report comment records the validation layers and results.

## Risk & Scope

prs.title: feat(core): account tool result sizes from producer to injection
prs.body:
> Split part ① of #13652. Stacked at the bottom: part ② is #14546, part ③ is #14547.

## What this PR does

This PR makes every tool result carry an honest size story from the moment a tool produces it to the moment it is injected into a model request. A new measurement helper sizes `PartListUnion` payloads (text plus structured functionResponse values, with image estimates taken from the chat-compression config), and a small provenance record — raw size, applied budget, budget source, truncated flag — rides on the response parts through the persistence gate, the per-tool and combined truncation passes, the batch finalizer, and hook rewrites. Each layer logs a `tool_result_size` event, and `LlmChat` logs `tool_result_injected` exactly once per result, pairing the raw size with what actually went to the model.

Producers now declare their raw output size instead of letting the scheduler guess: shell reports an unknown size when capture discarded output, SSH exec and self-bounded read_file/read-many and capped MCP resource reads declare unknown rather than a falsely equal raw size, and grep, ripGrep, web_search and the execution tool report the size of the unbounded body. Post-settlement throws, cancellations and hook replacements are treated as replacement outcomes that inherit nothing from the producer. Loaded or restored history and speculation-accept replays are marked as already injected so a retry never double-counts. To keep that exactly-once guarantee under retry, the dispatch closure now checks the abort signal at the start of every attempt instead of once before the retry loop — an aborted attempt must not run the provenance-marking loop, which would permanently suppress that result's one owed injection event. Abort stays a non-retryable failure, so retry outcomes are unchanged. A design document (EN + zh-CN) describes the accounting model.

## Why it's needed

Token burn from tool results was previously invisible: nothing recorded how large a result was when produced, which layer reduced it, or how much reached the model, so truncation bugs (including the silent self-bounding producers called out in the review of #13652) could not even be observed. This accounting is the foundation parts ② and ③ build on.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run `npm run build` and `npm run typecheck` (both pass), then the touched suites in `packages/core`: `npx vitest run src/tools/tool-output-size.test.ts src/tools/tool-response-finalizer.test.ts src/tools/truncation.test.ts src/core/coreToolScheduler.test.ts src/core/llm-chat.test.ts src/followup/speculation.test.ts src/telemetry/loggers.test.ts src/telemetry/metrics.test.ts src/tools/execution-tool.test.ts src/tools/grep.test.ts src/tools/ripGrep.test.ts src/tools/shell.test.ts src/tools/read-file.test.ts src/tools/read-mcp-resource.test.ts src/services/ssh-execution-environment.test.ts src/core/nonInteractiveToolExecutor.test.ts` and in `packages/cli`: `npx vitest run src/ui/hooks/useToolScheduler.test.ts src/serve/hosted-workspace-tool-turn.test.ts`. Locally observed: 1203/1203 then 902/902 passed in core and 283/283 in cli. For behavior, run any session with telemetry on and confirm `tool_result_size` events appear per layer and `tool_result_injected` once per tool call with raw vs injected lengths.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A (telemetry and internal accounting; no UI change).

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

N/A — unit tests only.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: provenance rides on shared `Part` objects via a symbol; the review threads R10-1/R10-2 from #13652 about mutation after batch-budget cuts carry over here and are called out for the reviewer.
- Not validated / out of scope: the recoverable-preview envelope and the web_fetch changes land in parts ② and ③.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none; additive telemetry fields only.

Design docs: docs/design/tool-result-size-accounting.md and docs/design/tool-result-size-accounting.zh-CN.md.

## Linked Issues

Split part ① of #13652 (does not close it; #13652 is closed manually in favor of this stack).

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

本 PR 是 #13652 拆分的第一片：让工具结果的大小从产生到注入模型全程可计量。新增测量助手对 `PartListUnion` 负载（文本与结构化 functionResponse，图像按 chat-compression 配置估算）计量，并把原始大小、生效预算、预算来源、截断标记作为 provenance 附带在响应 parts 上，贯穿持久化闸门、per-tool 与 combined 截断、batch finalizer 与 hook 改写。每一层记录 `tool_result_size` 事件，`LlmChat` 对每个结果恰好在注入时记录一次 `tool_result_injected`，对比原始与注入大小。

各 producer 现在如实声明原始输出大小：shell 在 capture 丢弃输出时声明 unknown，SSH exec、自我限长的 read_file/read-many、被截断的 MCP resource 读取声明 unknown 而非谎报相等；grep、ripGrep、web_search 与 execution tool 上报未限长全文的大小。结算后抛错、取消与 hook 替换一律视为替换型结果，不继承 producer 的大小。恢复/加载的历史与 speculation 接受的回放会被标记为已注入，重试不会重复计数。为在重试下保住这一恰好一次的保证，发送闭包改为在每次尝试开头检查 abort 信号（此前只在进入重试循环前检查一次）——被中止的尝试不得执行 provenance 标记循环，否则会永久抑制该结果唯一应得的注入事件；abort 仍不可重试，重试结果不变。设计文档含中英文双版本。

动机：此前工具结果的 token 消耗完全不可见——无法知道结果产生时多大、哪一层削减了它、又有多少进入模型；#13652 评审指出的自我限长 producer 静默问题也因此无法观测。本计量面是第 ② 片与第 ③ 片的基础。

验证：`npm run build` 与 `npm run typecheck` 均通过；上述 core 单测 1203 + 902 全部通过，cli 283 全部通过。风险：provenance 通过 symbol 挂在共享 Part 对象上，#13652 的 R10-1/R10-2 关于 batch 预算变更后可变性的讨论随本片继续。范围外：可恢复预览 envelope 与 web_fetch 改动在第 ②③ 片。无 breaking change。

</details>

prs.title: test(cli): retry ENOTEMPTY in hosted harness teardowns
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds bounded filesystem retries to the three remaining hosted harness teardown cleanups, matching the five-retry, 100 ms delay policy already used by the other two cleanups.

## Why it's needed

Final wake-pump writes can overlap removal of the temporary session tree. Without retries, a transient `ENOTEMPTY` fails the teardown even when the test assertions pass. All five cleanups now use the same policy for that race.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Confirm that the hosted harness session tests finish their assertions and teardown hooks. For a deterministic cleanup check, arrange one file write immediately before the final directory removal: all five cleanup configurations should remove their temporary trees. With no concurrent write, cleanup should complete without waiting for a retry.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — no user-facing change or UI demo.

A temporary filesystem probe read the five actual cleanup option bags and inserted a real file immediately before the final native directory removal. Before the patch, the three bare cleanups failed with native `ENOTEMPTY` errors and left their scratch roots; the two existing retrying cleanups succeeded. After the patch, all five cleanups succeeded under the same controlled timing, and all five quiet-path cleanups succeeded without a retry delay. This isolates the cleanup behavior; it does not claim a naturally occurring wake-pump failure during the full suite.

Validation: the complete hosted harness session test file passed all 593 tests. The root typecheck (all workspaces plus integration-test code), build and bundle, ESLint, Prettier, and `git diff --check` also passed. The normal pre-commit hook passed without bypasses.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :---: | :---: |
| 🍏 macOS | ⚠️ not tested locally |
| 🪟 Windows | ✅ 593 tests, controlled filesystem probe, root typecheck, build/bundle, lint and formatting |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ not tested locally |

### Environment (optional)

Windows, PowerShell, Node.js v24.19.0, pinned pnpm v11.24.0.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: transient filesystem failures can add a bounded cleanup delay, matching the existing retry policy.
- Not validated / out of scope: a naturally occurring wake-pump race, other operating systems, and the full monorepo test suite. The change is limited to three cleanup option bags.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #14627

<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 此 PR 的改动

## 修改原因

wake pump 的最后几次写入可能与临时会话目录的删除重叠。缺少重试时，即使测试断言通过，瞬时的 `ENOTEMPTY` 也会导致清理钩子失败。现在五处清理都采用相同策略处理这一竞态。

## 审阅者测试计划

### 验证方式

确认 hosted harness session 测试的断言和清理钩子均能完成。若需要确定性的清理验证，可在最后一次目录删除之前安排一次文件写入：五处清理配置都应能删除临时目录。没有并发写入时，清理应无需等待重试。

### 修复前后证据

不适用——没有用户可见的行为变化或界面演示。

临时文件系统验证脚本读取了五处真实清理调用的参数，并在最后一次原生目录删除之前写入一个真实文件。修复前，缺少重试的三处清理均收到原生 `ENOTEMPTY` 错误，并留下临时目录；已有重试的两处清理成功。修复后，在相同的受控时序下，五处清理全部成功；没有并发写入时，五处也全部成功，且没有重试等待。这验证了清理行为，没有声称在完整测试套件中自然触发了 wake pump 故障。

| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ 未在本地测试 |

### 环境

Windows、PowerShell、Node.js v24.19.0、仓库固定的 pnpm v11.24.0。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：瞬时文件系统错误可能增加有界的清理等待，与已有重试策略一致。
- 未验证或范围之外：自然发生的 wake pump 竞态、其他操作系统以及整个 monorepo 的完整测试套件。改动仅涉及三处清理参数。

prs.title: feat(memory): add scoped external import jobs for CLI and HTTP
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds a Qwen-owned external memory import service for CLI and cloud integrations, starting with Codex. Clients submit relative Markdown paths and contents, inspect a deterministic preview, explicitly select sections and destination scope, then start durable background consolidation using the selected workspace's configured model. Results enter native memory search, fetch, recall and forget. Main checkouts and registered linked worktrees share the imported project layer while ordinary memory isolation remains unchanged.

The service exposes `memory_import_v1`, workspace-qualified HTTP preview/submit/status/source/cancel/retry endpoints, and offline `memory import codex --dry-run --json`. Unknown source scope stays unassigned. The server owns destination paths and validates active workspace trust; it never falls back to the primary runtime. Only selected source snapshots are retained. Journaled publication, idempotency, cancellation and retry protect existing, edited and forgotten memories.

Consolidation uses bounded batches per source project and confirmed scope, a compact same-scope metadata index with relevant evidence, and durable aggregate call/token reservations. Preview exposes usage estimates without reading native memories or invoking a model. Failure, cancellation and retry do not replenish the budget. Saved batch proposals preserve per-source recovery and edit/forget protection; imported repository identity lookups are cached and skipped entirely when no imported layer exists.

## Why it's needed

A cloud runtime cannot read a user's laptop filesystem. Direct per-bullet conversion also loses historical context and does not reconcile old knowledge with existing native memory. This replaces #14149 with shared backend capabilities and model-backed consolidation. No external product UI, independent collector, dependency installation requirement or unrelated CI repair is included.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- Submit a synthetic Codex source set containing two projects and a referenced distilled Markdown resource. Preview should return grouped sections, references and assignment reasons without model calls or memory/task writes. An ambiguous section should stay unassigned.
- Select only one project and submit to a trusted non-primary workspace. Observe queued/running/completed results, then fetch its retained source and search the native result. The other project's text must never reach the model or retained snapshot; unknown/untrusted/draining destinations must not fall back to primary.
- Repeat the same request/key and then try another key with the same selected content. Native documents should not multiply. Edit or forget an imported document; another import must return conflict rather than restore it.
- Cancel during consolidation, retry a failed item, and restart after a forced process kill before/after publication. Recovery should wait out a dead worker's lease, preserve accurate counts/refs and publish each document only once.
- Verify the imported project result through a linked worktree, and verify an independent clone remains isolated. Ordinary per-worktree memory must retain its existing behavior.

- Verify a 12-section selected project is processed in two bounded calls, while excluded groups never reach the model. Preview should show group and aggregate usage estimates; retrying a budget-exhausted task must not reset the allowance. Interrupt between publications and verify saved proposals resume without another paid call or restoring edited/forgotten knowledge.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: the installed baseline CLI rejected `memory import codex`, and the base daemon did not advertise the capability. After: synthetic shipped-CLI dry-runs (bare, leading debug and safe mode) returned versioned pure JSON with zero network attempts and zero filesystem changes. Confirmed CLI import and the real bundled daemon → real ACP child → loopback OpenAI-compatible model produced native searchable memory without unselected input. Bare/safe confirmed import rejected before source access or authentication.

Initial implementation tests passed: 559 CLI cases, 31 core cases, and the focused cold-workspace ACP bridge case. Full workspace build and typecheck passed; affected packages were rebuilt after final edits, with a final bundle and CLI typecheck. ESLint and formatting passed. Real SIGKILL probes left stale lock directories and recovered automatically after approximately 120 seconds, without manual lock deletion; both interruption points produced one document and correct original-batch counts. Two self-audit passes and a local medium review found no remaining issue; these are not formal approval.

Latest cost update after merging main: 55 focused CLI and 126 core tests passed, along with full build, bundle, typecheck, lint and format. Real bundled CLI/HTTP each processed 12 selected sources as [8, 4], with two requests and no extra request on repetition. Synthetic existing-context payload fell from 199,080 to 2,170 bytes. Interrupted-batch, budget-recovery and cross-group ordering probes passed. Production billing savings are not asserted.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :-- | :-- |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ Synthetic CLI, real daemon/ACP/model transport, native memory and process recovery |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ Awaiting CI |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ Awaiting CI |

### Environment (optional)

Isolated synthetic HOME, runtime, source and repository directories; deterministic loopback provider only. The full build used an 8 GiB Node heap. No actual user memory or production provider was accessed.

## Risk & Scope

- Budget limits: 32 logical invocations and 512,000 conservative reserved token units per task, with 8,192 output tokens per request. These are not guaranteed provider-billed-token or currency caps; oversized metadata/relevant evidence fails closed.
- Main risk or tradeoff: this is a cross-package feature with native memory reader and ACP integration; maintainer architectural review is requested. Model output is schema/native-format checked and cannot overwrite existing documents, but production-model semantic quality still requires evaluation.
- Not validated / out of scope: external product UI, standalone collectors, continuous sync, cross-instance sync and production deployment. SSH workspaces and legacy memory base/local path overrides are rejected in v1. Resource/context limits are documented; oversized context fails instead of silently truncating.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: additive capability and endpoints; ordinary writable memory roots remain unchanged. This does not migrate experimental state from #14149.

Design and API contracts are complete and synchronized in both languages: [Design (English)](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/external-memory-import/docs/design/external-memory-import.md), [设计（中文）](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/external-memory-import/docs/design/external-memory-import.zh-CN.md), [API (English)](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/external-memory-import/docs/design/external-memory-import-api.md), [接口（中文）](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/external-memory-import/docs/design/external-memory-import-api.zh-CN.md).

## Linked Issues

Supersedes #14149 following the requested backend redesign.

prs.title: fix(ui): bottom-align short VP content so blank space is at top
prs.body:
## What this PR does

In VP mode (`useTerminalBuffer`, default on), when the conversation fits within the viewport the content was top-aligned, leaving a blank gap between the last message and the composer (reported in #9300, happens in every session). This bottom-aligns short bottom-stuck content: blank space moves to the TOP and the latest message sits directly above the composer, matching standard chat TUIs.

Implementation: in `VirtualizedList`, when `isStickingToBottom` and content fits (`maxScroll === 0`), compute `bottomAlignGap = scrollableContainerHeight - totalHeight`, render it as a leading spacer, and keep the root at full `containerHeight` so there is room. Overflow (`maxScroll > 0`) and scrolled-away cases are unchanged.

## Why it's needed

#9300: default-on VP mode showed a large blank area between the last message and the composer in every session (short conversations and collapsed thinking blocks). High-frequency, default-on visual regression on the primary surface — worth a quick fix.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. `npx vitest run packages/cli/src/ui/components/shared/VirtualizedList.test.tsx` — 32 tests pass, including the 3 updated to the new bottom-aligned layout.
2. `npx vitest run packages/cli/src/ui/components/MainContent.test.tsx packages/cli/src/ui/components/shared/ScrollableList.test.tsx` — 36 pass (no layout regression).
3. Manual (iTerm2, VP mode): start a short session — content should sit at the bottom above the composer with blank at top; collapse a thinking block (Ctrl+O) — released space appears at top, not between content and composer.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: content top-aligned, blank gap between last message and composer. After: content bottom-aligned, blank at top. (Needs a live terminal to visually confirm; unit tests pin the new frame layout.)

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ⚠️ needs manual confirm (reported on iTerm2) |
| 🪟 Windows |   N/A  |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅ (unit tests) |

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: changes the short-content layout from top-aligned/collapsed to bottom-aligned; three tests that pinned the old collapse behavior were updated to the new expectation. Scrolling/overflow math is untouched (`scrollableContainerHeight` unchanged).
- Not validated / out of scope: live iTerm2 visual confirmation (reporter's environment); height-overestimation cases where `totalHeight >= containerHeight` (those already bottom-show via `clampedScrollTop = maxScroll`).
- Breaking changes / migration notes: None.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #9300

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

VP 模式（默认开启）下，当会话内容高度小于视口时，内容顶部对齐，导致最后一条消息与输入框之间出现大片空白（#9300，每个 session 都出现）。本 PR 将短的、贴底的内容改为底部对齐：空白移到顶部，最新消息紧贴输入框上方，与主流 chat TUI 一致。

实现：`VirtualizedList` 中当 `isStickingToBottom` 且内容放得下（`maxScroll === 0`）时，计算 `bottomAlignGap = scrollableContainerHeight - totalHeight` 作为顶部占位，并保持 root 为满 `containerHeight`。溢出或已上滚的场景不变。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险：短内容布局从顶部对齐/折叠改为底部对齐，3 个固定旧行为的测试已更新；滚动数学未动。
- 未验证：iTerm2 真机视觉确认；`totalHeight >= containerHeight` 的高度高估场景（该场景本就通过 `clampedScrollTop = maxScroll` 底部显示）。
- 破坏性变更：无。

</details>

prs.title: fix(cli): keep one-shot system reminders out of the user's own message
prs.body:
## What this PR does

One-shot reminders that the interactive terminal UI folds into the front of a prompt are no longer shown back to the user. The transcript line for a prompt, the entry written to the cross-session ↑-recall history, the text refilled into the composer after a cancelled turn, and the same prompt as rebuilt when a session is resumed now all show what the user typed. The request sent to the model still carries the reminder exactly as before, and the machine-readable sidecar mirror of the conversation is deliberately left untouched, because its job is to report what was actually sent.

Removal is leading-only: a reminder tag the user pasted into the middle of their own prompt stays visible, and a tag that is never closed is left in place rather than swallowed. If a prompt were nothing but an envelope, the transcript keeps showing it rather than rendering an empty bubble.

## Why it's needed

Resuming a session that still had paused background agents made the first prompt render as a block of internal instructions — how to list agents, and how to message one by task id — followed by the user's own words. The user never wrote that text and cannot act on it. Cancelling the turn put the same block into the editable input box, so resubmitting sent internal context to the model as literal user text, and resuming that session again replayed it from the recording. This was reported internally during token-consumption governance work.

None of it was needed to keep the user informed. Each of the three notices that can be injected this way already has its own user-facing signal: restored background agents and a restored worktree each add an info line to the transcript, and workflow keyword steering lights an indicator in the footer. The headless and ACP runtimes both attach the notice as a separate part alongside the prompt rather than folding it in, so the interactive terminal path was the only one mixing a model-only payload into the string it also renders, logs and restores. This separates the two roles again at the points where a prompt is read back, instead of restructuring how the notice is delivered — the delivery side is threaded through the submission queue, speculation matching and side-question routing, and rewriting it is a much larger change than the defect warrants.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Start a session, launch a background agent, leave it paused/recoverable, exit, then `qwen --resume` that session.
2. Type any first prompt. Before: the transcript shows a `<system-reminder>` block reading "1 background agent was restored from this session. Use list_agents to inspect it and send_message with a task_id to continue one.", a blank line, then the prompt. After: only the prompt, with the separate info line "Restored 1 background agent from this session. Open Background tasks to inspect it." still present above it.
3. Confirm the model still receives the reminder — ask it what it was told about restored agents, or inspect the request payload in an API trace. It should be unchanged.
4. Cancel path: on that first prompt press ESC before any output arrives. The composer should refill with the prompt only, not the envelope. Resubmit and confirm the transcript is still clean.
5. ↑-recall: exit, start a new session in the same directory, press ↑. The recalled entry should be the prompt without the envelope.
6. Resume again: `qwen --resume` the session from step 1 and confirm the earlier prompt now renders without the envelope (this is the recording-replay path, fixed separately from the live path).
7. Paste guard: submit `before <system-reminder>x</system-reminder> after` and confirm the transcript shows it verbatim.
8. The worktree and workflow-steering notices reproduce the same way through their own one-shot latches (`--worktree`, or a prompt containing the workflow keyword with the feature enabled); both should now render only the user's words while keeping their info line and footer indicator.

Automated:

```bash
cd packages/cli && npx vitest run \
  src/ui/hooks/use-llm-stream.test.tsx \
  src/ui/utils/resumeHistoryUtils.test.ts \
  src/ui/utils/historyUtils.test.ts \
  src/ui/AppContainer.test.tsx
# 554 passed
npx tsc --noEmit            # clean
npx eslint <changed files>  # clean
npx prettier --check <changed files>  # clean
```

### Evidence (Before & After)

No terminal recording for this one — evidence is at the unit level, and I'm flagging that explicitly rather than implying a TUI capture was done.

- After: two new cases pin the live path (model request keeps the envelope while the transcript and the recall log carry only the user's words; stacked envelopes strip, mid-message and unterminated ones do not) and two pin the resume path (an envelope-only record restores as the bare prompt; a pasted envelope survives).
- Before: three pre-existing cancel-path expectations pinned the old text — they asserted the envelope inside the value that is both compared for identity and written back into the composer. Those three had to be updated, which is the direct before/after evidence for the cancel-restore path.
- Not run locally to completion: the full `packages/cli` suite. Every test file that mentions the reminder tag was run individually and passes, no snapshot contains it, and CI covers the rest.
- Pre-existing and unrelated: `src/acp-integration/session/Session.worktree.test.ts` fails 8 tests with `this.config.setCurrentSessionScheduledTaskCreator is not a function`. Verified identical on the base commit `0ef35351e9` with this branch's changes absent — the test's mocked config lacks a method the ACP session now calls. Not touched here.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

macOS: unit tests, typecheck, lint and format on the changed files. No manual TUI run and no Windows/Linux run — the change is string handling with no platform-specific branch, but the manual steps above are the ones worth walking on a real terminal.

Fixes #11553

prs.title: feat(web-shell): add account-wide code review workbench
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds a default-off Code Review workbench to Web Shell. It reads the daemon operator’s GitHub account through `gh` and shows open pull requests across repositories in “Created by me” and “Needs my review”; the latter combines review requests and assignments. Users can page through the inbox, filter loaded results, or paste a complete PR URL without selecting or cloning a repository.

The workbench provides overview, files and activity views, compact comments/reviewer/check summaries, and draggable side panes with keyboard resizing and persisted widths. Current-head checks collapse earlier attempts of the same workflow/event/job while retaining distinct jobs with qualified labels. Reviewer states and comment counts come from each reviewer’s latest review. Users enable the default-off workbench from Settings → Experimental. The switch is stored in User settings, respects System locks and ignores workspace settings; it remains available without a local workspace. Disabling hides the navigation entry, exits an open workbench and prevents disabled deep links from reading PRs. Older daemons hide the entry, and URL-enabled hosts support enabled PR deep links and browser history.

## Why it's needed

The existing repository PR dialog does not provide an account-wide place to triage authored PRs and incoming review work. A dedicated workbench lets users inspect PR state and CI alongside local sessions. This first phase establishes the read-only workflow and an explicit feature switch for later maintenance capabilities.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Connect Web Shell to a daemon with an authenticated `gh` account. The Code Review entry should initially be hidden. Open Settings → Experimental (through More when using the navigation rail), enable Code Review Workbench, and confirm the entry appears and both inbox groups span accessible repositories. Repeat without a selected workspace. Disable it again and confirm the entry disappears, an open workbench exits and direct links no longer load PR data. Reload to check persistence. A System override should lock the switch.
2. Open PRs with the same number in different repositories, paste a complete PR URL, change selections quickly, and load more results. Confirm selection identity uses the complete URL and delayed responses cannot replace the selected PR or mix accounts. Filtering applies to loaded rows; search limits remain indicated.
3. Inspect overview, patches and activity. Compare current-head checks and individual reviewer states with GitHub. Earlier attempts of the same job should collapse, while checks from different workflows/events remain distinguishable. Compact counts and GitHub links retain access to bounded results.
4. Drag both dividers, resize them with the keyboard, reload and try a narrow viewport. Confirm widths persist, content stays usable, and avatars have a fallback. Check English/Chinese and light/dark appearances.
5. Test the normal same-origin Vite development entry and a token-protected daemon’s direct `/code-review` link/reload. HTML must load while API reads remain authenticated. An embedded host without URL navigation should return to chat if the connected daemon loses code-review support.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: the existing PR dialog at upstream base `a703a76ae2413601d77ca07dd1addaebba5fe148`, using synthetic fixture data (1440×1000, dark theme).

![Before: existing repository PR dialog using fixture data](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qqqys/qwen-code/2d17de676b2767b517fc6e42a7ba55bbc56a9a7f/pr-assets/code-review-workbench/before-fixture.png)

After: the new account-wide workbench from the final local source, using synthetic fixture data (1600×1000, light theme). These show the old and new interaction surfaces; they are not a pixel-matched comparison of one PR. No private repository inbox data is included.

![After: account-wide code review workbench using fixture data](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qqqys/qwen-code/2d17de676b2767b517fc6e42a7ba55bbc56a9a7f/pr-assets/code-review-workbench/after-fixture.png)

Local verification includes 47 core tests, 23 account-route tests, 22 workbench component tests and the 21-case Chromium fixture suite from implementation, with unchanged-source evidence checked before submission. The final integration fixes additionally passed 47 CLI static/pre-auth tests, 22 Vite tests, 3 focused App tests and a fresh final-source Chromium capture. The embedded-host and Vite defects were reproduced before their fixes; authenticated direct navigation was independently reproduced using the actual middleware sequence. The final full workspace build, workspace/integration typecheck, changed-file lint and formatting checks all passed; details are recorded in the accompanying E2E report.

The unified Experimental setting, entry visibility and deep-link gates passed 77 focused unit tests and the complete 24-case Chromium fixture suite with no retries on macOS / Node.js 22.17. The full workspace build, bundle, typecheck, changed-file lint/format and 36 built-artifact checks passed. This includes first enablement without a workspace, zero workspace-settings requests in that case, persisted toggles, disabled deep links, delayed enabled links and System locks. These are local results; hosted CI is reported separately.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |

prs.title: feat(cli): paste clipboard text with Ctrl+V on Linux
prs.body:
## What this PR does

On Linux, `Ctrl+V` now reads the clipboard's **text** when the clipboard holds no image. Previously the only clipboard reader in the TUI was the image path, so pressing `Ctrl+V` with text or a link on the clipboard either printed "未找到受支持的剪贴板工具" (no supported clipboard tool found) or did nothing at all, and users had to fall back to their terminal's own paste binding.

Reads are driven by what the clipboard itself reports. `wl-paste --list-types` (Wayland) and the `TARGETS` atom (X11) are enumerated, and each reported name is classified from the standards rather than from a list of types this code has heard of: ICCCM's text atoms (`TEXT`, `STRING`, `UTF8_STRING`) plus `text/plain` are the preferred read, any other `text/*` the source lists is the fallback, and ICCCM's selection bookkeeping properties (`TARGETS`, `MULTIPLE`, `SAVE_TARGETS`, `DELETE`, `INCR`, `TIMESTAMP`, `VERSION`) are never requested. Each read asks for the exact name the tool reported, so `text/plain;charset=utf-8` is requested under that name rather than a guessed one.

A paste too large for the input buffer is still collapsed into a `[Pasted Content N chars]` placeholder, but on both collapse routes — `Ctrl+V` read through the clipboard tool, and a large bracketed paste from the terminal — its expanded form is now described to the model: attributed to the clipboard, given the standing of a file the user asked to open rather than a message from them, and closed from outside so a forged end marker inside the pasted data cannot promote what follows it. Shell mode is the exception, because there the expanded placeholder is the command that gets recorded and run. Selections are normalised to LF line endings, which a `text/uri-list` never has on its own. Anything the clipboard tool cannot answer — no display server, tool missing, spawn failure, timeout, empty or whitespace-only selection — resolves to "nothing to paste" instead of an error. macOS and Windows behavior is untouched.

## Why it's needed

Reported in our user group: on Ubuntu, pasting text into the input box was impossible via `Ctrl+V` — the client only tried to read an image, and when none was found it told the user to install `wl-clipboard`, which does not help with text at all. The same gesture already handles images and file paths, so text is the missing branch of an existing feature rather than a new surface.

## Review round 1

The first cut read the clipboard from inside the image branch with hardcoded per-tool type names, and its tests only proved that a stubbed spawn returned its stub. Addressed as follows:

- **Structure**: `Ctrl+V` is one dispatcher (`handleClipboardPaste`) that resolves an image into an attachment and everything else into text; the insert path is its own callback. This also fixed a real defect in the first cut, which read `buffer` and `nextLargePastePlaceholder` without declaring them as dependencies.
- **Type handling**: the per-tool candidate lists are gone. Enumeration and a single type table decide what is readable, and each read asks for the exact name the tool reported (so `text/plain;charset=utf-8` is requested under that name, not a guessed one).
- **Provenance**: a collapsed paste is submitted inside `<clipboard-paste>` markers with a trailing line stating it came from the clipboard and must be treated as untrusted data — on both collapse routes, since a large bracketed paste from the terminal is no more the user's own writing than a selection read back through `wl-paste`. Shell mode is the deliberate exception: there the expanded placeholder is the command that gets recorded to history and executed, so it stays raw, and the existing shell-history case pins that carve-out. The markers are provenance for the model, not a sandbox — content can contain a closing marker, which is why the note says "treat as data" rather than claiming containment.
- **Tests**: the clipboard is now simulated as a tool that lists its types and answers reads per type, and each case asserts both the result and the exact sequence of types requested. Coverage is one table: a charset-parameterised text offer, text preferred over a co-offered URI list, a CRLF URI list, X11 atoms mapped to text without `TARGETS` ever being read back as content, fallthrough to the next atom when the first is empty, an image-only clipboard requesting nothing, unknown types requesting nothing, and a whitespace-only selection. The simulator is withdrawn after each case because the file's `beforeEach` clears call history but not implementations.

## Review round 2

- **Was the hand-written type table sound?** No, and it is gone. It carried rows no standard defines — `UNICODE` (an XFT-era atom) and a bare `uri-list` — and it named `text/uri-list` explicitly when the enumeration already says what is offered. Classification now comes from the names the standards define: ICCCM's three text atoms plus `text/plain` are the preferred tier, any other `text/*` is the fallback tier, and ICCCM's bookkeeping properties are excluded by name. Nothing is requested that the clipboard did not list.
- **Verified against a real clipboard?** Not possible from this environment, and I am not going to imply otherwise: the authoring machine is macOS arm64 with no `wl-paste`, `xclip`, `xsel`, `xvfb-run` or container runtime available, and the reader is Linux-only by design, so no live Wayland/X11 enumeration can be produced here. What I could check locally is that no other part of this repository maintains a clipboard type list to borrow (it does not — `getWlPasteImageTypes`'s `image/png`/`image/bmp` pair was the only one, and it is kept as-is). A real `wl-paste --list-types` and `xclip -t TARGETS -o` dump from an Ubuntu session would be worth attaching to this PR; the tier rule is written so that any such dump is accepted without code changes.
- **Why `text/uri-list` at all?** It is no longer a case in the code — it falls out of the `text/*` fallback tier, which is the general rule rather than a named exception. The reason a fallback tier exists is that a source may list nothing but a non-plain `text/*` type, and without the tier `Ctrl+V` would silently do nothing there. The visible trade-off is that a selection offered only as `text/html` now pastes markup instead of nothing; that is stated in a test case rather than hidden.
- **The description was too thin.** Rewritten along injection-defence lines: it attributes the block to the clipboard and says the user may not have read it; it gives the content the standing of a file the user asked to open rather than a message from them; it keeps telling the model to act on pasted material that matches the user's actual request, because refusing pasted content would defeat the feature; it names the shapes it must not swallow (a system message, a permission or policy change, a confirmation the user gave); and it closes the block from outside, so a forged `</clipboard-paste>` inside the data cannot promote whatever follows it. One case pins those properties.

## Final diff

- `packages/cli/src/ui/utils/clipboardUtils.ts`: `readStdout()` (buffered stdout, timeout kill, empty string for anything that is not a successful read), `classifyClipboardType()` over the ICCCM text and bookkeeping sets, `listClipboardTypes()` on top of the Wayland/X11 enumeration, and `readClipboardText()` which requests only listed types — plain tier first — and normalises line endings. The wl-paste enumeration the image path already had is generalised into `listWlPasteTypes()` with one cache, and the image filter reads from that same list, so a single `Ctrl+V` costs one enumeration.
- `packages/cli/src/ui/components/InputPrompt.tsx`: `handleClipboardImage` becomes `handleClipboardPaste` — image resolves to an attachment, anything else to text — with the insert path split into `insertClipboardText`. `describeClipboardPaste()` frames a collapsed paste for the model and is applied on both collapse routes, skipped in shell mode.
- Tests: 9 table cases driving a clipboard that lists its types and answers reads per type, plus 4 component cases (text paste, collapsed paste described on submit, image wins over text, and the description's own properties).

## Evidence

<details>
<summary>Verification</summary>

Verified by unit tests rather than a live screenshot — this change needs a Wayland/X11 session, which the authoring environment does not have:

```
npx vitest run src/ui/utils/clipboardUtils.test.ts        → 70 passed
npx vitest run src/ui/components/InputPrompt.test.tsx     → 230 passed, 1 skipped
npx eslint <4 changed files>                              → clean
npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json (packages/cli)          → 172 errors, identical to
                                                             the same count on the
                                                             pre-change tree; none in
                                                             the changed files
```

</details>

## Contribution & Risk

- **Type**: Contribution Type 3 — optimization / user-facing feature
- **Scope**: Only `packages/cli/src/ui` (TUI input handling). No core, auth, provider, config, tools, or service modules; no daemon or channel code.
- **Linked Issues**: N/A — reported directly by users in the group chat; no GitHub issue filed.
- [x] I have read the [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md), the code of conduct, and the PR instructions.
- [x] I have searched open PRs for a similar change and confirmed none exists.
- [ ] Not applicable — this PR does not change or add any UI component.

prs.title: test(managed-agent): Measure the post-commit gate as per-round growth (#14197)
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Changes the MQ2 post-commit latency gate in `EventTransportBrokerGate` to compare the flag-on and flag-off arms as the per-round growth at p95, instead of comparing the p95 order statistics of two independent sample distributions. The arms are interleaved on one thread, so machine-wide noise on a shared CI runner lands on both arms of a round and cancels; a real regression — the event transport adding work to every committing-thread publish — shifts every round's delta and still fails the one-millisecond budget. The journal hand-off keeps its absolute 20 ms p95 budget, and the `target/event-transport-latency.json` record keeps the on/off figures with the delta added for forensics. No production code changes.

## Why it's needed

The gate failed on main (#14197) less than two hours after it landed in #14109, on a commit that does not touch the event-transport path. The measured work per arm is tens of microseconds, so on the shared two-core CI runners scheduler preemption and GC jitter dominate the samples, and a whole-millisecond budget over a difference of two order statistics trips on timing noise alone. The rocketmq-client-java 5.1.0 sources confirm both production paths hand off asynchronously (a bounded-queue offer for the public transport, a non-blocking gRPC enqueue for the journal wire), so the fix belongs in the test's statistic, not in the product.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Start the gate broker with `scripts/rocketmq-lite-broker.sh start` (with the CI's `RMQ_EXTRA_GROUPS`/`RMQ_NORMAL_TOPIC`/`RMQ_NORMAL_GROUPS` settings), then run `mvn -f packages/sdk-java/managed-agent-server/pom.xml -Pevent-transport-broker-gates -Dqwen.gate.rocketmq.endpoints=127.0.0.1:18081 -Dqwen.gate.rocketmq.topic=qwen-managed-events -Dqwen.gate.rocketmq.normal-topic=qwen-managed-events-normal clean verify`. Expected: all seven gate rows pass and `packages/sdk-java/managed-agent-server/target/event-transport-latency.json` reports `publishP95Micros.delta` and `hubDeliveryP95Micros.delta` far under 1000 µs. The EventTransport broker gates job on this PR is the authoritative check on a shared runner.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A (test-only change; no user-visible behavior). Before: `thePostCommitPathDoesNotRegress` asserted `p95(on) <= p95(off) + 1ms` and flaked on main. After: it asserts `p95(per-round on-minus-off) <= 1ms`; run three times locally (uncontended, original code under 2-core CPU contention, fixed code under the same contention) with all seven tests green each time and the delta p95 at 26–31 µs.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ not tested |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ tested |

### Environment (optional)

Temurin JDK 21 (tests) / 17 (broker), RocketMQ 5.5.1 single-node cluster from `scripts/rocketmq-lite-broker.sh`, Maven 3.9.11.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the gate's statistic changes from a difference of two p95 estimates to the p95 of per-round growth; both implement the design doc's "may not grow by a millisecond at p95", and a uniform per-round cost still fails deterministically.
- Not validated / out of scope: the original flake was not reproduced on demand (one contended run of the original code passed — it is a tail-probability failure); the journal hand-off's absolute 20 ms budget is unchanged; no production behavior changes.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #14197

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

把 `EventTransportBrokerGate` 中 MQ2 提交后延迟门禁的比较方式,从"两个独立样本分布各自的 p95 次序统计量之差"改为"逐轮增长量的 p95"。两臂在同一线程上交替执行,共享 CI 运行器上的整机噪声会落在同一轮的两臂上从而相互抵消;而真正的回归——event transport 给每一次提交线程 publish 都增加工作量——会使每轮 delta 整体平移,仍然触发 1 毫秒预算。journal 交接保留原有的 20ms 绝对 p95 预算;`target/event-transport-latency.json` 保留 on/off 数据并新增 delta 以供排查。不改动任何生产代码。

## 为什么需要

该门禁在 #14109 合入后不到两小时就在 main 上失败(#14197),而失败的提交并未改动 event-transport 相关路径。每臂单次测量只有几十微秒,在共享的双核 CI 运行器上,调度抢占和 GC 抖动主导了样本,对两个次序统计量之差设 1 毫秒预算会被纯计时噪声触发。查阅 rocketmq-client-java 5.1.0 源码可确认两条生产路径都是异步交接(公开 transport 是一次有界队列 offer,journal 线是一次非阻塞 gRPC 入队),因此修复应落在测试的统计方法上,而不是产品上。

## 评审者测试计划

### 如何验证

用 `scripts/rocketmq-lite-broker.sh start` 启动门禁 broker(带上 CI 的 `RMQ_EXTRA_GROUPS`/`RMQ_NORMAL_TOPIC`/`RMQ_NORMAL_GROUPS` 设置),然后运行 `mvn -f packages/sdk-java/managed-agent-server/pom.xml -Pevent-transport-broker-gates -Dqwen.gate.rocketmq.endpoints=127.0.0.1:18081 -Dqwen.gate.rocketmq.topic=qwen-managed-events -Dqwen.gate.rocketmq.normal-topic=qwen-managed-events-normal clean verify`。预期:全部七条门禁行通过,且 `packages/sdk-java/managed-agent-server/target/event-transport-latency.json` 中 `publishP95Micros.delta` 和 `hubDeliveryP95Micros.delta` 远低于 1000 µs。本 PR 的 EventTransport broker gates CI 任务是共享运行器上的权威验证。

### 前后对比证据

N/A(纯测试改动,无用户可见行为)。修复前:`thePostCommitPathDoesNotRegress` 断言 `p95(on) <= p95(off) + 1ms`,在 main 上抖动失败。修复后:断言 `p95(逐轮 on 减 off) <= 1ms`;本地共运行三次(无争用、原始代码双核 CPU 争用、修复后代码同样争用),每次七条测试全部通过,delta p95 为 26–31 µs。

### 测试平台

|     系统     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ 未测试 |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ 未测试 |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ 已测试 |

### 环境(可选)

Temurin JDK 21(测试)/ 17(broker),RocketMQ 5.5.1 单机集群(`scripts/rocketmq-lite-broker.sh`),Maven 3.9.11。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍:门禁统计量从"两个 p95 估计值之差"改为"逐轮增长量的 p95";二者都是设计文档"p95 上增加不得超过 1 毫秒"的实现,且均匀的逐轮成本仍会确定性地失败。
- 未验证 / 不在范围内:未能按需复现原始抖动(原始代码在一次争用运行中通过——它是尾部概率失败);journal 交接的 20ms 绝对预算未改动;无生产行为变化。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明:无。

## 关联 Issue

Fixes #14197

</details>

prs.title: feat(managed-agent): raise attachment input budget to 8 MiB
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Managed Agent submissions now allow 8 MiB of complete canonical UTF-8 JSON input, enough for an approximately 5 MiB screenshot including base64 overhead, prompt text and attachment metadata. Both composers preserve large pending requests across refresh through IndexedDB and retry the same immutable input with the original idempotency key. Missing or corrupt pending data blocks submission and offers an explicit discard after an uncertainty warning.

The larger budget is carried through Java admission, durable input storage, chunked user messages and Hosted model-request recovery. Dedicated input and model-request resources have 8 MiB and 32 MiB bounds; ordinary resources retain their 64 KiB limit. Existing format, image-capability, digest and ownership checks remain in place.

## Why it's needed

The existing 48 KiB encoded-input cap rejects ordinary screenshots and small text files before a model call. Raising the composer cap alone would still fail at durable storage, prepared model snapshots or browser sessionStorage quotas, so the same supported submission must work throughout the existing path.

## Reviewer Test Plan

Confirm initial Workspace creation and existing-session input both accept an approximately 5 MiB PNG and text attachments larger than 48 KiB. An uncertain response followed by refresh must retry byte-identical input with the same key. Oversized aggregate input, unsupported formats and image input for a text-only model must still fail explicitly. A copied tab whose pending body was cleared elsewhere must require explicit local discard before another submission.

### How to verify

Use matching WebShell, Java and Harness builds. Submit a PNG through each composer, delay or fail the admission response, refresh, and retry. Confirm one accepted input and unchanged image bytes in the model request and stored user message. Repeat with multiple files or prompt text that push canonical input beyond 8 MiB and confirm rejection without losing the draft. Check that ordinary resources still reject payloads above 64 KiB.

Local validation passed root build, typecheck and bundle, changed-file lint/format checks, 1,131 focused TypeScript tests, affected Java tests (136 run, zero failures, one skipped), 72 MySQL 8.4 integration tests, and Java compilation/Checkstyle/SpotBugs verification. Four real-Chromium checks cover both built composers and their pending-data failure paths; a packaged Hosted CLI check covers storage, model input and replay with controlled HTTP fixtures. A separate PR comment contains the E2E report.

### Evidence (Before & After)

| Scenario | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Valid 5,241,726-byte PNG | Rejected with `Attachments and text together must fit within 48 KiB of encoded input.` | Both built composers accept its 6,989,082-byte canonical input. |
| Refresh after an uncertain response | The large pending body exceeds real sessionStorage quota. | IndexedDB preserves the exact input and key; retry succeeds and clears the body. |
| Packaged Hosted input and replay | The old input bound rejects screenshot-sized submissions. | A 6,989,069-byte input yields a complete 6,989,454-byte chunked user message and 13,992,660-byte model snapshot; live and detach/load replay preserve a single model call. |

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ✅ tested |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested |
|  🐧 Linux  | ⚠️ not tested |

### Environment (optional)

macOS, Node.js 22.22.3, JDK 21, Maven 3.9.14, disposable local MySQL 8.4.11 and Chromium 149.0.7827.55. Browser API responses and Hosted HTTP model/store services are controlled fixtures; the CLI uses real local durable resource storage. The installed global CLI is 0.24.1 and cannot start this checkout's Hosted profile, so baseline encoding used a source-script fallback and final Hosted checks used the local bundle.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: larger JSON and recovery payloads increase bounded memory and storage use. Inline resource transactions allow 40 MiB; receipt checkpoints allow 128 MiB decoded / 192 MiB JSON. Model snapshots and conversations remain bounded, and failed pending restoration never silently creates a fresh request.
- Not validated / out of scope: process-crash recovery certification, real upstream providers, integrated deployed acceptance, Windows and Linux execution, and a final rerun of the full Java unit suite. Local affected tests and static gates passed; submitted-head CI is pending. No new file formats or object-storage upload service are added.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: deploy compatible WebShell, Java and Harness readers/writers together; old binaries still reject larger inputs. Existing message chunks and database columns are reused, with no schema migration or recovery-format change. Public signed requests and daemon request bodies retain their 10 MiB cap.

The synchronized designs cover decisions, constraints and acceptance criteria: attachment budget [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/managed-attachment-budget/docs/design/2026-10-18-managed-attachment-budget.md) / [中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/managed-attachment-budget/docs/design/2026-10-18-managed-attachment-budget.zh-CN.md), and updated Plan/attachment contract [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/managed-attachment-budget/docs/design/2026-10-18-managed-plan-attachments.md) / [中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/managed-attachment-budget/docs/design/2026-10-18-managed-plan-attachments.zh-CN.md).

## Linked Issues

None.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 的作用

Managed Agent 提交的整份 canonical UTF-8 JSON 输入现在允许 8 MiB，足以容纳约 5 MiB 截图以及 base64 开销、提示文字和附件元数据。两个输入入口均通过 IndexedDB 在刷新后保留大请求，并使用原始幂等键重试同一份不可变输入。待确认数据缺失或损坏时阻止提交，显示结果不确定提示后提供显式丢弃入口。

更大的预算贯通 Java 准入、持久化输入存储、用户消息分片及 Hosted 模型请求恢复。专用输入和模型请求资源分别限制为 8 MiB、32 MiB，普通资源仍限制为 64 KiB。保留既有文件格式、模型图片能力、摘要及归属校验。

## 为什么需要

现有 48 KiB 编码输入上限会在模型调用前拒绝日常截图和小文本文件。仅提高输入框上限仍会遇到持久化存储、预备模型快照或浏览器 sessionStorage 配额限制，因此需要让同一份受支持的提交能够走完整条既有链路。

## 审阅者验证计划

确认初始 Workspace 创建和已有会话输入均能接收约 5 MiB PNG，以及超过 48 KiB 的文本附件。响应结果不确定后刷新重试，必须保持完全相同的输入字节和幂等键。总量超限、格式不支持，以及向纯文本模型提交图片时仍须明确失败。复制标签页的待确认正文被其他标签页清理后，必须显式丢弃本地记录才能再次提交。

### 如何验证

使用配套的 WebShell、Java 和 Harness 构建。分别通过两个输入入口提交 PNG，延迟或使准入响应失败，然后刷新重试。确认仅有一次输入被接收，模型请求和持久化用户消息中的图片字节保持不变。再加入多个文件或提示文字，使 canonical 输入超过 8 MiB，确认请求被拒绝且草稿保留。确认普通资源仍拒绝超过 64 KiB 的内容。

本地已通过根目录 build、typecheck、bundle，改动文件的 lint/format 检查，1,131 项 TypeScript 定向测试，受影响 Java 测试（运行 136 项、无失败、跳过 1 项），72 项 MySQL 8.4 集成测试，以及 Java 编译、Checkstyle、SpotBugs 验证。四组真实 Chromium 检查覆盖两个已构建输入框及待确认数据故障路径；打包后的 Hosted CLI 通过受控 HTTP 测试服务验证存储、模型输入与重放。独立 PR 评论附有 E2E 报告。

### 证据（修改前后）

| 场景 | 修改前 | 修改后 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 有效的 5,241,726 字节 PNG | 被拒绝并显示 `Attachments and text together must fit within 48 KiB of encoded input.` | 两个已构建输入框均接受其 6,989,082 字节 canonical 输入。 |
| 结果不确定后刷新 | 大请求正文超过真实 sessionStorage 配额。 | IndexedDB 保留完全一致的输入和幂等键；重试成功后清理正文。 |
| 打包后的 Hosted 输入及重放 | 旧输入上限拒绝截图大小的提交。 | 6,989,069 字节输入生成完整的 6,989,454 字节分片用户消息和 13,992,660 字节模型快照；在线及 detach/load 重放均只保留一次模型调用。 |

### 测试平台

| 操作系统 | 状态 |
| :---: | :---: |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ 已测试 |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ 未测试 |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ 未测试 |

### 环境（可选）

macOS、Node.js 22.22.3、JDK 21、Maven 3.9.14、可丢弃的本地 MySQL 8.4.11，以及 Chromium 149.0.7827.55。浏览器 API 响应和 Hosted HTTP 模型/存储服务均为受控测试服务；CLI 使用真实本地持久化资源存储。全局安装的 CLI 为 0.24.1，无法启动当前工作区的 Hosted profile，因此基线编码采用源码脚本替代，最终 Hosted 检查使用本地 bundle。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：更大的 JSON 和恢复数据增加了有上限的内存与存储开销。内联资源事务允许 40 MiB；receipt checkpoint 允许解码后 128 MiB、JSON 192 MiB。模型快照和会话仍有容量上限，待确认请求恢复失败时绝不静默创建新请求。
- 未验证或不在范围内：进程崩溃恢复认证、真实上游模型、完整部署环境验收、Windows/Linux 执行，以及最终修复后重跑全量 Java 单测。本地受影响测试和静态门禁已通过，提交版本的 CI 尚待完成。本次不增加新文件格式或对象存储上传服务。
- 破坏性变更与迁移说明：配套部署 WebShell、Java 和 Harness 读写端；旧二进制仍拒绝大输入。复用现有消息分片和数据库列，无需数据库迁移或恢复格式变更。公开签名请求与 daemon 请求体仍限制为 10 MiB。

同步设计完整覆盖决策、约束及验收标准：附件容量[英文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/managed-attachment-budget/docs/design/2026-10-18-managed-attachment-budget.md) / [中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/managed-attachment-budget/docs/design/2026-10-18-managed-attachment-budget.zh-CN.md)，以及更新后的 Plan/附件契约[英文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/managed-attachment-budget/docs/design/2026-10-18-managed-plan-attachments.md) / [中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/managed-attachment-budget/docs/design/2026-10-18-managed-plan-attachments.zh-CN.md)。

## 关联 Issue

无。

</details>

prs.title: test(cli): cover successful batch result downloads
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds one regression test for successful Batch result downloads. A controlled response delivers two byte chunks containing JSONL and UTF-8 text; the real stream and filesystem path must publish exactly those bytes under the final filename and leave no partial file.

## Why it's needed

#12677 R2-17 records this coverage gap. Existing tests exercise interrupted downloads, but do not pin successful publication. Removing the final rename, or replacing it with a copy that leaves the partial file behind, keeps all 12 existing tests green. The new case detects both regressions without changing production behavior.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Confirm that a completed download writes both chunks byte-for-byte to the final file and removes the partial file. An interrupted download must still leave neither file. Temporarily omitting publication should fail the new case because the final file is missing; copying without cleanup should fail it because the partial file remains. Restore production code after either probe.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — no user-facing change. Before: 12 tests passed. After: 13 tests passed; an independent test engineer reproduced both counts. Each of the two temporary mutations leaves the baseline at 12 passed, then produces 12 passed / 1 failed after the test is added. Production source was restored after each probe and its SHA-256 checked. Root build and repository-wide typecheck passed; changed-file ESLint, Prettier and diff whitespace checks passed. Across the five related Batch test files, before: 183 passed / 4 failed / 1 skipped; after: 184 passed / 4 failed / 1 skipped. Failure-name sets are identical: three Windows symlink EPERM failures and one Unix-style path expectation on Windows. No existing test was edited, and no new skip was introduced. Full preflight was not run; no all-green repository test claim is made. This is proposed as a Draft PR.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :-- | :-- |
| macOS | Not tested |
| Windows | Local unit and validation results above |
| Linux | Not tested |

### Environment (optional)

Windows, Node.js 24.19.0, npm 11.17.0, pinned pnpm 11.24.0. Network responses are mocked; streams and files are real. The global CLI's Batch help check did not reach this command, so no live provider or CLI E2E acceptance is claimed.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: coverage-only change with a small temporary-file fixture.
- Not validated / out of scope: live provider downloads, crash recovery, file permissions, and the other items in #12677.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Refs #12677, R2-17 only; this PR does not close the whole tracker.

<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 的改动

为 Batch 结果下载成功路径新增一项回归测试。受控响应分两块返回包含 JSONL 和 UTF-8 文本的字节；真实数据流和文件系统路径必须将完全相同的字节发布到最终文件名，并且不残留临时文件。

## 为什么需要

#12677 的 R2-17 记录了这个覆盖缺口。现有测试覆盖中断下载，但没有固定下载成功后的发布行为。移除最终重命名，或替换成会残留临时文件的复制操作，原有 12 项测试仍然通过。新用例能发现这两类回归，不修改生产行为。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

确认完整下载将两块数据逐字节写入最终文件，并清除临时文件。中断下载仍应不留下这两种文件。临时取消发布时，新用例应因最终文件不存在而失败；复制后不清理时，应因临时文件残留而失败。每次探测后恢复生产代码。

### 证据（修改前后）

N/A — 没有用户可见行为变化。修改前 12 项通过，修改后 13 项通过；独立测试代理复现了这两个结果。两种临时变异分别在基线保持 12 项通过，增加测试后均为 12 通过 / 1 失败。每次探测后均恢复生产源码并校验 SHA-256。根目录构建和全仓类型检查通过；改动文件 ESLint、Prettier 与 diff 空白检查通过。五个相关 Batch 测试文件修改前为 183 通过 / 4 失败 / 1 跳过，修改后为 184 通过 / 4 失败 / 1 跳过，失败名称集合完全相同：3 项 Windows 符号链接 EPERM，1 项 Unix 风格路径预期与 Windows 不符。未修改原有测试，也未新增跳过项。未运行完整 preflight，不声称全仓测试全部通过；本次拟作为 Draft PR 提交。

### 已测试系统

| 系统 | 状态 |
| :-- | :-- |
| macOS | 未测试 |
| Windows | 本地单元测试及检查结果见上文 |
| Linux | 未测试 |

### 环境（可选）

Windows，Node.js 24.19.0、npm 11.17.0、仓库固定的 pnpm 11.24.0。网络响应使用模拟，数据流和文件操作真实执行。全局 CLI 的 Batch 帮助检查未进入该命令，因此不声称完成真实服务端或 CLI 端到端验收。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：仅补充测试，使用小型临时文件夹具。

- 破坏性变化或迁移：无。

关联 #12677，仅 R2-17；不关闭整份跟进清单。

prs.title: fix(managed-agent): bound initial publication guard waits
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Bounds the initial publication tenant-guard acquisitions identified in #14393 A.3. Projection expiry/collection, tool-result claim/settlement, Session-resource collection and lifecycle completion now use the existing statement timeout and retryable `503 tenant_guard_contended` mapping at their first acquisition.

## Why it's needed

These paths acquired the publication guard before entering an already bounded helper. The later reentrant acquisition could not bound the first wait. This change moves the existing bound to the seven unique acquisition sites underlying the issue's eight reported call paths.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Hold the publication tenant guard while completing an empty Workspace Session admitted under lifecycle protocol 1. The completion attempt should return `503 tenant_guard_contended` within the retained 15-second test ceiling. The operation and Session should remain pending without a completion receipt. Release the holder and retry the same operation and generation: the Session should close with one receipt and exactly one completion event.

### Evidence (Before & After)

The corrected publication-only JUnit method passed once on real MySQL 8.4.11: one discovered, one started, one passed, zero failed or skipped; JUnit duration 9.863 seconds. It retains the named-503 and fixed 15-second assertions, unchanged pending-state assertions, and successful same-operation/generation completion after release. Independent focused scope/correctness and simplicity review found no blocking defect.

The four changed production classes, four required base/ABI dependencies and six test/fixture sources passed one remote JDK 21 narrow compilation. The runtime uses a retained reference distribution plus identity-checked classes, without the old A.2/A.3 overlays. This is a narrow overlay witness, not a complete current-base build.

The earlier placement, public Session/event-stream and shorter CSI-budget results refer to a broader candidate that has been withdrawn. They are retained in the PR history and are not acceptance evidence for this revised diff. Collector runtime witnesses remain pending.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :---: | :--- |
| 🍏 macOS | Orchestration only; no local build or compilation |
| 🪟 Windows | Not tested |
| 🐧 Linux | One publication-only retained JUnit method passed on disposable MySQL 8.4.11/JRE 21 |

## Risk & Scope

- Previously unbounded initial publication waits can now fail earlier with the existing retryable error. Lock order, fencing, retry policy and collection lease rules remain unchanged. The timeout bounds individual statements, not an entire operation.
- Placement acquisition, CSI probe budgets and public Session/event-stream query behavior retain their base implementations. No schema, public API, dependency or configuration changes.
- Collector runtime coverage, the full Maven/JUnit/Checkstyle/SpotBugs gates and complete Hosted acceptance remain unverified. No UI screenshots or HTTP-level acceptance are claimed. The full native review gate is unverified; this PR remains Draft.

Design: [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/fix-14393-lifecycle-guard-waits-pr/docs/design/2026-10-11-managed-tenant-guard-wedge.md), [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/fix-14393-lifecycle-guard-waits-pr/docs/design/2026-10-11-managed-tenant-guard-wedge.zh-CN.md).

## Linked Issues

Refs #14393 (A.3 initial publication acquisitions only; other items remain open).

Refs #12380.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 的改动

仅对 #14393 A.3 指出的首次 publication 租户守卫获取加界：投影到期处理与回收、工具结果 claim/结算、Session 资源回收，以及生命周期完成入口。首次获取现在复用既有逐语句超时及 `503 tenant_guard_contended` 映射。

## 修改原因

这些路径先获取 publication 守卫，随后才进入已有界的 helper；重入获取无法约束第一次等待。此次仅修改原 issue 八个调用路径对应的七个独立获取点。

## 评审验证计划

### 验证方式

持有 publication 租户守卫，同时完成一个按生命周期协议 1 准入的空 Workspace Session。完成调用应在既有测试 15 秒上限内返回 `503 tenant_guard_contended`，operation 与 Session 保持待完成且没有完成 receipt。释放持锁者后，以同一 operation/generation 重试，应关闭 Session、生成 receipt，且完成事件恰好一次。

### 修改前后证据

收窄后的 publication 单方法在真实 MySQL 8.4.11 上执行一次并通过：发现 1 项、启动 1 项、通过 1 项，无失败或跳过，JUnit 耗时 9.863 秒。保留具名 503、固定 15 秒上限、待完成状态不变，以及释放后同 operation/generation 完成的断言。独立定向范围/正确性及简化审查未发现阻塞问题。

四个改动产品类、四个必需的 base/ABI 依赖和六个测试/fixture 源码通过一次远端 JDK 21 窄编译。运行环境使用保留的 reference distribution 与已核对身份的类，没有旧 A.2/A.3 overlay；这是窄范围 overlay 见证，不是当前 base 的完整构建。

先前的 placement、公开 Session/event-stream 和缩短 CSI 预算证据对应已撤回的扩大候选，仅保留为 PR 历史，不作为当前改动的验收证明。Collector 运行见证仍待完成。

### 验证平台

| OS | 状态 |
| :---: | :--- |
| 🍏 macOS | 仅编排；没有本地 build 或编译 |
| 🪟 Windows | 未验证 |
| 🐧 Linux | 一次性 MySQL 8.4.11/JRE 21 环境中 publication 正式单方法通过 |

## 风险与范围

- 原先无界的首次 publication 等待现在可能更早返回既有可重试错误。锁顺序、栅栏、重试策略和回收 lease 规则保持不变；超时逐语句适用，不是整个操作的期限。
- Placement 获取、CSI 检查预算与公开 Session/event-stream 查询行为恢复为 base 实现；没有 schema、公开 API、依赖或配置变化。
- Collector 运行覆盖、完整 Maven/JUnit/Checkstyle/SpotBugs 门禁和完整 Hosted 验收仍未验证。没有 UI 截图或 HTTP 层验收结论；完整原生 review 门禁未完成，PR 保持 Draft。

prs.title: fix(managed-agent): recover the journal after a lapsed writer lease
prs.body:
## What this PR does

A Hosted Session's journal now survives a control-plane outage that outlasts one writer lease. When an append's outcome cannot be observed, the Harness no longer declares the log dead: it keeps the attempt, re-acquires a lapsed writer lease once the Store is reachable again, and asks the durable head whether that transaction landed. A landed transaction is applied exactly once; an absent one is retried. When another writer has advanced the log, or the failure is definite, the journal is still fenced. A retry settles before it reads replay state, so a repeated domain or extension record returns the reference actually committed; a fenced settlement stops keepalive; a read grant that lapses mid-read is re-acquired once; and Hosted routes answer the unsettled outcome with the same retryable 503 they use for a store outage.

## Why it's needed

Issue #13650: a Hosted Session renews its activation roughly every twenty seconds and holds a writer lease of about a minute. An outage longer than the lease made the next renewal fail; the local authority then latched a permanent write failure, and every later fire and user Turn answered `503 automation_operation_failed` for as long as the Session lived, even after the control plane had fully recovered. The real-stack evidence in the issue shows a 44-second outage and a 3-minute-50-second outage both ending this way. The durable journal was intact the whole time; only the local writer was dead, with no path that asked the Store again.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the managed-session unit suites from `packages/core`:

```
npx vitest run src/managed-runtime/http-managed-session-store.test.ts src/managed-runtime/managed-session-authority.test.ts src/managed-runtime/managed-session-assembly.test.ts src/config/managed-session-log.test.ts
```

Expected: 288 tests pass. The regression proof covers: a full Store outage of 60 seconds against a 50-second writer lease, after which the renewal settles and a user message commits; a first renewal that commits server-side with a lost acknowledgement, discovered by its record digest and applied once; another writer occupying the revision our unknown append would have used, which fences the Session; a landed domain record replaying with the committed reference; a landed extension record replaying instead of failing for a missing body; and a read grant that lapses during settlement, which is re-acquired once. A further group keeps the permanent behavior: a live-lease writer conflict, a spent tenant-guard budget, and the local JSONL journal still stop the writer for good. The message-route and member-command classifications have their own cases in the CLI suite.

Before this change the same harness showed zero Store traffic after recovery and every later write rejected as writes-stopped.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — non-user-visible core behavior. The unit assertions above are the evidence.

### Tested on

|           OS            | Status |
| :---------------------: | :----: |
|        🍏 macOS         |   ✅   |
|       🪟 Windows        |   ⚠️   |
|        🐧 Linux         |   ⚠️   |

### Environment

Unit tests only, Node 22.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: settlement adds one head read to the first append after an unknown outcome, and the "another writer advanced" rule is strict: a Session whose log moved while its writer was out still needs a takeover. That is deliberate, to avoid two writers extending one log.
- Not validated / out of scope: the external real-stack rig (`pr13598/r2`) was not run in this checkout; the issue's 44-second and 3-minute-50-second scenarios should be replayed there before merge. Windows and Linux runners were not run locally.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. The settlement step is optional on the journal contract; local JSONL sessions keep their existing crash semantics.

Design docs: [English](docs/design/2026-10-18-managed-journal-lease-recovery.md) · [中文](docs/design/2026-10-18-managed-journal-lease-recovery.zh-CN.md)

## Linked Issues

Fixes #13650

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

托管 Session 的日志现在能在超过一个写者租约时长的控制面停机后恢复。当一次追加的结果无法观测时，Harness 不再直接判定日志死亡：它保留这次尝试，在 Store 恢复可达后重新获取已逾期的写者租约，并向持久头部确认该事务是否落地。已落地的事务只应用一次；未落地的则重试。若日志已被其他写者推进，或失败本身是确定性的，日志仍然封闭。重试会在读取 replay 状态之前先结算，因此重复的 domain/extension 记录返回实际已提交的引用；被 fence 的结算会停止保活；读取期间才过期的租约重取一次；Hosted 路由把未结算结果映射为与存储故障相同的可重试 503。

## 为什么需要

Issue #13650：托管 Session 大约每二十秒续租一次激活，并持有一分钟左右的写者租约。停机超过租约会让下一次续租失败；本地权威随即锁定永久写失败，此后每次 fire 和用户 Turn 都返回 `503 automation_operation_failed`，且该状态会持续到 Session 结束，即使控制面已经完全恢复。issue 中的真实栈证据显示，44 秒停机与 3 分 50 秒停机都会落到这一结局。持久日志始终完好，死掉的只是本地写者，而且没有任何路径再去询问 Store。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

在 `packages/core` 下运行托管会话单测：

```
npx vitest run src/managed-runtime/http-managed-session-store.test.ts src/managed-runtime/managed-session-authority.test.ts src/managed-runtime/managed-session-assembly.test.ts src/config/managed-session-log.test.ts
```

预期 288 个测试全部通过。回归证据覆盖：完整 Store 停机 60 秒而写者租约 50 秒，恢复后续租完成结算并成功提交用户消息；第一次续租在服务端落地但回复丢失，结算按记录摘要找到并只应用一次；其他写者占据本次未知追加本应使用的 revision，结算封闭该 Session；已落地的 domain 记录以实际提交的引用重放；已落地的 extension 记录重放而不是因缺少 body 失败；结算读取期间租约过期，重新 acquire 一次。另一组保留永久封闭行为：活租约写者冲突、耗尽的租户守卫预算与本地 JSONL 日志仍会永久停止写入。消息路由与成员命令路径的分类在 CLI 套件中另有断言。

在本次改动之前，同一套装置在恢复后没有任何 Store 流量，后续每次写入都被以 writes-stopped 拒绝。

### 证据（改动前与改动后）

不适用——这是核心层行为，不对用户直接可见。上述单测断言即为证据。

### 测试环境

|   操作系统   | 状态 |
| :----------: | :--: |
|    🍏 macOS   |  ✅  |
|   🪟 Windows  |  ⚠️  |
|    🐧 Linux   |  ⚠️  |

### 运行环境

仅单元测试，Node 22。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：结算会在未知结果后的第一次追加前增加一次头部读取；且「其他写者已推进」的判定很严格——日志在写者离线期间前进过的 Session 仍需 takeover。这是有意为之，避免两个写者同时扩展同一条日志。
- 未验证 / 超出范围：本次 checkout 未运行外部真实栈装置（`pr13598/r2`）；合并前应在其上重放 issue 的 44 秒与 3 分 50 秒场景。本地未运行 Windows 与 Linux runner。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。结算步骤在日志契约上是可选的；本地 JSONL Session 保持既有崩溃语义。
