issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Managed workspace synchronization includes OpenClaw's retained Vitest worker cache and Bun transpiler cache as authored changes. Ordinary tests can therefore leave a large generated payload in the pending result used by refresh, review and publication preparation.

### Steps to reproduce

The current source establishes the producer/consumer mismatch:

1. `scripts/lib/vitest-worker-cache.mts` retains compiled worker artifacts under `.artifacts/vitest-worker-cache/`.
2. `scripts/lib/vitest-process.mts` gives ordinary isolated test processes a reusable `.cache/bun-transpiler/` cache.
3. `src/gateway/worker-environments/workspace-path-exclusions.ts` excludes `.artifacts/vitest-workers/` and `.cache/openclaw/bun/`, but neither of those actual cache roots.
4. Capture a managed sandbox result after those test tools have populated their caches. The generated cache entries remain eligible for workspace reconciliation.

An inspected pending result contained 20,191 retained worker-cache files and 276 Bun transpiler-cache files. All four intended source/documentation changes matched across the managed and sandbox copies. This is observed result capture, not a claim that every cache entry conflicted.

### Expected behavior

Known disposable test caches stay with the runtime that produced them, using the existing exact-root exclusion policy. Authored source, ignored screenshots/reports, retained inputs and genuine source conflicts remain protected. Older authenticated pending results must apply the same classification without discarding actual work.

### Actual behavior

Generated cache files entered the pending payload, and refresh preparation returned a preserved-workspace conflict. The exact first entry that rejected that historical operation has not yet been isolated; the confirmed defect is the cache-classification gap. A source-only comparison is insufficient to recover the saved result safely.

### OpenClaw version

Observed at `20b6c7ae4e0e35239e14bca54c156575e4670d91`; the same producer paths and missing exclusions remain at `a842951a15cd79e22cdd0b4e1059021ee1c99c51`.

### Operating system

Linux sandbox. Exact distribution: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

### Install method

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Model

Not required to establish the workspace capture defect.

### Provider / routing chain

Sandbox command finalization and managed workspace refresh enter the existing workspace reconciliation path; inference routing is unrelated to this source-grounded classification mismatch.

### Logs

```text
Local sandbox edits conflict with the managed workspace; pending changes were preserved. Resolve the workspace conflicts before retrying.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

The producer paths and shared exclusion owner above are present on the stated revisions. The pending Git result was inspected without modifying the workspace or its stored receipt. No transcript or user source is needed to demonstrate the mismatch. Isolated capture and saved-result recovery proof remains part of the repair.

### Impact and severity

Ordinary managed coding work may accumulate tens of thousands of disposable test files in synchronization and become blocked during refresh/review preparation. The affected work is preserved; data loss is not established. Broader frequency is unknown.

### Additional information

This is a remaining producer-path gap after #175503 and #175956, not evidence those corrections were reverted. Excluding all ignored files, `.artifacts/`, or `.cache/` would be unsafe because those locations also contain legitimate guest-created work.

issues.body:
## Summary

Third-party **OpenClaw Chat iOS** uses a Mac-side chat adapter (operator `chat.send`, `operator.read` + `operator.write`, **no** `operator.admin`). User messages from the phone are forwarded over Gateway WebSocket with `connect.client.id = openclaw-ios`.

Today, `resolveChatSendCallerContext` always sets `Provider` / `Surface` / internal-route `OriginatingChannel` to **`webchat`**. Agents therefore see WebChat in trusted `openclaw.inbound_meta.v2`, even when the adapter prefixes the body with `[OpenClaw Chat iOS · device]`. Inbound meta docs correctly treat user-authored text as untrusted, so body prefixes cannot satisfy mobile provenance.

Admin-only fields (`systemInputProvenance`, explicit `originatingChannel` + `originatingTo`) are not available to this bridge without violating the companion threat model.

## Request

Add a **narrow, non-admin** `chat.send` extension for authenticated mobile-bridge clients so agents get trusted structural provenance separate from `message`.

### Proposed params

```ts
mobileIngress?: {
  deviceId: string;      // required when present — adapter-enrolled mobile device UUID
  deviceName?: string;   // optional, max 64, sanitized display name
  product?: "openclaw-chat-ios";
};
```

### Rules

1. Accept `mobileIngress` only for an allowlisted bridge client profile (recommend `GATEWAY_CLIENT_IDS.IOS_APP` / `openclaw-ios`, or a dedicated `openclaw-chat-adapter` id if preferred).
2. Map ingress to trusted context, e.g. `Provider` / `Surface` / `OriginatingChannel` = **`openclaw-chat-ios`** (internal, non-delivery channel id), plus `SenderId` / `SenderName` from `mobileIngress`.
3. Reject `mobileIngress` from Control UI / webchat-ui / other clients.
4. Backward compatible: bridge client without `mobileIngress` keeps current webchat classification.
5. Do not require `operator.admin`.

### Acceptance

- Trusted Message Context JSON shows `openclaw-chat-ios` and device identity when `mobileIngress` is sent from the bridge client.
- Spoofed `[OpenClaw Chat iOS]` lines in `message` do not override meta.
- Existing WebChat / channel ingress unchanged.

## Consumer

Spec and adapter follow-up: [OPVSYSTEMS/personal-mac-apps `apps/openclaw-chat-ios/docs/GATEWAY-MOBILE-INGRESS.md`](https://github.com/OPVSYSTEMS/personal-mac-apps/blob/main/apps/openclaw-chat-ios/docs/GATEWAY-MOBILE-INGRESS.md) (tracked via personal-mac-apps issue #24).

## Version checked

Gateway npm **2026.9.8** and **2026.10.5** — same `webchat` operator ingress behavior.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

When a `/dashboard` request spans several lines, only its first line reaches the agent; the remaining requirement lines are dropped without any notice.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run a Gateway with any model and send this message in one chat turn (Control UI, WebChat, or `chat.send`), with real line breaks:
   ```text
   /dashboard Show these panels:
   - CPU per agent
   - error count in the last hour
   - open approvals
   ```
2. Record the request that reaches the model.
3. Optionally, start the requirements on the line after `/dashboard` instead.

### Expected behavior

The agent receives every requirement line. `/dashboard` turns its argument into a multi-line `Dashboard requirements:` block for the Control UI skill, and the other commands whose free text becomes agent input keep every line: `/steer` since https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/146009, `/btw` and `/loop` since https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176293, and `/goal`.

### Actual behavior

The model request holds only the first line:

```text
Dashboard requirements:
Show these panels:
```

None of the three listed panels appear anywhere in the request. When the requirements start on the line after `/dashboard`, the agent gets the default "Create a dashboard for this session." request and none of the lines.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.4 (main at b42c33803a88dc210a96baeede6a9ba3cc48b483)

### Operating system

Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS

### Install method

Source checkout, `pnpm build`, `openclaw gateway run`

### Model

A local OpenAI-compatible mock model that records each request

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> local OpenAI-compatible mock provider (`api: "openai-completions"`)

### Additional provider/model setup details

The Gateway ran with an isolated home and state directory inside a network namespace with loopback only. The message was sent with `openclaw gateway call chat.send`. No real provider or account was used.

### Logs

```shell
# what reached the model (recorded by the mock provider)
requirementsBlock: "Dashboard requirements:\nShow these panels:"
linesReceived: ["Show these panels:"]
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

The output above was read from the recorded model request body.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: anyone who writes `/dashboard` with requirements on several lines, for example with Shift+Enter in the Control UI or WebChat, or a pasted list in a channel.
- Severity: the dashboard is built without the requested panels; nothing tells the user that the lines were dropped.
- Frequency: every multiline `/dashboard` request.
- Consequence: the user has to notice the missing panels and ask again on one line.

### Additional information

Commands that are not in the argument-preserving set of command normalization keep only their first line. `/dashboard` is the only handler that rewrites its argument into agent input and is neither in that set nor handled by the skill payload path (`/skill`, `/learn`).

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Doctor appends an instruction to restore a database backup when its final readiness check fails with a retryable SQLite snapshot-stabilization error.

### Steps to reproduce

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Expected behavior

Keep the readiness refusal, but preserve the underlying error's instruction to let writes settle and retry the inspection. An inability to obtain a stable snapshot should not itself produce an instruction to restore the database.

The concrete reference is the retry guidance emitted by [the snapshot owner in official 2026.10.5](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.10.5/src/infra/sqlite-readonly-location.ts#L591-L615).

### Actual behavior

The same error contains both “Wait a moment for write activity to settle, then retry the inspection” and “restore the affected database from a verified backup.”

After Doctor exited and its process ownership had ended, the supported shared-state schema lint passed. Normal Gateway startup then passed its persisted-state schema preflight without a restore or manual database/WAL/lock deletion. Full Gateway health was still being established when this evidence was captured.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.5, locally patched build `eb736e196dadce1aea1d2d7f92d80cb13a6edd8c`, based on official tag commit `1b58cb9a1b4f4353e1add63c8506db4d890962e8`.

`src/state/openclaw-database-preflight.messages.ts`, `src/infra/sqlite-readonly-location.ts`, and `src/commands/doctor-maintenance-inspection.ts` are unchanged from the official tag. The same formatter was also checked on current upstream commit `8cd41d4d3e7832ba19b812b6bb046e6acc19cbf6`. This is not a claim of a separate runtime reproduction on an unpatched release.

### Operating system

Windows 11 Pro, build 26200; Node.js v26.8.1.

### Install method

Locally built npm package, installed globally. Standalone native Windows Doctor, outside Gateway process ancestry.

### Model

Not applicable: local database readiness and CLI error output.

### Provider / routing chain

Not applicable: no model request is involved in the reported failure.

### Logs

Paths below are replaced with `<state-dir>`; the error wording is otherwise preserved.

```text
Doctor could not complete repair because persisted database readiness could not be verified:
state <state-dir>\state\openclaw.sqlite: SQLite read-only worker failed while creating its private snapshot: SQLite source did not stabilize after 10 read-only inspection attempts (the database may be under concurrent write activity): <state-dir>\state\openclaw.sqlite. Wait a moment for write activity to settle, then retry the inspection
Stop OpenClaw processes, then restore the affected database from a verified backup.
```

Observed recovery on 2026-10-19, all times UTC:

- 01:15:42: Doctor exited 1.
- 01:18:59: `doctor --lint --only core/doctor/state-schema --json --severity-min warning` exited 0:
  `{"schemaVersion":1,"ok":true,"checksRun":1,"checksSkipped":67,"findings":[]}`.
- 01:20:13: normal Gateway startup logged `startup phase: state.schema-preflight 1798.9ms total=26843.4ms`.

The selected lint is only a shared-schema check; it is not being presented as a full database integrity check.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

- [Official 10.5 formatter](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.10.5/src/state/openclaw-database-preflight.messages.ts#L50-L66): every indeterminate result with operation `doctor` receives the restore instruction, without distinguishing a retryable snapshot acquisition failure.
- [Same formatter on the inspected current upstream commit](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8cd41d4d3e7832ba19b812b6bb046e6acc19cbf6/src/state/openclaw-database-preflight.messages.ts#L50-L66).
- [Snapshot retry classification](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.10.5/src/infra/sqlite-readonly-location.ts#L591-L615): this exhaustion path catches `SqliteSourceChangedError` and supplies retry guidance. It is not an integrity-check result.

### Impact and severity

Observed once during a Windows 10.5 upgrade repair. The incorrect output led to extra recovery triage. No restore was performed and no data loss was observed. Frequency beyond this occurrence is unknown.

### Additional information

The snapshot-instability trigger has not been isolated into a deterministic reproduction. The production sequence above was observed once; no additional failure was induced.

The observed command was `doctor --fix --yes --non-interactive --no-workspace-suggestions`. Gateway was stopped during that repair. The logs do not identify the writer responsible for each failed snapshot attempt, and this report does not attribute the snapshot failure to a particular writer or claim database corruption.

Related snapshot-acquisition work: #160483 and #175774. This report is limited to Doctor's unconditional recovery instruction, which remains present after that work.

A focused acceptance target is that a retryable snapshot-acquisition refusal retains a settle-and-retry next step without automatically instructing a restore. Other readiness failures should retain guidance appropriate to their actual diagnosis.

AI assistance: Codex inspected the source and local receipts and prepared this report.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Crash (process/app exits or hangs)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

A managed chat `/update` starting on released OpenClaw 2026.10.4 and targeting 2026.10.5 remains in `validating / candidate-state-snapshot` for over 2 hours 48 minutes, repeatedly spawning shared-state snapshot workers and accumulating over 1 TB in process write counters, while the original Gateway remains healthy.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed once on this installation; a clean-state reproduction is not established.

1. Run npm-global OpenClaw 2026.10.4 (`383c124cc32f`) with its user-systemd Gateway active, Node 24.22.0, and the state described below.
2. Send `/update` in an owner-authorized chat. The managed handoff launches `openclaw update --yes` targeting stable/latest 2026.10.5. No explicit `--timeout` was supplied.
3. After runtime retention completes, observe `openclaw update status --json` remain on `candidate-state-snapshot` and repeatedly observe short-lived `sqlite-readonly-location.worker.js ... sync` children of the updater. Only read-only inspection was performed; no retry or interruption was attempted.

### Expected behavior

The progress-reader fix described in [the closing explanation for #171446](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/171446#issuecomment-6235757071) says updates starting on 2026.10.1 or later should use a reusable live reader rather than continuously copy shared state. Validation should progress or report an actionable bounded failure while preserving the serving installation. Whether this observation has the same underlying caller is unconfirmed.

### Actual behavior

All times below are 2026-10-19 **UTC+08:00**.

- Run `c3768b6f-a85e-4f96-92c2-9cb61b6ac6e1` starts at 07:31:12; handoff launches updater PID 17772 at 07:31:20.
- Runtime retention succeeds at 07:32:45: 43,244 entries, 630,947,840 estimated bytes, 39,082 linked / 1,498 copied.
- `candidate-state-snapshot` starts at 07:33:29. Last ledger change is **07:33:51.163**, `updatedAtMs=1792366431163`.
- Shared DB snapshot progress reports completed: 14,664/14,664 pages, 60,063,744 bytes, 0.188 seconds. Candidate DB mtimes remain around 07:34. Actual updater stderr, verified through `/proc/17772/fd/2`, is a handoff log whose mtime remains 07:34:54 and size remains 1,063 bytes.
- Nine periodic checks through 10:17 and another at **10:22** show the same run, phase, last step and timestamp, `status=running`, no terminal error and no activation. At 10:22 the installed and serving version is still 2026.10.4.
- Parent tree: Gateway 1442 → handoff 17704 → updater 17772 → continually replaced SQLite snapshot children. Cache directory names change between samples:

```text
node <retained-installed-runtime>/dist/infra/sqlite-readonly-location.worker.js
  --openclaw-sqlite-readonly-child sync
  ~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite
  ~/.cache/openclaw/openclaw-sqlite-readonly-v2-<changing-id>
```

The rapid churn is also visible between the approximately five-minute status checks. Process activity has not corresponded to any new completed update step.

### OpenClaw version

Installed/serving 2026.10.4; commit `383c124cc32ffee3f8e56f549b88da94d269a4af`; build `2026.10.4-release-383c124cc32f-2026-10-15T17-18-22.749Z`. Target 2026.10.5.

### Operating system

Debian GNU/Linux 12 (bookworm), Linux `6.18.18.c1126-trim`, x86_64, NAS.

### Install method

npm global under Linuxbrew; user systemd Gateway service. Node `v24.22.0`, npm `11.19.1`. Install, state, cache and `/tmp` are on the same ext4 NVMe-root filesystem, approximately 43 GiB free (54% used). Shared state DB approximately 57 MiB; two agent DBs approximately 724 MiB and 672 KiB. No tmpfs-space exhaustion was observed.

### Model

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Provider / routing chain

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Logs

Relevant status fields, with irrelevant origin/delivery information omitted:

```json
{
  "phase": "validating",
  "status": "running",
  "updatedAtMs": 1792366431163,
  "finishedAtMs": null,
  "before": {"version": "2026.10.4"},
  "after": {},
  "lastStep": {
    "step": "candidate-state-snapshot",
    "status": "in_progress",
    "startedAtMs": 1792366409188,
    "detail": "shared database snapshot $OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/state/openclaw.sqlite: completed, attempt 1, 14664/14664 pages, 60,063,744 bytes, 0.188 seconds."
  },
  "verification": {"runningVersion": "2026.10.4", "serviceRunning": true, "pid": 1442}
}
```

The handoff log ends after successful shared snapshot progress with:

```text
[sqlite/transaction] slow SQLite transaction hold async=false
database=~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite operation=update.run
elapsedMs=1003 isMainThread=false mode=immediate pid=17772 threadId=3
```

Updater PID 17772 `/proc/17772/io` samples:

| Time (UTC+08) | write_bytes |
| --- | ---: |
| 09:21:46.551 | 661637541888 |
| 09:21:58.575 | 662863360000 |
| 09:42 | 787784663040 |
| 10:12 | 977085616128 |
| 10:17 | 1008992063488 |
| 10:22 | 1038015549440 |

The first pair is approximately 102 MB/s over 12 seconds. These are Linux process I/O counters, **not SSD NAND-write measurements**. At 10:22, `rchar=3085975423358`, `read_bytes=439160832`.

Open files include shared state DB/WAL/SHM, `/tmp/openclaw/managed-update-handoffs.sqlite`, `~/.openclaw/tmp/plugin-captures/<id>/owner.sqlite` plus journal, and `~/.cache/openclaw/openclaw-sqlite-readonly-v2-<changing-id>/owner.sqlite` plus journal.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Original sanitized diagnostic comment: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/171446#issuecomment-6258264299

GitHub comparison confirms that the old progress-reader fix `6e6458a9` is an ancestor of this installed 10.4 commit: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/compare/6e6458a9...383c124cc32ffee3f8e56f549b88da94d269a4af (`ahead`, `behind_by=0`).

### Impact and severity

One observed NAS update is blocked for over 2 hours 48 minutes with more than 1 TB cumulative updater write_bytes. No repeated-attempt frequency is established. The existing 2026.10.4 Gateway remains active and `/readyz` returns HTTP 200, `ready=true`, `failing=[]`; no outage or data loss is established.

### Additional information

This is a follow-up to closed #171446 as requested in its closing explanation for failures starting on 10.4 or later. Unlike that report's 9.x installed driver, this updater starts on 10.4, which contains #162345. Also, `updater-runtime-retention` has completed, so the remaining stage differs from the deadline boundary in #175626. #174842 describes repeated snapshots on 10.4 through Doctor rather than this managed-update entry point; #170773 concerns Doctor capture/content-version workers. These are related observations, not proof of a shared cause.

All investigation was read-only: no database/config changes, process signals, debugger attachments, service restarts, repair commands or additional updates. The current run and original files are left untouched. No current-main reproduction or parent-stack attribution is available; please advise on a non-mutating trace that would identify the repeated snapshot caller.

issues.body:
## Summary

On 2026.10.4 (383c124), every execution-decision fact write (`operationLabel: "audit.execution-decision.record"`) holds an IMMEDIATE write transaction on the shared state DB (`~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite`) for ~1.1 s. It runs thousands of times an hour, so other writers on the same DB (Workboard plugin hooks, cron, transcript cold storage, agent DB cleanup) see `database is locked` and cron jobs fail.

The cost comes from `pruneDecisionFactsAfterInsert` in `dist/execution-decision-facts-*.mjs`. After **every** insert, inside the same write transaction, it runs the overflow query:

```sql
SELECT receipt_id FROM execution_decision_facts
WHERE receipt_id NOT IN (
  SELECT receipt_id FROM execution_decision_facts
  ORDER BY occurred_at DESC, receipt_id DESC LIMIT 250000)   -- EXECUTION_DECISION_FACT_MAX_ROWS
ORDER BY occurred_at ASC, receipt_id ASC LIMIT 1024
```

The table holds 230,277 rows, below the 250,000 cap, so this query always returns 0 rows. It still builds a 230k-entry list subquery every time: `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` shows a full covering-index scan + `LIST SUBQUERY`. Measured read-only on a copy of the live DB: **1,256 ms, 0 rows**. That matches the logged holds.

## Environment
- OpenClaw 2026.10.4 (383c124), Linux x64, Node 26, gateway as a user systemd service
- `logging.audit.enabled: true` (now false as a workaround), `logging.audit.executionIdentity: true`
- state DB ~700 MB; `execution_decision_facts` 230,277 rows over ~6 days; `audit_events` ~100k rows

## Measurements (gateway journal, `[sqlite/transaction] slow SQLite transaction hold`, thresholdMs=1000)

60 min before turning `logging.audit.enabled` off (15:21–16:21 local):

| operation | count | avg ms | max ms |
|---|---|---|---|
| audit.execution-decision.record | 2223 | 1113 | 1700 |
| database.prepareWrite | 23 | 3477 | 3791 |
| (unlabeled) | 17 | 3568 | 4039 |
| cron.history-maintenance | 3 | 1677 | 2524 |
| sessions.lifecycle-artifact-plan | 2 | 5345 | 5585 |

`database is locked` lines in the same window: 424. Almost all came from `[plugins] workboard external change check failed: SqliteWorkerError: database is locked`; the rest were workboard `agent_end`/`subagent_ended` hooks, lifecycle recovery, `[state/agent-db] idle cleanup` and `[health] transcript cold storage`. Command cron jobs that touch the state DB exited 1. Over the wider 15:07–16:07 window there were 1,285 lock lines.

After the change (config file written 16:21:07, `[reload] ... (logging.audit.enabled)` 16:21:17, accepted 16:21:21):
- `audit_events`: last row at 16:21:18 (count 99,968, max sequence 626,218), with no new rows through 16:36. Before that it was taking ~200–320 rows per 10 min.
- `execution_decision_facts`: last insert at 16:21:16. `audit.execution-decision.record` slow holds kept appearing at ~45/min until 16:23, tapered to 7 in 16:24, and stopped after that. My guess is that runs already in flight kept their old config snapshot for a short time.
- 16:22–16:36: 0 `database is locked` lines (the hour before had 424). The remaining slow holds are a few `session context snapshot read` (~1.2 s, agent DB) and `unlabeled` (~3.7 s) holds.
- Cron jobs that failed at 15:31 ran OK at 16:30–16:31.

## Workaround applied
`openclaw config set logging.audit.enabled false` hot-applies with no restart. It stopped both `audit_events` writes and the execution-decision fact writes (`logging.audit.executionIdentity` is still true), and the lock errors stopped with them. We will turn audit back on once a fix ships.

## Expected
A fact insert should not do O(table) work. Possible fixes:
- Check the row count cheaply (a maintained counter, or `MAX(rowid)-MIN(rowid)`) and only run the overflow prune when it is over `maxRows`, or
- Move overflow/expiry pruning to the periodic maintenance sweep, outside the per-insert transaction, or
- Use a keyset delete (`WHERE occurred_at < (SELECT occurred_at ... ORDER BY occurred_at DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET maxRows)`) on an `occurred_at` index, so there is no large `NOT IN` list.

Possibly related: #164427 (long cron.history-maintenance hold), #175281 (busyTimeout 0 on SQLITE_BUSY).

issues.body:
## Summary

Workspace synchronization can report success after deleting the last file from a directory but remove that directory from the managed checkout, even though the guest kept it. The accepted baseline still records the directory. A subsequent file addition beneath it can then be rejected as a workspace conflict without any competing edit.

## Steps to reproduce

Using the existing local-workspace-projection fixture with its real Git repositories and durable projection owner:

1. Create `retained/nested/old.txt` in the guest projection and synchronize it to the canonical checkout.
2. Delete only `old.txt`, leaving both directories in the guest projection, and synchronize again.
3. Observe that synchronization succeeds but `retained/nested` is absent from the canonical checkout.
4. Create `retained/nested/new.txt` in the unchanged guest projection and synchronize again.

The fourth step fails with `Local sandbox edits conflict with the managed workspace; pending changes were preserved.` No outside writer or directory cleanup is involved.

## Expected behavior

An accepted empty directory must remain present in the managed checkout. The next ordinary addition beneath that directory should synchronize normally, while a genuine independent directory deletion or replacement must retain its conflict protection.

The existing managed-worktree contract already preserves sandbox-created ignored files, symlinks and accepted empty directories.

## Actual behavior and cause

Git's patch application removes the now-empty parent directories while deleting the last leaf. `applyWorkspaceDirectoryChanges` recreates only directories listed as changed application paths, so it omits unchanged directories retained by the worker manifest. The synchronization owner then advances its baseline to the guest result without restoring those directories.

The first assertion fails with `ENOENT` for the canonical directory. Continuing the same production-path sequence reaches the false conflict and preserves a pending result.

## Environment and evidence

- Behavior bug; reproduced at `d79b0a4df0b24fd1e630e22da22cc2bb40af45ce` on Linux/Ubuntu24.04, with the repository's locked dependencies.
- Test entry point: `pnpm test src/gateway/worker-environments/local-workspace-projection.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, selecting the added last-file deletion regression.
- The reproduction changes only the test fixture; production code is unchanged. It uses the actual projection, reconciliation, filesystem, Git and durable-state paths. No model or provider call is required.
- The focused case fails at directory preservation; a second bounded run continuing beyond that assertion fails at the subsequent synchronization. It does not establish the historical sequence of any particular deployed incident.

## Impact

Guest commands that empty and later refill a directory can create an inconsistent accepted workspace and block later synchronization, review or publication preparation. The pending changes remain preserved; the demonstrated failure is false conflict detection, not loss of the new file's contents.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On native Windows, backup scratch cleanup repeatedly fails with `EPERM` when moving an owned scratch directory onto an empty retirement directory that the cleanup code has just created; the suggested `doctor --fix` retry reports the same failures.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed workflow on this existing installation, with OpenClaw-owned scratch directories already present:

1. With the Gateway stopped for upgrade maintenance, run the installed CLI's `backup create --output <archive-outside-state> --no-include-workspace --verify --json`.
2. The backup exits 0 with `verified: true`, but reports five `openclaw-backup-owned-*` → `openclaw-backup-retired-*` rename failures.
3. During the subsequent upgrade, run the installed CLI's `doctor --fix --yes --non-interactive --no-workspace-suggestions`.
4. Doctor removes five older retired scratch directories, then reports the same five owned-directory rename failures, now naming fresh retirement destinations, and again recommends `openclaw doctor --fix`.

The failing owned paths were matched privately between the backup result and later Doctor output. This is a real maintenance recurrence, not a fresh-profile or synthetic reproduction. The original creation histories of all five owned directories were not established.

### Expected behavior

Owned, inactive scratch should be reclaimed by the supported cleanup owner while preserving live or replaced directories. This is the behavior introduced in #154199 and advertised by the emitted `doctor --fix` recovery instruction.

### Actual behavior

Retirement fails repeatedly at the directory rename. Cleanup warnings remain for the same owned directories after the prescribed retry. The successful verified archive remains available; this report does not claim archive corruption or loss of user data.

### OpenClaw version

- Initial archive operation: locally patched 2026.10.4, source `ac18bfdbd144`.
- Recurrence: locally patched 2026.10.5, source `eb736e196dad`, including the local #169672 plugin-capture backport.
- `src/infra/backup-scratch.ts` is unchanged from each corresponding official release. The 10.5 runtime uses `@openclaw/fs-safe` 0.25.0.

### Operating system

Microsoft Windows 11 Pro x64, 25H2, build 26200.9457; Node.js 26.8.1.

### Install method

Global npm-layout installation, invoked from a native Windows maintenance process outside Gateway ancestry. Doctor was launched through the installed entry point with Node's `--stack-size=8192` option. The Gateway was stopped for maintenance.

### Model

Not applicable: local backup/Doctor filesystem maintenance; no model request is needed.

### Provider / routing chain

Local installed CLI → backup scratch lifecycle → fs-safe directory move → Node filesystem rename.

### Additional provider/model setup details

Not applicable.

### Logs

One representative diagnostic, with only private paths and random directory suffixes replaced:

```text
Backup scratch cleanup failed at <temp>/openclaw-backup-owned-<id>:
EPERM: operation not permitted, rename
'<temp>/openclaw-backup-owned-<id>' ->
'<temp>/openclaw-backup-retired-<new-id>'.
Run `openclaw doctor --fix` to retry cleanup.
```

The initial archive command returned exit 0 and `verified: true`. Later Doctor output reported `Removed abandoned backup scratch` for old retired directories, followed by five matching owned-directory rename failures.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Source inspection identifies a Windows-incompatible destination condition:

1. [`cleanupBackupScratchDirectory`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.10.5/src/infra/backup-scratch.ts#L156) creates a fresh retirement directory, obtains its identity, then calls `parent.move` with `overwrite: true`. Its assertion requires that reservation to still be a directory. [`createPrivateSqliteTempDirectory`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.10.5/src/infra/sqlite-private-directory.ts#L36) actually creates this directory on Windows; it does not merely allocate an unused pathname.
2. [fs-safe 0.25.0's overwrite compatibility path](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/blob/v0.25.0/src/root-impl.ts) calls `fs.rename(source.resolved, target.resolved)` after the caller's assertion.
3. [Node 26.8.1's Windows libuv rename implementation](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v26.8.1/deps/uv/src/win/fs.c) uses `MoveFileExW` with `MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING`. [Microsoft's documented contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winbase/nf-winbase-movefileexw) rejects an existing destination directory.

This establishes a portability problem in the precreated-directory retirement sequence and is consistent with the observed rename errors. No native syscall trace was captured, so additional host-specific denial causes are not excluded. No ACL changes, security bypass, manual scratch deletion, extra backup, or synthetic test was performed to manufacture a reproduction.

Current main, inspected on 2026-10-19, still creates the reservation and requests the overwrite move. Its newer exact-identity handling does not remove that destination condition. A separate `Scratch directory identity changed` warning was also observed but is excluded from this report's diagnosis.

### Impact and severity

Affected: this native Windows installation's archive-backup/Doctor scratch cleanup.

Observed frequency: the same five owned directories failed in the verified archive run and a later 10.5 Doctor cleanup pass.

Consequence: persistent leftover scratch directories and recurring warnings; the advertised retry does not complete retirement. The owner deletes payloads before this final cleanup stage, so these logs do not establish a multi-gigabyte payload leak. The report does not attribute the overall Doctor/upgrade outcome to these warnings.

### Additional information

This installation has other local Windows/browser/memory repairs; it is not a clean-stock or current-main runtime reproduction. The affected scratch owner matches the official release source, and no scratch fix was installed.

Deduplication: #95582 concerns payloads orphaned by hard kills before the current cleanup lifecycle; #175339 concerns private Git-backup cleanup reporting; #169469 changes exact Windows identity receipts. None covers the observed owned-directory move onto a precreated retirement directory. No matching open or closed issue was found by exact diagnostic and owner searches.

A focused repair should use a Windows-supported retirement operation while retaining the existing transaction custody, identity checks and preservation of live/replaced scratch. The acceptance target is the normal backup/Doctor cleanup path reclaiming the owned directory without recreating the same warning; this report does not prescribe bypassing those checks.

Prepared by Codex with AI assistance from retained command results, source inspection and primary Windows/Node documentation. Private paths, random IDs, configuration, database content and credentials are omitted.

issues.body:
### Summary

On OpenClaw 2026.10.4, the bundled Anthropic native-session catalog silently returns an incomplete inventory when Claude JSONL metadata discovery exhausts its global 64 MiB scan budget. A valid recent session can then be absent from both the list and an exact-ID search. The paired Windows node remains connected and other Claude sessions are readable.

### Environment and observed result

- Gateway: Linux, npm global OpenClaw 2026.10.4.
- Paired node: Windows, OpenClaw 2026.10.4, native Claude CLI.
- 478 candidate JSONL files in the actual projects tree.
- The wanted session exists on disk, approximately 6.8 MB, with a valid user record, matching session ID, entrypoint `sdk-cli`, and `isSidechain:false`.
- `anthropic.claude.sessions.list.v1` returns 17 records and no continuation cursor.
- An exact `searchTerm` for the wanted session returns an empty list.
- Reading another returned session succeeds, so this is not a disconnected-node or general authentication failure.

### Source-level confirmation

The shipped `extensions/anthropic/session-catalog-discovery.ts` defines `MAX_CATALOG_METADATA_SCAN_BYTES = 67108864`. `discoverCliRecords` consumes this shared budget while walking candidates, then breaks. `listLocalClaudeSessionPage` applies `searchTerm` only after discovery.

A read-only diagnostic instrumented the shipped discovery module in memory without changing installed files. Its actual result:

```json
{
  "catalogCount": 17,
  "targetReturned": false,
  "metadataFilesScanned": 80,
  "metadataBytes": 67108864,
  "targetScanned": false,
  "budgetHit": true
}
```

The target is later in the candidate order. A separate fresh-process call to the unmodified shipped listing function also returns zero matches for it.

### Reproduction outline

1. Populate a native Claude projects tree with enough valid JSONL metadata windows to exhaust the shared discovery budget.
2. Put a valid wanted session later in the directory/file enumeration order.
3. List native Claude sessions through the paired node, then search for that exact session ID.
4. Observe a successful-looking partial list with no resumable discovery cursor, and an empty exact search, although the file is present.

### Expected behavior

Keep bounded resource use, but expose incomplete discovery and allow continuation or a bounded targeted lookup. Do not represent budget exhaustion as a definitive complete/empty inventory. A newer-first scan alone would not make older valid sessions discoverable.

No native transcript contents, private paths, credentials, or live session identifiers are included here. No runtime patch was deployed. This report is verified on 2026.10.4; later releases have not been tested for this defect.

issues.body:
### Environment
- OpenClaw: 2026.9.9 (bcfc888) → target 2026.10.3
- Install: npm global package (`installKind: package`, npm 11.14.1)
- Node: v24.21.0
- OS: Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie), aarch64 (Raspberry Pi 5, NVMe root)
- Gateway: systemd user service, channel `stable`

### Summary
`openclaw update --tag 2026.10.3 --yes --timeout 600` installs the package into the staging directory, then stays in `validating — updater-runtime-retention` with no end. The phase ran past the 600 s `--timeout` (13+ minutes). In that time the worker process wrote about 94 GB to disk (`/proc/<pid>/io` `write_bytes`) while disk usage stayed flat, so it appears to rewrite the same files over and over. I interrupted it with SIGINT before activation. The live install and the running Gateway were not affected.

### Pre-existing state
Before the update, `openclaw update status --json` already reported:
```
"packageActivationError": "managed handoff lease database identity changed",
"recoverySets": []
```
Earlier the same day, an update had finished as `succeeded` with Doctor `skipped` (`GatewayStateOwnerContentionError`, state database busy). Running `openclaw update repair` with the Gateway stopped then completed every finalize step (doctor, plugins, config convergence). After that, the Gateway was healthy on 2026.9.9 and the handoff lease identity error was still present.

According to https://docs.openclaw.ai/install/updating#package-publication-recovery, if the lease database was lost or changed, `openclaw update` should settle the operation before admission. Instead, the update reached `validating` and looped.

### Steps to reproduce (on this host)
1. `openclaw update status --json` → `packageActivationError: managed handoff lease database identity changed`, `recoverySets: []`
2. `openclaw update --dry-run --tag 2026.10.3` → clean (`Admission: installed`)
3. `openclaw update --tag 2026.10.3 --yes --timeout 600`

### Observed
```
Phase: requested
requested — package-install...
  ✓ package-install (35.46s)
Warning: plugins.entries.acpx: Plugin "acpx" settings cannot be checked until its data/settings upgrade finishes. ...
Phase: staging
Phase: validating
validating — updater-runtime-retention...
validating — updater-runtime-retention — still running (30s)
...
validating — updater-runtime-retention — still running (791.35s)
exit=137   (after SIGINT)
```
- The worker child process used about 27% CPU the whole time (`STAT SNl`) and was not blocked.
- `/proc/<pid>/io` at about 15 minutes: `rchar` ≈ 289 GB, `write_bytes` ≈ 94 GB.
- Disk usage did not grow; the cache dir held about 3 GB.
- Open files of the worker included:
  - `$TMPDIR/openclaw/managed-update-handoffs.sqlite` (the handoff lease DB)
  - `~/.cache/openclaw/openclaw-sqlite-readonly-v2-*/owner.sqlite` (+ `-journal`)
  - `$TMPDIR/openclaw/openclaw-update-artifact-*`

### After abort
- `openclaw update repair` → `Gateway is healthy. Reconciled 1 abandoned update run. No maintenance or service restart was needed.`
- `lastRun`: `failed / finished / abandoned`; Gateway healthy on 2026.9.9.
- The `packageActivationError` (handoff lease identity changed) remains.

### Expected
- `updater-runtime-retention` should respect `--timeout`, or fail fast with an actionable error.
- If the handoff lease DB identity mismatch is the cause, admission should settle it (as documented) or refuse up front. It should not loop with heavy disk writes.

### Related
- #167506: deleted temporary handoff database blocks package recovery (same `/tmp` handoff lease root cause?)
- #169776: updater hardening proposal (ephemeral `/tmp` lease drift)
- #170182, #170019: other `updater-runtime-retention` failures. Those exit with an error; this one never exits.

### Questions
1. Is there a supported way to settle `managed handoff lease database identity changed` when `recoverySets` is empty?
2. Is the `updater-runtime-retention` loop a known issue in 2026.9.9 → 2026.10.x?

issues.body:
### Summary

In an isolated cron `agentTurn` run, an exec that is auto-backgrounded (it runs past the 10s yield) and then exits while the run is still working gets its "Exec completed" notice written into the live run transcript as a `role=user` turn. The run's next append then fails with `SqliteTranscriptMutationConflictError: SQLite transcript changed while preparing rewrite for <sessionId>`, and the cron run is marked failed.

### Version

OpenClaw 2026.10.4 (51aa1b7), Linux arm64, Gateway under systemd.

### Repro

1. Create an isolated cron `agentTurn` job with `delivery.mode: "announce"`.
2. In its prompt, have the agent run an exec that takes 20 to 60 s (no `awaitResults`), so it auto-backgrounds, and then keep making tool calls.
3. When the backgrounded process exits during the run, the run fails 0.5 to 3 s later with the error above.

Whether a given run fails depends on whether the model happens to pass `awaitResults: true` on that exec. Our news jobs failed on 4 of 4 runs today and intermittently on other days.

### Evidence (from exported trajectories: four failed runs, one successful run)

- Every failure follows the same order: the exec returns "Command still running", then "Exec completed (…)" is persisted as `role=user`, then `prompt-error`. Example run 37e51040: backgrounded at 14:34:33.7, notice persisted at 14:34:50.5, error at 14:34:51.0.
- In the successful run the model used `awaitResults: true`. The command ran in the foreground for 38 s and no notice was injected.
- Jobs with `delivery.mode: "none"` never fail this way. Cron sets `notifyOnExit: false` for them (`src/cron/isolated-agent/run-prepare.ts:686` → `run-prompt-executor.ts:675-680`).

### Code path (found by reading the source, not by stepping through it)

- The exit notice is addressed to the run's own cron session and is only suppressed after the run ends: `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-notify.ts:322-342`
- The handoff forces followup mode: `src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-handoff.ts:553`
- The active-run check uses `replyRunRegistry` (`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-run.ts:434-442`). Cron runs call `runEmbeddedAgent` directly (`src/cron/isolated-agent/run-prompt-executor.ts:624`) and never register there, so the followup is drained at once.
- The followup persists the user turn before any session-lane wait: `src/auto-reply/reply/followup-turn-execution.ts:360` (`recovery.admitUserTurn`)
- The run's next append uses `validateTurn: true` (`src/agents/sessions/session-manager-append.ts:128-132`). It sees a newer user message that it did not admit (`src/config/sessions/transcript-append-parent.ts:34-55`, via `session-accessor.sqlite-transcript-parent.ts:121-186`) and throws at `src/agents/sessions/session-manager-append.kernel.ts:74-82`.

### Workaround

Tell the agent in the prompt to pass `"awaitResults": true` on every exec call and not to use the process tool. This works because `awaitResults` disables auto-backgrounding (`src/agents/bash-tools.exec-run.ts:230`). One run tested with this change succeeded.

### Suggested fix

Either of these:

- Register cron/embedded runs where followup admission looks for an active run, so the exec notice waits until the run ends.
- Have `prepareExecExitNotification` suppress the notice, or queue it behind the active cron run, instead of draining it into the live transcript.

### Related (different triggers, same error)

#148280, #145551, #174994, #168082

OpenClaw `2026.7.1-2` can deliver a late reply from an old runtime after the session key has rebound, then fail to persist that delivered reply. In `dispatch-DnzGTpPs.js`, `routeReplyToOriginating()` runs before `mirrorDeliveredReplyToTranscript()`. The mirror passes an `expectedSessionId`; `transcript-uom_ZjhV.js` correctly returns `session-rebound` when the key now points at a fresh session. The user has already seen the answer, the mirror failure is verbose-only, and delivery bookkeeping is cleared.

**Reproduction:** start a long CLI-backed run, reset or rebound the session key before it finalizes, and let the old run deliver.

**Expected:** no externally visible reply lacks a durable canonical record.

**Suggested fix:** persist before delivery through a transactional outbox, or durably append to the captured old transcript and suppress/flag stale delivery on rebound. A mirror failure must remain actionable and must not clear the only delivery-pending record.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug. A native macOS GPT-Live Gateway-relay session closes immediately after successful creation.

### Beta release blocker

No.

### Summary

OpenClaw 2026.8.1 creates a native macOS GPT-Live Gateway-relay Talk session successfully, then emits `session.error` and `session.closed`. The macOS unified log reports:

```text
Realtime provider output has no live response owner.
```

This failure occurs even though v2026.8.1 already includes the owner guard and regression test that ignore an unowned, non-claiming provider clear. The remaining failure therefore needs provider-event or owner-phase tracing. It is not explained by backporting that existing clear-path fix.

This report supersedes #134749. That issue was closed by automation as already fixed on current `main`. A direct check of the release tag and cited commit found that disposition used the wrong provenance and covered a narrower provider event than the observed failure.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run OpenClaw 2026.8.1 with the native macOS app.
2. Configure realtime Talk with `gpt-live-1-codex`, `gateway-relay`, and `agent-consult`.
3. Start Talk from the macOS app.
4. Compare the Gateway file log with the macOS unified log for the same attempt.

Sanitized Talk configuration:

```json
{
  "agentId": "main",
  "realtime": {
    "model": "gpt-live-1-codex",
    "speakerVoice": "sol",
    "mode": "realtime",
    "transport": "gateway-relay",
    "brain": "agent-consult"
  }
}
```

The runtime resolves the realtime provider to `openai`.

### Expected behavior

The created GPT-Live relay session should remain open, accept microphone audio, and return provider audio until the user stops Talk or a real provider or transport failure occurs.

### Actual behavior

A correlated attempt on August 31, 2026 shows this sequence in local time:

```text
21:27:43.787  talk.session.create succeeds in 67 ms
21:27:45.660  talk event session.error
21:27:45.666  talk event session.closed
21:27:46.757  macOS unified log: Realtime provider output has no live response owner.
21:27:47.264  talk.session.close -> UNAVAILABLE -> Error: Unknown Talk session
```

The error and close events identify:

```text
talkMode=realtime
talkTransport=gateway-relay
talkBrain=agent-consult
talkProvider=openai
```

No `talk.session.close` request appears before `session.error` and `session.closed`. The client close is cleanup after the Gateway has already closed the session.

The same exact macOS error occurred on three attempts:

```text
21:21:25.324  Realtime provider output has no live response owner.
21:23:06.983  Realtime provider output has no live response owner.
21:27:46.757  Realtime provider output has no live response owner.
```

### Why the existing clear regression does not resolve this report

The prior automated closure cited current `main` behavior that suppresses an unowned provider clear through `resolve(false)`. That behavior is already in the failing release:

- v2026.8.1 has the same non-claiming owner guard at [`src/gateway/talk-realtime-relay-state.ts:127-143`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.8.1/src/gateway/talk-realtime-relay-state.ts#L127-L143).
- v2026.8.1 already has the exact regression named [`ignores provider clear with no live response owner`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.8.1/src/gateway/talk-realtime-relay.test.ts#L2973-L2993).
- Commit [`9046ecea7303`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/9046ecea730376a4b0f879c1d785108860e33c39) introduced that owner guard and regression on August 23. It is an ancestor of v2026.8.1.
- Commit [`7cef25ff115b`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/7cef25ff115b165b079cf3df4ed64cfb2dfab5b7), previously cited as the post-release fix, changes only `extensions/openai/realtime-transcription-provider.test.ts`. It does not modify relay ownership, the clear caller, or the relay regression test.

The existing regression proves only this state:

```text
onClearAudio -> resolve(false), phase=unowned
```

The same error text is reachable through other states and callbacks in v2026.8.1:

- Provider audio calls [`resolve(true)`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.8.1/src/gateway/talk-realtime-relay-session-create.ts#L217-L224).
- Assistant transcripts call [`resolve(true)`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.8.1/src/gateway/talk-realtime-relay-session-create.ts#L392-L405).
- Provider tool calls call [`resolve(true)`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.8.1/src/gateway/talk-realtime-relay-session-create.ts#L442-L449).
- A non-claiming clear can still fail when the owner phase is stale rather than unowned.
- Response ownership claiming can fail before those callbacks when an incoming response does not match the live owner.

The current logs do not identify which callback or owner phase triggered the error. That is the missing evidence this report asks the next diagnostic change to collect.

### Requested diagnostic or regression

Please add or expose enough bounded relay telemetry to identify:

- the provider event or callback that calls the owner state,
- whether the operation claims output,
- the current owner phase and mode,
- whether the active turn ID matches the stored owner turn,
- the provider response ID when one exists.

A focused regression should exercise the observed successful-create sequence and determine whether the failure comes from provider audio, assistant transcript, tool call, response ownership claim, or a stale-owned clear.

### OpenClaw version

```text
OpenClaw 2026.8.1 (ea80657)
```

Native app:

```text
CFBundleShortVersionString: 2026.8.1
CFBundleVersion: 2608000190
```

### Operating system

```text
macOS 26.6
Build 25G72
Apple Silicon Mac
```

### Install method

The Gateway uses the global npm package. The native app is installed at `/Applications/OpenClaw.app`.

### Local package modification

This runtime has one narrow local dist patch that was needed to get past an earlier bare-session-key owner-resolution failure and reach successful `talk.session.create`.

A comparison against the published `openclaw@2026.8.1` tarball found one modified shipped file:

```text
dist/agent-scope-CB42Y_8g.js
```

The change is inside `resolvePersistedSessionStoreOwner()`. It falls back from `agents.defaults.sessionStore.agentId` to `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId` and removes the per-agent-store early return. The original shipped file is preserved and matches the npm tarball by SHA-256.

No Gateway Talk relay, realtime session harness, or provider output file differs from the published package. The owner-resolution patch could still affect reproduction, so this is disclosed as a patched-runtime report.

### Related reports

- #134749, closed after the clear-path and commit-provenance mismatch described above.
- #88176, Control UI relay creates successfully, then emits `session.closed` and `Unknown Talk session`.
- #91007, iOS relay closes about 80 ms after startup, then audio append receives `Unknown Talk session`.
- #126730 and #126732, related bare-session-key owner-resolution work.

I am not claiming those reports share this root cause. The correlated event ordering, repeated native error, and release-source comparison are the evidence for this report.

### Impact

Realtime Talk through the native macOS Gateway relay is unusable with this configuration. Native fallback may start, but the configured GPT-Live session never reaches a usable audio turn.

issues.body:
# Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

# Beta release blocker

No

# Summary

The model-facing `automations list` action returns caller-scoped jobs, totals, pagination, and `snapshotRevision` without disclosing that inaccessible jobs were excluded, so an agent can report a restricted view as the complete automation inventory.

# Steps to reproduce

1. Configure two enabled automations on the same Gateway: one that a normal agent session may access and one that is hidden from that session by scheduled-tool authority.
2. From an operator/admin path, run `openclaw cron list --all --json` and confirm both jobs are present.
3. From the normal agent session, call the `automations` tool with `action: "list"` and `includeDisabled: true`.
4. Observe that only the accessible job is returned and that `total`, pagination, and `snapshotRevision` look like an unqualified complete inventory.
5. Inspect the model-facing tool description and observe that it does not say that list results are caller-scoped.

# Expected behavior

The tool description and caller-scoped list result should explicitly say that inaccessible jobs are excluded and that `total`, pagination, and `snapshotRevision` are not a global Gateway inventory. Operator/admin list results can remain unqualified.

# Actual behavior

The caller-scoped response returns ordinary list metadata with no visibility marker or warning. In a live reproduction, the normal agent session reported one active automation while the operator/admin list showed nine active automations on the same Gateway.

# OpenClaw version

2026.8.1 (a21bb59); also confirmed by source inspection on current `main` at `5c388e5e16c16ab504bc2d8513811d2a146fcfb0`.

# Operating system

macOS 26.6

# Install method

Source checkout / managed launchd Gateway

# Model

OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol

# Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw WebChat -> OpenAI

# Additional provider/model setup details

The model/provider is not causal. The defect is in the model-facing Automations tool contract and its Gateway caller-scoped list projection.

# Logs

```shell
# Operator/admin inventory
active automations: 9
all definitions: 31

# Normal model-session Automations tool
active automations returned: 1
```

# Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Current `main` filters jobs before pagination in `src/gateway/server-methods/cron-list-caller-scope.ts`, then returns the scoped `total`, pagination, and derived `snapshotRevision` without a visibility field. `src/agents/tools/cron-tool.ts` describes `list` and its pagination but does not disclose that the result is caller-scoped.

# Impact and severity

- Affected: agents using the model-facing Automations tool on Gateways with authority-scoped jobs.
- Severity: workflow-relevant UX/observability defect; no data loss.
- Frequency: deterministic whenever inaccessible jobs exist.
- Consequence: the agent can confidently make a false inventory statement, miss enabled automation coverage, and misdiagnose scheduler state even though the hidden jobs continue running normally.

# Additional information

This is distinct from #127858, which concerned Doctor counting disabled jobs while suggesting an enabled-only CLI command. Here the CLI/operator inventory is complete; the defect is that the model-facing caller-scoped list does not disclose its restricted view.

No fix or PR is proposed in this issue.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Tool Search advertises `query` and `queries` as independently optional model-facing inputs, but rejects requests that omit both or provide both, causing model calls that satisfy the published JSON Schema to fail at runtime.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start OpenClaw 2026.8.1 with structured Tool Search enabled.
2. Inspect the model-facing `tool_search` schema: neither `query` nor `queries` is required, and the mutual-exclusion rule appears only in descriptions.
3. Invoke `tool_search` with both fields, for example `{ "query": "calendar", "queries": [{ "query": "messages" }] }`.
4. Observe the runtime rejection `provide exactly one of query or queries.`
5. The empty object is also schema-valid but receives the same runtime rejection.

The same schema/runtime mismatch is present on current `main` at `0f3e17e56b4`.

### Expected behavior

Every request accepted by the model-facing JSON Schema should be accepted by the Tool Search request boundary. The model should receive one unambiguous request shape that cannot express the invalid mixed or missing states.

### Actual behavior

The model-facing schema accepts missing or mixed request shapes, while `readToolSearchRequest` rejects them. Models can retry the advertised-but-invalid shape instead of progressing to tool discovery.

### OpenClaw version

2026.8.1 (`ea806575e64`); source-confirmed on current `main` `0f3e17e56b4`

### Operating system

OS-independent source contract; regression test run on macOS arm64

### Install method

Source checkout

### Model

Provider-independent schema validation; no model inference is required

### Provider / routing chain

Direct Tool Search schema construction and runtime request parsing

### Additional provider/model setup details

Structured Tool Search mode is enabled. The reproduction uses OpenClaw's schema validator and request parser directly.

### Logs

```shell
tool_search failed: provide exactly one of query or queries.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Source evidence:

- `src/agents/tool-search.ts` publishes optional `query` and optional `queries` in the same object schema.
- `src/agents/tool-search-request.ts` rejects requests unless exactly one field is present.
- PR #118623 introduced the batched request shape; no later commit on current `main` reconciles the advertised schema with the runtime invariant.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: agents using structured Tool Search.
- Severity: workflow degradation; searches fail and models may retry repeatedly instead of progressing.
- Frequency: deterministic for every missing or mixed request.
- Consequence: wasted model turns and delayed tool discovery when a model selects an advertised-but-invalid shape.

### Additional information

The narrow compatibility-preserving repair is to advertise one required scalar `query` shape while retaining the existing internal batch parser/execution path for non-model callers. This removes impossible model states without adding provider-specific schema constructs or changing runtime validation.

issues.body:
## Bug description

When configuring `channels.telegram.apiRoot` to point at a self-hosted [Telegram Bot API server](https://github.com/tdlib/telegram-bot-api), the gateway receives raw updates from the local server but **never dispatches them to any agent session**. The bot can send messages, but inbound messages are silently dropped after the raw-update middleware.

## Environment

- **OpenClaw version:** 2026.3.23-2 (7ffe7e4)
- **OS:** Ubuntu 24.04, Contabo VPS
- **Node:** 22.22.0
- **Telegram Bot API server:** official Docker image (`aiogram/telegram-bot-api`), running with `--local` flag
- **Container port mapping:** `127.0.0.1:8083->8081/tcp`

## Configuration

```json
{
  "channels": {
    "telegram": {
      "enabled": true,
      "botToken": "<redacted>",
      "apiRoot": "http://127.0.0.1:8083",
      "dmPolicy": "allowlist",
      "groupPolicy": "allowlist",
      "allowFrom": [128586066],
      "groups": {
        "-1003841627937": { "requireMention": false }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Steps to reproduce

1. Set up a local Telegram Bot API server container with valid `TELEGRAM_API_ID` and `TELEGRAM_API_HASH`
2. Call `logOut` on the official API (`https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/logOut`) and wait 10 minutes
3. Set `channels.telegram.apiRoot` to `http://127.0.0.1:8083`
4. Start the gateway

## What happens

### 1. Raw updates are received but not dispatched

The gateway polls successfully and receives updates (visible in the detailed log as `gateway/channels/telegram/raw-update`):

```
[gateway/channels/telegram/raw-update] telegram update: {"update_id":401179648,"message":{"message_id":56,"from":{"id":128586066,...},"chat":{"id":-1003841627937,"title":"Jarvis HQ","is_forum":true,"type":"supergroup"},"date":1774449757,"text":"Jarvis"}}
```

But **no session is created, no `Inbound message` log appears, and no agent processes the message**. The update is silently dropped after the raw-update logging middleware calls `next()`.

Outbound works fine — `sendMessage`, `getMe`, `getChat` all succeed through the local server.

### 2. Update offset incompatibility

The file `~/.openclaw/telegram/update-offset-default.json` stores the `lastUpdateId` from the official API (e.g., `841948744`). The local Bot API server uses a completely different update ID sequence (e.g., `401179648`). When the gateway switches to the local server, it requests `getUpdates?offset=841948745`, which the local server will never satisfy — returning empty forever.

**Expected behavior:** OpenClaw should detect the endpoint change and reset the offset, or at minimum document that the offset file must be reset manually.

### 3. `deleteWebhook` crash loop during logOut cooldown

After calling `logOut` on the official API, there is a mandatory 10-minute cooldown. If the gateway restarts during this window, the startup `deleteWebhook` call fails with:

```
[gateway/channels/telegram] telegram deleteWebhook failed: Call to 'deleteWebhook' failed! (400: Logged out)
[gateway/channels/telegram] [default] channel exited: Call to 'deleteWebhook' failed! (400: Logged out)
[gateway/channels/telegram] [default] auto-restart attempt 1/10 in 5s
```

The gateway treats the `400: Logged out` response as a fatal error and enters a crash loop (up to 10 retries). This happens even when `apiRoot` is set to the local server — suggesting `deleteWebhook` may be hitting the official API instead of the configured `apiRoot`.

## What I expected

1. Messages received via the local Bot API server should be dispatched to agent sessions exactly like messages from the official API
2. The update offset should be reset or handled gracefully when `apiRoot` changes
3. `deleteWebhook` should use the configured `apiRoot`, and a `400: Logged out` response should not be treated as fatal (it's an expected transient state during migration)

## Debugging notes

- Confirmed the local server works: `getMe`, `sendMessage`, `getChat`, `getUpdates` (manual curl) all return correct results
- Confirmed the local server connects to Telegram's DC (active TCP connection to `149.154.175.52:443`)
- Confirmed raw updates arrive in the grammY middleware (logged as `raw-update`)
- The dispatch failure is silent — no error, no warning, no session state change after the raw update
- Reverting to official API (`api.telegram.org`) immediately restores full functionality

## Related issues

- #19454 — Same symptom (raw updates received but never dispatched), though that issue may have a different root cause
- #25877, #28535 — Feature requests that led to apiRoot implementation
- #27453 — PR that added apiRoot support

## Suggested fix areas

- Check if the inbound message adapter between grammY and the OpenClaw session dispatcher has assumptions about the API endpoint or response format
- The update offset file should be scoped per `apiRoot` or reset when the endpoint changes
- `deleteWebhook` should respect `apiRoot` and handle `400: Logged out` gracefully during local server migration

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

The exec tool via the Native SSH sandbox backend intermittently fails with SIGTERM / SSH exit 255 on trivial commands (whoami, pwd), and after the first failure all subsequent exec calls in the same session hang indefinitely. This reproduces on 2026.9.1-beta.1 which already includes the #110704 fix that closed #102006.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure Native SSH sandbox backend (backend: ssh) with ED25519 key auth to a Linux target (Rocky Linux 9.7, port 188 in our setup; any Linux SSH target with key auth should reproduce).
2. Set remote runtime root to a user-writable directory (/home/mars/.openclaw-sandboxes, owner mars:mars, mode 700).
3. Start a chat session with the SSH backend active.
4. Run whoami repeatedly (5–10 times) in the same session.
5. Observe intermittent SIGTERM or SSH exit 255 failures.
6. After the first failure, run pwd — it will hang indefinitely (no output until ~7 min session timeout).
7. Recover with gateway restart (launchctl kickstart -kp gui/$(id -u)/com.openclaw.gateway on macOS) or a fresh session.

### Expected behavior

Simple commands (whoami, pwd) should execute reliably through the Native SSH backend and return their output. After an aborted or failed exec, the per-session executor slot should be released so the next exec call in the same session can allocate a fresh slot and succeed. This is the behavior observed with the Docker sandbox backend on the same OpenClaw install, same session pattern, same model.

### Actual behavior

- whoami / pwd intermittently fail with SIGTERM or SSH exit 255.
- After the first failure, subsequent exec calls in the same session hang indefinitely (no output, no error, until ~7 min session timeout fires abort).
- The agent falsely concludes "exec tool is broken" and may enter retry loops.
- Linux sshd logs confirm sessions authenticate and close within tens of milliseconds (no server-side hang).
- Same-trace evidence shows GPT-5.6 Luna transport receives AbortError / "Request was aborted" simultaneously with the SSH exec failure, supporting a shared upstream AbortSignal.
- Docker sandbox baseline on the same install is 100% stable (pwd -> /workspace).
- Recovery requires gateway restart or fresh session.

### OpenClaw version

2026.8.1-beta.3 (5831b80) & 2026.9.1-beta.1 (1d96e5a)

### Operating system

macOS 26.6.2 (Apple M4, 16 GB) — OpenClaw host Rocky Linux 9.7 — remote SSH target (sshd on port 188)

### Install method

npm global (macOS)

### Model

gpt-5.6 (via Sol & Luna / ChatGPT OAuth)

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> Sol / Luna (ChatGPT/Codex OAuth) -> gpt-5.6

### Additional provider/model setup details

Inference uses ChatGPT/Codex OAuth (working, returns HTTP 200). The Memory plugin (memory-core) is enabled but its embeddings use a separate OpenAI API credit chain and hit 429 credit_balance_exhausted. This is ruled out as the primary cause because Docker sandbox exec works fine with Memory enabled on the same install.

### Logs

```shell
Linux sshd (remote side — confirms no server-side hang; multiple sessions open/close within tens of ms around a single whoami attempt):

Accepted publickey for mars from 192.168.1.75 ...
pam_unix(sshd:session): session opened for user mars(uid=1001)
pam_unix(sshd:session): session closed for user mars

OpenClaw trace (failed whoami, traceId=039078d9aff50108ad18fbf373fadf23):

10:27:02.992  GPT-5.6 Luna request start
10:27:03–04    Linux accepts multiple mars SSH sessions; all open->close in ms
10:27:07.611  provider-transport-fetch: AbortError — "This operation was aborted"
10:27:07.618  openai-transport: Request was aborted.
10:27:07.618  Same trace re-issues Luna request
10:27:12.048  Luna HTTP 200

The main agent model in this environment is gpt-5.6-sol, and the user-visible
exec failure occurs in the same main-agent session. However, the transport-level
AbortError captured in the gateway logs is from the Luna utility-model request,
so I am not claiming a captured Sol transport AbortError without a matching log.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

- A/B control: Docker sandbox backend (openclaw-sandbox:bookworm-slim) returns "pwd -> /workspace" 100% of the time on the same install, same session pattern, same model. Native SSH backend fails intermittently under identical conditions.
- SSH backend spawns multiple short-lived helper/probe sessions (all open/close in ~100ms) per logical exec — observed via Linux sshd logs. This fan-out may amplify the abort race.
- Full gateway debug logs and redacted session JSON available upon request.

### Impact and severity

Affected: Users running OpenClaw with Native SSH sandbox backend (macOS host -> Linux remote).
Severity: High — blocks all remote exec workflows after the first failure; requires gateway restart to recover.
Frequency: Intermittent on first command (simple commands may succeed 1–3 times before wedge); 100% of subsequent exec calls hang once wedged. Compound commands fail more reliably.
Consequence: Cannot use Native SSH backend as a stable research transport; agents enter "exec is broken" hallucination loops; remote project work (Constellar CRUD) cannot be accepted through this path.

### Additional information

- Last known good: Docker sandbox backend on the same version (2026.8.1-beta.3 & 2026.9.1-beta.1) works reliably.
- First known bad: Native SSH backend failure observed since initial configuration on 2026.8.1-beta.3, persists after upgrade to 2026.9.1-beta.1.
- This is the independent SSH-backend trigger path requested by the maintainer when closing #102006 (which was fixed for local/bash exec via #110704).
- The #110704 fix races tool execute promises at the wrapToolWithAbortSignal layer; the SSH backend's channel-close / completion-wake settlement path may lose the child-exit event under abort, leaving the per-session executor slot unreleased.
- Workaround: Use Docker sandbox backend, or run ordinary ssh client commands inside the Docker sandbox. After a wedge, recover with gateway restart or fresh session.

issues.body:
### Description

In OpenClaw `2026.8.1` and `2026.8.2`, GitHub Copilot models cannot be selected or used. This is a regression compared to `v2026.7.1-2` where Copilot models functioned properly.

When running interactive setup via `openclaw configure --section model` and selecting GitHub Copilot, authentication succeeds, but the wizard fails to select any model:

```
│  GitHub Copilot authentication succeeded, but no eligible live model could be selected.  │
│  Choose a model after checking your Copilot plan and organization policy.                 │
```

Furthermore, manually configuring Copilot models (such as `gpt-5.6-sol` or other preview models available on active Copilot subscriptions) fails at runtime with `403 unauthorized: not authorized to use this Copilot feature`. The error is classified under auth failure (`reason=auth next=none`), causing model fallback to fail and returning:
```
Authentication failed (provider returned HTTP 401/403). Your provider token may have expired — try the request again in a moment. If the failure persists, re-authenticate this provider.
```
while the exact same subscription works in other clients (e.g. VS Code / Hermes).

---

### Root Cause Analysis

1. **Overly Strict Starter Model Filter in `isCopilotCatalogModelSelectable`**
   In `extensions/github-copilot/models.ts`:
   ```ts
   function isCopilotCatalogModelSelectable(model) {
     const metadata = readCopilotModelSelectionMetadata(model);
     return Boolean(isCopilotCatalogModelVisible(model) && metadata?.streaming !== false && metadata?.toolCalls);
   }
   ```
   During `openclaw configure`, `resolveInteractiveCopilotStarterModel` calls `resolveCopilotStarterModel()`, which queries `/models` and filters models using `isCopilotCatalogModelSelectable`.
   GitHub Copilot's `/models` API returns items where `capabilities.supports.tool_calls` is not `true` or `model_picker_enabled` is missing/false when accessed via generic headers. Because all returned models fail the filter, `selectCopilotStarterModel` returns `undefined`, throwing:
   `"GitHub Copilot did not return an enabled, picker-visible chat model with streaming and tool-call support."`
   This is caught in `index.ts` and shows the error note above, rendering Copilot unconfigurable through the wizard.

2. **Missing VS Code Extension Header Emulation for Chat / Preview Models**
   Requests sent to Copilot endpoints lack complete VS Code editor / Copilot chat client headers (`Editor-Version`, `CopilotClient`, etc.), causing GitHub Copilot backend to reject requests to newer/preview models with 403.

---

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `openclaw configure --section model` on `v2026.8.1` / `v2026.8.2`.
2. Select `GitHub Copilot` and complete authentication.
3. Observe the error:
   `GitHub Copilot authentication succeeded, but no eligible live model could be selected.`
4. Alternatively, manually configure `github-copilot/gpt-5.6-sol` in `openclaw.json` with fallbacks configured (`openrouter/free`).
5. Send a message to trigger agent run.
6. Observe request rejection with HTTP 403 and fallback bypass (`reason=auth next=none`).

---

### Live Reproduction & Trace Evidence (`v2026.8.2`)

Re-tested and verified on **OpenClaw `2026.8.2` (commit `0965053`)** with an active GitHub Copilot subscription.

*(Sanitized Gateway & Provider Trace Log, timestamp `Sep 02 10:57:49` – `10:59:15`)*:

```log
Sep 02 10:57:49 [REDACTED-HOST] node[2664861]: 2026-09-02T10:57:49.209+08:00 [agent/embedded] [model-fallback] configured fallbacks disabled by user model override run=[REDACTED-RUN-ID] session=sha256:[REDACTED]
Sep 02 10:57:56 [REDACTED-HOST] node[2664861]: 2026-09-02T10:57:56.925+08:00 [provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] start provider=github-copilot api=openai-responses model=gpt-5.6-sol method=POST url=https://api.business.githubcopilot.com/responses timeoutMs=undefined proxy=none policy=custom
Sep 02 10:57:58 [REDACTED-HOST] node[2664861]: 2026-09-02T10:57:58.446+08:00 [provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] response provider=github-copilot api=openai-responses model=gpt-5.6-sol status=403 elapsedMs=1522 dispatcher=new contentType=text/plain; charset=utf-8
Sep 02 10:57:58 [REDACTED-HOST] node[2664861]: 2026-09-02T10:57:58.454+08:00 [openai-transport] [responses] error provider=github-copilot api=openai-responses model=gpt-5.6-sol name=Error status=403 code=undefined type=undefined causeName=undefined causeCode=undefined message=403 unauthorized: not authorized to use this Copilot feature
Sep 02 10:57:58 [REDACTED-HOST] node[2664861]: 2026-09-02T10:57:58.491+08:00 [channel] embedded run agent end: runId=[REDACTED-RUN-ID] isError=true model=gpt-5.6-sol provider=github-copilot error=⚠️ github-copilot/gpt-5.6-sol request failed (authentication failed, HTTP 403). Re-authenticate the provider and try again. rawError=403 unauthorized: not authorized to use this Copilot feature
Sep 02 10:59:11 [REDACTED-HOST] node[2664861]: 2026-09-02T10:59:11.224+08:00 [agent/embedded] Runtime auth refresh failed for github-copilot: Copilot authentication failed: timed out after 30000ms | The operation was aborted due to timeout | 23
Sep 02 10:59:11 [REDACTED-HOST] node[2664861]: 2026-09-02T10:59:11.245+08:00 [agent/embedded] auth profile failure state updated: runId=[REDACTED-RUN-ID] profile=sha256:[REDACTED] provider=github-copilot reason=auth window=cooldown reused=false
Sep 02 10:59:11 [REDACTED-HOST] node[2664861]: 2026-09-02T10:59:11.248+08:00 [agent/embedded] embedded run failover decision: runId=[REDACTED-RUN-ID] stage=assistant decision=surface_error reason=auth from=github-copilot/gpt-5.6-sol profile=sha256:[REDACTED] rawError=403 unauthorized: not authorized to use this Copilot feature

```

---

### Environment

- OpenClaw Version: `2026.8.2 (0965053)` (also reproduced in `2026.8.1`; worked in `2026.7.1-2`)
- Node.js: `v26.8.1`
- OS: Linux x86_64
- Account: Active GitHub Copilot Subscription
