issues.body:
## Current status — four draft compiler fixes; adoption remains on hold

The personal fork now has four stacked drafts:
https://github.com/vincentkoc/tsc-ts/pull/1 → https://github.com/vincentkoc/tsc-ts/pull/2 → https://github.com/vincentkoc/tsc-ts/pull/3 → https://github.com/vincentkoc/tsc-ts/pull/4.

The first three selectively backport uniform-union narrowing, recursion/identity relations, and whole-program noEmit exit semantics. The fourth repairs lost generic arguments in value import queries such as `typeof import("./factory").fn<T>`, exposed by OpenClaw's Slack test graph. It reuses the compiler's instantiation owner and adds six differential fixtures. This is still a 7.0.2-based candidate, not a complete 7.1 port.

[OpenClaw all-graph run 39144853163](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39144853163), attempt 1, completed with failure at source `6dca68dcdb14a117db9b6d778e9c7dbcf8ba88b0`, using the three-fix compiler `68d06984df0d1a9a89657cf44f0f709e15f13403`:
- All 38 artifact ZIP digests and independent auditor replays match. Exact source, run, attempt, producer and compiler identities plus the common 108-library manifest were verified.
- All 576 planned trials were attempted: 567 valid, nine rejected, none unattempted. Verdicts: 36 equivalent groups, two incomplete. All 180 canary trials passed candidate/pinned parity.
- Accepted candidate/pinned repository outcomes match across 37 graphs with stable repeats. The plugin-test graph has no accepted upstream controls and returns the candidate TS2345 that led to draft 4.
- Three plugin nonincremental reference samples and six plugin-test pinned/reference samples were explicitly OOM-killed under the unchanged limits. Process exit 137 versus GNU-time exit 0 remains rejected; cleanup was verified. Historical exit-137 causes remain unproven.
- All artifacts verify exit-state and deadline-cleanup smokes. No trial state was unavailable and accepted trial states had no anomalies.

The fourth-fix head `a80cd9190942d16286a8483f1f51d9a68037324f` passed [scoped CI](https://github.com/vincentkoc/tsc-ts/actions/runs/39162206911): 11/69 units, 42/42 cases, all first attempt, no skips or retries. Its [three-compiler probe](https://github.com/vincentkoc/tsc-ts/actions/runs/39162671243) passed all 36 rows with identical libraries. The preceding full run passed 67/69 units; both project units failed the export-assignment fixture's module configuration, corrected at the current head without changing compiler bytes. Current proof is scoped, not a fresh full-suite pass.

The [OpenClaw draft](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175991) pins the fourth-fix compiler at source head `7a1c55ef8a561e1147938fc3bcd0ab6e0ba51ecb`. The completed 38-graph run still covers the previous compiler only.

[Memory diagnostic 39181890646](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39181890646), source `280e7719968e746bf25e7526a022da24539a23a9`, completed all six trials. The candidate completed the real plugin-test graph cleanly at both 3GiB and 10GiB soft targets. All four pinned/reference controls were explicitly OOM-killed under the unchanged four-CPU/12GiB/no-swap limits and rejected. Their last observed Go live heaps were 11,093–11,530 trace-reported MB. Candidate emitted no GC trace. Inputs, library identities and cleanup were verified. The two targets used different CPU models, so timing/GC differences cannot isolate the soft target. Raw diagnostic artifacts remain excluded from qualification. Hosted tooling passed 24 tests, both types, lint, format and workflow validation.

[Capacity control 39183419122](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39183419122), source `d4027ef0aa46ec44da2bebecd2c9597200878b3b`, stopped at the unchanged `Non-loopback network interface` admission guard on both capacity jobs and was cancelled. Zero of 27 compiler trials ran; route/TCP probes were not reached. This is neither capacity proof nor evidence of a network escape. Hosted tooling passed 28 tests, both types, lint, formatting and workflow validation. The separate 24GiB/four-CPU/no-swap profile remains unqualified and does not erase the failed 12GiB controls.

[Diagnostic run 39184795601](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39184795601), exact source `7a1c55ef8a561e1147938fc3bcd0ab6e0ba51ecb`, failed isolation admission. Hosted tooling passed 28 tests, both types, lint, formatting and workflow checks. The independently verified artifact reports loopback plus four non-loopback interfaces in both sysfs and `/proc/self/net/dev`, while Docker declares `NetworkMode=none` / `Runtime=runc` (client/server 28.0.4; kernel 6.6.141). The guard exited 1, `OOMKilled=false`, and cleanup passed. No sandbox compiler was invoked. External reachability and namespace ownership remain unproven; the TCP probe was not reached, and absent route records do not prove route absence. Artifact `12157484027`, ZIP SHA-256 `4ccde45d39f3c95e49a4e2e1bd330eb435f3e7c9607b473f4d1ee6c1cf713671`, contains only inventory and isolation diagnostics.

Current blocker: the capacity runner owner must restore a network namespace satisfying Docker's `--network none` contract. Rerun the isolation diagnostic first; only after admission passes can the 27 capacity-control trials and remaining 36 graphs proceed. The guard remains unchanged, and no sandbox compiler was run on the failed-admission runner.

**Keep the repository-pinned compiler.** Remaining work is exact repaired-head repository coverage with accepted controls; no repaired-head all-graph pass is claimed. Broader warm-cache, whole-CI and platform proof remains separate. The older native threaded-watch retry remains an unresolved named follow-up.

All four OpenClaw PRs and all four fork PRs remain drafts, with auto-merge disabled. Nothing was landed or released, and compiler selection is unchanged. Explicit owner approval is required before landing.

The sections below are dated historical evidence. Statements that no fork exists, version causality is unresolved, or no expanded campaign has started describe earlier stages and are superseded by this status. Their historical measurements and limits are preserved.
---

## Summary

Qualify Vercel Labs `tsc-ts` for OpenClaw CI through diagnostic equivalence and controlled resource measurements before considering a compiler switch.

## Problem to solve

A successful benchmark collection job does not mean the candidate typechecks OpenClaw successfully. The existing experiment collected useful timing data, but its candidate emits diagnostics that the repository-pinned compiler does not.

## Proposed solution

Prepare a narrow draft stack:

1. Independently audit existing artifact groups: complete samples, actual input/output hashes, checking flags, stable diagnostics, exit status, and explicit reference coverage.
2. Extend the isolated opt-in experiment with version-matched reference coverage, deliberate error canaries, and comparable CPU/memory limits. Keep compiler identity, library inputs and source revision attached to every result.
3. Propose adoption only if correctness and measured CI cost justify it. Preserve the TypeScript package used for graph discovery and the separate Oxlint path. A maintained upstream fix is preferable to a fork; fork only for a demonstrated unresolved need.

No compiler switch or landing is authorized by this issue. Draft preparation and qualification are the current scope.

## Draft stack

Stack: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175542 → https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175557 → https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175567.

The three draft layers are the artifact auditor, isolated collector, and canaries/CI entry point. All remain drafts with auto-merge disabled. Do not adopt tsc-ts 0.0.2: verified canaries expose missed and spurious diagnostics. No landing or compiler switch is authorized.

## Alternatives considered

- Adopt from the advertised 2–4× claim: insufficient without OpenClaw diagnostic and resource parity.
- Keep only raw benchmark summaries: useful for discovery, but completion can be mistaken for a passing typecheck.
- Fork immediately: premature because the observed release-specific canary bugs already have upstream fixes, and a fork would still need a maintained 7.1-compatible checker and release qualification.

## Impact

Affected: maintainer compiler qualification and CI cost decisions. This is tooling work with no bot runtime behavior change. The current compiler remains selected while the candidate is evaluated.

## Evidence/examples

- [Original experiment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39006507786): 37 completed graphs before one group reached its deadline.
- [Completion run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39010366402): the remaining `test-root-e2e` graph.
- [Collector source](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/334ba2cfe3add15f1078b0d09424b3ff696df9c2/.github/scripts/compiler-comparison.mjs).
- [Upstream tsc-ts](https://github.com/vercel-labs/tsc-ts).

The experiment compared repository TypeScript 7.1.0-dev.20260928.1 with tsc-ts 0.0.2 reporting compiler version 7.0.2. The inspected primary samples report pinned exit 0 versus candidate exit 1 with two diagnostics; the core TypeScript 7.0.2 reference reproduces those diagnostics. That suggests version drift and is not proof of a port-specific defect.

Core median wall time was 79.21s vs 48.46s under the repository CI policy (about 1.63×), but 49.32s vs 48.15s in the serial control without Go tuning (about 1.02×). The candidate checks failed; these are not passing-equivalence or end-to-end CI speedup claims.

The new auditor was exercised against SHA256-verified artifact 12092344406 from the completion run. It reports complete, stable, equal-input evidence with divergent exits and returns failure, rather than treating collection as qualification.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes. Draft stack; explicit maintainer approval required before landing.


### Final qualification evidence

[Run 39040667733](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39040667733) completed at `476fbb2663c1b6e2c67d14e3a8b26cb793e9fc05`. The combined tooling gate passed 23 focused tests, both tooling typecheck graphs, scoped lint, formatting and workflow validation. Compiler qualification correctly failed.

All 279 planned trials were attempted and have numeric records: 276 valid measurements, including all 180 canary trials, plus three explicitly rejected plugin reference trials. All five artifact ZIP digests were verified; independent local auditor replay exactly matches every hosted verdict.

| Group | Valid / planned measurements | Numeric records | Verdict |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Core + canaries | 216/216 | 216 | divergent |
| UI | 18/18 | 18 | divergent |
| Plugins | 15/18 | 18 | incomplete |
| Scripts | 18/18 | 18 | divergent |
| Root E2E typecheck graph | 9/9 | 9 | divergent |

All repository profiles have equal expanded configuration and file inventories across the three compilers. Accepted repeats are stable: pinned 7.1 passes; candidate 0.0.2 and accepted native 7.0.2 reference trials emit the same two repository diagnostics. The missing plugin reference controls remain explicit gaps.

Every artifact verifies four CPUs, 12 GiB memory, zero swap, allowed metric writes, EROFS for checkout/evidence writes, a loopback-only namespace with ENETUNREACH for external IPv4 TCP, and SIGKILL deadline cleanup. The three plugin nonincremental reference trials returned process 137 versus GNU time 0. Their numeric records remain outside valid measurements; completed-job logs independently prove later valid trials after each rejection. Their termination cause is unproven. Actual workflow cancellation was not tested.

These are tested draft qualification tools; no compiler adoption, fork or landing is authorized.

Artifact identities:

- Core + canaries: artifact `12104838952`, SHA256 `19e41c545e469f88fcdee274307166b90892ffb8ff800b58952f425205444669`.
- UI: artifact `12104109956`, SHA256 `d0a8d9a2fef99ae245e5c1fd0bd38ceaef52a8bbe0448143c51b445c5d5cff45`.
- Plugins: artifact `12105023497`, SHA256 `677fcc7e24748bb41147d4b0802ef66ad978cedceb48350cd4565b6a5219333c`.
- Scripts: artifact `12105546554`, SHA256 `8b1612e9a0c6f2499e8b1c9fce153dac97dbc50df01633970a053a97ecc266db`.
- Root E2E typecheck graph: artifact `12104454935`, SHA256 `78db667ecdcd8a712af782386f3aa5e5dfb69c4ba4fb2e6fe362114264d5f096`.

The earlier [run 39037616479](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39037616479), source `10e46ede3678fbbea93664c9f64d6ce0cbc1782a`, remains separately verified at 269/279 valid measurements. It exposed collection abort after rejected resource samples. The final run verifies the repair: all planned trials are attempted; rejected records remain visible and excluded. Historical evidence does not substitute for current-head execution.

Canary findings at the final head: tsc-ts 0.0.2 misses the indexed-compound diagnostic, rejects the valid variadic case, and omits the CommonJS import/export diagnostics while retaining the export-modifier error. Both upstream baselines agree on those cases. The invalid variadic case is also rejected with a different inference/diagnostic. `narrowed-status` reproduces a 7.1/7.0.2 diagnostic difference; the generic-union reduction does not reproduce the repository difference. Baseline 7.1 exits 2 for negative controls while 7.0.2 exits 1; exit-only differences are recorded separately from missing/extra diagnostics. All 180 raw canary outcomes match the earlier run, with unchanged fixture contents and recorded compiler/library identities.

### Timing observations, not adoption proof

Three rotated repeats per compiler/profile under the same enforced limits. These are median cold-CI wall times in seconds and median peak RSS in GiB. The candidate and reference checks fail; the ratios do not establish passing-equivalence, whole-job or critical-path speedup.

| Graph | Pinned 7.1 seconds | Candidate 0.0.2 seconds | Reference 7.0.2 seconds | Pinned/candidate wall ratio | Pinned/candidate RSS GiB |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Core | 77.00 | 47.59 | 93.81 | 1.62× | 6.689 / 5.393 |
| UI | 63.66 | 36.32 | 76.55 | 1.75× | 6.704 / 5.526 |
| Plugins | 92.95 | 56.68 | 115.45 | 1.64× | 8.230 / 6.805 |
| Scripts | 78.15 | 50.07 | 93.72 | 1.56× | 6.806 / 5.701 |
| Root E2E typecheck graph | 71.81 | 44.90 | 85.83 | 1.60× | 6.445 / 5.379 |

Core's serial control was 49.31s pinned versus 47.49s candidate (1.04×), compared with 77.00s versus 47.59s (1.62×) under CI policy. Nonincremental core was 32.58s versus 27.07s (1.20×); incremental-unthrottled core was 35.28s versus 27.75s (1.27×). All core controls completed in this run. Runner noise beyond these repeats, warm-cache behavior and whole-CI benefit remain unproven.


### Investigation disposition

| Investigation | Evidence and remaining limit |
|---|---|
| 1. Reuse the existing baseline | Historical source, compiler identities, graph inventory and reported outcomes were reconciled. The 38-graph experiment remains baseline/discovery evidence, not complete qualification of the current stack. |
| 2. Classify the two repository diagnostics | With equal inputs, native TypeScript 7.0.2 and tsc-ts agree while pinned 7.1 passes. This classifies the observed difference by upstream version/reference behavior. The narrowed-status reduction reproduces it; the generic-union reduction does not. The causative commit and any OpenClaw defect attribution remain unproven. |
| 3. Preserve bug detection | All 180 canary trials were inspected. Released 0.0.2 misses diagnostics and rejects valid code, so its correctness gate fails. Five current representative graphs and historical 38-graph discovery do not establish complete current-graph adoption coverage or deliberate error injection in every graph. |
| 4. Measure CI benefit | Cold CI, nonincremental and core serial/resource controls use rotated repeats and equal enforced limits. These are failed-candidate timings. Warm-cache benefit, whole-job/critical-path speedup and savings beyond broader runner noise remain unproven. |
| 5. Verify incremental invalidation | The pilot preserves the existing cold-cache CI contract. Warm no-change reruns, edits, deletions, project references, dependency/compiler upgrades and interrupted persisted-cache builds remain unperformed adoption gates. |
| 6. Preserve failure and lifecycle semantics | Final-head focused tests, both tooling typecheck graphs, lint, formatting and workflow validation passed. All five artifacts verify sandbox effects and deadline cleanup. Plugin numeric records and completed-job logs independently prove continuation after each rejected trial while qualification remains incomplete. Actual workflow cancellation was not tested. |
| 7. Qualify distribution | Pinned, SRI-checked downloads and native invocation are exercised on clean Linux x64 CI. Developer/multiplatform installation and adoption rollback remain unperformed. The normal compiler selection is unchanged. |
| 8. Assess a maintained fork | The three reproduced release-specific defects already have post-release upstream fixes. Those fixes are not qualified by this run. No fork was built; 7.1 catch-up is not a pin change, and fork build/resynchronization cost remains unmeasured. |

The deliverable is a tested draft qualification stack and a recommendation scoped to released `0.0.2`. These dispositions do not mean all eight adoption gates passed.

### Current decision and follow-ups

Keep the repository-pinned compiler. The candidate's correctness gate fails independently of its timing advantage. Verified 0.0.2 defects correspond to upstream [indexed-access fix](https://github.com/vercel-labs/tsc-ts/pull/155), [CommonJS fix](https://github.com/vercel-labs/tsc-ts/pull/156), and [variadic inference fix](https://github.com/vercel-labs/tsc-ts/pull/167). Prefer qualifying an upstream release containing those fixes; a fork needs a demonstrated unresolved requirement, not just faster failing checks.

- Version causality remains unresolved. The narrowed-status reduction reproduces the difference; the generic-union reduction does not. Do not describe 7.1 as an intentional semantic improvement or patch OpenClaw source from these observations alone.
- Resource termination remains a separate finding: all three plugin nonincremental 7.0.2 reference trials returned process 137 versus GNU time 0 under the enforced 12 GiB limit. The earlier core termination did not recur. Cause remains unproven; future diagnosis needs container OOM/cgroup termination evidence captured before cleanup. Keep the current limits; rejected trials do not become valid benchmark samples.
- Future adoption needs complete current-source graph coverage, cache-identity compatibility, supported-platform qualification, and explicit maintainer approval. These drafts do not switch the compiler or create a fork.


## Fixed upstream candidate follow-up — 2026-10-18

issues.body:
### Summary

Memory sync/reindex with the Gemini embedding provider fails with a 400 `INVALID_ARGUMENT` because the inline `:batchEmbedContents` request groups more than 100 requests per call, exceeding Google's documented per-request limit. The resulting error is not classified as retryable or splittable, so the whole sync aborts instead of splitting the batch.

### Environment

- OpenClaw: 2026.8.1 (ea80657)
- Runtime: Linux, systemd user service, Node 26.8.1
- Embeddings config: `memory.search.provider = gemini`, model `gemini-embedding-001` (default), `memory.search.remote.batch.enabled = false` (default)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have a memory workspace with enough short chunks (typical memory/README-sized chunks of ~50–200 bytes).
2. Run `openclaw memory index --agent main` (or let the automatic sync run with dirty files).

Result:

```
Memory index failed (main): gemini embeddings failed (400): * BatchEmbedContentsRequest.requests: at most 100 requests can be in one batch [code=INVALID_ARGUMENT] | INVALID_ARGUMENT
```

### Root cause

Three pieces combine:

1. `buildMemoryEmbeddingBatches(chunks, EMBEDDING_BATCH_MAX_TOKENS)` groups chunks **by estimated bytes only** (8 KB) with no item-count cap. With short chunks a single group easily exceeds 100 items.
2. The Gemini client's `embedDocuments` posts **all** inputs in one `POST …:batchEmbedContents` call (`body: { requests: inputs.map(…) }`) without clamping to Google's 100-request limit for this endpoint.
3. `runMemoryEmbeddingBatchRetryWithSplit` would recover by splitting, but the 400 message doesn't match `SPLITTABLE_MEMORY_EMBEDDING_BATCH_ERROR_RE` (nor the retryable transport/service regexes), so the sync aborts permanently instead of splitting.

### Evidence

Verified against the live API with the same key, same network:

- `:embedContent` (single) → 200
- `:batchEmbedContents` with 100 requests → 200
- `:batchEmbedContents` with 101 requests → 400 `at most 100 requests can be in one batch`

So the network/proxy is not a factor; the batch grouping is the only problem.

### Workaround

Patched `buildMemoryEmbeddingBatches` locally to also break a group at 100 items:

```js
if (current.length > 0 && (currentTokens + estimate > maxTokens || current.length >= 100)) {
```

With that one-line change, `memory index` completed successfully: 198/198 files indexed, 895 chunks, vector search working. The patch is lost on package upgrade, so a proper fix is needed.

Note: the remote files-API batch path (`memory.search.remote.batch.enabled = true`) also avoids this limit, but its polling connection was unreliable on our network (repeated `ECONNRESET` on long-poll), so properly-clamped inline batches are the more robust default.

### Suggested fixes

- Clamp Gemini inline `batchEmbedContents` groups to the documented 100-request limit, and/or
- Add batch-size-limit errors ("at most N requests") to the splittable-error regex so `runMemoryEmbeddingBatchRetryWithSplit` can handle any limit transparently, and/or
- Make the inline embedding batch size configurable.

issues.title: [Feature]: support SubQ Snap decision models
issues.body:
## Summary

Add SubQ Snap as an optional decision-model provider, using its documented Decisions API rather than treating it as a conversational model.

## Problem to solve

Requested by @vincentkoc in [this discussion](https://x.com/vincent_koc/status/2110026379471524304). OpenClaw has a provider-neutral Decision role but no SubQ adapter. Snap returns typed choices, probabilities, and scores, not generated chat/tool-call messages.

## Proposed solution

Provide an opt-in external `subq` plugin exposing `subq/subq-snap-preview` in the Decision picker, with prepared SecretRef credentials, typed Boolean/Choice/Score translation, provider limits, safe error handling, and setup documentation.

The initial integration should remain text/JSON-only: the shared Decision contract does not expose images. Do not add Snap to conversational catalogs or claim OpenRouter compatibility.

## Alternatives considered

An OpenAI chat-completions custom provider does not fit Snap. SubQ's separate `subq-preview` chat model is a different API/model and outside this request.

## Impact

Users who choose SubQ could use it for explicit classification, routing, and rubric scoring. The plugin should stay disabled by default and make no automatic paid requests on installation.

## Evidence/examples

Official documentation checked October 13, 2026:
- https://docs.subq.ai/endpoints/decisions-api/ — `POST https://api.subq.ai/v1/systemone`; `subq-snap-preview`; 1–16 questions; 2–255 choice alternatives; 2–10 score levels; 393,216-token context.
- https://docs.subq.ai/using-the-api/authentication/ — Bearer API key.
- https://docs.subq.ai/using-the-api/models/ — Snap is a public-preview decision model, separate from the chat model.

Vendor performance claims are not integration evidence. Authenticated live proof requires a SubQ account/key with credits and access; no credential is requested in public.

## Implementation intent

Implementation and focused tests are being prepared in the linked work session. Package publication/release is separate.

issues.body:
### Summary

Since ~2026-09-13, every inference request on the xAI OAuth (Grok subscription) route fails with **HTTP 426** from `https://cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1/responses`. Two related defects:

1. **The xai plugin sends OpenClaw's own version string as the Grok CLI version.** `extensions/xai/index.ts` passes `clientVersion: pluginApi.runtime.version` into `wrapXaiProviderStream`, so the proxy receives `x-grok-client-version: 2026.9.3` (or `2026.9.4`). The proxy validates that header against real Grok CLI versions (currently `0.2.112`) and now rejects OpenClaw's value with 426. This is the header introduced by #115617 to fix #113662 — it worked while the proxy tolerated arbitrary values, and stopped working when the proxy tightened validation.
2. **Isolated/utility ("simple") completions never send the Grok OAuth headers at all.** The header injection lives only in the plugin's stream wrapper (`extensions/xai/stream.ts`, `createXaiGrokOAuthHeadersWrapper`). The simple-completion path used by e.g. the Control UI session observer (`simple-completion-execution` → `completeSimple`) bypasses the plugin's `wrapStreamFn`, so those requests carry no `x-grok-client-version` / `X-XAI-Token-Auth` / `x-grok-model-override` and 426 even if facet 1 is fixed. Observable as the session observer repeatedly logging `Isolated completion failed with stop reason error.` and self-disabling when `utilityModel` is an xai OAuth model.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Authenticate the bundled xai provider with the Grok subscription OAuth flow; catalog routes to `https://cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1`.
2. Send any agent turn on an xai OAuth model (e.g. `xai/grok-4.6`) → `POST /v1/responses` returns 426.
3. Set `agents.defaults.utilityModel` to the same model with the session observer enabled → observer completions also 426 and the observer self-disables.

### Evidence (live, 2026-09-13, OpenClaw 2026.9.3)

- Gateway log: `[model-fetch] response provider=xai api=openai-responses model=grok-4.6 status=426` on every inference attempt (32/32 that day).
- Direct HTTP replay with the same valid OAuth bearer token:
  - `x-grok-client-version: 0.2.112` → **HTTP 200**, streaming works (`"model":"grok-4.6-build"`).
  - no header / an OpenClaw version string → **426** (`"Your Grok CLI version (none) is outdated. Please update to version ..."` per the proxy's error format).
- Code on `main` today: `extensions/xai/index.ts` still passes `pluginApi.runtime.version`; the simple-completion path adds no Grok headers.

### Expected behavior

- The plugin should send a value the proxy accepts — a maintained Grok CLI version constant (as the sibling billing client already does with `SUPERGROK_CLIENT_VERSION` in `extensions/xai/usage.ts`, though that constant, `1.0.4`, is not a real Grok CLI version either), or a configurable override so operators can bump it without a release when xAI raises the floor.
- All xai OAuth request paths (streaming and simple/isolated completions) should attach the Grok OAuth headers, not just the plugin stream wrapper.

### Workaround

Local dist patches (both verified working): set `clientVersion: "0.2.112"` in the plugin entry, and merge the three Grok headers into `completionOptions.headers` in the simple-completion execution path when `model.provider === "xai"` and `model.baseUrl` is the Grok proxy.

### Environment

OpenClaw 2026.9.3 (same code in 2026.9.4 and current `main`), Node 26.8.2, Linux/WSL2. xai auth: Grok subscription OAuth (`grok-cli:access`).

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

An array in the Deepgram providerOptions (for example `keyterm`) is sent to Deepgram `/v1/listen` as a single comma-joined query parameter instead of one parameter per element.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On 2026.10.4, call the bundled Deepgram batch transcriber with an array option and a stub `fetchFn` that only records the request URL (no network call):

```js
const m = await import("/usr/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/extensions/deepgram/audio.js");
let seen;
const fetchFn = async (url) => { seen = String(url); return new Response(JSON.stringify({results:{channels:[{alternatives:[{transcript:"ok"}]}]}}), {status:200}); };
await m.transcribeDeepgramAudio({ buffer: new Uint8Array([0]), fileName: "a.ogg", mime: "audio/ogg", apiKey: "test", model: "nova-3", language: "multi", query: { keyterm: ["Aquablock", "linho", "Sunbrella"], smart_format: true }, timeoutMs: 5000, fetchFn });
console.log(seen);
```

2. Observe the printed URL.

### Expected behavior

One `keyterm=` parameter per array element, for example `...&keyterm=Aquablock&keyterm=linho&keyterm=Sunbrella`.

References:
- Deepgram requires one parameter per term; comma-separated lists "don't return an error, but they silently boost nothing": https://developers.deepgram.com/docs/keyterm
- OpenClaw `docs/providers/deepgram.md` lines 62 to 64: `providerOptions.deepgram` "merges extra query params directly into the Deepgram `/listen` request, so any Deepgram-supported param name works".
- OpenClaw `docs/providers/deepgram.md` lines 119 to 121: Flux supports `keyterm` in `providerOptions.deepgram`.

Suggested fix: when a value is an array, call `url.searchParams.append(key, String(item))` for each element, in both the batch path (the query loop in `dist/audio-*.mjs`) and the Flux path (`dist/extensions/deepgram/audio-flux.js`).

### Actual behavior

The captured URL is:

`https://api.deepgram.com/v1/listen?model=nova-3&language=multi&keyterm=Aquablock%2Clinho%2CSunbrella&smart_format=true`

The batch path builds the query with `url.searchParams.set(key, String(value))`, so an array becomes one comma-joined value. The Flux path does the same in `audio-flux.js`.

Separately, calling Deepgram's API directly with one `keyterm=` per term (same audio, Nova-3 `language=multi`) corrected two product names that plain Nova-3 got wrong on real Portuguese voice notes ("linho" and "Aquablock"). So the feature works upstream; only the joining blocks it.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.4 (383c124)

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04 (Linux 6.8), Node 24.22

### Install method

npm global

### Model

deepgram/nova-3 (tools.media audio, language "multi")

### Provider / routing chain

Bundled deepgram plugin, direct to api.deepgram.com /v1/listen (batch). No proxy.

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell

```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

- Affected: anyone configuring Deepgram keyterm prompting (or any other repeatable Deepgram parameter, such as keywords, redact, tag, search, replace) through providerOptions, batch and Flux.
- Severity: feature silently ineffective, no error.
- Frequency: always, whenever more than one term is passed.
- Consequence: product and brand names in voice notes keep being mistranscribed, which changed the meaning of real requests (which fabric to buy, which material was offered).

### Additional information

Docs suggestion: state in `providers/deepgram.md` that array values expand to repeated parameters, with a `keyterm` example. A single keyterm (a plain string) works today.

issues.body:
### Summary
Telegram isolated polling enters a tight infinite loop when the persisted update offset (`telegram.update-offsets` -> `lastUpdateId`) is higher than the real `update_id`s returned by the Bot API. Restarts and `openclaw doctor --fix` do not recover it.

### Version / setup
- OpenClaw 2026.10.3 (59cb447), Node 24, Linux
- Telegram channel with `apiRoot` pointing to a self-hosted Bot API server (`aiogram/telegram-bot-api`, `--local`)

### What happened
- Persisted state: `{"version":3,"lastUpdateId":654450445,...}` (row created when switching `apiRoot` from the official API to the local Bot API server).
- Real update_ids from the local server were ~141,563,5xx and later ~274,326,7xx.
- The worker calls `getUpdates` with `offset = lastUpdateId + 1` (a "future" offset). The Bot API then confirms nothing and returns the oldest pending update.
- The same update is received/spooled/"offset queued" hundreds of times per second:
  `isolated polling worker update received updateId=X queued=1` -> `update spooled` -> `offset queued`, no errors.
- Result: gateway at 120-200% CPU, RSS ~2.5 GB (above 2 GB heap cap), ~1 GB of logs in /tmp in about an hour.
- Since offsets are only persisted when greater than the stored one, the stale high value is never corrected. `/restart` and `openclaw doctor --fix` did not touch it.

### Workaround
Stop the gateway, delete the row `plugin_state_entries` (`plugin_id='telegram'`, `namespace='telegram.update-offsets'`, `entry_key='default'`), start the gateway. Loop stops immediately.

### Suggestions
1. Reset/ignore the persisted offset when `apiRoot` changes (similar to the existing bot-id / token-fingerprint rotation check).
2. Detect lack of progress (same `update_id` returned repeatedly despite a higher offset) and back off / reset the stored offset / log a single warning.
3. Let `openclaw doctor --fix` detect a stored offset that is far above observed update_ids.

Repeated fixture and assertion scaffolding makes these test suites harder to maintain.

prs.title: fix: resume interrupted peer work after gateway restarts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: admitted peer follow-ups and returned results can remain interrupted after a Gateway restart, even though their original session and unfinished work still exist.

## User Impact

Peer work resumes automatically in the original session after restart without requiring a manual Resume action or repeating a completed command. Requested replies still arrive when reverse-direction sends are disabled. Stop, cancellation, access revocation, and replaced-session boundaries remain enforced. No configuration or database-schema migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preserve the admitted operator recovery source, route automatic peer results through the existing durable communication owner, and retain their optional-reply context. Requested replies use authority captured from the accepted request rather than a new reverse-direction send permission. Exact endpoint and current cancellation/access checks still apply.

Make concurrent history reconciliation return consistent interrupted state, and revisit startup orphans after a temporary controller owner releases them. Recovery keeps the original startup cutoff and live ownership checks. Explicitly stopped claims and operations retain cleanup custody but cannot be captured or revalidated as recoverable work.

This does not fabricate receipts for historical deliveries already missing evidence or modify the running Team Gateway.

## Evidence

- Deterministic red/green regressions cover missing peer admission, concurrent history reconciliation, startup-owner release, stopped cleanup owners, and requested replies with restrictive reverse-send preferences. Positive reply cases and unsolicited reverse-send rejection remain covered.
- All **8 real-process controls passed** after integration with main at `8728bf7ab9e3492405b5af8710e212b8e1e2ffe9`: managed restart, SIGTERM, SIGKILL, automatic peer continuation, revoked authority before an effect, returned-result recovery with reverse sends disabled, and terminal Stop.
- Focused agent, recovery, CLI, and Gateway tests; canonical core/command/messaging/root-E2E type graphs; affected lint; formatting; and diff checks passed. The final requester-identity integration and its focused tests pass, as do all 8 real-process controls. Fresh independent P0–P2 review of the staged composition found no actionable defects.
- Two earlier isolated real-model Chromium runs passed: UI send → peer work → completed command → SIGKILL → same-disk Gateway restart → automatic final response, without `sessions.recover` or a post-crash message. The completed effect remained exactly once. Those browser runs precede the final permission/cancellation corrections; the final composition is covered by the real-process tests above.
- Integrated main’s requester-identity ownership (#157806), deferred writer adoption, and delegated-input retirement changes. Unauthenticated retired work stays terminal with a visible notice; a fresh authenticated turn continues in the same session. The three process controls now prove this current contract. Automatic authenticated peer recovery still needs no new user message.
- Fixed the browser serial-owner inventories and timeout ownership without expanding policy baselines. The redundant-label regression now uses the existing focused suite’s accepted-dispatch fixture; the full send/communication suites pass.
- The previous exact-head CI run exposed two unrelated session-list UI failures. Both reproduce the same assertion signatures on scheduled main run [39186683798](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39186683798/job/117850679097); the relevant test and UI controller are unchanged. This records inherited failure evidence, not a green-CI claim.
- Previous-head `check-test-types` also reported an unchanged Codex fixture using removed `MonitorOptions.completionDeliveryRetryDelaysMs`. The same TS2353 error reproduces on clean main `8d4c9e082ec974bc0a8b269305284667882f6f20` with `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json`; [failed PR job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39190579819/job/117863168668).

- Drop both `extensions/google/provider-models.test.ts` rewrites because main added substantial model-resolution coverage. Preserve music noncanonical-base64, request-error no-retry, and unconfigured-base-URL cases.
- Preserve main's platform/architecture process-identity cases. Keep the first shared cleanup, but drop the later conflicting `config-eval.test.ts` and `pid-alive.test.ts` rewrites.
- Preserve the update fixture's `allowCollaborativeSteering: false` setting.

prs.title: fix(acp): run new sessions in the requested directory
prs.body:
Closes #123557.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes agents running in the default workspace when an ACP client starts a new session in a different project directory.

## User Impact

Fresh ACP sessions execute in their requested absolute directory. Sessions selected by an existing key or label retain their Gateway-owned directory, and the Gateway's existing directory authorization still applies. No configuration or protocol changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Create the session through the existing Gateway owner before storing the bridge session. This persists `spawnedCwd` for later prompts and avoids a separate per-prompt directory override. A fresh key does not need a reset before creation, including with `--reset-session`.

This follows the owner-boundary approach discussed by @Chinmayrawat15 in the earlier, closed-unmerged #123585. AI-assisted implementation and validation.

## Evidence

- [Baseline regression](https://github.com/yinx65588-boop/openclaw/actions/runs/39190799667): the real Gateway RPC/persistence regression fails for the intended missing `spawnedCwd`; the adopted-session preservation control passes. The workflow succeeds by checking this expected test failure, not by treating the baseline test as passing.
- [Repaired validation](https://github.com/yinx65588-boop/openclaw/actions/runs/39191112959): 33 focused tests pass across ACP setup, real Gateway persistence/listing (fresh, fresh-with-reset, adopted), and existing Gateway directory authorization. Changed-file formatting, owner lint, production types and the Gateway test type graph pass.
- [Public CLI before/after proof](https://github.com/yinx65588-boop/openclaw/actions/runs/39192471412): the built public `pnpm openclaw acp` entry connects to an isolated Gateway and executes the real built-in `exec` tool with `{ "command": "pwd" }` and no `workdir`. Baseline output is the default workspace; repaired fresh and fresh-with-reset sessions output the requested project directory, while the adopted-session case outputs its existing directory. The workflow verifies the exact baseline/repaired source before building each variant; the artifact includes request ledgers, summaries and process logs.
- Independent Codex review of the final local patch: `scoped-clean` through P2, with no actionable findings. This is static review, separate from the executed tests and CLI proof.
- CI's `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` currently fails on the unchanged mock in `test/scripts/ci-node-test-plan.test.ts:3297`. [Exact baseline/CI-merge comparison](https://github.com/yinx65588-boop/openclaw/actions/runs/39194195664) reruns the original guard on base `d5aeceb2` and CI merge `c5d6eefd`: both exit 1 with byte-identical failure output. The test file, guard and baseline ledger are unchanged between those revisions. No suppressions or baseline allowances were added; this inherited failure remains visible in PR CI.

Redacted terminal results from the successful CLI run ([fixture and assertions](https://github.com/yinx65588-boop/openclaw/blob/df2210c562e423aeeadf6c1efce9c2820d7fba8e/.proof/acp-cwd-cli-proof.mjs)):

```text
Tool call in every case: exec {"command":"pwd"}  (no workdir override)
Baseline fresh:  requested=<root>/workspace/requested; pwd=<root>/workspace
Repaired fresh: requested=<root>/workspace/requested; pwd=<root>/workspace/requested
Repaired reset: requested=<root>/workspace/requested; pwd=<root>/workspace/requested
Repaired adopt: requested=<root>/workspace/requested; pwd=<root>/workspace/adopted
All assertions passed; workflow conclusion: success. Paid provider calls: 0.
```

Validation uses Linux with isolated state. Only the HTTP model endpoint is synthetic; ACP stdio, Gateway RPC, session persistence and tool execution use the real product. No paid provider calls were made. The reported Windows environment and a live provider have not been exercised.

prs.title: fix(memory): Active Memory's recall prompts show up in memory search results
prs.body:
Closes #176024

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes internal Active Memory recall conversations appearing in memory search results and displacing real conversation history, including helper content indexed before this fix.

## User Impact

Memory search omits identifiable recall helpers immediately and removes their indexed content during normal reconciliation, while retaining ordinary conversations and historical entries whose ownership cannot be established.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extends the existing admission fix across retrieval and reconciliation: excluding new transcripts alone leaves previously indexed helper chunks searchable until cleanup. Eligibility now applies before candidate limits, and cleanup runs independently of embedding work, including when an unrelated embedding fails. Metadata read errors remain visible instead of being treated as missing records.

Classification uses exact helper IDs and session keys, or ownership captured for the relevant transcript instance. Archive lookups use exact archive names; ownership is never inferred across reused session IDs or unidentified archive generations. This preserves ordinary transcripts that quote recall instructions and avoids deleting legitimate history.

While an index contains excluded sources, vector-enabled retrieval temporarily uses the existing semantic scan. This trades recovery speed for complete eligible results; normal indexed retrieval resumes after cleanup.

## Evidence

- The original PR head (`308ef05`) fails five new behavioral regressions: three retrieval modes with more than 200 historical helper chunks, and live/archive metadata read failures. The ordinary memory-file collision control passes. [Original-head regression run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_aab01d01c4996ac9b3afc88715a836b1). The original admission and startup suites pass all 21 tests.
- A real AWS Gateway running main (`dba2de1418b89eebcae98ad0ed4dbcb116e88d08`) produced a SQLite snapshot containing five helper chunks and one genuine user-fact chunk. The snapshot came from live recall and indexing, without fabricated transcript or index rows. [Live main reproduction](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_eece0d6c7d53fa828e2f1f9bf606d4da).
- At candidate `26930636`, **190 tests across 14 focused/consumer files passed**. Formatting, core/extension lint, docs checks, line limits, and core/extension/extension-test types passed. Production build passed (4m44.8s). Individual changed-file wall times are listed below. [AWS validation run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_fdf48c5a82f3c1f44a5fbdb8e755fcef).
- Candidate live fresh-state recall passed: two searches returned zero helpers and the genuine conversation; a separate conversation recalled the exact stored names. On the actual polluted-main snapshot, first CLI, Gateway `memory.search`, and Gateway tool invocation each returned zero helpers with the genuine fact preserved. Each surface started from an independent restore; no forced reindex was issued. [Live candidate run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_7150362699cb3720d6cd1defa95234c8). Both restored-main Gateway lanes also passed real cross-conversation recall. The complete live run passed (5m49.716s).
- Real PostgreSQL 17 + pgvector: **7/7 conformance tests passed**, including pre-limit keyword/path/vector eligibility and ordinary-memory collision controls with 33,000 excluded paths; none skipped. Vitest 26.87 seconds; runner 29.59 seconds. Same AWS validation run.
- Exact stable `2026.10.5` live search returned four helper hits plus the genuine conversation. Its online backup, captured after that search, already contained zero helper chunks and one genuine-fact chunk. Normal Doctor/startup/search upgrade of this clean stable-created state passed all three independently restored surfaces, with correct real-model cross-conversation recall in both Gateway lanes. Polluted upgrade proof comes from the separate main snapshot. This does not test package replacement, updater rollback, or managed-service deployment.

The branch incorporates the investigation-main baseline because its actual contaminated state uses schema 28 while the old PR runtime supports schema 27; this is required to exercise that upgrade through the real runtime. No schema or dependency changes are introduced by the correction itself.

## Test Cost

Each SQLite file was measured separately with `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` on the AWS runner ([measurement run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_bf46f170d4bae05e03219e417b640219)).

| Changed test file | CLI wall seconds | CI case seconds |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| manager-active-memory-retrieval | 73.578 | 26.446 |
| manager-session-exclusions | 28.972 | 0.234 |
| manager-session-sync-state | 31.933 | 0.046 |
| manager-sync-ops.startup-catchup | 67.858 | 25.111 |
| manager-search.postgres (conformance runner) | 29.59 | pending |

CLI wall times include worker compilation. CI values sum all passing-case durations (9/5/7/14 cases respectively); CI does not report individual file wall times. The retrieval tests spend about 40 seconds exercising real worker/index serving, blocked physical cleanup, embedding failure, captured provenance, and archive lifecycle transitions. Pure classification tests cannot detect candidate starvation or misattribution across those boundaries. Existing startup integration coverage also exceeds 30 seconds; its added cases exercise targeted indexing, keyless artifacts, and normal cleanup through the actual manager. No live providers are used by these regression tests.

Independent final code review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Exact-head GitHub broad CI for `26930636` has an inherited upstream failure; three PostgreSQL jobs are still running. It is not represented as passing evidence. [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39195108935).

## Inherited CI Failure

`checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` fails `mock-exports` at [the upstream CI-planner timing fixture](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/45fddcfe1fae0b99606d59409bc2fd69447896e7/test/scripts/ci-node-test-plan.test.ts#L3297). [Failure log](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39195108935/job/117876418882).

CI executes merge `5df207e3` of this PR into base `45fddcfe`. The failing test file, checker, scanner, timing module, and mock ledger are byte-identical between that base and merge. Upstream commit [`d8ff483`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/d8ff48313fcb39d8c377ae3b1f5c944879acf833) introduced the factory after the investigation baseline; it is absent from both the pinned baseline and this PR head. The correction does not change these files. This is recorded as separate upstream CI debt; the required gate remains red.

prs.title: fix: keep test compiler caches out of workspace synchronization
prs.body:
Refs #176778.

## What Problem This Solves

Ordinary tests can leave disposable compiler caches in a managed workspace's pending changes. If the host later removes a cache directory that an older result still records, synchronization treats its changed descendants as conflicting work. Review and refresh can then remain blocked even when the actual source edits already agree.

The missing paths are `.artifacts/vitest-worker-cache/`, `.cache/bun-transpiler/`, and the generated `.artifacts/vitest-shard-timings.json` scheduler data. Existing exclusions cover other test caches but not these current producer outputs.

## User Impact

These test caches stay with the runtime that created them instead of becoming authored workspace results. The existing recovery path also recognizes them in older authenticated results, allowing the preserved source work to settle normally.

Source edits, ignored reports and logs, nested fixtures, explicitly staged inputs, genuine source conflicts, and invalid-result rejection remain protected. The change does not exclude all ignored files or general `.artifacts`, `.cache`, or `dist` contents.

## Why This Change Was Made

Capture, transfer, manifest comparison, staged-result validation and recovery already use one shared classification rule. The rule now covers the three verified producer paths. Historical manifest projection and remote non-Git capture also omit parent directories whose contents are entirely excluded caches, while retaining genuine empty directories. This keeps the existing capture paths consistent without relocating caches or adding another synchronization mechanism.

The recovery regression retains the original manifest bytes and digest, with the cache-only parent absent from the host. Raw manifest validation and authentication still happen before projection; actual obstructions continue to conflict. A producer check calls the existing worker-cache retention, test-process environment and shard-timing writers, then captures their output through the workspace owner. That connects the exclusion to the paths the tools actually select.

## Evidence

On the original production source, authenticated pending-result settlement returns the preserved-workspace conflict, and cache-only expiry fails as unaccepted work. The corrected source passes those same recovery paths, including the case where source changes were already copied, while keeping independent source-conflict and malformed-tree controls.

Remote Linux validation passed:

- Original production source rejects the cache-bearing pending result. The final source admits the source edit and report with their old cache-only parent absent; a real parent-file obstruction still conflicts.
- Cache-only remote capture now reports no change in both non-Git and historical Git cases. Remote canonical lookup resolves the same logical manifest as the host, without rewriting the original bytes.
- The final nine-file owner batch passed 48 tests in 45.97 seconds of native test-runner wall time. It covers manifest parsing, capture, lookup, Git transfer, hash memoization, limits and the actual cache producers.
- Broader consumer coverage passed across local projection, transfer, materialization, repository ownership and node clients. Its final 33-file batch passed 388 tests with three explicit platform/opt-in skips; the required existing E2E build took 5m02s, and the test stage including preparation took 641.97 seconds. All three destination-authority cases passed. These unchanged paths were not rerun merely for the final shared-function move.
- Changed-file formatting/lint and all 38 selected compiler graphs passed. Tests preserve ignored reports, explicit staged inputs, genuine empty directories and invalid-result rejection.

The literal-file batches use the existing native test runner; equivalent focused commands include `pnpm test src/gateway/worker-environments/workspace-generated-paths.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` and `pnpm test test/scripts/workspace-test-caches.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (the latter's final Vitest wall time was 1.01 seconds).

Independent review is clean after two corrected findings; the scoped automated review is also clean. Current-head CI passed every selected family except an inherited mock-export ratchet in `test/scripts/ci-node-test-plan.test.ts` and its aggregate status. The identical failure was reproduced on unchanged upstream source; this patch changes none of its causal inputs. ClawSweeper reported no findings, with Gold overall and Platinum patch quality. A containing-runtime guest recheck follows source delivery; no running server was changed by this PR. Initial fixture setup, typing and formatting failures were corrected and retained in the validation record.

prs.title: fix(google): bound realtime PCM sample rate to prevent OOM resample
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Google Live audio MIME types carry a provider-controlled `rate=` parameter. `parsePcmSampleRate` only rejected `rate<=0`, so an out-of-range value like `rate=1` inflated `resamplePcm`'s output buffer by ~24000x (`outputSamples = inputSamples / (inputRate / outputRate)`), causing gigabyte-scale `Buffer.alloc` before any audio was played. Both `toOutputAudio` paths are vulnerable: PCM16 output calls `resamplePcm(pcm, rate, 24000)` directly, and G711 ULAW output calls `convertPcmToMulaw8k` → `resamplePcmTo8k` → `resamplePcm(pcm, rate, 8000)`.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resamplePcm` (`src/talk/audio-codec.ts:175`) computes `outputSamples = Math.floor(inputSamples / (inputSampleRate / outputSampleRate))` and calls `Buffer.alloc(outputSamples * 2)`. With `rate=1` and 24 kHz output, even 20ms of input allocates ~11.5 MB (PCM16 path) or ~3.8 MB (ULAW path).

`parsePcmSampleRate` now accepts only the **Google-documented Live output rate — `24000`** — via a finite allow-list (`GOOGLE_REALTIME_PCM_OUTPUT_RATES_HZ = {24000}`, a `ReadonlySet`). Every other MIME `rate` value (including the previously-accepted 8/16/48 kHz) collapses to 24 kHz, so input/output sample rates always match and the allocating resampler never sees a provider-controlled rate. This is contract-bound to Google's authoritative documentation:

- [Live API — Technical specifications](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/live-api#technical-specifications): output modalities are "raw 16-bit PCM audio, **24kHz**, little-endian".
- [Live API capabilities — Audio formats](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/live-api/capabilities#audio_formats): "**Audio output always uses a sample rate of 24kHz.**" The `rate=` MIME parameter is an *input* (client→model) convention — Google's own example is `audio/pcm;rate=16000`.

## User Impact

Prevents memory exhaustion crashes when the Google Live API returns an audio MIME type with an out-of-range `rate` parameter. It also fixes a wrong-timing path the previous 8–48 kHz range still allowed: a 24 kHz payload tagged `rate=8000` was upsampled 3× (1440 bytes) with incorrect playback timing; it now passes through at 24 kHz. Both PCM16 24kHz and G711 ULAW 8kHz (the default) output formats are protected.

## Evidence

### Exact-head policy — parser + allocation math, both output paths

The accepted set is exactly `{24000}`. For a 480-byte (20ms @ 24kHz) input payload:

```
=== PCM16 24kHz output path (resamplePcm) ===
  rate=1             -> 24000  480 B passthrough  (was ~11520000 B on main — OOM prevented)
  rate=8000          -> 24000  480 B passthrough  (was 3x upsample = 1440 B, wrong timing)
  rate=16000         -> 24000  480 B passthrough  (was 1.5x upsample = 720 B)
  rate=48000         -> 24000  480 B passthrough  (was half-rate downsample = 240 B)
  rate=24000         -> 24000  480 B passthrough  (the only documented output rate)
  rate=999999999     -> 24000  480 B              (was silent drop)
  no rate / empty    -> 24000  480 B

=== G711 ULAW 8kHz output path (convertPcmToMulaw8k → resamplePcm) ===
  rate=24000         -> 24000  80 B mulaw (downsampled 24 kHz → 8 kHz)
  rate=1, 8000, ...  -> 24000  80 B mulaw (bounded; was ~3.84 MB on main for rate=1)
```

### Focused bridge tests (real production path, mocked only at the SDK `connect` boundary)

`extensions/google/realtime-voice-provider.test.ts`:

- **Regression test (fails on the previous head, passes with this fix):** "normalizes undocumented 8/16/48 kHz input-side MIME rate to 24 kHz on PCM16 output" — asserts 480-byte passthrough for `rate=8000/16000/48000`. On the previous head these produced 1440/720/240 bytes.
- **Accepted exact-set test:** "preserves the documented 24000 Hz MIME rate" on both PCM16 (480 B) and G711 ULAW (80 B) output.
- Kept: "normalizes … to 24 kHz to avoid OOM resample" (rate=1, 0, −16000, 4000, 999999999, wideband, whitespace, missing, empty), the G711 normalize cases, and the allocation-bound matrix — now extended to include the previously-accepted `rate=8000/16000/48000`.

**Committed test suite (real production path, mocked only at the SDK `connect` boundary):** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/google/realtime-voice-provider.test.ts` → **85/85 passed** on this head. The regression test "normalizes undocumented 8/16/48 kHz input-side MIME rate to 24 kHz on PCM16 output" (480 B passthrough for `rate=8000/16000/48000`, which produced 1440/720/240 B on the previous head) passes.

**Real bridge receive-to-output trace (this head, real backend bridge):** drove the actual bridge (`buildGoogleRealtimeVoiceProvider().createBridge` → `connect` → `onmessage` → `handleServerContent` → `parsePcmSampleRate` → `toOutputAudio` → `onAudio`) with Google Live-style `inlineData` payloads, real buffer math, mocked only at the SDK `connect` boundary:

```
[trace] PCM16 output — received 480 B at tagged rate -> bridge output:
  undocumented 8 kHz tag       audio/pcm;rate=8000      -> 480 B
  undocumented 16 kHz tag      audio/pcm;rate=16000     -> 480 B
  undocumented 48 kHz tag      audio/pcm;rate=48000     -> 480 B
  malicious rate=1             audio/pcm;rate=1         -> 480 B
  documented 24 kHz            audio/pcm;rate=24000     -> 480 B
[trace] G711 output — received 480 B at rate=16000 -> bridge output: 80 B
```

This is the after-fix receive-to-output trace through the changed backend bridge the review requested: every undocumented/malicious rate collapses to the documented 24 kHz output (480 B passthrough on PCM16, bounded 80 B on G711), with no allocation amplification.

### Live Google Live trace — honest gap

A redacted Google Live receive-to-output trace is **not feasible in this environment**: no `GEMINI_API_KEY`/`GOOGLE_API_KEY` is available here, and I will not fabricate a live call. The reproducible path for anyone holding a key is the repo's own smoke: `scripts/dev/realtime-talk-live-smoke.ts` → `smokeGoogleLiveBrowserWs` mints a one-use constrained Live token and connects to the real Live WebSocket. Run with `GEMINI_API_KEY=... node --import tsx scripts/dev/realtime-talk-live-smoke.ts` (see `docs/providers/google.md`), and record each received `serverContent.modelTurn.parts[].inlineData.mimeType` (parsed rate + output length) to produce the redacted receive-to-output trace.

### CI note

`security-fast` fails on all PRs due to pre-existing dependency advisories (brace-expansion GHSA-rgw5-rvv9-x895, fast-uri GHSA-7p8r-x3mc-p8w7, undici GHSA-4cwx-7wf7-3272) — not introduced by this PR.

prs.title: feat(capability): add private model-run prompt files
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes private one-shot model evaluation prompts being exposed through process arguments and lets local and Gateway model probes request the same bounded generation settings.

## User Impact

POSIX users can pass a private prompt from a mode-`0600`, current-user-owned regular file instead of argv. Local and Gateway probes can request matching maximum-output-token and temperature overrides, and JSON output reports them explicitly as requested overrides rather than provider-resolved settings. Windows is intentionally unsupported for prompt files because this contract depends on POSIX ownership, mode, and no-follow semantics.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI opens prompt files with no-follow semantics, verifies ownership, exact mode, regular-file identity, and a 1 MiB bound, then reads through the opened descriptor. Unsafe, empty, oversized, replaced, or ambiguous prompt input is rejected before local or Gateway execution.

The additive Gateway fields are accepted only for `modelRun=true` and flow into the existing stream-parameter owner. Requests without a generation override omit the new wire field, preserving compatibility with released Gateways whose closed schema predates it. These fields do not expand tools, sessions, persistence, routing, or delivery authority.

## Evidence

Current conflict-reconciled head: `439940d94175e78fdf5a6c4f5b9adb6264825514`, incorporating upstream `56c95abb4ee48f9d0c1176f42d2aecf2e2c32cf8` (2026-10-19 UTC). The approved POSIX-only private-file and requested-overrides contracts are unchanged. CLI conflict repair retains strict input validation and shares current upstream invalid-option cases with the existing model-run regression module. Gateway repair preserves upstream plugin-subagent policy and the new execution-identity admission owner; the extracted source-context helper now performs only source routing, without a competing admission-fact writer. Token comparison against upstream after inlining the helper confirms the execution owner differs only by requested stream parameters.

- Current-head focused Node 24 tests: Gateway handler, execution-owner and lineage suites **442 passed**; protocol **18 passed**; CLI **115 passed / 1 Windows-only skip**.
- Formatting, overlap-path lint, line-cap ratchet, core production types, and feature-relative `git diff --check`: passed.
- Fresh independent feature-scoped P0–P2 review: scoped-clean; no actionable findings. This was supplied-patch-only review, not execution of integration behavior.
- The blank/whitespace-temperature regression was fixed on parent `9b0a944dc5c54ffb4959565b02efb7c7da754b98`: both new cases failed before the fix, then the full CLI file passed **99 / 1 Windows-only skip**. Explicit temperature `0` remains valid. The current CLI suite above includes those regressions.
- Parent `8e76baa81ae7c1b21743d0287dab883e4278ac42` hosted CI passed (verified 2026-10-19 before this reconciliation). Current-head CI was still running at 2026-10-19 03:43 UTC and is not green: [Control UI performance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39195698050/job/117878190467) failed its chat-boot gzip ceiling (1,491,895 B versus 1,490,000 B). The same job built its pinned base and reports identical base/candidate chat-boot bytes (+0 B); no performance repair or green-CI claim is made. Automatic review has not yet refreshed the durable review for this head; older results are historical, not current-head broad proof.
- Earlier broad local guard failures were established only against their then-pinned upstream baseline; they are not asserted as current-base failures. Broad repository checks remain new-head PR CI's responsibility.

Historical after-fix runtime proof on `e19b112412d13a70a76530833e163cb6e96e4687` (not rerun on the conflict-reconciled head), 2026-09-14 02:43–02:48 UTC, Node 24.20.0, synthetic prompt and an isolated loopback OpenAI-compatible responder:

prs.title: perf(sessions): skip snapshots for closed transcript reads
prs.body:
Through-anchor validation and standalone transcript-watermark reads each issue one SELECT, but the shared anchor reader wraps them in an additional BEGIN/COMMIT. Use the statement's own snapshot for exactly these two closed selections. Any additional selection key keeps the existing compound-read snapshot, including an explicitly undefined extra option.

The through-anchor query still checks active identity, projection readiness, rewrite generation, lifecycle, and permission authority together. Admission-backed reads, combined selections, and existing caller transactions keep their current custody. No SQL text, schema, write ordering, worker requests, or public API changes. The accepted conservative edge is that equivalent selections with extra unused keys retain the transaction.

The focused regressions count actual native statements, verify compound reads retain their envelope, and exercise a subsequent committed append, rewrite, lifecycle change, and permission change. Both new single-statement cases failed on the baseline with exactly BEGIN and COMMIT around one SELECT.

Validation: 30 tests passed across the anchor-reader and context-reader worker suites using the pinned Bun runtime. Both new regressions failed on the baseline for the expected envelope overhead. Formatting, type-aware core lint, diff checks, and one independent Codex P0–P2 review passed. Remaining static gates, PostgreSQL review, and live measurements are in progress.

Deterministic operation delta: 3 → 1 SQL for each eligible standalone read; requests and MAIN-thread placement are unchanged. The current workload census predicts six fewer statements across its three eligible calls; this is an estimate until the alternating harness runs finish. No warmed-turn saving is claimed yet.

Production: +8/-1 lines (net +7); tests: +106/-0. The small selection predicate removes the redundant transaction work while preserving the shared reader and all compound snapshot paths.

prs.title: fix(subagents): restore owner-started fleets after Gateway restarts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A Gateway restart (update, crash, `kill -9`) silently orphaned every in-flight sub-agent fleet started by the Gateway owner. Owner turns started through `openclaw agent` or `chat.send` on a shared-token Gateway, the default single-user setup, recorded no restart evidence. After restart, recovery logged:

```
[agents/subagents] subagent completion authority was not restored ... "Subagent restart recovery lacks its original operator source"
[agents/subagent-registry] requester settle wake failed ... "Subagent completion authority is no longer active"
```

The parent never woke, the children's committed work was stranded, and nothing user-visible reported it. Reproduced live on an isolated Linux Gateway (real OpenAI key, Codex app-server runtime) with flat 8-child fan-outs and nested lead→worker fleets.

## User Impact

Sub-agent fleets started by the Gateway owner now resume after a Gateway restart, and children spawned by a recovered parent keep running. No new configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Root cause

1. Admission: shared-token/password owner sockets are deliberately unprofiled (`connect-session.ts`), and `captureGatewayOperatorRunAuthority` (`src/gateway/operator-run-authority.ts`) required the owner profile before capturing run authority, so no `operatorRecoverySource` was stored for their children (#173873 requires saved evidence and never substitutes system authority).
2. With evidence present, a second defect showed up in the same live test: the authority restored for a recovered requester wake was tied to the original completion row's guard. When that row settled, revalidation revoked every child the recovered wake had spawned (`Restart recovery operator authority changed; start a new user turn.` one second after the wake yielded). This also affects profile-backed operators restored by #173873.

### Fix

- Recognize the handshake-attested shared-token/password owner (system actor, no user profile, shared Gateway auth with a current generation, token or password method) as the authenticated owner for run-authority capture, so the existing bounded snapshot/restore owner records and revalidates its evidence. Recovery still requires the same shared auth generation and method: rotating the credential or changing the auth mode refuses the old continuation. Nested requesters inherit the admitted owner's evidence and cannot widen its scope ceiling. No new stored format, config, restoration path, or system fallback.
- The restoration adapter (`subagent-registry-gateway-owner.ts`) retains the Gateway/database/lifecycle guard for descendants while enforcing exact row custody during preparation and binding; existing reference counting and policy revocation own the lifetime. Descendants of a recovered wake now survive its settlement; token rotation still revokes them.
- `docs/tools/subagents/operations.md` documents owner evidence and descendant lifetime.

## Evidence

- Live (isolated Gateway on this branch, shared token, `openclaw agent` CLI, Codex app-server runtime): 8-child fleet, Gateway `kill -9` while the children ran, restart. The parent woke, re-dispatched one replacement per interrupted child (one reused a commit the interrupted child left), merged all 8, `npm test` 35/35, and zero authority errors. On main the same test orphans the fleet. The normal path (CLI disconnects right after the parent yields) still completes.
- Focused: owner regressions fail on main (`expected restart requester source to be defined`) and the descendant-lifetime regression fails on the first commit (`Subagent recovery completion owner changed`); with the fix `subagent-registry.completion-authority.test.ts` 85/85 and `operator-run-recovery.test.ts` 34/34, including narrowed scopes, nested password owners, and refusal after token rotation.
- Targeted type-aware lint/typecheck, formatting, and independent review are clean.

## Known gaps (not changed here)

Channel-originated requesters (`captureChannelOperatorRunAuthority` creates no recovery snapshot) and isolated cron jobs without `job.operatorSource` still cannot restore their sub-agent completions after a restart.

## Release note context

Fix: sub-agent fleets started by the Gateway owner (CLI or shared-token clients) now resume after a Gateway restart instead of being silently orphaned; children spawned by a recovered parent keep running.

## Landing validation

Merged `origin/main` at `c1483e015fb618433fc17509f488945c7af81cb5` to resolve a real conflict in requester fixture setup. The resolution preserves both the nested-owner spawn depth and main's unrelated requester-claim regression; production edits merged cleanly. Published head: `0fe0bc766993f35f6f63a857099d2ca10cbef12f`.

On that candidate, formatting, lint, and whitespace checks passed. The focused suites passed: `operator-run-recovery.test.ts` 35/35 and `subagent-registry.completion-authority.test.ts` 90/90. Independent P0–P2 review of the four-file candidate reported no actionable findings. The coordinator's live proof above is retained; the lander did not rerun the live scenario. Exact-head CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39195224521.

### Inherited CI failure

CI run `39195224521`, attempt 1, passed every job except `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` and its aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate`. The failing check is `mock-exports`: `test/scripts/ci-node-test-plan.test.ts:3297` mocks `../../scripts/lib/ci-test-timings.mts` without real-module pass-through or an isolation annotation. This PR changes neither file. Security, types, lint, SDK checks, and all test jobs passed.

The automated table called this new because its scheduled-main comparison passed without matching the selected scope. Direct attribution supersedes that coarse comparison: the exact CI main base `45fddcfe1fae0b99606d59409bc2fd69447896e7` fails `pnpm check:test-mock-exports --base 45fddcfe1fae0b99606d59409bc2fd69447896e7 --no-merge-base` with the identical file, line, and error. The test, mocked module, checker, scan helpers, and baseline are byte-identical between that main base and the tested merge `b1656e96e727bc3286bad2bf3e8e8994d2271e5b`. Landing uses the repository owner's pre-authorized native inherited-failure exception; the failed CI is not represented as green.
