prs.title: fix(voice-call): long replies never play and the caller hears silence
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A long reply is synthesized as one request. `playTtsViaStream` hands the complete reply to `synthesizeForTelephony(text)` and races it against `synthesisTimeoutMs`, a fixed value (default 8000ms) that does not scale with text length. Playback is all-or-nothing: not one speech frame is sent until the whole buffer exists. So when a long reply loses that race, the turn fails **before a single speech frame is sent** and the caller hears nothing at all. The longer and more useful the answer, the more reliably it is lost.

## Why This Change Was Made

Splitting belongs inside the existing serialized Twilio playback owner, not beside it. Speech directives are resolved once, up front, over the complete reply; the resolved spoken text is then split into bounded segments and played back-to-back through the same queue slot, so ordered playback, barge-in and a single final mark per turn all still hold. Resolving before splitting means a split can never divide an inline directive block, and one resolved override set applies to every segment.

Segment length is capped by `MAX_TELEPHONY_TTS_SYNTH_CHARS = 320`, chosen so each synthesis request stays far inside the timeout that the whole-reply path was losing. It is a bounded internal of the stream synthesis path, not a new configuration surface: the limit exists to keep one request inside the provider synthesis timeout, which is not a property an operator is positioned to tune per call.

The playback body moves out of `providers/twilio.ts` into `providers/twilio/stream-tts-playback.ts`, which leaves the capped file **smaller** than before (831 to 742 lines).

### This revision was re-expressed against current main, not rebased

The previous head was based roughly 25,800 commits behind main and conflicted. Upstream had restructured `providers/twilio.ts` across ten commits — four "deslop" passes plus `refactor: simplify runtime adapters and remove obsolete code` — so this revision is **not** a replay of the old diff. It is the same intent re-applied to upstream's current shape, and re-scoped against what upstream now ships:

- **Dropped as already dead upstream.** The old head reintroduced a `chunkDelivered !== chunkAttempts` / `"incomplete audio delivery"` guard. Upstream deleted that in `398a85faeb6` because it was provably unreachable — the counter was incremented unconditionally right after the send-success check. It is not reintroduced here, and no test referenced it.
- **Dropped as out of scope.** The old head also added `webhook/auto-response-speech.ts` carrying duplicate-suppression for the auto-response turn. That is a separate defect on a different path, the module does not exist upstream, and it collides with #136847 which also creates it. This PR is now the playback fix only; the duplicate-suppression change belongs in its own PR.
- **Checked and deliberately not duplicated.** Upstream's newer adjacent machinery does not cover this symptom. `webhook/realtime-audio-pacer.ts` has exactly one non-test importer, `webhook/realtime-handler.ts` — the Realtime transport, a different path — and it paces frames it is handed rather than bounding a synthesis request. `MAX_PENDING_TTS_OPERATIONS_PER_STREAM` bounds how many playbacks a stream may queue, which is orthogonal, since this fix uses one queue slot per turn. Core `src/tts/tts-telephony.ts` passes `text` straight through with no length bound. `providers/twilio.ts` on current main still calls `ttsProvider.synthesizeForTelephony(text)` with the complete reply.

## User Impact

Long replies play. Previously the most substantial answers were exactly the ones that silently failed, and the caller heard nothing at all for that turn.

Short replies are unchanged. Text at or under the cap is returned as a single segment, so it remains one synthesis request ending in one completion mark.

## Evidence

### Baseline: the defect, captured

Neutralising only the new bound — `MAX_TELEPHONY_TTS_SYNTH_CHARS = 320` to `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`, which reproduces the whole-reply path exactly — fails six of the new tests:

```
× twilio.tts-segments.test.ts > synthesizes every segment in order and sends one completion mark
  -> expected 1 to be greater than 1
× twilio.tts-segments.test.ts > clears buffered audio when a later segment fails to synthesize
  -> expected 'resolved' to be 'rejected'
× twilio.tts-segments.test.ts > never interleaves keep-alive silence with a segment's speech frames
  -> expected 1 to be greater than 1
× twilio.tts-segments.test.ts > cancels every remaining segment when a barge-in aborts playback
  -> expected 1 to be greater than 1
× telephony-tts-segments.test.ts > resolves inline TTS directives once for the whole reply, not per segment
  -> expected 1 to be greater than 1
× telephony-tts-segments.test.ts > splits the resolved spoken text, so a directive block is never divided
  -> expected 1 to be greater than 1
```

Read honestly: four of those six are the structural precondition `expect(chunkTelephonyReply(text, CAP).length).toBeGreaterThan(1)`, i.e. an 813-character reply collapsing to **one** synthesis request. That is the defect stated directly, but it is a structural observation rather than a timing one. The substantive failure is `expected 'resolved' to be 'rejected'`: without the bound, a synthesis timeout part-way through a reply resolves as though playback had succeeded.

The guard was restored from a backup taken before editing, and `grep` afterwards confirms no neutralisation survives in any changed file.

### Shipped upstream coverage is preserved, not replaced

Every case in `providers/twilio.media-stream.test.ts` drives a short text — `"Timeout me"`, `"Dropped audio"`, `"Empty audio"`, `"hello"`, `"first"`/`"second"`, `"cancel me"`/`"play next"` — each of which is a single segment under the cap. So `expect(f.synthesize).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` and `.toEqual(["first", "second"])` still hold unchanged. No shipped assertion was deleted or weakened; the only edits to that file are two additive `prepareSpeech` stubs on existing fakes.

### Gates, on this exact head

| Gate | Result |
| ---- | ------ |
| `oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/voice-call/src` | `All matched files use the correct format.` |
| `oxlint extensions/voice-call/src` | `Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.` |
| `check:max-lines-ratchet --base upstream/main` | `max-lines ratchet OK: 702 grandfathered suppressions.` |
| `check:assertion-safety --base upstream/main` | `assertion SAFETY ratchet OK: 3206 files, 8257 grandfathered assertions.` |
| `vitest run` on the 8 affected files | `Test Files 8 passed (8)` / `Tests 62 passed (62)` |

The line-cap ratchet's bundled env-var budget step reported `OPENCLAW_* count 476/476` here, so it was not the binding check.

The one new type assertion in the diff (`mediaStreamHandler as never` on a test fake) carries a `// SAFETY:` comment, which is why the assertion ratchet stays at its baseline.

### Pre-existing failures, separated

Running the wider `extensions/voice-call` sweep surfaces two failures in files this PR does not touch. Both reproduce identically on clean `upstream/main`:

```
× index.test.ts > voice-call plugin > registers Twilio configs with SecretRef auth tokens
× index.lifecycle.test.ts > rejects retained concrete and cold-registry A tools once B activates
  -> expected '""' to contain 'superseded'
```

### What is NOT covered by real-behaviour evidence

Stated plainly rather than papered over:

- **There is no telephony capture at this head.** The previous revision of this body carried a real Twilio trace, but it was produced by a build of the pre-port code. Presenting it as proof of this revision would be false provenance, so it has been removed rather than reused. Nothing in this revision has run against a live call.
- **The timing premise is not measured here.** That a long reply actually exceeds a given provider's synthesis timeout depends on that provider. What this PR demonstrates is the structural property that makes it fatal when it happens: one unbounded request per reply, a fixed timeout, and no audio emitted until that request completes.
- **The whole-directory suite was not run to completion locally.** The run was cut by a local time budget. The eight affected files are green, and the two pre-existing failures above were isolated individually against clean main.

I can add diagnostics behind a temporary tag, capture a redacted exact-head trace, and strip them before merge if that would settle it.

prs.title: fix: skills appear ready when a PATH directory matches a required binary
prs.body:
Closes #146187

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: skills appear ready and are offered to the agent when `PATH` contains a directory named like a required binary, even though that program is not installed.

## User Impact

Skills and hooks now report the missing binary instead of failing later during use. Executable files in later `PATH` entries remain discoverable. No configuration or persisted-state changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

An executable-access check also succeeds for searchable directories. Both the synchronous and prepared binary probes now require a regular file, following symlinks. The asynchronous file check stays inside the existing shared pending probe, preserving bounded I/O and caller-specific cancellation.

This continues the prior unmerged repair #146188 by @masatohoshino, who also supplied the original report. That PR was closed by its author on October 18; current main remains affected, and a fresh search found no open replacement. The adjacent #162664 addresses working-directory cache identity, a separate issue.

prs.body:
## Problem and solution

The chat composer retained duplicate reactive subscriptions, DOM discovery, and imperative event registration after its Solid 2 migration. Use existing owner projections, live-value bindings, scroll-state handling, and timer/observer primitives, with explicit textarea, picker, mention, and transcript refs. Directly coupled New Session and custodian callers share those refs.

Preserve draft persistence, IME composition, native undo history, focus, menu node retention, and loading/empty transcript sizing. The native input subtree retains an intentional initial snapshot. Nested invocation-menu dismissal bubbles to the composer, queue focus returns after the action settles, and goal clocks sample current time on resume. Main's closed-picker laziness is retained on both plus-menu presentation memos. No new dependencies, tags, classes, routes, or lazy boundaries.

## Wave-zero measurements

Production composer/command/picker families, excluding test-support modules. The already-landed dictation platform-listener change is outside this diff.

| Pattern | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Controller lifecycle patterns | 0 | 0 |
| `createEffect` | 11 | 3 (73% fewer) |
| `createRenderEffect` | 2 | 0 |
| `untrack` | 15 | 3 |
| `addEventListener` syntax | 8 | 2 non-DOM Gateway subscriptions |
| `querySelector(All)` | 13 | 0 |
| Production `flush` / manual Solid owners | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |

Survivors under `ui/src/pages/chat/components/`: effects at `chat-composer.tsx:124` (dictation/catalog/prediction owner reconciliation), `chat-composer-question.tsx:83` (question takeover and interrupted IME draft), and `chat-composer-plus-menu.tsx:568` (open capability-owner loading). Initial snapshots at `chat-composer.tsx:30,62` retain pane identity and dictation initialization; `chat-composer-regions.tsx:34` retains the native input subtree. Paired Gateway frame subscriptions remain at `ui/src/pages/chat/composer-dictation-session.ts:106,362`. No owned-DOM listeners or queries remain in scope.

## Proof

Current head `4945183aa59d728f17386ce8aaa6a80e06936d70`, actual merge base `86fd44f6923617cb1435572d720cbfd4673ce90c`. Both builds use the same machine and Node 24.22.0 with compile/build caches disabled. Both strict checks fail the existing Chat and New Session gzip ceilings on base and head; no budget or bundler-policy change.

| Performance | Base | Head |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Startup JS gzip | 337,734 B | 337,734 B |
| Startup CSS requests / bytes | 1 / 38,500 B | 1 / 38,500 B |
| Chat boot JS | 1,492,598 B | 1,492,591 B |
| New Session boot JS | 1,050,500 B | 1,050,573 B |

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm tsgo:ui` | Passed with default tsrs; no override |
| Production builds | Passed on current base and head |
| Strict performance | Same existing Chat/New Session ceiling failures on both revisions |
| Production Knip | Passed on current rebased head, no findings or new ignores |
| Final scoped menu-retention test | All 5 cases passed after retaining main's lazy memos |
| Scoped lint, formatting, diff check | Passed |
| Independent autoreview | Full production delta and all three final test repairs clean through P2; all eleven commits replayed unchanged onto current base |
| Earlier focused behavior proof | Composer/sizing/comment-pin 22 passed; picker lifecycle 10; goal 10; targeted creation-owner and keyboard-scroll cases passed |
| Built-UI native input reproduction | Red before snapshot repair, green after repair |
| Current broad proof | [CI 39194410657](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39194410657): every UI unit/E2E, browser-extension, and real-Gateway job passed; overall failure only from the inherited checks below |

The preceding CI run exposed an unreliable scroll-test setup. An 8px raw offset remained inside the transcript's end-follow threshold; assuming a subsequent 100px wheel moved exactly 100px also ignored virtualizer geometry adjustments. The repaired probe first moves 200px into the transcript so a small virtualizer shrink cannot make its saved offset unreachable. It then samples settled geometry, moves farther with real wheel input, samples the full settled movement, returns to the **exact original offset**, and waits for final scroll idle before collecting the unchanged composer render-budget assertions. All six runtime-budget cases passed on the final head.

The managed-media capture also exposed a readiness gap: terminal run ownership retires before its final history refresh finishes. The existing pane adapter now waits for run/stream retirement and history loading to finish before decoding and capturing. Image counts, order, bounds, and node-identity assertions remain unchanged. This removes a demonstrated missing boundary; the earlier logs do not establish which media update replaced the images. The managed-media case passed on the final head.

The last CI run also exposed two stale Models-help expectations after main shortened the existing English copy. Update those two expected strings only; accessibility, pointer, keyboard, and narrow-layout assertions remain intact. The final head passes this E2E file.

An earlier local 22-case invocation stalled in an external-SSD filesystem rename before any assertion verdict and was stopped; it is not claimed as a pass. Full CI covers those files. The interim rebase also exposed main's missing sidebar export; main's fix #176799 is now incorporated, and current typecheck/builds pass.

Changed production files: **12,007 → 12,118 lines (+111)**. Changed tests: **9,566 → 9,624 (+58)**. **43 files, 722 insertions / 553 deletions.** Growth comes from explicit owned refs and JSX event wiring across consumers, plus small existing-primitive interfaces. This is an existing Solid refactor; a Lit codemod does not apply.

## Summary

Fixes the native Workboard/task lifecycle split described in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/118669.

The Workboard `subagent_ended` integration now reconciles only the currently running card whose persisted card and execution `runId` exactly match the terminal event. ## Guardrails

- Late, duplicate, stale-run, already-terminal, and newly redispatched-card events are no-ops.
- Existing explicit Workboard terminal actions remain authoritative.
- Managed-worktree cleanup remains intact after reconciliation.
- No polling, lease-expiry compensation, config, public API, or changelog changes.

prs.title: fix: let completion replies send photos and attachments
prs.body:
Fixes #176144

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: completion and settle replies reject requested photos and files, leaving the agent to send plain text or raw image markup instead.

## User Impact

Completion replies can send `media` and `attachments`, with or without text or a `caption`, plus normal filename/MIME metadata, to the current conversation. `MEDIA:` directives and remote Markdown images follow normal outbound delivery. Local files still require the normal allowed media roots; local Markdown paths remain literal text. Channel, account, destination, thread, and the `send` action remain locked. Explicit `replyTo` stays limited to the current message or thread; inline reply and audio directives remain restricted. No new config, SDK, or schema changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The execution allowlist continued to reject media after #175309 exposed the full stable message schema to completion turns. Permit media content and remove duplicate completion-only text validation. The existing outbound sender remains the sole owner of text-or-media validation and media access, without a new resolver or broader roots. Caption fallback validation preserves Markdown indentation so existing reply/audio restrictions still apply. Source policy checks reply/audio tags with the sender’s inline parser before media extraction, so media URLs cannot hide a directive that would later change the reply target.

The normal outbound preparation owner also canonicalizes the advertised `mimeType` alias to `contentType` before its explicit-media early return. This preserves MIME metadata for both ordinary and completion sends, using the existing contentType-first reader and preserving buffer validation behavior.

Product decision from Peter: “Allow media, keep target lock (Recommended)”. The completion-source tests move into a focused sibling suite because the existing test file cannot grow under the line-cap ratchet.

Fact/lifetime audit: this change captures no new state or deferred effects. Existing turn/session authority and binding checks remain at awaited preparation and the outbound handoff. Channel/account/target/thread identity and config remain the admitted send’s existing inputs; media paths, roots, and limits are resolved and enforced by normal outbound owners.

## Evidence

- `delivers completion media and attachments to the current source through normal sends` exercises the real message tool/action runner through a synthetic transport: remote media, media-only attachments, captions, filename/MIME metadata, `MEDIA:`, remote Markdown images, same-thread replies, and successful source completion.
- `applies normal local media roots and empty-send validation to completion replies` uses the shared media loader and requires the allowed-directory error, failed delivery, no source completion, and no platform send. Existing retargeting, non-send, and reply/audio refusal cases also carry media and metadata. The denial table additionally covers `reply directive inside a media-only URL`, `reply directive inside a media caption`, and `audio directive inside a media URL`, requiring rejection before secrets or dispatch.
- The existing outbound `dedupes resolved media while retaining first-entry metadata (%j)` regression covers MIME-alias preservation and `contentType` precedence, asserting both canonical send metadata and attachment payload metadata.
- PR CI is the test gate and covers the regressions, existing consumers, prompt-prefix stability, types, and broader checks selected by CI. Local tests, negative controls, typechecks, and live Gateway/Crabbox/Testbox proof were intentionally skipped per maintainer policy. No leases were created; local test wall time is not applicable.
- Changed-file oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` pass. Independent Codex autoreview in branch mode through P2 is scoped-clean, including the shared MIME-normalization correction and the inline-directive routing repair.
- Simplification removes duplicate completion-only content validation. Exact numstat totals: production +20/−11 (net +9), tests +333/−132 (net +201), docs +19/−0. Necessary growth covers three metadata allowlist entries, caption fallback validation, and four lines reusing the normal MIME reader. No parallel parser, resolver, or sender was added.

Current main at `b791dd0664e58c5f0c3776ee333b7be4bf8b524f` was fetched successfully and merged without conflicts. It includes the earlier UI and Codex test-type fixes and repairs the mock-export ratchet by preserving the real `ci-test-timings` module exports. The PR patch is unchanged by this merge; the only overlap is main’s independent requester documentation update. Changed-file oxlint/oxfmt and whitespace checks pass; the existing full-branch P2 autoreview covers the unchanged patch.

The completion fixture uses module spies after main retired private injection hooks, retaining the real outbound runner for media delivery/access-policy cases and restoring spies after every test.

[CI run 39196007075](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39196007075) is running for `618d52d5bdbd23acad113bc4aa3ac35a5a05e9a1`. ClawSweeper review of this head is pending. After CI completes successfully or with only proven inherited failures, one re-review request will be posted if no completed review or request already exists for this head, with a 90-minute review wait. PR CI is the proof gate per maintainer policy; live-proof-only review requests are intentionally not followed.

prs.title: perf(sessions): skip diff baseline scans without matching paths
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening an uncommitted session diff repeats checkout discovery and file inventory even when none of its changed paths can match the session's starting baseline.

## User Impact

Session diffs need fewer Git processes while preserving patches, counts, baseline filtering, and fresh filesystem reads. There are no new configuration options, caches, or schema changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Skip baseline preparation when no returned path can match. Let Git's merge-base resolve fallback branch names directly instead of resolving each name in a separate process first. Runtime code is 7 additions / 15 deletions (net −8 lines); the larger addition is a repeatable, synthetic Gateway benchmark.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule, recorded before measurement: compare identical synthetic tool-heavy history and 32 tracked/32 untracked checkout fixtures through real Gateway RPCs. Use concurrent baseline/candidate pairs with swapped 16-core halves and an exclusive measurement lock. Report within-pair candidate-minus-baseline p50/p95/p99, bytes, Gateway CPU, and worker queue/service diagnostics. Accept this production simplification if response behavior is preserved and no regression exceeds noise; investigate any metric worsening by 20% or more.

### Paired measurements

A is `d6ec4c7de8919a1711d0a87798776e1fd5264d97`; B is the same source plus only this PR’s two runtime-file changes. Both builds use identical dependencies and the committed driver. The final branch is rebased onto newer main and covered by exact-head CI; the A/B builds keep unrelated source identical.

Two concurrent pairs per scenario on a 128-core Linux host, using CPUs 96–111/112–127 and then swapping. An exclusive lock covers the pairs. Four clients × 50 cohorts gives 200 RPC samples per side per pair (4,000 RPCs total), with independent identical fixtures, synchronized start barriers, and per-pair `mpstat -P 96-127` records. All 20 runs passed response checks. A/B cells below are the mean of two per-run quantiles, not pooled quantiles; the decision uses the within-pair B−A differences.

| Scenario | A p50 / p95 / p99 (ms) | B p50 / p95 / p99 (ms) | Δp50, pairs 1 / 2 (ms) | Δp99, pairs 1 / 2 (ms) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| history-small | 5.38 / 9.83 / 75.69 | 5.27 / 9.36 / 75.88 | +0.00 / -0.21 | -114.73 / +115.11 |
| history-default | 25.08 / 46.71 / 183.96 | 24.39 / 46.11 / 123.46 | -0.70 / -0.68 | -128.25 / +7.26 |
| history-large | 30.59 / 52.99 / 77.32 | 30.89 / 55.68 / 125.07 | +0.10 / +0.51 | +99.09 / -3.58 |
| diff-all-full | 184.56 / 233.93 / 267.07 | 171.93 / 230.39 / 241.74 | -5.05 / -20.21 | -18.94 / -31.72 |
| diff-uncommitted-full | 235.82 / 274.32 / 343.40 | 208.37 / 244.16 / 250.44 | -25.52 / -29.37 | -141.41 / -44.51 |

| Scenario | Main CPU ms/RPC, A → B | Gateway process CPU ms/RPC, A → B | Payload bytes, both |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| history-small | 1.47 → 1.45 | 8.41 → 8.80 | 32,116 |
| history-default | 2.25 → 2.30 | 34.98 → 35.30 | 495,840 |
| history-large | 2.49 → 2.50 | 40.26 → 40.28 | 633,794 |
| diff-all-full | 7.07 → 6.72 | 11.78 → 11.18 | 107,366 |
| diff-uncommitted-full | 8.09 → 7.06 | 13.49 → 12.05 | 107,366 |

Both diff scopes improve in both CPU assignments. Uncommitted p50 improves 11.6% and p99 27.1%; all-scope p50 improves 6.8% and p99 9.5%. Response sizes and file counts are unchanged.

Representative invocation, repeated for each scenario and both built entries:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/history-diff-measure.ts \
  --state-dir /path/to/synthetic-fixture --entry dist/entry.js \
  --port 41443 --clients 4 --operations 50 --rounds 1 \
  --scenario diff-uncommitted-full --start-at <shared-epoch-ms>
```

### Attribution and limits

Diff latency is service time rather than queueing: Git-worker queue p99 is 0.08–0.19 ms and transfer p99 is below 0.05 ms, versus service tails of 186–451 ms. The existing in-flight owner reduced each 200-RPC block to 50 Git-worker tasks. The remaining expensive work includes one Git process per untracked file; clean-filter, encoding, and safety contracts are retained.

History already returns worker-encoded pages through `SerializedJsonArray`. Its queue and service costs rise with page size: transcript-worker queue p99 is about 2 ms for small pages, 20–21 ms for default pages, and 25–28 ms for larger pages; transfer p99 stays below 0.07 ms. Main CPU stays around 1.4–2.5 ms/RPC. The large request allows a 2 MiB budget but the actual projected payload is 634 KB.

The history controls retain an important caveat. Every >100 ms sample occurs in the first two concurrent cohorts, consistent with starting burst readers after one-client warmup. Large-page headline p99 worsens by 47.8 ms, triggering the prewritten investigation rule: pair 1 has three such early samples on B versus two on A; pair 2 improves. As a separately labeled, post-hoc attribution check, p99 after the first eight requests averages 56.6 → 58.2 ms, while process CPU is 40.26 → 40.28 ms/RPC and initial maxima are similar. All headline samples remain in the table. No history speedup is claimed; the control variation is concentrated in startup rather than steady projection or re-encoding.

The fixture has 5,000 sessions, 6,000 retained runs, 200 approvals, 100 cron jobs, and 12 projects. The agent database is about 235 MB; the seeded tool-heavy session contains 256 messages and 7,061,504 text bytes. This preserves the multi-session shape without reproducing multi-GB page-cache pressure. Four simultaneous clients and this checkout do not reproduce every production workload, rename-heavy repository, or huge diff. These results do not establish that the reported production tails have disappeared.

The benchmark excludes summary-only diffs because their existing 10-second cache would mostly measure cached throughput. Full diff scenarios exercise the changed path. Single-client warmup is recorded separately; concurrent cohorts can still start burst workers. Gateway process CPU excludes Git child-process CPU.

The real-Git regression fails on base: empty and nonoverlapping baselines each use 9 observed Git launches instead of at most 6. The fixed path passes. All 47 focused tests pass:

A narrowed run of the same scanner and baseline ledger on the benchmark host rejects the identical factory on this head and unchanged main parent `b34a4659de9c36a34e1f3ed8399dd9c357214509`. Both source files have SHA-256 `6cda11e587cab0fec4eedddb37789ae6c2817ef11e45141890db297158c514f0`; both report factory fingerprint `d8043912b7f8c4f23cfc00dcb5dd8811e97fee3994157e5484d3b46e45f8a836`. prs.title: refactor(ui): remove unselected private options and unread projections
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Private UI helpers expose modes, collaborators and return projections that no production caller selects or reads. They obscure the actual owners without providing a user-facing option.

## User Impact

No visible design or supported behavior change is intended. Gateway protocol, configuration, SDK exports, persisted data and user-facing text remain unchanged. Phase E standalone session memory is untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing native WebSocket, fetch, location, clock and overlay owners directly. Tabs retain their actual controlled, horizontal contract. Remove unused wizard cancellation alternatives, composer slots, widget forwarding, sidebar summary insertion, scroll options and duplicate dock width policy. Drop unread acknowledgment timing, activity refresh and reconciliation result projections, retaining the underlying Gateway facts and real admission/confirmation decisions.

This is the UI-area split of a private-option family spanning more than 80 files. Against conflict-repair base 4317598f2fb1ec0ff3e7dc25ffb3be02d0261962, the signed replacement head changes 46 paths: 129 net production lines removed and one net test line added. Main independently removed the activity-envelope family; it is not counted here. The desktop collaborator cut already landed independently and is also excluded.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Tabs no longer offer local selection or vertical keyboard behavior: every production caller uses controlled horizontal tabs. Current manual focus, reorder, activation and controlled rejection remain; future callers must establish an explicit different contract.
- Native overlay focus/hide and wizard cancellation use the existing direct operations. No caller supplies the deleted callbacks or requests the removed settle-without-abort mode. Real focus, occlusion, cancellation and request cleanup remain.
- Unread private acknowledgment timing and row-confirmation projections disappear; raw Gateway responses, shared row facts and confirmation decisions remain.
- Composer slots, sidebar summary and widget revision/latest overrides had no production producers. Native browser cards still support their real revision/latest contract, and no live markup is removed.
- Dock sizing uses its canonical layout.maxWidth owner. Real minimum width, viewport bounds and persistence remain; only an unused second cap disappears.
- Private long-date formatting and test-only fetch/location/clock/socket overrides disappear. Actual URL/opener checks, avatar/theme size limits, redirect refusal, deadlines and abort behavior remain. No human-incident safeguard, dormant feature foundation or security boundary is removed.

## Evidence

The latest two-file CI repair removes only the obsolete defaultActive shadow-style table case, retains items/controlled-active movement and final-consumer cleanup assertions, supplies the required active prop to unrelated style fixtures, and shrinks the chat-send-ack assertion allowance from two to one. No production code changed. The focused shadow-styles/tabs/hub-tabs selection passed 12/12 across three files (20.70 seconds engine/51.43 seconds wrapper). Targeted native UI types, scoped lint, the assertion ratchet, 14/14 suppression cases and whitespace passed. Fresh independent review of this exact delta completed scoped-clean through P2 with no actionable findings. Replacement-head hosted CI is pending, not claimed green.

The preceding exact 7be head's completed broad run 39192420658 tested merge 2c36cef54559f6ae24a776f09cf829a4490c705a, ordered parents main d694fe8c09ffa672ed1d144210730fc8dfd9f18e and PR 7be7c8cafa0f1a4f95ab6f0174ba3cb9b8ad163c. Every failed root job was inspected:

| Failed job | Attribution and disposition |
| --- | --- |
| checks-ui (1/2), 117868218445 | Ours: obsolete defaultActive fixture; repaired above without changing kept assertions. |
| check-test-types-core-2, 117868702688 | Ours: the same fixture's required active/retired defaultActive props; repaired above. |
| ratchets, 117868218511 | Ours: shrink-only chat-send-ack assertion baseline; repaired above. |
| Control UI performance, 117868218499 | Baseline absolute chat cap already exceeded: head 1,491,030 bytes vs base 1,491,409 (-379 bytes), both over 1,490,000. Scheduled main 39186683798/job 117850678777 has the same ceiling failure. Budget unchanged. |
| check-test-types-extensions, 117868702523 | Untouched Codex parent-retention.test.ts:37 still supplies completionDeliveryRetryDelaysMs retired by main #173768; same failure in that PR's run 39191174751. |
| bundled UI E2E (2/7), 117868218543 | Models-help test expects the old English thinking-help wording; actual main parent is #173768, which changed it. Test and catalog are byte-identical main/tested merge. |
| bundled UI E2E (5/7), 117868218610 | Two session-list-filter exact-query assertions reject ifRowsRevision: empty string; identical scheduled-main 39186683798/job 117850679097 signatures. |
| bundled UI E2E (7/7), 117868218612 | Pasted-text line 1280 retains only Keep this draft; identical scheduled-main 39176649118/job 117820740755 signature. |

Real-Gateway UI E2E (2/2) passed 63/63 in 28 files. The coordinator flake ledger and last six completed scheduled main runs were checked (39186683798, 39183785855, 39176649118, 39172446197, 39168070659, 39163574553); exact baseline logs and unchanged-source comparisons supply attribution. Historical cancellations are not passing proof. No broad local E2E, CI rerun, raised timeout, retry, skip or new suppression was used.

The latest conflict-only rebase preserves main's smaller dock fixture and its lazy composer memo owners. Dock assertions now select the canonical layout.maxWidth instead of the deleted duplicate override; no assertion or observable behavior was removed. All four replayed commits are signed. Fresh isolated frozen install passed in 19.1 seconds; targeted native types passed, and the dock/menu selection passed 20/20 cases in three files (67.31 seconds engine/116.98 seconds wrapper). Earlier replacement-head evidence: the preceding conflict repair preserved main's shared listen/stopScroll and createShadowStyles owners; it removed only the unused trackScroll, defaultActive and orientation alternatives. Its independent review completed scoped-clean through P2. Fresh targeted native types passed. The focused six-file conflict selection initially passed 34/37, exposing three draft-body assertions that did not await the owner's lazy NewSessionSubmission import. Strict targeted UI typecheck and scoped source-backed lint pass. Refreshed lint retains five warnings in unchanged blocks and no errors; no new suppression was added. Mandatory lint-suppression tests pass 14/14 (40.31 seconds engine,60.46 seconds wrapper). Refreshed standard runtime import-cycle proof reports zero cycles. The original bounded AST comparison found no added production edges; the subsequent axis-forwarding and test-only repairs add no production dependency edge. This is not a standard madge-command pass. Final three-file repair lint, oxfmt (48 ms) and whole-slice whitespace checks pass.

The focused 40-file run passed 724/725 tests before identifying one fixture migration defect in the Browser card owner. JSX bridge hosts are Solid-owned, so removing a host does not dispose its parent root. The fixture now uses the documented native BrowserTabCardHost.Element entry point, preserving its original disconnection lifecycle. All assertions stay unchanged. The complete repaired owner then passed 43/43 in 71.67 seconds (109.57 seconds including wrapper completion); the other 682 passing cases are unchanged. No full 725-test post-repair pass is claimed. The original selection took 385.00 seconds (407.98 seconds including wrapper completion); these owner/sibling tests protect transport, cancellation, keyboard, focus, row and resource-lifetime behavior, not merely argument plumbing.

The refreshed physical frozen installation passed, including the new native typechecker. Strict targeted types passed after horizontal restoration and again after the toast repair. prs.title: fix(mcp): a failed MCP server stalls every retry turn for its full initialize timeout
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated 30-second chat preparation stalls when a configured MCP server has already failed to initialize and its next retry becomes due.

## User Impact

After a startup failure, turns continue with the current tool inventory while MCP recovery runs in the background. Recovered tools join at the next turn boundary. A first connection for a new configuration/requester still gets bounded initialization and listing. The existing effective-tool-inventory surface keeps one unavailable notice per server and clears it after recovery, without appending chat or transcript messages.

## Why This Change Was Made

Maintainer decision (Peter, 2026-10-18): **“Retry in background”.**

Previously the catalog owner awaited every due retry until that runtime had successfully listed tools at least once. It now obtains an unavailable snapshot from the existing configuration/requester backoff owner and uses the existing background refresh path. Retiring a runtime during recovery preserves its shared failure record, so the next session cannot accidentally regain a blocking first attempt. Existing cooldowns, first-owner retry timing, transport ownership, and tool-call recovery remain in place. Existing resource/prompt pagination now lives beside tool listing so the runtime stays within its line-cap gate while retaining session-owned cancellation. No protocol, Plugin SDK, public configuration, or state migration changes.

## Evidence

Coordinator observations on main `7ef2a23236aa`, using four stdio servers (healthy, hung initialize, crash on startup, and garbage output):

- A hung initialize logged a 30-second initialize timeout. Gateway timing was `slow chat send 30439ms stage=startup`, including `preparation=30347ms`.
- New-session first delta was 34–36 seconds with that server, versus 3.3–6.1 seconds on an otherwise identical rig without MCP, for both built-in and Codex runtimes.
- A follow-up in the same session stalled again when backoff expired, producing a 37-second turn.
- Healthy server processes persisted across turns; new sessions owned new transports. Crash during `tools/call` produced visible `-32000: Connection closed` and the next call respawned. A hung call aborted in 226 ms. Garbage stdout was tolerated.

The fake-clock regression fails on the base with a 30,000 ms retry wait and passes after the fix with an immediate unavailable snapshot. Nine deterministic cases cover bounded first connect, pending retries across sessions, next-turn publication, one inventory notice, healthy siblings, exponential cooldowns, retirement, requester/config isolation, and explicit reload.

Focused Node suites cover the runtime, installed bundle, stdio/SSE recovery, reload, harness, materialization, prefix stability, and Codex configured-MCP path. Core types, targeted lint, import-cycle and line-cap checks pass. The nested retention fixture remains unverified: both attempts hit its unchanged 120-second no-output watchdog before completing. A separate one-second stdio startup fixture failed to reach its first initialize receipt in the full run and its exact-case retry; that setup gap is also recorded in the worker report. No watchdog, timeout, expected-failure, or baseline was changed.

Live fixed-head validation on the coordinator's badmcp rig remains pending; this change makes no new live latency claim.

prs.title: docs(install): add vendor-neutral NVIDIA Jetson install guide
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Adds `docs/install/jetson.md` — a vendor-neutral install guide for running the OpenClaw Gateway on NVIDIA Jetson hardware, mirroring the structure of the existing `raspberry-pi.md`.

This implements the docs gap raised in #94893, following the review recommendation on that issue: a hardware-tested neutral page that uses official NVIDIA links and keeps commercial turnkey products out of core docs.

## Why

`docs/install/` covers Raspberry Pi and ~20 cloud/VPS targets, but has no guide for Jetson-class edge hardware — an increasingly common always-on, local-first target. Jetson differs from the Pi in ways that justify a separate page: JetPack/L4T versioning, `nvpmodel` power modes, zram-by-default swap, NVMe, and thermal behaviour.

## Evidence

NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Super Developer Kit — L4T **R36.5.0 (JetPack 6.2)**, Ubuntu 22.04.5, kernel 5.15.185-tegra, 6 cores / 7.4 GB RAM, NVMe:

```console
$ uname -m
aarch64

$ node -p "process.arch"             # Node 22.23.2 via NodeSource
arm64

$ openclaw --version                 # runs natively, no build step
OpenClaw 2026.7.1

$ loginctl show-user "$(whoami)" | grep Linger
Linger=no

$ swapon --show=NAME --noheadings    # zram, not disk swap
/dev/zram0 /dev/zram1 /dev/zram2 /dev/zram3 /dev/zram4 /dev/zram5

$ grep POWER_MODEL /etc/nvpmodel.conf
< POWER_MODEL ID=0 NAME=15W >
< POWER_MODEL ID=1 NAME=25W >
< POWER_MODEL ID=2 NAME=MAXN_SUPER >

$ command -v tegrastats jetson_clocks
/usr/bin/tegrastats
/usr/bin/jetson_clocks
```

ARM64 prebuilds resolve (for example `@lydell/node-pty-linux-arm64/prebuilds/linux-arm64/pty.node`), so no compilation is required.

Two items in the guide come from testing rather than assumption:

- **Lingering is disabled by default** on these images, so a headless `systemd --user` gateway stops on logout. This is called out as its own setup step.
- **`nvpmodel` mode IDs are module-specific.** On this board `0` is the throttled 15 W mode and `2` is `MAXN_SUPER`, so the guide tells readers to list the available modes instead of hard-coding an ID.

## Disclosure

I work at ID-Robots, which sells Jetson-based hardware. Per the guidance on #94893 and the outcome of #87627, this page is deliberately **vendor-neutral**: no product names, no turnkey-device list, official NVIDIA links only. Happy to adjust scope, reword, trim, or drop it entirely if a Jetson page is not wanted in core docs.

prs.title: feat(mcp): prepare private context-bound server views
prs.body:
Related: #164690

## What Problem This Solves

A per-server MCP projection needs complete typed responses and the originating client's context, which the existing convenience-result interface cannot preserve.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible change. This prepares private owner operations without a public SDK export, HTTP route, or Claude configuration switch. Existing callers retain explicit legacy negotiation and the existing v1-shaped result boundary.

Manual `input_required` continuations are supported only for stdio upstreams. HTTP uses the SDK's `Client.callTool`, preserving parameter-header mirroring, and rejects input-required results for now.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing session/requester runtime keeps transport, admission, catalog and retirement ownership. Native views use context-specific child runtimes so they cannot alter ordinary callers' capabilities or negotiated era. Matching capability identity and snapshots reuse a child. Roots are immutable owner snapshots, available while idle; changed roots acquire a different upstream. View release joins admitted work before child retirement. Catalog refresh and reconnect use the current acquiring view, and acquisition waits for discovery to settle before binding.

Typed operations preserve full pages, metadata and cursors. Elicitation, sampling, manual continuations, progress, URL completion, cancellation and authority remain bound to the originating operation/view. Native clients expose the SDK-negotiated era for later mirroring. Startup failure state is scoped per child context.

Existing catalog and connection assembly moved into their owning modules to satisfy the unchanged file-size ratchet. Release-note context: internal MCP projection preparation; the projection cutover remains separate.

HTTP continuation follow-up: the SDK needs an overload preserving header mirroring while returning `Promise<CallToolResult | InputRequiredResult>` for `callTool(params, options: CallToolRequestOptions & { allowInputRequired: true })`, with output validation applied only to completed results. No private SDK import, copied encoding or SDK patch is included.

## Evidence

Real roots/capability-sensitive stdio peers and a modern v2 server exercise the session owner. A real modern HTTP server enforces `Mcp-Param-*` headers. Idle roots and the HTTP header/continuation regressions were reproduced before the fixes.

Fresh owner matrices passed 8/8 on macOS and 8/8 in local Linux: Node and pinned Bun, legacy and modern, main thread and real Workers. Every case also revoked the original borrower, killed the upstream, and reacquired through a surviving borrower. All leases returned to zero and all 32 recorded child PIDs were gone. Catalog-refresh and reconnect regressions failed before their fixes.

Independent review is clean through P2. Focused repository tests passed 13/13 on Node and 13/13 on pinned Bun (owner, HTTP and supervised negotiation); earlier unchanged consumer/prefix checks also passed. Wrapper wall times were 291.82 s and 161.27 s. The owner file bodies took 64.70 s and 36.44 s on this loaded host because they exercise actual subprocesses, separate contexts, callbacks, deadlines and joined cleanup at the real peer boundary.

Formatting, line-cap and whitespace checks pass. Local lint preparation hit the existing 300-second SDK declaration-build timeout before lint execution; no timeout was raised. Final lint/typecheck proof must come from exact-head PR CI.

Cold import of the private entry module (three fresh processes, excluding process startup and loader registration): Node median 5.71 ms; pinned Bun median 44.13 ms. These are local observations, not a controlled performance comparison.

Windows: AWS preflight failed during source synchronization before tests executed; the lease was released and was not retried. The PR CI planner did not select Windows jobs, so Windows runtime/Worker coverage remains unverified in this PR.

prs.title: fix(anthropic): recover known Claude sessions after bounded discovery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Valid Claude sessions disappear from exact-ID lookup when metadata discovery exhausts its 64 MiB budget, and the partial catalog looks complete.

Related: #176659

## User Impact

Users can search for, read, continue, or open a known Claude session even when ordinary discovery stops before its transcript. The final discovered page reports `DISCOVERY_TRUNCATED`, including on paired nodes, with a suggestion to search by exact session ID. Earlier pages remain pageable.

Discovery stays bounded at 64 MiB and 10,000 candidate files. Per-transcript metadata windows, path containment, sidechain exclusion, and Desktop archive precedence remain in force. There is no new configuration or public SDK surface. Ordinary discovery still does not provide continuation beyond its scan frontier; exact lookup is the bounded recovery path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The catalog owner now supports a separately cached, targeted scan instead of rearranging an ordinary discovery scan. Known-ID consumers use that same owner. Listing retains ordinary text matches and adds an omitted exact-ID match; its existing host-error channel reports the discovery frontier after the last available page. Paired-node parsing preserves that outcome. Control UI reconciliation consumes these successful partial-page rows, clears the exhausted cursor, and retains the warning during load-more and expanded refresh; genuine failures keep their existing recovery behavior.

Original fix by @sunlit-deng; maintainer cleanup replaces prioritization machinery with targeted lookup, covers the other known-ID consumers, and completes incomplete-discovery reporting. Contributor credit is retained in history and the cleanup commit.

## Evidence

- Source/history confirmation: current main still applies search after budget-limited discovery and discards its local truncation flag. The existing metadata-window, tree-watch, and catalog owners are retained.
- Regressions in `session-catalog-discovery-budget.test.ts`: **reports the discovery frontier and finds and reads an exact ID beyond it**; **keeps indexed and transcript sidechains out of exact lookup**. They cover the ordinary pagination boundary, exact read/search, missing-ID result, separate cached results, and paired-node error propagation. Existing catalog tests retain the assembled-cache identity contract. `app-sidebar-session-catalog-state.test.ts` adds **retains truncated final-page rows and warning through pagination and expanded refresh**, including cursor progress and removal of stale rows on refresh.
- Local changed-file `oxfmt` and oxlint passed. The installed dependencies lack the unrelated Solid lint plugin; the temporary core lint config retains every applicable repository rule and omits only the UI-only override, which matches none of these files. No dependency installation was performed.
- Independent Codex autoreview: **scoped-clean, P0–P2**, both before the catalog cleanup commit and after the page-consumer repair. Reviews were read-only on immutable candidates before commit.
- PR CI is the test gate. Current head `701d3bae8c9632ee46b8ddad1af98a8f71ab32fc` merges main `5ec30bfc7216adeb622700464db6dccae368e17e`, including the mock-export repair `b791dd0664e5`; fresh exact-head CI is pending. The PR's 12 files are unchanged by this mechanical merge, and changed-file lint/format passed again. Prior-head [run 39192976773](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39192976773) passed all selected Node/Anthropic and three UI test shards, UI E2E, production/test typechecks, lint, docs, security, and boundary jobs. Local tests, typechecks, negative controls, and live Gateway proof were intentionally skipped per maintainer policy (“relax testing and trust PR CI, just lint”). No Crabbox/Testbox leases were created.
- Test cost: the main regression uses 66 synthetic one-MiB transcripts, no real waits or polling, and an isolated filesystem/watch fixture. CI executed both regressions successfully in **221 ms** and **7 ms**. The extension lane passed **61 tests across 8 files in 42.91 s**, including module/setup overhead; the UI page-consumer regression passed in **1 ms** in [UI shard 3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39192976773/job/117869918966). Local test wall time is intentionally unmeasured.

ClawSweeper's P2 finding that the UI discarded successful truncated-page rows is addressed in the page-reconciliation owner, with a consumer regression covering pagination and expanded refresh. Its incomplete-discovery concern is addressed and the closing reference remains `Related`. Its live-proof request is superseded by the maintainer's PR-CI proof policy.

No new detached/background side effect is introduced. The continuation callbacks retain their existing authority, config, identity, session-binding, path, and lifetime ownership; only their read-only catalog lookup is narrowed to the requested ID.

Change size against main: production **+122/-46 (net +76)**; tests **+184/-1 (net +183)**; docs **+7/-0**. The original prioritization machinery is removed. Net production growth remains because this repair also carries truncation through the node boundary and updates every known-ID consumer and the UI page-reconciliation owner; unrelated deletions or weakened bounds would not be a sound way to offset those additions.

Fresh exact-head CI is pending after merging main's mock-export repair. prs.title: fix(browser): Chrome MCP cleanup test fails with write-after-end when a test already released its peer
prs.body:
Related: #176612

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome-mcp.cleanup.test.ts` intermittently fails with an unhandled `ERR_STREAM_WRITE_AFTER_END` ("write after end") during fixture teardown even though all of its tests pass. It is red locally on macOS and in CI on Linux (Bun shard `bun:changed-extensions-config-11`, run 39185036717), and the #176612 landing had to use the pre-existing-failure admin route for it.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. The browser extension test lane stops failing at random, so PRs touching it no longer need reruns or admin exceptions for this file.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three tests release the root peer themselves with `rootControl.end("release\n")`. The fixture drops a socket from its `sockets` set only on `'close'`, so when that socket has not finished closing by `afterEach`, `dispose()` called `end("release\n")` on it a second time. The socket's no-op `error` listener did not absorb the resulting error: `readline.createInterface({ input: socket })` forwards input errors to the Interface, which has no listener, so the error became an uncaught exception that Vitest reports after the file passes.

Teardown now releases only sockets whose writable side is still open (`!socket.writableEnded && !socket.destroyed`). Peers the test already released keep that release; the socket error listener and every test assertion are unchanged.

## Evidence

Local macOS (arm64), `pnpm test extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome-mcp.cleanup.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` in a loop. Each run counts as red when Vitest exits non-zero; every red run carried this exact `ERR_STREAM_WRITE_AFTER_END` unhandled error at the fixture's `socket.end("release\n")`, with all 4 tests passing.

| Runtime | Base (`f9da044ee301`) | Fixed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bun (repo default locally: pinned OpenClaw Bun fork; matches the CI `bun:` lane) | **9/10 red** | **0/20 red** |
| Node 24.22 (`OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node`) | 0/12 red | 0/15 red |

The race only shows up under Bun, where the root socket's `close` lands after `afterEach`, which matches the CI failure on `bun:changed-extensions-config-11` (run 39185036717, job 117845878737). A standalone Node 24.22 and Bun 1.4.3 probe confirms the mechanism is runtime-independent: a second `end(chunk)` on a socket wrapped by `readline.createInterface` throws an uncaught `ERR_STREAM_WRITE_AFTER_END` on both runtimes, while the same socket without readline stays quiet thanks to its no-op `error` listener.

Also ran oxlint (extensions shard, type-aware) and the formatter check on the file: both clean. Test cost is unchanged at about 3 s of test time and ~11 s wall per run on a quiet host.

prs.title: improve: reuse remote catalog snapshots between committed writes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway startup and reconnection repeatedly read the same remote model catalog, including its absent current and legacy slots.

## User Impact

The Gateway avoids redundant catalog database reads while preserving catalog refresh, activation, and offline inspection behavior. No configuration, schema, or migration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing machine-state mutation owner now publishes a lightweight catalog receipt after committed writes to the current or released legacy slots. The reader retains its last worker result per receipt and selected database engine. Unrelated writes preserve reuse; catalog writes, deletion, and admission retirement invalidate it. Maintenance and artifact-preserving inspections continue to read their selected store directly.

The receipt carries no catalog payload and adds no SQL, worker request, timer, or freshness probe. An in-flight read may return its captured snapshot when overtaken by a write; its retired receipt cannot serve the next read. Existing transaction comparisons, activation rules, and released v1/v2 compatibility remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- New production-worker regression fails on the base because a repeated absent read dispatches another worker request; passes with this change. It also covers unrelated writes, separate stores/engines, committed writes, caller mutation, rollback, deletion, legacy import, inspection bypass, and terminal admission failure.
- Focused catalog store, refresh, and overlay suites: 39 tests passed with the pinned Bun runtime. Formatting, basic lint, and diff checks passed.
- Independent Codex review completed with no actionable findings through P2. CI owns remaining type-aware lint, types, architecture, and ratchet checks; PostgreSQL review is pending.
- Source-attributed estimate against the current census: 10 catalog row reads become 5 across startup/connect/restart, removing 5 SQL statements and 3 worker requests; MAIN and warm-turn work are unchanged. These are **estimates, not measured results**. Three alternating baseline/candidate harness pairs remain pending. Acceptance: fewer catalog read operations, no increase in touched-owner or warm causal work; raw background variation is reported separately. No latency improvement is claimed.
- Production: +57/-1 lines (net +56); test: +97/-3; documentation: +7. The retained-result machinery is bounded by existing admission lifetime and avoids transferring the potentially large catalog through receipt publication.

prs.title: feat(state): local client credential cutover (R0 PR1b)
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

Native and CLI clients can bootstrap without opening the selected Gateway database, including a PostgreSQL-backed Gateway. Swift and TypeScript client identities, token caches, and native socket credentials move together to `<resolved-client-root>/client/credentials.sqlite`, including Gateway startup's pre-readiness CLI pairing. Approval policy stays shared; its semantics and effect-time authority are unchanged.

This implements Peter's R0 approval of 2026-10-14, following #174294 (PR1a) and #174360 (R14b). It replaces #174485, which ClawSweeper closed because frozen predecessor artifacts exceeded its 50,000 changed-line limit. This diff uses delta SQL, compact predecessor metadata, and regenerated current artifacts.

## Ownership and update behavior

The running app serves bounded authenticated operations. App-absent clients acquire exclusive local custody. Uncertain or post-dispatch failures are never replayed offline. There is one store and no timestamp reconciliation.

Canonical migration runs in updater/Doctor custody: capture → copy exact rows → verify → publish copied receipt → retire shared credentials → complete after shared commit. The local receipt binds source identity/generation and content hash. Stale local rows rebuild from shared state without merging; consumed-import claims prevent revoked credentials from reimporting.

Independent native sources remain byte-identical and read-only: no chmod, checkpoint, marker, private backup, retirement, or JSON unlink. Unchanged sources preserve local tokens and import claims; changed/restored sources trigger a bounded rebuild. Old native clients refuse retired canonical layouts and accept untouched independent sources.

PR1a enables no production local reader/writer, so there is no local store before the first cutover. Published SQLite drivers capture the shared credential tables. Rollback restores those tables and socket policy; old versions ignore the orphaned local store. **Credentials issued between upgrade and rollback are lost; affected clients re-pair.** PG-state installations begin with PR1a/R14b-capable drivers that capture shared families and local companions.

| R14b reconciliation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| SQLite retirement authorization | Reuse updater custody. Standalone Doctor takes a fresh same-custody backup and verifies row hashes. Exact table scope: `[device_identities, device_auth_tokens, gateway_origin_device_tokens, exec_approvals_config]`, plus `sqlite_stat1`/`sqlite_stat4` for retired indexes. Reused backups never authorize retirement. |
| Local companion attribution | Narrow extension at the existing capture coordinator; generations remain in backup owners. No parallel journal or borrow registry. |
| Native-v0→PG | Refuse with recovery guidance: start Gateway once on SQLite, run `openclaw doctor --fix`, then port. No automatic publication. Normal PG extraction verifies before retiring server rows. |

## Rebase and resolutions

eb4ecf4d7306f6425aa1b51814b42727e4d73d2d is based on d5aeceb2b89e253ba15d41976d0618e31842fb48. Shared schema/cutover is **29**; main's publication migration remains **28**. Local store schema and receipt version remain **1**.

- Identity assertions retain main's cases and require local credential custody or bounded authenticated operations; shared-state custody denial remains covered.
- Shared DB fixtures retain main's cleanup and add local credential cleanup. Historical fixtures retain their credential tables until captured migration.
- State contracts, maintenance, schema repair, and Voice Call Doctor combine main's additions with credential retirement. Read-only workers preserve both private-fork and updater-generation operations.
- Main's node-install helper stays deleted; its awaited local identity read moves into the CLI owner. Main's bundled fs-safe watcher and lifecycle proof stay intact alongside required Darwin native-addon/ACL proof.
- Doctor retains all new contention/corruption guidance cases and the captured schema migration case. Main's contributor-profile token field is preserved. The Goal product fixture now uses a separate local credential root per client; no authority assertion is weakened.
- The latest broker-admission conflict preserves main's two singleStatement variants, native-write count, phases, and row assertions, using shared diagnostic rows in place of the retired shared device-auth fixture. The native callback performs one INSERT so the autocommit case remains genuine. Main's preference/diagnostic/planner additions stay intact.
- Generated artifacts and inventories are updated through their owners. Main's app version metadata is retained. The latest rebase also keeps main's two-line Swift cancellation-test correction; no Swift production code changed.

## Evidence

| Boundary | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Credential and Gateway ownership | Retained unchanged-input proof: 14 files / 115 credential tests, cross-language receipt/wire fixtures, Gateway identity custody and startup CLI pairing pass. |
| State | Retained eight files / 97 tests pass. Public SQLite migration verifies exact rows and socket material before retirement. |
| Actual published-driver rollback | Stable 20→29→20 and beta 22→29→22 pass. Shared rows/socket policy restore; old readers accept untouched independent sources and ignore orphaned local credentials. |
| Actual PG driver rollback | PR1a public capture → candidate Doctor → rollback, 25→29→25, passes with exact shared rows/socket and local absence restoration. |
| Swift/Mac | Latest repair: 121 tests / nine shared suites pass; Mac build-tests and product build pass. Native sources, Swift manifests and lockfiles are unchanged by the subsequent rebase; root package.json changed only JavaScript export metadata, and native protocol regeneration checks pass. Earlier connection-suite reconciliation had 14 passes and three strict-sandbox temporary-directory setup failures; both variants of its changed cancellation case passed. No real app launch/install or Keychain mutation. |
| Reconciliation | Prior node-install reconciliation: 52/52 tests. Rebase12: schema-only 10/10 and runtime identity-token 20/20 passed; the Goal suite hit its unchanged 90-second beforeAll limit before the scenario, so final CI must supply that verdict. Latest CLI reconciliation: all eight model-output and persisted-catalog cases pass after maintained runtime preparation. Final rebase14: 126/126 tests across shared-state admission, Gateway preferences, and CI planner pass; both native transaction variants pass. Execution inputs verified. |
| Static/generated | Targeted production/test types, typed lint, format, line-cap ratchet, PG canonical/workboard/logbook and Kysely verification pass. Inventory regenerated (620 files / 2,296 calls). The mock-export ratchet failure at ci-node-test-plan.test.ts:3297 is proven inherited by byte-identical failure logs on clean main d5aeceb2. Retained import-cycle and wrapper-closure checks apply to unchanged dependency boundaries. |
| Independent review | Full diff and prior substantive repairs passed P0–P2 autoreview. Latest native/profile repairs and rebase14 delta: P0–P2 autoreview scoped-clean (private snapshots 58f59ae4cc8 and 9fe20cc177d); tree equivalence verified before commit. |
| PostgreSQL conformance | All three PostgreSQL conformance shards passed on prior published head fcb07f7c (CI run 39189893108). Final-head CI is required and will be recorded here before landing. |

**Signed real-Mac proof is pending with the coordinator after landing**, as instructed; it is not this PR's merge gate.

## CI and limitations

Final-head CI is pending publication. Prior-head run 39189893108 completed with 179 successful, 16 skipped, and 10 failed jobs (nine roots plus the aggregate):

| Prior failed job | Classification |
| --- | --- |
| control-ui-performance | Inherited: main and PR both 1,491,366 bytes against a 1,490,000-byte cap; zero PR growth. |
| check-test-types | Inherited: exact TS2353 obsolete completionDeliveryRetryDelaysMs option reproduced on clean main in native-subagent-monitor.parent-retention.test.ts. |
| checks-ui-e2e (2/9) | Inherited: both session-list-filter query fixtures omit ifRowsRevision, matching actual main CI. |
| compact-small-9 | Inherited: two Doctor diagnostics cases report retained schema 19, matching actual main CI. |
| compact-large-27 | Inherited candidate-agent expectation; main's fix 728c94809009 is included in this rebase. |
| compact-large-22 | PR-caused Goal fixture path, repaired; final-head scenario must pass. |
| changed-12 | SIGTERM active-permission refusal and SIGKILL recovery count reproduced on clean main. Managed restart passed on main, so that parameter remains unresolved. |
| changed-18 | Memory workspace-owner case passed on clean main; prior CI failure remains unresolved. |
| ios-screenshots | Build and all eight iPhone/iPad tests passed; watch simulator creation failed because its runtime was absent. Provisioning failure, not claimed inherited. |
| openclaw/ci-gate | Aggregate of those nine failed roots. |

CI run [39189893108](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39189893108), found the old Goal fixture path; that fixture is repaired without changing production authority. Its PR-context heading failure was corrected and the replacement check passed.

Retained investigated local failures are not claimed inherited: three Git-backup refresh child deadlines; two managed HOME-isolation deadlines; a Kysely packaging deadline; a Gateway assistant-media timeout where main passed; a package import-closure scanner timeout after its native/watcher assertions passed; and PG preflight/cleanup deadlines that invalidated the subsequent restore case. A fresh local run passed all 17 schema-admission/credential PG cases. Earlier host-denial/recovery replays timed out without reproducing their CI signatures, six E2E replays failed setup, and a 123-assertion run was invalidated by changed inputs. Runtime-dependent idle-WAL and separate PG→SQLite local rehearsal were incomplete. The local legacy agent-deletion case was not run because it invokes Trash; the case remains intact in CI. No deadlines or assertions were weakened.

## Review disposition

The final repair batch preserves the captured app profile/HOME for approval socket operations, settles legacy JSON imports before the app publishes its credential route, and aligns native-source timestamp/scope validation with TypeScript while preserving valid raw bytes. Existing fixes validate returned identity material at the Swift owner, reject arbitrary identity database paths, allow offline fallback only after pre-dispatch connection refusal, honor observed raw-token revocation, and restore against the captured canonical source path.

Two suggestions were declined. A valid empty native catalog is not zero-byte crash residue (already refused); later changed source credentials intentionally cause the approved bounded rebuild. Malformed receipt-digest hardening has no identified supported producer or incident: supported writers emit SHA-256 or null, and claim presence is intentionally the revocation tombstone. Digest spelling would not authenticate or recover consumption intent.

## Size

496 files; +20,341/−8,910 = 29,251 changed lines. Net production: **+3,698** across 156 files; **+3,672 excluding the generator** (+26). The complete recovery, cross-language custody, restore binding, and caller cutover exceed the +1,500–2,200 production-line estimate; LOC is reported, not a stop. The changed-line count remains below ClawSweeper's 50,000 limit.

prs.title: fix(update): stop retrying stalled snapshot progress forever
prs.body:
Fixes #176813

## What Problem This Solves

Managed updates can remain at `candidate-state-snapshot` indefinitely when update-history commit admission repeatedly exceeds its one-second allowance, even after the candidate copy finishes.

## User Impact

Future update drivers stop retrying a rolled-back history write after 120 attempts or a two-minute retry window and report an actionable error. Doctor and status also explain a snapshot phase with no recorded activity for 30 minutes, including when the driver remains recorded as running. Observation preserves the run and serving Gateway.

**Published-driver limitation:** a new candidate cannot patch an already-running 2026.10.4/2026.10.5 parent. Its retry loop remains installed-driver code, and candidate Doctor is reached only after the parent settles snapshot progress. Newer Doctor/status code provides diagnosis when invoked separately; this PR does not claim to terminate or repair that old process. Inspect its log/process, preserve the serving Gateway, and run `openclaw update repair` after the updater exits before retrying.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both release tags capture requester authority in ledger write options. The resulting synchronous policy reads can copy shared state during commit admission. #171493 deliberately released the writer after one second, but retried the rolled-back write forever. The reported retained-installed-runtime workers and 1,003 ms transaction match that path; the progress display already uses the live reader introduced by #162345.

Main's #168882 already removed requester-policy checks from bookkeeping while preserving checks before real update effects. This change completes the remaining retry bound at the ledger owner and uses the existing stale-run guidance owner for diagnostics. The shared retry helper checks elapsed monotonic time after rollback; an individual host admission can overrun the window before returning. The one-second writer-lock protection, fresh admission, FIFO ordering, rollback checks, and revocation remain intact.

| Driver | Candidate | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Released 2026.10.4 / 2026.10.5 | This branch | Parent retains its shipped retry loop; separately invoked newer Doctor/status can diagnose inactivity. |
| This branch | Supported candidate | Ledger bookkeeping avoids requester snapshots; repeated commit-admission timeouts terminate with guidance. |

No schema, protocol, config option, deferred side effect, or serving-Gateway mutation was added. Deslop retained the existing owners; production growth is necessary for the finite retry policy and diagnostic rather than unrelated deletions.

## Evidence

Source/history confirmation used `git show` on both release tags, current main, and `git log -p -S` for the retry and captured-authority paths. This is source attribution, not a reproduction of the reporter's installation.

- Regression: `releases the writer before retrying non-converging commit admission` exercises the actual ledger command and SQLite rollback with a deterministic stalled host. It checks bounded attempts, actionable failure, retained competing data, and writer-lock release. Existing delayed-success and revoked-authority cases remain.
- Regression: `reports an inactive candidate snapshot without abandoning its recorded driver` checks Doctor guidance, unchanged persisted history, and the recent-progress negative case.
- Changed-file `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json ...`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Independent Codex P0–P2 autoreview: `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings; review-only, no project code executed.
- PR CI is the test/typecheck gate and covers the changed regression files and affected lanes. Local tests, production negative controls, typechecks, and live Gateway/Crabbox/Testbox proof were intentionally skipped per maintainer policy. No leases or Gateways were started. Test wall times will come from CI; none were measured locally.
- Exact diff after merging current `origin/main` (b791dd0664e5), with no conflicts: production +22/-4 (net +18), tests +59/-7 (net +52), docs +16/-0.

Initial CI on `30655bb3fbf7` found an unrelated mock-export violation in `test/scripts/ci-node-test-plan.test.ts` ([job 117876582870](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39195138821/job/117876582870)). The latest scheduled main run's baseline job passed, so this is not claimed as a matching scheduled-main failure. Main separately fixed the fixture in [b791dd0664e5](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/b791dd0664e58c5f0c3776ee333b7be4bf8b524f); that fix was merged without changing this PR's six-file diff. Exact-head CI will run again on `bffe91e318e938dff62ce2f75dd7880a1cdc6459`.
