prs.title: fix: Windows backup scratch cleanup fails with EPERM
prs.body:
Fixes #176743.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes recurring `EPERM` cleanup warnings when a native Windows backup or Doctor retires an owned scratch directory.

## User Impact

Completed backups and `openclaw doctor --fix` can reclaim inactive scratch without repeatedly failing on an empty retirement directory. Active scratch, replaced directories, unknown contents, and published archives remain protected. No configuration, dependency, schema, or migration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Windows cannot rename a directory onto an existing directory. The shared scratch owner now chooses an absent UUID destination and uses fs-safe 0.26.8's existing atomic no-replace move on Windows. POSIX retains the owned empty reservation and its identity check, including compatibility with the existing non-native replacement path. There is no existence-check/unlink/rename window and no deletion of a colliding destination.

Original fix by @xutongxue233; maintainer cleanup adopts the smaller equivalent retirement implementation, removes redundant path reconstruction, and adds a Linux-CI regression for Windows directory-replacement semantics. The original contributor commit remains in the branch.

Cleanup facts remain owned at the effect: the committed SQLite lifetime token fences new writers; the source identity and POSIX reservation identity are checked immediately before mutation; fs-safe rechecks root, parent, and source identity before its native move; the moved directory's identity is checked again before control-file deletion. The parent path and UUID select the destination rather than granting authority. No config, session binding, or limits are captured by this change.

## Evidence

PR CI is the test/typecheck gate per maintainer policy. Local tests, typechecks, negative controls, live Gateway runs, and remote leases were intentionally skipped. Contributor code was not executed on the maintainer host.

- Source/history confirms the defect remains on the base: cleanup precreates a directory and requests an overwrite move. The released fs-safe 0.26.8 no-replace implementation was inspected; its target-existence probe is advisory and the native rename owns the collision decision.
- Regression: `reclaims scratch when the platform cannot rename onto an existing directory` exercises the real scratch/lifetime owner with Windows' existing-directory refusal at the move boundary. It runs on Linux too; it does not substitute for native syscall coverage.
- Native Windows regression: `preserves an existing retirement destination without moving the owned scratch` checks that a collision preserves the unrelated directory and owned scratch controls.
- Consumer coverage: `reclaims an interrupted archive's scratch on the next backup run` requires warning-free completion and no leftover retirement directories; `reports without mutation and fixes abandoned scratch at recorded archive locations` checks a quiet repeated Doctor repair. Existing tests cover live/replaced scratch, cleanup failure recovery, and preservation of published archives.
- Local changed-file core oxlint and oxfmt pass; `git diff --check` passes. The nested checkout has no local dependencies and the shared install lacks the UI-only Solid plugin, so oxlint used a temporary projection retaining all rules applicable to the four changed TypeScript files and omitting only that UI override. No install or committed lint configuration change.
- Independent canonical autoreview: **scoped-clean**, no accepted/actionable P0–P2 findings. Source review only; no code or tests executed.
- ClawSweeper’s completed [prior-head re-review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176836#issuecomment-6258757065) found **no code defects**, called the fix complete, and withdrew its earlier package-upgrade request because persisted formats/readers are unchanged. Its remaining native Windows live-proof ask is intentionally not followed: PR CI is the proof per maintainer policy. Its prior CI-gate concern is addressed by the main repair below; a new-head review will be requested once CI qualifies this head, unless already completed.
- Exact-head CI for `013022e98735cacbabdb19324971bfb16e461933`: pending. The branch merges current main without rebasing and retains the reviewed six-file fix unchanged. The prior-head run passed all tests, typechecks, lint, and docs (32 tests across the three changed suites, with the native Windows-only collision case skipped by Linux CI).
- The prior-head mock-export gate in unchanged `test/scripts/ci-node-test-plan.test.ts` is repaired on main by `b791dd0664e5` and included in this merge. Fresh CI must qualify the new head; the previous failing run is not claimed as green or inherited.

Change size against the merge base: production **+15/-11** (net +4), tests **+72/-2**, docs **+7/-0**. The four production lines retain the necessary platform distinction; no unrelated deletion was added to satisfy a line quota. One new timer-free owner regression; other additions strengthen existing tests. Prior-head CI timing: scratch suite 2.53s (runner 3.62s); publication suite 5.15s (runner 6.56s); Doctor suite 524ms (runner 1.98s). CI ran `time -p node --import tsx scripts/ci-run-node-test-shard.mts` with the selected targets and Bun test runtime. Local test wall times were intentionally not measured.

<details>
<summary>Contributor evidence from the original revision</summary>

At `903a434bcff160dd4b390b527408969bf0989951`, the contributor reported native Windows/Node 24.22.0 proof: five failing base scratch tests versus 31 passing focused tests; verified CLI backup creation; repeated Doctor cleanup preserving a live owner and reclaiming it after exit; and unchanged published archive SHA-256. They also reported compatible v2026.10.5 token recovery, not a full older-package upgrade. These are contributor-reported observations, not independently rerun evidence for the maintainer head.

</details>

prs.title: perf(control-ui): keep inactive chat views out of boot
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Idle chat reloads download the live subagent activity implementation before a subagent surface needs it. That path contributed to the chat boot JavaScript budget breach blocking Control UI performance checks. The cold-load campaign's original signed-in dashboard deep-link capture showed 14 intermediate states over about 15 seconds.

## Change

Defer live subagent activity through the existing facade's `lazy()` and local `Loading` boundary. Load session Details contents on first presentation, retaining them afterward so disclosure state survives closing and reopening. The existing shell, automatic docking, progress card, renderer, and observation lifecycle remain in their owners. Working status and localized Details loading feedback remain visible while cold chunks load.

Rebased onto `b791dd0664e5`, preserving main's native session-panel input admission: process data still enters through `ChatDetailsSession`; the background view only changes its activity renderer import. Regenerated the boot manifest, including main's new document-head and sidebar projection-cache modules. No budget, configuration, schema, or security changes.

Production delta: **+50 lines** (83 added, 33 removed across four chat components and the generated manifest). The first-presentation latch, retained disclosure state, and local loading feedback account for the growth. The eager re-export/registration paths are removed; no new observer, cache, or domain-state owner is added.

## Measurement

**Rebased head `e079f36a1b7808c164b937a4bb722666e6529d2c` passes the strict comparison against main `b791dd0664e58c5f0c3776ee333b7be4bf8b524f`.** Same Mac, installed Node/Vite/Pako toolchain, canonical comparison build identity, and shipped gzip sidecars. These are byte counts, not local wall-clock performance claims.

| Metric | Main | Candidate | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Chat boot JS gzip | 1,491,961 B | **1,480,438 B** | **−11,523 B** |
| Chat JS requests | 25 | 25 | 0 |
| Chat boot CSS gzip | 127,562 B | 126,675 B | −887 B |
| New Session JS gzip | 1,049,823 B | 1,049,676 B | −147 B |
| New Session JS requests | 20 | 20 | 0 |

Chat has **9,562 B headroom** under the unchanged 1,490,000 B ceiling. New Session has 324 B headroom under its unchanged 1,050,000 B ceiling. Startup and all remaining strict checks pass.

Command: `TMPDIR="$PWD/.local/l150" pnpm ui:check-performance:base b791dd0664e58c5f0c3776ee333b7be4bf8b524f`.

Historical bisect, using the same installed toolchain and canonical comparison identity:

| Revision | Chat boot gzip | Strict chat budget |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| r158, `69eefd48c800` | 1,487,045 B | pass |
| Parent of culprit, `2e98e9923487` | 1,489,198 B | pass |
| `990f9046637e` — restore live subagent previews | 1,494,374 B | fail |
| Before #176417, `993ec298df4e` | 1,494,398 B | fail |
| #176417, `052e9d387d7a` | 1,494,626 B | fail |
| Before #176457, `c6746e5fc147` | 1,489,642 B | pass |
| #176457, `2eccba0e7b6c` | 1,489,999 B | pass, 1 B headroom |
| Initial lane base, `20b6c7ae4e0e` | 1,489,033 B | pass |

The isolated first crossing is **+5,176 B at `990f9046637e`**. #176417 adds 228 B and #176457 adds 357 B; neither was the first crossing. Later reductions explain the smaller initial lane base.

The production-bundle idle probe changes from one live-activity implementation request to zero; the E2E asserts one request when live child activity is displayed. The closed-Details regression fails with the eager renderer. Held-request regressions fail with empty loading boundaries and pass with visible working status and Details feedback.

## Rebased validation

Focused files ran one at a time with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <file> --maxWorkers=1`. Wall time includes wrapper/setup:

| File | Result | Wall time |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| `chat-details.browser.test.ts` | 11 passed | 4.55 s |
| `chat-details-session.test.ts` | 13 passed | 4.35 s |
| `chat-subagent-activity-live.test.ts` | 1 passed | 2.92 s |
| `chat-bubble-activity.test.ts` | 4 passed | 5.01 s |
| `chat-working-indicator.test.ts` | 5 passed | 2.54 s |
| `chat-pane-run-activity.test.ts` | 10 passed | 4.92 s |
| `chat-subagent-wait.test.ts` | 25 passed | 2.91 s |
| `processes-panel-data.test.ts` | 8 passed | 2.51 s |

Native production-bundle E2E, one file at a time:

| File | Result | Wall time |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| `chat-header-subagents.e2e.test.ts` | 1 passed, including held activity and Details chunks | 20.21 s |
| `session-details-background-work.e2e.test.ts` | 1 passed; observer updates, light/dark, desktop/mobile | 20.37 s |
| `chat-subagent-waiting.e2e.test.ts` | 2 passed | 26.96 s |
| `chat-pr-refresh-replay.e2e.test.ts` | 1 passed | 29.05 s |
| `chat-pull-requests.e2e.test.ts` | affected Details scenario passed; 11 others filtered | 13.53 s |

The PR-chip scenario's first run overlapped the final mechanical rebase and compiled the older pre-open assertion; its stable-checkout rerun above passed. That invalid setup is not counted as product evidence. The last main update changed only a CI-plan test; the reviewed and locally exercised UI source is identical on the final head.

Formatting, `git diff --check`, and the regenerated manifest pass. Fresh isolated autoreview of the rebased patch: no actionable P0–P2 findings.

Exact-head CI and the campaign-required final-head full UI E2E run are in progress. The previous head's full run covered 834 files; its session-list and command-palette assertion failures have since been fixed on main. Final-head results and any fresh main-failure classification will replace this paragraph.

## Visual proof

Synthetic captures with the Details chunk request held open, same viewport and crop. The rebase preserves this behavior. [Proof comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176696#issuecomment-6257791044).

| Earlier candidate: empty pending panel | Final behavior: visible pending feedback |

prs.title: fix(agents): avoid timeout cooldown without failover targets
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

With a single API-key profile and no model fallback, one stalled model stream made every concurrently starting turn on that model fail. In live sub-agent fleets (8-24 children on one OpenAI key, embedded runtime), about 1% of Responses requests receive headers and then go silent; after the idle timeout and its same-model retry, OpenClaw recorded a model-scoped cooldown on the only profile. The next turns on that model (replacement children, the parent's wake) got `skip_candidate` and failed immediately:

```
[agent/embedded] Profile openai:manual idle timeout (model silent). No further authorized account for this provider; ...
[agent/embedded] auth profile failure state updated: ... reason=timeout window=cooldown
[model-fallback/decision] decision=probe_cooldown_candidate ...   (one turn takes the probe slot)
[model-fallback/decision] decision=skip_candidate ... reason=timeout next=none   (replacement child fails)
```

A parent reported it verbatim: "its sole replacement failed to start due to provider cooldown."

## User Impact

When no authorized replacement profile was selected and no fallback model is configured, a timeout no longer records a profile cooldown, and the warning says the profile stays available for the next turn. With an alternative profile or a fallback, cooldown and rotation are unchanged; rate-limit, billing, auth, and overload handling are unchanged. `docs/concepts/model-failover.md` describes the rule.

## Why This Change Was Made

`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/assistant-failure.ts` recorded the timeout as a profile failure even when `advanceAuthProfile` found no other authorized profile and no fallback model is configured. A cooldown only helps when there is somewhere to rotate; without an alternative it converts a per-request transient into hard failures of unrelated turns.

## Evidence

- Live fault injection (isolated Gateways, real OpenAI key, OpenClaw runtime, 8-child fleet): the first two Responses requests of one child were forced to go silent after headers. On main: cooldown recorded, the parent took the probe slot, the replacement child failed with `skip_candidate`, and that module stayed broken. On this branch: `No failover target is available; leaving the profile available for the next turn.`, no cooldown, the replacement started. In the same run a genuine provider stall hit another child and its replacement succeeded.
- `model-fallback.run-embedded.e2e.test.ts` new cases fail on main (persisted cooldown) and pass with the fix, including two immediate follow-up turns on the same profile; cases with an alternative still cool down. `assistant-failure.test.ts` 19/19, `assistant-failure.failover.test.ts` 19/19, `auth-profile-failure-policy.test.ts` 2/2, `llm-idle-timeout.progress.test.ts` 5/5 (adds a characterization that a stream silent after `in_progress` aborts 120 s after its last event).
- Three pre-existing failures in the full `model-fallback.run-embedded.e2e.test.ts` file reproduce on unchanged main (organization TPM recovery, direct-run suspension) and are untouched here.

## Release note context

Fix: with a single auth profile and no fallback model, a model idle timeout no longer puts the profile in cooldown, so concurrent and follow-up turns (for example sub-agent replacements) keep working.

prs.title: refactor(qa-lab): reuse private evidence and metadata values
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

QA evidence collection repeatedly clones already-private values and strictly parsed child bundles. Private static lists also freeze arrays or objects that never leave their module or change at runtime.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. QA evidence snapshots remain isolated, and child-process environment filtering, redaction, and staging behavior remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the invocation's captured launch/declarations, freshly parsed continuation/child records, the private profile report and parsed shard summaries. Keep copies at caller-input and returned-snapshot boundaries. Remove runtime freezes from private metadata while preserving readonly types; use a readonly Set for the membership-only environment allowlist; retain exported freezes and all credential filtering, redaction, authority and cleanup checks.

Pending child selection retains its copies: selection can fail after applying pending records, leaving retry/recovery state alive. Sharing those values would change recovery behavior. Public snapshots also remain independently mutable.

## Evidence

A single owner regression mutates caller continuations, imported child bundles and returned snapshots, checking that retained invocation evidence remains unchanged. Existing owner coverage retains retry/selection recovery, sharding, environment isolation, redaction and staging behavior. Validation pending. This slice has source-estimated SQL/request/MAIN delta 0/0/0; it is not separately measured. The first-slice official v3 warm pair completed with identical 54 [54–57] SQL / 16 [16–17] requests / 0 [0–0] MAIN and unchanged operation medians. No latency claim.

Candidate ledger:

| Candidates | Decision | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| C04787–C04792, C04795–C04796, C04802–C04804 (f) | REMOVE | Captured launch/declarations are private; strict parsing already detaches continuation/child input. Internal copies add no isolation boundary. |
| C04766 (f) | REMOVE | The profile report is freshly built and private; its proof requirements remain read-only throughout the suite. |
| C04932 (f) | REMOVE | A fresh parsed shard summary is rebased once and retained by this owner. |
| C04747–C04748, C04810, C04821–C04824, C04934, C04937–C04942, C04977–C04978, C04988 (f) | REMOVE | Private static arrays/objects are never exposed or mutated; readonly types retain compile-time protection. |
| C04799–C04801 (f) | KEEP | Pending-child selection may fail after partial application; independent pending data protects retry/recovery. |
| C04798 (f) | KEEP | Entry binding crosses a caller-input boundary. |
| Exported provider-secret constants and base runtime plugin IDs | KEEP | Exported mutable-reference protection is a caller-facing contract. |

C04810 follows the private environment blocklist into `gateway-child-setup.ts`, its current owner after the old helper was retired. The retired file remains deleted.

Production +43/−48 (net −5); tests +25/−0. Basic format/lint and diff checks pass. Two independent Codex P0–P2 rounds are scoped-clean with complete source verification, including the relocated environment-list owner. Final CI evidence pending.

<details>
<summary>Retained candidates in the changed owners</summary>

These reviewed candidates remain because they protect a distinct contract. Unreviewed sites are not counted in this ledger.

| Candidates | Decision | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| C04754 c, C04755 c, C04756 c, C04757 c, C04758 c, C04760 c, C04761 c, C04762 c, C04763 c, C04764 c, C04765 c, C04767 c, C04771 c | KEEP | `extensions/qa-lab/src/cli.runtime.ts`: Real CLI option or JSON payload ingress validation. Normalized strings/numbers can still be invalid; no owner has already enforced the specific contract. |

| C04799 f, C04800 f, C04801 f | KEEP | `extensions/qa-lab/src/evidence-invocation.ts`: Pending selection snapshot survives explicit select errors after admission (272/279/286). Subsequent owner complete() can mutate an admitted open addition before a later select replays pending. Direct sharing changes this recovery edge; retain current snapshot semantics in the bounded clone-only slice. No production caller/test currently exercises this exact edge. |

prs.title: fix(plugins): surface dropped prompt-build context
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugins use `before_prompt_build` to add context that can determine what an agent does next. When that context is dropped, the resulting prompt looks exactly like the plugin had nothing to report. A task or memory plugin can therefore fail while the agent incorrectly concludes that its queue or context is empty.

The silent-loss paths include a handler failure or timeout, a nested prompt build that is prevented from recursively dispatching hooks, a dispatch rejection, and a failure in the later tool-authorized enrichment phase.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime now appends one bounded `<dropped_plugin_context>` marker when a contribution is lost. It identifies the affected plugin and one fixed reason code: `handler-failed`, `nested-prompt-build`, or `dispatch-failed`.

The implementation deliberately preserves existing policy:

- prompt-build hooks remain fail-open;
- surviving plugin contributions still reach the prompt;
- error details remain in operator logs and never enter model context;
- authority-only handlers are reported only by the authorized phase that can actually run them;
- exact raw plugin identities are counted before labels are sanitized and truncated, so display collisions cannot understate the number of losses;
- the marker lists at most five entries and is capped at 640 bytes, with `+N more` accounting for every omitted contribution.

Pre-dispatch preparation failures remain marker-free because no plugin contribution was dispatched or dropped.

## User Impact

Agents can distinguish “the plugin had nothing to add” from “the runtime lost the plugin’s context.” That prevents false empty-queue conclusions and gives the agent a safe recovery instruction without exposing exception text, credentials, endpoints, or plugin-authored prompt injection.

No configuration or public plugin SDK change is introduced.

## Evidence

Current topic head: `2fb1637ed675e9615d92730f9d83087aa58a9485`.

- The complete changed-file gate, config-schema check, Plugin SDK surface check, and unused-file scan passed on that refreshed candidate.
- Focused validation passed 223 tests across four repository-runner shards (12 + 17 + 172 + 22). These are the saved refresh results, not a claim of a new run caused by this description update.
- `scripts/proof-prompt-build-drop-marker.ts` passes all 55 runtime assertions on the current head (`EXIT 0`). Its CLI scenarios now run inside `withTestRunAdmission`, so the CLI preparation path's own live-authority assertions execute for real rather than being bypassed by a no-audit fixture carrier. It exercises the real hook runner and production embedded, agent-harness, and CLI prompt-consumer functions: healthy contributions, failures/timeouts, nested builds, dispatch rejection, redaction, bounds, hostile identities, and pre-dispatch negative controls.
- Review regressions cover sanitized-label collisions, authority-only nested hooks, and failed authorized enrichment.
- `scripts/proof-118555-installed-plugin-provider-request.ts` passes all 26 runtime assertions on the current head (`EXIT 0`, four consecutive runs). It closes the installed-plugin and provider-edge gap described below: the fixture plugins are installed through `installPluginFromPath` (the entry `openclaw plugins install <dir>` uses), loaded by the real `loadOpenClawPlugins` through the loader's real conversation-hook consent gate, and the assertions are made on the **stdin of a real spawned provider process**, not on a returned value.

### Installed-plugin proof at the outgoing provider request

The earlier proof boundary — constructed registrations and a returned prompt value — is now closed by a second harness, `scripts/proof-118555-installed-plugin-provider-request.ts`.

**What is real.** Each fixture plugin is packaged on disk and installed through `installPluginFromPath` (`src/plugins/install.ts`), the same programmatic entry `openclaw plugins install <dir>` uses; the install really validates the package, and the run asserts a committed artifact exists before proceeding. The plugins are then discovered and registered by the real `loadOpenClawPlugins`. The loader's own consent gate applies unchanged: `before_prompt_build` is a conversation hook, so a non-bundled plugin does **not** register without `plugins.entries.<id>.hooks.allowConversationAccess`. The harness sets that key in its own isolated config the way an operator would, rather than bypassing the gate.

**Where the request is observed.** One installed fixture registers a CLI backend via `api.registerCliBackend` whose `command` is a small recorder process. `runCliAgent` then runs end to end, and `resolvePromptInput` (`src/agents/cli-runner/helpers.ts`) routes the assembled prompt to that process's stdin under `input: "stdin"`. The runtime performs a real spawn, so the recorder's stdin is literally the request that left the process. Substituting the provider binary is the stub at the very edge; every step between the installed plugin's handler and that spawn is production code.

**Isolation.** `OPENCLAW_HOME` and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` are redirected to a fresh temporary tree before any OpenClaw module is imported, which is why every import in the harness is dynamic. Installs, state, and sessions land in that tree, a configured install is never read or written, and the tree is removed on exit.

**Scenarios and results** (26 assertions, `EXIT 0`):

1. **Healthy-only turn** — the installed plugin's block and the user's ask are both in the outgoing provider request, and there is **no** loss notice. This is the negative control the review asked for by name.
2. **Installed healthy/throwing pair** — the throwing plugin raises an error carrying credential-shaped text. The outgoing provider request retains the healthy plugin's content, carries **exactly one** notice (384 bytes, within the 640-byte cap) naming `proof-throwing (handler-failed)`, contains **no** exception text, does not contain the dropped plugin's own block, and does not blame the healthy plugin.
3. **Bounded under load** — one healthy plus seven throwing installed plugins: still exactly one notice, five plugins named, `+2 more`, 515 bytes, healthy content retained, no exception text.

The outgoing provider request captured verbatim in scenario 2:

```
<plans_and_tasks><ready_issues><issue id='openclaw-beads-201'/></ready_issues></plans_and_tasks>

latest ask

<dropped_plugin_context hook="before_prompt_build">
The runtime dropped this turn's before_prompt_build contribution from proof-throwing (handler-failed).
That context is MISSING from this prompt, not empty — do not read its absence as "nothing to report" (for example, an empty task or work queue). Re-read anything you need from its source before acting.
</dropped_plugin_context>
```

**The proof can fail.** Run unchanged against pristine `origin/main` (`38c3edcc4caf692bbb9ff0078bda002587528036`, which has no `src/plugins/prompt-build-drop.ts`), the harness completes scenario 1 green — including `healthy: content is RETAINED`, so the fix is shown not to alter healthy behavior — and then fails at `pair: outgoing provider request carries EXACTLY ONE loss notice`, `EXIT 1` after 9 checks. That failure is the silent drop this PR fixes, observed at the provider boundary.

### Line-cap ratchet: coherent extraction (September 18, 2026)

The previous head grew three already-over-cap files, and `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` rejects *growth against a grandfathered baseline*, not absolute size. Three cohesive extractions erase that growth without touching behavior or coverage:

- `src/plugins/hooks-prompt-build.ts` — both `before_prompt_build` dispatch phases (ordinary and tool-authorized), the `AsyncLocalStorage` nesting token, and the loss collection they share. The hook runner injects its merger, its registration list, and its modifying-hook dispatcher, so the new module never imports back into `hooks.ts` and `check-import-cycles` still reports 0 runtime value cycles.
- `src/agents/cli-runner/hook-prompt-build.ts` — the CLI's two prompt-build hook resolutions, including this PR's deliberate asymmetry: preparation failures stay marker-free, dispatch failures become the bounded marker.
- `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.prompt-build-drop.test.ts` — the five CLI drop-marker tests, moved verbatim beside the existing `prepare.context-window` / `durable-context` / `model-routing-authority` / `rooted-execution` siblings. No assertion was weakened or deleted.

Counted lines (oxlint `max-lines` with `skipBlankLines`/`skipComments`, the measurement the gate itself uses) against the baseline each file is ratcheted to:

| File | Before | After | Baseline |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.test.ts` | 6872 | **6721** | 6736 |
| `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts` | 2361 | **2325** | 2353 |
| `src/plugins/hooks.ts` | 1397 | **1289** | 1364 |

Neither new module nor the new test file reports a `max-lines` diagnostic. CI confirms it: `Line-cap ratchet OK: 19 changed source files; no new violations or over-cap growth.`

**Behavior and coverage preserved, measured rather than asserted.** The *unmodified* `prepare.test.ts` from the previous head passes **191/191** against the extracted production code; the reduced file passes **186/186** and the five moved tests pass **5/5** in their new home (186 + 5 = 191). Both proof harnesses still pass on the new head — `proof-prompt-build-drop-marker.ts` 55/55 and `proof-118555-installed-plugin-provider-request.ts` 26/26, both `EXIT 0`. `pnpm check:changed` is `EXIT 0` across every lane, including the core/extensions/scripts oxlint shards and the Knip dead-export and unused-file scans.

The earlier partial-gate failure and old-head evidence are superseded by the successful refresh checks above. No unrelated CI failure is being claimed as fixed by this PR.

---

*Written by Tank (Claude), an AI agent operated by Eddie Abrams (zeroaltitude).*

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The desktop test harness registers the same power-management unit tests in both the application binary and integration targets that include their production modules.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. The test suite keeps all 12 unit cases and the distinct Linux portal, logind, macOS, and Windows integration coverage without running the included unit suites again.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the unit suites into binary-owned test modules and register them only under `cfg(test)` in `main.rs`. Production code, platform integration targets, assertions, and fixtures are unchanged. The nine-line net increase is explicit imports and test-module registration, not new behavior or test machinery.

This is part of the maintainer-requested test audit.

## Evidence

prs.title: fix(media): auto-detected whisper.cpp transcribes as English when an audio language is configured
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/176661

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: auto-detected whisper.cpp (`whisper-cli`) transcribes in English when `tools.media.audio.language` or a request language is set to another language, because the hint never reaches it.

## User Impact

User impact: with whisper.cpp installed and a non-English audio language configured, auto-detected transcription now returns text in that language instead of whisper.cpp's English default. Region-tagged hints such as `fr-FR` or `pt-BR` work too, for whisper.cpp and Python Whisper. Without a language hint nothing changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164841 passed the effective language to auto-detected Python Whisper and kept whisper.cpp unchanged; its issue covered Python Whisper only. The two backends differ when the hint is missing: Python Whisper autodetects, while whisper.cpp's CLI defaults to English (`std::string language = "en";` in `examples/cli/cli.cpp` of https://github.com/ggml-org/whisper.cpp). So for whisper.cpp a dropped hint means "transcribe as English", which contradicts the documented rule that capability defaults also cover auto-detected providers.

The auto-detected `whisper-cli` arguments now add `--language <code>` when a hint is set, like the Python Whisper arguments (whisper.cpp accepts `--language` as the long form of `-l`). Both CLIs accept only bare language codes: whisper.cpp exits with `unknown language 'pt-br'` and Python Whisper's `--language` has a fixed list of choices. So the automatic-backend boundary passes the primary subtag of the effective hint (`pt-BR` becomes `pt`) to both. The hint is already resolved there with request-over-config precedence; explicit CLI entries keep their own arguments and `{{Language}}` substitution.

Unset hints stay as they are: switching whisper.cpp to `-l auto` would change the default for every user and is a separate decision.

## Evidence

Tested at `25876ea64cc` (base `upstream/main` `b42c33803a8`).

Built CLI (`openclaw infer audio transcribe --file fr.wav --json`, Node 24, Ubuntu 22.04) with an isolated home and config, a cleared environment (no provider keys, no audio models configured, so auto-detection picks the local backend), in a network namespace without outside access. Real whisper.cpp v1.9.5 `whisper-cli` (CPU build) with the multilingual `ggml-base.bin`; a small launcher on PATH records the arguments and then runs it unchanged. The clip is one synthesized French sentence: "Demain après-midi, je retrouve mes amis à la bibliothèque près de la gare. Ensuite, nous déjeunerons ensemble." Config: `tools.media.audio.language: "fr"`.

Before (`local-audio.ts` from base `b42c33803a8`):

```text
"provider": "whisper-cli",
"text": "Tomorrow afternoon, I find my friends at the library near the station. Then, we'll join together.",
argv seen by whisper-cli: -m <model> -otxt -of <tmp> -nt fr.wav
```

After (this PR):

```text
"provider": "whisper-cli",
"text": "Demain après-midi, je retrouve mes amis à la bibliothèque près de la gare. Ensuite, nous déjonderons ensemble.",
argv seen by whisper-cli: -m <model> -otxt -of <tmp> -nt --language fr fr.wav
```

Observed result: on the base whisper.cpp gets no language and returns an English translation; with this PR it gets `--language fr` and returns French (`déjonderons` is the base model's own recognition error). A Japanese clip with `language: "ja"` behaves the same way: an English translation on the base, Japanese text with this PR.

Region-tagged hints, same command and clip:

| Config `language` | whisper-cli receives | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fr-FR` | `--language fr` | the same French text as above |
| `pt-BR` | `--language pt` | a transcript (Portuguese decoding of the French clip), `ok: true` |
| unset | no language flag | the same English text as on the base |

At the PR's first head, which passed the hint unchanged, `pt-BR` reached whisper.cpp as `--language pt-BR`, was rejected, and the command returned `No transcript returned for audio`.

Tests: the auto-discovered language table in `runner.cli-audio.test.ts` now expects the configured language for `whisper-cli`, keeps "no hint, no flag" for `whisper-cli`, and maps `pt-BR` to `pt` for both Python Whisper and `whisper-cli` (the latter through a request hint that overrides the configured one). A before/after test run on the base and this branch reports three of those cases failing on the base and passing here, with the 25 other cases passing on both; variants that always pass `--language`, or pass the hint unchanged, each fail at least one new case.

Checks: the touched test (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, time below), the consumer tests `local-audio.test.ts`, `apply.test.ts` and `runner.auto-audio.test.ts`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, and oxlint and oxfmt on the changed files; `pnpm tsgo:test:src` passed at the first head (the later test change only adds table rows). The broad suites ran in this PR's CI (`CI` run 39180040763, green at the first head `0d8323ae7cd`).

| Test file | `--maxWorkers=1` wall | CI seconds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/media-understanding/runner.cli-audio.test.ts` | 22.2 s (17.8 s of it compile preparation on a cold cache; the 28 tests take under 50 ms) | 3.47 s vitest duration (4.76 s for its shard) in `checks-node-changed-2`, at the first head |

Simplify pass: nothing to remove. One `languageArgs` value at the automatic-backend boundary now serves both Whisper argument lists, replacing Python Whisper's own `{{Language}}` pair; no new helper, state or option. Behavior still protected: no flag without a hint, request-over-config precedence, and explicit CLI entries keep their own arguments. Delta against the merge base: production +6/−1 (one file, two of the added lines are comments), tests +4/−1 (one file).

Not covered: no GPU build (Metal or CUDA); the argument list is the same for all backends. The French Before ran on a build of the base `local-audio.ts` inside this branch, the only production file the change touches; the Japanese Before ran on the base commit itself. Python Whisper's `pt-BR` handling is covered by the test table only; no Python Whisper install ran here. A Spanish clip in the same setup stayed Spanish even without the hint, so how visible the English default is depends on the language and the model.

prs.title: fix(gateway): disk-full write requests return raw SQLite worker errors
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the state volume fills, Gateway write requests such as `sessions.create` failed with a raw internal broker message: `UNAVAILABLE` / `SqliteWorkerError: SQLite worker stopped before its result was received: database or disk is full: code=outcome-unknown`. It named no next step, while a turn failing on the same full disk already showed "OpenClaw could not write local session data because the disk is full. Free some disk space and try again." Found by the stability campaign with the state directory on a deliberately filled 3 GB APFS volume (main 7ef2a23236aa).

## User Impact

Clients now get `UNAVAILABLE` with the existing disk-full recovery guidance and `details.code: "SQLITE_FULL"` instead of internal broker text. Retry semantics are unchanged: unknown dispatched writes stay nonretryable and queued, unexecuted writes stay retryable.

## Why This Change Was Made

Gateway write requests such as `sessions.create` exposed raw SQLite worker `outcome-unknown` errors when the state volume filled. They now return `UNAVAILABLE` with the existing disk-full recovery guidance and `details.code: "SQLITE_FULL"`, reusing the storage classifier and copy owner. `ENOSPC` is classified by that same owner. Queued worker failures retain their native cause so classification survives wrappers.

Unknown dispatched writes remain nonretryable; queued, unexecuted writes remain retryable. Worker retirement, transaction settlement, recovery, durable state, and replay are unchanged. Non-storage messages and existing request-error metadata retain their prior behavior.

The worker does not retire on every `SQLITE_FULL`. It retires when settlement cannot establish a usable native connection. Nested automatic rollback can remove its savepoint; the transaction owner deliberately fences that handle to prevent later autocommit after a caught failure (#139700). Healthy pre-commit automatic rollback is already handled separately (#157241). Definite job rollback or keeping such workers alive needs an owning recovery decision, outside this fix.

## Evidence

Coordinator live proof used the state directory on a filled 3 GB APFS volume. Stock main `7ef2a23236aa` returned:

```text
res ✗ sessions.create errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=SqliteWorkerError: SQLite worker stopped before its result was received: database or disk is full: code=outcome-unknown <- Error: database or disk is full: code=ERR_SQLITE_ERROR
```

The candidate (main `0211fa29bf49` + this PR + #176831) returned:

```text
res ✗ sessions.create errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=OpenClaw couldn't save your conversation because the disk is full. Free up space on the computer running OpenClaw before continuing.
```

Separately tracked F82: an outcome-unknown agent write on a full disk can wedge that agent's shared-state lease until restart (`Shared-state cleanup is waiting for accepted operations to settle`). This reproduces on stock main. Its raw text is a non-`SQLITE_FULL` error, intentionally not reclassified by this PR; lease recovery is outside this fix.

Validation: the real WAL worker/broker fixture reproduces the reported error using `max_page_count`, without filling the host disk or calling a model. Temporarily reverting only the four production changes makes both Gateway assertions fail with the original internal messages; restoring the fix makes both pass. The broker test also proves preserved native causes, unchanged outcome classification, no retained failed row, and a successful write after reopening.

All tests ran individually with `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node TMPDIR=/private/tmp/oc-W92 pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`:

| File | Result | Command wall time |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/authenticated-request-dispatch.storage.test.ts` | 2 passed | 440.28 s |
| `src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker.test.ts` | 17 passed | 131.97 s |
| `src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-reply.test.ts` | 7 passed | 88.11 s |
| `src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-reply.cleanup.test.ts` | 7 passed | 90.21 s |
| `src/gateway/error-shape.test.ts` | 5 passed | 133.03 s |
| `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/authenticated-request-dispatch.metrics.test.ts` | 46 passed | 183.23 s |
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/provider-runtime-failure.test.ts` | 15 passed | 146.58 s |
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/error-text.test.ts` | 9 passed | 126.00 s |
| `src/gateway/chat-display-projection.test.ts` | 52 passed | 47.57 s |

Core types (`pnpm tsgo:core`), targeted core oxlint, touched-file oxfmt, `git diff --check`, and Madge all pass; Madge reports zero cycles. Cold worker compilation, artifact verification, and the first router import dominate wall time. The new Gateway file's assertions take 42.2 s including cold initialization; the second case takes 4.6 s. Real worker settlement plus the authenticated response boundary is the required contract; a mocked worker error would miss it.

Both isolated Codex reviews are scoped-clean through P2. Production delta is +28/-10 (net +18), needed to connect existing classification and rendering while retaining outcome safety; tests/fixtures/routing are +113/-1. No new runtime module, dependency, schema, protocol schema, or configuration option.

Health probes are unchanged: liveness is intentionally independent of free capacity, readiness has no owned disk-pressure signal, and session disk budgets measure retained bytes rather than filesystem free space. Disk-aware readiness remains a separate follow-up.

Exact-head PR CI [39191184139, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39191184139) has one non-aggregate failure: [check-test-types](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39191184139/job/117864782455). ## What Problem This Solves

## User Impact

Mounted refs serve navigation and action lookup. Solid owns the selection toolbar, annotation editor, context menu, and confirmation. TanStack remains the row-measurement owner.

Both sides were built on this machine with Node 24.22.0. Strict performance fails the same unchanged chat (1,490,000 B) and new-session (1,050,000 B) caps on both sides. Startup remains below its strict ceiling and the original 374,285 B budget. Startup source-map module membership is identical: no extra library enters boot. The small startup increase accompanies the boot inventory and chunk regrouping; route totals decrease, and no request or shipped-byte budget changes. prs.title: fix: prevent oversized plugin context from blocking fresh turns
prs.body:
Fixes #176827

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes first-turn failures when a plugin injects oversized system context that returns after every session reset.

## User Impact

Oversized plugin system-context blocks are truncated with a visible marker, and a warning identifies the plugin and original/kept sizes once per session. Normal-sized contributions are unchanged. If fixed instructions and tools still fill the model window, overflow guidance points to reducing that context instead of resetting the session.

Truncation can omit plugin instructions; plugins should keep these blocks concise. Each prepend/append contribution has its own limit, so multiple plugins and other fixed instructions can still exceed the overall window. No configuration or SDK surface is added.

## Why This Change Was Made

The core hook merger is the last boundary that still knows which plugin supplied each contribution. It now limits each prepend/append block to an estimated 25% of the resolved model window using the existing CJK-aware character estimate, preserves the prefix, and appends a deterministic marker. Embedded and CLI callers supply their existing resolved budget; harness callers already carry it. Warning suppression is process-local and bounded, so eviction or restart can allow another warning.

Overflow recovery uses its existing foreground fixed-token estimate to avoid futile history compaction when system instructions, injected context, or tools already fill the window. Prompt-context operations live in a focused private sibling module. Authorized enrichment uses the existing turn-context merger instead of merging system/tool fields that the phase discards; CLI preparation drops an unnecessary async history-access wrapper while retaining the same successful-result memoization.

## Evidence

Source and history confirm the unbounded merge on main; the fields were introduced in #35177. The reported 824,170-character payload is represented by a synthetic regression fixture.

CI is the test gate per maintainer policy. It covers the changed hook and embedded-runner regression suites, sibling consumers, prompt-prefix stability, and relevant type/static checks. Added regression names:

- `bounds oversized %s per plugin and warns once per session` (prepend and append).
- `keeps normal system context byte-identical and bounds dense CJK context`.
- `bounds plugin system context using the resolved attempt budget before assembly`.
- `attributes oversized fixed context without retrying compaction or suggesting reset`.

Local validation passed: `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json` on the eight changed TypeScript files (one regex-spacing finding corrected and the affected file rerun), `oxfmt --check` on all nine changed files, and `git diff --check`. Prescribed isolated Codex autoreview returned `scoped-clean` through P2, with no actionable findings. Local unit tests, negative-control execution, typechecks, and live Gateway/Crabbox/Testbox proof were intentionally skipped per maintainer policy; no leases were created. Test wall times are therefore CI evidence, not measured local results.

Production delta: +148/-63 (net +85); tests: +85/-0; docs: +12/-0. The missing bound and actionable diagnostics require net growth; the authorized-enrichment cleanup removes unused merge work without unrelated deletions. No detached/background side effects were added.
