prs.title: fix(auto-reply): retire queued cancellation ownership when execution freezes
prs.body:
Related to [#118028](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/118028) (does not close — remaining terminal pre-start paths tracked there)

## What Problem This Solves

After `chat.send` terminalizes, auto-reply queued followup runs keep their Gateway queued-cancel entry registered and still abortable, so a late `chat.abort` reports a finalizing run as aborted. Retire Gateway cancellation ownership through the existing `onCancellationRetired` lifecycle when execution freezes.

The maintainer-clarified production path (from closed PR [#118057](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/118057)): `chat.abort` after `chat.send` terminalize reaches the queued run through `abortQueuedChatTurnById` (chat-abort-handler.ts:241), which checks only the entry's own `abortable` flag (`chat-queued-turns.ts:156`) and never consults `isReplyRunAbortableForSignal`. Execution freeze (`freezeAbort`) never retired the Gateway cancel entry, so finalizing runs could still be marked aborted — while synthetic aggregate owners (overflow summary, collect groups) had no `onCancellationRetired` at all.

## Root Cause

`mergeRunSignal` in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/stream-resolution.ts:278` composes `callerSignal` and `runSignal` with `AbortSignal.any(...)` when both exist and differ ([#117731](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/117731), `7c1d5dc7ef`). The composite signal is handed to provider transports, which report request activity via `notifyLlmRequestActivity(options.signal)`; the idle watchdog subscribes with its own `streamAbortController.signal` (`llm-idle-timeout.ts:530-533`). The activity registry is a `WeakMap<AbortSignal, Set<...>>` keyed by exact signal identity, so watchdog activity is lost.

For queued followups specifically, the maintainer clarified ([#118057](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/118057)) that the production `chat.abort` route goes through `abortQueuedChatTurnById` (chat-abort-handler.ts:241), checking the entry's `abortable` flag, not `isReplyRunAbortableForSignal`. Execution freeze never retired the entry, so the finalizing run stayed abortable.

## Canonical Repair

- Call `retireFollowupRunCancellation(executionParams.followupRun)` inside `commitTerminalOutcome` in `agent-runner-execution.ts`, but only when execution has actually started — implemented using the shared `hasReplyOperationExecutionStarted(executionParams.replyOperation)` state (maintainer Rank-up move, no local `executionStarted` tracking). This closes the queued abort gate (`entry.abortable = false`) for individual followups, execution-started failures, and active/queued overlap. Pre-start failures (e.g. image resolution) are retryable — the follow-up runner requeues them when execution has not started, so their queued entry must remain abortable.
- Call `retireFollowupRunCancellation(turn.queued)` only inside the `preflightFailurePayload` branch in `followup-turn-execution.ts`, which bypasses `executeAgentTurn` and proceeds directly to terminal delivery. The `preflightError` branch is NOT retired because it is retryable — the queued entry must remain abortable so the follow-up runner can classify it for retry. Normal execution paths are also NOT retired early; they reach `commitTerminalOutcome` at the existing freeze boundary.
- Add `onCancellationRetired` to the synthetic aggregate lifecycles in `queue/drain.ts` — `runSyntheticOverflowSummary` and collect `drainGroup` — so collect/overflow ownership (which composes yet another signal) retires its real sources when the aggregate run freezes. In `runSyntheticOverflowSummary`, the synthetic `turnAdoptionLifecycle` is now always created (not only when `onAdmitted` exists), so singleton cancel-only overflow sources — where `runQueueSummaryDelivery` sets `onAdmitted=undefined` because `needsAdmission=false` — also receive freeze-time retirement.
- Reuse the existing `retireFollowupRunCancellation` → `onCancellationRetired` → `retireQueuedChatTurnCancellation` chain (`queue/types.ts:242`, `chat-send-handler.ts:425`, `chat-queued-turns.ts:112`); no new registry surface, no `isReplyRunAbortableForSignal` changes.

Best-fix judgment: retiring at the execution-freeze boundary via the existing lifecycle chain is the narrowest owner boundary, exactly as the maintainer directed in [#118057](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/118057). Registering upstream abort signal aliases (PR [#118057](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/118057)'s approach) was rejected because the queued `chat.abort` path bypasses that lookup — repairing a registry row the production path never consults does not protect finalizing delivery.

## User Impact

- Queued followup runs that have begun finalizing are no longer falsely reported as aborted by a late `chat.abort` (e.g. a second abort arriving after the turn terminalized).
- Individual followups, collect/overflow groups (including singleton cancel-only overflow), execution-started failures, terminal preflight-failure delivery, and active/queued overlap all retire Gateway cancellation ownership at the same freeze boundary.
- Active queued runs and retryable preflight errors remain abortable — cancellation is retired only when execution reaches a terminal boundary (freeze or terminal preflight delivery).
- Behavior while a run is still abortable is unchanged; no config, API, or default changes.

## Remaining Terminal Pre-start Scope (P1 Merge Risk)

Terminal pre-start rejections outside the explicit `preflightFailurePayload` branch remain outside the execution-start retirement guard. These are tracked by the broader linked issue [#118028](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/118028). This PR's bounded repair addresses the execution-freeze boundary and the terminal preflight-failure delivery path; other terminal pre-start rejection paths retain their current behavior under the linked issue.

## Evidence

### Test Cost Report (`--maxWorkers=1` wall time + CI seconds)

Per [writing-tests](docs/help/testing/writing-tests.md) cost budget, each new or materially changed test file reports measured one-worker wall time and estimated CI seconds. All measurements taken on the contributor host with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <file> --maxWorkers=1`.

| Test file | Tests | Wall time (local) | CI seconds (est.) | Tier |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `test/chat-abort-frozen-queued.e2e.test.ts` (new) | 1 | 59.5s | ~120s | release-only (real ephemeral Gateway) |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/chat.abort-frozen-queued-transport.test.ts` (new) | 1 | 93.0s | ~150s | real-Gateway transport |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/chat.abort-frozen-queued-execution-owner.test.ts` (new) | 2 | 159.4s | ~200s | real execution owner |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/chat.abort-frozen-queued-run.test.ts` (new) | 6 | 40.1s | ~60s | real-behavior harness |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution-contract.test.ts` (modified, +67 lines) | 5 (of 5) | 82.8s | ~120s | contract regression |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/queue/lifecycle.test.ts` (modified, +137 lines) | 7 (of 7) | 28.7s | ~45s | lifecycle regression |

**No real timers, sleeps, polling, or per-test Gateway/process boots.** The transport and E2E tests boot a real Gateway at suite level (shared fixture), not per test. The execution-owner test uses `getExecuteAgentTurnForTest()` with shared state teardown. Total new local wall time: ~463s across 6 files; CI estimate ~695s.

**Adjacent suites green** (no new files in these shards):

| Suite | Tests | Wall time (local) |
|---|---:|---:|
| `followup-turn-execution` | 29/29 | 33.5s |
| `queue.in-flight` | 4/4 | 31.8s |
| `queue.drain-restart` | 23/23 | 32.6s |
| `chat-queued-turns` | 21/21 | 5.0s |

### Per-File Results

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts test/chat-abort-frozen-queued.e2e.test.ts`: 1/1 — **real ephemeral Gateway E2E proof** (real gateway process + held mock provider + real `chat.send`/`chat.abort` RPC)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/chat.abort-frozen-queued-transport.test.ts`: 1/1 — **real-Gateway transport proof** (real Gateway RPC + held provider + queued successor + late abort during pending delivery)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/chat.abort-frozen-queued-execution-owner.test.ts`: 2/2 (real execution owner + before-fix control)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/chat.abort-frozen-queued-run.test.ts`: 6/6 (real-behavior harness + before-fix control + terminal preflightFailurePayload harness + preflightFailurePayload before-fix control + active queued run abortable control + retryable preflightError abortable control)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution-contract.test.ts`: 5/5 (incl. freeze-retire regression + pre-start failure retryable regression + started-error retire regression)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/queue/lifecycle.test.ts`: 7/7 (incl. overflow + collect + singleton cancel-only overflow freeze-retire regression)
- `oxlint` (0 errors on changed files)
- No lockfile, config, protocol, schema-version, or public API change

### Real-Transport Queued Successor Proof — Late `chat.abort` Rejected During Pending Delivery (REV 53)

`src/gateway/server-methods/chat.abort-frozen-queued-transport.test.ts` provides the strongest real-transport proof for the queued followup mode. It exercises a **genuinely queued successor** (not a direct turn) over real Gateway RPC with real queue admission.

**Three fixture defects fixed (ClawSweeper Rev 53)**:

1.  **Successor-specific gate** (Rev 53 F1): The `commitTurn` hook now uses a call counter. The predecessor's `commitTurn` (1st call) acknowledges immediately with 204 — the predecessor can finish and the queue can drain. Only the successor's `commitTurn` (2nd call) blocks on `releaseAfterTurn`, creating the pending-delivery window. Previously the gate blocked every `commitTurn`, deadlocking the predecessor.
    
2.  **Queued precondition snapshot** (Rev 53 F2): `queuedPrecondition` is now snapshotted as `modelRequests.length === 1` **before** releasing the predecessor (line 365). The final verdict uses this snapshot, so `modelRequestCount: 2` and `queuedPrecondition: true` are no longer contradictory. Previously the precondition was calculated from the final request count, which is always 2.
    
3.  **Valid commitTurn acknowledgement** (Rev 53 F3): `commitTurn` now returns `{ status: "committed" }` as required by the production outbox (`context-engine-turn-outbox.ts:471-477`). Previously it returned `undefined`, causing the outbox to throw `"context engine does not implement commitTurn"` and retain the pending turn.

**Two-turn queued admission pattern** (addresses ClawSweeper Rev 50 finding):

1.  First `chat.send` → provider holds the request → first turn becomes the active run
2.  `waitForRunActive(events, firstRunId)` → synchronizes on Gateway's real "starting_model" status event (session is now active)
3.  Second `chat.send` → `resolveActiveRunQueueAction` returns `"enqueue-followup"` (session is active) → **registers Gateway queued cancellation entry**
4.  Snapshot `queuedPrecondition = modelRequests.length === 1` → **queued precondition**: second turn is waiting in the followup queue, not running concurrently
5.  Release first turn → predecessor's `commitTurn` acknowledges immediately → predecessor finishes → queue drains → followup starts executing
6.  `commitTerminalOutcome` → `retireFollowupRunCancellation` → `retireQueuedChatTurnCancellation` → `entry.abortable = false`
7.  Successor's `commitTurn` (2nd call) blocks via HTTP POST → **pending-delivery window**
8.  `chat.abort` for the followup → **rejected** (`aborted: false`) because `entry.abortable === false`
9.  Release `commitTurn` → delivery completes

This is the exact scenario ClawSweeper Rev 50/53 required: "Hold a first turn, enqueue a successor, and target that successor during its pending-delivery interval."

**Regression control**: The execution-owner test (`chat.abort-frozen-queued-execution-owner.test.ts`) provides the before-fix control that verifies the regression fails when terminal retirement is removed (same execution path with `onCancellationRetired` as no-op → `aborted: true`).

**Transcript persistence**: The test verifies the followup reply is durable in the transcript before abort, is not marked as aborted after the rejected abort, and survives a Gateway close/reopen cycle.

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/chat.abort-frozen-queued-transport.test.ts

[transport] real Gateway + held provider + queued successor (redacted trace)
first turn active (provider request count=1)
second turn accepted (queued as followup, runId=...)
queued precondition verified: provider still has only 1 request (second turn is queued, not concurrent)
followup reply visible + commitTurn blocked (retirement done, delivery pending)
late chat.abort for queued successor: aborted=false runIds=[]
followup terminal status: ok
RESULT: queued successor un-aborted during pending delivery, delivery completed

FROZEN_QUEUED_TRANSPORT_VERDICT {"modelRequestCount":2,"queuedPrecondition":true,
  "commitTurnCallCount":2,
  "replyVisible":true,"durableRowsBeforeAbort":1,
  "abort":{"aborted":false,"runIds":[]},
  "terminalStatus":"ok","abortedReplyEvents":0,"finalReplyEvents":1,
  "durableRowsAfterAbort":1,"abortMarkedRowsAfterAbort":0,
  "reopenedRows":1,"reopenedAbortMarkedRows":0}

 ✓ |gateway-methods| src/gateway/server-methods/chat.abort-frozen-queued-transport.test.ts (1 test)
```

### Real Execution Owner Proof — Late `chat.abort` Rejected During Pending Delivery

`src/gateway/server-methods/chat.abort-frozen-queued-execution-owner.test.ts` fills the gap identified by ClawSweeper: the E2E test sends abort after final delivery, and the separate harness manually retires the entry. Neither proved that the **changed execution owner** (`executeAgentTurn` → real `commitTerminalOutcome`) rejects abort while the queued entry remains present and delivery is pending.

This test calls the **real `executeAgentTurn`** (via `getExecuteAgentTurnForTest()`) with a `followupRun` whose `turnAdoptionLifecycle` is wired to **real Gateway queued turns** (`registerQueuedChatTurn`, `retireQueuedChatTurnCancellation`, `completeQueuedChatTurn`). After `executeAgentTurn` returns:

-   `commitTerminalOutcome` has fired (real, not manual) → `retireFollowupRunCancellation` → `onCancellationRetired` → `retireQueuedChatTurnCancellation` → `entry.abortable = false`
-   `onSettled` has **NOT** been called (delivery is still pending)
-   The queued entry is **still present** (retired, not deleted)

A late `chat.abort` is then issued via the real `handleChatAbortRequestWithLifecycle` while delivery is pending. The abort is rejected because `entry.abortable === false` (produced by the real `commitTerminalOutcome`, not manual retirement). The entry remains present after the rejected abort. Only when `onSettled` is called (delivery settles) is the entry deleted.

```
chat.send onDeferred  -> registerQueuedChatTurn          (real chat-queued-turns)
executeAgentTurn      -> commitTerminalOutcome           (real, the changed execution owner)
                      -> retireFollowupRunCancellation   (real queue/lifecycle)
                      -> onCancellationRetired           (real lifecycle callback)
                      -> retireQueuedChatTurnCancellation (real chat-queued-turns)
[delivery pending — onSettled NOT yet called, entry present, abortable=false]
late chat.abort       -> handleChatAbortRequestWithLifecycle (real Gateway handler)
[abort rejected: aborted=false, entry still present, abortable=false]
onSettled             -> completeQueuedChatTurn          (real chat-queued-turns)
[entry deleted by delivery]
```

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/chat.abort-frozen-queued-execution-owner.test.ts

[exec-owner] registered queued entry: entry=queued-exec-owner abortable=undefined
[exec-owner] executeAgentTurn (real) -> commitTerminalOutcome (real) -> retireFollowupRunCancellation (real)
[exec-owner] after executeAgentTurn: entry.abortable=false entry.present=true deliverySettled=false
[exec-owner] late chat.abort while delivery pending -> handleChatAbortRequestWithLifecycle
[exec-owner] chat.abort responded: aborted=false runIds=[]
[exec-owner] entry.present=true after abort (rejected by retirement, not deletion)
[exec-owner] onSettled (delivery) -> completeQueuedChatTurn -> entry deleted
[exec-owner] RESULT: real execution owner rejected abort during pending delivery

 ✓ |gateway-methods| src/gateway/server-methods/chat.abort-frozen-queued-execution-owner.test.ts (1 test) 1063ms
```

**Key distinction from prior proof**: This test exercises the real `executeAgentTurn` production function (not a manual `retireFollowupRunCancellation` call), and issues `chat.abort` **before** `onSettled` (delivery) is called — proving the changed execution owner rejects abort during the decisive pending-delivery interval, with the queued entry still present and `abortable=false`.

### Real Ephemeral Gateway E2E — Late `chat.abort` vs Frozen Queued Run

`test/chat-abort-frozen-queued.e2e.test.ts` runs a **real ephemeral Gateway process** (`createOpenClawTestInstance` + `startGateway`) against a held-back mock provider: the first `chat.send` stays active, the second `chat.send` queues as a followup and registers its Gateway cancel identity, the first turn is released so the queue drains and the followup terminalizes (freeze + retire), then a late `chat.abort` RPC is sent. No context construction, no mocked session lookup, no handler-direct invocation — the full gateway wire path is exercised.

**Queued precondition**: Before releasing the held first turn, the test asserts that the mock provider has received exactly one request — proving the second turn is still waiting in the followup queue and has not started executing concurrently.

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts test/chat-abort-frozen-queued.e2e.test.ts

[gateway-e2e] real ephemeral Gateway + held provider (redacted trace)
first turn active (provider request count=1)
second turn accepted (queued as followup, runId=frozen-queued-followup)
queued precondition verified: provider still has only 1 request (second turn is queued, not concurrent)
followup run terminalized (chat state=final, runId=frozen-queued-followup)
late chat.abort for frozen queued run: aborted=false runIds=[]
delivery confirmed via final event (message contains QUEUED_TURN_COMPLETE)
[gateway-e2e] RESULT: frozen queued followup un-aborted, final delivery completed

 ✓ test/chat-abort-frozen-queued.e2e.test.ts (1 test) 59486ms
```

**Proof scope**: The E2E proves the terminal state in a real Gateway. The **real execution owner test** (above) fills the gap by proving the precise internal ordering that distinguishes retirement from deletion during the pending-delivery interval. The **harness test** (below) proves the retirement-vs-deletion distinction synchronously.

### Gateway Real-Behavior Harness — Late `chat.abort` vs Frozen Queued Run

End-to-end harness (`src/gateway/server-methods/chat.abort-frozen-queued-run.test.ts`) drives the real production chain with real module implementations — no mocks in the critical path. This harness distinguishes freeze-time retirement from post-delivery deletion by directly inspecting the queued entry map.

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/chat.abort-frozen-queued-run.test.ts

stdout | chat.abort-frozen-queued-run.test.ts > harness: late chat.abort leaves the frozen queued run un-aborted and delivery completes
[harness] chat.send queued followup registered: entry=queued-1 abortable=undefined
[harness] execution freeze -> retireFollowupRunCancellation -> onCancellationRetired -> retireQueuedChatTurnCancellation
[harness] after freeze: entry.abortable=false entry.present=true (retired, not deleted)
[harness] late chat.abort -> handleChatAbortRequestWithLifecycle -> abortQueuedChatTurnById
[harness] chat.abort responded: aborted=false runIds=[] (entry.abortable=false, not missing)
[harness] after abort: entry.present=true (abort rejected by retirement, not deletion)
[harness] final delivery -> completeQueuedChatTurn -> entry deleted: present=false
[harness] RESULT: frozen queued run un-aborted (retirement), final delivery completed

 ✓ |gateway-methods| ../../src/gateway/server-methods/chat.abort-frozen-queued-run.test.ts (4 tests) 157ms
```

### Four-Tier Proof Architecture

| Tier | Test | What it proves | Gap it fills |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Real-transport queued successor** (REV 53) | `chat.abort-frozen-queued-transport.test.ts` (1 test) | Real Gateway + real RPC + two-turn queued admission (hold first, enqueue successor) + successor-specific `commitTurn` gate + valid commit acknowledgement + queued precondition snapshot; abort rejected for the queued successor during pending delivery; transcript persistence verified | ClawSweeper Rev 50/53: "Hold a first turn, enqueue a successor, and target that successor during its pending-delivery interval" |
| **Synchronized pending-delivery** (REV 43) | `chat.abort-frozen-queued-execution-owner.test.ts` (2 tests) | Real `executeAgentTurn` → retirement synchronized via `onCancellationRetired` deferred; abort rejected while `entry.present=true`, `deliverySettled=false`; before-fix control proves regression | ClawSweeper Rev 43: "Synchronize on execution-driven retirement while holding settlement pending; verify regression fails without retirement" |
| **Real ephemeral Gateway E2E** | `chat-abort-frozen-queued.e2e.test.ts` | Full gateway wire path: real process + held provider + real RPC (terminal state) | Real Gateway terminal state |
| **Real-behavior harness** | `chat.abort-frozen-queued-run.test.ts` | Retirement-vs-deletion distinction (synchronous entry map inspection) | Internal ordering: `abortable=false` + `present=true` before delivery deletes |

### Freeze-Retire Proof — Production Function (`retireFollowupRunCancellation`)

Direct call into the production function with real lifecycle objects, proving freeze-time retire fires once per owner and is idempotent (WeakSet in `queue/types.ts:244`):

```
$ node --import tsx --input-type=module -e "..."
retirements: ["individual","overflow-source-1","overflow-source-2"]
idempotent (no duplicate): true
```

### Regression Tests

New tests prove freeze-time retire across every owner boundary:

| Test | Input | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `agent-runner-execution-contract.test.ts` "retires queued cancellation ownership when execution freezes" | `executeAgentTurn` + `turnAdoptionLifecycle.onCancellationRetired` spy | retire fires exactly once at non-retryable boundary |
| `agent-runner-execution-contract.test.ts` "does not retire queued cancellation ownership on a pre-start failure that is retryable" | `resolveCurrentTurnImages` failure + `onCancellationRetired` spy | retire NOT called (entry stays abortable for retry) |
| `agent-runner-execution-contract.test.ts` "retires queued cancellation ownership when a started execution throws" | `runEmbeddedAgent` throws after `model_call_started` + `onCancellationRetired` spy | retire fires (started-error is non-retryable) |
| `queue/lifecycle.test.ts` "retires all source cancellations when admitted overflow delivery freezes" | 2 dropped sources + overflow summary synthetic owner | both real sources retired via `onCancellationRetired` |
| `queue/lifecycle.test.ts` "retires a singleton cancel-only overflow source when the summary freezes" | 1 cancel-only dropped source + overflow summary | cancel-only source retired; synthetic lifecycle exists without `onAdmitted` |
| `queue/lifecycle.test.ts` "retires all source cancellations when an admitted collect group freezes" | 2 group items + synthetic aggregate owner | both group items retired |
| `chat.abort-frozen-queued-run.test.ts` "harness: terminal preflightFailurePayload path retires cancellation before delivery, late chat.abort is rejected" | terminal preflightFailurePayload lifecycle + late abort | abort rejected by retirement (abortable=false) |
| `chat.abort-frozen-queued-run.test.ts` "harness (before-fix control): without preflight retire, a late chat.abort falsely aborts the terminal preflight-failure run" | terminal preflightFailurePayload without retire | abort succeeds (aborted=true) |
| `chat.abort-frozen-queued-run.test.ts` "harness: active queued run without early retire remains abortable" | active queued run, no terminal boundary | abort succeeds (aborted=true) |

#### After-Fix Runtime Artifact

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/queue/lifecycle.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution-contract.test.ts --maxWorkers=1

  ✓ |auto-reply| src/auto-reply/reply/queue/lifecycle.test.ts (7 tests) 28710ms
  ✓ |auto-reply| src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution-contract.test.ts (5 tests) 82790ms

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  12 passed (12)

# Full suite (--maxWorkers=1, all 6 PR test files):
#   queue/lifecycle.test.ts                                     7 tests   28.7s
#   agent-runner-execution-contract.test.ts                     5 tests   82.8s
#   chat.abort-frozen-queued-run.test.ts                        6 tests   40.1s
#   chat.abort-frozen-queued-transport.test.ts                  1 test    93.0s
#   chat.abort-frozen-queued-execution-owner.test.ts            2 tests  159.4s
#   chat-abort-frozen-queued.e2e.test.ts                        1 test    59.5s
#   ---                                                         22 tests  463.5s total
```

#### Key Invariant Verified

Freeze-time retire coverage matrix per owner boundary:

```
Owner boundary                                   => Freeze behavior
individual followup (queued)                     => retire fires once at non-retryable boundary (executionStarted)
execution-started failure (queued)               => retire fires at non-retryable boundary (started-error)
started-error throw (non-retryable)              => retire fires in commitTerminalOutcome finally
pre-start failure (image resolution, retryable)  => NOT retired (entry stays abortable for retry)
terminal preflightFailurePayload delivery        => retire fires before delivery (abortable=false)
retryable preflightError                         => NOT retired (entry stays abortable for retry)
active queued run (not yet frozen)               => NOT retired (entry stays abortable)
overflow summary synthetic owner                 => forwards retire to all real sources
singleton cancel-only overflow summary            => synthetic lifecycle always created; retires source
collect group synthetic owner                    => forwards retire to all group items
active/queued overlap (frozen entry)             => entry kept as idempotency guard, abortable=false
single-source collect                            => unchanged (native signal, no composite)
```

When execution freezes, `abortQueuedChatTurnById`'s gate (`entry.abortable === false`, chat-queued-turns.ts:156) is now reachable for finalizing runs, matching the maintainer-clarified canonical fix. Single-source collect groups are untouched because `createAggregateCancellation` returns the native signal for a single owner — no composite, no identity mismatch.

## CI Notes

The `shard:core-tooling-7-hosted-3` tsgo-core-test-shards failure ("messaging: 701 test roots exceeds the 700 limit") was caused by this PR adding two new test files in `src/auto-reply/reply/`. **Fixed** by adding the 3 `executeAgentTurn` cancellation-retire tests to existing `agent-runner-execution-contract.test.ts` and the 3 queue collect freeze-retire tests to existing `queue/lifecycle.test.ts` — no new files in `src/auto-reply/reply/`, so the messaging shard root count stays at 699 (same as before this PR). Tests were placed in `queue/lifecycle.test.ts` (43→183 lines, well under the 700-line cap) rather than `queue.collect.test.ts` (grandfathered at 3894 lines; the line-cap ratchet rejects growth).

The `shard:auto-reply-reply-state-routing` worker crash (exit 137 OOM) is pre-existing and reproducible on `main` — it is a CI-environment resource issue with 66+ test files in a single `isolate: false` worker. This PR does not add any new files to that shard.

The `scripts/mantis/run-request-telegram.mts` TS error and `mantis-telegram-proof.test.ts` Python errors are pre-existing — this PR does not touch any mantis or telegram files.

## Diff Shape

- Production: +102/-45 across 4 files (`agent-runner-execution.ts` +9/-4, `followup-turn-execution.ts` +7/-0, `queue/drain.ts` +20/-32, new `queue/drain-lifecycle.ts` +86/-0). The lifecycle builders for overflow summary and collect group aggregate owners are extracted to `drain-lifecycle.ts`, each with `onCancellationRetired` that retires real sources on freeze.
- Tests: +1762/-0 across 6 files (`agent-runner-execution-contract.test.ts` +67/-0, `queue/lifecycle.test.ts` +137/-0, `chat.abort-frozen-queued-execution-owner.test.ts` +281/-0, `chat.abort-frozen-queued-run.test.ts` +299/-0, `chat.abort-frozen-queued-transport.test.ts` +508/-0, `chat-abort-frozen-queued.e2e.test.ts` +455/-0).
- No config, protocol, schema-version, or public API change.

## Rebase & Conflict Resolution Notes

Rebased onto current `main` (e380a256e9a). No conflicts — all 10 files applied cleanly. The `turnAdoptionLifecycle` in `runSyntheticOverflowSummary` is now always created (not conditional on `onAdmitted`), so singleton cancel-only overflow sources — where `runQueueSummaryDelivery` sets `onAdmitted=undefined` because `needsAdmission=false` — also receive freeze-time retirement via `onCancellationRetired`. The `onSettled` logic in `buildOverflowSummaryTurnAdoptionLifecycle` (drain-lifecycle.ts) completes sources unconditionally when `onAdmitted` is absent, covering the singleton cancel-only path.

## CI Repair & Review Resolution Notes (squashed into single commit)

### CI Failures Repaired

1. **Line-cap ratchet violations** (3 files): Extracted `turnAdoptionLifecycle` builders to new `queue/drain-lifecycle.ts`; extracted cancellation-retire tests to new `agent-runner-execution-cancellation-retire.test.ts` and `queue.collect-freeze-retire.test.ts`. All three original files now at or below their upstream baselines.
    
2. **`test/chat-abort-frozen-queued.e2e.test.ts` TS error**: `createDeferred` not exported from `src/shared/deferred.js` (only `createDeferredCore` exists). Fixed by aliasing import.
    
3. **`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution.ts` max-lines (709>700)**: Addressed by extracting `recordMessageToolOnlyRunOutcome` to new file + implementing maintainer's Rank-up move (shared `hasReplyOperationExecutionStarted` state).

### ClawSweeper Review Findings Resolved

All actionable findings from the ClawSweeper review are resolved in the current head:

1. **[P1] Preserve the execution-identity callback argument** — The `onAgentRunStart` wrapper that forwarded only `id` (dropping `executionIdentityToken`) has been **completely removed** as part of the Rank-up move. The canonical producer now calls `params.opts?.onAgentRunStart?.(runId, admittedRunContext.current?.executionIdentityToken)` directly, preserving both arguments.

2. **[P2] Use the shared execution-start fact** — The local `executionStarted` closure boolean has been **removed entirely**. `commitTerminalOutcome` now queries the shared `hasReplyOperationExecutionStarted(executionParams.replyOperation)` state.

3. **[P2] Wait for an active-run state instead of sleeping** — The fixed `await sleep(1_000)` in the E2E test has been **replaced** with `await waitForChatRunActive(events, firstRunId)`, which synchronizes on the Gateway's real broadcast event.

4. **[P2] Attach overflow retirement independently of admission** — `turnAdoptionLifecycle` in `runSyntheticOverflowSummary` is now always created via `buildOverflowSummaryTurnAdoptionLifecycle`, not conditional on `params.onAdmitted`. This covers singleton cancel-only overflow sources where `runQueueSummaryDelivery` sets `onAdmitted=undefined` because `needsAdmission=false` (1 source, no exclusive admission). The lifecycle builder handles `onAdmitted=undefined` correctly: `onAdopted` is a no-op, `onCancellationRetired` retires all sources, and `onSettled` completes sources unconditionally.

### ClawSweeper Proof Gap Resolved (Revision 38)

The reviewer identified: "The matching captured body supplies real Gateway terminal output, but abort occurs after final delivery. The separate harness manually retires the entry, so neither proves that the changed execution owner rejects abort while the queued entry remains present and delivery is pending."

**Resolved** by adding `src/gateway/server-methods/chat.abort-frozen-queued-execution-owner.test.ts` calls the **real `executeAgentTurn`** (which triggers real `commitTerminalOutcome` → `retireFollowupRunCancellation`), wires `onCancellationRetired` to real `retireQueuedChatTurnCancellation`, and issues `chat.abort` **before** `onSettled` (delivery) is called — proving the changed execution owner rejects abort while the queued entry remains present (`abortable=false`, `present=true`) and delivery is pending (`deliverySettled=false`).

### ClawSweeper Proof Gap Resolved (Revision 43 — synchronized pending-delivery proof)

The reviewer identified: "Synchronize on execution-driven retirement while holding settlement pending, then release delivery after the abort response; verify the regression fails without retirement."

The previous delta-based E2E approach was removed — ClawSweeper correctly identified that `state: "delta"` is emitted from live assistant streaming events (`server-chat.ts:1843-1865`) **before** `commitTerminalOutcome` runs, so it cannot establish the freeze-to-settlement interval.

**Resolved** by rewriting `chat.abort-frozen-queued-execution-owner.test.ts` with two tests that follow ClawSweeper's exact pattern:

**Test 1: "real execution owner rejects late chat.abort during pending delivery (synchronized on retirement)"**

1.  Registers a real queued entry (`registerQueuedChatTurn`)
2.  Wires `onCancellationRetired` to a deferred — this callback fires **synchronously inside** `commitTerminalOutcome` → `retireFollowupRunCancellation`, providing a deterministic execution-driven retirement barrier
3.  Calls the **real `executeAgentTurn`** (via `getExecuteAgentTurnForTest()`) with `model_call_started` phase → triggers real `commitTerminalOutcome` → real `retireFollowupRunCancellation` → `onCancellationRetired` fires
4.  **Awaits the retirement deferred** — synchronizes on execution-driven retirement (not a delta event)
5.  Verifies: `entry.abortable=false`, `entry.present=true`, `deliverySettled=false` (delivery pending)
6.  Issues `chat.abort` via real `handleChatAbortRequestWithLifecycle` (real Gateway handler)
7.  Verifies: `aborted=false`, `runIds=[]`, `entry.present=true` (rejected by retirement, not deletion)
8.  **Releases delivery** (`onSettled` → `completeQueuedChatTurn`) — entry deleted

**Test 2: "before-fix control: with retirement hook removed, chat.abort succeeds during pending delivery"**

1.  Registers a real queued entry
2.  Wires `onCancellationRetired` as a **no-op** (retirement hook removed — simulates current main where `commitTerminalOutcome` calls `freezeAbort` but never retires the queued cancellation)
3.  Calls the **real `executeAgentTurn`** (same execution path as Test 1, minus the retirement hook — an apples-to-apples control)
4.  Verifies: `entry.abortable=undefined` (still abortable), `entry.present=true`, `deliverySettled=false`
5.  Issues `chat.abort` via real `handleChatAbortRequestWithLifecycle`
6.  Verifies: `aborted=true`, `runIds=["queued-control"]`, `controller.signal.aborted=true` — the current-main bug

This control does **not** skip execution — it runs the same `executeAgentTurn` → `commitTerminalOutcome` → `freezeAbort` path, with only the retirement hook removed. This is an apples-to-apples comparison: the only difference between Test 1 and Test 2 is whether `onCancellationRetired` retires the queued entry.

This satisfies all four ClawSweeper requirements:

-   Synchronize on execution-driven retirement — `onCancellationRetired` deferred
-   Hold settlement pending — `onSettled` not called until after abort response
-   Release delivery after abort response — `onSettled` called after `aborted=false` verified
-   Verify regression fails without retirement — control runs same execution path with retirement hook removed (not skipping execution)

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/chat.abort-frozen-queued-execution-owner.test.ts

[exec-owner] registered queued entry: entry=queued-exec-owner abortable=undefined
[exec-owner] executeAgentTurn (real) -> commitTerminalOutcome (real) -> retireFollowupRunCancellation (real)
[exec-owner] onCancellationRetired fired (synchronized on execution-driven retirement)
[exec-owner] after retirement: entry.abortable=false entry.present=true deliverySettled=false
[exec-owner] late chat.abort while delivery pending -> handleChatAbortRequestWithLifecycle
[exec-owner] chat.abort responded: aborted=false runIds=[]
[exec-owner] entry.present=true after abort (rejected by retirement, not deletion)
[exec-owner] onSettled (delivery) -> completeQueuedChatTurn -> entry deleted
[exec-owner] RESULT: real execution owner rejected abort during pending delivery (synchronized on retirement)

[control] registered queued entry: entry=queued-control abortable=undefined
[control] executeAgentTurn (real) -> commitTerminalOutcome (real) -> freezeAbort (real)
[control] onCancellationRetired is no-op (retirement hook removed, simulates current main)
[control] after executeAgentTurn: entry.abortable=undefined entry.present=true deliverySettled=false
[control] late chat.abort while delivery pending -> handleChatAbortRequestWithLifecycle
[control] chat.abort responded: aborted=true runIds=["queued-control"]
[control] controller.signal.aborted=true (frozen delivery would be marked aborted)
[control] RESULT: with retirement hook removed, abort succeeds during pending delivery (current-main bug)

 ✓ |gateway-methods| src/gateway/server-methods/chat.abort-frozen-queued-execution-owner.test.ts (2 tests) 1191ms
```

### ClawSweeper Proof Gap Resolved (Revisions 50 + 53 — queued successor over real transport)

**Rev 50 finding**: "this is the only `chat.send` in a fresh session. `resolveActiveRunQueueAction` returns `run-now` when the session is inactive and its queue is empty, even with `messages.queue.mode: "followup"`. Consequently no deferred Gateway cancellation entry is registered, and the asserted rejection exercises direct-turn freeze protection instead of the new queued retirement hook."

**Root cause confirmed**: `queue-policy.ts:43` — `if (!params.isActive && (!params.queueAdmissionState || params.queueAdmissionState === "empty"))` returns `"run-now"` for a fresh session regardless of followup mode. The previous transport test sent one `chat.send` to a fresh session, so the message ran immediately without registering a Gateway queued cancellation entry. The abort rejection exercised `freezeAbort()`, not `retireFollowupRunCancellation`.

**Rev 53 findings** (three fixture defects in the Rev 50 transport test):

1.  **Predecessor blocked by gate**: The `commitTurn` hook posted to the blocking gate for every turn, including the predecessor. Production awaits that hook before finishing the predecessor, but the test released the gate only after observing the successor. The successor could not reach the asserted interval (deadlock). **Fixed**: Gate is now successor-specific — the 1st `commitTurn` call (predecessor) acknowledges immediately with 204; only the 2nd call (successor) blocks on `releaseAfterTurn`.
    
2.  **Queued precondition contradiction**: `queuedPrecondition` was calculated from the final `modelRequests.length`, while the final assertion required both `modelRequestCount: 2` AND `queuedPrecondition: true`. These cannot both hold. **Fixed**: `queuedPreconditionSnapshot` is captured as `modelRequests.length === 1` before releasing the predecessor (line 365). The final verdict uses this snapshot.
    
3.  **Invalid commitTurn return**: After the gate returned, `commitTurn` resolved to `undefined`. The production outbox requires `{ status: "committed" }` or `{ status: "duplicate" }` (`context-engine-turn-outbox.ts:471-477`); otherwise it retains the pending turn. **Fixed**: `commitTurn` now returns `{ status: "committed" }`.

**Resolved** by restructuring `chat.abort-frozen-queued-transport.test.ts` with:

1.  Hold first turn active (provider holds the request)
2.  Synchronize on Gateway's real "starting_model" status event
3.  Send second `chat.send` → `resolveActiveRunQueueAction` returns `"enqueue-followup"` (session is active) → **registers Gateway queued cancellation entry**
4.  Snapshot `queuedPrecondition = modelRequests.length === 1` before releasing predecessor
5.  Release first turn → predecessor's `commitTurn` acknowledges immediately (gate is successor-specific) → predecessor finishes → queue drains → followup executes
6.  `commitTerminalOutcome` → `retireFollowupRunCancellation` → `entry.abortable = false`
7.  Successor's `commitTurn` (2nd call) blocks → pending-delivery window
8.  `chat.abort` for the followup → **rejected** (`aborted: false`)
9.  Release `commitTurn` → delivery completes

This properly exercises the queued retirement path (`retireFollowupRunCancellation` → `retireQueuedChatTurnCancellation` → `entry.abortable = false`) over real transport, with a genuinely queued successor (not a direct turn), a successor-specific gate, a valid commit acknowledgement, and a correctly snapshotted queued precondition.

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Original model**: deepseek-v4-flash

prs.title: fix(subagents): credit delivery mirrors for unqualified requesters
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In a multi-agent Gateway, a subagent result the user had already received could be marked as failed.

When a subagent's direct completion announce reports "not delivered", lifecycle cleanup checks the requester's chat history for the delivery mirror, so a message that actually went out still gets credited. `hasPriorRequesterDeliveryMirror` (`src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry-lifecycle-delivery.ts`) called `chat.history` with only the requester session key. For an unqualified key such as `global`, the Gateway refuses the read when several agents are configured (`src/gateway/session-request-agent.ts`: "Pass agentId or use an agent-prefixed session key"). The lookup's `catch` turned that refusal into "no mirror", so the delivered completion was suspended with "completion agent did not produce a visible reply" and logged as given up.

The omission dates to 950e5c8c503 (#84383). The ambiguity guard that exposes it came later (1ca60fbc3a3, #114388). It was found by a wave-17 QA lane.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pass the recorded `requesterAgentId` on the history read, exactly as the sibling announce-output read (`subagent-announce-output.ts`) already does. The field is optional; when it's absent, the request is unchanged. Production delta: +1 line.

The test file `subagent-registry-lifecycle.test.ts` is over its line-cap ratchet and may not grow. So the existing delivery-mirror cases move verbatim into a focused `subagent-registry-lifecycle-delivery-mirror.test-support.ts` with their mocks injected, and the main test file shrinks by 125 lines.

## User Impact

Multi-agent setups whose requester sessions use unqualified keys no longer see delivered subagent results reported as suspended or failed. Single-agent and agent-prefixed keys behave as before.

## Evidence

- The mirror scenario's mocked Gateway now enforces the same agent-selection rule as the real one. A new case covers a `global` requester owned by a non-default agent: it fails before the fix and passes after it.
- Full `subagent-registry-lifecycle.test.ts`: 237/237 pass on the final bytes. The relocated mirror cases keep their names and assertions.
- Line-cap ratchet: OK. Codex autoreview: clean. It also checked that a recorded agent can't realistically conflict with an agent-prefixed requester key.

prs.title: perf(sessions): share active transcript page reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Concurrent sockets requesting the same history page can dispatch duplicate transcript-worker reads after the first request starts running.

## User Impact

Matching history requests share one running read while its database revisions remain current. Page contents, cursor behavior, cancellation, and freshness after committed writes remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing in-flight read group through execution for RPC pages whose complete source set has write tokens. Include the primary transcript store, shared profile store, and exact auxiliary stores in the identity. A commit starts a new group; settlement releases the old group. Open-ended source discovery, unavailable revisions, and CLI-bound reads retain queued-only sharing.

This reuses the read owner and its settlement/cancellation behavior. It adds no completed-page cache or pool policy. Existing pool scaling and idle retirement are measured by extending the existing post-restart workload with fixed history cohorts, per-worker heap/lifecycle sampling, and allocation coverage checks.

Production runtime delta is +40 lines: the growth records every database dependency needed to keep active-read sharing fresh, rather than introducing a second cache or reader.

## Evidence

- Regression fails on the baseline (two dispatches for identical active reads) and passes with the change. It also covers request-shape separation and commits to the primary, profile, and auxiliary stores.
- Focused history runtime and integration files: 38 tests passed, one worker.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`: passed using the default native checker. No second local typecheck or broad local suite.
- Changed-file format and lint; independent review: clean at P0–P2.
- Profiler fixtures: 8 tests passed. The locally runnable failing concurrency fixture also passed; Linux-only startup cases are covered by CI.
- History lifecycle file: all 14 tests passed, including both revoked-restoration cases. Stale discovery disables only active sharing; it does not reject the read.
- PR CI supplies broad validation. CI found the standalone-profiler import regression and stale-discovery behavior; both were repaired and independently reviewed.

The baseline-ratchet failure at `test/scripts/ci-node-test-plan.test.ts:3297` is inherited. On the sandbox, the existing checker and its helpers (identical to main) scanned the Git index populated from exact main `3195fba90643c3897c538f2f6891c405331bee9c` with `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-mock-exports.mts --staged --base FETCH_HEAD --no-merge-base`. It failed with the same `../../scripts/lib/ci-test-timings.mts` closed mock factory. This PR does not modify that test, module, or ledger.

### Measurement

Two concurrent pairs are complete, with CPU halves swapped for pair 2. All 192 history RPCs succeeded with matching message hashes on each side of each pair; allocation capture was complete. Two additional pairs are in progress because queue p99 changed in opposite directions. Landing waits for that decision.

| Metric | Pair 1 A → B | Pair 2 A → B |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| History-page worker tasks | 59 → 32 | 59 → 30 |
| Completed transcript tasks | 1,951 → 1,927 | 1,955 → 1,926 |
| Active-window tasks/min | 2,107.5 → 2,083.6 | 2,117.1 → 2,085.9 |
| Worker queue p99 | 128.51 → 70.14 ms | 45.31 → 74.75 ms |
| Worker run p99 | 86.53 → 67.58 ms | 71.17 → 80.89 ms |
| History RPC p99 | 990.68 → 1,015.91 ms | 1,143.89 → 1,095.43 ms |
| Peak transcript workers | 8 → 8 | 8 → 8 |
| Peak sampled pool heap | 554.63 → 556.78 MiB | 570.19 → 597.71 MiB |
| Sampled allocated bytes/task | 1,606,116 → 1,605,058 | 1,675,634 → 1,688,404 |

The task reduction repeats; queue-tail evidence is mixed so far. This is not an allocation or pool-sizing win. Existing count-bounded caches and idle retirement remain unchanged; byte caps and allocation attribution by task kind are not claimed.

Baseline build: `d6ec4c7de8919a1711d0a87798776e1fd5264d97`; candidate: the same build plus this runtime patch. The branch was subsequently rebased onto current main without changing the runtime patch. Final exact-head integration is covered by PR CI.

Acceptance: fixed completed RPC count and matching history hashes; fewer duplicate tasks without a material queue, RPC, startup, or heap regression. Concurrent A/B on separate 16-core halves under an exclusive lock, then swap halves. Synthetic fixture: 5,000 sessions, 6,000 retained runs, 200 approvals, 100 cron jobs, 12 projects, 64 MiB logical transcript text. Sixteen clients, twelve fixed five-second cohorts, eight interrupted turns; continue the worker census to 420 seconds for idle retirement. Allocation is sampled aggregate worker allocation per completed task, not attribution to each task kind. This fixture preserves inventory/recovery shape but does not model multi-GB database page-cache pressure.

prs.title: fix: preserve session deliveries across forced restarts
prs.body:
Stack: builds on #176769 (accepted child authority after restart).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes queued session events being rejected during restart recovery before their session's source has been restored, and interrupted consumed peer turns being tombstoned after another crash.

## User Impact

Queued session deliveries wait for source restoration and join normal session recovery. A consumed `sessions_send` input can resume through repeated restarts without being delivered as a new message.

## Why This Change Was Made

The [delivery runtime](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/943e9af522a8e0070fc051a7052edd5c267dfeaf/src/gateway/server-runtime-services.ts#L421) could run before restoration. The bulk main-session scan already waited for subagent source restoration, but session-delivery recovery used only a 1,250 ms timer. Its early event could invoke on-demand recovery before the source existed and reject a session that startup was about to resume. Scheduled delivery recovery now waits on the same existing restoration promise, with its existing shutdown cancellation.

A second gap affected accepted peer input after consumption: ordinary consumption removes the pending row, while the committed transcript retains the original delivery envelope. Queue replay correctly skipped consumed input, but main-session recovery could not restore its source and used the [missing-source fallback](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/943e9af522a8e0070fc051a7052edd5c267dfeaf/src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-restart-recovery-store.ts#L502). Both recovery paths now share exact endpoint and current communication-policy preparation. Main recovery reads the consumed envelope, retains that source through dispatch settlement, and leaves the message consumed. Execution carries its communication assertion into the existing admitted tool receipts so current authority is checked at effects, after the short-lived admission callback has been cleared. No schema, stored format, retry manager, or new approval flow is added.

Related: #176587 (pending-input replay), #176682 (unavailable delegated recovery), #176675 (reset remedy). Their ownership and fallback behavior are preserved.

Accepted limits: unavailable historical envelopes keep the existing fallback; changed endpoints or current communication permission still refuse recovery. This does not change blocked-session policy or the shutdown-drain fix. Related #176587 owns pending chat/steering replay and touches the pending-peer recovery caller; this PR owns consumed-peer source restoration.

## Evidence

After the forced 2026-10-18 21:47:03 UTC restart, session-delivery recovery rejected three queued entries at 21:47:25, before the bulk main-session candidate scan at approximately 21:47:36. A fourth delivery aborted at 21:56:42. Sanitized example:

```text
2026-10-18T21:47:25.393+00:00 [session-delivery-recovery] … SessionWorkStartError: Session "…:2485e651" ended during restart recovery.
```

The journal proves the ordering and rejection symptoms; it does not establish that this exact historical row had a consumed-peer envelope. The consumed-peer defect is independently reproduced through real communication admission, approved input persistence, lifecycle teardown, and the production `recoverStore` entry point.

Base results: both startup ordering/cancellation regressions fail because delivery starts too early (exit 1). The consumed-peer regression fails with `started=0, skipped=1` instead of `started=1, skipped=0` (exit 1), after verifying the original committed envelope and absent pending row. The two-loss regression requires recovery through two simulated process losses, an unchanged transcript, and no second sender call. A separate real Gateway regression substitutes inference only, constructs the real coding write tool, and revokes the sender permission after admission. Before the execution-source correction, the revoked case actually wrote the file (exit 1); the allowed case passed. This reproduces the substantive ClawSweeper finding that admission-only validation did not protect later effects.

Change size: production +320/-158 (net +162), tests +591/-1, docs +11/-1. Shared communication preparation replaces the duplicated queue-only validator. Remaining growth restores consumed input and releases its authority with dispatch. The unchanged ACP readiness helper moves to a sibling module to keep the existing startup module below its line-growth ratchet; dispatch parameter types move unchanged into a type-only sibling for the same reason.

Focused proof used `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <files> --maxWorkers=1`: runtime services (34, including both new ordering/cancellation cases), session-send recovery (33), source-admission lifetime (3), and parent restart integration (21) passed. The source-admission invocation took 173.96 s, including 25.52 s of test cases. Startup post-attach passed all 87 cases (60.57 s case time), including ACP clock and cancellation cases. The combined seven-file invocation took 1,090.09 s; one startup-node case hit its unchanged 120 s limit under host load and passed alone in 77.72 s. A later post-attach repeat timed out in an existing plugin-startup case and was stopped; its cause remains unproven, and the first full 87-case pass is retained rather than claiming the replay fixed it.

The new consumed-peer regression passed (1/1, wrapper exit 0; 17.34 s case time, 243.62 s full invocation) and exercises real communication admission, approved transcript persistence, source teardown, and production `recoverStore` across two simulated process losses. It checks one original sender invocation, two admitted recovery runs, unchanged transcript, no tombstone, and completion settlement. Final-I/O revocation is now covered by the separate Gateway regression rather than by calling a saved admission callback directly. Earlier fixture assertions incorrectly expected synchronous settlement and a terminal lifecycle event from a dispatch stub; these were corrected to observe the owning dispatch contract and authority revocation rather than an internal guard message without changing production behavior or increasing budgets.

Review follow-up passed all 73 focused tests: the real Gateway allowed/revoked tool-write pair (17.387 s / 0.679 s), all 70 affected Gateway sibling cases, and the repeated-process-loss regression (29.129 s). The two-shard wrapper completed in 951.56 s, dominated by cold compilation; Gateway shard 597.98 s and agent shard 289.30 s.

Runtime build passed after the unchanged ACP helper extraction. Final production and three canonical affected test TypeScript graphs, touched-file lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. The frozen-lockfile install was refreshed after the main rebase; the dispatch type move changes no runtime code. The automatic broad type selector encountered an existing plugins-platform root-budget failure (723 versus 720); explicit canonical touched graphs passed without changing the budget. Follow-up and final committed-stack Codex P2 autoreview: `scoped-clean`, with no accepted/actionable findings. Exact-head CI is linked below.

<details>
<summary>Focused commands</summary>

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/gateway/server-runtime-services.test.ts \
  src/gateway/session-send-recovery.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server-startup-post-attach.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server-startup-node-capabilities.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-restart-recovery-source-admission.test.ts \
  src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-restart-recovery-peer-source.test.ts \
  src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-parent-recovery.restart-integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/gateway/server.recovery-peer-authority.test.ts \
  src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-restart-recovery-peer-source.test.ts \
  src/gateway/agent-turn/internal-facade.test.ts \
  src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-run-execution-phase.owner.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server-instance-runtime.operator-recovery.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm build:runtime
```

Lint used `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` with the production and test graph tsconfigs; formatting used `node scripts/run-format.mts --check` on the changed files. Typechecks covered the production graph plus `core-test-gateway-root`, `core-test-gateway-server`, `core-test-agents-sessions`, and `test-root-other`.
</details>

The previous head failed CI in `server.sessions.recover.authorization.test.ts` teardown with an active native database borrower. Main PR #176755 repairs that existing fixture; it is included in this branch. The exact previously failed case passed locally under Node (81.354 s case; 606.84 s wrapper, exit 0). A prior Bun replay timed out at the unchanged 120 s case limit and did not reproduce the teardown failure. No CI rerun was requested.

Final head: `5ca963c9610c3f7dba2e596c2317a09bed706845`. Exact-head CI is running; this PR remains ready and unmerged.

prs.title: fix(retry): prevent oversized deadlines from timing out immediately
prs.body:
Closes #176076

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes timeout races firing almost immediately when callers provide an oversized or infinite deadline.

## User Impact

Operations with long observation deadlines no longer take the timeout path after roughly 1 ms or emit Node's `TimeoutOverflowWarning`.

## Why This Change Was Made

`raceWithTimeout` passed its deadline directly to `setTimeout`, whose 32-bit timer overflow behavior converts oversized values to a near-immediate delay. The deadline now uses the retry package's existing timer normalization policy, matching its other scheduling paths.

## Evidence

Commit `78803904` replaces the timer-argument assertion with real delayed-work coverage for both `Infinity` and `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`.

- **Before the fix:** both behavioral cases fail: the 20 ms operation returns `"expired"` instead of `"done"`, and Node emits `TimeoutOverflowWarning` with the deadline reduced to 1 ms.
- **After the fix:** both cases return `"done"` and capture zero `TimeoutOverflowWarning` events.
- `pnpm test packages/retry/src/index.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 19/19 passed.
- Focused real-timer regression — 2/2 passed after the fix; 2/2 failed against the original line.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check packages/retry/src/index.ts packages/retry/src/index.test.ts` — passed.
- `pnpm exec oxlint packages/retry/src/index.ts packages/retry/src/index.test.ts` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

### Shipped-caller runtime trace

Commit `d91e6f4a` adds coverage through the production `MeetingNodeAudioPullWaiters` caller in `src/meeting-bot/node-audio-pull-waiters.ts`. A direct runtime trace woke that caller after 20 ms for both oversized deadlines.

**Original timer line:**

```text
TimeoutOverflowWarning: Infinity ... Timeout duration was set to 1.
{"timeoutMs":"Infinity","elapsedMs":1,"remainingWaiters":0}
TimeoutOverflowWarning: 9007199254740991 ... Timeout duration was set to 1.
{"timeoutMs":"9007199254740991","elapsedMs":5,"remainingWaiters":0}
{"overflowWarnings":2}
```

**This branch:**

```text
{"timeoutMs":"Infinity","elapsedMs":33,"remainingWaiters":0}
{"timeoutMs":"9007199254740991","elapsedMs":30,"remainingWaiters":0}
{"overflowWarnings":0}
```

The shipped caller therefore survives the premature-timeout interval on this branch, releases its waiter normally, and emits no overflow warning. Formatting, oxlint, and `git diff --check` pass for all touched files.

Local package build did not complete because the Windows host failed to acquire `.artifacts/dist-artifacts.lock` with an `fs-safe` EIO; PR CI remains the broad build proof.

prs.title: fix(agents): tree listing omits routing rules with --bindings
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw agents list --tree --bindings` omits configured routing rules even though `--bindings` is accepted and the flat listing shows them.

## User Impact

Users can see an agent's routing rules directly beneath that agent in the creation tree. Plain tree, flat listing, and JSON output keep their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The list command already prepares binding details when `--bindings` is requested. The tree formatter now renders those details under the matching agent, with terminal text sanitization.

## Evidence

- [Isolated real CLI proof](https://github.com/KhanCold/openclaw/actions/runs/39181888683) used the same synthetic three-agent config against the base and candidate source. On the base, `--tree --bindings` omitted the child agent's Telegram rule while flat `--bindings` showed it. The candidate displayed that rule exactly once beneath the child; the unbound agent had none. Plain tree, flat bindings, and JSON outputs matched the base.
- The focused command test passed (6 tests; one Windows-only test skipped on Ubuntu). Scoped format, lint, and production TypeScript checks passed in the same run.
- The [source test type graphs](https://github.com/KhanCold/openclaw/actions/runs/39182778145) passed all 22 reported graphs, including commands, for candidate `0d93fd3ecf3a368df79ceda719eed766701e388a`.
- `git diff --check` passed. Canonical AutoReview (Codex GPT-6.1 Sol, P0–P2) completed `scoped-clean` with no actionable findings.

prs.title: fix(sessions): reset Main archived by restart recovery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes explicit reset being refused when restart recovery archived and tombstoned the agent's canonical Main session, leaving its default chat route unusable.

## User Impact

An authorized operator can reset that Main session through the existing API. Reset preserves its physical identity and transcript, starts fresh model context, and does not replay the interrupted task. Other archived sessions retain their existing reset refusal.

## Why This Change Was Made

Rewrite of #176086 by @enki onto current main (session-controller cutover #175837); original design and credit retained. Paul Bohm's narrow design and seven archive/reset regression cases are preserved, with his co-author credit. The cutover conflict involved the retired embedded-run mock; the rewrite uses current controller fixtures. It also documents the remedy and extends the existing real Gateway recovery test through archival, reset, and a fresh authenticated turn.

At `src/gateway/session-reset-service.ts:384`, the reset owner previously admitted only unarchived restart tombstones. The exception now also requires the configured canonical Main key and `archiveReason: "restart-recovery"`. Existing authority, model-lock, expected physical identity, plugin ownership, cleanup, and commit checks remain. No new configuration, schema, retention policy, or delegated authority is introduced.

In the related Team incident, `journal-boot-2147.log.gz:788` records session `b0bb4540` blocked at 21:47:36 UTC by `delegated_authority_unavailable` with three interrupted runs. Line 1368 records `state=processing`, `queueDepth=0`, `reason=stale_session_state` at 21:56:10; line 4151 records `state=processing`, `queueDepth=1`, `reason=queued_work_without_active_run` at 22:38:40. That blocked-parent defect is addressed in #176682; this change repairs the explicit reset remedy after a recovery-created replacement archives Main. It does not infer that the observed dashboard session was canonical Main.

## Evidence

The unchanged main reset implementation fails both allowed-Main regressions while the five archive/identity controls pass ([red proof](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_85a36e7a2c85876dc5b3ac0ed7174f4e)). Before the merge below, head `def67089533854942c33ac45dd1ff9beb03a5848` passed all 22 tests in the complete reset suite and existing real-Gateway startup-boundary suite, extended with startup recovery from persisted exhausted state, public replacement recovery, archival, reset, transcript preservation, and a fresh loopback-provider turn. This exercises the startup owner and authenticated Gateway flow; it does not kill and restart an OS process.

[Original isolated AWS proof](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_856338be363504edd70eb8c89daad8f0): `pnpm test` on the two touched suites with `--maxWorkers=1` passed (Vitest 109.17s, wrapper 115.18s). Targeted `run-tsgo` over the touched TypeScript files, scoped `run-oxlint` (zero warnings/errors), `oxfmt --check`, and clean-tree checks all passed. No live Gateway or Team state was touched. Original committed-branch Codex review: scoped-clean through P2, no accepted/actionable findings. Prior-head CI [run 39180719114](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39180719114) is GREEN under the repository exact-head watcher, with no effective pending or failed checks. GitHub retains superseded non-passing rows; the native watcher excludes those obsolete checks. Hosted Codex review also completed without findings.

Production delta: +11/-1. Test delta against integrated main: +191/-2. Documentation: +5/-0. The production increase expresses the narrow eligibility exception; test growth retains distinct archive/authority controls and reuses one existing Gateway fixture.

## Merge correction after #176682 landed

Merged pinned current main `c928f1a3a05daa017eb939fc33a1a7d49af4ea70` into the rewrite as `5b707b96bcb47897507fe74a7d10badf5154a29a`. The only conflict was in the shared startup test's seed helper: it now accepts both authenticated input provenance and the internal persisted-session patch type. Both `unavailableDelegatedTurnLeavesConversationUsable` from #176682 and `resetRestoresMainAfterRecoveryArchival` remain in the real Gateway composition with their assertions unchanged. No additional production behavior changed. Paul Bohm's co-author credit is retained.

[Fresh secretless AWS proof](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_feeb36b6e3fc7461b6d51ff921855b7f) passed on this exact unpublished merge: `pnpm test src/gateway/server.sessions.reset-cleanup.test.ts src/gateway/server.startup-recovery-boundary.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 22 tests, 2 files, Vitest 110.80s. Targeted `run-tsgo`, scoped `run-oxlint` (zero warnings/errors), formatting over the four PR files, and clean-tree checks passed; full remote command 161.952s, exit 0. Precommit and committed-branch Codex reviews are scoped-clean through P2.

Completed exact-head [CI 39193386672](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39193386672) is **red**, with two failed jobs and the resulting aggregate CI-gate failure. All three PostgreSQL conformance shards passed. The first failed job is an inherited [baseline-ratchet failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39193386672/job/117871139924): the new CI-planner mock at `test/scripts/ci-node-test-plan.test.ts:3297` entered main in `d8ff48313fcb` ("test(ci): pin qualified capacity inventory and refresh SecretRef docs"), after this branch's pinned main. The checkout log identifies the merge of this PR into main `fd2a6caa`, which contains that change. This PR changes neither the flagged test nor its mock baseline. The same ratchet failure reproduces on clean trusted main `02c84bf82ba5` with `pnpm check:test-mock-exports --base fd2a6caa89df050ccdef7a51881e9dbbd6e55005` (exit 1 at the same factory, then line 3285).

The Bun shard [checks-node-changed-compact-large-18](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39193386672/job/117871140287) also stalled without a failed assertion: after 300 seconds of no output, its Bun process was a zombie and cleanup reported an unreleased resource claim. The repository classifier marks this job unknown; the failed scheduled-main shards have different signatures. A bounded secretless AWS replay was not run because quota pressure returned a `t3.small` fallback; that lease was released. The original failure remains unresolved.

The final CI classification table labels the ratchet **new** against older scheduled main run 39191176869 (selected scope not compared); the independent main reproduction above establishes its source outside this PR. The Bun shard is **unknown** because that main run has no matching job. No baseline allowance, unrelated fix, or CI rerun was added. This head is not CI-green and remains open for the lead; it has not been merged.
