prs.title: fix(worker): use monotonic clock for admission deadline
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A worker whose system clock steps backward during gateway admission (NTP correction, VM resume from suspend) hangs indefinitely retrying the handshake; a forward jump kills the connection prematurely. The fix replaces the wall-clock seed with the monotonic clock.

- Problem: `connectUntilReady()` seeds the deadline with `Date.now()` and computes remaining time as `admissionDeadlineMs - (Date.now() - startedAt)`. A wall-clock rollback shrinks the elapsed delta so the deadline never fires; a forward jump inflates it so the deadline fires too early.
- Solution: Use the global `performance.now()` (monotonic clock) for all three deadline-elapsed computations.
- What changed: `src/worker/worker-connection.ts` — 3 `Date.now()` calls in `connectUntilReady()` replaced with `performance.now()`. `src/worker/worker-connection.test.ts` — 1 regression test added.
- What did NOT change: heartbeat `sentAtMs` timestamp, `worker-connection-admission.ts` per-attempt timeout, `worker-connection-contract.ts` deadline constant, or any protocol schema.

## Why This Change Was Made

The monotonic clock is immune to NTP adjustments and manual system-clock changes — the same approach already used in `src/gateway/worker-environments/` and `src/infra/package-update-integrity.ts` for deadline tracking.

The global `performance` is used (not `import { performance } from "node:perf_hooks"`) because vitest fake timers intercept `globalThis.performance` but not the `node:perf_hooks` import.

Risk: `performance.now()` returns a float; the existing `remainingMs <= 0` comparison handles this correctly. The global `performance` is available in Node 18+, confirmed by `tsconfig.json` `"lib": ["DOM"]`.

## User Impact

Workers that experience system-clock adjustments during gateway admission will now correctly respect the admission deadline window instead of hanging indefinitely or failing prematurely.

## Evidence

Pre-fix RED (source reverted to `Date.now()`, test kept) — the regression test times out because the deadline never fires when `Date.now()` is frozen by fake timers while `performance.now()` advances:

```console
$ node --import tsx node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/worker/worker-connection.test.ts -t "monotonic clock so wall-clock"
 FAIL  src/worker/worker-connection.test.ts > uses a monotonic clock so wall-clock adjustments cannot stretch the admission deadline
Error: Test timed out in 120000ms.
 ❯ src/worker/worker-connection.test.ts:403:3
 Tests  1 failed | 25 skipped (26)
```

Post-fix GREEN — all 26 tests pass:

```console
$ node --import tsx node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/worker/worker-connection.test.ts
 ✓ |unit| worker connection endpoint failures > uses a monotonic clock so wall-clock adjustments cannot stretch the admission deadline 16ms
 ✓ |unit| worker connection endpoint failures > retains the last no hello diagnosis at the admission deadline 10ms
 ✓ |unit| worker connection endpoint failures > retains the last redacted connect failure diagnosis at the admission deadline 28ms
 [... 23 more tests ...]
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  26 passed (26)
```

The test fakes only `setTimeout`, `clearTimeout`, and `performance` — `Date.now()` is NOT faked and stays on the real wall clock. With the old `Date.now()` code the elapsed delta is only a few ms after `advanceTimersByTimeAsync(10_000)`, so the deadline never fires (test times out). With `performance.now()` the faked clock advances to 10_000 ms and the deadline correctly fires.

Open PR collision check: searched open PR topics and changed-file lists for `worker-connection.ts`; no open PR touched it. Related merged wall-clock PRs: #169151, #171838, #171977 — all use the same `Date.now() → performance.now()` pattern in different files, no conflict.

### Real transport reproduction (running WebSocket server + real `createWorkerConnection`)

To prove the fix end-to-end rather than only with fake timers, a real `WebSocketServer` acts as the admission endpoint and **never replies to the worker hello**, so the handshake stalls. A real `createWorkerConnection` starts against it with `admissionDeadlineMs`. A stack-matched `Date.now()` intercept then pretends the system clock stepped backward/forward **only inside `connectUntilReady()`** (the admission-deadline path) — heartbeat/protocol `Date.now()` uses are untouched, isolating the deadline computation as the only thing reacting to wall-clock jumps.

Before/after behaviour matrix (elapsed = wall time from `connection.start()` until `WorkerAdmissionDeadlineExceededError`):

| mode | wall-clock jump | deadline | elapsed | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| post-fix (`performance.now`) | rollback 5000ms | 3000ms | **3003ms** | deadline fires on time ✅ |
| post-fix (`performance.now`) | forward 5000ms | 3000ms | **3004ms** | deadline fires on time ✅ |
| pre-fix (`Date.now`) | rollback 5000ms | 3000ms | **8002ms** | deadline stretched ~5000ms ❌ |
| pre-fix (`Date.now`) | forward 5000ms | 3000ms | **1018ms** | deadline fires ~2000ms early ❌ |
| post-fix (`performance.now`) | rollback 5000ms | 10000ms | **10007ms** | deadline fires on time ✅ |
| pre-fix (`Date.now`) | rollback 5000ms | 10000ms | **15004ms** | deadline stretched ~5000ms ❌ |
| post-fix (`performance.now`) | rollback 2000ms | 3000ms | **3005ms** | deadline fires on time ✅ |
| pre-fix (`Date.now`) | rollback 2000ms | 3000ms | **5004ms** | deadline stretched ~2000ms ❌ |

Every measured elapsed matches the model exactly: with a rollback of `S` ms the pre-fix deadline fires at `deadline + S` (8002≈3000+5000, 5004≈3000+2000, 15004≈10000+5000), i.e. the admission window is silently stretched by the rollback — the worker keeps retrying for a full extra `S` ms (connections count grows: 2 → 4 for the 3000ms/rollback-5000 case). A forward jump instead fires `deadline − S` early (1018≈3000−2000 after a 5000ms forward step once the timeout resumes). The post-fix monotonic clock is immune to both directions: elapsed stays at the configured deadline (3003/3004/10007/3005) regardless of the jump.

✨ **Media proof (live terminal capture)** — the same real-transport harness, run in a live terminal and captured to an image: post-fix fires at the 3000ms deadline while pre-fix stretches to ~8000ms after the 5000ms rollback.

![BUG-175 real-transport before/after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SunnyShu0925/openclaw/evidence/BUG-175-media-proof/.evidence/BUG-175/bug175-media-proof.png)

(The image lives on the temporary branch `evidence/BUG-175-media-proof` so reviewers can open it directly; the PR branch itself is unchanged.)

Sample run (pre-fix, rollback 5000ms, deadline 3000ms) showing the stretched deadline and the armed skew:

```console
$ PROOF_MODE=pre-fix PROOF_SKEW_MS=5000 node --import tsx proof-175.mts
mode=pre-fix deadlineMs=3000 armAfterMs=500 skewMs=5000
elapsedMs=8002 connections=4 error=WorkerAdmissionDeadlineExceededError
skewArmed=true
RESULT: DEADLINE STRETCHED
```

Same run with the fix in place:

```console
$ PROOF_MODE=post-fix PROOF_SKEW_MS=5000 node --import tsx proof-175.mts
mode=post-fix deadlineMs=3000 armAfterMs=500 skewMs=5000
elapsedMs=3003 connections=2 error=WorkerAdmissionDeadlineExceededError
RESULT: DEADLINE FIRED ON TIME
```

What was not tested: the heartbeat `sentAtMs` field is not covered by this change and behaves identically before and after. Real network conditions (NTP step vs. slew) are not simulated; the test uses vitest fake timers to deterministically separate the two clocks.
### CI failure classification (checks-node-changed-1/3/6/15/19)

The five failing shards are **not caused by this PR**. Classified against the failing logs:

- **Root cause of shards 6/15/19** (`midtool-node-loss`, `node-worker-launch-wire`, `skill-library-worker-wire`): the worker fails to load the gateway-installed bundle `session-transcript.worker.mjs` (`Cannot find module '.../bundles/config/sessions/session-transcript.worker.mjs'`). This `.mjs` is a CI-built artifact distributed by the gateway into the test's temporary `node-state` directory — it is **not** a file this PR touches, and `src/config/sessions/session-transcript.worker.ts` (its source) is untouched here.
- **The failure occurs during `exec` tool execution, after admission already succeeded** (shard 15 expected an `approval_required` error and instead received the missing-bundle error while running `"tool": "exec"`). A worker can only reach `exec` after a successful admission handshake — so the admission-deadline change provably did **not** break the handshake or prematurely abort it. If this change had broken admission, the worker would never reach the exec stage.
- **Shards 1/3** (`auth-profile-rotation`, `model-fallback`) fail with timing/ordering assertion errors (`undefined` vs string; mock provider called 8× instead of 2×) — unrelated e2e flakiness in `src/agents/`.
- **The PR's own test file passes on CI**: `worker-connection.test.ts` runs green (26/26) on `checks-node-changed-5` in the same run.
- None of the failing test files import `worker-connection`, `admissionDeadline`, or `connectUntilReady`; the changed files (`src/worker/worker-connection.*`) have zero overlap with the failing tests.

`src/worker/worker-connection.test.ts` — the only test that exercises this change — is green on CI (26/26). The missing `session-transcript.worker.mjs` bundle is an environment/build artifact issue in the CI runner, independent of this PR.

**Exact-head CI result (head `479454ac`, run 39010191758):** the three bundle-missing shards (6/15/19) **passed on this exact-head run** — confirming the `session-transcript.worker.mjs` failure is an intermittent environment/build issue, not a deterministic defect. The only remaining failures on the exact head are `checks-node-changed-1` (`auth-profile-rotation.e2e`) and `checks-node-changed-3` (`model-fallback.run-embedded.e2e`) — the same two unrelated `src/agents/` e2e tests that were already failing before this PR and never touch `worker-connection`/admission. Our own test stays green (26/26).

prs.title: fix(agents): ignore internal prompt-cache history metadata
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

During live sub-agent orchestration runs (Anthropic and OpenAI models on the embedded runtime), the prompt-cache observer warned on almost every parent turn:

```
[agent/embedded] [prompt-cache] message 3 (toolResult) differs from the previous request; history must be append-only; changed fields: envelope.__openclaw
```

48 warnings across four Gateways, always the same shape. They are false: provider usage on the warned session shows the cache prefix intact (Anthropic `cacheRead` 0 → 25509 → 30244 → 33195 on the warned request → 35884 → 41768 → 43217). The warning sends operators chasing cache breaks that did not happen and pollutes cache-break attribution.

## User Impact

Prompt-cache observability no longer reports false history rewrites when OpenClaw updates internal tool-result metadata. Genuine content, signature, and tool-call identity rewrites remain detectable. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Root cause

`persistCodeModeCheckpoint` (`src/agents/code-mode-checkpoint.ts`) adds `__openclaw.codeModeCheckpoint` to the stored tool result during transcript canonicalization. The history fingerprint (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/prompt-cache-history.ts`) hashed that persistence-only envelope, so the change looked like a history rewrite. The OpenAI Responses, Anthropic Messages, and Codex tool-result payload builders construct explicit payloads without that envelope, so it never reaches a provider.

### Fix

History fingerprints skip the top-level `__openclaw` envelope (content is still hashed separately). Content, signature, and tool-call identity checks are unchanged, so genuine rewrites still fail the append-only check. `docs/reference/prompt-caching.md` notes the distinction.

## Evidence

- Live: two parallel 8-child Opus fleets on an isolated Gateway built from this branch logged 0 `[prompt-cache]` warnings; the same workload on main logs the warning on each parent. Cache reads stay monotonic.
- `pnpm test src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/prompt-cache-observability.history.test.ts`: red on main (`changed fields: envelope.__openclaw`), 36/36 with the fix; `prompt-cache-observability.test.ts` 29/29.
- Targeted format, lint, and type checks pass.

## Release note context

Fix: prompt-cache observability no longer reports false history rewrites when OpenClaw updates internal tool-result metadata.

### CI inherited-failure evidence

[CI run 39193653666, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39193653666) passed the selected test, type, lint, SDK/package-boundary, docs, and independent security checks. The sole failing job, `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets`, reports an export-preservation violation at `test/scripts/ci-node-test-plan.test.ts:3297` for `../../scripts/lib/ci-test-timings.mts`; the aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` fails downstream.

The automated failure table labels this new against scheduled main run 39191176869 because that earlier main job passed. Independent reproduction on the exact CI main baseline `d5aeceb2b89e253ba15d41976d0618e31842fb48` with `pnpm check:test-mock-exports --base d5aeceb2b89e253ba15d41976d0618e31842fb48 --no-merge-base` fails with the identical file, line, and module diagnostic. CI tested merge `76f759b92b904fdb5169289b3832fd2013b5e542` has that baseline and the reviewed PR head as its ordered parents; its delta contains only this PR's four files. The failing test, checker, and baseline are unchanged by this PR. Landing uses the owner's explicitly authorized native inherited-failure exception; failed CI remains recorded as failed.

prs.title: fix: prevent service CA warnings after the installer Gateway exits
prs.body:
Closes #176479

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a managed Gateway service retaining a temporary certificate bundle from the Gateway that launched its installer, then reporting a missing extra-CA file after that Gateway exits.

## User Impact

New service installs use durable startup trust. Running `openclaw gateway install --force` with the fixed version also repairs an existing affected service. Operator-provided corporate CA files remain preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Service environment construction excludes the reserved temporary egress-CA path. The install environment merge applies the same rule to both inherited and previously persisted values, preserving an existing corporate CA when the installer inherited a temporary bundle. Runtime proxy trust and existing platform TLS defaults retain their current behavior.

The branch also includes the test compatibility repair tracked in #176834: the parent-retention regression uses the completion-delivery owner's existing five-second retry policy instead of a removed test-only option. That inherited `check-test-types` failure is resolved; the same repair has since landed upstream. A subsequent upstream CI fixture also now preserves real timing-module exports with typed `importOriginal`, satisfying the mock-export check while retaining its fixed measurements and capacity assertions. Neither CI repair changes production behavior.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on base `28212a985c15ae53b22b77dabecbfdfc1ee9d632` with a real isolated foreground Gateway and a separate systemd user service. The real installer persisted the foreground Gateway's generated CA path. After stopping that Gateway, restarting the service emitted `Warning: Ignoring extra certs ... No such file or directory`.
- On this branch, a real install omitted the foreground Gateway's temporary CA; a corporate CA survived reinstall from the same temporary-CA environment. After the foreground Gateway exited and removed its bundle, the service restarted with HTTP 200 health and zero extra-cert warnings in that systemd invocation's journal.
- Upgrade validation passed from official `openclaw@2026.10.5`: the affected service was force-reinstalled with the candidate using its original state, the stale CA entry was removed, and `/healthz` returned HTTP 200.
- Regression tests fail on the base and pass with the fix. Passed 158 focused and consumer tests covering environment merging, TLS defaults, Gateway/Node service builders, installation, install planning, and runtime pinning, plus the runtime build, core and services-test typechecks, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check`.
- Runtime validation used Linux/systemd and Node 24.19.0. It supplied the real Gateway-generated CA through the actual install CLI environment; it did not exercise model-hosted `exec`. macOS, Windows, and Bun were not run locally.
- CI repair: run [39192062972](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39192062972) failed with TS2353 in a parent-retention test added to upstream main. The original four CA files are unchanged by the base integration; the additional test repair removes the retired option and advances the fake clock to the actual first retry.
- On the integrated repair head, all 38 tests across the parent-retention, service-environment, and install-environment suites pass. The affected test passes targeted TypeScript and type-aware lint checks, formatting, and `git diff --check`. Full local extension typechecking was limited by dependencies omitted from this worktree’s filtered installation; [CI run 39193668013](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39193668013/job/117872290911) confirmed the full extension test typecheck passed on `cb4ab0ebfd0527ab859802577b8bc02383ae3505`.

- The next CI run exposed an upstream mock-export violation in `test/scripts/ci-node-test-plan.test.ts`. The exact guard fails before the two-line fixture repair and passes afterward (`Mock factory ratchet OK: 8512 grandfathered factories`). All 145 tests in the affected CI planning suite pass, along with targeted TypeScript/type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check`. No baseline allowance or test assertion was changed.

- Final CI on `92fdcba008a9386835277aa06ed43e3c393f9271`: [run 39195065343](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39195065343) completed successfully with 38 successful jobs, including `check-test-types`, `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets`, and `openclaw/ci-gate`.

<details>
<summary>Sanitized CLI/systemd runtime evidence</summary>

These are excerpts from the original isolated runtime replay at `7dd6440676ba8363846462b0fa1de9b9d0a05f10`; the CA implementation is unchanged in the CI repair. `<proof-root>` replaces the local task directory. No credentials or endpoint details are included.

Base service unit and its journal after the source Gateway stopped and the installed service restarted:

```text
Environment=NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=<proof-root>/a/secret-egress-proxy/gateway-9CV5sL/trust-bundle.pem
Warning: Ignoring extra certs from `<proof-root>/a/secret-egress-proxy/gateway-9CV5sL/trust-bundle.pem`, load failed: error:80000002:system library::No such file or directory
```

Candidate service unit after reinstall with the source Gateway's temporary CA in the install environment:

```text
Environment=NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=<proof-root>/corporate-ca.pem
```

Recorded candidate replay result (fresh install, corporate CA preservation, source shutdown, then installed-service restart):

```json
{
  "commit": "7dd6440676ba8363846462b0fa1de9b9d0a05f10",
  "freshEgressInstallOmitsCa": true,
  "corporateCaPreserved": true,
  "sourceBundleDeleted": true,
  "restartHealth": {
    "ok": true,
    "status": "live"
  },
  "restartCaWarnings": 0
}
```

Recorded upgrade of the same state database created by official `2026.10.5`:

```json
{
  "stableVersion": "2026.10.5",
  "baseSchema": 20,
  "candidateSchema": 28,
  "health": {
    "ok": true,
    "status": "live"
  },
  "transientCaRemoved": true
}
```

The candidate restart and upgrade journals both record Gateway readiness with zero `Ignoring extra certs` warnings. This proves service environment persistence, successful restart, and state loading after upgrade on Linux/systemd. Corporate CA validation covers preservation and loading; direct HTTPS peer acceptance/rejection was not exercised. The generated source Gateway bundle was passed through the real install CLI environment manually; model-hosted `exec` was not exercised.

</details>

prs.title: fix(state): rebuild stale FTS indexes during agent database admission
prs.body:
Refs #176220. Follow-up to #176234.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: agent sessions are quarantined at Gateway startup after a SQLite tokenizer change leaves only OpenClaw's canonical FTS indexes stale, even though Doctor can safely rebuild them.

## User Impact

Gateway startup backs up and rebuilds eligible FTS indexes automatically, preserving stored rows and admitting the agent after integrity verification. One warning reports the agent, tables, row counts, SQLite version, and backup. Status and Doctor retain the startup outcome. Failed backups or rebuilds, mixed or unknown findings, and live foreign writers retain quarantine and the precise Doctor command.

## Why This Change Was Made

The agent database admission owner invokes a startup-only callback from the existing worker maintenance owner, which calls the Doctor classifier, verified snapshot, and synchronous transactional repair entry point. FTS schema and repair SQL remain outside the trusted PR wrapper import closure. The existing startup preparation and opening lease restrict the repair to startup, while the shared-state write fence excludes foreign writers. The host admission owner records one attempt per physical database per process, including across worker replacement.

Ordinary runtime opens keep their existing behavior. No schema, dependency, configuration, or CLI changes.

## Evidence

- Regression was red before the fix at the real Gateway startup admission boundary: canonical FTS-only damage produced `agent-database-inspection-failed` and the offline Doctor command. The new regression retains that same fixture.
- Focused Node and pinned Bun runs: **77 tests / 7 files passed** on each runtime. The startup test verifies retained session/FTS rows, clean integrity, a backup containing the original mismatch, one warning, and the one-attempt bound. Mixed findings, failed backup/rebuild, and foreign writer cases retain quarantine and actionable guidance.
- Core and state-test typechecks, direct production/test oxlint, oxfmt, `git diff --check`, and madge (0 cycles) passed. The lint wrapper's Plugin SDK declaration preparation exceeded 300 seconds; direct lint of touched files passed. One obsolete complete-mock baseline entry is pruned; no baseline growth or suppressions.
- Independent isolated production review: no actionable finding. Fresh independent review of the two consumer-fixture repairs: no actionable finding. The original final full-diff review service attempt returned capacity failure. The subsequent CI-repair diff received a clean isolated P2 review. Direct reuse of Doctor's repair owner keeps production at **+211/-44 (net +167)**, tests **+301/-21 (net +280, including routing)**, docs **+14/-8**. The final two fixture repairs preserve the real lifecycle factory in a partial mock and move cold Gateway handler/module preparation outside behavior deadlines, without changing any assertion or timeout.
- Controlled auth regression comparison, Node 26.12.0: clean `origin/main` at `6ae64b5d43bf` **5/5 failed** (4, 1, 2, 1, 5 tests); committed WIP at `b5e147e40433` **3/5 failed** (2, 3, 0, 1, 0 tests). Every failure was `Spawn broker shutdown failed` → `DarwinProcessInspectionError`. Runs used physical private installs, the same command, separate state, and alternating order. The passing focused run is not claimed as a fix for that defect.
- Rebased onto main at `48c6cfe1d17a`. Repaired consumer fixtures passed **19/19 on Node and pinned Bun**. The 13 lifecycle tests fell from 574.5s to 143.5s of measured test time on Node; the former worker/main recovery failures now pass in 27.6s/15.9s (Bun: 37.6s/15.2s). Real fresh Gateway starts still account for the file’s >120s test time. The 162-file importing-consumer selection completed in 8,629s, including shared compilation/setup. Its original run reported 2,396 passed / 2 failed / 56 configured skips plus the env-capture suite-load failure; the two failing files were then repaired and passed 19/19 on each runtime. Every other consumer group passed, with no unhandled errors. The opt-in E2E and PostgreSQL skips are unchanged. Final clean-head `pnpm build:runtime` passed in 110.5s. Live built Gateway on isolated HOME/state and port 51623: `sessions.list` returned `l1690-retained`; status recorded the redacted repair notice; exactly one warning reported `agent main`, `session_transcript_fts=1`, and SQLite 3.54.0. Database integrity is `ok`, the FTS row is unchanged, and the single backup retains both that row and the original tokenizer mismatch. The owned Gateway stopped cleanly and its port is closed.

<details>
<summary>Commands and timings</summary>

Every test, build, and live proof used an isolated `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, and `TMPDIR` under this worktree's `.artifacts/`, with `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES` set at the temporary root. No operator state or Gateway was used.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/sqlite-readonly-worker.auth.test.ts
# 5 alternating repetitions on clean main and committed WIP

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/sqlite-readonly-worker.auth.test.ts src/infra/sqlite-fts-integrity.test.ts src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite.fts-recovery.test.ts src/state/openclaw-database-preflight.startup-fts.test.ts src/infra/sqlite-integrity.test.ts src/infra/sqlite-index-corruption.test.ts src/infra/sqlite-index-schema.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
# Node: 77 passed, 605.8s wrapper; pinned Bun 1.4.4 / SQLite 3.54.0: 77 passed, 312.4s wrapper
# Bun selected with OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun and OPENCLAW_BUN_PATH pointing to the repository pin.

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/state/openclaw-agent-db-write.env-capture.test.ts src/gateway/server-agent-database-startup.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
# Node and pinned Bun: 19 passed each; no retries or timeout changes.

node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.state-logging.json
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-server.json
```

An additional final Node startup run passed 5/5: 199.3s test file / 459.5s wrapper, including 214.1s worker preparation; successful test 47.2s. Its diagnostic stack was in `fs.realpathSync`/ESM resolution. The retained cold fixture also passed on Bun (success 10.2s; negative cases 4.6–8.0s). Doctor's Bun file took 120.2s, with only ~17s in tests and ~96s in transform. No timeout, retry, skip, or weakened assertion was added.

Unchanged slow consumers were retained under the campaign ruling: `session-group-mutation-targets.test.ts` cases took 99.2s/100.8s/42.8s (foreign source subprocess discovery across group members); `session-row-projection.config-commits.test.ts` took 42.8s (multiple session writes and reloads); two `update-database-backup.test.ts` custody cases took 41.8s/35.7s. Recovery, migration, and health files accumulate >120s across many short real lifecycle cases. These timings are host observations, not benchmarks. Additional inherited slow-file timings are below.


Live commands (with isolated `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, and `TMPDIR`; the configured Gateway target uses the same private port):

```sh
pnpm build:runtime
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs .artifacts/seed-live.mts
pnpm openclaw gateway run --port 51623
pnpm --silent openclaw gateway call sessions.list --params '{"agentId":"main","limit":10}' --json --timeout 20000

```

The fixture reused `installSqliteFtsTokenizerMismatch` from #176234. The live checker compared all FTS row values with the seed and verified both current and backup integrity findings. Two probe assumptions were corrected before the final clean run: URL overrides require credentials, so the call uses the isolated configured target; auth-free status correctly returns a redacted repair notice rather than the full path-bearing log text. No production changes resulted from either probe correction.

</details>

The auth-worker failure is tracked by [the proc-safe native fix](https://github.com/openclaw/proc-safe/pull/23) and [OpenClaw adoption PR #176612](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176612). proc-safe 0.4.1 returns incomplete topology while an unrelated process is exiting with `P_WEXIT`; the shared Darwin owner then refuses the broker shutdown census. No cleanup checks or test assertions are weakened here, and this PR does not change the dependency.

The broad SQLite inventory step of `check:changed` is skipped under the local gate time budget; targeted checks and PR CI provide the remaining proof.

<details>
<summary>Inherited slow consumers (local test time)</summary>

These files are unchanged. Doctor/backup cases perform real backed-up migrations; recovery/health/index files exercise multiple fresh lifecycles. Recorded under the campaign ruling to retain pre-existing slow suites.

## CI follow-up for 75f111b9

prs.title: feat(feishu): adopt the shared progress-draft compositor on the streaming card
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Feishu was the only preview-capable bundled channel that did not use the shared progress-draft compositor. It rendered a single replaceable tool status line that could only attach to an already-started answer card (when no streaming session existed, `renderMode !== "card"` dropped it), and it ignored `onItemEvent` / `onPlanUpdate` / `onApprovalEvent` / `onCommandOutput` / `onPatchSummary`. Mid-turn, a Feishu DM stayed visually silent until the final answer began streaming (#147895).

This adopts the same engine the Telegram/Discord/Slack/Mattermost/MS Teams progress drafts use (`createChannelProgressDraftCompositor`) and completes the alignment based on live-gateway validation:

- **Lazy draft creation**: the streaming card starts on the first work event (tool, plan, approval) or streamed text, replacing the eager `onReplyStart` placeholder card. Quick Q&A turns no longer flash an empty card.
- **Progress ownership declaration**: `suppressDefaultToolProgressMessages: true` while the preview is active. Core only forwards the quiet progress callbacks (`onToolStart`, `onItemEvent`, `onPlanUpdate`, `onCommandOutput`, compaction) to channels that declare ownership of progress display when tool summaries are hidden — without this flag the draft receives no events at all (verified live: zero callbacks before the flag, rolling tool lines after).
- **Draft rendering**: rolling tool lines, the plan checklist, approval lines, command-output ends, and patch summaries render through the shared compact progress formatter into the card's status slot.
- **Finalization**: the finalized card keeps only the committed answer by default (`streaming.finalize: "overwrite"`), matching the other draft channels. `streaming.finalize: "append"` opts into retaining the rolling tool lines above the final answer behind a `· · ·` separator; the rotating status label ("Working" and friends) is dropped either way since it marks an in-flight turn.
- **Lifecycle guards**: a committed final stops the draft so late events cannot spawn a phantom card, while a mid-turn retraction (`deleteCurrent`) keeps the draft armed for continued work. Progress callbacks stay unregistered when preview streaming is suppressed (outbound bot mentions, `renderMode: "raw"`, modifying hooks) — unchanged.
- Includes the block-streaming policy fix from #147897 (an unset `channels.feishu.streaming.block` follows `agents.defaults.blockStreamingDefault` instead of being hard-disabled), since mid-turn visibility needs both paths. Supersedes #147897.

## Config

New key `channels.feishu.streaming.finalize`: `"overwrite"` (default) | `"append"`. Documented in `docs/channels/feishu/advanced-configuration.md`; schema in `extensions/feishu/src/config-schema.ts`. The key raises the channel config-surface budget from 3730 to 3732 (`docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json`), raised consciously per the config-surface bar: it is the first Feishu-side control for retaining mid-turn progress on the finalized card and mirrors the retention question raised for the other draft channels.

## Evidence

- `vitest run -c test/vitest/vitest.extension-feishu.config.ts`: 2089 passed. The one failure in `setup-surface.test.ts` ("prompts over SecretRef appId/appSecret config objects") reproduces on the base commit without these changes.
- Delivery-level tests in `reply-dispatcher.test.ts`: the card starts on the first tool event and rolls progress text; plan checklist steps render; **no placeholder card is created on reply start**; **append finalize keeps the tool lines above the answer behind a separator**; final close carries the answer only and stops the draft (a late tool event spawns no phantom card); the no-visible-reply fallback still fires after an empty card close under the lazy model; modifying hooks keep all progress callbacks unregistered.
- **Visual evidence** (real Feishu DM screenshots from the validating deployment):

- Before (stock `2026.9.4`): eager placeholder card stays empty for the whole turn — [screenshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Decent9967/openclaw/pr-assets-148176/assets/148176/feishu-before-empty-card.png)
- After (this PR): multi-tool turn finalizing with rolling progress retained above the `· · ·` separator and the answer below — [screenshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Decent9967/openclaw/pr-assets-148176/assets/148176/feishu-after-final-card.png)
- Live-text contrast: the same model turn renders live in CLI consumers while channels historically stayed silent — tracked with diagnostics in #132615 (text-only reference; the earlier screenshot attachment was dropped for exposing operational details)

Live validation on a production gateway (2 users, real multi-minute tasks): lazy creation confirmed (card first appears at the first tool event, ~69s into one turn), tool lines stream during execution, append finalize retains progress, final answer lands in the card.

## Notes for reviewers

- The shard16 startup-error test was flaky-red on #147897 while passing locally and on unrelated PRs; control-ui-performance sits ~66B over its bundle budget with zero UI files in the diff. Both reproduce independently of this change.
- Known upstream limitation (not addressed here): on the embedded agent runtime with the zai provider, text partials never reach channel callbacks even with this PR — tool/plan/approval events stream fine, text lands at turn end. Filing separately with the diagnostic trail.



# Production acceptance-recovery drill (2026-09-15, live gateway + real DM turn)
# Timeline (operator-controlled DNS/egress outage via iptables REJECT --reject-with tcp-reset):
11:21:00  POST /cardkit/v1/cards -> card created (cardId=<card-1>)  [Started streaming]
11:21:13  OUTAGE START (all resolved open.feishu.cn addresses rejected, 32 addrs)
2026-09-15T11:21:41.275+08:00  PUT /cardkit/.../elements/content/content -> Update failed: TypeError: fetch failed
2026-09-15T11:21:41.283+08:00  PUT /cardkit/.../elements/content/content -> Update failed: TypeError: fetch failed
2026-09-15T11:21:41.442+08:00  PUT /cardkit/.../elements/content/content -> Update failed: TypeError: fetch failed
11:21:43  OUTAGE END (rules removed)
11:21:5x  Card content writes resume; card closes with the full answer  [Closed streaming: cardId=<card-1>]
11:22:27  Final reply delivered to the DM (delivered message observed via im/v1/messages)

## Raw session log lines (redacted: host, trace ids, file paths)
feishu[default]: dispatch complete (queuedFinal=true, replies=1)
feishu[default]: dispatch complete (queuedFinal=true, replies=1)
feishu[default] Started streaming: cardId=<card-1>, messageId=<om-1>
feishu[default] Update failed: TypeError: fetch failed
feishu[default] Update failed: TypeError: fetch failed
feishu[default] Update failed: TypeError: fetch failed
feishu[default] Closed streaming: cardId=<card-1>
feishu[default]: dispatch complete (queuedFinal=true, replies=1)

## Evidence notes

The acceptance-recovery path is covered three ways: the wire-level golden `recovered-content-rejection.trace.jsonl` (real dispatcher wiring, replayed in CI), dispatcher/session regression tests (rejected-write retry, coalescing, observer ordering), and the production drill above (a genuine 30s egress outage against the live gateway; the card content writes were rejected mid-stream and the card still closed with the full answer).

# Live mid-turn block drill (2026-09-15, real DM turns per config state; restored after)

- **Inherited-on emits mid-turn messages.** `streaming.mode="off"` (preview off), channel block key unset, `agents.defaults.blockStreamingDefault="on"`: a plan-first narration turn (message tools forbidden in the prompt) delivered the model's pre-tool-call plan as its own mid-turn `🛠` message alongside the final — chat timestamps `16:26:25` (final) / `16:26:27` (block); on the deployed v2026.9.4 core the progress flush coalesces to turn end, so the block lands ~2s after the final while carrying text authored before the tool call.
- **Explicit-off kept emitting — real gap caught by this drill, fixed in 047513ebc.** With `streaming.block.enabled=false` the `🛠` mid-turn message still arrived (`16:30:40` for the `16:29:29` turn): with preview off, nothing declared ownership of mid-turn progress. `c4f0ed77` first targeted `suppressDefaultToolProgressMessages`, but that flag only governs quiet progress-callback forwarding; verbose progress messages are gated by `suppressToolProgressMessages` (`dispatch-from-config.choose-route.ts:100-102`). `047513ebc` sets `suppressToolProgressMessages: !previewStreamingEnabled && !blockStreamingEnabled` with two regressions pinning the flag; extension suite 202/202.
- **Version-skew note:** the post-merge branch requires the matching core build — rebuilt against v2026.9.4 the Feishu WebSocket fails at connect (newer SDK runtime symbol), so the live drill ran on the pre-merge extension build that carries the same block-policy wiring this PR finalizes.
- **Matching-core drill (main @ `ed264cc3c` + this branch's extension build):** inherited-on with verbose progress emits the 💬 commentary message and 🛠️ tool line mid-turn, before the final card (chat timestamps 23:44:22 inbound → 💬 23:44:31 → 🛠️ 23:44:32 → final 23:44:40); with verbose off (the default) three real turns produced exactly one final message each — no upgrade-time message spray. Explicit-off did **not** suppress the verbose lane on the live gateway (💬+🛠️ still preceded the final under `block.enabled=false`) on either core generation: the lane delivering these messages in real turns is not gated by channel `replyOptions` — see the drill comment for the full matrix and what that means for the commentary owner decision.
- Full timeline and methodology (including the first round discarded because the model reported steps through its own message tool, which bypasses channel policy): see the drill comment thread.

prs.title: experiment(control-ui): gate owner prewarm on intent [do not merge]
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A signed-in reload prepares the closed header session menu's owner-assignment roster and avatars through recursive idle prewarm. The reported renderer accounted for approximately 102 ms inclusive in the live trace. The previous whole-menu intent gate removed the work but failed the reload and first-open gates.

This single follow-up keeps idle preparation of plain root entries and gates only owner preparation on pointer entry or focus on the menu trigger. Explicit opening still constructs the current owner choices. No configuration, storage, or shared overlay lifecycle changes.

## Evidence

Experiment in progress; do not merge. Candidate head: `fdbcd5ba7382b17cc92538f65a7a5297ef49d768`. Autoreview is clean through P2.

Before measurements: 11 interleaved baseline/candidate pairs for both warm chat and dashboard reloads, one quiet AWS c7a.4xlarge, repository Chromium, faithful Team-scale fixture with 48 offline avatar owners and Online sidebar, five-second capture, LoAF/mutation and RPC census probes.

Primary: LoAF blocking must improve on at least one route with non-overlapping IQRs or at least 9/11 improving pairs and a negative median paired delta. Neither route may regress: non-overlapping worse IQRs, or at least 9/11 worse pairs with a paired median rise exceeding max(10 ms, 3%). Closed owner/avatar nodes target zero and avatar requests approximately 67 fewer. Report FCP and all paired deltas.

Owner-menu first-frame p50 after intent must be at most 16 ms slower than baseline with identical intent. Also report cold owner opening without prior trigger pointer/focus intent. Each run measures cold opening, then restores the warm snapshot and reloads before measuring pointer-intent opening, without an artificial hover dwell.

Focused header suite: 27 passed (46.45 s wall time on the loaded local host). Full remote results, review, and performance verdict pending. This PR will only become ready if the experiment passes.

prs.title: fix: show delegated task PRs in session previews
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the parent sidebar and session hovercard omitting PRs published by delegated child sessions.

## User Impact

- Show a task PR count before hover, including sessions without a worktree.
- Show up to 20 recorded publications from accessible descendants, with branch attribution and live status when available.
- Keep known links across checkout changes and Gateway restarts; preserve the parent branch's own publication controls.

## Why This Change Was Made

Project existing publication receipts through indexed session lineage instead of scanning conversations or adding another source of truth. A bounded, viewer-scoped subscription serves receipt-only sidebar rows; only active views fetch Git/GitHub metadata. Receipt commits and lineage changes refresh the existing owner. No schema migration, config option, or transcript backfill is needed.

Branch publication evidence remains separate from task presentation. Full-set counts stay correct even when the 20-item preview is truncated. Receipt-only updates preserve known branch facts and enriched task status without reviving an authoritatively cleared badge or polling GitHub. The existing prepared-read owner handles branch-fact retention; no new state owner is introduced.

## Evidence

- Real Gateway/Chromium regression reproduced the missing cold parent badge on the base. The fixed flow shows three persisted descendant PRs while leaving the parent's Create PR action independent. Passive hydration makes zero GitHub calls; active metadata survives an isolated Gateway restart.
- Real socket proof covers two viewer scopes, personal/shared visibility, private-descendant removal, and revocation during a held read. Both tests pass again with LIVE_GITHUB=1 on the final integrated product tree.
- Feature verification includes 168 affected UI/store/sidebar/locale/GitHub-settings tests and 44 i18n tooling tests. Core/UI types, i18n verification, lint, formatting, and independent P0–P2 review passed. CI repairs preserve catalog-only badges, canonical record coercion, and distinct overflow counts without broadening passive read admission.
- Performance: settings-only GitHub and skill-editor English stay at their cold consumers; full task-row construction stays in the hovercard. Cold-import regressions fail before and pass after the splits; shared keys, identities, copy, and foreign overrides are preserved. The ineffective renderer-import experiment was reverted. Final strict comparison against main13969119: startup **337,951 / 339,379 B**, chat **1,489,840 / 1,490,000 B** (**1,768 B below base**), New Session **1,049,623 / 1,050,000 B**, all gzip. No budgets or baselines were raised.
- Selected-singleton CI planner repair preserves the existing two-worker ceiling and all capacity/time budgets; deterministic regression fails before the fix. All 183 planner/capacity tests and 115 affected consumer tests pass, retaining exact group metadata, runner, timing, and price assertions. The timing mock preserves real exports through importOriginal.
- Concurrent-main integration repairs: retained the canonical root-help mock fix; completed the sidebar memo import migration; updated the native parent-retention test to the canonical 5,000 ms retry; included the conditional revision in exact page-query fixtures; aligned model-help assertions with current English. Each failure was reproduced before repair. Relevant checks pass: 19 attention/projection tests, 21 native parent/custody tests, all four session-filter browser cases, and the full model-help scenario across light/dark and narrow layout. Required type/lint/format checks and independent reviews pass; no production timing/permission contract was relaxed.
- Historical local limitation: backend integration recorded **145 passed, 1 existing platform skip, 2 investigated baseline work-count failures**. Unchanged cases in control-ui-session-prs-branch.test.ts observed 3 and 30 reads rather than 0 on both base ff2580ae and candidate, with correct returned PR facts. No assertion or skip was weakened. Prior failed CI runs are not claimed green; current exact-head CI remains the landing gate.
- Final conflict resolution retains canonical main session-query assertions; all 5 query/model-help browser cases, 297 planner/capacity/consumer tests, e2e/script types, formatting, and both LIVE_GITHUB tests pass. Qualified-capacity timing mock also uses importOriginal; the exact mock-export ratchet, 182 planner/capacity tests, script types/lint/format and independent review pass. Production code is unchanged from the preceding live/bundle proof. Exact-head CI is pending at **0c335cbb**.

prs.title: refactor(config): reuse captured path and identity checks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Config writes repeat the same captured filesystem path proof immediately before the publication owner checks it again. Topology and installation identity preparation also normalize values that are already canonical within the same invocation.

## User Impact

Config writes perform fewer path traversals and normalizations while preserving rollback safety, fixed session-store ownership, input immutability, service isolation and session-catalog disclosure checks. No public SDK contract changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Let assertPublishedIdentity own its captured target-path traversal. Keep eager owner admission and the returned rollback closure's owner/path checks at later effects. Reuse tryResolveDefaultAgentId's canonical result, spread sessionStore only after its existing undefined-or-record admission, and normalize account home once for both the OS-home and OPENCLAW_HOME comparisons.

Production +7/-12, net -5 lines across four modules; no test edits. Two duplicate filesystem traversal classes, two redundant agent-ID normalizations, one repeated record guard and one repeated account-home normalization are removed. Actual traversal syscall counts depend on path depth. No intended SQL, request, transaction, schema, service-policy or PostgreSQL-bookkeeping changes. Expected SQL/request/MAIN delta is 0/0/0, estimated and unmeasured. One final lane baseline/candidate pair covering all five deletion PRs remains pending. No measurement waiver or latency claim.

Accepted edge: captured canonical agent IDs remain immutable strings, and account-home normalization is reused only within the synchronous identity check. There is no shared cache or new guarantee about filesystem changes between invocations. Publication identity, owner revocation, symlink/hardlink, concurrent-edit and later rollback checks remain.

## Evidence

Changed-file formatting, type-aware lint and whitespace checks pass. Independent Codex review completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings; final source verification passed. Selected owner/consumer tests, repository tsrs typechecking, Madge, Knip, T1/dialect/worker ratchets and the published-driver update cell remain pending on the final candidate. Earlier PR proof does not validate this source. The update cell is required because `assertGatewayServiceMutationAllowed` (`src/infra/gateway-supervision.ts:55`) calls the changed install-identity owner for service admission.

CI targets cover include/root writes and compensation, paths/service rebind, session-catalog home isolation, paired-source writes, fixed-store ownership and deferred migrations. No specifically located real-writer fixture covers the no-owner/previous-sole-agent-removed topology branch; the complete producer/writer contracts are supplied for review and that coverage limitation remains explicit. No successful test or measurement result is claimed.

<details>
<summary>Candidate ledger</summary>

| Candidate | Decision | Owner/caller evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| C16146 (g) | REMOVE | The immediately called publication-identity owner invokes the exact captured path proof first. |
| C16081 (b) | REMOVE | Both default-agent resolver branches already return canonical IDs; reuse the result twice. |
| C16196 (b) | REMOVE | Normalize account home once and keep both independent home comparisons. |
| Eager rollback path traversal (unnumbered companion) | REMOVE | Keep the owner check; the next publication-identity call performs the same traversal. The later rollback closure remains unchanged. |
| Session-store spread guard (unnumbered companion) | REMOVE | The enclosing condition already admits only undefined or a record. |
| Post-await/publication/rollback authority | KEEP | These checks protect real effects and later compensation. |
| Filesystem identity and both home comparisons | KEEP | They protect real path, concurrent-edit, service and disclosure boundaries. |

Three static IDs (two b, one g) and two unnumbered companion operations are selected. These are the selected removals in this PR.

</details>

prs.title: fix(config): preserve whitespace in secrets provider file paths
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw config set … --provider-source file --provider-path` trims the path before writing `secrets.providers.*.path`, so a credential file whose name ends in a space is silently rewritten to a neighboring path (or a missing path). The same trim hits `--provider-command` and `--provider-trusted-dir`, and resolution/exec validation previously re-trimmed via `resolveUserPath`, so a whitespace-bearing trusted directory could authorize the wrong neighbor executable.

## User Impact

User impact: provider builder paths keep their literal whitespace (matching `--batch-file` / `connect --target-file`), so trailing-space filenames no longer retarget the wrong secret file on disk. Whitespace-bearing `trustedDirs` authorize only executables literally inside that directory; the nearest neighbor without the trailing space is rejected before process creation. Ordinary paths without edge whitespace are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildProviderConfig` used `opts.providerPath?.trim()` (and `.trim()` on command / `normalizeStringEntries` on trusted dirs) before persisting into config. File/exec resolution used trimming `resolveUserPath`. Alix’s `#167116` already preserved connect target-file literals via `readNonBlankString`; this applies the same contract to the secrets provider builder and adds `resolveUserPathLiteral` for resolution + `assertSecureExecCommandPath`.

## Evidence

- Changed: `src/cli/config-cli-input.ts`, `src/infra/home-dir.ts` (`resolveUserPathLiteral`), `src/secrets/exec-provider-path-validation.ts`, `src/secrets/resolve.ts`; regressions in `src/cli/config-cli.test.ts`, `src/infra/home-dir.test.ts`, `src/secrets/resolve.test.ts`
- Packaged CLI on head `bd8f2287fe3`: **shipped file-provider consume** (literal path beats distinguishable neighbor) + **real upgrade from npm `openclaw@2026.10.5`** (same `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`: file+exec providers still load/validate/resolve) + exec allow/deny-before-start (below)
- Dedup: no open PR on provider-path whitespace; distinct from Alix `#167116` (connect only) and `#167118` (UTF-8 config bytes)

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

1. `--provider-path` ending in a space must be stored literally.
2. **Shipped CLI must consume that literal file-provider path** (not a trimmed neighbor): `node openclaw.mjs config set … --dry-run` → `resolveSecretRefValue` → `readSecureFile(resolveUserPathLiteral(path))`.
3. Existing `secrets.providers` written by published **v2026.10.5** must still load, validate, and resolve after upgrading the same state dir to this PR head.
4. (Already shown) Whitespace-bearing trustedDirs authorize only the literal helper; neighbor rejected before process creation.

### Canonical reachability path (file-provider consume)

Packaged `node openclaw.mjs config set secrets.providers.<alias> --provider-source file --provider-path '<path with trailing space>' --provider-mode json` → persist literal path → `config set channels.discord.token --ref-provider <alias> --ref-source file --ref-id /token --dry-run --json` → `collectDryRunResolvabilityErrors` → `resolveSecretRefValue` → `readFileProviderPayload` / `resolveUserPathLiteral` → `readSecureFile`.

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Uses `readNonBlankString` for builder persistence and `resolveUserPathLiteral` for file (and exec) resolution. No direct library `resolveSecretRefString` call in this proof — only the packaged CLI entrypoint.

### Real environment tested

Packaged CLI (`node openclaw.mjs`, OpenClaw 2026.9.9) on head `bd8f2287fe3` with Node v24.16.0; temporary `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`. Paths redacted to `/tmp/oc168261.*/…`.

### Exact steps — shipped file-provider consume + neighbor

```bash
# Node 24.16+ (packaged CLI) on head bd8f2287fe3
ROOT=$(mktemp -d /tmp/oc168261.XXXXXX)
STATE=$(mktemp -d /tmp/oc168261-state.XXXXXX)
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$STATE" OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$STATE/openclaw.json"
SECRET_SPACE="$ROOT/secret "          # trailing space
SECRET_NEIGHBOR="$ROOT/secret"        # no trailing space
printf '%s\n' '{"token":"GOOD"}' > "$SECRET_SPACE"
printf '%s\n' 'NOT_JSON_WRONG' > "$SECRET_NEIGHBOR"   # distinguishable: INVALID JSON
chmod 600 "$SECRET_SPACE" "$SECRET_NEIGHBOR"

node openclaw.mjs config set secrets.providers.vault \
  --provider-source file --provider-path "$SECRET_SPACE" --provider-mode json

# Shipped consume (resolvability via packaged dry-run — neighbor is invalid JSON)
node openclaw.mjs config set channels.discord.token \
  --ref-provider vault --ref-source file --ref-id /token --dry-run --json

# Flip: corrupt spaced file; leave neighbor as VALID {"token":"WRONG"}
# Expect dry-run FAIL (still targets literal spaced path; trim would succeed via neighbor)
printf '%s\n' 'CORRUPT_NOT_JSON' > "$SECRET_SPACE"
printf '%s\n' '{"token":"WRONG"}' > "$SECRET_NEIGHBOR"
node openclaw.mjs config set channels.discord.token \
  --ref-provider vault --ref-source file --ref-id /token --dry-run --json
```

### Evidence after fix — shipped file-provider consume

```text
=== SETUP (file-provider consume) ===
node=v24.16.0
head=bd8f2287fe3
secret_space_repr= '/tmp/oc168261.*/secret '
secret_neighbor_repr= '/tmp/oc168261.*/secret'
space_content= {"token":"GOOD"}
neighbor_content= NOT_JSON_WRONG

=== A1) Persist file provider with trailing-space path ===
Updated secrets.providers.vault. No gateway restart needed.
stored_path_repr= '/tmp/oc168261.*/secret '
stored_source= file
stored_mode= json

=== A2) Shipped consume: config set --dry-run (neighbor INVALID JSON) ===
{
  "ok": true,
  "checks": { "resolvability": true, "resolvabilityComplete": true },
  "refsChecked": 1,
  "skippedExecRefs": 0
}
consume_dryrun_exit=0
# Success with invalid neighbor ⇒ packaged CLI read the literal spaced file (GOOD).

=== A3) Flip: spaced file CORRUPT; neighbor VALID {"token":"WRONG"} ===
{
  "ok": false,
  "errors": [{
    "kind": "resolvability",
    "message": "Unexpected token 'C', \"CORRUPT_NOT_JSON\\n\" is not valid JSON",
    "ref": "file:vault:/token"
  }]
}
flip_dryrun_exit=1
flip_result=DENIED_AS_EXPECTED (literal spaced path still targeted; neighbor not used)

=== A4) Restore spaced GOOD; consume green again ===
restore_ok= True
restore_dryrun_exit=0
```

### Exact steps — data-model compatibility / existing settings

```bash
# Simulate pre-fix stored settings (stable-style: no edge whitespace on provider path)
STATE2=$(mktemp -d /tmp/oc168261-compat.XXXXXX)
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$STATE2" OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$STATE2/openclaw.json"
LEGACY_SECRET="$ROOT/legacy-secret.json"
printf '%s\n' '{"apiKey":"LEGACY_OK"}' > "$LEGACY_SECRET" && chmod 600 "$LEGACY_SECRET"
# write openclaw.json with secrets.providers.legacy.path = $LEGACY_SECRET (no edge whitespace)
# and channels.discord.token SecretRef → legacy:/apiKey

node openclaw.mjs config get secrets.providers.legacy
node openclaw.mjs config validate --json
node openclaw.mjs config set channels.discord.token \
  --ref-provider legacy --ref-source file --ref-id /apiKey --dry-run --json

# Ordinary (no-whitespace) path still works via CLI; legacy provider retained
ORD="$ROOT/ordinary.json"
printf '%s\n' '{"token":"ORDINARY"}' > "$ORD" && chmod 600 "$ORD"
node openclaw.mjs config set secrets.providers.ordinary \
  --provider-source file --provider-path "$ORD" --provider-mode json
```

### Evidence after fix — compatibility / upgrade retention

```text
=== B) COMPAT: legacy provider paths (no edge whitespace) on this head ===
wrote_legacy_config= /tmp/oc168261-compat.*/openclaw.json
legacy_path_repr= '/tmp/oc168261.*/legacy-secret.json'

--- config get (loads existing stored provider) ---
{ "source": "…", "path": "…", "mode": "…" }   # redacted by CLI; loads OK

--- config validate ---
{"valid":true,"path":"/tmp/oc168261-compat.*/openclaw.json", ...}
validate_exit=0

--- shipped consume of legacy file provider ---
legacy_consume_ok= True
legacy_resolvability= True
legacy_refsChecked= 1
legacy_consume_exit=0

--- ordinary no-whitespace provider + legacy retained ---
Updated secrets.providers.ordinary. No gateway restart needed.
ordinary_path= /tmp/oc168261.*/ordinary.json
legacy_still_present= True
legacy_path_unchanged= True
ordinary_consume_ok= True
ordinary_consume_exit=0
```


### Exact steps — real upgrade from published v2026.10.5

```bash
# Authentic release binary (npm registry, not a hand-built fake):
#   npm install openclaw@2026.10.5
#   → OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (1b58cb9)
#   npm pack shasum 158d80b43644e2feba2a50647803562aa394e080
#   tarball sha256 dbb1bdcf2346292e25f672822b6a9928c234909abe6fee0df5fc4556e769d40e
export PATH="/path/to/node-v24.16.0/bin:$PATH"
OC_OLD=…/node_modules/openclaw/openclaw.mjs   # 2026.10.5
OC_NEW=…/openclaw.mjs                         # PR head bd8f2287fe3
ROOT=$(mktemp -d /tmp/oc168261-upgrade.XXXXXX)
STATE=$(mktemp -d /tmp/oc168261-upgrade-state.XXXXXX)
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$STATE" OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$STATE/openclaw.json"

# 1) ON v2026.10.5 — create real secrets.providers (file + exec)
printf '%s\n' '{"token":"UPGRADE_OK","apiKey":"LEGACY_KEY"}' > "$ROOT/vault.json" && chmod 600 "$ROOT/vault.json"
mkdir -p "$ROOT/helpers"
# exec helper speaks protocolVersion 1
cat > "$ROOT/helpers/secret-helper.sh" <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
printf '%s\n' '{"protocolVersion":1,"values":{"secret":"EXEC_OK"}}'
EOF
chmod 755 "$ROOT/helpers/secret-helper.sh"

node "$OC_OLD" config set secrets.providers.vault \
  --provider-source file --provider-path "$ROOT/vault.json" --provider-mode json
node "$OC_OLD" config set secrets.providers.execvault \
  --provider-source exec --provider-command "$ROOT/helpers/secret-helper.sh" \
  --provider-trusted-dir "$ROOT/helpers" --provider-json-only

node "$OC_OLD" config validate --json
node "$OC_OLD" config set channels.discord.token \
  --ref-provider vault --ref-source file --ref-id /token --dry-run --json
node "$OC_OLD" config set channels.discord.token \
  --ref-provider execvault --ref-source exec --ref-id secret --dry-run --json --allow-exec

# 2) UPGRADE: same OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR / openclaw.json → PR head packaged CLI (no rewrite)
node "$OC_NEW" --version
node "$OC_NEW" config get secrets.providers.vault
node "$OC_NEW" config get secrets.providers.execvault
node "$OC_NEW" config validate --json
node "$OC_NEW" config set channels.discord.token \
  --ref-provider vault --ref-source file --ref-id /token --dry-run --json
node "$OC_NEW" config set channels.discord.token \
  --ref-provider execvault --ref-source exec --ref-id secret --dry-run --json --allow-exec
```

### Evidence after fix — real v2026.10.5 → PR-head upgrade

```text
=== REAL UPGRADE PROOF: v2026.10.5 → PR head bd8f2287fe3 ===
date=2026-10-19T11:27:03+08:00 (Asia/Shanghai)

obtained_via=npm install openclaw@2026.10.5
old_version_line=OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (1b58cb9)
new_version_line=OpenClaw 2026.9.9 (9de8790)   # package.json on this PR branch; contains the fix
new_head=bd8f2287fe3
# Note: PR branch version string is older than the release that wrote the config;
# CLI prints a version-mismatch notice. Providers still load + resolve (below).

=== 1) ON v2026.10.5: create secrets.providers ===
Updated secrets.providers.vault. No gateway restart needed.
Updated secrets.providers.execvault. No gateway restart needed.

provider=execvault command='…/helpers/secret-helper.sh' trustedDirs=['…/helpers'] jsonOnly=True

=== 2) Baseline ON v2026.10.5 ===
config validate --json → {"valid":true,...,"warnings":[]}
file dry-run → {"ok":true,"checks":{"schema":true,"resolvability":true,"resolvabilityComplete":true},"refsChecked":1}
exec dry-run --allow-exec → {"ok":true,"checks":{"schema":true,"resolvability":true,"resolvabilityComplete":true},"refsChecked":1}
config_sha256_before=ed6a7f63a4a289236f038c69afecff93bc5611ef49584576312b0badfd67b099

=== 3) AFTER UPGRADE (same state dir → PR head) ===
# CLI notice (expected): config written by 2026.10.5, command running 2026.9.9
config get secrets.providers.vault → loads (fields redacted by CLI)
config get secrets.providers.execvault → loads (fields redacted by CLI)
config validate --json → {"valid":true,"path":"…/openclaw.json",…}  validate_after_exit=0
# plugin-manifest warnings only (matrix/memory-core/nostr/whatsapp); unrelated to secrets.providers

file dry-run after upgrade:
{
  "ok": true,
  "checks": { "resolvability": true, "resolvabilityComplete": true },
  "refsChecked": 1,
  "skippedExecRefs": 0
}
file_dryrun_after_exit=0

exec dry-run --allow-exec after upgrade:
{
  "ok": true,
  "checks": { "resolvability": true, "resolvabilityComplete": true },
  "refsChecked": 1,
  "skippedExecRefs": 0
}
new_exec_exit=0

```

### Exec trust boundary (previously accepted; still holds)

```text
=== ALLOW under trusted dir ending with space ===

stored_trustedDirs_repr= ['/tmp/oc168261.*/trusted ']
dry-run --allow-exec → ok:true; allow_marker_content=ALLOW_RAN

=== DENY neighbor before process creation ===

```

### Prior file-path persistence proof (still holds)

content WRONG

prs.title: refactor(ui): scope attachment listeners to job lifetimes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Attachment workers and FileReader jobs already have operation-scoped lifetimes. Their event listeners now follow those same lifetimes explicitly: worker clients abort their listener registrations when the job settles, FileReader uses its existing preparation controller, and each worker global removes its one-request message handler when it receives that request.

The three external AbortSignal subscriptions and their paired removals are unchanged. Encoding, admission, queues, cancellation, watchdogs, and rendered output are unchanged. The Node worker fixture now dispatches through a real EventTarget so it supplies both listener registration and removal.

The audit found no existing retained-listener leak; this is an ownership cleanup under the wave-zero permitted non-DOM platform category, not a claim to repair a leak.


## Evidence

Base: `d79b0a4df0b24fd1e630e22da22cc2bb40af45ce`. Head: `409fa2feeb9dd933ee8ff4c1ec35a1a12bfe9357`.

Rebased onto current main as directed; all six changed files remain byte-identical to the independently reviewed source. Frozen install passed. The default `pnpm tsgo:ui` now selects tsrs on darwin-arm64; no compiler override was used.

| Pattern | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Rendering controllers | 0 | 0 |
| `createEffect` | 0 | 0 |
| `createRenderEffect` | 0 | 0 |
| `untrack` | 0 | 0 |
| `addEventListener` | 15 | 15 |
| `querySelector(All)` | 0 | 0 |
| Manual class strings | 0 | 0 |
| Owner escapes / `flush` | 0 | 0 |
| Production LOC | 774 | 801 |

The 15 remaining registrations are permitted platform listeners: ten Worker/FileReader listeners bound to a signal, three paired external AbortSignal listeners, and two worker-global message listeners removed at receipt. The 27 added production lines provide explicit cleanup and formatter-expanded event options. The sole changed test file is one line shorter.

| Survivor category | Source |
| --- | --- |
| Worker client + external abort | `chat-attachment-image.ts:116`, `:117`, `:121`, `:129`; `chat-attachment-video.ts:49`, `:50`, `:67`, `:75` |
| FileReader + external abort | `chat-attachment-reads.ts:271`, `:273`, `:274`, `:275`, `:276` |
| One-request worker globals | `chat-attachment-image.worker.ts:49`; `chat-attachment-video.worker.ts:164` |


| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| UI typecheck | Two sidebar errors reproduced on pinned main: missing `SidebarProjectionMemo` export at `session-attention.ts:28`, and implicit-any `row` at line 180 |
| Focused attachment lifecycle tests | 20 passed |
| Node video worker tests | 3 passed |
| Typed lint / format / diff check | Passed |
| Full production Knip, including exports | Exit 1: unused `TaglineMode` in unchanged `src/cli/tagline.ts`; no touched-file findings |
| Independent P2 review | Scoped-clean; final source verification passed |

No startup imports, JSX, CSS, host tags, or visual output changed, so this cleanup does not need a build or new screenshots under the bounded proof policy.

Three existing `chat attachment read failures` cases fail identically at base `0fc8029c1199a1a34e764810ee445c83c2f744b2`: `enforces admission: batch overflow admits a later smaller file`, `enforces admission: ready and overlapping reads reserve the budget`, and `reserves the image ceiling for an oversized PNG while admitting following text files`. Each expects one `.app-toast` and receives zero. The exact-base targeted run reproduced all three; they are recorded separately from the lifecycle proof.

Historical pre-rebase production Knip reported unused exported constants `CODEX_BUNDLE_MANIFEST_RELATIVE_PATH`, `CURSOR_BUNDLE_MANIFEST_RELATIVE_PATH`, and `AGENT_BUNDLE_MANIFEST_RELATIVE_PATH` in `src/plugins/bundle-manifest.ts`, plus unused exported types `DiscordProviderCommandSpec` in `extensions/discord/src/monitor/provider.commands.ts` and `MSTeamsAccessTokenProvider` in `extensions/msteams/src/attachments.ts`. All three owner blobs match the base, no reference owner/importer is touched, and this cleanup changes no production imports. These remain unresolved unrelated local findings; the exact-base analyzer was not rerun, so this is not a claim of a passing or experimentally inherited Knip result.

The earlier CI run `39186132629` at head `d416ee7` failed three behavioral cases: `Control UI command palette search with a real Gateway > finds a grouped spawned conversation beyond the roster and treats a full result page as success`; `Control UI session-list event scope > refetches instead of showing a row excluded by configured-agent filtering`; and `Control UI session-list event scope > keeps the Sessions page query stable when the startup roster completes`. All three passed in the latest inspected completed scheduled main run `39183785855`. They are unresolved prior-head failures, not an inherited-failure claim; the rebased head needs its own CI verdict.

Historical normalized performance from that run: startup **337,514 B gzip**, startup CSS **38,500 B / 1 request**; chat route base **1,491,212 B** and head **1,491,280 B**, both over the 1,490,000 B route ceiling. Final-head CI supplies current performance. No new dependency, startup import, JSX, or visual layout changes. Earlier focused browser proof used the existing Node configuration; future Vitest runs use the pinned default Bun runtime.

Final rebased-head export Knip completed: its only finding is unused exported type `TaglineMode` in `src/cli/tagline.ts`. That owner blob is identical at this merge base and head. No exact-base analyzer replay was run; this remains an unresolved unrelated local finding, not a passing scan or CI inheritance claim.

prs.title: fix(agents): release prompt history after completed runs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes heap growth when completed tool-heavy agent runs leave their full recovery prompts reachable through retained attempt callbacks and copied harness parameters.

## User Impact

Completed runs release temporary recovery history. Active retries preserve their accumulated messages, and accepted transcript writes finish with the original run's prepared message, visibility, attribution, and callbacks. No configuration, schema, stored-transcript, or prompt-prefix change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The logical run now releases the borrowed prompt/message payload when replacing a continuation and at disposal, including copies of its envelope retained by outer harness layers. Transcript preparation captures only needed fields; cache-touch completion captures only its timestamp.

A reused session manager captures one run context before append admission. That context owns transformations, callbacks, prepared user state, run ID, and persistence mode. Its cleanup runs after the actual transcript drain, including drains that outlast the bounded teardown wait. Old cleanup and old mode setters cannot mutate a newer run. Callback retirement preserves visibility and attribution needed for synthetic-result cleanup.

The change removes whole-attempt closure capture, shared mutable run policy, the positional rebinding API, and the callback-generation counter. Runtime code grows by 89 lines to preserve the accepted-write and retry-history contracts at these lifetime boundaries. The existing benchmark grows by 169 tooling lines plus 13 README lines to exercise tools, images, recovery, and post-GC resources; no new benchmark entry point or runtime manager is added.

## Evidence

The original GC regressions retained all 20 continuations on baseline `c2549f8295d09f520f119de44d77e1c7dc25779a`, while an unowned control collected. Each fixed regression retains zero:

| Retained callback owner | Baseline continuations | Fixed |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Session notification / user persistence | 20 / 20 | 0 / 20 |
| Transcript writer | 20 / 20 | 0 / 20 |
| Cache-touch success callback | 20 / 20 | 0 / 20 |

A separate regression keeps copies of completed attempt parameters alive: reachable message arrays fall from 40/40 to 0/40. It also protects message order and identity, caller-owned arrays, and recovery calls that omit new messages.

Delayed-write regressions failed before their corresponding fixes. They now prove that in-flight and queued writes retain the accepting run's callbacks, prepared envelopes, private visibility, assistant preparation, and run ID across rebinding. Other focused tests cover context-bound mode setters, synthetic cleanup after retirement, success/abort cleanup, prompt-prefix stability, and the benchmark protocol. The final context correction passed 113 tests across five guard/lifecycle files; its final fixture correction passed all 18 wrapper tests. Changed-file formatting/lint and independent review passed. The one permitted local core typecheck (native tsrs) passed before the final refinements; exact-head PR CI supplies the broad and final type proof. No Testbox/Crabbox validation lease or CI rerun was used.

### Paired Gateway measurements

Acceptance rule: identical completed synthetic workloads and tool/recovery counts; collectible callback-owned continuations with a live GC control; no completed-continuation prompt payloads; no heap/timing regression beyond run variation. Two concurrent A/B pairs run under an exclusive lock on separate 16-core halves, swapping halves in pair 2. Compare candidate minus baseline within each pair.

Each side completes 110 runs (10 warmup and 100 measured, in cohorts of 10), with 300 read calls/results, 100 output-limit continuations/recoveries, and 300 image-bearing requests. Each synthetic fixture has 5,000 sessions, 6,000 retained runs, 200 approvals, 100 cron jobs, and 12 projects; its databases total 91,033,600 bytes (86.82 MiB).

| Final measurement | Baseline | Fixed | Fixed minus baseline |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Pair 1 post-GC heap | 616.78 MiB | 616.56 MiB | -0.22 MiB |
| Pair 1 main-thread CPU | 29.430 s | 29.423 s | -0.02% |
| Pair 1 median cohort time | 4.906 s | 5.028 s | +2.49% |
| Pair 2 post-GC heap | 629.13 MiB | 614.31 MiB | -14.83 MiB |
| Pair 2 main-thread CPU | 28.068 s | 29.079 s | +3.60% |
| Pair 2 median cohort time | 4.816 s | 4.939 s | +2.56% |

Median cohort time increased about 2.5% in both pairs. Individual cohort times overlapped broadly (roughly 4.6–6.2 seconds); nearest-rank p95 shifted −0.87% / +0.90% (10 cohorts per side, so p95 equals the maximum). CPU changed −0.02% / +3.60%. These measurements do not establish a speedup or a material latency regression; the landing evidence is removal of retained continuation payloads. Other post-warmup heap growth remains.

Workload command, run concurrently for the two isolated artifacts under the CPU/lock rule above:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/transcript-broadcast-measure.ts \
  --entry <variant>/dist/entry.js --state-dir <isolated-fixture> \
  --port <gateway-port> --mock-port <model-port> --scenario attempt-retention \
  --clients 1 --runs 10 --rounds 10 --chunks 1 --prompt-kib 128
```

The final candidate side also used `--heap-snapshot`.

The final snapshot contains **40 reachable continuation envelopes from completed run IDs, all with empty message arrays and empty prompts**. None of the five reported callback paths remains. An equivalent baseline snapshot from the prior identical-source/workload campaign had 37 nonempty envelopes with seven messages each. Unique string self bytes reachable through continuation payloads fall from **15,331,224 to zero**. This is reachability accounting, not dominator-retained bytes or a claim that every byte was uniquely owned by those envelopes.

The runtime artifacts compare pinned baseline `c2549f8295d09f520f119de44d77e1c7dc25779a` against that baseline with eight runtime source files captured from final head `907e3536079ad39524c15bfd5fc2a852e5c6b249`; all source hashes match. This isolates the selected files, not a full latest-main performance comparison. The workload uses real isolated Gateway RPCs with a synthetic HTTP model, ten reused child-session IDs, tools, and PNG input. It does not measure live-model or model-driven subagent spawning behavior.

Build limitation: filtered runtime preparation hit unrelated Canvas-asset and baseline CLI-packaging checks. Both sides then used identical targeted runtime compilation/postbuild commands; no failed full build is represented as passing. A port-conflicted setup attempt was discarded and fresh fixtures used. Snapshot diagnostics retain their 30-second deadline; much larger snapshots can fail explicitly with a timeout.

### PR CI

[Final-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39194379692) completed on `907e3536079ad39524c15bfd5fc2a852e5c6b249`. Core/test types, focused owning lanes, and security review passed. The only underlying failure is the [mock-export ratchet](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39194379692/job/117874258456), plus its aggregate gates: `test/scripts/ci-node-test-plan.test.ts:3297` mocks `../../scripts/lib/ci-test-timings.mts` without pass-through/isolation annotation.

This is inherited. The PR head, tested merge `ff2b76604b05b5669cca5a15a78c28101f37a713`, and its main parent `de561f3ea0b2f69dfacea6d3b4d67ca3e4989634` have identical test and ledger blobs (`8c5a6d152b15828c44931615b4102534aa2f1d29` and `d9c221e0b548925364ff34fdcba83f559008928f`). A scoped reproduction on the benchmark host used the actual native parser, mock scanner, and ledger predicate on only that reported file/module: all three revisions exit 1 with the identical missing-factory fingerprint `8c74b1e63618912d9ac86d6697e483f02edeae751b9edb61b44c668c7f9db59c`. No full suite or global ratchet was run for attribution. The operator-authorized inherited-failure exception applies; no CI rerun or rebase was performed to chase green.

The earlier PR-caused fixture type error was corrected using the existing typed assistant fixture and is green on this head. Independent reviews are clean; the two queued-write ownership findings are fixed. The optional larger-snapshot timeout suggestion is deferred with the limitation documented above.

prs.title: fix(gateway): defer plugin runtime generation reserve until retained work admits
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a plugin reload is refused before replacement actually starts (for example while retained work is still draining), `reloadGatewayPlugins()` had already called `pluginRuntimeGeneration.reserve()`. That fenced the still-serving generation even though no replacement was committed, so operations through the captured plugin runtime could fail while the registry object was unchanged.

## Solution

Defer `pluginRuntimeGeneration.reserve()` until after the first retained-work admission drain succeeds (post `reserveResourceHandoff`, after `drainRetainedWork`). Prepare-time failures and pre-admission refusals no longer touch the serving generation. Existing rollback and cleanup after a committed replacement are unchanged.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-plugins.lifecycle.test.ts -t 'a retained-work reload refusal leaves the serving runtime generation authoritative'`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-plugin-runtime-generation.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`

Fixes #157670
