prs.title: feat(exec): save command output for post-failure diagnosis
prs.body:
Related: #176116

## What Problem This Solves

Failed or timed-out shell tasks can lose diagnostic output when bounded process results expire or the Gateway restarts.

## User Impact

Users can request `saveOutput: true` for a Gateway-hosted exec and read its saved output after failure, timeout, or process-result eviction. Saving is off by default. Each artifact retains at most the first 2 MiB; files require manual cleanup, with no automatic expiry or aggregate disk quota. This explicit workspace write also applies in incognito sessions.

Paths precede large command results so the model-visible session cap preserves them. Capture failures remain visible without blocking command execution. The irreversible-loss warning is suppressed only when the saved prefix covers everything discarded from memory, preserving the intent of #128997 (`be67a8bdf62e04cd3ae4cc531371c5e8e582f390`).

## Why This Change Was Made

A bounded streaming writer captures sanitized stdout/stderr before the in-memory cap and closes before terminal collection. Exec, process poll/log, and completion notices expose the saved path and partial/capture-error metadata. Unsupported sandbox/node capture is rejected before launch. Authorization, exit outcomes, and completion routing retain their existing owners.

This proposes the explicit workspace-artifact stage of #176116. Manual cleanup, aggregate storage limits, and incognito behavior still need maintainer product acceptance. Saved output does not recover processes or guarantee durability across power loss.

The conflict with current main is resolved in `923ef07adf346b7c6331af7f7a1e8bbdfacac8a4` (source base `d6ec4c7de8919a1711d0a87798776e1fd5264d97`). The PR uses main's existing Gateway completion formatter and removes the earlier duplicate extraction. It adds no database, registry, or dependency. Production TypeScript is +258/-82 lines, tests +363/-2, and docs +7/-0, including the runtime type move needed by the line-count ratchet.

## Evidence

Windows / Node 26.10.0:

- The main-integration candidate passed 43 selected cases across saved-output artifacts, retention disclosure through SessionManager persistence, Git partial-clone behavior, approved-output formatting, and background notifications. One POSIX-only producer case was skipped; 22 unrelated cases were filtered.
- Fresh canonical autoreview of that candidate completed with one actionable P2: silent saved-output timeouts were no longer recognized as exec completions. An added regression exercises the actual notification producer and production event classifier; it failed before the fix and passes after it. The fix puts artifact notes in the existing supported completion body instead of loosening the parser.
- After that fix, all 22 background-notification cases and two focused parser cases pass (24 unrelated parser cases filtered). Unchanged-input artifact/approval/persistence proof is retained.
- After the mechanical formatter move, nine focused approval/output cases pass. Independent source review found no concern in moving the identical static/dynamic follow-up normalization into the existing formatter; callback and delivery ownership stay unchanged.
- Focused type-aware oxlint, agents-tools and agents-sessions test typechecks, core TypeScript, changed-file formatting, changed-file line-cap ratchet, and `git diff --check` pass. The line-cap check covers all 19 changed TypeScript files.

The saved-output cases run real child commands and cover nonzero exit with both streams, ANSI removal, explicit incognito saving, timeout and process collection, an 80k result through the persistence cap, UTF-8-safe 2 MiB capture with and without a memory gap, capture-directory failure, default opt-out, and unsupported hosts. The large-output path and capture-failure disclosure regressions also failed before the repair and pass with it.

The isolated Gateway restart qualification is running on final commit `923ef07adf346b7c6331af7f7a1e8bbdfacac8a4`. No successful restart/read-back result is claimed yet.

No live provider has been called. The isolated Gateway qualification uses the repository's deterministic loopback provider fixture, so it will establish the Gateway/agent/tool boundary rather than live-model behavior. No historical failure logs are available; this PR does not claim a root cause for the original report.

## Remaining Review and CI Context

The original `check-test-types-core-3` error (run 39108383474, job 117619589787) was PR-caused: `expectDefined` lacked its mandatory context argument. It is fixed, passes locally in the correct agents-tools lane, and [passed on the preceding integration head `4ed9a6eb3`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39194688317/job/117875386516). Fresh-head CI remains authoritative.

[OpenGrep on integration head `4ed9a6eb3`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39194689925/job/117874786019), like the original run 39108383587/job 117619053447, flags two inherited `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS` reads in `bash-tools.exec-request-preparation.ts`. This PR adds four unrelated argument-validation/type lines to that file; the Git-policy block is unchanged from both the original source base and integrated main. Its original-base SHA-256 is `9013d0a6f9adc03c25e3d117f5cb1391bead698228c612ba7af2ca2ff528d084`. Request overrides still reject `GIT_CONFIG_` keys; the block preserves trusted inherited local Git policy. No sanitizer, scan rule, or suppression is changed. This provenance is not a green scan or gate waiver.

The integration-head [baseline-ratchet job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39194688317/job/117875110077) failed at the mock-export guard in `test/scripts/ci-node-test-plan.test.ts:3297`. That file is unchanged from integrated main (Git blob `f12fd1e09c894509a64585630465f9881fcb066e`). Its line-cap warning is addressed by the formatter move. A separate local whole-tree suppression-baseline check reports three unchanged UI files; their blobs also match integrated main. No baseline or unrelated UI/test file is changed. This is source attribution, not a passing CI result.

Any exact-head CI/security requirement is independent of these local checks. Product/storage and incognito acceptance remain maintainer decisions.

prs.title: fix(sqlite): keep transaction-bound schema catalogs local
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Hourly `main` CI intermittently failed `checks-node-worker-e2e-2` in `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/skill-library-worker-wire.e2e.test.ts` ("pins the creator's bundle..."): the paired-node worker turn `bob-worker-first` failed before reply with `Failed to prepare skill resources ... Selected skill revision is unavailable. | NOT_FOUND`. Failing runs: 39079065853 (f8c3ba501c) and 39090751047 (51cf7e45b2). The second head already contained #175947, so that fix did not close this window.

The test's own fresh-database diagnostics showed the `skill_library_entries` row, the `skill_library_revisions` row with its manifest, and the revision directory all committed when the read reported the revision missing. (The `skills.library.read`/`mutate` INVALID_REQUEST lines just before are the test's expected negative checks for Bob, not the bug.)

## User Impact

Newly published skill-library skills could appear unavailable to pinned turns, so a reply failed before inference. No schema, config or data change.

## Why This Change Was Made

`skills.library.manifests` answers through `tableExists`, which trusts admitted SQLite schema facts. In `getAdmittedSqliteSchemaFacts`, a reader inside an outer native transaction whose catalog was already bound (`transactionCatalogBound`) could, after an inner schema pin ended, either borrow current shared facts or capture its historical catalog and publish it as the current admission. A later connection then adopted that stale catalog and reported the table missing for committed rows.

`observeSchemaLifetime` deliberately leaves `owner.processRevision` at the old generation while a bound transaction keeps its catalog, so a bound transaction whose `processRevision` no longer matches the published schema generation is historical. The existing `unknownSnapshot` check (previously limited to `transactionRead && !transactionCatalogBound`) now covers bound catalogs too: such a transaction recaptures locally and neither borrows nor publishes shared facts. Transactions holding a current catalog (state open, admission, migrations) keep publishing retained facts exactly as before; an earlier revision of this PR isolated every bound transaction and regressed retained-admission reuse (`openclaw-state-db-checkonce.test.ts`), which the narrowed condition fixes. This complements #175947 (reader-startup ordering) on the re-admission path.

## Evidence

- New regression in `src/infra/sqlite-schema-facts.test.ts` commits real sibling DDL after an ended inner pin, with and without a published sibling catalog. On the base, both cases fail: published=false reports `tableExists` false after the transaction for a committed table (the CI symptom); published=true borrows current facts inside a transaction whose native snapshot lacks the table. Both pass with the fix.
- Final head: `sqlite-schema-facts` + `openclaw-state-db-checkonce`: 55 passed (checkonce 10/10, base also 10/10). Sibling admission, readonly-state, native schema-facts, skill-library and resources suites: 181 of 182 passed; the one timeout (`service.test.ts` "discovers pinned commands", 120 s limit on a host at load ~120) passes alone on both the fix (99.9 s) and base (94.8 s).
- The e2e file passed through the gateway e2e lane with the fix (136.7s).
- `git diff --check` clean; independent autoreview reports no actionable findings.

prs.title: feat(macos,browser): keep approval prompts out of OpenClaw's own automation
prs.body:
Related: #174663

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's native computer input and agent browser automation can reach its own human approval surfaces. This adds explicit hardening at the native presentation/input owners and the browser URL-policy owner.

## User Impact

The native macOS Peekaboo path refuses input while an exec, pairing, consent, or menu-bar approval is pending, and excludes approval surfaces from screen snapshots. Human clicks and Command-Return keep working. Browser automation refuses the Gateway's known Control UI origins, including local DNS aliases and already-attached Chrome/extension tabs. No configuration or migration is required.

This is hardening, not an isolation boundary. The separate bundled CUA driver remains out of scope and bypasses the native guard; third-party automation can operate UI. Do not combine ask-mode exec with unrestricted computer use for a model you do not trust. Remote-node browsers depend on that node's known Gateway origins; this does not propagate separately saved endpoints or discover unadvertised remote aliases. macOS-owned TCC dialogs are not app-owned NSWindows. DNS alias checks use the current resolver answer; this hardening does not pin Chromium's independent DNS resolution or claim protection from adversarial DNS rebinding. Blocking every unknown hostname on the Gateway port would impose an unrelated navigation restriction.

## Why This Change Was Made

One observable native owner aggregates pending presentation sources without polling. Each presenter/queue clears only its own source. CLI installation, Dashboard JavaScript confirmation, and device-consent sheets use the existing alert presenter. The action service reads current pending state at admission and through its existing execution callback. Refusal settles only the requesting scope's held synthetic button through the existing queue cleanup owner, retaining failed-release retries. Panels disable window sharing; ScreenCaptureKit explicitly excludes the app while approvals are pending and withholds a frame if a prompt opened during capture.

The existing browser URL policy checks public, allowed, remote, and local Gateway origins before navigation, after DNS, and when selecting/focusing/closing an existing tab. Focus re-lists the exact target after transport preparation; close does so through the existing admission hook before its final authority check and dispatch. Navigation reuses its DNS result; tab management resolves aliases only at the Gateway port, preserving other local applications without imposing navigation's SSRF policy on tab management. No SDK export or new policy setting is added.

Deslop removes pass-through URL/CLI helpers, duplicate native admission/consent checks, direct confirmation-sheet presentation, a redundant capture branch, and an unused internal browser export. Informational alerts do not pause input. Exact numstat: production **+211/-50**, tests **+338/-22**, docs **+16/-0**. The remaining production growth supplies previously absent pending-state and origin checks; unrelated deletions would not simplify this change.

Stale facts: no new detached effect is introduced. Queued actions retain existing action/scope/lifecycle identities but read current approval state before effects. Scoped cleanup checks the current held-button owner before release. Focus/close retain the resolved target identity but reread its URL at dispatch admission; close retains the existing session-authority check after that awaited lookup. Browser config is reread from its published owner after awaited DNS. A capture retains its exclusion filter for that capture and checks newly pending approval state before returning pixels.

## Evidence

PR CI is the test gate per maintainer policy. Local tests, typechecks, production-only negative controls, live Gateway proof, and Crabbox/Testbox were intentionally skipped. No lease or Gateway was started.

Swift regressions: `pending approval refuses computer input before permissions or dispatch`, `closing one prompt does not enable input while another owner is pending`, `dashboard confirmation sheets refuse computer input until answered`, and `approval refusal settles only the requesting scope's held input`. The panel-layout test also checks non-sharing.

Browser regressions: `blocks its own Control UI origin despite permissive browser policy: %s`, `keeps other local apps reachable and follows the live Gateway port`, `rechecks the current Control UI origin after an awaited lookup`, `refuses %s on an existing Control UI tab before browser effects`, `refuses %s when the selected tab navigates to the Control UI before dispatch`, `refuses approval-like dialog actions on a current Control UI tab through %s`, `blocks a local Control UI DNS alias during $name using its existing lookup`, and `refuses %s on an existing Control UI DNS alias before browser effects`. Chromium relay E2E now serves its generic proof page from a separate origin from its fake Gateway, preserving the bootstrap/relay assertions while respecting the new guard.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Changed-file checks and hooks | SwiftFormat, strict SwiftLint, oxfmt, syntax oxlint, `git diff --check`, and commit hooks passed. After this merge: SwiftFormat 12 files, 0.68s; strict SwiftLint 12 files, zero violations, 1.40s; oxfmt 8 files, 0.40s; syntax oxlint 6 files, 3.13s. No local test wall time because tests were not run. |
| Autoreview | Fresh branch review through P2 on `7e190e821766`: scoped-clean, no actionable findings; overall verdict: patch is correct. This includes the final focus/close URL recheck. Tests and project code were not executed by the reviewer; CI supplies integration proof. |
| [Final-head automatic CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39192865303) | Completed on `33ef17b52b5a`: 32 passed, 24 skipped; only the mock-export ratchet and its aggregate gate failed (details below). Browser regression and E2E lanes passed. |

Four check failures plus their aggregate gate remain (details below). Swift default: 2,596 tests in 284.925s; rendered: 2 tests in 7.278s; named: 14 tests in 8.691s. |
| ClawSweeper | Its old-head direct-sheet P1 and held-input P2 are repaired, along with the external DNS-alias finding. The maintainer requested exactly one new-head re-review after CI is green or only proven-inherited; that request has not been sent yet. Live-proof-only requests remain superseded by the explicit CI-only proof policy. |

Final head: `33ef17b52b5a83e823502a748817a314786b1dab`, after merging fetched main `d694fe8c09ff` without rebase; it includes the upstream import fix `e070647a0cf2` (#176799). The merge changed none of the reviewed files. The final-head results are recorded above. The first native dispatch stopped at preflight because of an invalid validation-tier combination; the corrected dispatch uses the supported default tier.

The available scheduled run predates these additional failures; scheduled corroboration is pending.

prs.title: fix(auth): configured primary account blocks CLI fallback
prs.body:
Closes #158421. Thanks to @HerbertHuerto for the corrected report and @aoclaw-glitch for the per-agent reproduction.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a configured primary account is treated as an explicit conversation pin when a fallback switches CLI provider, so the destination CLI rejects a valid fallback account as belonging to the wrong provider.

## User Impact

Configured Chat and event-triggered fallbacks select the destination runtime's supported account. Explicit conversation and person-linked account pins remain strict, including edits while execution waits for preparation or placement. Scheduled jobs retain main's recorded-inference-account, route and native-account restrictions.

Public V1 CLI preparation/context types remain source-compatible. Plugin-owned transports can use V2, which requires the host's current-owner assertion and asynchronous account admission. The bundled Anthropic transport uses V2 for cold startup, warm prompts and injected input. No compatibility removal date, public option, database schema, wire protocol, permission or authored dependency change is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The auth-selection producer carries configuration provenance as a runtime-only fact. A fallback can scope that default account to its provider without discarding a real user/user-link pin. Queue/account edits and live model switches retire the earlier configuration fact. CLI owners re-read current account intent after their waits and preserve the existing check immediately before effects; durable reads stay worker-owned and incognito reads use the captured memory owner.

This maintenance resolves two conflicts with current main. It preserves main’s admitted-config/requester-origin flow and uses its final-root observer, removing the earlier duplicate observer from this branch. Both histories remain intact in a normal merge.

## Evidence

Current source: `41e550dbe2375dbaa439c435928d3b7ad5f24c3a`, a normal merge of previous PR head `687fd35db0ddd7fa2618624f25b073b3ba49a779` and official main `3ec17e0870238a84aeb337c9692b20e5f21b5b88`.

- **Conflict before/after:** GitHub metadata was temporarily inconsistent, so official main was pinned through `git ls-remote`. `git merge-tree` returned exit 1 with two actual conflicts. The resolved reply-execution import retains both main's `OpenClawConfig` type and the configured-account provenance producer; main's new `readAdmissionConfig`, requester-origin and queue-authority behavior remains intact.
- **One observer owner:** upstream commit `26c6a4090f1f21f9552aa801e4a42927d32ae8b8` independently provides final-root waiting (Peter's fix extracted from #176647). This branch now uses its exact helper blob `40eb5fb5580`: the custom request-scope spy, separate `rootRelease` state and extra wait are removed. Main delegates/restores an existing admission spy, captures final release only for owned roots, and leaves dispatch-only waits nonblocking. Our retained-root and borrowed-parent no-deadlock controls remain. This is integration of upstream work, not a claim that our PR was merged or credited by that commit.
- **Current focused proof:** Node passes all **41 cases** across actual CLI protocol-process controls and the in-memory request/admission file (195.295 s wrapper). Both retained-root controls exercise the real router/registry/authorization/envelope without a listening Gateway. Pinned Bun passes **130 reply cases plus the same 32 owner cases** (106.243 s wrapper; per-file phases 66.71 s and 31.07 s). Together with the 9 CLI controls this covers **171 distinct cases**; the Node per-file phases were 79.27 s CLI and 59.61 s owner. The repeated owner cases are not added again to the distinct total. The CLI controls use real isolated session-state SQLite workers and owned subprocess receipts to observe account pins after preparation/placement; stubbing those boundaries would miss the failure.
- Targeted types include the CLI process, reply, owner and Anthropic SDK consumer graphs and pass (18.206 s). Type-aware lint of the affected execution/helper/control files passes (33.446 s). Format, staged diff and line-cap against the pinned official base pass; the line-cap check was executed with Node 24.19.0. A normal full `pnpm build` passes (548.980 s wrapper, 541.1 s native phases), including unified SDK declarations, SDK exports, CLI bootstrap and Control UI artifacts. Non-failing UI size-budget notices remain in the build log and are not separately baseline-attributed here.
- Fresh independent P0–P2 review covers the complete **62-file authored candidate** and is scoped-clean (143.407 s; static review). The helper no longer appears as an authored source change against main. Review/source/index/commit hashes match. Node 24.19.0 / pnpm 12.11.1 match the integrated manifest; the frozen install passes. No authored root dependency, schema, protocol, permission or public-subpath change is introduced. SDK subpaths are unchanged; the native API-diff helper was not run because it creates worktrees prohibited for this task.

### Earlier, head-specific evidence

The preceding `687fd35` head passed [natural CI 39180158709](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39180158709): 101 jobs completed with no failures. It also passed 118 reply-file cases after the missing facade import was migrated to its defining session-controller query owner. These remain prior-head results, not a current-head CI claim.

prs.title: fix(deepgram): expand array-valued providerOptions to repeated query parameters (#176740)
prs.body:
Closes #176740

## What Problem This Solves

Array-valued Deepgram `providerOptions` (e.g. `keyterm`) were sent as a single comma-joined query parameter instead of one repeated parameter per element, silently making multi-term keyterm prompting ineffective.

- Problem: `url.searchParams.set(key, String(value))` stringifies an array `["a","b","c"]` into `"a,b,c"`, producing `?keyterm=a,b,c` instead of `?keyterm=a&keyterm=b&keyterm=c`. Deepgram treats the comma-joined form as one literal term, not three separate boost terms. Additionally, `ProviderOptionsSchema` in `zod-schema.core.ts` only accepted `string | number | boolean`, so array-valued options failed config validation before reaching the transport layer.
- Solution: When a query value is an array, call `url.searchParams.append(key, item)` for each element. Scalar values use `set` as before. The config schema, `ProviderQuery` type, and `AudioTranscriptionRequest.query` type now accept `string[]`.
- What did NOT change: No changes to the config file format (existing scalar values work identically), no new API surface, no changes to response parsing or model handling.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix uses the existing URLSearchParams API — `append` is the standard way to add repeated query parameters. No new abstraction or mechanism is introduced.

- Non-goals: Other Deepgram parameters that accept arrays (e.g. `redact`, `search`, `tag`) also benefit from this fix since it applies generically to all query values, but they were not individually tested against live Deepgram.

## User Impact

Users who configure `keyterm` (or any repeatable Deepgram parameter like `keywords`, `search`, `redact`, `tag`) as an array in `providerOptions.deepgram` will now have each element sent as a separate query parameter. Single-string values continue to work exactly as before.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof — shipped batch path (real fetch to local fake Deepgram server)

Config with saved array providerOptions passes validation; resolved query drives a real HTTP transcription that completes, and the captured real request URL shows one `keyterm=` per element:

```
saved providerOptions.deepgram (parsed): {"keyterm":["Aquablock","linho","Sunbrella"],"smart_format":true}
[REAL FETCH] Deepgram request: POST /v1/listen?model=nova-3&language=multi&keyterm=Aquablock&keyterm=linho&keyterm=Sunbrella&smart_format=true
transcription completed, text: "Aquablock and Sunbrella confirmed" model: nova-3
```

### Real behavior proof — shipped Flux path (real ffmpeg decode + real WebSocket)

A real WAV (440 Hz tone, ffmpeg-generated) was decoded by real ffmpeg and streamed over a real WebSocket to a local fake Flux server; the captured request URL shows array expansion, and transcription completed:

```
[REAL WS] Flux request URL: /v2/listen?model=flux-general-multi&encoding=linear16&sample_rate=16000&keyterm=Aquablock&keyterm=linho&keyterm=Sunbrella
transcription completed, text: "Aquablock and Sunbrella" model: flux-general-multi
```

### Data-model compatibility — existing scalar config still loads, new arrays accepted

```
v2026.10.5 scalar providerOptions (keyterm: string, smart_format: boolean, sample_rate: number): PASS (accepted)
new array-valued providerOptions (keyterm: string[]): PASS (accepted)
```

### Regression tests (pre-fix fail / post-fix pass verified)

- `audio.test.ts`: 17 passed (13 existing + 4 new `it.each` covering array/scalar/number/mixed)
- `audio-flux.test.ts`: 12 passed (11 existing + 1 new for array keyterm in Flux path)
- Pre-fix verification: reverted `audio.ts` fix → array test failed ✅ → restored → passed ✅

What was not tested: Live Deepgram cloud API with real audio (no Deepgram API key in this environment).

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used `git grep` and `node --import tsx` to analyze issue #176740, locate the array-to-string coercion in both Deepgram transport paths, and implement the fix. The implementer understands the code: `searchParams.append` adds repeated parameters while `searchParams.set` overwrites, so the fix checks `Array.isArray` before choosing which to call. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution. Per review, replaced the stub-fetch matrix with shipped-flow proofs (real fetch for batch, real ffmpeg + real WebSocket for Flux) and added data-model compatibility proof.

prs.title: refactor(ui): give chat panes explicit element ownership
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Retained chat panes discover their own controls through DOM queries and synchronize native inputs through a render effect. Those implicit handoffs make focus, eviction, attachment delivery, and plugin replacement depend on the rendered DOM shape.

## User Impact

Preserves retained-session rendering, composer focus, board and attachment actions, and plugin replacement behavior while moving these handoffs to renderer-owned refs. There is no intended visual or routing change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Native pane input publication now updates the existing synchronous owner, including while its rendered frame is parked. It publishes a buffered stream before the property change admits a frame; tracked frame preparation only captures render bookkeeping. Explicit registrations describe mounted panes, and typed refs connect their controls to the operations that use them. Each renderer releases its own registration; identity checks keep a retiring branch from clearing its replacement.

Test fixtures publish the same explicit registrations as the renderer: history sentinels, replacement panes, and the native DOM element behind the legacy pane test adapter. Existing focus, attachment-retirement, pagination, and visibility assertions remain. The composer runtime-budget fixture now uses real wheel input before returning to its original offset, so it retires pending end-follow through the same reader-input path as the product; the movement and render-budget assertions remain intact. The retained-comment fixture waits for startup scrolling to settle before selecting text, preserving the toolbar’s intentional scroll dismissal and all real click/edit/delete/history-clear assertions.

Owner projections replace presentation state copies. Progress watches retain the initial source identity to avoid a redundant first frame, and composer replacement refs stay lifetime-stable instead of initializing a lazy JSX conditional inside `onSettled`. Remaining committed-DOM effects retain the existing focus, layout, cancellation, and ordering boundaries. Optional renderers remain behind their existing lazy boundaries.

prs.title: fix(webchat): make voice transcript echo visible in WebChat/Control UI history
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing recognized speech in saved user-message history when transcript echo is enabled for a voice note sent from WebChat/Control UI or a native chat client.

## User Impact

The approved transcript stays with the original user message after reopening history. The existing `tools.media.audio.echoTranscript` setting remains opt-in, with no new configuration or default change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway prepares the transcript through the existing selected-agent media runner, then passes the display text through the ordinary approval and canonical user-turn writer. The agent-facing speech remains machine-generated/untrusted, and synthesized speech is not promoted to slash-command input. Completed audio selections, including empty/failed/dropped outcomes, are reused by later enrichment without repeating that selection. Telegram's first-note mention preflight and outbound echo remain separate.

Transcription can precede the durable input acknowledgment. Declared `audio/*` client requests therefore wait on the captured connection by default; cancellation, disconnect, and explicit native deadlines remain available. This is not an unlimited agent-run timeout or a promise to terminate an already-running provider request/process immediately.

## Durable State

- Successful, approved speech becomes ordinary content on the existing canonical user message. Existing pending-input custody can hold the same enriched message while it waits for transcript commit.
- Embedded dispatch may capture the separate model-facing rendering in the existing optional `__openclaw.modelPromptProjection` metadata. This adds no new field contract, table, column, schema version, or persistence owner.
- Audio files and `media://inbound/…` references keep their existing format and lifecycle. Selection decisions and already-transcribed flags are request-local reuse state, not a new durable STT cache or job queue.
- No historical backfill or re-transcription is performed. Disabling the setting or rolling back does not erase already saved speech. Incognito retains its existing memory-actor behavior; attachment/CLI file lifecycles remain separate.

## Current Main Integration

Current signed head `81dafe4025b9cc5af158c9e78d00089fddaf93e5` repairs the CI integration on top of `37dab765daee1f676a24c85345dba319ff804054`, preserving all contributor history. It changes only `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-placement.test.ts`; production code and the voice-transcript feature are unchanged.

Reuse main's existing [placement-fixture repair, 8dc973402856](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/8dc9734028569ef2319973cd7bf81971c8738ee1), and remove the two obsolete setup imports. The incoming branch still used the inline setup, while GitHub's merged CI tree already used the shared fixture and therefore rejected those imports as unused. Both the branch and merged tree now have one consistent setup, with every test case and assertion preserved. No rebase or unrelated main merge was performed.

### Earlier conflict repair

Historical conflict-repair head `5eeb132797fc2b8ed1ad8bb6da0736597a8b3a6d` incorporates main `1ae7b3c3590082865cc1bd6ba2bff20711c5eb33` through a signed merge, preserving incoming head `547532bde15cddd274c0b13f8be9a5480b695af1` and all contributor ancestry without a rebase or squash.

- Resolve three media-understanding conflicts while retaining main's removal of routine success diagnostics, guarded image-request handling, command-name simplifications, and compacted CLI-audio suite.
- Keep the PR's existing input-authority checks before provider upload, ffmpeg conversion, and CLI execution. Preserve the existing deferred admission-revocation regression in main's flattened test layout. The extracted conversion helper also retains main's removal of a redundant directory creation; no duplicate inline conversion owner is restored.
- Feature scope remains 26 files. Added/removed feature lines are unchanged in 22 paths; four paths are mechanically adapted to the current owners. There is no new configuration, default, schema, or public contract.

## Evidence

### Current CI repair

- Signed correction: `81dafe4025b9cc5af158c9e78d00089fddaf93e5`, tree `6e6150c31cd0668c68288f30c33a748e3bf260f8`. Signature, parent, contributor ancestry, single-file scope, and whitespace were verified.

The previously failing [check-lint-core-4 job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39194275101/job/117874102888) now passes on `81dafe4025b9`: changed-lint step 62 seconds, total job 92 seconds. CI subsequently exposed the three main-side failures below. No all-green CI, gate waiver, or merge-readiness claim is made; the PR remains open with auto-merge off.

### Remaining main-side CI failures

The tested checkout is merge `5944d01c08a10ebe46622aadb2269371576e450a`, with exact main parent `b34a4659de9c36a34e1f3ed8399dd9c357214509` and PR parent `81dafe4025b9cc5af158c9e78d00089fddaf93e5`.

### Prior conflict-repair evidence (`5eeb132797fc`)

The evidence below remains bound to its original source and tested tree, not a fresh runtime execution of the CI-repair head.

- Historical conflict-repair head: `5eeb132797fc2b8ed1ad8bb6da0736597a8b3a6d`; tree: `d44256349cbaeb239327c128e33cb2dad57876f9`. Signature, ordered parents, contributor ancestry, source scope, whitespace, and absence of unresolved entries were verified. The committed tree exactly matches the isolated tested and independently reviewed source.
- Secretless offline Linux Docker proof used the frozen lockfile with Node 24.21.0 and pnpm 12.11.1. `pnpm test src/media-understanding/runner.cli-audio.test.ts src/media-understanding/audio-preflight.attachments.test.ts src/media-understanding/runner.entries.guards.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed all 49 tests in three files; combined wall time was 267.96 seconds, including cold worker preparation and x86-64 emulation on the ARM host. No contributor runtime or tests executed on the operator host.

Current-head hosted CI seconds are not yet available; they are not inferred from this container run.
- Targeted formatting and lint passed for the four adapted files; the core TypeScript production check also passed. Fresh independent P0–P2 review of the complete 26-file feature delta reported no actionable findings. That review is patch-scoped; runtime proof is the separate isolated test execution.

prs.title: fix(memory): defer dreaming when no ambient owner resolves
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A valid multi-agent config with an explicit roster (`agents.ownership: "explicit"`) and no `agents.defaults.systemAgent` makes memory-core log a red error at Gateway startup and then once a minute, forever:

```
[plugins] memory-core: dreaming cron reconcile failed: Agent-less cron job has no resolvable owner. Pass --agent <id> when creating or editing the job, or set agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId.
```

Found while running live multi-agent sub-agent fleets on isolated Gateways; a base Gateway accumulated 107 of these error lines in a few minutes of uptime.

## User Impact

memory-core warns once when an explicit multi-agent roster has no ambient owner, then enables automatic dreaming when `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId` is set. Existing managed jobs keep their current reconciliation behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Root cause

`reconcileShortTermDreamingCronJob` (`extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming-cron.ts`) calls `cron.add` with an agent-less managed job. The Gateway cron service resolves the owner through the ambient owner (`src/gateway/server-cron.ts`), which an explicit roster without a system agent does not have, so `resolveCronJobEffectiveAgentId` throws `CRON_AGENT_SELECTION_REQUIRED_MESSAGE`. The runtime reconcile timer retries every minute and logs each failure as an error.

### Fix

The cron owner's no-owner failure now carries the stable code `AGENT_SELECTION_REQUIRED` (`CronAgentSelectionRequiredError`, message unchanged). memory-core keeps calling `cron.add`, recognizes that code with the existing `extractErrorCode` helper, skips creating the managed dreaming job, and emits one actionable warning per state change naming `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId`; the job is created as soon as an owner resolves. Reconciliation of existing jobs and all other errors are unchanged. No new Plugin SDK exports.

## Evidence

- Live: isolated Gateway built from this branch with the explicit-roster config above. Over 140 s (more than two reconcile intervals) it logged exactly one line, `memory-core: managed dreaming cron job was not created because no ambient agent owner is configured. Set agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId ...`, and no errors. The same config on main logs the error every minute.
- `pnpm test extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming.test.ts`: red on main (error logger called 4 times), green with the fix (20/20). Regressions cover warning suppression, coded owner failures, recovery once a system agent is configured, warning re-arming, existing-job updates, and propagation of unrelated errors.
- `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check`: exports 3810, callable 2208 (unchanged).
- Focused tests on the redesigned head: dreaming 20/20, cron agent-id, server-cron-notifications 25/25, services.cron 6/6.
- `pnpm test src/cron/service/failure-alerts.outcome.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 13/13 pass after updating the stale generic-error assertion to require the stable code and unchanged message (85.6 s local command wall time; CI file time 4.3 s on the preceding failing head).
- Targeted oxfmt/oxlint and `git diff --check` pass. Local tsgo for the plugin needs generated SDK declarations; PR CI covers types.

## Release note context

Fix: memory-core no longer logs a recurring "dreaming cron reconcile failed" error on explicit multi-agent rosters without a system agent; it warns once and enables dreaming when `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId` is set.

## What Problem This Solves

Model and media callers repeat alias, provider, terminal-event, limit and tool-choice facts that already have an owner. Parallel tables can drift independently.

## What Changed

The session-fork descriptor preserves both admission and point-of-effect checks, including both original refusal messages and fresh Anthropic tool-choice objects.

This is a dependency-closed area split under campaign rule11. Public SDK/config/CLI/protocol/persisted shapes and dependencies remain unchanged. Core does not import plugin internals. Main's newer reasoning-replay owner is deliberately excluded rather than duplicated or overwritten. Phase E is untouched.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- No authority, input-validation, concurrency, durability or recovery guard is removed; this consolidates immutable facts.
- Exact model matching remains distinct from existing normalized prefix/display-name matching. Manifest aliases and the remaining legacy xAI aliases preserve their established precedence.
- MiniMax duration/resolution maps retain their different membership and public capability shape; combining them would add projections rather than simplify the owner.
- Media default caches retain main's immutable manifest-generation lifecycle, and scope resolution retains main's first-match policy.

The subsequent 31-suite selection passed 457 cases, including prefix stability, session-fork request replay and authority withdrawal, Responses tool pairing/recovery, image execution, media defaults and provider routes. One bounded replay of only that case passed unchanged (196.80-second suite, including cold preparation). Combined: 507 distinct cases passed. The original timeout remains investigated evidence; the passing replay is not a claimed defect repair or inherited-CI attribution.

The MiniMax video suite has an investigated local setup failure: two Bun selections and a supported Node-runtime selection reached the existing180s dynamic-import hook timeout before any of its12case bodies ran. No timeout/retry/skip was changed, and no passing video claim or inherited-failure attribution is made. The changed duration/resolution checks are inside functions not invoked by that import hook; the import/helper/hook inputs remain unchanged.

prs.title: fix(gateway): render Claude CLI history turns once
prs.body:
Closes #123792

## What Problem This Solves

Claude CLI history could render one assistant turn twice in the Control UI and Android app. The rich imported turn appeared first with native tool cards. A flat persisted copy appeared below it.

Telegram delivery is not affected because it does not render merged history.

## Root Cause

The CLI runner persists one synthetic assistant aggregate with `api: "cli"` and `idempotencyKey: "cli-assistant:<runId>"`. The Gateway also imports the bound Claude transcript as native text and tool-call blocks.

The old merge compared one message at a time. It could not match one aggregate such as `text one\n\ntext two` to several imported blocks from the same turn.

Underneath that, nothing linked the two shapes at all. Only the producer sees both the flattened aggregate and the native records it came from, and it recorded no relation, which left every reader inferring one from text, provider and timing.

## Fix

The producer records the relation, and the merge resolves it instead of inferring one.

- Run settlement already resolves the native record id of a run's terminal assistant message, for resume. It now records that id, with the native session that owns it, on the aggregate it persists: `cliNativeTurn: { cliSessionId, terminalRecordId }`, a declared field on the transcript message contract.
- The Gateway history owner groups imported assistant messages into turns and indexes them by the native record their last message came from.
- An aggregate is only ever replaced by the turn it names, in the native session it names.
- The remaining text comparison is a completeness check on that identified pair, not an identity test: a trimmed or partially imported turn no longer covers the aggregate's text, so the aggregate is kept as the durable copy.
- Imported native blocks are unchanged, including `toolcall` IDs, names, and arguments.

This removes the five-minute window for aggregates, the text-and-provider keyed index, the ordered pairing and the nearest-turn selection. The resolver uses result identity so a one-for-one replacement still counts as an import.

**Fail-open by construction.** An aggregate that names no native turn is never replaced. That covers every record persisted before this field existed, every backend that writes no native transcript, and every run whose terminal record was not reported. The consequence is deliberate: the duplicate stays visible for history already on disk until those sessions produce new turns. Removing those would require exactly the text-and-time inference this design rejects, because no rule built from text, provider and time can tell a true duplicate from a distinct same-text turn when either history is partial.

The async snapshot reader projects any JSONL line past 1 MiB through a bounded worker. That projection rebuilds the entry from a fixed field list, so the turn-boundary facts the grouping reads have to survive it; an importer/resolver parity regression covers both readers over the same oversized transcript.

The rebase onto current `main` integrates #130463 and #133316, the commits that have touched `cli-session-history.merge.ts` since this PR's original base. #133316's prepared-facts refactor is the base — its injected identity key, its `localImageMediaCounts` map — and the aggregate/turn matching is layered on top, so its tests and this PR's regressions both hold. Preparing the whole import ahead of the merge loop is gated on the session actually holding a persisted aggregate, so a session without one keeps #133316's lazy, skip-on-identity path unchanged.

## Evidence

Head: `8a7447409ff9c3ae3118a029116e1ab7a83fa2c6`, rebased onto `43e9a3d817` (current `main`). The evidence below was measured on `b538e9752c`, the same four commits before that rebase; the rebase carried them across 409 upstream commits with no conflicts and no diff change.

Current-main reproduction, re-run on that exact base: applying this PR's regression file to `86b6ec0afa` and leaving main's merge owner in place fails 11 tests.

```text
Test Files  1 failed (1)
     Tests  11 failed | 77 passed (88)
```

Four of them:

- `replaces a persisted aggregate with the imported native turn blocks` — expected a length of 4, got 5. The persisted aggregate remains beside the imported native blocks.
- `keeps a skill instruction row inside the turn it belongs to` — expected 0 aggregates, got 1. #130269 already hides the skill instruction row on that base, and the turn still renders twice.
- `projects an oversized skill instruction row exactly as the sync reader does` — expected 0 aggregates, got 1. The same defect through the async snapshot's bounded worker projection.
- `keeps the only local aggregate when the import holds a different turn with the same text` — the aggregate is deleted. This is the crossed partial-history loss path, and it is the reason this PR resolves aggregates by recorded identity rather than by text and time.

Focused proof on the head:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/cli-session-history.test.ts
88 passed

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/cli-session-history.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server-methods/chat-history-pages.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server.chat-history-cursor.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server.chat.gateway-server-chat-b.test.ts \
  src/agents/tools/embedded-gateway-stub.test.ts \
  src/agents/cli-runner/cli-run-transcript.test.ts
273 passed (3 shards)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/lib/chat/message-normalizer.test.ts \
  -t 'detects tool messages by toolcall content blocks'
1 passed | 85 skipped
```

One of those, `carries the recorded native turn from the CLI producer through to the merge`, drives the real producer, the real SQLite store, the real display projection, the real JSONL importer and the real resolver, so a field lost at any of those seams fails the suite instead of silently disabling the fix.

Repo checks on the head: `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:test:src` clean, `run-oxlint src/gateway src/agents` 0 warnings and 0 errors, the assertion-safety and max-lines ratchets OK, `oxfmt --check` clean. The `cli-session-history.merge.ts` assertion-safety baseline entry shrinks `6 → 1`.

The resolver test reads a real Claude JSONL fixture. It asserts the retained imported content is exactly the text block plus `{ type: "toolcall", id: "toolu_1", name: "Bash", arguments: { command: "pwd" } }`. The UI normalization test confirms that shape remains a native tool card.

Repeated-text benchmark with 24,000 imported turns and 24,000 aggregates. Measured on `6e25b0ae`, an earlier head, and not re-run since:

| Matcher | Three samples | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Previous claim forests | 95–112 ms | 72,000 native messages, 0 aggregates |
| Ordered turn pairing | 80–95 ms | 72,000 native messages, 0 aggregates |

The Telegram fallback run, also on `6e25b0ae`, recorded one deterministic direct-message turn because this history-only change is not Telegram-visible. The bot typed and returned `OPENCLAW_E2E_OK`; the mock provider received one `POST /v1/responses`.

## Control UI Proof

Measured on two live Gateways, each built from source and serving its own `chat.history` from **the same store**: a copy of a production OpenClaw agent store holding 878 persisted `cli-assistant:<runId>` aggregates. Only the commit differs, and the Control UI is byte-identical on both sides because this PR changes 0 files under `ui/`.

| | commit |
| --- | --- |
| base | `86b6ec0afa` |
| head | `b538e9752c` |

The turn was produced by **running a real agent turn through the head build**, not by editing a store: Claude CLI 2.1.250 on the `claude-cli` backend, prompted for a line of text, then `pwd` through Bash, then a closing sentence — the two-text-blocks-around-a-tool-call shape this bug needs. The producer recorded the relation on that run:

```json
"idempotencyKey": "cli-assistant:be40a3bc-c230-4e59-bb83-c5fa6e8846c9",
"cliNativeTurn": {
  "cliSessionId": "881503c4-fa93-4da4-b514-b94ba6afd637",
  "terminalRecordId": "5d666065-18d8-4a2c-8651-d2dfa6e330c9"
}
```

`terminalRecordId` is the turn's terminal native assistant record.

| rendered rows | `86b6ec0afa` | `b538e9752c` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| imported native blocks | 3, incl. the `Bash` card | 3, unchanged |
| persisted aggregate `msg:id:687e4295-…` | present — the turn renders twice | absent |
| total | 6 | 5 |

The durable fallback holds on that same head: a session whose aggregate predates `cliNativeTurn` keeps its 6,781-character aggregate, because it names no native turn. In that store 1 aggregate carries the relation and 877 do not, and none of the 877 can be replaced.

Screenshots and the full measurement are in [this comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/124543#issuecomment-5477930396), including what the capture does not cover: that store holds no `Skill` turn, so the skill case stays covered by the regressions rather than by a capture.

prs.title: refactor(storage): unify transcript reader resource ownership
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Foreground transcript readers maintain a separate retained-store lifecycle beside the history database resource owner. Native reader residency is also tracked with numeric dispatch/retirement frontiers. Both duplicate facts already available at native rotation and reply acceptance.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible behavior or stored-data change. Reader cleanup and admitted writes retain their shutdown guarantees. The existing worker-pool SDK type gains one optional callback; existing constructor calls remain compatible.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing historyDatabases owner for foreground registration, pending reads, revocation, native residency, host-effect settlement and cleanup. Keep its exact lexical candidate cache for measured warm reuse. Replace numeric frontiers with lane residency and per-resource lane membership, published synchronously after actual native exit and before queued redispatch. Qualified exact idle close clears only covered membership before yielding and restores it on failure. Usage replies install closed-reader facts before the singleton successor can dispatch.

The optional WorkerTaskPool onRotationComplete constructor callback is SDK-reachable through the existing process-runtime export: this is an additive API option, not zero SDK impact. Existing constructor calls, exports and required capabilities remain compatible. Selected-engine workerData, 512+32 MiB reader bounds, independent lanes, FIFO/current authority, real host writes, failed-stop registration, original errors and cleanup retry remain. No schema/column, persisted shape, durability, retention, permission, config-key, protocol, dependency or Phase E change.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Numeric native frontiers introduced in #152691 (88004e9cc669) and later relocated in #167739 are replaced by publication at the actual native-rotation boundary, not by assuming a worker has stopped. The cited PR mechanism/synthetic interleaving is not a human incident requiring the duplicate counter protocol. Ordinary overlap, physical binding and accepted-write settlement stay protected.
- Competing foreground retained-store bookkeeping is removed; its existing physical/alias/family registration moves to the common resource owner. Alias changes during a read remain best effort as before. Native exit, revocation and failed-cleanup retry are still required before registration is released.

## Evidence

The current candidate is signed head `7eaef1124bfdf07c1d46358557e0fe6f0e34dc90`, from fresh-main base `55ce16b61cd5822f98be360d8297aca7de4353f3`:15 paths, seven production files +320/-291 = **29 production lines added**. This is a structural ownership recovery, not deletion credit. All15 postimages initially matched the reviewed donor; later local alias-key renames repaired no-shadow lint, and a separate signed one-line repair observes the physical maintenance registration on reuse, fixing the migration's discovered ownership gap.

Complete independent review is scoped-clean through P2, confidence0.88, with final source verification complete. Full report/status were personally read; the unchanged semantic cut reuses that review. Targeted native types include all15 changed paths plus the public process-runtime export and passed. The first lint scan found two introduced no-shadow errors; plain local renames repaired them, with no suppression or allowance. Repaired-file type-aware lint, formatting of all15 files, runtime value cycles0, static/Madge cycles0, the SDK registration/export check and whitespace pass. The normal signed commit hook formatted15 files in48ms without a source delta.

Initial package/bootstrap and low-level worker lifetime proof completed68 cases across6 files with final generation verification. The next four-file group found three genuine failures: maintenance.close retired the worker after an independent caller had reused it. The shared physical registration still belonged to the old maintenance scope, while only alias registrations were observed on reuse. One call to the existing registration-observation API transfers the physical claim too; no test or assertion changed. All36 cases in that group then passed, including exact/family/alias close behavior, with final generation verification complete (188.33s wrapper). The one-line repair also passed16-root targeted native types, owner lint/format and a fresh isolated P0–P2 review, scoped-clean0.96; the earlier complete cut review remains applicable to unchanged code.

Gateway performance (four cases) and search (seven cases) subsequently passed with final generation verification. Retained completed passing proof is115 cases across12 files. The usage-cache group completed all10 cases, six passing and four unresolved failures: fresh/partial usage times out at its unchanged30000ms budget; queued-selection pruning misses its second update notification; late-host-write cancellation and admitted-successor cancellation fail to reach their host-write observation. The first three also report a still-live worker at teardown. The wrapper completed final-generation verification (785.27s); this is not a passing group. The next four-file consumer batch was bounded after the deletion/environment case timed out at120472ms/unchanged120000, and its wrapper was deliberately interrupted. Its other cases and aggregate remain unproved locally. No test, assertion, timeout, retry or skip changed. Source inspection has not established a causal fix; these are explicitly unresolved local failures, not inherited-CI claims. Further local replay under the same loaded host is not treated as useful causal evidence; exact-head PR CI is the broad gate, and any changed-path hosted failure must receive the required serial tested-head/base attribution replay. Wrapper inventory passed its selected case (101.43s wrapper); source closure passed all three cases and suppression checks passed all14 cases (121.52s wrapper). The overall local driver exited130 because of the deliberately interrupted consumer group, not a guard failure. No aggregate runtime pass or exact-head hosted CI result is claimed; PR CI remains pending.

API-diff reporting is an explicitly unrun gap: ordinary PR CI does not select the dispatch-only report, and rendering/installing two full revisions at 8 GiB exceeds this campaign's local proof budget. Targeted types include the public process-runtime export and focused proof covers existing consumers. No report, build, or compatibility result is claimed before it exists; no workflow policy is changed or dispatched merely to obtain green.

Exact-head CI run39193374431 has reported five reader-test failures plus an untouched CI-planner mock-export finding; attribution and reader repair are in progress. ## What Problem This Solves

Refresh dependencies across the workspace and native/release tooling using a seven-day release cooldown (cutoff: 2026-10-11T19:49:25Z).

## User Impact

Updates supported dependencies without changing sandbox or termination guarantees. No configuration migration is required. MXC remains at 0.9.0, Gradle at 9.7.1, and windows-core at 0.62.2 because newer versions fail existing compatibility/security contracts. The maturity workflow retains Codex Action 1.12 until its custom runner is qualified for newer ACL requirements. Other upstream-constrained upgrades remain deferred.

## Why This Change Was Made

Update eligible npm dependencies and lockfiles, pnpm, Codex/CUA artifacts, Rust/Go dependencies, Swift resolution, and Ruby/Fastlane release tooling. Align compiler APIs, CI pins, fixtures, and documentation. Android’s 40 catalog pins were already current for the cutoff.

Reconcile with main through `5f637b6b3686`, retaining the canonical quota/publication owners from #176602 and tool-settlement owner from #176658 and removing the superseded monitor/global-wait repair. Keep tool settlement independent of presentation acceptance. Defer optional dialogs and attachment-only preview rendering at their existing visibility boundaries to meet the unchanged UI startup budgets; attachment reads, status announcements, and custody remain eager.

## Evidence

- Audited all 152 new npm package/version identities: zero unknown publication dates or seven-day cutoff violations.
- On the earlier main-60d candidate: 72 canonical owner tests and all nine real-Gateway quota scenarios passed with pinned Bun and CI two-CPU settings (196.449 seconds in cases). CI run `39182617676` then exposed 11 unit assertions across eight consumer files and two browser assertions that queried attachment previews before the new lazy boundary settled. All 288 affected unit tests and all five browser handoff scenarios pass locally; scoped types, lint, format, and independent P0–P2 fixture review pass. The maintained guard passes with 8,532 grandfathered factories and all three root-help tests pass. New published-head CI is still required; these are local repair results, not a green hosted run.

This takeover adds no cooldown exclusions. Local proof: frozen install, `pnpm tsgo:scripts` (tsrs), targeted lint/format, and 134 focused tests across the compiler, controller guard, database/preflight guard, Crabbox cancellation, ACP manifest, and root-help consumers passed. The typecheck first exposed the two obsolete imports and passed after their migration. Fresh isolated Codex review covers the conflict-resolution/lockfile delta and the supplemental import migration. The takeover candidate is `9caa4346caa50bf72ec95a466dbf62fc326c3f82`; fresh exact-head CI remains required before landing. The prior dependency head `f4ff7c41` passed run [39185925021](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39185925021) on attempt 2 after rerunning only the intermittent transcript-wait job.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Chat session panels synchronized their data owners through rendering effects, leaving old Stop authority or narration observation active until Solid flushed. Drive those existing owners from native input notifications: retire old authority immediately, coalesce the final session/agent inputs, and project owner snapshots into rendering.

Keep Details process observation at its stable native host across keyed content changes. Preserve hidden subagent selection, show-request identity, and immediate narration retirement when hidden or compact. Route Details `props` and `presented` notifications to its existing diff-summary owner, initializing it after the renderer settles. That owner retains request batching, polling cadence, session/connection result guards, cache, and disposal. The process/subagent owners, tags, classes, markup, styles, and lazy boundaries remain unchanged.

| Touched production scope | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| LOC, six files | 1,344 | 1,444 |
| `createEffect` | 4 | 0 |
| `createRenderEffect` | 0 | 0 |
| `untrack` | 0 | 0 |
| `addEventListener` | 0 | 0 |
| `querySelector(All)` | 0 | 0 |
| Controller patterns / production flush / owner escapes | 0 | 0 |

The 100 added production lines provide native input admission and paired teardown across the panel consumers. Tests add 365 lines for stale Stop authority, retained detail/request identity, narration retirement, Details observation through refresh/scope replacement/parking, and diff-summary input and polling lifecycle. No targeted-pattern survivors remain in the six production files. The diff-summary completion uses a private per-host callback; it adds no scheduler, synchronized state, shared abstraction, or request owner.

## Evidence

Base: `4317598f2fb1ec0ff3e7dc25ffb3be02d0261962`. Head: `ab8389b1e865e87ce107e2a3ebf5510d4bb363f3`. Main's sidebar import fix `e070647a0cf` is included. All ten touched files remain byte-identical to independently reviewed completion `aad2037e7dccce1a40cc2232f5ea91ca2ac3e229`.

prs.title: fix: stop reattaching historical images to CLI turns
prs.body:
Fixes #176629

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Claude CLI reattaches earlier inbound images and assistant media as new input when a later message contains only text.

## User Impact

User impact: later text-only turns stop acquiring historical image attachments, while current attachments, explicit image references, and channel-provided reply-to images remain supported. `/new` keeps its existing session-reset behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

CLI preparation can add conversation history and runtime context before image hydration. When callers omit `imagePrompt`, hydration scans that composed prompt, treating original image paths in the context as fresh attachments. Excluding generated CLI cache paths does not exclude those source paths.

The preparation owner now preserves the incoming prompt for image selection before adding context, while retaining explicit caller overrides. A single-use context-prompt alias is inlined. Production changes are +3/-2 lines (net +1 rationale comment, zero executable-line growth); there is no additional state or configuration and no new deferred side effect.

## Evidence

- Source/history confirmation: the reply adapter supplies current attachments but no `imagePrompt`; the CLI helper falls back to the composed prompt. Existing fixes #87523 and #100035 protect cached paths and callers that supply an explicit image prompt, respectively.
- Added `does not reattach historical images on a later text-only CLI turn` in `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.durable-context.test.ts`. It exercises production preparation and execution with a fixed transport, checking three turns against independent expectations: current PNG → one attachment; text-only with earlier inbound/outbound paths in context → none; explicit quoted media → one attachment with the expected bytes.
- Changed-file oxlint with `config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json`, oxfmt, and `git diff --check`: passed. The commit hook's line-cap ratchet also passed after removing the single-use alias.
- Autoreview: scoped-clean at P0–P2; no accepted/actionable findings. Review ran against the committed fix with the canonical isolated Codex helper. The exact-head GitHub Codex review also completed with no findings. ClawSweeper has acknowledged the PR but has not posted code findings.
- PR CI is the test gate and covers the regression, applicable agent-runtime tests, types, and repository checks. Exact-head CI: [run 39191592281](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39191592281), head `fc9b94ba96719235c51f4c051c47409f1c5b550a`; completed with 31 jobs passing, 27 skipped, and only the inherited test-type failure plus its aggregate CI gate failure. The changed test shards, production types, core test types, lint, docs, prompt snapshots, and boundary checks passed. The `check-test-types` failure is inherited: `extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-subagent-monitor.parent-retention.test.ts:37` references removed `MonitorOptions.completionDeliveryRetryDelaysMs` (TS2353). The identical error is present in the latest [scheduled main run 39191176869, job 117864340952](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39191176869/job/117864340952); [PR job 117866135801](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39191592281/job/117866135801).
- Local test execution, production-reverted negative controls, local typechecks, and live Gateway/Crabbox/Testbox proof were intentionally skipped per maintainer policy. No lease or Gateway was started. Local test wall time is unavailable. CI ran the regression in 848 ms; its full file passed all 20 tests in 24.02 s (25.88 s including shard cleanup), [job 117865691074](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39191592281/job/117865691074).

prs.title: perf(sessions): refresh process views on registry changes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Open Processes and Details views repeatedly fetch unchanged background processes every five seconds, even when those processes produce no new output.

Related: #176417.

## User Impact

Process views refresh when background processes start, accept Stop, produce output, exit, or are removed. Visible views keep a 60-second recovery poll; hidden panes and documents issue no process reads. Details and Processes continue sharing one observation per session and connection. Placement changes also refresh the current owner’s process list.

## Why This Change Was Made

The process registry now publishes coalesced, session-scoped invalidations without process output or command text. Local execution and retained workers feed the same Gateway event. Retained-worker notifications follow physical worker ownership and the current node connection, with current placement and pairing verified before broadcast.

Older node supervisors reject unknown worker frames, so workers emit the new frame only when negotiated. PTYs and dev servers already have their own events; iOS and Android progress cards already consume `progressCard.changed`; neither native client calls `sessions.processes.list`. Their protocol-coverage declarations therefore explicitly leave this Control UI event unhandled.

This removes the five-second client polling cadence rather than adding a second observation owner. The requested non-test/non-doc diff is **+288/−20 (net +268, including two event-coverage declarations and one retired mock allowance)** to supply the previously missing registry notification and retained-worker transport; the older-supervisor wire contract requires negotiation. No schema, config, or protocol-version change.

## Evidence

- Regression is red against the original client: 12 process-list requests over 59 seconds instead of the expected one initial request.
- Focused tests cover coalescing, teardown, retained workers, current connections, stale placement rejection, session authorization, shared observations, in-flight invalidation, and hidden views.
- Changed-file formatting and type-aware lint passed.
- CI caught missing mobile event-coverage declarations. Added the two source-verified entries; `node scripts/check-protocol-event-coverage.mjs` now passes (68 events covered). The two-line correction also passed independent review.
- CI also caught a component test still waiting for five-second polling. It now delivers the process-change event and retains both retirement/truncation assertions; its focused test, formatting, lint, and independent review pass.
- CI found a worker-command test mock replacing the entire process registry and hiding the new notification export. The partial mock now preserves real exports and overrides only its two lifecycle controls. All 28 focused worker-command tests pass (111.33 seconds runner wall time); changed-file formatting, lint, and independent review pass. The now-retired closed-mock baseline entry was also removed after CI requested that exact shrink; independent review passed.
- The export-name collision guard passed.
- Core typecheck passed with the native tsrs lane (`pnpm tsgo:core`).
- Independent Codex autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Browser measurements: **87.5–87.8% fewer process-list RPCs** in both paired runs. Full built Control UI, four isolated sockets per side, two synthetic processes per socket, half quiet and half receiving output/exit events. Identical base/head fixtures; concurrent 16-core sides under an exclusive lock, then swapped CPU halves. Counts exclude initial reads. Pair 1: **12.049 → 1.475 calls/min/socket** (B−A = −10.574); swapped pair 2: **11.803 → 1.475** (B−A = −10.328). Each ran for 61 seconds. Quiet sockets made one safety read; changing sockets made two event reads, and completed output rendered. Recorded CPU idle was 81.38% and 87.08%, respectively, for load context.

The browser measurement uses a mock Gateway to isolate client RPC demand; it does not measure whole-Gateway latency or production database load. Owner and transport behavior are covered by focused tests. Broad gates and the existing browser E2E scenario run in PR CI; no Testbox lease was allocated.

<details>
<summary>Focused validation</summary>

Run through `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <files> --maxWorkers=1`:

- `src/node-host/connection.test.ts`
- `src/node-host/node-worker-supervisor.idle.test.ts`
- `src/node-host/node-worker-supervisor.lifetime.test.ts`
- `src/worker/worker-process-observation.runtime.test.ts`
- `src/worker/worker-command.runtime.test.ts` (28 cases)
- `src/gateway/server-methods/nodes.event.test.ts`
- `src/gateway/server-runtime-subscriptions.test.ts`
- `src/gateway/server-runtime-subscriptions.shutdown.test.ts`
- `src/gateway/server-broadcast.board.test.ts`
- `ui/src/pages/chat/processes-panel-data.test.ts`
- `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-processes-panel.test.ts` (2 cases, 122 ms assertions; 6.09 seconds runner wall time)

All passed. The negotiation tests were repeated after moving feature selection into the frame builder; the moved coalescing/teardown test passed in the existing shutdown file. The two focused import-closure files also passed (22 assertions, 44.83 seconds runner wall time). Broad browser-E2E gates ran in PR CI under the host compute limit.

</details>

![Before: synthetic background process view](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/408c59d3-db19-47cb-8828-3f4146af6498)

![After: event-driven observation of the same synthetic processes](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e608c744-9bb4-43e7-a3bb-db2e9bb6b849)

### Authority boundary

The node-event handler revalidates pairing after placement preparation, then checks the placement owner’s current observation and environment binding immediately before synchronous broadcast. This event does not enter the broadcaster’s queued live-text path. Recipient session access is checked before socket admission, and process output remains behind the list RPC. Existing tests cover the real placement-observation contract, node-event rejection, and final-socket recipient filtering separately; they are not a single combined real-worker revocation scenario. The exact-head ClawSweeper re-review found no introduced code defect or reachable bypass and confirmed both invalidation fixes. Its requested combined real-worker revocation scenario and older-supervisor upgrade run remain proof limitations. The existing tests verify placement fencing, node rejection, final-socket access filtering, and feature negotiation separately; this is not a claim of a combined end-to-end or upgrade run. The additional scenarios are declined as merge blockers: no deferred broadcaster delivery exists between final authority validation and socket admission, and unsupported peers do not negotiate the frame. Existing transport byte buffering after that admission remains unchanged. Enforced security checks still apply.

### Follow-up review

Hosted review identified two missed invalidations: accepted Stop before final exit, and session placement changes. Cancellation now has one registry-owned transition used by all three callers, preserving their existing ordering. The worker regression asserts the Stop notification before any output/exit can mask it; the UI regression requires a placement event alone to replace the old process row. Both regressions failed at those boundaries before the fixes. All 20 focused worker, cancellation, observation, and UI tests passed afterward (89.42 seconds runner wall time; modified worker assertions 41 ms, modified UI assertions 71 ms). Changed-file formatting/lint and export-name checks passed; independent Codex review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. The repeated closure check passed 18/22 assertions; four wrapper-launch checks stopped on the local installation’s `@openclaw/proc-safe` 0.4.1 versus updated main’s required 0.4.2. No dependency reinstall was attempted under the lane’s one-install limit; fresh-install PR CI owns that remaining proof.

### Exact-head CI and inherited-failure landing

Reviewed head `e584124533cb1ecce05f1d131d2d78377c1686c5` contains the same six independently reviewed lane commits, rebased patch-identically onto main's typecheck repair #176834. [Run 39192879953](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39192879953) tested merge `603190861340b4d6af5c741a66c21ebdbde3fc79`, with verified ordered parents main `fcbcaad75f0db848b54df62275ff4beaacbd50d0` and this PR head. **87 jobs passed, 20 were skipped, and three root jobs plus their aggregate failed.** All three PostgreSQL conformance shards passed.

The three remaining root failures are independently reproduced or measured on the exact baseline:

- [UI performance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39192879953/job/117869653118): the same-toolchain base already exceeds the unchanged 1,490,000-byte chat-boot gzip cap at **1,491,409 bytes**. Candidate: **1,491,563 bytes**, **+154 bytes**, unchanged **25 requests**; new-page boot decreases 28 bytes. The policy owners and cap are unchanged.
- [Mock-export ratchet](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39192879953/job/117869652774): the real single-file scanner reports the identical unallowed factory in `test/scripts/ci-node-test-plan.test.ts:3285` for `../../scripts/lib/ci-test-timings.mts` on base and head, fingerprint `8c74b1e63618912d9ac86d6697e483f02edeae751b9edb61b44c668c7f9db59c`. The offending test and scanner are unchanged. Each revision's ledger lacks this entry; this PR only removes a different retired worker-mock allowance.
- [Startup-update test](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39192879953/job/117869653928): `src/gateway/server-startup-update-check.test.ts` fails at “scopes background update broadcasts to read-capable operator clients,” expecting one call and receiving zero. Running only that file on this head and the exact main parent reproduces the same assertion: **1 failed / 7 passed on each**. The test, startup owner, and scheduler helper are unchanged. No passing replay or speculative cause is claimed.

The aggregate fails downstream of these three jobs. Landing uses the standing inherited-failure exception after native evidence verification; this is not a claim of green CI. No CI reruns were requested. Production and test typechecks, five core test-type stripes, security-fast, native checks, and the other completed test lanes passed on this exact head.

An earlier run, [39191316346](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39191316346/job/117864949685), reported `runtime authority closed before node dispatch` on the repeated native turn in `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/codex-node-exec-server.e2e.test.ts`. Its first call completed; the second was rejected before dispatch. The fixture and invocation/grant owners are unchanged by this PR. This prior failure remains unexplained and is not classified as inherited or fixed; the exact file's execution in the current run has not been independently located. Source tracing suggests a pre-existing grant-receipt invalidation risk, but the log does not identify the failing predicate. The earlier worker-capacity failure also received no targeted fix. Later passing lanes do not prove either cause or repair.
