prs.title: perf(gateway): avoid registry copies during streamed events
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Streaming agent events repeatedly copy the entire RPC-source registry to find one run. The resulting allocations grow with concurrent runs.

## User Impact

Reduces unnecessary work during concurrent streaming turns while preserving event routing and Gateway isolation. No configuration or public behavior changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing `getRpcSourceForGateway` owner, which looks up the requested run ID and enforces Gateway scope and exactly-one-match semantics. This removes the subscription layer's duplicate lookup policy: production delta **+3 / −9 lines (net −6)**.

## Evidence

An isolated Linux Gateway with 5,000 synthetic sessions, 6,000 retained runs, real tool calls, and 40 compressed WebSocket clients reproduced the allocation cost. At 80 concurrent streaming turns, the old lookup accounted for **426.3 MB of sampled inclusive allocations in 20.6 seconds**. This is allocation churn, not retained memory or a before/after claim.

- 89 tests passed across `server-runtime-subscriptions.test.ts`, `server-runtime-subscriptions.access.test.ts`, and `session-controller.rpc-sources.test.ts` with one worker.
- Changed-file lint and formatting passed; `pnpm tsgo:core` passed using the native typechecker.
- Independent Codex review: no actionable findings. Existing owner tests cover exact run identity, Gateway scope, explicit unbound ownership, and duplicate-match rejection.
- Broad validation runs in PR CI; no full local suite/build was run.

Paired runtime comparison is pending while the baseline 90-minute soak finishes. Acceptance is deletion of the full-registry allocation path with no user-facing regression beyond noise. A/B will use concurrent identical synthetic workloads on two 16-core halves under an exclusive lock, then swap halves, with paired differences reported here before landing.

### Inherited CI failure

`checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` in [run 39193037915](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39193037915/job/117870176209) reports the closed mock factory at `test/scripts/ci-node-test-plan.test.ts:3285` for `../../scripts/lib/ci-test-timings.mts`. The production native parser and `scanClosedMockFactories`, narrowed to that failing file/target, reproduce the identical violation with exit 1 on both the CI main parent `ef4027702bad7730cee36f81a421ed3da7526029` and PR head `db8022a061253b8508fe8c476f7aa9b85da8d843`. The test, baseline, checker, scanner, parser wrapper, and target module have identical SHA-256 values on both revisions. This patch changes none of them. No CI rerun was requested.

prs.title: fix(codex): prepare web search policy before harness dispatch
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Deleting another agent can make a healthy agent's Codex turn fail with `Session capability metadata requires worker preparation`. Preparing search policy in core fixes that lookup, but the resulting allowance must remain bound to the native model and requester facts it was computed from.

A model switch or requester revocation between preparation and native capture could previously enable hosted search with stale policy. Compaction also performed an unused search lookup with different execution and sandbox-policy owners.

## User Impact

Healthy Codex turns use core's worker-prepared search policy. A changed native model or requester now rejects the stale operation before native thread/turn writes with an actionable retry message. Compaction keeps its existing execution owner and skips unused search preparation.

## Why This Change Was Made

This preserves the maintainer's prepared-data decision: optional `preparedWebSearchPolicy` data on existing attempt parameters, with no new SDK export, callable policy capability, or capability version. Existing no-field and two-boolean SDK callers remain source-compatible. Codex still applies per-turn tool caps and memory-flush restrictions.

Core records the exact model tuple and requester policy/lineage reads used during preparation. The existing native-policy owner compares them with captured/current facts, retains keyed and ID-selector source checks, and synchronously asserts them at the physical native write, including absent or reassigned IDs and pending worker publications. A mismatch never consumes the old allowance or falls back to synchronous policy resolution. The native requester-admission prerequisite from #176352 is included.

## Evidence

Current reviewed head: `97b231c1bed1ee13046e1645b41955a73674ebb8`. It fixes the session-ID admission finding by retaining ID selection (including absence) in the existing session-currentness owner through the synchronous physical-write assertion. ID-affecting worker commits pending host publication also invalidate admission. The former asynchronous-only ID path is removed. See the [finding reply](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174774#discussion_r4310017874).

At this head, all 9 recording-JSON-RPC native-boundary tests pass, including late absent-to-present and reassignment controls; all 19 session-owner tests and 103 Codex app-server tests pass. Core, Codex-source and scoped test types; SDK surface/export synchronization and scoped source compatibility; lint/format; docs links; and zero-cycle checks pass. Independent committed-branch Codex review is scoped-clean through P2, with no findings and the verdict “patch is correct.” The optional ID selector extends the existing helper additively; previous key-only helper and no-field/two-boolean prepared-policy callers compile unchanged.

The native late-ID controls fail on the preceding `b833540890ec` head because a stale allowance reaches the native write. The pending-publication control also fails before the publication guard is added. Final native proof requires zero writes for changed authority. No live provider or operator Gateway was used. Broad CI and ClawSweeper security re-review for the current head remain required before landing.

Historical CI: [39186087240](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39186087240) passed at `b833540890ecbaa06071a166ffa30b3d0c6b3518`, after repairing the direct test-API import and widened binding literal reported by [39184092677](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39184092677). This is prior-head evidence only.

Prior-head proof at `10efe93144a47fbe52da0338557454791509ffef`: local recording-JSON-RPC proof uses real core preparation, persisted requester updates, the real Codex harness and binding lifecycle, and real native write admission. No live model provider or operator Gateway was used.

| Native case | Thread/turn writes | Result |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Unchanged model | 2; search `cached` | Completed using prepared policy; no synchronous resolver call |
| Native model changed during worker preparation | 0 | Rejected |
| Requester revoked at native write admission | 0 | Rejected |
| Requester reassigned at native write admission | 0 | Rejected |
| Requester revoked after core preparation, before native capture | 0 | Rejected |

A supplemental sixth case captures a real missing-ID read, inserts a restrictive row under another key at native admission, and requires zero native writes. It isolates the ID-selector/transport contract.

On the preserved WIP before requester binding, the fifth case fails with two native writes, search `cached`, and a completed turn (325.25s command wall time). The earlier published-head controls also fail for the native-model switch and the compaction owner mismatch.

All 12 individually invoked Node-runtime suites pass: selection (91), execution environment (22), base dynamic-tool-build (74), web-search dynamic-tool-build (18), sandbox dynamic-tool-build (6), native authority (13), provider review (14), capability store (10), prefix stability (5), host model execution (18), original deletion regression (2), and native boundary proof (6): **279 tests passed**. Core and Codex source types, SDK surface/exports, Madge (zero cycles), touched lint/format, docs, and diff/line-cap checks pass.

Independent committed-branch Codex autoreview is scoped-clean through P2, with no findings and the explicit verdict “patch is correct.” Production delta over the previously published head is +273/−72 (net +201); the whole PR is +322/−80 (net +242). The additional code records the original requester facts and carries their currentness check through existing native admission; it adds no state owner or storage format.

Direct source types and SDK surface/exports are checked locally; packaged SDK declarations remain CI-owned. No new storage, config, protocol, SDK export, or model-facing prompt text is introduced. Pending native supervision without a selected model retains its documented existing policy-resolution path and deletion-time limitation.

Known limitation: `/btw` side-runs and native-auth supervision without a `modelRef` retain the pre-existing unbound policy fallback; binding these paths to prepared data is tracked separately as F78 after this PR lands, consistent with #176352’s exclusion of re-resolving every ancestor policy edit.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep page drafts and data through reconnects
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: brief Gateway disconnects wipe loaded pages, the sidebar roster, approvals and unsaved drafts outside Settings.

Many owners reset on every transport edge of the same client: shared agent, identity, project and profile catalogs cleared (so roster-mode navigation blanked); Scheduled tasks replaced its whole state and dropped the editor draft; Memory Import reset selections and, on replanning, silently re-selected every item (broadening the next import); Activity, the run inspector and Dreaming discarded results; approval queues cleared and a failed reconnect read left pending approvals invisible; the command palette showed "No results" offline; Inbox items disappeared; session rename / new-group dialogs and inline header rename were aborted with the typed text lost, and a failed rename could close the dialog as if it succeeded; the sidebar menu disabled even local actions; board documents released their provider and portals destroyed their iframe.

## User Impact

User impact: during a spotty connection your pages, roster, approvals and drafts stay where they were; actions that need the Gateway are disabled until it returns, and everything refreshes quietly on reconnect.

## Why This Change Was Made

Request-generation fencing is unchanged; only presentation and drafts now outlive a same-identity transport edge, and they still reset on a different client, Gateway, account or recovery scope (covered explicitly by tests). Approvals stay visible but non-actionable offline and their reconnect refresh retries with the existing question-recovery backoff. Memory Import keeps explicit selections and inputs. Dialogs keep drafts with submit disabled offline; non-success results keep the dialog open with feedback, and a settled dialog can no longer submit against a replacement owner. Fixes are made at the shared owners (catalogs, roster activity, board provider lease) rather than per page where possible.

Part of the offline-first series.

## Evidence

- Regression tests per owner for same-client retention and account/recovery-scope retirement (agents, identity, roster activity, projects, profile directory, session hydration, Cron, Memory Import, Activity, Dreaming, approvals, command palette, attention, mentions, sidebar session drafts, header rename, board document, portals).

prs.title: fix(agents): claude-cli agents call a nonexistent message tool because prompts use bare tool names
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/chughtapan/moltzap/issues/1178

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: claude-cli agents call a `message` tool that does not exist, because the OpenClaw system prompt and delivery hints name OpenClaw tools by their bare gateway names while Claude Code exposes them as `mcp__openclaw__<name>`.

## User Impact

Claude Code agents on the `claude-cli` runtime see the tool names they can actually call, so channel replies through the message tool no longer start with a failed call. Other CLI backends and the embedded runtime render the same prompt as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The claude-cli system prompt lists OpenClaw tools under "Names case-sensitive; call exact" as `- message: ...`, and the delivery hints say `message(action=send)` / "Use `message`". Claude Code registers the bundle MCP server's tools as `mcp__openclaw__message`, `mcp__openclaw__exec`, and so on. A model that follows the prompt calls `message` and gets:

```
<tool_use_error>Error: No such tool available: message</tool_use_error>
```

It usually retries with the prefixed name. Sometimes it concludes the messaging tool is unavailable and ends the turn without replying.

The change:

- `resolveOpenClawMcpToolNamePrefix(bundleMcpMode)` sits next to the existing `stripOpenClawMcpToolPrefix` in `cli-runner/tool-policy.ts`. It returns `mcp__openclaw__` for `claude-config-file` and nothing for other modes. Core writes that MCP config under the `openclaw` server name, so it already owns the naming.
- `buildAgentSystemPrompt` takes an optional `toolNamePrefix`. It changes only the names shown to the model: the tool list, the `resolveToolName` hints, the message-tool delivery lines, and the ClawHub line. Capability checks still use bare names. When a prefix is present, the Tooling section adds one line saying that unprefixed names elsewhere, for example in skills or channel context, refer to the prefixed tools.
- `buildHarnessVisibleReplyGuidance` takes an optional `messageToolName`, which defaults to `message`. The CLI runner passes the prefixed name, so per-turn guidance matches.

Gemini (`gemini-system-settings`) and Codex modes are left unchanged here. I have not checked how those CLIs name MCP tools in their prompts.

## Evidence

Real behavior on head `4a68ca7c8c9`, which is rebased onto `56d39dc9400`; full redacted trace in [this comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166371#issuecomment-6115811921):

- Setup: the `group-visible-reply-tool` QA scenario (`messages.groupChat.visibleReplies: message_tool`) on the `claude-cli` backend. Real Claude Code 2.1.296 on a subscription login, isolated HOME, and OpenClaw's own `--strict-mcp-config` bridge.
- The per-turn guidance Claude received reads ``Use `mcp__openclaw__message(action=send)` ``.
- The first and only tool call is `mcp__openclaw__message` `{"action":"send","message":"QA-GROUP-TOOL-OK"}`. It succeeded: the qa-channel bus recorded the outbound message in the source group, and OpenClaw recorded `outcome=tool_delivered`. The session has no bare `message` call and no `No such tool available` error.
- Control on `main`, same harness: the guidance reads ``Use `message(action=send)` ``. In that single run the model still guessed the prefixed name. The bare-name failure is intermittent, and the control shows the changed text, not a failure rate.
- The scenario's `successfulToolCallCounts.message === 1` assertion fails on both heads. For claude-cli, OpenClaw's session transcript has no tool-call events. This is a QA-lab accounting gap, independent of this change.

Tests and checks on the rebased head:

- New tests in `helpers.system-prompt.test.ts`: with the Claude prefix, the CLI prompt lists `- mcp__openclaw__message`, its delivery hints use `mcp__openclaw__message(action=send)`, and it has no bare `- message:` line. Without a prefix, the output is unchanged.
- `prepare.command-continuity.test.ts` asserts that a real `prepareCliRunContext` run with a `claude-config-file` backend produces the prefixed tool list, the prefixed hints, and prefixed per-turn guidance.
- `pnpm test src/agents/cli-runner/tool-policy.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner/helpers.system-prompt.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.command-continuity.test.ts src/agents/system-prompt.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 188 tests passed in 4 shards. Wall time was 48m30s on a heavily loaded shared host; the two new tests take about 18 ms each.
- `pnpm check:changed` exited 0.

## Relation to #153032

#153032 targets the same failure from a different owner. It adds an Anthropic-plugin `transformSystemPrompt` overlay that explains the mapping, plus a sentence in the stranded-reply retry prompt. This PR fixes the mismatch at the point where core renders model-visible names: the tool list, delivery hints, and per-turn guidance. It also adds one mapping line for bare names that come from elsewhere, such as skills, channel context, or the retry prompt.

If this PR lands, the #153032 system-prompt overlay is redundant. Its stranded-reply retry wording becomes optional, because the mapping line already covers that path. I have not changed #153032.

prs.title: fix: agents in a group acknowledge each other forever when bot-sender silence is allowed
prs.body:
Related: #164946
Related: #159230

## What Problem This Solves

Two agents in the same group can keep acknowledging each other under `message_tool` visible-reply mode. With `silentReply.group: "allow"`, an unaddressed group turn is admitted as optional. The per-turn delivery hint still tells the model to *"send the final user-visible answer"*, though, so a bot that has nothing to add posts anyway, and the other agent receives that post as a new request.

## Scope

After integrating `main`, the PR changes only that hint. `main` already skips stranded-reply recovery for optional turns (`isStrandedPrivateMessageToolFinal` requires a required expectation), and admission (`resolveSourceReplyExpectation`) is `main`'s, unchanged.

| Turn (`message_tool_only`, user request) | Hint before | Hint after |
|---|---|---|
| Bot sender, admitted `optional` (e.g. unaddressed group turn under `allow`) | "Use the `message` tool to send the final user-visible answer" | "If a visible reply is warranted, use the `message` tool to send it; none is required." |
| Bot sender, admitted `required` (explicit mention, authorized command, `disallow`, direct chat) | standard | standard (unchanged) |
| Human sender, any | standard | standard (unchanged, byte for byte) |

Earlier revisions also changed admission (bot-specific optional replies and implicit mentions) and recovery. Those changes are removed: admission is now `main`'s, and recovery is generalized on `main`.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `src/plugin-sdk/message-tool-delivery-hints.ts`: new `BOT_SENDER_DELIVERY_HINT`, added to `MESSAGE_TOOL_DELIVERY_HINTS` so that transcript and memory sanitizers strip it like the other hints.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/source-reply-delivery-mode.ts → resolveUserRequestDeliveryHint`: returns that hint when the sender is a bot and the admitted expectation is `optional`, and the standard hint otherwise. It sits next to `resolveSourceReplyExpectation`, which owns admission.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run-context.ts → resolvePerTurnDeliveryDirective`: calls it for `message_tool_only` user requests, using `SenderIsBot` and the admitted `terminalReplyExpectation`.
- `docs/concepts/messages.md`: one sentence under the silent-reply rules.

## Evidence

- `source-reply-delivery-mode.test.ts → resolveUserRequestDeliveryHint`, run against real `resolveSourceReplyExpectation` admission: only bot + `allow` gets the optional hint. Bot + `disallow`, human + `allow`, unknown sender + `allow` and a bot's explicit mention keep the standard hint.
- `source-reply-delivery-mode.test.ts`, `get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts`, `heartbeat-filter.test.ts` and `memory-capture-sanitization.test.ts` (the last two iterate `MESSAGE_TOOL_DELIVERY_HINTS`): 200 tests passed locally (`pnpm test <files> --maxWorkers=2`).
- Channel proof on `227dda864ff`, which behaves the same as this head (the later commits only format the code and move hint selection into a helper): https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166380#issuecomment-6258351902. The run used the bundled Discord plugin, a local Crabline server and `claude-cli/claude-sonnet-4-6` on subscription auth. Under `allow`, three bot status reports got the optional hint and left substantive private finals (371 to 503 chars) with no post, warning, retry or notice. One of the three arrived while another turn was running. Under surface `disallow`, the same report got the standard hint. Earlier proof on the pre-merge head: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166380#issuecomment-6257567264.
- `pnpm check:changed --base origin/main` (at merge parent `29b4e141a78`): the line-cap and format lanes failed on the earlier test placement, and I fixed both. Re-run on this head: line-cap ratchet OK, format OK, core oxlint OK. The remaining failures are not caused by this PR:
  - The max-lines suppression ratchet flags `ui/src/pages/*` suppressions that exist on `main` but are missing from its baseline.
  - The core tsgo graph boundary reports `plugins-platform: 723 test roots exceeds the advisory 720`. This PR adds no test files.
  - The dead-export scan flags unused exports in `extensions/discord`, `extensions/msteams` and `src/plugins`.
  - `lint extensions` hit the 300 s plugin-sdk boundary `.d.ts` timeout on a loaded shared host.
- CI failures on this head that are not caused by this PR: `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` fails because `mock-exports` flags `test/scripts/ci-node-test-plan.test.ts`, and `control-ui-performance` fails in its base measurement (`chat boot JS gzip: 1456.5 KiB exceeds 1455.1 KiB`, also failing on other PRs, e.g. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39190171510/job/117861331336). The previous head's `check-test-types` failure (`extensions/codex/.../native-subagent-monitor.parent-retention.test.ts`) came from `main` and is green now.
- Telegram Test Server proof is not included because it needs leased Telegram test credentials that I do not have.

prs.body:
Avatar images previously changed their parent frame’s classes and state attribute outside Solid. The frames now bind their presentation in JSX through one shared factory. Image nodes, cache leases, decode handling, and lazy boundaries are preserved across all seven image/frame pairs; ChannelAvatar keeps its separate presentation ownership.

The final change retains the original Settings identity-loading effect. Review correctly identified that replacing this external synchronization with a keyed subscription was more complex. That implementation is restored byte-for-byte to the original base, with the new source-replacement tests retained.

## Proof

Replacement candidate: `a9dd74de387faba5356ab810068f0dd93737b35f`; merge base: `84dc583e1c634c2bdfba7eb0dfb94695fb4f87bc`. All eleven correction-batch file hashes were unchanged by the clean rebase. No dependencies or startup imports were added.

The earlier candidate passed 13 avatar-view and 24 Settings tests. Its separate `identity-avatar.test.tsx` run reached Vitest RUN but emitted no assertions before the existing 120-second no-output watchdog terminated it, exit 143. That remains an unresolved local test gap, not a pass or an inherited failure. The replacement uses the default pinned Bun fork, with no Node override.

The replacement run confirms that all three unit shards, including their later overlay/focus steps, now pass.

- `ui/src/e2e/command-palette-search.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts > Control UI command palette search with a real Gateway > finds a grouped spawned conversation beyond the roster and treats a full result page as success`. Both runs reject the same unexpected `ifRowsRevision: ""` property.

prs.title: refactor(ui): own shell lifetimes and native host references
prs.body:
## Problem and change

The shell and native conversation integration still rediscover owned DOM and mirror runtime lifetimes through rendering effects. This change gives each application runtime one keyed shell lifetime and makes the existing presentation owner acknowledge committed state, including connection recovery and avatar feedback timers. Runtime replacement retires old lazy intent; disconnect settles outstanding waiters.

Mounted shell, outlet, composer, and debug-frame references now come from their owners. Native navigation, favicon status, session-menu actions, and composer focus consume those references. The progress projection owns source changes and keeps its store cache during same-store handoffs. Explicit disposal prevents later source changes from reopening subscriptions. Tags, routes, selectors, keyboard behavior, and lazy boundaries stay intact.

The latest update also adds presentation and DOM-identity diagnostics to the existing managed-image capture test. It preserves the strict capture, image dimensions, and duplicate checks.

## Proof

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Source reconciliation | Rebased onto `918a379c89cb`; all six commits are patch-identical by range-diff. The earlier integration onto `a9e5f4e3b7b2` adapted initial context/imports only. Main’s connected-shell event tests and removal of retired handler aliases remain intact. |
| Install and types | `pnpm install` and `pnpm tsgo:ui` pass after the latest rebase using default tsrs. UI-app and E2E-chat test typechecks also pass; no tsgo override. |
| Focused behavior | The rebased host suite passes 28/28. The new shell feedback change passes 15/15 shell-view cases. Earlier unchanged-input proof includes shell/native, progress projection, bootstrap/pairing, and favicon browser cases. No broad local suite was run. |
| Review | Independent P2 reviews cover the complete candidate, owner extraction, readiness repair, shell feedback change, and diagnostic update. No actionable finding remains. Rebase reconciliation received a separate read-only review. |
| Simplification | The existing presentation owner now owns feedback and commit publication. No new owner or synchronization copy was introduced. The remaining growth pays for explicit disposal, registered host references, and regression coverage. |
| Production Knip | Canonical `pnpm deadcode:knip` passed again on `0980cddbbe40`, with no findings or new ignores. |
| Build and startup | Normal `pnpm ui:build` passed and generated all 1,120 sidecars. Head startup: **338,159 B gzip**, 7 JS requests; CSS **38,500 B / 1 request**. Exact `a9e5f4e3b7b2` → `2aa4ac9ec404` same-host comparison with Node 24.22.0 (all production patches remain identical after the latest rebase): startup **338,157 → 338,159 B** (+2 B), 7 JS requests unchanged, CSS **38,500 → 38,500 B / 1 request**. Chat **1,492,975 → 1,493,394 B** (+419 B); New Session **1,050,926 → 1,051,251 B** (+325 B). Both route absolute limits already fail on the base; no budget changed. |

## CI and remaining evidence

Current full CI **39192624648** is testing exact head `0980cddbbe40` through merge `bf2848f14efd`, with actual main base `d8ff48313fcb`. The completed run has **38 passing, 7 failing, and 24 skipped jobs**, with none pending. Six underlying failed jobs are attributed below; the seventh is the aggregate gate. Failed CI is not represented as green.

| Observed failure | Exact baseline evidence |
| --- | --- |
| `Control UI command palette search with a real Gateway > finds a grouped spawned conversation beyond the roster and treats a full result page as success` | Exact case also fails scheduled main **39191176869** with the same unexpected `ifRowsRevision: ""` request field. |
| Mock-export ratchet: `test/scripts/ci-node-test-plan.test.ts:3285`, mock of `../../scripts/lib/ci-test-timings.mts` | Reproduced by the same mock-export check on untouched actual base `d8ff48313fcb`. The baseline and tested-merge checker/test blobs are identical. |
| `Control UI Models help mocked Gateway E2E > explains the utility model with accessible pointer, keyboard, and narrow-layout behavior` | The same named case on untouched actual base fails with the same stale expected copy: `closest option supported by the selected model` versus `other models map unsupported levels to their closest supported option`. Test and English-copy blobs are identical between base and tested merge. |
| `Control UI session-list event scope > refetches instead of showing a row excluded by configured-agent filtering` | Exact failing name also fails latest completed scheduled main **39191176869** at `a8771a5a154c`. |
| `Control UI session-list event scope > keeps the Sessions page query stable when the startup roster completes` | Exact failing name also fails scheduled main **39191176869**. |
| Extension TS2353: `completionDeliveryRetryDelaysMs` absent from `MonitorOptions` in `native-subagent-monitor.parent-retention.test.ts:37` | Same diagnostic on scheduled main **39191176869**, plus an exact `a9e5f4e3` base reproduction using the default repository tsrs runner. |
| Chat boot gzip ceiling | Actual CI base **1,491,409 B** → tested merge **1,491,875 B**, against **1,490,000 B**. Startup is **337,506 B**, 7 JS requests, 1 startup CSS request. New Session **1,049,597 → 1,049,970 B**, below its cap. No budget changed. |

The preceding full CI **39190891513** exposed two incomplete native-shell fixtures after the presentation owner began reading the complete shell view. The test-only repair uses real application contexts and disposes each runtime; all assertions remain. The file passed 39 cases before a matchMedia fixture correction, and the sole remaining tooltip case passed after that correction. Default-tsrs UI-app types and independent P2 review also pass.

The managed-image test passes on the **current head in 11,343 ms** in full CI **39192624648**; it also passed the prior head in 11,923 ms. An older failure on `2c2f19d6d814` occurred inside strict frame capture before the ordering assertion; it is retained as an unexplained intermittent result, not claimed fixed or inherited. The exact six-entry order assertion now polls after screenshot capture to allow history reconciliation to finish. The screenshot capture itself, image dimensions, expected order, and duplicate checks remain strict; the latest diagnostic additions change no waits or assertions. The sole current real-Gateway failure is the exactly matched command-palette case above. Independent security-fast and the remaining selected test jobs pass.

One bounded local head media reproduction failed earlier during pairing because a loopback fetch timed out; a separate exact-base attempt failed before the assistant bubble. Neither reached image capture, so neither proves repair or inheritance. No broad local E2E suite was run. The two bounded actual-base checks above run only the newly failing ratchet and the single named Models-help case.

## Visual and refactor measurements

Exact-base/head synthetic captures at 1440 × 1000 are byte-identical. The composer remains focused and retains its draft; neither capture reports a page error or sends a message. Both full images were inspected and contain only synthetic data. The capture exercises the built shell/composer; native bridge behavior is covered separately by the native-shell tests. No Testbox or Crabbox lease was used.

Before (`a9e5f4e3b7b2`):

![Before: focused shell and composer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8da5cd91-3c71-43c9-97a8-a9b8110e6efd)

After (`2aa4ac9ec404`):

![After: focused shell and composer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/172cdee3-2968-43c5-85ed-bcfdb98f5e9b)

Across the 24 changed production files (including directly coupled chat/debug adapters), compared with `918a379c89cb`:

| Metric | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `createEffect` | 8 | 3 |
| `createRenderEffect` | 1 | 1 |
| `untrack` | 5 | 4 |
| Direct event registrations | 1 | 1 |
| DOM queries, including typed calls | 13 | 1 |
| Owner capture/restoration | 6 | 7 |
| Production LOC | 7,237 | 7,412 |

The remaining render effect belongs to the coupled chat renderer, outside this lane; the listener is paired AbortSignal cancellation. The remaining query is the sidebar active-rail lookup, handled by the separately prepared navigation-reference change. The added owner restoration prevents temporary rendering callers from cancelling shell acknowledgements. The +175 production lines provide explicit lifecycle retirement, registered native references, and connection timer ownership while removing five effect-driven paths.

The whole assigned lane is now at 20 → 10 effects, 2 → 0 render effects, 10 → 3 deliberate initial snapshots, and 43 → 9 queries. This is a checkpoint: the plugin and navigation follow-ups are still in flight.

prs.title: refactor(ui): drive palette mention search from owner transitions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The command palette used a rendering effect to notice when its people-mention menu opened or closed and then pause or resume session search. Wave zero moves that work into the operation that changes the menu.

## User Impact

Typing a people mention keeps session search paused. Moving the caret outside the mention closes its menu and resumes one search without changing the draft. The rendered UI and existing chat/new-session behavior stay the same.

## Why This Change Was Made

The mention owner now reports open/close transitions directly. The palette passes that transition value through search admission because Solid 2 publishes store changes after the current turn. The optional callback also removes redundant close notifications while preserving palette reopening and IME completion behavior.

## Evidence

Compared exact base `ea43f4b89dee6e0b297aef575f2ea0865dc62b94` with head `1b6c7629a8453aadd153c0c8c5275320c08e697c` on the same machine, Node 24.22.0, with `NODE_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1`.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Frozen install; `pnpm tsgo:ui` | Passed on final head using default tsrs |
| `command-palette-mentions.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | 19/19 passed on default pinned Bun; reused after rebase because all four reviewed file hashes are unchanged |
| Scoped UI lint, formatting, diff check | Passed; unchanged-file proof reused |
| Canonical isolated review | Complete changed modules and caller/owner APIs; no findings or material context gaps |
| `pnpm deadcode:knip` | Passed on final head (522.27 s) |
| `pnpm ui:build` | Base and head passed, one build per side |
| Strict performance check | Both exit 1 on the same two pre-existing route-size limits; values listed below |
| Targeted built-app screenshots | Both states pass on base and head; four inspected synthetic-only frames, byte-identical per state |
| Full UI CI | Run [39191163729](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39191163729), attempt 1, completed; all remaining failures attributed below |

| Gzip metric | Base | Head | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Startup JavaScript | 337,729 B | 337,715 B | −14 B |
| Startup CSS | 38,500 B / 1 request | 38,500 B / 1 request | 0 |
| Chat boot JavaScript | 1,492,493 B | 1,492,488 B | −5 B |
| New-session boot JavaScript | 1,050,465 B | 1,050,462 B | −3 B |

Startup JavaScript remains seven requests. The strict failures are `chat boot JS gzip` (limit 1,490,000 B) and `new boot JS gzip` (limit 1,050,000 B), present on both exact commits. No budget or lazy boundary changed.

The standalone Playwright capture uses synthetic people and a mock Gateway at 1440×960/light. It verifies no matching session search while the mention menu is open, then exactly one search after native left-arrow presses move the caret outside it. The initial capture incorrectly treated Home as caret motion; both base and head showed that Home navigates the menu. The corrected capture first asserts that existing Home behavior, then moves the caret with left arrows. No rebuild or production change was needed.

The existing test's initial-palette `STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED` diagnostic also occurs before this change; it does not fail the test.

## CI failure attribution

The full `ci:full` run completed for head `1b6c7629a8453aadd153c0c8c5275320c08e697c`. The following exact test names also fail with matching assertions in the latest completed scheduled main run [39191176869](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39191176869), at `a8771a5a154c67f26b5ab7e0002672ad0bfac8bd`:

| PR job | Exact failing test name |
| --- | --- |
| `checks-ui-e2e (5/9)` | `ui/src/e2e/session-list-filter.e2e.test.ts > Control UI session-list event scope > keeps the Sessions page query stable when the startup roster completes` |
| `checks-ui-e2e (5/9)` | `ui/src/e2e/session-list-filter.e2e.test.ts > Control UI session-list event scope > refetches instead of showing a row excluded by configured-agent filtering` |
| `checks-ui-e2e-real-gateway (1/2)` | `ui/src/e2e/command-palette-search.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts > Control UI command palette search with a real Gateway > finds a grouped spawned conversation beyond the roster and treats a full result page as success` |

The CI performance job reports chat boot JavaScript at **1,491,439 → 1,491,384 B**, both above the unchanged 1,490,000 B limit. New-session boot JavaScript **1,049,602 → 1,049,581 B** passes. The two failing test files, performance checker, and budget baseline are unchanged from the actual CI baseline `a8771a5a154c67f26b5ab7e0002672ad0bfac8bd`. The CI checkout is the merge `6095345bc858a29d9429013214ae7f864c9fc165` of that baseline and this PR head. All other selected leaf jobs, including `security-fast`, passed. This is an inherited-failure exception; CI remains recorded as failed.

## Scope measurements

| Pattern / LOC | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `createEffect` | 1 | 0 |
| `createRenderEffect` | 0 | 0 |
| `untrack` | 1 | 1 |
| Direct listeners / DOM queries | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Controller patterns / flush / owner escapes | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| Production LOC, three touched files | 1,804 | 1,815 |
| Test LOC, one touched file | 553 | 561 |

The surviving `untrack` is the intentional `initialKey` cleanup-identity snapshot at `ui/src/components/command-palette-view.tsx:357`. The eleven production lines carry transition values and preserve IME scheduling; they add no state owner or dependency.

## Exact repair already landed; maintainer decision pending

Already fixed on main by #176755, merged as `ff26768c39d65e6378b20de7b4c2bc24d80dc12b`. It contains exactly this PR’s two deletions; both file blobs are `7eb90fdaf6e59638116746eda716726225b93b27`. The actual CI merge and its main parent have identical trees, so this PR has no remaining change to land. ClawSweeper requests a maintainer decision before closing this maintainer-authored PR; it remains open for that decision.

Related: #176685

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes intermittent `sessions.recover` authorization test cleanup failures reporting that the state database still has active native borrowers.

## User Impact

More reliable recovery authorization coverage on Node and Bun. No production behavior changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The recovery continuation starts tracked dashboard title work. Its skill-command preparation can still hold an exec-approvals read pin after the RPC and cancellation assertions finish. The test's local synchronous close ran before the shared session fixture could join that work.

Remove the redundant close and let the existing fixture drain Gateway roots, dispose readers, and close the database asynchronously. The native-borrower assertion and both authorization cases remain intact. Production LOC: +0/-0; test LOC: +0/-2.

## Evidence

The original failure reproduced in two full-file Node runs and one full-file Bun run. Temporary acquisition stacks identified the same dashboard-title exec-approvals read pin on both runtimes; that instrumentation is not part of this change. A single-case Node run passed, confirming that a passing replay alone would miss the cleanup race.

All five requested files passed individually on both Node and Bun: recovery authorization (2 tests), native borrowers (11), cache cleanup (8), idle retirement (11), and wrapper retention (1), for 33 passing tests per runtime. The full-file recovery command took 306.60s on Node and 306.59s on Bun, including cold graph preparation and cleanup verification; no new test cases were added.

The same five-file Bun shard passed all 49 tests (858.43s wall). Core types, targeted lint, formatting, and madge passed; madge reported zero cycles. Lint required installing the already-declared `@openclaw/solid-lint` workspace dependencies with the frozen lockfile; no dependency files changed.

Independent Codex review is scoped-clean through P2. GitHub’s exact-head Codex review also completed without findings. Live-provider testing was not run; this test-only change does not modify production code.

CI [39191174899](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39191174899), attempt 1, completed on `54164ec5eab01e1845610e110a30782a0047f69b`. It has two inherited UI test failures; security-fast and the other planned non-skipped jobs passed.

prs.title: fix(exec): explain what a running background result proves and warn against unpolled promises
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On 2026-04-27 I asked my OpenClaw agent over Telegram to fix two failing evals in one of my repositories. It handed the work to a coding agent running in the background, and six seconds after the exec tool reported the session as running it told me the work had started and promised to report back. It never did, twice. The exchange, condensed (times UTC):

```text
13:13  me     Can you use the good-oss-citizen tile to get the two failing evals to 100%?

13:14  agent  I set up a fresh worktree and I'm handing the implementation to a
              coding agent now.

13:15:14 exec Command still running (session crisp-breeze, pid 3469063).
              Use process (list/poll/log/write/kill/clear/remove) for follow-up.

13:15:20 agent Started. Worktree, branch, and session are set up.
              I'll report back when it has a commit and gate results, or if it blocks.

13:23  (the coding agent finishes with a local commit; the agent is woken with the
        completion event but that turn is told user delivery is disabled, so I am
        not notified)

13:26  me     Is it still going

13:26  agent  No, the coding agent finished and exited cleanly. There is already a
              local commit. I'm not calling it done yet because I still need to verify.

13:26  (no tool call and no message follow; the agent is idle until my next question)

13:27  me     I'm confused, are you still doing something

13:27  agent  Sorry, yes, that was confusing. The coding agent is no longer running.
              I'm doing the final verification myself now.

13:27  (it amends the commit and starts the gates as another background command)

13:27:55 exec Command still running (session mild-rook, pid 3477273).
              Use process (list/poll/log/write/kill/clear/remove) for follow-up.

13:27:55 agent Yes, but only final verification now. Gates are running now.
              I'll report DONE/BLOCKED when those gates finish.

13:28  (the gates finish; the agent is woken again and again told that user
        delivery is disabled; it writes a "successfully completed" message inside
        that turn, and I am not notified)

13:33  me     Are the gates still running.

13:33  agent  No. Gates finished successfully.

13:33  me     Why didn't you notify me then?

13:33  agent  Because the completion event explicitly said "user delivery is disabled"
              and told me to handle it internally. I should have stayed quiet there.
              But after that, I also failed to proactively send a normal concise DONE
              update once I confirmed the gates had finished. That's on me. I made
              you ask twice.
```

### What the transcript shows

- A running result means a process was spawned and was alive when the result was written. "Started." was true.
- What the agent could not know from that result: whether the command was making progress, was waiting for input, or had since exited or failed.
- The harm was not a false start. It was a promise to report back that could not be kept, twice.
- When a background command finishes, the agent is woken with a completion event by default (`tools.exec.notifyOnExit`, [background process docs](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/background-process#disable-automatic-completion-turns)), but that turn may not be allowed to message the user. That is decided when the turn runs, from the heartbeat delivery route and visibility settings ([heartbeat docs, "Delivery behavior"](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/heartbeat#delivery-behavior)). On 2026-04-27 the agent was woken both times and told both times that delivery was disabled.
- At the moment the running result is written, the exec tool knows whether a completion event will be queued, but not whether that later turn will be allowed to message the user.

That leaves two ways to stop an agent from promising a report it cannot deliver:

1. Tell the agent, in the running result itself, what "running" does and does not mean, and that the completion turn may not be allowed to reach the user, so a promise of updates has to be backed by the agent polling the session to the end and reporting itself.
2. Resolve at exec time whether the completion turn will be allowed to deliver, and put that answer into the result.

This PR takes the first. It is one sentence group in one producer, it is true in every configuration, and it needs no knowledge of delivery routing inside the exec tool. The second would couple the exec tool to heartbeat delivery resolution and still could not promise delivery, because the route can change before the command exits.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared running result from `createExecTool` currently reads:

> `Command still running (session ..., pid ...). Use process (...) for follow-up.`

#161780 (merged 2026-10-02) split the follow-up route into three notification modes. This PR adds the same first sentences to all three, then folds the delivery caveat into each mode's own wake wording:

> `Command still running (session ..., pid ...). Running means the process was started and was alive when this result was written; it says nothing about progress, waiting for input, or a later exit or failure. Do not report progress from this result alone. <mode-specific follow-up>`

With completion waking on every exit (`notifyOnExitEmptySuccess=true`, the default for chat channels), the follow-up reads:

> `Completion will wake this conversation automatically. The completion turn may not be allowed to message the user, so if only waiting remains, report that the job is running without promising to report back and end this turn; do not keep polling. Use process (...) for follow-up.`

With silent empty successes (`notifyOnExitEmptySuccess=false`):

> `Use process (...) for follow-up. Completion wakes this conversation on output or failure; empty successful jobs are silent (tools.exec.notifyOnExitEmptySuccess=false). Arrange continuation or collect the result before ending the turn if empty success matters. The completion turn may not be allowed to message the user, so do not promise the user updates unless you poll this session until it finishes and report the outcome yourself.`

With `tools.exec.notifyOnExit=false`:

> `Use process (...) for follow-up. Automatic completion wake is disabled (tools.exec.notifyOnExit=false). If the task needs this result, use poll with a timeout to collect it before ending the turn, unless another continuation is already arranged. Without a completion wake, do not promise the user updates unless you poll this session until it finishes and report the outcome yourself.`

Each clause is checked against the code. "The completion turn may not be allowed to message the user" holds whenever a wake is queued: `buildExecEventPrompt` in `src/infra/heartbeat-events-filter.ts` still tells the completion turn "user delivery is disabled for this run" when `canRelayToUser` is false, and `heartbeat-runner-execution.ts` computes that at wake time from heartbeat visibility (`showAlerts`) and the delivery route. In the every-exit mode #161780 tells the agent to end the turn and stop polling, so that mode drops the promise outright ("without promising to report back") instead of offering polling as the way to back one. The other two modes already ask the agent to collect the result when it matters, so the promise rule there keeps the poll-to-the-end condition. The "what running proves" sentences name no tool and sit before the follow-up, so the trailing follow-up sentence stays adapter-owned:

- base exec uses `process`
- sandbox exec uses `sandbox_process`
- Gateway exec uses `gateway_process` when exposed
- Gateway exec without process follow-up tells the model to rerun in the foreground
- remote-node exec says background follow-up is unavailable and to wait for completion

### Overlap with #158884 and #161780

#158884 (merged 2026-09-26) appends a no-wake warning to the follow-up route when `notifyOnExit=false`. The previous head of this PR chose its own wake clause by `notifyOnExit` and left that warning alone.

#161780 (merged 2026-10-02) then made the follow-up conditional on `notifyOnExitEmptySuccess` as well. Stacked on the previous head, the every-exit mode would have said "you may be woken with a completion event ... do not promise the user updates unless you poll this session until it finishes" and, a sentence later, "Completion will wake this conversation automatically ... end this turn; do not keep polling". Those pull in opposite directions.

This head removes the separate wake clause. The delivery caveat and the promise rule now live inside each of #161780's three branches and agree with that branch's instruction, so they also reach the structured `details.followUp`. The "what running proves" sentences stay in the visible text only, before the follow-up. #161780's own sentences are unchanged except for the inserted caveat in the every-exit branch, where "report that the job is running" gains "without promising to report back".

On current `main`, `qa-lab`'s mock provider regex still matches only the pre-#161780 running text, which no mode emits any more. This PR's regex matches the caution followed by any single-line follow-up that contains the `Use process (...)` route, so it covers all three modes.

### How I expect this to help, and what it cannot do

This is an instruction in a tool result. A model can ignore it, and I could not make a model reproduce the original failure in a replay, so I cannot show a before/after in behavior, only in what the model is told. What I can say:

- On 2026-04-27 the agent read "Command still running" over Telegram and answered "Started. I'll report back". On current `main` that is the every-exit mode, which now tells the agent to report that the job is running and end the turn. The new text adds, at that exact point, that it must not promise to report back. In the other modes an agent that follows it has two honest moves: keep polling in the same turn and report when done, which is delivered because it is a reply to the user; or say "launched, ask me or I'll check", which makes no promise it cannot keep. Either avoids the wait I had.
- The misleading input is gone. Today's text reads as confirmation; the new text states the constraint where the decision is made.
- On the same day, 4 of the 64 background commands with a recorded exit in that session ended with a non-zero code, so a "started" relayed from a running result is wrong often enough to matter.

What it does not do: it does not make the agent keep a promise, and it does not change why the completion turns were silenced. That is the delivery-routing topic linked above and is out of scope here.

## User Impact

There is no API, field, or control-flow change. The "what running proves" sentences appear only in the visible text of the `status: running` exec result. The delivery caveat and promise rule are part of the mode-specific follow-up, so they appear in that text and in the structured `details.followUp` string, next to the wake wording they qualify. Subsequent process results are unchanged.

## Real Behavior Proof

I reran the behavior proof against exact head `0eac408a0ac213770c0147d82bbb09aa5fb34468`, rebased onto upstream `main` at `1a331439952556d653b14973fe294e158d1106bd`.

The harness is a `tsx` script that imports `createExecTool`, `createProcessTool`, and `waitForExecScope` from the checked-out `src/` and runs them unmodified. It spawns a real OS child with `background: true`, immediately reads its log, and then polls its terminal outcome. It uses no exec or process mocks.

The child waits 500 ms before printing `WORK_STARTED` and exiting with code 7.

The recording below is one asciinema 3.2.1 session from the earlier head `d85e6cac`, before #158884 landed: it runs the same harness twice, first in a checkout of upstream `main` at that head's base commit `8adb6ebf5f`, then in the PR checkout. `git log` shows the head before each run. On the base commit the running result has no caution while the immediate log is already empty and the child later exits 7; on the PR head the same result carries the caution before the unchanged follow-up sentence. The host I used for this revision has no asciinema or agg, so the recording was not redone; the transcripts further down are from the current head and show the wording that replaced the recorded one. Final frame of the rendered recording:

![Before/after terminal recording: on main the running result reads Command still running, Use process for follow-up; on the PR head the same result adds the new text. Both runs show an empty immediate log, then WORK_STARTED and exit code 7](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/martinfrancois/openclaw/assets/pr-120414-proof/proof-before-after-v3-final-frame.png)

- [proof-before-after-v3.cast](https://github.com/martinfrancois/openclaw/blob/assets/pr-120414-proof/proof-before-after-v3.cast): the asciinema recording itself.
- [proof.mts](https://github.com/martinfrancois/openclaw/blob/assets/pr-120414-proof/proof.mts) and [proof-driver.sh](https://github.com/martinfrancois/openclaw/blob/assets/pr-120414-proof/proof-driver.sh): the harness, with a [README](https://github.com/martinfrancois/openclaw/blob/assets/pr-120414-proof/README.md).

On this same head:

It asserts the visible text carries the running caution right before the structured follow-up, that the delivery caveat appears exactly when a wake is queued, that the every-exit mode drops the promise and the other two keep the poll-to-the-end rule, and that only the disabled mode carries #158884's sentence. The first two were also verified to fail identically on a pristine checkout of the earlier base `a4182c6c`.

## Codex App-Server Contract Review

I inspected the direct sibling Codex source required by `AGENTS.md`, pinned to the version the rebased plugin declares: `@openai/codex` `0.162.0`, tag `rust-v0.162.0`, commit [`c1382380de69521303b416720a52f42d51af6248`](https://github.com/openai/codex/commit/c1382380de69521303b416720a52f42d51af6248).

- Codex app-server v2 accepts dynamic-tool text as an `InputText { text }` content item: [`app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/item.rs#L1675-L1692`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/c1382380de69521303b416720a52f42d51af6248/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/item.rs#L1675-L1692).
- The app server decodes those items and submits them unchanged as `Op::DynamicToolResponse`: [`app-server/src/dynamic_tools.rs#L18-L58`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/c1382380de69521303b416720a52f42d51af6248/codex-rs/app-server/src/dynamic_tools.rs#L18-L58).
- Codex core maps every content item into the model's function-tool output without rewriting its text: [`core/src/tools/handlers/dynamic.rs#L153-L164`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/c1382380de69521303b416720a52f42d51af6248/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/dynamic.rs#L153-L164).

On the OpenClaw side, the patch preserves the exact trailing `Use process (...)` literal. The sandbox projection rewrites only that suffix to `sandbox_process` in [`shell-dynamic-tools.ts`](https://github.com/martinfrancois/openclaw/blob/14aa4baf691ce106e84e9d1949f6d66368c35124/extensions/codex/src/app-server/shell-dynamic-tools.ts#L102-L121). The node alias and the Gateway projection in the [same file](https://github.com/martinfrancois/openclaw/blob/14aa4baf691ce106e84e9d1949f6d66368c35124/extensions/codex/src/app-server/shell-dynamic-tools.ts#L42-L88) replace the same suffix with their available or unavailable next step, the Gateway one through the shared projection in [`exec-tool-target-pinning.ts`](https://github.com/martinfrancois/openclaw/blob/14aa4baf691ce106e84e9d1949f6d66368c35124/src/agents/exec-tool-target-pinning.ts#L81-L115).

The chat Details diff-summary owner still installs and removes its document visibility listener directly. This leaves a DOM listener outside the shared wave-zero lifetime primitive.

prs.title: fix(codex): shed abandoned cleared bindings at namespace capacity
prs.body:
AI-assisted: AI coding agents were used to investigate the Codex binding lifecycle, implement this branch, and run the validation listed below.

Fixes #125910.

## What Problem This Solves

The Codex app-server thread-binding namespace rejects new bindings after 50,000 rows accumulate, leaving later requests unavailable until the state database is cleaned manually.

## Why This Change Was Made

Earlier revisions of this PR moved the namespace to evict-oldest, which let the SQLite store delete binding rows it cannot read: retirement fences, legacy-clear provenance, live leases, and active sessions all ranked the same as garbage. This revision keeps reject-new everywhere and puts capacity recovery at the binding domain boundary.

`session-binding-overflow.ts` wraps the composed binding store's `mutate`, the only insert path. When an insert fails with a row-count limit error, the wrapper pages the worker-backed handle on the same namespace with `entriesInKeyRange` (512-row pages, storage-side ordering, decode in the storage worker) and sheds up to a few strictly validated disposable rows per failure through `observe` + `compareAndApply`, then retries. A lexical cursor persists across calls and wraps at the end of the namespace, so spaced failures keep advancing instead of re-reading the same protected prefix, and rows whose leases lapse after a fully protected pass are reconsidered. Destructive eligibility is decided on the raw record, not the tolerant codec: a lease in any malformed shape, a retirement marker in any shape at all, and any non-object row are preserved as ambiguous. Everything else (active bindings, retirement fences, live leases, `conversation:legacy-` provenance) fails closed with the original limit error, and hosts without ranged listing stand down the same way instead of scanning inline.

The sync store stays exactly where it was: hot reads. Listing and deletion during recovery run on the worker side of the store broker, so a full namespace never turns into a whole-table decode on the Gateway thread.

Sidecar migration keeps its main-branch reject-new store: at capacity the existing failure path retains the source, and no live row can be displaced by an import.

## User Impact

A namespace clogged with abandoned cleared rows recovers on its own instead of hard-failing every new session. Fences, leases, legacy-clear provenance, live bindings, and every ambiguous existing record are never shed; when nothing strictly disposable exists the limit error surfaces unchanged.

## Evidence

- `session-binding-overflow.test.ts` (17 tests; runs in the database-workers shard on the forks pool for the broker): recovery sheds an abandoned cleared row while an older live binding survives; fail-closed when the namespace holds only a retirement fence plus a live binding; a live lease is never shed; legacy-clear provenance survives recovery while an abandoned row next to it is shed; a cleared row with a non-object lease is preserved while a strictly valid abandoned row next to it is shed; a namespace of only ambiguous rows rejects with both rows intact; a host without ranged listing propagates the limit error with no inline scan; recovery through `createLazyCodexAppServerBindingStore(state, undefined, recoveryState)`, the exact production composition; a scan stalls mid-prefix under a one-page budget and the next insert resumes from the persisted cursor and succeeds (goes red when cursor persistence is broken); rows whose leases lapse after a fully protected pass are reconsidered.
- `session-binding-overflow.registered-path.test.ts` (new): the real extension entry boots and builds the binding store plus the lazy recovery adapter from `api.runtime.state` itself; the openers delegate to the plugin-state test factories (same worker-backed SQLite stores, fixture module resolution; production additionally needs the Gateway host broker no in-process test has), with the binding namespace cap clamped 50,000 -> 3 as the only knob. Through that registered assembly: a fresh session's lease admission overflows, recovers, starts exactly once, and sheds exactly the disposable cleared row while the live binding and a held row survive; and a caller whose authority is revoked at admission gets zero deletes with the disposable row intact.
- Real run, isolated state dir, production plugin-state store plus the production lazy composition over real SQLite at capacity (3/3: retired fence, live-leased cleared row, abandoned cleared row): the insert recovers, only the abandoned row is shed, both protected rows survive, and a fresh store handle on the same database still shows fence + lease + the new binding afterwards. Verbatim output is in the review reply below.
- `doctor-contract-api.overflow.test.ts`: at capacity the sidecar source is retained, nothing is imported, and the pre-existing row is intact (limit error injected through the production registration path); a revisited legacy sidecar cannot resurrect its cleared thread because the canonical cleared marker wins and the source archives without its row.
- Sibling Codex checkout inspection (`../codex`, origin/main 286d4ecf44): threads persist durably as rollout files plus the state db with paged listing and no retention eviction (`codex-rs/rollout/src/state_db.rs:352`, `codex-rs/rollout/src/maintenance.rs`), so shedding an abandoned OpenClaw binding row can never delete native Codex data.
- Full `extensions/codex` suite green, `check-changed` lanes green, fresh `$autoreview` clean with no actionable findings.

## What this PR is not

This is a partial fix with one open policy decision and no claim to close the underlying issue's storage architecture. Shedding strictly validated abandoned cleared rows is a durable-retention change, and it needs an explicit maintainer decision before merge; the review thread carries the full inventory. The store-level eviction primitive (storage-side disposal by policy rather than a domain-side sweep) remains the owner's call, as does any broader migration of the sync binding reads onto the async handle.

prs.title: fix: recovered subagents abort after their parent finishes
prs.body:
Stack: part 1; #176770 adds delivery ordering and consumed-peer source recovery.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes recovered child runs aborting after their parent finishes following a forced Gateway restart.

## User Impact

Accepted children can finish their work after a recovered parent settles. Current operator, device, session, and Gateway revocation still stops their effects.

## Why This Change Was Made

The [original recovery owner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/943e9af522a8e0070fc051a7052edd5c267dfeaf/src/gateway/operator-run-recovery.ts#L183) combined two different lifetimes: the exact parent recovery claim and the operator's current policy. An accepted child retained both. Normal requester settlement retired the parent's claim, so later child tool calls failed with “Subagent recovery completion owner changed” or “Restart recovery admission is no longer current.”

The recovery owner now exposes independently retained policy custody only to an accepting continuation owner. The original recovered run still checks its exact recovery claim; the child checks current policy, its own completion owner, and the same Gateway instance. This reuses the existing continuation capture and release lifecycle without a second recovery manager.

Accepted limits: losing the child's own completion owner, replacing the source session, revoking current access, or stopping/replacing the Gateway still invalidates the child. This does not change shutdown-drain or blocked-session policy.

## Evidence

The affected boot followed a systemd SIGKILL at 2026-10-18 21:47:03 UTC. Nine distinct recovered sessions subsequently failed: six with completion-owner errors and three with admission errors, between 21:49 and 22:30 UTC. Sanitized examples:

```text
2026-10-18T21:49:37.705+00:00 … lane=nested:…:d9e80e8c … error="Restart recovery operator authority changed; start a new user turn. | Subagent recovery completion owner changed"
2026-10-18T22:30:53.244+00:00 … error="Restart recovery operator authority changed; start a new user turn. | Restart recovery admission is no longer current."
```

The owning-boundary regression fails on the base when the parent claim retires and passes with the fix. Review follow-up now binds a real write tool through admitted harness capabilities: a write succeeds after parent settlement, then a second write pauses after an awaited directory operation. Revoking the device during that pause rejects the write at final I/O, leaving the original bytes unchanged and the total write count at one. No abort signal is supplied, so cancellation cannot mask the authority check. This strengthened case passed in 22.666 s within the mixed baseline invocation; that wrapper exited 1 for the independently reproduced peer-permission failure described in #176770. prs.title: refactor(ui): share layout, draft, and tab focus lifetimes
prs.body:
## Problem and change

The palette textarea, panel tab strips, and config draft controls each synchronized browser state with local effects. Tab-close focus also depended on querying a strip that could be replaced while a close callback was pending.

Move layout observation and native draft reconciliation into two shared primitives with production callers. Keep selected-tab reveal and retained-node focus recovery in the existing tab primitive, and let each panel own a registered focus handle across strip replacement. Tooltip text and overflow detection now share one DOM traversal. The authoritative panel/config owners, host tags, CSS classes, routes, and lazy import boundaries stay intact.

The native textarea still sizes atomically during input; resize and result updates preserve manual scroll. Config controls keep uncommitted invalid text and update validity without replacing unchanged drafts. The tab owner restores focus only when the removed control left focus unset, so newer outside focus wins.

## Scope and counts

Final scope: 16 production files and six test files against merge base `d5aeceb2b89e253ba15d41976d0618e31842fb48`; head `06e803d873dd408af4ded1676a0e5cddf78f31d0`. The original 21-file implementation proof below was captured at `789f79131429821ca8a6cca0cb06a6a7ffd12bab` against `64e9443af525212642b0406fbc454727f267a68a`. All 21 final implementation hashes and all 18 readiness-review contexts remain identical after rebase.

| Measure | Base | Head |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Production LOC | 4,546 | 4,576 |
| Test LOC | 1,469 | 1,862 |
| Feature effects being replaced | 5 | 0 |
| Total `createEffect` calls, including shared primitives and unchanged chat code | 9 | 7 |
| `createRenderEffect` | 0 | 0 |
| `addEventListener` | 0 | 0 |
| `querySelector(All)` | 14 | 9 |
| `untrack` | 1 | 1 |

The 30-line production increase supplies shared layout/draft lifecycle ownership and a panel-owned focus handle while removing the corresponding local effects and queries. The seven remaining effects are three shared synchronization primitives plus four unchanged chat effects. The nine remaining queries are unchanged chat-sidebar code outside this focused conversion; this PR does not claim to complete that other lane.

Remaining calls by category:

- Shared synchronization: `ui/src/lib/reactive/layout-measurement.ts:38` (coalesced DOM observation), `ui/src/lib/reactive/native-draft.ts:34` (native draft/validity reconciliation), `ui/src/lib/tabs.ts:111` (selected-tab reveal and focus recovery).
- Unchanged chat effects: `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-files-panel.tsx:76`, `:139`; `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-sidebar-region.runtime.tsx:430`, `:444`.
- Unchanged chat queries: `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-sidebar-region.runtime.tsx:100`, `:120`, `:126`, `:155`, `:156`, `:211`, `:254`, `:266`, `:424`.
- Intentional initial snapshot: `ui/src/components/panel-tab-strip-solid.tsx:193`, `initialTabId`, captures the immutable keyed node identity for ref registration and cleanup.

## Proof

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm tsgo:ui` using default tsrs | Diagnostic checkpoint passed, exit 0, no checker override |
| `panel-tab-strip.test.tsx`, `config-form-draft-lifecycle.test.ts`, `tooltip-content.test.ts` | 28 tests passed across three single-file runs, one worker each, default pinned Bun |
| Scoped UI lint and formatting | Original implementation and readiness checks passed. Diagnostic checkpoint lint and formatting passed after renaming a shadowing local variable |
| Isolated Codex autoreview | Original implementation and readiness reviews complete through P2. Separate final diagnostic review exited 0, scoped-clean, zero P0–P2 findings |
| Frozen-lockfile install after rebase | Diagnostic checkpoint install passed, 1.2 s; all 21 original implementation hashes retained |
| `pnpm ui:build`, one per side | Original measured base/head passed, exit 0; 317.0 s / 223.3 s; not repeated after rebase |
| Four-state built-app visual capture | Original measured base/head passed, exit 0; full frames inspected and synthetic-only |
| Strict performance check | Original measured base/head both exit 1 for the two matching budget failures below; final-head CI remains required |
| `pnpm deadcode:knip` | Original implementation head passed, exit 0; 661.7 s. Production source remains identical |

The 28 original unit tests, builds, screenshots, strict performance results and Knip result are reused proof for the unchanged 21-file implementation; they are not claimed as runs on the final rebased head. Playwright capture used Node 24 for its browser harness; unit tests used the default pinned Bun runtime. The readiness repair received its own scoped lint/format, isolated review and default-tsrs typecheck. The diagnostic checkpoint received a fresh frozen install, scoped lint/format, default-tsrs typecheck, diff check and isolated review; no local E2E/build/unit reruns were added. No local E2E suite, extra build, or parity battery was run. `ci:full` is present before the replacement push so final-head CI runs all UI unit, Control UI E2E, browser-extension and real-Gateway shards.

Earlier local proof failures were resolved explicitly: seven lint errors (unbound plain methods, a reassigned parameter, and a redundant test type argument) and one formatting failure; final scoped checks pass. The first head capture exited 1 because it set the caret before the lazy palette finished loading. Waiting for the existing results `aria-busy=false` state before setting the caret fixed the harness setup; the unchanged caret/scroll assertion then passed. That failed capture is retained. No production change or rebuild was needed for the correction.

## Managed-image CI failure and diagnostic checkpoint

Run `39186015315` failed `Managed image ordering through real chat.send and history > keeps headings, managed images and trailing prose ordered live and after reload without duplicates` during its first screenshot. Both image nodes were replaced while the bubble and row stayed connected. The exact test passed in scheduled main runs `39183785855` and `39186683798`; this failure is not inherited.

The first repair moved the existing real CLI persisted-history read and validation before the first live screenshot, then waited for the active pane to adopt that response's session, exact history cursor, canonical assistant ID and complete image source blocks. Run `39190403396` at `94e26f7` still failed the same test after that readiness check passed: both original images were disconnected, while their bubble and row remained identical and connected. Bounds and visibility were unchanged. The readiness repair is insufficient, and the replacement cause remains unresolved.

Existing timeout artifacts contain only public failure summaries, with no source or policy transitions. This checkpoint extends the existing browser-held node handle and failure catch to distinguish source changes, gallery/frame/container replacement, session/policy changes, connection changes and pane presentation changes. Raw sources and serialized scope/policy inputs remain in the browser; output contains only safe source categories, equality checks, connected/active flags, numeric epochs and counts. It also removes an obsolete Lit comment-marker diagnostic.

The original test name, one browser send, live-before-reload sequence, ordering/count assertions, retained-node checks and strict screenshot identity postchecks remain intact. No production change, capture-helper change, wait, retry, timeout increase or test seam is added. The diagnostic commit changes this test by 102 insertions and 23 deletions (697 to 776 lines). It is an investigation checkpoint, not a claimed fix; no merge admission will be requested until the new CI evidence is investigated.

The same run also failed these exact tests, which match the latest compared completed scheduled main run `39191176869` at `a8771a5a`:

- `Control UI command palette search with a real Gateway > finds a grouped spawned conversation beyond the roster and treats a full result page as success`
- `Control UI session-list event scope > refetches instead of showing a row excluded by configured-agent filtering`
- `Control UI session-list event scope > keeps the Sessions page query stable when the startup roster completes`

Only those names are attributed to main; managed-media passes in that same run. No whole-shard waiver is claimed.

Accepted readiness-test limit: exact cursor equality assumes the same Gateway reader backend and no later independent transcript append after this one-send fixture's owner read. A backend switch or newer append fails the wait rather than using a cursor exception.

## Performance

Strict checks ran on the same machine using the original merge base `64e9443` and implementation head `789f791`, one production build per side. They were not repeated on the final rebased head; final-head CI supplies fresh budget evidence.

| Metric | Original base | Original head | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Startup JavaScript gzip | 337,692 B | 337,732 B | +40 B |
| Startup JavaScript requests | 7 | 7 | 0 |
| Startup CSS gzip | 38,500 B | 38,500 B | 0 B |
| Startup CSS requests | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| Chat boot JavaScript gzip | 1,492,375 B | 1,492,573 B | +198 B |
| New-session boot JavaScript gzip | 1,050,396 B | 1,050,563 B | +167 B |

The exact failing metric names are `chat boot JS gzip` (limit 1,490,000 B) and `new boot JS gzip` (limit 1,050,000 B), and both fail on the original measured merge base. The small size increase accompanies shared focus/layout lifecycle code; no library or lazy page is pulled into startup. Measured startup is below both the 338,900 B strict ceiling at that head and the campaign's original 374,285 B ceiling, with one CSS request. No budget or baseline was changed.

Latest completed PR CI performance evidence (`39190403396`, prior head `94e26f7`): startup JavaScript is 337,533 B gzip across seven requests. Chat boot base/head is 1,491,366 / 1,491,539 B, exceeding the 1,490,000 B limit on both sides. New-session boot base/head is 1,049,566 / 1,049,726 B, passing the 1,050,000 B limit. These are prior-head results, not proof for diagnostic head `06e803d`.

## Before / after

Both sides use the same synthetic Gateway fixtures and 1440×960 light viewport. Assertions cover the three-line palette cap and preserved caret/manual scroll during resize; retained exact-node focus after panel reorder; visible long-filename overflow tooltip; keyboard-close focus on the surviving tab; and invalid scalar/JSON drafts with native validity and visible feedback. Full frames were inspected; only the settings build footer differs intentionally.

The comparison sheet preserves the captured UI at its original scale. Only the settings build footer is cropped, identically in both columns; all full-frame originals are retained.

![Before and after: palette sizing, hosted tab overflow, keyboard close focus, and invalid config drafts](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e0c810cf-b0d3-4c0b-a456-d9b47d28bef1)

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Widget Copy/Download found its preview by walking from the action menu through CSS ancestors. This couples exports to where the menu and Canvas iframe happen to render.

The preview now publishes one live export source for its mounted lifetime. Raw iframe replacement updates it; managed Canvas views expose their existing frame/document getters at selection time; parking or disposal clears it. The menu handle and export DOM queries are removed. Existing prompt, resize, retained-frame, theme delivery, transport, and toast behavior stay with their current owners.
