prs.title: refactor(plugins): remove repeated same-stack authority checks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Bundled plugins repeat authority assertions after synchronous local work or immediately before a callee that performs the same assertion first. Legacy Agents API migration also repeats the client's session-ID validation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove nine same-stack checks and let the Agents API client own remote session identity validation. Keep ingress rejection, no-op rejection, abort checks after awaits, and authority validation immediately before execution, disclosure, or external effects. No SQL, worker request, schema or SDK changes.

Accepted edge: an already disconnected and revoked MCP pairing caller may receive the disconnected error first. Neither path performs an effect or returns protected data. The private callee still rejects revoked authority before pairing.

## Evidence

The real-client migration regression sends a mismatched session ID through the transport, verifies rejection and preservation of the legacy binding, then retries successfully. Existing owner suites cover cancellation, reset, revocation, reasoning callbacks, upload dispatch and transcript recording. Basic checks and independent Codex review run before publication; final CI gates are recorded below before landing. This slice has a source-estimated SQL/request/MAIN delta of 0/0/0, not a separately measured reduction. The completed first-slice harness v3 warm pair measured identical 54 [54–57] SQL / 16 [16–17] requests / 0 [0–0] MAIN, with all operation medians unchanged. No latency claim.

Candidate ledger:

| Candidates | Decision | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| C00310 b, C00311 g | REMOVE | Each attachment-resolution branch already checks authority and cancellation after its final await; only a closure is constructed before the removed checks. |
| C00362 b, C00363 g, C00365 b, C00366 g | REMOVE | The private session-deletion callee immediately performs the same two checks before effects or awaits. |
| C00426 b, C00427 g | REMOVE | Reasoning entry checks authority; synchronous local text state cannot revoke it before the callback. Post-callback authority remains. |
| C01156 b, C01157 g | REMOVE | Every target-resolution path checked authority after its last await; only synchronous request routing intervenes. Upload and dispatch boundaries remain. |
| C04103 g | REMOVE | The private authority validator begins with the same callback; disconnected pairing remains effect-free. |
| C04568 b | REMOVE | Workspace/approval branches check active authority after their awaits; only local policy calculation precedes continuation preparation. |
| C00587 g | REMOVE | Native transcript recording checks the identical callback as its first operation. Post-await validation remains. |
| Supplemental migration session-ID guard | REMOVE | AgentsApiClient.session rejects a mismatched ID before returning; migration retains its post-await authority check. |

Production +4/−16 (net −12); tests +6/−1. Thirteen indexed candidates across nine physical repeated checks are removed, plus the supplemental client-owned session-ID check. No public API or documentation behavior changes. Formatting, basic lint and diff checks pass. One independent Codex P0–P2 round is scoped-clean with full source verification.

Final head 8f64f902770cd8c6a971a24ed172d2315700595e integrates UI repair #176799 and the landed private-tagline export fix; all nine reviewed extension blobs are unchanged. Frozen install passes. [Ordinary CI 39191363273](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39191363273) passes all selected owner tests, production types, five core test-type stripes, type-aware lint, source contracts, Madge and the T1/dialect/worker ratchets. The real-client migration admission/retry regression also passed in the original full persistence suite (973 ms).

The sole ordinary static failure is TS2353 in untouched `extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-subagent-monitor.parent-retention.test.ts:37`: `completionDeliveryRetryDelaysMs` is absent from `MonitorOptions`. [Candidate job 117865334308](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39191363273/job/117865334308) and [current-main job 117861494392](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39190227860/job/117861494392), main a9e5f4e3b7b2114caa573554766ab7b4850b39e4, emit the identical diagnostic. This inherited failure and the aggregate are covered by the approved inherited-failure landing route.

Final Knip reports the unused `settleInterruptedRestartRecovery` export in untouched main-session recovery code plus the two baseline unused files `scripts/bench-channel-ingress-writer.ts` and `src/process/spawn-diagnostics.test-support.ts`. prs.title: refactor(ui): drive account usage from native scope receipts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Account usage loading was driven by a reactive effect even though each native profile row already supplies live client, agent, and profile properties. Move request invalidation to those native receipts: each scope write immediately retires the previous request, then one microtask loads the complete same-turn tuple.

The existing PageRequest owner remains responsible for cancellation and rejecting late success/error publication. Explicit button, event, and method refreshes consume queued automatic work and still run immediately; a later native write in that turn schedules the final tuple without another generation or token mechanism. Setup and cleanup share one onSettled block. Pending, empty, error, quota, and balance rendering stay unchanged.

## Evidence

| account-usage.test.ts | 5 passed, including same-turn scope/refresh and disposal contracts |
| model-providers-page.usage.test.ts | 7 passed; config-save preservation and page refresh convergence |

Production LOC: 154 → 162 (+8). Direct test LOC: 105 → 171 (+66). No tracked-pattern survivors. Growth pairs native receipt registration with retirement and preserves batching. Final head `3580a1a343c9113e4cb003fc6e48193264bf6bc8` is rebased onto `9d495c33ff4e479780fe83cd0e8d62b2264fa53d`. Frozen install passed in 2.35 seconds. prs.body:

Model Accounts independently watched Gateway state and copied Profile's identity props through an effect, even though Profile already owns the canonical `users.self` target. Profile now exposes that target through a plain read/subscribe source. The account view consumes its initial value and owner receipts once per lifetime, while its existing state owner keeps request retirement, authorization polling and same-client draft retention.

The person label stays live. A parent-boundary regression starts with a presence alias, waits for the canonical profile, and verifies that a label refresh retains the account inventory without another fetch. No markup, styles, routes, dependencies or startup imports change.

prs.title: refactor(ui): scope question resource operations to Solid lifetimes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resource questions used an effect, a captured identity, and a generation/revision pair to retire local work. Their two lifetimes are different: changing the request must clear uploaded rows, while disabling the question must retain those rows and retire only pending work, errors, and previews.

Express those lifetimes with keyed, non-rendering Solid owners beside the existing controls. Request scope owns uploaded rows; disabled transitions own operation lifetime. Cleanup aborts transport without publishing UI state. Busy state derives from the pending operation, while a plain abort handle still prevents two clicks in the same turn from starting duplicate work. Existing current-client, Gateway scope, request identity, host-connection, and upload-authority checks remain intact.

Controls keep their existing DOM across these changes. Tags, styles, routes, preview loading, and lazy imports are unchanged. The nearby draft-recovery `initialDrafts` snapshot remains intentional and was not modified.

prs.title: fix(cli): Windows state-dir mismatch hint cannot run in PowerShell
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when the CLI and a local Gateway use different state directories on Windows, the refusal message suggests a POSIX environment assignment that PowerShell cannot run.

## User Impact

Windows PowerShell users can copy the suggested command to run the requested CLI action against the Gateway's state and config paths. The command restores their previous environment variables afterward. The message retains a bash/zsh alternative.

## Why This Change Was Made

The mismatch guard already knows the Gateway paths. Its repair hint now uses PowerShell assignment and command invocation syntax on Windows, with the existing PowerShell path quoting helper. POSIX guidance remains unchanged on other platforms.

## Evidence

- Baseline commit `5428b0214c7d7269eeaa919c7cdc441362ed7855` ran the real token Gateway fixture on a standard Windows runner. The emitted command failed in `powershell.exe` because `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=...` was treated as a command. The baseline assertion was validated as the expected failure in [proof run 39175188285](https://github.com/KhanCold/openclaw/actions/runs/39175188285).
- Candidate `1d52bd4309643ad3b3b72c0f708ead47b9319b17` passes the unchanged Windows regression test, including correct paths inside the command and restoration of prior environment values. The related guard unit suite, scoped format, and lint passed in the same run.

prs.title: refactor: bind sidebar subscriptions to component lifetimes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Sidebar and session renderers still use effect-driven subscriptions and state copies that make their mounted ownership harder to maintain during the Solid 2 migration.

## User Impact

User impact: no intended appearance or behavior change; sidebar selection and hovercard focus remain stable across owner updates.

## Why This Change Was Made

Sidebar and session renderers used effects to copy owner state, bind subscriptions, and discover owned controls. This checkpoint binds subscriptions to component lifetimes, consumes existing owner projections, and uses shared timer and Markdown primitives. Owned gesture events move into JSX.

The synchronous sidebar owner now retains the last presented roster selection. Hovercard client replacement preserves its open portal and focused children; its remaining commit effect waits for Markdown reconciliation before restoring focus. Catalog and background loading keep their existing lazy boundaries. Tags, classes, routes, selectors, and appearance are preserved.

Head `91ca5f01f6dd` is rebased onto `fd2a6caa89df`. The focused 17-file implementation retains the synchronous roster selection and native bridge contracts from current main.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |

| Install and UI types | Frozen install and `pnpm tsgo:ui` passed on rebased head; default tsrs, no override or branch dependency changes |
| Focused behavior | Retained unchanged-source proof: parked-roster and People sorting; catalog retries and quiet startup; hovercard client replacement/focus; Details/composer and locale cases passed |
| Prior runner exception | Parked-roster proof used Node with `--fsModuleCache=false` after cached workers stalled in SSD filesystem-cache rename; all interrupted attempts were joined. No runtime override was used in the refresh |
| Scoped lint | Retained pass for the unchanged 17-file implementation using `tsconfig.ui.json` |
| Independent review | Rebased candidate scoped-clean through P2 |

| Build/startup | Exact-base and head `pnpm ui:build` completed on the same machine. Startup 337,719→337,718 B gzip (−1 B), 7 JS requests; CSS 38,500 B / 1 request both. Lazy boundaries preserved |

| Broad proof | New exact-head `ci:full` run pending. Prior head `eb0c703` passed all 3 UI unit, 9 Control UI E2E and 2 real-Gateway shards in [run 39181713974](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39181713974); that is prior-head evidence |

## What Problem This Solves

Custodian page used two reactive effects to refresh a provided transcript owner and admit initial onboarding channel inventory. Replace those effects with native host property receipts plus subscriptions to existing owner projections. One stable session projection now retargets on store replacement, and the page releases receipt delivery and owner subscriptions on disposal.

The channel owner remains authoritative: refresh only while onboarding is open, connected, empty, idle, and error-free. Explicit retry and the existing forced reconnect refresh are unchanged. Cold store replacement is hydrated by `CustodianSurface` connecting the store: `connect` → `synchronizeClient` → `startSession(client, true)` → `initializeSession` loads history before welcome. prs.body:
## Current candidate and proof

Current head: `f907bdbe9742ffe0bddf7b868f790d9f199c1c99`. Main base: `918a379c89cb5f3e7de913fce9eade020317d117`. The rebase includes the upstream sidebar import and unused `TaglineMode` fixes. All six changed files, the stable patch ID, and the range-diff are identical to original reviewed head `52ddda21acbbf62cc0a3ba0fc61234cfdd0f858a`.

| Current-head check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Frozen install | Pass |
| Default `pnpm tsgo:ui` | Pass, 8.65 s |
| Full production/export Knip | Fails: one unused export, `settleInterruptedRestartRecovery`, 320.23 s |
| Same full analyzer on exact main base | Same sole named unused export; exit 1, 184.28 s |
| Source equivalence and `git diff --check` | Pass |

The unresolved export is `src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-restart-recovery-failure.ts:settleInterruptedRestartRecovery`. The identical full analyzer reproduces it on the exact main base. Candidate/base source snapshots remained clean and the manifests/lockfile are identical. This is local baseline analyzer attribution only; no inherited-CI claim is made. The candidate was restored after the baseline run.

Behavioral tests were not repeated because the reviewed source blobs are unchanged. The runtime, browser, startup, and CI evidence below belongs to the original reviewed head and is retained as historical proof. Current-head CI remains pending. No remote lease was acquired.

## What Problem This Solves

Chat sidebar panels discovered caller-owned elements with DOM queries and mounted their content through a separate imperative Solid root. Geometry and narrow-panel focus also relied on effects, despite their inputs already arriving through the native bridge.

Pass the owning sidebar view's existing shell/header/primary/outlet refs to the lazy region, render its content through a Solid Portal, and schedule geometry/focus from native input receipts and hosted-tab events. Panel container refs and the existing native panel-host contract replace subtree queries. Native Close still yields to registered dialogs through their closing animation, when the native dialog can remain open after its logical open state clears.

The tags, classes, route loading boundary, panel parking, tab identity, keyboard focus, and native/hosted Close contracts are preserved. This checkpoint deliberately leaves the first-enabled-main-header-action query until the separately owned header interface lands; that is unfinished zero-query work, not a claimed survivor exception.

## Historical original-head evidence

Base: `5f637b6b3686b0aa193ebe7a579a444c87dcec01`. Candidate: `52ddda21acbbf62cc0a3ba0fc61234cfdd0f858a`.

| Check | Result |

The focus failure exposed an extra microtask before `onSettled`; registering directly from the native receipt keeps the transfer in the same commit cycle. The registry-backed native-dialog test protects the closing interval that a logical-open-only check would miss. Local tests use the Node runner with its filesystem module cache disabled because external-SSD cache renames stalled prior runs.

| Touched production pattern | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Rendering controllers | 0 | 0 |

prs.title: feat(providers): add Bifrost provider and allow anonymous self-hosted gateways
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

[Bifrost](https://getbifrost.ai) is an OpenAI-compatible LLM gateway that unifies 20+ providers with failover, load balancing, and virtual-key governance. OpenClaw ships bundled providers for LiteLLM, SGLang, and vLLM, but not Bifrost — so operators had to configure it by hand in `models.providers`.

## What This Changes

**New bundled provider** (`extensions/bifrost`), built on the LiteLLM provider shape:

- Interactive setup asks for the gateway base URL, then whether a virtual key is needed, then lists the models the gateway advertises via `/openai/v1/models` and defaults to the first.
- Discovery failures name the reason (`HTTP 404`, `empty model list`, `unreachable`) before falling back to manual entry, and a config change during discovery aborts before credentials are sent to a stale endpoint.
- Non-interactive setup accepts `--custom-base-url`.

**Provider artwork**, which every other user-facing bundled provider ships and Bifrost initially did not:

- `extensions/bifrost/assets/icon.png` — 512×512, the official Apache-2.0 mark inverted to dark-on-white so it matches the other bundled provider icons, which are all light-background (verified: LiteLLM, SGLang, vLLM and OpenRouter icons are 0% transparent with a dominant white background). Geometry unchanged.
- `extensions/bifrost/assets/activity.svg` and `ui/public/provider-icons/ProviderIcon-bifrost.svg` — OpenClaw-authored gateway glyph (many upstreams converging on one routed endpoint), `currentColor` so it renders on light and dark. Neither Simple Icons nor LobeHub ships a Bifrost glyph, so these are drawn in-repo and labelled in-file as *not* a Bifrost trademark, matching the precedent where SGLang's activity icon is an unbranded server box.
- Registering `bifrost` in `PROVIDER_ICON_NAMES` also fixes a visible defect: `resolveProviderIconName("bifrost")` returned `null`, so the model picker was rendering a **letter "B"** avatar for this provider.

Provenance is pinned to upstream commit `a30e57dd` in `ATTRIBUTION.md`, following the format of the existing third-party entries.

**Two design decisions worth review:**

1. **Base URL is `http://localhost:8080/openai`**, Bifrost's OpenAI-compatible surface, not the core `/v1` API. Both serve chat completions, but only the `/openai` surface makes discovery and inference share one base URL. Bifrost's own OpenAI SDK and OpenCode guides use this path.

2. **Keyless gateways use `auth: "none"`.** A fresh Bifrost has no authentication — that's the documented zero-config default — so setup records the provider as explicitly anonymous rather than storing a key that resolves to nothing. This reuses the existing explicit-no-auth owner (`resolveExplicitProviderNoAuth`) instead of adding a second mechanism. Re-running setup for a URL change keeps an already-configured key.

**Shared-helper change:** `promptAndConfigureOpenAICompatibleSelfHostedProviderAuth` forced a non-empty API key, which pushed SGLang and vLLM users toward a placeholder value for servers that accept anonymous requests. It now accepts an empty key and records `auth: "none"`, matching what the config schema already models. The Bifrost provider does not use that helper — it uses the LiteLLM path, which already prompted for a URL and a key.

**Config-surface budget, raised deliberately:** the Bifrost plugin schema grows the plugin config surface from 4693 to 4714 keys (+21), which trips the `config-docs` baseline ratchet. I regenerated `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` and raised the budget in `config-baseline.counts.json` rather than leaving it failing. The +21 is the provider's own declared schema — a base URL, an optional virtual-key auth profile, and the provider's setup metadata — not a new core config surface. Core stays at 2565 and channel at 4043, both unchanged. If a maintainer would rather the provider ship without declaring those keys, say so and I will trim the schema rather than hold the budget increase.

## Evidence

Verified against a running Bifrost gateway at `http://bifrost` (port 80), with isolated state via `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` / `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

**Discovery through the production code path** (`discoverOpenAICompatibleLocalModels`, the real function the plugin calls):

```
base url passed to discovery: http://bifrost/openai/v1
discovery kind: success | rows: 12
first row: {"id":"Nvidia/nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b","object":"model","owned_by":"nvidia","created":735790403}
rows reporting context_window: 6/12
```

**End-to-end agent turn** through the shipped CLI, provider configured with `auth: "none"`:

```
winnerProvider: "bifrost"
winnerModel: "Vercel/poolside/laguna-s-2.1-free"
result: "success",  fallbackUsed: false,  runner: "embedded"
finalAssistantMessageRawText: "LOCAL_BIFROST_OK"
```

`openclaw models list --provider bifrost --refresh --json` returns the nested-slash key `bifrost/Vercel/poolside/laguna-s-2.1-free` with `available: true`.

### Two findings the live gateway surfaced that mocks did not

**1. Model IDs are multi-segment.** Bifrost returns IDs like `Nvidia/nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b` and `Vercel/alibaba/qwen3.7-flash`, so refs become `bifrost/<vendor>/<provider>/<model>`. Verified this round-trips exactly: `parseProviderModelRef` splits on the **first** slash (`packages/model-catalog-core/src/model-catalog-refs.ts:54`), and `normalizeAgentModelRefForConfig("bifrost/Nvidia/nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b")` returns the input unchanged. The committed tests cover the single-slash case, so I noted this rather than claiming the nested case is regression-guarded.

**2. The gateway echoes a different model string than requested.** Requesting `Vercel/poolside/laguna-s-2.1-free` returns `"model": "poolside/laguna-s-2.1-free"` — the `Vercel/` prefix is a routing selector the gateway drops when reporting the resolved upstream model. OpenClaw surfaces this as `modelRouteChange: "Model route changed: bifrost/Vercel/… → bifrost/poolside/…"`. **This is expected behavior, not a defect**: `agent-run-terminal-receipt.ts:66` reports `effective.responseModel || effective.model`, so it is faithfully relaying the gateway's echo. Worth documenting so operators don't read the notice as a misroute.

### Parity control

The `--refresh` path prints `Model discovery could not refresh all providers`. I checked whether Bifrost caused it by pointing the **proven LiteLLM provider** at the same gateway: identical warning, identical single-authored-model result. It's pre-existing behavior in an isolated state where credential-less bundled providers can't refresh, not a Bifrost defect.

### Live authority-chain proof on an enforcing gateway

The earlier anonymous proof ran against a keyless gateway, which cannot demonstrate the authentication defects. I repeated it against the same Bifrost deployment after enabling **Enforce Virtual Keys on Inference**, so it now rejects unauthenticated inference with `401 virtual_key_required`. That makes the defect observable rather than merely arguable.

Non-interactive onboarding with the key supplied **only through `BIFROST_VIRTUAL_KEY`** — no `--bifrost-api-key`, no inline `apiKey` — which is precisely the case the old `hasKey` check missed:

```jsonc
// config written by onboarding
"models": { "providers": { "bifrost": {
  "baseUrl": "http://bifrost/openai",
  "api": "openai-completions",
  "models": []            // non-interactive preset: discovery-backed
} } },
"auth": { "profiles": { "bifrost:default": { "provider": "bifrost", "mode": "api_key" } } }
```

No `auth` field is written, and the credential lands in the profile. Agent turn through the shipped CLI:

```
winnerProvider: "bifrost"
winnerModel: "Vercel/poolside/laguna-s-2.1-free"
result: "success"        fallbackUsed: false      runner: "embedded"
authMode: "auth-profile"
finalAssistantMessageRawText: "KEYED_OK"
```

`authMode: "auth-profile"` is the load-bearing line: it shows the credential was resolved and sent, not silently stripped.

Now inject `auth: "none"` into that same row — which is exactly what the pre-fix code wrote — and re-run:

```jsonc
"bifrost": { "baseUrl": "http://bifrost/openai", "api": "openai-completions", "auth": "none" }
```

```
virtual key is required. Provide a virtual key via the x-bf-vk header.   (x8)
401
no winnerProvider, no fallbackUsed
```

Remove the field again and the same turn returns `RECOVERED_OK` with `authMode: "auth-profile"`. So the single `auth` field is the whole difference between a working and a failing credential: **live failure with the marker, live success without it.** This is the authority-chain evidence the review asked for, and it only became obtainable once the gateway stopped accepting anonymous requests.

The third instance has the same live shape. Starting from a row carrying `auth: "none"` alongside an active
`bifrost:default` profile, re-authenticating with the key and **no** `--custom-base-url` clears the marker and the turn
succeeds:

```
before:  models.providers.bifrost.auth = "none"   (profile bifrost:default present)
action:  onboard --non-interactive --auth-choice bifrost-api-key      (no --custom-base-url)
after:   auth = <unset>
turn:    winnerProvider: "bifrost"   authMode: "auth-profile"   fallbackUsed: false
         finalAssistantMessageRawText: "REAUTH_OK"
```

### Authentication defects found in review, and their regression proof

ClawSweeper's review found that Bifrost onboarding could discard a supplied credential. I confirmed both against source before changing anything, and traced the runtime consequence to `resolveExplicitProviderNoAuth`, which is terminal on `auth: "none"` and strips the `Authorization` header via `applyLocalNoAuthHeaders`.

1. **`applyBifrostConnection` merged `...existing` and only ever *added* the marker.** Re-running interactive setup against a gateway that now has a virtual key inherited `auth: "none"` through the merge and through `applyBifrostModelConfig` (`applyProviderConfigWithMergedModels` spreads `existingProviderRest`). The keyed branch now clears the marker, which is how the `omlx` and `llama-cpp` gateway providers already drop anonymous state once a credential exists.
2. **`runNonInteractive` inferred anonymity from `--bifrost-api-key` and the inline provider `apiKey` only**, while the delegated method also resolves `BIFROST_VIRTUAL_KEY` and existing profiles. A key in either of those made the wrapper write `auth: "none"`, which the delegate then preserved while saving the key it had just resolved. The ad-hoc check is removed: the delegated method owns the decision and returns `null` when no credential resolves, so this path always applies one.
3. **`runNonInteractive` still skipped the fix when `--custom-base-url` was absent.** My own refactor added an early return that handed the delegate the original config, so `applyBifrostConnection` never ran and an earlier `auth: "none"` survived — the delegate saved the key, the preset spread `existingProviderRest` through, and the marker stayed terminal. Caught in the Revision 2 re-review. This path always applies a credential, so a gateway already on file counts as configured: the base URL now resolves from the flag *or* the existing row, and either way the credentialed update runs.

Base-fail/head-pass evidence — both new tests fail against `4d2478c4a6` and pass against `838b5e17cc`:

```
pre-fix  (4d2478c4a6):  Tests  2 failed | 16 passed (18)
post-fix (838b5e17cc):  Tests  18 passed (18)

pre-fix failures:
  × clears a previous anonymous marker once the operator supplies a virtual key
  × stays credentialed when the key resolves from a profile rather than a flag
```

`resolveExplicitProviderNoAuth` is core-internal with no Plugin SDK subpath, so the tests assert its precondition — that `auth` is not `"none"` whenever a credential is available — rather than importing across the extension boundary.

### Gates on this head

- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, and the `tsconfig.core.test.plugins-platform.json` lane — pass
- `oxlint` on all changed files — clean
- `oxfmt --check` — clean; `format-docs --check` clean (1365 files)
- `docs:check-links` — 15646 links, 0 broken; `docs:check-config-examples` — pass
- `generate-config-doc-baseline.ts --check` — pass after the budget raise above
- `pnpm plugins:inventory:gen` — no diff (artwork is not part of the generated inventory)
- Tests: **106 across the 9 Bifrost/SGLang/vLLM/shared-setup test files** (Bifrost 19 on this head), 561 package-manifest + extension-runtime-dependency contracts, 65 boundary invariants, 126 manifest-registry + bundled-manifest contracts, 31 provider-icon/public-asset — all pass

### Known Gaps

- **The UI browser-test project could not run locally.** Its Playwright Chromium binary is absent from this machine's cache (`chrome-headless-shell` not installed), so that project reports `no tests` with a launch error. This is environmental and unrelated to the change; every other project in the same run passed (3217 UI tests + 166 + 65). Worth a CI confirmation rather than trusting the local run for that project.

- **Full `pnpm lint` fails on three inherited `max-lines` violations** in files this branch does not touch: `extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-warm-image-store.ts` (718/700), `extensions/oc-path/src/cli.test.ts` (1125/1000), `extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-coalescing.e2e.test.ts` (1028/1000). None are in `config/max-lines-baseline.txt`. Every file changed here lints clean.
- **Discovery contributed no additional models under `--refresh`.** The live catalog/discovery refresh path did not merge the gateway's 12 models into the model list; only the authored model appeared. LiteLLM against the same gateway behaves identically, so this is existing merge-mode semantics rather than something introduced here. The onboarding path *does* call discovery directly and receives all 12. This is the `models.mode=replace` half of #121584 ("Auto-discover all models when configuring a provider"): this PR delivers the interactive-configuration half, and does not attempt to close that issue — it carries `clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr` and `needs-product-decision`, so the refresh-merge semantics are a product decision, not a side effect of adding a provider.
- **Related pre-existing bug, not fixed here, and no issue tracks it:** the same helper still passes `initialValue: params.defaultBaseUrl` for its base-URL prompt, so a typed URL appends to the prefilled default under the shipped wizard. This is the defect #173164 fixed for LiteLLM, still live for SGLang and vLLM. Fixing it changes their behavior, so it is left as a follow-up rather than bundled here. I can file it as a separate issue if that is wanted.
- Interactive onboarding was not driven interactively over a pty; the base-URL and model prompts are covered by tests through the registered plugin.
- **Proof the review asked for that this head still does not carry.** I want to be explicit rather than let the checklist imply otherwise:
  - ~~*Authenticated onboarding against a real gateway.*~~ **Now closed** — see the authority-chain proof above: the credential reaches the gateway (`authMode: "auth-profile"`) and the anonymous marker alone flips the same turn from `KEYED_OK` to `401`.
  - *Revocation at egress.* The narrower half is still open: showing that a revoked or replaced setup authority blocks a credential-bearing request **before** any network effect. Deactivating the virtual key mid-flow would show Bifrost refusing it, which proves Bifrost's enforcement, not OpenClaw's. The OpenClaw-side proof needs a stale credential held locally while authority changes underneath it.
  - *The key is sent as `Authorization: Bearer`, not Bifrost's native `x-bf-vk`, and this must not be "fixed" with a static header.* **Now documented for users**, not just in this body: `docs/providers/bifrost.md` carries a support matrix stating plainly that a legacy key (no `sk-bf-` prefix) or a gateway with `auth_config.is_enabled` will not work, plus the `x-bf-vk` provider-row configuration to use in that case. Verified against a local listener that the configuration sends both headers, and that an unset env reference sends the literal `${BIFROST_VIRTUAL_KEY}` — which Bifrost rejects with `401` while ignoring the valid `Authorization` on the same request.

    **`x-bf-vk` takes absolute precedence over `Authorization` for virtual keys.** Bifrost does not fall back once `x-bf-vk` is present:

    | Request | Result |
    |---|---|
    | valid `Authorization` + empty `x-bf-vk` | `401 virtual_key_required` |
    | valid `Authorization` + literal `${BIFROST_VIRTUAL_KEY}` | `401 access_not_found` |
    | valid `Authorization` alone | `200` |

    So sending both is not a hedge — it is "`x-bf-vk` decides, `Authorization` ignored." Declaring `request.auth` or `headers` with a `${BIFROST_VIRTUAL_KEY}` reference would therefore send an empty or unresolved `x-bf-vk` whenever that variable is unset — which is every interactively-entered key — converting a provider that works today into one that returns `401` by default.

    **`x-bf-vk` must carry the resolved credential or be absent**, and no current seam can place a profile credential there: `SecretInput` accepts only `env`/`file`/`exec`/`store` refs with no auth-profile source; `apiKeyHeader` is hardcoded to the `api-key` header and only participates in Model Setup resume; `wrapStreamFn` explicitly excludes credential material; and `prepareRuntimeAuth` receives `apiKey` but can only return a replacement credential and base URL.

    Fixing this properly needs a narrow provider capability — declare a credential-header name, host places the resolved credential there — which is a Plugin SDK boundary expansion rather than a config change. Filed as #175583 rather than bundled here, so the shared-SDK decision can be made on its own merits and Bifrost's bundling question stays separate. The shipped path stays on `Authorization`, which is correct for `sk-bf-` keys with HTTP auth off; a legacy key without that prefix, or a deployment that later enables `auth_config.is_enabled`, would still fail.
  - *Shared SGLang/vLLM anonymous inference.* The shared helper's optional-key change is covered by `provider-self-hosted-setup.interactive.test.ts`; I have not run a live anonymous turn through SGLang or vLLM.
  - *Before/after model-picker screenshots.* The artwork is a visual change and the repo's gate wants inspected captures in the PR; none are attached yet. I rendered the assets at 16/28/64/96px locally to verify legibility, but a picker capture needs the UI browser-test project, which cannot run on this host — Playwright's `chrome-headless-shell` is absent from `~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright/`. CI's `checks-ui-e2e` is the available path.

### Data-model compatibility

No stored data changes shape. The provider adds a new `models.providers.bifrost` row and reuses the existing `auth: "none"` field that `ModelProviderConfig` already declares, so there is no migration and no change to how an existing config is read. The one behavior change to existing consumers is the shared helper's optional key, and that is the documented intent: a gateway that was previously forced to store a placeholder key can now record `auth: "none"` instead.

prs.title: refactor(config): trust validated reads and audit ownership
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Config preparation repeats successful worker-reply validation and adjacent authority checks already performed by the same owner. Audit preparation also deep-clones records before recursive redaction rebuilds their arrays and plain objects.

## User Impact

Config reads and audit preparation do less repeated work. Unavailable health/journal results, error behavior, caller-owned audit arrays, secret redaction, and runtime publication authority keep their existing behavior. No public SDK contract changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Consume replies already validated at runtime by executeExistingOpenClawStateRead. Remove two synchronous authority assertions whose identical callbacks have just run after the await. Preserve post-await, publication, activation and error-path checks. Use a shallow audit-record copy before replacing argv fields and recursively redacting the record's scalar/string-array contract.

Production +2/-7, net -5 lines across four modules; tests +19/-1. There are no intended SQL, request, transaction, schema, audit-policy or PostgreSQL-bookkeeping changes. Expected SQL/request/MAIN delta is 0/0/0 from source inspection, estimated and unmeasured. One final lane baseline/candidate pair covering all five deletion PRs remains pending. No measurement waiver or latency claim.

Accepted edge: unchanged owner contracts remain authoritative. This does not remove the worker's real reply validation, unavailable-result handling, or any guard across an actual yield/effect.

## Evidence

Changed-file formatting, type-aware lint and whitespace checks pass. Independent Codex review completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings; final source verification passed. Exact-head CI [39190677549](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39190677549) passed all five owner files (89 Bun cases), production/core types, lint, source contracts, Madge and T1/dialect/worker ratchets. The extension test-type failure at `native-subagent-monitor.parent-retention.test.ts:37` is identical to current-main [39190189076/job117861351867](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39190189076/job/117861351867): `completionDeliveryRetryDelaysMs` is absent from `MonitorOptions` in an untouched file. No static check is waived; aggregate CI is not claimed green.

The X publication case failed in candidate CI [39190677549/job117862847360](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39190677549/job/117862847360) after 120285 ms. A focused whole-file replay on current main `3d8c860ac6ac9edb81bacd524680cc85f1d229c0` also failed after 124354 ms with the same `Test timed out in 120000ms` and `X publication allowed: waiting for child transcript write` messages. The local command was `pnpm test src/gateway/x-publication-owner-composition.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, using repository-default Bun, internal-disk TMPDIR, clean pinned source and unchanged test/timeout; retained evidence is `pr3a-main-x-replay.log` lines 256–259 and exit code 1. This reproduces the failure without the PR. Candidate CI ran on Linux and this main comparison ran on macOS; no identical root cause or fix is claimed. Earlier main `c2549f8295d09f520f119de44d77e1c7dc25779a` [passed in 6436 ms](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39188738444/job/117856625179), while historical base `0319200bb1b72e8ec2f0601cbb53d61f865313bd` [failed with the same signature](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39190375503/job/117861643918). Revision or execution-context sensitivity remains possible.

[Hosted Codex review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176820#issuecomment-6258438210) completed on `f08aecb` with no findings. [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176820#issuecomment-6258596749) likewise reports no code or security findings; its P3 next step was to attribute the failing typecheck and X jobs. The exact-main type diagnostic and current-main X reproduction above address that attribution request. The lane-wide measurement remains pending as disclosed above.

Knip [39190681923/job117862831566](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39190681923/job/117862831566) reports no unused exports in production/full-tree/scripts and zero new findings. Its two unused files (`scripts/bench-channel-ingress-writer.ts`, `src/process/spawn-diagnostics.test-support.ts`) match exact-main [39190227860/job117861494417](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39190227860/job/117861494417). The unused supplemental remainder is canceled and its watcher is settled.

The published-driver update cell is not applicable to this split scope: no update, migration, plugin-loading or service-lifecycle operation changes. The concrete Doctor lint call (`src/commands/doctor-lint-runner.ts:376`) supplies no authority callback to the cold loader, so both deleted assertions are already no-ops there. Doctor config migration uses the unchanged `setAppliedRuntimeConfigSnapshot` path (`src/commands/doctor-config-flow.ts:115`). The shared read owner still rejects unsuccessful or mismatched replies, and audit output remains unchanged. The separately prepared service-admission change retains its required update cell.

The existing audit persistence test is extended to verify redacted argv/execArgv, independent output arrays, unchanged input and persisted secret removal. It is expected to pass before and after this behavior-preserving refactor, not a claimed base-red defect regression. Runtime snapshot, health/scope and journal owner tests passed in the exact-head CI above. No new adversarial mismatched worker-reply test was located; that correlation guarantee is established by the complete runtime owner in the review packet.

<details>
<summary>Candidate ledger</summary>

| Candidate | Decision | Owner/caller evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| C15956 (f) | REMOVE | Only top-level argv fields change before recursive redaction rebuilds the contract's arrays and plain objects. |
| C16209 (g) | REMOVE | The same authority callback just ran after the await; only a snapshot-presence/early-return branch intervenes. |
| C16214 (b), C16215 (g) | REMOVE | Two scanner IDs identify the same second adjacent assertion, again dominated by the identical callback. |
| Health/journal reply guards (two unnumbered companions) | REMOVE | The shared read owner runtime-validates success and requested type; callers preserve empty/null outcomes. |
| Post-await/publication/activation/error guards | KEEP | They protect authority across real yields or effects. |
| Owner reply validation and unavailable-result handling | KEEP | They establish protocol correlation and preserve missing-state behavior. |

Four static IDs (one b, one f, two g) represent three numbered source locations. Two unnumbered reply operations are counted separately. These are the selected removals in this PR.

</details>

prs.title: refactor(ui): bind Channels to its application lifetime
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Channels kept a context-rebinding effect, an initial snapshot, and source-replacement bookkeeping for an optional prop used only by its tests. Its production route supplies no props, and the application capability object is stable for the mounted page’s lifetime. The page now consumes `useApplication()` as a plain service argument and binds existing Gateway, Channels, and config receipt subscriptions once with paired cleanup. Disconnects, client replacement, authorization changes, pairing reconciliation, icon loading, and request retirement remain with their existing owners.

The fixture now uses `ApplicationProvider`, matching production. Only the artificial application-source replacement variation is removed; real disconnect, client replacement, admin-access loss, unmount, caller-abort, reconnect, and retained-editor cases remain.

## CI repair

Run [39183243315](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39183243315) failed `Agents catalog publication with a real Gateway > refreshes an open Agents editor after catalog publication without losing drafts` at `agent-file-lifecycle.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts:245`, before catalog publication. The fixture expected `{ primary: "fixture/selected", fallbacks: ["fixture/anchor"] }` but read `"fixture/selected"`. That is the canonical primary-only shape, so the primary save succeeded while the fallback was absent.

The fixture typed a fallback and immediately pressed Enter without observing the actual option or selected chip. Its next “some mutation happened” check could already pass on the primary/identity save. Model controls are disabled during config writes, and the fallback uses a menu with its own readiness. The test now waits for the primary to persist and the fallback input to be enabled, clicks the visible `fixture/anchor` option, and requires its chip before the unchanged persisted-object assertion. No product code or expected persisted value is changed by this repair. The exact timing of the missed interaction is not proven by the CI log; this closes the concrete readiness gap without adding sleeps or retries.

This failure is not claimed as inherited. Scheduled main run `39176649118` passed both Gateway shards; current scheduled main run `39183785855` passed the shard containing this case. Full PR CI must prove the repaired real-Gateway case; no local E2E run was used.

## Lifetime evidence

The production route lazily invokes `ChannelsPage` with `{}`. The app captures one `ApplicationRuntime.context` for its provider; Gateway, Channels, runtime-config and theme capabilities remain stable for that mounted lifetime. `lib/reactive/context.ts` deliberately snapshots this capability for Solid consumers. A fresh application epoch disposes the old tree and services. The final rebase preserves the original two-file Channels patch exactly (`git range-diff` reports `=`).

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Frozen install after latest main refresh | Passed on `b410235890e`; 7.40s |
| `pnpm tsgo:ui` after latest main refresh | Passed on `b410235890e`; 20.78s |
| Actual UI E2E test typecheck leaf after latest main refresh | Passed on `b410235890e`; 14.39s |
| Focused type-aware lint of repaired E2E | Passed |
| Formatting and whitespace | Passed |
| Independent isolated P0–P2 full-PR review with owner/test context | Scoped clean before refresh; all three reviewed blobs remain identical |
| Original Channels test file, one worker | 31 passed on prior head; no local rerun |
| Production Knip (`pnpm deadcode:knip`) | Reused pass on `bcd950d5b9a7c09e99224b183e653deee83c380f`; 501.19s; all three reviewed blobs remain identical after refresh |
| Repaired real-Gateway scenario | Awaiting new full PR CI on refreshed head; prior run blocked before execution |

The prior Channels run emitted 148 strict-read development warnings. A named baseline diagnostic did not collect tests because its Bun worker timed out in filesystem rename; it provides no warning-attribution verdict. No warning suppression was added. The original targeted Channels lint also reports the pre-existing max-lines finding: this PR shrinks that test file, and its recorded base run fails the same limit. The repaired E2E has its own focused lint gate above.

| Production checklist | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `createEffect` | 1 | 0 |
| `untrack` | 1 | 0 |
| `createRenderEffect`, raw listeners, DOM queries | 0 | 0 |
| Controller patterns, manual class strings, production `flush`, owner escapes | 0 | 0 |

| LOC against `0a6268fb1fe1930e59a47ba8e89799bcd0a31740` | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Channels production | 412 | 387 |
| Channels tests | 1216 | 1202 |
| Repaired real-Gateway E2E | 447 | 454 |

Production shrinks by 25 lines; total touched tests shrink by 7. No markup, styles, host tags, selectors, startup imports, lazy boundaries, or visual output changed, so no local build or visual capture was needed.

## Replacement-head CI

Run [39188373179](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39188373179), head `bcd950d5b9a7c09e99224b183e653deee83c380f`, failed before the repaired Gateway scenario could execute. The UI build, Gateway builds and performance build report `SidebarProjectionMemo` missing from `sidebar-projection-memo.ts`; production/test types identify the stale import in `ui/src/components/session-attention.ts:28` and a consequent implicit row type at line 180. That file is held by #176477 and is untouched here.

The unit logs also emit 36 failed test names across the two jobs that end with exit 137: 25 have explicit missing-export/constructor errors, and 11 have preceding same-test halted-reactivity diagnostics before assertions, DOM access failures, timeouts, or a truncated failure. These are unresolved results, not passing tests or an inherited-failure claim. Exit 137 alone does not establish OOM. Unit shard 2's saved log contains no terminal diagnostic, so its cause remains unknown. All exact names and source log lines were retained for the next comparison. No runtime admin exception is being requested on this evidence; fresh CI must prove the repaired Gateway scenario after the shared build repair.

## Latest main refresh

Head `b410235890e2d6cb527d24a57bd2bb3d26ef24e7` is rebased onto `0a6268fb1fe1930e59a47ba8e89799bcd0a31740`, whose `session-attention.ts` imports `SidebarProjectionMemo` from `sidebar-projection-cache.ts`. Both PR commits remain patch-equivalent and all three changed source/test files are byte-for-byte identical to the reviewed candidate. The frozen install and the two type checks that failed on the stale shared import now pass. The prior focused tests, lint, formatting, isolated review, and production Knip are retained as prior-head evidence; no local E2E or additional runtime change was made. New full PR CI must still prove the repaired Gateway scenario and resolve the previously recorded runtime test names.

## Fresh full-CI qualification

Full run [39190171510](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39190171510) failed only the same three runtime test names present in completed [scheduled main39186683798](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39186683798), plus the existing chat byte ceiling and downstream gate. The failing names are `refetches instead of showing a row excluded by configured-agent filtering`, `keeps the Sessions page query stable when the startup roster completes`, and `finds a grouped spawned conversation beyond the roster and treats a full result page as success`. Test/assertion signatures and all failure-source blobs match main.

The corrected real-Gateway case, `refreshes an open Agents editor after catalog publication without losing drafts`, passed in23650ms; both cases in its file passed, and Gateway2 finished with28 files/63 passing tests. This replaces the previous unqualified run where Sidebar setup prevented the case from running.

CI compared exact merge `2b9ff90f66c0fa4b0f8f938070a4cb3f998703f3` to base `ffa14d0e0bf00b9accf1aae7d063b9e9801ee570`: chat1,491,366→1,491,407B (+41), both above1,490,000; new1,049,566→1,049,613B (+47), below1,050,000. Startup passes at337,507B with7 JS/1 CSS requests. Ordered merge parents, reconstructed tree, complete failed-job accounting and artifact hashes are retained for native inherited-failure admission. No tests or builds repeated. Full CI is not reported as green.

Fixes #118185.

## Summary
- Carry the existing Claude native assistant UUID (`resumeCheckpointId`) and bound Claude session id onto the durable CLI assistant transcript record.
- Let the existing CLI history merge deduplicate the durable and imported native representations by their shared authoritative identity, rather than rendered text.
- Preserve imported-only rows, cross-session UUID protections, existing run-key idempotency, and the current importer fallback behavior.

## Regression coverage
- Add a focused fixture containing one durable Claude CLI assistant record and one imported native JSONL assistant row for the same native assistant UUID with deliberately unequal text; assert history renders one assistant message.
- Assert the CLI durable writer records no Claude identity for non-Claude/identity-less output, and records the complete `(importedFrom, cliSessionId, externalId)` tuple only when both existing parsed facts are available.

## Release-note context
This corrects a user-visible duplicate reply in Claude CLI WebChat history. Do not edit `CHANGELOG.md`; release automation owns it.

prs.title: fix(gateway): keep recovered subagent follow-ups alive and repair restart suites
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Gateway restart-recovery live suites (widget and subagent) could not prove recovery at all, and running them exposed two product bugs.

The suites killed the Gateway through the process group, which fails under the process relay (the Gateway is not the group leader) and, once routed through custody, also killed detached descendants the recovery path depends on. Their fixtures also re-identified the same device for the widget observer and used a device-less backend client for the subagent parent, so the Gateway correctly revoked operator authority and the suites failed for fixture reasons.

With the fixtures fixed, two real bugs remained:

- Recovered subagent follow-ups were cancelled after restart because the retained operator authority was tied to the lifetime of the settled completion row; once that row was consumed, the child follow-up lost its authority even though the requester and operator were still valid.
- `openclaw dashboard` failures printed nothing actionable on stderr, so a failed handoff looked like a silent exit.

## User Impact

- Subagent runs recovered after a Gateway crash or restart now deliver their follow-up instead of being cancelled.
- `openclaw dashboard` handoff failures now explain what went wrong and what to do next.
- Restart-recovery live suites are runnable again as regression proof.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `instance.crashGateway()` in the test instance helper sends SIGKILL to the Gateway command process only, awaits its exit, and keeps custody, which mirrors a real crash without killing recovery-owned descendants.
- Restart suites keep a stable operator identity: the widget observer uses a separate device, and the subagent parent uses an identified TUI operator. New e2e suites cover operator authority across restart for direct operator runs and subagent authority.
- The subagent registry Gateway owner now separates completion-row lifetime from retained operator authority. Authority stays bounded by the Gateway lifecycle, requester validity, and operator access checks; only the dependency on the settled completion row is removed.
- The dashboard command writes the failure reason to stderr.

## Evidence

- Unit/e2e: new `openclaw-test-instance.crash`, `gateway-operator-restart.e2e`, `gateway-subagent-authority-restart.e2e`, and updated operator-run recovery/authority worker tests pass locally.
- Live widget restart suite passes end to end, including real browser interaction after the crash.
- Live subagent restart suite now passes the duplicate-send recovery check that previously failed. Its final step still depends on the parent model choosing a `sessions_history` call with tools included, which it did not do in the last run; that assertion is model tool-choice dependent and is tracked separately.
- Autoreview (Codex, P1 scope): scoped-clean, no accepted findings.

Fixes #72504.

The Feishu inbound parser previously removed the receiving bot's own mention from the agent-facing body. In multi-bot groups, that could leave each bot without its own addressing context even when event metadata had already activated it.

This preserves all normalized `<at>` markup for the agent and keeps group command handling separate: `CommandBody` uses the command-only normalized probe, so `@Bot /model` continues to dispatch as `/model`.

Credit: this repair carries forward analysis from @AxelHu in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/72532 and @Bojun-Vvibe in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/72661. Their closed PRs are not reopened.

prs.title: perf(test): share compiled Vitest workers across worktrees
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

**Round 2 stop-report: this revision is not accepted for landing.** The measured candidate is local commit `d51079bcf273d20651baa99d9509d340a8c767ab`; it has not been pushed. The PR still contains `66ff3c666b49cf1c740ccd2ea997155e184ee927`.

Worker preparation previously rebuilt identical artifacts for different slots and worktrees. The first shared-store proposal reduced incremental compiler writes but copied a full private tree for every borrower and deleted it at disposal. This revision restores slot-local rename reuse and keeps shared storage as a second level.

## Why This Change Was Made

L1 is an exclusively owned per-slot generation under `.artifacts/vitest-worker-local`. Borrow and joined disposal transfer its roots by rename. A warm L1 hit never copies or deletes the payload tree and does not publish a missing L2 snapshot. L2 is the shared content-addressed store, consulted only when L1 misses. Verification and publication use per-signature locks; publication stages then atomically renames. A competing publisher reuses the winner. Retention keeps eight shared generations and cleans abandoned stages under their generation locks.

The existing `@openclaw/fs-safe/copy` API seeds an empty L1 or publishes a snapshot using APFS directory cloning where available, with the existing independent-copy fallback elsewhere. No native code, dependencies, configuration, or environment variables were added. Outputs remain relocatable, manifest hashes are verified before lending, and ownership, signal/crash cleanup, and CI opt-in behavior remain enforced. This run does not establish native Linux/Windows performance.

On an incremental miss, the verified L1 tree is reused in place. The compiler still loads and compiles its closure, but writes only changed output bytes. Publishing a new L2 generation still creates a full logical snapshot.

The round-1 diagnosis was confirmed: warm borrowers cloned the entire tree and cleanup deleted it, while one store-wide lock covered verification/materialization. Both mechanisms are removed from the warm path. The old cold 3× regression was mostly in the load/build bucket (32.7s baseline versus 111.6s candidate in the earlier unpaired probe), not snapshot publication alone. That historical probe cannot establish a causal compiler slowdown on this noisy host; the fresh paired phases below are the current evidence.

## User Impact

Warm-slot and second-slot reuse improve substantially in this campaign, and the one-line edit still rewrites exactly one compiler output. However, this change misses the acceptance gate:

- Fresh-worktree observed median events increase from 1,498 to 3,540; edit events increase from 345 to 379.
- The fresh worktree compiles in all three attempts instead of sharing the existing generation. The primary install contains two unused `fs-safe@0.26.7` package directories absent from its fresh frozen-install peer; all roots resolve `fs-safe@0.26.8`. Directory names participate in the compiler namespace signature. This real existing-to-fresh install difference was preserved, not pruned to manufacture a hit.
- Production code grows instead of shrinking: against baseline, production **+522 / -225 = +297** lines; tests **+523 / -117 = +406**; docs/CI **+33 / -24 = +9**. Round 2 adds another **66 net production lines** over round 1's +231.

Per the work order's stop option and the latest instruction to push only an accepted candidate, implementation is stopped and the local revision is not pushed. No merge or auto-merge is requested.

## Evidence

Three interleaved A/B repetitions per case on the same Mac, Node 26.12.0, APFS. A is baseline `20b6c7ae4e0e35239e14bca54c156575e4670d91`; B is local candidate `d51079bcf273d20651baa99d9509d340a8c767ab`. Both have the same application-source base, with only this PR's changes in B. Separate frozen-install peer worktrees were used for the fresh-worktree case. No concurrent task checks or builds ran during measurement windows.

Each cell is **median [min–max]**. Prep is the actual prepare promise; full cycle includes import, reservation, preparation, verification, and joined disposal. The new/modified-file count is a before/after inode/mtime/size census across invocation, L1, and L2 directories. It counts logical file identities, including APFS clones, not physical block writes; it excludes ephemeral files gone before the final census. Baseline compiler-write counts are the full output inventory on misses; B reports actual compiler emissions. Zero means no compilation. The clone seeding/publishing cost remains visible in the file census and events.

The supplied `fsev3` sampler ran on three disjoint scopes, including the shared store, with fixed nominal 240-second windows. Event delivery is coalesced and noisy. One candidate fresh-worktree cycle lasted 240.84s; all sampler processes were still alive at action completion, but the end-of-window boundary makes that run's event coverage uncertain. Its observed count is sufficient to establish failure even if it undercounts. These are observed event counts, not claims of exact kernel event totals.

A host/provider outage interrupted cold-2-B after its action but before event results. Its incomplete attempt is preserved separately and excluded. Only that unfinished measurement was repeated, followed by the final pair; all completed data and the hash-verified protocol stayed unchanged. This pause limits how closely paired cold repetition two is in time.

| Case | Revision | Prep s | Full cycle s | New/modified file identities | Compiler writes | FSEvents |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| warm | A | 25.65 [19.39–41.38] | 39.96 [36.93–73.86] | 3 [3–3] | 0 [0–0] | 1 [0–9] |
| warm | B | 16.35 [7.72–61.76] | 25.45 [9.97–89.06] | 3 [3–3] | 0 [0–0] | 0 [0–6] |
| slot | A | 34.04 [21.96–154.01] | 36.76 [22.95–159.52] | 21656 [21656–21656] | 21654 [21654–21654] | 1028 [1022–1838] |
| slot | B | 9.42 [7.06–12.53] | 11.45 [9.05–16.01] | 21657 [21657–21657] | 0 [0–0] | 265 [113–1302] |
| root | A | 82.71 [80.18–114.71] | 90.49 [85.61–125.01] | 21656 [21656–21656] | 21654 [21654–21654] | 1498 [1276–2373] |
| root | B | 55.69 [41.83–224.28] | 64.78 [44.42–240.84] | 43314 [43314–43314] | 21685 [21685–21685] | 3540 [1131–3954] |
| edit | A | 25.66 [21.15–42.21] | 29.55 [23.31–46.46] | 21656 [21656–21656] | 21654 [21654–21654] | 345 [294–1074] |
| edit | B | 25.28 [24.60–26.49] | 27.77 [26.30–29.08] | 21661 [21661–21661] | 1 [1–1] | 379 [105–963] |
| cold | A | 24.69 [19.45–25.25] | 26.36 [20.32–26.58] | 21656 [21656–21656] | 21654 [21654–21654] | 1310 [776–1554] |
| cold | B | 27.30 [24.56–36.78] | 30.30 [26.28–39.39] | 43314 [43314–43314] | 21685 [21685–21685] | 992 [571–2860] |

`warm` = retained same-slot hit; `slot` = empty second slot; `root` = fresh installed peer with no L1; `edit` = one-line worker-source change; `cold` = no local generation or matching L2 snapshot.

All median full-cycle timing gates pass: warm -36.3%, second slot -68.8%, fresh worktree -28.4%, edit -6.0%, cold +14.9% (25% cold allowance). The fresh-worktree and edit event gates fail. Fresh-worktree reuse and the production-size requirement also fail.

### Cold phase breakdown

Independent phase medians [min–max], seconds; phase medians need not sum to the median full cycle. Cache lookup includes namespace/input preparation and any attempted generation verification, so it is not pure lock wait or hashing.

| Phase | Baseline A | Candidate B |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| cache lookup | 2.23 [1.92–2.45] | 4.30 [3.38–6.50] |
| load and compile | 19.96 [15.91–20.66] | 20.96 [17.49–26.94] |
| output verification | 1.59 [1.11–1.80] | 2.30 [2.14–2.64] |
| snapshot copy and publish | — | 0.53 [0.43–0.53] |
| joined disposal, total | 1.06 [0.82–1.84] | 2.56 [1.67–2.94] |

The incremental miss still has a full-compiler floor: load/compile median is 20.0s baseline versus 17.4s candidate, plus lookup, verification, and publication. Candidate snapshot publication is 0.53s median; its edit L2 events are 374 median while invocation events are 5 median. Reducing payload writes alone does not make total event cost proportional to the source edit. Individual scope medians are not additive to the median total.

### Validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/vitest-worker-cache.test.ts test/scripts/vitest-worker-cache-lifecycle.test.ts test/scripts/vitest-worker-output.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **33 passed** on the final source. Regression coverage includes L1 rename reuse without a payload copy, slot/cross-root sharing, changed-only writes, known-input overlays, bounded GC, concurrent publishers, corruption/verification, and unrelated-generation locking.
- The same three suites plus `test/scripts/vitest-worker-shutdown.test.ts` and `test/scripts/vitest-worker-slots.test.ts`: **63 passed**. The three cache suites were rerun after the final cache-only refactor; shutdown/slot source did not change.
- `pnpm tsgo:scripts`: **passed**. `pnpm tsgo:test:root`: **all four groups passed**.
- Targeted `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.scripts.json <touched scripts>` and root-test lint with `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.json`: **passed**. `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check <seven round-2 files>` and `git diff --check`: **passed**.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base 20b6c7ae4e0e35239e14bca54c156575e4670d91`: **completed, exit 1**. Exactly three failing categories reproduced on baseline: max-lines suppressions in three unrelated UI files; core test graph 723 roots versus 720; identical production/full-tree dead-export findings. Script dead-export scan had zero entries. The remaining selected checks, typechecks, extension/scripts/root-test lint, formatting, and guards passed. No baseline, timeout, retry, or assertion was weakened.
- Fresh independent Codex review of the complete candidate: **scoped-clean through P2** before commit. No production changes followed that review.

Detailed protocol, raw per-run JSON/logs/events, resumption record, and statistics are retained locally in `.artifacts/w1-round2/`. The final stop-report is `.artifacts/w1-proof/final-report.md`. Earlier round-1 results are preserved separately and are not relabeled as paired proof.

### Open risks and stopping point

This is not ready to land. A follow-up would need to narrow installed namespace identity safely, avoid full logical L2 snapshot churn on edits without weakening independent ownership/verification, and simplify the production implementation. Native fallback execution and high-concurrency burst throughput remain unmeasured here. No native/dependency escape hatch was used. No CI run is claimed for local `d51079b`, because the failed candidate was not pushed.

prs.title: feat(google): support params.serviceTier (Flex/Priority) for direct Gemini models
prs.body:
Closes #69102

## What Problem This Solves

Users running direct Google AI Studio (Gemini) models had no way to request the Flex service tier from OpenClaw. The Gemini API accepts a top-level `serviceTier` request field (`flex` / `priority` / `standard`), but OpenClaw never serialized it, so users who wanted Flex pricing/latency trade-offs had to route through OpenRouter workarounds instead of using their direct Google access.

## Why This Change Was Made

The per-model/global `params` config surface now accepts `serviceTier` (or `service_tier`) for Google models and the Google provider stream hook maps it onto the outbound payload's top-level `serviceTier` field. This reuses the existing `params` mechanism (same shape as `cachedContent`), so no new config keys are introduced.

The serialized values are the documented lower-case wire literals, verified against the API discovery document (`GenerateContentRequest.serviceTier` enumerates `unspecified` / `standard` / `flex` / `priority`).

Two deliberate boundaries, matching the direction flagged in the issue:

- Vertex (`google-vertex`) ignores a request-body service tier, so the mapping only applies to the direct `google-generative-ai` transport; sharing a tier contract with the Vertex alias path (#90243) is left as a separate maintainer decision.
- An explicit payload `serviceTier` (e.g. set by an `onPayload` hook) wins over the param.

## User Impact

Users can now select the Flex (or Priority) service tier for direct Gemini models:

```json5
{
  agents: {
    defaults: {
      models: {
        "google/gemini-2.5-flash": {
          params: { serviceTier: "flex" },
        },
      },
    },
  },
}
```

Values are case-insensitive on input and serialized to the documented lower-case wire values; invalid values are ignored. Documented in `docs/providers/google.md`.

**Upgrade note:** if an existing configuration already sets a generic `params.serviceTier`/`service_tier` value on a direct Google model, that value was previously inert and will become an active tier selection after upgrade. Review saved configs before upgrading if this is a concern.

## Evidence

**Live after-fix proof (real Gemini API, redacted):** OpenClaw's real transport + provider hook, `params.serviceTier: "flex"` on `gemini-2.5-flash`:

```
=== live request with params.serviceTier=flex ===
response text: "service tier ok"
stopReason: stop

=== raw API contract check (generateContent, serviceTier:"flex") ===
text: "service tier ok"
usageMetadata: {..., "serviceTier": "flex"}
```

Google accepted the tiered request and echoed `"serviceTier": "flex"` in `usageMetadata`.

**Wire-level proof (local HTTP server at the fetch boundary):**

```
=== params.serviceTier=flex (direct AI Studio) ===
request path: /v1beta/models/gemini-2.5-pro:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse
top-level serviceTier: "flex"
body keys: contents, serviceTier

=== no serviceTier param (regression) ===
top-level serviceTier: undefined
```

**Tests (31 passed):** `extensions/google/service-tier.test.ts` (normalization incl. `service_tier` alias, case-insensitivity, invalid values) and `extensions/google/provider-hooks.test.ts` (direct AI Studio gets `serviceTier`, Vertex does not, explicit payload value wins, invalid ignored). Adjacent suites (`transport-stream.test.ts`, `thinking.test.ts`, 143 tests) also pass.

prs.title: feat: support picking a specific on-device TTS voice for Talk Mode
prs.body: ## What Problem This Solves On-device Talk Mode text-to-speech on iOS and macOS always fell back to Apple's low-quality default voice, even when a user had downloaded and selected an Enhanced or Premium voice in Settings > Accessibility > Spoken Content. macOS had no on-device voice or speech settings UI at all. ## Why This Change Was Made On-device synthesis only ever resolved a voice via `AVSpeechSynthesisVoice(language:)`, which returns Apple's undocumented per-language default and ignores any specific voice the user picked. This adds a specific-voice picker (enumerated via `AVSpeechSynthesisVoice.speechVoices()`) to both platforms' Talk Mode settings, filtered by the current recognition language, with graceful fallback to the previous language-only behavior if a selected voice is later uninstalled. macOS gains a new "Speech" settings section for this. Investigated and intentionally did not attempt to support selecting Siri voices specifically: Apple does not expose Siri voice identity to any third-party app via `AVSpeechSynthesizer`/`AVSpeechUtterance` on any current iOS version (confirmed via WWDC20 session 10022 and Apple engineer forum responses) — even `prefersAssistiveTechnologySettings` silently substitutes a same-language non-Siri voice. This is a permanent Apple platform restriction, not a gap in this change. A macOS global keyboard shortcut to toggle Talk Mode was developed alongside this but is being split into its own follow-up PR to keep this PR to one topic, per repo policy. ## User Impact Users can now pick a specific downloaded Enhanced/Premium on-device voice for Talk Mode in Settings, on both iOS and macOS, instead of always hearing the default system voice. ## Evidence - Full `OpenClawKit` shared package suite: 1311 tests / 101 suites, all passing. - Focused iOS Swift Testing suites (`TalkSystemVoiceSelectionTests`, `TalkModeConfigParsingTests`, `TalkGatewaySpeechClientTests`, `TalkSpeechLocaleTests`) green via `xcodebuild test` on iOS Simulator; one pre-existing, unrelated locale-dependent test failure confirmed present on `main` before this change (`git log -p -S` verified) and unaffected by this diff. - macOS `SettingsViewSmokeTests` and `TalkModeRuntimeSpeechTests` green via `swift test`. - Manual on-device verification on a physical iPhone (iOS 26.6, Russian system locale) and the macOS app: downloaded Enhanced voices via system Accessibility settings, selected one in the new OpenClaw picker, triggered Talk Mode with no external TTS provider configured, and confirmed the selected voice (not the default) was used for playback on both platforms. ### Screenshots macOS — picker showing installed voices, "Yuri (Enhanced)" selected: iOS — same picker in a Russian-locale device, "Ruslan" selected: ### Fixes from review Two issues found during this review round, both fixed and covered by new regression tests: 1. **Directive-language override bug**: an explicitly-picked voice was applying even when a Talk directive requested a different language mid-conversation (e.g. a French reply could be spoken in a picked English voice). Fixed in `TalkSystemSpeechSynthesizer.resolveVoice` — an explicit voice now only applies when its primary language subtag matches the resolved synthesis language. 2. **Doubled quality suffix**: the macOS screenshot above was captured before this fix and shows the bug it caught — Apple's own `AVSpeechSynthesisVoice.name` already includes a localized quality suffix for many modern Enhanced/Premium voices (e.g. "Yuri (Enhanced)", Russian "Милена (улучшенный)"), so appending our own suffix doubled it. Fixed in `TalkSystemVoiceCatalog.label(for:)` to detect an already-decorated name and skip the extra suffix.

prs.title: refactor(macos): reuse native Gateway client in wizard
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The macOS wizard CLI maintains a second Gateway WebSocket client: connect-frame construction, challenge handling, device signing, response matching, and payload decoding duplicate the maintained native transport. Replace `GatewayWizardClient` with `GatewayChannelActor`, leaving wizard prompts and the `wizard.start`, `wizard.next`, and `wizard.cancel` flow in the CLI.

Challenge payload decoding now belongs to the existing challenge value's failable initializer, with the shared channel and its boundary tests migrated together. The separate parser namespace is removed; its validation is not.

## User Impact

The CLI still supplies explicit operator scopes and endpoint credentials. Stored device-token lookup and persistence remain disabled. Every wizard request is bound to the initially connected socket generation, so a reconnect cannot replay an answer into a different session. `timeoutMs: 0` keeps wizard-operation deadlines with the Gateway, and shutdown is awaited on success and failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the macOS wizard area split of the broader native-owner cleanup. The split-size floor is waived to keep attribution narrow: **134 net production lines removed** across three production files. The existing parser test file changes three call sites and uses the package's standard `@testable import` for the internal implementation value; no cases or expectations are deleted.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- The deleted client hard-codes a 0.75-second connect-challenge deadline; the maintained `GatewayChannelActor` owns a 6-second deadline. The wizard now accepts that shared policy instead of retaining a CLI-only timeout. A silent endpoint can therefore take longer to fail; this is an intentional runtime difference, not a byte-identical refactor.
- Transport encoding, response errors, connection lifecycle, and client metadata now follow the shared native owner rather than an independently maintained implementation. Wizard-specific server error messages remain translated for CLI output; exact incidental transport diagnostics are not promised to remain identical.

## Evidence

The original wizard cut has a completed independent source review with no actionable findings. prs.title: feat(plugins): expose outbound session key to channel adapters
prs.body:
Related: #117210

## What Problem This Solves

Plugin outbound adapters cannot correlate a send with the canonical agent session even though the delivery pipeline already carries that session context. Plugins currently have to reconstruct or omit that relationship.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds an optional `sessionKey` to `ChannelOutboundContext` and forwards `OutboundSessionContext.key` through the existing channel-handler boundary. The field is additive and omitted when no session is present, so existing adapters and callers keep their current behavior.

## User Impact

Plugin authors can make session-aware outbound decisions and correlate sends with the originating session without deriving identity from unrelated fields. Existing channel adapters remain source-compatible.

## Evidence

- Regression test: `forwards the canonical session key to plugin outbound adapters`
- Focused regression test passes under Node 25.9.0.
