prs.title: fix(codex): preserve whitespace in /codex bind --cwd paths
prs.body:
Closes openclaw/local-code-analysis#BUG-202

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a quoted workspace path with significant whitespace silently binds a Codex conversation to a different directory when passed via `/codex bind --cwd`.

- Problem: `normalizeOptionalString` in `parseBindArgs` and `requestedCwd?.trim()` in `resolveCodexSessionPermissionCwd` both strip whitespace from the `--cwd` argument, so `--cwd "/repo/job "` becomes `/repo/job`.
- Solution: replace both trim points with the existing `readNonBlankString` helper, which preserves significant whitespace while rejecting blank-only input.
- What changed: `extensions/codex/src/command-handler-args.ts` (parser), `extensions/codex/src/app-server/session-permission-policy.ts` (permission owner), `extensions/codex/src/commands.test.ts` (command-boundary regression via `it.each`).
- What did NOT change: blank-only input is still rejected, `isPathInside` containment is unchanged, default cwd resolution is unchanged.

## User Impact

Users who pass workspace paths containing significant whitespace via `/codex bind --cwd` will now have the exact requested directory bound. All other users are unaffected.

## Why This Change Was Made

Filesystem path bytes are significant on Unix; trimming them silently selects a neighboring directory. `readNonBlankString` is the existing SDK helper that already encodes the intended "reject blank, keep content" contract, so no new owner or configuration option is needed. Production delta is +4/-3; test delta is +22/0 across 3 files total.

- Best fix: yes, both trim points must preserve path identity and the existing SDK helper supplies that behavior.
- Risk / non-goals: Windows `CreateProcessW` trims trailing whitespace from `lpCurrentDirectory` at the OS level; that is an OS limitation outside this PR's scope.

## Evidence

Input: `--cwd "/tmp/.../work/job "` (trailing space). Single continuous capture (`proof-202-gateway-native.mts`) on head `cc956be3e35` (Linux, Codex 0.162.1): `/codex bind` → shipped Gateway dispatch → binding store → shipped permission resolver → real Codex `thread/start` → MARKER read.

### Before/after matrix

| Stage | Before (main) | After (head `cc956be3e35`) |
|---|---|---|
| `parseBindArgs` cwd | `/work/job` (trimmed) | `/work/job ` (preserved) |
| Gateway binding `workspaceDir` (shipped SQLite) | `/work/job` (trimmed) | `/work/job ` (`endsWithSpace=true`) |
| `resolveCodexSessionPermissionCwd` | `/work/job` (trimmed) | `/work/job ` (`endsWithSpace=true`) |
| native `thread/start` cwd | `/work/job` (wrong dir) | `/work/job ` (correct dir) |
| `MARKER.txt` read | `MARKER_NO_SPACE` (wrong) | `MARKER_TRAILING_SPACE` ✅ |

### Raw terminal output (inline, current head `cc956be3e35`)

```
[proof-202-gw-native] trailingSpaceDir="/tmp/.../work/job " (len=50)
[proof-202-gw-native] /codex bind dispatched (runId=idem-bind-53738137-189c-4b8f-9bd5-1983830aaa71)
[proof-202-gw-native] Part 1 bind reply: Bound this conversation to a new thread in /tmp/.../work/job.
[proof-202-gw-native] Part 1 binding read from sqlite on attempt 1
[proof-202-gw-native] Part 1 workspaceDir="/tmp/.../work/job " endsWithSpace=true
[proof-202-gw-native] Part 2: stored session permissionMode="read-only" (truthy → exercises changed line)
[proof-202-gw-native] Part 2: stored session sessionRoot="/tmp/.../work"
[proof-202-gw-native] Part 2: isPathInside(sessionRoot, requestedCwd)=true
[proof-202-gw-native] Part 2: resolveCodexSessionPermissionCwd resolvedCwd="/tmp/.../work/job " endsWithSpace=true
[proof-202-gw-native] Part 2: thread/start params cwd="/tmp/.../work/job " (len=50)
[proof-202-gw-native] Part 2: initialize OK, userAgent=codex_vscode/0.162.1 (Linux Unknown; x86_64) dumb (bug202-gw-native; 1.0.0)
[proof-202-gw-native] Part 2: thread/start ACCEPTED, threadId=01a151da-9983-7c92-9766-0b7b5fa2aa59
[proof-202-gw-native] Part 2: native response cwd="/tmp/.../work/job " (len=50, endsWithSpace=true)
[proof-202-gw-native] Part 2: native response sandbox={"type":"readOnly","networkAccess":false}, approvalPolicy="on-request"
[proof-202-gw-native] Part 2: MARKER.txt from resolved cwd: MARKER_TRAILING_SPACE
[proof-202-gw-native] Part 2: MARKER confirms correct directory (trailing-space dir) ✅
========== PROOF COMPLETE ==========
```

Key facts established inline (current head, no external retrieval): fix point #1 `workspaceDir=".../work/job " endsWithSpace=true` read from shipped SQLite; fix point #2 `permissionMode="read-only"` (truthy → exercises changed line), `isPathInside=true`, `resolvedCwd=".../work/job "`, real Codex 0.162.1 `thread/start ACCEPTED threadId=01a151da-...`, native `cwd=".../work/job " (len=50)`, `MARKER_TRAILING_SPACE ✅`.

### Pre-fix / post-fix bidirectional verification

**Fix point #1** (`commands.test.ts` `it.each`, 3 cases: trailing/leading/both-sides whitespace) via `runCommand("bind --cwd ...")` → `dispatchCodexCommand`. With both fixes reverted to origin/main, all 3 cases **fail** (`expected '/tmp/job ' to be '/tmp/job'`). With fix on head, all 3 **pass** (6175ms / 5460ms / 5549ms).

**Fix point #2** (`proof-202-part2-permission.mts`, `PROOF_MODE=pre-fix|post-fix`): pre-fix (reverted to `.trim()`): `resolvedCwd=".../work/job"` (`endsWithSpace=false` — STRIPPED). Post-fix (`readNonBlankString`): `resolvedCwd=".../work/job "` (`endsWithSpace=true`) → `thread/start ACCEPTED` → `MARKER_TRAILING_SPACE ✅`.

### Linked artifact (full unedited capture, supplementary)

https://gist.github.com/SunnyShu0925/9fc8b2661c757eb88a579310f815f41b — the inline log above is a verbatim subset; the gist is supplementary, not required for verification.

oxfmt clean, oxlint clean, tsgo extensions shard passes. Runtime (Linux, head `cc956be3e35`): `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs proof-202-gateway-native.mts`; `PROOF_MODE=pre-fix|post-fix node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs proof-202-part2-permission.mts`.

prs.title: feat(imessage): add bounded native history reads
prs.body:
Closes #117109

## What Problem This Solves

The shared `message` tool cannot explicitly read a small recent-history window from a known native iMessage DM.

## User Impact

An owner or `operator.admin` can request one existing DM with `message(action="read", channel="imessage", target="chat_id:42", limit=10)`. Reads are text-only, use an enabled configured account, and work with inbound DM/group intake disabled. They do not send, mark messages read, launch the private bridge, or change configuration.

**Native dependency:** this draft requires `chats.get` from https://github.com/openclaw/imsg/pull/338. Released imsg builds without that method are not supported for this new action. There is no shell fallback; update the native binary on the Messages Mac after the companion is released and refresh channel status. No native release or installation is included here.

## Why This Change Was Made

The implementation now stays at the iMessage plugin boundary: the existing authority-fenced RPC client reads exact-chat metadata and then `messages.history` over one connection. Native imsg owns chat classification; the plugin owns requester/account checks and bounded text output.

- Removed the previous generic process, broker, effect-authority, and SDK expansion entirely. The aggregate OpenClaw diff touches only the iMessage plugin and two documentation pages.
- Defaults to 10 messages, permits 1–50, caps each body at 4 KiB UTF-8 and the complete serialized result at 32 KiB, and explicitly reports truncation and incomplete-window coverage.
- No chat enumeration, name/handle lookup, groups, search, pagination, or attachments. Delegated native reads remain bound to their current DM/account.

This updates the original contribution and preserves @futuredescriber’s author credit.

## Evidence

- 102 focused tests across reader/shared-message boundary, action discovery, and RPC-client suites passed (`--maxWorkers=1`; 37.49 s wall including cold worker preparation). Native-context adapter restrictions are tested separately from the admitted operator harness.
- Real shared message tool + registered iMessage adapter + the uninstalled companion native binary passed six checks against synthetic SQLite: exact old DM beyond 1,000 newer chats, bounded newest-message output, group/unknown-chat refusal, spoofed authority refusal, and revoked-turn refusal. The 1,103-chat/1,168-message database remained byte-identical; no operator Gateway was contacted. Largest result: 32,736 / 32,768 bytes.
- `pnpm build` passed (297.19 s). The existing Control UI bundle budget report still prints a startup-JS size advisory; no UI source or budget was changed.
- The complete base-relative changed-scope gate passed: extension production/test types, changed-file lint/format, architecture/import/dependency guards, and applicable ratchets (346.10 s). Both changed documentation pages passed the MDX check. Complete-candidate independent review found no actionable P0–P2 issues.

No full-repository test run, live personal/Remote Mac conversation proof, or exact-head hosted-CI success is claimed. CI seconds for the new tests were not measured. This PR remains draft and is not merged.

---
[View the OpenClaw team session](https://openclaw.tail6ab937.ts.net/chat/clawforce/dashboard/92faec0d-8782-49d2-a06b-49491d942c05)

prs.title: refactor(ui): publish MCP inputs through their owner
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

MCP App input changes cross four renderer effects before reaching the existing iframe/protocol owner. This change publishes native property changes and gateway events directly into that owner, coalescing each burst into one complete settled binding.

## User Impact

MCP Apps retain their iframe, retry, reconnection, graceful retirement, RPC cancellation, and negotiated frame height. Host tags, classes, markup, styles, and lazy boundaries are unchanged; no migration is required.

## Implementation

The existing owner consumes the complete client/session/view/agent/generation/scope/access binding, cancels connection-bound requests synchronously, and owns subscription cleanup. Unchanged queued publications cannot reopen a retired host; a changed binding or explicit restart can. Title, locale, and surface updates preserve negotiated height. Mounted-host registration and synchronous cleanup from #176489 remain intact. A companion type module keeps the owner within its line cap without moving runtime decisions.

Full CI exposed two browser-fixture races. The collapsed-sidebar test now pauses virtual time, advances the gateway's two-second offline grace, preserves the four-second expiry assertion, and resumes for pointer/focus/resize checks. The selection helper now settles scrolling and brings the source into view before creating a selection: the toolbar deliberately dismisses on scroll. Both fixes preserve every original assertion, and the shared selection helper replaces duplicate setup in the scrolling case.

## Evidence

Base: `35aa52a55da8c407d9156a4c5aabc474ec6f13ef`. Head: `177460dbe3c61e39ed77e73b2961e2ad8f1ab225`. All three commits are patch-identical after the coordinator-requested rebase. `ci:full` runs every UI unit, E2E, browser-extension, and real-Gateway shard.

prs.title: fix(backup): reclaim abandoned staging without touching live owners
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A hard-killed backup can leave a multi-gigabyte `.openclaw-backup-publish-*` directory beside the requested archive. The config/database scratch half of the original PR was superseded by #154199, so this revision is narrowly scoped to publication staging.

## Implementation

- Reuses the current SQLite lifetime-token and fs-safe scratch owner for publication staging.
- Recovers abandoned publication staging before the next backup in the same output directory.
- Preserves live owners, completed archives, symlinks, legacy/unowned directories, unexpected payloads, and no-clobber publication.
- Keeps directory and archive identity receipts bigint-safe.
- Allows private unregistered staging only when the destination cannot support SQLite locking; backup still succeeds, but automatic recovery is explicitly disabled and reported.
- **Fails explicitly when Windows cannot establish stable file identity**, rather than completing successfully while potentially retaining a full staged archive.
- Carries publication maintenance, fallback, and retirement/cleanup warnings into the structured backup result and `--json` output.

## Evidence

Rebuilt as one commit on current `main`.

Current exact-head focused checks:

- publication recovery and ownership: **11/11 passed**
  - real subprocess kill and abandoned-staging reclamation
  - live-owner preservation
  - unexpected payload/symlink preservation
  - bigint identity collision defense
  - Windows unknown identity fails explicitly
  - SQLite-unavailable destination fallback remains supported
  - publication cleanup failure is recorded for result propagation
- targeted `oxfmt`, `oxlint`, and `git diff --check`: passed

Prior exact-head checks for the unchanged surrounding implementation:

- backup creation/publication integration: **6/6 passed**
- scratch ownership: **20/20 passed**
- eager import closure: **16/16 passed**

The structured-result E2E regression is committed. On this 3.7 GiB VPS its current-base compiled subprocess import exited 137 before the test executed; GitHub Actions is the authoritative integration run for that file and native Windows behavior.

## Safety Decisions

- Ordinary ownership/admission failures remain fail-closed.
- Unknown Windows identity no longer downgrades to unrecoverable staging.
- SQLite-incompatible destinations retain the availability fallback because stable file identities still permit safe post-publication cleanup.
- Cleanup warnings are deduplicated before entering structured output.

Fixes #95582.

prs.title: fix: prevent wiki ingest failures during concurrent Gateway imports
prs.body:
Closes #176635

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes `wiki ingest` failing after it has already saved its source when a Gateway bridge import updates the same vault during compilation.

## User Impact

CLI ingest and Gateway bridge imports wait for each other to finish, so both source changes become available in the compiled wiki. Cross-process lock acquisition times out after five minutes if the vault remains busy.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing vault coordinator serialized work only within one process. It now holds the SDK file lock for the same source-write-and-compile transaction across processes, while retaining nested-call support and parallel work on different vaults. Lock recovery requires a definitely stale owner, so a long-running live compiler keeps its lock.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on base `28212a985c15ae53b22b77dabecbfdfc1ee9d632` with a real isolated Gateway, `wiki ingest`, and `gateway call wiki.bridge.import` on a synthetic 1,500-page vault. Controlled SIGSTOP/SIGCONT scheduling of the owned CLI forced the overlap: ingest exited 1 with `Memory Wiki vault changed while its compiled cache was being built.`, despite persisting its source; the bridge import exited 0.
- Replayed the same overlap on this branch: the bridge waited for the CLI transaction, both commands exited 0, and public `wiki.search` results contained both the ingested content and the updated bridge content. `wiki.overview` reported 1,502 source pages. Verification reads did not trigger another compilation.
- The committed regression holds a real vault transaction in a separate process, then calls the ingest boundary. It fails on the base because the source is written before the other process releases its transaction, and passes with the fix.
- Passed 54 tests across ingest, compile, source synchronization, apply, mutation coordination, and ChatGPT import/rollback, plus the runtime build, targeted type-aware lint, TypeScript checks, formatting, Markdown lint, and `git diff --check`.
- Runtime validation used Linux and Node 24.19.0. Bun and other operating systems were not run locally.

prs.title: fix(sessions): keep conversations usable after delegated recovery fails
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a Gateway restart permanently blocking a conversation when its interrupted turn came from another session and the sender's authority cannot be restored.

## User Impact

When no reply, harness completion, or independent run remains owed, recovery ends only the old input. The session keeps its identity, transcript and working context and accepts a fresh authenticated message. Recovery never replays the delegated request or claims that its result was delivered. There is no schema or configuration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the guarded, atomic interruption settlement introduced for unrestorable requester inputs in #174177. Record one local notice and terminal source/run identities, including a source-only claim whose operational delivery ID has already been cleared. Later startup must not turn that settled interruption back into recoverable work.

Pending final delivery, owed harness completion and independent unretired run fences retain their existing owners and blocking behavior. Exhausted attempts and message-tool-only authority failures retain their explicit recovery path. Existing tombstones are not automatically cleared. This deliberately narrows whole-session tombstoning only for an interrupted input without remaining custody; maintainer security review is requested for that policy change.

Related: #161719. Builds on merged #173579's explicit in-place Resume; it does not duplicate that API or restore old sender authority. #173747 explicitly leaves this delegated-authority gap unresolved. The separate archived-Main reset remedy is #176086.

The unchanged pending-final action classifier moves to its existing delivery module so the coordinator stays within its strict file limit; no lint rule is suppressed.

## Behavior decision

The [review asks whether an unrestorable delegated input may retire without disabling its conversation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176087#issuecomment-6246188762). I recommend conditional retirement once no other work or delivery obligation remains. Losing authority for the interrupted request should keep that request inert; it need not prevent an independently authenticated future request.

[#150702](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/150702) deliberately prohibits delegated dispatch after sender authority is lost. This patch preserves that prohibition: no replay, synthesized sender authority, or System-authorized followup. [#174177](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174177) supplies the precedent for retiring an unrestorable input while preserving its conversation.

The [custody checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b66816d9c9199c8f12cd73949a36e8f7c6642740/src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-restart-recovery-failure.ts#L130) keep existing blocking when a final, harness completion, or independent unretired execution remains. Otherwise the [existing guarded transaction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b66816d9c9199c8f12cd73949a36e8f7c6642740/src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-restart-recovery-failure.ts#L85) records one local interruption and terminal identities. New work still requires fresh authentication. The remaining owner choice is requiring manual session recovery even after conclusive non-executing settlement. Earlier settlement precedent supports this extension; it does not already approve the delegated-input case.

### Current upstream conflict repair

Refreshed head `cabf35a82b6be78d46adcb442629a206dfa5b029` merges the prior PR head with pinned upstream `00575becc9fce53efc73b319a16fa71e6f4123b9`, preserving both parent histories. Conflict resolution uses upstream's extracted completion-checkpoint owner and the PR's shared pending-delivery classifier. It removes duplicate retired helpers and migrates fresh authenticated follow-up coverage to current controller admission. A small test-target helper extraction keeps the merged shutdown suite within its existing line limit, preserving store incarnation and configured agent identity.

Fresh checks pass: all four selected startup/delivery/native/shutdown suites (222 tests across three canonical shards; 222.92 seconds), production core types, owner Gateway-server and agents-sessions test types, scoped typed lint, formatting, and whitespace. After the fixture extraction, the complete shutdown suite passed again (27 tests; 11.20 seconds wrapper wall), with owner test types and scoped lint. Independent P0–P2 review found no actionable issue in the full PR diff, including the helper extraction; a subsequent local expression hoist is behavior-preserving. Unprovided unchanged upstream dependencies and actual runtime execution were outside independent review coverage.

New-head CI is pending. Prior Gateway/native recovery captures retain their original source qualifications and are not new runtime captures on this merged head. Pending final delivery, harness completion, and independent recovery obligations remain guards against early settlement. No delegated authority is recreated; the behavior decision above remains for maintainer review.


## Evidence

Synthetic production-owner regression: actual shutdown marking → recovery's SQLite notice/settlement → next startup → visible-turn admission in the same canonical Main session. Before the fix, the delegated case produces a session-wide tombstone. Afterward, no delegated dispatch occurs, one notice remains, source/run IDs are terminal without delivery evidence, the next startup does not replay it, and a fresh visible turn is admitted without reset or identity rotation. A source-only variant separately reproduced next-startup resurrection before its terminal identity was preserved.

### Current revision and regression checks

Current head `b66816d9c9199c8f12cd73949a36e8f7c6642740` records a cycle-derived terminal bookkeeping identity when neither saved run ID exists. Second-startup marking no longer rediscovers that settled input. Existing source/operational IDs retain their semantics; the fallback receipt grants no execution authority and requires no schema change.

The two failing native controls now assert interrupted settlement and terminal receipts while retaining no-`startTurn` and zero-automation-effect checks. **191 recovery/native cases pass** (179 recovery-owner and 12 native controls). The no-ID second-startup regression failed before this repair. Core production types, focused changed-test types, scoped typed lint, formatting, diff checks, and fresh complete-candidate independent P0–P2 review pass. The canonical runtime build passes on this exact commit. Current-head broad CI remains separate.

### Captured real Gateway and latest-stable upgrade evidence

Runtime proof on candidate `b66816d9`: official latest-stable `2026.10.4` CLI wrote synthetic history, followed by the unchanged stable shutdown marker on an offline delegated claim lacking surviving authority and saved run IDs. Candidate Doctor/startup preserved the exact history and physical session, settled it as interrupted without a tombstone, and did not replay the old input. A fresh authenticated turn then traversed the real Gateway, OpenAI SDK loopback transport, and actual filesystem read tool to a correlated final reply (two HTTP requests).

Captured real `agent.wait` after an authenticated reset at the prepared-effect boundary returned `status: error`, `Error: Chat admission ended or was cancelled; submit a new turn.` No additional provider/tool I/O occurred. The test-only pause retained the unchanged production guard. Actual Gateway logs capture the read-only rejection (`FORBIDDEN`, `missing scope: operator.write`) and invalid-token handshake rejection (`failurePhase: auth`, `failureCause: unauthorized`, `reason: token_mismatch`) before I/O. Provider responses were scripted; this is not an external-provider or live-outage claim. Gateway/provider cleanup completed.

The captured terminal result and selected saved RPC/log observations are below. Identifiers/messages belong only to disposable synthetic fixtures; no operator Gateway, private conversations, credentials, or external model provider were used. Comparison booleans are harness assertions against the full saved objects; error strings are copied from the actual Gateway/agent responses. The latest-stable fixture qualification is explicit rather than claiming an actual provider turn was killed in the first process.

prs.title: perf(postgres): avoid writer locks for pure read snapshots
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Pure read callbacks using the deferred SQLite transaction helper take the store-wide PostgreSQL writer mutex. This serializes descriptive reads against writers and adds an advisory-lock statement per call.

## User Impact

Read results and authority checks stay the same. The audited multi-statement reads keep one consistent snapshot while PostgreSQL writers can proceed independently. No schema, stored format, configuration, or permission change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing `runSqliteReadSnapshotSync` owner for 84 pure multi-statement read sites. PostgreSQL uses REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY and its existing snapshot facts scope; SQLite retains a deferred snapshot. Nested reads join their outer read or write transaction, including uncommitted state and outer rollback. Receipt/revision guards remain intact.

No class (a) or (c) sites qualified: all converted callbacks can issue multiple related reads, including conditional alias, metadata, or schema reads. Potential writers retain their writer transactions. `adapters.ts` already selects the correct PG read helper and remains fenced.

## Evidence

- Real PostgreSQL 17 with CI extensions (`unaccent`, `pg_trgm`, `vector`); internal-disk HOME/TMPDIR, UTF-8 server locale.
- Regression: the original background kernel fails with `55P03` while another connection holds the store advisory lock. The fixed arm passes (6.25s test time), including nested read-only visibility, uncommitted outer-write visibility, and outer rollback. The original red test took 12.27s. Touched-family conformance: all 50 tests in 6 files pass (state, agent, meeting transcripts, admitted read facts, and transaction protocol).
- Isolated `pg_stat_statements`: background snapshot 5 → 4 statements; avatar inspection 5 → 4. Same two SELECTs; legacy `READ COMMITTED + advisory lock + COMMIT` becomes `REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY + ROLLBACK`. The legacy envelope is applied to the same kernel for comparison. These are per-call measurements; aggregate workload frequency is unmeasured.
- Core and scripts typechecks, source-backed type-aware lint, formatting, and diff checks pass.
- Codex autoreview: three passes for the product changes and one fresh pass for the classifier repair, zero P0–P2 findings, `scoped-clean`. Review covers supplied sources; the separate inventory records the transitive audit.
- SQLite owner suites: all 61 selected files exercised; 872 tests passed, 3 failed, and 1 was skipped. The first 37 files produced 609 passes and the three failures; the remaining 24 files passed all 263 tests. The failures were the full Doctor ownership test exceeding 120 seconds, transcript retry-budget observation reading `expandedSQL` after statement finalization, and one nonresident foreign-avatar case exceeding its existing 5-second read budget. A focused replay passed both foreign-avatar variants (3.48s and 3.82s), but reproduced the Doctor 120-second timeout and finalized-statement failure. No assertions or timeouts were weakened; those initial failures are retained as historical results and classified by the base/head A/B below. The one suite skip is the existing Unicode-normalizing-filesystem case in `workspace-alias-rebind.test.ts`.
- All three PostgreSQL conformance shards and the baseline-ratchet job passed on final head `3327274d3cc273ec816a573f18cdd89d85f8168b` ([run 39180672556](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39180672556)). Overall CI is red in six test jobs; all 25 failing cases are classified below against scheduled main, including the five cases now passing after upstream fixes.
- CI exposed a worker-inventory classification gap: it recognized synchronous deferred callbacks but not the existing read-snapshot helper. The classifier now recognizes that exact helper too, without changing any threshold. New regression fails without the mapping; both classifier suites pass (101 tests). The worker ratchet keeps T1 counts unchanged; scripts typecheck, lint, and formatting pass.
- Production readers: +146/−152 (net −6); classifier: +7/−1 (net +6); tests: +133; total net +133 (+286/−153).

Local SQLite proof used Node 24.22 with internal-disk HOME/TMPDIR. A filesystem-cache continuation stalled in native `rename` before producing any test verdict; its task-owned processes were stopped, and the 24-file continuation passed with the supported `--configLoader=runner --fsModuleCache=false` path. Assertions, authority guards, and timeouts were unchanged.

## Coordinator follow-up: completed base/head A/B

The requested comparison is pinned to original merge base `1cc1efe021d83b670b545308d5cc65f7ab409292` and unchanged PR head `3327274d3cc273ec816a573f18cdd89d85f8168b`. Both exact files ran **three times on each revision under the original failure runtime, Node 24.22.0**. The test files, package manifest, frozen lockfile, and Bun pin match byte-for-byte. Each invocation used isolated internal-disk HOME/TMPDIR and the same repository wrapper/flags; no assertion, timeout, or source change was applied.

```text
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/test-projects.mts src/transcripts/store.test.ts src/state/openclaw-state-ownership.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --configLoader=runner --fsModuleCache=false --reporter=verbose
```

| Exact case | Base, runs 1 / 2 / 3 | Head, runs 1 / 2 / 3 | Classification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `TranscriptsStore > bounds exact retry lookups to one caption ID without adding statements` | FAIL / FAIL / FAIL: `statement has been finalized`, observer at `store.test.ts:465` | Same FAIL / FAIL / FAIL and stack | **Inherited**; base-confirmed on all three runs. |
| `external shared-state ownership > refuses unauthorized Doctor admission before staging a public snapshot` | PASS 74.110s / PASS 81.111s / 120s timeout (121.954s reported) | PASS 68.020s / PASS 96.972s / 120s timeout (121.449s reported) | **Inherited timing failure**; the same case times out once on each revision. |

Full-file totals: base runs 1/2 each 55 pass + 1 fail, run 3 has 39 pass + 17 fail; head runs 1/2 each 55 pass + 1 fail, run 3 has 40 pass + 16 fail. After the Doctor timeout, unchanged afterEach guards report plugin-capture custody files (`plugin-captures/.../owner.sqlite` and its journal) still open; these cause 15 additional baseline and 14 additional head cleanup failures. They are retained in the evidence, rather than counted as passing cases. The exact unfinished Doctor stage remains unlocalized, but the timeout and cleanup failure pattern are now base-confirmed. No timeout was extended.

The transcript observer retains native statement receivers and accesses `expandedSQL` after `appendMeetingTranscriptUtterance` returns. Existing Kysely one-shot disposal finalizes those statements; the failing write path and observer are unchanged by this PR. A fresh audit traced **all 84 converted sites in 62 production files**, including `iterateSqliteQuerySync`, prepared factories, generators, cursors, retained closures, archive staging, and paged lifecycle planning. No live SQL iterator/statement/cursor escapes a converted snapshot. Nontrivial generators are materialized or closed inside their scope, or yield only eager page results. Standalone SQLite read snapshots call the old deferred helper directly; nested reads omit savepoints without introducing statement disposal. The changed ownership inspection also opens a fresh read-only handle, so its changed call cannot take the nested branch.

Separately, **three default pinned-Bun full-file runs passed all 56 tests each (168 passes)**. Doctor times were 119.733s, 97.304s, and 67.115s; the transcript case passed in each. Bun pin: `1.4.4-canary.1+7bd4fdff3`. This is additional normal-runtime proof; it does not replace or erase the original Node failures. The original-runtime A/B above occurred before any fix push; **no fix was needed or pushed**.

The first baseline setup attempt stopped before any test verdict because a shared root dependency link omitted workspace-local dependencies. An independent `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --offline` completed successfully, and all three counted baseline runs used that installation. Setup attempts are excluded from the A/B counts.

**No follow-up source changes, reverted conversions, new fix commit, or rebase.** A diagnostic observation patch was prepared but never applied after the baseline timeout reproduced. The initial foreign-avatar budget failure remains recorded; its focused replay passed without source changes. All six CI jobs are fully classified below, including current-main case output and named upstream repairs. Stop remains READY for coordinator review, with no merge.

prs.title: refactor: remove redundant private freezes and checks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Private admission payloads, requester tuples and channel lookup tables pay for runtime freezing despite staying inside their owner and having no mutation path.

## User Impact

No intended behavior change. Public admission/requester snapshots remain frozen, caller-owned input remains copied, and credential admission, voice-session ownership and final-effect checks remain intact.

## Design

Remove private freezes. Model Setup reuses its parsed provider choice and dispatches saved authentication before the generic role check it already bypasses. Keep readonly types and narrow projections. The Talk projection still copies six primitive fields from the parsed record; its sole production consumer reads it synchronously.

Production: +47/-54, net -7 lines across eight files. The assertion-safety baseline also drops the retired one-assertion allowance for `src/channels/ids.ts`. No test additions or deletions. The simplification pass retained owner-held values and existing parsers, without new helpers, public exports or compatibility paths.

No SQL, requests, transactions, schema, SDK surface or service lifecycle changes. SQL/request/MAIN impact for this diff is estimated 0/0/0, unmeasured. The lane comparison for the first two cleanup commits measured identical warm medians: 54 [54–57] SQL, 16 [16–17] requests, 0 [0–0] MAIN, with no normalized statement-shape change. That pair does not include this diff. Its candidate completed all turns but failed final restart teardown with Darwin process-inspection unavailable in spawn-broker cleanup; no full-workload or latency claim.

## Evidence

Changed-file formatting, type-aware lint and `git diff --check` pass. Independent Codex source review and the second/final baseline-correction review both completed scoped-clean with final source verification. Frozen install passed.

All owner shards passed on reviewed production head `9418d918c1c` in [ordinary CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39191581963). Final head `1bba74d6892` changes only the obsolete assertion allowance; all eight production blobs are identical. [Final CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39192629539) confirms the corrected assertion-safety, database-worker and dialect ratchets pass. Production/core types, lint and source-contract checks passed; the unrelated failures are recorded below. Knip evidence is reused because the correction changes none of its inputs.

The final skill-library worker test failed at `bob-worker-first` with an unavailable selected skill revision. The same test already fails on [scheduled main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39186683798/job/117850680977), but at the earlier advertised-skill-count assertion. This different-step symptom remains an unresolved CI signal, not an identical-failure or fixed-test claim. No blind rerun was requested.

Inherited diagnostics: the unchanged Codex `completionDeliveryRetryDelaysMs` TS2353 matches [main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39190189076/job/117861351867). The missing Swedish translation catalog matches [main i18n](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39190227860/job/117861487352). Chat boot gzip exceeds its existing budget on [main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39190227860/job/117861486872); this candidate's own comparison reports 1,491,439 → 1,491,439 bytes, zero growth. The generated credentials-matrix mismatch also matches [main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39190227860/job/117861488396): the same `plugins.entries.subq.config.apiKey` entry is absent. No budget was raised and no test assertion was weakened.

Knip on the unchanged production head adds zero findings versus [current main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39192299097/job/117867682382): `settleInterruptedRestartRecovery` and the two unused files are inherited. The supplemental run was cancelled after its required evidence completed. No new main-baseline or supplemental run was dispatched for the one-line baseline correction.

The final aggregate ratchet failure is independently reproduced on fetched main `8e2ea72d83acceb73a9b5876dc31cd29807fc37a`: `test/scripts/ci-node-test-plan.test.ts:3285` lacks real-export pass-through in its `ci-test-timings` mock. The unchanged native checker ran through the proof semaphore against an isolated index of that exact main, exiting 1 with the identical rule/file/line. The actual PR correction passes assertion-safety. All inherited failures and the distinct worker signal were routed to the main-repair queue. Landing uses the authorized relaxed policy; aggregate CI is not claimed green.

## Candidate Ledger

| Candidate | Decision | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| C12808 | KEEP | The copied profile is returned by getRequesterProfile; retain the snapshot copy and freeze at that public read boundary. |
| C12809 | REMOVE | requesterBinding creates a fresh tuple of primitive context fields held only in #binding and read with every; it never escapes. |
| C12810 | KEEP | The symbol-carried RequesterProfile object escapes with the context; preserve its frozen opaque carrier surface. |
| C12906 | REMOVE | The derived entries array is module-private and only read by set/order/alias construction and label lookup. |
| C12907 | KEEP | CHAT_CHANNEL_ORDER is exported and shared with CHANNEL_IDS and the channel registry; retain its public array freeze. |
| C12908 | REMOVE | The alias map is module-private and only indexed by normalization/label lookup; no writer or escape exists. |
| C12927 | REMOVE | The parser still validates and copies primitive fields; its only production caller stores the fresh result in private ingress binding. |
| C12928 | KEEP | AdmissionEvidence escapes as an opaque public carrier; retain its frozen outer surface and private-field brand. |
| C12929 | KEEP | PreparedChannelAdmissionEvidence crosses the exported prepare/bind handoff; retain its frozen outer carrier. |
| C12930 | REMOVE | Both writeContextAdmission callers construct fresh records; #value is only read inside this module and never returned publicly. |
| C12931 | KEEP | ContextAdmission is attached to the external context under a symbol; retain the frozen opaque carrier surface. |
| C12932 | REMOVE | The new timestamped payload is private to AdmissionEvidence; public readers return evidence/resolver or a fresh consumed projection. |
| C12933 | REMOVE | The unsupported contribution is a fresh private payload and is only read when deriving the consumed projection. |
| C12934 | REMOVE | The no-audit unsupported payload is freshly spread into the private evidence slot and has no external reference. |
| C12935 | REMOVE | participantContribution constructs a fresh private wrapper read only by the local payload pipeline. |
| C12936 | REMOVE | The present participant record is newly constructed from primitive fields and never escapes the evidence owner. |
| C12937 | REMOVE | The unknown participant record is a new private constant-shaped value with no writer or external reference. |
| C12938 | REMOVE | The fresh ingress binding is held in #binding; only the separately mutable handoff subrecord is written, as before. |
| C12939 | REMOVE | The scope and conversation snapshot stay private; retain the conversation spread to detach caller-owned data while removing both freezes. |
| C12940 | REMOVE | The unknown contribution is freshly constructed inside the private mint path and is only read. |
| C12941 | REMOVE | The contribution wrapper is freshly spread during the private handoff-to-evidence map and has no external reference. |
| C12942 | REMOVE | The decision record contains locally computed primitive facts and remains inside the private evidence payload. |
| C12943 | REMOVE | Retain [...evidence] to snapshot the caller-owned array; its private copied array has no mutation site and needs no freeze. |
| C12944 | KEEP | consumeChannelAdmissionEvidence returns this public projection; its frozen result is an explicit existing test contract. |
| C12945 | KEEP | The nested invoker is publicly exposed by the consumed projection; retain its frozen result contract. |
| C33299 | DEFER | Keep the credential clone: the supported precommit review path refuses necessary credential-owner source context. No credential-copy change is included. |
| C33412 | REMOVE | Six fresh primitive facts are consumed synchronously; retain the readonly projection, stored-data parsing and ownership/open-state checks. |

Keep caller-input copies, public carrier/result freezes, one-use/scope/live-owner checks, and all untrusted-input parsing. There is no support added for callers mutating private implementation values.

| ID | Category | Source | REMOVE reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C33287 | b | `src/system-agent/setup-inference-activate.ts` | Handle saved-auth first (it already unconditionally bypasses generic role validation), then parse the provider-auto choice once and reuse it for role selection and dispatch. Also removes one unindexed saved-auth prefix check. |

Saved-auth retains its existing generic-role-validation bypass and delegates role and credential ownership to the same staging owner. Malformed saved-auth choices keep their current error.


| ID | Decision | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| C29821 | REMOVE | Drop only the returned guard's entry assertion; synchronous owner policy reads have no intervening authority mutation. Factory-entry and final execution assertions remain. |
| C29726 | REMOVE | The staging environment is privately copied, only read by executable resolution, and merged into fresh spawn environments. Keep its copy and both public pinned-environment freezes. |

prs.title: refactor(ui): observe widget placement through shared lifecycle
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Widget action placement rebuilt its ResizeObserver on every options update. The view now uses the shared observer for target and visibility lifetime, retaining its subscription across content refreshes. Resize deliveries schedule the existing batched clipping measurement; hidden retained widgets disconnect, hidden queued measurements do not write, and disposal cancels pending layout work. The iframe stays mounted through hide/show.

The Chromium regression fixture also needed a correction. It resized the observed thread ancestor inside a descendant ResizeObserver callback, then redrew. The old options-dependent effect disconnected its observer during that redraw, incidentally dropping the ancestor notification. Stable observation exposed the fixture's resize feedback. The fixture now resizes the ancestor after delivery while keeping redraw and `flush()` inside the callback. Every above/beside/above alignment and zero-error assertion remains, with an additional zero-error check immediately after redraw. This correction changes no production code.

## Evidence

Base: `d694fe8c09ffa672ed1d144210730fc8dfd9f18e`. Candidate: `51abd63f254e7d53ca01d6092e9d393b12aedb27`. No markup, CSS, host tags, selectors, routes or lazy boundaries change.

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Exact Chromium regression, pinned Bun runner | Original head `8817f7f3` reproduced the CI failure at line 129: one ResizeObserver loop error (14.42 s wall). Fixture-only correction: 1 passed, 1 unrelated case skipped; 236 ms case / 2.44 s wall. Same production source on both runs |
| Existing `widget-card.test.tsx --maxWorkers=1` | 12 passed; 31.789 s wall. Covers initial clipping placement, stable observation across options refresh, hidden queued work, show placement and retained iframe identity. Prior focused proof reused through exact source equality; its host was the former default runner |
| Final frozen install and default `pnpm tsgo:ui` | Passed on the candidate after rebase; no runtime override |
| Targeted lint, format and diff check | Passed |
| Full production Knip, including exports | Candidate and exact base both exit 1 with the identical sole unused export: `src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-restart-recovery-failure.ts: settleInterruptedRestartRecovery`. Candidate 100.90 s; exact-base replay 179.49 s. No widget finding; source blob and reference list also match |
| Independent review | Existing production P0–P2 review retained; fixture correction P0–P3 review scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Relevant source hashes stayed identical through rebase |
| Current-head CI | Pending; `ci:full` supplies chat performance, retention and broad UI proof |

Knip used the same command on candidate and exact base: `pnpm dlx --package knip@6.40.0 knip --config config/knip.config.ts --production --no-progress --reporter compact --no-config-hints --exclude duplicates`. This is a local baseline comparison, not an inherited CI classification. No ignores were added.

Historical CI on old head `8817f7f3` measured startup JS at **337,508 B gzip** and normalized chat boot **1,491,439 → 1,491,357 B (-82 B)**. These are old-head measurements; current-head CI and performance remain pending. The old-head widget-placement failure is fixed by the red/green fixture correction above. No inherited CI claim is made for the replacement head.

Production LOC **753 → 731 (-22)**. Combined test LOC **763 → 792 (+29)**. Three files, **60 additions / 53 deletions**; total LOC **1,516 → 1,523 (+7)**. The added test coverage preserves geometry and lifecycle behavior while the whole feature effect and per-options reattachment are removed.

| `createEffect` | 1 | 0 |
| `createRenderEffect` | 0 | 0 |
| `untrack` | 1 | 1 |
| Raw listeners | 0 | 0 |
| `querySelector(All)` | 1 | 1 |
| Manual class strings / flush / owner escapes | 0 | 0 |

Chat keyboard handoff and rename discover elements owned by other renderers through selectors.

Chat consumes the composer's textarea ref and modal registrations. Menu shortcuts read the existing focus owner's live item list; the legacy model picker publishes filtered rows through that same reader. Rename owns settled focus and selection. Shortcut admission stays available to New Session; activation stays in the lazy chat bundle and checks the owned root followed by registered event-path surfaces.

This revision also fixes a prerequisite inherited from main: `session-attention.ts` now imports `SidebarProjectionMemo` from its canonical `sidebar-projection-cache.ts` owner. The old import makes the exact merge base fail both typechecking and production bundling. No attention behavior changes.

prs.title: fix(sessions): preserve requester identity at execution admission
prs.body:
Related: #150705.

## What Problem This Solves

Preserves the authenticated requester when delegated work is queued, forwarded or recovered, so each new execution uses the right person's current applicable permissions.

## User Impact

Each execution keeps its admitted identity and prepared permissions. Human input waiting for admission uses current policy when admitted; already-admitted native work retains its prepared policy while waiting to run. New delegations resolve current destination policy for their requester. Accepted asynchronous work survives normal source-turn completion, while cancellation, revocation and current-owner checks remain authoritative. Intentional delegation to a more capable agent remains supported.

**Human steering is opt-in across people.** `messages.queue.allowCollaborativeSteering` defaults to `false`. When Bob attempts to steer Alice's active turn with collaboration disabled, the runtime refuses without invoking the model or queueing executable work, and directs Bob to `/followup <message>`. The refusal remains terminal through redelivery and recovery. `/followup` requests one new execution as Bob, respects existing queue ordering, and reports whether it actually queued, started or was rejected without changing the conversation's persistent queue mode.

With explicit `true`, Bob's admitted input may influence Alice's continuing execution using permissions Alice has that Bob does not. Alice's execution identity and prepared permissions remain unchanged; Bob remains the message author. Existing queue modes, conversation access, backend compatibility and live-authority checks still apply. Explicit cross-session `sessions_send(mode="steer")` requires the same authenticated requester and compatible policy; incompatible steering is refused with followup guidance. Approvals and cancellation commands keep their separate handling; natural-language “stop” does not imply cancellation.

**Participant selection extends main's existing `user` selectors.** Unqualified session operations and delegation use the incumbent execution's requester. A supported explicit `user: Bob` selection binds a live accepted participant's authority and requester facts together, including for a new child execution. Native delegation retains the original requester. Source-tool authorization and selected destination scope still apply. The model can select a participant's authority; this does not establish that person's intent or approval. Permissions are not combined, and shared history remains shared.

**Configuration:** new configurations explicitly contain the default. Doctor uses the existing backed-up, include-aware writer to persist an absent setting as `false`, preserving explicit included `true`/`false` values. Repair is idempotent and retains existing include-refusal behavior. Managed updates invoke candidate Doctor; older read-only Doctor phases and manual/package-manager/container replacements may leave the setting absent. The runtime default applies immediately; `openclaw doctor --fix` persists it. Ordinary reads and startup remain read-only.

**Audit and rollback:** existing opt-in child admissions and session-action receipts record a bounded, installation-local pseudonym for the prepared human authority subject separately from the invoking agent. The inspector labels this **Recorded authority subject**; generic receipt provenance remains unverified. This records authority selection, not human intent, approval or causal attribution. Collection scope, retention, row bounds and approval records are unchanged. Older released readers show new subject-bearing receipts as unknown/corrupt on otherwise compatible databases; upgrading again makes retained records readable. Full database/updater rollback is not established, and existing database-write rollback guards still apply.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing admission, queue, transcript-custody and execution-authority owners carry authenticated requester facts separately from previously calculated policy. Delegation binds authority and requester origin together instead of pairing one person's authority with another person's identity. The same facts survive native execution, worker transport, replies, recovery and compaction. Existing audit and inspector owners expose the selected subject without adding an attribution manager, store or causal graph.

## Evidence

Current candidate: `d4fb6dcc6543c0ae362115b0147acbd5fb5409f1`, tree `24647861d8861e79218c86a1ff1bcfdbedc6fdfe`, rebased onto pinned main `fcbcaad75f0db848b54df62275ff4beaacbd50d0`. [Current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39193181340) is running; GitHub reports the branch conflict-free. Execution results below remain bound to their recorded source.

The rebase retains main’s combined turn-adoption/writer owner while carrying the authenticated requester facts through it. Main’s pending-final classifier remains the sole owner of that decision. `/dashboard` routing and explicit `/followup` admission remain supported. Retained cron requester authority cannot bypass the interrupted-occurrence no-replay rule. These are narrow adaptations to existing owners, with no new product scope or unresolved product-direction conflict. The final replay preserves all 65 commits: 64 patch-identical and one mechanical resolution retaining main’s stabilized CI capacity test alongside this branch’s assertions.

Focused integration proof on `d892648266`: the prior guard permitted an unexpected recovery dispatch in the retained-requester cron fixture. The repaired full file passed all 12 cases, including an explicit check that requester facts survive shutdown. The test and repaired owner match the recorded passing bytes. Both runs used the canonical wrapper with `--maxWorkers=1` on Node 24.21.0: 61.903 s for the counterfactual and 62.933 s for the full file. Five existing adoption, requester-snapshot and command files then passed all 59 cases in 141.869 s grouped wall time. This is 71 passed cases across six files, not an end-to-end production or live-provider claim. The cron extension adds no cases or process boots; CI cost for its changed fixture is pending. All six tested files and the affected recovery owners are byte-identical after the final rebase; this is retained focused proof, not a new whole-candidate execution.

Fresh scoped P0–P2 reviews of the `d892648266` integration and subsequent line-cap repair found no actionable issues. The line-cap repair moves two parameter types into the existing companion file and removes two redundant expressions; it adds no runtime owner. Type-aware lint and formatting passed for all six integration files, and whitespace checks passed against the pinned base. That reviewed integration is unchanged in the final replay. The final capacity-test resolution preserves the upstream test block byte-for-byte; its type-aware lint, formatting and final base-wide whitespace checks pass. The full CI planner file passed all 145 cases on `d4fb6dcc6543` in 138.874 s command wall time, using the canonical wrapper with `--maxWorkers=1` on Node 24.21.0. Its current-head CI cost is pending. A new full build and current-source provenance E2E were not completed; the prior build and CI remain qualified below.

The new base includes [main’s updater-fixture correction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/728c94809009fdd4b34aaeaef0290977c836ee93) and [Codex parent-retention fixture correction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f9da044ee30180ecf0f65692608d5c438df58692), addressing the two identified inherited assertions/type failures. Inclusion is not a passing candidate replay. Main’s bounded worker shutdown, SQLite admission and reserved-system-store recovery changes preserve the campaign’s authority contracts on source inspection; they do not establish that the remaining teardown or rollback failures are fixed.

**Remaining limits:** current-source provenance E2E, live Telegram and published-updater proof are not established. The earlier authority teardown and hook `Error.cause` failures remain unexplained. [Rollback observation](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_0bc2d9fe27b92063cce72e079e41004d) failed when the candidate recovery path classified a daemon schema1 store as agent schema31; its relevant owners matched that prior base. Neither full rollback restoration nor healthy retained-candidate recovery was proven. No matched-performance proof exists, and an earlier order-sensitive latency observation remains unexplained. The task-owned AWS lease has been released and that release verified; no broader host-cleanup completion is claimed.

<details>
<summary>Prior-source behavior and CI evidence</summary>

These results establish earlier behavior and integration outcomes. They remain bound to the recorded source; the current owner adaptations require their own validation.

- [Two real human Telegram clients](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/157806#issuecomment-6254936495): seven scenarios and 13 authenticated non-bot inputs on `42a6bffeeb`. Default/false refusal, same-requester steering, busy/idle `/followup`, changed policy at drain, explicit-true incumbent authority, and subsequent delegation had correlated transport IDs, admission records and observable effects. Refusals settled without later execution during the run. Model output was scripted; Telegram transport, native tools and effects were real.
- [Selected-participant native-child effects](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_7f3e5020e17d3b055119573e3dde9382): five rows passed on the prior candidate, including visible/hidden Bob children after Alice completed, zero final writes after unlink/reassignment, and capacity-queued work using current admission policy. Queued revocation was compositional proof, not one live trace.
- [Published updater through cold recovery](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_981ffbd0d48bebe76adbeff0638a554f): published `2026.10.4` updated real released state to exact `42a6bffeeb`, preserved include-owned true and history, then candidate-created selected-Bob work survived source completion and SIGKILL, executed once under Bob, retained FIFO and did not revive withdrawn work after another restart. The released profile catalog was empty; this does not prove continuity of a pre-upgrade human profile or independently changed policy across restart. The original outer carrier's export-permission failure and artifact-only recovery remain recorded.
- Published updater/config cells covered [absent default persistence](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_35138799e8c60b96456c66c89cd303b2) and [include-owned false preservation](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_5a4dd0cee1b70512baa13c58f2388adf), backed-up writes, idempotence, read-only config reads and explicit new-install configuration on their recorded pre-rebase package. The [older receipt reader](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_233464c4022f929ffba2c7765ed02815) confirmed the documented unknown-reader limitation on compatible storage.
- Prior repair/default-fixture proof passed [294 cases in 19 files](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_cf0aa650ea42c65bc5fcac7a1484330c) and [101 cases in eight files, with 22 existing skips](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_c67ab0496a1b19b491b008aa828f280b). Counts overlap with other proof and are not additive.

[CI on `8bfc18dfd2`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39190228636) tested merge `270b8f4e8d` against actual base `a9e5f4e3b7`. It settled with 156 successful jobs, five underlying failures, a failed aggregate gate and 18 skips. Architecture, guards, production types, all five core test-type graphs and core/root lint passed. Strict refusal→explicit followup passed all three cases; worker steering passed all ten, including three request-credit cases; command execution identity passed all eleven. The provenance E2E is excluded from automatic PR CI.

Delegated-authority proof passed all 20 body cases but failed during its 300-second Gateway teardown and subsequent controller cleanup. The hook test expecting rejection of shared memory in `Error.cause` instead resolved. Both reproduce earlier signatures and are not labeled unrelated. The other failures had source-backed inherited causes: an upstream Codex parent-retention test supplied an option absent from `MonitorOptions`; the updater assertion omitted reserved database candidates; and the UI base already exceeded its chat budget. The measured UI delta was 1,491,366B→1,491,410B (+44B), with 25 requests each against a 1,490,000B cap. This is not a production-performance finding. The updater and Codex fixture corrections are now included in the new base as noted above.

[Isolated validation on `8bfc18dfd2`](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_463775ad49d58cdd9cb9cec25d9d0a0f) used verified raw bytes / tree `96b88f4962`. The build and all three strict-followup cases passed, with source bytes unchanged after each. The provenance phase reached the canonical wrapper’s additional private-QA build and test Gateway startup, then exceeded the carrier’s 360-second phase budget and received SIGTERM without an assertion verdict. The owned process group was absent afterward, but natural descendant completion was unverified; final source/runtime closeout was withheld and the carrier reported `source-unverified`. This was not an overall proof pass. The later worker-credit, command-identity and public-settle remote files did not run; the prepared authority diagnostic was also unrun.

The older frozen `9e78318ac5ab` replay passed build, TUI, reply composition, private completion, registry completion authority and public settle/recovery files, while reproducing other fixture, strict-followup, provenance and chat/Doctor failures. Its authority process lacked the canonical completion receipt after assertion/teardown failures, so the overall carrier was unsuccessful. Original failures, diagnostics and costs remain recorded; no passing replay is treated as proof of an unexplained fix.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Inspector screenshots</summary>

Inspected before/after captures from the inspector implementation, delivered in chat and uploaded. The rebase changes its tests, not the renderer. The existing attachment URLs returned images that were decoded and inspected; actual GitHub browser rendering remains unverified because the browser tool could not authenticate.

Before:

![Before: unverified receipt detail](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d6db37db-6b18-4cce-9280-04f36518fafb)

After:

![After: recorded authority subject with unverified provenance retained](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0c4b6db4-c9c8-4eaf-a3d5-6be1c93d6559)

</details>

<details>
<summary>Prior-source measured test costs</summary>

Prior-source `8bfc18dfd2` validation used Node 24.19.0, pnpm 12.11.1 and pinned Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+7bd4fdff3`. The canonical wrapper owned all preparation; reported command walls include that preparation.

| Prior-source check | Command wall | Result |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Build | 292.222 s | Passed; source unchanged |
| Strict followup, standalone file with `--maxWorkers=1` | 65.124 s | Three passed; source unchanged |
| Provenance E2E phase | 360.464 s | Outer phase budget expired; SIGTERM; no assertion verdict |

The interrupted proof carrier took 746.747 s overall and did not complete final verification. The separate prerequisite bootstrap passed in 58.043 s command time / 431.186 s total; setup is not behavior proof. Later remote test files and the prepared authority diagnostic were not run.

These measurements belong to frozen `9e78318ac5ab`, using the canonical wrapper and `--maxWorkers=1`. Grouped wall times are not standalone per-file costs. Counts overlap other evidence and are not additive.

| Check | Command wall | Result |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Build | 292.271 s | Passed |
| Authority / reply / Gateway groups | 125.926 / 155.325 / 258.131 s | 112 pass / 2 fail; 503 pass / 4 fail; 189 pass / 1 timeout |
| TUI / reply composition | 42.368 / 463.426 s | 142 / 245 passed |
| Private completion / registry completion authority / public settle replay | 105.175 / 92.870 / 91.218 s | 25 / 84 / 18 passed |
| CI capacity files | 133.622 s | 180 passed |
| Original chat1 / chat2 / Doctor processes | 138.230 / 170.317 / 116.027 s | Reproduced retained failures |
| Original authority process | 479.738 s | Assertion and teardown failures; canonical completion receipt absent |

The strict-followup and provenance diagnostic carriers took 182.064 s and 90.730 s, both failed and restored their original source. Diagnostics add no recurring CI cases and do not establish a repair. CI 820 reported 40,023 summed job-wall seconds across concurrent jobs; this is neither workflow elapsed time nor production performance. The availability counterfactual/restored commands on earlier `d95895d4c317` took 62.278 s and 62.129 s. CI on `8bfc18dfd2` measured the repaired strict-followup case at 12.669 s and its two siblings at 1.872/1.375 s; the three worker request-credit cases took 0.393/0.406/0.463 s. These are CI case times, not standalone file costs. The remaining `8bfc18dfd2` standalone costs are unmeasured because its carrier stopped before those phases. These are not measurements of the candidate rebased onto `fcbcaad75f`. Historical Telegram, selected-child and updater costs remain attached to their original source-qualified evidence.

</details>

## Scope and LoC churn

Current committed candidate against pinned main `fcbcaad75f0db848b54df62275ff4beaacbd50d0`. Counts include moved and blank lines.

| Category | Files | Added | Deleted |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Production | 248 | 5,590 | 2,091 |
| Tests and support | 202 | 10,514 | 2,105 |
| Docs | 21 | 297 | 97 |
| Tooling | 6 | 14 | 7 |
| Total | 477 | 16,415 | 4,300 |

Gross churn: **20,715 lines**; net growth: **12,115 lines**. The rebase adds no new product scope.

prs.body:
## Current candidate and proof

Current head: `48d2e87f72f008e26c7d3f54c87cd29669b290d1`. Main base: `b5767340ed5765e196d5403041a5f7e4dee14f4f`. The rebase includes the upstream sidebar import and unused `TaglineMode` fixes. Both changed files, the stable patch ID, and the range-diff are identical to original reviewed head `c6012f668b56f913b9b6f6b859cab6f353495cfb`.

| Current-head check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Frozen install | Pass |
| Default `pnpm tsgo:ui` | Pass, 29.78 s |
| Full production/export Knip | Pass, no findings, 463.00 s |
| Source equivalence and `git diff --check` | Pass |

Behavioral tests were not repeated because the reviewed source blobs are unchanged. The runtime, browser, startup, and CI evidence below belongs to the original reviewed head and is retained as historical proof. Exact-head CI run 39191727539 remains failed; the current-head attribution below accounts for every failed root. No remote lease was acquired.

## Current-head CI attribution

Run [39191727539](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39191727539), attempt 1, tested this exact head. It has 33 successful jobs, 26 skipped jobs, and no cancelled jobs. Three failed roots plus their aggregate remain red.

The three failing test names exactly match latest completed scheduled main [39186683798](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39186683798), observed at 03:05:53 UTC. There are no additional failing test names:

- ui-e2e-bundled  ui/src/e2e/session-list-filter.e2e.test.ts > Control UI session-list event scope > keeps the Sessions page query stable when the startup roster completes
- ui-e2e-bundled  ui/src/e2e/session-list-filter.e2e.test.ts > Control UI session-list event scope > refetches instead of showing a row excluded by configured-agent filtering
- ui-e2e-serial-standalone  ui/src/e2e/command-palette-search.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts > Control UI command palette search with a real Gateway > finds a grouped spawned conversation beyond the roster and treats a full result page as success

The only performance failure is the existing 1,490,000 B absolute chat ceiling: the normalized main base is **1,491,439 B** and this candidate is **1,491,437 B** (-2 B). Startup is **337,515 B gzip** and CSS is **38,500 B in one request**. New-session JS decreases 1,049,602→1,049,599 B; all other budgets pass.

The CI table only matched job names; the saved independent comparison matches every failing test name and the baseline logs. Native version-1 evidence binds the actual tested merge and ordered main/head parents, verifies merge-tree reconstruction and unchanged failure source blobs, and accounts for each failed job plus the aggregate. CI is reported as failed, not green.

## What Problem This Solves

The Files panel used two rendering effects to announce hosted tabs and resolve an MCP commit promise. Native panel properties already own the tab inputs, and the MCP unmount gate already schedules restart after the renderer commits.

Use the bridge’s native `previews` and `activeId` receipts to coalesce a hosted-tab notification from current values. Subscribe through the existing i18n projection so locale and lazy catalog changes still update the header; remove that subscription and the native callback with the panel lifetime. Let the MCP gate use its existing commit restart path. The browse icon now stays lazy when only tab metadata is read.

## Historical original-head evidence

Pinned base: `77a403f1c15380ce71fcc53f0bb68ce5f4f2794e`. Candidate: `c6012f668b56f913b9b6f6b859cab6f353495cfb`.

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Files panel suite, including close/reopen/disconnect during MCP teardown and retained unsaved editor | Pass, 30 cases |
| Native input batch, detach/reconnect, locale notification tests | Pass, 3 cases; new suite 4.484 s test time |
| UI typecheck | Pass, 15.91 s; frozen install supplied the already-pinned `tsrs` dependency |
| Chat test type graph | Pass, 16.96 s wall / 13.6 s graph |
| Focused typed lint / format / diff | Pass; lint 144.06 s including artifact-lock wait, with the unchanged icon-getter warning |
| Full-context P2 autoreview | `scoped-clean`; final source verification complete |
| Production Knip | Pass, no findings; 518.72 s |
| Historical original-head ci:full run39181982315 | All behavioral jobs pass; two inherited checks below keep the aggregate gate red |

Refactor checklist for `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-files-panel.tsx`:

| Pattern | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Rendering controller | 0 | 0 |
| `createEffect` | 2 | 0 |
| `createRenderEffect` | 0 | 0 |
| `untrack` | 0 | 0 |
| `addEventListener` | 0 | 0 |
| `querySelector(All)` | 0 | 0 |
| Class-string assembly | 0 | 0 |
| `flush` | 0 | 0 |
| `runWithOwner` / `getOwner` | 0 | 0 |

Production LOC: **227 → 249** (+22). Tests: **+80 lines** in a dedicated native-input suite. The growth makes batching and disposal explicit at the bridge boundary; it replaces both effects and the MCP promise handoff. Existing markup, CSS, host tag, lazy imports, and domain owners are unchanged, so no visual capture is needed. No checklist survivors remain in this file. No remote lease was acquired.

The focused run passed 33 cases in two files (74.18 s Vitest / 115.37 s wall). Earlier Bun and Node runs produced no test result and were stopped after a process sample identified a filesystem `rename` stall; the successful Node run used `OPENCLAW_VITEST_FS_MODULE_CACHE=0 --fsModuleCache=false`. No passing test was repeated. The retained, unchanged `For` code emits `STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED` diagnostics; this is recorded for a focused follow-up, without suppressing warnings.

Implementation and proof took about 27 minutes, including the diagnosed runner fallback and the single Knip scan. No lease was acquired; external proof artifacts are retained for coordinator cleanup.

## Historical original-head CI attribution

Run [39181982315](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39181982315) has 35 successful jobs and no failing behavioral job. Startup is **337,475 B gzip**, seven JS requests; startup CSS is **38,500 B**, one request. Chat boot is **1,491,258 → 1,491,319 B** (+61 B); both the normalized main baseline and candidate exceed the existing 1,490,000 B absolute ceiling. New-session boot is **1,049,533 → 1,049,566 B** (+33 B), within its ceiling.

The other failing check is the exact mock-export violation `src/cli/program/root-help.test.ts:33: ./subcli-descriptors.js`. The unchanged command reproduces it on GitHub CI’s actual main parent `5f637b6b3686b0aa193ebe7a579a444c87dcec01`. The earlier branch fork `77a403f1c15380ce71fcc53f0bb68ce5f4f2794e` passes; main changed the offending test and subject afterward. Checker/test/subject blobs match the tested main parent and merge. Native inherited/admin evidence retains both baseline outcomes, exact checkout identities, normalized performance, and job inventory. Strict performance and aggregate CI are reported as failing, not green.

prs.title: refactor: share native adapter and approval facts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Native adapters and approval presentation repeat the same click, bundle, decision and terminal-label facts in separate callers. The copies can drift even though each plugin or core contract already has an owner.

## What Changed

CUA desktop and window clicks share plugin-owned button/count metadata and the existing wire action roster. FaceTime shares its exact two dial-helper bundle IDs while keeping general helper admission distinct. Discord decision labels/colors share one plugin-local descriptor; Discord, Google Chat and Slack reuse the already-exported SDK decision formatter where their existing text is identical.

## What Problem This Solves

Storage request adapters repeatedly copy privately owned inputs, and session publication projects the same committed row a second time. Three profile setters also repeat the same transaction/publication body.

## User Impact

The standalone session-memory backend and its factory, registry, expiry, federation machinery and tests are untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the owned-input/projection area split of the closed z05 storage cleanup. It forwards private native request values after their real producers have captured them, correlates retirement replies with their typed operation, and removes owner-proven scalar checks. Actor capture paths remain unchanged.

Sharing equality borrows a private selector while the public projector detaches the complete result once. Entry writes reuse the frozen full entry already produced by publication; unchanged actor/postimage writes still project and outward results still clone. Role, display-name and avatar updates share the existing transaction owner while retaining role-only gateway-owner refusal and authority invalidation. Provider-review owners share exactly the same deep snapshot/freeze construction, without removing either security snapshot.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Native session requests: registry #163208/#166259, goals #165785, recovery #163119, reactions #162434, headers #165401, anchors #172915 and cohorts #170712 use privately owned requests. Unsupported mutation of a pending private request is best effort rather than another downstream deep copy. Actor/public snapshots and current native effects stay. The synthetic throwing-capture test in #166259 is not a human incident.
- State/profile metadata: #168301/#164630 and profile owners #153508/#162571 use request-local values and await settlement. Unsupported private request mutation is best effort; actual database conflicts, credential/authority snapshots, callback copies, owner refusal and role revocation remain.
- Onboarding #152445: already decoded private expected records no longer receive another deep copy. Match-schema parsing stays before persistence: ClawHub search metadata is not fully runtime-validated upstream, so that parse remains a real boundary. Timestamp/database capture, namespace confinement, current-row CAS, nested match capture and reopen equality stay covered.
- Internal result tags and scalar facts: typed operation/result correlation and registered identity owners replace repeated impossible-state checks. A future buggy internal handler is an owner defect rather than independently guarded at each consumer. Physical admission/current authority and missing-row outcomes remain.
- Private projection/publication values are reused only after existing owners create them. An unsupported internal ownership violation is not separately isolated; public mutable results still detach once. Native SQL retains the transcript navigation byte bound before transfer.

The journal's missing-table preprobe is removed, not its query error handling or deleted-database/history protection (#155024 and human report #154002). The first GitHub command snapshot remains before FIFO (#168953); only its second private traversal goes. Provider-review snapshots (#155214) keep their original deep capture/freezes and acknowledgment/current-source checks. Measured cache ownership (#168316/#169090/#163030) remains, with no invalidation fence removed.

prs.title: refactor(ui): share pending focus requests across choice and preview views
prs.body:
OptionCard and FilePreview now share one pending-focus primitive instead of each managing focus in a view effect. A recommendation can wait while the card is disabled, a replacement request can cancel it, and the request is consumed before the caller checks whether another control owns focus. Description and disabled updates retain the existing choice nodes and selection.

FilePreview keeps its immediate selection-handler focus and connected/open guards. Its remaining effect separately compares content-reset and active-row-reveal inputs, so sibling inventory updates can reveal the selected row without resetting the document being read. Focus still runs only initially or when the active path changes in document layout; switching layout alone does not refocus. Tags, classes, routes, and lazy boundaries are unchanged.

### Scope and counts

| OptionCard effects | 1 | 0 |
| FilePreview effects | 2 | 1 |
| Shared pending-focus effect | 0 | 1 |
| Render effects / untrack / direct listeners / DOM queries | 0 | 0 |
| Production LOC | 647 | 671 |
| Test LOC (three affected files) | 1,114 | 1,207 |

The 24-line production increase is the 22-line shared lifetime primitive plus two lines in FilePreview. The remaining feature effect at `ui/src/components/file-preview-modal.tsx:184` synchronizes the preview body's scroll reset and active-row reveal with committed DOM; the other effect lives once in `ui/src/lib/reactive/pending-focus.ts:14`.
