prs.title: fix: streamed replies with a leaked model control token no longer re-scan the whole reply
prs.body:
Fixes #175444

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a streamed reply that contains one leaked model control token (for example `<|assistant|>`) re-scans the entire reply on every later delta, costing seconds of Gateway event-loop CPU per reply and growing quadratically — 5.6 s at 65 KB and 23.4 s at 128 KB on `main` at 51ebf30c8e0. One 128 KB reply made the token scan read 2.05 billion characters to strip a single token. Leaked control tokens are a reported user-visible path (GLM-5 in #44179, the `<|...|>` leaks behind #40020), and any reply that quotes a token — tokenizer help, F#/Elm `<|` examples, documentation — takes the same code path. The sanitizer runs for every streamed reply on the single-threaded Gateway, so the repeated work delays session updates and channel deliveries while the reply streams.

## User Impact

Replies that contain or quote a control token now scan each appended delta once instead of re-running the whole-reply scrub. End to end, the streamed delivery projection drops from 5.6 s to 0.65 s of CPU at 65 KB and from 23.4 s to 2.2 s at 128 KB; the token scan itself drops from 528 M to 65 K characters at 65 KB and from 2.05 G to 128 K at 128 KB. Tilde-dense prose drops from 21.2 s to 0.64 s at 65 KB. Visible output is unchanged: tokens outside code are still removed, code examples are still preserved, and streamed deltas still concatenate to the batch result.

The one-pass bound covers token/backtick-sparse replies, which is the reported case. Inline-code-dense replies still revalidate once per backtick delta, because a backtick can change ownership of an earlier token; the cost is bounded by the number of backtick deltas, not every delta, and output stays exact. A follow-up could skip revalidation inside a settled fence. Other sanitizer stages are unchanged and keep their own pre-existing per-delta costs.

## Why This Change Was Made

`stripModelSpecialTokens()` was registered with `activationTokens`, so once any `<|`/`<｜` appeared every delta ran the canonical transform over the whole cumulative reply. The transform cannot settle the input because the leaked token remains in the source, so it also re-ran `findCodeRegions()` and the full match scan each time.

The filter now provides a projector that keeps the stripped output and appends a delta directly only when that delta cannot change the result: no token opener, no token split across the boundary, no pending separator after a token at the end, no surrogate-pair split after it, no backtick, and no 3+ tilde run (two characters are carried so a split fence opener still revalidates). Backtick and tilde-fence deltas are the only ones that can change code ownership, so they re-run the canonical transform and can emit a corrected replacement; everything else appends directly. Token boundaries are found from their pipes rather than the last `<`, so a token body containing `<` is handled too.

`transform` remains the canonical batch path, so history and delivery extraction are untouched.

## Evidence

Minimal repro (through the shipped `createAssistantVisibleStreamText()` projection, 4-character deltas, one `<|assistant|>` followed by ordinary prose), measured on Windows 11 / Node 26.11.1:

| Reply | Before: total / token-scan chars | After: total / token-scan chars |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 32 KB | 1,295 ms / 128,144,037 | 243 ms / 32,041 |
| 65 KB | 5,616 ms / 528,417,537 | 651 ms / 65,041 |
| 128 KB | 23,384 ms / 2,048,576,037 | 2,176 ms / 128,041 |

Output matched the batch result in every case (`matchesBatch: true`). A tilde-dense 65 KB reply (many `~12 ms`-style numbers) measured 21,223 ms before the tilde narrowing and 639 ms after, with the token scan at 65,041 characters.

Independent review found and this branch fixed four boundary problems across earlier heads:

- A token inside an inline code span whose closing backtick arrived after more text was stripped and never restored when the span closed. A backtick delta now re-runs the canonical transform, so the closing delta emits the corrected replacement.
- The first gate used the raw inline-code scanner, which treats a lone or escaped backtick as an open span forever and disabled the fast path for the rest of the reply (16 KB: 12.1 s). The gate now keys on the deltas that can change ownership: stray and escaped backticks cost one revalidation (16 KB: 58–76 ms) instead of disabling the fast path.
- The ownership gate matched any tilde delta, so tilde-dense prose paid a full scan per tilde. It now matches only 3+ tilde runs.
- A token that batch sanitization stripped inside a reference definition stayed stripped after a later suffix invalidated the definition (the image became unresolved and its code span became code-owned again), and the mirror case left a standalone definition label's token kept where batch strips it. The projector now keeps the token decision unsettled while a definition has no blank-line boundary after it - the same boundary the canonical parser uses for its stable-prefix rule - for tokens currently stripped and for kept tokens in a line-start label whose `]` is missing, is the last character, or is followed by `:`. Appends re-run the canonical transform until the definition settles.

Regression coverage in `src/shared/text/model-special-tokens.streaming.test.ts`:

- 37 fixtures × chunk sizes 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 64 vs `stripModelSpecialTokens()` and delta accounting
- per-prefix parity: every 1-character prefix equals the batch transform of that prefix
- split opener, token at the end with a pending separator, replacement replay, inline-code ownership change, closer-run revocation, escaped backticks, tilde fences, token body containing `<`, astral and combining-mark boundaries, image-label revocation, and reference-definition settlement (strip, restore, and standalone-definition label cases)
- three bounded-work assertions (plain, stray backtick, tilde-dense prose): fewer than 4× the source length scanned by the token pattern, versus about 32 M characters on the pre-fix path for the 16 KB fixture

Checks run locally:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/shared/text/model-special-tokens.streaming.test.ts` — 49 passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run` on the filter consumers (`assistant-visible-text*`, `text-projection`, `strip-markdown`, `embedded-agent-utils.strip-model-special-tokens`) — all passed
- `pnpm tsgo:core` — exit 0
- cross-check fuzz: 4,000 randomly assembled markup sources × chunk sizes 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 16 (24,000 streamed runs) vs the batch transform — zero divergences
- `pnpm test test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts` — 14 passed, 5 skipped
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` on the three touched files — clean
- `pnpm exec oxlint --type-aware --config .oxlintrc.json` on the three touched files — 0 warnings, 0 errors
- `pnpm check:max-lines-ratchet` reports the three inherited `ui/` suppressions already present on the base commit; no `ui/` file is touched by this PR.

Only one problem is addressed. No configuration, migration, or dependency changes.

## AI disclosure

AI disclosure: this change was drafted with AI assistance at my request, under my direction and review. I set the scope (bounded incremental work with batch parity), required the before/after reproduction, and reviewed the code and evidence before opening this PR.

## Shipped Gateway behavior proof (2026-10-19)

Added after review. The streaming path is now exercised through a real `gateway run` process, not only the shared module, and the image-ownership finding has a base-failing / repaired-head-passing regression.

**65 KB reply that starts with a leaked `<|assistant|>` token, provider streaming four-character deltas** (16,254 SSE events in 3,332 ms from a local OpenAI-compatible fixture provider). Run against this head (`d0cf858d45a0`) through `gateway run`; Gateway process CPU sampled, control round subtracted.

```json
{
  "providerEvents": 16254, "providerEmitMs": 3332, "chunkChars": 4,
  "deliveredChars": 65000,
  "deliveredSha256": "28570f36dc0a15ff736fc4845448d73daccd4e8eb8e59a247fef4fe76483ce72",
  "deliveredDeltas": 51, "chatDeltas": 51,
  "deliveredHasRawToken": false, "deliveredDeltasHaveRawToken": false,
  "streamWindowMs": 3970, "firstDeltaMs": 553, "lastDeltaMs": 4523,
  "terminalStatus": "ok", "terminalMs": 4698,
  "gatewayCpuSec": 6.02, "controlCpuSec": 0.83, "streamingCpuSec": 5.19
}
```

The delivered 65,000 characters are byte-identical to the canonical batch transform of the source (`stripModelSpecialTokens()`), so streamed delivery and batch delivery agree exactly (stream sha and delivered sha verified against the source in-process).

<details><summary>Raw client transcript (redacted)</summary>

```text
[client] warm-up turn completed in 13867ms
[client] control turn completed in 652ms (gateway cpu delta 0.83s)
[client] terminal=ok deltas=51 streamedChars=65013 streamedHasRawToken=true   # raw agent stream, pass-through
[client] gateway cpu delta during measured turn: 6.02s
[client] streamWindowMs=3970 firstDeltaMs=553 terminalMs=4698
[client] delivered final: chars=65000 rawToken=false sha256=28570f36dc0a15ff…
[client] delivered head: "The gateway keeps the session transcript and streams the rep"
[client] chat stream: deltas=51 chars=129516 rawToken=false
```

</details>

**Ownership revocation (P2) regression now has a base-failing / head-passing pair.** Same test file, same command:

```text
base 2a53f78dda0 (without d0cf858d45a0)
  $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/shared/text/model-special-tokens.streaming.test.ts
  Test Files  1 failed (1)
  Tests  8 failed | 28 passed (36)
    token inside an image label resolved by a late definition at 1 chars:
      expected '![a `<|assistant|>`][id]\n\n[id]: /ur…' to be '![a ``][id]\n\n[id]: /url\n'
    token inside an image label with an inline destination at 1 chars:
      expected '![a `<|assistant|>`](/img.png)\n' to be '![a ``](/img.png)\n'
    (plus inline title, shortcut label, definition-continuation, prefix-33, and the two dedicated revocation tests)

  $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/shared/text/model-special-tokens.streaming.test.ts
```

Also re-run on this head: cross-check fuzz (24,000 streamed variants vs the batch transform, including the image late-definition and inline-destination prefixes) with zero divergences, plus tsgo, type-aware lint, and format checks clean.

**Definition settlement (P2) regression now has a base-failing / head-passing pair.** Same test file, same command:

```text

  Test Files  1 failed (1)

      expected '![a ``][id]\n\n[id]: /url x' to be '![a `<|assistant|>`][id]\n\n[id]: /ur…'
```

prs.title: fix(goals): keep pursuing after delegated work finishes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Goals stopping after delegated children finish, even though the objective remains active and the requester produces a normal final reply.

## User Impact

Built-in chat Goals can continue through the normal follow-up queue after child settlement. Pause, Stop, session/Goal replacement, budget limits, pending user input, and unsettled children still take precedence. Independent command runs do not become autonomous.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preserve the original admitted Goal's reply route and live operator restriction across committed child custody. Record the real requester outcome, then return to the existing Goal queue only after the child completion batch commits. Session Stop also revokes retained returns before enqueue, not only queued work.

This is a same-process handoff, not restart recovery. It deliberately does not migrate a retained return across compaction that replaces the session ID or lifecycle revision; the stale-identity check declines that return. No schema, configuration, or permission changes.

## Evidence

- Current reviewed head: `43d0356c12896c1cc32e4f5d3c49142878b8ebbb`, integrated with main `d48d36d7c2053b464b68e5024f3229612ad09eca`. Existing session-controller, cloud Goal, and descendant owners are preserved; controller custody is reserved before asynchronous Goal admission so Stop covers the pre-enqueue interval.
- Real product regression: isolated TLS Gateway and scoped-profile WebSocket → local HTTP Responses provider → real spawn/yield/committed settlement → two hidden nudges → real `update_goal` completion and original-recipient replies. Pinned-main runtime reproduced the defect at 4 parent provider calls instead of 8. Repair passes; parent independently replayed the full composition (66.45s wall).
- Final-effect authority proof: forbidden sibling spawn is denied by the original main-only human role during requester completion and the first nudge. Actual role revocation before enqueue and profile reassignment before dispatch produce no additional provider/tool/reply effects. The fixture is non-admin `operator.read/write`, `agents: [main]`, `sessions.others: write`; it does not claim own-only delegation support.
- Final affected regressions: 122 tests across 8 files passed (131.02s wall), including real controller Stop capture before enqueue. prs.title: fix(gateway): bound worker cleanup already pending at shutdown
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes slow Gateway shutdown when worker-environment reconciliation has already started waiting for a node to acknowledge worker stop or workspace drain.

## User Impact

Worker-environment shutdown limits pending remote stop/drain acknowledgments to five seconds (or the shorter remaining process budget), including requests started before shutdown. An unconfirmed worker retains its attachment for recovery; local writes and transfer cleanup still settle.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reconcile guard joins admitted recovery before teardown. An earlier node stop captured normal 60-second RPC timeouts outside the shutdown context, and shutdown reused that pending promise. The node transport owner now publishes one shutdown cancellation signal to its existing and subsequent acknowledgment waits. The guard still drains accepted work rather than detaching writes.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule, set before timing: run the identical synthetic node-cleanup fixture on baseline and candidate concurrently under the sandbox quiet lock, then swap CPU halves for the next pair. Each transport acknowledgment is delayed 40 seconds; cleanup starts before shutdown. Candidate must finish remote-ack waiting within five seconds plus scheduling noise, report unconfirmed cleanup rather than physical-stop success, and retain local cleanup joins. Compare paired shutdown durations, with outside load recorded for context.

- Regression: the real environment service, SQLite store, placement guard, and node transport owner reproduce shutdown remaining pending after five seconds on baseline; candidate passes. It verifies the attachment and bootstrap receipt remain, with no install or destroy.
- 78 targeted tests pass across runtime refresh, node teardown, node tunnel lifecycle, provisioning shutdown replay, environment access, and startup authority. The initial reconciliation regression fails on the base at the five-second completion assertion. The cleanup-retry regression fails on the previous PR head and passes with the original timer retained; the final affected two-file run passed 28 tests in 75.51 seconds including transformation.
- 22 import-closure checks pass. Changed-file lint, formatting, and export-name collision guard pass.
- The one local core typecheck identified a missing `beginClose` in a test double; corrected. Current-head CI passed the core typecheck lanes and all focused runtime jobs; the remaining extension test-type failure is inherited, as documented below.
- Independent review: clean through P2; final code and removal of the superseded deadline reviewed. Simplification keeps a single node-transport shutdown signal and preserves existing local settlement. Removed the superseded per-owner ten-second deadline. Runtime production delta: +16 lines; propagation of cancellation into preexisting waits and a lifetime-wide timer require growth. Existing types moved to a sibling to preserve the file cap.

Measured on an isolated Linux sandbox, Node 26.8.2, with concurrent A/B runs under the exclusive measurement lock and swapped 16-core halves:

| Pair | Baseline | Candidate | Candidate − baseline | Sampled CPU busy |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| A on 112–127, B on 96–111 | 80,026.709 ms | 5,035.226 ms | −74,991.483 ms | 2.02% |
| A on 96–111, B on 112–127 | 80,025.446 ms | 5,034.593 ms | −74,990.853 ms | 1.66% |

Both candidates returned `WorkerTunnelOwnerDisconnectedError` after aborting the pending stop acknowledgment; both baselines waited for stop and drain acknowledgments. This reduces the reproduced remote wait by 93.7%. The earlier pre-simplification pair is excluded.

Workload: `scripts/perf/worker-environment-shutdown-measure.ts`, identical source SHA-256 `ea7e4dd6071ab7a14a4669571810876baffab9675b5e3f0225859d6583586240`; baseline `84dffb7ec632911fd351ba9a974891540cc2422a` versus the runtime cancellation patch on `7ed19152a21ff8b4e48f0911755681b749d17d75` (subsequent rebases did not change the affected runtime files; the later timer-retention fix changes retries after early cleanup, not this already-expired-timer path). Build each workload with `esbuild --bundle --platform=node --format=esm --packages=external`, then run `node <artifact>.mjs --state-dir <fresh-directory> --ack-delay-ms 40000`. Separate state directories; synchronized start; `mpstat -P 96-127` recorded per pair. Dirty pages remained below 2 GB.

- Scope limit: timing fixture exercises the production node-cleanup owner with synthetic delayed acknowledgments. It is not a full Gateway restart or a real background exec workload. The incident's aggregate guard timing does not identify its inner wait, so this PR does not claim definitive attribution for that incident.
- No Testbox/Crabbox leases; focused local checks and PR CI follow the compute limits.

CI initially found three omitted `beginClose` test doubles across two environment-access test files. Those fixtures are corrected and all 34 tests in the two files pass. GitHub review also found that clearing the timer after an early cleanup failure could leave a retry unbounded; the timer now stays armed for the full shutdown lifetime, with a red/green regression. Independent review is clean through P2. Final-head [CI run 39190672577](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39190672577) completed with 55 successful jobs and 26 unselected/skipped jobs. Its only nonaggregate failure is `check-test-types`; `openclaw/ci-gate` failed downstream. All selected runtime, core typecheck, lint, documentation, and security-fast jobs passed. The [Security Review run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39191319756) succeeded for the exact PR head, with successful dependency-review and security-sensitive-review statuses.

### Inherited CI failure

Landing under the authorized inherited-failure exception for exact head `de44d8916e9e227ff4d76ccc90f4e9ddef29c23f`. The [PR typecheck job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39190672577/job/117863188758) and the [main baseline job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39190227860/job/117861494392) report the identical error:

```text
extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-subagent-monitor.parent-retention.test.ts(37,5): error TS2353: Object literal may only specify known properties, and 'completionDeliveryRetryDelaysMs' does not exist in type 'MonitorOptions'.
```

The baseline is main commit `a9e5f4e3b7b2114caa573554766ab7b4850b39e4`, an ancestor of this PR's base `fdf327a2f49fc520164aebc73f5bc527d2b61d42`. The entire `extensions/codex` subtree is unchanged from that baseline to this PR head, and both jobs invoke the same extension test-typecheck command and config. prs.title: fix(context-engine): wrap JSON.parse in try/catch in context-engine-turn-outbox.ts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In `src/agents/harness/context-engine-turn-outbox.ts`, two `JSON.parse()` calls are not wrapped in try/catch:
1. `writeContextEngineTurnOutboxPayload` parses `existing.payload_json` without error handling
2. `recoverContextEngineTurnOutbox` parses `row.payload_json` without error handling

If the stored JSON is corrupted, this throws an unhandled `SyntaxError` with no context about which row or advancement key caused the failure.

Worse, a corrupted row left in the table also breaks every pending-work query: `outboxPayloadRequiresAdvancement()` projects `json_extract(payload_json, '$.state')`, and SQLite raises `malformed JSON` on the invalid row before the query can reach later valid rows. The agent-run attempt path recovers the outbox and immediately drains it, so one corrupted durable row degrades the lease and blocks valid session turns from advancing.

## Fix

1. **writeContextEngineTurnOutboxPayload**: Wrap `JSON.parse` in try/catch, re-throwing with a descriptive error including the `advancementKey`.
2. **recoverContextEngineTurnOutbox**: Wrap `JSON.parse` in try/catch, logging a warning with the `advancement_key` and skipping the malformed row (`continue`). The row stays durable as audit evidence, matching how blocked rows are retained.
3. **outboxPayloadRequiresAdvancement**: Guard the JSON projection with `json_valid(payload_json)` before `json_extract(...)`, so malformed rows are excluded from every pending-work selection path (pending-session grouping, the per-session row pick, and `hasPendingContextEngineTurn`) instead of faulting the query. This follows the existing containment pattern used by the subagent SQLite registry (`json_valid(payload_json) AND ...`).

## Evidence

Regression tests in `src/agents/harness/context-engine-turn-outbox.test.ts` (the whole file — 11 tests — passes in CI):
- `throws a descriptive error when existing outbox payload JSON is malformed` — the write path re-throws with the `advancementKey` instead of a bare `SyntaxError`.
- `skips outbox rows with malformed payload JSON during recovery` — recovery logs a warning naming the `advancement_key` and keeps the row as inspectable audit evidence.

### After-fix production-path proof (real context plugin persisting messages + database reopen + context reassembly)

`persists real turn messages through a durable plugin and reassembles them after a reopen past a malformed row` drives the **production entry point** `drainPendingContextEngineTurnsBeforeRun` against a **real durable context plugin** — there is no mocked `commitTurn` and no pass-through `assemble`. The plugin's `commitTurn` persists each accepted turn's **actual messages** (`{ role, content }` records, shaped exactly like the entries the transcript hands to `commitTurn` in production) to its own on-disk JSONL context store, and honours the `atomic-idempotent-v1` contract so a host retry of an already-committed key returns `{ status: "duplicate" }` instead of storing the same messages twice. Its `assemble` reconstitutes a session's persisted turns from that store and appends the incoming run's messages — the same contract a real retrieval-oriented engine implements.

The test:
1. Enqueues a turn, corrupts its stored `payload_json` to `{not-valid-json`, then enqueues a later valid turn **carrying real user/assistant messages** in the same session.
2. Runs the pre-run owner (`drainPendingContextEngineTurnsBeforeRun`) — **corruption recovery + message persistence**: the malformed row is skipped with a warning, the later valid turn commits through the real plugin and its **messages are written to the plugin's durable store**, and the lease is **not** degraded. (Before the `json_valid` guard the pending-work projection faulted on the corrupted row, so the owner reported a retry failure and degraded the lease.)
3. **Closes and reopens the existing database**, then continues — **persistence across reopen**: a later accepted turn (`session-a:after-reopen`) advances and its messages are appended to the same on-disk store, while a host retry of the already-committed `session-a:later-valid` turn stays idempotent (`duplicate`, never stored twice).
4. Calls `assemble` for a **subsequent run** — **context reassembly**: the plugin returns the messages persisted before and after the reopen, followed by the next run's prompt, proving committed turn content is reused rather than dropped.
5. Asserts the reopened database reports `pending: false`, the corrupted row is the only retained outbox row (kept as audit evidence, excluded from pending work), and neither run degraded the lease.

Trace emitted by the test's terminal `console.log` and captured in CI output (reformatted below for readability; values are exact) — shard `agentic-agents-support-hosted-1`, job [`checks-node-compact-large-10`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34037447490/job/101498164469), where the full `context-engine-turn-outbox.test.ts` file passes 11/11:

```json
{
  "scenario": "durable-plugin-message-persistence-and-reassembly",
  "database": "openclaw-agent.sqlite",
  "persistedTurns": [
    { "advancementKey": "session-a:later-valid", "messages": [
      { "role": "user", "content": "later valid user turn" },
      { "role": "assistant", "content": "later valid assistant turn" } ] },
    { "advancementKey": "session-a:after-reopen", "messages": [
      { "role": "user", "content": "after reopen user turn" },
      { "role": "assistant", "content": "after reopen assistant turn" } ] }
  ],
  "assembledContext": [
    { "role": "user", "content": "later valid user turn" },
    { "role": "assistant", "content": "later valid assistant turn" },
    { "role": "user", "content": "after reopen user turn" },
    { "role": "assistant", "content": "after reopen assistant turn" },
    { "role": "user", "content": "next run user prompt" },
    { "role": "assistant", "content": "next run assistant reply" }
  ],
  "assembledTokenEstimate": 6,
  "retainedOutboxRows": ["session-a:malformed"],
  "leaseDegradations": 0
}
```

Read against the fix, the trace shows — through a real context plugin that persists message content, on a **reopened** database:
- **later-turn message persistence**: `persistedTurns` records the **actual `{ role, content }` messages** the plugin's `commitTurn` received and wrote to its durable store, not merely keys, session IDs, or a status;
- **database reopen**: `session-a:after-reopen` messages are persisted **after** the database is closed and reopened, and the retried `session-a:later-valid` turn is **not** duplicated (idempotent across the reopen);
- **subsequent context assembly**: `assembledContext` is the plugin's `assemble` output for a later run — the persisted turns reconstituted from the on-disk store, followed by the next run's prompt (`assembledTokenEstimate: 6`);
- **corruption containment**: `retainedOutboxRows: ["session-a:malformed"]` — the corrupted row survives as audit evidence but is excluded from pending work, and `leaseDegradations: 0` — no run degraded its context path.

Before the `json_valid` guard, step 2 fails: SQLite raises `malformed JSON` inside the pending-work query, the pre-run owner reports a retry failure and degrades the lease, so the later valid turn's messages are never persisted.

prs.title: fix(sqlite): avoid lock failures during worker commits
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes SQLite lock failures when a synchronous caller overlaps a worker that is waiting for its host commit grant. Hourly 39186683798/job 117850681136 exposed this during `SessionManager.open` in the synthetic-repair Gateway integration test.

## User Impact

Synchronous SDK session calls can complete while Gateway workers commit, retaining their supported return and persistence behavior. No timeout, authority, schema, configuration, or public API changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

#176545 moved the agent-admission timestamp update to the single-statement path. That path bypassed the existing `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` owner which services pending worker grants: the synchronous update waited for the worker's lock while the worker waited for the same host to grant its commit.

Single statements now enter through that existing transaction owner when the same database has an active admission service. The callback runs once, after lock admission, with its existing authority checks. Calls without a matching service retain autocommit. No new retry or lifecycle machinery.

## Evidence

- Extended the existing real-worker admission test with a single-statement caller. On main, the transaction arm passes and the new arm fails with `database is locked` after the existing 5-second budget. The fixed arms pass in 336 ms and 313 ms. Both committed tokens, both grant stages, and exactly one native callback remain asserted.
- Pinned Bun, `--maxWorkers=1`: **80 passed across four files**, including the full shared-state worker, transaction helper, state-transaction suites, and the synthetic-repair Gateway integration. Total wrapper time: 138.99 s; Gateway case: 31.71 s. The full worker/transaction suite protects cancellation, ownership refusal, publication, rollback, and no-service autocommit.
- Targeted production and state-test typechecks, type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Isolated P2 autoreview, including the complete transaction owner and admission callers: no actionable findings.

The initial local Gateway baseline timed out during startup at its unchanged 90-second budget; it did not reproduce the CI lock stack. The deterministic real-worker regression is the direct red proof. The final Gateway run uses the original fixture and assertions unchanged.

prs.title: fix(sqlite): retire private snapshot admissions before deletion
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Doctor can finish a read-only report and remove its private inspection database while leaving that database's cached admission in the parent process. A subsequent status inventory then reports the deleted image. Main hourly 39186683798 exposed this as schema 19 versus current schema 28 in the per-store diagnostics tests.

Retire the host's admissions within the owned snapshot directory before delegating deletion to the native child. Check every registered nested reader before changing any retirement state, so an active reader still refuses cleanup and unrelated source/sibling admissions remain intact.

The private writable-inspection forks from #176334, followed by the compatible staging sessions in #176665, exposed the missing parent-process retirement. Their intended behavior remains. The two reported obsolete snapshots are still live: the schema assertion aborted before reaching them. This change neither removes nor regenerates any snapshot and preserves all store, Matrix-root, remedy, schema, and source-byte assertions.

## Evidence

prs.title: fix(gateway): workspace sync captures retained test compiler caches
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #176778

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where users running ordinary tests inside a managed coding workspace would have OpenClaw's retained Vitest worker cache (`.artifacts/vitest-worker-cache/`) and Bun transpiler cache (`.cache/bun-transpiler/`) counted as authored workspace changes, so a single test run could add tens of thousands of disposable generated files to the pending result used by refresh, review, and publication preparation.
- **Related:** #175503 / #175956 established the exact-root exclusion policy this gap slipped through (their producer roots were added, these two were not); maintainer triage labels this P2 `impact:session-state` with `clawsweeper:queueable-fix`, `clawsweeper:fix-shape-clear`, `clawsweeper:source-repro`.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** Known disposable test compiler caches stay with the runtime that produced them: both roots are added to the existing exact-root derived-path inventory that workspace capture, transfer, manifest projection, and retained-result recovery all consume, so neither fresh capture nor older authenticated pending results count these files as authored work.
- **Out of scope:** No producer changes (`vitest-worker-cache.mts` / `vitest-process.mts` keep writing the same roots), and no blanket exclusion of `.artifacts/` or `.cache/` — guest-created files under those directories, nested paths, staged inputs, and genuine source conflicts still reconcile exactly as before.
- **Highest-risk area:** Over-exclusion would hide real guest work under the two roots; mitigated by exact-root prefix matching plus negative assertions that neighboring user files (`.artifacts/vitest-worker-cache-notes.md`, `fixtures/.cache/bun-transpiler/input.txt`, etc.) are still captured, transferred, and recovered.

## User Impact

- **Success criteria:** After tests populate both caches, capturing a managed sandbox result no longer includes cache entries; workspace refresh/review preparation is not blocked by them; recovery of an older pending result applies the same classification while preserving authored artifacts and still failing on genuine concurrent source conflicts.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `src/gateway/worker-environments/workspace-path-exclusions.ts` (two added roots) and the regression fixtures in `workspace-generated-paths.test.ts` / `local-workspace-generated-paths.test-support.ts` (capture/transfer plus legacy-manifest expiry/recovery proofs).

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** Isolated worktree of openclaw at commit `8a23c56a833` on Linux (EL8, Node v26.7.0), running the real manifest-capture, rsync-transfer, and projection recovery code paths (real filesystem, real `git fast-import`, no mocks).
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # 1. Regression tests on the unpatched worktree first (RED):
  NODE_OPTIONS="--max-old-space-size=2048" OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=2 capped.sh \
    node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
    src/gateway/worker-environments/workspace-generated-paths.test.ts \
    src/gateway/worker-environments/local-workspace-projection.test.ts
  # 2. Apply the exclusion fix, then the same suites plus full validation:
  skills/fix-pr/scripts/validate.sh \
    src/gateway/worker-environments/workspace-path-exclusions.ts \
    src/gateway/worker-environments/workspace-generated-paths.test.ts \
    src/gateway/worker-environments/local-workspace-generated-paths.test-support.ts
  # 3. Directed test-type shard for the touched directory:
  OPENCLAW_TYPECHECKER=tsgo capped.sh \
    node scripts/run-tsgo.mts -b test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-other.json --builders 1
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  workspace-generated-paths.test.ts > excludes only generated runtime roots from capture and transfer
    ✓ 363ms  (capture manifest, remote manifest, rsync transfer, size-limit assertions)
  local-workspace-projection.test.ts: Test Files 1 passed (1) — Tests 27 passed | 1 skipped (28)
  validate.sh: oxfmt ✓  oxlint ✓  vitest ✓  tsgo:core ✓ (exit 0)
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** Cache entries under `.artifacts/vitest-worker-cache/` and `.cache/bun-transpiler/` are absent from captured manifests and rsync transfers; projection expiry and legacy pending-result recovery succeed with cache churn present while neighboring authored files (`-notes.md`, nested `fixtures/` paths) are preserved in both copies and concurrent source edits still produce a conflict.
- **Before evidence:** Same suites on the unpatched worktree fail through the real production paths: `Error: Cloud workspace result is too large: .artifacts/vitest-worker-cache/run-cache-0/package.json` (manifest comparison) and `Error: Local sandbox has unaccepted edits; restore its worktree before cleanup` (projection expiry) — 4 failed / 24 passed before the two-root fix.
- **What was not tested:** A live managed sandbox refresh against the reporter's historical 20,191-file pending result was not executed locally; the classification behavior is proven through the repo's own integration fixtures (real capture/recovery code paths) instead. CI lanes (full `check:test-types`, `test-projects --changed`) run on GitHub Actions.
- **Proof tier:** L2
- **Proof limitations:** none
- **Review state:** Awaiting CI + maintainer review

prs.title: fix: preserve assistant answers when media delivery reuses response indexes
prs.body:
Current candidate: `b117f1cdda06525f0e30f7428760de4470efbaa5`. **Wrapper inventory is byte-identical to incorporated main `b569c88b9274e61a12b8d7eb9f170d18ac48a1d7`; all 20 existing wrapper tests pass.** [Fresh CI run 38199808511](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38199808511) **passed on this exact head** (61 successful jobs, 26 skipped). The [current-head ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166568#issuecomment-6036679963), updated 2026-10-12 at 03:50:42 UTC, reports **zero code findings** and a remaining real-behavior proof hold. Upstream Telegram Test Server QA remains outstanding; this is not merge approval.

Closes #166536

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes earlier assistant answers being changed or later replies being suppressed when media delivery follows streamed content or a retry that reuses response indexes.

## User Impact

Media enrichment keeps the original model content and signatures intact and attaches display media to the response that actually produced it. Distinct responses can deliver the same text or image without being mistaken for duplicate sends.

This prevents future corruption; it does not restore already-altered history. There is no schema migration, model change, approval-policy change, or session reset. Released unreceipted CLI/SDK paths retain their existing separate contract.

Native runtime proof is recorded. Review and CI results below are bound to their stated historical heads; the latest conflict refresh and exact-candidate Telegram QA handoff are recorded in the final evidence section. A real locally activated package, normal-model media-bearing turns, subsequent genuine multi-turn compaction and retained canonical content were observed on the earlier integrated candidate. Full reused-index retry/plan reproduction, Telegram Test Server proof and the repaired Android attachment-tap flow remain pending; no physical-print success is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Stream indexes count content items and can restart during retries, so they cannot identify a committed transcript row. The existing session owner now publishes an ephemeral receipt for each physical assistant message and fills its exact row ID after persistence, without delaying streaming callbacks or changing synchronous listener semantics. Delivery carries that same receipt; deduplication retains stable occurrence and per-content identity, and the worker-owned transcript correction selects its committed ID with existing generation, turn and live-authority gates. Content indexes distinguish media supplements; they never grant committed-row authority.

Display enrichment preserves canonical provider bytes and uses the committed response's own caption, not a streamed tail. Hook-suppressed responses may contribute occurrence-owned non-text media supplements without recreating model-facing text.

The fixture follow-up associates existing runtime test producers with their actual append-returned receipts, preserving canonical signed content separately from the display projection. It also removes two genuinely unused test imports and narrows the existing transcript-entry union without casts or suppressed assertions. Separately scoped plan-follow-up prompt/documentation changes are not included in this PR.

## Evidence

- Before-fix reproduction through the actual worker-backed persistence entry point corrupts a distinct signed completion; the issue contains the failing snapshot invariant. A separate real session/subscriber regression fails on the unmodified base because physical message receipts do not exist.
- Delivery regressions fail on the original implementation: reused indexes/content suppress later physical responses, and final dispatch sends one response instead of two. After-fix checks preserve distinct deliveries and legacy/messaging-tool behavior.
- Historical pre-reconciliation selected local run: 13 files, 390 tests passed across 6 native Vitest shards using `pnpm test <files> --maxWorkers=1`; wall time 415.06 seconds, including 39.069 seconds of initial compiled-worker preparation. This covers source publication and synchronous listener replacement, kept/segmented/yielded output, identical responses, streamed tails, superseded media-only output, suppressed appends, canonical signature preservation, generation/session revocation, and existing delivery safeguards. These results describe the earlier candidate and fixture follow-up, not the reconciled October 9 head. The current-base integration checks are recorded below. These are local results, not new exact-head GitHub CI.
- New worker-backed media-source integration: 4 cases, 32.78-second local shard (approximately 21.1 seconds in tests). The new actual session/subscriber regression: 1 case, 9.55-second local shard (669 ms in test). These exercise real persistence/materialization owners; no new Gateway boot, timers, polling, remote media requests or printer effects. CI elapsed seconds remain unmeasured.
- Existing directive suite: the original fixture run had 124 passed / 3 failed; repaired fixtures passed all 127 cases. The final suite took 60.66 seconds in a 209.14-second grouped run with the commentary sibling. The final actual session/subscriber check passed 1/1 in 30.72 seconds. No new directive/commentary cases were added.
- Historical pre-reconciliation production core typechecking passed. All 27 native test-type partitions passed after correcting the test's union discrimination and completing the remaining native partitions; the original aggregate type command failed before that correction and is not reported as green. Full-scope changed lint initially found the two unused imports; after removal, resumed native lint and the eight remaining guards passed. All three Knip scans passed with zero unused exports. The complete four-fixture changed gate independently passed, including gateway-methods types (17.0 seconds), agents-sessions types (88.2 seconds), formatting, ratchets, lint and the three Knip scans.
- Independent repository autoreview completed scoped-clean for P0/P1 findings on the full repair and scoped-clean for P0–P2 findings on the final four-fixture delta. The final review preserved all canonical/display, GC and cancellation assertions. No additional CI run, ready-for-review transition or merge was requested.


### Real local setup: media turns and subsequent compaction (2026-10-07)

The supported native updater activated committed candidate `190042328f3e7d88570a388163820e4b67836c5e` after a verified backup and canonical full package build. Gateway readiness, channel readiness, settled state and expected running build all passed; the installed Lossless plugin bytes remained unchanged. This local candidate contains the same receipt/media production repair as the PR plus the separately scoped completion-preservation prompt change; it is not claimed as a deployment of the pure PR head. Existing sessions, model selection and thresholds were preserved.

Actual native `chat.send` turns used the operator's unchanged normal vision-capable model and installed CAD tools, not mocked completions or supplied test receipts. The initial preview completed in 506578 ms; a subsequent reference-based visual iteration completed in 697324 ms and delivered actual front/isometric PNG media; genuine same-session print preparation completed in 190180 ms. The agent inspected real image blocks and a fresh camera image and stopped before sending because objects visibly occupied the plate. Preparation and tool-generated confirmation do not constitute human print approval.

An initial single-user trial's supported `sessions.compact` returned `compacted:false`, `rounds:0`; that was explicitly recorded as a no-op, not summary proof. After genuine multi-turn preparation, the same supported path returned:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "compacted": true,
  "reason": "compacted",
  "tokensBefore": 33532,
  "tokensAfter": 23777,
  "rounds": 1,
  "targetTokens": 196608
}
```

The installed package's documented read-only LCM CLI independently reports newly created nonempty leaf summaries at 13:23:29 and 13:23:44 UTC, using the normal model, without deterministic fallback markers. Their content retains the current capacity target and revision. The resulting context has five summaries totaling 2092 tokens and a protected fresh tail of 33 messages/21685 tokens. No raw SQL, manual history repair, session reset, context padding, threshold reduction or model switch.

Supported native `sessions.get`, privately filtered by the exact committed response ID, preserves the full media-bearing response across this compaction: 2596 characters, SHA256 `1f44f3cec9c55f9409e2be82ff55a80bd6c6603d07d54262ad2c418b1d1bf328` before and after, both own MEDIA directives retained, and two separate managed-image display blocks retained. The default redacted export truncates path-containing canonical strings at 2000 characters; that export truncation was not misclassified as another transcript mutation.

**Limits:** this proves real native turns, actual summaries and canonical preservation across this observed compaction. It does not provide an independent full pre-delivery provider reference, exercise every reused-index retry/plan boundary, demonstrate a provider signature absent from this normal-model output, or prove Android attachment tapping. The original damaged session remains preserved and unrepaired. Raw private transcripts, media, credentials and endpoint URLs are not published.

### Unresolved local commentary failures

The uninstrumented native commentary sibling is **not reported as fixed or green**. Its latest original-order run had 15 passed / 2 failed: the `aborted` case encountered `ENOENT` when checking the outgoing-originals directory, and `gc-with-unknown-commit` found zero first-original records where one was required. An earlier run also encountered the same zero-first-record condition in `gc-with-revocation-after-commit`. These failures occur before the transcript rewrite and remain investigated but unattributed.

`pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-commentary-media.test.ts src/agents/sessions/agent-session-assistant-source.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` took 143.48 seconds; the commentary shard took 97.45 seconds. A focused GC-revocation check passed 1/1 in 35.00 seconds. An independently bootstrapped, unchanged `5077ad4` baseline passed all 17 commentary cases in original order (180.80 seconds including compilation). A single diagnostic run observing the existing preparation boundaries also passed 17/17 (143.68 seconds including compilation), capturing only expected post-revocation writer-claim errors, not the missing first-original failure. Temporary observation was removed and exact source bytes restored.

An additional October 8 selected run also remains unresolved: the first six-file group had 98 passed / 1 failed, and the combined selected suite had 159 passed / 1 failed. The commentary `worktree` case observed one HTTP request where zero was expected (line 420), before the transcript rewrite. Bounded inspection found the upstream local-root/path-normalization owner unchanged by this PR, but no matched baseline reproduction was obtained. No subsequent resolution was established; this is not attributed to main and the commentary suite is not reported as green.

Those passing runs do not establish the earlier failures' cause or prove a fix. No GC/cancellation expectation was weakened, no failure was masked, and no inherited-CI exception is claimed. The unresolved first-original preparation behavior, full reused-index retry/plan proof, independent pre-delivery canonical reference, and Android attachment-open checks remain explicit evidence gaps. The scoped real native compaction result above is not a repair claim for these remaining gaps.

### Current-main conflict reconciliation (2026-10-09)

Earlier reconciled head: `765ae320713714128a68b3f8b8b4e5da12fb8695`. Two normal merges retain the original `bcaf716cb78e8f2c7119e643ce379af0f36a54b4` ancestry: the previously prepared `57dd17b4ea39b5f5d87db9faabaa2f0b10fa83f4` integration, followed by current-main snapshot `063f8a1cc4a015351e4b2d3aecf15d8483df930a`. Current head is normal follow-up `78d6b55e32d6a93db691ff77e7e7d798e0692ec8`, whose parent is the CI/review repair `89425ebe0c7315ba5fa09d287969de34a4a93f62`, both described below. No force-push or history replacement.

The repair retains exact committed-response receipts, canonical content preservation and occurrence-scoped media deduplication while incorporating upstream directive, media-normalization and captured-read-source changes. The fallback single-answer guard now uses upstream's `answerDirectives.length` after its earlier `answerTexts` variable was removed. Both new fixture conflicts resolve to byte-identical current-upstream dispatch test/helper files; their captured-boundary and revocation assertions remain intact.

- Final current-main worker-backed check: 4 files, 64 tests passed across 3 native shards in 418.79 seconds, including 51.56 seconds of current-source worker compilation. The selected files are `chat-send-reply-dispatch.test.ts`, `chat-send-reply-dispatch.media-source.test.ts`, `chat-transcript-persistence.mirrors.test.ts`, and `agent-session-assistant-source.test.ts`. This covers the upstream delivery snapshot/captured-boundary cases and the repair's exact-row media/canonical preservation cases. Local elapsed time is not measured CI seconds.
- Before the second integration, 6 files / 99 tests passed in 172.95 seconds, including payload directive handling, occurrence-scoped block suppression and final dispatch deduplication. That is prior-candidate evidence, not a claim that every file was rerun on the published head.
- Fresh independent AutoReview of the full final candidate against the incorporated main completed scoped-clean for P0/P1 findings. It is static review, not live or test-execution evidence.
- The final native changed check passed its completed ratchets, formatting/config/plugin guards and compiler-graph admission, then stopped before production type diagnostics on a retained artifact lock from the terminated October 8 worker. The exact task-owned lock was inspected; its owner and associated build/check descendants were absent, and it was moved recoverably outside the worktree. The interrupted aggregate is **not reported as green**. The earlier pre-refresh changed run was also intentionally interrupted after guards when newer upstream fixture conflicts were found.
- Recovered and completed author checks on published head `765ae320`: production core typechecking passed; relevant native test graphs passed (`agents-root` 149.1 seconds, `agents-other` 207.8 seconds, `agents-sessions` 137.2 seconds, `gateway-methods` 143.0 seconds, `messaging` 121.9 seconds). The final four-graph serial batch completed with exit 0 in 613 wall-clock seconds. Exact 30-path native type-aware lint passed with zero errors and warnings in 53.9 seconds. This is bounded affected-graph proof, not a new run of all 27 test partitions.
- Coercion-declaration and deprecated-API checks passed. The completed native database-first legacy-store, media-download, runtime-sidecar-loader, import-cycle, native-state-schema, webhook-body-order, pairing-store-group and pairing-account-scope guards passed. Import-cycle checking found zero runtime value cycles.
- The native unused-export guard is **not green**: its production scan flags `bindCliQuestionAnswerAuthority` (`src/agents/cli-runner/tool-authority.ts`), `prepareSessionEventTargetForHost` (`src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-handoff.ts`), `readSessionEntryCreationTransition` (`src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-entry-cache-publication.ts`), and `RESTART_CONTINUATION_CONTEXT_PREFIX` (`src/infra/heartbeat-events-filter.ts`). The full-tree scan flags the latter two; the script scan passes with zero entries. The guard finished with exit 1 in 199 seconds. Bounded inspection verifies those four files are byte-identical to incorporated main `063f8a1`, and none of those symbol names occurs in the introduced diff. No matched baseline scan was obtained; this is not an inherited-failure attribution, a claim that main caused it, or a passing aggregate.
- Current-head ClawSweeper revision 4 completed October 9 at 04:35 UTC with zero findings, sufficient scoped native proof and readiness for maintainer review ([review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166568#issuecomment-6036679963)). This is independent review, not an assertion that the outstanding behavior gaps are repaired. Before the October 9 ready-for-review transition, current-head hosted CI, including `openclaw/ci-gate`, was **SKIPPED**; that is historical skipped coverage, not a passing result. Required CI after readiness must be evaluated separately on this exact head.

The PR was marked ready for maintainer review on October 9 after current-head ClawSweeper revision 5 reported no remaining contributor-facing blockers. Exact-head GitHub CI and maintainer review are separate gates; no bypass, model change, operator Gateway restart, session mutation or printer action was performed. The historical commentary failures and the full retry/plan, independent provider-reference and Android attachment-open gaps above remain unresolved; passing focused checks do not establish their cause or repair them.

### New CI and review follow-through (2026-10-09)

Hosted [CI run 37957596281](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37957596281) completed **failure** on author head `765ae320`. Its substantive failed job is `check-guards-architecture`; the required aggregate also fails. The runtime-value import-cycle check passed with zero cycles, but the subsequent Madge static-import check found one large strongly connected component. GitHub tested merge `9713ff5fae46f002f15a9535d6e1793c8e49b0bc`, whose parents are base `62355575c041dee0491658d4d1bc024d9fb3fc6b` and author head `765ae320`, not the latest fetched main.

The matched native comparison uses separate frozen-lockfile installs and the unchanged repository guard: the exact base passes both checks with zero cycles (static check 44 seconds); the exact tested merge passes the runtime-value check but fails the static check with one cycle (50 seconds). The local and hosted failures contain the same 958 component members. This is an introduced architecture failure, not an inherited failure. The follow-up below cuts the receipt-only import from `reply-payload.ts` into the broad session type module over to a dependency-free receipt contract; no guard exception or weakened baseline.

A [new P1 review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166568#discussion_r4232262707) identifies a separate missing case: multiple streamed media blocks within the same assistant occurrence can collapse to the last block when execution aborts before aggregate `message_end`. Existing distinct-occurrence tests did not cover this case. The following pushed repair addresses content-index-aware finalization and supplemental persistence; the earlier no-findings verdict alone does not establish current merge readiness.

### Published CI/review repair: `89425ebe0c7315ba5fa09d287969de34a4a93f62`

- Moved the existing two-field readonly receipt contract to dependency-free `src/agents/sessions/assistant-transcript-source.ts`, migrating receipt-only imports without a compatibility re-export, duplicate definition, stored schema or public setting. Both unchanged native cycle guards now pass with zero cycles: runtime 33 seconds, static/Madge 34 seconds. This fixes the introduced SCC; it does not waive it.
- Finalization and fallback supplemental append identity now retain occurrence plus content index, including the legacy index-only fallback. Repeated same-index delivery replaces its earlier payload; distinct indexes survive interrupted execution, including identical image URLs and identical failure cards. Committed row selection, generation/session/live-authority gates and canonical provider bytes remain unchanged.
- A private, in-memory producer fact identifies actual complete aggregates. It is emitted only by `message_end`'s parsed final reply or the selected canonical final-answer producer, not inferred from a generic final flush, a committed receipt or URL coverage. Recovery clears it when replacing source custody. Coalescing additionally requires actual coverage of preceding URLs and counted failure tuples. No serialized transcript/config/model-prompt contract changes.
- Red-first cases reproduced the reviewed attachment loss. A first fixture lacked visible failure content and was corrected rather than counted as target proof. Independent review then found an equal-failure-card edge in the first coverage heuristic; equal-card and identical-URL partial cases both failed before the producer-owned marker correction. All those diagnostics remain preserved; the heuristic is not the published repair.
- Final candidate native verification: **153 tests across five files/shards**, runner 288.91 seconds / wrapper 290 seconds: payload owner 51, actual session receipt publication 1, media-source persistence 12, existing dispatcher 45, terminal preparation 44. The real session regression verifies the producer's completed-response marker; recovery cases verify clearing it. Media-source shard duration 62.33 seconds. These are owner-boundary proofs, not a new full live provider/retry or Android run.
- Native production core types passed in 108 seconds. Four affected native test graphs passed serially: agents-root 109.2 seconds, agents-other 89.8 seconds, agents-sessions 82.1 seconds, gateway-methods 106.8 seconds; aggregate wrapper 389 seconds. Exact 15-path lint passed with zero warnings/errors (37 seconds); formatting, whitespace, line-cap and max-lines ratchets passed without exceptions.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a visible `sessions_spawn` child can fail before its first reply when an agent-written task contains slash-command prose such as `/model command`.

## User Impact

Agents can discuss slash commands in delegated tasks without executing them. The child starts on the requested model and receives the complete task as prompt text. Use the spawn `model` parameter to choose its model.

## Why This Change Was Made

Visible spawns create the child through `sessions.create` with trusted spawn metadata. The opening turn now carries an internal-only agent-authored-input option into the existing command-suppression path. No public wire field, configuration option or additional authority is introduced.

External authority admission remains intact. Ordinary human commands, direct send/steer behavior, custody and lifecycle controls are preserved. The correction also updates creation fixtures to observe the actual creation entry point and integrates current-main test helpers without restoring obsolete fixtures.

## Evidence

Published correction: `7acafc456bcd72c26beee1fff30db5978297f9b2`.

- [Current focused remote proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39190221175): **247 passing cases** across all 12 complete candidate test files, with no failures, errors or skips. All 19 changed paths passed formatting; scoped production/test lint and delta whitespace checks passed.
- Retained causal negatives failed at the intended command-suppression boundaries, while ordinary-command and provenance controls passed. Their production blobs and baseline preimages remain unchanged through integration. Earlier verifier failures remain preserved rather than rewritten as passes.
- [Real isolated Gateway flow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39187789597): visible `sessions_spawn` reached trusted creation and completed with the full literal task intact. Both child provider requests and public session metadata retained the requested child model; history, the second waited `sessions_send` and no-announce assertions passed.
- The complete integrated 19-path candidate received a fresh structured review with no actionable findings. Source/dependency restoration and owned-child joins were verified, and native cleanup completed. The Testbox workflow was cancelled during owned cleanup after its proof payload had passed; that Actions conclusion is not the test result. The initial cleanup settlement timeout remains recorded, and supported same-ID reconciliation completed successfully.

The Gateway flow uses a synthetic Responses SSE provider, not an authenticated external model provider. It is retained old-base evidence with unchanged production and relevant fixture/helper sources, not a newly executed integrated-head E2E. Changed-check planning was a dry run, not a passed broad gate.

Exact published-head hosted CI, including required type/build checks, is pending: [CI run 39192429492](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39192429492), currently in progress. Native publication records pending GitHub gates, not successful CI. Completed-hosted preparation and all enforced checks/reviews remain required before landing.

prs.title: perf(gateway): simplify connect preparation and measure reconnect waves
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Connect preparation repeats work, and reconnect investigations need to separate authentication, profile attachment, hello snapshot/descriptor assembly, and transport writes.

## User Impact

Admin snapshots consistently report the config and state paths selected at startup. Connect preparation avoids one redundant profile catalog lease when access policies are enabled. Authentication, revocation, scopes, disclosure, and uncompressed hello replies retain their existing contracts. No migration or configuration change is required. **The measured connect-latency result is neutral; this does not claim to fix the previously observed one-second tail.**

## Why This Change Was Made

Profile authority already owns catalog preparation, so its caller no longer prepares/releases that catalog first. Snapshot assembly reads the runtime selector's live `CONFIG_PATH` alongside `STATE_DIR` instead of constructing config I/O for its path. Work removed per applicable connect: catalog preparations 2 → 1 when access policies exist; snapshot config-I/O constructions 1 → 0. Live authority checks remain at their existing boundaries.

Nested snapshot/descriptor timings extend existing connect logs. The existing restart benchmark gains warm reconnect waves with signed paired devices, trusted-proxy attribution, negotiated permessage-deflate, retained per-attempt timings, and synchronized starts. Model catalog publication already runs after hello; hello itself intentionally remains uncompressed because it can contain credentials.

Runtime production delta: six redundant preparation lines removed, six instrumentation lines added, net zero. The requested non-test/non-doc diff is +351 lines: benchmark/helper +316 and benchmark README +35. The behavioral regression adds 33 test lines; logging documentation adds six. No new cache or competing owner is introduced.

## Evidence

Focused proof passed: 68 health/connect tests, 5 WebSocket helper tests, changed-file formatting/lint, and one targeted `pnpm tsgo:core` lane using the native checker. The pinned-path regression failed on the base and passes with the change. Independent Codex review and focused correction reviews completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings. PR review caught two reporting issues, both addressed: descriptor timing now includes hello feature construction, and warm reconnect ELU samples exclude intervals beginning before measurement.

### Paired reconnect measurement

Two simultaneous A/B pairs on an isolated 128-CPU Linux host, 16 allowed CPUs per side, under an exclusive measurement lock. Pair 2 swaps the CPU halves. Separate fixtures use the same seed and timestamp: 5,000 sessions, 6,000 retained runs, 200 approvals, 100 cron jobs, 12 projects/worktrees, and 1 MiB of transcript text. Each side holds 40 clients; 30 reconnect while 10 poll bounded session/catalog/project lists every five seconds. Twenty waves per pair cross the periodic device-access bookkeeping interval.

Baseline is `c2549f8295d09f520f119de44d77e1c7dc25779a`; candidate applies the two preparation simplifications. Both builds contain the corrected phase instrumentation. Relevant connect/profile/path owners remained unchanged through the required main rebases. The later ELU reporting-only correction is applied when analyzing retained samples; it does not change individual connect timings.

All **2,400 measured connects** and **2,400 background RPCs** succeeded. All 2,400 connect responses matched server phase logs and contained 41 presence rows. Measured starts differed by 0 ms and 1 ms. Values below are milliseconds; differences are candidate minus baseline within each pair.

| Pair | Connect p50 A → B | Δ p50 | Connect p95 A → B | Connect p99 A → B | Δ p99 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 3.426 → 3.466 | +0.040 | 5.798 → 5.534 | 8.376 → 8.586 | +0.210 |
| 2, CPUs swapped | 3.426 → 3.444 | +0.018 | 5.513 → 5.457 | 7.911 → 8.276 | +0.366 |

| Server phase p99 | Pair 1 A → B | Pair 2 A → B |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Auth | 0.439 → 0.411 | 0.438 → 0.415 |
| Attachment | 0.661 → 0.574 | 0.637 → 0.613 |
| Snapshot | 0.226 → 0.184 | 0.200 → 0.197 |
| Hello descriptors | 0.187 → 0.172 | 0.149 → 0.177 |
| Whole hello preparation | 0.755 → 0.580 | 0.637 → 0.582 |
| Send | 0.252 → 0.239 | 0.238 → 0.261 |
| Logged connect response | 2 → 2 | 2 → 2 |

Socket-open/challenge p99 was 123.54 → 96.94 ms and 103.34 → 97.67 ms, much larger than server response time. Full socket-to-hello p99 was 128.31 → 100.49 ms and 107.76 → 101.57 ms. These differences do not establish a causal speedup from this small cleanup. Background RPC p99 held or improved in both pairs.

Maximum connect RPC time flipped direction: 22.17 → 12.33 ms, then 11.97 → 16.13 ms. The latter candidate outlier correlates with a 2 ms server response (1.77 ms summed auth/attach/hello/send), so its extra latency is outside those preparation phases. The small p99 movements (+2.5%, +4.6%) are treated as neutral, not a performance win. The old one-second handler tail was not reproduced.

Outside CPU activity from `mpstat -P 96-127` averaged 8.26% and 4.93% during the paired captures, recorded for context rather than rejecting either run. Full-interval ELU medians were 0.486 → 0.487 and 0.494 → 0.473 after excluding the initial warmup-spanning sample.

Acceptance was recorded before measurement: compare paired p50/p99, retain errors, investigate movements over 20%, and allow an explicitly requested simplification with neutral results. Default fixture authentication is shared-token plus signed-device auth; the additional access-policy catalog deletion is source-proven but not represented by this fixture. External identity-provider latency and detached Control UI model catalog publication are outside this workload.

Setup failures were excluded before a valid pair: the baseline's temporary `dist-a` name broke worker resolution, then its relocated runtime lacked a root launcher. A canonical runtime layout fixed both; an unmeasured setup check passed before the two successful pairs. No failed measured attempts were removed.

Reproduce after generating isolated fixtures; run both revisions concurrently with separate ports/state and the same future start:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/post-restart-burst-measure.ts \
  --state-dir /path/to/team-shape --entry <revision>/dist/entry.js \
  --reconnect-waves --clients 40 --waves 20 \
  --start-at <shared-future-unix-ms> --port <isolated-port> --mock-port <distinct-port>
```

### CI attribution

Final-head [CI run 39191045816](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39191045816) completed for `378a22a9b9791ca8ecbcfcd1a580f8d558025293`. Every substantive job passed except [`check-test-types` (117864285446)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39191045816/job/117864285446); `openclaw/ci-gate` failed downstream. Security, lint, production types, core test types, and selected test jobs passed. The sole error is inherited: the unchanged `extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-subagent-monitor.parent-retention.test.ts:37` passes the removed `completionDeliveryRetryDelaysMs` option (TS2353). The same single-test typecheck on unchanged main parent `05ba3b9f64899c183ca3cbeb9beab6963340d9ee` reproduced exactly TS2353 (exit 2), with no other errors. Test and options file SHA-256 values match Git blobs from that parent. The CI classifier called it new because its selected scope was not compared; the direct parent reproduction establishes inheritance. No retry was used to chase green.

Baseline proof used the canonical checker wrapper with a temporary config extending `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json`, retaining its declaration includes but selecting only `native-subagent-monitor.parent-retention.test.ts`:

```sh
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p .local/parent-retention-types.json --incremental
# native-subagent-monitor.parent-retention.test.ts(37,5): TS2353
# completionDeliveryRetryDelaysMs does not exist in MonitorOptions
# exit 2 on unchanged main parent
```

Landing uses the explicitly authorized inherited-failure exception, not a claim that CI is green. The native PR workflow requires an additional canonical worktree, contrary to this lane's one-worktree constraint; the authorized fallback pins the exact reviewed head for the squash merge.

prs.title: fix(gmi): GPT-5.6 tool turns fail with a reasoning_effort 400
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: every agent turn that uses tools on `gmi/openai/gpt-5.6-sol` fails with `400 Function tools with reasoning_effort are not supported for gpt-5.6-sol in /v1/chat/completions`.

## User Impact

User impact: GMI Cloud's OpenAI GPT-5.x models can call tools again. For tool turns, GPT-5.6 sends `reasoning_effort: "none"`, and GPT-5.5 / GPT-5.4 Mini omit the field, matching what OpenAI's Chat Completions API accepts. Turns without tools, other GMI models, and other providers are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

GMI forwards OpenAI's Chat Completions contract verbatim. OpenClaw already applies this tools-plus-reasoning rule, but only to known OpenAI endpoints and unprefixed ids, while GMI uses vendor-prefixed ids (`openai/gpt-5.6-sol`).

- The rule moves into one shared helper, so the native OpenAI path and GMI use the same owner.
- GMI's payload hook applies it to its `openai/` models. The prefix is stripped only to classify the model; the outbound model id is unchanged.
- No new config option or public SDK contract; the helper goes through the existing private provider-stream seam.

OpenRouter is deliberately untouched: it translates requests to Responses and accepts reasoning with tools.

## Evidence

- Live, before: tool round trip on `gmi/openai/gpt-5.6-sol` failed with GMI relaying OpenAI's 400 (`param: reasoning_effort`). The same model answered without tools, and a raw GMI request with the same tools and no `reasoning_effort` returned `tool_calls`.
- Live, after: the real agent run (`openclaw agent --local`, read tool on a workspace file) on `gmi/openai/gpt-5.6-sol` returned the exact file nonce 2/2. Native `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` still passes.
- Same sweep for context: 18/22 providers completed the tool round trip on main. The others were account-side (NVIDIA 403, a Qwen plan mismatch, OpenRouter billing on one model) plus this GMI bug.
- Unit: 47 core completions-param tests and GMI tests (both stream paths, affected model families, no-tools, unrelated routes).
- Autoreview: scoped-clean at P2.

### CI qualification

[CI run 39191076150](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39191076150) completed on `8a0baadcf78c4a78059d72ff5b49c068639e4922`, after a conflict-free, patch-identical rebase incorporating the upstream root-help repair `e63269c28a2` and SidebarProjectionMemo export repair `e070647a0cf`.

The only underlying failure is inherited: `check-test-types` reports TS2353 at `extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-subagent-monitor.parent-retention.test.ts:37`, because `completionDeliveryRetryDelaysMs` is no longer a `MonitorOptions` property. Scheduled-main run [39191176869](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39191176869), job `117864340952`, reports the identical diagnostic. Both the test and its type-owner blobs match that main head (`a8771a5a154c67f26b5ab7e0002672ad0bfac8bd`) exactly. A clean detached main checkout at `a9e5f4e3b7b2114caa573554766ab7b4850b39e4` also reproduces the same error with `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --pretty false`.

All other 71 jobs completed without failure; the aggregate CI gate failed downstream of the inherited type error. CI is not green. No failed job was rerun and no tests or baselines were weakened. The GMI patch itself is unchanged by the rebase; coordinator live proof and scoped-clean review are retained.

prs.title: fix(workers): reclaim idle buffers and reduce catalog decoder memory
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Catalog decoder workers retain unrelated runtime modules, and completed large buffers can remain uncollected when JavaScript heap growth stays below the idle-GC threshold.

## User Impact

Lower decoder overhead and reclamation of dead external buffers while keeping workers warm. No configuration, schema or supported public SDK change. This is a bounded improvement, not a demonstrated fix for the separate multi-GiB Gateway report or a guarantee that RSS returns to the OS.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep catalog routing, terminal text helpers and admission transport on lightweight imports. Heap and external-memory growth have independent anchors in the existing idle collector, preserving its threshold, burst debounce, cancellation and warm-worker reuse. The terminal facade remains official-plugin-private.

Shared transport state and task scopes use one lightweight context; native clean-close seals remain at the native owner. Current decoded-fact envelopes, process-lived physical facts, loader custody, revocation, reader scope and worker publications are preserved.

## Evidence

Signed head `71f0fae2b5a0d36e81a656053fb6509dd0f496d5` integrates all three canonical main repairs: [#175964](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175964) (`5b64c3d0`), [#176337](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176337) (`6c9dbe3c`), and [#176380](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176380) (`11185974`). Each landed under required exact-head CI: [first repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39084888904), 52 passed / 26 skipped; [QA fixture](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39156211808), 34 passed / 27 skipped; [timeout handoff](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39161556482), 33 passed / 28 skipped. Landed repair blobs, signatures, main ancestry and native completion receipts are verified.

The worker feature remains **27 paths (+420/−300)**. The state-owner conflict preserves all five current-main error constructors unchanged in the existing lightweight owner, re-exported through the record facade; current-main holder diagnostics, process-lived physical facts and ownership identity logic remain intact. No additional runtime behavior, authority relaxation, schema or public SDK surface was added.

Qualification on macOS arm64, Node24.16 and verified repository-pinned Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+7bd4fdff3`:

- Reviewed candidate `62f531b5b73c0f31077f7705bfb66e7f0d257d4b` passed **111 cases / 9 files**: admission retention/publications, current state-owner contracts, worker lifecycle/idle GC, real warm-worker heap/external payload finalization and reuse, catalog worker/preview behavior and SDK generation. Core/infra/state-logging types, owner typed lint, SDK contracts and formatting passed. Fresh whole-feature P0–P2 review was scoped-clean.
- Final signed tree `2249e92f37487849ae6f25fa011e8df2e3e28c04` preserves all 27 reviewed authored line deltas and every worker-feature blob. Worker/catalog source/tests, dependency lock, Bun pin, runner and type configurations are unchanged. The earlier 111-case proof and whole-feature independent review are **reused**, not represented as new final-tree replays/reviews.
- Main changed state-owner and catalog dependencies, so the three affected test files were replayed on this final tree: **64 cases passed**, across two native shards in **56.43 seconds** (21 state-owner cases; 43 catalog worker/preview cases). Core and infra-test type checks, meaningful staged 27-path size admission and whitespace checks pass. Earlier SDK export/surface, typed lint and formatting proof remains valid on unchanged inputs; the normal signed-commit hook passed.


Exact-head [worker CI39163774101](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39163774101), attempt 1, **passed: 150 jobs passed / 20 skipped**. It was triggered naturally by the signed integration push; no unchanged push, rerun or manual dispatch was requested. Both reported required `openclaw/ci-gate` checks pass. GitHub confirms signed head `71f0fae2b5a0d36e81a656053fb6509dd0f496d5`, a verified signature and conflict-free, mergeable state. The completed [exact-head ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171524#issuecomment-6225770266) has no actionable findings and no before-merge items; its production-memory proof limitation remains explicit below. **The feature PR remains open and unmerged, with auto-merge off.**
