prs.title: fix: preserve Error identity for structured retry failures
prs.body:
Closes #126227

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes structured retry failures losing their `Error` identity when a parsed JSON payload contains an own enumerable `__proto__` field. Callers can otherwise receive a value typed as `Error` for which `instanceof Error` is false.

## User Impact

Retry failures and direct error normalization retain `Error.prototype`, the original cause, and diagnostic fields such as `code` and `status`. Existing Error values retain their identity. No configuration, dependencies, or data migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing coercers assign diagnostic fields onto a new Error. Assigning `__proto__` invokes an inherited setter and replaces that Error's prototype. Copy enumerable fields in their existing order and read each value as before, but skip only the `__proto__` target assignment. Single-field `Object.assign` preserves target assignment/throw behavior and existing field descriptors.

Apply the same repair to the canonical normalizer, the dependency-free retry package, and both standalone bootstrap-script copies. The stricter `toStructuredErrorObject` has a different isolation contract and remains unchanged.

This resumes the closed, unmerged #126237; credit to RabbitDong-on for the report and ruel225 for the previous implementation and compatibility analysis.

## Evidence

**Built public SDK proof, before and after:** Node 26.8.2 on macOS arm64, baseline `b0f778e76`. A standalone Node consumer resolved the actual built package exports for `openclaw/plugin-sdk/retry-runtime`, `error-runtime`, and `provider-oauth-runtime`. A real loopback HTTP peer returned status 503 with the synthetic JSON body `{"__proto__":{"tag":"synthetic"},"code":"E_UPSTREAM","status":503}`. The consumer rejected with the parsed response and exercised the real retry runner; no retry or normalizer internals were mocked.

| Public entry | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `retryAsync`, after two actual HTTP attempts | `instanceof Error=false`; prototype replaced | `instanceof Error=true`; `Error.prototype` retained |
| `toErrorObject` | `instanceof Error=false`; prototype replaced | `instanceof Error=true`; `Error.prototype` retained |
| `withOAuthLoginAbort` rejection normalization with a live signal | `instanceof Error=false`; prototype replaced | `instanceof Error=true`; `Error.prototype` retained |

In all candidate cases `code=E_UPSTREAM`, `status=503`, and the original cause were preserved. Native Error passthrough and unchanged global Object.prototype controls passed. This is public SDK runtime proof using a local HTTP fixture, not an authenticated external-provider claim.

**Regression red/green:** before implementation, eight cross-owner coercion cases and the terminal retry/history regression failed for the intended identity check; 45 compatibility controls passed. Afterward, all **108 focused tests** passed across:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  packages/retry/src/index.test.ts \
  packages/normalization-core/src/error-coercion.test.ts \
  src/infra/retry.test.ts \
  test/scripts/bounded-response.test.ts \
  test/error-coercion-compatibility.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

The shared compatibility table checks all four independent copies: symbol fields, late enumerability changes, native Error field descriptors, harmless `constructor`/`prototype` fields, and propagation of ordinary/proto getter and descriptor failures. The terminal regression also checks the original attempt history.

Runtime builds, targeted strict types for all changed owners/tests, owner lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Fresh independent P0–P2 review is scoped clean with no actionable findings. Broader validation runs in native PR CI.

<details>
<summary>Scope and simplification</summary>

The retry package remains dependency-free, and bootstrap scripts still run without built workspace packages. Those existing boundaries retain their local compact coercers rather than adding a new abstraction or dependency. No new exports, state, or test-only production seams. Production: +41/-4 lines; tests: +135/-0. The new compatibility table supplies one contract across the four existing copies.

</details>


### CI follow-up (current head `7c7966ba96e9`)

[CI run 39131302833](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39131302833) has two failing jobs; this PR is not CI-green.

- `checks-node-changed-8`: five quiet-child restart cases fail because persisted records already lack `operatorRecoverySource` before shutdown. The recovery owner rejects them with “Subagent restart recovery lacks its original operator source.” The source-capture, codec, recovery owner, and failing test are unchanged between this PR's base and head. That native `Error` also takes the unchanged `instanceof Error` return in the modified coercers. These facts do not establish whether the missing source originates in the fixture or an existing production path; there is no passing-baseline claim.
- `android-test-wear`: `appAbortWaitsForRpcOutcomeWhenTerminalPrecedesAck` fails in Robolectric `Flow()` setup while controlling a background Looper (`Flow.idle`), before its abort assertions. Wear sources and build configuration are unchanged by this TypeScript repair. The fixture lifecycle repair is being handled separately in #176119.

The requested secops review of `scripts/lib/bounded-response.mjs` remains outstanding. No CI reruns or unrelated test relaxations were used to obtain a green result.

A local baseline attempt on original base `b0f778e76d5e932d833dbcffb89d2c4c8abf8e0c` selected only the failing complete/unchanged-child case. It stopped before test execution because the required full declaration build lacks optional plugin dependencies on this checkout. This is an environment gap, not a baseline reproduction or passing control; the Node failure attribution remains unresolved.

prs.title: fix(signal): re-probe managed daemon liveness so hangs surface as disconnected
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The managed signal-cli daemon is only proven alive once, at startup (`waitForSignalDaemonReady`). After that, the daemon's SSE endpoint stays idle between inbound Signal events, so a daemon that hangs (deadlocked, wedged on a syscall, etc.) without exiting its process keeps reporting `connected: true` forever — there is no other liveness signal, so the gateway health monitor has nothing to act on and never restarts it (#116295).

## Why This Change Was Made

Added a periodic (60s) liveness probe that re-checks the daemon's own `/api/v1/check` endpoint via the existing `signalCheck` adapter, started once `autoStart` brings the managed daemon up and stopped in the same `finally` block that already tears down the ingress monitor. A successful probe publishes a connected + transport-activity status patch (`createConnectedChannelStatusPatch`/`createTransportActivityStatusPatch`, the same factories the SSE path already uses); a failed probe marks the account `connected: false` with the probe error in `lastError`, which is what the gateway health monitor reads. Wiring reuses the account's existing `setStatus` sink (`createAccountStatusSink`), the same one `startAccount` already writes an initial snapshot through.

## User Impact

A wedged managed signal-cli daemon now flips to disconnected within ~60s of going unresponsive instead of appearing healthy indefinitely, letting the gateway's existing restart/alerting machinery react to it.

## Evidence

- `autoStart` (and therefore the heartbeat) only ever applies to `managed-native` transport, the exact case this issue is about — container-transport accounts don't spawn a daemon here and are unaffected.
- The probe reuses `signalCheck`, the same function `waitForSignalDaemonReady` uses for startup readiness, applied periodically instead of once.

Fixes #116295

prs.title: fix(doctor): archive the removed user-scope systemd unit instead of deleting it
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `dueling` systemd repair in `openclaw doctor` deletes the redundant user-scope gateway unit outright: `uninstallUserSystemdGatewayUnit` in `src/daemon/systemd.ts` calls `fs.unlink(unitPath)` after `systemctl --user disable --now`.

The ownership guard in front of it is sound — the system-scope unit must be both running and enabled at boot, and anything uncheckable fails closed to hints — but the deletion itself is unrecoverable. The unit file is operator-authored and can carry a custom `ExecStart`, drop-in `Environment=` lines, a different `User=`, or resource limits, so the one case the guard cannot cover (a correct-looking ownership signal that was still the wrong call) costs work that is not recoverable from the OpenClaw side.

## Why This Change Was Made

Archive-then-remove is the better default for a file OpenClaw did not author. The unit is now moved rather than unlinked:

- `resolveSystemdUnitArchiveDir` builds `<state dir>/backups/systemd-units/<ISO date>/`, matching the existing doctor-migration archive convention (`resolveStateDir(env)` + `backups/<topic>/`, as in `src/commands/doctor-tools-md-migration.ts`).
- The move is `mkdir` + `copyFile` + `unlink`, not `rename`. `rename` fails with `EXDEV` when the state dir and `$HOME/.config` sit on different filesystems, and copy-before-unlink means a failed write leaves the operator's unit exactly where it was. The `mkdir` runs first so a missing destination directory cannot raise the `ENOENT` that the catch block interprets as "there was no unit file here".
- No retention policy, no restore command, no new config surface. Recovery is the `cp` line printed in the doctor note.

The result field `removed: boolean` is replaced by `archivedPath: string | undefined` rather than adding a second field next to it: the boolean was exactly derivable from the path, and the repo's guidance is to avoid a derived boolean plus a nullable field that callers must keep in sync. The ownership guard, the dueling detection, and the `disabled` semantics (a file-only removal cannot evict a loaded unit, so the conflict is only claimed resolved when `systemctl` actually released it) are unchanged.

## User Impact

An operator who accepts the dueling-scope repair keeps a copy of the unit. The doctor note now names the destination and the exact restore command instead of only stating that the file was removed:

```
Moved user-scope unit <unit path> to:
- <state dir>/backups/systemd-units/<ISO date>/openclaw-gateway.service
Restore it with: cp <archive path> <unit path>
```

Operator-facing wording follows the behavior: the confirmation prompt asks to "Archive the redundant user-scope gateway unit…", and the success/`systemctl`-unavailable/failure lines say "Archived" instead of "Removed". The systemd-side effect is identical to before — the unit is gone from `$HOME/.config/systemd/user`, and `daemon-reload` still runs when systemd was reachable, so the detector and the manager agree.

## Evidence

- `src/daemon/systemd.ts`: `fs.unlink(unitPath)` replaced by `mkdir(archiveDir, {recursive, mode: 0o700})` → `copyFile(unitPath, archiveTarget)` → `unlink(unitPath)`. The `ENOENT` catch branch is preserved, so an already-absent unit still returns without throwing and still logs "User-scope systemd unit not found at …". The `daemon-reload` condition moves from `removed && disabled` to `archivedPath && disabled`, i.e. the same predicate.
- Path shape: `resolveStateDir(env)` is the same helper the other doctor archives use, so the destination honors `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and legacy state-dir discovery instead of hardcoding a home-relative path. This is the operator-facing "backup of a file the operator authored" artifact class, not runtime state, so a file on disk is the right store.
- `src/commands/doctor-gateway-services.ts`: only the messaging branch changed — `result.archivedPath` selects the note text, and the `result.disabled` branch that decides whether to claim the conflict is resolved is untouched.
- Existing tests updated to the new result shape and wording: `src/daemon/systemd.test.ts` now asserts the archived file exists with the original unit bytes (the reversibility invariant this change is for), that the source path is gone, and `archivedPath === undefined` on the already-absent path; `src/commands/doctor-gateway-services.test.ts` fixtures return `archivedPath` and assert the "Archived the redundant user-scope gateway unit…" log line. No new test files.
- Call-site audit: `uninstallUserSystemdGatewayUnit` has exactly one production caller (`maybeResolveDuelingSystemdGatewayScopes`), so the result-shape change has no other consumers. `uninstallLegacySystemdUnits` in the same module still unlinks — it removes units OpenClaw itself generated under retired names, which are regenerated by install, not operator-authored survivors of a scope guess.

Fixes #116130

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`handleControlUiAssistantMediaRequest` in `src/gateway/control-ui.ts` served every Control-UI image/audio/video request from a `FileHandle` and closed it through `closeOpenedHandle`, which discarded any failure with `.catch(() => {})`. The read stream is created with `autoClose: false`, so that explicit close is the only thing that releases the descriptor. A rejected close therefore leaked one descriptor per affected media request with nothing in the logs; the same silent swallow sat in the `meta` probe path in `resolveAssistantMediaAvailability`. In a long-running gateway the accumulation ends at the process descriptor limit, where config reads, state writes, and new connections all start failing for every user — with no trace pointing at media serving.

## Why This Change Was Made

A close failure is exactly the kind of outcome that must be recorded where it happens instead of being inferred later from unrelated `EMFILE` errors. Both close sites now go through one helper, `closeAssistantMediaHandle`, which logs a `warn` on the `gateway/control-ui` subsystem logger and then retries the raw descriptor close. The retry needs the numeric descriptor captured *before* `FileHandle.close()` is called, because the promise API clears `fd` before the underlying close settles — reading `handle.fd` after the rejection yields `-1` and no fallback is possible. A single shared helper keeps the two paths from diverging and keeps `handleClosed` semantics untouched: the flag still prevents concurrent close attempts from the stream `end`/`close` and response `close` handlers.

## User Impact

- A failed media handle close is now visible in gateway logs instead of silent.
- The descriptor is retried rather than abandoned, so a rare close failure no longer walks the process toward descriptor exhaustion that takes down the whole gateway.
- No behavior change on the success path: the same handle lifecycle, the same response bytes, no new config or public surface.

## Evidence

- `src/gateway/control-ui.ts`: `closeOpenedHandle` sets `handleClosed = true` and then awaited `opened.handle.close().catch(() => {})`; the flag is set even when the close throws, so no later handler retried it. The `finally` block in `resolveAssistantMediaAvailability` had the identical swallow.
- The stream in the same function is created with `autoClose: false`, and its `end`/`close`/`error` handlers plus the response `close` handler all delegate to `closeOpenedHandle` — confirming the explicit close is the sole descriptor release path.
- `FileHandle.close()` resets its internal descriptor before the underlying close resolves, which is why the helper reads `handle.fd` first and guards the fallback on `fd >= 0`; the raw `fs.close` callback logs its own failure rather than swallowing a second error.
- Logging matches the surrounding gateway convention: a module-level `createSubsystemLogger` and `log.warn(\`...: ${String(err)}\`)`, as in `src/gateway/server-lifecycle.ts` and `src/gateway/config-reload.ts`.
- Accepted tradeoff, noted for reviewers: the raw retry can target a descriptor the runtime already released for error classes such as `EIO`. The alternative is an unbounded, invisible leak, so the retry is bounded to one attempt and logged.

Fixes #116346

prs.title: fix(signal): align autoStart daemon bind with local connection URL port
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When Signal is configured with a managed-native connection URL on a non-default port (for example `http://127.0.0.1:8082`) and `httpPort` is omitted, OpenClaw bound the autoStart signal-cli daemon to the default port 8080 while the client probed 8082. Config validation succeeded, so the daemon and the readiness URL diverged.

A URL-only local HTTP endpoint with no path prefix is the provisional bind. If that port is free, the daemon binds it and the probe uses the same URL. If another account already reserved it, fallback allocation rewrites that bind-aligned URL to the port that was actually assigned. Remote hosts, HTTPS, path prefixes, and cross-family addresses stay independent connection endpoints. An explicit `httpPort` wins over a divergent URL. Doctor migration uses the same allocation instead of a second copy of the rule.

Ref #116165

## Evidence

Exact-head production autoStart on `d6c1fa9452cbffdbb7e9bd12b082519a54c7618e` (parent `e5b62e7c791427a300d0049d33918501605f1a80`). macOS 26.6.2 arm64 (Darwin 25.6.0, build 25G83), Node v26.10.0. Isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `HOME` under `/var/folders` (not `~/.openclaw`). Production `monitorSignalProvider` resolved the account, then `spawnSignalDaemon` started a local HTTP stand-in. That stand-in records `daemon --http host:port` and answers `GET /api/v1/check` with 204 only on the bound port. The path-prefix case also runs a separate proxy on 8082 that answers only `/signal/api/v1/check`.

```console
$ sw_vers
ProductName: macOS
ProductVersion: 26.6.2
BuildVersion: 25G83
$ node -v
v26.10.0
$ git rev-parse HEAD
d6c1fa9452cbffdbb7e9bd12b082519a54c7618e
$ PROOF_HEAD=$(git rev-parse HEAD) ./node_modules/.bin/tsx proof-116176-autostart.mts
HEAD d6c1fa9452cbffdbb7e9bd12b082519a54c7618e
OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR /var/folders/7_/3g02szlx2h3_4pdqp0knlw740000gn/T/oc-116176-state-XCm1lt
HOME /var/folders/7_/3g02szlx2h3_4pdqp0knlw740000gn/T/oc-116176-home-4bF9YS
free_url_only argv daemon --http 127.0.0.1:8082 --no-receive-stdout
free_url_only request /api/v1/check
collision_fallback argv -a +10000000002 daemon --http 127.0.0.1:8080 --no-receive-stdout
collision_fallback request /api/v1/check
path_prefix_proxy argv daemon --http 127.0.0.1:8080 --no-receive-stdout
path_prefix_proxy proxy /signal/api/v1/check
path_prefix_proxy proxy /signal/api/v1/check
PROOF_OK bind_and_probe_aligned
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Managed-native Signal autoStart keeps the daemon `--http` argument and the readiness URL on the same port. A free URL-only `http://127.0.0.1:8082` binds and probes 8082. When a sibling local endpoint already reserves 8082, fallback binds and probes the allocated port (here 8080) and rewrites the URL. A path-prefixed `http://127.0.0.1:8082/signal` stays on that proxy while the daemon binds 8080.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS 26.6.2 arm64 (Darwin 25.6.0, build 25G83), Node v26.10.0, OpenClaw worktree `/tmp/oc-116176` at head `d6c1fa9452cbffdbb7e9bd12b082519a54c7618e` on `e5b62e7c791427a300d0049d33918501605f1a80`. Isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` `/var/folders/7_/3g02szlx2h3_4pdqp0knlw740000gn/T/oc-116176-state-XCm1lt`. Isolated `HOME`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

  Step 1: frozen install in `/tmp/oc-116176` at `d6c1fa9452c`.

  Step 2: production `monitorSignalProvider` for a free URL-only port, a sibling reservation of that port, and a path-prefixed proxy.

  ```bash
  cd /tmp/oc-116176
  CI=true pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
  PROOF_HEAD=$(git rev-parse HEAD) ./node_modules/.bin/tsx proof-116176-autostart.mts
  ```

- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output above. Free URL-only spawned `daemon --http 127.0.0.1:8082` and the readiness request was `GET /api/v1/check` on that process. With 8082 reserved by a sibling external endpoint, the managed account spawned `daemon --http 127.0.0.1:8080` and the readiness request hit that same process. The path-prefixed URL stayed on the proxy (`proxy /signal/api/v1/check`) while the daemon argv was `--http 127.0.0.1:8080`.
- **Observed result after fix:** Daemon bind argv and the readiness URL stay on one port for a free URL-only local HTTP endpoint and for fallback after that port is reserved. A path-prefixed proxy URL is not used as the daemon bind.
- **What was not tested:** A registered signal-cli with a real phone number. Two live signal-cli processes at the same time.

## Summary

- Prefer a local connection URL port when `httpPort` is omitted and the URL has no path prefix
- On a reserved preferred port, rewrite the bind-aligned URL to the allocated port
- Remote, HTTPS, path-prefixed, and cross-family URLs stay independent
- Explicit `httpPort` wins over a divergent URL
- Doctor migration uses the same allocation
- Production autoStart transcript: resolver, daemon `--http`, readiness, including collision and a path-prefixed proxy

## Test plan

- [x] Single URL-only `http://127.0.0.1:8082`
- [x] Two URL-only managed accounts sharing 8082
- [x] Sibling local endpoint reserving 8082, fallback bind and probe aligned
- [x] Path-prefixed `http://127.0.0.1:8082/signal` stays independent
- [x] Remote, HTTPS, and cross-family URLs stay independent
- [x] Explicit `httpPort` precedence
- [x] Doctor legacy `httpUrl` migration, including a reserved 8082 rewrite

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Memory applied URL agent selection in a child effect while Config already admitted the route. Plugin Settings also observed an incomplete combination of reactive state and owner subscriptions. Config now owns route admission and exposes its existing admitted route through a plain read/subscribe source. Memory publishes accepted catalog, route, transport epoch, configuration, agent and locale changes through one complete source shared by both plugin placements.

The catalog has one plain storage owner and a thin Solid projection. The plugin renderer consumes its source once for its lifetime; its compensating effect, Memory's revision signal and duplicated per-placement upstream subscriptions are removed. Request generations, intent-revision guards, canonical redirect deduplication, runtime aborts, mounted-view disposal and post-await authority checks remain in their existing owners.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Frozen install after rebase | Passed |
| Default tsrs UI and actual UI test type leaves | Passed after refreshing onto main’s Sidebar repair; all three scoped type gates passed |
| Memory renderer, default pinned Bun | 31 unique cases passed; one new initial-availability expectation corrected from unknown to existing loading state, then only that case rerun |
| Plugin Settings lifecycle, default runtime | 12 passed |
| Actual loopback Gateway transport, canonical unit-node project | 7 passed; project needs Node, no runtime override |
| Original Config route and Security extractor proof | 9 route cases and 1 extractor case passed on prior reviewed head; retained contracts |
| Focused lint, formatting, whitespace | Passed; source-backed extraction lint passed without warnings. Earlier lint attempt timed out preparing SDK declarations before lint ran; existing Solid development diagnostics remain unsuppressed |
| Complete isolated review | Passed, complete 19-file source/context review; no P0–P2 findings |
| Final production Knip | Pending |

The new regression cases exercise the actual Config owner: delayed catalog acceptance updates an already mounted plugin without another owner event, and a route-only admission retires old callbacks. The reconnect case now checks immediate epoch retirement without a Solid flush between disconnect and reconnect. Existing lifecycle and real transport tests retain failures, reentrant disposal, operator scope and post-await reply retirement.

The earlier head's full CI run 39186110523 failed `Control UI mocked Gateway E2E > keeps composer edits local after scrolling returns to the same offset` during scroll setup, before its render probe or typing. It is not claimed as inherited or passing. This replacement adds the completed source contract and requests fresh full CI. The exact chat test file is held by other open lanes and remains untouched.

No markup, CSS, selectors, route loading boundary or startup import changes. No local build, broad E2E, or visual capture was needed. Strict-read diagnostics from existing shared renderers remain visible; no warning-free claim.

| Complete touched production scope | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| createEffect | 3 | 1 |
| createRenderEffect, untrack, raw listeners, DOM queries | 0 | 0 |
| Controller patterns, manual class assembly, flush, owner escapes | 0 | 0 |
| Production LOC | 2346 | 2365 |
| Test/support LOC | 2251 | 2356 |

The sole effect survivor is Config's existing navigation-input admission at config-page-state.ts, which synchronizes external request lifetimes. The pure Security extractor relocation from the original head is unchanged. A small plain Memory route-admission module keeps Config within its existing line cap; normalization stays in Config and route admission is recorded before reentrant context replacement. The full 13-file PR adds 19 production lines to complete notifications and retain that ownership boundary. No SDK contract, dependency or second route store was introduced.

prs.title: fix(agent): stop treating ..cache directories as workspace escapes
prs.body:
Closes #114206

**What Problem This Solves**

Fixes: an already-processed image stays in replayed agent history when it sits under a workspace directory whose name starts with two dots, such as `..cache`.

**User Impact**

Processed media under those directories is pruned like any other workspace image. Nothing previously rejected as an escape becomes reachable.

**Why This Change Was Made**

The media alias check used `relativePath.startsWith("..")`, which matches any name beginning with two dots, but only a `..` segment leaves the root. It now uses `isPathInside`, which compares the first segment. `main` has since fixed the other four sites (grep in #131621); their regression tests stay here and pass against those fixes.

**Evidence**

Real `pruneProcessedHistoryImages` on a Windows `..cache` workspace, fix reverted, then applied:

```
=== reverted to the pre-fix predicate ===
replayed content: "[media attached: ..cache/photo.png (image/png)]"
replayed content: "[media attached: ../outside/photo.png (image/png)]"
=== this branch, head 35db4b1d ===
replayed content: "[media reference removed - already processed by model]"
replayed content: "[media attached: ../outside/photo.png (image/png)]"
```

The second line in each run is a file outside the workspace. Written with Claude Code, which ran this harness both ways; the full suite and the build were not run.

prs.title: fix(skills): honor Codex agents/openai.yaml invocation policy
prs.body:
Fixes #115337

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw discovers skills from the same shared Agent Skills roots as Codex (`~/.agents/skills`, `.agents/skills`), but it derives invocation policy only from the SKILL.md `disable-model-invocation` frontmatter field and ignores Codex's per-skill `agents/openai.yaml` -> `policy.allow_implicit_invocation`. So a skill an author marks explicit-only for Codex is still exposed to the model for implicit invocation when OpenClaw loads the same on-disk installation. The repo's own bundled `openclaw-test-performance` skill ships `allow_implicit_invocation: false` with no `disable-model-invocation`, so it is currently mis-exposed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The core Agent Skills specification defines neither field; both are client-specific extensions that now meet on the same shared skill installation. Rather than require authors to maintain two equivalent declarations, OpenClaw honors the Codex sidecar the same way it already reads SKILL.md frontmatter.

- New `readCodexImplicitInvocationDisabled(skillDir)` reads the colocated `<skill>/agents/openai.yaml` sidecar through the same root-scoped boundary helper (`openRootFileSync` + `readFileDescriptorBoundedSync`) used for SKILL.md, so a symlinked sidecar cannot escape the skill root and reads are byte-bounded.
- Only an explicit `policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false` disables invocation. An absent sidecar, a missing policy key, a non-boolean value, or an unparseable file leaves behavior unchanged (returns `false`), so malformed input can never restrict a skill that would otherwise load.
- `resolveSkillInvocationPolicy(frontmatter, codexImplicitDisabled = false)` ORs the two declarations: a skill is hidden from implicit model context when **either** declaration disables it. The merge lives in the shared helper, so every consumer of `invocation.disableModelInvocation` (session loader, local loader, workspace `includeInAvailableSkillsPrompt`) picks it up. The helper stays free of filesystem I/O; only the new module reads disk.
- Remote (node-hosted) skills are intentionally out of scope: they have no local sidecar and `resolveSkillInvocationPolicy` is called there with the default.

## User Impact

A shared `~/.agents/skills` installation now behaves consistently across Codex and OpenClaw: a workflow an author marked explicit-only (`allow_implicit_invocation: false`) is excluded from the model's available-skills prompt in both clients, while remaining invocable via explicit `/skill:name`. Skills without the sidecar, or with `allow_implicit_invocation: true`, are unaffected.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/skills/loading/codex-invocation-policy.test.ts` - 7/7 passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/skills/loading/frontmatter.test.ts` - passed (incl. new merge cases)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/skills/loading/session.test.ts` - passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/skills/loading/workspace-load.test.ts` - passed
- `oxlint src/skills/loading/**` - passed (no findings)
- `oxfmt --check` on all changed files - passed
- `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json` - passed

Real behavior proof at exact PR head `893df76e42b6520b73941684e08004fe0c992909`. The proof loads the **real** local skill loader (`loadSkillsFromDirSafe`) and the **real** prompt formatter (`formatSkillsForPrompt`, the public API that assembles the model's available-skills prompt) from source, against a temp skill carrying `agents/openai.yaml`:

```text
[before fix, clean upstream/main c193ffd554642c4b5b2e0e11b1c12dbb6348c66b]
case: explicit-only via Codex sidecar (allow_implicit_invocation: false)
  disableModelInvocation: false (expected true)   <- BUG: explicit-only skill treated as implicit-invocable
  appears in prompt     : true                      <- BUG: exposed to the model
  ok                    : NO
RESULT: MISMATCH

[after fix, PR head 893df76e42b6520b73941684e08004fe0c992909]  pnpm exec tsx scripts/proof/skills-codex-invocation-policy.mjs
case: explicit-only via Codex sidecar (allow_implicit_invocation: false)
  disableModelInvocation: true (expected true)
  appears in prompt     : false
  ok                    : YES
case: implicit-allowed via Codex sidecar (allow_implicit_invocation: true)
  disableModelInvocation: false (expected false)
  appears in prompt     : true
  ok                    : YES
case: no sidecar (OpenClaw default behavior)
  disableModelInvocation: false (expected false)
  appears in prompt     : true
  ok                    : YES
case: sidecar present but policy key absent
  disableModelInvocation: false (expected false)
  appears in prompt     : true
  ok                    : YES
case: malformed sidecar (unparseable YAML)
  disableModelInvocation: false (expected false)
  appears in prompt     : true
  ok                    : YES
RESULT: ALL CASES MATCH EXPECTATION
```

Notes on what was not tested locally: two pre-existing Windows-only flakes are unrelated to this change and were verified to fail identically on clean `upstream/main` -- `compact-format.test.ts` (`~/` path compaction on Windows HOME) and `agents-directory.test.ts` (`EBUSY` on `openclaw.sqlite-shm` during teardown). Both are environmental and do not reproduce on Linux CI.

prs.title: fix(state): messages to agents fail right after a Gateway restart instead of waiting
prs.body:
## Landing stopped: unmatched current-head CI failure

**Not merged.** Current head is `b86fbe28959bdca4aa05ecfc31f93e04006a3893`. The maintainer land order stops on “a CI failure not matching main.”

[CI run 39186761763](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39186761763), attempt 1, completed with 93 successful jobs, 19 skipped jobs, six underlying failed jobs, and the resulting aggregate gate failure. In [checks-ui (3/3), job 117851083527](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39186761763/job/117851083527), `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-transcript-replies.test.ts` fails loading with `EnvironmentTeardownError`: `tool-display.json` is imported by `tool-display-icon.ts` after environment teardown.

The comparable [scheduled-main job 117850678944](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39186683798/job/117850678944), on main `9d013baeb67c283c51bdcc3928b4330c7ccf5d97`, succeeded and its log confirms that the same suite executed successfully. All three UI jobs also passed in the prior scheduled-main run [39183785855](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39183785855). PR causation is not established, but there is no matching-main failure supporting an inherited-failure exception for this job. Attribution of the other five underlying failures is incomplete; no claim is made that they are all inherited. No CI rerun or merge request was submitted after this stop.

[ClawSweeper round 10](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174958#issuecomment-6228317758) completed on this exact head at 2026-10-19 02:15 UTC: Findings None; Security None. Its remaining before-merge item is current-head CI attribution. F77 remains separately tracked and explicitly non-blocking.

## Current candidate after main integration

Current head: `b86fbe28959bdca4aa05ecfc31f93e04006a3893`. This signed merge incorporates main `c5111f4067a3978c989e061293056659b264c5c4` after a conflict in `ui/src/plugins/control-ui-host.test.ts`. The resolution keeps main’s factored parameters and automatic fixture cleanup, while preserving the startup timeout and owner cancellation assertion. No other manual source change was made.

The integrated candidate passed **219 focused tests**: 103 UI host/catalog/session/startup tests, 31 client request tests, 23 Gateway lifecycle/deadline tests, 35 TUI tests, and 27 cron queue/worker tests. UI-chat types, scoped lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed. Independent review of the full candidate against the incorporated main found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Gateway coverage uses production request/router and database lifecycle owners with synthetic transports; no current-head live-provider or campaign Gateway proof is claimed.

Current-head CI and ClawSweeper results are recorded above. Earlier CI and review results below remain historical evidence for their named heads and do not qualify this new head. F77 remains the separately tracked, non-blocking follow-up described below.

## Follow-up: explicit-agent send admission

The pre-existing operator `send` admission gap with explicit `agentId` and no `sessionKey` is tracked separately as **F77** in [#176685](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176685) ([source finding](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174958#discussion_r4308819092)). ClawSweeper classified this path as pre-existing on the base; it is not introduced by this PR. The maintainer explicitly directed that F77 does not block this landing. The three main-matching CI failures below concern the previous head only; that historical exception does not qualify the current failed head.

## What Problem This Solves

Messages and new sessions fail immediately after a Gateway restart while their agent is still preparing, and preparing cron jobs can hold work that should remain queued.

## User Impact

TUI and Control UI sends and new sessions wait up to five minutes for the selected agent, while preserving Stop, timeout, target replacement, and disposal cancellation. A ready agent can proceed independently of another agent that is still preparing. Submitted messages remain owned by the outbox when a retained pane is parked. Scheduled cron work keeps its queued receipt without consuming a running slot or holding Gateway initialization.

## Why This Change Was Made

Peter's maintainer decisions are “Wait for that agent” (2026-10-16), “Readiness handoff” for cron (2026-10-16), and “Longer UI waits” (2026-10-17: TUI/Control UI sends and new sessions use a startup-budget deadline, client-owned and cancellable; SDK/native/tool callers keep their deadlines).

The Gateway refuses pending startup writes before handler dispatch. The client retries only that method-bound refusal using the identical request frame, original deadline, and cancellation owner. Accepted requests and generic retryable errors are not replayed. Direct execution and channel ingress use the existing bounded admission wait; real inspection or ownership failures remain errors. Startup readiness never holds a write past the client deadline.

The native cron queue remains the receipt and capacity owner. Background readiness observation wakes that queue; it does not transfer event custody, allocate a running slot, or block initialization. Interactive creation lifetimes now reach the same request owner, including catalog close/target replacement and pane disposal. No protocol field, schema, public configuration, migration, or SDK option is added.

Current-main integration preserves its newer UI state and reconnect handling alongside these cancellation signals. It retains all nine resolved paths' existing behavior, including reply source preparation, TUI request assertions, catalog reconnect discovery, and draft/voice ownership.

## Evidence

The signed merge candidate `232fb666f45e13e0d9cbff67a4ed8fe5c742054e` incorporates main `1398ba9837e19da853bb6b1d6623cb6fee5421f6`. Its reviewed tree passed **349 focused tests**: catalog/pane 54, state/voice/draft 200, protocol 31, TUI 35, real client/router deadlines 10, cron queue 17, and wrapper inventory/extracted dependencies 2. Core/UI types, scoped lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed. Full candidate autoreview returned zero findings through P2. Dependencies were refreshed with frozen installs. ClawSweeper round 8 reviewed the incoming `bcd86e6ced57` head with no findings or security concerns; its only remaining item was the merge conflict now resolved. Published-head CI and ClawSweeper review remain required before landing.

The catalog regression uses the mounted component, real session capability, and pending-request owner with a synthetic wire. Restoring its old production lifetime produces three failures: close, agent replacement, and conversation replacement each allow a late create. The fixed implementation prevents those writes and still creates once for the live target. Client/router and cron regressions likewise cover cancellation, deadlines, independent agents, terminal admission failures, queued custody, and nonblocking startup.

The earlier live restart comparison used a cloned 22-agent state and predates the final client-deadline correction; it is historical evidence, not a live run of this head. Current validation uses production owners with synthetic transports. No live provider or campaign Gateway is exercised.

Earlier CI run 39023245668 had catalog-worker and session-message failures matching scheduled main 39021393912. Its presence-audience health-barrier failure remained unattributed; a passing diagnostic replay was not treated as a fix. Earlier macOS provisioning and subagent failures also remain historical failures, not waived successes. The published merge candidate requires its own CI, including investigation of any new or unknown failure.

The first combined server run completed its router cases but was interrupted during reply-test collection. No passing result is claimed for those two reply tests or a bounded import diagnostic that timed out. The isolated cron run then passed all 17 cases; its 626-second wall time was dominated by cold compiler preparation and verification. These observations do not establish a product failure.

## Published-candidate CI follow-up

CI run [39167401066](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39167401066) tested published head `232fb666f45e13e0d9cbff67a4ed8fe5c742054e`. The historical presence-audience test executed and passed in job 117793464900 (11,509 ms); its group passed all 89 tests. This is current-head execution evidence, not a claim that the historical failure's root cause was repaired.

The UI chat test typecheck and controller guard found one obsolete `requestUpdate` fixture assignment left by the Solid migration. Removing it preserves the Stop cancellation assertions. The focused MCP pane suite passes all seven tests, the UI-chat typecheck passes, and the retired-controller guard passes.

The `control-ui-performance` failure is inherited: candidate chat boot is 1,495,430 bytes versus a 1,490,000-byte limit; its base is already 1,494,544 bytes. Scheduled main run [39168070659](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39168070659), head `d851443cdc69a13e2b20f5834078b1e3b2f1b679`, job 117795289336, fails the same check at 1,494,544 bytes. No performance threshold is changed.

The cron job passed 360 tests but failed loading `service.pr-automation.test.ts` with `EnvironmentTeardownError`. Its recorded import chain originates in the preceding heartbeat busy-poll fixture's watchdog recovery. That recovery checks current ownership again after the import. The correction joins watchdog recovery imports after the scheduler stops and before fixture databases, mocks, and environment are retired. The unchanged Bun pair passed 9/9 in 453 seconds; the corrected pair passed 9/9 in 803 seconds, with most wall time in graph preparation/loading. The CI failure did not reproduce locally, so this is a source-supported fixture repair, not a proven red/green reproduction. It is not classified as inherited.

Signed correction `3b9ce9abc28531332f23eb0f3ea39615459b8918` changes only those two test files. Focused UI-chat types, the retired-controller guard, scoped core lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed. Isolated correction autoreview completed with no actionable findings through P2. One earlier local lint command selected the test typecheck config and timed out preparing unrelated plugin declarations before lint ran; using the repository's core lint config completed successfully. ClawSweeper round 9 completed on this exact head with Findings None and Security None. Its sole before-merge item was CI attribution; the matching main failures are recorded below.

## Historical CI attribution for 3b9ce9abc285

Run [39172271801](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39172271801), attempt 1, tests head `3b9ce9abc28531332f23eb0f3ea39615459b8918` through merge `e083a403c14fab78ddec744ae4a442447b1d339d` (parents: main `50bb09d7ba13a37c8982b91afb3fcd52e13b09ae`, then the exact PR head). The UI-chat typecheck and lint checks that previously failed now pass.

The remaining reported failures match scheduled main run [39172446197](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39172446197), head `4812f059427b2db240fbefd3af4411c9d701538a`:

- `control-ui-performance`, PR job 117808026321: chat boot is 1,491,032 bytes against 1,490,000. Its base is already 1,490,230; main job 117808337159 fails at the same 1,490,230-byte baseline. No budget was changed.
- `checks-node-compact-small-1-1`, PR job 117808027287: `changed-lanes.test.ts` expects the format script to start with `oxfmt`, but main now uses `node scripts/run-format.mts --check`. Main job 117808338593 fails the identical case and assertion (`expected 'node' to be 'oxfmt'`).
- `checks-node-changed-compact-large-15-1`, PR job 117808027505: two chat lifecycle cases fail fixture settlement with `ws:chat.send: expected 1 to be 0`; the sessions-recover case fails synchronous teardown with an active native borrower. Main job 117808338765 fails those same three cases with matching errors. The failed tests, settlement helper, and chat work-admission cleanup owner are unchanged by this PR's tested merge. These errors do not establish a post-cancellation write, and cleanup errors may hide earlier assertions, so they are retained as failed tests rather than claimed passing behavior.

The final attempt is complete: 100 jobs passed, 19 skipped, and these three failed jobs caused the aggregate gate failure. All PostgreSQL shards and independent security checks passed. prs.title: fix(sessions): keep conversations usable after delegated recovery fails
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A conversation can remain unusable after restart recovery loses sender authority for an interrupted delegated turn. Its recovery claim blocks new messages, and a pre-dispatch failure can leave diagnostics showing `processing` after the controller has finished.

## User Impact

When no other execution or delivery is owed, recovery records one local interruption notice, retires the exact input, and lets a fresh authenticated message continue in the same conversation. Pending deliveries, harness completions and other interrupted runs retain their existing protection. Missing authority still cannot execute work.

## Why This Change Was Made

Rewrite of #176087 by @enki onto current main (session-controller cutover #175837); original design and credit retained. The native refresh route cannot refresh the unsigned incoming head, so this maintainer rewrite preserves Paul Bohm's design and co-author credit. The original PR remains open for the lead's landing decision.

At `src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-restart-recovery-store.ts:474`, the recovery owner now distinguishes a failed individual input from a session with other outstanding custody. The maintainer correction preserves the controller-cutover ownership and projects idle from `src/sessions/session-controller.state.ts:510` (`clearReplyRunState`) before waking successors, without consuming message-owned queue counts. An already-idle or absent diagnostic entry is left alone, preserving adopted session identity and last activity.

Started cron occurrences remain owned by cron after restart. The checkpoint owner retains their source classification and checks it before earlier operator exemptions. Confirmed same-turn steering cannot turn a cron occurrence into replayable human input; a normal new user turn still establishes a new source. The steering marker comes from the existing transcript-commit owner. No operator authority is copied or widened. A distinct unresolved run retains its visible Resume block.

The final branch integrates main's independent CLI mock-ratchet repair `e63269c2` to clear the named inherited CI failure. No unrelated CLI repair or baseline allowance is added by this PR. Related canonical-Main reset remedy: #176675.

## Evidence

Team session `b0bb4540`: decompressed `journal-boot-2147.log.gz:788` records `delegated_authority_unavailable`; lines 1368–3897 show stale `processing` with queue depth 0, and 4151–5943 show queue depth 1 without an active run. Eight post-block child-announcement failures begin at line 789. Shutdown line 195 records the interrupted active run. The deployed revision predates #176422; these journals do not identify the original admission source precisely.

On pinned main `5d0148f9`, the original Gateway regression remains `processing` after its run disappears, startup recovery fails to retire the interrupted input, and both authenticated cron restart cases dispatch the old input. Initial isolated proof passed 694 focused tests. CI subsequently exposed redundant idle observations in cron; the correction preserves the original cron assertions and passed 63 focused tests plus types/lint/format ([diagnostic correction proof](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_09c802f5972a45b070ec720be2523416)).

The hosted P1 review finding is fixed in `ad2a5392`. With the prior rewrite's checkpoint or pinned main's checkpoint, the new real cron → authenticated steering → transcript commit → shutdown → recovery regression dispatches generic recovery once. The fixed checkpoint suppresses that replay. The ordinary new-user-input controls also pass. The final isolated proof is [run_0d5a7747971d9a862e90a11792b1bc1b](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_0d5a7747971d9a862e90a11792b1bc1b).

Head `548346c9`, before main's later test-fixture cleanup, passes all 261 focused tests: 184 recovery, 12 cron continuation, 2 checkpoint, 61 controller/diagnostic, the Gateway stale-processing regression, and the real startup composition. Every test command uses `pnpm test <files> --maxWorkers=1`. Production and targeted test `run-tsgo`, scoped `run-oxlint` (zero warnings/errors), and `run-format --check` pass. The first negative run stopped before the cron shard; the completed negative proof uses the repository's continue-on-failure option and shows the expected replay assertion in both earlier checkpoint implementations.

The cron suite takes 32.84s and the existing startup suite 47.23s; those cases exercise authenticated admission, persisted transcript/lifecycle state, and the actual recovery/Gateway boundary. The two checkpoint cases take 0.322s. The full unchanged recovery suite takes 174.64s. The exact obsolete closed-mock baseline entry for the cron transcript reader was removed, generated and verified by the native ratchet (8,532 → 8,531 entries; [prune proof](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_32e10a82532c0a39a579d77e70855a11)). Main subsequently changed the generation-test fixtures in #176648 while CI ran. The conflict resolution preserves that cleanup and adapts the same regression to its existing helpers; no production recovery/controller code changed.

Head `5e182775b18ab814a0330cf4f320074c7abe0204` passes the 23 affected tests (full generation suite, Gateway regression and startup composition), targeted test types, scoped lint/format and the mock ratchet ([conflict-repair proof](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_cb0136443c1beef7b5dd8b330e6ecabd), exit 0, 198.63s command time). The adapted regression was also run on actual pinned main `d0c681cc`: it reaches the expected assertion with no active run but `state: processing`, `queueDepth: 1`. A temporary sibling-checkout dependency-link error was corrected before this completed red/green run. The production fix is unchanged.

Final committed-branch Codex review at `5e182775b18ab814a0330cf4f320074c7abe0204`: scoped-clean through P2, no accepted/actionable findings. Exact-head CI [run 39186313299](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39186313299) is GREEN under the repository watcher: no effective pending or failed checks; 19 superseded obsolete rows excluded. The PR is mergeable. The prior CI failure was independently reproduced on exact main `d4114bb2` at untouched `src/cli/program/root-help.test.ts:33`; main repaired it in `e63269c2`.

Accepted existing behavior from #174177: a legacy requester input with no recoverable original completion authority records its saved reply text locally as delivery unconfirmed and retires once. A current delivery-queue owner defers earlier. The unchanged startup regression verifies this terminal outcome and no replay on another restart; the new generic delegated-custody guard does not replace that requester policy. The hosted suggestion to tombstone this legacy case was declined for that reason.

The announcement retry fixture already terminally settles on current main, so no speculative announcement change is included. The incident's specific retry path and the producer of its later queued item remain unproven. The controller correction preserves queued work rather than hiding it; it does not claim to settle the unidentified queue-depth-1 item or suppress legitimate queued-work diagnostics. Startup proof uses persisted restart state and an authenticated Gateway with a loopback Responses provider; it does not kill an OS process. No live Team state was touched.

Production: +184/-79 lines (net +105); tests: +608/-30 (net +578); docs: +22/-9; test baseline: -1 entry. Production growth expresses retirement eligibility and the controller-owned idle transition; existing pending-final policy is moved without a competing implementation.

prs.title: fix(ui): resample Inbox overflow through shared scroll state
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Inbox overflow fades could stay visible after a resize made the list fit. The component sampled reactive content changes and scroll events, but did not observe list resizing.

## User Impact

The Inbox now refreshes its fades when the list resizes, while preserving the two-pixel scroll threshold, tab reset, approval focus recovery, lazy panel loading, host tags, and selectors.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing shared scroll-state ref for the Inbox list so initial layout, content changes, scrolling, and resizing share one observation lifetime. The attention owner revision invalidates mutable content; the tab handler already resets scroll and samples after commit. Remove the component effect and obsolete panel scroll callback. The observer supplies a nonnull element for sampling, and the existing list ref still owns focus and tab reset. No new abstraction, domain state owner, dependency, or budget change.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Regression on original base `711ffb0d5178` | Fails at the intended stale-bottom-fade assertion |
| `sidebar-attention.test.ts` | 23/23 pass on the first implementation; owner-revision refinement: 2 relevant tests pass; final nonnull callback: resize regression passes (1 passed, 22 skipped) |
| UI types | `pnpm tsgo:ui` passes with tsrs after the rebase and final callback refinement |
| Targeted lint and formatting | Pass; existing reactivity warnings on unchanged handlers |
| Production Knip | Pass; subsequent refinements preserve this change's import/export/dependency graph |
| Strict build/performance | Startup passes; Chat/New caps fail on both fresh base and head, with all three JS totals smaller on head; details below |
| Synthetic visual capture | Inspected normal Inbox, overflowing list, resized list on fresh base and final head; resized fade fixed, focus preserved |
| Independent review | Full change, owner-revision refinement, and final nonnull callback clean at P0–P2 |

The focused test checks the two-pixel boundary, resize without a scroll event, retained list focus, and tab scroll reset. The browser fixture change only removes the retired callback from its typed props. Captures use two synthetic approval requests at 1440×960 and fixed list dimensions. The fresh base reproduces the stale fade at `scrollHeight = clientHeight = 400`; the final head clears it without moving focus.

Initial full-file proof used Node with the Vitest filesystem module cache disabled after a process sample identified a filesystem `rename` stall. Both later targeted refinements passed on the default pinned Bun fork with `--fsModuleCache=false`. No broad local E2E suite or compute lease was used; `ci:full` ran every UI unit, Control UI E2E, browser-extension, and real-Gateway shard.

The branch was rebased onto `e63269c28a22` before the fresh build comparison. Base and head were built sequentially in the same internal-disk checkout on the same machine with `NODE_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1`. Both strict checks report the same two failing metrics; this does not label the whole performance check green. Earlier candidate growth was reduced by using the observer's guaranteed nonnull element directly. The final comparison is:

| Gzip / requests | Base `e63269c28a22` | Head `b354d086a1ad` | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Startup JS | 337,692 B / 7 | 337,651 B / 7 | −41 B |
| Startup CSS | 38,500 B / 1 | 38,500 B / 1 | 0 B |
| Chat boot JS | 1,492,375 B / 25 | 1,492,346 B / 25 | −29 B |
| New Session boot JS | 1,050,396 B / 20 | 1,050,363 B / 20 | −33 B |

The inherited Chat/New caps are 1,490,000 B and 1,050,000 B respectively. Both base and head exceed them. Lazy boundaries and request counts are unchanged.

| Pattern in the two production files | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Controller lifecycle | 0 | 0 |
| `createEffect` | 1 | 0 |
| `createRenderEffect` | 0 | 0 |
| `untrack` | 0 | 0 |
| Direct `addEventListener` | 0 | 0 |
| `querySelector(All)` | 0 | 0 |
| Manual class strings | 0 | 0 |
| `flush` | 1 | 1 |
| Manual Solid owner restoration | 0 | 0 |

Production LOC: **809 → 808** (−1); test LOC: **1,268 → 1,340** (+72). No feature effect survives in these two files. The existing `flush()` at `ui/src/components/sidebar-attention.tsx:213` remains at approval focus recovery to inspect committed rows.

| Before resize recovery | After resize recovery |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: stale bottom fade after the list fits](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/257d9e9b-5680-4e57-ac1d-6f09d1b96157) | ![After: bottom fade clears after the list fits](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/44c22b2e-c7a7-447b-a291-6cc18e7a530c) |

CI run [39184544506](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39184544506) completed on the exact head. Only `control-ui-performance` and its aggregate failed; all other nonaggregate jobs passed or were skipped. The job directly compared baseline `e2b6418635ec` with tested merge `06b775d03d91` (parents: that baseline, then `b354d086a1ad`). Chat boot gzip was **1,491,264 → 1,491,223 B (−41 B)**, already over the unchanged 1,490,000 B cap on the baseline. New Session was **1,049,534 → 1,049,498 B (−36 B)** and passed its cap. Startup was **337,427 B**; startup CSS was **38,500 B / 1 request**. The latest completed scheduled main run, `39176649118`, passed performance and is not used as evidence of inheritance. The exception is based on the exact CI job’s direct baseline measurement, reinforced by the separate local base/head comparison above.

prs.title: feat(memory): report duplicate Markdown blocks
prs.body:
Related: #176036

## What Problem This Solves

Operators consolidating copied Markdown memory need source locations for repeated content, rather than only more diverse search results.

## User Impact

`openclaw memory duplicates` reports identical blocks and their file/line references without changing files or printing memory text. Both same-file and cross-file repeats are included. `--agent`, `--min-chars`, `--max-groups`, and `--json` support focused local inspection.

This is a proposed optional CLI feature, not an accepted product direction. It follows existing offline CLI ownership rules and refuses another plugin's memory slot. File paths can still be sensitive and should be reviewed before sharing reports. Maintainer edits are disabled because the author has not authorized fork workflow/secrets access.

The first version is local-workspace-only: configured remote mappings overlapping any scanned root, and declared or registered Memory ownership at scan paths or their ancestors, are rejected before local discovery. It never substitutes Gateway-local files for remote-owned files. Bundled product acceptance still needs a maintainer decision.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse Memory Core's existing Markdown discovery, authorized file reader, and chunker. Group exact, non-overlapping chunks locally, normalizing CRLF and empty boundary lines. Return bounded location lists with explicit total and omitted counts. No new model-facing tool, SDK contract, database, configuration setting, background task, deletion, or search-ranking change.

The command inspects live files, not persisted index contents. It does not find paraphrases or arbitrary matching substrings across chunk boundaries. Repeated content can be intentional; consolidation remains a separate manual decision.

The review repair preserves the existing `declareAgentWorkspaceAccess` / `getAgentWorkspaceAccess` contract: stopped or unavailable workspace adapters must not expose a stale local copy. Offline CLI loading may not register that adapter at all, so configured `file-transfer` mappings are checked against all actual discovery roots and the selected workspace itself. This includes normalized extra directories/files, mapped descendants of recursive roots, shared directories, and existing canonical aliases. The workspace participates only in remote-ancestor/equality checks, not descendant checks: it is not a recursive scan root, and its canonical identity remains relevant when every default memory root is absent. Declared ownership is checked on lexical/canonical workspace and scan-root ancestry. No remote transport or SDK surface is added. Patterned extra roots conservatively refuse overlap even when a narrower pattern might exclude it; use a narrower local root instead. Unscanned remote siblings remain allowed.

## Evidence

Repair head: `0a8cd97884c6429fbf4cca3402cb07b8aabf896c`. Current implementation SHA-256: `229ef74bd916568eb0ea058f89fc5545a6ae000b56d2ddf642977aa9e1d5ab8a`.

- Focused CLI and ownership tests: **44 passing** (wrapper wall time 10.72s, Vitest 9.13s; the new regression used 13ms). The new empty-workspace alias regression was red at `c737c129` because the command resolved instead of rejecting. The real official CLI independently reproduced exit 0 with a zero-file report before repair. Existing recursive-root, declared-ownership, unrelated-remote-directory, duplicate, scope, privacy, output-limit and admission coverage remains passing.
- Production Memory Core package typecheck, targeted two-file test typecheck with the repository's ambient declarations, targeted lint, and formatting passed.
- Real official source-CLI evidence is captured below. Current-head proof covers refusal of an empty mapped workspace through an alias and acceptance of a genuinely local empty alias with an unscanned mapped descendant. Earlier local duplicate reports and mapped extra-root/nested-root proof are retained with their original commit labels; unchanged-input proof is not relabeled as current-head execution.
- Line-cap, assertion-safety, and mock-export ratchets passed. The full max-lines suppression check reports three existing `main` UI paths outside this diff: `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.test.tsx`, `ui/src/pages/config/config-page-state.ts`, and `ui/src/pages/sessions/sessions-page-state.ts`. Their suppressions are already present in the base; no baseline or unrelated UI files are changed.
- Fresh independent Codex autoreview completed, `scoped-clean` for P0–P2, confidence 0.98. It assessed the repair with supplied workspace, SDK, path-containment, discovery and filename-resolver context; it did not execute project code. Typechecks and actual CLI execution provide separate integration proof. The preceding head `c737c129` has a [successful CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39098387194/job/117593280535); that is not current-head CI proof. New-head CI and hosted re-review remain separate pending evidence. This is official source-CLI proof, not an installed release or model-generated conversational workflow claim.

### Current repair: empty workspace alias

Only synthetic notes/configuration, isolated profile/state and a free port were used. The default `MEMORY.md`, `USER.md` and `memory/` were absent throughout. An unrelated synthetic `private.md` marker stayed unchanged and unscanned. Runtime: Node 24.16.0 through the supported `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node` source-CLI setting. Default Bun startup could not be qualified locally because its supported SQLite dylib is unavailable; no software was installed to bypass that prerequisite.

At `c737c129`, a selected alias pointing to the same physical workspace mapped for another agent incorrectly returned exit 0 with `filesScanned: 0`. After this repair, the same scenario returns:

```text
$ pnpm openclaw memory duplicates --agent main --json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "memory duplicates requires a local workspace and local scan roots; run it on the workspace host with a local-workspace configuration. Remote workspace mappings cannot be scanned offline."
  }
}
Exit 1: remote-owned empty alias refused; no local report.
```

Negative control: select an alias to a genuinely local empty workspace, mapping only its unscanned `docs/ops/` descendant for another agent. The same command exits 0:

```json
{
  "agentId": "main",
  "filesScanned": 0,
  "skippedFiles": 0,
  "minChars": 80,
  "duplicateGroupCount": 0,
  "duplicateOccurrenceCount": 0,
  "omittedGroups": 0,
  "groups": []
}
```

The two-call harness verifies source bytes and the alias target unchanged, all default scan roots still absent, no agent index database created, and implementation bytes unchanged during capture. It inherits no credentials and does not modify a live service or contact a remote node.

### Previous repair proof (`c737c129`): extra paths and nested mapped roots

The official source CLI was run with isolated synthetic configuration/state/profile and no inherited credentials. Two pre-repair scenarios at `2b657775` incorrectly exited 0 with `filesScanned: 2`, one duplicate group and two occurrences: an extra path inside another mapped workspace, and a mapped workspace nested under `memory/`.

With the repair, each scenario runs the same command and returns the following actual error instead of a local duplicate report:


The three-call harness re-read every synthetic source file unchanged, checked that no agent index database was created, and verified the implementation bytes did not change during capture. It did not stop or modify any live service, contact any node, or access private notes.

Only synthetic refund-policy notes and synthetic node identifiers were used. The child environment did not inherit credentials or the user's home/config. prs.title: fix(codex): unblock replies after native children finish
prs.body:
Related: #172837

## What Problem This Solves

Replies can fail with “Codex thread … is claimed by active work; stop it first” after every native child has finished, because pending completion delivery still protects the parent against the cold resume needed to receive the result.

## User Impact

The parent can resume after all child results have been captured. Pending results retain delivery ownership and retry; running and resumable children, accepted submissions, and current foreground owners keep their existing protection. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Release the existing parent execution pin when every registered child is terminal, and reuse that rule when unregistering a child. Completion custody, receipts, retry budgets, successful delivery, and durable abandonment remain with their existing owners. #173018 already handles exact-assignment retirement on give-up; #173563 preserves it. This PR fixes the separate pin-timing gap, not historical exhaustion lacking durable evidence.

The human review identified three contention tests that treated the execution pin as a proxy for delivery custody. They now verify delivery admission and pending-result retention directly, including receipt arrival, retired-turn receipts, retry, and retirement while a handoff is in flight. No protection-holder taxonomy or additional lifecycle state is needed.

Original fix by @quqi1599; maintainer cleanup updates the contention contract, regression cleanup, and documentation. The focused contention-test repair is adapted from @Stronggenetics's #176177. That PR's broader catalog and completion-context changes are not superseded; #174900 also integrates this pin fix in a broader contributor proposal.

Deferred-effect facts: the pin-release decision reads the monitor's current child states and retention map synchronously, with no intervening await. Completion status/result and child/parent identities are the captured terminal facts; existing delivery checks revalidate monitor identity, requester binding, and completion custody at admission and after awaited delivery. This change adds no deferred configuration, path, limit, or authority snapshot.

## Evidence

Candidate `4aa2c5c1635fa318957c02fbb2200353ffb87473` cleanly merges main `64e9443af525212642b0406fbc454727f267a68a`, including CLI ratchet repair `e63269c28a22a6eec7c0758d54dc6dbe674e2886`. The four PR files are byte-identical to the reviewed previous head. Changed-file oxlint/oxfmt pass after the merge. Fresh exact-head [CI run 39183982150](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39183982150) is **successful**: 32 jobs passed, 30 skipped, zero failures. The baseline ratchet, both changed-extension bundles, production/test types, and lint pass. No inherited-failure exception is needed. The completed [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175246#issuecomment-6230935578) covers this exact head (2026-10-19 01:42:52 UTC), reports **findings=0**, and retains only a proof hold. Verbatim verdict: “Codex review: needs real behavior proof before merge.” PR CI is the proof per maintainer policy; live proof and negative controls were intentionally skipped.

- Source and history confirm the remaining pin-timing defect on main `bc529a16db05b80e3baca5455e9ff6e263aed3be`; no additional durable-assignment implementation is added. Native source inspected at `be2951ea34f0d295ed0becf97079f92fa5f6950e`: `codex-rs/core/src/agent/control.rs::maybe_start_completion_watcher` and `multi_agent_v2_followup_task_completion_notifies_parent_on_every_turn` in `codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/multi_agents_tests.rs`.
- Regression: `permits parent cold resume once every child is terminal, while preserving undelivered results`. It reaches the production release guard, retains protection with a running sibling, then permits release and preserves both result retries.
- Updated regressions: `rechecks receipt while completion delivery is in flight`, `rechecks retired-turn-receipt while completion delivery is in flight`, and `rechecks retirement while completion delivery is in flight`.
- Previous-head (`9b2a9c9dd64d`) PR CI ran **609 tests across 39 extension test files**, all passing. The parent cold-resume regression passed in **19 ms**; the receipt / retired-turn-receipt / retirement contention cases passed in **16 / 9 / 3 ms**. [Bundle 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39181207427/job/117834460116) ran 271 tests across 21 files (228 s job wall time); [bundle 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39181207427/job/117834460143) ran 338 tests across 18 files (243 s). CI invoked `time -p node --import tsx scripts/ci-run-node-test-shard.mts` with its selected plans. Production types, test types, and lint passed in jobs 117834769707, 117834769756, and 117834769748. Local tests, typechecks, live Gateway/Crabbox/Testbox proof, and production negative controls were intentionally skipped per maintainer policy. No leases were created. The case timings above are CI-reported test time, not isolated full-file wall time; no local runtime duration is claimed.
- Changed-file oxlint passes (3 files, 231 rules, zero diagnostics), oxfmt passes (4 files), and the standard commit content/format hook passes. The borrowed formatter is 0.68.0; CI owns validation with the pinned 0.72.0 formatter. Lint uses the existing repository core rules with the unrelated UI-only Solid override omitted because the borrowed install lacks that plugin. No Codex rule is disabled. `git diff --check` is included.
- Isolated Codex precommit and prescribed committed-branch autoreviews are both scoped-clean through P2, with no accepted/actionable findings. Reviews executed no repository code or tests.
- The exact-head ClawSweeper re-review acknowledges the contention repair and successful CI, with no actionable code findings. Exactly one [re-review request](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175246#issuecomment-6257793151) was posted for this head after the 20-minute post-CI window. Its live/negative-control proof request is intentionally not acted on under the explicit maintainer proof policy; the bot still displays that proof hold.

Exact numstat against the merged main base: production **+15/−5**, tests **+104/−4**, docs **+5/−0** (total **+124/−9**). The necessary production growth is one shared terminal-aware release rule replacing the unregister-only rule; no new owner, state, exported helper, schema, or configuration was added. Unrelated deletions would obscure the fix.

### Previous CI failure repaired on main

Previous-head [run 39181207427](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39181207427) passed the Codex tests, types, lint, and docs but failed the unrelated `root-help.test.ts` mock-export ratchet. Main repaired it in [e63269c28a22](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/e63269c28a22a6eec7c0758d54dc6dbe674e2886) by preserving real sub-CLI exports and removing the obsolete baseline row. The new merge commit includes that repair and triggers fresh CI; the old merge-ref run was not rerun.

prs.title: refactor(ai): remove fixed private provider options
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Private provider helpers accept policies and callbacks that every production caller fixes at the same value. Keeping the unused alternatives obscures the actual transport contracts.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change or operator action is intended. Public contracts and live transport protections remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep fixed policy at its existing owner: Mistral's 16 MiB response bound, schema caches' eight variants, Google's header API and tool-ID fallback, Anthropic's bounded error reader, and Responses reasoning/first-event/service-tier preparation. Remove only unselected private arguments and forwarding. Public SDK/package options, config, protocol, persisted data, security boundaries and standalone session memory are unchanged.

This is the AI-provider area split of a family spanning more than 80 files. Against base `29b4e141a78f79213207263fa89150f08b44adf2`: 15 paths, **55 net production lines and 2 net test lines removed**. Signed replacement head: `1ee832227286d0197959a2ceaffa57678b2f332b`.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Private Mistral/cache callers can no longer vary their fixed 16 MiB/eight-variant policies. Every production caller selected these values. The bounded-reader work #97648 and cache performance work #147543 remain; no resource protection is removed.
- Google's private lifecycle owns its process-lifetime tool-ID counter instead of receiving its sole implementation. The header helper requires the model/base URL already supplied and uses the same API literal. The opt-in Interactions capability from #149880 remains; this does not delete dormant preparation.
- The Anthropic reader no longer accepts unused byte/character/deadline/error-factory alternatives. Its 8 KiB/10 s bound, nonblocking cancellation, reader unlock and final redacted 400-character diagnostic cap remain. Transport extraction #111669 and cancellation repair #174238 remain; no incident guard is removed.
- Responses' lifecycle no longer accepts unselected overrides for first-event timing, abort or service-tier resolution, and managed replay no longer offers a never-selected reasoning-off mode. Real option-derived deadline/abort behavior, pricing, observation, replay identity and recovery remain. Any future internal alternative must establish an actual caller contract.

## Evidence

Whole-tree caller/export closure covers src, extensions, ui/src, packages and tooling. All twelve changed production blobs are byte-identical to independently reviewed head `74118e0fe34eb6d61bea8e23c2d02a3847e27e96`. The conflict repair retains main's inline Google header assertion and adds the now-required model argument. The author simplification pass retains existing owners and adds no framework, dependency, suppression, retry, skip or raised timeout.

Replacement-head proof completed successfully, serially under `nice -n 10` with isolated HOME/state: frozen install (10.2 s), both targeted native type graphs, 320 tests in 19 files (19.42 s engine/33.47 s wrapper), scoped lint for all 15 paths with one thread, 14 suppression tests (10.87 s engine/18.50 s wrapper), the runtime-cycle guard (zero value cycles), and whitespace checks. Focused Vitest used one worker. Earlier-head results are retained as historical evidence only.

The prior static/madge command did not complete under host load and is not claimed as passing. Its configured source graph includes src/extensions/ui, none of which this packages/ai-only slice modifies. No whole-graph typecheck, full check-changed, build, broad local suite, live-provider, billing or performance measurement is claimed. Exact-head hosted CI is required before landing.

## Prior-head CI and recovery

Old head `74118e0f` had an inherited closed-mock-fingerprint failure in root-help.test.ts plus the downstream aggregate gate; it was not green. Source/scanner replay established the protected-main defect. The replacement base includes its upstream repair `e63269c28a22a6eec7c0758d54dc6dbe674e2886`.

Two native merge attempts aborted before dispatch at GitHub's mergeability deadline. The campaign-authorized exact-head direct fallback then returned HTTP 405, merge conflicts; it did not merge. That conflict authorized this rebase. The old inherited-failure exception/evidence does not qualify the replacement head. No CI rerun or head update merely to chase green was used.

## Exact-head CI: inherited-failure exception

Run [39188674900](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39188674900), attempt 1, tested merge `169c847f105773bfcd057262eb1a5eb372bd9f91`: protected-main parent `26c6a4090f1f21f9552aa801e4a42927d32ae8b8`, reviewed PR parent `1ee832227286d0197959a2ceaffa57678b2f332b`. CI is not green. The full exact-head check census is terminal: 59 successes, 48 skips, one neutral CodeQL projection, nine failures and one cancelled historical metadata attempt. The neutral projection is not claimed as passing scan coverage. `security-fast`, dependency-review and security-sensitive-review succeeded.

The seven root failures below have one protected-main cause: #176453 moved the runtime `SidebarProjectionMemo` class to `sidebar-projection-cache.ts` while `session-attention.ts` still imports it from `sidebar-projection-memo.ts`. The importer and old-owner blobs are respectively `6e3f10c3e6e144d573427511a9f2760d8c2dd988` and `a72a97f4f64c74e615fd12a7c1ec99a586da68ed`, identical in protected main and the tested merge. Their static named-export binding cannot be affected by this packages/ai-only diff. Every typed diagnostic in the six failed type jobs is the same missing export or its downstream untyped `row`; no changed Provider path is named.

| Job | Failure and attribution |
| --- | --- |
| check-prod-types, 117857844843 | UI TS2724 missing export and downstream TS7006, protected-main defect above. |
| check-test-types-core-1, 117857844916 | Same two UI diagnostics only. |
| check-test-types-core-2, 117857844901 | Same two UI diagnostics only. |
