| Cancelled metadata attempt, 117856433557 | Superseded by the same completed successful metadata successor; not counted as passing or inherited failure. |

The coordinator flake ledger and the last six completed scheduled main runs were checked. No matching open signature was found; older bundled-UI successes predate this main cutover, so they are not claimed as reproductions. Session state readers repeat reply checks already enforced by their shared read owner. History request preparation also clones a freshly constructed CLI binding, and maintenance-config error handling repeats the same assertion on the immediately following line.

## Why This Change Was Made

Consume the shared reader's typed reply or undefined result directly. Preserve unavailable fallbacks, errors, projections, and every final authority check. Reuse the fresh CLI binding produced by its normalizer, including its independently constructed reseed receipt. Keep one unconditional maintenance-config assertion for both success and unavailable-config paths.

Production: net -3 lines across six files. Five repeated reply predicates, one duplicate clone, and one adjacent assertion are removed. No SQL statement, worker request, transaction envelope, schema, public API, or PostgreSQL bookkeeping changes. SQL/request/MAIN delta is estimated, unmeasured 0/0/0; no latency claim.

| Candidate | Decision and reason |
| --- | --- |
| C17692 | REMOVE: `getCliSessionBinding` constructs a fresh binding and nested reseed receipt before request capture. |
| F158 | REMOVE duplicate ambient-target reply discriminator; retain undefined-to-empty fallback. |

C17692 (f) and C18295 (g) are the two removed inventory IDs; C18297/C18298 are kept. F158–F162 are five separate census findings and are not counted again as static-inventory coverage.

No test assertions are weakened.

prs.title: perf(gateway): reduce startup lease inspection overhead
prs.body:
## Outcome

Withdrawn after real Gateway measurements. This transport selection removes a supervisor from an isolated cold lease read, but removes no workers from actual CLI startup and does not improve the targeted lock phase. No change was merged.

## Investigation

The reported near-one-second phase is not an unconditional sleep. `acquireWithWait` tries acquisition first. Ordinary contention retries at 250 ms; unverifiable foreign owners use a separate bounded heartbeat wait. Both paths report contention. The examined 4,534.5 ms startup had no corresponding contention message, but its historical log lacks the substep timing needed to attribute that individual outlier.

An instrumented baseline acquisition with synthetic state spent about 2–12 ms obtaining physical custody. A fresh acquisition then spent about 1,299 ms awaiting heartbeat-worker readiness. Existing-state acquisitions additionally spent 1,340–1,455 ms inspecting the prior lease and 1,265–1,269 ms awaiting the heartbeat. All recorded contention-sleep lists were empty. These are source-runtime diagnostics, not estimates of packaged production timings.

The candidate selects the reader's existing awaited-only transport. The independent safety review found that it preserves owner, foreign-namespace, damaged-index, admission, and native-cleanup protections. Removing the preflight would lose the unindexed/ambiguous-owner checks before repair. Moving the read to the main thread would lose worker-retirement guarantees for native handles when explicit SQLite close is unproven, including Bun.

## Measurement

Baseline: `330184b959d013867ddb2345a83e89216aa0d222`. Candidate: `87ac5ee95c24134953a9c4e92061da2a37b58a83`.

Acceptance recorded before measurement: synthetic free-lock and real Gateway startup/restart workloads; count sleeps and workers; preserve ownership safety; compare concurrent A/B under the exclusive measurement lock, swap 16-core CPU halves for the next pair, and reject an overall startup regression above 20%.

Two valid cold-process pairs used the real `src/entry.ts gateway run` path, Node 26.8.2, identical prepared 1.4 MiB state databases, separate state directories and ports, and disabled plugins/channels. Setup ran on CPUs 64–95; measurements ran concurrently on 96–111 and 112–127, swapped in the second pair. Observed `mpstat` load (context, including both benchmark arms): pair 1 mean CPU busy 23.0% across cores 96–127; pair 2 mean CPU busy 16.9% across cores 96–127. Both sides used matched module-loader indirection. Dirty pages remained below 2 GiB.

| Metric | Pair 1 baseline → candidate | Pair 2 baseline → candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `cli.bootstrap.gateway-lock` | 592.2 → 603.4 ms | 591.2 → 630.3 ms |
| `/readyz` | 47,486.8 → 47,296.2 ms | 43,851.1 → 43,486.0 ms |
| Process-tree CPU | 79 → 80 s | 76 → 73 s |
| Peak RSS | 3,106.5 → 3,069.9 MiB | 3,117.7 → 3,142.6 MiB |
| Workers started / active at startup | 9 / 7 → 9 / 7 | 9 / 7 → 9 / 7 |

Paired candidate-minus-baseline lock differences are **+11.2 ms and +39.1 ms**. Readiness differences are **−190.6 ms and −365.1 ms**, below 1% with no worker-count reduction. Every boot starts one native supervisor and three shared-state readers. This does not establish a useful startup improvement.

The isolated lock-only experiment saved 204.1 ms and 87.5 ms per pair on existing state, but that saving did not transfer to the real CLI flow. It is insufficient evidence for this change.

The full-flow workload was based on `scripts/bench-gateway-startup.ts --case skipChannels --runs 1 --warmup 0 --entry src/entry.ts --timeout-ms 120000 --gateway-runtime <baseline-or-candidate-wrapper>`. Temporary harness adaptations selected the prepared synthetic root and captured the existing `worker startup state` log. Early comparisons with listener collisions were discarded; final ports were separated by 200 and above the Linux ephemeral range. These source-mode, small-state runs do not reproduce the original production deployment or establish production p95 latency.

## Validation and review

- The new focused test fails on baseline and passes on the candidate: free acquisition never polls and avoids the supervisor in the isolated cold-reader case.
- 84 focused tests passed across `gateway-owner-lease.test.ts`, `gateway-lock.test.ts`, and `gateway-lock.namespace.test.ts` (66.84 s Vitest wall time). Changed-file oxfmt, oxlint, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent Codex autoreview was scoped-clean at P0–P2. The subsequent review request to measure total startup was accepted; the real-flow result led to withdrawal.
- [CI run 39188979252](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39188979252) failed seven jobs on the same missing `SidebarProjectionMemo` UI export (TS2724/TS7006 and bundler MISSING_EXPORT). The two changed files do not touch that UI code. No CI rerun or inherited-failure merge exception was used.
- No Testbox/Crabbox allocation, local build, or local benchmark. Production services and data were untouched.

Production delta: +7 lines; test delta: +35 lines. The experiment adds a transport choice without reducing work in the requested real flow, so it is withdrawn.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an automatic-reply heartbeat that calls the offered `heartbeat_respond` tool is incorrectly told that the tool is only accepted during a heartbeat run.

## User Impact

User impact: rejected `heartbeat_respond` calls now tell the model to follow the run's configured reply instructions. This remains correct for automatic-reply heartbeats and ordinary message-tool turns. Tool offering, acceptance, default prompts, and delivery policy are unchanged.

Heartbeat-enabled sessions offer `heartbeat_respond` on every turn to keep tool definitions stable for prompt caching, but only accepting heartbeat turns can use it. The rejection must describe that distinction without overriding the configured reply mechanism.

The follow-up also addresses the review finding that “reply with plain text” could strand an ordinary message-tool response. The existing rejection owner now gives delivery-mode-neutral guidance; no new routing or configuration is introduced.

## Evidence

Closes #126521

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes automatic exec command chains stopping early on zsh hosts when generated commands contain literal separators such as `===` or unmatched globs.

## User Impact

Commands such as `echo before; echo ===; echo after` now reach the final command. Automatic zsh exec passes unmatched patterns through literally. Explicitly selected zsh session shells retain native expansion behavior; no configuration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing shell resolver disables `EQUALS` and `NOMATCH` only for automatic exec, retaining startup-file suppression and ordinary tilde, brace, and matching-glob expansion. The macOS test list now includes the shell resolver, snapshot, and real-process regressions.

This resumes the bounded repair from the closed, unmerged [#126556](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/126556). Thanks to @bilzeng for the original repair and @TomSchuman for the report and macOS field evidence.

## Evidence

- [Installed CLI stable-to-repair proof](https://github.com/yinx65588-boop/openclaw/actions/runs/39142777649) passes on macOS 15.7.9 / zsh 5.9 / Node 24.21.0. The workflow verifies that every tracked file outside its proof fixture/workflow matches reviewed head `99d4aa60f95ca24932fd0cc13b717c9df659e75a`, builds and checks the canonical self-contained package, installs published `openclaw@2026.10.4`, reproduces both failures through the public local-agent CLI, and replaces that installation with the reviewed package in the same prefix. The documented `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` step migrates the existing agent database from schema 24 to 31; the subsequent public `sessions --agent main --json` readback retains the original session ID. Package replacement leaves config bytes unchanged. Doctor adds canonical defaults/metadata while preserving every pre-existing authored setting, and the repaired agent run leaves that migrated config unchanged. The workspace marker also survives. [Reproducible fixture and assertions](https://github.com/yinx65588-boop/openclaw/blob/fa07e4105fa7a41c56a299f540213802dfba6cad/.proof/agent-zsh-cli-proof.mjs).

  Redacted real tool results, returned through the HTTP adapter:

  ```text
  openclaw agent --local --agent main --session-id <isolated-session> \
    --message "Run the two specified shell command checks." --thinking off --timeout 60 --json

  Command: echo before; echo ===; echo after
    Stable: before / zsh:1: == not found / exit 1
    Repair: before / === / after

  Command: echo before; echo no-such-file-*.txt; echo after
    Stable: before / zsh:1: no matches found: no-such-file-*.txt / exit 1

Shell snapshots are disabled identically before and after; this proof covers automatic exec without a snapshot, not native PTY or an already-running Gateway. Session readback verifies the persisted entry, not full transcript replay. The checked package SHA-256 is `b96e2e97455163d534ba820ec19a34efb33e7a7c1818f02b9090dac03b003016`; the workflow retains the package and raw stdout/stderr, request-ledger and summary artifacts.

- [Final native baseline and repair proof](https://github.com/yinx65588-boop/openclaw/actions/runs/39107470779) on macOS 15.7.9 / zsh 5.9: identical regressions produce four intended failures and 42 passing controls with the original resolver; the repaired resolver passes all 76 tests across shell resolution, snapshots, host spawn and exec runtime. prs.title: fix(hooks): ignore sub-second timeoutSeconds instead of disabling the timeout
prs.body:
Closes #176027

## What Problem This Solves

`POST /hooks/agent` with a sub-second `timeoutSeconds` (e.g. `0.5`) runs the agent turn with no timeout at all. The value is floored to `0`, and `0` is the "no timeout" sentinel in `resolveAgentTimeoutMs`.

## User Impact

A caller asking for a very short timeout got the opposite: an effectively unlimited run (2147000000 ms, ~24.8 days), longer than omitting the field (48 h default). After this change, values below one second are ignored like other nonpositive values, as `docs/gateway/config-hooks.md` already documents.

## Why This Change Was Made

`normalizeAgentPayload` (`src/gateway/hooks.ts`) accepted any `timeoutSeconds > 0` and then floored it. It now accepts `>= 1`, so the documented flooring stays the same for values ≥ 1 and anything that would floor to `0` is ignored instead of becoming the unlimited sentinel. The hook-mapping path is unaffected: its config schema already requires a positive integer.

## Evidence

- Regression test in `src/gateway/hooks.test.ts` (1, 1.9, 2 → 1, 1, 2; 0.5, 0.999, 0, -1, NaN → ignored). On unmodified `main` it fails at `0.5`: expected `timeoutSeconds: undefined`, received `0`. Passes with the fix, along with the gateway hooks test files.
- HTTP-level regression test in `src/gateway/server.hooks.test.ts` (240124f): posts `timeoutSeconds: 0.5` and `1.9` to `/hooks/agent` through the real hooks server and checks the dispatched isolated run's payload: `0.5` leaves `timeoutSeconds` unset (inherits the configured budget), `1.9` becomes `1`. Green in CI (`checks-node-changed`) on 240124f.
- `pnpm tsgo` and oxlint clean on the changed files.
- Real gateway, `curl -X POST /hooks/agent -d '{"message":"ping","timeoutSeconds":0.5}'` (mock model server, temp state), reading the run's persisted `trace.metadata`:
  - before (main `cd4a350`): `"runtime":{"timeoutMs":2147000000,...}`
  - after (this branch): `"runtime":{"timeoutMs":172800000,...}`

prs.title: fix(auto-reply): multiline /dashboard drops requirement lines after the first
prs.body:
Fixes #176663

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: multiline `/dashboard` requests silently lose every requirement line after the first before reaching the agent.

## User Impact

Users can paste an indented list of dashboard requirements on the command line or start it on the next line. Every requirement reaches the agent with the bundled Control UI skill selected. Bare and single-line `/dashboard` requests and other commands retain their existing behavior. No configuration change or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add `dashboard` to the shared free-text argument-preserving set used by `/btw`, `/side`, `/loop`, `/goal`, and `/steer`. Reuse `matchSlashCommandToken` so the handler recognizes a newline after the command. Without both changes, the shared normalizer discards requirements or the dashboard handler misses the command.

Original fix by @masatohoshino; maintainer cleanup removes a redundant trim already owned by the shared parser and consolidates regression coverage through normalization and dashboard skill expansion. There is no second dashboard-specific normalization path.

## Evidence

prs.body:
Fixes #176750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Doctor tells operators to restore a database backup when its final readiness check fails because a read-only SQLite snapshot did not stabilize.

## User Impact

Doctor still refuses to complete repair, but retryable snapshot contention now tells operators to let writes settle and retry. Integrity failures retain restore guidance for the affected database, including when another database in the same report has a retryable failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

The snapshot worker already returns a typed `SqliteReadOnlyInspectionContentionError`. Readiness now retains that error in its existing cause map, and the message owner chooses Doctor guidance per database without matching error text. Gateway guidance, database checks, update refusal, and recovery behavior stay unchanged. No database writes, deferred effects, config, schema, or worker protocol changes are added.

The simplification pass retained the existing error and cause owners. Production grows by 15 lines (+25/-10) to preserve classification and distinguish mixed reports; deleting unrelated code to offset that would broaden this fix. Tests: +58/-0. Docs: +6/-0.

## What Problem This Solves

Typecheck graph discovery opens native TypeScript projects just to enumerate files, making local and CI planning slower and more memory hungry.

Related: #175711

## User Impact

Developers get faster graph discovery while retaining complete type-only dependency coverage, shard ownership, buildinfo checks, and the tsgo fallback. The completed noncore planner used 1,923 MiB instead of 7,246 MiB in this loaded-host measurement.

The full core planner remains blocked by the inherited `plugins-platform` budget failure: **723 test roots / 720 limit**, identical before and after. This PR does not change budgets. Full successful core-planner completion is therefore unproven; per-config membership is independently proven below.

## Why This Change Was Made

One `readTsconfigFileMembership` owner now calls `--listFilesOnly` through `resolveTypeCheckTool`: tsrs by default, tsgo where unsupported or explicitly forced. Both the boundary guard and CI planner use it. Config expansion remains on tsgo because tsrs rejects `--showConfig`.

Membership excludes the selected compiler package's own library directory, identified from the resolved compiler executable. It retains repository and dependency declarations, even when named `lib.es5.d.ts`. The old boundary already ignored compiler libraries for its `extensions/` finding filter, but its returned planner inventories included them. Bundled compiler libraries describe compiler identity, not repository membership; typechecking has already used tsrs's libraries since #175711.

The eager native snapshots, query adapter, and serial/snapshot branch disappear. The retired `OPENCLAW_CI_TYPE_PLAN_SERIAL` workflow env expression and obsolete test cases are removed; no tracked references remain. A maintainer can delete the repository variable `OPENCLAW_CI_TYPE_PLAN_SERIAL` because no workflow consumes it anymore. Production is 66 lines smaller; tests gain 27 lines net for the regression while removing duplicate mode replay and obsolete workflow assertions. No dependencies or compiler versions change.

## Evidence

Measured back-to-back on the same checkout based on main `dba2de1418b89eebcae98ad0ed4dbcb116e88d08`, using `/usr/bin/time -l`, Node 24.22.0, pnpm 12.11.1, macOS ARM64. The first two entry points exit 1 with the same existing budget finding; they are time-to-failure measurements. Avoiding eager snapshots explains the faster failing planner; the boundary CLI reaches its budget check before membership and is effectively unchanged. Noncore planning completes successfully in both versions, with identical returned graph names, configs, roots, and normalized file sets.

prs.title: fix(audit): avoid slow overflow pruning on decision writes
prs.body:
Fixes #176625

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes long audit decision write transactions that block Workboard, cron, and other shared state database writers even when retained decisions are below the row cap.

## User Impact

Audit decision inserts avoid rebuilding a list of up to 250,000 retained receipt IDs. The 30-day retention window, 250,000-row cap, oldest-first ordering, and combined 1,024-row expiry/overflow cleanup budget remain unchanged. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The retention owner now reads the current row count inside the existing write transaction, skips overflow deletion at or below the cap, and selects only the oldest excess rows within the remaining cleanup budget. SQLite uses its native fast-count operation and the existing ordering index; no process-local counter or schema change is needed. Fast count visits index pages, so this is not a claim of strict constant-time counting or measured end-to-end latency.

Cleanup remains synchronous in the existing writer transaction. The admitted database handle owns lifetime and path binding; retention time and limits remain the per-call snapshot; current rows are counted after expiry immediately before overflow deletion. No new deferred authority, configuration, identity, or session facts are introduced.

The simplification removes the retained-ID exclusion query. Production delta is +11/-8 (+3): the small increase is the explicit overflow guard, without adding caching or unrelated cleanup. Tests are +77/-0; docs are unchanged because the operator contract is unchanged.

## Evidence

Source and history confirm the reported query is still on main; it originated in #119815. The issue reports a 1,256 ms query returning zero overflow rows at 230,277 retained facts; this PR does not claim a new timing measurement.

PR CI is the test gate and covers the audit owner regressions, affected suites, typechecks, and static checks. New regressions in `src/audit/execution-decision-facts.test.ts`:

- `skips overflow deletion below and at the cap using SQLite's fast count`: observes real executed statements and checks native `EXPLAIN` opcodes; the old owner executes six deletes instead of three.
- `prunes exactly the oldest overflow within the remaining expiry budget`: checks expiry/overflow budget sharing, equal-time receipt ordering, and backdated inserts.

Changed-file checks passed:

```sh
changed_files=(src/audit/execution-decision-facts.ts src/audit/execution-decision-facts.test.ts)
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json "${changed_files[@]}"
node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check "${changed_files[@]}"
git diff --check
```

Independent Codex autoreview through P2: scoped-clean, no actionable findings; retention equivalence and regression coverage reviewed. Exact-head PR CI: [run 39186896785](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39186896785) passed for `41744df99a86081e1568435c0eb8caf587c4d468` (36 successful jobs, 28 planned skips; no failures or retries). The selected Node tests, production and test typechecks, lint, UI tests, and planned guards passed. GitHub’s automatic Codex review also completed on this head without findings.

Local unit tests, production-reverted negative controls, local typechecks, and live Gateway/Crabbox/Testbox proof were intentionally skipped per maintainer proof policy. No lease was created. Per-file test wall times are unavailable because GitHub rate-limited the detailed log request. ClawSweeper has acknowledged the PR; no code findings were posted at closeout.

prs.title: refactor(sessions): reuse memory actor input and snapshot copies
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Memory-session adapters copy registration inputs, reset entries, fork inputs, and participant snapshots a second time even though their actor owner already provides isolation. These extra deep copies do no useful work.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. Memory-session adapters retain input and snapshot isolation with fewer deep copies.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove five immediate caller copies before `actor.storage.mutate`, whose executor synchronously captures the complete mutation before admission callbacks or queuing. Return the participant array from the already deep-cloned memory snapshot directly. The durable branches, callback-facing copies, reset compare-and-swap expectation, and live authority checks remain unchanged.

Production: +5/-12 lines, net -7 across four files; six deep-copy operations removed. No SQL statement, worker request, transaction envelope, schema, public API, or PostgreSQL bookkeeping changes. SQL/request/MAIN delta is estimated, unmeasured 0/0/0. No latency claim.

<details>
<summary>Candidate ledger</summary>

| Candidates | Decision and reason |
| --- | --- |
| C16300, C16301 | REMOVE: registration identities and query are synchronously captured by the mutation executor. |
| C16396 | REMOVE: the reset entry immediately enters that same executor capture. |
| C17757, C17758 | REMOVE: fork data and patch immediately enter that same executor capture. |
| C16804 | REMOVE: the memory actor snapshot already deep-clones participants. |
| C16299, C16303, C16304, C16308 | KEEP: caller-owned durable inputs must survive asynchronous worker admission. |
| C16302 | KEEP: the eligibility callback must not receive mutable owner records. |
| C16307 | KEEP: synchronous authority callbacks run before selection and can mutate the caller-owned query. |
| C16395 | KEEP: a mutating reset builder must not alter the compare-and-swap expectation. |
| C16397 | KEEP: the callback receives the same immutable environment contract as the durable lifecycle path. |

14 inventory candidates reviewed: 6 removed, 8 kept, all category f.
</details>

## Evidence

Existing production-path memory suites cover registration eligibility and private returned records, intervening reset writes and a mutating builder, patched parent forks, and participant reads. No test assertion is weakened. The actor's sole request capture and snapshot copy remain in their original owners.

The simplify pass retains only the six duplicate copies. One independent Codex review completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings, with full capture, snapshot, storage-consumer and existing test context. Focused formatting, lint, and `git diff --check` pass. Exact-head CI [39185955670](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39185955670) passes all type, lint, source-contract, architecture/Madge, T1, dialect and worker-ratchet checks. All three PostgreSQL conformance shards pass. The ordinary run finished with 78 successful checks, 26 skipped checks, and three failing test groups plus their aggregate gate. Knip [117848875212](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39185961436/job/117848875212) reports zero new findings: all eight distinct symbols across production/full scans match main [117846593700](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39185301352/job/117846593700). The frozen dependency install passed after SSD clearance; dependency inputs match the previous successful install. Under the campaign WAVE-28 SSD-stall policy, the warm pair is deferred to the combined census; all counts above remain estimated and unmeasured.

CI failure attribution: the chat MAIN-count failures match main run 39176649118/jobs 117820741687 and 117820741767; recovery borrower cleanup matches main 39172446197/job 117808338765; the session-row-delta timeout and resource cleanup match main 39176649118/job 117820741627. prs.title: fix(telegram): route model-confirmation edit through rich funnel
prs.body:
Closes #123886

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with `richMessages: true` on their Telegram account and who complete the `/models` picker would see the final "✅ Model changed to…" confirmation rendered on top of / mixed with the stale rich-text markup from the picker's prior provider/model-list step, instead of a clean confirmation message. The picker's intermediate steps (provider list, model list, pagination) already fully replace the rich body correctly; only the terminal confirmation edit was affected.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `/models` picker sends its initial body as a rich message when `richMessages` is enabled, and every lifecycle edit to that message (provider list, model list, pagination) already routes through the rich funnel in `createTelegramCallbackMessageActions`. The final selection confirmation was the one exception: it always fell back to the legacy HTML `editMessageText` path. Editing a rich-sent message through that legacy text path does not fully replace the prior rich body — Telegram renders the new plain/HTML text mixed with the stale rich markup underneath it.

The fix converts the model-confirmation call site to author rich content via hand-built `RichText`/`InputRichBlock[]` when `richMessages` is enabled, following the existing `progress-draft-preview.ts` precedent for opting a `parse_mode: "HTML"` edit back onto the rich funnel:

- `TelegramCallbackRichTextOverride` lets `editCallbackMessage`/`editCallbackMessageWithButtons` accept an optional `richTextOverride`; when supplied, the edit routes through `getTelegramRichRawApi(bot.api).editMessageText(...)` with hand-built `rich_message` blocks instead of the legacy text funnel.
- `buildModelSelectionConfirmation` (new file) builds both the HTML and rich-block confirmation bodies from one shared text-building function, so the two representations can't drift apart — only model-id HTML-escaping and the runtime placeholder spelling differ per funnel.
- Non-rich accounts (`richMessages` disabled or unset) are unaffected; the legacy HTML path is unchanged for that funnel.

As a side effect of this fix, `bot-handlers.callback-router.ts` grew past the repo's 700-line oxlint `max-lines` cap, so the pre-existing ~290-line `handleTelegramModelCallback` function was extracted verbatim into a new file, `bot-handlers.model-callback.ts`, with no logic changes — pure file-split, kept in this PR so CI stays green (`AGENTS.md`: "Split files around ~700 LOC... never add a `max-lines` suppression").

This PR supersedes closed PR #124173, which introduced rich-block sending but left the confirmation edit on the legacy HTML path — ClawSweeper's own review of that PR classified it as `partial_overlap`, i.e. it fixed the picker's rich-block plumbing but not the actual reported bug (the confirmation still overlapped stale rich text). This change closes that exact gap.

## User Impact

Telegram operators with `richMessages: true` now see a single clean confirmation message when they finish the `/models` picker — no more stale/mixed rich-text markup left behind. Operators without `richMessages` enabled see no behavior change.

## Evidence

- Targeted tests: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.callback-actions.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.model-callback.ts extensions/telegram/src/model-confirmation-message.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot.test.ts` (and related callback-router/harness specs) — 151/151 passing, including a new regression test asserting `richTextOverride` routes through the rich funnel and 3 new `buildModelSelectionConfirmation` tests asserting HTML vs rich-block parity/escaping.
- Full extension suite: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram` — 3593/3594 passing; the 1 failure (`setup-surface.test.ts > accepts numeric sender ids only`) is a pre-existing, unrelated sandbox-locale artifact (`zh`-locale string vs expected English string), reproducible on `main` before this change.
- Typecheck: `pnpm tsgo:extensions` clean.
- Lint: `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on all touched/added files — exit 0, confirms the `max-lines` violation from the file-split is resolved (`bot-handlers.callback-router.ts` now 395 lines, down from 706).
- Format: `pnpm format` — no diff.
- Pre-land `$autoreview` (Codex `gpt-5.6-sol`, high reasoning): `autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported`, `overall: patch is correct (0.96)`.
- Live Telegram bot-to-bot proof was not feasible in this environment (no bot token configured); the mock-harness/unit proof above exercises the exact changed rich-funnel edit path per the ClawSweeper Review Policy real-behavior-proof gate for channel-visible changes.

## Update (commit 6973bab29b9)

Two fixes on top of the original commit:

- **ClawSweeper P1 finding addressed** — `editCallbackMessage`'s rich-routing branch previously fell back to `buildTelegramRichMarkdown(text)` for *any* rich-account callback edit that wasn't `parse_mode: "HTML"`, not just the model-picker confirmation. That silently ran markdown parsing over arbitrary un-authored text from approval receipts (`terminalizeApprovalMessage`), the plugin SDK's `respond.editMessage`, and the model picker's own intermediate pagination/provider-list/model-list/error edits — none of which are markdown-authored, so incidental `*`/`_`/backtick/`[` characters (e.g. in provider/model ids or user-controlled error text) could be reinterpreted as formatting instead of sent literally. Fixed by making rich routing strictly opt-in per call: it now only fires when the caller explicitly supplies `richTextOverride`'s hand-built blocks (as the model-picker confirmation does); every other caller — regardless of `richMessages`/`parse_mode` — stays on the legacy literal-text funnel, exactly as before this PR. `buildTelegramRichMarkdown` is no longer imported by this file (still used correctly elsewhere: streaming draft previews and the general outbound-delivery pipeline, where callers genuinely author markdown).
- **CI fixes**: `check-test-types` (two `bot-handlers.callback-actions.test.ts` blocks needed explicit `vi.fn<T>()` typing plus a null-check helper for `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`-safe `.mock.calls.at(0)` access) and `check-dependencies`/knip (`ModelSelectionConfirmationParams`/`ModelSelectionConfirmation` had no external importer and shouldn't have been exported).

**Correction to my earlier claiming comment on #123886**: I stated "clean typecheck" there; at that point `check-test-types` and `check-dependencies` were actually failing on CI (fixed now, in this commit). Apologies for the inaccurate evidence claim — flagging it here so the record is accurate.

### Updated evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.callback-actions.test.ts` — 7/7 passing, including a rewritten test asserting plain-text edits with no `richTextOverride` stay on the legacy funnel even when `richMessages` is enabled (inverts the prior test, which asserted the now-fixed over-broad behavior), and updated fallback/error-path tests that now supply an explicit override to exercise the rich funnel.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram` (full extension suite) — 3593/3594 passing; same single pre-existing unrelated `setup-surface.test.ts` locale failure noted above, reproduced identically on this branch's pre-fix HEAD via `git stash`.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — both clean.
- `knip` production + all-exports check — clean, no new dead exports.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt` — no diff. `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on touched files — exit 0.
- Pre-land `$autoreview` (Codex `gpt-5.6-sol`, high reasoning) rerun on this commit: `autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported`, `overall: patch is correct (0.98)`.
- Live Telegram bot-to-bot proof remains not feasible in this environment (no bot token configured), unchanged from the original PR evidence.

## Update (commit a0dec118a21): delete-and-reply instead of legacy-edit on rich-edit failure

ClawSweeper's follow-up P2 finding on the prior commit: `editCallbackMessage`'s
catch block fell back to `legacyEditCallbackMessage(text, editParams)` whenever
the rich raw-API edit failed for a non-terminal reason. `richTextOverride` is
only ever supplied for a message that was itself sent as rich (the model
picker's final confirmation edit), so a legacy-text retry there reproduces the
exact stale-rich-markup symptom #123886 reported — the new text lands mixed
with the prior rich body instead of replacing it.

Fixed by extracting a shared `deleteAndReplyCallbackMessage` helper (delete
the rich-sent message, then send a plain reply) and using it both for this
new failure path and for `editCallbackMessageWithButtons`'s existing "no text
in the message" recovery, which had the same delete-then-reply logic inlined
already — a small dedup alongside the fix, not just a symptom patch.

### Updated evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.callback-actions.test.ts`
  — 8/8 passing, including a new test ("deletes and replies instead of
  legacy-editing when the rich edit fails for a non-terminal reason") and the
  `editCallbackMessageWithButtons` describe block's "deletes and replies,
  through the real /model-picker-confirmation call shape, when the rich edit
  fails" case, now reusing the shared helper.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram` (full extension suite) —
  3594/3595 passing; same single pre-existing unrelated `setup-surface.test.ts`
  locale failure noted above (reproduces identically on `origin/main`, not
  touched by this branch).
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` — clean.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on both touched files — exit 0.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt` on both touched files — no diff.
- `knip` (production + dependencies) — clean, no new unused exports.
- Pre-land `$autoreview` (Codex `gpt-5.6-sol`, high reasoning) rerun on this
  commit: `autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported`,
  `overall: patch is correct (0.97)`.
- Live Telegram bot-to-bot proof remains not feasible in this environment (no
  bot token configured), unchanged from the original PR evidence.


## Update (commit f082965e64c): correct inline comment on rich-funnel invariant

ClawSweeper's re-review on `a0dec118a21` surfaced one actionable finding:

- **[P3] Correct the callback-funnel explanation** — `extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.model-callback.ts:294-298`. The inline comment claimed the picker's provider/model-list edit steps "already edit through the rich funnel when richMessages is enabled." That's inaccurate: `editCallbackMessageWithButtons` only takes the rich path when the caller explicitly supplies `richTextOverride`, and none of the list/pagination/error edit calls in this file pass one — only the terminal confirmation does.

Verified the finding against real code before fixing:
- `bot-handlers.callback-actions.ts` gates rich routing on `if (!richMessages || !richTextOverride)` falling back to legacy — both conditions are required, not just `richMessages`.
- Grepped all 10 `editMessageWithButtons`/`editCallbackMessageWithButtons` call sites in `bot-handlers.model-callback.ts`: only the final confirmation call supplies rich blocks; every provider-list/model-list/pagination/error edit omits `richTextOverride` and stays on the legacy funnel.

Fix: reworded the comment to state the true invariant — those list/pagination/error steps stay on the legacy HTML funnel, and this terminal confirmation is the one call that explicitly opts into the rich funnel via `richTextOverride`. Comment-only change, no behavior difference.

Validation:
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.callback-actions.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot.test.ts` — 149/149 passing.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.model-callback.ts` — clean.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.model-callback.ts` — applied.
- `git diff --check` — clean.

Note: ClawSweeper's proof-confidence score on this PR is driven by the disclosed, unresolved "no bot token configured in this sandbox" limitation — real Telegram behavior proof for the rich-edit/delete-and-reply path is still outstanding and I can't produce it here. That gap remains honestly disclosed rather than worked around.



## Update (commit 952e6f88239): correct remaining rich-funnel comment (late finding)

ClawSweeper's re-review on `f082965e64c` surfaced one actionable finding:

- **[P3] Correct the remaining rich-funnel explanations** — `extensions/telegram/src/model-confirmation-message.ts:4-7`. Flagged as a late finding: the same inaccurate claim fixed at `bot-handlers.model-callback.ts:294-298` in the prior commit was still present in this file's JSDoc header ("the picker's provider/model-list edits already went through the rich funnel"), and duplicated in a regression-test comment at `bot.test.ts:2881`.

Verified before fixing: grepped every `richBlocks` usage in `extensions/telegram/src/**` — `model-confirmation-message.ts` is the sole producer, and the terminal confirmation edit in `bot-handlers.model-callback.ts` is the sole consumer. Provider/list/pagination/error edits never supply `richTextOverride` and stay legacy-only, confirming the same corrected invariant already landed in the previous commit.

Fix: reworded both comments to state that legacy HTML is used by every other picker step (and as this confirmation's fallback), while rich blocks are used only by this terminal confirmation, which explicitly opts into the rich funnel via `richTextOverride`. Comment-only change, no behavior difference.

Validation:
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.callback-actions.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot.test.ts` — 149/149 passing.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt` on both touched files — clean, no reformatting needed.
- `git diff --check` — clean.

Note: the disclosed "no bot token configured in this sandbox" real-Telegram-proof gap remains unresolved and unchanged from prior updates.



## Update (commit d55b43e32ef): send fallback before deleting the picker

ClawSweeper's re-review on `952e6f88239` (reviewed_at `2026-08-16T01:39:38.304Z`) surfaced one actionable finding:

- **[P2] Send the fallback before deleting the picker** — `extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.callback-actions.ts:115-118`. `deleteAndReplyCallbackMessage` deleted the rich picker before awaiting `sendMessage`. If that send failed, the model selection had already been applied but the user lost both the picker and its confirmation — a silent-failure outcome per this repo's own severity doctrine (silent failure ranks above crash or missing feature).

Verified before fixing:
- Read `deleteAndReplyCallbackMessage` in full: it awaited `deleteCallbackMessage()` (swallowing its own errors) and only then called `replyToCallbackChat(text, replyParams)`. Exactly as described.
- Confirmed via `git log --oneline -- extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.callback-actions.ts` that this helper (and its ordering) was introduced by this PR's own commit `a0dec118a21`, not a pre-existing unrelated defect — squarely in-scope to fix here.
- Confirmed via grep that no existing test covered this ordering (only that both calls occurred, not their order or the rejection path).

Fix: reordered `deleteAndReplyCallbackMessage` to call `replyToCallbackChat` (send) first, then make `deleteCallbackMessage` best-effort only after a successful send. A send failure now propagates untouched and never triggers a delete, so the picker is never destroyed without a working replacement.

Added two regression tests in `bot-handlers.callback-actions.test.ts`:
- asserts `sendMessage`'s invocation order is before `deleteMessage`'s (fails pre-fix: order was reversed);
- asserts a `sendMessage` rejection propagates and `deleteMessage` is never called (fails pre-fix: delete already happened unconditionally before the send was even attempted).

Both new tests were confirmed to fail against the pre-fix code (via `git stash` of the production change alone) for the intended reason, then pass after the fix.

Validation:
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.callback-actions.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot.test.ts` — 151/151 passing.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt` on both touched files — applied, clean.
- `git diff --check` — clean.
- `.claude/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local` (Codex, gpt-5.6-sol, high reasoning) — clean, no accepted/actionable findings.

Note: the disclosed "no bot token configured in this sandbox" real-Telegram-proof gap remains unresolved and unchanged from prior updates.


## Update (commit 4ebf2f18165): forward business context to the fallback picker's deletion

ClawSweeper's re-review on `d55b43e32ef` (reviewed_at `2026-08-16T03:37:58.723Z`) surfaced one actionable finding:

- **[P2] Forward business context when deleting the fallback picker** — `extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.callback-actions.ts:119-121`. `deleteAndReplyCallbackMessage` sends the replacement with the callback's business context but then calls `deleteCallbackMessage`, whose delete omitted it. On a Business callback whose rich edit fails, the replacement could be sent while deletion silently failed and was swallowed, leaving the stale interactive picker behind.

Verified before fixing:
- Re-read `deleteCallbackMessage`: it called `bot.api.deleteMessage(chat_id, message_id)` unconditionally, while its siblings `legacyEditCallbackMessage` and `replyToCallbackChat` both forward `business_connection_id`.
- Checked grammY's typed API surface (`node_modules/grammy/out/core/api.d.ts`): `deleteMessage(chat_id, message_id, signal?)` has **no** `business_connection_id` parameter at all — unlike `editMessageText`/`sendMessage`/`editMessageReplyMarkup`, which all accept one.
- Cross-checked against the Telegram Bot API's own method list (`@grammyjs/types/methods.d.ts`): `deleteMessage` genuinely has no such field. Telegram instead exposes a dedicated method for this exact case, `deleteBusinessMessages(business_connection_id, message_ids)`, which grammY surfaces as `bot.api.deleteBusinessMessages(...)`. Deleting a business-sent message is a different Bot API call, not `deleteMessage` plus an extra field.

Fix: `deleteCallbackMessage` now calls `bot.api.deleteBusinessMessages(business_connection_id, [message_id])` when the callback carries business context, and falls back to the existing `bot.api.deleteMessage(chat_id, message_id)` otherwise.

Added a regression test in `bot-handlers.callback-actions.test.ts` asserting that a Business callback's rich-edit-failure recovery deletes via `deleteBusinessMessages` with the right connection id and message id, and never calls `deleteMessage`. Confirmed it fails against the pre-fix code (via `git stash` of the production change alone — `deleteBusinessMessages` is never called pre-fix) for the intended reason, then passes after the fix.

Validation:
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.callback-actions.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot.test.ts` — 152/152 passing.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — clean.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt` on both touched files — applied, clean.
- `git diff --check` — clean.
- `.claude/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local` (Codex, gpt-5.6-sol, high reasoning) — clean, no accepted/actionable findings ("patch is correct (0.99)").

Note: the disclosed "no bot token configured in this sandbox" real-Telegram-proof gap remains unresolved and unchanged from prior updates.


## Update (head 6328eb54392): mock-gateway harness — executed transcript + verdict JSON (real-behavior proof)

ClawSweeper's `needs real behavior proof` gate asks for the added Gateway harness to be *executed* against this head, with its terminal output **and** verdict JSON supplied together. This section supersedes and consolidates my two earlier (separately-posted, and confusingly-worded) proof updates into one honest, co-located block.

Per `AGENTS.md`'s real-behavior-proof gate — "a mock-gateway harness run (mock channel API + mock provider + ephemeral gateway, verdict JSON in the PR body) satisfies it for channel-visible changes covering the changed path; live-channel proof is stronger evidence."

prs.title: fix(trajectory): session.ended timestamp matches model.completed before cleanup
prs.body:
Closes #102014

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where trajectory exports showed `session.ended` with the same timestamp as `model.completed`, so cleanup duration looked like zero even when teardown took real wall-clock time.

## Why This Change Was Made

`session.ended` was recorded at finalize time, right after model completion, so its timestamp preceded session teardown. This PR captures the terminal payload at finalize and records `session.ended` only after attempt cleanup completes, on both the embedded runner and the Codex app-server. No new event types or exporter knobs; payload fields are unchanged, only emit timing moves from finalize into post-cleanup.

Rebased note (2026-08-26): the original branch predated the embedded-attempt lifecycle rewrite, so this was re-implemented onto current `main` (`attempt-finalize.ts` / `attempt-session-settle.ts` / `attempt-settle.ts` on the embedded side, `run-attempt-finalize.ts` / `run-attempt-cleanup.ts` / `run-attempt-turn-start.ts` for Codex). Review findings from the previous round are addressed:

- P1 "Guarantee terminal recording when Codex cleanup throws": `cleanupCodexAttempt` now records `session.ended` (captured payload, or the derived fallback) inside its `finally` block as the `codex-trajectory-terminal` step, followed by a terminal flush, so a teardown failure can no longer skip terminal recording.
- P2 "Finish startup-failure teardown before ending the session": the Codex turn-start failure path now captures the payload and records it only after binding clear, thread unsubscribe, route release, sandbox release, and shared-client lease release all finish.

## User Impact

Operators reading trajectory traces can measure real session end time versus model compute time, including cleanup latency.

## Evidence

Verified at head `0d46a743604` (current `origin/main` `636e21b1985` plus these two commits), Windows 11, Node v24.15.0.

Embedded runner tests:

```

Test Files  16 passed (16)
     Tests  141 passed (141)
```

Codex app-server tests (new ordering coverage: `session.ended` recorded after `thread/unsubscribe` and after the one-shot client `closeAndWait`, on both the success path and the startup-failure path):

```
npx vitest run extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts -t "session.ended"

Tests  2 passed | 146 skipped (148)
```

Full `run-attempt.test.ts` A/B on this machine: 13 failures are `EBUSY: resource busy or locked, unlink *.sqlite` temp-dir cleanup flakes that reproduce identically on unmodified `origin/main` (13 failed / 133 passed baseline vs 13 failed / 172 passed with this PR's files in the same run); the failure set is identical test-for-test, so they are pre-existing Windows-only flakes, not regressions.

Revert-red check: with only the production hunks stashed, the new Codex ordering tests fail (2 failed) and the new/updated embedded cleanup tests fail (12 failed); all pass with the hunks restored.

Repo checks: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` all clean. `oxfmt --check` clean on touched files. `pnpm check` guards pass, including the assertion SAFETY comment ratchet (the one new field uses a typed spread instead of an `as` assertion).

### Live embedded trajectory artifact (2026-08-26, this head)

Ran on this PR head (`0d46a743604`), Windows 11, Node v24.15.0, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, embedded `openclaw agent --local --json`, model `mistral/mistral-small-latest` (no Telegram / Vertex / gateway secrets).

Runtime event order from `trajectory_runtime_events`:

```

seq=1 trace.metadata       2026-08-26T10:52:02.680Z

`session.ended` is recorded after `model.completed` and after `trace.artifacts` (7ms delta on this short no-tool turn), matching the fixed ordering: the terminal event now carries the post-cleanup wall-clock time instead of sharing the `model.completed` timestamp.

prs.title: refactor(plugins): remove repeated private preparation work
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin preparation repeats normalization, freezes private readonly objects, and clones MCP subscription arguments a second time after the request owner already captured them.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior or public SDK contract changes. Plugin preparation does less allocation and repeated work while preserving caller snapshot isolation and final execution authority.

## Why This Change Was Made

Private provider catalogs, loader defaults, command runtime state, and core-only match results already have explicit readonly ownership. Their freezes are redundant. Runtime consumers still receive separate method-table spreads, provider membership is still copied at admission, and public runtime/catalog/dispatch capabilities retain their existing protections.

Reuse prefix and web-search normalization results inside the same invocation and the normalized model ID passed to the private runtime-properties helper. Provider-key comparisons remain lazy because eager normalization would add work when channel checks short-circuit. The generation codec reuses its same-call native classification while retaining native snapshot admission. MCP identity preparation borrows arguments from the request's already deep-cloned private snapshot; the ingress clone and live request/credential/cleanup checks remain.

Accepted edge: internal readonly contracts govern private values; unsupported mutation through casts is not a supported caller contract. No SQL, worker requests, transactions, schema, PostgreSQL bookkeeping, or SDK surface changes. Expected SQL/request/MAIN delta is 0/0/0, estimated and unmeasured; one final lane baseline/candidate warm pair remains pending after the sequential landings; no local workload has run. No latency claim.

## Evidence

Production +37/-47, net -10 lines; tests +9/-1. Changed-file formatting, type-aware lint, and whitespace checks pass. The first independent Codex review was incomplete because evidence batching separated required context; the second reviewed one complete packet and found no actionable P0–P2 defects. Exact-head [ordinary CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39187595165) passed: all 13 owner files ran under Bun (153 passing cases), and lint/types, source contracts, Madge, T1/worker and dialect ratchets passed. Supplemental [Knip](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39187607653/job/117853487355) completed all three export scans with zero new findings: production 5, full-tree 5 and scripts 0. Every finding and the single unused file match [scheduled main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39186683798/job/117850679944) by rule/file/symbol. The [published-driver update cell](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39187607653/job/117858565938) passed against final candidate `8ad518cb44415aab8f301975f75f98f07a838ece`; the actual update step completed successfully in 7m06s.

The existing MCP cleanup test is extended to mutate nested caller arguments immediately after subscription begins and verify both outbound renewal and eventual cleanup retain the original arguments. Existing provider catalog, loader-copy, command-retirement, codec, URL/network, hook-context and web-search tests cover the other ownership boundaries.

<details>
<summary>Candidate ledger</summary>

| IDs | Category | Decision and reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| C30801, C30802, C30803, C30804 | f | REMOVE private prepared-catalog freezes; consumers only read/project. KEEP the copied outer providers array to isolate caller membership changes. |
| C31040 | f | REMOVE the second clone of MCP subscription arguments already owned by a deep-cloned admitted request. KEEP the original caller-request snapshot. |
| C30531, C30532, C30533 | f | REMOVE freezes on private loader defaults with existing explicit readonly types; consumers still receive their facade spreads. |
| C30682, C30683 | f | REMOVE freezes on private WeakMap command state and its fresh command list. |
| C30689, C30690 | f | REMOVE freezes on core-only match results. KEEP the opaque dispatch capability freeze. |
| C30385 | b | REMOVE repeated prefix normalization in one synchronous hook-context invocation; preserve original-case output and absent-provider behavior. |
| C30386 | b | KEEP: eager provider-key normalization would add common-path work when channel comparisons short-circuit, plus one production line. Preserve the lazy comparisons. |
| C31122, C31123, C31124 | b | REMOVE repeated scopes, credential-label and docs-URL normalization; preserve optional-property omission. |
| F140 (census-only) | b | REMOVE repeated native ownership predicate; reuse the boolean computed earlier in the same synchronous encoder. KEEP snapshot ownership/disposal admission. |
| F145 (census-only) | b | REMOVE private helper's repeated model-ID normalization; sole caller already normalizes/rejects empty IDs. KEEP the optional branch, encoding, network/SSRF/body limits and live authority. |
| C30525, C30526, C30527, C30528, C30529, C30530, C30534 | f | KEEP: these freezes supply inferred readonly types; removal needs additional type scaffolding and has no accepted smaller cut. This is not a security claim. |
| C30684, C30686, C30687, C30688 | f | KEEP: public SDK runtime/catalog snapshots and opaque dispatch have different ownership contracts. |
| F144 (census-only) | b | KEEP: public SDK provider factory promises fresh mutable config; sharing would change alias behavior. |
| F141, F146 (census-only); C31098 | c | KEEP: cycle-aware allocation/exhaustiveness and nonempty-tuple witnesses preserve type-safe control flow; no accepted smaller cast-free rewrite. |


Sixteen unique static IDs and two census-only findings are selected for removal.

</details>

prs.title: perf(sessions): skip inactive requester resolution for owner counts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repeated `sessions.list` owner-count requests resolve every retained subagent requester into the session roster, including requesters whose descendants have all finished. This repeats scope selection work across connected viewers even when the response rows are unchanged.

## User Impact

Reduces server work for the sidebar ownership summary while preserving visible sessions, owner counts, sharing checks, and conditional/delta responses. No configuration, schema, or protocol changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Filter requester candidates through the existing clock-specific active-descendant index before resolving roster entries. Direct active-run candidates and projected follow-up activity remain included, so completed child lineage can still keep a parent running during a later turn. Existing selection sharing, ordering, row presentation, and delta history retain their current owners; no new cache is introduced.

Production code grows by two lines to retain all three live-activity contracts while skipping terminal-only history. The larger script change replaces the old one-socket timing mode with a reproducible 35-socket, six-variant Gateway workload and phase/CPU capture.

## Evidence

- Regression is red on baseline: two terminal requester scope lookups; green with the filter: zero, with unchanged counts. The existing test also covers nested live descendants, completed-parent/live-grandchild state, later child follow-up turns, queued work, and sharing/ownership changes.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-read-owner-counts.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 3 passed.
- Existing cross-viewer/invalidation proof: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/session-list-viewers.perf.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 3 passed.
- Changed-file oxfmt and scoped core/scripts oxlint passed. `pnpm tsgo:core` passed using the native checker. Broader proof is delegated to PR CI.
- Independent Codex autoreview: scoped clean through P2.

### Measurement rule, recorded before comparison

The driver adds five dashboard sessions through the real RPC for persistent child lineage. Compare first requests after reconnect and warmed steady requests separately across sidebar, general, compact, involving, owner-count, and child variants. Capture handler/queue timings, selection/preparation, row presentation, decoration, response serialization, and main-thread CPU where existing diagnostics distinguish them.

Run baseline and candidate concurrently under one exclusive measurement lock on separate 16-core CPU sets, then swap sets. Use identical options and five steady cohorts, five-second polling, and one synthetic label mutation per second. Decide using within-pair differences. A useful reduction must improve attributable work or handler/CPU cost without a reproducible latency regression; a move above 20% requires investigation.

| owner-counts / steady | 55.649 → 10.765 | 48.562 → 9.244 | 3.032 → 0.369 | 0.184 → 0.167 | 0.000 → 0.000 | 0.094 → 0.080 |
| children / steady | 8.812 → 7.714 | 7.605 → 6.528 | 0.061 → 0.073 | 0.162 → 0.183 | 0.000 → 0.011 | 0.045 → 0.048 |

</details>

### Adverse cells and limits

The control variants do not invoke the changed owner-count filter. Pair 2 general reconnect happened before the first owner query, so the changed filter had not executed. It nevertheless had handler mean 10.272 → 12.965 ms (+26.2%), p50 11.339 → 14.270 ms (+25.9%), client p50/p99 +25.1%/+36.2%, and CPU/call 2.959 → 3.977 ms (+34.4%); pair 1's same control was neutral. There is no repeatable control CPU increase and GC does not explain this cell specifically. This is evidence of host/workload variation, not a demonstrated owner-filter regression.

Other adverse tails are retained: pair 1 children steady handler p95 2.861 → 3.438 ms (+20.2%, +0.577 ms), while mean/p50 and client latency improve and CPU is unchanged; pair 2 general steady handler p99 13.816 → 17.656 ms (+27.8%) and client p99 87.068 → 107.228 ms (+23.2%), while its mean is +8.8%, median +2%, CPU +2.6% and pair 1 improves; pair 2 children steady handler p99 3.731 → 6.009 ms (+61%, +2.278 ms), while mean/p50, client latency and CPU improve. The separate rounded list-diagnostic timer also reports adverse children tails (pair 1 steady p95 2.006 → 3.006 ms, pair 2 reconnect p95 3.006 → 4.014 ms, pair 2 steady p99 3.006 → 6.014 ms).

Pair 2 first-sidebar materialization differs (A: 100 materialized / 0 reused; B: 93.143 / 6.857 per call) because of startup publication before the owner filter executes. Other row-work blocks match. No extra runs were added to seek favorable control cells. The owner-query reduction holds in both swapped pairs, in both reconnect and steady phases, and in CPU work as well as handler wall time.

CPU-half mean busy percentages were 5.67% / 5.89% in pair 1 and 6.97% / 6.11% in pair 2; maximum one-second half averages were 32.82% / 36.97% and 63.48% / 63.94%. `mpstat` includes the benchmark itself and concurrent host work. The fixture uses 64 MiB logical transcript text (agent/state DB sizes 235,630,592 / 11,771,904 bytes); it does not reproduce multi-GB transcript page-cache pressure or real model/channel traffic. The 35 clients run controlled query cohorts, not an observed production query mix. No production-wide CPU or latency reduction is claimed.

Reproduce with the committed fixture and measurement scripts (Node 26.8.2, pnpm 12.11.1 used here). Build and generate fixtures sequentially on preparation cores; run both sides under one exclusive lock on separate 16-core sets, same `--start-at`, then swap sets:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts sourcePerformance
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/team-shape-fixture.ts \
  --state-dir <side> --now 1792375086000 \
  --sessions 5000 --runs 6000 --transcript-mib 64
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/team-shape-measure.ts \
  --state-dir <side> --entry <built-entry> --port <loopback-port> \
  --clients 35 --samples 5 --poll-ms 5000 --mutation-ms 1000 \
  --start-at <shared-epoch> --revision <revision>
```

### Final-head CI and inherited failure

[CI run 39189023210, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39189023210) tested head `e3cec381066868105251a117a73a59790a15eb48` merged into main `4761d3278209afe7d13130d385cbd00f4f5eaec0` as `3147579776739fa54f931e56773aa8fe827a3d48`. It completed with 30 successful jobs, 25 skipped jobs and nine failures (eight root jobs plus the aggregate gate). Security-fast, lint, selected Node tests, documentation and source/architecture guards passed. Exact-head hosted Codex review completed with no findings; local independent reviews were also clean.

All eight root failures are the same inherited UI import defect: `session-attention.ts` imports `SidebarProjectionMemo` from `sidebar-projection-memo.ts`, which no longer exports it. Build and UI E2E fail with `MISSING_EXPORT` before UI tests; production types and all five core test-type stripes report TS2724 plus the downstream TS7006. The failing files are byte-identical between the tested main parent and this PR; they also match the baseline in [the already-merged repair #176799](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176799), which records the failing baseline production build/native typecheck, then passing UI typecheck, 4/4 attention tests and production UI build after the one-line import fix. Main now contains that repair as `e070647a0cf28d966a8a1d2022c1dc0b4083505d`.

This is an inherited-failure landing, not a green-CI claim. Failure logs were inspected once and retained; no CI reruns or unrelated fixes were added. Full UI E2E coverage remains unrun because its setup failed. Runtime LOC is +2; benchmark/docs LOC is +446; regression LOC is +8. The runtime growth preserves the existing direct-run and follow-up activity sources while deleting unnecessary history resolution work.

The separate [Blacksmith Build Artifacts Testbox run 39189023160](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39189023160), on the same head, also failed its build job with exactly the same `SidebarProjectionMemo` missing export. Its log was separately inspected; this adds no different failure cause.

prs.title: refactor(gateway): refresh session discovery watches in place
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Auxiliary session-history source discovery hands shared watches through a chain
of retired cache generations and keeps an unused synchronous acquisition path.

## User Impact

Normal history source selection, external-path refresh, cancellation and shutdown
retain their existing owners. Auxiliary topology can change between preparation
and receiver selection; physical-path and disclosure checks remain mandatory.

## Why This Change Was Made

Refresh the existing bounded memo in place. One pending refresh shares its
outcome, retains intersecting watches, and prunes retired unique paths. Delete
the unused synchronous acquisition, unused returned currency closures, and
copies of prepared facts that the producer and receiver do not mutate.

This is one session-history discovery AREA recovered from the parked family,
not a replay of its wider changes. Three paths: production +55/-106, 51 net
lines removed; tests +90/-47, 43 net lines added. Whole packet: eight net lines
removed. The test growth adapts the existing synchronous cases to the actual
async acquisition and adds shared-rejection/next-request recovery coverage.
The worker resolver stays in its existing leaf owner.

No public config, protocol, SDK, persisted shape, schema, permission, retention,
durability or dependency change. Phase E standalone session memory, its factory,
registry, expiry, federation machinery and tests are wholly untouched.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- The recursive replacement chain came from #172838, which measured native
  macOS watch-close stalls of 0.4–19 seconds. Keep that measured performance
  benefit by retaining common watches directly; no generation custody is needed.
  Failure, bounded eviction and root close still release owned observations.
- The wrapper no longer repeats the registry-token check after the producer
  has validated its canonical snapshot. Auxiliary topology may change afterward;
  the receiver still validates captured physical candidates and primary/live
  disclosure authority. The next request refreshes invalidated auxiliary facts.
- The synchronous acquisition introduced in #150625 no longer has a production
  caller. Its human coordination-visibility issue #150488 does not require this
  dead wrapper: actual history lineage remains on the async worker path.
- Prepared request facts are shared without an extra deep copy. The sole
  production consumer serializes and forwards them without mutation; the worker
  resolver likewise does not mutate them. Unsupported internal mutation is not
  given a second copy/ownership protocol.

## Evidence

Exact-head CI39187864520 attempt1 is failed, not green. The native inherited-only
exception is requested for the following independently attributed baseline break.
All eight failures have the same determining source pair, unchanged between actual
main baseline af1e1fe8d465 and tested merge003bc6badbba. CI's informational report
labels these new/unknown against an older scheduled main; actual signature/source
inspection and main repair #176799 establish the later inherited regression.

| Failed job | ID | Attribution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| build-artifacts |117854377688|UI MISSING_EXPORT SidebarProjectionMemo, before artifacts finish|
| checks-ui-e2e (1/2)|117854377704|Same missing export during bundling, not browser-test failure|
| check-prod-types|117855154539|UI TS2724 missing export plus resulting TS7006 row implicit-any|
| check-test-types-core-1|117855154509|Same two UI diagnostics|
| check-test-types-core-2|117855154565|Same two UI diagnostics|
| check-test-types-core-3|117855154557|Same two UI diagnostics|
| check-test-types-core-4|117855154569|Same two UI diagnostics|
| check-test-types-core-5|117855154659|Same two UI diagnostics|

Main repair e070647a0cf changes only the stale UI import to the existing cache
module. Its published main-baseline proof reproduces both diagnostics and the
build failure, then passes targeted UI types, four attention cases and UI build.
All three determining UI modules compare byte-identical between our actual CI
baseline, tested merge and that repair's recorded main baseline c2549f8295d.
No authored source-discovery path changes these modules. Aggregate117855806405
reports exactly these eight executable roots; all63 attempt jobs and192 exact-head
checks are terminal. Independent security-fast117854377690 passes; ancillary
cancelled auto-response has a successful same-head successor. No executable suite
is missing. The last six completed scheduled main failed-job maps and coordinator
flake register were checked; no matching missing-export entry exists. No CI rerun,
green repush, broad local build/typecheck or underlying-UI repair by this lane.

Independent P0-P2 review of the complete fixture-repaired cut completed
scoped-clean in one pass before the coordinator's tooling rebase. The entire
three-file diff and 34 complete source/context files verified unchanged around
that review. The rebase retains main's removal of the custom watcher recovery
interval; no receiver validation is removed. The shared target resolver has
return paths without a physical candidate check, so the final binding check stays.

Pre-rebase formatting passed (three files, 21ms); whitespace checks pass. Final producer
path/registry publication checks remain unchanged, including canonical snapshot
rejection. The adapted pending-publication case requires one shared rejection,
watch release, then successful fresh preparation; it does not promise stale
successful topology or weaken the registry witness.

The first migrated suite reported five failures. One serial exact-base production
control with the same adapted tests reproduced all five: 85 native reads against
the resolver's original 48 bound, three alias cases still allowing the legitimate
canonical fallback, and replacement of a missing-file parent without changing its
physical path string. This is adapted-test diagnosis, not inherited CI clearance.
The repair configures the selected alias, physically redirects the parent through
a symlink, and measures the unchanged original resolver budget after asynchronous
host capture. No numeric bound, timeout, assertion, retry or skip is relaxed.
The earlier repaired runtime attempt was stopped by the coordinator before a verdict.

After the tooling rebase, the refreshed isolated frozen install passes (191.05
seconds; all 1,577 packages reused). The full focused source-owner suite now
passes all 15 cases, including both replaced-candidate negative controls,
discovery budgets, warm zero-FS, watch reuse/pruning, root close, independent
cancellation and shared rejection/recovery. Vitest reports 443.55 seconds;
the isolated wrapper completes in 514.78 seconds, including worker preparation
(264.234 seconds, 16,759 inputs). The owner cases intentionally exercise real
physical-store/state lifetimes and bounded multi-agent discovery; this is not
a latency improvement claim. Current targeted native types pass (23.68 seconds).
The first official lint attempt used the custom targeted-type config, triggering
plugin-SDK declaration preparation that timed out at its unchanged 300-second
deadline before lint diagnostics. The wrapper explicitly supports a maintained
source-backed core config without that unrelated package preparation. Using that
config with the same three explicit files, type-aware lint passes (163.21 seconds).
Three-file formatting passes (49ms; 1.93 seconds wrapper), and the mandatory
suppression audit passes all 14 cases (40.87 seconds configuration; 75.39 seconds
wrapper). No lint rules, suppressions, retries or timeouts were changed.
The selected existing cross-agent dashboard history/disclosure integration case
also passes (49.958 seconds). It exercises worker history pages and deltas;
the other ten cases were excluded by name filter, not changed to skipped tests.
Vitest reports 201.53 seconds and the isolated wrapper completes in 325.61 seconds,
including reused worker preparation (56.582 seconds). Exact-head PR CI remains
pending after publication. No
performance improvement, live Gateway, deployment or real-state
proof is claimed. Broad architecture/build/platform proof belongs to PR CI.

prs.title: fix(telegram): stop terminal callback failures blocking chat updates
prs.body:
Related: #169176

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated Telegram callback failures and stalled chat updates when a button action loses requester authority or fails with an expired callback query.

## User Impact

Recorded terminal callback failures release the chat lane without scheduled retries or repeated handler replies. Transient failures retain their existing retry policy. An expired acknowledgment alone still allows the authorized button action to run. Existing at-least-once behavior in the crash window before durable settlement is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Telegram's ingress classifier treated these callback failures as transient, keeping them ahead of later chat updates until both eight attempts and 24 hours had elapsed. The Telegram delivery owner now carries callback context through thrown, returned, and deferred failures. The classifier recognizes the exact requester-authority rejection and Telegram's `answerCallbackQuery` 400 expired/invalid-query response only in that context. Ordinary message authority failures and the core retry policy are unchanged.

Current channel startup already uses its Gateway owner without inheriting the initiating client, agent-run, or operator-tool authority (#164848 and #159396). No sending-run requester snapshot was found in the current callback path. The original incident's exact invalidation trigger remains unverified, so this PR leaves the issue open. The distinct agent-versus-plugin typed-button routing work remains in #169504.

No new detached effects are introduced. Deferred settlement carries the immutable update kind and original error; the existing claim owner still controls cancellation and durable settlement. The simplification pass kept production changes in the two Telegram ingress owners. The necessary production growth is 37 lines; no unrelated deletions were added to offset it.

## Evidence

Current candidate: `354f780122fa4869284dae9a6d89d4dd0b20fecd`, after a clean merge of main containing `e63269c28a22`. Exact-head CI is green.

[Exact-head CI run 39184167193](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39184167193) completed successfully with **39 successful jobs**, including all selected tests and typechecks. No inherited failures remain. Both changed Telegram suites passed in [job 117843529787](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39184167193/job/117843529787):

- `bot.callback-retry.test.ts`: **3 passed**, covering `classifies a spooled callback failure` (terminal authority rejection and transient failure) and `processes a callback action after its acknowledgment expires`. Test times: 295 ms, 232 ms, and 8 ms. File wall time: 39.22 s, with 90% spent transforming the existing bot harness.
- `telegram-ingress-drain.test.ts`: **22 passed**, including direct/deferred terminal failure, expired-query settlement, next same-chat update delivery, and the ordinary-message authority-error negative case. File wall time: 8.99 s.

The prior candidate's only substantive CI failure was the untouched `src/cli/program/root-help.test.ts:33` mock-export check. Main repaired it in `e63269c28a22`; this candidate includes that repair, and [baseline job 117843529437](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39184167193/job/117843529437) passes against the fresh merge ref.

The [initial CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39180923180) caught a missing test-host registration: the new bot suite needed the existing database-worker host. A one-line registration repair fixed that setup failure; production code and assertions were unchanged. The initial run also reported the CLI baseline failure.

Changed-file oxlint, oxfmt, `git diff --check`, and staged freshness checks passed. Independent Codex autoreview passed twice, including the test-host repair: **scoped-clean**, no actionable P0–P2 findings. The review's unchanged source scope was preserved through the main merges.

PR CI is the test/typecheck proof gate per maintainer policy. Live Gateway proof, Crabbox/Testbox leases, local typechecks, local test runs, and production-reversion negative-control execution were intentionally skipped. The proof-only restart request was [answered with that policy](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176679#discussion_r4309448682). [ClawSweeper re-review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176679#issuecomment-6257849293) completed on this exact head: “Codex review: needs maintainer review before merge.” Its “Before merge” and “Findings” sections both say “None.” It identifies the fix scope as partial, consistent with the Related reference above, and records the intentional CI-only proof policy.

Diff against the merge base: production +46/−9 (net +37), tests and test routing +210/−7 (net +203), docs +6/−0.
