prs.title: perf(audit): reduce shared writer waits during retention pruning
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Reduces inbound-message and interactive-write delays when enabled execution-identity audit storage reaches its retention caps and competes for the shared SQLite writer.

## User Impact

Audit-heavy installations spend less time holding the writer, so channel ingress and interactive state writes can proceed sooner. Retention membership, oldest-first deletion, expiry budgets, transaction boundaries, FIFO ordering, and ingress dedupe/durability remain unchanged. No schema, configuration, or migration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each identity/decision insertion previously materialized up to 100,000/250,000 retained IDs for an overflow `NOT IN` query. The replacement finds the first overflow `(timestamp, id)` through the existing ordered index, then deletes the oldest eligible rows within the remaining expiry-cleanup budget. It still derives the boundary from database state inside the same transaction.

The shared writer remains the sole owner. Existing ingress batching is retained; another worker would still contend for the same SQLite database. This removes retained-set construction instead of introducing another queue, cache, or priority policy. Runtime production delta is +4 lines (14 added, 10 removed): the typed tuple cutoff needs an offset, a one-row limit, and tuple typing to preserve exact bounded retention. The rest is two compatibility cases (+59 test lines), documentation, and a rerunnable synthetic benchmark. The requested diff filter excluding tests and `docs/*` totals +522 lines: +4 runtime, +495 benchmark, and +23 benchmark README. The benchmark growth supplies the requested reproducible concurrent-writer workload and persistence/dedupe checks; it adds no product runtime state.

## Evidence

Acceptance was recorded before measurement: preserve every accepted audit/ingress/interactive operation and bounded retention; reduce audit service time and ingress queue wait without an interactive p99 regression. The benchmark drives the real audit FIFO, channel-ingress queue, and machine-state writer with 100,000 retained contexts and 250,000 retained decisions. Each 60-second run offers 180 audit records (90 identities/90 decisions), 60 ingress messages, 12 duplicate attempts, 60 idle-drain polls, and 60 interactive writes.

Four concurrent A/B pairs completed on an isolated Linux sandbox, swapping 16-core CPU halves for each successive pair under one exclusive measurement lock. A is main `8a23c56a8338`; B differs only in the two retention queries. Fixtures were seeded sequentially with the same timestamp and sizes; separate databases were reused across pairs, retaining the same caps. The branch was subsequently rebased onto latest main without conflicts; the audit/ingress/state paths were unchanged by that refresh.

Results below are medians across the four runs. Decisions use each pair's B minus A difference, not the difference between unpaired medians.

| Metric | A median | B median | Median paired B−A | Paired B−A range |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Ingress queue wait, s/min | 15.316 | 0.847 | -14.145 | -25.489 to -11.698 |
| Audit queue wait, s/min | 0.103 | 0.105 | +0.007 | -0.002 to +0.025 |
| Interactive execute queue wait, s/min | 2.232 | 0.175 | -1.753 | -6.294 to -0.587 |
| Audit service, s/min | 19.690 | 0.744 | -18.942 | -20.033 to -18.153 |
| Interactive write p50, ms | 2.112 | 2.048 | -0.020 | -66.839 to +3.439 |
| Interactive write p95, ms | 161.209 | 5.454 | -155.751 | -174.712 to -54.980 |
| Interactive write p99, ms | 171.514 | 7.442 | -149.357 | -180.671 to -4.201 |
| Ingress p99, ms | 253.001 | 16.335 | -237.298 | -266.028 to -186.040 |

| Pair | Ingress queue Δ, s/min | Audit queue Δ, s/min | Audit service Δ, s/min | Interactive p99 A → B, ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | -25.489 | +0.001 | -19.354 | 185.478 → 4.807 |
| 2 | -14.566 | -0.002 | -18.531 | 157.549 → 9.688 |
| 3 | -13.724 | +0.025 | -20.033 | 594.553 → 590.351 |
| 4 | -11.698 | +0.013 | -18.153 | 156.050 → 5.196 |

The improvement is reduced audit **service** time and contention on other request classes; audit's own queue wait is neutral (+7 ms/min median paired difference). Pair 3 retained a shared ~590 ms interactive tail stall on both sides rather than discarding it. Interactive p50 is roughly neutral overall; pair 2 moved from 2.0 to 5.4 ms while its p95/p99 improved, reflecting the phase-sensitive contention at these low rates.

`mpstat -P 96-127` recorded mean CPU occupancy for the two halves (including the experiment): 10.5%/9.0%, 7.2%/7.6%, 13.5%/12.0%, and 4.6%/5.6% across pairs 1–4. This is context, not an invalidation threshold. Both sides ran concurrently at the same offered start time.

All eight processes exited successfully, all submitted audit records persisted, duplicate attempts retained one ingress tombstone, no ingress/writer work remained unsettled, and no diagnostic samples were dropped. Row counts stayed at the existing caps.

Reproduction (run each side from its source tree with separate synthetic state):

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-channel-ingress-writer.ts \
  --state-dir "$STATE" --seed-only --fixture-time-ms "$FIXTURE_TIME"
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-channel-ingress-writer.ts \
  --state-dir "$STATE" --seconds 60 --start-at-ms "$SHARED_START" --output "$REPORT"
```

Prepare outside measurement, then run both sides concurrently with `systemd-run --scope -p AllowedCPUs=96-111` / `112-127`, swapping halves for the next pair. See `scripts/perf/README.md` for workload details.

Validation: 31 focused tests passed across `execution-identity-context.test.ts`, `execution-decision-facts.test.ts`, and `audit-event-writer.worker.test.ts`; changed-file oxfmt/lint and the single `pnpm tsgo:core` lane passed. The export-collision guard and 22 tests across `eager-import-closure.test.ts` / `pr-wrapper-source-closure.test.ts` also passed. Independent isolated Codex review was scoped-clean with no actionable P0–P2 findings. PR CI supplies broad validation; no Testbox/Crabbox lease was used.

Limits: this is storage-owner evidence, not Gateway transport, external-channel, model, or deployment end-to-end proof. It intentionally stresses opt-in identity/decision storage at retention caps; it does not establish current production table sizes, ordinary run/tool-only audit mix, or the fraction of reported production queue delay this change removes. The added tests protect retention equivalence; performance evidence comes from the benchmark, not a timing assertion in unit tests.

CI follow-through: initial run [39188739353](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39188739353) found one benchmark-only TS2345: `assert.deepEqual(errors, [])` narrowed the error accumulator to `never[]`. The follow-up uses length assertions with error diagnostics, preserving the measured workload, and received a fresh clean independent review. All selected audit/changed-code test shards, lint, docs, and architecture guards passed on that run.

The remaining initial-run failures share an inherited Control UI import mismatch introduced by #176453. Unchanged main `d79b0a4df0b24fd1e630e22da22cc2bb40af45ce` reproduces the identical `SidebarProjectionMemo` missing export in [UI build job 117857506284](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39188938288/job/117857506284), and TS2724/TS7006 in [production-types job 117857507285](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39188938288/job/117857507285). `session-attention.ts` and `sidebar-projection-memo.ts` are byte-identical on that main baseline and this PR; no UI files are changed here. These errors also propagate to the core test-type stripes and build-artifact workflow. No CI jobs were rerun to chase green.

The repaired head `296419aeacee94456faa2528cc4c80716d589a8d` passes `check-test-types` in [CI run 39189406757](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39189406757), including the benchmark script typecheck.

prs.title: fix(process): preserve broker crash classification through cleanup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A spawn-broker crash can disconnect IPC before its native exit event arrives. If the caller closes the host after receiving the command failure, the later exit was incorrectly recorded as a new shutdown failure. The hourly process-group custody test exposed this as `Spawn broker shutdown failed` with `SIGKILL`.

Capture whether shutdown had started at the first failure event, and retain that classification while joining native exit, stderr, and process-group cleanup. Actual shutdown errors still reject with their complete diagnostics. Pending commands still report broker loss; no command is replayed and no signal or cleanup policy changes.

## Evidence

The host source is identical at the previous hourly, failing hourly, and investigated current main. This is an existing event-order race in the shutdown classifier introduced by #168587 and refined by #170829 and #173154, rather than a broker change from #176578. Their PR bodies and owner history were inspected.

The unchanged real-process file failed with the reported error in two of three Node runs (Node 24/26); three pinned-Bun runs passed. The added table row makes disconnect → close → native exit deterministic and fails on the unchanged owner with the same error. It retains the existing exit-before-close and real shutdown-failure assertions.

## What Problem This Solves

Approval, Question, and Cloud Workers page requests should follow their authoritative input receipts without waiting for reactive rendering to settle.

## User Impact

Changing an Approval ID immediately retires the previous decision, rapid Approval and Question ID changes issue only the final lookup, and Cloud Workers retires catalog reads as soon as connection or permission receipts change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Approval and Question consume their existing native bridge property receipts; Cloud Workers consumes Gateway and RuntimeConfig receipts. Existing request generations, access checks, cancellation, and polling remain authoritative. The shared Gateway page adapter gains a plain `readEpoch()` accessor so receipt handlers can read the exact owner epoch without reading a rendering projection. The embedded Cloud Worker inventory receipt likewise reads its raw Gateway owner.

The catalog key still includes client, phase, exact epoch (including disconnected state), and nullable applied config hash. prs.title: refactor(gateway): let the session patch own initial reuse
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agent session preparation evaluates reuse and selects an identity that the
initial patch immediately evaluates again. The actual writer must still
re-evaluate its fresh row before committing. Remove the preparation-only
decision and let the existing patch owner lazily select the initial identity.
Carry that selected identity as the stable fallback into writer re-evaluation.

This is a narrow agent-session AREA of the previously parked lifecycle family:
three production files +13/-38, **25 net lines removed**; five test files
+164/-20, **144 net lines added**. The area-split exception applies. No new
owner, cache, manager, production test seam, config, protocol, SDK, dependency,
persisted shape, permission, durability or retention change is introduced.
Phase E standalone session memory and its factory, registry, expiry,
federation and tests remain untouched.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible change. Agent turns keep their selected session identity
through admission and persistence while avoiding a redundant reuse evaluation.
No configuration migration or operator action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The initial patch and final writer already own session reuse decisions. Removing
the earlier preparation-only decision leaves one initial identity selection and
the required current-row writer check.

## Kept behavior

Preparation still selects and authorizes the physical target and enforces
expected, deleted, archived and continuation state. The patch owner retains
reuse/expiry policy, transcript facts and concurrent replacement handling. The
writer still reads its current row and checks live source/effect authority
before mutation. Fresh-child initial-patch/persistence bypass and actor
acquisition/release are unchanged. Usable existing/requested IDs do not allocate
a UUID; the initial selected fallback remains stable across the real writer.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- The shared reuse policy introduced in #140960 (40ad90a012eb) describes
  isolated tests and fresh-row evaluation, not a cited human actual-use report
  requiring two pre-admission observations. Transcript metadata can change
  between the removed preparation observation and retained initial patch.
  If the earlier observation would have reused an old ID but the initial patch
  now rotates, the initial patch selects a fresh ID instead of reusing that old
  observation as its fallback. Final-writer policy and live authority remain.

## Evidence

Fresh independent P0-P2 review of the complete eight-file diff, including the
constant-fallback and identity-fixture repairs, completed scoped-clean in one
pass. All 111 captured source/context inputs verify unchanged. Static author simplification/test-audit
retains one patch decision owner, a local stable fallback and existing consumer
fixtures.

The existing connected Gateway suite adds missing-row, expired-row, requested-ID
and internal-effects cases. It consumes the existing execution observer's effect
admission calls, then checks provider command identity and the actual committed
row. A separate five-case owner table protects lazy UUID allocation, including
a positive fixed-UUID case that detects a broken named-import spy. Existing
concurrent replacement, worker-only SQL and native/private-child authority
assertions are retained.

The isolated seven-root runtime attempt reported 24 individual passes: all 21
reuse-owner cases and all three native-requester/private-child liveness cases.
This includes the positive fixed-UUID allocation case under the compiled loader,
transcript changes without row replacement and concurrent replacement. It was
intentionally stopped to prioritize qualifying the trusted landing toolchain,
with no aggregate verdict or established assertion failure. Wrapper settlement
was SIGINT after 1,629.10 seconds; compiler preparation accounted for 731.803
seconds (16,743 inputs). Gateway identity, patch/persist, preparation-worker and
artifact-case acceptance remains unproved by this run. This is not passing
seven-root coverage or a load-only attribution. No test, deadline, retry, skip or
assertion was weakened. Hosted exact-head CI remains the broad proof.

Before the final constant-fallback repair, targeted eight-root types passed
(277.29 seconds) and eight-file formatting passed (82ms). Lint found a
prefer-const violation in the delayed fallback assignment; the repaired local
builder takes an optional fallback, with a constant selected value captured by
the final writer callback. No suppression or mutable box is added. Fresh
post-repair eight-root typecheck passes (325.82 seconds), and all eight files
pass formatting (50ms). Official lint of the repaired service passes (210.27
seconds); the other seven files are unchanged from the eight-file lint attempt
that reported only the repaired prefer-const violation. The mandatory
suppression audit passes all 14 cases (35.99 seconds configuration, 61.94 seconds
isolated wrapper). No production import cycle is introduced: the UUID import
moves to the existing patch owner, and the preparation-to-patch import disappears.
Broad graph checks remain exact-head CI under the local proof budget. This is
not an aggregate runtime-proof claim. Fresh-child actual
service-entry proof remains a named gap; its host-bound WeakMap capability is
not fabricated in network JSON. No live provider, operator Gateway, deployment,
device or real state has been exercised.

Old exact-head CI39177001442 on 2fda13c99e7fd4d3922cf0e290486eed4bf7d997
failed checks-node-changed-compact-small-12 (117821965286), with the aggregate
ci-gate (117824967601) downstream. All four added Gateway identity rows failed
with Maximum call stack size exceeded. This was our fixture defect, not an
inherited failure: a second beginSessionEffect spy replaced the execution
observer's existing spy and then recursively called that same spy. The local
repair reads its existing recorded calls instead, preserving the real admission
and all identity/persistence assertions.

The coordinator requested a one-round rebase onto newer test/typecheck tooling.
All three production files are unchanged at the locally rebased head
77718ca14edd172a5aace5ac4da395a27bb7f8ee; the only later edit is the test repair
above. Its refreshed isolated
frozen install passes (220.83 seconds). A current four-row Gateway run finished
with two passes and two failures (830.85 seconds configuration, 909.48 seconds
wrapper; cold worker preparation 396.529 seconds). Requested-ID and internal-
effects cases pass through real admission, command dispatch and persisted-row
assertions. Missing-row RPC times out at the unchanged deadline (28.326 seconds);
that failure remains unattributed, not load-only or repaired. The expiry fixture
used 1970 timestamps and correctly reached archive rejection rather than expiry
reuse. Its latest repair uses one timestamp two minutes in the past, still
beyond the configured one-minute idle reset but not archive-aged. All assertions
and deadlines remain intact. The focused two-row replay now passes both missing
(14.484 seconds) and expired (6.008 seconds), with a passing one-file aggregate
(418.87 seconds Vitest, 463.37 seconds isolated wrapper). The other eleven tests
were excluded by the explicit name filter, not newly skipped in source. This
passing replay does not establish a cause or fix for the original missing-row
timeout, which remains investigated and unattributed. Fresh
independent review including this fixture repair is scoped-clean; all 111 inputs
and the eight-file diff verify unchanged. Refreshed targeted native eight-root
types pass (20.37 seconds), official type-aware lint of the repaired test passes
(138.43 seconds), and formatting passes (38ms; 1.88 seconds wrapper). The current
mandatory suppression audit passes all 14 cases (59.21 seconds wrapper).
Exact-head hosted CI39184402069 now passes, with openclaw/ci-gate117849270424
successful. A complete paginated census finds all 121 checks terminal, with no
failures or pending jobs. Cancelled ancillary dispatch117843654334 and
context117843653975 have successful same-head successors117843678548 and
117843678516; no executable suite is missing. The exact-head watcher is GREEN;
its older superseded rollup is not a current-head failure. No CI rerun or extra
code push was used for green.
Earlier local proof is historical, not current-head acceptance. No successful
prior check is being rerun merely for green.

The signed repair is pushed at exact head
821140b47c4d8fea7fb76db4dd0bb601e1930ade using a lease pinned to the previous
remote head. No auto-merge request was active during head replacement.

prs.title: fix(process): macOS process cleanup reports uncertain while unrelated processes exit
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/proc-safe/pull/23, https://github.com/openclaw/proc-safe/pull/25, release https://github.com/openclaw/proc-safe/releases/tag/v0.4.2

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: macOS process containment (Codex app-server cleanup, service child-group ownership) reports `cleanup: "uncertain"` or fails a census whenever any unrelated process on the Mac happens to be exiting, which is frequent on a loaded host.

## User Impact

User impact: on macOS, Codex app-server shutdown and other process-tree cleanup confirm completion reliably instead of intermittently reporting uncertain cleanup under load. No API or configuration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

proc-safe 0.4.1's Darwin census returned a bare `{ pid, owner: "unknown" }` row for a process in its exit window. At that point libproc reports `ESRCH`, while the kernel record still shows the process with `P_WEXIT`. OpenClaw's shared Darwin owner (`src/process/darwin-process-inspection.ts`) correctly fails closed on unreadable topology, so every full census failed while an unrelated process was mid-exit. proc-safe 0.4.2 fills that topology from the kernel record, as it already did for zombies (proc-safe#23). It also omits a row whose own trailing identity read proves the process gone, instead of returning topology without identity (proc-safe#25), which closes the rarer `permission` failure for selected lineages. OpenClaw's fail-closed contract and production code are unchanged; this PR pins 0.4.2 and adds an OpenClaw-boundary regression test.

The release-age exclusions move from the 0.4.1 set to the 0.4.2 set (root + 10 native packages, remove after 2026-10-26T00:51:31.079Z = publish + 7 days). The lockfile changes only proc-safe entries, and the root integrity matches npm.

## Evidence

**Regression test.** `src/process/darwin-process-inspection.native.test.ts` holds a `setsid` child inside XNU's exit window: the child's last pty close drains output nobody reads, for a stable ~600 ms. A C fixture verifies libproc `ESRCH` + `P_WEXIT` + non-zombie before and after inspection, so a late sample cannot pass. The test requires `readDarwinProcessTree` and `readDarwinProcessCensus` to keep the child with its parent, group, and `R` state. It fails on 0.4.1 with `Darwin process inspection unavailable` at `hasReadableTopology` and passes 3/3 on 0.4.2.

**Full-census failure rate** (`readDarwinProcessTree(deadline, [process.pid])`, unchanged owner code, Mac Studio). The 0.4.1 control and published 0.4.2 were interleaved at load 80–109, 1,000 calls each:

| mode | 0.4.1 | 0.4.2 (published) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| natural load | 59 failed (5.9%, `unavailable`) | 0 |
| plus 4 exit-churn loops in the caller's own lineage | 44 failed (40 `unavailable`, 4 `permission`) | 0 |

Earlier at agent load ~110, 0.4.1 failed 627/2,000 (31%). A parallel investigation measured 408/600 (68%) under 16-way exit churn on 0.4.1, and 0/600 on the fixed build.

**`pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport.process.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`**, 6 runs each:

| | runs green | test failures |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0.4.1 (load 80–107) | 0 / 6 | 26 / 78, all `cleanup: 'uncertain'` |
| 0.4.2 published (load 21–124) | 6 / 6 | 0 / 78 |

The 0.4.1 failures were "reaps descendants in independent and root process groups before close returns" and the "revalidates identities while quiescing" variants.

**Gates on this head:** native test 3/3; 51 process and 30 Codex consumer tests pass; `deps:pins:check` (768 specs), `deps:patches:check`, 105 npm lock mirrors, frozen install, targeted lint/format, services typecheck, `git diff --check`; Codex autoreview clean through P2.

prs.title: Control UI: consolidate local usage onto Usage and rebuild Models provider access
prs.body:
## Problem

- **Models page:** it showed accounts, plan limits and actions as tall cards, which went unreadable with a few providers. It had no way to remove a provider, and it fetched local session cost it barely used.
- **Usage page:** one interrupted turn (a response that ended before final usage arrived) marked the whole range "unknown" and hid every chart. On a busy install that means the analytics never show.
- **Usage loading:** the route blocked on `usage.status`, which can call provider APIs. Each "refreshing" provider retry also re-read the full ~195 KB `sessions.usage` report.

## Solution

**Usage page (one owner for local usage):**
- Totals show a lower bound ("≥ 3.1B tokens", "≥ $5,759.15") instead of "unknown". Analytics stay visible, with one note that explains "≥".
- New **By Provider** mode (now the default) on the existing daily chart. It stacks each day by provider from `aggregates.modelDaily`, uses stable colours and has a legend. Day selection, shift-range and By Type still work.
- Provider plans load beside session usage, not ahead of it (`provider-usage-load.ts`):
  - The route loader reads only `sessions.usage`.
  - Retries for incomplete plans re-read only `usage.status`.
  - A read cut short by a disconnect resumes on reconnect.

**Models page (provider access only):**
- Removed: the local-usage overview, per-row cost, the range control and every `sessions.usage` read, including main's per-card `costByProvider` fetch. A **View usage** button links to the Usage page.
- Each provider is a dense row that expands in place:
  - When open: window tiles ("% left", "Resets {date} · in {time}"), a banner when a window is used up, one line per account, and a footer with **Add account**, **Test connection**, **Set API key** and **Remove provider**.
  - **Remove provider** asks for confirmation. It then signs out every saved account and deletes the config API key, and it names any credential it can't remove (an environment variable or an external login).
- Providers that are usable count as connected: stored credentials, available models, a ready catalog, or reported usage.

**Shared:**
- One `ProviderUsagePanel` (windows, balances, provider-billed cost) and its chips serve Models rows, Codex accounts and the Usage page. It replaces `renderProviderUsageDetails` and its CSS.
- Codex account limits are a plain Solid component (an async memo inside `Loading`) instead of a custom element with a registry.

## Impact

- One place for local usage, with truthful totals and per-provider days.
- Models is a fast, short provider list.
- **Behavior changes:**
  - Models no longer shows local spend.
  - Limits read "% left".
  - The per-account Codex refresh button is gone; the page Refresh re-reads.
  - "Remove key" became the confirmed "Remove provider".
- **Not addressed:** `model-providers-controller.ts` already fails `max-lines` on main (742 > 700). Its owner is mid-refactor, so this change leaves it.

## Evidence

**Usage page, before → after.** Same sanitized studio-shaped fixture with interrupted turns, 1280px, dark:

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Usage before: unknown totals, charts hidden](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/20473356-4cf4-43b1-bdc7-9c5cb9e533e6) | ![Usage after: lower-bound totals, by-provider chart, insights](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d0440491-34e2-4aad-a320-0d7fd1f776dd) |

**Models page after, and an expanded row:**

![Models page after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ddc3f041-0e7e-4d8c-b62a-33a43948a087)
![Expanded Copilot row](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e8c88560-843f-40ab-ac32-e3c00f82bda7)

**Performance.** Production bundle, instant mock Gateway, 8 untraced in-app navigations each, host load average about 30–40:

| Route | Median time to content | Layout shift |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Models (rows) | 133 ms | 0 in all runs |
| Usage (chart), from another workspace page | 15 ms | 0 in all runs |

From Settings to Usage, the shell swaps the settings chrome for the workspace chrome. The resulting 0.24–0.44 layout shift comes from that page-type change, not from loading.

**Tests:**
- Unit (Models, Usage, components, gateway-source-replacement): 598 passed.
- E2E: 22 files, 94 passed. That includes the new `usage-studio-shape` and the Models suites.
- Typecheck, `oxlint`, `pnpm lint:ui:styles` and `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` are clean, apart from the existing controller `max-lines` failure above.

**Size against merge base `63991b9752e`:**
- Production: +1849 / −1359 (net +490).
- Tests: +1226 / −707.
- Moving usage to the Usage page removed about 1,050 production lines compared with the previous revision of this PR.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Invalid numeric plugin settings were silently discarded while the configuration wizard advanced to the next field. A user could finish setup without the value they had just entered.

## User Impact

Invalid plugin numbers now show a validation error and stay on the same field so the user can correct the answer, instead of silently leaving the setting unwritten. Valid decimal, scientific-notation, and integer answers are unchanged; no migration or operator action is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing text-prompt validator rather than discarding invalid values after the prompt returns. Preserve the finite JSON-number and integer restrictions introduced in #107346. Both setup and configure share this owner. Add matching English, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese copy and document the behavior.

This is a silent-failure bug fix, using the campaign's below-500 bug-fix exception: **22 production lines added net**, 24 test lines added net, and one documentation line. No config key, schema, protocol, dependency, or SDK signature changes.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

Numeric admission belongs to the existing prompt-validation boundary, not a second post-prompt check that silently drops rejected input. The built-in terminal and hosted wizard enforce that validator; custom prompters must likewise honor the supplied validator. No security, data-durability, or realistic-concurrency guard is removed.

## Evidence

- The real `WizardSession` regression fails on the base because an invalid answer is accepted without validation feedback. It now verifies the same pending step, a corrected answer, and the final typed plugin configuration for malformed, overflowing, hexadecimal, and fractional-integer inputs.
- Focused plugin configuration, wizard-session, and i18n suites: **55 passed**. Production lint-suppression guard: **14 passed**. Combined wrapper: 66.59 seconds; three-file wizard shard: 4.71 seconds; changed regression: 5 milliseconds. The baseline selected regression failed as intended in 15.00 seconds.
- Targeted native typecheck passed. Focused type-aware lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed.
- Independent complete-context P0–P2 review found no actionable findings; final captured-source verification passed.

Broad builds, cycle checks, and repository-wide suites are left to exact-head PR CI under the campaign's local CPU limit. No full Gateway boot, live-provider, or rendered-terminal proof is claimed. Production imports are unchanged.

prs.title: refactor(infra): reuse private usage and delivery preparation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Usage and outbound delivery preparation clone values that their preparation owners just created privately. Diagnostic usage reads also parse the same session marker twice before any yield.

## User Impact

Usage results, environment capture, retained-transcript access, delivery settlement, and media cleanup keep their existing behavior. Missing sources still return unavailable, and final disclosure and cleanup authority stay intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

Usage preparation owns fresh location, store, and archive arrays; production callers do not mutate or publish them. Reuse them when building the worker request, while retaining the copy of the caller-owned operation. Pending-delivery preparation serializes the caller entry and builds fresh scalar retention/terminal values before admission, so its immediate deep clone is redundant. The diagnostic reader can reuse its first parsed marker.

No SQL, worker-request, transaction, schema, SDK, or PG bookkeeping changes. No fallback or new accepted security edge.

| Candidate | Decision | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| C27837 / C27838 | REMOVE | Prepared location and stores are private fresh values; the adjacent archive-array copy has the same ownership. |
| C27121 | REMOVE | Terminal preparation already captures caller data into fresh values before admission. |
| C27824 | REMOVE | Reuse one pure marker parse on the same string before any yield. |
| C27839 | KEEP | The public operation can contain caller-owned arrays across awaits. |
| C27848 / C27851 | KEEP | Distinct reads and disclosure boundaries still require their own checks. |

## Evidence

Existing usage-owner tests cover environment mutation isolation and retained inventory after an in-process write. Pending-delivery worker tests mutate the caller entry, media, cleanup preference, and state directory after admission; settlement and cleanup must retain the admitted values. Diagnostic reporting tests cover retained and missing sources. Production delta is +4/-9, net -5 lines; tests are unchanged.

Formatting, basic lint, and whitespace checks pass. One independent Codex P0/P1 review is scoped-clean with complete owner/caller context and final source verification. The initial fresh-main frozen dependency install passed; after integration, the additional install stayed behind the SSD gate and was stopped before execution. Validation of the integrated head comes from CI.

Initial PR CI [39187154725](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39187154725) completed with 42 passing jobs and 28 skipped. Main was then merged to include its obsolete-export cleanup; all three reviewed source blobs remained unchanged. Final-head PR CI [39188035660](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39188035660) has 34 passing jobs, 28 skipped, and eight failing jobs. Owner tests, type-aware lint, source contracts, Madge, and T1/dialect/worker ratchets pass. The six type jobs, one UI E2E job, and aggregate fail from an inherited Control UI import error:

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Private extension owners still pass forwarding callback bags to helpers used by only that owner. Codex completion tests also select retry policies that serving code never supplies. This keeps a parallel assembly path alive for fixtures without adding a production capability.

## What Changed

- Let the existing Codex submission owner own its history read and supply its three operations directly, preserving method receivers. Pass the monitor's stable live maps instead of map-get forwarding closures. Remove two private completion-retry overrides and exercise the unchanged real defaults with fake clocks.
- Pass Discord voice's immutable bot identity and stable session/recovery maps directly. Preserve genuinely late-bound operations and the existing construction order.
- Put realtime delegation directly in its existing OpenAI bridge. Keep the same admission, connection checks, transcript, callbacks, prompt, and asynchronous replies.

This is the extension-area split of the wider private-owner family whose core slice is #176657. It does not change public SDK/config/CLI/protocol contracts, dependencies, SQL/schema/durability, security guards, or Phase E standalone session-memory code or tests.

## Best-effort Tradeoffs Accepted

- None newly introduced. The removed overrides have only test suppliers; serving retry delays and limits are unchanged. All authority, realistic concurrency, recovery, FIFO, and accepted-write settlement checks remain.

## Size

16 paths: **85 net production lines removed**, **5 net test/support lines removed**, **90 overall lines removed** against main `77a403f1c15380ce71fcc53f0bb68ce5f4f2794e`. Algorithm movement is counted on both sides, not as gross deletion. This is an area split, not a final residue or whole-tree exhaustion claim.

## Evidence

- All 16 remaining fresh-main preimages matched the qualified packet, and their applied postimages matched its signed source manifest. Four ordinary Memory Core paths were dropped intact after the commit hook found both inlines exceeded the current 700-counted-line growth cap. They are parked for a coherent owner-level restructuring; no cap, baseline, or hook is bypassed. This PR changes no Memory Core file.

prs.title: refactor: remove repeated control authority checks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

ACP, skill preparation and Talk control paths repeat method-capability checks and actor assertions that the same call path already guarantees.

## User Impact

No intended behavior change. Runtime methods, advertised option keys, and authority at each runtime effect remain checked. Missing backends and retired actors keep their existing errors.

## Design

Capability normalization already adds each control whenever its runtime method exists, so callers need only the method-presence check. Remove same-stack actor/caller assertions where a retained combined assertion or final callback assertion covers the same authority without an intervening yield or mutation. Keep post-await checks and queued-owner validation.

Candidate ledger (multiple IDs may describe one physical site):

| ID | Decision | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| H-ACP-CAP-1 | REMOVE | resolveManagerRuntimeCapabilities unconditionally adds session/set_mode when runtime.setMode exists; keep only !runtime.setMode. |
| H-ACP-CAP-2 | REMOVE | Same normalization guarantees session/set_config_option when setter exists; keep only !runtime.setConfigOption. |
| H-ACP-CAP-3 | REMOVE | Canonical capability normalization already encodes setMode presence; retain direct method check. |
| H-ACP-CAP-4 | REMOVE | Canonical capability normalization already encodes setConfigOption presence; retain direct method check. |
| C06104 | REMOVE | Same-thread duplicate of retained C06106 at runtime callback entry; only pure option/key construction occurs between, and withAcpRuntimeErrorBoundary calls run synchronously before its first await. |
| C06105 | REMOVE | Same physical locus as C06104; retain final actor check in the runtime callback at line209. |
| C06049 | REMOVE | input.assertActive at152 repeats assertCurrent150, which already checks the same callback; only the discardPersistentState condition intervenes. |
| C06054 | REMOVE | Actor check166 is dominated by assertCurrent150 on the no-discard arm and assertCurrent162 on the discard arm; no intervening await/effect. |
| C06055 | REMOVE | Same physical locus as C06054; retain all preceding post-await and final runtime-close authority checks. |
| C06147 | REMOVE | Same-stack actor assertion immediately precedes either assertControlBindingCurrent (whose first statement is combined assertCurrent) or combined assertCurrent at217. Remove this one assertion, retaining217 before prepareFreshSession. Both readAcpControl callers are pure closures. |
| C06281 | REMOVE | Same-stack duplicate of params.assertActive at72. The only intervening branch with awaited controls always returns at98-101, so paths reaching105 have not yielded or changed authority. Retain72,87,118 and downstream closeSession final authority. |
| C31920 | REMOVE | Remove assertion before synchronous eligibility filtering, retaining the final preparation assertion before returning and the runtime early-return guard. Filter consumes prepared facts, with no effect or database read. |
| C31921 | REMOVE | Same physical preparation.assertCurrent statement as C31920, indexed again in category g; count one deleted statement. |
| C33527 | REMOVE | Private boundOwner.read is called only by resolver read, which unconditionally calls binding.assertCurrent (including this owner assertion) immediately beforehand. |
| C33528 | REMOVE | Inside assertRequestCurrent, request.assertCurrent unconditionally calls binding.assertCurrent including the same owner assertion; preserve signal checking, request/binding authority, no-op rejection and final effect checks. |

KEEP: runtime method-presence checks, status-derived advertised option keys, final authority/effect checks, post-await straddle checks, binding refresh, and metadata commit guards.

Accepted edge: captured runtime facades have stable method surfaces; the bundled adapter uses fixed bound methods. This does not add support for plugins mutating that same facade during capability discovery. Assertion and control-reader callbacks are synchronous authority checks/reads. A stale skill preparation may perform pure synchronous eligibility filtering before its retained final assertion rejects it; no result publication or external effect occurs. Talk private owner access remains behind the resolver binding check.

Production +4/-15 (net -11); tests unchanged. No SQL, worker-request, transaction, schema, SDK, or Gateway service-lifecycle changes. The measured lane pair below confirms a 0/0/0 warm statement/request/MAIN delta.

Changed-file formatting, type-aware lint and diff checks pass. One independent Codex P0–P2 review is scoped-clean, with frozen-source verification. Exact-head CI [39185027917](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39185027917) passes all selected owner tests, types, lint, source contracts, Madge, and T1/dialect/worker ratchets. Relevant selected owner suites cover runtime options, actor retirement, close/reset, persistent bindings, skill discovery cancellation, and voice RPC run/call/speaker retirement. The measured warm pair below shows no count regression; no latency improvement is claimed.

One v3 baseline/candidate pair compares the contiguous changes in #176699 and #176746 (8b5d3c98 → 18504a59), with identical lockfiles, Node 24.22.0 and proc-safe 0.4.1. prs.title: perf(github): refresh expired preview avatars in background
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

GitHub hover previews wait for public avatar downloads again whenever the shared image cache expires, even though a usable image is already cached.

## User Impact

Previews can display the cached author and coauthor images while they refresh. Updated images appear on a subsequent server preview load; the existing UI preview cache can continue showing the previous public image for another five minutes. This bounded cosmetic staleness is an intentional latency tradeoff. Metadata refreshes, public repository visibility checks, and current-identity checks keep their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the avatar cache's `allowStale: false` override and use its existing stale-while-revalidate behavior. This preserves the five-minute refresh interval, one in-flight request per image, independent request deadlines, transport isolation, failure eviction, and 200-image bound. No new cache or background lifecycle is introduced. Production delta: **−4 lines**.

## Evidence

Four concurrent A/B replay pairs, with 16 CPU cores per side and core halves swapped between pairs, exercised the production preview loader and view projection. Each side replayed eight overlapping readers against identical synthetic GitHub responses. Avatar delays varied from 300–800 ms; repository replies took 60 ms and item/commit replies 100 ms.

| Scenario | Samples per side | p50 before → after | p99 before → after | Summed latency before → after |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Expired avatars | 384 | 611.9 → 223.0 ms | 972.2 → 255.8 ms | 245.44 → 85.89 s |
| Cold images | 32 | 481.4 → 479.0 ms | 484.9 → 484.9 ms | 15.40 → 15.34 s |
| Warm previews | 384 | 0.029 → 0.048 ms | 0.192 → 0.122 ms | 0.016 → 0.021 s |

Every paired expired-avatar comparison improved: p99 differences were −715, −741, −741, and −740 ms; mean summed-latency difference was −39.89 s per 96 reads. API/image request counts and credential-check counts matched exactly. CPU time was neutral. This removes foreground waiting rather than upstream work.

Scope: these are controlled Linux boundary-replay results, not full Gateway RPC or production latency measurements. Authentication was a counted fixture; no live credentials or GitHub network traffic were used. The final formatted source compiled equivalently to the measured candidate.

Validation:

- Both new issue/PR cache regressions fail on the original code because readers remain blocked by the pending image refresh.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/github/src/preview-cache.test.ts extensions/github/src/preview.test.ts extensions/github/src/session-reader.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **48 passed**, 3 files; runner wall time 82.38 s, mostly preparation. Changed-file test bodies total under one second.
- Changed-file `oxfmt`, focused repository lint (`--openclaw-focused-config --config .oxlintrc.json`), and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Independent Codex review: clean through P2, with the final source verified.
- Type-aware lint and the extension typecheck are delegated to PR CI: local lint first required broad SDK declaration preparation, so that preparation and the queued typecheck were stopped to respect the host compute limit. No local typecheck success is claimed.

PR CI completed its test, production/test typecheck, type-aware lint, documentation, security, and package-boundary jobs successfully on `dd44dd5b02e7b276c027ba843f710c7ec94fc58b` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39188460837)); the required aggregate CI gate also passed. Release-note context: GitHub hover previews no longer wait for expired public avatar images to refresh when cached images are available.

## What Problem This Solves

The usage cost-analysis E2E fixture could become a day stale while the test file waited to run. Its `daily` rows were built during module collection, but the selected date range and provider history were built inside the case. When collection occurred before UTC midnight and execution after it, the cost cards showed `$27 / $0 / $11 / $20` instead of `$32 / $11 / $20 / $27`.

prs.title: chore(release): close out 2026.10.5 on main
prs.body:
## Problem

OpenClaw 2026.10.5 is published to npm `latest` from `release/2026.10.5` (tag `v2026.10.5` → `1b58cb9a1b4f4353e1add63c8506db4d890962e8`), but `main` still says 2026.10.4. It does not have the shipped notes, the 2026.10.5 update-compat entry, or the shipped Plugin SDK surface.

## Solution

Stable main closeout, following `.agents/skills/release-openclaw-maintainer/references/stable-main-closeout.md`:

- Root version → `2026.10.5`, plus `pnpm release:prep` generated outputs: plugin/package versions, official channel catalog, matrix plugin changelog alignment, and macOS `Info.plist` base version `2026.10.5` / `2026100500`.
- `scripts/lib/update-compat-inventory.json`: records `openclaw@2026.10.5` (52 chunks). It was regenerated with `pnpm update:compat:gen` from npm tarballs of every recorded release, each verified against its published `dist.integrity` before extraction. All 15 existing entries are byte-identical. The recorder ran cleanly, so no `pnpm build` reproduction was needed.
- `scripts/lib/plugin-sdk-shipped-surface.json`: regenerated with `pnpm plugin-sdk:shipped-surface:gen -- --release v2026.10.5`, per `docs/reference/RELEASING.md`. 151 typed subpaths, 3645 named exports. `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check` reports no unauthorized removals.
- `CHANGELOG/2026.10.5.md` and `CHANGELOG/records/2026.10.5.md` match the tag byte for byte (read through `scripts/release-changelog.mjs read --ref v2026.10.5`, with and without `--record`). The root `CHANGELOG.md` index was refreshed by the owner script (`release-changelog.mjs split`). Other release entries are unchanged. No appcast change, because the macOS build is not published yet.
- `config/ci-test-timings.json`: refreshed by `scripts/ci-shard-timings-refresh.mts --run 39149281720`. That run is the normalCi child, attempt 4, of Full Release Validation 39148728797, which passed on the candidate SHA. 131 hosted shard costs; the generated output was committed unedited. The GitHub jobs API returned HTTP 502 twice at `per_page=100`. For that run only, the script was changed locally to request `per_page=30`; the change was reverted and is not in this PR.

## Release-branch audit

`git log origin/main..v2026.10.5 --no-merges` lists 475 commits. 220 are patch-equivalent to commits on main. Of the remaining 255, 168 map to main through `(cherry picked from commit …)` trailers, PR numbers, or identical subjects. The other 87 are:

- **Release-only, intentionally not forward-ported:** release prep/changelog commits; the Kova calibration pin `b99dbbfb24d`; the OpenCode Go `glm-5.2` pin `1b58cb9a1b4`; the revert of #167443 (`c3d21618840`); the revert of #173580 (`bbd850c4422`, dropped from this stable only and kept on main); the 2026.10.2 update-compat backport (`5290333cada`, which main got in its own closeout).
- **Branch adaptations of backports that mirror existing main behavior:** for example `836fd79faa0`, `d357abf71be`, `9564061ab79`, `ddd39ecb5bc`, `b8602f4c8ba`, `2cbefebf1c3`, and the "after the #N backport" import, format and test adapters.
- **Release-line test/harness fixes absent from main:** listed for a separate follow-up PR and not included here.

No release-only product fix missing from main was found.

## Evidence

- `pnpm deps:npm-lock:check`: pass.
- `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check`: pass.
- `pnpm release:generated:check`: everything passes except `Control UI locale bundles` (`pnpm ui:i18n:check`: `ui/src/i18n/.i18n/sv.tm.jsonl does not contain sv translations`). This is pre-existing on main: the same failure reproduces on clean `origin/main` `50bb09d7ba1`, and this PR touches no `ui/` files. The `control-ui-locale-refresh` workflow was mid-run on main when I checked. `pnpm release:prep` stopped at the same step, because `ui:i18n:sync` needs a translation provider. Every other refresh task completed.
- `pnpm check:changed` (local): fails on 2 checks. Both fail the same way on the clean base `70ad1ad66edf`, and this PR changes no TS/JS files:
  - `lint`: 34 `eslint(max-lines)` errors in untouched files. Running `scripts/run-lint.mts` on the base gives the identical error set. Lint ran repo-wide because the root `package.json` changed.
  - `core tsgo graph boundary`: `plugins-platform: 723 test roots exceeds the advisory 720 limit`. The base reproduces it exactly.
  - Everything else passed, including `typecheck all`, format, plugin boundaries, the npm package-lock guard, and the Plugin SDK surface budget.
- Per operator policy for release work, checks ran locally rather than on Testbox.

prs.title: fix(codex): account and trace every provider response
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Codex app-server can emit more than one `rawResponse/completed` notification during a single turn, especially around tool handoffs.

OpenClaw previously had two related observability gaps:

- `attemptUsage` retained only the final provider response, under-counting multi-response turns.
- Codex diagnostics emitted only one turn-level model-call span. Consumers that reconstructed individual LLM calls from transcript timestamps could place the LLM span after its tool call and make several calls overlap until the final answer.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Accumulate exact `rawResponse/completed` usage once per `responseId` for attempt-level accounting.
- Keep the final response's usage and `contextUsage` as the assistant/current-context snapshot, so summed billing buckets do not inflate the active context window.
- Emit one request-level `model.call.completed` diagnostic per unique response.
  - Response samples and tool lifecycle boundaries are buffered and paired by order at turn completion.
  - A tool start closes the current LLM interval; completion of the final active tool opens the next LLM interval.
  - This remains correct when Codex delivers `rawResponse/completed` after the tool triggered by that response has already run.
  - Parallel tools form one tool phase. When one provider response emits several sequential tools, the shortest surplus tool-to-tool gap is discarded instead of being reported as an LLM call.
- Add `sourceTimestampMs` to completed model-call diagnostics so the OTel recorder can backdate completed-only request spans to their real completion time.
- Attach exact per-response usage to request spans when present, while still emitting a timing span when Codex omits optional usage.
- Attach accumulated `attemptUsage` to the turn-level model span.
- Hash the upstream response ID before exposing it in diagnostics and deduplicate repeated completion notifications.
- Map `reasoningOutputTokens` into `reasoningTokens`.
- Reuse the same response accumulator in bounded/settled-turn paths.
- Fail closed to thread-last usage when an exact response aggregate becomes incomplete.

Transcript timestamps are intentionally unchanged: an assistant tool-call message records when the model produced the tool call, not when that provider request began. Per-response diagnostics now own the LLM timing boundary.

The assistant-completion idle timeout configuration is not part of this PR: `#97233` already exposed `appServer.turnAssistantCompletionIdleTimeoutMs` on current `main`.

This change was AI-assisted. I reviewed the diff and validated the event contract directly against `openai/codex` app-server source and a real app-server turn.

## User Impact

- Token and cost accounting is accurate for Codex turns containing multiple upstream responses.
- Current-context reporting continues to reflect only the latest provider response.
- OTel consumers can render:

  `LLM request -> tool execution -> LLM request -> tool execution -> final LLM request`

  without deriving LLM starts from assistant-message timestamps.

## Upstream Codex Contract

Checked against immutable `openai/codex@95637f7056835fea66bdd0044414af480fc0fd74`:

- [`rawResponse/completed` is emitted once per upstream Responses API completion with exact, non-accumulated usage](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/95637f7056835fea66bdd0044414af480fc0fd74/codex-rs/app-server/README.md#L1450)
- [`response_id` is required and `token_usage` is optional](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/95637f7056835fea66bdd0044414af480fc0fd74/codex-rs/protocol/src/protocol.rs#L1820-L1827)
- [The sampling loop alternates provider responses with tool work](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/95637f7056835fea66bdd0044414af480fc0fd74/codex-rs/core/src/session/turn.rs#L137-L149)
- [`RawResponseCompleted` is emitted when the provider response completes](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/95637f7056835fea66bdd0044414af480fc0fd74/codex-rs/core/src/session/turn.rs#L2348-L2360)

## Evidence

### Real App-Server Proof

Ran the local authenticated Codex CLI (`0.146.0-alpha.3.1`) as `codex app-server --listen stdio://` with raw events enabled. The prompt required two separate sequential shell calls followed by `DONE`. The proof script used an ephemeral thread and redacted response/tool IDs.

Observed lifecycle, relative to model-turn start:

```text
LLM response-1   0ms .. 8878ms      total=23030
tool-1                 8913ms
LLM response-2         8913ms .. 11874ms   total=23125
tool-2                           11896ms
LLM response-3                   11896ms .. 13492ms   total=23178
turn terminal                                      13496ms
```

No LLM request span overlaps either tool phase. In this run each shell command completed within the millisecond resolution of the captured events.

Redacted projected output:

```json
{
  "rawResponses": [
    {
      "responseId": "response-1",
      "usage": {
        "inputTokens": 22967,
        "cachedInputTokens": 0,
        "outputTokens": 63,
        "totalTokens": 23030
      }
    },
    {
      "responseId": "response-2",

        "inputTokens": 23078,
        "cachedInputTokens": 22272,
        "outputTokens": 47,
        "totalTokens": 23125
      }
    },
    {
      "responseId": "response-3",
      "usage": {
        "inputTokens": 23173,
        "cachedInputTokens": 22272,
        "outputTokens": 5,
        "totalTokens": 23178
      }
    }
  ],
  "projected": {
    "attemptUsage": {
      "input": 24674,
      "cacheRead": 44544,
      "output": 115,
      "total": 69333
    },
```

prs.title: fix: prevent unrelated coauthors on shared-main channel tasks
prs.body:
Related: #176366

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Discord-originated tasks can credit unrelated people and omit the requester when several conversations share the main routing session.

## User Impact

User impact: delegated tasks retain the verified requester's eligible Git credit without importing the routing session's lifetime participant roster. Ordinary collaborative tasks and credit opt-out remain unchanged.

A verified channel-to-profile link is still required. Unlinked requests get no inferred main-session credit. Existing commits and child snapshots are not rewritten. Direct publication from canonical main, without a task contributor snapshot, adds no automatic human credit.

## Why This Change Was Made

The producer treated a routing-session roster as task contribution. The existing contributor-inheritance owner now selects only the host-verified requester for canonical main. That attribution-only fact travels through native, visible, ACP, and CLI delegation independently of owner/admin authority. Requester trailers stay in per-turn context; changing requesters does not rebuild stable instructions. A different main requester uses the existing follow-up path rather than the original task's tool closures.

Reported and investigated with @obviyus. The incident's parent explicitly supplied wrong trailers to its worker; the worker complied. The original head already lacked the reporter's credit. Historical system/developer prompt bytes were unavailable.

## Evidence

- **Current head:** ead47408870068d8a92fb3eb43340e97a99dd735. Ready for review, with the latest observed merge conflict cleared. Nothing merged or deployed.
- **ClawSweeper:** reviewed production head 5405403b62509717317c92d5ad9c833ff7f61fc7 with zero actionable findings; both earlier findings resolved. Subsequent changes are test-fixture repairs and history-preserving main integration. A final-head re-review is requested separately.
- **Behavioral red/green:** the original controlled Discord → registered ingress → core reply → actual child spawn/exec → Git reproduction created wrong A/B credit and omitted C on base d0dcce33fd710433af596a4022466a0f41b59265. Fixed runs verify Git-native parsed trailers for visible/hidden children, unlinked and opted-out requesters, collaboration, and nested delegation. The provider derives trailers from actual product prompts, not expected identities.
- **Simplification proof:** 215 retained regression tests passed in 200.08s; six manual Discord-to-Git scenarios, 18 steering-custody cases, and four provenance cases passed together in 156.01s. The large one-off E2E harness was then removed from the shipped diff; replayable task evidence remains available in the work session.
- **Backend prompt repair:** a producer/actual-CLI-renderer regression failed on absent requester trailers, then passed after using the existing inbound-context append owner. Four suites passed 41 tests in 51.74s, plus five unchanged Codex consumer tests in 28.37s. Core typecheck, lint, and independent source-bound review passed.
- **CI fixture repair:** deterministic retained-chat-root regression failed before joining the actual root-release signal, then passed without sleeps, retries, or weaker assertions. Original six-file chat composition plus root-help passed 46 tests in 100.97s. Root-help preserves real exports; the owner-generated mock exemption baseline shrank by exactly one row. The equivalent landed upstream fixture from e63269c28a22 is now reused verbatim; its three tests passed in 6.68s.
- **Conflict refresh:** normally merged pinned main d48d36d7c2053b464b68e5024f3229612ad09eca to resolve an actual conflict, preserving all published history. Frozen-lockfile install passed. The resolved candidate passed 131 tests across eight files in 272.25s, production typecheck, scoped lint (46 files), line-cap and whitespace gates, and fresh independent Auto Review with no P0–P2 findings. Final alignment changes only the already-tested root-help fixture. Hosted current-head CI is still pending, not claimed green.

<details>
<summary>Scope, simplification and proof limits</summary>

The fix extends the existing contributor-inheritance owner with one host-verified requester. It removes a separate selector module, duplicate test owner, standalone CLI test-registration module, and one-off cross-plugin E2E/export scaffolding. The first simplification removed 584 net lines from the prior revision (1,261 added lines reduced to 673 before subsequent fixes). Current delta against pinned integration base d48d36d7c2053b464b68e5024f3229612ad09eca is +753/-97 across 48 files. Most production changes carry a single attribution-only fact through existing transport boundaries; no new persistence, identity authority, or configuration is introduced.

Controlled Discord events and a deterministic local provider do not establish autonomous live-model compliance. Earlier live Discord plain-reply transport passed, but live linked-human Discord-to-Git tool use remains unproven; broader lifecycle testing encountered Discord 429. Full isolated build passed on earlier integrated head 19800386e80eba867129ccea71c28d9019f7dcc8, not the final head; its report-only UI gzip budget was exceeded and is not claimed passing.

Prior hosted CI failures and attempted reproductions were retained, not relabeled green: a Code Mode cancellation-cleanup failure did not reproduce in its original four-file composition (105 tests passed), while the recurring chat-root cleanup and root-help mock failures received the test-only repairs above. Later CI must qualify the final composition. No retries, weakened assertions, expanded mock baselines, credential changes, or live identity-link mutations were used.

</details>

prs.title: feat(workboard): add durable status_changed notification event
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Workboard subscribers currently cannot opt into durable card status transitions such as `todo`, `ready`, `running`, or `review`. Downstream consumers can observe terminal `completed` / `failed` / `stale`, but routine status movement is not exposed as a durable notification event. That leaves Telegram/all-stage consumers dependent on polling or ad-hoc board scans.

## Summary

Adds a durable, strictly opt-in `status_changed` notification kind for Workboard cards.

The final design persists status transitions in an additive SQLite table and projects them into notification reads only for subscriptions that explicitly include `status_changed`. Existing subscriptions without that event kind keep the historical `completed` / `failed` / `stale` stream.

## Design

- Persist status transitions separately from the capped recent card event ring.
- Add the transition table as an additive schema-3-compatible table; do not bump `SCHEMA_VERSION`.
- Keep the additive table in fresh-store schema setup, but lazy-create it for existing schema-3 stores only when a real status transition is written.
- Capture transition-time `sessionKey` / `runId` scope when the status changes, not at later read time.
- Use immutable transition ids for stable notification ids: `status:<cardId>:<transition.id>`.
- Emit `status_changed` only when `subscription.eventKinds` explicitly contains `status_changed`.
- Preserve existing no-filter behavior for `completed` / `failed` / `stale`.
- Ignore no-op status writes and position-only moves.

## Evidence

Focused local proof on current branch after the lazy additive-table repair:

- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/workboard/src/sqlite-store.ts extensions/workboard/src/store.test.ts` -> pass.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/workboard/src/sqlite-store.ts extensions/workboard/src/store.test.ts` -> pass.
- `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run extensions/workboard/src/status-changed-notifications.test.ts extensions/workboard/src/store.test.ts` -> 118 tests passed.
- `git diff --check` -> pass.

Redacted persisted-store runtime proof on current head:

```json
{
  "db": "temp-sqlite-redacted",
  "subscriptionEventKinds": ["status_changed"],
  "firstDelivery": {
    "kind": "status_changed",
    "fromStatus": "todo",
    "toStatus": "ready",
    "revision": 1,
    "idPrefix": "status:<redacted-card-id>",
    "cardMatches": true,
    "message": "Status changed todo → ready."
  },
  "replayAfterReopen": {
    "kind": "status_changed",
    "fromStatus": "todo",
    "toStatus": "ready",
    "revision": 1,
    "idPrefix": "status:<redacted-card-id>",
    "cardMatches": true,
    "message": "Status changed todo → ready."
  },
  "replaySameEventId": true,
  "replaySameRevision": true
}
```

The proof command created a temporary SQLite Workboard store, created an explicit `eventKinds:["status_changed"]` subscription, updated a card from `todo` to `ready`, read the delivered notification, closed the store, reopened the same database, and read back the replayed notification with the same event id and revision.

Redacted upgrade/lazy-create proof on safe Node v25.9.0:

```json
{
  "legacyBeforeOpenHasTransitionTable": false,
  "afterOpenAndListHasTransitionTable": false,
  "afterTransitionHasTransitionTable": true,
  "firstKind": "status_changed",
  "firstFromStatus": "todo",
  "firstToStatus": "ready",
  "replaySameEventId": true,
  "replaySameRevision": true
}
```

The upgrade proof simulated an existing schema-3 database by dropping only the new additive transition table, reopened the store, listed cards and subscribed without creating the table, then wrote `todo -> ready`; only that real transition created the table and produced a durable replay-stable `status_changed` notification.

## Current CI

Latest current-head CI for `a6e26ce` is still running after the lazy-table fix; merge should wait for exact-head CI plus ClawSweeper/maintainer review. Previous head `b3b93866` had failures: none, pending: none, success: 83, skipped: 33, neutral: 1.

## Notes

This is intended as the upstream producer for an opt-in downstream Telegram/all-stage consumer. It does not alter behavior for existing subscriptions that only request `completed`, `failed`, or `stale`.

prs.title: feat(workboard): add explicit decomposition orchestration
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Workboard's hard parent/child dependency contract is correct for ordered work, but aggregate planning also needs an explicit non-blocking mode for independently runnable children. This PR adds that mode without changing the existing default or rewriting ambiguous stored state.

- Omitted `decompositionMode` remains `hard`.
- `decompositionMode: "hard"` creates reciprocal dependency links, so children wait for the parent.
- Explicit `decompositionMode: "orchestration"` records parent/child provenance without a hard dependency, so independently runnable children can be claimed while the aggregate parent remains open.
- Graph diagnostics identify broken dependencies, dependency cycles, and stale hard links on explicitly orchestrated decompositions.
- Operator-scoped unlink and repair tools are idempotent, declared in the plugin/tool contracts, and preserve audit history with one truthful `link_removed` event per changed card.

## Compatibility and stored-state policy

This head does **not** reverse Workboard's documented default and does **not** add an automatic Doctor migration.

Historical rows without an explicit decomposition mode are treated as existing hard intent and are left unchanged. `workboard_repair_decomposition` only proposes or removes a reciprocal hard link when both the parent and child are explicitly marked `orchestration`, the parent's decomposition manifest contains the child, and child provenance points back to the parent. Ambiguous or manually linked relationships are skipped.

Idempotent retries cannot silently change an existing child's decomposition contract. A retry that reuses a child with an incompatible explicit mode fails before the parent records the conflicting mode. An orchestration retry may reuse a child only when the parent and child already carry matching orchestration provenance and no hard dependency remains; ambiguous historical rows fail closed. Rollback preserves both cards unchanged.

## Evidence

### Disposable SQLite behavior proof

The proof used a fresh temporary Workboard SQLite database, closed and reopened it before verification, redacted identifiers, and removed it afterward. No production or live Workboard state was read or changed.

```json
{"path":["sqlite-open","create-hard-default","create-explicit-orchestration","seed-explicit-stale-link","seed-unmarked-historical-link","sqlite-reopen","verify-contract"],"omittedModeIsHard":true,"omittedModeHasParentLink":true,"omittedModeClaimRejected":true,"explicitOrchestrationRunnable":true,"invalidModeRejected":true,"invalidModeCreatedNoCards":true,"dashboardPreservedOrchestrationMode":true,"dashboardDroppedInvalidMode":true,"repairDryRunCandidateCount":1,"repairAppliedCount":1,"repairedLinksRemoved":true,"repairedEventsRecorded":true,"historicalRepairCandidateCount":0,"historicalRepairSkippedCount":1,"historicalStatePreserved":true,"database":"ephemeral","identifiers":"redacted","productionModified":false}
```

- Repaired the three current durable-review findings: ambiguous historical orchestration retry, partial multi-card repair, and dropped Control UI recovery actions.
- An orchestration retry now requires matching explicit parent/child provenance and no retained hard link; the mode-less historical hard-link regression proves both cards remain byte-for-byte unchanged on rejection.
- Applied repair now preflights the parent and every candidate child before removing any link; a later claimed child causes a fail-closed rejection with the earlier candidate and parent unchanged.

- Merged current `upstream/main` at `92e522cade4c8c04a0eee3d2851e3dd4a127eb68` without source conflicts.
- Exact focused behavior proof: **316 tests passed** across the Workboard store and Control UI suites.

The exact-head extension test-type process remained active without diagnostics for an abnormal no-output interval and was terminated; hosted `check-test-types` remains required. All four production/test type gates passed on the immediately preceding repair head before this conflict-free main-only merge.

Changed-file type-aware Oxlint, exact-file Oxfmt, `git diff --check`, UI i18n verification, UI production build, docs listing, MDX validation, and **6,425-link** audit all passed.

The final run passed **19/19** contract checks across omitted/explicit-hard blocking, explicit-orchestration claimability, invalid-mode atomicity, incompatible and ambiguous retry fail-closed behavior, dry-run/apply/idempotent repair, scoped all-candidate preflight, and reopened SQLite persistence.

prs.title: fix(openai): drop transient reasoning replay state
prs.body:
Closes #113868

## What Problem This Solves

Native Codex Responses can emit temporary reasoning items whose IDs start with `rs_tmp_`. OpenClaw persisted those items in assistant `thinkingSignature` fields and replayed them on later turns even though the IDs are not durable replay state. A follow-up request could then fail with `invalid_encrypted_content`.

## Why This Change Was Made

This current-main rewrite places the rule at the two canonical owners:

- the stream writer keeps the human-readable reasoning summary but omits replay signature and provenance metadata for temporary native Codex reasoning;
- the consolidated replay converter drops matching signatures already present in older transcripts and clears adjacency state, so a later signed text item cannot inherit pairing from an earlier stable reasoning item.

The check is intentionally limited to the native Codex Responses backend. Stable `rs_*` items and temporary-shaped IDs from compatible proxy endpoints retain the existing behavior.

The old branch changed a duplicate provider conversion path that was later consolidated by #123762. This rewrite removes that obsolete surface instead of rebasing it.

## User Impact

Multi-turn native Codex Responses sessions no longer carry temporary encrypted reasoning state into later requests. Visible reasoning summaries and valid stable reasoning replay remain unchanged.

## Evidence

Exact head: `d54dd8160fa40ac3d090502891ebf5ef6ac170de`, based on current `upstream/main` `ed6e3aabf0`.

- Pre-fix owner regression: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-transient-reasoning.test.ts` failed in exactly two places: native `rs_tmp_*` state was persisted, and the same item was replayed after a stable reasoning item. Stable native reasoning and proxy behavior passed.
- Exact-head focused and sibling tests: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-transient-reasoning.test.ts packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-stream-parity.test.ts packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-prompt-role.test.ts src/agents/openai-responses.reasoning-replay.test.ts` -> 43/43 passed.
- Both consolidated replay facades are covered by the stable -> temporary -> signed-text ordering regression. The temporary item is absent and the text ID is not replayed.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --type-aware ...` -> passed for all three changed files.
- `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` -> passed.
- `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-import-cycles.ts` -> 0 runtime value cycles.
- Scope: two production files, +25/-5 (net +20), plus one focused 161-line test file. The previous implementation was four files with production net +39 and edited an owner removed by #123762.

Direct dependency-contract check:

- OpenAI Codex source at `90854393966b21e9ebfd21b122334eb09a20c93d` models reasoning as a first-class Responses item carrying an optional provider item ID and encrypted content: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/90854393966b21e9ebfd21b122334eb09a20c93d/codex-rs/protocol/src/models.rs#L950-L999
- Server item IDs are deliberately read as opaque/permissive values: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/90854393966b21e9ebfd21b122334eb09a20c93d/codex-rs/protocol/src/response_item_id.rs#L17-L34
- Codex forwards reasoning items as model request input rather than normalizing their provider lifetime: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/90854393966b21e9ebfd21b122334eb09a20c93d/codex-rs/core/src/client_common.rs#L53-L90
- The OpenAI Responses contract documents encrypted reasoning as state to replay for stateless multi-turn use, which is why excluding only observed temporary native items must happen before persistence/replay: https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/cli/resources/responses/methods/create

Known proof gap: this machine does not yet have a redacted exact-head two-turn native provider trace showing a real `rs_tmp_*` response followed by a request that omits it. No live-provider claim is made. No additional AutoReview was run.

prs.title: fix(goals): count tokens from post-creation baseline
prs.body:
## Summary

- start Goal token-budget accounting from the first fresh post-creation token snapshot instead of importing earlier session usage
- accumulate subsequent usage from a persisted cursor, rebasing safely across counter resets and saturating at safe-integer bounds
- advance Goal accounting from CLI session finalization while preserving concurrent durable Goal changes
- keep `/goal status` and `get_goal` projections read-only and align scoped/global session-store routing
- reject token budgets that are not positive safe integers

## What Problem This Solves

A new Goal could inherit cumulative token usage from before Goal creation. For example, a fresh post-creation snapshot could be compared with an older or stale creation-time value and immediately exhaust a new budget.

The session token total is a snapshot that can cross accounting epochs (including compaction/reset), so repeatedly subtracting one absolute `tokenStart` is not reliable.

## Approach

`SessionGoal` now carries an optional `tokenCursor`:

1. The first persisted fresh snapshot after Goal creation establishes `tokenStart` and `tokenCursor` with zero charged usage.
2. Later fresh snapshots add only positive deltas from the cursor.
3. Equal snapshots are idempotent; lower snapshots rebase the cursor without reducing accumulated usage.
4. Legacy Goals reconstruct a cursor from `tokenStart + tokensUsed` where safe.
5. Goal resume/reset opens a new accounting window at the current fresh snapshot when one is available.

CLI session finalization projects accounting after fresh usage metadata is assembled and before concurrent snapshot reconciliation, allowing compatible token metadata to advance without overwriting concurrent Goal edits, completion, replacement, or clearing.

## Regression coverage

- stale/missing creation baseline followed by fresh snapshots
- incremental charging (33,107 → 33,124 charges exactly 17)
- duplicate and decreasing snapshots
- safe-integer validation and saturation
- legacy Goal migration and resume charging
- read-only status/tool projections
- global and scoped session-store routing
- CLI persistence and concurrent durable Goal changes

## Evidence

- `src/agents/command/session-store.test.ts` + `src/agents/tools/goal-tools.test.ts`: 67 passed
- `src/config/sessions/goals.test.ts`: 19 passed
- `src/tui/embedded-backend.test.ts`: 60 passed
- `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-goal.test.ts`: 10 passed
- `oxfmt --check`: passed
- type-aware `oxlint --deny-warnings`: 0 warnings/errors
- core `tsgo`: passed
- `git diff --check`: passed

## Scope

This is intentionally limited to Goal accounting and its persistence/status surfaces. It does not change global context/token limits or redesign session usage accounting.

## Redacted live behavior proof

An isolated live session was exercised against a deployed patched OpenClaw `2026.7.1-2` runtime implementing this accounting path. Identifiers, local paths, endpoints, and deployment hashes are omitted. This demonstrates the after-fix behavior; it does not claim that this PR head is already shipped upstream.

```text
Goal created after the session already had historical usage:
  session totalTokens: 32987 (fresh)
  Goal tokenStart: 0
  Goal tokenStartFresh: false
  Goal tokensUsed: 0
  Goal tokenBudget: 30000

First fresh post-creation snapshot:
  session totalTokens: 33110
  Goal tokenStart: 33110
  Goal tokenCursor: 33110
  Goal tokensUsed: 0

Next fresh snapshot:
  session totalTokens: 33133
  Goal tokenCursor: 33133
  Goal tokensUsed: 23
  observed charge: 33133 - 33110 = 23

Later fresh process readback:
  session totalTokens: 33339
  Goal tokenStart: 33110
  Goal tokenCursor: 33339
  Goal tokensUsed: 229
  cumulative charge: 33339 - 33110 = 229
```

The same acceptance also verified:

- `/goal status` and `get_goal` returned the same accounting state.
- Direct read-only status calls left the persisted Goal unchanged before vs. after the calls.
- A separate process reread the same persisted `tokenStart`, `tokenCursor`, and `tokensUsed` values.
- Focused regression tests cover legacy cursor reconstruction/resume behavior and concurrent durable Goal replacement/completion/clear preservation; the live transcript above specifically proves post-creation baselining and later delta charging.
