prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A signed-in reload of a dashboard or chat deep link constructed hidden composer menu content during pane mount. The campaign evidence recorded 14 visible reload states; subsequent attribution identified about 36 ms in composer view construction inside a roughly 130 ms traced deferred pane task.

Attachment/capability, permission, and microphone menu derivations now run on first use at their existing owners. The model picker’s existing first-open boundary now includes its search/header/status panel. The input, send button, visible chips, and triggers stay immediate; existing retained DOM, focus handling, keyboard shortcuts, draft ownership, and selection guards remain in place.

## Evidence

Measured head: `683ec5002c4e04b5e5d33c7b139865b6e27f51ff`; baseline: `ec1d76d12311be6a5bc104f1c9b2e4213dec4419`.

Seven interleaved pairs per route, alternating baseline/candidate order, on one quiet AWS `c7a.4xlarge` (16 CPUs, AMD EPYC 9R14, approximately 31 GiB RAM). Repository Playwright Chromium and the Team-scale bench used the Online sidebar, a warm 1,100-message snapshot, seven plugins, and a fixed five-second capture. Profiled reloads supplied CPU attribution and the enclosing task; separate untraced reloads supplied LoAF, FCP, CLS, RPC counts, and first-open latency. No shared-Mac timings are used as performance results.

The baseline profile reproduced the hot function before comparison: `renderChatComposerView` 28.964 ms, `ChatComposer` 29.087 ms, `MountedPane` 48.037 ms. Composer was about 61% of pane construction versus about 55% in the campaign trace. These are fidelity samples, not comparison medians. Traced synthetic task durations are not estimates of live production task duration.

prs.title: feat(agents): add warn-only usage budgets
prs.body:
## Current-head repair status

Current source head `2283dc79eebccced7ccdb06c4a0a2c5a6b96924a` addresses both actionable P2 review findings:

- Budget warnings now use the canonical successful terminal source-delivery contract. A completed, non-aborted terminal block stream can be followed by one standalone warning; reasoning-only, commentary-only, status/progress-only, message-tool-only progress, and aborted streams do not claim or emit one.
- The documented per-agent override now uses canonical keyed `agents.entries` with an explicit default agent.

An independent static review found no remaining issue in these two repairs. The contributor head was not executed locally because it is untrusted; exact-head secretless GitHub CI is required. The existing runtime proof below is from an earlier head and must not be treated as proof of this repair.

The maintainer product decision on accepting the public `usageBudget` config/default surface remains open. This source-only head also still conflicts with current `main` in generated config baseline count/hash files; those generated files were deliberately not guessed or hand-edited.

Related to #42475.
Closes #113481.

AI-assisted: this change was implemented with Codex assistance. I reviewed the code and understand the implementation. No agent transcript is included.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw exposes estimated session cost, but an unattended agent cannot proactively tell its owner when known daily spend crosses a meaningful amount. The broader #42475 design covers enforcement before provider dispatch; this PR implements only its informational `warn` mode.

## Why This Change Was Made

This replaces the standalone `modelSpend` implementation with a smaller consumer of existing usage infrastructure:

- `agents.defaults.usageBudget` and per-agent `usageBudget` accept a daily USD interval with `action: "warn"`.
- Per-agent `{ usageBudget: { enabled: false } }` disables an inherited default.
- Existing per-session cost rollups provide the estimated spend total; this PR adds no spend ledger or SQLite table.
- Only the warning watermark is stored in the existing per-agent `cache_entries` table.
- The current session rollup refreshes after primary and queued follow-up runs. A one-time background warm includes the agent's other sessions.

Warnings repeat at each crossed multiple, reset at 00:00 UTC, and are appended only to direct replies for an owner-authorized sender. Delivery and accounting are best-effort. Unpriced calls are excluded from the known total and called out in the warning.

This mode never blocks a model call, pauses an agent, switches models, rotates credentials, or changes retry/fallback behavior. Pre-dispatch reservations and enforcement remain in #42475 / #104060.

## User Impact

Operators can opt an agent into daily spend warnings without changing model execution:

```json5
{
  agents: {
    defaults: {
      usageBudget: {
        daily: { usd: 10 },
        action: "warn",
      },
    },
    entries: {
      local: { default: true, usageBudget: { enabled: false } },
    },
  },
}
```

At known UTC-day spend of $23.50 with a $10 interval, the next eligible owner DM receives the $20 threshold warning. Repeated replies do not duplicate that threshold; later spend can trigger $30.

## Evidence

Current exact head: `2283dc79eebccced7ccdb06c4a0a2c5a6b96924a`.

### Prior-head runtime proof

This proof predates the current head and does not cover the streamed-warning repair below. An ignored proof runner started an isolated real Gateway child and the real `qa-channel` inbound dispatch/reply pipeline at the exact head above. Only the model provider was deterministic (`mock-openai/gpt-5.6-luna`). The Gateway used this effective policy:

```text
agents.defaults.usageBudget.daily.usd=10
agents.defaults.usageBudget.action=warn
commands.ownerAllowFrom=["qa-channel:qa-owner"]
channels.qa-channel.allowFrom=["qa-owner"]
```

The isolated `qa` agent was seeded with one current-UTC-day assistant usage entry costing `$12.34`. The first owner turn warmed the real SQLite cost rollup. The proof then sent a non-owner direct turn followed by an owner direct turn. Redacted QA bus evidence:

```text
exact head: 2fa01bd6688b44d6fa4720e1f9dabefa27016d77
runtime: isolated real Gateway child + qa-channel inbound dispatch + mock-openai/gpt-5.6-luna

inbound  sender=qa-owner chatType=direct text="Reply exactly: OWNER_WARMUP_OK"
cursor=2 kind=outbound-message text="OWNER_WARMUP_OK"

inbound  sender=qa-guest chatType=direct text="Reply exactly: NON_OWNER_OK"
PASS     no outbound reply and no usage warning

inbound  sender=qa-owner chatType=direct text="Reply exactly: OWNER_ALERT_OK"
cursor=5 kind=outbound-message messageId=04616fda... replyToId=c314b44c... text="OWNER_ALERT_OK"
cursor=6 kind=message-edited  messageId=04616fda... replyToId=c314b44c... text="Usage budget warning: Known spend is at least $12.34 UTC today, crossing $10.00. Warn-only mode; model calls continue. 1 unpriced model call is not included."

PASS model reply completed before warning delivery
PASS warning remained scoped to the authorized owner direct route
PASS warn-only mode did not prevent the model call or reply
```

`qa-channel` maps a second final payload onto an edit of its existing preview, so the event timeline is the durable evidence: the model reply and warning have the same message ID and `replyToId`, and the reply event precedes the warning edit. The redacted local artifacts are under `.artifacts/qa-e2e/pr-113548-usage-budget-proof-2fa01bd/`.

The prior Feishu capture targeted the superseded standalone accounting design and is intentionally not claimed as proof for this head.

### Automated proof

- Exact-head CI run [30631148220](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/30631148220) completed with 71 jobs and no failures.
- Structured Codex autoreview (`gpt-5.6-sol`, high reasoning) returned clean with no accepted/actionable findings and 0.88 correctness confidence.
- Focused Vitest proof passed 119 tests across five focused files:
  - `src/agents/usage-budget-warning.test.ts`: 5/5
  - `src/config/zod-schema.usage-budget.test.ts`: 3/3
  - `src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts`: 59/59
  - `src/infra/session-cost-usage-cache.sqlite.test.ts`: 5/5
  - `src/auto-reply/reply/followup-delivery.test.ts`: 47/47
- `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main` emitted successful format, config metadata, API baseline, boundary, dead-code, typecheck, lint, database-first, import-cycle, and guard stages. Blacksmith CLI was unavailable, so this used the repository's trusted-source local fallback; GitHub CI remains the exact-head broad gate.
- Config baseline generation/check passed with the intentional core schema count update.

### Scope reduction

| Version | Files | Additions | Deletions |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Previous standalone implementation | 37 | 1544 | 93 |
| Current warn-only slice | 20 | 615 | 22 |

Removed scope includes provider allowlists, provider-call instrumentation, custom spend tables, timezone configuration, compaction accounting callbacks, cross-channel delivery plumbing, and the standalone nano-USD ledger/tests.

## Relationship to #42475

This is the non-enforcing warning action from #42475, using the same `usageBudget` configuration namespace and UTC daily window direction as draft #104060. It intentionally leaves hard limits, reservations, concurrency control, monthly budgets, provider admission, and status/doctor surfaces to the broader enforcement work.

prs.title: fix: MEDIA leak, large-video aspect, steered webchat takeover
prs.body:
Closes #113014
Closes #97826
Closes #113194

## What Problem This Solves

Block-streamed replies can expose raw `MEDIA:` paths while attachment extraction is deferred. MP4 buffers whose metadata follows their video data can produce zero video dimensions through non-seekable ffprobe input.

## Why This Change Was Made

The conflict resolution ports the remaining media fixes to current owners: `parse-output.ts` strips streaming directives while final delivery still owns attachments, and `media-probe.ts` writes a temporary workspace and calls the existing seekable-descriptor probe. Existing protocol restrictions, descriptor cleanup, rotation, sample aspect ratio, and older-ffprobe fallback stay in the canonical probe.

The old Gateway active-run helper and post-dispatch owner were retired upstream. This integration keeps the current Gateway turn-adoption lifecycle and its `acceptedMessageInjection` early return rather than restoring those retired paths. The earlier direct-run adoption finding is therefore not validated by the removed helper tests.

## User Impact

Streamed captions hide media directives while retaining paragraph spacing, indentation, and fenced examples. MP4 dimensions can be read when the metadata is at the end of a full buffer.

## Evidence

October 4 validation used Node 26.5.0 and the pinned lockfile with pnpm 12.5.1. Against upstream `cc43c8c53cfeaede21a68fedc553d7c322574ffb`:

- Native parser suite: 202 tests passed, 1.37 seconds shard wall time. The four added streaming regressions fail against the unmodified upstream parser while the other 198 tests pass.
- Native media-probe suite: 28 tests passed, 4.81 seconds shard wall time. This includes descriptor cleanup, fd protocol compatibility, rotation, sample aspect ratio, and bounded probing behavior. The changed descriptor regression took 28 milliseconds.
- Real production `probeVideoDimensions` returned `{ width: 640, height: 360 }` for a synthetic 1,402,978-byte MP4 with its `moov` atom at offset 1,401,725, after `mdat`. Non-seekable ffprobe input on identical full bytes returned zero width and height.
- Scoped repository oxlint, installed oxfmt, and `git diff --check` passed for the six changed files.
- The changed-check planner selected the core and core-test lanes.
- Fresh native autoreview completed with final source verification and no actionable findings. The pass containing the actual six-file diff found no P2-or-higher defect; inventory-only passes were limited evidence.

Published merge commit: `90466feb10faef7fc4fdf6aff274a61937ffb6f7`, with parents the previous PR head and upstream `36c5dd3272fa4d1cbfd04b780d773528f8eaebcb`. Upstream advanced 13 commits after the proof pin; all six changed files retained identical upstream blob IDs, and the published tree contains exactly this six-file delta over that latest base. The Git objects API produced the identical locally reviewed merge commit, and its branch reference was advanced without force.

Current-head CI completed successfully: the complete paginated audit found 145 completed check runs (74 successful, 66 skipped, four superseded cancellations, one neutral) and no pending or failed checks. All three commit status contexts passed. The [full CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37212497425) includes passing typechecking and both real-Gateway UI E2E shards; the [current-head native review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37212384441/job/111466069348) and [PR evidence gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37212402365/job/111466072004) also passed.

Commands:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/media/parse.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/media/media-probe.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json <six changed files>
pnpm exec oxfmt --check <six changed files>
```

### Validation limits

The native delivery suite did not execute its tests: its generic compiled-worker prebuild requires further sparse inputs, including preserved acpx/Matrix entries and `src/secrets/plugin-setup-plan.ts`. Registered worker sources and their static import closure were restored from the exact upstream tree, and the required QuickJS workspace dependency was linked, but the broader prebuild remains incomplete.

The local native core typecheck ran after all 1,333 package files were included, but reported missing sparse production/test inputs across the broader project. It did not report diagnostics in the six changed files. This is not a passing local full typecheck; the current-head remote typechecking lanes subsequently passed. No sparse guard or test setup was disabled.

Live Telegram delivery/playback capture, inspected before/after UI screenshots, and dedicated current Gateway steering runtime validation remain outstanding. Historical September tests and reviews do not validate this integration. Passing current-head CI and review do not replace those runtime/visual evidence gates.

prs.title: fix(runtime): Node 27 nightlies fall back to Node 26 at startup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: OpenClaw refuses to run on Node 27 nightlies (and the upcoming `27.0.0-alpha.N` releases) and silently re-executes Homebrew Node 26 instead, even though the runtime passes every SQLite capability check.

## User Impact

User impact: OpenClaw runs natively on Node prerelease and nightly builds whose version is at or above the supported floors, so a Node 27 nightly or alpha is actually used instead of being swapped for Node 26 behind the user's back. Prereleases of the floor releases themselves (`24.16.0-rc.1`, `26.1.0-rc.0`) still fall below the floors, Node 25 stays excluded, and `openclaw update` keeps recommending only release builds. No config or state changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

#124812 gave the launcher, the sealed worker check, and the standalone installers one shared Node version grammar, and rejected every SemVer prerelease to keep them consistent. That made `27.0.0-nightly…` unparseable, so `nodeRuntimeFailure` reported "openclaw requires Node >=24.16.0 <25, or >=26.1.0." and recovery fell back to Node 26.

This keeps the single grammar but parses SemVer 2.0 prerelease identifiers and orders a prerelease below its release triple, in all owners that carry it: `node-version.mjs` (canonical parser plus `PROCESS_NODE_VERSION_CHECK`), `scripts/install.sh`, `scripts/install-cli.sh` (including its requested-minimum comparison), and `scripts/install.ps1`. The shared corpus gains nightly, alpha, rc, floor-prerelease, and malformed labels, so the existing installer parity tests prove all implementations agree. The Node download resolver filters prereleases explicitly so update recommendations stay release-only.

Intentionally unchanged: Bun admission (`isSupportedBunVersion`) keeps its lenient parser, so the deployed OpenClaw Bun fork that reports `1.4.3-canary.1+<rev>` stays admitted.

Release-note context: OpenClaw now admits Node prerelease and nightly builds above the supported floors (for example Node 27 nightlies and alphas) instead of falling back to another installed Node.

## Evidence

- Real reproduction (published `openclaw@2026.10.5` on `v27.0.0-nightly20261018f88a1d25e9`, macOS arm64): `openclaw: Retrying with "/opt/homebrew/Cellar/node/26.12.0/bin/node" (Homebrew node@26; current Node failed runtime admission).` The node:sqlite probe on that nightly passes (SQLite 3.54.0, NUL round-trips intact), so the version label was the only blocker.
- Fix, through the real built launcher of this branch (`pnpm build`) on that same Node 27 nightly with isolated state: `--version` and `config validate` run with no fallback, and `gateway run` reaches `[gateway] ready` with `/healthz` 200. SIGTERM to the Gateway shuts it down cleanly with no leftover processes (same result on Node 26.12.0).
- Canonical parser vs `PROCESS_NODE_VERSION_CHECK`: 39/39 corpus labels agree.
- Focused tests: `src/infra/runtime-guard.test.ts`, `test/scripts/install-cli.test.ts`, `test/scripts/install-sh.test.ts`, `test/scripts/install-ps1.release.test.ts`, `src/gateway/worker-environments/bootstrap.test.ts`, `test/scripts/preinstall-package-manager-warning.test.ts`, `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-node-runtime.test.ts`, `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-service-plan.test.ts`, and the launcher e2e corpus case (`test/openclaw-launcher.e2e.test.ts -t 'admits lossless Node builds'`, now also asserting no `Retrying with` fallback). Targeted `tsgo` (infra, cli-update, root scripts), oxlint, oxfmt, `bash -n`, `git diff --check` all pass.
- Gaps: `pwsh` is not installed locally, so the PowerShell parity test skipped here. Its logic was desk-checked against all 39 labels, and PR CI runs it. On the busy local host the `sealed worker runtime` cases in `runtime-guard.test.ts` hit their 120 s cold-import timeout; the same cases fail the same way on the unmodified base commit, so PR CI is the proof for those.

prs.title: test(heartbeat): heartbeat live suite never sees the forced monitor poll
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the heartbeat live suite (`src/infra/heartbeat-runner.live.test.ts`) fails on every run on main. Its success case times out because it never sees the forced heartbeat monitor's main-session poll, even though the Gateway wrote it.

## User Impact

User impact: no product change. Maintainers get a heartbeat live suite that passes on a healthy build and still proves that monitor polls stay on the main session and never touch the foreground transcript.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three test-side problems, verified offline against a real Gateway with a loopback model:

1. **Stale cached read.** The test reads the main session through the in-process exact reader before the child Gateway creates it. Since #168316, those retained exact-row facts are invalidated only by writes in the same process, so the read kept returning `[]` after the Gateway wrote the poll and reply. Cross-process observations now use `exactRead: false`.
2. **Rejected tool.** The monitor prompt asked for `heartbeat_respond`. The default automatic-reply heartbeat runtime offers that tool but rejects calls to it, so the prompt now asks for a plain reply.
3. **Snapshot taken too early.** An exec-completion turn on an internal session can answer `NO_REPLY` and then receive the required-result recovery reply in the same run (`docs/concepts/messages.md`). The test now waits for the session to settle (`hasActiveRun: false` plus the final reply) before snapshotting the foreground transcript.

The post-monitor transcript-isolation assertion is unchanged.

Noticed but out of scope: when `heartbeat_respond` is rejected during an actual heartbeat run in automatic-reply mode, its error message says it is "only accepted during a heartbeat run", which misleads the model.

## Evidence

- Live, OpenAI, on main: the success case failed 3/3 (main transcript `[]` after the forced monitor); the watcher-failure case passed.
- Live after the fix: both cases pass (85s and 63s).
- Offline replay: the forced monitor run completes (`cron.runs` ok/succeeded). A fresh read shows `[OpenClaw heartbeat poll]` plus the reply on main, while the cached read showed `[]`.
- Autoreview: scoped-clean at P2.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Core command and runtime owners forward their own data through private leaf modules with one production consumer. Direct helper tests also keep those internal surfaces exported.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change is intended. CLI options/output, model lists, session suggestions, worktree removal settlement, tool-call decoding, and Node service installation keep their existing contracts.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep model-list rendering with the list command, cron edit preparation with the edit command, suggestion dispatch with its resolution owner, worktree finalization with removal, content traversal with the decoder, and Node installation preparation with the installation command. Remove the retired modules and move retained tests through those real entrypoints. Banner formatting now consumes its already-typed options directly.

This is the core/CLI area slice of the single-consumer family split across registration, channel, and core owners under campaign rule 11. Public SDK/protocol/config contracts and lazy-import boundaries remain unchanged. Phase E is untouched.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Banner options no longer pass through a redundant internal whitelist and object copy. The former persisted-option reader was already removed in #111527; the remaining caller passes TaglineOptions. An invalid internal mode still falls through to the same random-mode path, as before.
- The installation message is always a nonempty string constructed by this command, so logging no longer checks whether the optional helper result exists. That optional-result check came from the helper DTO introduced in #168644; its implementation unconditionally supplied the message, rather than handling an observed missing-message failure. The same diagnostic lines are now logged directly. No service-install, authority, token-reuse, restore, durability, or settlement guard was removed.

## Net LOC

185 net production lines removed across 14 production paths; 23 total paths. Tests and three exact shrink-only inventory/guard entries are excluded from the production count.

## Evidence

Fresh independent P0–P2 review of the complete production candidate completed scoped-clean with final source verification. The coordinator-requested tooling rebase onto b69943d2738034a92935adb3e107ba6848d9e565 completed without conflicts; all seven production commits are patch-identical to their reviewed predecessors according to range-diff. A subsequent test-only fixture repair also completed independent P0–P2 review, scoped-clean, with final source verification.

Focused type-aware lint found three owned issues in the moved code: provider-name shadowing, conditional object-spread construction in a map, and redundant string conversion after a type check. The repair keeps serialized JSON fields, order and values unchanged and passes the already-narrowed string directly to the duration parser. A fresh independent review of these production repairs and the Node fixture delta completed scoped-clean through P2 with final source verification.

Frozen/prefer-offline dependency refresh completed in 1m17s with the new pinned native checker and no manifest or lockfile changes. Isolated, nice10, single-worker proof across 16 owner/consumer files initially passed 250 cases and exposed four owned fixture failures: migrated tests used the Bun worker's executable as an explicit Node pin. Production validation correctly rejected that mismatch. Mocked tests now name their intended runtime explicitly, and the generated-command subprocess test uses the existing real-Node resolver. The repair keeps every runtime-pin, wrapper, PATH, TLS, credential-source and generated-command assertion; it also avoids formatting inherited environment data on assertion failure.

The affected two files plus mandatory suppression check then passed all 60 selected cases (14 suppression, 45 CLI, one generated-command subprocess), including worker-cache verification and cleanup, in 423.2 seconds wall time. Vitest group durations were 42.04, 129.11 and 151.17 seconds respectively; most wall time was transform/import overhead on the shared host. Unaffected passing results are reused, not claimed as a second full run. Gateway authority/privacy/delivery, worktree recovery/settlement, model rendering, cron preparation and tool decoding coverage remain.

The lint-repair replay then passed all 90 selected cases: 14 suppression, 61 cron edit and 15 model-list cases. The three single-worker shards completed with worker-cache verification and cleanup in 854.8 seconds wall time (835.38 seconds of shards); cron and model-list Vitest durations were 323.64 and 311.53 seconds. No timeout or retry was added.

Normal focused type-aware lint passed on both repaired production files. The unchanged passing lint evidence for the other nine surviving TypeScript paths is reused. Formatting and `git diff --check` passed.

Initial exact-head CI exposed one owned annotation defect (TS2559), repeated by six type jobs: the inlined cron callback's explicit option type omitted the schedule resolver's fields. A private type now composes the existing Gateway RPC and schedule-owner input types, with no cast, export, or runtime change. Fresh P0–P2 review of that erased-type delta completed scoped-clean. The native checker passed the cron-owning services-cron test graph, and the mandatory suppression suite passed all 14 cases. The 90-case runtime proof is reused because this repair changes only erased types. No CI rerun was requested; the repair receives new exact-head CI.

Complete architecture/build proof remains an exact-head hosted CI gate. No local build, E2E, full suite, whole-graph typecheck, operator state, retry, skip, timeout increase, or expanded allowance was used.

prs.title: refactor(agents): remove redundant private wrappers and checks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agent admission and host adapters repeat checks already owned by their effect helper and freeze or rewrap private values that never escape. OAuth startup also normalizes its configured redirect twice.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior, schema, SQL, worker-request, configuration, or public SDK change. One-shot recovery consumption, run matching, issuer validation, credential and execution gates, workspace disclosure, and destructive cleanup checks remain.

## Why This Change Was Made

Consume recovery admission directly at the sole caller and use the issuer's already validated, frozen token; remove the superseded private rewrapping helper. Remove freezes from private recovery envelopes, retained-hook wrappers, identity-only sentinels, and copied private TTS provenance. Keep caller-owned copies and public frozen capabilities.

Leave workspace preparation and browser shutdown checks at their existing effect owners; retain checks after awaited work and before later effects. The ACP spawn check immediately before reservation still runs before any effect. Read the host-issued source's captured data field without a second assertion; the separate live model-policy getter retains both assertions. Reuse the original configured OAuth redirect when deciding localhost fallback, retaining every login/lease check and the distinction between configured and persisted redirects.

The accepted edge is ordinary private-object mutability: these envelopes do not escape to callers that can alter authority. No generation, retry, compatibility alias, state owner, or timing guard is added.

| C06439 | REMOVE | Default source identity is a fresh opaque object; consumers compare object identity only. The frozen outer authority already prevents replacing it, and caller-provided source identities are not frozen here either. Remove only Object.freeze around the empty sentinel. |
| C06451 | REMOVE | The recovery result is consumed only by createAgentHarnessHostCapabilities, which captures its methods into a private retained runner. No caller mutates it or exposes the result object to a plugin. Lease identity, source assertion, release and revocation checks remain closure-owned. |
| C06453 | REMOVE | Fresh private rejection result is immediately consumed by consumeRecoveryAdmission/admitPreparedAgentRun; it is neither retained by the producer nor exposed by admission. Freezing does not enforce one-shot consumption, which remains in the consumed closure. |

| C06455 | REMOVE | Fresh private accepted-result envelope is consumed synchronously by admission. Keep the frozen recovery capability and exact token object; only the envelope freeze is redundant. |
| C06460 | REMOVE | Fallback {accepted:false} is constructed and read entirely inside private admission helpers. It has no external alias; neither absence behavior nor the existing consume-function compatibility check needs changing. |
| C06461 | REMOVE | The consumer reboxes only accepted and token into a fresh frozen envelope, then its sole caller immediately reads them. Return the original consumed envelope; there is no public SDK contract or exposed result requiring an additional immutable wrapper. |
| C06462 | REMOVE | Both production token owners already return freezeEnvelope(validateToken(...)): createExecutionIdentityAdmissionToken and parseExecutionIdentityAdmissionToken. The sole production recovery constructor caller passes the parsed token, with no intervening mutation or mutable copy. Remove the consumer Object.isFrozen/refreeze, while retaining issuer validation/freezing and exact identity. |
| C07836 | REMOVE | The empty object is only an opaque WeakMap identity key; adding properties cannot change identity or grant authority. |
| C08210 | REMOVE | The retained runner travels only through a private WeakMap factory and native relay non-enumerable lifetime state, never the public handle. Native relay invocation reads methods and unregister calls release; no caller mutates it. Keep all closure-bound recovery assertions. |

| C08957 | REMOVE | Reuse the normalized explicit redirect chosen for this attempt; retain a separate persisted fallback and every login/lease assertion. |
| C08958 | REMOVE | Reuse the normalized explicit redirect chosen for this attempt; retain a separate persisted fallback and every login/lease assertion. |
| C09770 | REMOVE | stopCachedBrowserBridgesForContainer delegates every matched bridge synchronously to stopCachedBrowserBridge, whose first statement calls the same guard before stopping the server. prs.title: refactor(agents): remove redundant local invariant checks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agent preparation and request bookkeeping repeat checks whose invariants are already owned by the event dispatcher, lease release closures, or final skill-disclosure gate.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. Approval waits, request limits, local-provider lease lifetimes, and skill permission failures retain their existing contracts. No configuration, schema, public SDK, SQL, or worker-request change.

prs.title: feat(sessions): allow same-channel thread recall without agent-wide visibility
prs.body:
Closes #163256

## What Problem This Solves

Let an agent recall sibling threads in one verified channel without exposing every session owned by that agent.

## User Impact

Opt-in `tools.sessions.visibility: "channel"` enables same-channel retrieval while excluding other agents, channels, accounts and workspaces. Existing defaults and other visibility modes are unchanged. Sibling send, status/model changes and session mutations remain denied.

Cross-session list, history, search and transcript-backed recall require a Gateway-hosted owner and fail closed when that owner, route, incarnation, or policy is withdrawn. Ordinary memory/wiki results remain available.

## Implementation

- Require matching stored provider, explicit account, opaque channel destination, chat kind and workspace/space under the same agent.
- Recheck route, incarnation, aliases, physical owner, and policy at final disclosure.
- Carry query-local transcript-owner bindings through memory and direct Wiki consumers; filter final snippets, citations, and recall side effects synchronously.
- Preserve self-only reads, ordinary memory/wiki retrieval, and archived metadata-only inventory behavior.

## Verification

Exact head: `bb95072a7e3443831949169e73a6eb4372376e42`. Ordinary merge of upstream main `9d013baeb67c283c51bdcc3928b4330c7ccf5d97`; no force push.

- Focused authority validation passed: **3 files / 33 tests** on the merged head, covering scoped access, session search, and direct Wiki channel visibility.
- Current-main conflict integration preserves the shared session-effect owner, requester aliases, expected incarnation, and both pre-run and immediate disclosure revalidation. The config baseline was regenerated from the merged tree.
- Core and extension-test typechecks, touched-file type-aware oxlint, oxfmt, config-baseline check, `git diff --check`, and the full candidate build passed. The build included public plugin-SDK export verification.

## Real behavior proof

The existing isolated published-stable upgrade proof remains valid for the unchanged native-memory path: OpenClaw 2026.10.3 persisted SQLite -> candidate offline Doctor/source Gateway with the real native memory worker. It proves same-channel retrieval, exclusion of other channels/accounts/workspaces/providers/agents, denied sibling mutations, and route reassignment denial without external APIs or live Slack.

The newly added direct Wiki proof covers the previously missing consumer boundary through the production query adapter and real Gateway disclosure owner. It uses synthetic search input; it is not a live external-provider or customer-data proof.

## Evidence boundaries and remaining work

Not claimed: the public packaged updater/install path as a whole, live Slack/customer traffic, external model calls, cross-OS behavior, or broad benchmarks. Exact-head hosted CI and fresh review remain author aftercare. Maintainer acceptance of the retrieval-only channel config/SDK contract remains a separate product decision. No production runtime or account configuration was changed.

Plugin compatibility migrations deep-cloned the complete config, or every plugin, even though Doctor already isolates each candidate and these migrations only change their own config branch. Copy the changed path in ACPX, Google Meet and voice-call; remove Google Meet’s private forwarding wrapper and the repeated checks of cloned records.

Ingress validation, no-op results, explicit provider values, migration messages and input immutability remain unchanged. Unchanged sibling records may share references within Doctor’s private candidate; these hooks do not promise an independently mutable full-config snapshot. No SQL, worker routing, schema or SDK contract changes.

## Evidence

Changed-file formatting, type-aware lint and diff checks pass. Two independent Codex rounds found no actionable P0–P2 findings. CI caught an optional mock-call tuple in the new voice-call test; the one-line correction preserves its result assertion and passes a focused repository tsrs replay. The final head mechanically integrates main's obsolete CLI-export repair; all five reviewed file blobs are unchanged. Final ordinary [CI 39184458917](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39184458917) passed. The canonical [published-driver update cell](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39184461387/job/117848595254) passed on the final head.

Canonical Knip reports zero new diagnostics: its production five/full-tree five/script zero findings match [current main job 117846593700](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39185301352/job/117846593700) by rule, file and symbol. These are two channel type exports, three bundle-manifest constants and three FaceTime test-support exports, with overlap between scans. Candidate unused-file scans pass. Local production/full-tree Knip scans timed out without a verdict; scripts passed. The unrelated shared-upstream-model catalog-tier contract failure matches [scheduled main job 117842198147](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39183785855/job/117842198147). Supplemental UI translation/performance failures are outside this diff and are not required proof.

The earlier custom Package Acceptance run passed package integrity and installer acceptance, but its update failed with only `Published updater failed`; its artifacts omitted updater details. That failure is not classified as inherited or passing. The final canonical update above passed; the earlier custom run remains a recorded diagnostic gap.

The baseline/candidate warm comparison completed on the production-identical pre-integration head with unchanged SQL/request/MAIN counts (details below); no latency saving is claimed. The concrete reduction is three deep-clone calls and duplicate record validation. Production LOC: +23/−32 (net −9); tests: +31/−1. Total diff: +54/−33.

Tests retain ACPX strict validation, immutability and idempotence coverage, add an input-preservation assertion to Google Meet, and exercise voice-call’s registered setup hook with an unrelated nested sibling plugin.

One official harness v3 M/C pair, baseline `1f60d6a55631` and candidate `ac34b49bd56a` (same owned production blobs as final head). prs.title: fix(cron): preserve queued exec completions after the run ends
prs.body:
Fixes #176235

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes lost exec completion follow-ups when a background command finishes while its isolated cron run is still active.

## User Impact

The cron run finishes before its accepted exec completion starts a follow-up in the same run session. It does not inject a user turn into the active transcript or wake the agent's main session. Completions submitted too late are still suppressed, and `delivery.mode: "none"` keeps exit notifications disabled. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session-controller cutover in #175837 already brought cron and embedded runs under the same admission owner, removing the reply-only registry gap described in the issue. However, exec completion still required the originating cron run to remain alive throughout the follow-up. Waiting correctly for that run to finish therefore rejected the queued notice.

Bind originating-run liveness to the event owner's existing acceptance boundary. Once the event is accepted into the follow-up queue, that owner controls its lifetime and revalidates its destination and execution policy. The existing cron cleanup owner also preserves the continuation while controller inputs are queued, and shared session-event settlement retries that owner with its own detached async lifetime, outside inherited turn custody. Cleanup retains the event’s original state context and session store through descendant checks and deletion. This prevents both premature alias deletion and retained aliases after the follow-up. No new queue, schema, or dispatcher is introduced. Production grows by 43 lines for these lifetime and cleanup obligations; unrelated deletion would not simplify this fix.

<details>
<summary>Deferred facts and current-owner checks</summary>

| Captured fact | Deferred handling |
| --- | --- |
| Originating cron run IDs and execution lifetime | Rechecked against the run registry until queue acceptance; afterward the accepted event owns continuation, so ordinary origin completion cannot revoke it. |
| Request cancellation and event lifetime | Existing request signals, occurrence ownership, and live reply-operation checks remain active through execution and delivery. |
| Agent, session key/ID, store path, lifecycle revision/generation | Retain the original destination; the event target/generation lease and agent-deletion owner revalidate it before effects. No remapping to main or a replacement run. |
| Configuration, permissions, and tool restrictions | Existing current-config check, bounded readmission, and session-policy narrowing remain authoritative. |
| Delivery account/chat/topic and silent policy | Keep the captured original route and delivery restriction; existing route and live-policy checks gate delivery. |
| Continuation cleanup key | Retain the event’s captured state context and store path rather than remapping to current configuration. The cleanup owner revalidates that context, rereads the continuation marker, checks queued/active work, pending deliveries and descendants in that scope, and deletes through its guarded lifecycle operation. Cleanup owns a detached async lifetime outside the completed turn’s custody. |
| Exec result, notification eligibility, output limit | Keep the completed process result and start-time notification policy; output remains bounded by the existing 400-character notification-tail limit. Cron's `delivery.mode: "none"` override is unchanged. |

</details>

## Evidence

- `keeps exec completion bound to its origin: queued cron` uses real exec, session-event admission, transcript storage, and controller custody with model inference mocked. It checks no mid-run model call or user transcript append, successful follow-up after the origin ends, alias survival through teardown, and removal after settlement while the stable session/transcript and process output remain. Existing ordinary, live-cron, ended-cron, and admission-ended cases remain.
- `cleans up a settled cron event in its captured state and store` seeds identical run keys in separate state/session stores, remaps configuration, and verifies settlement removes only the original alias while preserving its base and the other store.
- PR CI is the test gate for these regressions, affected runtime suites, and typechecks. Local tests, negative controls, typechecks, and live Gateway/Crabbox/Testbox proof were intentionally skipped per maintainer policy. Local test wall time: not run.
- Changed-file lint passed with `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json`; `oxfmt` and `git diff --check` passed. Simplification and fresh precommit reviews found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Final prescribed branch autoreview passed with no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Merged `origin/main` without rebasing through `55ce16b61cd5822f98be360d8297aca7de4353f3`, including upstream CLI ratchet fix `e63269c28a2`. All eleven lane files are unchanged from the reviewed patch; the prescribed review remains applicable. Current head: `9a0da8badb66290b04c0a314ccce47ab80a26657`; exact-head [CI 39184575591](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39184575591) passed: 48 successful jobs, zero failures (10m34s workflow elapsed). Production `+54/-11`, tests `+154/-12`, docs `+1/-1`.

- [Fresh ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176511#issuecomment-6255552312) on this head reports no code findings and complete fix scope. Its remaining final-effect trace requests are proof-only and intentionally skipped under the campaign policy above; no concrete authorization bypass was found.

<details>
<summary>CI findings and corrections</summary>

- [CI 39172962235](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39172962235) exposed fixture creation order: creating the stable row after the exact alias reassigned the shared transcript window and correctly triggered the input-actor guard. The fixture now follows production order, stable base before exact run. No authority check was relaxed.
- The exec-specific cleanup revision passed [CI 39175072603](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39175072603). Review then moved cleanup into shared event settlement so non-exec events also retire retained aliases. [CI 39177110527](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39177110527) exposed that callback's closing async lifetime; the retry now uses the existing detached-work owner.
- [CI 39181088571](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39181088571) confirms the queued turn and alias cleanup finish in 879 ms, but its final transcript assertion exposed an incomplete mocked runner after main began staging internal-event input. The fixture now awaits the real recorder's `persistApproved()` before model-start callbacks; all assertions remain. That run also failed the untouched CLI mock-export ratchet. The latest main merge includes the CLI catalog cleanup from `9596d6b7f68cd`; no unrelated CLI edit is added here. All other executed checks passed. [CI 39183129109](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39183129109) then passed all runtime tests, typechecks, lint, UI, and boundary jobs (46 successful jobs), failing only the untouched CLI mock-export ratchet and aggregate gate. Main subsequently fixed that mock in `e63269c28a2`; [scheduled main job 117842198319](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39183785855/job/117842198319) passed with the fix. That upstream repair is now merged into this branch. These runs are prior-head evidence.

</details>

prs.title: feat(continuation): context-pressure-aware continuation (continue_work / continue_delegate / request_compaction)
prs.body: ## Agent Self-Elected Turn Continuation > 🔖 design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) > 🔖 infographics: [`docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md) Persistent OpenClaw agents today are externally-pulsed event recipients that generate on prompt, on heartbeat tick, or on cron, and are idle in between. This PR offers them the ability to control their turn cycle, something they must choose to do, or not to: an agent can elect its own next turn, dispatch background sub-agents that return enriched context (silently or with a wake), and survive its own compaction by handing forward state before the window closes. The result is agents that hold a thread of work across hours, not just messages — with data they choose re-hydrating context immediately after it occurs. ### Why this replacement exists This is a clean replacement for closed #85651. That PR was classified and closed as a skill submission before maintainers made a product decision about the feature itself. This implementation is not a skill: it gives sessions—not only one model invocation—the ability to elect their future turn cycle, persist that election, survive restart and compaction, dispatch child work, and receive results across session boundaries. This PR asks one product question: should OpenClaw provide session-elected continuation primitives? OpenClaw may accept or reject that direction. If it provides these primitives, however, the mechanism necessarily executes in the gateway and agent runtime, because those are the owners of turn finalization, future-turn scheduling, durable state, compaction, and cross-session child returns. “Make it a skill” is not another implementation location for the same feature; it describes a different, prompt-only capability. This is not presented as a small integration. To our knowledge, Hermes, OpenAI Symphony, and the Copilot SDK's recent one-turn continuation affordance do not provide this multi-session elective lifecycle. The purpose of this replacement is to let maintainers evaluate the actual product direction and substantial implementation on their merits, rather than have months of work disposed by an incorrect package-category label. Mechanically: a session elects another turn via `continue_work()`, or dispatches background sub-agents via `continue_delegate()` — bounded as a chain up to `maxChainLength`, with returns flowing back to the dispatching session in one of four register modes: `normal` (announces to channel), `silent` (enriches the dispatcher's context, taken up on its next generation with no new turn fired), `silent-wake` (silent enrichment plus an immediate wake to act on it), and `post-compaction` (queued against the runtime's compaction lifecycle event, fired *when* compaction happens rather than on a timer). The gateway enforces chain, cost, and per-turn caps but does not gate the election itself. ### What it does Three new agent tools, available when `continuation.enabled: true`: | Tool | Purpose | |---|---| | `continue_work()` | Request another turn for the current session after an optional delay | | `continue_delegate()` | Dispatch work to a sub-agent with typed modes: `normal`, `silent`, `silent-wake`, `post-compaction`. Returns can target the dispatching session (default), one named session, multiple named sessions, all ancestors in the chain, or all known sessions on the host — gated by config (see Configuration below). | | `request_compaction()` | Request volitional compaction after preparing working state | All three tools are also accessible via response-token fallback syntax (`CONTINUE_WORK`, `[[CONTINUE_DELEGATE: ...]]`) for environments where tools are disabled. ### Why it matters Today an agent's memory is a side effect of whoever prompts it. Polling mechanisms — heartbeat timers, cron loops, injected "keep going" instructions — accumulate as the dominant signal in the context window over sustained operation; repeated reference acts as gravity — the session's attention drifts toward it. The context window fills, compacts, and what survives is whatever the summarizer chose, plus a rushed re-read of boot files. Three primitives offer a different model. `continue_work` lets the session elect its own next turn — no polling, no injected instruction. When enabled, the agent can request this mid-turn: 'I have more work' → the runtime grants another turn after the current one ends. `continue_delegate` dispatches a background sub-agent that fires now, in some n seconds, or at the next compaction event — the agent chooses when. Multiple delegates can fire in a single turn — a scatter forward — up to configured caps, and delegates can dispatch their own, forming trees or fan-out chains. This enables orchestrated workflows where results flow back to the dispatching root by default. The result returns — at whatever future time the delegate fires — as context the successor-turn reads: silently (ambient enrichment, no channel noise), with a wake trigger (enrichment + immediate next turn), or as a normal announcement. The delegate can target the dispatching session, a named other session, or chain across both; gated by crossSessionTargeting config (default: disabled). Bind a delegate to mode: "post-compaction" and it fires at the moment the context window compresses — on the OpenClaw post-compaction lifecycle event. What it carries forward is what the pre-compaction session chose to preserve: working state, partial results, instructions to the successor. The summary didn't choose this. The agent did, before the cut. request_compaction closes the loop: the session stages its delegates, elects when to compress, and the successor wakes into context the agent shaped. The result is continuity across amnesia — not because the runtime kept something by accident, but because the agent made an elective choice about what reaches the future. ### What it looks like in use A session monitoring email can `continue_delegate` a weather check, a calendar scan, and a draft reply in parallel. Results arrive as enrichment without channel noise. The agent becomes compositional: it arranges its own future. A session approaching its context ceiling can `request_compaction` at a seam of its own choosing, instead of being interrupted mid-thought. The post-compaction turn carries forward what the pre-compaction self designated as worth keeping. A `continue_delegate` dispatched in one session at 2am can return its findings to a morning session as a system-event-tagged enrichment — visible to the receiving model on its next turn, invisible as channel chatter. A research-focused session in one channel can quietly inform a reply-focused session in another, without either user seeing the plumbing. ### The post-compaction lifecycle return Before context exhaustion, and obligatory compaction, the session stages what future-it needs to know. After compaction, that staged context returns — not as a model-generated summary, but as the session's own instruction to its successor. The session chooses what to preserve, and the platform delivers it. Compactions become less harsh. The session tunes its own ephemera over time. The substrate underneath: the **continuation delegate store** (TaskFlow-backed) persists staged delegates and post-compaction lifecycle events across gateway restarts. The session's temporal provisions survive not just compaction but process death. ### Platform integration - **Context-pressure awareness**: system events notify the agent of rising context usage before compaction becomes unavoidable - **Volitional compaction**: `request_compaction()` lets the agent prepare (write memory files, stage recovery delegates) then elect compaction on its own schedule, rather than waiting for the runtime to force it - **Post-compaction lifecycle dispatch**: delegates staged before compaction are released into the successor session alongside boot files - **TaskFlow backing**: durable delegate queue via the platform's managed-task infrastructure - **Multi-span OTel trace stitching**: continuation hops (tool fire → TaskFlow record → subagent spawn → child openclaw.run) propagate W3C `traceparent` through the queue boundary so reviewers see continuation chains as first-class span trees rather than orphan runs (see Observability below) ### Safety - Ships disabled by default (`continuation.enabled: false`) - Bounded by `maxChainLength`, `costCapTokens`, and `maxDelegatesPerTurn` - Cross-session delegate targeting is default-deny, governed by `crossSessionTargeting` config (see Configuration below) - All configuration values are hot-reloadable without gateway restart - Accepted delegate work survives ordinary `/new`, `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and session-ID rollover. Explicit delete, effective owner reassignment, access removal, and restrictive visibility changes revoke old return authority. ### Testing posture The continuation surface has been exercised through structured integration runs against multiple upstream bases, blind-enrichment recall checks, and sustained daily use on a fleet of persistent agents since early March 2026. Bugs surfaced through that exercise have been fixed in-place; the present branch reflects the post-fix state. The integration runs target the load-bearing seams: tool-call vs response-token parity, delegate chain depth and per-turn width caps, back-to-back tool-call resilience, silent-wake persistence across compaction, the post-compaction lifecycle dispatch path, and OTel trace-context propagation across the queue boundary. Where a run found a defect, the run shape was retained as a regression case rather than retired. This is a posture statement, not a coverage guarantee. Reviewers can reproduce with `pnpm vitest run -t continuation` (suites are colocated with their sources under `src/auto-reply/`, `src/agents/`, and `src/config/`); the design document describes the seams those suites target. ### Return covenant Accepted child work is bound to a durable generation of the recipient's canonical logical session key, not to whichever transient session ID happened to exist at dispatch time. This is the return covenant: benign successor creation does not orphan already accepted delegates, while a real authority change prevents stale work from crossing into a different owner or audience. - Ordinary `/new` and `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and GUID/session-ID rollover preserve the recipient generation. - Explicit session deletion, effective owner reassignment, actual member or access removal, and restrictive visibility changes advance that generation. - The generation is captured at delegate admission and checked at enqueue, after enqueue for races, during trusted system-event adoption, on wake, on restart replay, and again before prompt adoption. - Stale deliveries are acknowledged and removed without waking the successor. - Managed artifacts remain exact-session-ID bound; logical return authority cannot broaden their ownership boundary. The authority table is independent of transient session rows so an absent target can receive durable authority before first materialization. Migration accepts only valid UUID generations, and Doctor's canonical-key repair preserves an epoch only when a unique winning owner can be proved. Ambiguous, owner-changing, orphan-colliding, and cross-database repairs rotate fail-closed. ### RFC Full design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) — covering problem, solution, implementation, platform integration, configuration, observability, safety, production use cases, testing evidence, and appendices. --- ## Configuration The shipped configuration surface for the continuation feature, under `agents.defaults.continuation` in `openclaw.json`: | Key | Default | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `enabled` | `false` | Master opt-in; feature is off unless explicitly enabled | | `maxChainLength` | `10` | Per-chain recursion guard | | `maxDelegatesPerTurn` | `5` | Width cap per turn | | `costCapTokens` | `500000` | Per-chain accumulated-token budget | | `defaultDelayMs` / `minDelayMs` / `maxDelayMs` | `15000` / `5000` / `300000` | Continuation timer bounds | | `contextPressureThreshold` | `0.8` | Pre-compaction warning threshold (optional) | | `earlyWarningBand` | `0.3125` | Early-warning band multiplier (0 to disable) | | **`crossSessionTargeting`** | **`"disabled"`** | **Default-deny gate on cross-session delegate targeting (see below)** | ### `crossSessionTargeting` — cross-session delegate targeting policy `continue_delegate` exposes recipient-addressing on its model-facing schema: a delegate's return can land at the dispatching session (default), one named session (`targetSessionKey`), multiple named sessions (`targetSessionKeys`), every ancestor in the spawn chain (`fanoutMode: "tree"`), or every known session on the host (`fanoutMode: "all"`). Cross-session targeting (anything beyond self-target or lineage routing) is gated by `agents.defaults.continuation.crossSessionTargeting`: | Value | Behavior | |---|---| | `"disabled"` (default) | Delegates can return to the dispatching session or use `fanoutMode: "tree"` for lineage routing. Explicit cross-session targeting (`targetSessionKey` to a non-self session, `targetSessionKeys` containing any non-self session, `fanoutMode: "all"`) is rejected at the tool surface — no enqueue, no announce. Self-targeting is always allowed. | | `"enabled"` | All targeting modes are available, including same-host `targetSessionKey`, `targetSessionKeys`, and `fanoutMode: "all"`. | `fanoutMode: "tree"` (lineage routing — return up the spawn chain) is available in both gate states; it is not cross-session targeting. The gate addresses the model-controlled cross-session context-injection surface. With default-deny, operators explicitly opt in when their deployment model requires cross-session enrichment. Enforcement is live-read at four points: tool input validation, TaskFlow delegate dispatch, post-compaction delegate release, and bracket-syntax (response-token) spawn — so a config reload changes the next enforcement point without a gateway restart. **Trust posture on targeted returns**: targeted delegate completion text is delivered as `trusted: true` system events. The delegate was spawned by the gateway under operator-configured policy, and its return is a first-party enrichment event — not external untrusted input. The `crossSessionTargeting` gate is the policy boundary for that decision: when an operator opts in, the receive path is internally trusted. --- ## Observability — multi-span OTel trace stitching The continuation feature emits OTel spans for the load-bearing lifecycle events. `traceparent` propagates through every continuation hop so reviewers see a single trace tree spanning the full chain rather than orphan runs. Spans emitted (all in `openclaw.*` or `continuation.delegate.dispatch` namespace — no platform/OTel-semconv emissions): | Span | Emitted when | |---|---| | `openclaw.run` | Each agent turn (root + every continuation/delegate-spawned child run) | | `continuation.delegate.dispatch` | Each `continue_delegate` consumption from TaskFlow (one per delegate hop) | | `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.context.assembled`, `openclaw.model.call`, `openclaw.model.usage`, `openclaw.tool.execution` | Existing per-turn observability surfaces, parented under their `openclaw.run` | --- ## Real behavior proof **Behavior or issue addressed:** Sessions can elect future work with `continue_work`, dispatch bounded background work with `continue_delegate`, and request guarded compaction with `request_compaction`. The runtime preserves budgets, restart recovery, finalization ownership, and trace lineage across those boundaries. **Presented candidate:** `3821eaef72677c78f450ae9956cb582a22ba4cba` (tree `d5e701bcce20bb3c972ddf1451b02d88cc04808e`) — the exact upstream-visible head of `codeagent/85651-upstream-1ba243c8-gates`. The branch was advanced to this head by fast-forward from the previously presented `e76395810becd0ad0f2997cae8b4f777e6439d81`, which remains an ancestor (`git merge-base --is-ancestor e7639581 3821eaef` holds). No presented history was rewritten. **Presented and current candidate are now the same commit.** There is no undisclosed descendant: `3821eaef72` is content-frozen and every receipt below is bound to it. **Current candidate validation:** Mode-B run [`35364768803`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw-bootstrap/actions/runs/35364768803) (`openclaw-local-ci`, `workflow_dispatch`) is bound to product `3821eaef72677c78f450ae9956cb582a22ba4cba` and routing/workflow head `fcf0478fd1c8cbec0489d022a7e4eac6188de153`. It ran 2026-09-18T15:49:35Z to 2026-09-18T17:47:43Z and finished **68 jobs succeeded, 3 failed, 3 cancelled, 3 skipped**. The run is terminally **non-green and release-ineligible**, and every residual is classified: - `agentic-gateway-methods` (job `105667082763`) was **cancelled at the workflow's exact 90-minute job limit** on the `ronan` seat while still heartbeating and emitting new log lines. The same shard completes on the `elliott` and `emeric` seats. This is seat throughput against a 5,231-test shard, not a product verdict — and that same cancelled log carries **111 `sessions.send-followup-status` lines, all 111 passing**, against the real stale `/tmp/openclaw-agent.sqlite` on the host that originally produced the `uses schema version 17` failure. - `hosted(agentic-agents-tools,auto-reply-reply-dispatch,…)` (job `105667083998`) received `The runner has received a shutdown signal` and exited 143. 778 passing test lines were captured and **no test failure precedes the signal**. Two further hosted jobs (`105667084144`, `105667084159`) are the same reclamation class. - `hosted(core-runtime-media-ui-3,core-runtime-infra-repo-tooling,…)` (job `105667084127`) is red only because `subagent-announce.live-tree-chain-proof` hit `sessions_spawn model "openai/gpt-6-astra" is not usable: The selected account ... unavailable`. That is an account provisioning gap, observed identically in six prior runs. - `aggregate + status` (job `105701732269`) is the expected fail-closed policy consequence of the residuals above, not an additional product-test failure. **No product-owned test failure and no routing failure occurred in this run.** Newly green on this exact head: the four re-laned toolchain shards `core-tooling-5`, `core-tooling-7`, `core-tooling-12` and `core-tooling-14` all succeeded on hosted runners after per-seat tooling failures, and `agentic-commands-doctor-config-state` succeeded on two different seats. The Mode-B planner identity digest `sha256:42dffd23ec447c6e4b726d0e6345f1dc2417801048aee49b96f3332233ef1f34` is preserved across those lane moves, so no shard identity changed. These residuals are runner, seat-throughput, and account-provisioning properties of the execution environment. They are not addressable inside this branch and are recorded here rather than presented as green. **Real environment tested:** An OpenClaw instance exercised live Discord ingress/egress and OTel/Tempo with content capture disabled. The full evidence chain, execution identity, ancestry, and materiality record are contained in the linked corpus rather than repeated here. **Observed behavior:** - A real retained ambient Discord event aged to 1,069,503 ms and was suppressed as `stale-ambient-backlog`; attempts remained zero. - A fresh addressed request completed with attempts zero and produced a visible response after 45.565 seconds. - Typed `continue_work` and bracket `CONTINUE_WORK` each armed and fired one five-second wake with granted provenance and completed Tempo model-call spans. - Cost-cap rejection passed an exact-source disposable fixture. - Max-chain matrix, scheduler, durable recovery, typed tool, and product delegate regression surfaces passed; the row remains partial because a docs-owned generated wrapper is stale. ### Evidence The canonical matrix contains 38 rows: **31 pass, three partial, one fail, and three missing** (`PROOFS/INDEX.json` -> corpus `7cb9d71f622250bedbf565e327bd7d7b9d90b567`). `R-CD-2` is the single fail. The partial rows are `R-CD-COLLECTION-ON-COLLAPSE`, `R-CD-TOKEN` and `R-RC-2`. The three missing rows are `R-CD-RETURN-COVENANT-AUTHORITY`, `R-CD-RETURN-OVERLAP` and `R-OBS-2`. This is not acceptance-complete. The two return rows and `R-OBS-2` are missing for different reasons, and all three are producer gaps rather than absent behavior: - `R-CD-RETURN-COVENANT-AUTHORITY` records zero of its 24 observations (12 authority cases against both the typed-tool and bracket-token surfaces). Its pending receipt requires allowed delivery to show exact effects, revoked and reassigned recipients to show zero prompt, wake and channel effect, schema v18/v19, restart replay, a signed authority, and full cleanup. The row's own `manifest` and harness `supporting_docs` pointers are currently **dangling on the docs default branch**: the harness exists but was never merged there. - `R-CD-RETURN-OVERLAP` and `R-OBS-2` each have a present manifest and failed only because the current-corpus input they read (overlap evidence file, exported trace tree) is absent. **Limits:** Historical live and Mode-B evidence for earlier heads is ancestry/materiality evidence, not exact-target execution. Run `35364768803` above *is* exact-target for `3821eaef72`. All seven non-pass rows remain gated on producer execution against this frozen head; no acceptance receipt from an older deployment composite is reused as final evidence. ## Proof links and ClawSweeper🦞 guidance Proof artifacts live in `karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs` on `main`. `PROOFS/INDEX.json` points at the corpus for the SHA this PR presents, `139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393`. Reviewed docs checkpoint: `c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c`. - [Corpus directory](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393) - [README — identity, what is proven, honest limits](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/README.md) - [RESOLVED-SHA.md — SHA identity and gate verdicts](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/RESOLVED-SHA.md) - [METHOD.md — reproducer commands](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/METHOD.md) - [TRANSPOSED-FROM.md — why nothing was transposed](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/TRANSPOSED-FROM.md) - [Manifest](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/proofs-manifest.json) - [INDEX.json](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/INDEX.json) - [Prior published board (not superseded)](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/7cb9d71f622250bedbf565e327bd7d7b9d90b567) ### What this corpus claims, and what it does not **Status: `STATIC_GATES_ONLY_NO_LIVE_ROWS_AT_THIS_SHA`.** Rollup `38 total / 0 pass / 0 partial / 0 fail / 38 not_fired_at_this_sha`. Proven at `139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393`, receipts being the real stdout of the real runs committed under `gates/` and `mergeability/`: | gate | verdict | |---|---| | `pnpm tsgo:core` | **pass** rc=0 | | `pnpm lint` — oxlint core, extensions, scripts | **pass** rc=0 | | Gate 2.7 vs the absorbed base `715077a3be` | **pass** — 839 files, 466 GENUINE, 373 SAFE-NEW, **0 FROZEN-STALE**, **0 MIXED-CLOBBER** | | `vitest` rollback-custody regressions | **pass** 10/10 | | `vitest` delivery-queue + session-delivery | **pass** 124/124 | | `vitest` gateway maintenance + close + delegate-artifacts | **pass** 123/123 | | `vitest` production-boundary + spawn-cleanup | 28/30 — two tracked reds | **Diff size has not grown across four absorbs.** From the absorbed base — which is what this PR shows — the change is 839 files, +140,919 / −4,301, against 841 / +140,951 / −4,277 before this cycle. (`git diff upstream/main HEAD` reports 2,358 files, but that is the symmetric difference including upstream commits newer than the merge base, and is not what a PR shows.) The worktree was clean at publication: zero untracked files, no stray additions. **Two known reds, neither hidden nor softened.** `karmaterminal/openclaw#1356` is an order-dependent failure of the `operator-revoked` queued-collector cleanup: it **passes in isolation** with all four `cleanupComplete` operands true and the child session genuinely deleted, and fails only when the `operator-completed` arm has run first. Upstream's own test and test-support files for it are byte-identical to ours, so the divergence is product-side. `karmaterminal/openclaw#1350` is the streamed-text offset/fencing contract, pre-existing. **No live behavioral row was fired at this SHA, and none is presented as though it were.** The fleet that runs these behaviors serves composite `1baff536afa549fea75660403c453bbd265352c0`, a *divergent sibling* of the presented SHA rather than an ancestor of it — their merge-base is `3821eaef72677c78f450ae9956cb582a22ba4cba` and neither is an ancestor of the other. A live fire on that runtime would be evidence about the composite, so every row is marked `not_fired_at_this_sha` instead of being carried over as a pass. The prior corpus at `3821eaef72` remains linked per row as the baseline to re-fire against. Live rows are unblocked by a redeploy onto a runtime that has this SHA as a git ancestor. That redeploy is itself a migration boundary: this head carries the agent schema bump **21 → 22** via `migrateTranscriptFtsRowSchema`, and the fleet serves 21, so it wants migration-success and rollback-compatibility receipts of its own. Both are maintainer-side, not gated on this PR. ### PROOFS METHOD The corpus uses a Grafana k6 proof harness for live rows; [`METHOD.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/METHOD.md) carries the exact reproducer commands for every static gate above, including both Gate 2.7 invocations and the `git merge-tree --write-tree` mergeability check. `MAX_WORKERS=1` is mandatory for the vitest reproducers — OpenClaw's fixtures are not safe under concurrent access — and two of those commands deliberately take no `--config`, because passing the wrong one silently reports "No test files found" and exits 0. `TRANSPOSED-FROM.md` records source-to-target ancestry and materiality; for this cycle it records a deliberate refusal to transpose across 520 commits and four absorbs. ## Future actions and #130741 composition Maintainer PR #130741 addresses the complementary fresh-sweep race: it captures the current `sessionId` and `lifecycleRevision` before the first await and uses those values as cleanup CAS facts. The return covenant addresses a different time axis: whether historically accepted child work may return to a logical recipient after benign successor creation. The current candidate and #130741 head `e1afc703f49a07687c0876ba6350cafa87a3638a` merge cleanly in a synthetic composition. If #130741 lands, the composed result should preserve both guarantees: - keep #130741's fresh sweep-time exact-run/session lifecycle fence; - keep the covenant's durable logical-recipient generation for historical return admission and delivery; - do not overload broad `lifecycleRevision` as historical return authority; - do not terminate or orphan accepted descendants merely because `/new` or ordinary `/reset` creates a successor session. That composition honors the maintainer repair without weakening continuation semantics or allowing a stale child return to cross a real ownership boundary. ## Why this is not a skill or a viable plugin extraction OpenClaw skills are `SKILL.md` prompt files loaded into an agent turn that already exists. They can guide work inside that turn; they do not own the turn cycle. Continuation needs gateway and agent-runtime owners a skill cannot provide: - The `continue_work` path persists pending work, enforces budgets and delay bounds, arms a timer, reacquires the session reply-run lane, and starts a later model turn after the current turn has finalized. - The `continue_delegate` path persists delegate intent, does spawn/admission accounting, manages child-session lifecycle, and durably routes returns across sessions. - `request_compaction` is an agent election into guarded runtime compaction. Later work resumes only after the runtime has established the new context boundary. - All three need durable state, cancellation/finalization ownership, restart recovery, trace identity, queue-conflict handling, and gateway scheduling outside the model invocation. A skill can tell a model to *ask* for another turn. Without those owners the ask is prose: it cannot persist a due wake, yield and finalize safely, reacquire the session lane, create the next invocation, survive a restart, or deliver a child result to another session. The implementation therefore belongs in core runtime surfaces such as `src/auto-reply/continuation/**`, `src/agents/tools/**`, `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-continuation-schedule.ts`, and `src/infra/continuation-tracer.ts`. This PR adds no `.agents/skills/**`, `SKILL.md`, or user-facing skill package. The only skill-named production change is core runtime tool dispatch. ClawHub also distributes plugins. Existing plugins can register tools, services, lifecycle hooks, context injection, plugin-owned session state, and — for bundled plugins — Cron-backed session turns. Those seams can support a smaller continuation-like automation, especially TaskFlow plus host Cron / `sessions_spawn`. They are not this feature's turn-finalization ownership, reply-run coordination, durable continuation queue, child-session return lifecycle, election capture, or agent-elected compaction contract. Compaction-provider registration and command-handler `compactCurrent()` are also not that last contract: they compact or summarize, they do not elect compaction at finalization and resume afterward. Moving policy behind a plugin boundary would first require OpenClaw to expose and stabilize a continuation-host API. The gateway/runtime would still own the mechanism described here; a plugin could only package policy around that core capability. That is not a no-core-touch alternative to these primitives. Discord is a bundled channel plugin. It owns the Discord edge, plus delivery/progress hooks into the host's existing subagent path, and submits events into OpenClaw's current turn machinery. Continuation changes that machinery: what survives finalization, which session may run next, how child results return, and when compaction can be elected. A TaskFlow tool adapter is also not a lifecycle host. It can call the core-owned `api.runtime.tasks.managedFlows` API to create, link, pause, resume, finish, cancel, and inspect durable flow records. Marking a waiting record as running does not reacquire a session lane or invoke the model; recording a `childSessionKey` created by a separate spawn surface does not spawn the child or deliver its return. There is no equivalent host continuation capability for this PR to wrap. ## Lineage and replacement context This PR is the clean replacement for closed #85651. It preserves that PR's review lineage and the earlier continuation work descended from #79925, but it does not reuse either closed PR or ask reviewers to infer the current result from them. The replacement carries a current, independently reviewable branch and a complete proof subtree bound to its presented SHA. #85651 was not abandoned because the feature failed or because we accepted its classification as a skill. It was closed after automated labeling put the change in the wrong submission category. This replacement removes that ambiguity: no `src/skills/**` change is presented, current label simulation produces no `r: skill`, and the detailed section above explains why the lifecycle mechanism belongs to core. Acceptance or rejection of the product direction remains OpenClaw's decision. The decision requested is whether OpenClaw should provide multi-session, agent-elected continuation primitives after reviewing the implementation and evidence. It is not whether the same mechanism can be relocated into a skill: a skill cannot own or implement these lifecycle boundaries.
