prs.title: fix(gateway): refuse sends before agent database admission
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes operator sends reaching external delivery before their agent passes database admission when the request supplies `agentId` without `sessionKey`.

## User Impact

Pending agents return a retryable startup refusal before delivery. Failed inspection returns the recorded reason and repair guidance, including after startup has no pending agents. Admitted agents remain usable while another agent prepares.

## Why This Change Was Made

Agent-only sends bypass the handler's session-based admission resolver. Request authorization now uses the existing resolver before dispatch. Explicit agent selection and implicit-main selection follow the existing handler semantics. Delivery, inflight joining, and route binding are unchanged.

Related: #174958.

## Evidence

The original real Gateway router and send-handler reproduction reached the captured external delivery adapter once for both pending and failed inspection. With the fix, refusal precedes delivery; clearing admission and replaying the same idempotency key delivered and bound the route once. The committed owner-boundary regressions independently failed with only the production fix reverted: each invoked the downstream handler once despite refusal (2 failed, 1 skipped; 604.98 seconds wall, including worker compilation and verification).

Final Node runs passed individually: request authorization, 3 tests in 321.04 seconds wall; unchanged send suite, 82 tests in 195.47 seconds wall. Core types, scoped lint, formatting, line-cap checks and Madge passed (zero import cycles). Isolated branch autoreview was scoped-clean through P2. The initial exact-head CI run and its attribution are recorded below.

An earlier expanded send fixture timed out in the existing Telegram live-owner case. That fixture was removed and the send suite restored exactly to the integrated base; the Telegram case passed in the final run. The timeout cause is not established, and no timeout or assertion was weakened.

PR #174958 remains open. Its startup-deadline suite is absent from integrated main, so that dependent suite could not run. No live provider was used; live proof remains with the campaign coordinator. Production: +18/-0 lines; tests: +122/-0; docs: +5/-0. The bounded production growth reuses the admission owner without introducing state, a helper module, or duplicate policy.

## CI attribution and baseline integration

Initial exact-head CI run [39181203090](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39181203090), attempt 1, tested `6fce6fd9a5b974066267511b7f3d27230af44371` and had two failed jobs:

- `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets`: the mock-export ratchet rejected `src/cli/program/root-help.test.ts:33` for `./subcli-descriptors.js`. The same failure reproduced on main `0319200bb1b72`. Main commit e63269c28a22a6eec7c0758d54dc6dbe674e2886 fixes it by preserving the real exports with `importOriginal`; this named failing gate is the reason for integrating main.
- `checks-node-changed-compact-small-3`: `sessions.recover retains source revocation for its accepted own successor` failed during cleanup in `closeOpenClawStateDatabaseForTest` with `OpenClaw state database still has active native borrowers` on the Bun shard. This PR's only production addition is gated on `params.method === "send"` without `sessionKey` in `request-authorization.ts`; `sessions.recover` cannot enter it. The selected test passed once on main, which does not establish either a fix or matching-main failure. The borrower-release race is under separate investigation; a recurrence on the integrated head will stop landing rather than trigger a rerun or another push.

The prior exact-head ClawSweeper review reported no findings and no security findings, requesting only this CI attribution. Its live-channel proof limitation remains as stated above.

Merged main `28212a985c15ae53b22b77dabecbfdfc1ee9d632` into the branch with merge commit `749a692d5db4df76a529073d81cd4f7c9b94213e`. The integrated diff remains the same three files and 145 added lines; the admission, selector, authorization, and send-handler context is unchanged. The root-help mock-export fix is included. The integrated-head CI result is recorded below. ClawSweeper revision 2 completed on this exact head at 2026-10-19 01:45 UTC with no findings, no security findings, and no before-merge action items; its previously stated live-channel proof limitation remains.

Integrated-head CI [39186380104](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39186380104), attempt 1, reproduced the same Bun cleanup failure in [job 117850064087](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39186380104/job/117850064087), `checks-node-changed-compact-small-13`: `sessions.recover retains source revocation for its accepted own successor` → `OpenClaw state database still has active native borrowers`. The stack runs through `assertStateDatabaseBorrowersReleased` (`openclaw-state-db-borrow.ts:153`) and `closeOpenClawStateDatabaseForTest` (`openclaw-state-db-cache.ts:584`). The run completed with this sole non-aggregate failed job and the resulting `openclaw/ci-gate` failure. The baseline-ratchet and `security-fast` jobs passed. Landing stopped on the recurrence; no CI rerun, further push, preparation, or merge was attempted. The separate borrower-release investigation must be resolved before another landing attempt.

prs.title: perf(diagnostics): reuse empty private payloads for OTel
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

With the OpenTelemetry exporter subscribed, diagnostic dispatch clones and freezes an empty private payload even when the event carries no private content or host-plugin attribution.

## User Impact

Less allocation and main-thread CPU in diagnostic dispatch, with unchanged event contents, filtering, private-content isolation, and exporter attribution. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the dispatcher's existing frozen empty private payload unless there is private content or OTel host-plugin attribution to deliver. Real private payloads retain their independent copies, including opaque mutable values; attributed events retain the existing private host transport and spoof sanitization. Public plain event snapshots already share one frozen copy, and no-interest events already skip dispatch.

This removes one empty `structuredClone`, traversal, and freeze per eligible OTel delivery. Production diff: +5/-5 lines. Resolve applicable host attribution once and skip deleting the field immediately before assigning its authoritative value; no new helper, cache, owner, or compatibility path. Test diff: +16 lines.

## Evidence

- Regression fails on the original implementation because OTel receives a different empty object; passes after the fix. Focused dispatcher and listener-interest tests: 38 passed (8.88s Vitest, 15.60s wrapper). Final dispatcher file: all 32 tests passed (7.12s Vitest, 14.42s wrapper).
- Exact-source Linux dispatcher comparison: four concurrent A/B pairs under an exclusive measurement lock; 16 CPUs per arm, CPU halves swapped on alternating pairs, outside load recorded. Each arm delivered 480,000 events in the timed run and another 480,000 in an allocation-sampled run, using identical four-event fixtures and one marked OTel subscriber. No event loss.
- Mean CPU/event: **2.689 → 2.009 µs (-25.3%)**. Paired B−A differences: -0.683, -0.670, -0.699, -0.666 µs/event.
- Sampled allocated bytes/event: **3,466 → 2,562 (-26.1%)**. Paired B−A differences: -904, -906, -911, -899 bytes/event. V8 sampling includes collected objects; CPU was measured separately without the heap profiler.
- Changed-file format, core lint, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent Codex autoreview: scoped-clean through P2; full dispatcher/snapshot context supplied.
- These dispatcher measurements isolate this delivery path, not whole-Gateway CPU or production event throughput. Broad validation belongs to PR CI. No Testbox/Crabbox was allocated.


### Supplementary 48-turn Gateway comparison

Two concurrent pairs, CPU halves swapped in pair 2. Each arm completed 48 measured turns (8 concurrent × 6 rounds), with 16 subscribers and actual bundled OTel exporting to a synthetic loopback sink. Zero dropped diagnostics; 0–2 ms paired round-start skew. Each arm dispatched exactly 20,713 diagnostic events across the two pairs: 473.2/469.9 events/s in pair 1 and 386.8/382.4 in pair 2 (A/B).

| Metric | Pair 1 A → B | Pair 2 A → B |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sampled allocation/turn | 93.319 → 92.973 MB (−0.37%) | 93.690 → 95.248 MB (+1.66%) |
| Main-thread CPU/turn | 260.475 → 256.688 ms (−1.45%) | 327.223 → 340.613 ms (+4.09%) |
| Samples under direct private `structuredClone → dispatchDiagnosticEvent` | 1,706,616 → 0 bytes | 1,969,064 → 0 bytes |

**No whole-Gateway speedup is demonstrated:** small paired differences change sign. The targeted clone allocation disappears in both pairs. Total Gateway allocation/dispatch across both pairs is 433,373/436,181 bytes and CPU/dispatch is 1,361.9/1,384.2 µs (A/B); these include all Gateway work and are not isolated dispatcher costs.

Limitations: both Gateway arms use existing built runtime `39ca16f1f9e504924ec4302f2827160e3c155e32`; B applies the empty-payload guard in memory through a verified module-load hook, while A passes through. That runtime predates shared public event snapshots. Fixtures have 64 synthetic sessions and ~5.6 MB of databases, not production-sized state. This supplementary experiment avoids large sandbox writes; the dispatcher microbenchmark uses current source. Live production event rate was not instrumented. All owned Gateway processes and ports were closed, and their sandbox removed.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes intermittent Bun gateway-check failures when the bootstrap artifact test reads a tarball after starting its disposal.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39163574553/job/117782017483

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. Node installation and update behavior remains unchanged: provider close owns archive retirement under the existing plugin-reload policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

#168747 deliberately removed completed-artifact borrower retention and accepted that a plugin reload may retire the old bootstrap archive. This test retained the earlier expectation that a preparation signal keeps the archive alive after close starts.

Check the existing readability assertion before close, then await close while that preparation signal remains unaborted and require ENOENT afterward. Every archive hash, sharing, canceled-peer, and off-caller-thread assertion remains. No production code, retries, timers, timeouts, skips, suppressions, or shared helpers change. The diff is two added lines and three removed lines.

Related #176204 concerns preparation overtaken by close; its diff does not change this already-returned artifact assertion or restore borrower retention.

## Evidence

- Forced the original close-before-access ordering with production unchanged: exact ENOENT reproduced in 967 ms. The ordinary isolated case and original shard replay passing alone were not treated as proof of a fix.
- After restoring the frozen install, all four artifact/worker/prebuilt/bundle owner files pass under pinned Bun with `--maxWorkers=1`: **69 tests**, **175.27 s wrapper wall**, **127.05 s Vitest**; affected worker case **508 ms**.
- The original shard's separate gateway-client portion passes **15 files / 135 tests** under Bun, one worker: **112.60 s wrapper wall**.
- Gateway-other test typecheck, typed and boundary oxlint, formatting, diff check, and independent P2 review pass.

The initial 71-file gateway-core replay passed the affected case but encountered an unrelated workspace-upload worker heap OOM (726 passed, one failed, one existing skip). That run preceded correction of local install drift: the worktree linked proc-safe 0.3.0 while main already pinned 0.4.1. Frozen installation corrected the link without tracked dependency changes; final focused proof and types use the declared dependencies. prs.title: fix(slack): keep progress updating after native streams expire
prs.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users watching a Slack native progress card see frozen or failed-looking progress after Slack expires the stream, even though the agent continues working. Later text can fail or arrive in a separate reply.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep a bounded projection of the streamed message and use `chat.update` on the same timestamp after an explicit `message_not_in_streaming_state` rejection. Subsequent progress, final text, and final metadata use that same message, following [Slack SDK recovery guidance](https://github.com/slackapi/node-slack-sdk/pull/2611).

The existing scoped writer and user Stop handling remain in control. Ambiguous writes are not replayed. If the full message cannot be reconstructed within the limits, or an update definitively rejects pending text, only the undelivered tail uses normal chunked delivery. This includes `edit_window_closed` and `cant_update_message`, so workspace editing restrictions do not discard an otherwise deliverable final reply. Once ordinary delivery succeeds, its retained recovery projection is retired, so native cleanup cannot replay that delivered tail onto the original card.

A stream started with a custom agent name or avatar retains the established identity-aware route: because `chat.update` cannot preserve custom authorship, explicit expiry retires that stream and sends only its unacknowledged tail through ordinary delivery with the same custom identity. The acknowledged prefix is not replayed.

## User Impact

Progress and eligible final replies continue on the existing card after stream expiry. Task state, source links, narration order, and accumulated detail/output text are retained. Recovered task details and outputs use plain rich text, so embedded Markdown syntax is not interpreted. Customized agent authorship is preserved by using ordinary tail delivery instead of editing the customized message.

## Evidence

- Before the fix, a real-SDK regression failed on the first expired append with `SlackStreamNotDeliveredError`.
- On final head `e09af9ae6480498f819843e034ac86da2fde372f`, **155/155** focused tests passed across streaming, real-SDK delivery traces, and preview fallback. These include same-message recovery, edit-restriction fallback, cleanup non-replay, and the custom-identity expiry regression proving no `chat.update`, no acknowledged-prefix replay, and identity-aware ordinary delivery of only the pending tail.
- Extension production and test typechecks passed. Type-aware lint on the five touched Slack files reported 0 warnings/errors; formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh AutoReview completed at P0-P2. Its sole P1 concern claimed the initial stream payload was absent from the projection; source and passing recovery assertions show `startSlackStream` installs the projection before invoking `appendSlackStream`, which records the initial text/chunks. No code change was made for that false positive.
- Slack `blocks.validate` previously accepted synthetic plan and timeline projections, including rich-text details/output and source elements.

### Real Slack recovery proof

Executed the actual compiled `streaming.ts`, `streaming-projection.ts`, and their client modules from measured revision `2fec06eb352ffb4fc89178b5130aa594c7c1a4d0` with the real Slack SDK **8.0.0** and installed public OpenClaw SDK modules. API responses were not mocked. A separate `chat.stopStream` call closed only each synthetic test stream on Slack, leaving the SDK stream object active, so the next real append exercised `message_not_in_streaming_state`.

```text
Baseline owner (4d7a33874):
  chat.startStream -> ok
  chat.stopStream  -> ok (test-induced server closure)
  chat.appendStream -> message_not_in_streaming_state
  readback: rejected tail absent; no recovery update

Candidate owner (2fec06eb):
  chat.startStream -> ok
  chat.stopStream  -> ok (test-induced server closure)
  chat.appendStream -> message_not_in_streaming_state
  chat.update -> ok; readback: same message, task in_progress, working text present
  chat.update -> ok; final answer and complete task appended
  chat.update -> ok; final metadata acknowledged

Independent native-CLI readback:
  expected bot identity: true
  same message: true
  all tasks complete: true
  acknowledged prefix occurrences: 1
  final answer occurrences: 1
  final metadata preserved: true
```

Task details, output, and source links also survived the recovery. The executed bundle hashes matched after the run. The custom-identity repair does not change the measured default-identity `chat.update` path; it keeps customized messages on the ordinary identity-aware route. Only synthetic content was used; identifiers and private environment details are omitted here.

This proves the real server-closed-stream recovery contract and Slack message readback. It does not measure Slack's undocumented natural expiry duration or claim screenshot-based rendering verification. The installed production plugin and Gateway were not replaced or restarted.

## Current-main refresh (2026-10-18)

Current head: `e09af9ae6480498f819843e034ac86da2fde372f`. Non-destructively merged main `7aab596ad005c15824143c482e9d6da732c6f102`; the prior PR head remains an ancestor. No force push.

The merge preserves current main's serialized-HTTP progress fixture and its refactored delivery-trace harness while retaining the PR's expiry/fallback/Stop traces. The reviewed custom-identity defect is repaired at the stream owner and covered at both the production stream boundary and ordinary dispatch boundary.

Live Slack was not rerun for the custom-identity branch because the supported API contract is deterministic: stream start accepts identity overrides while `chat.update` does not. The earlier live recovery measurement remains historical evidence for the unchanged default-identity recovery path. Full-suite and full-build proof were not run locally; canonical PR CI owns broad validation. Production plugin, Gateway, Slack channel, and auth configuration were not changed.


## Review follow-up (2026-10-19)

Current head: `781f315d1448f1de4cd1a8342166372927e105ac`. Removed the unused stopped-stream assertion, duplicate recording client, and their exclusive imports/type while retaining the three called recovery assertions.

Verification on Node 26.10.0: `delivery-trace.test.ts` 32/32 passed; extension test typecheck passed; touched-file type-aware lint reported 0 warnings/errors; formatting and `git diff --check` passed. Independent P0-P3 AutoReview produced one rejected P3 claim that `stripToken` was dead; the retained ordinary-fallback cleanup assertion still calls it when recording the failed native cleanup payload. No production behavior or prior live-proof boundary changed.

prs.title: fix(codex): recovered dashboard turns fail before reaching the model
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after a Gateway restart, an interrupted Control UI session running on the Codex harness is "resumed" by restart recovery but its turn fails within seconds with `Session capability metadata requires worker preparation`, and the session stays stranded.

## User Impact

User impact: restart recovery now actually resumes interrupted Control UI (dashboard) sessions on the Codex harness instead of starting a turn that dies before reaching the model. Ordinary Codex turns on dashboard and subagent sessions no longer depend on the Gateway's session projection being warm. No config, schema, stored-data, or update change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Codex resolves hosted `web_search` permission on every turn. It called the synchronous `resolveWebSearchToolPolicy`, which, for dashboard and subagent session keys, reads the session's stored delegation envelope. That read only succeeds inside a prepared capability read or when the Gateway session projection can serve the row. Normal turns usually found the projection warm. A turn resumed during startup, on a row recovery had just rewritten, did not, so the read threw. The prepared-read requirement arrived in #169622, and this caller (from #93446) was missed.

The policy owner now offers `resolveWebSearchToolPolicyAsync`, which prepares those stored facts before resolving, and Codex awaits it. No fallback reader is added; the synchronous SDK export is unchanged. Restart recovery itself was already correct (it started the run); the defect was entirely inside the harness turn.

Every other core caller of this policy was checked and is already covered: a prepared wrapper, a pre-resolved requester policy, or no session key.

SDK surface: one additive export on `openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-harness`, so the export and callable budgets in `scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mts` go up by 1 each. The bump was flagged to Peter before landing and accepted with the land instruction.

<details>
<summary>Incident trace</summary>

Seen on a production Gateway on 2026-10-18 after `openclaw gateway restart --force`. Main-session restart recovery logged `decision=started`, `nextOwner=background-lane` for an `agent:main:dashboard:<uuid>` session. About 2.6 s later `agents/harness` logged `Codex agent harness failed; not falling back to embedded OpenClaw backend` with the error above, and the lane task errored. The failing stack is `buildDynamicTools` → `resolveWebSearchToolPolicy` → `resolveRequesterToolPolicies` → `resolveDelegatedPolicy` (the senderless own-envelope read) → `createSubagentSessionStore().get` → `readDurable`. Startup at that moment showed agent-database queue waits around 9 s.

</details>

Release note: Codex sessions resumed by restart recovery no longer fail with "Session capability metadata requires worker preparation".

## Evidence

- **Regression, red then green:** `run-attempt.dynamic-tools.test.ts` › "prepares hosted search policy for a recovered dashboard turn". It runs a full Codex attempt with a fake app-server, using a recovered dashboard turn: restart-recovery provenance, hosted search enabled, no projection. On the base it fails with the production error and stack. With the fix the turn is accepted and completes. That also shows this was the only unprepared capability read on the recovered Codex attempt path.
- **Focused suites, all passing:**
  - `run-attempt.dynamic-tools.test.ts`: 11 tests, about 69 s for the file on a loaded host; the new case takes about 6 s.
  - `dynamic-tool-build.test.ts`: 74 tests.
  - `dynamic-tool-build.web-search.test.ts` and `dynamic-tool-build.sandbox.test.ts`: 21 tests.
- **Gates, all passing:**
  - `tsgo:core`
  - format check on the touched files
  - `plugin-sdk:check-exports`
  - `plugin-sdk:surface:check`
  - `check:import-cycles`
- **Review:** Codex autoreview at P0–P2 came back scoped-clean.
- **Not run locally:**
  - oxlint: the worktree install lacks `eslint-plugin-solid`.
  - `tsgo:extensions`: one unrelated `qa-lab` module-resolution error from the partial install; no errors in the touched files.
  - Live end-to-end restart: not run. Whether the projection serves the row is timing-dependent, so an isolated quiet Gateway would not reliably reproduce the failure on the base. The deterministic full-attempt regression covers that path instead.

prs.title: fix(subagents): delivered children stay pending while siblings run
prs.body:
Closes #166267

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an already-delivered child keeps appearing as pending and retains its requester wake when an unrelated sibling remains running.

## User Impact

Busy requesters can retire redundant single-child wakes without waiting for all their workers to stop. Grouped and yielded continuations, failed deliveries, and suspended deliveries keep their existing ownership. No configuration, schema, retention-policy, or operator data edits are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing decision that a wave owes no continuation ran after descendant waiting. Move that decision before the wait and continue using the lifecycle owner’s generation-aware completion operation. This removes the redundant wait rather than hiding results in the renderer or expiring legitimate obligations. Restored markers use the same decision through normal recovery.

The simplification reuses the existing predicates and persistence owner: production changes are +5/-4 lines, with no new state, timers, or policy helpers. Regression coverage adds 62 lines and the lifecycle guide adds four.

Thanks to @assimetria-ai for the report and @Oldrich333 for clarifying why delivered grouped results can still owe a continuation.

Contributor: @Marvinthebored.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/79630ff9-afb5-4b4a-b825-de346e00b533)

## Evidence

- The new delivered-singleton regression failed on the unchanged production source; the other eight cases passed. With the repair, all 76 focused tests passed across requester settlement, private batches, runtime-context projection, and lifecycle wake retry/persistence coverage. The five-file run took 89.94 seconds including shared preparation; CI timing is pending.
- An isolated real Gateway with a scripted OpenAI-compatible model used actual parent tool calls to spawn a long-running child and a short private-completion child. After the parent turn ended and the short child delivered, SQLite contained its retained result but no requester wake; the long child was still running. The next parent model request omitted the short child’s pending-result row. This probe passed in 13.52 seconds of test execution, 109.02 seconds total including preparation. No registry rows were seeded or edited for this flow.
- The first disposable Gateway attempt timed out during cold startup. The subsequent run passed after runtime/declaration artifacts were prepared, without extending the timeout. No live external provider or cold-process Gateway restart is claimed.
- Targeted repository lint: zero warnings/errors; core typecheck, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent Auto Review (GPT-6.1 Sol, P0–P2): scoped clean, no actionable findings; static review, not test execution.

The committed regression table explicitly preserves grouped private, yielded, failed, and suspended wake obligations behind a running sibling. This is not a blanket cleanup of every delivered row, and it does not replace the renderer-only proposal in #166270.

### CI follow-up — not ready to merge

The first ready-head CI run [39182121588](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39182121588) failed. The liveness fixture declared no completion obligation while asserting that a continuation must wait; the local repair now uses required/pending completion and retains all liveness assertions. A 20-test focused rerun passed. The unrelated root-help mock-export failure has an upstream repair; main was integrated through the managed workspace at `afa7fccb9a2f4483d404a6b64814afe5d001ca21` for that gate. All 87 tests across six focused files, the prepared-base mock-export ratchet, targeted lint, core typecheck, and a fresh independent P0–P2 review passed on the local integrated candidate.

A third failed shard also reports requester-receipt timeouts and callback-identity assertions; their complete attribution and repair remain unfinished. The local E2E reproduction has not reached a test verdict because runtime build preparation was interrupted. A managed workspace synchronization conflict now blocks further source changes and publication; pending changes were preserved. These follow-up repairs are **not yet on this PR head**. The original Gateway probe above is prior-head evidence, not proof of the integrated candidate or of the unresolved receipt cases. No CI waiver or merge is claimed.

## Worked on by

- @Marvinthebored

prs.title: improve: speed up database-first legacy-store checks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The database-first legacy-store guard adds several minutes to normal local checks by repeatedly traversing the same syntax and rebuilding scope facts for files that cannot write legacy state.

## User Impact

Local checks run substantially faster with identical findings and every live policy retained. There is no runtime behavior change. In a back-to-back full-corpus comparison, wall time fell 61% (2.56× faster); peak RSS increased by 30 MiB because the guard retains per-file syntax facts.

## Why This Change Was Made

Collect immutable call, literal, import, and marker facts in one syntax pass. Reuse those facts during the existing ordered dataflow walk, and skip that walk when a file has neither a possible filesystem source nor a transcript marker. Keep scope-dependent resolution and wrapper replay ordered.

Replace the sole semantic binding query, in the restart preflight exception, with an explicit default-import and lexical-shadowing proof. The native syntax parser and existing 32-file batching remain unchanged; no rule requires a semantic checker query after this change. No dependencies, policy exemptions, or dated migration contracts change.

The simplify pass removed duplicate boundary/import traversal and repeated expression subtree walks. Net source growth is 164 implementation lines and 106 test lines, chiefly the lexical proof and its binding regression cases.

## Evidence

Full main at task-start commit `96e6d2d00cb442a8c1d8a884dffd3f4037845cfc` versus this branch, scanning the same 20,642-source corpus plus native files on the same loaded host:

| Unprofiled full run | Wall time | Peak RSS | 1-minute load, start → end |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Main | 492.45 s | 317.03 MiB | 91.79 → 100.68 |
| This branch | 192.11 s | 347.05 MiB | 100.68 → 85.49 |

Runs were sequential, using `/usr/bin/time -l node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-database-first-legacy-stores.mts`. The frozen baseline used the original script with only its repository-root lookup redirected to the same worktree. Both exited 0 with byte-identical full findings output. This is one pair under shared-host load, not an isolated benchmark.

The preceding `node --cpu-prof --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs ...` pair also had identical findings: 739.46 s → 198.83 s. Inclusive sampled time fell from 436.95 s to 52.32 s in the collector, 242.00 s to 22.71 s in wrapper execution, and 90.21 s to 4.72 s in literal-candidate evaluation. Profiling materially inflates RSS, so the table uses unprofiled runs.

Validation completed:

- 99/99 focused tests passed, including 30 lexical-binding cases; default pinned Vitest runtime.
- Seeded red/green probes on both revisions matched for all seven diagnostic kinds: filesystem writes, transcript markers, restart references/imports, approval references/imports, and native PortGuardian references.
- Targeted tsrs typecheck, typed oxlint, formatting, script erasability, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent Codex review through P2, with the full unchanged dataflow context supplied, found no actionable defects.

PR CI supplies broad validation. No merge is requested by this change.

prs.title: refactor(postgres): remove redundant result and search checks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The PostgreSQL bridge and search expression builder repeat work after their owners have already established the necessary result or index facts.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible behavior change. This removes three redundant checks or branches while preserving PostgreSQL admission, transaction, recovery, and error behavior. There are no schema, configuration, dependency, or durability changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Unreachable result guard: 1.** A successful `pg` query always returns a `Result`, or a nonempty array of results. `pg/lib/query.js` initializes the result before execution and only creates an array when appending another result. Keep the last batch result without a second missing-result check.
- **No-op transaction branch: 1.** The outer COMMIT/ROLLBACK condition only did work for COMMIT. Use the equivalent exact-COMMIT condition and retain the rolled-back-instead-of-committed error.
- **Duplicate admitted-index evaluation: 1.** Trigram `contains` built an unused tsvector reference before validating the same index again for its declared text field. Select the field once and retain the existing open-store and index-identity check.

The final diff is **+6 / -11 lines, net -5**, across three PG-only files. No file in PR #174599's supplied exclusion list is changed. No SQL query was removed: the inspected catalog, capability, and metadata queries belong to admission, explicit inspection, or recovery. No per-call freshness probe was found in this scope beyond the explicitly retained idle connection check.

Kept on purpose:

- Fail-closed namespace/storeId/admissionId, scoped-token, receipt, and `admission: null` checks.
- Eager BEGIN and advisory-lock envelope.
- Bridge worker idle `SELECT 1` on client reuse.
- Lost-COMMIT recovery.
- DSN and credential redaction.
- Lock and statement timeouts, user-visible statement-timeout and connection-error mapping.
- Security boundaries and runtime SQL binding/output validation.
- The byte-array copy: the current SQL output contract requires a non-shared buffer; removing it without changing that contract fails typechecking.

## Evidence

- Core typecheck passed: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` with task-local incremental build info.
- Targeted `run-oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent autoreview: scoped-clean through P2; no actionable findings.
- Targeted unit proof passed: 29 standalone protocol/query-compiler tests, plus the connection and transaction cases in local shard 1.
- Local PostgreSQL engine search conformance passed, including literal trigram `contains`, wildcard/escape handling, float32 vector scoring, and index-drift rejection. The isolated replay also passed all six memory-search worker tests and the public memory-search tool flows.
- [CI run 39162952787](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39162952787) passed on `536d51829ba4b4fbec89f4588d12da9d233442ea`, including all three PostgreSQL conformance jobs (`1/3`, `2/3`, `3/3`); none of those jobs was skipped.

All three local shard commands ran against Homebrew PostgreSQL 17 with `LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8`, internal-disk HOME/TMPDIR, and `unaccent`, `pg_trgm`, and pgvector 0.8.7. Schema/trigger parity passed. The entrypoint was `node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres --connection <throwaway-dsn> --shard N/3`.

**The broad local conformance run is not green:**

| Local shard | Passed | Failed tests | Skipped |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1/3 | 222 | 3 | 0 |
| 2/3 | 453 | 37 | 37 |
| 3/3 | 129 | 19 | 15 |

Shard 1's failures were the one-shot CLI child deadline, Matrix multi-root portability's 650-second deadline, and its following resume assertion. Shard 2 failed backup, interactive setup, port-command/recovery, Gateway bootstrap, and Doctor media-inspection cases. Shard 3 failed migration/port/update/auth cases, two extension-admission statement timeouts, and recovery assertions. It also had two setup-hook failures, blocking five Doctor diagnostics tests and six memory-search tests. These failures were not reproduced on clean main and remain local proof exceptions.

A bounded single-worker follow-up used a fresh internal-disk PostgreSQL data directory with the same locale/extensions and default durability (`fsync`, synchronous commit, and full-page writes enabled). It finished with **38 passed, 8 failed, and 28 excluded by the selection filter**:

- All **25 unstarted shard-1 extension tests passed**, covering Team Reports, memory publication, public memory tools, and memory forgetting.
- All **six previously setup-blocked memory-search tests passed**.
- Lost-COMMIT recovery passed, as did the custody/refusal checks and unresolved-credential CLI behavior.
- The canonical port round-trip, Matrix multi-root portability, and one-shot CLI child deadline failed again. Doctor diagnostics reached all five test bodies; all five timed out.

No timeout, assertion, production safeguard, or expected-failure baseline was weakened. The initial interrupted/default-Bun attempts are not counted as passing proof. Two Node 26 SQLite catalog-loading timeouts passed after switching to Node 24.22.0 with the supported filesystem module cache disabled; shards 2/3 and the follow-up used that environment. Host load was observed above 60; this is context, not proof that every failure is environmental.

The diff is **READY for coordinator review with the local proof exceptions above**. No merge or automatic merge requested; the coordinator owns the landing order.

prs.title: fix(gateway): settle recovery and row-delta test fixtures
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the row-delta socket test hanging before its assertions and recovery authorization teardown closing a database that still has native borrowers.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. CI can verify the same delivery and authorization contracts without racing fixture cleanup or waiting for frames that production intentionally coalesces.

## Why This Change Was Made

The row-delta socket fixture publishes three-message bursts but waits for thirteen individual message frames before continuing. #176410 intentionally coalesces pending same-lifecycle publications into history resets, so that wait can never finish. Pace the same messages through their real commit and socket receipts, including the first user message, while preserving the exact count, body omission, legacy/exact delivery, consumer parity, clocks and zero-root assertions.

The recovery authorization fixture also closes shared-state SQLite synchronously before its shared fixture finishes cleanup. #176426 exposed that premature close. Remove the duplicate close and let the existing fixture settle work and close its databases in order. Every authorization assertion remains.

The related shared root-observer repair is covered by active non-draft #176647. Its current diff was inspected, and the overlapping helper change was withdrawn from this patch. Production custody and media persistence remain unchanged. No retries or timeout changes. Production delta: 0 lines; test delta: +84/-64 (net +20), keeping receipt pacing at the existing socket fixture owner.

## Evidence

Current main `1f60d6a55631` reproduced the row-delta 120-second timeout. Its impossible receipt gate also stranded fixture teardown; the failed baseline was stopped after more than five further minutes, and its owned processes were verified gone. This is failure evidence, not a passing run.

The original five-file historical comparison was completed with `--maxWorkers=1` at #176426's merge and first parent, under Node 24 and pinned Bun:

| Revision | Node | Bun |
| --- | --- | --- |
| First parent `766e2adfd2dd` | 24/26 pass; two 10-second event/RPC waits | 26/26 pass |
| Merge `dbe55ccb20e7` | 23/26 pass; the same two waits plus the premature database close | 25/26 pass; premature database close |

After the fixture repair, both recovery cases passed under Node. The row-delta case still hit the same 10-second `sessions.create` setup timeout seen on both historical Node revisions, before reaching the changed message pacing. This Node gap is retained; its timeout was not changed.

Final two-file validation:

- Native Bun affected-file proof: both files passed, 3/3 cases; 142.52 seconds in Vitest, 180.27 seconds including the native wrapper.
- Gateway-server and Gateway-root test type lanes: pass.
- Targeted type-aware core lint, formatting and `git diff --check`: pass.
- Full `pnpm check:architecture`: pass.
- Independent P2 review of final two-file scope: scoped-clean, no actionable findings.

The earlier three-file candidate passed all 26 affected tests under Bun (423.23 seconds Vitest / 502.61 seconds native wrapper), including the real-socket row-delta scenario in 20.65 seconds. The final two-file run passed independently after removing the helper hunk covered by #176647.

prs.title: refactor(gateway): snapshot node catalogs once
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Node catalog construction clones statistics, capacity, bundle status and issues before the catalog owner clones and freezes the complete result again.

## Design

Borrow those leaves only during the synchronous catalog construction, then retain the one full clone/freeze at `readKnownNodeCatalog`. Build the private catalog as its final sorted array and remove the unused Map/list conversion and `listKnownNodes` export. The unique node-ID set already owns deduplication.

Transport proof copies, mutable getter results, admission copies, pairing validation and cache invalidation remain unchanged. Intermediate collector results are private borrowed data; the published catalog remains immutable and detached from registry updates.

## Evidence

Production +12/−19 lines (net −7); total diff +89/−67 across seven files. Changed-file formatting, type-aware oxlint and `git diff --check` pass. Independent Codex review is scoped-clean at P0/P1 (one completed round). Exact-head [CI 39186167516](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39186167516) passed all 51 selected checks, including changed tests and consumers, types, lint, source contracts, Madge and T1/dialect ratchets (28 skips). No behavioral failure occurred in this run.

The supplemental [Knip job 117849271718](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39186174012/job/117849271718) exactly matches [main job 117846593700](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39185301352/job/117846593700): production exports `DiscordProviderCommandSpec`, `MSTeamsAccessTokenProvider`, and the three bundle-manifest relative-path constants; full-tree exports are the same two types plus the three FaceTime helpers; the unused file is `src/process/spawn-diagnostics.test-support.ts`. Script exports and production unused files are clean. Zero new findings; none are in changed files. The supplemental remainder was canceled after the mandatory evidence was captured.

The existing node-read test now verifies frozen capacity/bundle values, rejection of caller mutation, preservation of registry authority and an old snapshot surviving a later capacity update. Existing normalization, duplicate selection and ordering coverage remains; tests asserting intermediate copy identity are removed.

No SQL, worker request, schema, PostgreSQL bookkeeping, SDK or update-lifecycle changes. Warm SQL/request/MAIN deltas are estimated 0/0/0, unmeasured under the campaign SSD-stall policy. No latency improvement is claimed.

prs.title: fix(irc): SecretRef IRC passwords fail validation and service-only NickServ overrides skip the inherited ref
prs.body:
Closes #176238

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: IRC config validation rejects a SecretRef on `password` / `nickserv.password` (even though the secret contract and docs support it), and an account whose `nickserv` block only sets other fields (e.g. `service`) never gets the inherited top-level `nickserv.password` ref resolved.

## User Impact

User impact: IRC server and NickServ passwords can be supplied as SecretRefs at the channel or account level, and service-only NickServ overrides keep identifying with the inherited password instead of an unresolved ref.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The IRC config schema and `IrcAccountConfig` types now use the shared secret-input schema/type for `password` and `nickserv.password`.
- The top-level NickServ inheritance predicate in `secret-contract.ts` now follows the same field-by-field merge that `resolveIrcAccount` uses: the top-level ref is active unless the account sets its own `nickserv.password`, and `enabled` is read from the merged block.
- Regenerated the bundled channel config metadata and config baseline.

## Evidence

- New tests: `extensions/irc/src/config-schema.test.ts` (SecretRef accepted at all four password paths) and `extensions/irc/src/secret-contract.test.ts` (service-only override resolves the inherited ref end to end through `resolveIrcAccount`; an account-owned password keeps the top-level ref inactive; inherited `enabled: false` stays inactive).
- `vitest` on `extensions/irc`: on `main` 5 of the new tests fail (2 files); with this change 21 files / 144 tests pass.
- `scripts/generate-bundled-channel-config-metadata.ts --check` passes.
- Gap: I couldn't finish a local tsgo run (my machine ran out of memory), so I'm relying on CI for the typecheck.

## Real behavior proof (branch CLI, head f457bd72b)

Run from this branch with `node scripts/run-node.mjs`, each scenario in a fresh `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`. Secret values are throwaway env vars and are redacted; IRC points at `127.0.0.1:16667` with nothing listening, and `channels status` runs without `--probe`, so it reports config-only status.

| Scenario | `config validate` | `secrets audit` | `channels status --channel irc` |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 channel `password` ref | valid | clean, unresolved=0 | default enabled, configured |
| S2 `accounts.work.password` ref | valid | clean, unresolved=0 | default + work enabled, configured |
| S3 `accounts.work.nickserv = { service }` only, top-level nickserv password ref | valid | clean, unresolved=0 (inherited ref resolved) | default + work enabled, configured, no secret warning |
| S4 top-level `nickserv.enabled=false`, account nickserv password ref to an unset env var | valid | unresolved=2 (see note) | both refs reported inactive ("NickServ is disabled for this account"), no resolve failure |
| S5 same as S4 plus `accounts.work.nickserv.enabled=true` | valid | unresolved=2 | account ref is active, so the missing env var is reported |
| main, S1 config | `channels.irc.password: must be string`, exit 1 | config invalid | config invalid |

Note on S4: `secrets audit` statically resolves every configured SecretRef regardless of whether its owner is active (`collectConfigSecrets` in `src/secrets/audit.ts` doesn't consult activity), so it flags the unset env var for every channel, not just IRC. The runtime path, shown by `channels status`, honors the inherited disablement.

Upgrade / existing data: I installed the published `openclaw@2026.10.5` into an isolated prefix and created a state dir with an existing IRC setup using plain string passwords (channel, NickServ, and one account). 2026.10.5 validates it, then this branch's CLI validates the same state dir and `channels status` lists both IRC accounts as enabled and configured. The config file's sha256 is identical before and after both runs and `diff` is empty, so existing string credentials keep loading unchanged. One caveat: the npm 2026.10.5 build reports the IRC plugin as a missing external plugin, so on that version the IRC fields are only schema-validated, not exercised.

prs.title: fix(moonshot): type anyOf branches so Kimi accepts MCP tool schemas
prs.body:
Related: #113130

## What Problem This Solves

Native Moonshot/Kimi requests can reject MCP tool schemas when `type` is declared on a parent node but its `anyOf` branches omit their own type.

## Change

- Consolidates the Kimi schema transform into the shared provider SDK.
- Uses the same implementation from native Moonshot and OpenRouter.
- Applies native normalization only to exact supported Moonshot endpoints:
  - `api.moonshot.ai`
  - `api.moonshot.cn`
- Leaves custom, proxy, missing, query-modified, and other endpoints unchanged.
- Preserves conservative behavior when a branch cannot be rewritten safely.

## Evidence

Rebuilt as one commit on current `main`.

Current exact-head checks:

- shared provider SDK: **32/32 passed**
- measured shared test cost: **12.94s wall**, **380,928 KB peak RSS** (Vitest: **5.89s**)
- targeted diff/whitespace validation: passed
- exact GitHub tree matched the tested local tree before publication

Earlier focused provider checks for the unchanged patch:

- OpenRouter schema tests: **34/34 passed**
- Moonshot tests: **30/30 passed**
- direct boundary probe:
  - official native Moonshot endpoints normalize
  - custom endpoints pass through unchanged
  - OpenRouter receives the same shared output

### Moonshot test-file measurement

A current-head attempt to run only `extensions/moonshot/index.test.ts` spent **978.67s wall** in the repository's compiled extension-provider bootstrap, peaked at **1,575,332 KB RSS** in the parent process, and was terminated by the no-output guard (exit 143) before tests executed. This 3.7 GiB VPS cannot honestly provide a current-head per-file provider result; GitHub Actions is the integration/platform authority.

## Remaining External Proof

I do not have a Moonshot credential. The final requested proof requires one redacted authenticated native Moonshot request using an MCP tool schema with parent `type` plus untyped `anyOf` branches, showing the provider accepts the request after normalization. Local routing/schema tests cannot substitute for that service response.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep palette typing responsive during model updates
prs.body:
Related: #172924.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: typing and result navigation in the command palette redo model-catalog work and rewrite the live input during unrelated updates.

## User Impact

Palette editing and navigation avoid unrelated catalog work while preserving the current input, selection, composition lifecycle, and undo. No configuration, permission, or migration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Catalog publications now carry the cache owner's scope predicate, including the cross-scope initialization transitions that cold readers still need. Scoped subscribers consume that receipt, the palette refreshes model choices through its existing reader lifecycle, and the input reuses the shared equality-checked native value binding. The conflict repair keeps the current Solid owners; main already replaced the looping Models controller adapter and covers its route-input behavior, so neither the obsolete adapter nor a duplicate regression is retained.

## Evidence

### Current conflict-resolution head

The October 19 composition is 6248c08d39b36e686e112cec0282c0748a64be60, based on canonical main e63269c28a22. The last passing CI was [run 38782232010, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38782232010), on f3cf3b1ac0b1; it is historical evidence, not current-head proof. The corrective push resolves nine actual conflicts. Current-head [CI run 39184423623, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39184423623) completed with two failed jobs plus the aggregate gate. Native landing is blocked pending their resolution; no rerun or waiver has been requested.

- `control-ui-performance`: the exact comparison reports chat boot 1,491,264 B on its main parent and 1,491,275 B on the tested merge, both above the 1,490,000 B limit. The classifier labels this new because the matching scheduled-main job passed; the comparison itself establishes the inherited threshold overage, not a passing gate. Scheduled-main run 39183785855 independently fails the same chat budget at 1,491,264 B. The existing repair is in [PR #176535](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176535); no duplicate repair was started.
- Real-Gateway shard 1/2: the managed-image ordering case fails its strict post-capture identity check. The bubble and row remain the same, while both image nodes are replaced during capture. This is distinct from the historical pre-capture failure. The assertion is retained. On exact executed source 7cfd9666, the unmodified real-Gateway case passed (54.64 s Vitest; 163.74 s including fresh build prerequisites), and one observation-only image-lifetime run passed (25.81 s Vitest; 31.30 s total). Diagnostic source was restored byte-for-byte. Only fixture capture markers were verified in that second run: renderer instrumentation had not been rebuilt, so it provides no image-lifetime attribution. A qualified diagnostic build then observed the concrete handoff: capture began at 3,139 ms, and both images changed from local paths without artifact IDs to managed artifact sources at 3,313 ms. The prepared correction waits for two managed image nodes before the unchanged decode and strict capture assertions. With a rebuilt, uninstrumented production UI, the real-Gateway case passes (9.618 s case; 18.45 s Vitest / 22.55 s invocation). Targeted type-aware lint, format/diff checks and independent P0–P2 review pass (0.96 confidence). The eight-line fixture correction is local and will be batched with the canonical boot-budget repair; it is not yet in the hosted head. The earlier passing replays remain non-repair evidence, and CI’s exact handoff timing was not recorded. Scheduled-main’s same media case also passed; its shard failed a different desktop Gateway-start timeout, so that job failure cannot justify an inherited-media exception.

- Current-main reproduction: the unchanged native Chromium regression fails at **18,944 model-name reads on ArrowDown**, and all four scoped reader cases fail. With the fix, the browser case passes in 406 ms (8.94 s invocation), with zero navigation/unrelated-publication catalog reads, zero equal-value writes, retained backward selection and undo, relevant model updates, and disposal/remount controls.
- 70 focused cache/reader/chat-metadata/provider cases passed (9.03 s); 37 migrated Agents/Cron/Models sibling cases passed (9.66 s). The duplicate standalone route test was then removed because the passing main-owned Models test already exercises that contract. No production caller or assertion was removed to make a failure pass.
- Three production-bundled palette cases passed (25.16 s invocation): background discovery preserves manual scrolling, and search/prompt transitions retain geometry and keyboard behavior at 1280 px and 390 px. This is native-browser/mock-Gateway proof, not physical mobile/IME or production latency measurement.
- Production UI types and normal UI build pass; targeted type-aware lint reports zero warnings/errors (12.3 s), and formatting/diff checks pass. Both same-host baseline and candidate builds report the existing advisory boot-byte overages: chat 1,492,375 → 1,492,401 gzip bytes; New Session 1,050,396 → 1,050,435 bytes. No budget, dependency, configuration, or baseline exception was changed.
- Simplification: keep the migrated palette/Agents/Cron/Models owners and remove superseded route-adapter/test changes. The original 18-file proposal is now 13 files; production delta is +85/−46 lines, required for scoped receipts and lifecycle-owned projection/native binding. Fresh independent review of the exact committed candidate with complete owner-file evidence is scoped-clean through P2 (confidence 0.89); it closes the earlier local-merge review’s source-context limitation. The reviewer inspected source rather than executing tests; the runtime proof above was run separately.

### Historical proof and limitations

The following records predate this conflict resolution. They explain the original defects, canonical prerequisite repairs, and unresolved incident attribution; they do not claim current-head CI or current WebKit proof.

- Mounted Chromium and WebKit regression with 512 models: ArrowDown model-name reads fall from 29,696 to zero, and another agent's catalog publication falls from 512 reads to zero. Neither navigation nor publication rewrites the unchanged textarea value; relevant catalog replacement, backward selection, undo, composition lifecycle, and shortcut disposal/remount remain covered.
- Reader/cache contracts: 19 passing tests cover own-scope updates, first unrestricted admission, restricted policy transitions, failed discovery/recovery, successful refresh invalidation, eviction, clear, and changing scoped subscription intent.
- Production UI typecheck and targeted type-aware lint pass with physically independent, frozen dependencies. Five affected route/preload/retry/search checks pass. Formatting and diff checks pass. Fresh canonical independent reviews through P2 found no actionable defects.
- The original performance fix is behavior-only. Exact merged-source CI also exposed a mobile palette label hidden by a newer main stylesheet; its canonical New Session row-scoping repair is qualified below and integrated. Mobile hardware/real IME input and a production latency benchmark were not exercised.

### Follow-up: mobile palette label scope

The executed merge hid the default AgentSelect label at 390 px because mobile New Session styling also matched the palette. Canonical main repair 93f2e424 scopes agent styling to the New Session trigger row, preserving the palette full-width labelled layout. It is integrated with canonical lazy Menu fixture repair 3b2ba1c6 and shared screenshot identity repair 36638f7a; no duplicate patch was published. Final corrected-head CI remains required.

**Before**

![Mobile palette settings before: selected agent label missing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2e0983c4-ac83-4c68-92c3-c9dcd786b24c)

**After**

![Mobile palette settings after: selected agent Main remains visible](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a35d022c-1734-4924-a6b7-ad8248c1039d)

Actual production UI, light theme, 390x900 viewport (304x205 same-frame crops). The canonical repair preserves this visual outcome. Four selected production-bundle cases pass in 29.72 seconds, including dark desktop and dark/light 390 px geometry/keyboard checks plus compact New Session siblings. Nine repaired lazy Menu fixture cases pass through the repository wrapper in 6.00 seconds. The original scoped investigation also passed stylelint, format, diff and independent P0-P2 review; temporary capture assertions were restored byte-for-byte.

Historical run 38755387064 failed UI2, E2E5 and real-Gateway1; the workflow classified all three new, with no inherited exception or rerun. The menu and palette failures have canonical repairs and passing affected proof. Canonical shared screenshot repair 36638f7a fixes a separately reproduced mixed-node observation defect: the actual exported capture entry failed when a visible same-geometry target was replaced during native intersection delivery. It retains one element identity during observation and re-prepares replacement before capture; strict post-capture visibility, geometry, identity and scroll checks remain.

The original CI pre-capture failure and the related forms PR post-capture failure remain causally unproven. Exact-merge unmodified and observation-only real-Gateway runs passed (77.73s / 67.03s), with late image-node replacement observed; those passes are not repairs or inherited-failure evidence. After the helper repair, seven deterministic boundary cases and its existing high-DPR/scroll/paused-clock sibling pass, as does the unchanged real-Gateway media scenario (53.28s). The canonical current-main composition passes all eight boundary/sibling cases using Playwright 1.64.0 and Chromium 156.0.8078.4 (23.73s), plus targeted types/lint/format and independent P0-P2 review. Original failure evidence and uncertainty are retained.

The corrected task head preserves all eighteen reviewed task blobs. Its 66 scoped unit cases pass in 8.96s; the native Chromium palette case passes in 423ms (10.66s invocation). Normal production UI types pass. Earlier WebKit success is prior-context evidence; one later WebKit attempt failed before executing tests because its browser session did not connect. Final corrected-head CI remains required; no prior-green or inherited-job waiver is selected.

<details>
<summary>Focused validation cost</summary>

Earlier integration proof: 66 scoped catalog/provider tests passed (7.43 seconds of invocation wall time), plus four Chromium/WebKit palette and main-theme cases (9.03 seconds). The production-bundled New Session input scenario passed in 1.979 seconds (24.54 seconds including its build/test invocation), retaining the exact all-methods zero-RPC, catalog-work, input, node-identity, and sidebar-update assertions. That structural E2E uses a paused browser clock and crosses the full 5,001 ms event-collection window; none of these timings are INP or per-keystroke latency measurements. Production UI types, targeted type-aware lint (16 files, 292 rules, zero warnings/errors), formatting, and full owning-boundary independent review through P2 pass.

The first two UI test invocations took 340.56 and 347.31 seconds, each with 6,882 passing tests and one new palette-fixture failure. Visible settled rows were not keyboard-navigation admission during the existing 200 ms debounce, and six typed keys were not guaranteed to share one native undo group. The fixture now waits for the active descendant and checks one native edit against its exact undo target without removing or broadening assertions.

[Historical run 38735385904](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38735385904) completed all 65 jobs in 1,463 seconds of workflow wall time, with failures; it is not current-head green proof. Its remaining roots are integrated from canonical main: Talk/video/debug repair `9e3514ae`, the landed resting-theme fixture `354f067a` (preserved exactly, with no theme-file delta in this PR), and input-fixture qualification `6b5f0f4c`. The latter keeps the changed row inside the admitted 200-row window: promoting the prior rank-500 row to rank 1 correctly required an authoritative list read. It does not relax any RPC filter or change the production roster owner. No whole-job inherited waiver, prior-green waiver, or CI rerun was used. Final pushed-head CI remains required.

Local prerequisite failures were retained and resolved through the normal owners: existing frozen Workboard dev dependencies for E2E setup, and complete SDK declaration preparation for type-aware lint. No source-root guard, expected-failure baseline, or production dependency manifest was changed by this PR.

The affected route checks took 3.71 seconds of invocation wall time. The Models controller now passes the existing 700-line rule; no suppression, baseline change, or gate override was added.

</details>

prs.title: fix: retain safe causes when provider catalog discovery fails
prs.body:
Related: #165888

## What Problem This Solves

Live provider catalog failures discard the safe cause needed to distinguish authentication, HTTP, timeout, and unexpected failures during model discovery.

## User Impact

Operators receive bounded diagnostic fields when discovery skips an unavailable catalog. Catalog outcomes, authentication handling, sibling discovery, and existing deadlines remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The inner catalog boundary and outer provider discovery deadline now share a fixed warning with validated provider identifier, phase, closed failure reason, elapsed milliseconds, and optional numeric HTTP status. Exception messages, stacks, URLs, response bodies, and credentials are excluded. Accessing an adversarial thrown value cannot replace the existing graceful failure.

This improves diagnosis; it does not establish or repair the underlying cause of intermittent refresh failures. The installed runtime remains unchanged pending an upstream release.

## Evidence

- Focused native owner tests: 30 passed, including real fetch-guard timeout classification, 401/403 preservation, successful discovery, outer timeout fencing, sibling isolation, and secret-rich/adversarial thrown values.
- Baseline qualification against the unchanged owner: 9 diagnostic assertions failed and 1 successful-discovery case passed; candidate source was restored afterward.
- Native scoped AutoReview: clean.
- All 27 selected core-test type graphs, core and extension production/test types, export scans, and the remaining native changed-source lint/policy plan passed.
- Full native `pnpm build` passed (exit 0; 23m 19s), including SDK declarations, import/bootstrap checks and the UI build.

The deployed package's build stamp could not be resolved to a public upstream commit. Its bundled inner failure handler was independently inspected and matched the relevant outcome contract; no exact deployed commit match or durable live refresh fix is claimed.

prs.title: feat(ui): add setting to opt out of right-click message actions
prs.body:
Related: #106765

## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI chat thread binds a `contextmenu` handler that calls `preventDefault()` on every message bubble to show the message actions menu. There is no way to get the browser's native context menu back on a message, so users who rely on native Copy, Search or spell-check on chat text have no escape hatch.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds an explicit opt-out rather than changing the default: a **"Right-click message actions"** setting under Settings → Appearance → Chat, **enabled by default** so existing behaviour is unchanged. When it is turned off, `handleChatContextMenu()` returns before `preventDefault()` and the native menu opens normally.

The setting follows the existing `composerHoldToRecord` pattern — a browser-local preference persisted only when explicitly disabled. No gateway config schema change, and no change to the actions menu itself.

**Relationship to #106765 and #107137.** #106765 asks for native-menu access on *selected text* and lists three options; #107137 already implements option 2 (a Copy selection entry in the actions menu) and is further along. This PR is option 3 and is deliberately complementary, not a competing fix: it does not change selection behaviour at all, so it can land alongside #107137 or on its own. I am happy to close this if maintainers would rather keep the surface to one change.

Non-goals: no new menu entries, no change to selection handling, no change to link handling (which already falls through).

## User Impact

- Users who want the browser's native context menu on chat messages can turn off **Right-click message actions** in Settings → Appearance → Chat.
- Everyone else sees no change: the setting defaults to on and the actions menu behaves exactly as before.

## Evidence

Real-browser proof captured headless with `OPENCLAW_CAPTURE_UI_PROOF=1`.

### Screenshots

**1. Default — the actions menu opens on right-click**

![Actions menu opens on right-click by default](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tangotrick/openclaw/pr-proof-assets/04-actions-enabled-default.png)

**2. The new setting, Settings → Appearance → Chat (on by default)**

![The new Right-click message actions setting, enabled](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tangotrick/openclaw/pr-proof-assets/05-setting-on.png)

**3. Setting switched off**

![The setting switched off](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tangotrick/openclaw/pr-proof-assets/06-setting-off.png)

**4. After opting out — no custom menu, native menu restored**

![Right-click after opting out shows no custom menu](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tangotrick/openclaw/pr-proof-assets/07-actions-disabled-native-menu.png)

### Tests

New e2e case in `ui/src/e2e/chat-message-actions.e2e.test.ts` covering the whole chain in Chromium: the menu opens by default, the Settings toggle is clicked in the real UI and `aria-checked` flips to `false`, and the thread then leaves the event untouched. Suppression is read from `dispatchEvent()`'s return value, which is `false` only when a listener called `preventDefault()` — a browser-level fact rather than an assertion about internals.

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner \
  ui/src/e2e/chat-message-actions.e2e.test.ts -t "restores the native context menu"   → 1 passed

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/chat/chat-view.test.ts                        → passed
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/config/config-page.test.ts                    → passed
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/app/settings.node.test.ts                           → 38 passed
oxfmt --check / oxlint / git diff --check                                              → clean
```

Two notes in the interest of full disclosure:

- The pre-existing case `offers Reply inline and mirrors every assistant action in the context menu` fails in my environment on a tooltip assertion. I verified it **fails identically on an unmodified `main` checkout**, so it is not caused by this change.
- `pnpm ui:i18n:check` exits non-zero, but it also does so on unmodified `main`, and none of the reported keys are the two added here.

I could not run a full-repo `tsc --noEmit` locally — it exhausts memory on my machine — so type checking on the changed surface is covered only by the test runs above and CI.

The wrapper was already uncapped by #176368: it runs one formatter process locally, with no thread limit, batching, niceness, or lock. There is no remaining throttle to remove. Switching the existing default is the complete implementation; no new execution path or configuration is needed.

`test/scripts/dev-tool.test.ts` updates the selector expectations for the requested local default (bucket 2: test contract update, not a Bun API defect), adds missing-fork fallback coverage, and retains override and CI parity coverage. The three changed expectations fail on the old selector and pass with this change. No failures are skipped or timed out.

The canonical fork reference and scripts guide include the measurements and the loaded-Mac caveat. CONTRIBUTING already links to the canonical reference.

## Evidence

Pinned revision verified: `1.4.4-canary.1+7bd4fdff3`, as specified by this checkout's unchanged pin. Benchmark source: `5d0148f95578c8e63beb1901a370742063d07eb9`; oxfmt 0.72.0, pnpm 12.11.1; Node 24.19.0 on AWS and 26.12.0 on the Mac.

prs.title: feat(ui): modernize the Control UI dashboard
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The web Control UI dashboard (`ui/`) looked dated and busy — the accent color was on every page heading, the active nav item was a filled "boxed" pill, provider quota bars were a single color that looked the same whether a plan was full or nearly empty, and Settings was a long flat wall of sections. This is a UI/UX refresh to make the dashboard calmer, more modern, and easier to scan.

## What Changed

- **Nova theme** — a new coral-on-slate theme family (dark + light), alongside the existing Claw / Knot / Dash.
- **Neutral page headings** — accent is reserved for primary actions, selection, and live status.
- **Level-aware quota meters** — provider bars shift green → amber → red as a plan depletes, so a near-empty plan reads at a glance.
- **Flatter, calmer surfaces** — left accent-bar active nav (instead of a filled box), a gradient send button, and a translucent glass command palette.
- **Collapsible Settings groups** — advanced items are tucked away by default and still one click (or search) away.

No changes to routing, gateway protocol, config schema, or feature availability.

## Before / after

Captured at 1440p (the layouts you'd actually see on a 27" monitor) — previous look on the left, refreshed UI/UX on the right. This PR is the visual-refresh layer on top of the newer dashboard shell.

prs.title: fix(memory): prevent active session ingestion starvation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session-transcript ingestion is capped at 240 messages per sweep. Under sustained activity, lexical file ordering can repeatedly consume that budget before a recently active direct session is reached. The prior state rebuild also omitted checkpoints for discovered transcripts that the capped sweep did not visit, causing unnecessary rereads and weakening continuity.

## Changes

- Prioritize discovered transcript sessions by current session-store activity before applying the sweep-wide cap.
- Preserve prior checkpoints for discovered-but-unvisited transcripts.
- Add an adversarial regression with more than one sweep of transcripts, a real Discord direct-session key, and an appended message on an earlier checkpoint. The test proves the active direct session is ingested, the capped-out checkpoint stays unconsumed during that sweep, and the appended message drains on the next sweep.

## Evidence

Rebased without conflicts onto upstream `main` at `752f059753e89806ce3bbe3b9e6136484e5a3f93` and validated at exact head `3116795698bd048a588bb6e929ff357b9326dfe3`:

- `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming-phases.test.ts` — 48/48 passed.
- `pnpm exec vitest list extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming-phases.test.ts` — 48 tests collected, including `prioritizes current sessions and preserves capped-out checkpoints`.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming-phases.ts extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming-phases.test.ts` — passed.
- `pnpm exec oxlint extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming-phases.ts extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming-phases.test.ts` — passed.
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` — passed.
- [Exact-head Real behavior proof run 29804428893](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29804428893) — passed.

Immediately before push, upstream had advanced to `56bc39e689b4d9d374d5742e67c823b8d277831d` by two commits affecting agent session reset and AI context accounting only. Neither commit touched memory-core ingestion, session storage, plugin state, or this PR's two-file surface, so the exact-head proof remained applicable.

### Redacted after-fix runtime proof

This is a standalone run from the exact checkout, outside Vitest. It uses OpenClaw's real SQLite plugin-state store, real SQLite session store, and the production `runDreamingSweepPhases` path in an isolated temporary state directory. The probe seeds only synthetic redacted messages; it does not read or mutate production state.

```json
{
  "schema": "openclaw.memory-session-ingestion-runtime-proof.v1",
  "exactHead": "3116795698bd048a588bb6e929ff357b9326dfe3",
  "backend": {
    "pluginState": "sqlite-runtime-store",
    "sessionTranscript": "sqlite-session-store",
    "environment": "isolated-redacted-runtime"
  },
  "scenario": {
    "discoveredSessions": 26,
    "seededBacklogMessages": 288,
    "sweepMessageCap": 240
  },
  "assertions": {
    "activeDirectSessionIngestedBeforeBacklog": true,
    "discoveredButUnvisitedCheckpointPreserved": true,
    "deferredMessageAbsentDuringCappedSweep": true,
    "deferredMessageDrainedNextSweep": true,
    "preservedCursorAdvancedAfterDrain": true
  }
}
```

The change does not broaden workspace or agent selection; it only reorders already-authorized discovered transcripts and preserves their existing ingestion state.

prs.title: refactor(exec): remove redundant authorization preparation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Exec preparation clones a worker-owned policy before copy-on-write reducers, checks delayed policy-snapshot presence twice, freezes a private signal list, and repeatedly normalizes the same executable within one synchronous validation path.

## User Impact

Exec policy, host floors, agent deletion fences, shell/runtime rejection, abort propagation, and returned authority immutability remain intact. Missing delayed policy snapshots now use the final authority owner's existing "Exec approval changed before execution" error.

## Why This Change Was Made

The worker already serializes and reparses each changed policy into a new snapshot. Its reducers copy every changed branch, so cloning the current file before reduction adds no isolation. The unconditional final usage-authority check already rejects a missing delayed snapshot before mutation. The signal list is newly deduplicated and private; the returned authority remains frozen. Shell validators reuse one normalized executable without removing any validation.

No SQL, worker-request, transaction, schema, SDK, or PG admission/publication changes. Caller-owned request copies and final security checks stay. No new compatibility path or accepted security edge.

| Candidate | Decision | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
