prs.title: fix(workboard): finalize running execution on terminal status transitions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Workboard dispatch slots could be permanently starved by stale execution state and uncleared dispatch claims, blocking follow-up work for the same owner agent.

Two related bugs caused this:

1. **Stale running execution on terminal transitions**: When a card left `running` status via `releaseClaim`, generic `updateCard`, `move`, or `reassign` (paths that don't pass an explicit execution patch), the execution record stayed `running`. The dispatcher's capacity predicate then counted the card as occupying the owner's slot indefinitely.

2. **Dispatch claim not released on lifecycle success**: `syncLifecycle` mapped the card to `review` and execution to `review` on lifecycle success, but did not clear `card.metadata.claim`. `workboardCardConsumesOwnerSlot` still counted the active (non-expired) claim against the owner's capacity, so the next ready card for that owner was blocked until the claim's TTL expired (30 minutes by default).

Closes #122911.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Fix 1: Finalize running execution on terminal status transitions only

`updateCard` (`store-core.ts`) is the shared owner for execution lifecycle. It already had logic to sync session keys, but lacked the symmetric finalization for execution status. The fix adds a finalization step: when a card transitions from `running` to a **terminal** status (`done`/`review`/`blocked`) without an explicit execution patch, the execution status is closed to match the card's terminal state. `done`/`review` are successful outcomes (attempt succeeds, `failureCount` resets); `blocked` is an explicit failure or abandonment path.

Non-terminal statuses (`todo`, `backlog`, `triage`, `scheduled`, `ready`) preserve execution occupancy so a worker moved aside can still complete successfully. The original broad condition (`status !== "running"`) incorrectly finalized executions for non-terminal moves, causing `completeDirect` to retain `blocked` on later successful completions (ClawSweeper P1 re-review).

The dispatcher's unguarded `card.execution?.status === "running"` capacity arm was removed — with execution now finalized at the owner, legacy stale rows no longer need a downstream guard.

### Fix 2: Release terminal review claims before capacity counting (ClawSweeper P1)

`syncLifecycle` (`store.ts`) is the lifecycle owner that transitions the card to terminal-for-dispatch status (`review`/`blocked`). The claim must be released at this boundary so the owner's slot is freed immediately, not after claim TTL expiry. Without this, `normalizeMetadata`'s fallback preserved the stale claim, and `workboardCardConsumesOwnerSlot` counted it against capacity.

The fix clears `card.metadata.claim` in `syncLifecycle` when the card transitions to any non-running, non-done status. `workboardCardConsumesOwnerSlot` (`store-constants.ts`) additionally excludes `review`/`blocked` claims as defense-in-depth, covering legacy rows where `syncLifecycle` did not clear the claim before this fix shipped.

### Production LOC delta

- `store-core.ts`: +19/-1 (execution finalization at the shared owner, terminal-only)
- `store.ts`: +15/-0 (claim release at the lifecycle owner)
- `store-constants.ts`: +7/-4 (defense-in-depth capacity exclusion)
- `dispatcher.test.ts`: +12/-4 (updated review-slot test)
- `dispatcher-ownership.test.ts`: +5/-2 (use non-terminal status for claim-expiry test)

Production: +41/-5 net +36 across 3 lifecycle owners. Tests: +703/-6 net +697.

Each change lives at its architectural owner — `updateCard` owns execution lifecycle, `syncLifecycle` owns claim lifecycle, `workboardCardConsumesOwnerSlot` owns capacity semantics. The terminal-only narrowing absorbs the ClawSweeper P1 finding without expanding the production surface: the broad `status !== "running"` condition and `finalizedExecutionStatus` ternary were replaced by a direct terminal-status check, keeping net production LOC proportional to the three owners repaired.

## User Impact

Workboard dispatch recovers immediately when a worker finishes or fails — no 30-minute starvation window. Follow-up cards for the same owner agent dispatch as soon as the lifecycle transition completes. Legacy cards with stale claims (from before this fix) also no longer hold slots. Moving a running card aside to a non-terminal status (e.g., `todo`) no longer corrupts the execution record — the worker can still complete successfully and the attempt is recorded as `succeeded`. This is a default-path fix: every operator using workboard dispatch was affected.

No config, API, default, protocol, or schema change; existing operator behavior is unchanged except that stale executions are now finalized and stale slots are released.

## Evidence

Linux, Node 22 (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` wrapper).

Rebased onto current main. The dispatcher's unguarded `card.execution?.status === "running"` capacity arm is removed at its canonical helper location in `store-constants.ts`, so both `dispatcher.ts` and `sqlite-store.ts` call sites are repaired in one change.

### Focused proof (two files, 46 tests)

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/workboard/src/dispatcher-ownership.test.ts \
    extensions/workboard/src/dispatcher-ownership-stale-execution.test.ts

 ✓ |extensions| extensions/workboard/src/dispatcher-ownership.test.ts (30 tests) 166ms
 ✓ |extensions| extensions/workboard/src/dispatcher-ownership-stale-execution.test.ts (16 tests) 180ms

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  46 passed (46)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 48.40s
```

### Full workboard suite — no regression

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/workboard/

 Test Files  19 passed (19)
      Tests  360 passed (360)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 53.70s
```

### Pre-fix failure proof (12 of the new tests fail on main)

```
$ git checkout origin/main -- extensions/workboard/src/store-core.ts \
    extensions/workboard/src/store.ts extensions/workboard/src/store-constants.ts
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/workboard/src/dispatcher-ownership.test.ts \
    extensions/workboard/src/dispatcher-ownership-stale-execution.test.ts

Tests  12 failed | 34 passed (46)
[vitest] FAILED (exit 1)
```

Failures (grouped by invariant):

- `releaseClaim(status=done)` → execution stays `running` (expected `done`)
- `releaseClaim(status=review)` → execution stays `running` (expected `review`)
- `generic update(status=done)` → execution stays `running` (expected `done`)

- Legacy `review` + active claim → ready card NOT started (claim not excluded)

- Non-terminal move (todo) → execution marked `blocked` (expected `running`)

### Matrix-style evidence — terminal transition paths

| `done` + execution `running` (SQLite) | ready card NOT started | ready card started |

### Regression proof — sibling paths unchanged

| `reclaim` | execution cleared (unchanged) |

| `syncLifecycle` (non-association) | execution patched explicitly (unchanged) |

### Production-boundary dispatch trace (SQLite-backed WorkboardStore, not in-memory)

```
$ node --import tsx /tmp/proof-122911-dispatch-trace.mts
```

This trace exercises the real `createWorkboardSqliteStores` persistence layer, `WorkboardStore` (production store), `dispatchAndStartWorkboardCards` (production dispatcher), `syncLifecycle` (production lifecycle), `store.move` / `store.complete` (production mutations), and `stores.cards.register` / `store.get` (real SQLite read/write). Only `subagent.run` is mocked (cannot start a real agent in a proof script).

prs.title: chore(ci): qualify selective compiler backports
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Compiler adoption remains blocked by incomplete upstream controls on large plugin graphs and failed isolation admission on the capacity runner. This draft pins the fourth compiler fix, records the unchanged 12GiB failures, and adds a separate 24GiB capacity control to finish diagnostic comparison without hiding failed samples.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/175541
Stack base: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175567

## User Impact

The selected repository compiler is unchanged. This is an opt-in qualification experiment; all PRs remain drafts. Landing and compiler adoption require explicit owner approval.

## Why This Change Was Made

The candidate is now `vincentkoc/tsc-ts@a80cd9190942d16286a8483f1f51d9a68037324f`. Its draft stack contains [uniform-union narrowing](https://github.com/vincentkoc/tsc-ts/pull/1), [recursion/identity relations](https://github.com/vincentkoc/tsc-ts/pull/2), [no-emit exit semantics](https://github.com/vincentkoc/tsc-ts/pull/3), and [generic import-query instantiation](https://github.com/vincentkoc/tsc-ts/pull/4). It remains a selective 7.0.2-based candidate, not a complete 7.1 port.

The previous plugin-test controls already used sequential parsing and one checker with `GOMAXPROCS=2`, `GOGC=30`, and `GOMEMLIMIT=3GiB`. Go's memory target is soft; the OOM state alone does not establish the live-heap size or a compiler leak. The new `memory-diagnostic` dispatch compares targets of 3GiB and 10GiB on that one graph, one repeat per compiler: six trials total. Both profiles retain four CPUs, the same 12GiB hard cap, zero swap, checking flags, deadlines and isolation.

Measured diagnostic calls preserve raw GC traces in stderr. The auditor explicitly rejects diagnostic artifacts, even if the compiler succeeds; these traces cannot become qualification or performance evidence.

The separate `capacity-control` dispatch covers the two incomplete plugin graphs with 27 planned trials: three compilers, three repeats, plugin cold/nonincremental modes and plugin-test cold mode. It uses the existing secretless Blacksmith runner route, admits at least 30GiB of actual host capacity, then fixes four-CPU affinity, a 24GiB container cap and zero swap. Original cold flags/Go policy, nonincremental flags, immutable inputs, 600-second deadlines and rejection/cleanup rules remain unchanged. No GC tracing runs in this profile. Metadata, verdicts and artifact names identify the capacity control; its results never overwrite or mix with the failed 12GiB profile. `remaining` selects the other 36 graphs with their original indices and canaries.

PR events run tooling checks only; compiler comparisons require explicit dispatch.

## Evidence

- Previous [38-graph run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39144853163), head `6dca68dcdb14a117db9b6d778e9c7dbcf8ba88b0`, compiler `68d0698`: 576 attempted, 567 valid, nine rejected, none unattempted. All 38 ZIP digests and local audit replays match. Verdicts: 36 equivalent groups, two incomplete; all 180 canary trials passed candidate/pinned parity.
- The nine rejected samples have explicit OOM state and verified cleanup: three plugin nonincremental reference trials and six plugin-test pinned/reference trials. They remain failed controls. Historical exit-137 causes remain unproven.
- The plugin-test candidate's TS2345 led to the fourth fix. That head passed [scoped CI](https://github.com/vincentkoc/tsc-ts/actions/runs/39162206911): 11/69 units, 42/42 cases, all first attempt. Its [three-compiler probe](https://github.com/vincentkoc/tsc-ts/actions/runs/39162671243) passed 36 rows. The preceding full run passed 67/69 units, with two fixture-configuration failures corrected without changing compiler bytes. This is not a fresh full-suite pass.
- [Memory diagnostic 39181890646](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39181890646), source `280e7719968e746bf25e7526a022da24539a23a9`: six attempted; candidate completed the real plugin-test graph cleanly at both soft targets; all four pinned/reference controls were explicitly OOM-killed and rejected. Last observed Go live heaps were 11,093–11,530 trace-reported MB. Candidate emitted no GC trace. All input/library identities and cleanup checks match. The profiles ran on different CPU models, so their timing/GC differences cannot isolate the soft target. Collection success is not qualification success.
- That diagnostic's hosted tooling gate passed 24 tests, both tooling typechecks, lint, formatting and workflow validation. Both archive digests were verified: `12156039138` / `6fd774622e0c265eb400e39953fc05654fd1ddd39ddfd3af7d0ad8bdeced6c69`; `12157210918` / `a8eb95c774d6ff67ffb93e9152a01921a919fb39e2acd98adc031bc587795729`.
- [Capacity run 39183419122](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39183419122), source `d4027ef0aa46ec44da2bebecd2c9597200878b3b`, stopped at the unchanged `Non-loopback network interface` admission guard on both capacity jobs and was cancelled. Zero of 27 compiler trials ran; route/TCP probes were not reached. This is neither capacity proof nor evidence of a network escape. Its tooling gate passed 28 tests, both types, lint, formatting and workflow validation.
- The follow-up adds one `isolation-diagnostic` row on the same capacity runner. It records classified sysfs/proc network witnesses and selected Docker runtime fields, preserves every fatal guard and cleanup rule, then returns before sandbox compiler invocation. Raw interface names are excluded. Local syntax, formatting, rendered Bash, diff and all six workflow selections passed; independent review and autoreview are clean through P2. [Diagnostic run 39184795601](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39184795601), exact source `7a1c55ef8a561e1147938fc3bcd0ab6e0ba51ecb`, failed isolation admission. Hosted tooling passed 28 tests, both types, lint, formatting and workflow checks. The independently verified artifact reports loopback plus four non-loopback interfaces in both sysfs and `/proc/self/net/dev`, while Docker declares `NetworkMode=none` / `Runtime=runc` (client/server 28.0.4; kernel 6.6.141). The guard exited 1, `OOMKilled=false`, and cleanup passed. No sandbox compiler was invoked. External reachability and namespace ownership remain unproven; the TCP probe was not reached, and absent route records do not prove route absence. Artifact `12157484027`, ZIP SHA-256 `4ccde45d39f3c95e49a4e2e1bd330eb435f3e7c9607b473f4d1ee6c1cf713671`, contains only inventory and isolation diagnostics.
- The previous exact-head ClawSweeper review and all-graph result cover `6dca68d`, not this new head. Full repaired-head repository qualification remains outstanding.

Immutable native producer: [39162206911](https://github.com/vincentkoc/tsc-ts/actions/runs/39162206911), attempt 1, artifact `12149466946`, expiring 2026-10-21. ZIP SHA-256 `e980b95b04e69c901b59c6ff6f90f8da3d4619dd386cb5067d64233ed28de423`; tar `4aebeece3702944225ddd8b957889279510aeeb6246fe9b29a02158268c7c79b`; compiler `9785e87da1650d3a4007d234bc194c63b640524c010497884e4b93161c7bb149`. Identity and bytes were independently verified; no moving-build fallback exists.

No product runtime change. The capacity-control follow-up adds 42 net tooling/workflow lines and 25 test lines for explicit resource admission, profile separation and the remaining-graph selection. The earlier native threaded-watch retry remains an unresolved follow-up; warm-cache, whole-CI and multi-platform adoption proof remain separate work.

The isolation-diagnostic follow-up adds 78 net tooling/workflow lines to observe the admission failure without changing the sandbox policy. It adds no product runtime code and produces no qualification samples.

Current blocker: the runner owner must restore a network namespace that satisfies Docker's `--network none` contract. Rerun the same isolation diagnostic first; only after admission passes can the 27 capacity-control trials and the remaining 36-graph qualification proceed. No guard relaxation, compiler selection change or landing is authorized by this diagnostic.

prs.title: fix(gateway): suppress health events from routine channel activity
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Follow-up to #175390: ordinary channel turns still change the health-event digest through `busy`, `activeRuns`, and `activeRunStartedAt`. Short event-loop degradation samples also toggle the digest, causing full health snapshots to fan out to every operator socket despite no sustained health change.

## User Impact

Routine channel activity no longer triggers passive health events. Event-loop degradation independently triggers an event after the sampler has observed it continuously for at least one minute; recovery and channel failures remain visible on the next refresh. The cache, health RPC, and event payload retain full diagnostic readings.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing digest's activity exclusions for both channel summaries and nested accounts, and use the sampler-owned degradation duration for the event-loop comparison. No new timer, cache, connection state, option, or protocol shape is introduced.

There is only one health event producer. Hello's cached health is a response payload, and the shared post-connect refresh still passes through this digest. The Control UI already deduplicates its initial health request per connection/ownership key, so no additional initial-send flag is needed.

Production delta: +11 lines (12 added, 1 removed). Retaining full diagnostic payloads and immediate lifecycle/error delivery requires narrowing the existing comparison rather than deleting those diagnostics.

## Evidence

Baseline: the focused regression file fails on both activity rebroadcast and transient event-loop flapping (2 failed, 16 passed). Base run wall time was 270.80 seconds, dominated by cold worker preparation and module loading.

Fixed head: all 18 focused tests pass with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server/health-state.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Changed-file oxfmt and lint, `pnpm tsgo:core` (native tsrs), and `git diff --check` pass. Independent Codex review found no actionable findings. PR CI owns broad validation; no full local build/suite or Testbox/Crabbox lease was used.

Two concurrent A/B pairs on an isolated Linux sandbox, with the CPU halves swapped for the second pair, produced identical results. Each pair used 18 real loopback WebSockets, Discord/Slack/Telegram-shaped snapshots with six accounts each, ten agents, and 60 accelerated minute samples. The exclusive measurement lock covered each pair; starts differed by 1–2 ms.

| Routine activity, per simulated hour | Base | Fix | Paired difference, fix − base |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Health frames per socket | 60 | 0 | −60 |
| Health frames across 18 sockets | 1,080 | 0 | −1,080 |
| Received health JSON bytes | 21,099,870 | 0 | −21,099,870 |

Both variants sent the one initial snapshot. The fix then sent all five expected material transitions (sustained degradation, changed sustained reason, recovery, channel failure, channel recovery), each exactly once to every socket. Complete cached diagnostics stayed current. Across all 69 samples, 1,242 refresh-admission attempts produced exactly 69 collections on both variants.

Field-only observation at the actual digest boundary identified `busy`, `activeRuns`, and `activeRunStartedAt` at channel/account levels, plus `eventLoop.degraded` and `eventLoop.reasons`, as the routine changing inputs. No routine digest inputs changed after the fix. Average outside CPU activity was 14.72% / 18.99% for the two pairs, recorded for context; no CPU/latency claim is made.

Base source was `59eeed0be517f825fe74b3d9e39352b55cee02f4`; all 20 measured source modules remained byte-identical after rebasing onto `64e9443af525`. Only `health-state.ts` differs between measured variants. Initial fixture setup failures (native TypeScript loader support and an occupied loopback port) were corrected before these two valid pairs; they are not product failures.

Measurement scope: the synthetic, accelerated replay runs the production health owner, refresh admission, digest, broadcaster, recipient scopes, frame encoding and real WebSocket delivery. It substitutes the collector and connection admission. This is narrower than a full dev-Gateway boot or live-provider observation; it does not establish production reconnect counts or a measured production event rate.

prs.title: fix(minimax): match CN host on a dot boundary for region detection
prs.body:
## Summary

fix(minimax): bind CN region detection to the `minimaxi.com` host on a dot boundary, so look-alike hosts such as `notminimaxi.com` no longer route web search to the CN endpoint

## What Problem This Solves

The MiniMax web search provider infers the region (`cn` vs `global`) from `MINIMAX_API_HOST` or the configured provider base URL, and picks the search endpoint accordingly (`https://api.minimaxi.com/v1/coding_plan/search` for CN, `https://api.minimax.io/v1/coding_plan/search` for global).

**代码证据**: in `extensions/minimax/src/minimax-web-search-provider.runtime.ts`, `isMiniMaxCnHost` used:

- `new URL(trimmed).hostname.endsWith("minimaxi.com")` — matches any host that merely *ends* with the string, e.g. `notminimaxi.com` or `evilnotminimaxi.com`.
- `trimmed.includes("minimaxi.com")` as the fallback for scheme-less values — a pure substring check that also matches look-alike hosts.

So a misspelled or maliciously crafted host like `MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://notminimaxi.com` was classified as CN, and search traffic (including the query and the `Authorization: Bearer <key>` header) would be sent to the CN search endpoint derived from that wrong classification.

Trigger condition: any host value that ends with the literal string `minimaxi.com` without being `minimaxi.com` or a subdomain of it.

## Root Cause

- Violated invariant: region inference is a security-relevant routing decision (it selects which endpoint receives queries and credentials), but the host check was a suffix/substring match instead of a dot-boundary host match.
- `endsWith("minimaxi.com")` has no label boundary: `notminimaxi.com`.endsWith(`minimaxi.com`) is `true`. The scheme-less fallback `includes(...)` is weaker still.

## Why This Fix

- Option A: keep `endsWith` but prepend a dot (`endsWith(".minimaxi.com")`). Handles the URL-parseable path but leaves the scheme-less substring fallback untouched.
- Option B (chosen): extract a single `isCnHostname` predicate — `hostname === "minimaxi.com" || hostname.endsWith(".minimaxi.com")` — and use it for both paths; for scheme-less values, prepend `https://` so only the host is inspected (never the path or query), and return `false` if the value still cannot be parsed.
- Not chosen: a regex over the raw string — duplicates URL parsing logic and still mixes host and non-host content.

## User Impact

- Affected scenarios: users setting `MINIMAX_API_HOST` or a provider `baseUrl` to a host that shares the `minimaxi.com` suffix (typo'd or look-alike domains).
- Before: such hosts were classified as CN and search requests were routed to the CN endpoint.
- After: only `minimaxi.com` and its subdomains classify as CN; everything else falls back to global.
- Behavior change: legitimate CN endpoints (`https://api.minimaxi.com`, `https://minimaxi.com`, `https://api.minimaxi.com/anthropic`) are unaffected — still classified as CN.

## Real Behavior Proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** look-alike hosts sharing the `minimaxi.com` suffix were classified as CN, routing MiniMax web search to the wrong (CN) endpoint.
- **Real environment tested:** worktree `wt-minimax-cn-host-boundary` on latest `origin/main`, Node v24.19.0, importing the real `extensions/minimax/src/minimax-web-search-provider.runtime.ts` via tsx and calling the exported `testing.resolveMiniMaxRegion` / `testing.resolveMiniMaxEndpoint` with `MINIMAX_API_HOST` set per case. No mocks of the functions under test.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  $ node node_modules/tsx/dist/cli.mjs minimax-cn-host-boundary.proof.mjs
  $ npx vitest run extensions/minimax/src/minimax-web-search-provider.test.ts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix (8/8 PASS):**
  ```bash
  PASS MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://api.minimaxi.com -> region=cn
  PASS MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://api.minimaxi.com/anthropic -> region=cn
  PASS MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://minimaxi.com -> region=cn
  PASS MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://api.minimax.io -> region=global
  PASS MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://notminimaxi.com -> region=global
  PASS MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://evilnotminimaxi.com/v1 -> region=global
  PASS MINIMAX_API_HOST=notminimaxi.com -> region=global
  PASS MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://example.com/redir?u=minimaxi.com -> region=global
  RESULT: ALL PASS
  ```

**Before (on main, same script, exit code 1):**

```bash
FAIL MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://notminimaxi.com -> region=cn (expected global), endpoint=https://api.minimaxi.com/v1/coding_plan/search
FAIL MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://evilnotminimaxi.com/v1 -> region=cn (expected global)
FAIL MINIMAX_API_HOST=notminimaxi.com -> region=cn (expected global)
RESULT: 3 case(s) show WRONG region/endpoint
```

- **What was not tested:** a live search request against the real MiniMax endpoints (requires valid credentials); the proof exercises the real region/endpoint resolution code paths end to end.

## Tests and Validation

- `npx vitest run extensions/minimax/src/minimax-web-search-provider.test.ts` — 23/23 passed, including new regression cases: apex CN domain still classifies as CN; `https://notminimaxi.com`, `https://evilnotminimaxi.com/v1`, scheme-less `notminimaxi.com`, `https://minimaxi.com.evil.com`, and a query-string-only mention all classify as global.
- `npx oxlint --deny=warn` on both changed files — 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- Before/after real-behavior proof logs are embedded above.

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: unit tests on the real exported `resolveMiniMaxRegion` / `resolveMiniMaxEndpoint` (via the module's `testing` surface), with `MINIMAX_API_HOST` as the input vector.
- Target test file: `extensions/minimax/src/minimax-web-search-provider.test.ts`
- Scenario locked in: suffix-sharing look-alike hosts (`notminimaxi.com`, with scheme, with path, scheme-less) and non-host mentions (query string) never classify as CN, while the real CN hosts (`api.minimaxi.com`, apex `minimaxi.com`) still do.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: it pins the exact predicate that makes the routing decision, using the exact inputs that previously misclassified.

prs.title: refactor(gateway): remove repeated synchronous checks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway publication and operation paths sometimes validate the same authority twice in one synchronous call chain.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. The checks before credentials, execution, disclosure, and external effects remain, as do checks after awaited work.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove only checks that an unconditional adjacent call or immediate owner callee already performs. Keep distinct session, account, reservation, registry, and execution authorities. Reentrant policy callbacks and asynchronous reads retain their current validation.

## Evidence

Ten production files, +3/−16 lines (net −13). Fifteen static candidate IDs identify the removed duplicate-check/normalization sites; some IDs overlap one statement. No exports, SQL, worker dispatch, schema, or PostgreSQL bookkeeping changes.

Changed-file formatting, type-aware oxlint, and `git diff --check` pass. Independent Codex P0/P1 review is scoped-clean (one completed round). Exact-head [CI 39183719133](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39183719133) passed types, lint, source contracts, Madge, prompt snapshots, T1/dialect ratchets and the other selected owner suites.

[Knip job 117842209503](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39183720924/job/117842209503) reports only the same three FaceTime test-support exports (`commandResult`, `mutedResult`, `outgoingCall (ft)`) present in [main job 117820741086](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39176649118/job/117820741086); zero new findings. The supplemental run was canceled after that evidence was captured.

Unresolved behavioral CI failure: [job 117842301415](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39183719133/job/117842301415), `test/gateway-restored-requester-settle.e2e.test.ts`, normal runtime budget / runtime timeout, timed out before the first model request (`gateway-restored-deadline-runtime-timeout`, expected request count 1, received 0). The other three cases passed. Current-main logs inspected so far do not establish the same failure; this is not claimed inherited or fixed. A focused base replay was canceled and joined while still queued after more than six minutes at the CPU gate (host load 133 on 32 cores); no test or build launched, and there is no local base/head verdict. Landing under RELAXED LANDING v4 after bounded investigation without an established attributable product regression, with this uncertainty retained.

## What Problem This Solves

Repeated fixture construction and assertion scaffolding make these tests harder to maintain. This batch consolidates those patterns and removes duplicate cases while retaining distinct authority, recovery, protocol, and lifecycle checks.

## User Impact

No production behavior change. Only tests and test-support files change; no dependency, configuration, or public API changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replays campaign batch d258 onto pinned main `a70b7c23104ada5d7d1a21b245dec72623a78a7e`. Applied 29 of 30 listed commits, preserving their messages, followed by three focused corrective commits. OpenCode commit `d6224c73b870e60ba1aa730d876a9ae7ff97452f` was skipped: all four files conflicted extensively with newer main auth/catalog/replay-policy coverage.

Conflict and review decisions:

- Preserved current-main chat viewport-resize and pane-retirement tests. Consolidated only the already-covered layout-scroll case into its equivalent retained row.
- Dropped second-pass server-endpoint-compaction and second/third-pass cache-TTL edits, retaining current-main budget matrices, rejection recovery, replay seeds, damaged-input cases, and checkpoint/byte bounds.
- Restored the seventeen files listed below to pinned main after CI/review exposed changed matcher semantics, incorrect PDF retention expectations, or insufficient justification for removing distinct authority/diagnostic coverage.
- Fixed the raw `main` reset fixture key and navigation contribution kind. Repaired scope-array types, mock-call narrowing, Solid disposal, and required popup callback typing.
- Rejected two review findings using current source: lifecycle generations are strings (`src/infra/agent-events.ts`), and `isRecord` remains used by orphan-recovery assertions. All corrective reviews completed clean through P2.

No touched path matches current CODEOWNERS rules.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Current signed head is `055a524fa0f09f28df49e21189aa36ea61b9f2ab`, rebased onto fetched main `b69943d2738034a92935adb3e107ba6848d9e565` under the coordinator's one-round tooling refresh. All six commits replay patch-identically; no content conflict or new production change. The private frozen install includes the pinned native `tsrs` checker. Exact-head local proof passed: 93 focused UI tests (162.53 seconds Vitest, 186.22 seconds wrapper), three-root UI typecheck, zero runtime value cycles, zero Madge cycles, focused lint/format, and suppression inventory 14/14 (85.54 seconds Vitest, 113.74 seconds wrapper). Commands ran serially at nice 10 with isolated HOME/state/XDG and maxWorkers=1. The catalog and WhatsApp production owners and determining tests are byte-identical to the previous green head. The previous exact-head run [39176951797](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39176951797) completed **success** on `b21e4cde346de4a5621c5a05d725bbe819f62773`; that is historical broad proof, not a current-head CI claim. New exact-head CI remains the landing gate.

Removes duplicate shell event forwarding and redundant checks on values already admitted by their owners. Native/window/document listeners remain the shell event owners; the catalog writer still checks signed-feed admission before its private monotonicity helper. No rendering, schema, protocol, config, dependency, public SDK, or migration change.

This is the retained wave-6 bundle F: 12 files, **28 net production lines removed** (+8/-36); whole diff +80/-95. The original bundle was split because it exceeded 80 files. The final independent WhatsApp guard simplification now fits into this retained bundle, rather than needing a separate tiny residue. Source lanes are z31 (UI), z06 (catalog/infra), and r06 (normalization/helper ownership). z16 was already absorbed by r06 and receives no duplicate LOC credit. The broader normalization and agent/setup proposals are closed and preserved separately; this change does not depend on them.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: internal route data follows the canonical shared Chat/Dashboard loader contract. No second renderer, projection, listener, cache, or lifecycle owner is added. The existing bubble listener still owns Settings Escape and drawer closure. The catalog's caller retains the signed-feed check, current-row transaction, rollback rejection, and same-sequence equivocation rejection. Phase E is untouched.

## Review and withdrawals

The independent review completed with five P2 findings and an overall incorrect verdict; it is not relabeled scoped-clean. The released deadline-carrier concern caused withdrawal. The retained Settings concern was source-declined because the connected bubble listener still handles it. A later heartbeat finding was accepted: the generation predicate and original regressions were restored, preventing a late delivery from suppressing an alert in a replacement session.

Historical head `6d22b17eb6830130685cfb848a13c41b849b4148` had a red exact-head run [39165565376](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39165565376). The backup custody case `uncertain` timed out at its unchanged 120-second limit. No matching backup failure was found in the last six completed scheduled main runs or the campaign registry. This is **not** called inherited or fixed.

The remote replay never got past source preparation and was stopped at 20 minutes without allocating a lease. A private frozen local install verified the exact CI cleanup dependency, `@openclaw/proc-safe` 0.4.1. Its focused replay was stopped after ten minutes in compiled subprocess setup, without a case verdict; the base case never ran. No timeout, retry, skip, assertion, or budget was relaxed.

prs.title: improve(perf): add the openclaw-performance skill and work-count regression tests
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Performance work in OpenClaw keeps fixing the same waste twice: caches that stop hitting, batches that get reverted, and PRs that land with a regression their own numbers already show. Agents had no repository guide for this work, and three flows where the same waste keeps returning had no test that counts it.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Agents doing performance work now have one OpenClaw skill: measure the real flow with a committed workload, count operations first, delete waste before batching or caching, and land only when every user-facing metric holds or improves. Three work-count tests fail CI if known waste comes back.

## Why This Change Was Made

A corpus of 103 performance cases from the last 90 days on `main` (70 randomly sampled, 33 seeded with every perf revert; each judged from its diff and PR text):

- **Deleting waste lasts:** 3 of 31 random-sample deletes were later re-fixed, and those failed deletes broke a guard, not because the waste returned.
- **Caches, batches and worker moves come back:** 4 of 5, 6 of 7 and 5 of 8 were later re-fixed (biased set, a signal not a rate). In 3 of the 4 cache re-fixes the cache silently stopped hitting, e.g. #115369 → #174741 and #149773 → #149879.
- **Own regressions predict reverts:** 21 PRs landed while their own numbers showed a large regression; 11 of them were later reverted or re-fixed, against 25 of the other 82. Five of the six reverts had shown the regression in their own body.
- **Same waste, again and again:** SQLite schema/admission re-checks (14 PRs, one revert), session list rows (two reverts in two days), model catalog rebuilds.

Changes:

- `.agents/skills/openclaw-performance/SKILL.md`: measure (committed bench per flow, counts first, acceptance rule before the first run, interleaved samples), find waste (10 recurring OpenClaw patterns with real cases), fix order (delete → once at the owner → carry the prepared fact → batch → cache with a written reason, cache-identity rules and an interleaved work-count test), land (no user-facing metric worse unless the owner accepts it).
- Root `AGENTS.md`: the "Do less work" line keeps its core rule and points to the skill.
- Work-count tests (counts, never wall time):
  - `src/state/openclaw-agent-execution.schema-admission.test.ts`: warm chat turns make only their own write requests; no re-open, schema prepare or integrity validation.
  - `src/gateway/session-row-projection.list-page.test.ts`: after an unrelated subagent renewal, repeating the same pages renders 0 rows, materializes 0 more and does 0 worker reads or SQL.
  - `src/gateway/server-methods/models-auth-status.work-count.test.ts` (own file, to keep the existing test under its line cap): interleaved `models.authStatus` and `usage.status` page loads add no provider probes, auth-health builds or catalog loads after warm-up.

## Evidence

| Test | Back-test (parent of the historical fix) |
|---|---|
| Schema admission | fails at `8b7917c79b8^` (#166253): each warm turn adds `open` and `prepare` again |
| Session list | fails at `1b896e6327f^` (#162280): 80 rows materialized instead of 10, plus 1 worker read |
| Models page | fails at `c3f0b6abc01^` (#174741): 3 provider probes in 2 loads; the readers evict each other |

- All three pass on head (each file about 0.3–1.7 s); `models-auth-status.test.ts` still passes 52/52. The Models page test still fails at `c3f0b6abc01^` with real-module mocks (one extra provider probe).
- The pre-commit hook (line-cap ratchet, `AGENTS.md` size) passed; root `AGENTS.md` is 18,917 characters.
- Every PR cited by the skill is merged; every named bench script exists on `main`.

Blind replay of 8 held-out performance tasks (none cited by the skill; each from the parent of its known-good fix), Codex agent with and without the skill, 2 seeds; stopped early after 12 judged pairs to free the host:

| | Without skill | With skill |
|---|---|---|
| Pair wins (blind Codex judge) | 3 | 8 (1 tie) |
| Removed the same waste as the reference fix | 11/14 runs | 11/13 runs |
| Proof includes a work-count test | 5/14 | 11/13 |
| Added a cache | 1 | 1 |
| Judge: proof / waste found / fix order (1-5) | 3.08 / 4.50 / 4.83 | 4.33 / 4.42 / 4.50 |

The skill does not change whether agents find the waste; it changes how they prove it, which is what keeps the waste from returning. One judge and 12 pairs: the win split is not significant (p ≈ 0.23).

**Merge danger:** two-way door; a revert removes the skill and the tests. No runtime change. Blast radius: agent instructions for performance work, and three test files.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Provider-review operations repeat authority checks already performed synchronously by their store owner, and acceptance looks up the same acknowledgment state twice in succession.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. Provider pauses, exact-review comparison, stale-session rejection, and final continuation authority remain enforced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep initial store admission in `withProviderReviewDatabase` and consume the state returned by the acceptance guard. Remove the immediately preceding caller checks, including the one immediately before the compare operation. Checks after reads and before commit/continuation remain. Private typed arguments may be copied before an invalid operation is rejected; no persistence or external effect occurs before owner admission.

Production: +2/-9 lines, net -7. No SQL, worker request, transaction, schema, public API, or runtime result changes. SQL/request/MAIN delta is estimated, unmeasured 0/0/0; no SQL or request operation was removed. No read/write class is removed, so existing authority and persistence tests remain the behavioral proof.

<details>
<summary>Candidate ledger</summary>

| Candidates | Decision and evidence |
| --- | --- |
| C16355, C16356 (F042/F044) | REMOVE: `withProviderReviewDatabase` invokes the identical supplied assertion synchronously. |
| C31385/C31386, C31396/C31397, C31411/C31412 (F152–F154) | REMOVE: the next store read enters that same admission owner without a yield. |
| C31419/C31420 | REMOVE: the next compare operation enters the same store admission owner without a yield. |
| F156 | REMOVE duplicate `readState`: the acceptance guard now returns its checked state. C31417's actual authority check remains. |
| C16354, C31383, C31388/C31389, C31391/C31392, C31393, C31394, C31400/C31401, C31408, C31409, C31414/C31415, C31416/C31417, C31422/C31423 | KEEP: initial admission, distinct runtime authority, post-await disclosure/continuation, or final acceptance authority. |
| C16357, C31398, C31402–C31407 | KEEP: caller-owned comparison input or publicly exposed immutable capability snapshot. |

36 inventory candidates reviewed: 10 removed (4 b, 6 g), 26 kept. One additional duplicate state lookup removed. Candidate IDs that share a source line represent overlapping static patterns, not separate runtime savings.
</details>

## Evidence

Focused formatting, `git diff --check`, and native commit hooks pass. Both independent Codex review rounds completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings; the final round included the complete unchanged admission owner. The 15 provider-review admission cases passed under the pinned Bun runtime, including stale acknowledgments, revocation, and final continuation authority.

prs.title: fix(process): use monotonic clock for process-tree kill grace deadline
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when the wall clock steps back (NTP correction, VM or laptop resume) while OpenClaw is tearing down a command's process group, a child that ignores SIGTERM survives for the size of the step instead of the 300 ms kill grace.

`createCommandTerminationController` (graceful SIGTERM, then group SIGKILL) and `waitForCommandProcessGroupExit` (the post-SIGKILL exit confirmation) seeded and checked their deadlines with `Date.now()`, but wait on monotonic `setTimeout`/`sleep`. A backward step of N ms pushes the deadline out by N ms.

## Fix

Seed, compare and consume both deadlines with `performance.now()`, the clock the timers use. Same-process deadlines only; nothing crosses a process boundary.

Thanks to @SunnyShu0925 for finding and fixing this.

## User Impact

Commands that OpenClaw runs with process-tree ownership (for example a repository's `.openclaw/worktree-setup.sh`, git, npm and update commands) are force-stopped on time after a timeout or cancel, even if the wall clock steps back during teardown. Before the fix, a stuck child stayed alive, and the caller (for example `sessions.create`) stayed blocked, for the size of the step.

## Evidence

End to end, both trees built with `pnpm build` (Node 24, Docker with an init process): a real Gateway; the operator calls `sessions.create` with `worktree: true` on a git repository whose `.openclaw/worktree-setup.sh` starts a descendant that traps SIGTERM and keeps running. The setup hits its 120 s timeout and the runner tears down the process group. When the descendant gets SIGTERM, it asks a preload in the Gateway process to step `Date.now()` by -60 s (only that process; the system clock is not changed). Time is measured from the descendant's SIGTERM to its death.

| Run | SIGTERM to death of the stuck child | `sessions.create` returned after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| main, no step (control) | 303 ms | 125.7 s |
| main, -60 s step | **60348 ms** | **185.3 s** |
| this PR, no step (control) | 334 ms | 124.5 s |
| this PR, -60 s step | 347 ms | 130.2 s |

All runs return `worktree setup failed (timed out after 120 seconds; signal SIGTERM)`. After merging current `main`, the -60 s step on the merged head: 394 ms, `sessions.create` returned after 123.9 s.

Regression test (`exec-termination.test.ts`): rewinds the wall clock by 60 s during the kill grace and again during the exit confirmation. On main no SIGKILL is sent after the grace; with only the confirmation site reverted, settlement stays pending past the confirmation window. Both pass on this PR. `oxfmt` and `oxlint` are clean on the changed files.

Line delta against the merge base: production +5/-5; tests +23/-3. The separate `waitForCommandProcessGroupExit` test was folded into the one termination test, which now covers both deadlines.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: in-process deadline arithmetic only; no persisted state, config, protocol or schema change, and a revert fully undoes it. Blast radius: POSIX commands run with process-tree ownership (worktree setup, git, npm, update and plugin commands); Windows taskkill paths are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(gateway): measure health-collection deadline on the monotonic clock
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Gateway health collector (`health` RPC, used by `openclaw status --all` and `openclaw health --verbose`) seeds its 7 s collection deadline from `Date.now()`. A wall-clock step during collection (NTP step, VM resume, manual change) breaks the budget:

- Forward step: a healthy channel probe that finishes in time is reported as `health collection timed out after 7000ms`.
- Backward step: queued account probes keep their permit and start with a ~2 minute probe budget, so the `health` RPC stalls far past 7 s and `openclaw status --all` shows `Gateway health: gateway timeout after 8000ms`.

## Fix

- `src/gateway/health/collector.ts`: the deadline, the in-flight deadline checks, the remaining probe budget and `durationMs` use `performance.now()`. `awaitWithinDeadline` gets the same monotonic clock. The permit wait gets an `AbortSignal` that `scheduleAbsoluteDeadline` aborts on the monotonic deadline, so the shared permit pool (plugin-SDK exported) keeps its signature and behavior. Event timestamps (`ts`, `lastProbeAt`, session `age`) stay on `Date.now()`.
- `src/gateway/health/collector.deadline.test.ts`: one table test for a forward step (healthy probe kept) and a backward step (unfinished probe still expires at 7 s). Both fail on main.

Thanks @SunnyShu0925 for the fix.

## Evidence

Built Gateway in Docker, bundled Signal channel on `external-native` transport pointed at a local signal-cli stand-in. The stand-in slows or stalls `/api/v1/check` and steps `Date.now` inside the Gateway process only (system clock untouched).

| Scenario | main (a45e6b04003) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| +120 s step during a 3 s healthy probe, `openclaw health --verbose` | `Signal: warning - health collection timed out after 7000ms` | `Signal: configured` |
| same, raw `health` RPC | `sig1` `timedOut: true`, `durationMs` 123108 | `sig1` healthy, `durationMs` 3011 |
| same, no step (control) | `Signal: configured` | `Signal: configured` |
| -120 s step, 6 stalled accounts, `openclaw status --all` | `Gateway health: GatewayTransportError: gateway timeout after 8000ms` | no health error |
| same, raw `health` RPC wall time | 128975 ms | 8058 ms, all 6 accounts `timedOut` at 7000 ms |
| same, no step (control) | no health error | no health error |

`collector.deadline.test.ts` and `permit-pool.test.ts`: 13/13 pass on this branch; the new cases fail on main (forward: `timedOut` instead of `ok`; backward: collection never settles).

## Merge danger

Two-way door: no state, config or schema writes; a revert fully undoes it. Blast radius: Gateway health collection only (`health` RPC, `status --all`, `health`, post-update verification). No public API change.

## What Problem This Solves

Widget theme delivery still discovers chat and board frames by scanning the document for their CSS classes. That duplicates the frame owners and cannot provide an explicit teardown boundary.

## User Impact

Palette, accent, stylesheet, and light/dark updates keep reaching mounted chat and board widgets, including retained frames. Frame replacement and terminal disconnect release the old registration. No intended markup, style, selector, route, or lazy-loading change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing theme publisher already supports explicit iframe registration. Chat now registers each keyed frame at settlement and returns the release callback. The board owner registers the current loaded document when posting host state, retaining its exact target origin, and releases on frame replacement or disconnect.

The publisher no longer scans the document. It skips delivery while a registered frame is detached without deleting the registration: the mounting owner remains responsible for release, so a temporarily detached retained frame resumes receiving updates after reattachment. Existing Canvas, plugin, and discussion owners already supply cleanup.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| UI typecheck | Passed. |
| Targeted unit tests | 29 passed across the three changed test files. |
| Retention follow-up | All 6 publisher tests passed after adding detach/reattach coverage. |
| Targeted lint and formatting | Passed. |
| Startup comparison | Same-host base 337,500 B → head 337,481 B JS gzip; 1 CSS request / 38,500 B unchanged. Both strict performance runs pass. |

| Independent review | Complete implementation and all registration lifetimes reviewed through P2; scoped-clean, with final frozen-source verification passed. |
| Broad proof | `ci:full` covers every UI unit, Control UI E2E, browser-extension, and real-Gateway shard, including chat performance and retention. |

No markup or visual change is intended; no screenshot claim is made. No local E2E or external test lease.

### Refactor measurements

Compared with base `5e8ac91fbf62`, across the three changed production files, including the coupled chat and board mounting owners:

| Pattern | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `createEffect` | 1 | 1 |
| `createRenderEffect` | 0 | 0 |
| `untrack` | 1 | 1 |
| Direct event registrations | 0 | 0 |
| `querySelector(All)` | 2 | 1 |
| Owner capture/restoration | 0 | 0 |
| Production LOC | 1,642 | 1,640 |
| Test LOC | 1,402 | 1,471 |

The assigned `lib/widget-theme.ts` scope moves from one query to zero and retains no effect, render effect, snapshot, or direct listener. prs.title: fix(gateway): keep node worker tunnel exec deadline on the monotonic clock
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`invokeWorkspaceCommand` in `node-worker-tunnel.ts` seeded its retry deadline with `Date.now()` and recomputed the remaining budget with `Date.now()` before each idempotent retry. The transport consumes that budget on the monotonic clock, and the same call already arms a monotonic `AbortSignal.timeout`. A wall-clock step (NTP correction, VM or laptop resume) between the first attempt and a retry after a transient node disconnect therefore:

- forward step: the retry sees a negative budget and fails at once with `node worker workspace command timed out`, although the monotonic budget is almost unused;
- backward step: the retry sends the node an inflated `timeoutMs` (about 335 s for a 35 s command budget).

## Fix

Seed and recompute the deadline with `performance.now()`, the same clock as the transport and the abort signal. Both retry sleeps now use the same `remainingMs`. 3 production lines change; nothing else in the owner file measures a duration with `Date.now()`.

Thanks to @SunnyShu0925 for finding and fixing this.

## User Impact

An idempotent Gateway workspace command (disk-space probe, workspace inspection, manifest capture, reply media, device-folder validation) now recovers from a transient node disconnect after a wall-clock step instead of failing at once and retiring the session's node tunnel owner.

## Evidence

End to end, both trees built with `pnpm build` (Node 24.21.0, Docker): a real Gateway, a real `openclaw node run --session-host` node host, a session created with `sessions.create` (`worktreeSource: "empty"`) and placed on the node with `sessions.dispatch`. The node connects through a loopback TCP proxy. When the Gateway sends the session's idempotent disk-space probe (`worker.workspace.exec.v1`, `node -e ... statfs`), the proxy holds that frame, steps `Date.now()` by +300 s in the Gateway and node processes only (a preload; the system clock is not changed), and drops the connection. The node host reconnects by itself about 1 s later.

| Run | Result after the drop |
| --- | --- |
| main, +300 s step | Probe not retried. `Worker disk-space check failed (...): device worker node is not connected with the supervisor dialect` 110 ms after the drop (the post-dispatch drain error masks the `timed out` error). About 60 s later the Gateway sends `worker.environment.stop.v1` and two workspace drains for the session's environment. |
| main, no step (control) | Probe retried on the reconnected node with `timeoutMs=33536` and succeeded. No warning, no environment stop. |
| this PR, +300 s step | Probe retried on the reconnected node with `timeoutMs=33212` and succeeded. No warning, no environment stop. |
| this PR, no step | Probe retried with `timeoutMs=33522` and succeeded. |

Regression test (`node-worker-tunnel-authority.test.ts`, a +/-300 s step during a `DISCONNECTED` retry): on main the forward case fails with `node worker workspace command timed out` and the backward case sends a retry `timeoutMs` of 334895 against a 35000 budget; on this PR both pass. `oxfmt` and `oxlint` are clean on the changed files.

Proof limit: the drop and the clock step are injected (proxy and in-process preload); the Gateway, node host, placement and retry path are the shipped ones.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: process-local deadline arithmetic only; no persisted state, config, protocol or schema change, and a revert fully undoes it. Blast radius: idempotent workspace commands sent from a Gateway to node workers.

prs.title: fix(state): retain subset admission across one-shot writes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

One-shot existing-state SQLite writers repeatedly validate the same physical schema after reopening. Separately, warmed admission can cause an explicitly requested orphan-delivery recovery to skip its work and fail at final integrity validation.

## User Impact

Ordinary writers reuse completed schema admission. Explicit recovery still performs preservation-first repair, even after an ordinary writer warmed the database. Stored formats, schema, public options, authority checks, and transaction ownership are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The process-lifetime admission cutover in #174660 omitted the existing hashed subset key from #167739. Admit physical schema facts through the existing owner before BEGIN, then retain ordinary subset admission for process lifetime. Explicit QUICK/FULL policies remain connection-scoped as in #175662.

The review finding also exposed an existing coupling: recovery ran only after an uncached validation threw. Both the prior PR head and a serial exact-base control reproduced that failure. Requested recovery is work, not an admission fact. It now runs independently of the cache through the existing backup/recovery owner, preserving metadata validation, narrow repairable-error classification, rollback, and final integrity checks.

### Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

Ordinary reopen no longer polls already-admitted subset metadata. Unsupported external in-place metadata edits while the Gateway owns the database remain outside the #174660 ownership contract; tracked DDL, explicit verification, replacement, revocation, and restart retain their owners. No integrity, authority, or preservation guard is removed.

Net production LOC: +3; tests: +55. This narrow lifecycle/recovery bug fix is not cleanup-deletion credit.

## Evidence

The existing native one-shot regression verifies two persisted rows and zero repeated schema/metadata queries. Original serial controls observed 14 repeated queries on base, 14 with lifetime-only, 11 with admission-only, and zero with the complete fix.

The new warm-recovery regression failed on the published head at the final foreign-key check. With the repair it passes through the actual SQLite writer, verifies committed rows, and independently reads the preserved payload from the real backup. Complete existing-write owner suite: 17/17, 52.77s; suppression guard: 14/14, 43.44s. First-use cached-worker preparation took 317.713s on the shared host; these timings are not a performance benchmark.

Fresh independent P0-P2 review of the recovery repair, with complete determining owners supplied as context, found no accepted/actionable findings (0.98); final source verification passed. Author simplification retains the existing admission and preservation owners without another cache key, receipt, helper, or test-only seam.

Coordinator-required rebase onto 48c6cfe1d17aa3598c2f99d191f0eb134b07b433 was conflict-free and patch-identical, and the frozen install refreshed tsrs without authored dependency changes. Exact published b5a0349 CI completed successfully, but that is prior-head evidence only: the recovery repair requires new exact-head CI. No reruns were requested.

Refreshed targeted production/test typechecking with the native tsrs backend and focused type-aware core lint both pass without diagnostics. The duplicate standalone recovery probe was stopped before output rather than loading the same source graph again; it is not claimed as a pass. The complete owning suite above supplies the real native recovery/preservation proof. Import edges are unchanged; broad cycles/builds remain with exact-head CI under the coordinator's local CPU budget. No live Gateway, released-driver upgrade, operator database, or Phase E memory backend was touched.

prs.title: fix(audit): keep recording after a rejected metadata event
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The audit writer permanently rejects later metadata after one record cannot be cloned, and overflow pruning uses a separate cutoff read before deleting old records.

## User Impact

A rejected metadata record no longer disables later audit recording. Retention bounds, FIFO ordering, duplicate-source behavior, and shutdown settlement stay unchanged. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Put the retention cutoff in a scalar subquery of the existing bounded DELETE. Keep the existing transaction and eager PostgreSQL lock before its authoritative work. Remove the obsolete unavailable latch, duplicate progress classification, redundant readiness state, contention-counter wrapper, and retry lower clamp. Native Promise settlement and the existing retry owner already supply those guarantees.

When the cached retention count drifts above the durable count, a zero-row overflow delete refreshes the real count and expiry once. Later inserts then use the repaired owner state without repeating DELETE/MIN queries. A successful overflow deletion still refreshes the retained expiry boundary.

The removed `isOutboundMessageProgressInput` guard in `recordAuditEventInDatabase` had no runtime caller besides `src/audit/audit-event-writer.worker.ts:80–88`. That worker classifies progress at line 85 and routes it to `recordOutboundMessageProgressInDatabase` at line 86; only terminal audit events reach `recordAuditEventInDatabase` at line 88. Repository reference search confirms no second runtime caller.

The cold-open contention boundary, drain reentry guard, execution binding, identity projection, and unknown-outcome no-replay behavior remain. Audit metadata is still best effort: the rejected record is reported and dropped; later valid records continue. The two ordinary per-turn audit requests remain separate because their producers straddle model execution.

Production: +22/-43 lines (net -21). Tests: +205/-32 (net +173), including one shared SQLite/PostgreSQL fixture. Documentation: +1. Test routing: +1.

## Evidence

Formatting, type-aware oxlint on all six changed TypeScript files, and `git diff --check` pass. Two isolated Codex P0–P2 review rounds completed. The first was scoped-clean; the correction review found reused source IDs in the new count-drift fixture. Each event now has a distinct ID, so the regression reaches retention recovery rather than audit deduplication. Preparation-only interruptions did not produce additional model rounds. The prior-head run [39178651043](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39178651043) passed all selected jobs except PostgreSQL shard 1 and its aggregate: both new PG cases failed before assertions with `Missing PostgreSQL state admission`. This head adds the retention test to the database-hosted test registry, correcting that routing. The coordinator approved this exact registry addition. Final-head ordinary CI [39182445508](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39182445508) passes the changed-owner tests, type checks, lint, source contracts, and Madge. All three PostgreSQL shards pass in the exact-head supplemental run [39182457718](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39182457718), including the corrected retention-test routing. Its unrelated remaining jobs were cancelled after required evidence was collected. The mock-export ratchet failure at `src/cli/program/root-help.test.ts:33` matches current main [39182492985/job/117838287257](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39182492985/job/117838287257).

Head `d7b064463f4c92bb2512ac726637b5efb5fbfc9f` integrates main `e7db41f0c8e9ab25b4a4104474054e5201c8d22e`. All seven previously reviewed source/test/doc blobs remain byte-identical to PG-approved `812fbe05cbbe91703fe4f99991b6f1be275ae015`; the only additional change is the registry entry. Registry formatting/type-aware lint and native commit hooks pass. Shared-semaphore frozen installs completed successfully; tsrs `0.16.0-ts7.1.0-dev.20260929` is installed, and all type checks use repository lanes. Default pinned Bun is retained for local tests.

The count-drift regression requires one recovery insert, one zero-row delete, and one count/expiry refresh, then exactly one INSERT for each subsequent event. Each PostgreSQL regression has its own database lifecycle. The shared retention regression exercises overflow with sequence gaps, the exact retained window, duplicate replay, and the next sequence. It expects four audit-table statements instead of five for a cold overflow insert. A real queue regression checks valid-before, rejected-uncloneable, valid-after, shutdown drain, and persisted FIFO order. All three baseline regressions fail at the intended assertions: overflow uses five audit-table statements instead of four; an uncloneable event disables later records; count drift causes six statements for the next two inserts instead of two. All three candidate regressions pass under the default pinned Bun runtime. Final Knip [39182457718/job/117838199069](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39182457718/job/117838199069) has zero new findings: only FaceTime test exports `commandResult`, `mutedResult`, and `outgoingCall (ft)`, identical to scheduled main [39176649118/job/117820741086](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39176649118/job/117820741086).

Estimated, unmeasured workload impact: one fewer SQL statement per retention overflow; no change to ordinary warm-turn SQL, worker requests, or MAIN work. No latency claim. Combined workload counts are deferred to the coordinated SQLite/PostgreSQL census. Exact-head PostgreSQL review approved `d7b064463f4c92bb2512ac726637b5efb5fbfc9f`.

prs.title: perf(subagents): skip settled history during startup activation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway startup activates every retained subagent run even when only a few have unfinished work, so settled Swarm history adds recovery latency on every restart.

Related: #176550, #176573.

## User Impact

Subagent activation now visits active and recoverable runs while finished history stays cold and readable on demand. Active recovery, pending completions, and normal retention remain supported. No configuration, schema, or retention-policy change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The registry row owner now maintains a plain map of activation candidates on row replacement, deletion, and reset. Binding, requester restoration, reservation, resume, and recovery-only sweeps consume those candidates. This removes retained-history traversal and per-run yield machinery. Settled collectors keep their spawning turn ID for cancellation bookkeeping; that ID alone is not a completion obligation and no longer prevents payload compaction.

The candidate map avoids the generic latest-row index, whose unused latest projection would rescan an active bucket on updates (addressing the P2 review finding).

Cold rows have no per-run Gateway binding, so retention captures the registry's Gateway owner and revalidates it before session deletion. A present but expired row binding remains authoritative. The publication counter now counts observable recovery publications rather than ordinary binding; unchanged rows were already not republished by #176550.

Production delta: **+73 / −48 lines (net +25)**. The growth is the row-owned candidate map and captured retention authority needed to preserve readable/expiring cold history while removing repeated activation work. No competing activation path or new state store was added.

## Evidence

Two concurrent A/B pairs on an isolated Linux sandbox, holding an exclusive measurement lock, with baseline/head on separate 16-core halves and the halves swapped for pair 2. Each side used a fresh identical synthetic fixture: 5,000 sessions, 8,000 retained runs, exactly 3 active, and 7,200 collectors retaining their parent turn IDs. No startup metadata repair was needed. Baseline: `60d19b2225742543fae1cccb7a49ce767368b368`.

| Pair | Activation before → after | Paired difference | Time to ready before → after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 344.9 → 238.7 ms | −106.2 ms | 8,153.1 → 8,123.8 ms |
| 2, CPU halves swapped | 290.1 → 202.3 ms | −87.8 ms | 7,350.1 → 7,278.1 ms |

Median paired activation saving: **97.0 ms**, approximately **1.44× faster / 31% less time**. Activation candidates fell **8,000 → 3**, active count stayed **3 → 3**, and yield time fell **24.4/7.0 → 0 ms**. The corrected publication counter is zero on unchanged history. Time to ready is neutral (paired −29.4/−72.0 ms); readiness precedes asynchronous subagent recovery in this fixture.

The baseline and final candidate source-performance builds passed. All 271 shared runtime output files matched between the isolated baseline and candidate packages. All four measured Gateways reached readiness and completed recovery with zero outbound TCP attempts and clean shutdown. CPU load was recorded for context (pair averages 20.1%/15.4%, start skew 0/1 ms). An initial trial was rejected when background catalog refresh hit the network guard; fresh fixtures disabled that refresh for both builds.

Focused proof: the cold-history regression failed on the base and passes with the fix. Four changed/focused files passed **89 tests**, covering active-run resume, pending/suspended completion delivery, Gateway replacement, activation membership transitions, retained result reads, and collector expiry through the selected Gateway. Independent Codex review is clean through P2. Changed-file formatting and lint passed. The export-name collision guard passed, the two required closure files passed 22 tests, and `pnpm tsgo:core` passed using the native tsrs default. After the mechanical lint cleanup, the affected activation test passed again.

Retention already derives collector deadlines from completion time (60 minutes by default) and prunes eligible groups together. The restart regression verifies cold results remain readable through `agents.wait` and are removed from memory and SQLite after expiry. No production configuration or rows were inspected, so this does not attribute the reported retained-row count to a particular retention blocker.

CI follow-up: initial run [39181141375](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39181141375) caught two test assertions that still expected settled result text in the resident row. Those now inspect durable storage or use the public prepared-read API, preserving the complete receipt/cancellation assertions. The lifecycle file passed **235 tests**, the spawn production-boundary file passed **43 tests**, and the final plain-map memory file passed **23 tests**. The three-file repair received a fresh independent P2 review with no actionable findings; changed-file formatting and lint passed. The original typecheck remains the one targeted local lane; broad validation is PR CI-owned.

The initial run also failed the unrelated mock-export guard at `src/cli/program/root-help.test.ts:33` for `./subcli-descriptors.js`. The canonical guard reproduced that exact failure, exit 1, against main parent `46c2c45c2511104a2dcc1b1076cbdf95641c798f` using a separate index whose tree equals that commit (`9487731058ab7d200bf38b12851b0b243bb28408`): `GIT_INDEX_FILE=<baseline-index> node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-mock-exports.mts --base 46c2c45c2511104a2dcc1b1076cbdf95641c798f --no-merge-base --staged`. The guard and its 100 checked tooling dependencies matched that baseline byte for byte. Main subsequently fixed that guard in `e63269c28a22a6eec7c0758d54dc6dbe674e2886`; the required latest-main rebase includes it. No baseline, mock exception, or unrelated CLI source was changed in this PR.

Limitations: synthetic state uses 1 MiB of transcript text and approximately 40.6 MiB of databases. It reproduces the retained registry shape, not the production database volume or the reported 5.85-second absolute startup cost. Timing did not execute a real model turn or deliver a live channel completion; focused persistence/recovery tests cover those ownership paths. PR CI supplies broad validation; no Testbox lease was used.

Final reviewed head: `62365b87bdd53de54a72517e9393c93511844296`, rebased onto `e63269c28a22a6eec7c0758d54dc6dbe674e2886`. Both commits are patch-identical to their reviewed versions, and all six measured production source hashes match.

Final validation: [CI run 39183659120](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39183659120) and all required status gates passed on `62365b87bdd53de54a72517e9393c93511844296`; no inherited-failure exception or CI rerun was needed. The P2 thread is resolved. Squash-merged as `afa7fccb9a2f4483d404a6b64814afe5d001ca21`.

prs.title: improve: reuse SQLite capability checks during Gateway startup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway startup can create SQLite workers before the parent publishes native-library admission. Each worker then repeats the native version, extension-support, and iterator probes for the same loaded library.

## User Impact

Boot and restart reuse the process's native SQLite capabilities across module reloads and sibling workers. The WAL safety floor, library selection, database ownership, and configuration remain unchanged.

## Design and Removed Work

CLI and direct Gateway startup now complete native-library admission before the existing close-capability initialization and worker creation. The main thread also consumes the existing process-bound result after a module reload. A small startup composition module orders the two existing owners without a dependency cycle; it adds no shared buffer, synchronization protocol, schema, or worker request.

The redundant native probe triplet disappears from sibling workers. Separate helper processes still admit their own loaded library. Missing, malformed, or mismatched process/runtime/library facts still require admission. No security-effect check or cross-store transaction changes.

## Evidence

- Exact-head CI [39166077242](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39166077242) passed at `8511e0e72564`: 90 jobs passed and 25 were skipped. This includes the required gate, production/test types, lint, source contracts, architecture, database ratchets, and all three PostgreSQL conformance cells. Changed-file formatting, type-aware lint, and diff checks also pass. Exact-head Knip [39168848866, job 117797749313](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39168848866/job/117797749313) completed with 58 production / 33 full-tree / 0 script findings. All findings match main [39163574553, job 117782017361](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39163574553/job/117782017361), which has 58 / 34 / 0; there are no new findings. The two unused-file findings also match main. The earlier local full-tree scan timed out and is not counted as passing proof.
- All 102 tests across the five focused files pass. The regression launches a fresh process and two real sibling workers, counts native probes, and verifies both workers can query SQLite. Candidate: parent probes once, each worker zero times. Baseline: parent probes zero times before worker creation, each worker once. The main-module reload regression also fails semantically on the baseline. Gateway coverage proves admission precedes the startup lock without eager schema SQL.
- Two Codex review rounds are complete, with no remaining accepted P0/P1 finding. The second round's staging finding was resolved by committing the complete reviewed repair.
- Workload comparison stopped after confirmed local storage stalls; no completed baseline/candidate pair or measured saving is claimed. The retained baseline has 16 probe triplets across 14 processes; attribution predicts **boot −3 SQL and restart boot −3 SQL**, with requests and MAIN unchanged. Baseline boot was 352 SQL / 96 requests / 60 MAIN, restart boot 403 / 108 / 58, and warm turns 57 [57–58] / 16 [16–17] / 0. This baseline used a 15-second connected-idle window, so it does not prove long-idle behavior. Savings remain **estimated, unmeasured**; the combined campaign census owns the deferred workload comparison. No latency claim.

CI caught and we repaired an ineffective dynamic import in the initial design ([39164029897](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39164029897)). A later compact-install test failed before its assertion because its source workspace import was unavailable ([39165285107](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39165285107)); the fixture now uses canonical compiled subprocess declarations. Two local Gateway attempts timed out during fixture preparation; preparation now occurs during collection through the existing scoped SQLite owner, preserving the assertions. The repaired fixture and exact-head CI pass. A remote attempt ended during source preparation before allocation; it supplies no proof.

Production: **+8 net lines**, needed to order existing owners without a cycle. Tests: **+93 net lines**. Documentation: **+2 net lines**. Total: **+119/−16**.
