prs.title: refactor(ui): share mascot playback and update stream lifetimes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Mascot animation and update output retain feature-local synchronization that belongs with their existing canvas and stream-follow owners.

## User Impact

The mascot preserves its animation phase when visibility or reduced motion changes. Update logs and installation steps follow new output at the bottom, preserve deliberate scrollback, and reset following for a new run without replacing the scroll elements.

## Why This Change Was Made

The mascot derives one configuration identity and uses one effect to configure the canvas animator and synchronize playback. Visibility-only changes do not reset the tease timestamp. The existing stream-follow helper accepts an optional content trigger; the update view's two scroll regions use it, while Logs and Activity retain their existing event-driven scheduling. Host tags, CSS, routes, selectors and lazy boundaries are unchanged.

## Evidence

Exact comparison: base `56827d40f0dc2bed61e6dd3fe306f1a8d260d687`, head `01e7ccb26e3a6bcb78874926e11e2352fc5b9802`, same machine and Node 24.22.0.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Frozen install | Passed on base and head |
| UI typecheck | `pnpm tsgo:ui` passed with the default tsrs checker. Initial invocation stopped before checker startup on a stale lock left by the interrupted build; the exact task lock was released after verifying its owner and descendants had stopped, then the real check passed. |
| Focused tests | 16 update-view tests passed on the final rebased head with the resolved default pinned Bun runtime and `--maxWorkers=1` (42.01s). The unchanged mascot suite's 2 passing assertions are retained from the prior source; playback sources were unchanged by rebase. No Node override used for the final run. |
| Lint / format / isolated review | Passed; canonical isolated autoreview scoped-clean through P2 after one capacity-only retry. Four source hashes remain unchanged. |
| Production build | Base and head passed (`pnpm ui:build`, exit0 on both). Finalized assets passed sidecar validation and served the three capture states. |
| Strict performance | Both exact revisions fail the same two existing route budget names shown below. Startup stays within its budget; no threshold changed. |
| Visual behavior | Three synthetic 1440×960 states per side passed: mascot reduced-motion cycle, both update streams retaining scrollback, and both following a replacement run without starting an update. All six full frames inspected. Mascot frame identical; update frames differ only in ordinary build metadata. |
| Production Knip | `pnpm deadcode:knip` passed on the final rebased head, exit0, no findings (671.87s). |
| Broad CI | `ci:full` run 39182224508 attempt 1 completed: all 64 jobs are terminal. Every UI unit, Control UI E2E, real-Gateway, and security-fast job passed. The only failed roots are the two exact-base-matched checks below; the aggregate fails because of them. |

| Bytes (gzip) | Base | Head | Delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Startup JS (7 requests) | 337,540 | 337,549 | +9 |
| Startup CSS (1 request) | 38,500 | 38,500 | 0 |
| Chat boot JS (limit 1,490,000) | 1,492,084 | 1,492,137 | +53 |
| New Session boot JS (limit 1,050,000) | 1,050,194 | 1,050,253 | +59 |

The strict failures are `chat boot JS gzip` and `new boot JS gzip` on both the exact base and head. The small measured increases accompany the shared content-trigger option and retained configuration identity. This records the overruns; it does not claim a green strict check or change any budget. CI failure attribution still requires matching exact failing test names on main/base.

| Pattern / LOC | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Component `createEffect` | 3 | 1 |
| All effects including shared helper | 3 | 2 |
| `createRenderEffect` / `untrack` / direct listeners / DOM queries | 0 | 0 |
| Production LOC | 418 | 425 |
| Test LOC | 368 | 385 |

Survivors: `ui/src/components/openclaw-mascot.tsx:97` synchronizes the external canvas animator; `ui/src/lib/reactive/stream-auto-follow.ts:47` owns shared scroll synchronization. The feature count drops 66.7% in this focused checkpoint; the lane-wide 70% target remains separate. The seven added production lines replace duplicated scheduling admission with the existing owner and preserve animation timing.

The focused tests emit visible Solid strict-read diagnostics. Static review found complete dependency coverage and preserved live frame-delivery checks; diagnostics are not suppressed or claimed proven inherited.

## Screenshots

![Synthetic playback before and after: reduced-motion mascot, update scrollback, and new-run tail](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/98619811-0108-4c93-8b29-e9874ce0c9a2)

## CI failure attribution

The latest completed scheduled main run `39176649118` at `943e9af522a8e0070fc051a7052edd5c267dfeaf` passed both checks below. Attribution therefore uses separate executions at this PR's exact merge base `56827d40f0dc2bed61e6dd3fe306f1a8d260d687`, not the scheduled run.

| Failed check in run 39182224508 | Exact-base evidence |
| --- | --- |
| `mock-exports`: `src/cli/program/root-help.test.ts:33: ./subcli-descriptors.js` | Same signature, exit 1. Supported `--staged` mode read all source and manifests from an isolated index whose tree equals the base tree; all 95 helper/loader closure files matched that base. The changed flag alters source transport, so this is not claimed as a literal identical CLI invocation. |
| `chat boot JS gzip`: 1,491,341 B exceeds 1,490,000 B | The independently built exact base fails `pnpm ui:check-performance --json` with the same named check at 1,492,084 B. Host-specific byte totals differ from CI; the named failure and absolute threshold match. |

These are the only two failed root jobs in the completed run; `openclaw/ci-gate` is their failed aggregate. Native inherited-failure admission uses the exact-base proof above. The actual CI merge has only the four intended changed files, and recomputing its merge tree matched the tested tree exactly.

## Review disposition

The automated LOC-only P1 suggestion is declined: this campaign explicitly permits growth required by a shared primitive or correctness. The seven added production lines add the content trigger to the existing stream-follow owner and preserve mascot timing; there is no separate correctness finding in that suggestion. The complete change was independently reviewed through P2.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Local exec-policy, MCP, proxy capture, sandbox recreation, and model refresh repeat the admission check that their shared local-state owner has just performed synchronously.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. Commands retain the same online/offline routing, refusal behavior, cleanup, and authority checks after awaited work and before effects.

## Why This Change Was Made

`runWithLocalStateOwner` checks authority after loading config support and synchronously invokes `runLocal` through `AsyncLocalStorage.run`. Its config getter checks authority around config loading as well. Delete the six callback-entry assertions that repeat this admission without any intervening await or effect; the MCP callback consequently needs no async wrapper.

prs.title: fix(agents): use monotonic clock for ask_user question expiry
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an agent calls `ask_user`, the question expiry deadline was seeded and read with `Date.now()` (wall clock) at two layers — the tool-local budget in `ask-user-tool.ts` and the Gateway owner in `QuestionManager` — but consumed through `setTimeout` (monotonic), crossing clock domains. A wall-clock forward jump (NTP correction, sleep/resume) caused the question to expire before the user could answer, through both the direct `get()`/`list()` epoch comparison and the scheduled `expire()` wake.

- Problem: `expiresAtMs` was seeded/read with `Date.now()` but consumed by `setTimeout`; wall-clock jumps stretch or shrink the timeout at either layer.
- Solution: both layers now use monotonic clocks — the tool-local budget uses `performance.now()`, and `QuestionManager` retains a private `expiresAtMonotonicMs` seeded with `scheduler.monotonicNow()`. The scheduled wake re-checks the monotonic deadline and reschedules if it has not passed. The client-visible `expiresAtMs` remains an epoch timestamp.
- What changed: `ask-user-tool.ts` — 4 sites switched to `performance.now()`; `question-manager.ts` — private `expiresAtMonotonicMs` on `QuestionEntry`, used in `get()`, `runPendingContinuation()`, `resolveWithCommit`'s `assertCurrent()`, and the `expireScheduled()` wake; `gateway-scheduler.ts` — exposed `monotonicNow()`.
- What did NOT change: client-visible `expiresAtMs` (epoch), RPC `timeoutMs`, delivery state machine, any persistence.

## Why This Change Was Made

The maintainer (obviyus) reproduced the end-to-end flow: advancing only the Gateway's `Date.now()` by 120s caused a 30s question to expire early via `question.list` → `get()` (~0.7s). After that path was made monotonic, the scheduled `expire()` wake still terminated it at ~17s because `GatewayScheduler.remaining()` takes `min(wallDelay, monotonicDelay)` and a wall-clock jump makes `wallDelay` negative.

A follow-up review found a deeper race: when a wall-clock jump wakes the callback while `resolveWithCommit()` awaits its write, the committing guard ran before the rearm, so the scheduler deleted the one-shot wake with no replacement — a later rejected commit left the question pending with no expiry job. `expireScheduled()` now re-arms the remaining monotonic budget before the committing guard.

## User Impact

The `get()`/`list()` direct checks and the scheduled `expire()` wake are now monotonic, so a wall-clock forward jump no longer causes premature expiry. A wall-clock wake overlapping an in-flight commit no longer loses the expiry job: a failed commit still reaches automatic terminal expiry without a later read.

## Evidence

Native-timer proof through the production `QuestionManager` + `GatewayScheduler` (native `setTimeout`/`performance.now()`). A 30s question is seeded, `Date.now()` is forward-jumped 120s, then a short trigger trips the scheduler's wall-clock-due wake. The wake fires at ~1.8s (monotonic) but the question stays pending. A second scenario covers the commit-overlap race:

```console
$ node --import tsx/esm proof-scheduler-wake.ts
[proof-jump] PASS: scheduled wake re-checked the monotonic deadline and did not expire early
[proof-commit] PASS: wall-clock wake overlapping an in-flight commit re-armed expiry; failed commit reached terminal expiry
```

Running-Gateway E2E through a live WebSocket transport (not in-process). A Gateway started with `pnpm openclaw gateway run --auth token --port 19876 --dev`; a CLI client connected over WebSocket, completed the token-auth handshake, and called `question.request` → `question.get` through production RPC dispatch:

```console
$ node proof-gateway-e2e.cjs
[proof-e2e] WebSocket connected to running Gateway
[proof-e2e] Authenticated connect handshake complete
[proof-e2e] question status before jump: pending
[proof-e2e] wall clock jumped forward by 120s
[proof-e2e] question status after jump: pending
[proof-e2e] PASS: question stayed pending after +120s wall-clock jump
[proof-e2e] question status after ~3s: expired
[proof-e2e] PASS: question expired within 2s budget (monotonic)
```

Gateway-level regression tests (66 passed, 5.72s wall-clock):

```console
$ npx vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/question-manager.test.ts src/gateway/question-manager-monotonic-deadline.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  66 passed (66)
   Duration  5.72s
```

The wall-clock-jump regression now also advances past the remaining monotonic budget and asserts expiry, proving the re-armed job is not lost (per maintainer suggestion). Lifetime is **awake time**: a suspend that advances only the wall clock does not consume the window — the question stays pending past public `expiresAtMs` and expires on the monotonic budget.

Tool-local tests remain green: `ask-user-tool.test.ts` (29 passed) plus the wall-clock regressions split into a sibling `ask-user-tool.wall-clock.test.ts` (2 passed) so the original file stays under the lint line budget. The outbound delivery suite (`deliver.question-generation.test.ts`, 4 tests, 58s) also passes.

prs.title: refactor: remove redundant proxy setup checks and freezes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Proxy setup repeats checks already guaranteed by its decimal parser and keeps a frozen agent-options object solely to spread one boolean.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. Proxy bypass matching, malformed-input rejection, and forced HTTP/1 dispatch remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Inline `allowH2: false` in the same override positions and delete the private frozen agent-options object. Once an octet matches one to three decimal digits, its numeric value is already a finite nonnegative integer; the upper bound remains. The mandatory decimal CIDR prefix likewise needs only its upper-bound check.

No SQL, worker request, transaction, schema, SDK, or authority changes. No new fallback or accepted security edge. Production delta: +5/-9, net -4 lines; tests unchanged. Simplification pass retains only the direct deletions and the HTTP/2 rationale.

Candidate ledger:

| Candidate | Decision | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| F117 / C27013 | REMOVE | Private frozen HTTP/1 options only feed spreads into fresh objects. |
| F118 / C27014 | KEEP | Pinned Undici dispatch runtime supports allowH2 but DispatchOptions omits it. Restore the existing adapter unchanged; no type workaround. |
| F114 | REMOVE | Decimal octet grammar already proves integer and nonnegative; retain 255 bound. |
| F116 | REMOVE | Decimal prefix capture already proves nonnegative; retain 32 bound and unavailable-network rejection. |
| Remaining parser/dispatcher guards | KEEP | External environment and URL input, missing runtime support, and HTTP/1 policy remain real boundaries. |

## Evidence

Both permitted Codex autoreview rounds completed scoped-clean at P0/P1, including the final narrowed diff. Format, type-aware lint, and diff checks passed. Initial CI exposed TS2353 in the global-dispatcher inline change, so that file was restored to base. Final-head CI run [39182512690](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39182512690) completed with 41 successful jobs, 28 skipped, and only the inherited mock-export ratchet plus aggregate gate failing. Types, lint, source contracts, Madge, owner tests, T1 (178 to 178), and dialect ratchets (0 to 0 changed-file groups) passed. Main was integrated to include the upstream CLI export cleanup identified by the first Knip scan. prs.title: fix(gateway): restore reserved agents after deferred startup
prs.body:
Fixes #176355
Related: #164799

## What Problem This Solves

Existing reserved system-agent databases can be skipped or refused during deferred Gateway startup because they have no authored agent entry.

## User Impact

Existing `openclaw` and `crestodian` databases receive startup inspection and preparation without artificial `agents.entries` members. Non-reserved unowned registered stores remain skipped, preserving #164929. No configuration or schema migration is required; integrity, ownership, and deletion checks remain enforced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Gateway listing, native database targets, and scheduler eligibility share one configured-plus-reserved roster. Configured ACP/session-store claims remain eligible. Expected native targets require no filesystem probes. Doctor/port inventory restricts expected native additions to configured agents and uses its existing asynchronous directory discovery and registry for unconfigured reserved stores, avoiding phantom missing roots. The duplicate listing map and membership accumulation are removed.

Current-main source confirms that reserved targets are excluded before deferred preparation; this is not a current-main live reproduction of the older release's sticky refusal. This addresses the reserved-agent part of #164799, not version-change admission timing. #176355 was closed as a duplicate, not as fixed. Thanks to @yozakura-ava for the discriminator and workaround evidence.

## Evidence

- Exact-head [PR CI run 39174464392](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39174464392) remains red on `9089e6bd9fdf45db71dea136bde4ade775be1aee` only for the carried-forward session-row timeout and aggregate gate below. The backup job passed its one authorized retry. Production/test types, lint, guards, docs, UI E2E, and all three PostgreSQL conformance lanes passed. PR CI remains the test and typecheck gate per maintainer policy.
- Regressions: `prepares the deferred reserved %s store without a configured roster entry` covers both reserved IDs; the existing HTTP fleet fixture exercises real scheduler eligibility, recovery, readiness, bounded opening, and preservation of corrupt unowned-store bytes. Target-selection layouts cover reserved ownership; `resolves reserved startup targets without probing their files` protects request-thread target resolution. The port fixture includes discovered `crestodian` while excluding absent `openclaw`; existing Doctor snapshots remain unchanged.
- Changed-file oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` passed. Final independent Codex branch autoreview through P2: scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- ClawSweeper's latest exact-head review has no actionable code findings and confirms the scheduler P2 and request-thread probe P1 are resolved. The requested backup CI attribution is documented below. Earlier PostgreSQL failures exposed phantom reserved inventory roots; final-head PostgreSQL 3/3 passes without changing Doctor snapshots.
- [Node job 117814483735](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39174464392/job/117814483735) repeats the 120-second `server.session-row-deltas.integration.test.ts` timeout. This is inherited: the identical test times out in [scheduled main run 39172446197, job 117808338766](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39172446197/job/117808338766). Attempt 2 carries that result forward as [job 117831434765](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39174464392/job/117831434765), with the original execution timestamps; it was not retried.
- [Original backup job 117814483869](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39174464392/job/117814483869) hit a pre-existing timing-dependent scratch allocation race, detailed below. No matching failure was found in the last three scheduled main runs, so this is not claimed as an inherited CI failure. The exact requested command, `gh run rerun --job 117814483869 --repo openclaw/openclaw`, was issued once; [replacement job 117831434028](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39174464392/job/117831434028) passed on the unchanged head in 196 seconds. Its Bun `core-runtime-infra-diagnostics-state` shard passed all 84 tests across five files; the formerly failing external-config case passed in 636 ms.
- Production +44/-33 (net +11), tests +62/-16, docs +6/-0. Necessary growth completes scheduler eligibility and separates expected native additions from physical inventory. No unrelated code was deleted to meet a quota.
- Live Gateway proof, Crabbox/Testbox leases, local typechecks, and production-revert negative controls were intentionally skipped per maintainer policy. The follow-up explicitly allowed only `src/infra/backup-config-capture.test.ts` locally: it passed three times per runtime on both the PR head and merge base (12 file runs, 192 test executions, zero failures). No broader local suite was run.

Deferred work retains the original agent ID, paths, environment/state root, and startup lifetime. Current-config path checks, signal/runtime/admission guards, database identity checks, and deletion fences remain at their effect boundaries. No new session binding, authority snapshot, or scheduling limit is introduced.

<details>
<summary>Backup failure diagnosis and scoped local comparison</summary>

The failing allocation creates a random `openclaw-backup-owned-*` directory, then awaits boundary/stat work before acquiring its token (`backup-scratch.ts:34–48`). Concurrent backup maintenance can discover that directory, create its missing token with `allowMissing: true`, and retire it with `PRAGMA user_version=1`. The creator then sees an existing retired token and throws. The original CI log shows `backup-create.test.ts` archive cases overlapping the failure at 23:00:17.509 UTC. [Commit 5588de47 / #175983](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/5588de47ba5cbec1cbd5bd997b446b8f2b27014e) removed allocation retries and explicitly described the reclaimer-before-`BEGIN IMMEDIATE` window.

`backup-create.ts`, `backup-scratch.ts`, and `sqlite-staging-token.ts` are identical between head and merge base. The test imports the changed port inventory through `backup-sqlite-snapshot`, but the failure occurs at scratch allocation (`backup-create.ts:477`), before snapshot collection (`:490`) reaches that inventory. Backup planning still uses unchanged `listAgentIds`; the added roster import contains constants and a `Set`, with no token disposal or module-level retirement. Preflight is dynamically imported by the later admission diagnostic. None of the changed code receives the newly generated scratch path before token acquisition. No code was changed for this failure; the passing retry does not repair the underlying race.

Only this file was run, using the documented runtime selector:

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/backup-config-capture.test.ts
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/backup-config-capture.test.ts
```

All commands used the task's isolated temporary directory. Node was 26.12.0; Bun was the repository-pinned 1.4.4 fork. Each completed run passed all 16 tests. Wall times include runner preparation and verification.

| Revision | Runtime | Passed / failed | Wall seconds per completed run |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Head `9089e6bd9fdf` | Node | 3 / 0 | 172.40, 202.73, 250.05 |
| Head `9089e6bd9fdf` | Bun | 3 / 0 | 335.65, 215.66, 245.30 |
| Merge base `e2a97a7e0dba` | Node | 3 / 0 | 539.27, 335.10, 271.90 |
| Merge base `e2a97a7e0dba` | Bun | 3 / 0 | 173.81, 140.09, 142.89 |

One earlier cold Node attempt was interrupted during runner preparation/verification after 776.31 seconds, without a test verdict; it is excluded from pass/fail totals. All test wrappers have exited, and the clean task branch is restored.

</details>

prs.title: fix(slack): inherit root action gates in account overrides
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes partial Slack account-level `actions` overrides discarding channel-level restrictions for gates the account did not name.

With this configuration

```json
{
  "channels": {
    "slack": {
      "actions": { "messages": false, "pins": false },
      "accounts": {
        "work": { "botToken": "xoxb-...", "actions": { "reactions": true } }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

`work` resolved to `{ "reactions": true }`. Missing gates default to enabled, so discovery advertised disabled message and pin actions, and the runtime gate let them proceed to later checks. Target policy and API authorization still apply.

## User Impact

Account overrides now change only named gates. `actions: {}` previously reset every gate to enabled and now inherits channel-level gates. Anyone relying on replacement must explicitly enable the desired account gates. Root-only and account-only settings resolve as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The five-file delta adds `actions` to the nested merge list in `extensions/slack/src/accounts.ts`, three tests and one sentence in `docs/channels/slack/access-control.md`. The schema already accepts partial objects. Both consumers are unchanged.

The docs add a previously undocumented contract. Replacement predates refactor `ff759f991e6f`, but the inspected history establishes neither its introduction nor an intended reset contract. Earlier introduction-date and affected-release-range claims are withdrawn.

## Decision Needed

A maintainer must decide whether partial or empty account `actions` should inherit unset keys or replace the whole block. Acceptance remains pending.

## Evidence

On October 18, head `ec516390d97512019f058caafcda267b35d00317` merged cleanly against main `55ce16b61cd5822f98be360d8297aca7de4353f3` in a merge check. No code changed and no tests were rerun.

Prior evidence records main `2d6f7a3052a0` merged with upstream test deletions retained, 28 tests in 74.17 seconds, changed-file checks in 1103.52 seconds and no actionable review findings through P2. Those records were not independently reconstructed today. Exact-head [CI 38024921612](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38024921612) passed, including `openclaw/ci-gate` and `security-fast`. Its published-driver job was skipped.

### Historical behavior checks

Earlier published results compare `fbae6ae9573f54f1504f40476ee2c9af0a5c635a` with baseline `cf0f8f90a7b6317a5a618ac5d5a7e69e01c050d2`. They were not rerun or independently reconstructed today.

- The account regression expects `work` to resolve to `{ messages: false, pins: false, reactions: true }` and the default account to retain the root object.
- With all root gates false and only account reactions enabled, discovery lists exactly `send`, `react`, and `reactions`.
- The runtime regression rejects `listPins` with "Slack pins are disabled" before any API call, while a `react` control runs.

The recorded baseline failed all three regressions. A discovery-only change left account and runtime checks failing. The runtime test uses a sibling file to respect the line limit.

Built CLI results with the example config and placeholder tokens were

| Check for account `work` | Baseline | Fixed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Capability discovery | exit 0, all 15 actions | exit 0, `send`, `broadcast`, `react`, `reactions`, `member-info`, `emoji-list` |
| `message pins --channel slack --account work` | exit 1, "Slack read target channel is not allowed." | exit 1, "Slack pins are disabled." |
| `message react --channel slack --account work` | exit 1, "Slack read target channel is not allowed." | same exit and error |

The unchanged reaction error proves gate passage, not delivery. The recorded default-account control without an override failed at the pins gate on both builds.

Historical records report 165 focused tests, 170 files/3124 extension tests, 145 files/2739 source tests, and passing type, lint, format, docs and assertion-safety checks, not current-head reruns.

### Supplementary forward upgrade on October 11

The PR declares `2026.9.9`. October 11's stable baseline was `2026.10.1`. Candidate [`b682ad79204c`](https://github.com/marmar9615-cloud/openclaw/commit/b682ad79204c585b345e1628746679812df81a00) applies the exact five-file delta to published [`2026.10.5-beta.1`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.10.5-beta.1), parent `f283c3c71226c2e1d9ca06b11972f8bdb3969bd8`. This proves release-line integration, not an exact-head forward upgrade. No release or extra PR was published.

[Run 38155906533](https://github.com/marmar9615-cloud/openclaw/actions/runs/38155906533), harness [`53f5600b88877`](https://github.com/marmar9615-cloud/openclaw/blob/53f5600b88877ac7d81610cd5f0b4773a7b6ed0c/proof.mjs), passed 47 checks, 28 tests in 52.040 seconds and changed-file checks in 918.444 seconds. Packaging passed. Source and harness reviews found no actionable P0 through P2 findings.

Both fixtures used published core and official Slack `2026.10.1`, all root gates false, and `work` set to `{ reactions: true }` or `{}`. Normal core plus external Slack retained the `@openclaw/slack@latest` selector. A sealed local registry supplied the matching companion without fabricated ownership.

Captured command and result excerpts are

```text
$ openclaw update --channel beta --tag /app/package/candidate.tgz --yes --no-restart --json
both fixtures exit=0, status="ok", run.status="succeeded"
before.version="2026.10.1", after.version="2026.10.5-beta.1"
slack plugin status="updated", sync.errors=[], integrityDrifts=[]

$ openclaw channels capabilities --channel slack --account work --json --timeout 1000
before update, both fixtures exit=0, all 15 actions
after update, partial exit=0, ["send","broadcast","react","reactions"]
after update, empty exit=0, ["send","broadcast"]
```

Installed core matched `b682ad79204c585b345e1628746679812df81a00`. External Slack loaded at `2026.10.5-beta.1` with matching SHA-512 integrity in both install records. Account actions, `channels.slack`, `gateway` and `plugins` were unchanged. Whole-file equality is false. Only empty webhook migration arrays for `telegram`, `feishu` and `nextcloud-talk`, `agents.entries.main`, `meta.lastTouchedVersion`, `wizard.lastRun*` and requested `update.channel` changed.

No live actions were sent. Offline probes returned expected connection-refused errors. These checks cover update completion and discovery, not live delivery or managed Gateway activation. Restart was skipped. Dummy plaintext credentials caused plugin status `warning`. Automatic database restoration was unavailable because an unknown writer changed databases after capture. Snapshots remained and cleanup was deferred. Rollback, complete data-resource recovery and production health were not proven.

Recorded SHA-256 identities follow. The [transcript, command records, plugin indexes and config snapshots](https://github.com/MarMarLabs/openclaw/actions/runs/38155906533/artifacts/11709788486) expire November 10, 2026.

| Item | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- |
| Exact source delta | `40103994e51b960236893dbede3245cadbc168172524a9dfee6390e2664c80a9` |
| Candidate core | `f4c232fab8b16189ecea85d24fef545bdaab14ec70fba4a0704b646dbb4e76aa` |
| External Slack | `b82815544cd80c9aaa14b87590fb6f33c20419d4632ba11cb607ca839202bc2b` |
| Registry manifest | `ef974ec5c6325aeb58cbd015c71dd45cb6cfdd90f4acca7727dc6910b53e9d80` |

Earlier attempts [38155267259](https://github.com/marmar9615-cloud/openclaw/actions/runs/38155267259) and [38155468679](https://github.com/marmar9615-cloud/openclaw/actions/runs/38155468679) stopped on harness environment problems before updater fixtures ran. The latter had passed the 28 focused tests.

### Exact-head downgrade failed

[Run 38151741290](https://github.com/marmar9615-cloud/openclaw/actions/runs/38151741290) built and installed the exact PR head with `--bundle-plugin slack`. This custom `2026.9.9` package contained matching Slack source, unlike stock core. Its SHA-256 was `8f59b0067b4f6d39b4cf780f9e41c34bab27da713f3644525984357cc290e8d2`.

The baseline used published core `2026.10.1`, commit `e178c39e9aae3fa440735217f9aef9574f286677`, and official Slack `2026.10.1`. Action configs matched the cases above. The update command omitted `--channel beta`. Candidate action lists matched the forward results. Explicit account actions and the Slack, Gateway and plugin sections were preserved.

Both updater fixtures failed with exit 1. This was a downgrade/replacement from `2026.10.1` to `2026.9.9`, not forward-upgrade proof. Installation, candidate checks, startup canary, swap and configuration repair succeeded, but plugin handling reported `Plugin "slack" has no authoritative package-owner metadata`. Backup retention and recovery were unverified, the updater returned `state-migrated-no-rollback`, and a later cleanup import failed. The internal plugin index was not captured, so the deeper cause remains unestablished. Whole-file configuration preservation is not claimed.

These package proofs ran in isolated CI containers without repository or environment secrets or live Slack actions. The [transcript, commands, identities and configs](https://github.com/marmar9615-cloud/openclaw/actions/runs/38151741290/artifacts/11707372026) expire November 10, 2026. The forward result neither erases this failure nor establishes its cause.

prs.title: fix(plugins): stop reload waits from blocking agent runs indefinitely
prs.body:
Related: #173061

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a parked `openclaw plugins reload <id> --wait` can block new agent runs across the Gateway indefinitely while `openclaw status` looks healthy.

## User Impact

Explicit waits now share a ten-minute admitted-work drain budget. On expiry the reload reports an error and rolls back to the previous generation without cancelling its admitted work. Ordinary reloads retain their 60-second budget. New runs can still wait during maintenance; later cleanup and recovery retain their separate deadlines. Ctrl+C and connection-disconnect cancellation remain available.

`status` shows the affected plugins, reload phase, and waiting or failure reason; `status --json` includes the existing owner's `pluginReload` record and drain deadline. CLI help and reload guidance explain the Gateway-wide admission impact. The generic isolated-agent setup timeout wording is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The drain owner returned no deadline for `waitForDrain`, while the hot-reload owner held the prepared-model admission gate until the transaction settled. This is present in the merged main baseline and traces to #158688. The repair applies the existing ten-minute plugin lifecycle wait budget at the drain owner, shares one deadline across drain stages, and uses the existing rollback and gate-release path.

Status projects the plugin-runtime generation owner's facts directly. Maintainer cleanup removes extra age state, the inferred `newRunsBlocked` flag, duplicate projection tests, and a second Gateway boot. The existing reader fixture covers status before, during, and after rollback. No new config, schema, SDK surface, detached work, or background side effects are introduced. Existing request ownership checks, observer cancellation, and rollback custody remain authoritative.

Original fix by @yxshee; maintainer cleanup completes the bounded-wait fix and simplifies status and regression coverage.

## Evidence

PR CI is the test and typecheck gate per the maintainer proof policy (October 13, 2026: “relax testing and trust PR CI, just lint”). Real CLI/Gateway behavior proof, latest-stable upgrade runs, Crabbox/Testbox leases, local tests/typechecks, and negative controls are intentionally excluded by that policy. ClawSweeper's request for additional real behavior proof is therefore not being pursued. The contributor's earlier live observations apply to the original status-only revision, not the repaired implementation.

Regression coverage submitted for CI:

- `server-plugin-reload.recovery.test.ts`: existing `explicit drain wait preserves %s beyond 60s and can %s` matrix adds `retained work / time out` and `active call / time out`. Fake timers verify the 600-second deadline and error, rollback, continued old-generation service, released replacement reservation, and unchanged siblings. Existing completion and cancellation cases remain.
- `server-plugins.lifecycle.readers.test.ts`: `reports plugin reload status and serves metadata throughout an admitted call drain` uses the existing Gateway RPC fixture to check absent → waiting with deadline → absent after rollback, while model/chat metadata remains available.
- `status-overview-rows.plugin-reload.test.ts`: `shows pending plugin reloads in the status-all overview` covers human rendering in a small standalone test. Existing status-scan cases cover CLI projection; the config-reload timeout fixture is migrated to the explicit budget argument.

Local static checks on the implementation: changed-file `oxfmt` and `oxlint` passed with all core rules. The initial full-config lint could not load a missing UI-only Solid dependency. The successful run used a temporary config retaining all core rules and omitting only the UI-only JS override; no repository configuration or dependency installation changed. `git diff --check` passed.

Docs-only follow-up: changed-file `oxfmt docs/cli/status.md` and `git diff --check` passed. The wording was checked against `finishReload` and the existing post-rollback status assertion. GitHub could not start CI on the docs-only commit because main had changed the reload owner. Main `48c6cfe1d17aa` was merged without rebasing; the single import/type conflict kept main’s simplified owner and this PR’s shared status type. Formatting and whitespace checks passed after resolution. Candidate head: `25f2a2e1be2a438790498b35966c98455bc9cbd7`.

Isolated Codex autoreview: **scoped-clean through P2**, no accepted/actionable findings on implementation candidate `634e079efe5b4c1a77ee425bceb8fbc6f97c9248`. It confirmed the deadline, observer cancellation, rollback, and hot-reload admission release in `finally`. Historical implementation head `bb7bd7b06311f629744bd943c15eacb26c360737` passed [CI run 39171714634](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39171714634), including changed test shards, production and test typechecks, lint, docs, guards, UI E2E, and all three PostgreSQL conformance shards. That run is prior-head evidence.

**Final-head CI (`25f2a2e1be2a438790498b35966c98455bc9cbd7`):** [run 39178339357](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39178339357) completed with 56 passing jobs and the same inherited timeout in [`checks-node-changed-compact-large-22`, job 117825849392](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39178339357/job/117825849392); the aggregate CI gate failed consequently. The Bun shard's `src/gateway/server.session-row-deltas.integration.test.ts > capable and legacy sockets produce identical session payloads and consumer state` timed out at 120 seconds, followed by stalled-worker cleanup errors. This also fails identically in the latest scheduled main run checked, [39176649118](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39176649118), [`checks-node-compact-small-1`, job 117820741627](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39176649118/job/117820741627), on main head `943e9af522a8e0070fc051a7052edd5c267dfeaf`. The docs, lint, production/test typechecks, other selected tests, and all three PostgreSQL conformance shards passed. No change-caused CI failure was found; the inherited timeout was not repaired or rerun in this PR.

**Inherited CI failure on head `e885f9876d7b0f5650fd4f6044ada24b079950b4`:** [CI run 39174282509](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39174282509) failed in [`checks-node-changed-compact-large-21`, job 117813914521](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39174282509/job/117813914521). Its Bun shard times out after 120 seconds in `src/gateway/server.session-row-deltas.integration.test.ts > capable and legacy sockets produce identical session payloads and consumer state`, followed by stalled-worker cleanup errors. The identical test and 120-second timeout occur in [scheduled main CI run 39172446197](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39172446197), [`checks-node-compact-small-1`, job 117808338766](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39172446197/job/117808338766), on main head `4812f059427b2db240fbefd3af4411c9d701538a`. This is an inherited failure outside this diff; no unrelated repair or rerun was made. The PR run's aggregate gate failed as a consequence; 56 other jobs passed.

Test cost: two additional fake-clock cases and assertions in existing fixtures, plus one small standalone rendering case, with no additional Gateway boot or real sleep. prs.title: fix(process): stdout.pause() is ignored on a spawn broker command after ready()
prs.body:
Closes #162135

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `stdout.pause()` is ignored on a broker-launched command when it is called right after `await child.ready()`.

## User Impact

User impact: a caller that pauses a command's output gets it paused, so it can apply backpressure instead of receiving data it asked to hold.

## Why This Change Was Made

While the pipe is held, the broker now records the caller's last `pause()` or `resume()` and replays it after Node's own release-time resume. Before, it replayed only a past `resume` event and Node then resumed the stream anyway.

## Evidence

Real broker (`createSpawnBrokerHost`, real child process, Linux, Node 24): pause right after `ready()`, child writes `held`, then `resume()`.

- before: paused stream still delivers `held` (`received while paused = "held"`)
- after: `isPaused = true`, `received while paused = ""`, then `received = "held"` after `resume()`

A readable listener's own `resume()` now wins over an older held `pause()` (regression test in `pipe.test.ts`).

Test from the issue, on current `main`: `2 failed | 10 passed`. With the fix: `12 passed`. Both cases fail on `isPaused()`.

`pipe.test.ts` covers a `pause` or `resume` made right after release, which a first version of this fix got wrong (found in review, fails if the wrappers are restored early).

`src/process/spawn-broker`: 25 files, 118 tests pass. `oxlint`, `oxfmt` and `tsgo:core` clean. `check:changed` passed every gate and all core test graphs except `ui-components`, which my shell timeout killed at 25s (this change does not touch UI).

Test wall (`--maxWorkers=1`): `handoff.test.ts` 12s (2 cases added), `pipe.test.ts` 2s.

autoreview could not run (Codex and Claude not logged in). An independent read-only review found the post-release gap above; fixed.

prs.title: fix(anthropic): reject altered local session cursors
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Local Claude session and transcript pagination accepts altered spellings of an OpenClaw-issued cursor, including appended junk, padding, and extra JSON fields.

## User Impact

Valid local continuation cursors still advance to the next page. Altered or non-emitted local cursors are rejected with the existing Anthropic error labels. Paired-node cursors remain bounded opaque strings and are forwarded unchanged across version-skewed nodes. No stored-data migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Anthropic local offset codec now delegates to the existing shared session-catalog paging owner. This removes the permissive local decoder instead of maintaining a second canonicalization policy.

The patch is refreshed onto `44cdd57720efa937c35a40037a2ac290c854f042`. Current main's line-cap gate also requires moving the two existing transcript short-read/pagination tests and their private helpers into a sibling test file; their assertions and the shared fixture builders are preserved.

## Evidence

Final candidate: `dd9577292229490d61f65a27c77f3790e062a94f`.

### Real Gateway and CLI

The built Gateway and `pnpm openclaw gateway call` ran against an isolated on-disk two-session Claude catalog at exact revision `d3ec47248aad31eec285e205fd22fbfae9681f66`. The final candidate has byte-identical production code; its only differences from that proof revision are the test-layout changes described above.

- `sessions.catalog.list`: first page returned the newer real fixture session; its issued cursor returned the older session.
- `sessions.catalog.read`: first page returned the two newest transcript items; its issued cursor returned the two older items without overlap.
- Appending `!`, appending `=`, and adding an extra JSON field were each rejected in both flows. Catalog responses contained host error `LOCAL_READ_FAILED`; transcript calls exited 1 and the Gateway reported `INVALID_REQUEST`, with `transcript cursor is invalid`.

This exercised plugin registration, Claude file discovery, Gateway handlers, authenticated WebSocket transport, and the CLI. Only synthetic data was used. Update checks, telemetry, and hosted model-catalog refresh were explicitly disabled; state and processes were cleaned up. The supported memory-bounded `qaRuntime` build passed, including the CLI bootstrap guard and 53 built-module/doctor-closure checks.

### Regression and static checks

- Restoring the unchanged main decoder under the final split tests makes exactly the two cursor-rejection cases fail because the promises resolve instead of rejecting. Restoring the fix makes all 42 catalog/transcript tests pass across both files: 43.9 seconds wall time, approximately 3.3 seconds test execution; the new transcript file's two cases take 28 ms.

- Changed-file type-aware lint, formatting, plugin import-boundary checks, line-cap/max-lines guards, and `git diff --check` pass.
- The assertion-safety baseline was regenerated with the canonical shrink-only command; only the Anthropic parser row changes from 5 to 3.

prs.title: refactor(cron): reuse mutation inventory rows
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A guarded cron mutation loads its job inventory, then repeats a point lookup for grant-generation fields and reads every job name again before returning the committed result.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. Cron mutations use fewer database statements while preserving job names, definition generations, retained grants, and mutation authority.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing transaction-owned inventory: include the grant-definition projection and raw SQL names, pass the loaded row to the existing upsert contract, and update the names map after successful canonical writes or physical deletions. The guarded worker returns that map. No new cache, owner, request, transaction, or schema is introduced.

Unsupported-delivery rows retain their definition-equality check; malformed rows keep their raw SQL names. UTF-8 normalization matches SQL binding. Retained-grant floors, generation predicates, conflict checks, commit/rollback publication, and final authority remain unchanged. Generic save modes retain their separate final name/fingerprint reads. Change-save hooks own receipts/runtime state, not definitions or grants; production callers provide canonical job identities rather than aliasing several raw IDs to one stored ID.

## Evidence

Two isolated Codex review rounds found no actionable P0–P2 issues. PostgreSQL owner review approved `1a4c39c4d9a08f664dc2f7468e56afbdbcd1d2fe`; its sole requested follow-up documents that repeated upserts of a canonical job would need the preceding write's generation copied into the inventory. The follow-up is comment-only and covered by that approval.

[CI 39182635642](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39182635642) completed with 40 successful jobs, including all selected changed tests, production/test types, lint, source contracts, architecture, and worker/dialect ratchets. The only failure and aggregate failure are the inherited mock-export rule at `src/cli/program/root-help.test.ts:33`: main `7d4233353cf` reproduces the identical diagnostic in [39182492985 / job 117838287257](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39182492985/job/117838287257). Initial CI correctly caught a test expectation that declarative convergence renamed a job; the fixture now expects its documented preserved name.

Canonical [Knip job 117838746071](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39182644247/job/117838746071) reports zero production/script unused exports and zero unused files. Its three full-tree FaceTime test-helper exports exactly match [main job 117820741086](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39176649118/job/117820741086), with no new findings. Supplemental UI checks also reported missing Swedish translations (outside this diff, not claimed inherited) and a chat-size budget violation with identical base/candidate output (+0 B); these are non-required for this change. Remaining supplemental work was cancelled after required evidence completed.

The real-worker inventory regression fails on baseline production at the intended `add: expected 3 to be 1` SELECT-count assertion, then restores the candidate bytes. Current-head CI supplies the green proof. Local candidate reruns were retired after CI completed; no aggregate local pass is claimed. The local partial `check:changed` run passed worker/dialect/mock-export/format checks and reported three untouched UI max-lines suppressions; full static evidence comes from CI.

The regression checks names and durable generations across add, disable, rename, and delete. Expanded service tests cover repeated definition changes and retained name resolvers, including malformed/unsupported rows and SQL string normalization. Required current-main integration was conflict-free and preserved all six reviewed cron files.

Source-derived savings are **estimated, unmeasured**: canonical guarded add/update removes two SELECTs; delete removes one. Requests, transaction envelopes, and MAIN statements are unchanged. A queued Testbox was cancelled before executing tests. Per the campaign's queued-capacity policy, workload pairs defer to the combined census; this PR makes no phase-total or latency claim.

Production +18/-8 (net +10, including the review-requested comment); tests +149/-5 (net +144). The small production increase carries already-read facts instead of issuing two redundant queries. No SDK or update/Doctor/migration/plugin-loading/service-lifecycle implementation change.

prs.title: feat(matrix): add configurable read receipt timing
prs.body:
Related: #110603
Related: #25840

## What Problem This Solves

Matrix currently marks accepted inbound messages read as soon as processing starts. Operators cannot keep messages unread when OpenClaw intentionally stays silent, suppresses a final payload, or fails to deliver its reply.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a configurable `readReceiptMode` at channel and per-account scope:

- `immediate` preserves the existing behavior and remains the default.
- `on-reply` sends the receipt only after an actual visible final Matrix delivery succeeds.
- `off` disables inbound read receipts.

The `on-reply` path observes successful normal delivery or successful draft/live-preview finalization rather than relying on queued-final counts. Suppressed, empty, `NO_REPLY`, and failed-delivery outcomes therefore remain unread. Read-receipt errors remain non-fatal and do not alter inbound dedupe commit behavior.

## User Impact

Matrix operators can choose read-receipt timing globally or override it per account without changing existing installations. Accounts left unset continue to send immediate receipts.

## Live Matrix behavior proof

Run against a real Synapse homeserver with two real accounts (bot + sender) in an
unencrypted private room, driving this branch through the real Matrix channel
(`openclaw gateway`) with the `claude-cli` agent backend.

Timings are measured from the sender's `/sync`: `t=0` is the inbound send, "receipt"
is the bot's `m.read` for *that* event, "reply" is the bot's visible message.

| # | `readReceiptMode` | Scenario | Reply | Receipt | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `immediate` | normal turn | 6.55s | **0.55s** | receipt **6.01s before** reply — existing behavior preserved |
| 2 | `on-reply` | normal turn | 7.64s | **7.70s** | receipt **0.06s after** reply |
| 3 | `off` | normal turn | 7.75s | none | reply delivered, never marked read |
| 4 | `on-reply` | agent returns `NO_REPLY` | none | none | stays unread |
| 5 | `on-reply` | delivery fails (403) | none (send blocked) | none | stays unread |

Scenarios 1 and 2 are the same code and the same room, with only the config changed:
the receipt moves from 6.01s *before* the reply to 0.06s *after* it.

### Scenario 1 — `immediate` (baseline, unchanged)

```
[   0.00s] SENT      $<inbound>
[   0.55s] RECEIPT   m.read from bot for OUR event
[   6.55s] BOT REPLY $<reply>
ordering: receipt came BEFORE reply (delta -6.01s)
```

### Scenario 2 — `on-reply`, successful visible delivery

```
[   0.00s] SENT      $<inbound>
[   7.64s] BOT REPLY $<reply>
[   7.70s] RECEIPT   m.read from bot for OUR event
ordering: receipt came AFTER reply (delta +0.06s)
```

### Scenario 3 — `off`

```
[   0.00s] SENT      $<inbound>
[   7.75s] BOT REPLY $<reply>
receipt : NONE (stayed unread)
```

### Scenario 4 — `on-reply`, suppressed final (`NO_REPLY`)

The turn ran to completion; it was not skipped. `outBytes=8` is exactly `NO_REPLY`:

```
[agent/cli-backend] cli exec: provider=claude-cli model=<model> trigger=user
[agent/cli-backend] claude live session turn: durationMs=1710 rawLines=13 outBytes=8
[diagnostic]        message processed: channel=matrix outcome=completed duration=2703ms
[turn/execution]    visible channel turn dispatched with no queued reply payloads
```

No read receipt was sent. The inbound message stayed unread.

### Scenario 5 — `on-reply`, failed final delivery

The bot's power level was held below `events_default` so the send is rejected. The agent
did produce a reply (`outBytes=9`, distinct from the 8-byte `NO_REPLY` above); only the
*delivery* failed:

```
[agent/cli-backend] cli exec: provider=claude-cli model=<model> trigger=user
[agent/cli-backend] claude live session turn: durationMs=1670 rawLines=13 outBytes=9
[matrix]            final reply failed: M_FORBIDDEN: MatrixError: [403] You don't have
                    permission to post that to the room. user_level (0) < send_level (50)
[turn/execution]    visible channel turn dispatched with no queued reply payloads
```

No read receipt was sent — confirming the `finalReplyDeliveryFailed` path leaves messages
unread rather than acknowledging an undelivered turn.

### Coverage note

The live run covers channel-scope `readReceiptMode` across all three modes and all three
`on-reply` delivery outcomes. Per-account override inheritance is covered by unit tests
(`extensions/matrix/src/matrix/accounts.test.ts`) rather than the live run, since it
exercises config resolution rather than delivery timing.

## Note on the `accounts` schema

`channels.matrix.accounts` moves from `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())` to a record of
`.passthrough()` objects so the per-account `readReceiptMode` can be typed and validated.

- Unknown per-account keys are still passed through unchanged, so there is no
  silent-stripping regression for existing account settings.
- One behavior change: account values that are not objects (`null`, string, number,
  array) previously validated and now fail. Nothing in the repo uses such a value, and
  they were never functional at runtime — `resolveMatrixAccountsMap` and
  `findMatrixAccountConfig` already coerced them to `{}`.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test:extension matrix`: 117/118 files and 1473/1480 tests passed; the seven failures were isolated to the unrelated `reaction-events.test.ts` runtime-state fixture and passed immediately when rerun alone (9/9).
- Focused changed-surface tests: 176/176 passed across Matrix config schema, account resolution, and inbound handler tests.
- `pnpm build`: passed.
- `pnpm lint:extensions`: passed with 0 warnings and 0 errors.
- `pnpm config:channels:check`: passed.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` on changed files: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

Tests cover all three modes, the backward-compatible default, channel inheritance and account overrides, invalid account values, successful visible final delivery, suppressed final delivery, delivery errors, and missing event IDs.

Implementation and review were AI-assisted; the final diff was independently reviewed and all actionable findings were addressed before submission.

prs.title: fix(sqlite): normalize BLOB-stored text during STRICT migration
prs.body:
Closes #110186

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw rebuilds legacy SQLite tables as STRICT tables during shared-state, agent-state, and plugin-store upgrades. The migration copied source values unchanged. A legacy BLOB value stored in a declared TEXT column therefore reached the STRICT destination as BLOB and stopped startup or Doctor with `cannot store BLOB value in TEXT column`.

The earlier version of this PR also added a separate unique-index preflight. That duplicate policy became large and still allowed `ON CONFLICT REPLACE` to discard rows after conversion.

## Why This Change Was Made

`src/infra/sqlite-strict.ts` is the one migration owner used by runtime open, Doctor repair, agent databases, memory, proxy capture, Logbook, Workboard, and plugin state.

The owner now carries each canonical column's declared type into the copy and applies `CAST(... AS TEXT)` only to TEXT destinations. The copy uses `INSERT OR ABORT`, which overrides table conflict policies so a normalized key collision rolls back the whole transaction instead of deleting a row.

The redundant unique-index introspection and its 20 implementation-specific tests are removed. SQLite's destination INSERT remains the authoritative constraint check.

## User Impact

- Databases with valid legacy BLOB-stored TEXT values upgrade to canonical STRICT TEXT storage.
- A conversion collision fails atomically and preserves all legacy rows.
- No schema version, configuration, protocol, or public API changes.

## Evidence

### Current-main red

Baseline `107a39797825e93e4021329f92e4057ed53bc2f9` was current `origin/main` when captured. Later main movement did not touch the migration owner or its test.

Product command: `pnpm test src/commands/doctor.strict-sqlite-migration.test.ts`

Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m1dqa899s8z5898mczahzdpp`, [Actions run 33474045433](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33474045433): **RED**.

Observed Doctor result: `Failed migrating shared state database schema ... Failed migrating SQLite table workspace_path_aliases to STRICT`.

Owner-boundary command: `pnpm test src/infra/sqlite-strict-blob-text-upgrade.proof.test.ts`

Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m1dnr4xzpmye30d2herw02ex`, [Actions run 33472292698](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33472292698): **RED**.

Observed cause: `cannot store BLOB value in TEXT column __openclaw_strict_migration_0_entries.value`.

### Contributor-head safety red

Untouched contributor head `cfc78fcba3dcc79b14fb4fed9278e507212c8a14` was tested with two legacy rows that collide after TEXT conversion under `UNIQUE ON CONFLICT REPLACE`.

Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m1dnwss9vtm6em7qsxm9efre`, [Actions run 33472451779](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33472451779): **RED**. The migration returned successfully instead of rolling back, and its existing test expected one of the two rows to disappear.

### Repaired-head green

Head `2d10bb5dbf1dda78544d532d168511e56ccda8bf`:

- `pnpm test src/commands/doctor.strict-sqlite-migration.test.ts src/infra/sqlite-strict.test.ts`: **17/17 passed** on Testbox `tbx_01m1dqjfqapzjf5c517n3sex79`, [Actions run 33474334890](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33474334890).
- Targeted `oxfmt`: **passed**.
- Targeted `oxlint`: **0 warnings, 0 errors** on the same Testbox.
- Pre-commit Codex Sol Autoreview after the product-path repair: **no P0 findings**, confidence `0.99`.

The branch-only changed gate stopped on eight expired compatibility records outside this PR. The same plugin-boundary gate passed on the current-main baseline with zero eligible records on Testbox `tbx_01m1dpgge87ej4w1hvxq3kvpvw`, [Actions run 33473143480](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33473143480). Pull-request CI validates the current-main merge tree.

## Attribution

Original repair and reproduction: @wangyan2026. Maintainer simplification and landing: @obviyus.

prs.title: fix(path): keep frontmatter values the strings they were written as
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`docs/cli/path.md` promises that Markdown frontmatter values are **string leaves** and that values are literal. `openclaw path set` and frontmatter insertion do not honor that: `formatFrontmatterValue` (`extensions/oc-path/src/oc-path/frontmatter-format.ts`) writes any value without structural characters unquoted, so YAML decides the type instead.

Base (`e2a97a7e0db`), real CLI, isolated state dir:

```
$ openclaw path set 'oc://note.md/[frontmatter]/version' '1.10'
{"ok": true, ...}
$ head -3 note.md
---
title: note
version: 1.10          → any YAML reader sees the number 1.1
```

- `1.10` → number `1.1`
- `0123` → number `123`
- `true` → boolean, `~` / `null` → null
- `- draft` → `note: - draft`, which is **not parseable**: the entire frontmatter block (including keys the user did not touch) becomes unreadable, and for a skill file `parseSkillFrontmatter` then throws, so the skill stops loading.

The command reports success in every one of these cases. Same class as #173099 (an edit changing content it does not own), on the write side.

## Fix

`formatFrontmatterValue` now quotes unless the value **reads back as the identical string** through `parseDocument` (the same `yaml` parser that owns frontmatter in this module):

```ts
function readsBackAsString(value: string): boolean {
  const node = parseDocument(`value: ${value}`).get("value", true);
  return isScalar(node) && typeof node.value === "string" && node.value === value;
}
```

The existing trim/leading-quote/structural-character checks stay, so this only adds quoting where the written form would change type or break the block. Ordinary values are unchanged: `café`, `$1`, and `plain value` still write bare. Insertion (`[frontmatter]/+key`, `universal.ts`) uses the same formatter and gets the same guarantee.

There is no single-correct-solution problem here: a denylist of `-`/`~`/`true` can never cover `1.10`, `0123`, `0x1F`, `1_000`, or hyphen-leading values, so the round-trip predicate is the only rule that holds for arbitrary strings. `1_000` stays bare because this parser reads it back as the same string.

Classification: behavior-preserving for existing valid output, behavior-completing for the documented string-leaf contract.

## Evidence

### Shipped CLI run (no Gateway, no credentials)

Environment: Node v24.18.0 in `lexiflow-all:latest`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` isolated per run, plugin enabled with `openclaw plugins enable oc-path`, files a user owns (`note.md` in a work directory). Commands run through the repo's own CLI entry. Base tree = `git archive` of `e2a97a7e0db`; head tree = base + this file (`01d7f458b84a56e80e74e8137e5ca5d6` → `2d9d4657f816054328be06c3d1cfd547`), everything else byte-identical.

| Command | Base file line | Base parse | Head file line | Head parse |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path set …/version 1.10` | `version: 1.10` | `1.1` (number) | `version: "1.10"` | `"1.10"` (string) |
| `path set …/note "- draft"` | `note: - draft` | `PARSE-ERROR: Unexpected block-seq-ind on same line with key` | `note: "- draft"` | `"- draft"` (string) |
| `path set …/version 0123` | `version: 0123` | `123` (number) | `version: "0123"` | `"0123"` (string) |
| control: `path set …/note café` | `note: café` | `"café"` (string) | `note: café` | `"café"` (string) |

The control row is the no-over-quoting proof: valid plain text stays bare and byte-identical on both trees. Parsing was done with the repo's pinned `yaml` (`parse()` over the raw frontmatter block), not by re-reading through the tool.

Raw capture, base:

```
##### case1: set version to 1.10
version: 1.10
parsed version = 1.1 (number)
##### case2: set note to '- draft'
note: - draft
PARSE-ERROR: Unexpected block-seq-ind on same line with key at line 3, column 7:
##### case3: set version to '0123'
version: 0123
parsed version = 123 (number)
```

Head:

```
##### case1: set version to 1.10
version: "1.10"
parsed version = "1.10" (string)
##### case2: set note to '- draft'
note: "- draft"
parsed note = "- draft" (string)
##### case3: set version to '0123'
version: "0123"
parsed version = "0123" (string)
```

### Regression tests

`pnpm test extensions/oc-path/src/oc-path/tests/edit.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`

- Base production code + new tests: **7 failed | 13 passed** — every type-changing value (`1.10`, `0123`, `true`, `~`, `null`, `- draft`) and the insertion case fail; the ordinary-string cases and all pre-existing tests pass.
- Head: **20 passed (20)**.

New cases assert both the written line and the parsed value: `parseYaml(frontmatter).<key>` must be the exact string that was set, so a future formatter that drops the quoting fails here.

## Not tested

Frontmatter values written through `openclaw path insert` on a file that has no frontmatter block yet (the `+key` path that prepends `---`) — the formatter is shared, and the insert case above covers the quoting decision, but I did not capture a separate CLI run for the no-frontmatter file shape. Flow-style and multi-line values keep their previous quoting behavior and are not changed by this diff.

prs.title: fix(outbound): keep newline-mode paragraphs as separate outbound units
prs.body:
Fixes #109032

## User-facing bug

With `chunkMode: "newline"` configured, automatic visible replies from the Codex agent runtime can collapse multiple intended paragraphs into a single WhatsApp bubble, while the OpenClaw runtime delivers the same response shape as separate bubbles under identical channel configuration.

## Root cause

`chunkByParagraph` (src/auto-reply/chunk.ts) splits on blank-line boundaries but then **packs adjacent paragraphs back into one chunk whenever they fit under the transport limit**. The OpenClaw runtime path streams block-by-block — the planner sees one block per call, so packing never has two blocks to join. The Codex runtime hands `planOutboundTextMessageUnits` (src/infra/outbound/message-plan.ts) the full reply text in one call, so its blank-line-separated paragraphs get packed into one outbound unit → one bubble.

The transport-size limit was doing double duty as a packing target. Newline mode's paragraph boundaries encode the author's visible-reply boundaries; a limit should only *split* oversized payloads, never *join* logical blocks (exactly as the issue states).

## Fix

- `chunkByParagraph` gains a `packAdjacent` option (default `true` — every existing caller keeps current behavior).
- `chunkMarkdownTextWithMode` forwards the option for the markdown path.
- The outbound planner's `newline` branch — the one place where logical block boundaries must survive — passes `packAdjacent: false` for both text and markdown chunker paths.

Length-splitting of oversized single paragraphs is unchanged, fence handling is unchanged, and all other chunker consumers (Slack/Telegram/Matrix/Feishu/Mattermost/plugin-sdk streaming paths) are unaffected by default.

Two existing `deliver.test.ts` expectations pinned the old packing behavior ("Line one\n\nLine two" → 1 send; "Alpha\n\nBeta" packed); they are updated to the issue-expected behavior with comments referencing #109032.

## Targeted tests

- `chunk.test.ts`: `packAdjacent: false` keeps paragraphs separate; still length-splits an oversized paragraph; does not join across fence-preserved boundaries.
- `message-plan.test.ts`: two blank-line paragraphs → two units, for both text and markdown chunker modes.
- `deliver.test.ts`: end-to-end `deliverOutboundPayloads` produces one send per paragraph in newline mode.

## Real behavior proof

Real environment: branch checkout at `8e3700901e` (based on current main `c08ce42cef`), Node v22.23.1.

Driving the actual production planner (`planOutboundTextMessageUnits`) via tsx with the issue's config shape (`chunkMode: "newline"`, WhatsApp-scale `textLimit: 4096`):

```ts
import { planOutboundTextMessageUnits } from "../src/infra/outbound/message-plan.ts";
import { chunkText } from "../src/auto-reply/chunk.ts";

const text = "First short paragraph.\n\nSecond short paragraph.";
const units = planOutboundTextMessageUnits({
  text, textLimit: 4096,
  chunker: (t, limit) => chunkText(t, limit),
  chunkMode: "newline", overrides: {},
});
console.log("units:", units.length);
for (const [i, u] of units.entries()) console.log(`  [${i}]`, JSON.stringify(u.text));
```

Before fix (HEAD `c08ce42cef`) — the collapsed single bubble from the issue:

```text
units: 1
  [0] "First short paragraph.\n\nSecond short paragraph."
```

After fix (`8e3700901e`) — separate bubbles matching the OpenClaw-runtime behavior:

```text
units: 2
  [0] "First short paragraph."
  [1] "Second short paragraph."
```

Verification against the committed head (`git status` clean): `tsgo` core / core-test / extensions all exit 0; `deliver.test.ts` 159/159, `message-plan.test.ts` 6/6, `chunk.test.ts` 74/74; `oxlint` clean on all touched files.

## Not tested / known gaps

- Not exercised over a live WhatsApp connection (no channel credentials); the issue is labeled `clawsweeper:source-repro` and the proof above drives the exact production planner code path that feeds WhatsApp delivery.

## AI-assisted disclosure

This patch was prepared with AI assistance, with source-level reproduction, targeted regression tests, and real planner-invocation proof as shown above.

prs.body: Closes #107928 ## What Problem This Solves The chat composer footer renders compact status values — `claude-opus-4-8 · Off · 10%` — without any labels, `title` attributes, or tooltips. A sighted user hovering over "Off" has no way to discover it represents the thinking/reasoning level, and hovering over "10%" in the context ring shows "Open context usage details" rather than explaining what the percentage measures. This affects the main chat composer footer (`ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-composer.ts`). ## Why This Change Was Made Both values already had complete accessible descriptions via `aria-label` — they existed for screen readers but were not surfaced to sighted users via hover. The fix reuses existing localized strings as `title` attributes — no new i18n keys, no new concepts, no layout changes, and no behavioral modifications. Changes: - `chat-composer.ts`: replaces the generic "Open context usage details" title with the actual context usage summary, keeping "Open context usage details" as a second line - `chat-model-controls.ts`: adds a focused title that labels the thinking level value, explaining what "Off" refers to ## User Impact - Hovering over the thinking-level value in the model selector (e.g. `Off`) now shows: "Chat thinking level: Off" - Hovering over the context usage percentage (e.g. `10%`) now shows two lines: "Thread context usage: 46k of 200k (23%)" followed by "Open context usage details" - Screen reader behavior is unchanged — existing `aria-label` values are preserved - All localized languages are fully supported since the change reuses existing translation keys ## Evidence ### Before | Model/reasoning trigger | Context usage ring | |---|---| | | | | No tooltip on hover. "Off" meaning is ambiguous. | Tooltip shows "Open context usage details" — tells what clicking does, not what the value means. | ### After | Model/reasoning trigger | Context usage ring | |---|---| | | | | Tooltip explains "Chat thinking level: Off". | Tooltip shows "Thread context usage: 0 of 200k (0%)" followed by "Open context usage details". | ### Validation - `pnpm format:check` — format clean - `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` — i18n clean (no new keys added) - `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-composer.test.ts` — confirm no regressions - `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-controls.test.ts` — confirm no regressions - `git diff --stat`: 2 files changed, 2 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-) --- This PR is AI-assisted. prs.title: feat(plugin-sdk): expose bounded status projections from command-status
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #76759. Plugin authors building status integrations had no public types for the gateway `/status` payload: an external plugin (`lossless-claw#516`) guessed the session-row shape from formatted output and navigated fields that do not exist (`sessions.byAgent[].entries[].usage.*` instead of `sessions.byAgent[].recent[]`), so its number extraction returned `null` on every field. Without a public type, this drift recurs for every status-consuming plugin.

## Why This Change Was Made

The previous revision re-exported the host `StatusSummary`/`SessionStatus`/`HeartbeatStatus` types verbatim. ClawSweeper's review correctly rejected that: `StatusSummary` is a mutable host aggregate with transitive gateway, channel, task, audit, plugin, and degraded-secret details, and freezing it into the public SDK would make evolving host-owned nested shapes an implicit compatibility commitment (the old test even had to cast `tasks`/`taskAudit` through `unknown` to compile).

This revision defines **bounded SDK-owned projections** in `openclaw/plugin-sdk/command-status` instead — the smallest shape status-consuming plugins actually need:

- `StatusSessionRow` — one session row: identity (`agentId`, `key`, `sessionId`, `updatedAt`) plus token usage (`inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `totalTokens`, `remainingTokens`, `percentUsed`, `contextTokens`, `model`, `flags`).
- `StatusSessionsProjection` — the session portion of a `/status` payload (`count`, `recent[]`, `byAgent[]`).
- `StatusHeartbeat` — per-agent heartbeat schedule state.

Drift protection runs in the other direction now: `src/plugin-sdk/command-status.types.test.ts` compiles projection functions from the real host types (`SessionStatus → StatusSessionRow`, `StatusSummary["sessions"] → StatusSessionsProjection`, `HeartbeatStatus → StatusHeartbeat`), so renaming a projected field on the host side breaks the build loudly — with zero `unknown` casts. Host-only fields stay free to evolve.

## User Impact

Third-party plugins can `import type { StatusSessionRow, StatusSessionsProjection, StatusHeartbeat } from "openclaw/plugin-sdk/command-status"` and bind the exact session/heartbeat data the `/status` RPC exposes, without copying host internals or acquiring an implicit contract over unrelated host aggregates. Types only — no runtime surface, no startup cost.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/plugin-sdk/command-status.types.test.ts` — green; the test is a compile-time assignability contract from real host types plus behavioral assertions on projected values.
- Plugin SDK surface gate `scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mts --check` — green with the `+3` budget entry ("SDK-owned command-status projection types for plugin status consumers").
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` — green (format, oxlint, tsgo core + test shards, `api-baseline` test 22/22, boundary guards).
- Real consumer proof against the built package (fresh `pnpm build` on this head `e06332c90de`): a standalone strict `nodenext` TypeScript project outside the repo resolving `openclaw/plugin-sdk/command-status` binds all three projections and compiles with **exit 0**:

  ```ts
  import type { StatusHeartbeat, StatusSessionRow, StatusSessionsProjection } from "openclaw/plugin-sdk/command-status";
  export function summarizeStatus(sessions: StatusSessionsProjection): string {
    const rows: StatusSessionRow[] = sessions.recent;
    return `${sessions.count} sessions\n` + rows.map((r) => `${r.key}: ${r.totalTokens ?? "?"} tokens`).join("\n");
  }
  ```

  Runtime probe of the built subpath: `import("dist/plugin-sdk/command-status.js")` exposes exactly `buildCommandsMessage`, `buildCommandsMessagePaginated`, `buildHelpMessage` — the projections are type-only and correctly absent at runtime.
- Branch was rebased onto current `main` (post pnpm-12 bump) and squashed to one commit carrying the projection design.

prs.title: fix(signal): reject hex/exponent text-style span offsets
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Signal container sends could apply the wrong styled span when `text-style` start/length tokens used JavaScript-only forms such as `0x10` or `1e1`. Those tokens were coerced with `Number(...)` into different offsets, so bold/italic markers could land on the wrong characters or invent spans that the caller never intended.

## Why This Change Was Made

Parse `text-style` `start`/`length` at the canonical Signal container translation boundary (`containerRpcRequest` → `/v2/send`) with the same `parseStrictNonNegativeInteger` helper already used for container quote timestamps. The parser lives in `client-container-text-style.ts` so oversized `client-container.ts` stays LOC-neutral.

Boundaries: no config keys; no native signal-cli path; incomplete `start:length:style` entries still drop the same way.

Collision check: searched open PRs for `path:extensions/signal/src/client-container.ts` and `parseStrictNonNegativeInteger text-style` — **0** competing PRs. Open Signal PRs #101380 / #100906 do not touch `text-style` `Number()` parsing.

## User Impact

- **Before:** `0x10:4:ITALIC` silently styled offset 16; `1e1:2:BOLD` silently styled offset 10; fractional lengths like `1.5` were accepted.
- **After:** Non-decimal tokens are dropped (same drop path as incomplete entries). Ordinary decimal spans such as `0:4:BOLD` are unchanged. All-invalid lists omit `text_mode=styled` and keep the plain message.

## Evidence

Exact product head: `5904fe91e4f642e338c56a04735812cae92fd1ef`

Real-container proof run (fork Actions, product sources identical to product head; proof branch only adds the harness):  
https://github.com/Pick-cat/openclaw/actions/runs/29426993121  
Proof checkout: `83dd475df702295cbc654bcf84f6e231326f403f` = `5904fe91e4f642e338c56a04735812cae92fd1ef` + proof-only files.

Image: `bbernhard/signal-cli-rest-api:latest` (`MODE=native`, about version `0.100`)

```text
node=v22.22.3
head=83dd475df702295cbc654bcf84f6e231326f403f
real_container=http://127.0.0.1:8080

[case 0] real container /v1/about
  ok: /v1/about HTTP ok
  info: status=200
  info: body={"versions":["v1","v2"],"build":2,"mode":"native","version":"0.100","capabilities":{"v2/send":["quotes","mentions"]}}
  ok: /v1/about returns JSON
  info: keys=build,capabilities,mode,version,versions
  info: version=0.100
  info: build=2
  ok: containerCheck(ok) against real image
  info: containerCheck status=200 error=null

[case 1] current-main Number() negative
  ok: Number("0x10") path yields start=16
  info: raw=0x10:4:ITALIC Number(start)=16 Number(length)=4
  ok: Number("1e1") path yields start=10
  info: raw=1e1:2:BOLD Number(start)=10 Number(length)=2
  ok: Number("1.5") path yields length=1.5
  info: raw=0:1.5:BOLD Number(start)=0 Number(length)=1.5
  ok: strict helper rejects same hex token
  ok: strict helper rejects same exponent token
  ok: strict helper rejects same fraction token

[case 2] positive — parseContainerTextStyleEntry rejects non-decimal
  ok: parseContainerTextStyleEntry("0x10:4:ITALIC") returns undefined
```
