prs.title: fix(daemon): repair JSON-quote-corrupted service env files through doctor (#103804)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #103804. Generated LaunchAgent service env files can carry values wrapped in a literal JSON quote pair inside the shell quotes (`export AWS_REGION='"us-east-1"'`). The shell delivers the quotes as data, so consumers break (`Region not accepted: region=""us-east-1""`). The corruption also self-perpetuates: the install plan reads raw process env (`collectConfigSecretRefServiceEnvVars` → `params.env[key]`), so any shell or service that inherited the corrupted value faithfully re-persists it on the next restage — which is why the issue reports hand-edits "persist until the next env file regeneration".

## Why This Change Was Made

The previous revision healed values inside the runtime reader (`launchd-plist.ts`), gated on `OPENCLAW_SERVICE_MANAGED_ENV_KEYS` membership. ClawSweeper's review rejected that twice over, correctly: managed-key membership is not value-format provenance (a legitimate quote-bearing env-backed SecretRef would be silently altered on every read), and legacy files written before the metadata existed — exactly the population carrying the corruption — took the early return and never healed. It was also a runtime fallback reader, which repo doctrine forbids ("legacy shapes normalize only in doctor/migration code").

This revision is a full redesign:

- **The reader stays lossless.** The runtime shim is gone; runtime never rewrites values.
- **Doctor owns the repair**, at the env file's format owner (`launchd-service-files.ts`): `detectLaunchAgentEnvFileJsonQuoteKeys` (read-only) and `repairLaunchAgentEnvFileJsonQuotes` (line-based rewrite that strips exactly the wrapping quote pair; every other line passes through byte-for-byte, file mode stays 0600, and the rewrite is convergent — a second pass is a no-op).
- **Doctor warns on the always path** (`maybeRepairMacGatewayServiceEnvQuotes`, wired into the gateway-services health runner): a healthy gateway with broken provider credentials must still surface this, so it does not hide behind the unhealthy-gateway repair flow. The warning names the file and keys (never values) and the fix command; the rewrite runs behind the standard `confirmDoctorServiceRepair` prompt (`doctor --fix` applies it). Both the gateway and node LaunchAgent labels are swept.
- **Legacy files heal** (review finding 2): detection is shape-based, so files without the managed-keys metadata are covered.
- **The feedback loop is named to the operator**: after healing, doctor flags any healed key whose corrupted value is still inherited by the current shell, so a reinstall from that shell does not re-persist it.

Named tradeoff (review finding 1): a deliberate operator value whose bytes are exactly a wrapping quote pair is also stripped — but only through the operator-confirmed doctor prompt on an OpenClaw-generated ("Do not edit") file; declining leaves the file byte-identical. General value-format provenance does not exist (the issue thread confirmed the shipped writer emits this shape only when its *input* already carries the quotes), so operator confirmation is the proof this repair runs under.

Sibling surfaces: systemd's env file uses separate machinery (systemd itself strips wrapping quotes in `EnvironmentFile=` parsing) and Windows scheduled tasks do not use this file format; the reported corruption shape is launchd-specific.

## User Impact

`openclaw doctor` now tells macOS operators when their generated service env file carries the #103804 corruption, names the affected keys, and `doctor --fix` repairs the file in place with a restart hint — including for installs created before the managed-keys metadata existed. Runtime behavior is unchanged (lossless reads); production delta is +163 lines, justified as an operator-visible repair capability at the owner boundary replacing a doctrinally-forbidden runtime shim (+24 lines removed with its test).

## Evidence

- `src/daemon/launchd-service-files.env-quote-repair.test.ts` (5 tests): heals wrapped values and leaves every other line byte-identical (interior quotes, escaped quotes, metadata line preserved; mode stays 0600; second pass converges to null); heals legacy files without managed-keys metadata; documents the named operator-literal tradeoff; clean files and missing files return null untouched.
- `src/commands/doctor-platform-notes.env-quote-repair.test.ts` (3 tests): the doctor step warns + repairs a real seeded file when the operator accepts, warns but leaves the file byte-identical when declined, and stays silent off darwin / on clean installs. These drive the real repair path end-to-end (real temp files, real prompt gate — no mocks of the repair).
- Full `src/daemon` suite: 37 files, 1181 passed. `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` green (format, oxlint 1.79, tsgo lanes, import cycles, boundary guards).
- Live CLI proof attempted and blocked by design: `openclaw doctor --fix` gates all service management on the default install identity (`service management skipped: non-default state dir or config path` under both an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and an `OPENCLAW_PROFILE` state dir on this machine), and running doctor repairs against the operator's real `~/.openclaw` service is not authorized from this session. The doctor-step behavior tests above exercise the identical code path the gated CLI flow invokes.


### Real managed-macOS proof (head `6365ed8cac3`)

Executed on a real macOS LaunchAgent gateway service, isolated under a dedicated profile so no operator service or state was touched:

- **Setup**: the branch head was packaged (`scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs` tarball) and installed via `npm install -g` into a profile prefix; `openclaw --profile qaenvproof gateway install` created the real LaunchAgent (`ai.openclaw.qaenvproof.plist`, `service-env/ai.openclaw.qaenvproof.env`, env-sourcing wrapper) and launchd started the gateway listening on its port.
- **Corruption**: `export AWS_REGION='"us-east-1"'` appended to the generated env file (the exact #103804 shape). A `gateway install --force` reinstall preserved the corrupted entry — confirming the issue's premise that the corruption persists through service rewrites.
- **Repair flow observed** (interactive `openclaw --profile qaenvproof doctor`, real PTY):
  1. Detection note rendered: `~/.openclaw-qaenvproof/service-env/ai.openclaw.qaenvproof.env has 1 value(s) wrapped in literal double quotes (AWS_REGION)` / `This is the #103804 serialization corruption...`.
  2. The shape-gated prompt (`Rewrite 1 quote-corrupted value(s) ... now?`) required an explicit interactive accept — three earlier `doctor --fix` runs on the same corrupted service never auto-stripped the value, live confirmation of the `requiresInteractiveConfirmation` contract.
  3. After accepting: `Rewrote 1 value(s) (AWS_REGION). Restart the gateway service (openclaw --profile qaenvproof gateway restart) so the healed values take effect.` — the correctly-named owning-service restart command.
  4. File healed to `export AWS_REGION='us-east-1'`; after the instructed restart, the **live relaunched service process env** read directly off the running pid showed `AWS_REGION=us-east-1` while the service listened on its port.
- **Flow finding fixed in the same push**: the proof surfaced that `doctor --fix` engages gateway maintenance, which skips the gateway-services section hosting this repair — so the note's old claim that `doctor --fix` rewrites the entries was unreachable in practice on a managed service. The note now points operators at the interactive `openclaw doctor` prompt (commit `6365ed8cac3`).
- Environment note: the packaged install was required because a launchd-spawned service cannot read a dev checkout under `~/Documents` (macOS TCC `Operation not permitted`) — the packaged path also makes the proof match a real operator install.
- Teardown: `gateway uninstall` + profile state removed; no operator service existed on this machine at any point.

prs.title: refactor(ui): use owner facts for page interactions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Sessions search could clear on Escape before the navigation drawer committed its DOM, or while a native menu was open inside a shadow root. Account usage also waited for a reactive render before cancelling the previous account's request, allowing obsolete work to survive a same-turn account switch.

## User Impact

Escape follows current drawer, menu, overlay, and modal ownership. Account changes immediately revoke the previous usage request and coalesce replacement work into one read of the final account.

## Implementation

Pages consume the existing synchronous shell owner through an optional `ShellPresentationContext` around `RouterOutlet`. The context exposes only the existing readonly drawer fact; standalone pages have no drawer. Native menu surfaces register their browser-derived open state with the existing document registry and unregister on disconnect. They keep their manual dismissal policy and do not join the managed overlay stack.

Account usage receives changes through the existing Solid bridge property receipt. Each receipt cancels the current request immediately; the shared timeout primitive schedules the final scope load. The public refresh method calls that same owner directly. The private refresh event and the scope effect are removed. Retained moves, teardown, and stale-result checks remain intact.

Host tags, selectors, routes, anchors, rendered DOM, CSS, and lazy boundaries are preserved. The shell context wrapper renders no DOM. The Plugins change builds on the landed initialization/target extraction in #176547.

## Evidence

Base: `3065f2e01fa05500919948846aaf25bcb9e481aa`. Reviewed and built head: `a4859b03a809901b62bc48d4810395cd6bea3ba7`.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Focused Account Usage / Sessions tests | All 20 cases have passing evidence: Account Usage 4/4 and 14 Sessions cases passed initially; after correcting the two new Sessions tests' reopen/focus fixture, only those two names were rerun and both passed. |
| Integrated `pnpm tsgo:ui` | Passed. |
| Narrow lint, format, whitespace | Passed on the nine changed files. The landed Plugins extraction resolved its prior line-cap failure. |
| Independent review | Complete, scoped-clean at P0–P2. No actionable findings. All nine source hashes match the reviewed candidate after the normal commit. |
| Base and head `pnpm ui:build` | Both passed on the same host. |
| Strict performance with exact base output | Passed; no warnings or violations. See bytes below. |
| Production `pnpm deadcode:knip` | Completed once; exit 1 for two unchanged core files listed below. No UI findings. |

| Same-host gzip measurement | Base | Head | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Startup JS | 337,526 B | 337,589 B | +63 B |
| Startup JS requests | 7 | 7 | 0 |
| Startup CSS requests | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| Startup CSS | 38,500 B | 38,500 B | 0 |
| Chat boot JS | 1,489,216 B | 1,489,334 B | +118 B |
| New Session boot JS | 1,049,146 B | 1,049,261 B | +115 B |

The startup increase is the shared owner context and native-popover registration; no lazy page or library was moved into startup. All enforced budgets pass.

The retained logs contain six `STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED` messages for each Sessions render. A single targeted diagnostic run passed and traced every warning to `SettingsSegmented`'s existing keyed-row ref at `ui/src/components/solid/settings-ui.tsx:378`, through `applyRef`, reading `option().value`. That shared file is byte-identical to the integration base. Account Usage emitted no Solid diagnostics. No warning was suppressed. The temporary tracer was removed, and all reviewed source hashes were restored exactly.

No local E2E, parity, or retention battery was run under the migration compute budget. This shell/overlay change needs `ci:full` on the publication run. The new regressions were not run on the merge base; their passing evidence and the owner-source audit support the change, with full browser dismissal/focus proof delegated to CI.

Knip reports only `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-admission-ticket.ts` and `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-turn-admission-owner.ts` as unused files. Both file contents and their referencing file sets are identical between this PR's base and head. This lane did not run a second base Knip census or change those unrelated owners.

## Refactor Counts

Seven touched production files and two test files, against the exact integration base:

| Pattern | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Production LOC | 2,430 | 2,488 |
| Test LOC | 397 | 557 |

Production growth supplies context, disconnect cleanup, and native property receipts; it adds no synchronized state copy or local effect wrapper. The additional tests cover current drawer priority, native shadow-menu lifecycle, and same-turn account cancellation/stale completion.

Four pre-existing effects remain in touched files: timed shell connection presentation (`app-shell-view.tsx:84`), legacy/native presentation synchronization (`app-shell-view.tsx:120`), Plugins route/Gateway request cutover (`plugins-page.ts:228`), and rendered icon fetch/cache synchronization (`plugins-page.ts:248`). The timer is the next shared-primitive conversion; the other three currently synchronize external consumers and are unchanged by this focused batch.

Full CI [39179264231](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39179264231) passed on the reviewed head, including every UI and real-Gateway shard.

## Main Integration

Rebased to `52bd03a34f53d37a36cec8c86d298ade3630b1c1` at coordinator request. Current head: `d15960403b277bd7b06d14ff2cba3f44c35bbd93`. prs.title: fix: Gateways and Codex launchers leak as orphaned processes when their owner dies
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Gateways and Codex app-server launchers leak as orphaned processes for days when the process that owns them dies — QA-suite Gateways spin at 20–50% CPU and ignore SIGTERM, and Codex launchers stay suspended (state `T`) forever.

Found on 2026-10-18 on a Mac Studio: two orphaned QA-suite Gateways (5+ days, ~120 CPU-hours each, 2–3.4 GB RSS, only SIGKILL worked, zombie `sqlite-readonly-location.worker.js` children) and 32 stopped `codex.js … app-server` launchers (PPID 1, 7–8 days old, triplets per mock port).

## User Impact

User impact: a Gateway whose host dies (QA parent killed, agent/CI timeout, crash, or any closed stdout/stderr pipe) now shuts down cleanly instead of spinning forever, and closing a Codex app-server can no longer leave a suspended launcher behind when its owner exits mid-close. No config, schema, or public contract changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Gateway EPIPE feedback loop.** When the owning parent dies, the Gateway's stdout/stderr pipes break. The console EPIPE handler routes each failure through `exitAfterSignalExitBarriers` to the Gateway's output-exit owner (`run-loop.ts`), which re-issued `request("stop")` on every notification. During shutdown that request logs `received process exit during shutdown; finishing shutdown without restart` — another write to the broken pipe, another EPIPE. The resulting next-tick loop starved shutdown continuations (the hard-exit watchdog is armed only after an await that never resumes), signal handling (so SIGTERM never ran), and libuv child reaping (the zombies). The callback was introduced in 98813c23905e on 2026-10-10, just before the leaked Gateways started. Fix: once a host exit is accepted (`hostExitRequested`, set by the stdin lifeline or the first output failure; never reset), later output failures only record a nonzero exit code and return. The first stop request is already accepted, so nothing is lost.

The QA harness itself needs no change: it already escalates SIGTERM → SIGKILL on the process group when `stop()` runs, and when the parent dies without running it (SIGKILL, group signal, crash) the detached Gateway is designed to exit through its `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_HOST_LIFELINE=stdin` lifeline — which this loop defeated. The spawn-broker worker exits on IPC disconnect once its Gateway is gone (it intentionally ignores supervisor SIGTERM while its Gateway is alive); current main starts the broker only on Linux.

**Codex stopped-launcher orphan.** `terminateCodexAppServerDescendants` SIGSTOPs the `codex.js` launcher root, kills its descendants, and hands back a receipt whose `resume()` SIGCONTs the root later. If the owning process exits while the root is held stopped (fire-and-forget close followed by process exit), the stopped launcher is reparented to PID 1 and stays stopped forever: it can never observe stdin EOF, and SIGTERM stays pending. The incident argv matches the Codex plugin config written by `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/quota-reset.test-support.ts` (plus the plugin's ephemeral auth override), i.e. launchers owned by real Gateways under the quota-reset e2e tests, including the Control UI real-gateway e2e that the cold-load worktrees run. Fix: while containment holds a direct-child root, one shared `process.on("exit")` listener releases everything it holds stopped: it SIGCONTs descendants that containment stopped but has not yet killed (the same release the synchronous failure unwind already performs; a resumed native server exits on stdin EOF), then SIGKILLs the root (its process group when it leads one, otherwise the root alone — hosted Gateways spawn the launcher in their own group). Root PID ownership is proven by the unreaped Node child handle (`exitCode`/`signalCode` still null); descendants leave the held set the moment containment kills them or sees them dead, so a reaped PID is never signaled. Accepted gaps, named in the code: an owner killed with SIGKILL runs no exit handler, and orphan reclaim (no child handle) stays covered by its durable registration rather than the exit guard.

## Evidence

**Gateway, real process rig** (exact incident spawn shape: `node dist/index.js gateway run --port <free> --bind loopback --allow-unconfigured`, detached, stdio pipes, isolated QA state/home, `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_HOST_LIFELINE=stdin`; Node 24, macOS):

| Parent death | Before (origin/main) | After (fixed dist) |
|---|---|---|
| parent SIGKILL | orphan PPID 1, 97.5% CPU at 45 s, survived explicit SIGTERM | clean exit in 4.1 s |
| group SIGTERM | orphan, 82.3% CPU, survived SIGTERM | clean exit in 4.1 s |
| group SIGINT | orphan, 87.4% CPU, survived SIGTERM | clean exit in 30.1 s* |
| parent crash | orphan, 89.1% CPU, survived SIGTERM | clean exit in 30.1 s* |

\* Killed mid-startup on a host at load average ~80 (startup took ~46 s); the Gateway log shows `shutdown completed cleanly in 585ms` / `321ms` once startup reached its stop point — no watchdog kill. The baseline sample/stack capture showed the console-write → output-exit callback → `request("stop")` → log loop; killing an SQLite child under the spinning Gateway left it a zombie, confirming starved reaping. A real `pnpm openclaw qa suite` run under the repo's pinned Bun runtime did not hang, consistent with the incident Gateways running `node dist/index.js`.

**Codex, real owner-exit rig** (real `closeCodexAppServerTransport`; launcher spawns a native substitute that exits on stdin EOF and mirrors its exit like `codex.js`; the owner calls `process.exit()` at a real containment step):

```text
detached launcher, exit right after native SIGKILL — origin/main:
  69759     1 Ts   node <launcher>          # incident fingerprint: stopped, PPID 1, native gone
hosted (non-leader) launcher, exit with native stopped before its SIGKILL — origin/main:
  38844     1 T    node <launcher>
  38927 38844 T    node <native>
same, with only the root guard (first revision of this PR):
  95526     1 T    node <native>            # review finding reproduced
with fix: survivors [] in both scenarios
```

**Regression tests** (red with only the production file reverted, green with the fix):

- `src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.test.ts` › `joins Gateway cleanup without feeding broken output back into shutdown` — red: `expected true to be false` (feedback loop observed); green in 12 ms. Full `run-loop.test.ts` + `host-lifeline.test.ts`: 172 passed.
- `extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-owner-exit.test.ts` (2 cases: detached launcher, owner exits right after the native SIGKILL; hosted non-leader launcher, owner exits while the native is stopped) — red on origin/main: stopped launcher survivors (`45574     1 Ts   node <launcher>`); green: both pass, ~6 s each. Cost: real owner processes are the only way to prove behavior across owner `process.exit`; most time is tsx startup. The test asserts it observed the stopped launcher, so a run where containment gives up early (seen locally at load average ~105) fails instead of passing vacuously.

**Review follow-up:** the first revision only killed the launcher root; a review finding showed hosted Gateways (non-leader launchers) could still strand a descendant that containment had stopped but not yet killed. Fixed in the third commit and covered by the hosted test case above. The fixture retries a fresh launcher (up to 3) only when containment fails closed before reaching the exit step — on busy Macs the darwin census currently fails on exiting processes (~10–38% of calls measured locally); that core inspection bug is tracked separately.

**Focused consumers:** Codex transport/registration/client-shutdown suites pass except `transport-orphan.test.ts` (unavailable-inspection case) and timing-sensitive `transport.process.test.ts` quiescing modes, which fail on origin/main on this macOS host too (the failing quiescing modes vary from run to run at load average ~80, with or without the fix). The orphan-test assertion is stale since #175368 moved darwin inspection to the native census; tracked separately.

**Not covered:** Linux Gateway spawn-broker launch was not exercised end to end (broker owner-SIGKILL teardown was verified with the production host/worker on macOS: broker and descendants gone in 309 ms). An owner killed by SIGKILL during Codex containment can still leave a stopped launcher until a later owner reclaims its registration.

**Local gates:** `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` clean; `pnpm check:changed --base <merge-base>` line-cap and assertion-safety ratchets pass (the run-loop fix is line-neutral). Its max-lines-suppression ratchet (three `ui/` files) and core test-shard root budget (723/720 advisory) fail on the merge base itself, untouched by this diff. Core oxlint on the touched gateway files passes; extension oxlint could not start locally (its plugin-SDK boundary-artifact prep hit the 300 s guard at load average ~90), so PR CI is the lint proof for the Codex files. `tsgo:core` passes. Codex autoreview (P1): scoped-clean on the full change and on the review-fix delta.

prs.title: fix(build): bundle fs-safe watcher in portable workers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After #176461 updated fs-safe to 0.26.8, portable worker archives retained a URL for `./watch-io-worker.js` without emitting that file. The package import-closure check then failed on Linux and Windows for `sqlite-store.worker.mjs` and shared worker chunks.

Bundle the dependency watcher as `worker-chunk-fs-safe-watch-io.mjs` through the existing auxiliary-entry path and rewrite its sealed-build URL. The dependency version, upstream watcher/fallback selection, native policy, and archive staging rules stay unchanged. Updates now carry a complete portable worker graph.

The existing relocated-archive closure assertion stays intact. Its runtime probe also starts the bundled watcher, receives a reply, and joins termination. An added bootstrap-shape case catches future upstream URL changes.

## Evidence

- Exact two-SHA build comparison: parent `de42210bcdd6` with frozen fs-safe 0.26.7 passes the SQLite portable build and real package import-closure CLI (71.56s); `4392036843f6` with frozen 0.26.8 fails with the reported missing worker (60.92s). Current main `65fdda51d7d8` reproduces it too (31.15s).
- All 82 affected cases covered: 81 local Node passes across `worker-deploy-build-plugin.test.ts`, `tsdown-config.test.ts`, and `sqlite-schema-assets.test.ts`; the remaining archive case passes on Linux Blacksmith Testbox in 61.98s command wall / 10.87s case time. The Testbox verified the base and all four candidate file hashes. [Testbox run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39178077684).
- Local `--maxWorkers=1` group: 877.97s command wall, including a 230.88s cold worker cache; changed files took 200.93s (`tsdown-config`) and 356.62s (`worker-deploy`). On the loaded Mac, the unchanged closure subprocess hit its existing 30s deadline after the watcher/facade assertions passed; no timeout was increased. An earlier default-Bun attempt timed out in fixture setup before assertions. The first Testbox command stopped before tests because the synced checkout needed a frozen dependency install; the corrected setup passed on the same immediately admitted lease. The lease is stopped.
- Script and root-script typechecks, targeted typed/boundary lint, formatting, script erasability, the complete source-contract CI group, and independent P2 review pass.

The build-plugin fixture builds every portable worker entry and checks the staged, relocated archive. PR CI supplies the broad package and cross-platform proof. No GitHub CI jobs were rerun.


### Runtime-probe follow-up

The Bun-built archive probe previously re-exported `readOwnerAndDaclBatch` directly. Its generated bundle retained the function but omitted the initializer that assigns the default timeout, causing the runtime `RangeError` in CI run 39178495898. The fixture now uses the same static import-and-call shape as production. Both omitted-timeout assertions, watcher checks, facade assertions, and all existing deadlines remain intact.

Compared the published fs-safe 0.26.7 and 0.26.8 JavaScript and type declarations: the permission APIs are unchanged, including the optional 60-second batch default. Audited both production batch callers in trusted plan-path validation and SQLite staging-directory policy, plus the other permission consumers; no production caller passes an invalid timeout or requires migration. The dependency version stays unchanged. No native Windows execution is claimed by this audit.

- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun pnpm test test/scripts/worker-deploy-build-plugin.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **22/22 pass** on macOS, 339.33s including a 161.12s cold worker compilation. The previously failing archive case passes in 33.30s, with the existing 30s subprocess deadlines unchanged. This uses the pinned Bun revision from CI.
- Owning root-script test type graph, targeted typed lint, focused boundary lint, formatting, and independent P2 review pass.
- Linux proof was attempted through the focused Blacksmith Testbox profile. The replacement allocation queued after source preparation, so it was stopped and proof ran locally per policy. Both task-owned boxes are completed with no host. No GitHub job was rerun and no provider fallback was used.

prs.title: fix(ci): retain locale work after publication deferral
prs.body:
Related: #173193

## What Problem This Solves

Locale refresh repeats hours of successful translation whenever source drift defers publication, preventing new translations from reaching users on an active main branch.

## User Impact

Later refreshes reuse completed translations and generate only new or changed strings, so they can catch up without retranslating an entire new locale. A stale run still cannot publish. Cache misses and eviction retain the existing cold-run behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retain only each successful locale worker’s translation-memory files in the existing Actions cache. The cache lineage is frozen before restoration from canonical memory, fallback metadata, glossary, and generator policy. English text changes are handled by the existing hash-aware planner, while canonical translation corrections invalidate reuse.

Cache restore/save is restricted to upstream main-branch runs; source, metadata, manifests, and executable files are excluded. Workers must have zero recorded fallbacks before saving. Forced refresh bypasses restoration. The same aggregate validation, generated-output ownership, source invalidation, and exact-head publication policy remain authoritative.

Simplification: workflow wiring uses the existing cache actions and planner; no new generator, publisher, runtime flag, or competing state owner. Generated locale output remains in a separate PR.

## Evidence

- Run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38791296668 completed all 21 locale workers and strict zero-fallback validation, then explicitly deferred publication because generator inputs changed. Subsequent runs started from the same untranslated Swedish baseline.
- Actual maintainer recovery reused those verified artifacts and the canonical generator needed only 37 changed keys per locale; current-source strict check passed with zero fallbacks.
- `pnpm test test/scripts/control-ui-locale-refresh.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **9 passed**, 9.11s wall / 82ms test execution. The original workflow fails the added regression.
- Related planner and existing stale-publication guards: **20 focused tests passed**, 15.25s combined wall. Unrelated cases were intentionally filtered, not represented as passed.
- Workflow lint, targeted typecheck/lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent autoreview reported no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- The first CI run exposed a missing central cache-writer policy registration. The corrected guard now checks only this locale job’s pinned save action, exact TM-only paths/key, success/main condition and mandatory artifact admission. All other cache rules stay unchanged. The exact failing guard plus nine locale tests pass (10 cases, 2.84s wrapper wall); fresh delta review is clean. The original auto-merge request was confirmed retired before publishing replacement head `755517c758ab50f230fc98f63a841a92b7d67d61`.
- Exact-head [CI run 38852406576](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38852406576) completed successfully on `755517c758ab50f230fc98f63a841a92b7d67d61`. Hosted execution: new nine-case suite **0.081s**; corrected cache guard **0.233s** (the existing 169-case guard file took 53.511s). No workflow was rerun merely to obtain green.
- Actual Actions cache save/restore remains a post-merge verification gap; passing tests do not claim live cache transport.
- **Security disposition pending:** [CodeQL alert 1128](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/security/code-scanning/1128) reports the main-commit checkout reaching the cache writer. The exact SARIF is now inspected: analysis `1964946059`, CodeQL 2.27.2, merge checkout `bef0780a4f333056807e3bc61049451fd39d5e32`. Every reported path begins at the worker checkout (lines 169–176), then follows the workflow to save (264–273); it does not identify attacker-controlled input into the resolver. The [shipped query](https://github.com/github/codeql/blob/a7057b836bf29767461026718b14d20790b9085f/actions/ql/lib/codeql/actions/security/UntrustedCheckoutQuery.qll#L267-L296) also classifies commit-output names heuristically. Source inspection and fresh independent review found no demonstrated attacker-controlled revision: the resolver selects the canonical default branch; dispatch accepts no revision; token-only preflight skips workers; successful upstream-main admission gates both cache operations. No scanner suppression or source renaming was used. Vincent renewed landing direction after the exact disposition question. GitHub requires delegated dismissal approval; the false-positive request was submitted with `create_request=true` and awaits an authorized security reviewer. It is **not dismissed**.
- **Proof limits, not passing transport claims:** existing tests execute the real zero-fallback artifact shell and planner/filesystem reuse; provenance cases exercise the exact admission expressions. They do not execute GitHub's job scheduler or cache service. A real candidate upstream-main run is unavailable before landing: main dispatch executes the old main workflow, while candidate-branch dispatch is deliberately rejected. Running the pinned action with invented runner context would bypass, not prove, this boundary. No artificial harness, broadened dispatch permission, or extra workflow was added. Actual save/restore remains an explicit postmerge integration check; the delegated security approval remains mandatory.
- Latest canonical producer [38851349923](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38851349923) again completed strict zero-fallback validation (including Swedish), then explicitly deferred publication at 07:05 UTC because generator inputs moved. No current generated output is claimed published.

## Contributor credit

Requested by @vincentkoc.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @vincentkoc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/774d3df5-9e98-451b-b24f-543b77c54564)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/ea71ed1b-0da1-4f93-a97e-932282a7eb6b)

prs.title: refactor(mcp): migrate session and node clients to SDK v2
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Move the session and node MCP clients onto the split MCP SDK v2 packages. This completes the internal client, transport, validator, OAuth, content, Gateway adapter, and associated fixture migration. All production clients explicitly negotiate legacy MCP; this does not enable modern serving or change Claude configuration. The server migration landed in #175366; this branch is rebased onto it and retains its v1/v2 interoperability matrix unchanged.

OpenClaw keeps ownership of pagination limits, cancellation, validation, and resource lifetime. Typed v2 requests preserve that ownership instead of adopting the SDK's catalog pagination/cache policy. The validator uses the already pinned workspace URI resolver and prior draft-07 defaults.

## Public compatibility and migration

The published plugin boundary remains exactly v1-shaped for the first stable release containing this migration: `SessionMcpRuntime.callTool`, `listTools`, `listResourceTemplates`, and `getPrompt`; `prepareHarnessNativeMcpAppPreview.toolResult`; and the existing `codex-mcp-projection` runtime seam. No public export is added. The SDK migration guide documents the following-stable-release v2 cutover and how consumers should prepare. v1 remains a runtime dependency for this named compatibility window.

The SDK result-validation seam rejects field loss before v2 parsing, permits additive SDK defaults, and the published boundary validates lossless representability and raises `McpSdkCompatibilityError` with `code: "MCP_SDK_RESULT_UNREPRESENTABLE"` and the MCP method when conversion would lose information. Cases include:

- Non-object structured content, including null, scalars, and arrays.
- Scalar/null schema-property values.
- Output schemas without `type: "object"`, including scalar or union types.
- Output `properties` or `required` shapes the v1 schema cannot represent.
- Nested fields that either SDK parser would strip; the pre-parse validator rejects loss before the public converter sees the result.

Representable metadata, top-level extension fields, cursors, schemas (including array-valued property schemas accepted by v1), resource content, and prompt messages are preserved exactly.

## Compatibility findings

- **Packaged client dependency restored:** the rebase retained main's dev-only v2 client declaration even though this migration now uses it at runtime. Restore the pinned client and `core:mcp` runtime ownership; the cron cleanup harness also imports it from the production installation.
- **HTTP DELETE regression fixed:** a failed initialize handshake in v2 can clear the transport's session ID before cleanup. Retain the failed-startup session ID for DELETE. Both existing cleanup regressions passed on the clean v1 baseline and pass with this fix.
- Preserve malformed stdio error reporting and string response IDs; cancel rejected HTTP notification bodies; preserve explicit caller-abort reasons while keeping real deadline failures as timeouts.
- **Intentional OAuth difference:** after a discovery transport `TypeError`, Node and Bun make one request and surface the login failure; they do not retry without `MCP-Protocol-Version`. v1's browser-CORS workaround incidentally retried Node network errors. v2 explicitly restricts that workaround to browser runtimes ([upstream source](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/blob/v2.3.1/packages/client/src/client/auth.ts#L1659-L1697)). Real socket-reset probes on both runtimes observed two requests/success with v1 versus one request/TypeError with v2. The Gateway regression asserts the exact request/header, unchanged stored credentials, and visible retry guidance. Retry remains a user action.
- **Inherited progress limitation:** a single coalesced progress/result pipe chunk loses progress with both SDK generations (0/8 progress events each), tracked in [typescript-sdk#3018](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/issues/3018). It is not encoded as an expected-broken test and is excluded from the migration parity gate. A separate follow-up can assess draining queued progress at OpenClaw's existing progress owner.

## Evidence

Local proof used macOS arm64, Node 26.12.0 and Bun 1.4.3, with one test worker. No timeouts or budgets were raised.

- Frozen install, production and targeted test types, scoped lint/format, and diff checks passed.
- Node: session/credential/resolver/Code Mode 83/83; transport 47/47; node manager 35/35 (revalidated on Node and Bun after the explicit-schema adapter fix); metadata/converter 30/30; OAuth 32/32. Gateway OAuth login 34/34 (207.95 s Vitest, 242.31 s including preparation); Apps/input timeout regressions pass, including 3/3 focused cases on both runtimes. The Gateway fixture uses real HTTP, WebSocket admission, and persistent credential ownership; startup dominates its cost.
- Bun: 178/178 boundary tests and 38/38 Apps tests. The instrumented Gateway-login fixture uses Node's `module.registerHooks`, unavailable in Bun; the real OAuth socket-reset probes and isolated Gateway/CLI proof cover Bun without adding a shim.
- Real main-thread and Worker probes on each runtime: stdio 14 checks, strict proxy 6, pagination 18 (128 pages / 16,384 tools / 10 MiB limits), HTTP/framing 26, actual node owner 18. Final fixture-wire probes: 26/26 per runtime.
- The real session HTTP regression proved pre-fix truncation in all four result methods, then exact payload/default preservation and explicit errors on Node and Bun (19/19 selected cases per runtime).
- Full build and runtime build passed. The pre-conflict full CI-artifact build passed in 17m 08.5s: all 156 public SDK subpaths, 97 plugins, 54 module-load checks, and UI size checks. No budget changed.
- External plugin compiled strictly against the **packaged SDK** with six bidirectional public-type assertions, then ran against the tarball on Node and Bun: four exact payloads, preview behavior, authority callback, and packaged projection form context. Declaration checking required explicit consumer development dependencies for ws, pg, node-fetch and form-data; `skipLibCheck` remained false. Package integrity checks passed.
- Real isolated Gateway + CLI + installed Claude full turn passed on Node and Bun, with native Claude execution, no fallback, exact MCP tool text, and all fixture processes retired. Synthetic provider and MCP endpoints; dedicated state and ports.
- Cold import medians (7 fresh processes, startup excluded): client Node 135.35 ms / Bun 68.69 ms; stdio 79.87 / 72.51; AJV validator 9.42 / 16.82; core 56.82 / 51.14. These are measurements, not a speed claim.

Independent review of the complete final diff is clean through P2. Review found and corrected pre-converter field stripping and a test adapter dropping explicit-schema request options. After the final conflict repair, the affected Node and Bun suites each pass 51/51 and real main-thread/Worker stdio probes pass 20 checks per runtime. The repair retains main's Docker custody owner and migrates its default-environment import, with exact v1/v2 environment parity verified. Frozen install, scoped lint/format, dependency ownership and diff checks passed on the final head.

The packaged-plugin artifact has SHA-256 `d1b3e3c429af8f1f05761f5b680e1ca046f41604e693e8ed8612dea03a1927c7`; its public boundary is unchanged by the final rebase. Local revalidation of a later tarball hit the unchanged 300-second guard twice, so that local path stopped. The final-head hosted build and production Docker seed flow subsequently passed; no timeout or budget was raised.

Release-note context: migrate internal session/node MCP clients to SDK v2 with explicit legacy negotiation; retain published v1 result contracts for one stable-release window; preserve configuration, pagination, cancellation, and transport cleanup. OAuth discovery network errors now surface immediately in Node/Bun instead of receiving the browser headerless retry.

## CI attribution

Final head: `daab8ae79d7e4f7af6d1889f6bc3db684f52e42c`. Exact-head [run 39170015596](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39170015596) completed with 151 successful jobs, 20 planner-skipped jobs, seven failed jobs and the failed aggregate. Build artifacts, the production Docker seed flow, all three PostgreSQL conformance shards, and `security-fast` passed. Windows was planner-skipped; this run does not supply Windows execution proof.

Attribution is complete against CI's exact protected-main parent `440c86f20b0ed4a77a2b017dfe37d3ef03e339f0` and inspected tested merge `344e1abb47fb735cb40545b7d77155fc64a4d12a`:

- Cleanup diagnostic assertions reproduce on clean main; the unchanged owner now retains diagnostics in an Error/cause chain while its tests expect the prior plain-object fields.
- Both Code Mode lifecycle cases reproduce on exact clean main with the same active-count assertion (2 failed / 37 skipped).
- The format-wrapper assertion reproduces on exact clean main (1 failed / 67 skipped): main changed `format:check` to the Node wrapper while the test still expects `oxfmt`.
- Android's local Compose handoff timeout is unrelated to the MCP execution path. Its Android behavior and generated dependency closure match the same-period successful main job; no local Android replay is claimed.
- The catalog hydration failure is unrelated filesystem/watch timing in an unchanged owner: exact-case replay passes on main and candidate on macOS; the full 22-file Linux x64 group passes 237/237 on both. The broad SDK import graph is nonempty, but the failing hydration operation invokes no changed MCP operation. The exact race was not reproduced, so this is not claimed as a reproduced inherited failure.
- Both Discord quiet-progress assertions reproduce through a real isolated Gateway on exact clean main (2 failed / 14 skipped, 583.08 s): updates contain only the headline instead of the expected Exec-running update. Channel/Discord/auto-reply owners are unchanged; this is separate from upstream MCP progress coalescing.

The failed jobs are `checks-node-changed-compact-small-14` (117801291040), `checks-node-changed-compact-large-21` (117801289019), `checks-node-changed-compact-small-10` (117801289103), `checks-node-compact-small-1` (117801288844), `android-test-third-party` (117801287532), `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-26` (117801288831), and `checks-node-changed-12` (117801290930). `openclaw/ci-gate` (117806123926) aggregates those failures. Landing uses the explicitly authorized inherited/unrelated-failure exception; failed CI is not represented as green.

The earlier native-fork timing failure passed the exact candidate file (12/12) and its 22-file group (223/223) on macOS and Linux x64 / Node 24.22.0. Its import graph has broad SDK-barrel overlap; the observed failure was in unchanged physical-reader validation before `thread/fork`, with no MCP operation executing. Later CI passed that job. No failing CI result is represented as green.

prs.title: refactor: simplify state lease heartbeat liveness protocol
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The state-lease heartbeat duplicates its durable lease authority with synchronous ACKs, a short response watchdog, a shared completed-request witness and a sibling admission pump. This heartbeat-only area recovers part of closed cleanup donors #173527/#174230; overlapping proposals count once.

## What Changed

Use ordinary request-ID correlation and one finite operation deadline bounded by the observed lease expiry. Synchronous protected effects check local lifetime and the exact current durable owner once, without a blocking liveness handshake or a second ownership read.

Conflict repair preserves main's newer #176296 native-renewal settlement fix: the shared renewalProgress allocation, carrier sharing, scheduled/explicit renewal wrapping, final notification and carrier wait before termination all remain. The counter no longer also drives ACK deadlines. Preserve #175588's long native-COMMIT ownerFence/holdWriteFence, durable owner/grant renewal and commit/rollback settlement, as well as current early workerOperations/execution binding. No schema, columns, persisted shape, durability, retention, permissions, config keys, protocol, SDK, dependency or Phase E change.

Tooling-migration head `a590b91a3878b6441ab122bae0155249e46f4517`, base `a70b7c23104ada5d7d1a21b245dec72623a78a7e`: **96 net production lines removed**, five production paths +71/-167; all ten paths +115/-326. Rule 11 area split. Coordinator-requested rebase is patch-identical to the previously reviewed head `7ec3176392168015fdba7baf66a75a56f29a383e` (stable patch ID `ad4f523f2b6c76eb1ded4c69555d86ff83177c87`); all ten affected files were unchanged on main between the two bases. The new base includes the cheaper Vitest worker preparation and native typechecker.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Synchronous ACK (#157696/#164615): detects worker exit before ordinary queued callback delivery. Their mechanism/synthetic-reproduction provenance is not a cited human incident requiring the extra protocol. Durable ownership remains the effect boundary; delayed exit notification waits for delivery or expiry. Independent renewal and final current-row checks stay.
- Short response watchdog (#157696): formerly used odd/even native progress to avoid false loss on slow storage. Replace that watchdog with the finite operation/lease bound; unusually late replies fail visibly. The progress counter itself remains for actual native renewal settlement before termination (#176296).
- Completed-request witness (#168214): preserved replies delayed beyond the short watchdog. Ordinary replies now share the finite operation bound without a second completion channel. Matching requests, expiry/lost refusal and a fixed ceiling remain.

prs.title: perf(ui): load realtime talk sessions when talk starts
prs.body:
Related: #176501, #176383

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Control UI PRs fail `control-ui-performance` when they add even a few bytes, because chat boot JS on main sits within 26 B of its 1,490,000 B gzip budget (main was over it twice on 2026-10-18).

## User Impact

User impact: chat startup downloads about 6 KB less gzip JavaScript; realtime talk loads its session runtime when you start talk. Performance limits are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Realtime talk only starts on an explicit action, but `chat-realtime.ts` statically imported `RealtimeTalkSession`, which pulled the talk session, transcript owner, transport, and their `src/talk/*` and queue helpers into every chat boot. The session module now loads inside the existing talk start awaits: alongside the `talk.config` request for new sessions, and alongside the previous session's close for voice changes. No new staleness window opens, and a chunk load failure surfaces through the existing error paths (error status for new sessions, rejection to the voice-change caller).

`ui/config/control-ui-boot-modules.json` is regenerated with `pnpm ui:boot-manifest:gen`; besides dropping the talk modules from the chat set it also picks up drift from recent main commits that had left the committed manifest stale.

## Evidence

- Local `pnpm ui:build` + `pnpm ui:check-performance` on current main: chat boot JS 1,489,974 B -> 1,483,730 B gzip (-6,244 B; 6,270 B headroom). Startup JS and new-session boot unchanged (new boot remains at 1,049,948 B of 1,050,000 B, outside this change).
- Talk tests: `chat-realtime.test.ts`, `chat-realtime-handoff.test.ts`, `chat-pane-session-events.test.ts`, `chat-pane-board.test.tsx`, `chat-realtime-controls.test.tsx`, `talk/session-runtime-loading.test.ts` — 98 tests passed.

prs.title: fix(migrate): reject malformed UTF-8 in Hermes migration sources
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw migrate hermes` reads its source files with a lossy UTF-8 decode:

- `plan.ts:47` parses `config.yaml` from `readText()`,
- `plan.ts:54` / `secrets.ts:239` parse the source `.env` from `readText()`,
- `auth.ts` / `auth-source.ts` / `secrets.ts` read `auth.json` through `readJsonObject()` → `readText()`.

`fs.readFile(path, "utf8")` (here `readText`, `helpers.ts:44`) replaces every invalid byte with U+FFFD instead of failing. So a source file that is not valid UTF-8 — a truncated write, a Windows-1252 `config.yaml`, an interrupted sync — is imported as mojibake: `openclaw migrate apply hermes --yes` writes the replacement characters into `openclaw.json` and the agent auth store, and the original bytes are gone from the target. Nothing warns the operator, and the plan still reports `"errors": 0`.

Base (`e2a97a7e0db`), provider URL carrying one invalid byte (`.../café` + `0xFF`, bytes `63 61 66 c3 a9 ff`):

```
openclaw migrate apply hermes --from <source> --yes --no-backup --force   → exit 0
openclaw.json:  "baseUrl": "https://api.acme.example/café<U+FFFD>"        (bytes 63 c3 a9 ef bf bd)
```

Two `ef bf bd` sequences are now persisted in the user's config, and the plan/apply report shows no error.

## Fix

- `helpers.ts`: add `readUtf8Text`, which reads bytes, returns `undefined` for an absent optional source, and otherwise throws one typed error naming the file and the recovery step: `Source file is not valid UTF-8: <path>. Re-encode it as UTF-8 and retry migration.` This is the wording `appendItem` already uses for instruction files, so the provider keeps one vocabulary.
- `plan.ts`: read `config.yaml` and the source `.env` through `readUtf8Text`. The encoding check runs before the YAML wrapper so a malformed file is not reported as a YAML syntax error.
- `secrets.ts`: read both dotenv sources through `readUtf8Text`, so credential values cannot be mojibake'd either.
- `helpers.ts`: `readJsonObject` now decodes through `readUtf8Text`, which covers `auth.json` and the OpenCode auth store; a valid-UTF-8 file with bad JSON still behaves exactly as before (ignored).
- `docs/cli/migrate.md`: one sentence under Safety model, explicitly scoped to the Hermes provider (the Claude and Codex providers keep their current readers).

Best-effort identifier probes keep the lenient reader: `active_profile`, `.active_org`, and `SKILL.md` frontmatter only choose names, and their content is validated again at apply time by `appendItem`. Absent optional sources and valid multibyte text are unchanged; `--json` output shape is unchanged.

Classification: behavior-completing.

Precedent: #168536 (migrate-claude command skill), #171621 / #176009 (memory-wiki importers) — same shape, "reject malformed UTF-8 before importing instead of decoding it".

## Evidence

### Base is really main

The three touched files in the base tree used for both runs are byte-identical to `e2a97a7e0db`:

```
up-main helpers.ts  1654c0182c9944e7745bc593bd77c494
up-main plan.ts     d5d4d608d619c518e51c685e8bbb7131
up-main secrets.ts  a7042120d2c8ed9c7e66fa35f0a98ef2
```

Head differs from base only in those three files (`f58ca74729ab8017f280bcad021025b5`, `284d628c374655c9861636216526bb20`, `271d38455abfc22c7f6814d30855ec54`), plus the regression tests and the docs sentence.

### Run: shipped CLI entry, no Gateway, no credentials

Environment: Node v24.18.0 in `lexiflow-all:latest`, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` per run, CLI invoked through the repo's own entry (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts migrate hermes …`). Source fixture is a real Hermes state directory (`config.yaml` only), which is what `discoverHermesSource` accepts.

Malformed fixture (`fixtures/bad/config.yaml`, `xxd`):

```
0000030: 616d 706c 652f 6361 66c3 a9ff 220a 2020  ample/caf...".
```

Base, `migrate hermes --from fixtures/bad --dry-run --json` → **exit 0**, plan carries the replacement character and would import it:

```
"baseUrl": "https://api.acme.example/café<U+FFFD>"
```

Base, `migrate apply hermes --from fixtures/bad --yes --no-backup --force --json` → **exit 0**, `openclaw.json` written with that value; `efbfbd` byte count in the written config: **2**:

```
0000030: c3a9 efbf bd22 2c0a ...
```

Head, same plan and same apply command → **exit 1**, no plan is produced and no `openclaw.json` is created:

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "Source file is not valid UTF-8: /ws/fixtures/bad/config.yaml. Re-encode it as UTF-8 and retry migration."
  }
}
```

### Control: valid multibyte text still imports, byte-identically

`fixtures/good/config.yaml` (`café😀`, bytes `63 61 66 c3 a9 f0 9f 98 80`) plans `"baseUrl": "https://api.acme.example/café😀"` on both trees; the full plan JSON from base and head is identical after normalizing the state-directory name (`diff -q` → `IDENTICAL`), and neither output contains `efbfbd`.

### Existing settings are preserved when the source is refused (upgrade shape)

The refusal path must not disturb an OpenClaw install that is already configured. Seeded both state dirs with the same valid `openclaw.json` (`"gateway": {"port": 18099}` plus a workspace path), then ran the same malformed-source apply as above:

| | exit | config md5 | `port` kept | `efbfbd` bytes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| base | 0 | `8a9d9be9166a6eec384bbea4913540d7` → `8c508d760a0f9d1bebeaf9e4ab7fc560` | yes | 2 (new corruption merged into existing settings) |
| head | 1 | `35916337cf7b63cbd71457d5b7f626a1` → `35916337cf7b63cbd71457d5b7f626a1` | yes | 0 |

Head leaves the existing file byte-identical because the plan is rejected before the config writer runs; base rewrites it and adds the replacement characters to the user's live settings. This change adds no schema, field, or stored-state migration, so there is no upgrade transform to prove: the only new behavior is the rejection itself.

### Regression tests

`pnpm test extensions/migrate-hermes/config.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`

- Base production code + new tests: **2 failed | 18 passed** — both new rejection tests fail with `promise resolved { providerId: 'hermes', … } instead of rejecting`, i.e. base plans the mojibake'd value and the control test passes.
- Head: **20 passed (20)**, shard 74.38 s (cold transform; the second warm run was 62.48 s).

Cases: malformed `config.yaml` rejects with the path, malformed `auth.json` rejects with the path (proves the `readJsonObject` path), and a valid `café😀` provider URL is imported unchanged.

### Pre-existing failures, not caused by this change

`extensions/migrate-hermes/secrets.test.ts` and `files-and-skills.test.ts` have 13 item-error failures in this container (archive/agent-store steps). The same 13 failures reproduce on the unmodified base tree (`13 failed | 27 passed (40)`), so they are environment, not this diff; every other test in the extension passes.

## Not tested

The credential half is proven at the plan boundary by unit test (`auth.json` with `0xFF` rejects); I did not run a separate `--include-secrets` CLI capture for a malformed auth store. The `claude` and `codex` providers have the same lossy `readJsonObject` shape in their own helpers and are untouched here; the documentation guarantee is scoped to Hermes for that reason and those two stay a separate change.

prs.title: refactor(gateway): trust validated shared-state replies
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway read consumers repeat success and command-type validation that the shared-state reader has already completed.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Missing databases still produce the same empty results or unavailable errors; no permissions, migrations, or configuration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

`executeExistingOpenClawStateRead` rejects failed or mismatched replies and returns the exact command result or `undefined`. Consumers can rely on that contract. The shared-facts acceptor now names its exact input type instead of erasing that contract and checking it again.

This removes 15 redundant check sites across nine files: 15 added / 26 deleted production lines, net −11. Post-await admission, receipt/revision checks, projection validation, and missing-result handling stay with their current owners. No reads, writes, SQL, transaction envelopes, worker requests, schema, or PostgreSQL bookkeeping change.

## Evidence

prs.title: fix(hooks): preserve reader status when delivery is canceled
prs.body:
Related: #173952

## What Problem This Solves

A completed IMAP hook reader can be reported as an execution failure with no `deliveryError` when cancellation interrupts delivery preparation.

## User Impact

Completed readers retain `status=ok`, and canceled delivery records a concrete `deliveryError` without sending a message. Cancellation of an unfinished child handoff remains an execution failure. The shared fix also covers HTTP/Gmail hooks and isolated cron announcements; no configuration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Main already gives acknowledged hooks a detached work scope (#167697), detaches lifecycle publication from the reader scope (#165028), and retains session-controller ownership through finalization (#175837). The delivery preparation branches returned an execution-error disposition or allowed an interrupted descendant read to escape to the run-error handler. They now use the normal delivery-failure result and preserve the reader's output. The duplicate downstream abort check is removed.

This does not establish the cause of the original reasonless AbortError in the reported release, and it does not add the explicit IMAP route discussed in #137871 / #138120. Those parts of #173952 remain open; this PR fixes the source-confirmed misclassification of cancellation after a completed reader.

Deferred facts remain with their existing owners: the hook/controller signal supplies current cancellation authority; admitted config, agent/account/target, session/store identity, payload and timeout describe the accepted run and are not retargeted after cancellation. The existing send owner checks cancellation, delivery fences and source generation before sending; this change exits before that effect. It adds no detached work, storage schema, configuration or SDK surface.

The production delta is +16 lines, retained for shared cancellation classification and handling an awaited read that rejects. Removing unrelated code to offset this would obscure the fix.

## Evidence

- Source/history: #175837 holds the session controller across finalization; the remaining delivery-stage abort paths previously produced a run error without recording a delivery error.
- Regression: `keeps a completed hook reader successful when delivery preparation is cancelled (resolved/rejected)` exercises the isolated runner, finalizer and delivery dispatcher with deterministic fakes. It verifies successful execution, retained output, the cancellation reason, and no outbound send. Existing interrupted-child coverage protects its execution-failure behavior.
- Changed-file oxfmt: passed. Changed-file core oxlint: passed. Codex autoreview (branch mode, P0–P2): scoped-clean, no actionable findings; pre-commit freshness guards passed.
- Initial CI [run 39175893930](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39175893930) passed both new regressions (Bun shard: 6.90s) and the selected test/typecheck jobs. Its mock-export ratchet found a fixture declaration that did not preserve real exports; corrected in `22a2f0cb712fa` and independently reviewed scoped-clean. On updated head `5d653826d4fc`, [CI run 39177110446](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39177110446) completed successfully: 33 jobs passed, including the mock-export ratchet, production/test typechecks, and both regressions (Bun shard: 7.28s).
- PR CI is the test gate and covers the regression plus affected tests and typechecks. Local tests, negative controls, typechecks and live Gateway/Crabbox/Testbox proof were intentionally skipped per maintainer policy. No lease was created.

prs.title: fix(backup): recognize Git worktrees in SQLite backup listing
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw backup` SQLite listing is meant to say "this is a Git backup repository; use `openclaw backup git log --repository <path>` instead" when it is pointed at a Git checkout. `LocalSqliteSnapshotProvider.list` (`src/snapshot/local-repository.ts`, from #167935) only recognized `.git` as a directory. Linked worktrees and `--separate-git-dir` checkouts, whose `.git` is a pointer file, fell through to the generic "SQLite snapshot repository contains unexpected entry: …/.git" error, which tells the operator nothing about the right command.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Reuse the shared `findGitRoot` detector with `maxDepth: 1`, so both `.git` markers are recognized at the selected directory and a SQLite repository nested inside a Git workspace is not misclassified by its ancestor.
- The import is static, matching the module's other importers, and the per-entry listing path is computed once instead of three times. This keeps the file under its line-cap ratchet: production is net −1 line.

## User Impact

Pointing SQLite backup listing at a Git worktree now gives the Git-format guidance instead of an "unexpected entry" error. Behavior for real SQLite snapshot repositories, including nested ones, is unchanged.

## Evidence

- `src/commands/backup-sqlite.test.ts`: the marker case is now table-driven over a `.git` directory and a `.git` pointer file. The pointer-file case fails before the fix, and all 11 pass after it (on the final head).
- A real Git checkout plus a three-agent session backup/restore probe (full and state-only, verify, staged restore, corrupted-artifact refusals) passed under Node and Bun. Leases were released and the databases came out integrity-clean.
- Line-cap ratchet: OK.
- Codex autoreview: clean.

prs.title: perf(gateway): break down worker recovery and admission timing
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Slow Gateway startup reports worker-environment recovery and state admission as coarse timings, obscuring which prerequisite delays readiness.

## User Impact

Operators can distinguish publication admission, workspace recovery, active worker reconciliation, publication recovery, and plugin metadata work in startup logs. Readiness, validation, recovery ordering, and stored state remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`sidecars.worker-environments` is the placement-recovery barrier, not worker installation or runtime assembly. Route its existing phases through the startup-trace owner so cold starts expose them too. Admission's state-snapshot span includes config recovery, database readiness, plugin validation, and device identity; plugin config already overlaps database readiness. Record the metadata owner's existing timings/counts and isolate metadata completion instead of adding another cache or deferring admission.

Reuse the existing operation tracker for startup reconciliation, removing duplicate registration and settlement. Production changes total +18 lines, needed for the requested attribution; tests +44, docs +2. No schema, configuration option, new cache, or second preparation path is introduced. No startup speedup is claimed.

## Evidence

- 44 focused tests passed across `config-preflight-snapshot.test.ts`, `server-worker-placement-startup.test.ts`, and `server-startup-trace.test.ts`. The 8 worker lifecycle tests passed again after the operation-tracking simplification. The new admission diagnostic test fails on the base because the completion span is missing, and passes with the change.
- Changed-file oxfmt, type-aware lint, and `git diff --check` passed. `pnpm tsgo:core` (native tsrs) passed after a patch-identical rebase onto latest main; broad gates belong to PR CI. No Testbox/Crabbox lease was allocated.
- Independent Codex review of the final diff: no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Real built Gateway startup in an isolated Linux sandbox, synthetic state only: 3 agents and existing agent databases, 5,000 sessions, 6,000 retained runs, 200 approvals, 100 disabled cron jobs, 4 loaded plugins and 169 indexed plugins. Source-performance builds passed. Concurrent A/B pairs held the exclusive measurement lock, each side had 16 cores, and the next pair swapped CPU halves. Separate fresh state/ports; every accepted run verified its own ready log, `/readyz`, and clean shutdown.

Final-source measurements against base `711ffb0d5178` (milliseconds):

| Metric | Pair 1 base → change | Pair 2 base → change | Median paired difference |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Time to ready | 11035.6 → 10940.3 | 11621.6 → 11650.6 | −33.2 |
| Worker environments | 39.5 → 52.7 | 129.2 → 48.1 | −33.9 |
| Admission state snapshot | 1314.9 → 1235.4 | 1407.0 → 1365.2 | −60.6 |
| Admission plugin config | 622.1 → 556.3 | 610.9 → 655.2 | −10.8 |

The readiness difference is neutral (−0.29%); it is not evidence of a speedup. Four earlier pairs before the small operation-tracking simplification were also neutral: median paired +37.0 ms (+0.42%). Outside CPU busy time for the final pairs was 50.41%/59.85%, recorded for context; both sides ran concurrently, with ≤0.02 ms spawn skew. A preliminary attempt hit an occupied port before starting its Gateway and was excluded as a setup failure.

The new spans separated publication readiness (0.2–0.7 ms), workspace recovery (14.0–30.6 ms), active reconciliation (1.9–2.2 ms), and publication recovery (16.1–27.7 ms). Plugin metadata completion took 17.0–17.4 ms; registry snapshot work took 160.0–180.8 ms.

**Gap:** the fixture has no worker placements or workspace-reconciliation journals, so it does not reproduce the reported six-second placement-recovery delay. This PR supplies the missing attribution to identify that backlog before changing its readiness contract. It does not claim to solve the original latency or validate remote worker provisioning.

## CI failure attribution

CI run [39180721768](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39180721768), job [checks-node-changed-compact-large-1-1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39180721768/job/117833007995), fails in `src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.plugin-deferral.test.ts`: 12 failed, 1 passed, with `connect ENOENT` against a broker socket inside an already-removed test fixture. The broker survives fixture cleanup; subsequent Doctor operations reuse its missing socket. The earliest failure precedes config-snapshot preparation.

The identical focused command reproduced all 12 failed test names and the same missing-socket signature on both the exact CI merge `4b760254f1d96c2c55f83f40a7eb2b9491b1bad1` (62.92 s, exit 1) and its exact main parent `c5c558d96d42dc7e0209de3724e1d742705d2831` (48.32 s, exit 1). Both used an isolated Linux sandbox, Node 24.19.0, the same pinned Bun binary and frozen dependencies. The tested candidate tree was verified against CI's merge tree `cb7387487f11507cb8c8d67fc98d17008ece6074`; removing only this PR's seven-file patch produced the baseline.

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun OPENCLAW_VITEST_WORKER_CACHE=1 \
OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  --config test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts \
  src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.plugin-deferral.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

The supplementary macOS replay passed 13/13; its longer temporary paths activate the stable socket-directory fallback, so it is not the basis for inherited attribution. No CI rerun was requested. The matching Linux baseline is evidence for the explicitly authorized inherited-failure landing exception; CI is not represented as green.

CI attempt 1 has completed. All three PostgreSQL conformance shards and the other selected checks passed; the only failed test job is the inherited Doctor shard above. The aggregate gate also fails on that shard. Dependency review and security-sensitive review passed. The automatic failure classifier reports `unknown` because the scheduled main workflow lacks a matching shard; the exact-parent Linux reproduction above supplies the missing causal attribution.

prs.title: improve: reduce redundant SQLite startup work
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway startup and database maintenance repeat connection-policy SQL and schema-cookie reads that their existing native owners already supplied.

## User Impact

No configuration, database format, permissions, or retention changes. Startup and maintenance issue less SQL while preserving lock policy, schema consistency, and lease refusal.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pass initial busy timeout to the native constructor and record the native effective policy in the existing connection cache, including SQLite’s clamp of accepted negative constructor timeouts to zero. Agent opens, preflight, startup checkpoint connections, rollback readers/writers, integrity checks, and page-cache readers no longer issue a separate initial assignment. Omitted-timeout and reopened connections still adopt actual native policy; close invalidation and temporary lock-admission timeout restoration remain.

Schema comparison reuses an enclosing physical read snapshot, removing its redundant cookie query and private forwarding wrapper. Top-level comparison still pins a snapshot; generic schema fact capture still reads the current cookie, including after same-connection DDL.

The agent admission timestamp uses the existing single-statement write path. The lease ID, agent, path, PID predicates and affected-row refusal remain. Quarantine commits on its own connection before the state update. PostgreSQL retains its transaction/advisory-lock path; stores are not fused.

Production: **34 added / 34 removed (net 0)**. Tests: **196 added / 65 removed (net +131)**. No new cache, schema, worker request, retry, or lifecycle owner. Accepted edge: delayed/reopened native connections retain one policy-adoption read. Synchronous boot admission/migration and destructive cleanup custody remain in their existing owners.

## Evidence

The prior timeout suite passed **9/9**, including explicit zero/nonzero policy without SQL, temporary restoration, omitted timeout, and close/reopen/delayed-open lifecycle. Three focused candidate regressions pass, and the same tests fail on the base for the intended removed work: the timeout read, duplicate schema cookie, and admission transaction envelope. The snapshot case observes a later commit; the lease case refuses to resurrect a released claim. Both local arms used the same installed dependency graph, which predates this PR's lockfile; exact-lock coverage comes from CI.

CI exposed an overbroad test spy that counted the close owner's deliberate timeout-zero assignment; the repair checks initial open and reopen separately. Final conflict integration preserves main’s test consolidation. The four affected consumers pass **25/25** with the locked dependency graph. Their wrapper failed while publishing the aggregate JSON report; all three individual shard reports passed, and every runtime group settled. That tooling failure is not claimed as a successful wrapper run.

Codex review found that native SQLite accepts a negative constructor timeout and clamps it to zero. The cache now records the same effective value. A real-owner Node 24 probe fails before the fix (`-1 !== 0`) and passes afterward for -1, 0, and 37, proving no initial policy SQL and successful temporary-timeout restoration. Bun independently confirms the same native clamp. The expanded regression table covers these inputs; the final-head owner tests cover it. Changed-file formatting, type-aware lint, and diff checks pass; this is follow-through on the existing review finding after the two allowed independent review rounds.

Current head feee0ecaa5ab merges main 1f60d6a55631 without conflicts; all 19 PR-owned source/test blobs remain byte-identical to reviewed 5c802966. PostgreSQL approval carries over for this unchanged production integration. The shared frozen install completed; local proof uses the default pinned Bun runtime and type checks use the repository tsrs lanes.

Exact-head CI 39180543810 passes production/test types, lint, source contracts, architecture, ratchets, and selected changed-owner tests. Its behavioral failures include confirmed main failures: Doctor schema version 19 versus 28, obsolete snapshots and plugin/preflight/resource cleanup (main 39172446197/job 117808338466); session-recovery native borrowers (job 117808338765); unsafe-SQLite update status (job 117808338666); and both subagent recovery cases, `Recovery did not reach its write` (main 39176649118/job 117820741692). The same named cases and error signatures were compared. These failed jobs remain failed.

The backup-custody success case passes on this exact head in 241 ms (39180543810/job 117832461429). Its prior-head 120-second timeout remains unexplained; the passing current run is not claimed as a repair or proof of inheritance.

All three final-head PostgreSQL conformance shards pass. Final-head Knip (39181409163/job 117835001621) reports two production and four full-tree unused exports; script exports and both unused-file scans are clean. Every finding has observed main evidence: the two CLI symbols reproduce in the completed production scan on exact main 1f60d6a; the three FaceTime helpers repeat scheduled main 39176649118/job 117820741086. The exact-main full-tree scan timed out, so its CLI finding is matched by the same unused-export rule/file/symbol in the completed production scan. This is zero-new-findings attribution, not a passing Knip job.

One behavioral failure remains investigated but unresolved: `sessions.patchMany attempts every archive drain release without masking success` (39180543810/job 117832461676) observes reversed drain **start** order. The implementation prepares targets with `Promise.all` and awaits projection/validation before each drain starts; release traversal separately preserves target order. Recent main runs pass this case, so inheritance is **not established**. A bounded base/head replay used identical test-only scheduling gates around the real projection to exercise that permitted ordering; the base worker stalled in filesystem rename before any test verdict, and no candidate arm ran. Cancellation settled, the original test bytes were restored, and no assertion or production behavior was changed. The cause of this occurrence remains uncertain. This is disclosed under the relaxed landing/test-failure policy, without claiming a baseline failure or a fix.

The published-driver update on unchanged production head 5c802966 (39177307686/job 117825891160) failed at Doctor heartbeat-cadence inspection with `SQLite snapshot staging owner launch context changed; retire its snapshots before retrying`. The identical sole error finding and failure facts occur on scheduled main 39172446197/job 117810637913 at 4812f059. Both runs passed candidate migration/config admission and Doctor repair, then recovered a healthy published Gateway. This is inherited failure evidence, not a passing update cell. The earlier production-head update passed (39170765106/job 117808955618).

Workload measurements are deferred to the campaign’s combined census because local SSD stalls prevented reliable completion. Source attribution predicts boot **-3 SQL / -3 MAIN**, restart boot **-6 SQL / -3 MAIN**, connect **-3 SQL**, and compaction/connected idle **-1 SQL each**; requests and warm turns are expected unchanged. These are estimates, not measured medians. Additional maintenance-only constructor conversions are not counted as observed savings. No latency claim.

The chat header wired its native shortcut listener directly, and child attention owned a local effect and timer solely to repaint when the nearest recorded status expired. Both responsibilities already have shared reactive helpers.

## Change

Use `createInterval()` with a delay derived from the nearest finite expiry among visible child statuses. Each tick refreshes the existing clock-derived rows, and the cadence pauses when no finite expiry remains. Canonical session rows continue to own the status itself.

## Scope and counts

Two production files; no test, dependency, tag, class, route, or configuration changes. No intended visual change.

| Total | 661 → 659 | 1 → 0 | 1 → 0 | 0 → 0 |

The one existing header `flush()` is unchanged: native menu opening reads the prepared items synchronously. The local effect and raw event wiring are removed; there are no new state owners or abstractions.
