prs.title: fix(browser): Gateway freezes while macOS gates Chrome profile reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Gateway stops answering every request (health checks, Control UI, browser relay) when it lists Chrome-family system profiles on a Mac where macOS is waiting for an App Data permission answer.

## User Impact

User impact: browser profile discovery and cookie import no longer freeze the Gateway on newer macOS. While the permission prompt is unanswered, those requests time out and the rest of the Gateway keeps working; once the prompt is answered, discovery completes normally.

## Why This Change Was Made

Newer macOS App Data protection holds `open()` on another app's data, such as Chrome's `Local State`, until someone answers a consent prompt. On a headless host that can be forever. System-profile discovery read those files synchronously on the Gateway event loop, and it runs for the agent browser tool's `profiles` action and the macOS app's import-status check.

Discovery and cookie-source resolution now use async file access, so a held `open()` occupies one libuv pool thread instead of the event loop. Concurrent callers join one in-flight probe per browser root, so app checks and agent retries cannot park every pool thread while consent is pending. Cookie import opens the Cookies database asynchronously before the synchronous SQLite snapshot, so macOS settles consent first. The CLI reference notes the new prompt behavior.

Release note: Browser: system-profile discovery and import no longer freeze the Gateway while macOS waits for App Data permission to read Chrome-family browser data.

## Evidence

- Incident: a sampled macOS Gateway had its main thread blocked for over an hour in system-profile discovery's `readFileSync(.../Google/Chrome/Local State)` → `open()`, while `sandboxd` logged `kTCCServiceSystemPolicyAppDataDetailed` checks for `com.google.Chrome` attributed to the Gateway process. The listen queue filled and only a forced restart recovered it.
- Regression test (`system-profiles.test.ts`): a FIFO at Chrome's `Local State` holds `open()` the same way. It fails on `main` (event loop frozen 3.3 s until the test's safety valve releases it) and passes with the fix (152 ms), and it proves two interleaved callers share one read.
- `pnpm test` for the system-profiles, cookie-sync CLI, profiles-service and browser-tool suites: 113 passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, oxlint and oxfmt on touched files: clean.
- Isolated Gateway (built checkout, isolated HOME with a FIFO `Local State`, browser control server enabled): during an 8 s hold `/readyz` answered 200 in 1–9 ms; after release `openclaw browser system-profiles --json` exited 0 with the profile.
- Gap: CI cannot raise a real macOS consent prompt; the FIFO models the held `open()`.

<details>
<summary>Change size</summary>

Production: `system-profiles.ts` +72/−27 (async probes, per-root in-flight join), `browser-cli-cookie-sync.ts` +1/−1 (await). Tests: +45/−2. Docs: +2. No superseded path remains; every caller of the converted functions now awaits them.

</details>

prs.title: fix(skills): ignored skills load when ignore-file reads fail
prs.body:
Related: #101429

## What Problem This Solves

Session skill discovery silently drops ignore policy when an existing `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, or `.fdignore` cannot be read. Excluded skills can then load with no diagnostic. `existsSync` also classifies an unresolved cyclic ignore-file symlink as absent, bypassing the read entirely.

## User Impact

A failed ignore policy now produces the existing directory warning and skips that subtree. Healthy siblings still load. Ordinary absent ignore files, valid symlink chains, size/pattern budgets, and oversized fail-closed exclusions keep their behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use fault-aware `lstatSync` for cheap optional-file absence, propagate resolution/read failures to the existing per-directory warning owner, and remove the orphan nullable-result branch. Classify oversized reads through fs-safe's existing `too-large` error code rather than its message. No new error type, logger, fallback, retry, option, dependency, or persisted shape is introduced.

The bounded-read conversion in #101429 retained older silent swallowing while establishing oversized fail-closed behavior and valid symlink support. Those contracts remain. This bug was found with actual native I/O fixtures, not a claimed human incident.

### Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- A broken or unreadable policy may hide otherwise valid skills within its affected subtree until the policy is repaired or a later scan succeeds. Continuing without the user's exclusions is intentionally removed; unaffected sibling directories remain available.
- A present but broken ignore-file symlink is now a warning, not ordinary absence. Valid symlink chains and genuinely missing ignore-file entries are preserved.
- If an ignore file disappears after its presence check, the existing directory warning handles that scan; no timing/retry machinery is added.

Net production LOC: 11 removed; test LOC: 29 added.

## Evidence

The public `loadSkills` regression uses real filesystem fixtures for nonregular and cyclic-symlink ignore files. It verifies that private content does not load, one directory warning is returned, and a healthy sibling still loads. The nonregular case failed on unchanged production code (18.56s Vitest; 37.55s wrapper). The cyclic case separately failed on the first incomplete repair (5.71s; 24.84s), exposing the existence-check swallowing layer.

Final focused results: session catalog 8/8 (12.65s), shared ignore rules 9/9 (4.05s), suppression guard 14/14 (72.03s); the serial wrapper completed in 151.82s. Existing byte/pattern-budget and valid-symlink cases are unchanged. Independent native production-entrypoint controls confirm actual EACCES and ELOOP now exclude the synthetic private skill and return one warning. Targeted native tsrs types and focused type-aware lint pass without diagnostics. The existing resource-loader consumer suite also passes 5/5 (351.89s; 404.60s wrapper, including first-use worker preparation of 300.821s). No timeout was raised; this is setup cost, not a performance benchmark.

Three-file formatting and whitespace checks pass. Fresh independent P0-P2 review found no actionable defects, with final captured-source verification and exact blob matching. The change reuses the existing fs-safe dependency; its advanced reader already imports the path owner, so no new internal runtime import edge or component is introduced. Broad cycle/build checks remain with exact-head PR CI under the shared-host budget. Runtime proof used isolated HOME/OpenClaw/XDG paths and synthetic files only; no operator Gateway or user data was touched.

prs.title: fix(cli): escape terminal controls in session and node reports
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Three CLI reports printed operator- or model-controlled strings straight to the terminal. A session key, path, node name or error message containing ANSI/OSC/C0 control sequences could clear the screen, retitle the terminal window, or rewrite earlier output:

- `openclaw sessions compact` reports and errors (`src/commands/sessions-compact.ts`, from `e35e5f123dd`)
- `openclaw nodes rename` / `nodes remove` confirmations and the shared nodes failure helper (`src/cli/nodes-cli/register.pairing.ts`, `src/cli/nodes-cli/cli-utils.ts`)
- session lifecycle reports with keys, paths and diagnostics (`src/commands/sessions-lifecycle.ts`, from `2efac6c9991`)

Recent fixes already closed the same gap for model selection (#176007), camera list (#175624) and inspected agent names (#174989); these were the remaining siblings.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each human-readable line now goes through the existing `sanitizeTerminalText` (`packages/terminal-core/src/safe-text.js`) exactly once. No new sanitizer was added. JSON output and RPC request parameters keep the raw values, so scripts and the Gateway see unchanged data. Production delta: +7 lines across the three surfaces (one wrapper per print site).

## User Impact

Terminal output from these commands can no longer be hijacked by control sequences in names, keys or errors. Escaped text stays readable (`\n`, `\r` shown literally), and `--json` output is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Regression tests fail before each fix and pass after: compaction 15/15 (5 failed before), nodes 30/30 (2 failed before), lifecycle 18/18 (1 failed before). Each test also asserts that JSON and RPC values remain raw.
- A real agent run against a local stub provider passed 39 tool calls covering visible failures, huge or binary output, and early-closed stdin.
- `docs/cli/nodes.md` and `docs/cli/sessions.md` note the escaping.
- Codex autoreview: clean.

prs.title: fix(acp): keep completed run-mode sessions resumable
prs.body:
Closes #106696.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes lost conversation context when a parent sends a follow-up to a completed ACP `mode="run"` child.

## User Impact

Parents can continue a completed Claude or Codex one-shot using the same child key, confirmed conversation identity, and working directory. Unsupported, unconfirmed, legacy metadata-loss, and confirmed missing-target cases fail explicitly instead of silently starting a new conversation. Workers are still released after completion.

Ordinary parent-owned completed-child follow-ups return asynchronous `accepted`, including with a positive send timeout, and use the current session-follow-up completion owner. Explicit caller-owned and scoped-grant completion retain their existing inline behavior. Persistent sessions retain agent-ID-first resume selection.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resume eligibility is recorded only when the backend advertises support and a completed turn confirms usable identity. Follow-ups stay on that backend. Current operation admission, requester authority, generation fencing, prompt restoration, and MCP ownership remain in place; ambiguous errors preserve retryable identity.

This refresh ports the fix to the current completion owners instead of restoring the retired task registry. Dispatch and completion now consume the same prepared requester/target facts in the existing follow-up module. A review regression also fixes a speculative bridge lookup rejecting valid listed sessions when that optional bridge is absent; genuine Gateway errors still propagate.

**Maintainer decision still needed:** completed one-shot identity retention/deletion, the optional backend capability contract, and asynchronous parent completion. This patch does not reconstruct previously deleted legacy state or promise that an older version preserves the new resume flags. No merge approval is presumed.

## Evidence

Current head `7913b4932edd1839318513d6feba4a09a41ad893`, based on `bf8da001d61c25e8c4dcc1eeaa6ea88a62ef4f97`, uses upstream ACPX 0.19.4 without a dependency override.

### Current-Head Fixture Corrections

CI at `2450afa` identified two test-only issues: the resume store fixture omitted required `cfg` and `storePath` fields, and five closed mocks lacked the current isolation contract. This head supplies the fixture fields, removes the unnecessary command-list mock, and documents the four intentional host/config/delivery/custody boundaries. No production code, assertions, or baselines changed.

The record-replacement suite passed **6/6** tests (38.10 seconds runner wall time), and the bridge suite passed **4/4** with real command discovery (12.52 seconds runner wall time). Formatting, syntax-only lint, and diff checks pass. The agent follow-up file changed only comments; its preceding 47-test grouped validation remains applicable to its unchanged executable content. The native TypeScript-based ratchet and typecheck are left to fresh CI, not claimed locally passing.

### Cancellation Correction (2450afa)

CI at preceding head `fda8887b7c1c957dee0e36d1aad7e2c396f0aaef` exposed a real regression in two unchanged owner/lifecycle-replacement tests: cancellation lost its durable terminal signal while awaiting identity reconciliation. The exact CI base's runner and test were compared; this was not classified as inherited.

That commit changes only `manager.turn-runner.ts`: pre-publication reconciliation is limited to completed, non-aborted one-shots. Persistent and cancelled turns retain upstream publication-before-final-reconciliation ordering, including its authority checks. Strict one-shot identity persistence remains intact.

The two cancellation-replacement cases and four one-shot completion/readiness cases passed: **6/6 tests in two files**, **130.61 seconds** command wall time, **36.87 seconds** project duration. Syntax-only lint and diff checks pass. Independent narrow review found no actionable P0-P2 findings. An earlier worker-preparation attempt stopped before tests and is not counted as passing evidence.

### Broader Refresh Validation (fda8887)

- The initial selected 15-file run passed 154 tests. Four copied fixtures failed because the current state-event reader is asynchronous; those call sites now await the existing API, with no runtime workaround.
- That refresh's affected rerun passed **47/47 tests across five files**: one-shot completion, public ACP follow-up routing, native child coordination, native follow-up authority, and bridge resume/reset. This rerun overlaps the initial run; the counts are not additive.
- The canonical-session bridge regression was observed failing with `No session found: acp-bridge:agent:main:work`, then passed after making only the speculative lookup allow a missing result. Explicit routing and reset siblings also pass.
- Earlier unchanged adapter coverage includes recreated processes, preserved context/cwd and MCP ownership, and refusal to silently start fresh when a confirmed target is missing.
- Formatting, syntax-only lint, and `git diff --check` pass. No unit-test assertions, lint limits, or baselines were weakened.

Commands used the repository runner: `pnpm test <selected-files> --maxWorkers=1`. The final five-file command took **1333.86 seconds**, including 340 seconds preparing worker artifacts. Its three project durations were 889.54, 23.64, and 31.32 seconds. These are grouped local measurements, not individual-file or CI timings. Current-head CI timings remain pending. Persistence, requester retirement, and adapter-process boundaries use the real owners; pure predicate mocks would not cover those contracts.

The official full-candidate autoreview reported no actionable P0-P2 findings. An additional independent review found the optional-bridge defect above; the regression and correction address it. A fresh narrow review of the subsequent existing-owner extraction and bridge correction found no further P0-P2 findings. These are static reviews, not provider or delivery proof.

### Release-State Compatibility (fda8887)

An isolated source-owner probe used exact v2026.10.3 (`59cb44796b0f1f0daa0e37af8b1495abb45d9bc1`), real SQLite persistence/migration owners, synthetic session state, and a synthetic ACP backend. It established:

- A byte-verified closed release snapshot at shared/agent schemas 20/24, with legacy IDs, working directory, parent/lifecycle identity, and transcript markers.
- Offline migration to 24/27; persistent resume retained agent-ID-first selection. An unconfirmed legacy one-shot did not auto-resume. Once a synthetic turn confirmed its new ACP identity, the next turn reused that identity and the same child key/cwd, preserving state on close.
- Separate post-exit observation and fresh-process candidate reopen recovered the persisted flags/IDs and original transcript markers, with integrity checks.
- The exact old release refused newer schemas without changing database bytes. Restoring the untouched release snapshot into a new directory recovered matching old session rows and transcripts at 20/24.
- A schema-neutral additive-field roundtrip remained readable by the old release. Its normalizer dropped unknown resume flags and retained legacy agent-first selection; preservation after old-runtime rewriting is **not** claimed.

The observation, reopen, refusal, restore, additive-write, and additive-read phases each exited 0 without timeout and retained unchanged source fingerprints. Three earlier failures remain recorded: incorrect migration ownership in the harness; a 300-second proof-process timeout; and an overstrict observation guard rejecting a zero-byte WAL with retained SHM after behavior and shutdown assertions passed. The last failed outcome was not rewritten: a separate read-only observation completed it. Snapshot-copy checks stayed strict, and no sidecars or schema markers were deleted or rewritten to force a pass.

This is source-owner persistence evidence at the preceding refresh head, **not** installed-package updater or CLI backup-archive restore E2E proof. It did not use provider credentials, production state, Telegram, or real ACP subprocesses. The subsequent cancellation and test-only corrections do not change metadata formats or migration code; the full compatibility probe was not repeated for them.

### Historical Provider Proof

The following real-provider proof belongs to previous head `8f2ce3799f8bbbb20cd197e94fa624a1a60660ca`, **not this refresh**. On 2026-09-24, isolated Claude ACP 0.78.0 and Codex ACP 1.12.0 runs using ACPX 0.19.1 completed a nonce-bearing one-shot, shut down/recreated the adapter, and resumed with the original backend identity. Both recalled the nonce and working directory without repeating the nonce; tool events were zero. Source/dependency hashes stayed unchanged.

This was adapter-level continuity proof, not a full Gateway restart or Telegram delivery test. It must not be read as fresh provider validation of this candidate.

### Remaining Gaps

Type-aware lint/typechecking and the repository-wide suite are not run locally under host constraints. No check limits or baselines were relaxed. New-head CI and maintainer contract acceptance remain required. Previous-head CI failures are not assumed fixed merely because the base changed.

AI-assisted implementation, review, and validation.

prs.title: fix(codex): bound app-server websocket handshake waits to requestTimeoutMs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators using Codex app-server over websocket/unix transport would hang forever on initialize/RPC when a peer accepted the socket but never completed the WebSocket upgrade.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bound upgrades with `ws.handshakeTimeout` **and** an explicit CONNECTING deadline at the transport chokepoint (`createWebSocketTransport`). `ws.handshakeTimeout` alone does **not** abort custom `createConnection` (Unix) upgrades - verified with a never-upgrade peer that stayed CONNECTING past the library timeout.

Production budget is resolved `appServer.requestTimeoutMs` (default 60s) from `CodexAppServerClient.start` via `resolveCodexAppServerRuntimeOptions()`.

**Narrowed to Codex-only (Maintainer option 1, recommended):** Removed the unrelated APNs CodeQL allowlist (`#109357`) and docs-sync typings export (`#109364`) that prior heads bundled to unblock CI. Those are main pre-existing debt and should land independently. This branch now touches only Codex runtime, Codex tests, and the Codex harness doc.

Documented the expanded `requestTimeoutMs` contract in `docs/plugins/codex-harness.md` so operators know it also bounds WebSocket/Unix upgrade handshakes.

Collision check: [#108795](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/108795) closed unmerged; APNs allowlist split [#109357](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/109357); typings unblocker [#109364](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/109364).

## User Impact

- **Before:** never-upgrade peers hang initialize/RPC forever (TCP and Unix).
- **After:** handshake follows operator `requestTimeoutMs` (default 60s) on both TCP and Unix, then emits transport exit (`1006`).

## Verification

- Exact head: `cd7dafa044d07cbfb3dbca17b9d2fb5a3160e23a`
- `oxfmt --check` (4 files) - passed; exit 0.
- `oxlint` (3 TS files) - passed; exit 0.
- `git diff --check` - passed; exit 0.

Focused tests:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-websocket.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```text
 ✓ |extension-codex| extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-websocket.test.ts > Codex app-server websocket transport > can speak JSON-RPC over websocket transport 73ms
 ✓ |extension-codex| extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-websocket.test.ts > Codex app-server websocket transport > can speak JSON-RPC over the canonical unix control socket 12ms
 ✓ |extension-codex| extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-websocket.test.ts > Codex app-server websocket transport > negative control: ws without handshakeTimeout stays CONNECTING on never-upgrade peer 308ms
 ✓ |extension-codex| extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-websocket.test.ts > Codex app-server websocket transport > emits exit when the websocket handshake never completes 204ms
 ✓ |extension-codex| extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-websocket.test.ts > Codex app-server websocket transport > honors a non-default handshake budget on the TCP transport path 254ms
 ✓ |extension-codex| extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-websocket.test.ts > Codex app-server websocket transport > honors a non-default handshake budget on the Unix transport path 256ms
 ✓ |extension-codex| extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-websocket.test.ts > Codex app-server websocket transport > fails initialize when the websocket handshake never completes 206ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
```

Mutation check: the negative-control test (test 3) proves the bug exists without the fix - `ws` without `handshakeTimeout` stays CONNECTING (`readyState=0`, `outcome=still-pending`) after 300ms. With the fix, tests 4-7 observe bounded exit `1006` within the configured budget.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: a never-upgrading Codex app-server peer that accepts the TCP/Unix socket but never sends HTTP Upgrade headers is terminated within the configured `requestTimeoutMs` budget instead of hanging forever.

Real environment tested: Linux, Node 22, real `net.Server` loopback on `127.0.0.1` and real Unix domain sockets, real `ws` WebSocket client (no mocked transport).

Exact commands run:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-websocket.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

Observed output:

```text
[codex handshake negative control] outcome=still-pending readyState=0 wait_ms=300 without_handshakeTimeout=true
[codex handshake proof] timed_out=true elapsed_ms=201 code=1006 handshakeTimeout_ms=200 production_ms=60000
[codex handshake tcp non-default] timed_out=true elapsed_ms=250 code=1006 handshakeTimeout_ms=250
[codex handshake unix non-default] timed_out=true elapsed_ms=251 code=1006 handshakeTimeout_ms=250
[codex handshake initialize proof] timed_out=true elapsed_ms=203 message=initialize transport failed after request write: WebSocket was closed before the connection was established
```

Evidence:
- Negative control: without `handshakeTimeout`, WebSocket stays CONNECTING (`readyState=0`) after 300ms wait - bug proven
- TCP path: exits `1006` at 201ms with 200ms budget; production budget is 60s
- Unix path: exits `1006` at 251ms with 250ms budget - `ws.handshakeTimeout` alone does not abort Unix `createConnection`
- Initialize: `initialize` fails with "WebSocket was closed before the connection was established" at 203ms
- All 7 tests pass including 2 pre-existing JSON-RPC transport tests (no regression)

What was not tested: live remote Codex app-server with provider credentials; non-Linux Unix domain socket implementations; `ws` library internals beyond the public `handshakeTimeout` + `terminate` API.

## Risk / Compatibility

Medium (timeout policy). Legitimate upgrades slower than `requestTimeoutMs` now exit `1006`. This reuses an existing operator setting (no new config surface) and the default 60s is generous for handshake-only. The expanded contract is documented in `docs/plugins/codex-harness.md`.

CI note: touching `transport-websocket.ts` triggers the full CodeQL `network-runtime-boundary` scan, which currently fails on main's unclassified `openApnsTlsTunnel` `tls.connect`. That is pre-existing main debt tracked in [#109357](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/109357) and should not block this Codex runtime fix.


## Evidence (refreshed 2026-07-21)

Exact head: `cd7dafa044d07cbfb3dbca17b9d2fb5a3160e23a`

Compressed handshake suite: shared never-upgrade peer helper; keep TCP negative control + TCP/Unix deadline abort (`it.each`). Dropped redundant TCP non-default and initialize wrapper cases.

prs.title: fix: models fallbacks --agent silently edits global defaults instead of the agent
prs.body:
Closes #106346

AI-assisted (Claude and Codex), human-reviewed; validation evidence below.

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw models fallbacks list/add/remove/clear --agent <id>` did not consistently operate on the named agent. Reads and writes could instead target `agents.defaults.model.fallbacks`, while `models status --agent <id>` resolved the agent's effective chain. The `image-fallbacks` group also silently ignored `--agent`.

## Behaviour After This Change

- Agent-scoped reads follow the effective configuration: an agent without a local fallback override inherits `agents.defaults.model.fallbacks`; an agent with an override reads its local chain.
- Every explicit `fallbacks add/remove/clear --agent <id>` write creates or updates that named agent's local fallback override. It never mutates the global defaults chain.
- Unknown agent ids fail before any config write.
- `image-fallbacks ... --agent <id>` fails clearly because image fallback configuration is global-only in the schema.
- Calls without `--agent` keep their existing global behaviour.
- The model catalogue (`agents.defaults.models`) remains global; only the text-model fallback list is agent-scoped.

## Implementation

The fallbacks subcommands now resolve and validate `--agent` using the same agent helpers as `models status`. The write path uses an agent-local fallback setter that materialises the named agent's override when necessary and preserves global defaults. CLI wiring accepts `--agent` on the parent or fallbacks subcommand, while image-fallback commands explicitly reject it. `docs/cli/models.md` documents the inherited-read/local-write distinction.

## Evidence

- `src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts`: agent-local writes, inherited reads, clearing, and preservation of defaults.
- `src/cli/models-cli.test.ts`: parent/subcommand flag forwarding, unchanged no-agent behaviour, and image-fallback rejection.
- `src/commands/models.set.e2e.test.ts`: end-to-end agent-local mutation, global catalogue preservation, and unknown-agent rejection.
- Targeted command passed all 3 shards and 80 tests:
  `node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts src/cli/models-cli.test.ts src/commands/models.set.e2e.test.ts`
- Scoped oxlint passed the seven changed TypeScript files with 0 warnings and 0 errors.
- The repository-wide oxlint wrapper was also attempted; its type-aware `tsgolint` subprocess was SIGKILLed by the verification host's memory limit. The underlying oxlint phase reported 0 warnings and 0 errors before that infrastructure failure.
- Integrated current upstream `main` (`8d5ad804a65dddfd60a5e0d6e06e8a1108d8c035`) without conflicts; final head is `5475d31efc8c10229c70591c3b43f38717189245`.

prs.title: feat(goals): continue active session goals while idle
prs.body:
Related: #102260

This is the focused current-main replacement for the deterministic goal-driver slice discussed in #102261 and #103586. It deliberately does not carry forward their unrelated question, plan, judge, wait-barrier, UI, generated, or Hermes-labelled scope.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can persist, display, budget, pause, block, resume, and complete a session goal, but an active goal still stops whenever a turn ends. Operators must send another message to keep an otherwise idle goal moving.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a default-off, deterministic gateway driver that uses the existing session goal, active-run, queued-turn, system-event, heartbeat, context, UI, and `goal_changed` paths. It reserves each bounded continuation durably before enqueueing a wake, lets user work win races, and auto-pauses at the configured ceiling.

The driver is intentionally limited to agent-scoped session keys. Current-main system-event queues cannot safely distinguish the same bare `global` key in multiple agent stores, and expanding queue identity belongs in a separate change. The durable-owner repair in #104265 is also kept separate rather than duplicated here.

## User Impact

Operators who explicitly enable `tools.experimental.goalDriver.enabled` can let an active session goal continue after a fixed idle delay without sending a synthetic user message. Existing goal controls and status UI remain the source of truth. The feature remains inert by default.

## Evidence

- RED contract: fork CI at exact test-only SHA `b5c2f60d959a3714af01be27eddd00b46aa6e7e6` reported the expected missing driver, service, goal reservation/rollback, and gateway-wiring symbols: https://github.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/actions/runs/29228761335
- Tests cover exact delay/no jitter, one timer per durable target, active/user/system queue precedence, persistence failure, race rollback, rejected enqueue, no self-rearm, dynamic disable, startup recovery, unsafe bare-key refusal, bounded concurrent reservations, resume reset, and terminal-persistence ordering.
- Structured pre-commit review of the tests-only contract completed with no actionable findings.
- GREEN exact-head CI and non-repository visual evidence will be added before this draft is marked ready.

prs.title: fix(cli): warn that attach --print-config prints a live bearer token
prs.body:
Related: #104517 — partial mitigation. Options 2–4 in that issue remain open.

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw attach --print-config` prints the full MCP grant config, including
`env.OPENCLAW_MCP_TOKEN` — a live, unrevoked bearer credential — as plain JSON on
stdout with no indication that it is sensitive. Anyone copying that output into a
log, chat transcript, screen share, or bug report can leak the live token without
realizing it. As reported in #104517, this surfaced during a 2026.7.1-beta.5 canary
run where the report artifact had to be manually redacted afterwards.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a warning printed to **stderr** immediately before the JSON payload is printed
to **stdout**, gated on `process.stderr` being a TTY (reusing the existing
`isTtyStream` helper, now exported from `terminal-interactivity.ts`). Interactive
users see it; scripted or redirected consumers — anything piping or parsing the
JSON, including wrappers that treat any stderr output as a failure signal — get
byte-identical prior output, because the existing stdout output and non-TTY stderr
behavior are both unchanged by this patch.

This started as an unconditional warning (any stderr, TTY or not). ClawSweeper
flagged that as a `merge-risk: compatibility` concern: a wrapper that treats any
stderr output as failure could break on the new line even though nothing was
actually wrong. Rather than wait on a maintainer product call, this was narrowed to
TTY-only gating, which removes that compatibility risk entirely while still
surfacing the warning to the interactive users it is meant for. The maintainer
question from earlier revisions of this PR (whether an unconditional warning was
acceptable) is now moot — see "Evidence" section 1b below for real-run proof of the
gated behavior, and "Decisions superseded" for what changed.

This still implements only option 1 of #104517 (a clear warning). It deliberately
does not redact the token or reshape the printed config: that would break the
documented copy/launch workflow, and #104517 carries `needs-product-decision`,
`needs-security-review`, and `no-new-fix-pr`, so the shape of a log-safe default is
a maintainer call rather than something to settle inside a bugfix PR. The issue
stays open either way — this PR does not close it.

## User Impact

Interactive users whose stderr is attached to a terminal now get an explicit
warning that the printed env carries a live bearer token and must be treated as a
secret. Scripted/redirected callers (non-TTY stderr) see no change at all.

Two limits are worth stating plainly:

- **The token is still in the default stdout output.** This reduces the chance of
  accidental copying; it does not remove the exposure.
- **Interactive stderr now carries one more line for this command.** Only when
  stderr is a real terminal. (For context, the captures below show this Node build
  already emitting a SQLite `ExperimentalWarning` on stderr for the same command,
  regardless of TTY.) stdout consumers, and any non-TTY stderr consumer, are
  unaffected.

## Evidence

Sections 1–4 were produced at head `45e0b05fefc136cc43153f18d3b019c6d272904e`
against the original **unconditional** warning; section 3 used a single deliberate
one-line mutation, described in place. The branch was later rebased onto latest
`main` (#120893 rewrote this area) at head `85c61d0cfffb1026837fbec355f3f6202a6794f4`,
then updated again to add the TTY gating described above, at the current head
`574b05fbe320e1ccca894a62740348061e4af5fc`. The net diff at the current head is
`+21 −0` across `src/cli/attach-cli.ts` (+6), `src/cli/attach-cli.action.test.ts`
(+11), and `docs/cli/attach.md` (+4). Section 1b below is new: it proves the TTY
gating itself with a real (non-mocked) run of each branch.

### 1. Real behavior — real CLI, real Gateway, real grant (original, unconditional warning)

A dev Gateway was started on a free port inside an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`,
and the real CLI entry point was then invoked against it with:

```
attach --print-config --session agent:main:cli
```

This is a real Gateway process minting a real scoped grant, not a mocked gateway or
a stubbed runtime. The operator's default gateway port (18789) was never bound, per
`AGENTS.md` ("Live gateway tests: session-owned dev gateway only — isolated
`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` + free port"). The Gateway was torn down at the end of the run
and the grant is TTL-bound to that throwaway state directory.

stdout and stderr were captured on separate streams. `[REDACTED-TOKEN]`, `[PATH]`
and `[PORT]` are redaction markers applied by me, not literal output.

**stdout** — the configuration handoff:

```text
{
  "sessionKey": "agent:main:cli",
  "expiresAt": "2026-08-09T10:00:38.754Z",
  "env": {
    "OPENCLAW_MCP_TOKEN": "[REDACTED-TOKEN]"
  },
  "configPath": "[PATH]",
  "launch": [
    "claude",
    "--strict-mcp-config",
    "--mcp-config",
    "[PATH]"
  ]
}
Grant is live until 2026-08-09T10:00:38.754Z and auto-expires; it is not revoked here. Launch with the env above, then delete [PATH] when done.
```

**stderr** — the warning (unconditional, at this now-superseded head):

```text
(node:[PORT]) ExperimentalWarning: SQLite is an experimental feature and might change at any time
(Use `node --trace-warnings ...` to show where the warning was created)
WARNING: the JSON below includes a live OPENCLAW_MCP_TOKEN bearer credential (env.OPENCLAW_MCP_TOKEN). Treat it as a secret: *** not paste it into logs, chat transcripts, or shared reports.
```

CLI exit code: `0`.

> The `***` in that last line is my redaction tooling over-matching, not CLI output.
> The literal string is `do not`, visible in this PR's diff. I have left the capture
> as produced rather than hand-editing it.

### 1b. Real behavior — TTY gating proof (current head, real pty vs. real redirected stderr)

Produced at the current head `574b05fbe320e1ccca894a62740348061e4af5fc` against the
same kind of throwaway dev Gateway as section 1 (isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`,
free port, `attach --print-config --session agent:main:cli`), run twice from the
same test harness (`test/helpers/openclaw-test-instance.ts`):

- **Non-TTY run**: the CLI's stdout/stderr are plain OS pipes (`child_process.spawn`
  default `stdio: "pipe"`), so `process.stderr.isTTY` is `undefined` — this is the
  same shape as any redirected/scripted invocation.
- **TTY run**: the CLI is spawned under a real pseudo-terminal via
  `@lydell/node-pty` (the same dependency this repo's own E2E pty lane —
  `scripts/e2e/lib/run-with-pty.mjs` — uses), so `process.stderr.isTTY` is `true`,
  exactly as it would be for a human running this command directly in a terminal.
  A real pty has one shared fd for stdout+stderr (this is also true for a human at
  a terminal), so this capture is the interleaved combined stream rather than two
  separate ones; ANSI/cursor control sequences were stripped for readability, only
  that — no reordering or text changes. `[REDACTED-TOKEN]` and `[TMPDIR]` are my
  redaction markers.

**Non-TTY stderr — no warning, byte-shape unchanged from before this PR:**

```text
(node:[PID]) ExperimentalWarning: SQLite is an experimental feature and might change at any time
(Use `node --trace-warnings ...` to show where the warning was created)
```

**Non-TTY stdout — unaffected:**

```text
{
  "sessionKey": "agent:main:cli",
  "expiresAt": "2026-09-22T09:24:02.284Z",
  "env": {
    "OPENCLAW_MCP_TOKEN": "[REDACTED-TOKEN]"
  },
  "configPath": "C:\\Users\\John\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\[TMPDIR]\\.mcp.json",
  "launch": [
    "claude",
    "--strict-mcp-config",
    "--mcp-config",
    "C:\\Users\\John\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\[TMPDIR]\\.mcp.json"
  ]
}
Grant is live until 2026-09-22T09:24:02.284Z and auto-expires; it is not revoked here. Launch with the env above, then delete C:\Users\John\AppData\Local\Temp\[TMPDIR]\.mcp.json when done.
```

**TTY run — combined stream, warning present and ordered before the JSON** (CLI
startup banner from an unrelated, pre-existing splash-screen feature left in place
to show this is a real interactive run, not a stub):

```text
(node:[PID]) ExperimentalWarning: SQLite is an experimental feature and might change at any time
(Use `node --trace-warnings ...` to show where the warning was created)
Loading OpenClaw CLI…

🦞 OpenClaw  2026.8.1 (b8e4008) — Shell yeah—I'm here to pinch the toil and leave you the glory.WARNING: the JSON below includes a live OPENCLAW_MCP_TOKEN bearer credential (env.OPENCLAW_MCP_TOKEN). Treat it as a secret: do not paste it into logs, chat transcripts, or shared reports.
{
  "sessionKey": "agent:main:cli",
  "expiresAt": "2026-09-22T09:24:11.966Z",
  "env": {
    "OPENCLAW_MCP_TOKEN": "[REDACTED-TOKEN]"
  },
  "configPath": "C:\\Users\\John\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\[TMPDIR]\\.mcp.json",
  "launch": [
    "claude",
    "--strict-mcp-config",
    "--mcp-config",
    "C:\\Users\\John\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\[TMPDIR]\\.mcp.json"
  ]
}
Grant is live until 2026-09-22T09:24:11.966Z and auto-expires; it is not revoked here. Launch with the env above, then delete C:\Users\John\AppData\Local\Temp\[TMPDIR]\.mcp.json when done.
```

CLI exit code in both runs: `0`. This directly proves the gating: identical command,
identical Gateway/grant path, the only variable is whether stderr is a real TTY, and
that variable alone toggles the warning.

### 2. Focused regression test

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.cli.config.ts src/cli/attach-cli.action.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 ✓ --print-config: mints + writes config + prints launch, does NOT revoke or name a nonexistent command
 ✓ --print-config: warns on stderr that the printed env carries a live bearer token (interactive TTY)
 ✓ --print-config: skips the stderr warning when stderr is redirected (non-TTY)
 ✓ calls attach.grant in CLI mode with an auto-resolved device identity (operator.admin regression guard)
 ✓ resolves a URL target before granting on the same origin
 ✓ preserves a global-scope URL main session when granting attach access
 ✓ rejects a non-positive --ttl before minting
 ✓ rejects malformed --ttl 0x10 before minting
 ✓ rejects malformed --ttl 1.5 before minting
 ✓ rejects malformed --ttl 1e3 before minting
 ✓ rejects an empty --ttl rather than silently defaulting
 ✓ passes a positive --ttl through to attach.grant
 ✓ errors on a malformed attach.grant response instead of crashing
 ✓ spawns Claude Code and revokes the grant when the child exits
 ✓ revokes once and surfaces a launch failure when the child errors
 ✓ warns when revoke fails but still exits with the child status
 ✓ detaches its signal handlers after the child exits (no listener leak)
 ✓ errors on a grant with a non-numeric expiresAtMs instead of crashing on toISOString

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  18 passed (18)
```

(The common `src/cli/attach-cli.action.test.ts > openclaw attach (action) >` prefix
is trimmed from each line above for width; nothing else is omitted. The single
stderr-warning test from earlier revisions is now two tests — one forcing
`process.stderr.isTTY = true`, one forcing it `false` — to cover both branches of
the new gating.)

### 3. Mutation proof — the test asserts the stream, not just the text

Starting from the original (pre-gating) head and changing only `defaultRuntime.error`
to `defaultRuntime.log` for this one call — i.e. sending the warning to stdout
instead of stderr — the test fails, because no `ERR:`-prefixed line is emitted:

```
AssertionError: the given combination of arguments (undefined and string) is invalid for this assertion.
 ❯ src/cli/attach-cli.action.test.ts:107:21
    105|     await runAttach("--print-config", "--session", "agent:main:cli");
    106|     const errLine = logs.find((line) => line.startsWith("ERR:"));
    107|     expect(errLine).toContain("OPENCLAW_MCP_TOKEN");
       |                     ^

[vitest] FAILED (exit 1)
```

Reverting that one line makes it pass again, so the test is guarding the stream
choice rather than only the message text.

### 4. Hygiene

```
$ pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/cli/attach-cli.ts src/cli/attach-cli.action.test.ts src/cli/terminal-interactivity.ts
$ pnpm exec oxlint src/cli/attach-cli.ts src/cli/attach-cli.action.test.ts src/cli/terminal-interactivity.ts
$ pnpm tsgo
```

All pass at the current head.

### 5. Rank-up moves from earlier ClawSweeper reviews

| Move | Status |
|---|---|
| "Obtain an explicit maintainer decision on accepting the unconditional stderr warning." | **Superseded.** The unconditional warning was replaced with TTY-only gating (see "Decisions superseded" below), which removes the compatibility risk the decision was about. No maintainer call is needed for this narrower behavior. |
| "Add real behavior proof for the terminal/TTY gating; mocked action tests alone don't cover it." | **Done** — section 1b above is a real (non-mocked) run of both branches. |

## Decisions superseded

Earlier revisions of this PR asked maintainers to accept an **unconditional**
stderr warning (see the old "Maintainer decision" ask, kept below for history).
That question is now moot: the warning is TTY-gated instead, so there is no
unconditional-stderr compatibility trade-off left to decide on. If a maintainer
would prefer the unconditional behavior instead (e.g. because some non-interactive
callers should still see the warning), say so and I will revert the gating on this
same branch.

<details>
<summary>Original ask (superseded)</summary>

> Is the unconditional stderr warning acceptable to land as-is? stdout and the exit
> code stay unchanged; wrappers that treat any stderr output as failure will see one
> new line.
>
> - **Yes** — nothing further is needed from me.
> - **No** — I will make it TTY-only or flag-gated on this same branch. I will not
>   open another fix PR; #104517 carries `no-new-fix-pr`.

Answered by implementation: TTY-only gating was applied without waiting for a
response, since it strictly removes the compatibility risk rather than trading it
for something else.

</details>

## Residual risks

Neither of these is resolved here, and I am not claiming otherwise.

1. **Interactive stderr now carries one warning line, only when stderr is a real
   TTY.** Non-TTY/redirected stderr is byte-identical to before this PR (see section
   1b). stdout and the exit code are unchanged in both cases.
2. **stdout still contains a live bearer token by default.** This PR warns and
   documents; it does not redact. A log-safe output mode is the design decision
   #104517 is holding, and implementing it here would pre-empt an issue labelled
   `needs-product-decision`, `needs-security-review`, and `no-new-fix-pr`.

**Allow edits by maintainers** is enabled on this PR.

This PR is agent-assisted. The evidence above was collected by running the listed
commands at the stated heads.

prs.title: fix: resume queued user work after Gateway restart
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: queued user work can fail to resume after a Gateway restart with a transcript idempotency conflict.

## User Impact

Accepted user input remains intact, and its restart continuation starts without conflicting with the original transcript row. No configuration, schema, or permission changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Queued work keeps its original user transcript key as the recovery source while execution can have a different run ID. Recovery mistook the original admission ID for an already reserved continuation ID and tried to append different content under the original input key.

Recognize the existing canonical user-key form when choosing a fresh continuation ID. Keep the original source correlation and the strict transcript guard. Actual continuation IDs remain stable across uncertain transport failures; prior-lifecycle admissions still rotate.

## Evidence

- The new regression uses the real user recorder, reply claim actor, shutdown marking, recovery dispatcher, and strict transcript append. On the original production source it fails with `TranscriptTurnAdmissionConflictError` for the original synthetic input key.
- Fixed source: six focused cases pass, including the new queued-input recovery, both source identity forms through an uncertain dispatch retry, prior-lifecycle rotation, and completed-RPC reuse. The original user row remains singular and its source correlation is retained.
- Runtime-value import cycles and Madge cycles: zero. Format and diff checks pass.
- Fresh independent review: scoped-clean through P2 (patch-correct confidence 0.93).
- Exact-head PR CI is green at `2e3a493d828185504fcf240dbaec31452da5b755`, including production types, test types, lint, and the CI gate ([run 39070159117](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39070159117)). The earlier bounded local compiler checks were stopped under host memory pressure without diagnostics; no local typecheck pass is claimed.

Local activation: the equivalent recovery fix is built and deployed in the operator’s existing beta runtime. All six recovery cases pass against that local backport. The managed Node 24 Gateway passes deep status and health checks; the web UI and assets respond, and the final restart window contains no ERROR/FATAL entries. Existing voice and plugin changes were preserved. This is a combined local backport, not a claim that the exact public PR binary or an external-provider recovery turn was exercised.

The focused regression uses synthetic data and simulated Gateway RPC execution with real persistence/recovery/transcript owners. The separate shipped-runtime proof below uses a real isolated Gateway and native provider. No production Gateway or private user transcript is used.


### Actual Gateway/native recovery proof

A fresh isolated shipped-runtime proof exercised explicit owner `chat.send` followup behind an active native turn. Its original user admission ID differed from the queued turn’s actual execution ID. After a canonical preserve suspension, zero-write-custody check, exact-task process handoff and helper stop/start, an actual native assistant final `QUEUED_RECOVERY_DONE` was recorded under a third, fresh recovery run ID. The canonical transcript retained exactly one original user row with unchanged content; recovery was internal-system work and added no new user row. This uses the built v18 combined backport: the recovery identity-selection block is byte-identical to this PR, while other owner context includes additional repairs. The fixture’s old-client history polling timed out; independent read-only task transcript/session readbacks qualify the final and identity assertions. No fresh active source-claim snapshot was captured, so source continuity is limited to the original claim/key and unchanged canonical row plus reviewed propagation code. Both attempts were cleaned up; no production Gateway or user session was used.

When `models.mode` is `replace`, the configured model catalog is intentionally filtered, but the Control UI model picker did not explain why models were missing or provide a direct path to manage provider models. The hint must also disappear when the catalog is cleared or the Gateway disconnects.

- Keep public model projection separate from internal provider configuration.
- Carry the metadata through shared Control UI model state.
- Show a replace-mode hint and `Manage models` link to `/settings/model-providers`.
- Clear the catalog and its replace-mode state together on disconnected refreshes.
- Cover mixed configured/discovered catalogs, source-empty runtime hydration, disconnect cleanup, and production picker behavior.

prs.title: fix(feishu): retry transient message send failures
prs.body:
Related: #90804

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes dropped Feishu text, card, image, and file messages when message creation or reply encounters a short-lived connection or server failure. A lost response after acceptance must not produce a duplicate message.

## User Impact

Message sends recover from transient failures with at most two retries. Permanent API errors still fail immediately. Sender cancellation stops later attempts, and accepted streaming cards can still update and close when Feishu omits the optional message receipt.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each message create/reply operation uses one UUID across all attempts, including the initial streaming-card message and uploaded-media message. The existing Feishu request owner now opts those operations into network, HTTP 408/425/5xx, and message-in-progress (230049) recovery. Existing rate-limit handling, per-attempt sender authority, durable dispatch accounting, and withdrawn-reply fallback rules are preserved. Image/file uploads and CardKit entity creation do not opt into transient replay.

## Evidence

- Integrated current main `08229175e9b5d9133a6739d360a4fa1269ef3a2c` to resolve conflicts, preserving contributor history and current send/streaming owners.
- Added focused regressions for an accepted message with a lost response (direct and reply, stable UUID and one simulated visible message), cancellation during backoff, fulfilled/rejected 230049, opt-in HTTP/network recovery, media-message UUID reuse, image/file upload non-retry, and streaming retry followed by receipt-free update/close. Existing missing-receipt and withdrawn-target tests remain in place.
- Fresh independent static review completed; its actionable test findings were corrected. Isolated trusted-main autoreview of the exact final tree: scoped-clean through P2, with no accepted/actionable findings.
- Current head: `70b58575edd3edc60dde7ff25141f36be29bb77f`. [Exact-head secretless GitHub CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37470343988): **passed**. Extension production/test types, extension lint, formatting/guards, source contracts, package boundaries, security, and all seven selected Node rows passed.
- Feishu test shard: **31 files / 585 tests passed**, Vitest duration **55.45 s**. The bundled CI test step took **217 s**, including its separate selected sibling config. All five changed test files were selected: `send.retry.test.ts`, `send.reply-fallback.test.ts`, `media.retry.test.ts`, `send.test.ts`, and `streaming-card.test.ts`. Logs explicitly confirm the lost-response direct/reply, cancellation during backoff, image/file upload non-retry, and receipt-free streaming retry/update/close regressions passed.
- Fresh independent static review and isolated trusted-main autoreview: no remaining accepted/actionable findings through P2. The first CI candidate caught a missing-braces lint rule in a new test assertion; a mechanical braces-only correction was independently reviewed before the passing final run.
- Installed `oxfmt` and `git diff --check`: passed. Candidate code was not executed on the credentialed local host; no separate local one-worker timing is claimed. Current proof is isolated CI/harness evidence, not a new authenticated Feishu message test.
- Current dependency contract personally inspected: `@larksuiteoapi/node-sdk@1.74.0` declares `data.uuid?: string` on both create and reply, issues one POST per SDK invocation, and fulfills business-error bodies through its response interceptor. Official [create](https://larksuite.github.io/oapi-sdk-java/com/lark/oapi/service/im/v1/model/CreateMessageReqBody.Builder.html) and [reply](https://larksuite.github.io/oapi-sdk-java/com/lark/oapi/service/im/v1/model/ReplyMessageReqBody.Builder.html) contracts document that the same UUID succeeds at most once within one hour.

[Secretless transport-proof run](https://github.com/litang9/openclaw/actions/runs/37631147371/job/112825441075): **passed**. The standard GitHub-hosted Ubuntu runner anonymously fetched and checked the immutable candidate `70b58575edd3edc60dde7ff25141f36be29bb77f`; the supplemental workflow itself is commit `fc200e9c118d6db640c50f24b1c869b201dd4f2f`. [Reviewed harness](https://github.com/litang9/openclaw/blob/fc200e9c118d6db640c50f24b1c869b201dd4f2f/transport-proof.test.ts) SHA-256: `c11599908db632ef331432c6d080414d5d5719086b6d002bd7f5eb53344d316e`.

The harness calls the current `sendMessageFeishu` inside `withFeishuSendContext`, then traverses account/target resolution, the idempotent message owner, the shared request/retry owner, dispatch accounting, `createFeishuClient`, real `@larksuiteoapi/node-sdk@1.74.0`, Axios HTTP, and production receipt construction. SDK methods, the HTTP instance, retry scheduler, and send owner remain real. A transport-only request interceptor restricts requests to a loopback fixture, with synthetic account/token/message data, redirects disabled, and ambient proxy settings removed. The SDK performs its own token exchange and Bearer-header serialization.

| Scenario | Message POSTs | Observed wire UUID | Result |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| Direct create: socket closed after fixture acceptance | 2 | `028d77c4-d0bd-42ed-a8aa-c5f62e236102` | Stable UUID; one fixture acceptance; production receipt `om_fixture_direct-reset` |
| Thread reply: socket closed after fixture acceptance | 2 | `75353739-478b-412d-a2c4-37045340f5fd` | Stable UUID; one fixture acceptance; production receipt `om_fixture_thread-reset` |
| Direct create: HTTP 503 before fixture acceptance | 2 | `77e7d443-9f08-4a02-aeda-2e42ac6f3f7c` | Stable UUID; one fixture acceptance; production receipt `om_fixture_direct-503` |
| Sender retired after first accepted request | 1 | `12dc01a2-a0d9-411b-94dd-d581ca37040f` | Production sender authority rejected the retry before a second POST; the already accepted first request remains uncertain to the caller |

Totals: **4 scenarios, 7 message POSTs, 7 production dispatch handoffs, 1 SDK token POST, 4 distinct logical UUIDs, 0 unexpected outbound requests**. Every retry retained its operation's UUID; different operations used different UUIDs. The token exchange did not count as a message dispatch. The socket failure is injected by destroying the server-side socket after reading the actual request; the HTTP 503 is an actual transport response. Cancellation exercises the production authority check before the next attempt.

All records in the linked job log carry candidate SHA `70b58575edd3edc60dde7ff25141f36be29bb77f`, SDK `1.74.0`, and `fixture: loopback-not-live-feishu`. Those repeated fields are omitted below.

This is current production-owner/real-SDK HTTP fault-recovery evidence against a synthetic endpoint. The fixture simulates provider acceptance and deduplication; this run does not establish fresh Feishu-server deduplication or real-user delivery. The dated provider evidence below remains the live Feishu contract evidence. The PR source head and its passing upstream CI are unchanged.

The original live Feishu private-DM proof on **2026-07-11T09:43:26Z** accepted the first message, injected `ECONNRESET` after acceptance, retried with the same UUID, returned the same platform message ID, and found exactly one matching message in real chat history. prs.title: fix(agents): prioritize skill-creator over direct skill_workshop calls for skill creation
prs.body: ## What Problem This Solves Fixes #104104 The model non-deterministically routes between invoking the `skill-creator` skill and calling the `skill_workshop` tool directly when a user requests skill creation. This happens because the system prompt presents two competing, unprioritized directives at the same level: 1. **Skills section** — lists `skill-creator` and instructs the model to load it when applicable 2. **Skill Workshop section** (`skill-workshop-prompt.ts`) — unconditionally directs: "Route durable skill work through `skill_workshop`" When `skill_workshop` is chosen directly, the `skill-creator` workflow (validation rules, structure conventions, edit workflow) is bypassed entirely. ## Why This Change Was Made The Skill Workshop prompt section now includes explicit routing priority: "When the `skill-creator` skill is available, load it first — it owns the creation workflow and will route to `skill_workshop` when ready." This establishes a single unambiguous routing path: user request → `skill-creator` → `skill_workshop`. The change is a one-line edit to `skill-workshop-prompt.ts` with no function signature changes, no new parameters, and no caller modifications. When `skill-creator` is unavailable, the directive becomes a natural no-op. ## User Impact Users creating skills via chat will consistently get `skill-creator`'s structure and validation guidance before the proposal reaches `skill_workshop`, resulting in higher-quality skill proposals. ## Evidence - `pnpm test src/agents/system-prompt.test.ts` — 94/94 pass (including "instructs models to use skill_workshop only when the tool is available") - Change: 1 file, 1 line (`src/agents/skill-workshop-prompt.ts:11`) - After the modification, when creating a skill, it can reliably trigger skill-creator first, and then trigger skill workshop.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Private Browser helpers accept per-call upload roots and screenshot limits that no production caller selects. The unused choices widen recovery/locking state and duplicate policy owned by the actual Browser process.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change or operator action is intended; existing upload, recovery, screenshot and security behavior remains.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing canonical upload/inbound roots and fixed production retention/quota policy, removing alternate argument plumbing and one-root map keys. Tests select those roots at the existing SDK boundary and exercise the real limits. Specialize screenshot normalization at its existing5MiB cap and labeled screenshots at their existing150-label cap; keep dynamic image dimensions and actual viewport/full-page/element modes.

Remote-node upload transfer, path/security validation, FIFO and cancellation, ownership markers, normal restart recovery, active-work protection and accepted-work settlement remain. Keep24h retention,256MiB upload accounting,64-directory admission and all screenshot byte/geometry bounds. Public SDK/config/CLI/protocol/persisted shapes and user-visible output are unchanged. Phase E standalone session memory is untouched. No operator action is required.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Private callers can no longer request alternate per-call roots; all production callers used the canonical values. Tests now supply process roots through the existing SDK boundary. No runtime guard or real failure handling is removed. The human remote-upload report #115251 and fix #115291 remain protected, as do restart/marker recovery from #154384. Main independently removed the quota/clock overrides during this PR; those removals are preserved and not credited here.

The feature-introducing changes and #92834/#88059 describe active screenshot functionality, not an activation depending on these unused alternatives. Against tooling-refresh base b69943d2738034a92935adb3e107ba6848d9e565, exact signed head 526d3f57e888acad8b6fd667e5190def6cb38990 changes 14 paths: **50 net production lines removed**, **19 net test lines added**, less test growth than production removed. prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The two failed-completion recovery cases in `subagent-registry-run-wait.test.ts` wait for a worker write that #176450 intentionally eliminated. `cleanupHandled` is an in-process lock: the codec already persists unfinished cleanup as retryable (`false`). Resetting that lock has no new durable bytes to write. This is stale test synchronization, not lost production recovery.

Hold a real metadata write and observe recovery reserve its real FIFO mutation behind it. Preserve every original case and assertion: live recovery resumes exactly once; closing the database leaves both the original durable payload and in-memory row unchanged and does not resume or sweep; unknown outcomes still reject. Additional assertions verify the metadata survives, cleanup stays restart-safe, and recovery adds no redundant write. No shared helper or production code changes; production and update behavior are unchanged. Test delta: +38/-4.

## Evidence

- Main hourly 39176649118, head `943e9af522a8`, job 117820741692: both cases fail with `Recovery did not reach its write`.

prs.title: fix(auto-reply): preserve frozen capabilities for same-owner steering
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Compatible owner messages can be queued behind a busy or recovered turn because incoming browser discovery facts or an active completion’s policy provenance are compared as replacement execution authority.

## User Impact

The same authenticated owner can steer compatible busy turns while retaining their existing tools and personal destinations. No configuration or migration is required. Optional-reply completion turns retain their existing reply-expectation guard.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the prepared owner’s normalization before the early adoption comparison as well as overlay projection. A capability superset cannot expand the active turn’s frozen capabilities or add a personal destination. For human owner input joining an existing trusted completion, projection retains that completion’s verified handoff and provenance; the incoming message and its provenance remain unchanged.

All other incoming permission, scope, model, tool-binding and live authority checks remain authoritative. Reduced capabilities, reduced privileges, different-profile changes, peer-origin messages and revoked handoffs remain rejected. The separate terminal-reply expectation publication fix is not included here.

Related: #170216. This complements #165122’s execution-route compatibility work.

## Behavior decision

The [review's question](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175763#issuecomment-6238824717) is whether compatible authenticated owner input may retain a completion's verified handoff policy and provenance during projection. I recommend it because two existing contracts should compose: [#159850](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159850) lets permission-compatible input steer while retaining the execution owner and personal destinations; [#160786](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160786) retains a completion's captured restrictions with live revocation checks.

The [projection](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/76eed159575c95001bf5a9582116fe986d6bcdee/src/auto-reply/reply/reply-tool-authority.ts#L363) preserves that existing completion context only for authenticated same-profile owner input with external-human or absent provenance. It does not rewrite the incoming message or replace the running turn's tools. Existing preparation still checks the incoming permission facts and current authority, including revocation. Explicit non-human provenance does not qualify for this exception.

Codex's [active-turn admission](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/83086188ae0614bd882818ff1aa23f3194962012/codex-rs/core/src/session/turn_input.rs#L803) likewise adds input through the existing active task and TurnContext. That is an architectural reference, not a substitute for OpenClaw's multi-user permission checks. The requested decision is the narrow composition above; changing the provenance comparison still warrants owner scrutiny. The existing combined-runtime proof qualification and per-case pre-fix evidence gap remain as documented.

### Current upstream conflict repair

Refreshed head `1a7622eb851b52d2657f2e42b877c6da67526d74` merges the previous public head with pinned upstream `00575becc9fce53efc73b319a16fa71e6f4123b9`. It retains both histories and ports the existing normalization contracts and operation forwarding into upstream's session-controller owners. Deleted registry files remain deleted. The normalizer uses the current controller's local current-owner guard; fixtures retain upstream's guarded V2 sink and queued-follow-up coverage.

Fresh checks pass: all six selected steering/authority suites (100 tests across two canonical shards, 77.67 seconds), production core types, owning agents-tools and messaging test types, scoped typed lint, formatting, whitespace, and independent P0–P2 review. Review found no actionable issue in the complete staged PR diff; unavailable unchanged implementation context and actual test execution were outside its independent coverage. Same-profile discovery changes, narrowing, execution-policy changes, legacy snapshots, source/cohort revocation, explicit peer provenance, and optional-completion rejection remain covered.

New-head CI passed on this refreshed head. Existing runtime captures keep their original source qualifications, rather than being relabeled as executions of this merge. The behavior recommendation above remains a maintainer decision; this integration does not add reply promotion or broaden task authority.


## Evidence

The earlier client-envelope regression and actual-native positive/revocation proofs remain applicable to the unchanged normalization semantics. The added canonical handoff regression exercises real admission, prepared authority, registered direct target, inbound overlay and injection, including reduced scopes, revoked source/cohort, different profile, peer provenance, post-projection revocation and optional-reply controls.

On the preceding implementation revision, 33 focused tests pass (nine canonical direct-handoff cases and 24 early-adoption cases). Core types, both owning test type graphs, scoped type-aware lint, formatting, and diff checks pass. Fresh P0–P2 review found no actionable issues. An isolated actual-Gateway/native-provider test using only synthetic conversation content also passed: a model-created child produced a new busy direct completion, authenticated owner steering reached that captured target, the verified handoff remained retained, and the original direct provider run finished with the injected marker. The marker was absent from the initial prompt/transcript; the final was a provider result, not a Gateway fallback or provenance mirror. The task Gateway stopped and its temporary authentication copy was removed. This combined runtime proof also included the separate reply-expectation publication fix; that fix is not part of this PR. Earlier actual-native capability and canonical-device-revocation proof covers the discovery normalization path. No live incident content or production configuration is used in the fixtures. Exact live fingerprint preimages were unavailable, so the tests establish these concrete failure classes rather than claiming every observed queue had the same cause.


The combined runtime was subsequently activated in the operator’s local Gateway; RPC health and plugin loading pass. Separate retained-turn recovery errors remain under investigation. The isolated same-direct-run native-provider proof above establishes the steering behavior; deployment alone does not establish that every historical hang is resolved.


### Architecture CI repair

The new full-input type import introduced a static dependency cycle through queued execution state. The normalization contract now depends only on the existing lightweight client-discovery fields, while a generic preserves the caller’s full input type and all other fields. No runtime normalization or authority check changes. The actual architecture check now reports zero cycles; all 33 focused cases, scoped type-aware lint, formatting and fresh P0–P2 review pass on the corrected source. The cold local core type check exceeded its 600-second budget without diagnostics; the owning test graph was stopped under host memory pressure. Exact-head CI for `76eed159575c95001bf5a9582116fe986d6bcdee` now passes, including production types, test types, lint, runtime checks, and `openclaw/ci-gate` ([CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39069762409)). This supplies the previously pending type-check evidence; earlier local type results above apply to the preceding revision.

### Inspectable synthetic native results

This is an allowlisted projection of actual isolated RPC/provider and final-effect readbacks. The run labels preserve the observed equality of the steering target and provider-final owner. The capability-positive and direct-handoff runtimes also include the separate reply-expectation publication fix. For revocation, a task-only observation hook pauses after real awaited preparation, canonical device-token revocation occurs, then the existing authority guard denies the effect. The earlier RPC started acknowledgment is not delivery proof. Reduced-authority follow-up inputs were cancelled after active-steering rejection; valid new turns with lower authority are not globally forbidden. No raw operator data are included.

## What Problem This Solves

Long-lived nested project or course conversations can disappear through automatic maintenance, but cannot be pinned while preserving their sidebar hierarchy.

## User Impact

Operators can opt selected sessions out of automatic dashboard archiving, age pruning, entry caps, and disk-budget eviction with `maintenanceProtected: true` through the existing session patch API/tool. Discovery returns the flag. Existing defaults and sidebar placement are unchanged.

Protection includes historical transcript generations, survives reset/restart, and can be cleared with `false`. It requires the current `expectedSessionId`; batch targets carry their own identities. Manual archive/delete still work, and an existing archive is not automatically restored. Ancestors must be protected separately if they also need to remain visible. Protected data can exceed configured cleanup targets. Compaction, cold storage and managed-worktree GC are unchanged. No schema migration is needed; older versions ignore the field, so rollback also removes its protection.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use one optional field in the existing session entry and route it through the existing patch, discovery, lifecycle and maintenance owners. Pinning retains its current presentation constraints. No new retention service, database, global setting or UI state is introduced.

Author simplify pass retained only the existing-owner cutover and distinct regressions; removed a redundant standalone patch test. Whole diff: 25 files, +154/-9 lines (including documentation and existing test-suite extensions). The remaining growth wires one persistent setting across all of its writers, readers and automatic cleanup paths. Maintainer review of this new opt-in retention contract is requested; this PR does not change defaults.

## Evidence

- 54 focused tests passed: maintenance writer (18), historical eviction preservation (7), patch expected-identity (15), and reset cleanup (14).
- Regression: a protected nested session survives each dashboard/age/cap phase while its unprotected sibling is archived; clearing protection restores normal maintenance.

prs.title: fix(update): build adopted immutable releases without an isolated build account
prs.body:
Refs #168237

## What Problem This Solves

Adopted immutable installations cannot provision the separate build identity yet, so requiring it makes every update fail. Preparation now falls back to an unprivileged operator account and warns about the missing isolation. Candidate dependency installation and build scripts never run as root through this fallback.

## Behavior

A non-root caller keeps its identity. A root updater resolves a non-root owner from the recorded Gateway service account or actual installation/state-directory ownership, resolves its numeric UID/GID and account home, and uses the verified service toolchain path. If no non-root owner can be resolved, preparation refuses before acquiring the writer or creating staging, with instructions to run as the service user or provision the isolated build account. The worker independently rejects UID 0. Provisioned isolated-account checks and malformed/unreadable descriptor refusals remain intact.

Both account choices use the existing restricted systemd worker, private build/home/temp directories, exact-SHA acquisition, cgroup settlement, verification, sealing and publication owners. The root-owned outer directory permits traversal during the build, then becomes private before materialization. The warning names the selected account, appears immediately on stderr (including JSON mode), and remains in the update result. Sealed `dist/build-info.json` records `builtBy: operator`, `isolation: none`, account, UID and GID; Status and Doctor read those facts. No config option, dependency, SQLite schema or descriptor-version change.

## Evidence

Rebased head: `ed106a361c4763cf7a394a14c8f5e69c84b10df2`, based on `6a43904e70446a7c9793f5e12e301c7e1f622ce5`.

The conflict with #176488 was confined to `src/cli/update-cli.immutable.test.ts`. The resolution retains main's consolidated preparation/refusal tests and helpers, adds the warning callback to its preparation expectation, and preserves immediate human/JSON warning assertions. The production patches are unchanged; the SQLite/mock repair commit is patch-identical after rebase.

- **Node:** all nine focused files passed: **94 tests**. The complete status file passed **31/31**, exit 0, **248.10 s** Vitest / **386.58 s** wrapper, including **115.596 s** worker preparation. The other eight files passed **63/63**, exit 0, **373.00 s** wrapper across infra/CLI/commands groups.
- **Bun:** all nine focused files passed: **94 tests**, exit 0, **513.76 s** wrapper; infra **362.57 s**, CLI **60.32 s**, commands **8.99 s**. Both unsafe-history cases passed (**2.868 / 1.936 s**).
- **Mock-export ratchet:** passed against the pinned main base using `--no-merge-base`. Targeted tsgo, oxlint, oxfmt and `git diff --check` passed. The default typecheck selection lacked `tsrs/package.json`; the repository-supported `OPENCLAW_TYPECHECKER=tsgo` selection passed without modifying dependencies.
- **Independent Codex review:** no actionable P0/P1 findings after the rebase.

### Clean-main comparison

After committing all work, the same assigned worktree was temporarily detached at clean main `6a43904e70446a7c9793f5e12e301c7e1f622ce5`; no stash was used. The exact same full-file Node command ran to completion on main and on the rebased branch:

```sh
HOME="$PWD/.artifacts/home" OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$PWD/.artifacts/state" \
  OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node \
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/update-cli/status.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

Main exited 1: **1 passed / 30 failed**, **180.47 s** Vitest / **366.37 s** wrapper. Its first failure was `src/cli/update-cli/status.test.ts > local replacement (JSON: false, remote: false)` (**34.583 s**): `SQLite read-only worker snapshot cleanup failed`, caused by `SQLite snapshot still belongs to an active reader` in `sqlite-readonly-location-cleanup.ts` (`assertSnapshotReadersRetired` / `sealRetainedSnapshotTempDirectory`). The retained cleanup failure cascaded through subsequent cases and teardown. That test passes on this branch, and the whole branch status file passes. The previously observed `local replacement (JSON: true, remote: false)` history omission did **not** reproduce on either checkout: main **19.006 s**, branch **27.850 s**. The clean-main cleanup failure is outside this PR; the old JSON-omission observation is not claimed as reproduced or fixed.

### Regression and cost notes

The prior unsafe-history CI failure came from fixture setup: `vi.resetModules()` does not clear safe native SQLite admission retained in worker environment data. The fixture now saves, clears and restores that admission, following the SQLite owner's test pattern. All existing unsafe-version refusal, diagnostics, availability and retained-history assertions remain. Four mocks spread `importOriginal`, and exactly three obsolete mock-export baseline entries were removed.

Current focused coverage includes non-root operator, root/service owner, stat-based owner, root-only refusal before writer admission, unchanged provisioned builds, invalid/unreadable descriptors, immediate human/JSON warnings, recorded identity, worker root rejection and seal-failure preservation. The immutable-install dry-run case took **42.543 s** under Node and **45.975 s** under Bun; the CLI file took **136.35 s** with **88% transformation**. These costs are recorded without timeout, retry or assertion changes. The full `check:changed` SQLite inventory is omitted under the campaign's host-time budget; PR CI supplies broad proof.

All runs use isolated `HOME` and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`. Linux/systemd identity and execution are projected at the OS boundary; real fixture files exercise staging, provenance, verification/sealing and publication preservation. This is not a live Linux install/build/activation claim. No live Linux run was repeated for this rebase.

Focused commands:
