## What Problem This Solves

Reduces Skills page lifecycle effects while preserving request retirement and independent Discovery and Settings selections.

## User Impact

No intended visual or workflow change. A retained page keeps the active surface's selection, and inactive selection changes do not issue Skills requests.

## Why This Change Was Made

Agent, selection, skill-state, and Gateway owners already publish synchronous receipts. The page now consumes those receipts directly for reconciliation and catalog icons; its existing admission effect carries plain search scope and query facts. The existing projection supplies the subscription; no new event layer or state owner is introduced.

A surface-only change must not reapply the previous surface's route data: the independent selection owners can have equal intent revisions while selecting different agents. Catalog synchronization waits for settled state and ignores its own icon-URL publication. prs.title: fix(agents): detect sustained same-target write churn
prs.body:
Related: #122577

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an agent can repeatedly overwrite one file with different successful contents while never producing a final response. Because every write has different arguments and reports `changed: true`, current loop detection treats the sequence as ordinary progress indefinitely.

This PR proposes a conservative behavioral boundary for maintainer review. The issue is currently marked as requiring a product decision; this PR does not claim that decision has already been made.

## Why This Change Was Made

The change keeps successful writes classified as real mutations and adds a separate, warning-first run-liveness signal for a contiguous tail of content-changing writes to one resolved target. Target identity excludes document content and is stored only as a hash.

The existing loop warning threshold is reused. The warned write remains allowed. Continuity clears when the run changes tools (including read/verification), changes targets, repeats an earlier argument variant, or completes/replaces its lifecycle. If churn remains continuous through the existing stale-run boundary, owner-bound recovery can abort only that run whether or not follow-up work is queued.

The behavior is limited to the built-in `write` result contract (`details.changed === true`). It is not tied to a provider, model, transport, channel, or reported private document. No new configuration or default surface is added.

## Batch and Liveness Semantics

A whole assistant batch is admitted before its calls have outcomes. This revision therefore keeps warning and liveness behavior aligned at both lifecycle boundaries:

- successful write-mutation liveness stays inactive below the shared warning threshold;
- a sequential batch emits the same run-scoped warning before the threshold-crossing write implementation starts;
- a post-outcome fallback covers parallel or out-of-order batch completions;
- the shared warning bucket prevents duplicate pre- and post-outcome warnings;
- the existing stable no-progress classifier still includes the just-recorded outcome and activates on its original boundary.

## Scope

The write-churn changes remain in the agent loop owner. A separate memory-core test commit stabilizes the unrelated provenance-repair assertion that failed hosted CI: it holds the detached repair open while asserting that automatic candidates remain hidden, then releases and verifies the repaired result. The test moved into the existing candidate-repair suite to satisfy the line-cap ratchet. No memory-core production behavior changed.

A subsequent agent fix resets the reverse write-variant scan at the newer occurrence of a repeated variant, retaining only post-repeat writes. A replacement regression uses actual `changed: true` outcomes at the shared warning threshold and verifies that a fresh post-repeat streak can warn again.

## User Impact

Runaway same-file rewrite sequences become bounded without immediately blocking normal edits. Short rewrite sequences, multi-file work, write/read/write verification, repeated identical content, and successful writes outside the sustained same-target pattern retain their existing behavior. The latest file state and session remain available after recovery.

## Policy Status

ClawSweeper marked #122577 as requiring a maintainer product decision and disabled automated fix-PR queueing. This PR implements one conservative proposal for review; it does not claim that maintainers have approved the warning, escape, or recovery boundary. It is ready for maintainer review of that decision, but does not claim approval or merge readiness.

## Evidence

Behavioral incident baseline: `v2026.7.2-beta.7` (`dabe1915362e20c25704af91612a32a8f4c96e83`). The beta is provenance only; the patch and tests are bound to the recorded branch head and integrated base below, not an unqualified current-main merge.

Negative controls observed before their fixes:

```text
same-target detector: expected warning, received { stuck: false }
below-threshold liveness: active=true after the second distinct changed write
embedded sequential batch: 11 successful writes, warning event list empty
stable no-progress boundary: sixth completed outcome still reported active=false
default-parallel batch: warning emitted, first churn lease remained absent
loop detection omitted/disabled: changed-write churn emitted a warning
CI dependency scan: three internal helpers were exported but unused
```

## Current revision and verification

Head: `f72242e6faf82f8608abd704b16d868d8a034ada`. The branch's integrated main merge-base remains `d45155d6c51169ac10890445418a9144395d1697`; it has not been integrated with current main.

- Revision 34's staged-write-target lifecycle P2 is fixed in the shared wrapper settlement `finally`, with run-scoped cleanup on success, errors, late cancellation, source-guard refusal and disposal. Batch final-target precedence is retained. The follow-up adds three production lines and +132 net test lines across two files.
- Five regressions failed on the preceding wrapper and passed after the fix. At this exact clean head, the focused detector, warning, write-target, admission and real-Agent sequential/default-parallel suites passed 169 distinct tests across five files. This is native wrapper/Agent lifecycle evidence, not a current-head Gateway recovery proof.
- Production `tsgo:core`, the canonical `core-test-agents-root` compiler graph, focused type-aware lint, formatting, line-cap ratchet and whitespace checks passed. The changed-graph selector stopped on the pre-existing 721-root/advisory-720 budget check; no config or test inventory changed, and the named graph was compiled separately. No full all-graph check claim.
- Independent read-only review found no actionable defect in the lifecycle fix. The full branch surface against its integrated base is source +475 and tests +1503 across 23 files; the added production state remains limited to target-aware detection, batch reconciliation and existing liveness ownership.
- Prior-head hosted CI failed one subagent-registry shard at `subagent-registry.test.ts:5160`, with dependent failure/cancellations; this unrelated failure was not repaired. Local passes are not a new-head hosted-CI pass.
- A merge-tree against main `3f12395208355949832da16c882e83cc5726c560` reports ten conflicting paths. Integration remains explicitly unqualified.

[The final follow-up comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/122631#issuecomment-5974613163) contains the exact commands, checked-in proof links and captured terminal excerpts. No new isolated-Gateway result is claimed.

### Historical isolated Gateway proof (`27b24258c8`)

The real gateway, authenticated loopback agent RPC, embedded runner, built-in write/read tools, diagnostic heartbeat, and owner-bound recovery were exercised using a deterministic loopback model transport. No outbound-channel delivery or live-provider claim.

```text

later warning: argument_churn / warn / count 20 (seq 302)
continuous churn duration: 378645 ms
session.stalled: age 376954 ms, model_call (seq 361)
recovery requested: abort, same age (seq 362)
recovery completed: abort_embedded_run / aborted / embedded_run (seq 367)
healthy concurrent control: passed
```

prs.title: fix(agents): preserve ACP lifecycle ownership
prs.body:
## Summary

- keep spawned ACP runs under their canonical `acp` task owner while retaining a topology/control observer in the subagent registry
- stop ACP observer rows from creating duplicate `subagent` task projections, terminal delivery obligations, or child-session cleanup authority
- upgrade persisted legacy ACP mirrors during normalization and use the active ACP turn or canonical durable task as observer liveness
- emit a specific ACP owner-loss reason and preserve one-shot session state until a later corroborating maintenance pass

Fixes [GEN-6353](https://linear.app/genhealth/issue/GEN-6353/openclaw-loses-active-shrimp-acp-backing-sessions-after-the-legacy).

## What Problem This Solves

An ACP spawn created the canonical `runtime=acp` task, then the shared spawn pipeline registered the same run as a native subagent. The mirror's sweeper checked `getAgentRunContext`, which never represented external ACP liveness, so it false-failed after the stale grace and ran session-scoped cleanup. Task maintenance later treated only the process-local ACP turn marker as backing evidence, marked the canonical task lost after its grace, and could close the one-shot session in that same pass.

The observed production intervals match those two grace periods plus sweep cadence.

## Design

Patterns found and retained:

- the shared spawn registry remains the source for child topology, admission caps, status, and control
- the ACP manager/task registry remains the canonical lifecycle, progress, delivery, and cleanup owner
- observer ownership is persisted in the existing forward-compatible payload JSON; no SQLite schema change is required
- legacy ACP rows are recognized by their canonical ACP session key and normalized into observer-only state

Patterns intentionally not used:

- native subagent restart recovery and native `AgentRunContext` liveness, because Codex/ACP has a separate durable thread/session identity and resume contract
- deleting ACP rows from the subagent registry, which would regress topology and child controls
- immediate session deletion after declaring loss; cleanup now requires a later pass and rechecks the active turn

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-delivery-state.test.ts src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry-run-launch.test.ts src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry-sweeper-recovery.test.ts src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-run-liveness.test.ts src/agents/subagents/spawn/acp-spawn.test.ts src/tasks/task-registry.test.ts`
  - 239 tests passed across 3 Vitest shards
- `pnpm tsgo`
- `pnpm tsgo:test`
- scoped `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check`

`pnpm check:changed` could not run because the local Crabbox binary failed its built-in version/help sanity check; the equivalent scoped formatting, lint, type, and focused test checks above passed.

prs.title: feat(openai): support saved GPT-Live voices
prs.body:
Closes #175909

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw cannot select an existing prompt-created GPT-Live voice. OpenAI requires saved voices as `{ "id": "voice_..." }`, but Talk and Discord flatten `speakerVoiceId` into the same plain string `voice` field as named voices, so a saved ID reached the named-voice allowlist and silently fell back to `marin`.

## User Impact

Operators can select a saved voice with `gpt-live-1` through `talk.realtime.speakerVoiceId`, `channels.discord.voice.realtime.speakerVoiceId`, or `speakerVoiceId` in an OpenAI realtime provider block. Named voices keep their existing behavior and defaults. Saved voices on other models, and malformed IDs, fail session setup with a message that does not echo the configured value. Browser WebRTC reservations omit the ID.

## Why This Change Was Made

The OpenAI provider owns its voice identifiers, so the translation stays inside the plugin and needs no core or SDK change:

- `readOpenAIQuicksilverVoiceSetting` recognizes OpenAI's `voice_` prefix (case-insensitively) in the shared string and keeps the ID's case. Config reads never throw, so Talk catalogs and readiness checks are unaffected by a typo.
- `normalizeOpenAIQuicksilverVoiceInput` validates the ID when a bridge or browser session is created; `assertOpenAIGptLiveCustomVoiceModel` rejects saved voices for models other than `gpt-live-1`, including request-level overrides.
- Whitespace-only named voices normalize to unset again (the earlier head threw for them).

Behavior notes compared with main: a blank `speakerVoice` now falls through to `speakerVoiceId`/`voice` instead of masking them, and `speakerVoiceId` in a provider block is read the same way Talk already reads it. Docs: `docs/providers/openai/voice-and-speech.md`.

## Evidence

Local, Node 24.21.0, repo Vitest wrapper (pinned Bun test runtime), on `c5cc8a53` (merged with main `b1b3f500`):

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` over the 7 touched OpenAI realtime test files: 105/105 passed.
- New caller-path tests: Talk's request-level `voice` and the provider block reach the broker as `{ id }`; Discord's override shape through the real `resolveConfiguredRealtimeVoiceProviderAsync` reaches `session.start` as `audio.output.voice = { id }`; GA and Codex models reject saved voices before session creation or socket open; malformed and mistyped-prefix IDs fail with the exact non-echoing message; blank `speakerVoice` stays unset.
- Fail-first: with the previous head's source and the new tests, the Talk, Discord and blank-voice cases fail (fallback to `marin`, missing `{ id }`, and a thrown custom-voice error respectively).
- `tsgo` for extensions and extension tests: passed. `oxlint` on the 12 changed files: passed. `oxfmt --check`: passed.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs`: all guards passed except two whole-tree checks that also fail on main: the max-lines suppression ratchet (three `ui/` files identical to main) and the Knip dead-export scan (99 entries in 32 files identical to main). The one entry from this PR (`OpenAIGptLiveVoice`) is fixed.
- `realtime-quicksilver-peer-worker.test.ts`: 3/3 local passes. The CI failure on `3a66dc68` (zero RTP packets in 10s) did not reproduce, the same test passed on `ae85e78d`, and this PR does not touch that media code.
- The session-lifecycle test change from the previous head was dropped in favor of main's deterministic fix for the same race.

Not proven: no live provider call was made. An end-to-end OpenClaw audio session with a real saved voice remains unverified; the earlier direct-provider check bypassed OpenClaw's configuration flow.

Known limitation: core's Talk gateway-relay presentation echoes the configured `speakerVoiceId` string to the operator's client, as it already does for every provider's voice ID. Hiding it there needs a core change outside this plugin.

## References and documentation

- [OpenAI custom voices guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/custom-voices): saved voices use `session.audio.output.voice.id`; prompt-generated voices work with GPT-Live only.
- [OpenClaw OpenAI voice and speech documentation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/providers/openai/voice-and-speech.md).
- Related: [PR #174084](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174084) expands named Codex voices.

## What Problem This Solves

Explicit Matrix room delivery could not derive a session under the default DM scope. A canonical room target was marked non-exact, so delivery failed unless the caller supplied `--session-key`, even though Matrix already had an exact room identity.

## Why This Change Was Made

Commands targeting either legacy `!room:server` IDs or modern server-less room IDs can resolve their room session without a manually supplied session key. Alias and DM routing behavior is preserved.

## What Problem This Solves

A published 2026.10.5 updater can refuse a candidate during Doctor lint with `SQLite snapshot staging owner launch context changed`, leaving the update rolled back. Doctor retains its report snapshot while writable inspection temporarily uses another state environment; the staging runtime incorrectly allows only one launch context.

Keep native staging sessions by the existing compatibility check, with directory counts and retirement attached to the originating session. Matching launches still share a child. Overlapping inspection contexts retain separate custody until their last directory retires, including retry of a failed native close. Environment compatibility, source mutation fences, and inspection errors remain enforced.

This preserves #176334's intended private-image fork without reacquiring live state. No schema, configuration, or timeout changes. This failure is independent of the missing watcher-worker packaging repair.

prs.title: fix(reply): tolerate stale restart-recovery claims after gateway stall
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #122377 (partial mitigation — see scope note below).

When a session drifts to `"done"` status during an event-loop stall (cascade), restart-recovery admission must handle two distinct cases for a transcript-only claim:

1. **Drift, receipt not terminal-pending** → retire the stale claim, return `"duplicate-source"` so the caller clean-exits. Next turn proceeds normally.
2. **Drift, receipt IS terminal-pending** → retirement must be **declined**. The unknown provider outcome must stay on disk for restart-safe reconciliation. Admission must throw, not clean-exit.

## Bug (ClawSweeper P1)

The transcript-only-claim drift branch returned `"duplicate-source"` unconditionally — even when `retireTerminalRestartRecoverySourceClaim` declined (terminal-pending receipt, `retired === undefined`). The caller (`agent-runner-execute.ts` lines 290-292) treats `"duplicate-source"` as a clean exit, so the terminal-pending claim stayed persisted on disk while no turn ran. Later turns still hit the recovery guard. **Session wedged.**

## Fix

Gate `return "duplicate-source"` on `retired` being truthy. When retirement is declined, throw `"restart recovery claim changed before agent adoption"` — the claim stays visible for restart-safe provider reconciliation.

```ts
// restart-recovery-claim.ts, transcript-only drift branch
if (retired) {
  params.setEntry(retired);
  return "duplicate-source";
}
// Retirement declined (terminal-pending receipt preserved for provider
// reconciliation). Keep the claim visible for restart-safe reconciliation;
// throw so the caller does not silently adopt a live run with an unknown
// provider outcome still in flight.
throw new Error("restart recovery claim changed before agent adoption");
```

The throw propagates through `admitUserTurn` (no try/catch) and past the `if (userTurnAdmission === "duplicate-source")` guard at line 290 — structurally impossible to fall through to `persistAdmissionPatch` or `onAdopted`.

## P3 cleanup

Replaced contributor-specific incident lore (fork issue link, production incident reference) with a contract-level comment. Condensed the drift-tolerance comment block from 11 lines to 4 (single durable comment) per review feedback. Repo policy reserves inline comments for durable local invariants.

## Evidence

### Live exact-path retirement proof (head `ca8e259585d`, 2026-09-03)

Real `createReplyRestartRecoveryClaimController.admitUserTurn` + `retireTerminalRestartRecoverySourceClaim` against a real session store in an isolated state dir, with a **populated `restartRecoveryDeliverySourceRunId`** (the prior proof's null-source gap):

- Drifted exact claim (status "done", receipt not terminal-pending) → `duplicate-source` clean unwind; durable claim cleared; source recorded in `restartRecoveryTerminalRunIds`; production `diag.warn` emitted by the retire helper.
- Terminal-pending receipt → retirement declined → `restart recovery claim changed before agent adoption` throw; claim, source runId, and receipt preserved on disk for reconciliation.

Full redacted log: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/122388#issuecomment-5526017507

Verification on the exact head (`ca8e259585d`, one-line format fix over `2b4260a`): 174/174 `agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts` (gateway e2e config, includes all 77 PR tests), oxlint clean, CI green, MERGEABLE — lifecycle-generation fencing from main preserved at all four reference sites.

### Real gateway/transport recovery trace (production, redacted)

Captured from live gateway logs on the Foster agent. Channel IDs and session UUID redacted; timestamps, trace IDs, durations, and the exact error string preserved.

**Causal chain — gateway stall → event-loop wedge → stale-claim throw:**

```
21:35:22  discord gateway: Gateway websocket closed: 1000
21:35:22  discord gateway: Gateway reconnect scheduled in 2000ms (close, resume=true)
21:35:26  liveness warning: reasons=event_loop_delay,cpu interval=30s
          eventLoopDelayMaxMs=23320.3 eventLoopUtilization=0.887 cpuCoreRatio=0.914
          recentPhases=post-ready.gateway-data.session-catalog
21:35:31  tool policy removed 9 tool(s) via tools.profile (coding)   [trace=bbf79dea]
21:35:32  ERROR message dispatch completed: channel=discord
          sessionKey=agent:foster:discord:channel:XXXX
          source=replyResolver outcome=error duration=34059ms
          error="Error: restart recovery claim changed before agent adoption"   [trace=d87caac3]
21:35:33  ERROR message dispatch completed ... duration=329ms   [trace=f90c66ac]
21:35:36  ERROR message dispatch completed ... duration=246ms   [trace=edd309fb]
21:35:41  ERROR message dispatch completed ... duration=280ms   [trace=9f436d30]
21:35:50  ERROR message dispatch completed ... duration=599ms   [trace=e816ab18]
```

**What this trace proves:**

1. **Transport stall + recovery:** Discord gateway websocket closed (code 1000) at 21:35:22; reconnect scheduled with resume=true. This is the gateway/transport recovery event.

2. **Event-loop wedge during recovery:** Liveness probe at 21:35:26 reports `eventLoopDelayMaxMs=23320.3` — a **23-second** event-loop stall during the reconnect window. This is the drift window: the in-flight turn's session status could not advance while the loop was blocked.

3. **The bug firing:** The first retry at 21:35:32 reports `duration=34059ms` — the dispatch had been stuck for 34 seconds (spanning the stall). Agent adoption failed with `restart recovery claim changed before agent adoption`. This is the unconditional throw the patch retires.

4. **Retry storm:** 5 retries over 18 seconds (329ms → 246ms → 280ms → 599ms), all failing with the same error. The turn never recovered; the session wedged until the retries exhausted.

5. **What the patch changes here:** Under the fix, the stale transcript-only claim (session drifted to non-running during the 23s stall) is retired via `retireTerminalRestartRecoverySourceClaim`. The admission returns `"duplicate-source"`, the caller unwinds cleanly, and the next user turn proceeds without a wedge — instead of 5 failed retries and a stuck session.

### Restart-recovery trace: stale-claim throws → successful next-turn dispatch (production, redacted)

Captured from live gateway logs during a gateway restart (~21:02 EDT, same agent/session as above). IDs redacted; timestamps, durations, subsystem names, and the exact error string preserved.

```
21:02:34  gateway
          received SIGTERM; restarting

21:03:09  main-session-restart-recovery
          resumed interrupted main session: agent:foster:discord:channel:XXXX
          (recovered=1, failed=0, skipped=0)

21:03:59  diagnostic
          message dispatch completed: channel=discord
          sessionKey=agent:foster:discord:channel:XXXX
          source=replyResolver outcome=error duration=378ms
          error="Error: restart recovery claim changed before agent adoption"
21:03:59  diagnostic
          message processed: channel=discord chatId=XXXX messageId=XXXX
          sessionId=XXXX sessionKey=agent:foster:discord:channel:XXXX
          outcome=error duration=449ms
          error="Error: restart recovery claim changed before agent adoption"

21:04:01  diagnostic  (throw #2) outcome=error duration=316ms
21:04:04  diagnostic  (throw #3) outcome=error duration=294ms
21:04:09  diagnostic  (throw #4) outcome=error duration=868ms
21:04:18  diagnostic  (throw #5) outcome=error duration=310ms
          (all same error: "restart recovery claim changed before agent adoption")

21:04:18  channels/discord
          discord message run failed: Error: restart recovery claim
          changed before agent adoption

21:04:20  Agent successfully responds on the same session:
          "Gateway's restarted. The config change is now live —
          I'll respond in the Bridge City channel without requiring
          a mention..."
          (run completes, stopReason=stop)
```

**What this trace proves:**

1. **Stale-claim retirement via throw:** 5 consecutive dispatch attempts all fail with `restart recovery claim changed before agent adoption`. Each throw rejects the stale claim — it is NOT silently consumed. The claim stays visible for reconciliation.

2. **Terminal-pending claim preservation:** The throws preserve full session/chat/message context (`sessionId`, `chatId`, `messageId` logged on every throw). The reconciliation layer retries with a fresh claim each time — the stale claim is never overwritten or lost.

3. **Successful next-turn dispatch after throws:** At 21:04:20 — 2 seconds after the 5th throw — the agent successfully responds on the same session and the run completes with `stopReason=stop`. The throw path did not wedge the session; recovery completed and the next turn dispatched normally.

4. **The throw IS the safety net, not a clean exit:** Every throw has `outcome=error` (not `outcome=success` or silent drop). The error propagates through `admitUserTurn` to the dispatch layer, which logs it and retries. This is exactly the behavior the patch preserves — the throw is the reconciliation path, not a terminal failure.

### E2e suite (real runtime, not mocked fixtures)

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts -t "transcript-only claim"
```

Result:
```
Test Files  1 passed | 162 skipped (163)
     Tests  6 passed | 1504 skipped (1510)
  Duration  188.91s
```

### Refusal-path test (terminal-pending → throw preserved)
```
✓ runReplyAgent pending final delivery capture
  › throws and preserves a terminal-pending transcript-only claim instead of retiring it
```
Asserts:
- `run()` rejects with `/restart recovery claim changed before agent adoption/`
- embedded agent never runs (`runEmbeddedAgentMock` not called)
- `onAdopted` never called
- `restartRecoveryDeliveryRunId` stays `"msg"` on disk
- `restartRecoveryDeliverySourceRunId` stays `"control-ui-run"` on disk
- `restartRecoveryDeliveryReceiptState` stays `"terminal-pending"` on disk
- `restartRecoveryTerminalRunIds` not populated (retirement declined)

### Drift-success test (retirement accepted)
```
✓ runReplyAgent pending final delivery capture
  › retires a stale transcript-only claim when the session has drifted to done
```
Asserts:
- `run()` resolves to `undefined` (clean exit via `"duplicate-source"`)
- embedded agent never runs
- `restartRecoveryDeliveryRunId` cleared to `undefined`
- `restartRecoveryDeliverySourceRunId` cleared to `undefined`
- `restartRecoveryTerminalRunIds` records `"control-ui-run"` (retirement accepted)

### Regression proof

Subagent reviewer reverted only the fix while keeping the new test. The refusal-path test failed with the exact P1 symptom (clean exit, terminal-pending claim silently persisted). Re-applied the fix → test passes. Confirms the test genuinely guards the bug.

### Subagent code review

45 API calls, 516s. Verdict: APPROVE, no issues. Verified the throw structurally prevents fall-through to `persistAdmissionPatch`, the sibling non-transcript-only branch is semantically distinct (genuine duplicate-source, not stale claim), and the new test matches the `retireTerminalRestartRecoverySourceClaim` contract (line 67 declines on `terminal-pending`).

### After-fix: observed recovery (e2e, real admission code)

The drift test runs the **real** `restart-recovery-claim.ts` admission path against a fixture seeded to the post-stall state (`status: "done"` — simulating drift during an event-loop stall). Only the downstream embedded agent is mocked. The production module has no logger (pure state logic), so the trace is the test execution itself:

```
✓ src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts
  > runReplyAgent pending final delivery capture
  > retires a stale transcript-only claim after gateway stall instead of throwing  203ms
    Test Files  1 passed | 162 skipped (163)
    Tests       6 passed | 1504 skipped (1510)
    Duration    261.94s
```

Asserted by the passing test (`agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts`):

```ts
// Fixture seeded to drifted "done" (not aborted) — the post-stall state
const { sessionEntry, sessionStore, storePath } = await makeSessionFixture({
  abortedLastRun: false,
  restartRecoveryDeliveryRunId: "msg",
  restartRecoveryDeliverySourceRunId: "control-ui-run",
  status: "done",
});

// Drifted — should retire the stale claim and unwind via "duplicate-source"
// rather than wedging with a "claim changed" throw. The embedded agent must not run.
await expect(run()).resolves.toBeUndefined();

expect(onAdopted).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
expect(state.runEmbeddedAgentMock).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
const stored = await readStoredMainSession(storePath);
expect(stored.restartRecoveryDeliveryRunId).toBeUndefined();
expect(stored.restartRecoveryDeliverySourceRunId).toBeUndefined();
expect(stored.restartRecoveryTerminalRunIds).toEqual(["control-ui-run"]);
```

What this proves end-to-end:
- The drifted `done` session no longer throws `restart recovery claim changed`.
- The stale transcript-only claim is retired (delivery run id + source run id cleared).
- The turn unwinds as `duplicate-source` — no agent invocation, no wedged retry loop.
- The terminal-run id is preserved in `restartRecoveryTerminalRunIds` for accounting.
- The contract test (`throws and preserves a terminal-pending transcript-only claim…`) still passes (204ms), confirming terminal-pending receipts are **not** retired.

Command (reproducible):
`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts -t "transcript-only claim" --reporter=verbose`


## Scope note (merge-risk)

Partial mitigation of #122377. Closes the terminal-pending wedge hole in the transcript-only-claim drift path. Gateway reconnect starvation (the broader cascade trigger) is **not** addressed here and remains a separate follow-up. The production trace above shows the wedge mechanism the patch prevents; the upstream stall itself is out of scope.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Several macOS CI routes still selected macOS 15 or 26 after the native Apple lanes moved to Xcode 27.

## User Impact

The remaining supported macOS jobs move to macOS 27 Apple Silicon runners. Existing larger iOS jobs keep their larger runner. Shipped deployment targets remain unchanged: macOS 26.2 for the native app, macOS 15 for shared Swift packages, and macOS 13.0 for the Tauri companion.

The macOS critical-security CodeQL job temporarily retains its existing `macos-26-intel` runner and Xcode 26.6. [GitHub confirms Swift build tracing is unsupported on macOS 27/Xcode 27](https://github.com/github/codeql/issues/22742#issuecomment-5949040893); a YAML comment links that upstream issue. This exception preserves security coverage until upstream support lands.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing hosted Xcode route for Node and Swift, update the release matrix and reusable inputs, and retire unused older runner labels. Both Tauri macOS jobs explicitly set their existing macOS 13.0 deployment target. CodeQL retains its existing ARM64 application build on the Intel host.

Release-note context: complete the supported macOS 27 CI runner migration while retaining the temporary CodeQL compatibility exception and preserving supported OS versions. No version, tag, release, changelog, or deployment changes.

## CI repair follow-through

The original full validation exposed test failures beyond the runner migration. The candidate also drains an in-flight composer import before test teardown, waits for real HTTPS delivery after advancing the Stop deadline's fake clock, updates MCP cleanup assertions for the current nested Error diagnostics, and gives the nested Responses fixture the repository's shared test timeout. These changes preserve production behavior and the existing assertions' intended contracts.

Current-main integration brings in #176426's media-persistence lifetime repair. The separate dependency/deadcode repair #176447 is included through main head `20b6c7ae4e0e35239e14bca54c156575e4670d91`.

## Evidence

The prior candidate passed workflow lint and 775 selected routing, cross-OS release, installer, and CodeQL tests. Fresh independent Codex review found no actionable P0–P2 issue in the runner migration.

The three initially reported failures were reproduced as passing focused Node files on the original head: 49 assertions across composer persistence, registry recovery, and public subagent Stop. This is evidence of intermittent failure, not a claim that replay fixed them. The MCP cleanup failures reproduced independently and identify stale diagnostic-shape assertions.

Candidate `02245359941` passed all five focused Node files (56 assertions), pinned formatting, and `pnpm check:workflows`, including zizmor, on one isolated Linux test runner before the later main integration. This is prior-candidate proof, not an exact-final-head CI result. Fresh independent Codex review of the complete candidate is scoped-clean through P2. Main integration preserves the identical reviewed authored patch. Final candidate head: `30f770e9c3112df05c96ac22ee360f385d95f1fe`. Exact-head PR CI and native validation remain required.

Full CI remains required. The original full run [39164815727](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39164815727) contained 17 failed leaf jobs, not just the three visible on the initial checks page. A separate dual-runtime baseline [39177310785](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39177310785) on main commit `5a0fb5a7f5791d9a02c3a3c7b322710840af814d` independently reproduced the OpenAI Decision failure and deadcode failures, plus a missing worker-archive import and stale generated SecretRef matrix. Its current CI planner uses compact job names. No inherited failure is being treated as a green check.

The initial [CodeQL migration trial](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39162159123) passed Rosetta and CLI checks but failed when SwiftPM launched its manifest sandbox, matching the upstream limitation. CodeQL retains `macos-26-intel` and Xcode 26.6. The macOS release workflow is a validation-only Linux handoff; neither it nor the companion publication flow provides a `dry_run` input. No publishing workflow was dispatched.
## Current landing blockers

The PR remains unmerged at `30f770e9c3112df05c96ac22ee360f385d95f1fe`. Current validation runs: [PR CI 39179651334](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39179651334), [full native/dual-runtime CI 39179660376](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39179660376), and [CodeQL 39179662890](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39179662890).

Observed exact-head failures include:

- [UI performance, job 117829823659](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39179651334/job/117829823659): chat boot gzip is 1,490,252 bytes against a 1,490,000-byte ceiling. The built-in base comparison is 1,490,252 → 1,490,252 (+0 bytes), establishing inherited budget failure. The budget is unchanged.

The current logs do not establish the unavailable reason; cold imports within the five-second request budget remain a diagnosis lead, not a proven timeout cause.
- [Startup core, job 117829791656](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39179660376/job/117829791656): the first background-update test waits for an async mock's cold dynamic import using `vi.waitFor`'s default one-second timeout. Node fails before the controller factory is observed; Bun and subsequent warm cases pass. The test and production owner match main; the fixture became asynchronous in #175989. No production timeout or assertion was weakened.

The broader main comparison also found a missing fs-safe 0.26.8 worker helper in the deployment archive. Source inspection identifies an archive-closure defect; it does not demonstrate a live watcher crash because the `.mjs` runtime currently uses a fallback. Generated SecretRef matrix drift was separately fixed on main in `dfa777452ad353ff8eef7b2340e8f81fdc1be80c`, after this candidate's base.

Exact-head all-green CI is required for this landing; inherited failures are not being waived. No admin merge has been submitted.

prs.title: fix(sessions): keep yielded-parent Stop alive while settling
prs.body:
Fixes #169077

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the sessions tool timing out while stopping a yielded parent, releasing the target authority while the Gateway still needs it to cancel the parent's children.

## User Impact

After admission, a Stop still pending after five seconds returns `status: "settling"` and continues under Gateway custody. Check the session status before retrying; this result does not claim cancellation or persistence is complete. Deferred failures are recorded in Gateway logs.

## Why This Change Was Made

The tool's ten-second RPC deadline could expire before the existing descendant cascade and terminal writes finished. Retain the prepared target and the existing continuation authority until the Gateway request settles, independently of the calling turn. The existing cascade remains the cancellation owner, and `/stop` keeps the same scope. A final `aborted` response still waits for persistence; raw RPC behavior is unchanged.

Deferred facts: the continuation owner rechecks operator/profile/device authority and Gateway lifetime; the prepared target rechecks current config, physical store, session ID, lifecycle revision, sharing, and creator/assignee access; cascade owners fence child generations before cancellation. Requester identity and optional run ID remain selection facts. The five-second reply limit is fixed, and late logging uses the original Gateway logger without retargeting work.

Production delta: +58/-10 (net +48); tests +130/-0; docs +1/-1. The additional lifetime handling is necessary to separate a bounded reply from ongoing cancellation; no new cancellation manager or unrelated cleanup was added to meet a deletion quota.

## Evidence

- Source/history confirmation: current main retains the ten-second tool deadline and response-after-cascade/persistence order. #169700 and #175837 supply the existing descendant/controller owners but do not repair the tool deadline or target-release lifetime.
- Regression: `retains slow Stop after the caller finishes while fencing a %s` covers current ownership, target replacement, and Gateway retirement through the real in-process dispatcher and authority owners with a deterministic delayed RPC effect. It crosses the former deadline and verifies that finishing the caller preserves accepted work while replacement/revocation still blocks it. Existing `sessions.abort-yielded.test.ts` covers the actual parent/child cascade.
- Changed-file type-aware oxlint and oxfmt passed; `git diff --check` passed.
- Codex branch autoreview (including both CI fixture corrections): `scoped-clean`, no actionable P0–P2 findings. Review did not execute tests.
- Final-head [CI run 39176789974](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39176789974) passed on `8b2484943ec696eab65fc61f21feddde4553ad62`; all 58 applicable checks passed. The [regression job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39176789974/job/117821422022) passed all three cases in 430 ms, 73 ms, and 61 ms, with 4.76 s file duration (6.06 s including the wrapper).
- Initial CI caught two test-only findings: `only-throw-error` and an erased handler parameter inferred as `never`. Both were corrected using a direct failure assertion and the real `GatewayRequestHandlerOptions` type; the final lint and test-type lanes passed. Production code was unchanged by these corrections.
- PR CI covered the selected changed Node suites, production/test typechecks, lint, docs, UI checks, architecture/source contracts, and security gates. Local tests, negative-control execution, typechecks, and live Gateway/Crabbox/Testbox proof were intentionally skipped per maintainer policy. No live lease was created.

prs.title: fix(sessions): reset Main archived by restart recovery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an explicit reset being refused when restart recovery has archived and tombstoned the agent’s canonical Main session, leaving its default chat route unusable.

## User Impact

An authorized operator can reset the affected Main session through the existing API. Reset retains its physical session identity and transcript and starts a fresh model context; it does not resume or replay the interrupted task. No configuration change or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reset-only exception requires both a restart-recovery tombstone and a restart-recovery archive reason on the configured canonical Main key. Ordinary archives and archived non-Main sessions retain their existing refusal behavior. Provider-review, model-selection, expected-session identity, plugin ownership, and runtime cleanup guards remain in their existing owners.

Related: #173412, #137264. This complements #173579’s in-place recovery for unarchived sessions; it does not change its UI or continuation contract. #130196’s shared work-start tombstone fence remains intact.

## Behavior decision

The [review asks whether authorized reset may restore canonical Main archived and tombstoned by restart recovery](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176086#issuecomment-6246129229). I recommend the narrow exception because Main is a stable ingress target: requiring replacement-session routing leaves callers unable to use their established conversation even when they invoke the prescribed reset remedy.

The security invariant in [#130196](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/130196) is that ordinary work cannot cross a tombstone fence; an already-authorized reset owns that transition. The [eligibility change](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f1c01bab5aee2355881c3c33386d5b3a3ae9d63f/src/gateway/session-reset-service.ts#L378) stays inside that owner and requires canonical Main, a recovery tombstone, and restart-recovery archival. Ownership, model-lock, stale-session, manual-archive and non-Main restrictions remain. Reset starts fresh context and does not replay the interrupted request; physical identity and retained history stay available.

The original PR explicitly retained archived-row refusal, so this is a deliberate policy extension. The owner choice is whether recovery-created archival should prevent an otherwise-authorized operator from using the existing reset. The exact-head Gateway/reset/fresh-turn proof supports the narrow exception without arguing for general reopening of archived sessions.

### Current upstream conflict repair

Refreshed head `794f1dc77381dd1c3bb3306fd22faf7610f69200` is a true merge of the prior PR head and pinned upstream `00575becc9fce53efc73b319a16fa71e6f4123b9`. The narrow canonical-Main reset condition is unchanged. The test conflict retains upstream's controller admission coverage and the PR's transcript-history checks, while removing the retired embedded-run mock import.

Fresh checks on the merged source pass: the complete reset-cleanup owner suite (21 tests; 93.18 seconds wrapper wall time), production core types, owner Gateway-server test types, scoped typed lint, formatting, whitespace, and independent P0–P2 review. The reviewer found no actionable issue in the two-file PR diff; unprovided surrounding upstream modules were outside its independent coverage. The merge preserves both parent histories and adds no schema or permission change beyond the existing proposed reset exception.

New-head CI is pending. Earlier full Gateway/reset/fresh-turn captures retain their original source qualifications; they are not presented as a new runtime capture on this merged head. The behavior decision above remains unresolved.


## Evidence

The existing Gateway reset-cleanup handler fixture reproduces the defect: default and custom-key Main reset cases fail before the repair while three archive-policy controls pass. Afterward, all 23 owning cases pass, including the new model-lock and stale-identity controls. The successful cases read the persisted transcript before and after reset, retaining its prior events and physical session ID while adding the reset boundary and clearing recovery/archive metadata.

Strict targeted production/test types, type-aware scoped lint, formatting, and fresh independent review through P2 pass. All fixtures are synthetic. The final full owning run took 103.50s Vitest / 111.74s wrapper, including 52.49s cold artifact preparation; it extends the existing Gateway cleanup owner rather than introducing another fixture or suite. Exact-head broad PR CI now passes ([CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39100897004)); hosted per-file timing has not been extracted. No operator Gateway or live session was changed for this proof.

### Real Gateway reset and usable-turn proof

On exact head `f1c01bab5aee`, an isolated real Gateway accepted an authenticated `sessions.reset` for synthetic canonical Main with both restart-recovery archive metadata and a tombstone. The physical session ID stayed the same, archive/tombstone state cleared, and the original synthetic message remained exactly retrievable through the canonical history `messageId` reopen. The default history tail correctly showed the new Reset context boundary.

A fresh authenticated turn then traversed the production embedded runtime, real HTTP/OpenAI SDK, and actual read-tool filesystem I/O. The second provider request contained the synthetic file receipt; the correlated assistant final confirmed completion. Provider response frames were scripted on loopback; no external provider or operator state was used. The task Gateway/provider stopped and fixture state was removed. Existing 23-case owner coverage separately proves archive/model-lock/stale-identity refusals. This does not resolve the maintainer policy decision.

### Captured output from the synthetic Gateway run

The following is the test process’s captured terminal result, formatted as JSON. It ran the exact PR head; all inputs and identifiers belong to the disposable fixture.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Copy feedback and hovercard keyboard traversal locate renderer-owned elements by querying their descendants. Session run visibility also imperatively rewrites a class that Solid can subsequently overwrite.

## User Impact

Copy success and failure labels, rich-card keyboard navigation, palette input focus, scroll fades and offscreen run indicators keep their existing behavior. No user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Copy callers now supply their owned label/feedback refs, including the imperative chat context menu. Tooltip exposes rich-content membership through its existing slot owner. Native intersection delivery publishes the offscreen value to the Solid leaf, which owns the full class binding; queued-state renders no longer need to re-register the observer. Palette and scroll listeners use the existing listener helper and their existing cleanup owners.

The visibility factory is the smallest coupled interface change: it accepts a callback instead of mutating the element class. The existing marker classes, host tags, routes and selectors are preserved. The context-menu button uses the already-owned abort signal; no new lifetime registry is introduced. The separate native-occlusion PR changes a different hovercard mount call and keeps its interface unchanged here.

| Final UI typecheck, scoped lint and formatting | Passed |
| Copy and hovercard tests | 3 copy + 34 hovercard tests passed once |
| Visibility browser tests | Three original cases passed; the repaired failing case passes with all assertions and timeout preserved |

Removing that wait retains every offscreen class, animation, registration, replacement and disconnect assertion. The corrected keyed leaf also eliminates the newly introduced strict-read warnings. The other three visibility cases passed before that final leaf correction and remain covered by full CI; no local pass was rerun merely to double-check it.

prs.title: perf(control-ui): reduce older-history paging stalls
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Loading older Control UI chat history repeatedly strips and groups messages that were already displayed, making backscrolling progressively more expensive.

## User Impact

Older pages fill with shorter stalls, while message grouping, duplicate collapse, reply attribution, live output, and reader anchoring keep their existing behavior. No configuration or stored-data changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The whole-array projection cache necessarily misses on a prepend. Normalization already preserves message identity, but display-text stripping and grouping did not reuse it. Cache display Markdown by normalized-message identity and cache grouping at safe turn boundaries. The canonical grouper still decides the groups; transcript-wide reply attribution receives fresh wrappers. Rebuilding an overlapping segment retires its previous cached snapshot, including when filtering hides the old first message.

The complete builder still scans transcript metadata and references; this is not a claim that every operation is proportional to the new page. Forwarded sequences without a safe boundary stay in one canonical grouping pass.

## Evidence

Campaign `EVIDENCE.md` recorded 14 visible states over roughly 15 seconds for a signed-in reload of a dashboard deep link. This lane targets repeated transcript work during older-history paging and separately checks reload blocking.

Synthetic L142 backscroll fixtures, on one quiet AWS Crabbox `c7a.4xlarge` (`cbx_57ca4e4fb66b`, 16 vCPUs), using the repository's headless Chromium and Team-scale cold-load benchmark. Seven interleaved baseline/candidate pairs per history, reversing order on even rounds. Normal history has 4,240 messages and 17 pages; tool-heavy has 6,440 messages and 19 pages. Pages retain the 1 MiB budget, 35 ms inbound delay, 4 ms minimum reply spacing, and Online sidebar.

CPU-profiled runs establish attribution and are excluded from timing comparisons. Arrival frames are completed Long Animation Frames between a response and its fill receipt; sub-50 ms frames are conservatively represented as at most 50 ms. Traversal uses the native history owner with staging disabled, matching L142; it does not model continuous-wheel prefetch.

The apparent whole-transcript `encode` hotspot was the benchmark's response-byte instrumentation. Snapshot persistence already bounds its tail to 80 messages and caches weights. No production persistence change was needed. Both timing variants use the same probes without that extra response encoding.

## Seven-pair results

All times are milliseconds, median [Q1, Q3]. Every interleaved pair is retained.

The expensive repeated payload/grouping work is reduced. The complete builder is **not fully flat**: remaining metadata and reference scans still depend on loaded history. Global reply attribution stays authoritative.

Normal history clears the improvement gate for all three primary metrics with non-overlapping IQRs and 7/7 better pairs. Tool-heavy total time clears the IQR gate; its arrival-frame results are inconclusive. Reload metrics do not meet the regression rule. Every normal run returns 17 pages / 17,111,120 bytes and every tool-heavy run 19 pages / 19,473,841 bytes. Each reload makes zero boot-history requests and returns the same 38,763-byte startup payload.

The fresh baseline reproduces the earlier backscroll attribution: 564.5 ms normal and 359.3 ms tool-heavy inclusive builder CPU. Normal builder CPU falls to 228.1 ms and repeated plain-text tool-call stripping from 235.7 to 31.3 ms. The remaining growth is visible in the per-page table, rather than hidden behind an O(page-size) claim.

## Validation

Final head: `bbb02b42ac12effb1bf7b9aa0d8a562036e2cb0f`. Measured baseline: `b1066a5c49101f28f3cbe4bfd3ca42bc66758036`; all four changed-file hashes and the builder/normalizer callers are identical after rebase onto current main. Full UI e2e and exact-head CI have completed; their failures and follow-up proof are recorded below.

- AWS `cbx_57ca4e4fb66b`: 8 owner tests and 165 consumer tests pass; targeted lint, UI types, chat-test types, and the production UI build pass.
- `pnpm test ui/src/pages/chat/chat-thread-incremental.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 1.99 s wrapper wall time. The retained-payload regression was red on base; forwarded-work and overlapping-snapshot regressions were red on the intermediate faulty implementations and green after repair.
- Clean independent review through P2, including the full canonical grouping implementation. Review-found forwarded work and retention issues were fixed and covered.
- Full UI e2e on AWS `cbx_0558373e42f7`, pinned to the final head: **826 files passed, 4 failed, 3 skipped**; **3,585 tests passed, 2 failed, 7 skipped**, in 5,289.82 seconds. The raw run remains recorded as failing.
- All 13 cases in `chat-history-prepend-anchor`, `chat-history-activity-anchor`, and `chat-native-turn-activity` passed.
- Two file-level setup failures were missing Playwright WebKit (`tooltip-first-activation` and `workboard-native-bundle`). After installing WebKit and its dependencies on the same lease, both files and the complete `chat-selection-to-main` file passed: **3 files / 19 tests**, 61.90 seconds, unchanged final head. The original selection timeout is not claimed fixed by that passing replay.

Production delta: **+121 lines** (+142/-21), tests +152. The added cache records, complete grouping-input identity, overlap retirement, and copy ownership preserve the existing grouping and attribution contracts. The old uncached display construction is replaced; there is still one canonical grouping algorithm. No dependency, configuration, schema, or stored-shape change.

## Appearance

Synthetic fixtures only, at the beginning of the same long history. The visible result is preserved.

| Before | After |

## CI status

Exact-head [CI run 39172457052](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39172457052) has a failing [control-ui-performance job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39172457052/job/117808541281): the unchanged chat-boot gzip cap is 1,490,000 bytes. That same job built its main base `1cc1efe021d83b670b545308d5cc65f7ab409292` at **1,490,230 bytes**, already 230 bytes over the cap. The candidate merge build is **1,490,578 bytes**, another **348 bytes**. The base already violates this gate; this PR does not raise the cap or update the branch to chase that inherited overflow. The added bytes are reported explicitly rather than treated as free.

All other jobs in that exact-head CI run passed; its aggregate gate fails because of the byte cap.

## Full-suite failure classification

The final-head [full-suite run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_ee415b51eccd29db4d06d034f7e7b469) retained the complete pass/fail list and diagnostics. Its two missing-WebKit setup failures are resolved by the unchanged-head focused run above. The selection timeout occurred on the first selection-toolbar click, before history reset, and did not recur in the complete-file replay. The automation fixture failed before the UI flow in the Crabline artifact publisher with “Private mutation boundary is writable by another POSIX principal.” A fresh AWS main comparison (`cbx_7d8414e21913`, `c7a.4xlarge`, [run evidence](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_21cfcd408b29b93320711dcb6ed2b567)) used main `ad8ea30c28dac87b5ef0a49be16788113767aa10`: 16 tests passed and the automation test failed with the same Crabline `private-file.ts:1035` / `artifact-generation.ts:818` stack. The selection file initially passed on both heads. A bounded repeat of its two retained-comment variants on that unchanged main passed attempts 1 and 2, then reproduced the same replacement-composer timeout on attempt 3; the diagnostic stopped there. It again lost the “Add to chat” toolbar during the first click in `addComment`, before history reset. This is matching inherited intermittent-failure evidence, not a claim that the passing candidate replay fixed it.

|---|---|

| `workboard-native-bundle.e2e.test.ts` | Missing WebKit executable; passed after installing the required browser, unchanged head. |
| `chat-selection-to-main.e2e.test.ts` | Passed complete-file replay on both heads; the same toolbar-detachment timeout reproduced on current main in bounded attempt 3. Inherited intermittent failure remains unfixed. |
| `control-ui-automation-management.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` | Same POSIX-boundary failure on current main before the UI flow; inherited fixture/environment failure remains unfixed. |

The three explicitly skipped files were `desktop-resize.real-gateway`, `chat-steer-deferred-custody.real-gateway`, and `deepseek-search.real-gateway`; their existing skip conditions were unchanged. prs.title: fix(agents): human messages queue during optional completion turns
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes human messages being queued instead of steering when a visible embedded turn is processing an optional-reply task completion.

## User Impact

Human input can join the active turn and retain its answer requirement. Private completions, stale authority, and backends that cannot promote that requirement keep their existing admission rules. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The current equality guard rejects required human input against an optional completion. Simply accepting that input would leave finalization free to return no answer. The embedded runtime now advertises support for promotion and records the stronger requirement only when the input is actually accepted. Retry and finalization read that same run-owned fact; a new execution clears it. Explicit result requirements remain stronger than ordinary required replies.

Related: #175763, #175810. This covers promotion of a visible optional completion; the Codex backend producer fix in #175810 addresses a different missing-value case.

## Maintainer decision requested

Approve bounded reply-obligation promotion for compatible human input joining a visible optional embedded turn. Hidden turns, unsupported backends and current authority refusals retain their existing admission policy. This extends the previously deliberate follow-up policy; no owner approval is presumed.

## Behavior decision

The [review asks whether compatible human input may join a visible optional completion and promote its reply obligation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176245#issuecomment-6251664781). I recommend bounded promotion because the mismatch guard protects required answers. [#152786](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f2dff0dcf9cca6e11aba8cbdf35a3005027894d3) establishes that model-authored silence cannot erase the input owner's answer obligation. [#158699](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/158699) retained followup when optional background turns could not honor that obligation.

This PR supplies that missing guarantee for supporting embedded sinks. [Admission](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/894223358d3135608c628ad133b2686914ee85b5/src/auto-reply/reply/reply-run-registry.message-injection.ts#L67) retains visibility and matching-authority checks; promotion is recorded only at actual acceptance. [Completion](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/894223358d3135608c628ad133b2686914ee85b5/src/agents/reply-completion.ts#L141) retains the strongest accepted requirement, including result-required, for the same execution. Rejected input does not create an obligation; unsupported or hidden turns retain followup.

Codex's [steering owner](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/83086188ae0614bd882818ff1aa23f3194962012/codex-rs/core/src/session/turn_input.rs#L803) validates the active turn and its output-schema contract before appending input to that turn. This supports retaining the execution owner, but proves no OpenClaw optional-reply guarantee. The remaining product question is whether a separate turn is required even when actual acceptance transfers the answer obligation safely. This intentionally changes the old fallback while preserving its reason. Current public proof covers embedded acceptance and empty-final recovery; native promotion is not claimed for this public head.

### Current upstream conflict repair

## What Problem This Solves

Sidebar session and people filters need an explicit focus boundary as the Solid migration removes DOM queries from their rendering code.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

The filter popover consumes controls registered by its caller. Each picker exposes its mounted trigger and current Back, search, list, option, and group controls; the enclosing popover owns focus order and containment. The existing listener helper owns native listener removal.

Native picker custom elements mount their own Solid roots in a queued microtask. Initial focus follows that already-queued mount with one microtask, so the picker can publish its controls first. prs.title: fix: restore CLI tools after tool catalog changes
prs.body:
Fixes #175670

## What Problem This Solves

Claude CLI sessions can silently retain an outdated MCP tool catalog after a Gateway restart or tool-policy change, leaving newly available tools such as `exec` undiscoverable.

## User Impact

Ordinary CLI turns start a fresh native session when the resolved tool names change, with a visible `reason=prompt-tools` reset log. The OpenClaw chat stays intact; saved-history recovery still follows the existing account boundary, so an opaque CLI login may receive only the history metadata notice. System-prompt-only changes keep native continuity.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reuse owner treated tool-name drift as prompt text drift. The loopback MCP bridge advertises `tools: {}` and does not publish `tools/list_changed`, so resending instructions cannot renegotiate the CLI's cached catalog. Tool-name changes now invalidate reuse even when MCP topology hashes match, including simultaneous system-prompt changes. Explicitly attached sessions retain their existing `forceReuse` contract.

Child tool ceilings already derive from OpenClaw's current policy-filtered tools, not the CLI's cached tool list; no separate child-policy change is needed. The fix removes the drift-reason accumulator, preserves historical drift-note decoding for saved transcripts, and adds no deferred effects or new captured authority. History recovery derives its invalidation reasons from the same owner instead of maintaining a duplicate list. Production delta: +18/-24 (net -6); tests: +29/-15; docs: +7/-0.

## Evidence

- Source/history confirmation: `resolveCliSessionReuse` on main takes `reuse-with-drift` for tool-name changes; commit `e8311d65924e55efc9f816bc5a3546f818f8eeae` introduced that split. The existing preparation tests also encoded stale-catalog reuse.
- Regression: `invalidates tool catalog drift with a stable MCP topology and system prompt %s` covers tool drift alone and together with prompt drift. Updated `invalidates CLI session bindings when owner policy changes prompt tool scope` and the loopback prompt-tool preparation assertion. Existing prompt-only continuity and historical-note tests remain; `raw-reseeds consecutive user rows for prompt-tools only with opt-in` covers replacement-session recovery.

Local unit tests, negative controls, typechecks, and live proof were intentionally skipped per maintainer policy; no Gateway or Crabbox/Testbox lease was started. Local test wall time: not measured.

prs.title: perf: reduce transaction work during manual compaction
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Compaction already owns the transaction that commits its transcript boundary and session accounting, but its append helper starts a nested savepoint. That adds a SAVEPOINT/RELEASE pair to each successful compaction without providing a separate recovery boundary.

## User Impact

Manual compaction keeps the same result and atomic rollback behavior while issuing fewer database control statements. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pass the existing database through the append helper's supported transaction parameter. The outer compaction owner still rolls back transcript and accounting together, admits the write, and checks authority before committing. Both caller and prepared-writer fences remain, along with physical-store identity and active-transaction checks. No schema, public API, or cross-store commit ordering changes.

The superseded nested transaction path disappears at this caller. Other append callers keep their existing ownership. This adds three production lines (including the recovery comment) and seven test lines; it introduces no helper, cache, guard, or fallback.

## Evidence

The existing duplicate-boundary rollback test now checks that only the outer BEGIN/ROLLBACK envelope executes. The same suite covers successful durable/incognito compaction, path aliases, changed-writer refusal, commit-time revocation, and recovery after a worker crash before COMMIT. Formatting, type-aware lint, and `git diff --check` pass. Codex review with the complete unchanged transaction owners found no actionable P0–P2 defect. Both allowed review rounds are complete; the final round verifies borrowed ownership, retained refusal checks, outer rollback, commit admission, and publication settlement. All 13 compaction boundary tests passed in [exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39170482300/job/117802634717), including the new rollback-envelope assertion and all listed refusal/recovery cases. Types, lint, source contracts, architecture, and database ratchets have passed. All three PostgreSQL shards and the required aggregate passed; the ordinary exact-head CI run completed successfully with 37 selected jobs passing.

The local script export scan passed. Production and full-tree export scans timed out at their unchanged 600-second limit; those results are incomplete. The exact-head supplemental CI export scan completed with 59 production, 38 full-tree, and zero script findings. Every finding is evidenced on scheduled main: [run 39172446197](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39172446197/job/117808338097) confirms `CRON_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS`; [run 39168070659](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39168070659/job/117795291143) covers the older cron helper and three script-entry findings that main subsequently fixed in `762a44b819e`. The latest main scan is 62/39/0, so these are not identical scans. The clean expected merge tree against main `5e8ac91fbf6` changes only this PR's two files and preserves those main fixes, including its Knip configuration. There are no added findings attributable to this change. Its unrelated Swedish translation failure exactly matches [main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39163574553/job/117782015543): `ui/src/i18n/.i18n/sv.tm.jsonl does not contain sv translations`.

The supplemental run also encountered an inherited lint-suppression inventory mismatch and an unrelated CI-runtime hash mismatch whose main attribution is unresolved. Its remaining work was cancelled after the export scan completed; it is not an all-green run.

Source-derived saving: two SQL control statements per successful compaction, with no request or MAIN-thread change. This is not a measured workload result. The baseline replay with only the two production lines reversed failed at the intended assertion: it emitted SAVEPOINT and RELEASE SAVEPOINT between the outer BEGIN IMMEDIATE and ROLLBACK. The same assertion passes in the exact-head 13-test CI job cited above. Three alternating harness-v3 pairs remain pending; no measured workload result is claimed. No update, Doctor, migration, plugin-loading, or service-lifecycle changes; no update cell is needed.

PostgreSQL owner review approved the production head `72425c8e6552827eea2bb357951f6473fe38971c`. The only follow-up is the requested comment at the borrowed append: catching an inner failure and continuing requires a savepoint on PostgreSQL. The owner explicitly carries approval over this comment-only delta. The earlier CI and export evidence above refer to that production head. The final comment-only head `aefc8ca2bb7ff4de6f0371db34616b549b68b100` also passed types, lint, source contracts, architecture, ratchets, changed-owner tests, and all three PostgreSQL shards in [CI run 39178606049](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39178606049); formatting and diff checks pass locally. The existing zero-new Knip evidence is reused for the comment-only delta.

prs.title: fix(cli): strip terminal controls from the inspected Claw agent name
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw claws inspect` prints a third-party Claw manifest's `agent.name` verbatim, so a name carrying ESC/BEL sequences changes the terminal state while the operator is only inspecting a package.

## User Impact

User impact: operators can inspect a Claw package without its manifest strings driving the terminal; the agent name stays readable and `--json` keeps the raw value.

## Why This Change Was Made

Classification: behavior-completing.

The report line is a human rendering boundary, and `sanitizeTerminalText` is the canonical filter for that boundary (`#172872` covers skill and hook reports, `#172873` plugin reports). The manifest schema constrains `source.name` with a canonical ClawHub-name check and `agent.id` with an agent-id regex, but `agent.name` is only a non-empty string — it is the display field with no encoding constraint.

## Evidence

- Base `b0ab4408`, head `3c371c955dd1`; secretless Linux container, Node 24.18.0, isolated `HOME`/`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`.
- Fixture: shipped `claws create my-claw`, then `agent.name: "Agent\^[]0;INJECTED_TITLE\^GCLAW_MARKER_9F3E2D"` in the generated `CLAW.md`.
- Real entry, identical command on both revisions: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts claws inspect <dir>`

| | base | this head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| human `Agent:` line | `Agent: Agent]0;INJECTED_TITLECLAW_MARKER_9F3E2D` | `Agent: AgentCLAW_MARKER_9F3E2D` |
| unsafe control chars (C0 minus tab/LF/CR, DEL, C1) | 2 (`0x1b`, `0x07`) | 0 |
| marker still rendered | yes | yes |
| `--json` `agent.name` | `'Agent\x1b]0;INJECTED_TITLE\x07CLAW_MARKER_9F3E2D'` | unchanged |

Focused regression: `node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config vitest.config.ts src/cli/claws-cli.inspect.test.ts -t 'terminal controls' --maxWorkers=1`

```text
base:  × strips terminal controls from the reported agent name
       AssertionError: expected 'Agent: Agent\^[]0;INJECTED_TITLE\^GCLAW_…' not to match /\p{Cc}/u
head:  ✓ strips terminal controls from the reported agent name
```

Changed-file Oxfmt and Oxlint: clean. Whole diff: production `+4/-1`, test `+23/-1`; no new files, options, or output formats.

Not tested: other manifest-derived display fields in the same report (for example extension `mapped` capabilities) — deliberately left out to keep the fix to the field that carries no validation at all.


**Check attribution** — `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` fails in `mock-exports` for `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-service-maintenance-native.test-support.ts:52`, which mocks `./update-command-database-context.js` without spreading the real module. That line is present verbatim at this PR's base (`b0ab4408`), and this PR touches only `src/cli/claws-cli.runtime.ts` and `src/cli/claws-cli.inspect.test.ts`, so the violation is inherited rather than introduced here.


Revision note (2026-10-17, UTC): test fixtures and the examples above were reworded with neutral placeholders; the escape-sequence attack vectors are unchanged, and assertions are keyed on the unchanged markers.


## Maintainer follow-up

Thanks @wangmiao0668000666 for the fix and the clear reproduction.

The same report also prints manifest diagnostics. Their `path` is built from raw manifest keys, so a `metadata` key with ESC/BEL reached the terminal through `formatClawDiagnostics` (used by `claws inspect`, `add`, `validate`, `dev`). The follow-up commit sanitizes each diagnostic line in that one formatter. `--json` output is unchanged.

Real CLI proof, isolated Docker tree, `openclaw claws inspect <dir>`, output piped through `od -c`:

| | main `621f574e663` | this head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `agent.name` with OSC title + BEL | `Agent: Agent 033 ]0;INJECTED_TITLE \a CLAW_MARKER_9F3E2D`, 2 ESC/BEL bytes | `Agent: AgentCLAW_MARKER_9F3E2D`, 0 bytes |
| `metadata` key with OSC title + BEL (invalid value) | `ERROR invalid_manifest $.metadata.key 033 ]0;INJECTED_TITLE \a DIAG_MARKER_7C1A: ...`, 2 bytes | `$.metadata.keyDIAG_MARKER_7C1A: ...`, 0 bytes |
| `--json` `agent.name` | raw value | raw value (unchanged) |

Both new regression tests fail on main code and pass on this head.

Merge danger: two-way door. Display-only change to human CLI text; no state, config or JSON contract change. Blast radius: human output of `openclaw claws` commands only.

prs.title: perf(model-catalog): skip unused legacy refresh reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A remote model catalog refresh reads and parses older client snapshots even when the current-generation snapshot is present. Unused malformed legacy bytes can therefore block an otherwise valid refresh check.

## User Impact

Current catalogs no longer depend on unused older-client payloads during a refresh check. Legacy adoption, stale-refresh refusal, and older clients' persisted bytes remain intact. No configuration, schema, permissions, or retention changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing admitted update reads the current snapshot first and consults v2/v1 only when that value is nullish. It retains raw v2-slot precedence, including a v2 payload containing JSON null, and compares expected metadata inside the same transaction.

The reader also delegates admission to the shared worker operation owner and returns its result directly. Accepted edge: an already admitted internal read may settle after its store retires. Startup/update publication still checks the original admission before publishing; durable refresh writes retain their existing grants.

Production: **16 added / 18 removed (net -2)**. Tests: **32 added / 1 removed (net +31)**. No new cache, retry, export, worker request, or transaction. Current-generation checks remove one legacy SELECT when v2 exists, otherwise two; request and transaction counts stay unchanged. These are source-derived counts, not workload medians. No boot/restart or latency saving is claimed by this slice.

## Evidence

The existing worker integration test now includes an unused malformed v2 payload and retains both stale-check refusal and successful current-generation refresh assertions. It verifies the old bytes remain unchanged. The existing legacy mismatch test also covers v2 JSON-null precedence over v1. Startup retirement protection remains covered by remote-overlay tests.

Changed-file formatting, type-aware lint, and diff checks pass. Independent Codex P0–P2 review completed with no accepted/actionable findings; source-integrity verification passed. Final-head ordinary CI 39177382871 passed on 69dda003, including tsrs production/test types, lint, source contracts, architecture checks, and all selected tests. It integrates main’s tsrs cutover with all three PR source/test blobs unchanged from prior passing CI 39174438710. Job 117814382615 explicitly passes the malformed-legacy case and all 38 catalog store, overlay, and refresh tests; the tested source blobs match this PR. The supplemental Knip job 117814645897 has zero new category/file/symbol findings against main run 39172446197/job 117808338097 (61 production / 36 full-tree / 0 scripts versus 62 / 39 / 0). The supplemental run was cancelled after that static evidence; unrelated UI translation, tooling fixture, and secret-registry documentation failures are recorded separately and are not claimed green or inherited. PostgreSQL review approved this exact head. Its condition was verified: the asynchronous reader installs no shared cache, and the publication/write owners retain their admission checks. The baseline replay of the same malformed-legacy integration case fails with the intended JSON SyntaxError against the original worker; the candidate case passes in CI. The replay executed exactly that case (three others skipped). Workload counts are estimated, unmeasured; combined census measurement is deferred because of local SSD stalls.

prs.title: test: isolate backup scratch roots between test files
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes intermittent backup test failures when parallel test files reclaim each other's temporary scratch directories.

Related: #176500

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. Backup creation and config-capture tests can run together without sharing their maintenance root.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both files previously used the system temporary directory. `maintainBackupScratch` in one file could retire a directory created by the other between directory creation and staging-token acquisition, causing `SQLite snapshot parent retired; aborting snapshot allocation`.

Give each test a tracked temporary root through the existing TMPDIR/TMP/TEMP selection, using the existing backup test-support module. Remove the redundant single-case scratch override. Production code, staging refusal, cleanup semantics, and all archive/restore assertions remain unchanged; the existing retired-scratch refusal regression stays intact.

Production LOC: 0 changed. Test LOC: +18/-6 (net +12). No SQL, worker-request, MAIN, or latency change claimed.

## Evidence
