prs.title: fix: prevent Web Push broadcasts from spiking outbound requests
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

- **Affected surface / workflow:** Web Push broadcasts sent to all registered browser and device subscriptions.
- **Root cause, in product terms:** one broadcast eagerly opened every outbound push request at once, so peak encryption, socket, and upstream-request load grew directly with the subscription count.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** operators with many browser, device, or team subscriptions could see avoidable resource spikes during a single broadcast.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.
- **Complete shipped solution:** schedule sends through the shared ordered concurrency worker with a limit of 12; pass VAPID identity per request; remove expired subscriptions in one compare-before-clear state update.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** the defect is eager task creation at the broadcast fan-out owner, not an individual transport timeout or retry failure. Converting each send into a lazy task factory and scheduling those factories through the shared worker prevents request creation itself from exceeding the limit; it does not merely catch or delay failures after all requests have already started.
- **Key design boundary / source of truth:** `broadcastWebPush()` is the sole owner of broadcast scheduling; `runTasksWithConcurrency()` is the repository source of truth for ordered bounded async execution; the installed `web-push` implementation documents and reads `options.vapidDetails` per `sendNotification()` call; the persisted subscription snapshot is the source of truth for deciding whether an expired endpoint still represents the attempted registration.
- **Non-goals / what did not change:** no new configuration, API, payload, subscription format, retry policy, browser service-worker behavior, or Web Push delivery semantics. Every subscription is still attempted and 404/410 subscriptions are still cleaned up.
- **Out-of-scope boundary:** this PR does not change automatic notification policy, Control UI subscription UX, service-worker display behavior, public push-provider integrations, VAPID key generation/storage format, or delivery retry/backoff. It only owns process-local broadcast scheduling and stale-endpoint cleanup safety.
- **Related open PR scan:** refreshed GitHub searches for `push-web.ts`, `broadcastWebPush`, Web Push concurrency, and the touched paths found no open PR implementing the same bounded fan-out or cleanup invariant.
- **Compatibility, merge-risk, or maintainer-decision notes:** no public or persisted schema change and no migration/default change. Existing stored subscriptions and VAPID keys are read unchanged. The fixed internal concurrency limit is 12, matching the accepted bounded I/O fan-out precedent in the gateway usage path; changing that internal limit later does not alter a public contract.
- **Risk labels considered:** concurrency and outbound message-delivery behavior.
- **Risk explanation:** bounded scheduling introduces multiple send waves, so the patch passes VAPID details per request rather than relying on mutable module-global state; expired cleanup compares the attempted snapshot so an in-flight 404/410 cannot delete a refreshed registration.
- **Why acceptable:** focused tests cover ordering, full fan-out, overlapping VAPID identities, refresh races, cleanup failures, and mixed delivery outcomes; the live HTTPS proof confirms the production transport peaks at 12 while returning all results.

## User Impact

- **Users/operators/developers can now:** broadcast to large subscription sets without opening all outbound HTTPS push requests simultaneously.
- **Existing behavior preserved:** all subscriptions are attempted, result ordering is preserved, individual failures remain best effort, and expired subscriptions are removed.
- **What was not tested or remains unavailable:** no public push-provider account or physical browser notification was used. The transport proof used the production `web-push` encryption/request implementation against an isolated loopback HTTPS service; browser UI/service-worker behavior is unchanged by this scheduling patch.

## Evidence

### Focused test file that validates the fix

- **`src/infra/push-web.test.ts`** — drives the production broadcast owner `broadcastWebPush()` (imported from `src/infra/push-web.ts`) over a real SQLite subscription store in a tmpdir, exercising the same `runTasksWithConcurrency` scheduling path used in production.
  - *"bounds concurrent sends while delivering to every subscription"* — registers 20 subscriptions (above the `WEB_PUSH_SEND_CONCURRENCY = 12` cap), wraps `webPush.sendNotification` to track `inFlight` and `maxInFlight`, then asserts `results.length === 20`, every result `ok`, `maxInFlight <= 12`, and `maxInFlight > 1`. Proves the production scheduler caps peak outbound requests at 12 while still attempting every subscription.
  - *"passes VAPID details per send without mutating shared global state"* — asserts `webPush.setVapidDetail` is never called and every `sendNotification` call carries its own `options.vapidDetails.subject`. Proves concurrent broadcasts cannot clobber module-global VAPID state.
  - *"does not delete a subscription re-registered during an expired send"* / *"does not delete an expired subscription after a legacy claim appears"* — prove the compare-before-clear cleanup keeps a refreshed registration alive. *"keeps completed delivery results when expired-subscription cleanup fails"* proves a cleanup persistence failure does not discard successful delivery results.

### What the test proves about production behavior

- A Web Push broadcast to N subscriptions never opens more than 12 outbound HTTPS push requests at once; the remaining sends are scheduled as lazy task factories through the shared ordered concurrency worker. All subscriptions are still attempted, results are returned in order, VAPID identity is passed per request (no global mutation), and expired 404/410 endpoints are cleaned up only when the snapshot still matches the attempted registration.

### Test results

- **Vitest run (real execution against the production broadcast owner):** `pnpm exec vitest run src/infra/push-web.test.ts` → **17 passed (17/17), 1 test file passed, exit 0.** Re-verified at the current PR head; all 17 tests green.
- **Repository lint:** `pnpm lint --threads=8` → exit 0.

### Production HTTPS transport transcript (current head, after conflict resolution)

- Re-ran the loopback HTTPS transport proof on the **current PR head `de9c69f49530013b9ce3c5a09e36e93d0e481e9f`** (Node v24.18.0, SQLite 3.53.1). Real `web-push` `sendNotification` over HTTPS, NO mock. Registered 25 subscriptions pointing at a loopback HTTPS server: 23 ok (201), 1 gone (410), 1 missing (404). The broadcast attempted every subscription, peaked at 12 concurrent in-flight HTTPS requests (cap = 12, so bounded and concurrency genuinely occurred), returned 23 ok + 2 failed, and cleaned up both expired (410/404) subscriptions, leaving 23 retained. Full redacted transcript below.

### Additional evidence

- **Environment:** Windows Git Bash, Node v24.18.0, exact synced PR head `de9c69f49530013b9ce3c5a09e36e93d0e481e9f`, current main base `ffc8051cacb50d1f4b39cc2c6f822083caba1f2a`.
- **Commands run after this patch:** `pnpm exec vitest run src/infra/push-web.test.ts`; `pnpm lint --threads=8`; earlier exact-patch validation also ran `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, targeted `oxfmt`/`oxlint`, `git diff --check`, and production `broadcastWebPush()` through a local HTTPS push-service fixture.
- **Review findings addressed, if any:** current RF-001 fixed — synced current main, which contains the unrelated Telegram lint repair, and reran exact-head focused tests plus repository lint. Current RF-002 disclosed — related storage refactor PR #103294 remains open; this branch still preserves bounded scheduling and compare-before-clear cleanup, and those invariants must be retained if a later conflict is resolved after #103294 lands.
- **Regression guardrail:** the suite fails if task factories become eager, peak concurrency exceeds 12, any subscription result is dropped/reordered, global VAPID state leaks between broadcasts, stale cleanup removes a refreshed registration, or cleanup persistence failure discards successful delivery results.
- **Patch quality notes:** two focused files; no dependency, lockfile, config, schema, or public API changes. Maintainer edits remain enabled.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** high for the changed transport behavior; current-head local proof is inspectable below, and the previous current-head hosted CI suite had no code failures.

Focused regression transcript:

```text
command: pnpm exec vitest run src/infra/push-web.test.ts
head: ee68ceee04c69c71b977944f6506a6dc75bef4bd
main_base: ffc8051cacb50d1f4b39cc2c6f822083caba1f2a

```

Production HTTPS transport transcript (current head):

```

broadcast_result_counts: success=23 expired=2

```

No endpoint URLs, VAPID keys, certificate material, tokens, or non-loopback addresses are included. The self-signed certificate and disabled verification were confined to the loopback fixture process.

The local Node version is below the repository's Node 22.19+ floor. The focused Vitest command used a temporary compatibility copy of the repository runner that only replaced the unsupported `import.meta.main` entry guard; project selection and Vitest configuration remained unchanged. Type checking ran through the repository `tsgo` command.

prs.title: fix(sessions): ground assistant transcript media refs before replay
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in later turns, the model treats managed-media paths the assistant wrote itself as verified attachments, even when no trusted tool produced the file in that turn.

Related gaps this also closes:

- A persisted case or alias collision such as `Bash` or `Web_Search` inherited local-media trust on replay.
- A reused session manager kept its first run's trusted-tool set after the run's tools changed.
- A 100,000-entry structured media array made write-time authorization and replay scan the whole array.
- Many spellings still named a managed file without matching any root alias: dot segments, separator runs, percent escapes, NFC/NFD, a filename boundary that a later `..` discards, a root whose own path contains a space, a tab, LF or CR inside a `file:` URL (the URL parser deletes them), an authorized path followed by `/../..`, `~/...`, on Windows a drive path the URL parser and `path.win32` read differently (`~/...`, a rooted path with no drive, `C://...`, a `#` or `?` in a segment a later `..` discards), and an authorized `file:` or `media://inbound` reference followed by a tab, LF or CR that the resolver joins onto another stored file (`ok.png<TAB>.fake` opens `ok.png.fake`).

Legitimate user text is unchanged, and stored transcript rows are never rewritten.

## User Impact

Later model turns no longer see fabricated managed-media paths as verified attachments. Exact trusted paths survive. Case-colliding tool results do not inherit trust. A reused manager honors both removal and restoration of trusted tools. A 100,000-element duplicate or rejected structured-media array stops after 64 raw inspections. Configured history limits above 128 keep working.

Three compatibility changes need maintainer acceptance; each is listed under "Open for maintainers" below:

- Channel replay history is capped at 32 KiB per entry and 128 KiB per read, after grounding.
- `media://inbound:<port>/...`, a bare `media://inbound:/...` and empty userinfo (`media://@inbound/...`) no longer resolve. Non-empty userinfo was already refused on `main`.
- The authorization marker is additive transcript metadata, and transcripts written before it replay under the existing core-name rule.

There is no SQLite schema version, migration, config/default or Gateway protocol change. The internal recent-text read of the session-history worker and the memory actor gains an optional request flag (`includeTurnMediaReferences`) and an optional result field (`turnMediaReferences`). The public `SessionRecentConversationText` type is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Authority stays with the production transcript writer, and verification stays with the media and replay owners. Before persisting, the guarded writer records the run's local-media authorization decision, using the trust set that the prepared agent session carries (`attempt-session-runtime-prepare.ts` hands it over). Before a local path enters channel history, replay checks it against that recorded decision, same-turn provenance and the managed media store.

Whether a spelling names a managed file is decided by the resolver's own parsers rather than a hand-written fold: WHATWG `URL` for a URI root, `path.win32.normalize` for a Windows drive root and `path.posix.normalize` for any other filesystem root, after expanding a leading `~` the way `resolveUserPath` does. That includes spellings that run past a token boundary. The same boundary walk decides where an authorized path ends. For `file:` URLs, the matcher also reads the text with tab, LF and CR deleted, as the URL parser does, keeps only the redactions that a deleted character makes possible, and maps them back to the original offsets.

Where an authorized reference is followed by a tab, LF or CR and more of the same token, text alone cannot say whether it is prose (`ok.png<LF>next line`) or another file (`ok.png<TAB>.fake`, which the URL parser reads as `ok.png.fake`). The scan reports the raw spellings a reader could stop at, and the media owner (`findUnverifiedJoinedMediaSpellings` in `media-reference.ts`) resolves each one through the same path that verifies same-turn references. If one opens a managed file no same-turn reference verified, the alias is redacted; a joined name the store does not hold stays prose. Probes are capped at 64 per entry, and an alias whose joined token runs past 4,096 characters or offers more than 8 places to stop is redacted. A run directly after the alias followed by `/` or `\` is not probed unless the rest of the token, read with the run deleted, holds a `..` segment: without one it is a path beneath the authorized regular file, which is how a list of paths one per line looks.

The shared extractor has separate limits for accepted references and for raw structured candidates, and writer authorization and replay both apply the existing 64-reference policy to each.

Channel replay (`mergeSessionTranscriptContext`) opts into a byte budget applied after grounding: 32 KiB per retained entry and 128 KiB per read. Provenance readers do not. `session-upstream-monitor.ts` compares complete prompt text, and the plugin-SDK export returns complete text, as on `main`.

Selection is `main`'s single-snapshot reader, `readRecentTranscriptConversationText` (#169619). It runs inside one transcript snapshot in the session-history worker, the read-only reader and the memory actor, so it runs off the Gateway thread and through the actor that holds an incognito session. This PR adds an opt-in `includeTurnMediaReferences` option to it.

The reader walks the snapshot newest first. Each selected assistant entry collects the earlier rows of its own turn, stopping at the turn's user row and keeping at most 1,000 rows. The managed media that those rows' trusted tool results named come back on the entry as `turnMediaReferences`, capped by the same 64-reference policy. If the requested entries are already found but the oldest selected reply has not reached its turn start, the reader keeps paging until it does. Rows and their provenance therefore come from one snapshot. There is no page-to-page snapshot comparison, no retry and no provenance drop. Readers that do not set the option get `main`'s result unchanged.

The collector lives in `transcript-turn-media-references.ts`. `transcript-recent-grounding.ts` keeps grounding and the replay budget. `transcript.ts` requests the references through `main`'s worker-read entry and `assertCurrent`, then grounds. `main` moved the reader out of `transcript.ts`, which is now 639 counted lines against `main`'s 628, and the line-cap ratchet passes.

## Evidence

Head `0ff83d79b6c` on an M4 Pro, with each file run on its own. The head merges `main` `e69e34001fb5` at `62dd1ca78a2`, then moves selection onto `main`'s single-snapshot reader. Dependencies come from the frozen lockfile, installed with pnpm 12.10.1 because the local install of the pinned 12.11.1 was broken.

```
transcript-grounding.unit.test.ts                        113 passed
transcript-grounding.test.ts                              15 passed
transcript-turn-media-references.test.ts                   5 passed
transcript.test.ts                                        44 passed
transcript.media-identity.test.ts                         14 passed
embedded-agent-subscribe.tools.media.test.ts               7 passed
embedded-agent-subscribe.tools.test.ts                    27 passed
attempt-session-runtime-prepare.test.ts                   11 passed
session-transcript-context.runtime.test.ts                 9 passed
media-reference.test.ts                                   12 passed
media-reference-comparison.test.ts                        13 passed, 1 skipped
session-upstream-monitor.test.ts                          25 passed
session-tool-result-guard.transcript-events.test.ts       18 passed
session-transcript-memory-read.test.ts                     8 passed
transcript.memory.test.ts                                  3 passed
session-history-readonly-reader.test.ts                   17 passed
session-transcript-readers.test.ts                        11 passed
session-transcript-readers.markers.test.ts                10 passed
                                                         362 passed, 0 failed
```

`openclaw-agent-execution-incognito.history.test.ts` is gone from `main` (#170712). The memory-actor recent-text route is covered by `session-transcript-memory-read.test.ts`, `transcript.memory.test.ts` and the actor case in `transcript-turn-media-references.test.ts`. The last five rows are `main`'s tests of the three reader backends.

`transcript-grounding.test.ts` > "bounds every retained entry and the complete replay prompt after grounding" failed 2 of 9 whole-file runs before the merge with `database is locked` while opening the state database (`openNativeStateDatabase` -> `requireRollbackJournalMode`); on the merge it passed 6 of 6 at load average 9 to 23. The new probe never runs in that test and reads no SQLite. Not changed. On the redesign, the file passed 5 of 5 whole-file runs. Two of those runs came before the type-only lint fixes.

`embedded-agent-subscribe.tools.media.test.ts` holds only this PR's cases now: main deleted the rest of that file (#158721, #160205, #166619). Its fixture now sets an empty runtime config snapshot. `main`'s session-history worker reads the prepared runtime config and throws `Runtime config is not prepared` without one.

Fail-before, pass-after, run with the new tests against the production files from before each fix:

- `1b81028477e` (tab/LF/CR in `file:` URLs): the 6 new matcher cases and the resolver-to-replay test fail. Without the fix, the three `file:` spellings replay verbatim even though `resolveInboundMediaReference` opens each of them to the real `media/inbound/x.png`. A prose-boundary control test passes both before and after. Mutating any one of the fix's three rules fails exactly the test that pins it.
- `b77491c03dd` (authorized path run-on and `~`): 7 new matcher cases fail, as does a resolver-to-replay test for two `~/...` spellings that `resolveInboundMediaReference` opens with `OPENCLAW_HOME` set to a temp dir. A control test for `~` spellings that reach no root passes both before and after.
- `9faa6bd04d4` (Windows drive roots): with `transcript-grounding.ts` from the merge commit, 11 of the 111 unit cases fail. Ten win32 spellings replay verbatim and `C:/Users/Bot/.openclaw/%6dedia/x.png` is redacted. Injected Windows groundings only; not run on Windows.
- `0ff83d79b6c` (provenance inside the single-snapshot reader). Each mutation was applied to the head and reverted. They were measured on the redesign before two type-only lint fixes.
  - Grounding skipped in `transcript-recent-grounding.ts`: 13 of 15 `transcript-grounding.test.ts` cases fail, and so do both channel-context cases in `embedded-agent-subscribe.tools.media.test.ts`.
  - Grounding kept, but `transcript.ts` not requesting `includeTurnMediaReferences`: the 6 grounding cases and 2 channel-context cases that need a trusted reference to survive fail.
  - The reader stopping at the limit instead of reading on to the oldest reply's turn start: 5 cases fail, 2 in `transcript-turn-media-references.test.ts` and 3 in `transcript-grounding.test.ts`.

  The two page-read tests from `ef8a251fe9a` are replaced:
  - "never lends a later same-turn result to a reply at a page boundary, before or after a write" reads the 251-row session, appends a turn and reads again.
  - "reads past the requested limit for a reply's provenance on an earlier page" puts the reply's image result 300 rows back in its own turn.
- `2d2b895f508` (joined names): with `transcript-grounding.ts`, `transcript-recent-grounding.ts` and `media-reference.ts` from `a2e8eca58cf`, the resolver-to-replay test "refuses an authorized reference the resolver joins onto another stored file" fails in 5 of 5 runs (the spellings replay verbatim although `resolveInboundMediaReference` opens `ok.png.fake` for each), and the unit case "keeps prose boundaries around file URLs and reports the names a resolver could join" fails. Both pass on the head; `ok.png<LF>next line` and a one-per-line path list stay verbatim.

Gates at `0ff83d79b6c`, `--base e69e34001fb5`. These pass:
- the line-cap, assertion-safety, SQLite worker, test-timeout-race and mock-export ratchets;
- `config:docs:check`, `plugins:inventory:check` and the deprecated-API guard;
- the history-reader import boundaries (`session-history-read.imports.test.ts`) and the PR-wrapper inventory (`eager-import-closure.test.ts`);
- tsgo core, src tests and root tests;
- oxfmt, and the repo's oxlint wrapper on the 22 changed files.

Two fail identically on `e69e34001fb5` alone, in files this PR does not touch: the max-lines ratchet (new suppressions in three `ui/` files) and the env-var budget (456 `OPENCLAW_*` names against 452). Not rerun at this head: the core tsgo graph boundary and the dead-export scan.

Grounding cost is linear in input size. An M4 Pro at load average 17 to 22, before the tab/LF/CR fix:

```

128 KiB token of comma-separated managed paths     3589.7 ms        8.8 ms
512 KiB token, same shape                         58704.0 ms       29.2 ms
128 KiB prose, no managed root                       13.5 ms       12.5 ms
128 KiB "/a /../" flood                              15.3 ms      120.0 ms
512 KiB "/a /../" flood                          not measured      491.0 ms
128 KiB "/managed/state/x y/../z " flood             13.9 ms      103.6 ms
```

The tab/LF/CR scan runs only when the text holds both `file:` and one of those characters. At `1b81028477e`, on a MacBook Air at load average 50 to 60 (read the ratios, not the absolute times), a `file:///managed/state/x y/../me<TAB>dia/x ` flood took 229/457/961/2182 ms before and 653/1281/2572/5211 ms after, at 64/128/256/512 KiB.

The extent flood test now redacts 16,000 comma-separated paths in one token (474 KiB) with a 10 s timeout as the assertion: 41-43 ms at the head, and a timeout at 46,351 ms with `reanchorToken` forced to discard the extent.

Runtime evidence, older. At `6876d24023832cd12ddb23b5a4036645e2242f7d`, a sanitized run used the production guarded writer, a persisted `SessionManager` transcript, the canonical SQLite projection and `mergeSessionTranscriptContext`, reusing one manager across an allowed and a denied run:

```json
{
  "sameManagerReused": true,
  "writerAuthorizationCandidateCount": 100000,
  "writerAuthorizationCandidateInspections": 64,
  "persisted": [
    { "runId": "run-allowed", "authorized": true },
    { "runId": "run-denied", "authorized": false }
  ],
  "firstRunTrustedReferenceSurvives": true,
  "secondRunStaleReferenceAbsent": true,
  "result": "PASS"
}
```

That run predates the current trust handoff and matcher.

Upgrade from v2026.9.9, on an M4 Pro with an isolated state dir and no Gateway. Phase 1 ran from the tag's source (`bcfc88812a35`), not the npm tarball, and wrote one session through that release's guarded `SessionManager`; v2026.9.9's own replay returned every path verbatim, a forged one included. Phase 2 ran on this branch merged with `main` `657f09fea181`, before the rule for runs followed by `/` and before the merge of `c30579e85091`, which moved the read onto `main`'s async page reader, in place on the same state dir, after the owner `openclaw doctor --fix` uses moved the agent database from schema 24 to 25 (a `main` change, #167932). Both phases were rerun after the merge, phase 2 on `ef8a251fe9a` merged with `main` `7b125134f386`, and every line below came out the same. Neither phase was rerun at `0ff83d79b6c`. Paths shortened to `<media>`:

```
schema 24 -> 25
rows equal to phase 1: true (11)
session entry equal to phase 1: true
replay of the v2026.9.9 rows:
  inspect the files
  exact <media>/inbound/exact.png; collision [unverified media reference removed]/generated/collision.png; core-named <media>/generated/core-named.png; forged [unverified media reference removed]/inbound/forged.png; joined [unverified media reference removed]/inbound/exact.png\t.fake
  and now?
  stale [unverified media reference removed]/inbound/exact.png
head run appended with only exec trusted; markers on its rows: exec true, music_generate false

replay of the head turn:
  head exact <media>/inbound/exact.png; head core-named [unverified media reference removed]/generated/core-named.png
```

No gateway has run at the current head. The live trust handoff, a plugin under a core tool name and newly revoked trust through channel-history publication are covered by in-process tests (`embedded-agent-subscribe.tools.media.test.ts`: `bounds and refreshes persisted media authority through channel context` and `denies media authority until the run hands over its trust set`) and by the head-written rows above. A production-boundary run needs a channel that merges session history into the next prompt and a mock provider that can be told which tools to call. QA Channel does not merge session history, and the QA Lab mock provider has no such control; QA Lab with Crabline Telegram plus a new mock-provider behavior, a fixture plugin and a scenario would do it, as a follow-up PR.

Not run locally: the full suite and a gateway.

Open for maintainers:

- Replay budgets: 32 KiB per entry and 128 KiB per read, channel replay only.
- Persisted authorization marker: additive. Transcripts without it replay under the existing core-name rule.
- Recent-text reader option and PR-wrapper inventory: `includeTurnMediaReferences` on `main`'s recent-text reader is off by default, and other readers' results are unchanged. The reader now eagerly imports `transcript-turn-media-references.ts`, which imports `embedded-agent-tool-media.ts`. So `scripts/pr-lib/wrapper-components.txt` gains 18 files: the collector, plus the 17 files of its eager import closure that the inventory lacked. One of those, `media-grounding-limits.ts`, was already missing before the redesign: at the merge commit `62dd1ca78a2` the inventory check failed on exactly that file, because this PR's `media-reference.ts` imports it.
- Port-bearing inbound URIs: `parseInboundMediaUri` now refuses `media://inbound:<port>/...`, a bare `media://inbound:/...` and empty userinfo. Non-empty userinfo was already refused on `main`. All in-tree writers use `media://inbound/${...}`, so only a hand-written or model-written form like these in an existing transcript stops resolving. No real transcripts were scanned.
- Worker runs: `src/worker/embedded-agent.runtime.ts` guards without a trust set. A worker's tool results persist without the marker and replay under the core-name rule, as all tool results do on `main`. Not changed here.
- Not covered: a name that continues across a boundary the resolver keeps in the name, such as a space, quote, NBSP, VT or FF (`ok.png .fake`), and a directory named the authorized file name plus a trailing tab or line break. The URL parser deletes only tab, LF and CR.

prs.title: feat: let plugin tools yield turns
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin tools can send work to an external interaction surface, but before this change they could only return a normal tool result. The agent loop could then continue in the same turn before the external callback arrived, which races native approval and form-card flows against the eventual user response.

## Why This Is Better Than The Current Behavior

This adds a narrow runtime control request on `AgentToolResult` and exposes `yieldToolResult(...)` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/tool-results`. After a plugin tool returns that result, OpenClaw retains the successful tool result and routes through the existing `sessions_yield` turn-handoff path. A later inbound event can then resume the same session.

Control is applied only after the complete `afterToolCall` finalization lifecycle. Hook-added and hook-replaced controls therefore affect the actual runtime action, and runtimes without a control handler fail explicitly instead of silently continuing.

Tools that may yield must declare both `canYield: true` and `executionMode: "sequential"`. Agent-core validates both declarations; the scheduler sees the sequential identity before starting the batch, so a successful yield aborts the turn before later sibling tools run. Only `canYield` tools remain model-visible and are excluded from Tool Search, Code Mode, and headless catalogs because those outer bridges cannot preserve the target tool's pre-execution scheduling identity. Existing non-yielding sequential tools retain their prior catalog behavior.

The implementation remains channel-agnostic. Existing tools and plugins are unchanged when they return no `control` field.

## User Impact

Plugin authors can implement native interaction tools, such as approval or form-card prompts, without racing the model loop against the user callback. Existing plugin tools do not need migration; only tools that opt into yield declare the new capability and sequential execution.

## Implementation

- Add `AgentToolResult.control` and the public `yieldToolResult(...)` helper.
- Add a host-owned finalized-result control seam in agent-core.
- Add the explicit `canYield` tool capability and preserve it through tool-definition adapters.
- Wire embedded OpenClaw sessions to the existing `sessions_yield` lifecycle.
- Reject unsupported controls and controls from tools missing either required declaration.
- Stop a sequential batch after yield so later side-effectful sibling tools never start.
- Keep only `canYield` tools on the direct execution surface; ordinary sequential tools remain catalog-eligible.

## Evidence

### Real external plugin runtime proof

Environment: macOS arm64, Node 22.23.1.

A standalone external plugin was loaded from its real manifest through `loadOpenClawPlugins`, registered and resolved `proof_ask_user`, imported `yieldToolResult` from the public Plugin SDK entrypoint, and executed through a real `Agent`. The first run yielded; the finalized successful tool result remained in the transcript; a later inbound prompt on the same Agent completed normally.

Redacted observed output:

```json
{
  "plugin": {
    "id": "yield-proof",
    "loaded": true,
    "registeredTools": ["proof_ask_user"],
    "resolvedTool": "proof_ask_user"
  },
  "finalizedResult": {
    "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "Question card sent." }],
    "details": {
      "status": "pending",
      "question": "Approve the deployment?",
      "cardId": "proof-card-1"
    },
    "control": {
      "type": "yield",
      "message": "Waiting for proof card answer"
    }
  },
  "runtime": {
    "sessionId": "proof-session-1",
    "yieldEvents": ["Waiting for proof card answer"],
    "yieldDetected": true,
    "modelCalls": 2,
    "retainedToolResult": {
      "toolName": "proof_ask_user",
      "details": { "status": "pending", "cardId": "proof-card-1" },
      "isError": false
    },
    "resumedAssistant": {
      "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "Answer accepted." }],
      "stopReason": "stop"
    }
  }
}
```

### Finalization, scheduling, compatibility, and resume coverage

- Agent-core tests prove controls added or replaced by `afterToolCall` are applied only after finalization.
- Agent-core rejects yield from tools missing `canYield` or sequential execution before invoking the runtime handler.
- Agent-core proves a valid yielding tool prevents a later side-effectful sibling from starting.
- Adapter tests prove `canYield` survives AgentTool → ToolDefinition → AgentTool conversion.
- Catalog tests prove only `canYield` tools remain direct across Tool Search and Code Mode, while ordinary sequential tools stay cataloged; headless catalog behavior is covered too.
- Embedded orchestration proves a yielded run reports `paused` / `end_turn`, releases the active session, and accepts a later inbound turn on the same session.

### Verification

- Scheduler TDD RED: run `29575710823` failed before the sequential guard existed.
- Scheduler TDD GREEN: run `29576120720` passed after the guard landed.
- Catalog scheduling TDD RED: run `29577281682`, job `87874669293`, failed before yield tools were kept direct.
- Compatibility TDD RED: run `29578570258`, job `87878675234`, failed when generic sequential tools still bypassed catalogs.
- Current-main rebase GREEN: exact head `16f0fa605fffee4861388077d31f7ee81cd1ae37` is rebased onto `main@9d2f5d4dbb639ecfcb95b6f5772895534f687691`; GitHub reports 87 successful jobs, 30 conditional skips, 0 failures, and 0 pending.
- `build-artifacts`, SDK declarations/surface checks, docs, lint/format, production types, test types, all selected Node shards, CodeQL, OpenGrep, and workflow sanity passed.
- GitHub reports the refreshed PR `MERGEABLE`; the rebased Plugin SDK module baselines, SDK surface budgets, core production types, and core test types pass on the exact head.

## Notes

Prepared with AI assistance.

## Linked Issue

Closes #109761

## Codex and Copilot Unsupported-Runtime Compatibility Proof

Direct upstream inspection was completed against `openai/codex` `main@bb5054fe47abe73ecbbd454751066a28c89f4bb9`:

- Codex app-server defines `DynamicToolCallResponse` with exactly `contentItems` and `success`; it has no result-control, yield, or terminate field: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/bb5054fe47abe73ecbbd454751066a28c89f4bb9/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/item.rs
- Its response handler deserializes that closed shape and submits `Op::DynamicToolResponse` back to the active conversation; there is no yield or turn-termination branch: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/bb5054fe47abe73ecbbd454751066a28c89f4bb9/codex-rs/app-server/src/dynamic_tools.rs
- The upstream round-trip test projects the response into `function_call_output` and then waits for `turn/completed`: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/bb5054fe47abe73ecbbd454751066a28c89f4bb9/codex-rs/app-server/tests/suite/v2/dynamic_tools.rs

Codex app-server therefore cannot faithfully carry an OpenClaw result control today. This branch fails explicitly with `Tool requested yield, but yield is not supported in this runtime` instead of silently discarding the control or attempting an unsupported transition. Focused exact-head coverage is in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/09666f330b473e12ef4cb85d985e7ce16b99fff9/extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.test.ts#L441 and the equivalent Copilot bridge coverage is in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/09666f330b473e12ef4cb85d985e7ce16b99fff9/extensions/copilot/src/tool-bridge.test.ts#L1477.

Current exact head `09666f330b473e12ef4cb85d985e7ce16b99fff9` has 135 completed checks: 90 successful, 38 conditional skips, 6 superseded cancellations, 1 neutral, 0 failures, and 0 pending.

prs.title: fix(zalouser): sanitize outbound tool traces
prs.body:
## Merge Brief

- **Problem / value:** Zalo Personal's custom monitor callback bypasses its standard adapter, so a `message_sending` hook can reintroduce internal tool traces immediately before transport. This patch keeps recipient text and captions clean while preserving configured Markdown-table rendering.
- **Relevance:** Independent P1/security report #90684 tracks this leakage class. Merged #112621 sanitizes the standard adapter only; current `main` still leaves this distinct callback seam open.
- **Smallest complete fix / review map:** Keep configured table conversion in `delivery.preparePayload`, where durable final delivery sees it, and sanitize only the effective post-hook payload in the custom callback. Scope is 4 files, `+76/-20`: two small helpers, two focused regressions, and the boundary wiring.
- **Risk / proof:** Risk is limited to ordering between two existing transforms. Exact head `41e305a4a4f4fd73973bac5858b07766db1791f9`; full Zalouser `317/317`; production/test type graphs, changed-scope format/lint/diff checks, and the deterministic pre-PR gate are green. ClawSweeper Revision 30's durable-table P1 is covered by the new regression.
- **External proof limit:** Authenticated recipient-visible transport is `blocked_external` because no safe configured account/recipient route exists. Exact-head tests reach both lifecycle boundaries; no live send is claimed.
- **Non-goals:** Standard adapter, sanitizer parser dialects, Zalo Bot, authentication, configuration schema, and protocol changes.
- **Maintainer ask:** Please apply `no-stale` while authenticated recipient proof is coordinated; the assigned-PR age clock otherwise ignores substantive updates.

## What Problem This Solves

Zalo Personal's custom inbound-reply path in `monitor.ts` can deliver a post-hook payload without passing through the standard outbound adapter. That leaves one route for compact tool-failure lines or tool XML to reach recipients. The repair must also preserve `channels.zalouser.markdown.tables` for final replies handled by durable delivery. Related: #90684.

## User Impact

Recipients get intended assistant text and media without internal tool-trace scaffolding, while existing table preferences such as `markdown.tables: "bullets"` continue to apply to durable final replies. Ordinary prose, captions, chunking, and media delivery remain unchanged; users have no migration step.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `delivery.preparePayload` owns configured table conversion before the lifecycle can return through durable delivery.
- The private custom callback owns sanitization after `message_sending`, so a supported hook cannot reintroduce internal traces.
- Merged #112621 covers the standard adapter only; this remains a narrow, distinct callback repair.

## Evidence

- Exact signed candidate head: `41e305a4a4f4fd73973bac5858b07766db1791f9` on frozen maintenance base `b464d49019995ec229595bdcbba9d3b61ff035f7`.
- `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/zalouser`: `33` files and `317/317` tests passing, including configured bullet-table preparation before durable delivery and post-hook trace sanitization at custom delivery.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`: passing.
- Changed Zalouser scope passes type-aware Oxlint, Oxfmt, and `git diff --check`. Repository-wide extension lint's only failure is unchanged frozen-base debt in `extensions/amazon-bedrock/stream.runtime.test.ts` (`max-lines`).
- Deterministic `openclaw-pre-pr.sh` gate: passed for frozen base `b464d49019995ec229595bdcbba9d3b61ff035f7`, exact head `41e305a4a4f4fd73973bac5858b07766db1791f9`, and merge tree `1d2e0ad6dc09fd07dfa21423c38602b80e92ae9d`.
- Current-`main` negative control: the custom monitor callback still resolves and delivers the post-hook payload directly. This head restores pre-durable table preparation and sanitizes immediately before custom text/caption resolution.
- Remaining proof state is `blocked_external`, not a claimed live pass: authenticated recipient-visible proof still requires a safe Zalo Personal account and recipient route.

AI-assisted change, manually reviewed and validated.

prs.title: fix(feishu): add video preview covers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes videos sent through Feishu appearing without a preview cover.

## User Impact

Outgoing videos gain a preview when cover preparation succeeds. Existing caption recovery, inline/thread replies, allowed reply fallback, stickers, and send-authority checks are preserved. Cover failures leave the video-only send available.

## Why This Change Was Made

Refreshes the PR onto pinned upstream main `07e9a251942099b22f16813e36ada02f2b76ab91` and carries optional `image_key` alongside `file_key` through the current shared `sendUploadedMediaFeishu` sender. It retains the upstream reply/direct implementation rather than restoring the retired image/file helpers.

The [Feishu media-message contract](https://open.feishu.cn/document/server-docs/im-v1/message-content-description/create_json?lang=zh-CN), reconfirmed September 9, documents the optional cover field. Extraction and upload each retain a 5-second deadline; the cover client also uses a 5-second HTTP timeout. JPEG extraction caps dimensions at 1280×720, and output validation enforces the smaller of configured `mediaMaxMb` and Feishu's 10 MiB image limit. Missing ffmpeg, extraction errors, oversized/empty output, upload rejection, or upload timeout fall back to video only.

## Current Integration Refresh (2026-10-08)

This candidate integrates pinned upstream main `1aa96aeb45311aaa49612c1bfb35feb0da9d3d47` at published head `c572b2739daa75793deaec3a10c275d5161e51ab`. It preserves optional `image_key` forwarding through the shared sender, caption/reply behavior, the 5-second bounds, `mediaMaxMb` and Feishu's 10 MiB cover cap, and video-only fallback. Image, audio, and sticker routes remain on their existing path.

The aggregate changed-check wrapper could not initialize its default `pnpm dlx` cache; the exact production, full-tree, and scripts dead-export scans were rerun with a task-local cache and passed.

An exact normalized proposal-line comparison found the additions byte-identical; the only removed-line difference is an upstream duration-probe warning string. No new autoreview was run because this refresh adds no new Feishu semantics.
- GitHub reports the open, non-draft PR as mergeable.

## Previous Integration Refresh (2026-10-07)

## Previous Published Revision Evidence

The following evidence is retained from the previously published head `9550ae873bb7165cc519bef19b7f7f975d08c29c`; it is historical context and does not replace verification of the current candidate above.

## Evidence

prs.title: fix(session): defer flushPendingToolResults by one event-loop tick
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the Feishu (and any channel) "missing tool result in session history" race (#84134): when an agent calls a tool whose HTTP response is still in-flight at idle, the runner flushed a synthetic error before the real result landed.

The earlier one-tick `setImmediate` defer (prior PR head `db2e0ab`) only let results already queued in that event-loop phase win; a real HTTP result settling on a later turn was still replaced with a synthetic error. ClawSweeper correctly flagged this as a heuristic, not a settlement guarantee (P1: "Replace the one-turn heuristic with a settlement barrier").

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the fixed event-loop delay with a **runner-owned settlement barrier**:

- The tool-result guard already owns pending tool-call tracking (`trackToolCalls` / `delete(id)`). Each `delete(id)` is the synchronous signal that a real result just landed.
- This change promise-ifies that signal: each pending id now carries a deferred that resolves when its real result is appended (`session-tool-result-state.ts`).
- Before flushing synthetics, `flushPendingToolResultsAfterIdle` awaits the guard-owned settlement (`waitForPendingToolResultSettlement`) or a timeout — not a guessed tick count.

A real in-flight HTTP result that settles after the agent reports idle now wins over the synthetic flush. A result that never settles is still flushed once the timeout elapses (fail-safe preserved).

The settlement is skipped when idle itself timed out (agent stuck) so cleanup does not double-wait before the fail-safe flush. The abort path (`timeoutMs <= 0`) still flushes immediately.

This is prevention at the flush boundary; #84419 (transcript repair) remains a complementary after-the-fact mitigation for already-persisted transcripts.

## User Impact

Feishu users who saw "Something went wrong" after the agent used the message tool should now receive the real tool result. The fix applies to all channels — any tool call with a pending HTTP response benefits from the settlement barrier.

## Evidence

### Real Behavior Proof

**Behavior addressed**: `flushPendingToolResultsAfterIdle` now awaits the guard-owned tool-result write completion before flushing synthetics, so a real in-flight result that settles after idle wins over the synthetic error.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node v24.15.0, branch `fix/feishu-message-tool-result-84134-v2` @ commit `fc66e80ac8d`

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner.guard.waitforidle-before-flush.test.ts --run
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/session-tool-result-guard.test.ts --run
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.subscription-cleanup.test.ts --run
pnpm tsgo:core
```

**Evidence after fix**:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner.guard.waitforidle-before-flush.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  8 passed (8)
     ✓ waits for idle so real tool results can land before flush
     ✓ flushes pending tool call after timeout when idle never resolves
     ✓ flushes pending on cleanup timeout instead of leaving orphaned tool calls
     ✓ clears timeout handle when waitForIdle resolves first
     ✓ clamps oversized idle wait timeouts before scheduling
     ✓ immediately flushes pending tool results without waiting when timeoutMs is 0 or less
     ✓ settlement barrier awaits a real result that lands in a later event-loop turn
     ✓ flushes synthetic when a pending result never settles within the timeout

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/session-tool-result-guard.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  38 passed (38)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.subscription-cleanup.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)

$ pnpm tsgo:core
tsgo:core exit=0  (core source typecheck clean)
```

**Discriminating proof — the rejected one-tick `setImmediate` heuristic fails this regression**:

To prove the regression actually locks the multi-turn race (not just microtasks in the current turn), the implementation was temporarily reverted to the prior `await new Promise(r => setImmediate(r))` defer and the same suite re-run. The settlement-barrier regression then fails exactly as the rejected heuristic would in production:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner.guard.waitforidle-before-flush.test.ts --run
     × settlement barrier awaits a real result that lands in a later event-loop turn 10ms
 FAIL  src/agents/.../waitforidle-before-flush.test.ts > settlement barrier awaits a real result that lands in a later event-loop turn
AssertionError: expected true not to be true // Object.is equality
    253|     expect((messages[1] as { isError?: boolean }).isError).not.toBe(true)
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  2 failed | 6 passed (8)
```

Under the one-tick defer, the real result lands in the second check phase (nested `setImmediate`) but the defer's flush runs in the first check phase and injects a synthetic error (`isError: true`) before the result arrives. Under the settlement barrier, the guard awaits its own `delete(id)` signal, so the real result wins. The implementation was restored to the settlement barrier afterward (working tree clean).

**Observed result after fix**:

- The "later event-loop turn" regression (nested `setImmediate`) proves a real result landing in the second check phase is NOT overwritten by a synthetic — and the discriminating run above proves the prior one-tick `setImmediate` heuristic fails this exact scenario, which is the behavior gap ClawSweeper flagged.
- The "never settles" regression proves the fail-safe still flushes a synthetic once the timeout elapses, keeping the transcript structurally valid for provider replay.
- 38 guard tests + 6 cleanup caller tests pass — no regression in `flushPendingToolResults`, `guardedAppend`, or the abort/cleanup paths.
- Core source typecheck passes (`tsgo:core` exit 0).

**What was not tested**: Live Feishu DM end-to-end with real CardKit streaming; production agent-runner trace. A live run requires Feishu channel credentials and a running gateway, which are not available in this contributor environment. The settlement barrier is guard-owned and the discriminating proof above exercises the exact flush boundary (real result arriving after idle via a later event-loop turn) that a live Feishu HTTP response would trigger through the same `pendingState.delete(id)` → deferred resolve path.

## Root Cause

`flushPendingToolResultsAfterIdle` called `flushPendingToolResults()` immediately after `waitForAgentIdleBestEffort` resolved. When a tool call (e.g. Feishu message tool) had an in-flight HTTP response, the agent could report idle before the response callback fired. The immediate flush saw the still-pending tool call and injected a synthetic error; the real result then arrived but the synthetic was already persisted.

A one-tick `setImmediate` defer only drains callbacks already queued in that event-loop phase — a real HTTP result settling on a later turn was still pending and received a synthetic error. The settlement barrier awaits the guard-owned `delete(id)` signal instead, so any valid result that lands within the timeout wins.

## Regression Test Plan

Target: `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner.guard.waitforidle-before-flush.test.ts`
Added scenarios:

- `settlement barrier awaits a real result that lands in a later event-loop turn` — real result appended in the second check phase (nested `setImmediate`) still wins (no synthetic). A one-tick `setImmediate` defer fails this regression (proven by the discriminating run above), which is the exact behavior gap ClawSweeper flagged.
- `flushes synthetic when a pending result never settles within the timeout` — fail-safe: real result never lands → timeout → synthetic injected.

Existing scenarios preserved (idle wait race, idle timeout, cleanup timeout, timer clamp, abort `timeoutMs <= 0`).

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Feishu (and all channel) users who previously saw "Something went wrong" after the agent used a tool with a pending HTTP response should now receive the real tool result. Non-abort cleanup adds up to one settlement-timeout wait when results are genuinely in-flight; the abort path is unchanged.

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- New/changed network calls? No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: settlement barrier waits for a multi-turn-delayed real result; fail-safe synthetic on never-settling result; all existing guard + cleanup tests unaffected; core typecheck clean.
- Edge cases checked: abort path (`timeoutMs=0`) skips settlement and flushes immediately; idle-timeout path skips settlement (agent stuck) to avoid double-wait; no-pending path returns immediately.
- What you did NOT verify: Live Feishu DM end-to-end with CardKit streaming.

## Best-fix Verdict

- Best fix: Yes — the settlement barrier is the runner-owned completion boundary ClawSweeper asked for. It awaits the guard's own `delete(id)` signal (the exact point a real result lands) rather than a scheduling guess, with a defined timeout/cancellation path.
- Refactor needed: No
- Alternative considered: keeping the one-tick `setImmediate` defer (rejected — fails any result settling after one event-loop phase, which is the bug); adding a guard in `guardedAppend` (unreachable — toolResult branch returns before the flush check); deferring in the Feishu dispatch layer (channel-specific fix that leaves the race for every other channel).

## AI Assistance 🤖 (required for AI-assisted PRs)

AI-assisted: Yes
AI model: GLM-5.2
Human confirmed understanding of code changes: Yes

## Change Type (select all)

- Bug fix
- Refactor required for the fix

## Scope (select all)

- Gateway / orchestration
- Skills / tool execution
- API / contracts — Session tool result guard

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #84134 — Feishu message tool "missing tool result" regression
- Related: #84419 (transcript repair dedup mitigation), #84708 (replay poison recovery)

## Risks and Mitigations

- Highest-risk area: the settlement barrier adds up to one `timeoutMs` wait to non-abort cleanup when results are genuinely in-flight. For the abort path (`timeoutMs=0`) and the idle-timeout path, settlement is skipped, preserving immediate flush behavior.
- Mitigation: the settlement only awaits already-tracked pending ids; a real result resolves its deferred immediately (microsecond-scale), so the timeout is a ceiling, not the common case. `clear()` resolves all deferreds to avoid dangling promises.
- Compatibility impact: None — the `flushPendingToolResultsAfterIdle` signature is unchanged; `waitForPendingToolResultSettlement` is optional and no-op when absent.
