prs.title: fix(cron): expose flat cron job fields and normalize malformed tool args
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Less-capable models (tested locally with Gemma 4 26B and Qwen3.8 27B) often flatten cron `add`/`update` arguments beside `action`, or send a malformed `job` string. Validation then fails and the automation is never created or changed.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Advertises ten flat fields for ordinary add/update: `name`, `enabled`, `sessionTarget`, `at`, `everyMs`, `expr`, `tz`, `message`, `toolsAllow`, `text`. The prompt says to prefer them only when nested objects are unreliable.
- `prepareCronToolArguments` turns flat input into the existing nested job before schema validation. The Gateway still receives one canonical job format.
- Nested jobs keep main's boundary (#12124). A nonempty `job` takes main's route unchanged, including normalization of stale schedule/payload fields. Flat recovery runs only when `job` is missing, malformed, or `{}`. Nested and flat fields are never merged.

Deliberate differences from main:

- **Mixed input is rejected.** A nonempty `job` plus any advertised flat field except `name` fails before the Gateway call. Main silently ignored these, which would drop a `tz`, `toolsAllow`, `enabled` or `sessionTarget` and change timing or tool access without telling the user. Blank filler strings are ignored, and `name` beside `job` is still ignored as on main.
- **Text-only updates keep the stored type.** Flat or nested, a text-only update keeps the stored reminder/task kind. On main, a nested `{payload:{text}}` update turns a task into a reminder. If the stored kind is unreadable or incompatible, the update errors without writing.
- **Flat guards.** Only one of `at`/`everyMs`/`expr`; `tz` only with `expr`; `text` or `message`, not both (unless identical).
- **Empty wrapper.** `job: {}` with no flat content fails with `job required` before the Gateway call.

## User Impact

Weaker models can create and edit automations with flat fields. Existing nested callers are unaffected apart from the two deliberate differences above.

Maintainer decision still open: whether to adopt the flat form as a supported model-facing contract. ClawSweeper recommends adopting the narrow flat form.

## Evidence

- **Real scheduled run (attached):** a flat-created job with `payload.toolsAllow:["read"]`. `tools/list` showed only `read`, the allowed `read` succeeded, and a raw `write` call was denied (`Tool not available: write`) with the sentinel file still absent.
- **Regression tests (`cron-tool.flat-params.test.ts`), through prepare → validate → execute:**
  - ClawSweeper's nested reminder with `tz:""` inside the `at` schedule
  - main's `STALE_AT_SCHEDULE` fixture
  - nested leftover `text`/`message`
  - blank filler fields beside `job`
  - mixed-input rejection
  - end-to-end text-only updates for stored task and reminder jobs, flat and nested
  - every prompt example run verbatim (the test also checks each example appears in the tool description)
- **Test results:** on this head (merged with main `fa86f99a19`), `cron-tool.flat-params`, `cron-tool.schema`, `cron-tool` and `src/cron/normalize` pass, 218/218. On the previous head `56e8b31ce653`, ClawSweeper's nested reminder fails with `tz needs expr`; the new test reproduces that input.
- **Prompt snapshots:** regenerated on Linux for the updated cron tool description.

Related: #3569, #64721, #12124, #121645

[create.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33535971/create.json)
[run.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33535973/run.json)
[scheduled-run-toolsallow-read-proof.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33535976/scheduled-run-toolsallow-read-proof.json)

*Everything below is a chronological log of earlier review cycles, kept for history purposes.
Where it conflicts with this summary (e.g. field counts, head SHAs, test totals) this summary
is current as at the time of writing*




PR #97339 ClawSweeper proof

## Identity

- Main: `7ff455860b90a1c63070952cf1cbd190b6a8e22b`
- PR source: `LinuxMum/openclaw` `fix/cron-tool-schema-fix` at `6c5069e1cdc573df86d5099455482594663d7d04`
- PR delta base: `74db4da9de9f042215ac5bdf1966987daacc020f`
- Built staged tree: `78baf2562a7f6f2d09a0f51ae68f1d6202aac65c`
- Build: `qaRuntime` passed

## Main changes affecting PR files

- `src/agents/tools/cron-tool.ts`: kept main `CronToolOutputSchema` import plus PR `prepareCronToolArguments` import.
- `config/assertion-safety-baseline.txt`: updated to current counts: `cron-tool.ts 9`, `dashboard-tool.ts 2`.
- Prompt snapshots conflicted; not regenerated. Main snapshots were kept only for this rehearsal build.

## Proof achieved

- raw MCP `tools/call` to `cron` using flat fields created job `2bf5e1a0-1ab6-4651-9288-6fcfd8ddad4d` with initial `payload.toolsAllow:["automations"]`, `sessionTarget:"isolated"`, and account scheduled-tool policy.

- real scheduled restricted run through the genuine Gemini CLI package tree:

- allowlist: `payload.toolsAllow:["read"]`
- `tools/list`: only `read`
- allowed `read`: succeeded
- raw omitted `write` call: denied with `isError:true`, `Tool not available: write`
- sentinel: `proof/DENIED-WRITE-SENTINEL.txt` remained absent

This proves final-boundary denial for a scheduled restricted run: an omitted raw MCP tool call was denied and had no side effect.

## Remaining gap

Exact scheduled proof with `payload.toolsAllow:["automations"]` did not complete. 

Finding: the genuine Gemini package passes durable executable binding, but `toolsAllow:["automations"]`/`["cron"]` materializes a non-usable OpenClaw MCP settings entry, however `toolsAllow:["read"]` materializes and proves the denial boundary.

Related: #3569 
Related: #64721

## Current status as at 2026-09-04

Summarised from the below PR body to save reading time:

**What this adds:** ten flat top-level fields to assist lower capability models usable for 
`add`/`update` - `name`, `enabled`, `sessionTarget`, `at`, `everyMs`, `expr`, `tz`, `message`, `toolsAllow`, and 
`text` (previously documented for `wake` only). Nine are new properties: `text` is existing, newly
documented for add/update. This set has narrowed since the PR opened as earlier revisions
advertised fourteen fields, several of which became unnecessary as cron changed in main.
The nested `job` form is unchanged and still works

**Scope:** ten files, all under `src/agents/tools/` plus regenerated prompt snapshots.
Flat input is canonicalised into the existing nested job before dispatch

**Head `6c5069e1cd`:** `cron-tool.flat-params.test.ts` 41/41 green in CI, including creator
capability capping for both an allowed and an unavailable tool. The only red lane is
`control-ui-performance`, a repo-wide Control UI (this PR changes no UI code)

**Local models used for testing.** Local models Gemma 4 26B Q5 K_S and more recently Qwen3.8 
27B Q5 K_S (Llama.cpp) were used as test subjects for the model-facing schema in my
live Openclaw

**Open items:** maintainer review - whether to adopt the flat contract as a supported
model-facing form


---

## What Problem This Solves

`src/agents/tools/cron-tool.ts` exposes a TypeBox schema to models in Openclaw where almost everything is `Type.Optional`. However the contract is enforced downstream in `normalize.ts` and `persisted-shape.ts` meaning fields that looked optional become required depending on which `kind` was chosen. The code says at ln 54–55:

> "Spell out job/patch properties for model-facing schema; runtime validation still happens in
> normalizeCronJob* to avoid nested union schemas."

In practice this means that openclaw gets no useful feedback from mistakes. Typical failures seen in testing: emitting the `job` argument as a truncated string instead of an object; supplying a top-level `mode` (valid only for the `wake` action); choosing a schedule kind without its required field (e.g. `kind: "cron"` with no `expr`, or omitting `payload.kind`); and passing `toolsAllow`/`fallbacks` as a scalar string instead of an array. Rejection gives generic error messages such as "jobId required" and "job required" with no field-level detail, so the openclaw doesn't have sufficient information to fix the problem. 

## Why This Change Was Made

I mostly use local Gemma 4 26b Q5 which became  completely unable to amend my cron jobs following upgrade to v6 Openclaw. However this is not simply a local LLM issue as Codex also had difficulties. Codex's greater reasoning power allowed for workrounds but with clearer schema these workarounds and iterative fixes wouldn't be needed.

I see that #3569 reported the same issues and the report was later closed through PR #10776. But #10776 did not address the TypeBox schema. @gerroon reported that fails still happen on their Qwen-30b-Instruct after the fix.

Also #64721 reports the same kind of problem: `payload.model`, `payload.timeoutSeconds`,
`payload.contextTokens`, and `maxSpendUsd` are accepted at runtime but the schema rejects
them as unexpected properties.

 Fix could be with a discriminated union, making the model reason about nested conditional types. However my concern is that lower-reasoning local LLMs will not manage this reasoning adequately.

Therefore instead the patch adds a flat top-level field set as an alternative to the nested `job` object:

| Field           | Type    | Notes                                          |
| --------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `name`          | string  | job name                                       |
| `enabled`       | boolean |                                                |
| `sessionTarget` | string  | `main \| isolated \| current \| session:<id>`  |
| `at`            | string  | ISO-8601, one-shot                             |
| `everyMs`       | integer | recurring interval in ms                       |
| `expr`          | string  | cron expression                                |
| `tz`            | string  | IANA timezone for `expr`                       |
| `message`       | string  | agentTurn prompt — implies `agentTurn` payload |
| `anchorMs`      | integer | start anchor for `everyMs` schedules           |
| `model`         | string  | agentTurn model override                       |
| `fallbacks`     | string[]| agentTurn fallback models                      |
| `toolsAllow`    | string[]| agentTurn allowed tool ids                     |
| `thinking`      | string  | agentTurn thinking override                    |
| `timeoutSeconds`| number  | agentTurn timeout override                     |

The canonicalizer (`cron-tool-canonicalize.ts`) infers `schedule.kind` and `payload.kind` from whichever fields are present, so the model never has to deal with the nested union. Also
descriptions for `text` (implies `systemEvent`) and `mode` (wake only, not delivery mode)
have been tightened up.

The implementation now also normalises scalar toolsAllow / fallbacks into arrays and reconstructs job / patch from recoverable flat fields when the request is clearly a cron add/update call.  This deals with an issue found in testing where openclaw incorrectly tries toolsAllow as a scalar string, or emits a malformed non-object job / patch alongside flat fields.  

## User Impact

Upstream already recovers flat params at runtime: 
`recoverCronObjectFromFlatParams` in `cron-tool-canonicalize.ts` (with
`CRON_FLAT_PAYLOAD_KEYS` / `CRON_FLAT_SCHEDULE_KEYS`)

The patch simply exposes in the model-facing schema what the runtime already accepts but doesn't show. Note the nested `job` form still works also.  There is no negative user impact to the fix.

## Evidence

Tested on OpenClaw gateway version 2026.6.10
OS: Linux Mint 22.3 (Zena)
Kernel: Linux 6.17.0-23-generic (x86_64)
LLMs used for testing: Local Gemma 4 26b Q5 (llama.cpp); openai/gpt-5.4
Tests designed and run by: Claude (Anthropic Claude Opus 4.8); OpenAI Codex (gpt-5.4)

Focused validation on `fix/cron-tool-schema-fix` (`~/code/openclaw-main`) currently passes for the actual patch surface:

- `corepack pnpm test src/agents/tools/cron-tool.schema.test.ts src/agents/tools/cron-tool.test.ts`
  - schema shard: `20 passed`
  - agents shard: `135 passed`

These tests cover:

- flat-field exposure in the model-facing cron schema
- canonicalization of malformed flat `toolsAllow` / `fallbacks`
- synthesis of `job` / `patch` from recoverable flat arguments
- the drift guard that ensures any advertised flat field is still recoverable by the canonicalizer

Earlier branch testing also included:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/cron-tool.schema.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/cron-tool.test.ts`
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test`

Live installed testing on patched OpenClaw 2026.6.10 also succeeded in creating disposable cron jobs through the flat-field interface, confirming the path works in a real installed gateway and not only in unit tests.

This four-file branch is green on the patch-local validation that actually exercises the cron-tool
change. The remaining PR-guide blockers are upstream baseline failures outside this patch scope.

Current upstream-baseline validation also shows:

- latest `origin/main` still fails `corepack pnpm deps:shrinkwrap:check` with
  `npm-shrinkwrap.json is stale. Run pnpm deps:shrinkwrap:generate.`
- clean `origin/main` is also currently red in unrelated test areas, including
  `src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts` and `src/media-understanding/image.test.ts`
  (reported for completeness only)

So the branch is green for the cron-tool patch itself, while the remaining `check` / full-suite
`test` reds are upstream, pre-existing, and unrelated to this four-file change. codex review --base origin/main stated the patch appears to correctly expose the flat cron fields and normalize them before validation without introducing a concrete regression in the touched surfaces.

## Update 2026-08-18 

The sections above are kept for history. Current state and evidence requested by ClawSweeper below.

### Current flat contract (10 fields) 

As per my https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/97339#issuecomment-5310292373 below, the advertised flat top-level contract is now deliberately limited to ten fields:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | Job name |
| `enabled` | boolean | Enabled state for add/update |
| `sessionTarget` | string | `main`, `isolated`, `current`, or `session:<id>` |
| `at` | string | One-shot ISO-8601 schedule |
| `everyMs` | integer | Recurring interval in milliseconds |
| `expr` | string | Cron expression |
| `tz` | string | IANA timezone used with `expr` |
| `message` | string | `agentTurn` prompt; implies an `agentTurn` payload |
| `text` | string | `systemEvent` text; implies a `systemEvent` payload |
| `toolsAllow` | string[] | `agentTurn` tool allowlist, e.g. `["read"]` |

- An add requires exactly one of `at`, `everyMs`, or `expr`. Updates remain partial jobs under main's unified API.
- The nested `job` form remains supported and takes precedence if both nested and flat forms are supplied.
- Earlier flat aliases for pacing, triggers, streams, model routing, fallbacks, thinking, timeout, and anchoring were removed; those advanced settings remain available through the nested `job` contract.

### Codex harness

This PR changes no `openai/codex` source or Codex harness/runtime code. The change runs end-to-end on an installed build using the OpenClaw Codex harness (noted in my https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/97339#issuecomment-5317476910 below)

### Mode invariant (addressed ClawSweeper P2)

Top-level `mode` is wake-only. `prepareCronToolArguments` now rejects a top-level `mode` on `action="add"` and `action="update"` (including when a nested `job` is present) before any Gateway write, and returns guidance to remove the field. This replaces the earlier guard that only rejected `mode` when no nested job was supplied, that dropped `mode` silently on the nested path.

### Evidence (final head `18cdfb2`)

```
node --import tsx - <<'EOF'
import { createCronTool } from "./src/agents/tools/cron-tool.ts";
const prep = createCronTool().prepareArguments;
console.log("[1] flat:", JSON.stringify(prep({ action:"add", name:"REPORT", everyMs:3_600_000, message:"status summary" }).job));
for (const c of [
  { action:"add", mode:"now", job:{ schedule:{ kind:"every", everyMs:300_000 }, payload:{ message:"x" } } },
  { action:"update", id:"job-1", mode:"now", job:{ enabled:false } },
]) { try { prep(c); console.log("NO THROW"); } catch (e) { console.log("reject:", e.message); } }
EOF
```

Output:

```
[1] FLAT add {name,everyMs,message} -> prepared.job =
    {"name":"REPORT","schedule":{"everyMs":3600000,"kind":"every"},"payload":{"message":"status summary","kind":"agentTurn"}}
[2] NESTED add + top-level mode -> REJECTED: Remove the top-level "mode" field and retry. "mode" is only valid for action="wake".
[3] UPDATE + top-level mode -> REJECTED: Remove the top-level "mode" field and retry. "mode" is only valid for action="wake".
```

- [1] confirms flat-field recovery: a low-capability-model shorthand call (`name`/`everyMs`/`message`, no nested structure) is prepared into the canonical nested `job` (`schedule.kind="every"`, `payload.kind="agentTurn"`).
- [2]/[3] confirm the wake-only `mode` guard rejects a top-level `mode` on both `add` and `update`, including with a nested `job` present.

A live gateway session where the model (local Gemma as before) emitted a top-level `mode` on an `add`; the Gateway returned the rejection end-to-end with head `18cdfb2`'s exact message, and no job was created:

```
MODEL   -> automations { action:"add", mode:"now", name:"MODETEST-1", … }
GATEWAY -> isError=true : Remove the top-level "mode" field and retry. "mode" is only valid for action="wake".
```


## Update — 2026-08-19

Resynced onto current `main` and closed the last flat-schedule invariant. `prepareCronToolArguments` now rejects, before canonicalization, an `add` that supplies more than one schedule field (`at` / `atMs` / `everyMs` / `every` / `expr` / `cron`), or a bare `tz` without `expr`. Schedule ambiguity is rejected because a wrong schedule fails invisibly and time-shifted; payload conflicts (`message`/`text`, `toolsAllow`) stay recoverable by documented precedence.  Rejecting these would negatively impact the low-capability-model tolerance this contract exists for.

Verified live on my installed openclaw (v2026.8.1-beta.2 carrying the PR97339 fixes, local Gemma model as before):

```
add (flat)        -> FLATLIFE-1 created
get               -> persisted: schedule {everyMs:3600000, kind:"every"}, payload {kind:"agentTurn", …}
update (flat)     -> everyMs -> 7200000; get confirms persisted
add everyMs+expr  -> error: "A cron add takes exactly one schedule field; received everyMs, expr…"; list -> no job created
add expr+tz       -> created (a single schedule + tz is valid; only orphan tz rejects)
cleanup           -> FLATLIFE-1 removed
```

`cron-tool.flat-params.test.ts` adds regression tests for schedule-conflict rejection, `tz`-without-`expr`, and the deliberate payload-conflict tolerance; all cron suites pass.

# Update — 2026-09-03: mode-guard proof

The earlier evidence is retained above for history. This update addresses the
current ClawSweeper proof request after the final resync at head
`92d5db6f333bad2a02cd6a1df1bdaea458adf9b8`.

## Live testing

The live run used my installed build based on upstream tag `v2026.9.1-beta.1` at
`1d96e5aee2d49cde999ed055eda113e2523a7b5c` and has the updated PR #97339
mode/recovery implementation folded into it. The local model was
**Qwen 3.8 27B Q5_K_S**. I supplied each case separately through the installed
OpenClaw desktop UI and let the model call the real `automations` tool; these
were not direct calls to a mocked tool.

The tested `prepareCronToolArguments` mode/recovery block is the same block now
present at the current PR head. 

At the exact PR head, the focused `cron-tool.flat-params.test.ts` and
`cron-tool.schema.test.ts` suites pass. The flat-stream regression test covers
both `mode:"line"` and `mode:"match"`; for each mode it asserts that:

- recovery produces `job.schedule.kind="stream"` with the mode preserved;
- the wake-only top-level `mode` is removed before validation; and
- execution reaches `cron.add` with the recovered stream schedule.

The rejection cases also assert that nested or non-stream top-level modes throw
the actionable wake-only error and that the Gateway mock is not called.

## Telegram

This PR changes the transport-independent `automations` tool schema and cron
argument-preparation path. It changes no Telegram source, Telegram parsing,
channel routing, or delivery code.

After any chat transport has delivered a prompt to the agent, the relevant
path is the same:

```text
agent/model -> automations tool schema and argument preparation -> Gateway cron.add
```

The installed Control UI run crosses that complete affected path: a real model
emitted the tool arguments, OpenClaw prepared and validated them, and the real
Gateway either persisted the canonical job or returned the visible error.
Starting the same prompt in Telegram would add Telegram ingress before this
path, but would not exercise a different cron schema, canonicalizer, mode
guard, or Gateway write. A Telegram-specific E2E run therefore would not add
extra evidence about this PR.

## Mode invariant and silent-failure protection

Top-level `mode` remains wake-only. For add/update:

- a nested job plus a top-level `mode` is rejected before any Gateway write;
- a non-stream flat schedule plus any top-level `mode` is rejected before any
  Gateway write; and
- the legacy unadvertised flat-stream shape is accepted only when recovery
  yields `schedule.kind="stream"`. Its stream mode is preserved inside the
  schedule and the copied top-level field is removed before schema validation.

This prevents the two silent-drop cases: `normalize.ts` cannot silently erase a
mode from a non-stream job, and a top-level mode alongside a nested job cannot
be orphaned. Invalid input fails visibly with:

```text
Remove the top-level "mode" field and retry. "mode" is only valid for action="wake".
```

## Live installed-build results — 2026-09-02

| Case | Result | Observed behavior |
|---|---|---|
| T1: nested stream + `mode:"match"` | PASS | Job was created; readback contained `schedule.kind="stream"` and `schedule.mode="match"`. |
| T2: nested stream + `mode:"line"` | INCONCLUSIVE | Qwen entered a visible validation/correction loop. It did not report success, and this was not counted as a pass. The exact-head regression test covers this mode. |
| T3: flat `everyMs` + top-level `mode:"now"` | PASS | The actionable wake-only error was returned; list showed no job. |
| T4: flat `everyMs` + top-level `mode:"line"` | PASS | The actionable wake-only error was returned; list showed no job. This is the former silent-drop case. |
| T5: nested non-stream job + top-level `mode:"match"` | PASS | The actionable wake-only error was returned; list showed no job. This is the former orphaned-mode case. |
| T6: `action:"wake"`, `mode:"now"` | PASS | Wake succeeded and created no cron job. |
| T7: ordinary natural-language flat add | PASS | `MODETEST-7` persisted as `schedule.kind="every"`, `everyMs=300000`, with an agent-turn message payload. |

The retained Gateway log independently records the T7 write:

```text
cron: job added  jobName=MODETEST-7
res ✓ cron.add 52ms
```

Only T1 and T7 created jobs. The Gateway log records two successful
`cron.remove` calls immediately after the run (`55ms` and `65ms`), completing
the cleanup.

This evidence covers both sides of the change: valid flat and stream inputs
survive canonicalization and persist, while invalid mode placements return a
visible error before any write rather than being silently ignored.


## Update 2026-09-03

Live validation tests were run on an installed bespoke OpenClaw build combining PR head
`92d5db6f333bad2a02cd6a1df1bdaea458adf9b8` with then-current upstream main
`740b2447b4d762bfb7a5ca53fc6794cff778f526`. The model was local Qwen 3.8 27B
Q5_K_S.

- Flat add recovered `everyMs` and `message` into canonical `schedule.kind="every"`
  and `payload.kind="agentTurn"`.
- A self-contained flat add/update changed the returned job from
  `everyMs=3600000` to `everyMs=7200000`; the returned persisted job confirmed
  the update.
- A non-stream top-level `mode="line"` was rejected before any write with the
  wake-only guidance. It was not silently dropped.
- An exact installed-build probe recovered the legacy flat stream input into
  `schedule.kind="stream"`, preserving `mode="match"` and `match="ERROR"`,
  removing top-level `mode`, and then stopping at the explicit trusted-run gate.cd

During testing, main advanced to
`3e8bda1d0aaae7cbcee19924370e5d743371584d`. There was no upstream overlap in
the cron implementation or tests; the only non-snapshot overlap was the
generated assertion baseline. The branch was resynced and prompt snapshots
were regenerated. The Telegram files in the diff are generated prompt
snapshots reflecting the automations schema; this PR does not change Telegram
runtime code.

# Update - 2026-09-04

Automated proof: `cron-tool.flat-params.test.ts` passes 39/39 at `3a34311e37`, including
`rejects incomplete flat schedule updates before Gateway dispatch` and
`accepts a complete flat cron schedule update with a timezone`.

The guard requires a flat update to recover exactly one complete, kind-consistent
schedule; ambiguous or incomplete schedules fail visibly before dispatch.

Live corroboration: I fetched upstream immediately before building
(`origin/main` = `0c2da1da0315`, the latest main available when the build began),
applied pushed PR head `3a34311e37`, built it, and ran the compiled output through
the live Gateway. Local Qwen3.8 27B Q5_K_S (as before) created a flat `expr` + `tz` job;
a timezone-only update was rejected, no `cron.update` was logged, and readback
retained `{kind:"cron",expr:"17 4 * * *",tz:"Europe/London"}`.

The tested checkout was not byte-identical to `3a34311e37`, so to be exact: 
`cron-tool-prepare.ts` differs only in that the pushed head passes `action` 
as a parameter where the tested tree read `next.action`

The guard path exercised live is the guard path in the pushed head.

prs.title: fix(webchat): preserve interleaved MEDIA image order
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

WebChat loses the original text/image order when an assistant reply contains multiple interleaved `MEDIA:` directives.

For example, an agent replies with:

1. Text A
2. Image A
3. Text B
4. Image B
5. Text C

During streaming, the order can appear correct. After the response finishes or chat history is reloaded, the saved assistant message places the images after the text instead of preserving their original positions.

This breaks image-heavy agent replies where each image belongs beside its explanation.

## Fix

- Preserve the original text/media segment order in private reply payload metadata.
- Propagate that metadata through outbound reply normalization without changing serialized outbound fields.
- Reconstruct ordered assistant content using the existing managed-media preparation and safety pipeline.
- Preserve existing behavior when the original text cannot be matched.
- Cover duplicate attachments, missing media, and persisted assistant content.

## Evidence

### Regression tests (Red -> Green)

Before the fix:
- Auto-reply test failed because ordered media metadata was undefined.
- Gateway test failed because the final content order was `[text, image, image]` instead of `[text, image, text, image, text]`.

After the fix:
- Auto-reply: 34/34 tests passed.
- Gateway media: 18/18 tests passed.
- Total: 52/52 tests passed.

### TypeScript

- `pnpm tsgo:core` passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test` passed all 29 shards.

### Formatting and lint

- Scoped oxlint: 0 errors, 0 warnings across all 7 changed files.
- Oxfmt check passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.

### Known limitations

Full-repository checks encounter unrelated existing max-lines and suppression-baseline violations in files outside this patch.

Live Gateway/WebChat validation has not yet been completed.

prs.title: fix(quota): preserve recovery across concurrent sessions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Concurrent Codex sessions could fail quota recovery because a pending write to one session binding denied reads of another binding. Separately, an older exhausted WHAM response could re-block a credential after a newer successful request.

## User Impact

Independent session bindings remain readable during non-evicting sibling writes, and a newer successful request keeps its recovered quota state when an older failure probe finally replies. Relevant pending writes and uncertain outcomes still deny effect guards.

## Why This Change Was Made

#171458 replaced repeated binding/revocation reads with owner-published facts and correctly denied queued or unknown writes. Its database-wide pending guard also rejected unrelated bindings. The same publication owner now records each known write scope: a non-evicting keyed write denies that key, an eviction-capable write denies its namespace, and unscoped native/compound writes retain database-wide denial. Unknown settlement remains denied for the database identity until restart. Receipt publication, rollback, expiry, and final lifecycle checks stay with their existing owners.

#174632 removed broad WHAM health fingerprints and explicitly accepted late quota observations superseding newer health. The existing Gateway regression demonstrates a real failure in that accepted edge. The failure reducer now compares the probe's start timestamp with the current persisted `lastProbeAt`, which successful use advances for shared, inherited, and personal credentials. This preserves ordering without restoring whole-store fingerprints, extra reads, or a new generation counter. `lastUsed` remains selection-owned and is intentionally unchanged by inherited success.

The fixes have separate commits and share the quota-reset concurrency proof. No schema, storage format, retention, dependency, configuration, or service lifecycle changes.

## Evidence

On baseline main `5e8ac91fbf6` with only the new tests added, the independent-binding regression fails with `Plugin state authority is unavailable` (1 failed, 1 eviction control passed). All three quota ownership regressions fail because the held exhausted response reinstalls a block over newer successful health.

On exact head `bb06a1b1e4124f83879121982f87feb6d05f49a3`:

- Six focused owner suites: **100 tests passed**. Type-aware lint for all touched TypeScript files, core typecheck, formatting, and diff checks pass. Both independent Codex autoreviews are scoped-clean at P0–P2.
- Original failing Gateway file: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/quota-reset.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **9 passed**, wrapper and remote command exit 0, Node 24.19 on [Blacksmith Testbox](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39177229108). A fresh clone's full head and hashes of every changed file plus the target test were verified before execution. This is the external Testbox command result; lease cleanup may cancel the hosting workflow.
- ClickClack production service/state boundary: **5 passed** in `service-state-persistence.test.ts`, using real SQLite owners and stubbed external channel calls. Unchanged published authority reaches `updateChannel`; revoked/replaced authority rejects before it and asserts no update call. Pending/unknown settlement denies session targets, and stale reverse indexes reject previous routes. These complement the deterministic sibling-write scope regression; no live ClickClack server is claimed.

[PR CI run 39175283306](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39175283306) is green on this head. Its changed-test selection does not include the original Gateway file, which is covered by the explicit Node proof above. No inherited-failure exception is needed.

prs.title: fix(discord): batch queued messages by thread
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves
When a user sends several Discord messages while an earlier turn is still running, the next follow-up turn should be able to see the whole compatible queued intent instead of only the last message. At the same time, Discord transport must keep every inbound event flowing into core admission so active-run steering and `/stop`-style control inputs are not delayed behind a local plugin queue.

Related: openclaw/openclaw#103287

## Summary
- remove the previous Discord-local same-session batch lane from `message-run-queue.ts`
- keep Discord inbound work event-keyed through the plugin queue so each message reaches core admission promptly
- carry Discord batch message IDs through typed preflight/finalized context fields when the dispatcher has an aggregate context
- add core follow-up queue support for aggregate `messageIds` on collected follow-up runs
- project collected queued message IDs into execution context as `MessageSids`, `MessageSidFirst`, and `MessageSidLast` while keeping `MessageSid` as the current/latest message
- add a focused Discord dispatcher boundary proof that two debounced Discord source messages become one processed turn with both source IDs preserved

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

### Ephemeral Gateway + qa-channel proof on pushed head

Verdict: PASS on pushed PR head `6df1189d660a9320a83f04408154e1a502581ff6`.

This is the new qualifying proof path requested by ClawSweeper: it starts an ephemeral Gateway child, enables the real `qa-channel` plugin against the QA bus, uses the `mock-openai` provider, injects three inbound channel events, and verifies that the two queued channel messages become one executed provider turn.

Committed proof test:

- `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/qa-channel-queued-message-ids.e2e.test.ts`

Redacted runtime evidence from the test:

```json
{

  "provider": "mock-openai",
  "gateway": "ephemeral-child",
  "receivedMessageIds": [
    "qa-msg-pr122238-active",
    "qa-msg-pr122238-queued-first",
    "qa-msg-pr122238-queued-last"
  ],
  "collectedProviderRequestCount": 1,
  "queuedNeedlesPresent": [true, true],
  "sameSessionForAllIngressMessages": true,
  "executedTurnChannel": "qa-channel",
  "executedTurnChatId": "pr-122238-qa-channel",
  "secrets": "none"
}
```

What this proves at the boundary ClawSweeper asked for:

- `qa-channel` receives three real inbound channel messages via the QA bus, including explicit provider message IDs.
- All three inbound messages resolve to the same Gateway session.
- While the first turn is active, two later source messages are queued through core admission.
- The queued pair is collected into exactly one mock-provider request, and that executed request contains both queued source bodies.
- This path does not mock Discord preflight or processing; it exercises a complete mock-channel/mock-provider/ephemeral-Gateway run.

Current-main merge evidence:

- Pushed PR head: `6df1189d660a9320a83f04408154e1a502581ff6`
- Current `origin/main`: `39b39ca6eec684f0675cd93500646b578f6e7021`

- Merge status: conflict-free `ort` merge

Additional code cleanup in this proof update:

- Removed Discord preflight `batchMessageIdFirst` / `batchMessageIdLast` fields.
- The finalized context now derives `MessageSidFirst` and `MessageSidLast` from the aggregate `batchMessageIds` array, avoiding duplicate Discord-only preflight fields.

Commands run:


The after-fix boundary is owned by core follow-up collection rather than a Discord pre-admission lane:

prs.title: improve(openai): vary provisional voice launch acknowledgments
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Voice delegation repeated a fixed English launch receipt even for callers speaking another language. This uses a short natural acknowledgment in the caller's language, with varied wording on repeated requests. The receipt confirms hearing the request; it does not establish admission or task completion. A fresh later result is still delivered through the existing completion owner.

## User Impact

Callers hear a short varied acknowledgment in their language, followed separately by a confirmed result or failure. Launch phrasing does not promise admission.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing delegation controller supplies a bounded launch-only instruction and retains the existing completion and failure owners.

### Refinement from live evidence

The launch acknowledgment now confirms hearing the request only. Real voice testing exposed that “on it” and even “checking that” could imply work had started before admission. The refined note explicitly excludes checking/doing claims, remains limited to this launch acknowledgment, and preserves natural wording, the caller’s language, variation, and the under-eight-word limit. Later confirmed results remain unchanged.

Live synthetic proof used the real subscription WebRTC transport, canonical production instruction builder, locally synthesized English/Polish input, and isolated callbacks. Repeated English acknowledgments were “Okay, I hear you.” and “Right, got it.” Polish acknowledgments were “Jasne, rozumiem.” and, for injected rejection, “Jasne, słyszę prośbę.” The rejected request’s spoken result was “Nie udało się tego wykonać. Spróbować jeszcze raz?” Three successful callbacks spoke the synthetic file’s correct first word. The synthetic terminal readback is included below; source recordings remain local and are not required to interpret these observed results.

Validation: final 26 owner tests, scoped extension lint, formatting, and fresh P0–P2 independent review pass. Previous unchanged bridge sibling proof is reused; no API or type shape changed.

Limits/decision: the rejection is injected at the consultation callback, not a real Gateway scheduler denial. One call demonstrates observed phrasing, not guaranteed compliance. Maintainer approval of provisional conversational receipts remains required; no approval is inferred from this evidence.

## Behavior decision

The [review's question](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175603#issuecomment-6235266061) is whether launch receipts may use localized, varied wording. I recommend bounded caller-language acknowledgments because [#164324](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/164324) identifies a concrete language failure: exact-speech instructions prevent ordinary call-language guidance from translating the fixed receipt.

The important intent in [#134003](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/134003) is that a launch acknowledgment must not establish admission, progress, or completion. This patch preserves that distinction at the [existing controller](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/15ff9e2b9e4ca5f29c31c09a8525153845547ed8/extensions/openai/realtime-quicksilver-delegation-controller.ts#L470). The [launch-only instruction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/15ff9e2b9e4ca5f29c31c09a8525153845547ed8/extensions/openai/realtime-quicksilver-delegation-controller.ts#L34) permits confirming hearing, explicitly excludes checking/doing claims and tools, and leaves later authoritative outcomes with the existing completion/failure owners.

The counterargument is valid: generated wording is less deterministic than a fixed sentence. The supplied synthetic real-WebRTC observations demonstrate the intended English/Polish behavior and callback rejection, not universal speech compliance or a real Gateway scheduler denial. The remaining product choice is accepting bounded generated wording rather than retaining fixed speech; localization supplies the practical reason, while the proof limits remain unchanged.

## Evidence

Code CI for head `15ff9e2b9e4ca5f29c31c09a8525153845547ed8` passed, including production/test types and lint ([CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39063056563)). The synthetic live-output observations below are separate from code CI; their callback-injection and Gateway-coverage limits are described above.

```json
[
  {
    "turn": 1,
    "language": "english",
    "injected_rejection": false,
    "acknowledgment": "Okay, I hear you.",
    "spoken_result": "First word: glacier.",
    "voiced_pcm_bytes_after_settlement": 65280
  },
  {
    "turn": 2,
    "language": "english",
    "injected_rejection": false,
    "acknowledgment": "Right, got it.",
    "spoken_result": "First word: glacier.",
    "voiced_pcm_bytes_after_settlement": 63360
  },
  {
    "turn": 3,
    "language": "polish",
    "injected_rejection": false,
    "acknowledgment": "Jasne, rozumiem.",
    "spoken_result": "Pierwsze słowo to „glacier”.",
    "voiced_pcm_bytes_after_settlement": 75840
  },
  {
    "turn": 4,
    "language": "polish",
    "injected_rejection": true,
    "acknowledgment": "Jasne, słyszę prośbę.",
    "spoken_result": "Nie udało się tego wykonać. Spróbować jeszcze raz?",
    "voiced_pcm_bytes_after_settlement": 141120
  }
]
```

The source-qualified fixture used existing subscription authentication with entirely generated speech, a task-owned synthetic file, and no real conversations or workspace data. The launch note remains within the existing single-append 500-byte bound. The callback rejection occurs before the synthetic file read. Provider transcripts and actual voiced PCM are observed outputs; this is not independent speech recognition or an all-language guarantee. Earlier ambiguous baseline wording is retained locally as evidence of why the note was tightened. No production Gateway restart or deployment was performed for this revision.

prs.title: fix: recover Responses streams stalled on bookkeeping events
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Responses requests remaining busy indefinitely when the transport keeps sending bookkeeping events, empty reasoning deltas, or repeated snapshots without advancing model output.

## User Impact

Nonproductive requests reach the existing timeout/recovery path. Nonempty hidden reasoning remains progress even when chat shows no new text. Streams without request-activity notifications keep their existing yielded-output fallback. No migration or new configuration is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Responses currently reports every wire event as progress. The reducer now distinguishes physical activity from model progress, using existing output trackers. The watchdog also preserves that producer classification when an active caller consumes assistant events; empty emitted events cannot overwrite it. Canonical identity validation retains its original ordering, including active tool-call index rejection. Transcript and assistant event contents are unchanged.

Related: #165983 (separate progress deadline), #140335 (parked-consumer liveness), #152705 (SSE comments as physical activity).

## Behavior decision

The [review asks whether bookkeeping-only Responses activity may expire despite possible opaque computation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175733#issuecomment-6238257630). I recommend applying the existing bounded-progress policy while keeping connection liveness distinct. A stream can prove its connection is alive without showing that it will ever return an answer; refreshing progress for every bookkeeping frame disables the independent recovery deadline.

The earlier [Responses activity change](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/5ebbc3c0037acdbd7de58d5d838f412088bbef8d) intentionally protected opaque computation. The later [#165983](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/165983) established a separate progress budget for Completions, and [#152705](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/152705) distinguishes SSE keepalives from progress. These support the two-clock design; they do not already approve extending this classification to Responses.

The [shared reducer](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/379c46b036afc601e07be6925e3d56b65d7d863d/packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-stream-internal.ts#L307) preserves physical activity while counting advancing output, including nonempty hidden reasoning. The existing watchdog and recovery owners remain responsible for expiry. The cost is explicit: legitimate computation with no observable progress can be retried after twice the effective idle budget. Existing provider timeout controls can raise that budget within finite run limits. The owner choice is bounded recovery versus continued tolerance of opaque computation; the transport evidence establishes the mechanism, not whether a particular provider's opaque computation has stalled.

## Evidence

On the previous PR revision, both the native wrapper chain and an actively consuming real HTTP/SDK client reproduce the empty-reasoning and repeated-snapshot failures. Each has passing bookkeeping and hidden-reasoning controls. With the repair, 98 focused cases pass, including existing identity rejection coverage, structural streams without notifications, and actual transport recovery. Production types, owning test types, scoped lint, formatting, and fresh independent review through P2 pass.

The retained real-time behavior trace (production source identical to this revision) uses a real isolated loopback HTTP server, Node fetch, OpenAI SDK Responses client, shared reducer, composed run-signal relay, canonical watchdog, and real timers. Only the wire frames are scripted. A real SDK warmup request separates lazy initialization from the measured progress deadline. Idle/progress budgets are 1000/2000ms; frames arrive every 200ms. After each scenario, a second watched request completes. The recorded output is:

```jsonl
{"proof":"real Responses HTTP transport","activity":"bookkeeping","consumer":"active","injectedFrames":10,"outcome":"expired: no model progress","recovery":"second request completed","elapsedMs":2106}
{"proof":"real Responses HTTP transport","activity":"empty reasoning","consumer":"active","injectedFrames":10,"outcome":"expired: no model progress","recovery":"second request completed","elapsedMs":2046}
{"proof":"real Responses HTTP transport","activity":"repeated snapshot","consumer":"active","injectedFrames":11,"outcome":"expired: no model progress","recovery":"second request completed","elapsedMs":2247}
{"proof":"real Responses HTTP transport","activity":"hidden reasoning","consumer":"active","injectedFrames":16,"outcome":"completed without timeout","recovery":"second request completed","elapsedMs":3311}
```

This proves the transport boundary and subsequent-request recovery; it does not claim an external provider was contacted, full Gateway automatic failover was exercised, or that these events caused a particular live incident. This consumer-path revision has not been activated in the operator Gateway. All fixtures and exported output are synthetic; no real messages, logs, credentials, endpoints, or incident identifiers are included.

### Controlled-clock regression

The committed regression retains the real HTTP/fetch/OpenAI SDK/Responses reducer and watchdog, with claimed ports and body-receipt barriers. Only the watchdog clock is advanced: no real timer intervals, sleeps, or polling. The first completed snapshot establishes progress; unchanged repeats must not extend that deadline. Four scenarios pass in 4.0 seconds of test time (9.17 seconds wrapper wall time); CI seconds are pending. Owning test types and scoped type-aware lint pass. Fresh independent review through P3 found no actionable issue; subsequent edits only add the three braces required by lint. The earlier 98-case result remains prior-revision evidence; this revision reruns the four affected transport cases and retains unchanged production and sibling-test source.

### Maintainer decision requested

Apply the existing bounded no-observable-progress policy to Responses. Keepalives establish a live connection; nonempty reasoning and tool-argument deltas establish model progress. Opaque computation emitting only bookkeeping is indistinguishable from a stalled stream and will expire at twice the configured idle budget. That availability tradeoff is intentional and needs maintainer approval. Existing provider model-request timeout opt-ins can increase the budget, subject to finite run/agent limits; increasing only an outer agent timeout does not raise the cloud idle ceiling. No approval is inferred from passing tests or earlier deployment smoke checks.


### CI qualification

The prior revision’s tested merge encountered a full-core `typescript/await-thenable` failure in `src/infra/sqlite-readonly-location.worker.ts:381`. The historical source comparison found identical blob `95284fc6047a248a64eb0b2db2e02ed67108d129` in that tested base `a34f1be0bc1e` and merge `c0be3cfc`. [Historical failed job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39062786478/job/117484562218). Current-main integration changes that upstream file; this historical classification is not a claim about the new merge head’s CI. This PR does not modify the SQLite owner. Exact-head broad CI on `379c46b036afc601e07be6925e3d56b65d7d863d` now passes ([CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39074079624)); changed-file scoped lint also passes without rule suppression or blind retries.

### Current-main integration

Integrated the current main snapshot with a true merge preserving both parent histories. The only manual conflict was the upstream WebSocket-chain fixture cleanup: the shared fixture/model/fork helpers and silent-provider coverage remain, while the existing activity-versus-progress cases replace main’s bookkeeping-only liveness expectation. The three production owners are byte-identical to the previous PR revision. All 98 focused cases pass on the merged source, including the real HTTP/SDK recovery cases, native wrapper-chain activity cases, structural-stream fallback, and Responses identity rejection coverage. The prior real-time trace remains evidence for identical production owners, rather than a new external-provider or Gateway deployment claim. The maintainer policy decision above remains pending.


Merged head `379c46b036afc601e07be6925e3d56b65d7d863d` preserves prior PR head `50cf2c63c4f630cf35a140388800241573d5e6df` and pinned main `bcd6ab322aeb6d7a1bd3550477c1875213889e64` as its two parents. Published tree exactly matches the frozen qualified merge tree `5338b44d48f8e7cda93d4c728897873e52a147d5`. Exact replacement-head CI now passes ([CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39074079624)).

prs.title: fix(codex): first Codex start after a Gateway crash fails on macOS
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on macOS, the first Codex start after a Gateway crash fails with `Cannot reap registered Codex process <pid>. Stop it before retrying.` (one failed start per orphan), and closing a live Codex app-server can intermittently report process cleanup as `uncertain`.

## User Impact

User impact: after a crash on macOS, OpenClaw reaps orphaned Codex app-servers and starts a fresh one on the first attempt again. Closing a Codex transport on a loaded Mac no longer reports spurious uncertain cleanup. Linux behavior is unchanged, and inspection failures still fail closed at the existing 2 s containment deadline.

## Why This Change Was Made

Since #175368, macOS process inspection uses the native `@openclaw/proc-safe` census for both Node and Bun. During the few milliseconds between SIGKILL and exit, that census reports the dying process as a bare `{ pid, owner: "unknown" }` row while `readProcessIdentity` still sees it. The shared Darwin inspection owner correctly fails closed on that (the SDK contract says inspection errors never prove absence). But the Codex reaper's two post-SIGKILL confirmation loops gave up on that first failed observation. The reaper's own kill puts the process into exactly that window, so confirmation failed almost every time even though the kill had worked.

The fix is local to the caller that caused the window. After our own SIGKILL, a failed observation is retried every 20 ms until the existing containment deadline, instead of being treated as lost custody. The stopped root keeps custody while we retry, and runs that never sent a SIGKILL behave exactly as before.

The orphan test is also fixed. Its macOS "inspection unavailable" step put a failing fake `ps` on `PATH`, but macOS no longer runs `ps`. The step therefore stopped testing inspection failure; it became the first real reap attempt, which hit the bug above. It now uses proc-safe's documented `PROC_SAFE_NATIVE=off` mode (native-only operations throw `helper-unavailable`, already used by `src/daemon/systemd-loaded-unit-inventory.test.ts`). The fixture owner applies that mode per start. That makes the step a genuine inspection failure, which fails closed and leaves the orphans alive, and it exposed the reap regression in the following step. Linux still runs every start with the fake `ps` to prove procfs never needs it. The test's old generic-`ps` branch is gone because the test needs a pinned native Codex binary, which exists only for macOS, Linux, and Windows.

Release-note context: Codex plugin, macOS only. Fixes orphaned app-server reaping after a Gateway crash (regression from #175368) and spurious `uncertain` cleanup on transport close.

## Evidence

On macOS 27 (arm64, Node 24.22, `@openclaw/proc-safe` 0.4.1), host load average 40–63:

- **Root cause probe:** an orphaned process that is SIGSTOPped and then SIGKILLed shows `{ pid, owner: "unknown" }` from `listProcesses({ pids: [pid] })` while `readProcessIdentity(pid)` returns `exited: false`. The window lasted until the process vanished about 2–4 ms later, and it appeared in 4 of 5 runs.
- **Standalone repro with the real orphan fixture:** before the fix, every reap attempt killed the tree but reported `Cannot reap registered Codex process` (the native root, then the Node root on the retry). After the fix, one start reaps both orphan trees and spawns a fresh child.
- **`pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-orphan.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`:**
  - before, on main: fails with `expected 'Cannot inspect Codex processes…' but got 'Cannot reap registered Codex process …'`
  - with only the test seam fixed: fails at the fresh start with `Cannot reap registered Codex process 57614`, which is the regression this PR fixes
  - with this PR: passes (28.7 s test time at load ~40, 35.6 s at load ~61; about 110–200 s wall including Vitest worker preparation). The test cost is unchanged and dominated by the cold native app-server boots it needs.
- **`transport.process.test.ts`, three runs each at the same load (~50–63):**
  - before: **3/3 runs failed, 10 failing cases.** The "revalidates identities while quiescing" modes `late`, `reparented`, `root-resumed`, `traced`, and `uninterruptible` failed in varying combinations, plus "reaps descendants in independent and root process groups" in 2 runs.
  - after: all 30 quiesce-mode executions passed. One run still had a single "reaps descendants…" failure; see the remaining gap below.
- **Siblings:** `transport-process-registration{,.procfs,.lifecycle}.test.ts`, `transport-process-snapshot.test.ts`, and `transport-stdio.test.ts` pass.
- **Static checks:** `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` are clean on the touched files. `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` pass.
- **Review:** a Codex autoreview at P2 on this exact diff came back scoped-clean, with no accepted findings.

Remaining gap: a *full* census also fails whenever any unrelated host process is mid-exit (I measured about 0.8% of `readDarwinProcessTree` calls at load ~56). That is the likely source of the remaining rare "reaps descendants…" flake. The right fix is in proc-safe (fill topology for exiting processes from the kernel record, as it already does for zombies), followed by a dependency bump; I've filed that as a separate follow-up.

prs.title: perf(agents): reduce model request preparation allocations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Model lifecycle diagnostics compute prompt statistics even when no listener consumes those events. Responses continuation fingerprints also assemble a complete canonical JSON string before hashing it, adding a large temporary allocation for long prefixes.

## User Impact

Less transient work during model request preparation, with unchanged wire payloads, prompt-prefix stability, diagnostic sizes, and persisted continuation fingerprints. No configuration or migration is required. A listener attached after a request starts may lack optional prompt stats on that already-running request's terminal event.

## Why This Change Was Made

The lifecycle owner now captures prompt stats only when diagnostics are enabled and a listener is interested in started, completed, or error events. All three interests are checked because terminal-only consumers also need the stats. Continuation fingerprints use the existing incremental stable-value hash owner while retaining JSON normalization.

Source tracing found full request encoding and hashing at request/attempt boundaries, not once per streamed chunk. Ordinary session forks already share the transport's encoded Blob. Continuations need their immutable full-prefix snapshot while the transport sends only a suffix; that boundary is preserved. The existing native string sizing and attempt-local size cache are retained: paired probes rejected handwritten escape counting and cache removal because they increased CPU.

## Evidence

Baseline: `0f56bc0b2b8e`; measured/reviewed candidate: `7a425339c24f`. All benchmark production files were verified byte-for-byte against that commit. Two concurrent, swapped-core pairs of production-import probes (768 invocations per side per pair) measured the retained prefix hashing change:

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate | Paired change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Prefix sampled allocation/invocation | 1,947,340 bytes | 1,163,306 bytes | -40.26% |
| Prefix CPU/invocation | 0.593755 ms | 0.534156 ms | -10.03% |

The prefix fixture contains approximately 256 KiB text. The separate request-parameter fingerprint reduces to a 19-character normalized payload in this fixture; its allocation was neutral and CPU increased by 0.000320 ms/invocation. These probes do not attribute all generic production hash samples to continuation fingerprints.

Four final-candidate concurrent 48-turn Gateway pairs ran under the exclusive measurement lock, on 16-core halves 96–111 and 112–127, swapping halves each pair. All pairs completed 48 primary turns, 3,456 agent events, and 1,764 session-message events per side. The two pairs with matching model-request counts (2–3, 99 per side, opposite halves) were neutral for allocation; no overall Gateway speedup or GC win is claimed:

| Matched-pair metric, per primary turn | Baseline mean | Candidate mean | Mean paired B − A |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Sampled allocation | 123,060,214 bytes | 122,958,233 bytes | -101,981 bytes (-0.108%) |
| Main-thread CPU | 277.300 ms | 273.132 ms | -4.168 ms (-1.091%) |
| Main-thread GC | 14.968 ms | 15.745 ms | +0.777 ms (+5.052%) |

Percentages are the mean of within-pair percentage differences. GC variation, differing time-coalesced chat counts, and the small number of matched pairs limit inference; the observed increase is reported, not presented as an improvement.

All four pairs are retained here, including unequal utility workloads:

| Pair | Model requests A/B | Allocation B − A / turn | CPU B − A / turn | GC B − A / turn |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 98 / 99 | +11.016 MB (+9.32%) | +16.479 ms | +3.230 ms |
| 2 | 99 / 99 | +0.521 MB (+0.40%) | +16.694 ms | +1.631 ms |
| 3 | 99 / 99 | -0.725 MB (-0.62%) | -25.030 ms | -0.077 ms |
| 4 | 123 / 99 | -17.081 MB (-12.86%) | -26.528 ms | -2.338 ms |

Pair 1's excess allocations are dominated by unchanged session/attempt lifecycle stacks; the same categories reverse in pair 4. The harness did not record utility-purpose categories, so we cannot attribute all allocation differences to extra requests. Core utilization was recorded with `mpstat -P 96-127` for context, including the benchmarks' own work; outside load did not invalidate runs.

The synthetic fixture preserves 5,000 sessions, 6,000 retained runs, 12 projects/worktrees, 200 approvals and 100 cron jobs, with 8 MiB logical text and approximately 56 MB agent/12 MB state databases per side. It is smaller than the multi-GB fixture. Each side uses 12 subscribers and 100 chunks per turn. The Gateway scenario uses short, non-reasoning Responses histories and does not exercise continuation fingerprints; separate production-import probes cover those. Per-site samples cover roughly 1.37–1.90 MB for session-fork encoding callbacks and 1.11–1.64 MB for prompt stats per roughly 13.5–16.5-second capture; these are sampled inclusive totals, not exact callback costs. Generic crypto hash samples include unrelated owners. This is synthetic loopback provider proof, with no live-provider cache or billing claim. Both sides use the same task-owned overlay for required build dependencies and shared read-only dependencies; inactive unrelated plugin dependencies may be older. These benchmark-build qualifications do not replace PR CI.

## Validation

All 29 final diagnostic tests pass. With only the lifecycle module reverted to the pinned baseline, the unobserved and unrelated-listener regressions fail as expected; the disabled case passes. Final lifecycle source was then restored byte-for-byte. Fresh independent Codex review of the full final patch is clean through P2, with no accepted/actionable findings. The unchanged continuation compatibility tests passed (42), including independent canonical digests, JSON normalization, toJSON count, Unicode/lone surrogate, key order, correlation-field omission, and mutation sensitivity. Existing simple-completion and prompt-prefix stability proof passed (8). Changed-file formatting, scoped lint, and `git diff --check` pass. The final isolated source-performance build passed, including 54 native control-plane modules. Exact-head [PR CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39177868181): 43 successful jobs, no failed jobs, including broad build, typecheck and suite coverage. The required CI gate and current-head GitHub Codex review are clean. No CI rerun or Testbox/Crabbox lease was used.

Production delta against the pinned base: +7 lines across two files. This growth is the lifecycle-interest guard preserving started-only, completed-only, and error-only consumer contracts. The change removes unnecessary canonical-string construction and unobserved stats work without adding a cache, dependency, config option, or alternate encoding path. Test delta: +95 lines across two existing test files.

prs.title: refactor(sessions): skip redundant fresh-input identity reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Turn preparation reads the transcript identity table even when the session actor already owns a complete, current identity index.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. Eligible fresh inputs avoid one database lookup; worker-request count is unchanged. There is no schema, durability, or transaction-ordering change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the complete resident index to prove a fresh key is absent. Matching keys still load canonical stored bytes; truncated indexes and assistant-body scans keep their existing readers. Existing write receipts invalidate resident facts after in-process writes. The accepted edge is unchanged: sessions exceeding the bounded identity window use SQL.

The actor also drops six empty transaction callbacks and a deep clone of a scalar row whose nested values are replaced immediately. Custody checks and eager PostgreSQL writer locks stay with their current owners.

Production delta: +9/-9 lines, including the clarified completeness comment. Tests: +51/-5. Documentation: +3/-2. No new owner, cache, handshake, or fallback.

## Evidence

Formatting, basic oxlint, and `git diff --check` pass. One isolated Codex review completed clean with no actionable findings. [CI run 39163461131](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39163461131) passes types, core lint, source contracts, architecture/Madge, database ratchets, and all four changed-test jobs on `7184172e588aa0f21664f02ba2ef59a29512f278`. The SQLite resident-turn suite passes all 10 cases; related actor/entry coverage totals 136 cases across 14 suites. All three native PostgreSQL conformance shards pass, including all 10 PostgreSQL resident-turn cases (job 117781733817). [Exact-head Testbox Knip](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39165245774) reports no new findings: all 58 production and 33 full-tree findings also occur in [main CI job 117782017361](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39163574553/job/117782017361) at `3020cb46d4737c0a1b1085e9d5eb6985bf33821b` (58 production/34 full-tree). Its script scan is clean. These unchanged findings are outside the changed files and are inherited.

The shared SQLite/PostgreSQL resident suite covers zero-read fresh preparation, canonical retry bytes after an actor append, invalidation after a native write, truncated-index fallback, and assistant scans without event identities. Existing rollback, reset, move, eviction, and restart cases remain. Local test runners stalled before results under host I/O contention; a Testbox attempt was cancelled during local source preparation before allocating a machine. Neither attempt counts as test evidence.

Harness v3 completed two alternating baseline/candidate pairs and the third baseline, comparing `af7c0d2398befaf60d8c90e6705297aaf14ce2a5` with `7184172e588aa0f21664f02ba2ef59a29512f278`. All five completed workloads pass restart, shutdown, and child cleanup. The third candidate failed twice during synthetic account setup before any turn. Its second attempt was observed waiting on a filesystem-bound `git ls-files --deleted` scan in CLI startup. This is **two completed pairs, not three**; the remaining workload comparison is deferred to the combined census. No timeout or harness assertion was weakened.

Each warm cell is the median [min–max] across ten turns. MAIN is zero throughout these causal phases.

| Pair | Phase | Baseline SQL / requests / MAIN | Candidate SQL / requests / MAIN |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Warm | 57 [57–58] / 16 [16–17] / 0 | 56 [56–57] / 16 [16–17] / 0 |
| 1 | First turn | 169 / 54 / 0 | 168 / 53 / 0 |
| 1 | Restart first turn | 132 / 43 / 0 | 131 / 43 / 0 |
| 2 | Warm | 57 [57–58] / 16 [16–17] / 0 | 56 [56–57] / 16 [16–17] / 0 |
| 2 | First turn | 169 / 53 / 0 | 168 / 54 / 0 |
| 2 | Restart first turn | 134 / 43 / 0 | 131 / 43 / 0 |

Both per-request warm ledgers attribute the saving to `session.turn.prepare`: 1→0 SQL in every warm turn, with its worker request retained. Every other warm-operation median is unchanged. The complete SELECT inventory shows no replacement entry, actor hydration, cache snapshot, row-facts, or watermark read. First-turn SQL differs only by the removed identity SELECT in both pairs; first-turn request variation is unrelated zero-SQL scheduling and is not credited. Restart pair 2 also has two baseline-only quarantine reads, which are not credited.

Raw windows include variable background work: warm SQL/request medians are 59/17→56.5/16 in pair 1 and 58/16→58/16.5 in pair 2. Raw first-turn totals are 478/95→475/93 and 492/99→280/90; raw restart totals are 177/66→202/78 and 206/79→183/69. The causal ledger above separates that background work; no work moves to MAIN. The host is loaded, so no latency improvement is claimed.

PostgreSQL maintainer review approved `7184172e588aa0f21664f02ba2ef59a29512f278` and its comment-only follow-up `f1d54921e92c327c8d4930eb4791b106561dc49d`. The follow-up explicitly states that a complete resident index contains every identity row for the session, not only the bounded window. Final-head CI [39176758515](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39176758515) passed all 42 jobs, including all three PostgreSQL shards. [Final security and aggregate gates](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39178078903) also passed. Merged as `20b6c7ae4e0e35239e14bca54c156575e4670d91`; GitHub state, main ancestry, and the exact expected merge tree against its actual parent are verified. All reviewed code/test blobs are unchanged; the documentation also includes intervening main updates. The combined PostgreSQL census follows the turn-path wave; it is not a per-PR measurement gate.

prs.title: perf(sessions): batch remote session creation refreshes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Remote session creation bypasses the Control UI's list-refresh pacing, so a stream of new sessions can trigger one `sessions.list` request per creation in every observed view.

## User Impact

Remote sessions appear through the existing four-to-five-second collection window, with a five-to-fifteen-second cooldown after slow automatic reads. Locally accepted creations still update observed lists immediately, independently of a slow primary read or chat bootstrap.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing per-query refresh owner for remote create events and delete the urgency state, callback arguments, and queued-urgency propagation. Keep one in-flight request plus bounded trailing invalidation, authoritative owner/search filtering, hidden-page catch-up, explicit refreshes, and existing row-delta reconciliation. This narrows the immediate-creation behavior introduced by #171768 to locally accepted user actions.

Production change: **30 lines removed net**. No new cache, configuration, dependency, storage shape, or protocol field. Activity reconciliation and Swarm descriptor-only child discovery remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Regression through the real session capability: 60 remote creations in one simulated minute produced **60 reads per observed view on base and 12 after the fix (80% fewer)**. The regression fails on base with `expected 12, received 60`; the fixed case verifies membership every five seconds and no extra trailing reads after traffic ends.
- Four focused files: **27 tests passed**, 4.15 seconds Vitest / 14.68 seconds wrapper wall time. Covers local-create immediacy, filtered views, in-flight invalidation, hidden pages, row deltas, and three minutes of event volume.
- Direct sibling `session-roster-refresh.events.test.ts`: **31 tests passed**, 30.62 seconds Vitest / 38.70 seconds wrapper wall time.
- Changed-file formatting, repository UI lint, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent Codex autoreview: scoped clean through P2, no actionable findings.
- CI run [39173402346](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39173402346) found two additional tests asserting the removed immediate remote-create behavior: `swarm-activity.integration.test.ts` and `sessions-page.typing.test.ts`. Both failures reproduced locally. Updated only their timing expectations while preserving membership, phase/log chronology, visibility, resubscribe, and cleanup assertions; **20 tests passed** in 18.02 seconds Vitest / 26.06 seconds wrapper wall time. Changed-file lint/format passed; a fresh independent autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 issues. Production code is unchanged by this repair.
- Final-head CI [39176845079](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39176845079) passed: all three UI shards, applicable UI end-to-end, types, lint, docs, changed-node checks, and `openclaw/ci-gate`. PR CI supplies broad validation; no Testbox/Crabbox lease used.

No appearance change; browser evidence concerns request counts and membership freshness. The separate descriptor-only Swarm child-discovery path still performs its own read and is outside this fix.

## Measurement results

Across the three qualified pairs, mean list traffic fell from **985 to 198.33 calls/minute across four sockets**, or **246.25 to 49.58 calls/minute/socket (79.9% fewer)**. Mean paired candidate-minus-baseline differences were **−786.67 calls/minute**, **−2.535 seconds of main-thread CPU**, and **−2.383 seconds of Gateway process CPU**. Main-thread CPU averaged **9.195 → 6.661 seconds (27.6% lower)**; process CPU averaged **14.801 → 12.418 seconds (16.1% lower)** per capture.

| Pair | Baseline / candidate cores | Calls baseline → candidate | Δ calls | Δ main-thread CPU | Δ Gateway process CPU |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 96–111 / 112–127 | 1,123 → 230 | −893 | −2.594 s | −1.657 s |
| 2 | 112–127 / 96–111 | 799 → 160 | −639 | −2.848 s | −3.318 s |
| 4 | 112–127 / 96–111 | 1,033 → 205 | −828 | −2.162 s | −2.172 s |

Per-socket mean calls/minute, including each view's sidebar:

| Browser view | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Sessions | 288.00 | 54.33 |
| Activity | 238.67 | 55.33 |
| Streaming chat 2 | 229.00 | 44.67 |
| Streaming chat 3 | 229.33 | 44.00 |

Mean requests/minute by caller/row mode/filter, summed across the four sockets:

| Caller source | Row mode | Filter class | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| sidebar | sidebar | general | 480.00 | 88.00 |
| sidebar | compact | general (owner counts) | 240.00 | 45.00 |
| sidebar | compact | children | 192.00 | 41.33 |
| sessions-page | compact | general | 60.00 | 11.00 |
| activity | compact | active | 11.00 | 11.00 |
| chat-pane | compact | children | 2.00 | 2.00 |

This identifies remote creation as the bypass; existing Activity pacing and chat-pane child reads remain unchanged. Covered row deltas already avoid list refetches, and ordinary stream-message traffic does not trigger broad list reads. Equivalent observed queries already share a refresh owner. No new debounce layer or cache is added.

Every accepted pair has exact browser/Prometheus total and source/row-mode/filter parity, successful list replies, no unexpected socket closure or event-sequence gap, matching starting/ending session counts, four completed concurrent primary streams, and visible final-root membership in all four sidebars. First-create skew was 2 ms, 0 ms, and 0 ms. Incidental utility-call counts were 27/28, 29/27, and 27/27. `mpstat` busy percentages on the low/high halves were 16.02/13.55, 27.40/28.12, and 13.15/15.11; these are context, not rejection criteria. Sampled Dirty stayed below 2 GiB; pair 1's post-run sample was delayed by 78.5 seconds.

**Excluded pair 3:** captured calls were 922 → 194, but the candidate metric interval counted 196, and the baseline synthetic model reported a disconnected utility stream. The four primary streams completed on both sides. Its CPU differences (−2.497 s main, −2.969 s process) are diagnostic only and excluded from all averages above. No replacement pairs were added.

## Measurement method

Four concurrent baseline/candidate pairs were attempted under the shared exclusive measurement lock. Pairs 1, 2, and 4 qualified; pair 3 is excluded for the gaps above. Each side gets 16 CPU cores; the halves swap on alternating pairs. The comparison uses per-pair candidate-minus-baseline differences. Outside load is recorded with `mpstat` as context.

Each side starts from the same seeded synthetic inventory: 5,000 sessions, 6,000 retained runs, 200 approvals, 100 disabled cron jobs, 12 projects with worktrees, and 64 MiB logical transcript text. Four real headless Control UI sockets show Sessions, Activity, and two streaming chat panes, each with an All owners / All statuses sidebar. State evolves equally across pairs; accepted starting/ending session counts were 5,074/5,134, 5,138/5,198, and 5,266/5,326 after setup and earlier attempts. Each timed minute creates 59 parent-linked children and one final root while four real agent turns stream against a deterministic local SSE model. This exercises concurrent agent execution and RPC creation; it is not a tool-driven `sessions_spawn` run or a replay of production traffic.

Browser WebSocket capture provides per-socket/source/row-mode/filter counts, corroborated by `openclaw_sessions_list_requests_total`. Gateway IPC samples measure process and main-thread CPU, beginning about 500 ms before the common stimulus barrier. Equal per-pair inventories and controlled creation/primary-stream work, successful list replies, no socket sequence gaps, rendered streaming content, and eventual final-root visibility in all four sidebars are required. Visibility is checked after a six-second drain with up to ten seconds for the DOM assertion; this does not measure a five-second rendering bound.

The measured candidate UI is built from `ab46b7156a35433233a111527b22f05ae0b76624`. The follow-up changed only two tests, then a required rebase produced `86cdcf1f96c9d2f778427da0b12ad8872212060f`. The production commit is patch-identical and all six changed production files remain byte-identical to the measured UI. Both sides use the same original baseline Gateway runtime, `50bb09d7ba13a37c8982b91afb3fcd52e13b09ae`; these are a controlled pinned-runtime comparison, not measurements of the rebased runtime. The sole rebase conflict was an upstream test-harness refactor; preserving that refactor with the same timing correction passed all 19 tests in the affected file (10.36 seconds Vitest / 13.95 seconds wrapper).

Incidental utility requests receive the same single-chunk synthetic response but are not the controlled stimulus; their counts are recorded per pair rather than required to match. Pair 1 initially stopped on that overly broad equality check; after inspecting the fixture, it was retained because its four primary streams, 2,480 chunks, creation schedule, inventory, counters, and browser checks matched.

An initial pilot was discarded because its first-page Sessions membership assertion ignored pinned fixture ordering; the final root belonged after the 25-row visible page. The corrected campaign checks actual sidebar visibility and retains the Sessions response for membership qualification. An expanded Swarm hydrator panel and external model-provider performance are outside this measurement.
