prs.title: fix: queued internal events fail after another session completion
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes queued internal events being rejected as outside the current transcript turn when another completion advances the same session before the event executes.

## User Impact

Queued restart notices and other internal events keep their input until execution without being mistaken for orphaned user turns. External-user eager persistence, source deduplication, current-policy admission, cancellation, and the strict keyed-current-turn guard remain intact. No configuration or schema migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Internal events now stage input in the existing durable pending-input owner, adopt lifecycle state without prematurely appending that input, and carry its custody into execution. Settlement joins pending-input cleanup. Policy re-admission retains the stable source identity and transport bytes and uses existing completion tracking; it does not create a parallel queue or relax recovery validation.

Requested by @steipete.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @steipete](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/ad63e3d4-86e4-499d-bd06-4ae3e4b88338)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/subagent/3f95955d-0e16-4018-8211-39efd6354b66)

Current-main integration and final verification were completed in the original discussion session.

## Evidence

- Integrated candidate: 160 focused tests pass across event handoff, real SQLite/actor admission, orphan repair, reply preparation, and all five config-policy re-admission scenarios (including a recoverable channel route).
- Three selected strict replay/pending-history tests passed on the preceding candidate; the strict keyed-current-turn guard remains unchanged.
- Core typecheck, changed TypeScript lint, formatting, and diff checks pass.
- Fresh independent review after the current-main integration reports no P0–P2 findings. Controller migration conflicts preserve the new operation owner and pending-input custody; the redundant mocked wiring test identified by ClawSweeper was removed.
- Current head `4981970ee26a1e29c9be515adafac28b45cc4d05`: real isolated Gateway and OpenClaw embedded harness completed four authorized OpenAI `gpt-4.1-mini` turns (response model `gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14`), with four HTTP 200 responses. Verified queued input absent from the active transcript before execution, durable pending custody, FIFO event-before-announcement execution, settled pending inputs, successful fresh-user continuation, and no keyed-turn/orphan diagnostics. No shared Gateway changes or real-channel messages.
- The experimental live fixture then hit an incorrect display-count assertion (expected four visible assistant messages, observed three). A zero-inference reopened-state check passed: all four replies are persisted across eight raw messages; the existing pre-session-start announcement-pair filter accounts for the three visible replies. It also verified pre-execution cancellation leaves no transcript input or model call. The original failing test result is not relabeled green.
- Exact-head CI run [39159891785](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39159891785) succeeded; final read found all 137 check runs completed without failures and the CI, dependency-review, and security-sensitive-review statuses successful.

The real SQLite/actor boundary reproduced the keyed-input failure. The historical full-Gateway baseline did not reproduce overtaking, and cold-process event re-adoption remains unproven. Durable staging is not a claim of automatic replay permission after restart.

The long experimental Gateway fixture is one-off proof evidence rather than routine CI; the real-model current-head proof and zero-inference assertion reconciliation are complete. The shipped change reuses existing state and authority owners (50 production insertions / 11 deletions); no new recovery manager or storage format.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Sidebar and session menus still discovered their own controls through DOM searches and carried redundant tracking suppression after the Solid migration. This checkpoint gives menu controls, section headers, rail pins, presence facepiles, and person triggers renderer-owned refs. The existing Menu focus owner exposes `focusFirst()` and `itemElement(id)` so callers retain control identity.

## User Impact

Existing navigation, keyboard focus, host tags, classes, routes, selectors, and lazy boundaries are preserved. Authoritative sidebar reads stay synchronous in plain TypeScript owners; Solid consumers receive live owner accessors and scoped projections.

## Current Candidate

Head `ca4bf52f226e0b07d068c0424133f2df4179abd7` merges current main `c8c8e886daae866027b976d606e83a8ceb6c114c` to resolve repeated GitHub mergeability computation timeouts. The five overlapping files now retain main's mounted-row and Inbox focus ownership. Three files match main exactly; the session row keeps main's settled mount/focus callback plus live host accessors, and Inbox keeps main's focus registry plus route-derived open state.

The initial CI exposed section-reorder focus, hidden landscape startup, and two catalog retry regressions. This PR fixes those at their owners: retain the reorder trigger in a component-owned lifetime; allow shell startup inputs while later hidden owner updates stay parked; and keep reactive view reads separate from synchronous owner callbacks. This is one checkpoint; the remaining effect, timer, focus, and measurement conversions continue in the follow-up sidebar PRs.

prs.title: perf(sessions): reuse compaction admission and display facts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Manual compaction repeats corpus admission through a discarded session read, then rereads and backfills display facts that compaction did not change.

## User Impact

Manual compaction does less database work while preserving the visible message tail and accounting. No configuration, schema, migration, or public API changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing agent-database execution preparation for writable corpus admission. Carry a validated display projection from the already-read session window through the existing compaction write and publication receipt. The append-state query selects three existing bounded cache columns; it adds no query, worker operation, cache owner, or cross-store transaction.

The obsolete empty-key read disappears. Transcript-rewrite reconciliation moves unchanged to the existing reconciliation module to keep the append owner within its size cap. Physical-store identity checks, captured environment, writer-claim refusal, and sandbox execution-policy checks remain. Missing or stale display caches, unknown assistant facts, branch changes, and projection rebuilds retain their existing fallback. Actor hydration is unchanged. Actor-backed appends retain their existing display fallback; the targeted durable manual-compaction command runs through the metadata worker outside the actor transaction. Carrying resident actor display facts is a separate follow-up and is excluded from the savings claim.

## Evidence

Formatting, type-aware oxlint, the line-cap ratchet, and `git diff --check` pass. Production is +52/-38 lines (net +14); regression tests add 149 lines. The small production increase carries the existing display projection through its producer instead of triggering a later worker read and backfill.

Both allowed independent Codex review rounds completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings. A subsequent predicate factoring removes a duplicate compaction check without changing behavior; the line-cap ratchet passes. New real-worker regressions cover visibility after an in-process metadata patch and compaction display preservation after an intervening assistant write, including branch invalidation.

The final-head [changed-owner CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39167435270/job/117793793298) passed all 23 tests: 16 corpus tests and 7 publication tests, including both new regressions. The display fixture needed two setup corrections (required store path, then the existing process-based suite with a host database owner); neither changed production code or weakened assertions. Earlier local runners stalled before assertions in external-storage renames. After storage clearance and moving temporary data to the internal disk, both new regressions failed at their intended assertions with the production patch reversed, then passed with the landed production patch: compaction avoids the unnecessary display backfill while retaining branch invalidation, and repeated corpus listing sees an in-process metadata update without discarded admission reads. The full suites remain covered by the exact-head CI run.

The queued Testbox attempt was stopped and reconciled without executing tests, and its campaign slot was released. The original PR run has passed the changed tests, production/test types, type-aware lint, source contracts, Madge/architecture, and T1/dialect/worker ratchets; all three PostgreSQL shards and the required `openclaw/ci-gate` are green. The supplemental [Knip job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39168670086/job/117797187580) completed with zero new findings: production 58, full-tree 33, scripts 0 versus [scheduled main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39163574553/job/117782017361) at 58/34/0, compared by exact file/symbol. None is in a changed file. The remaining supplemental workflow was cancelled after the scan to avoid duplicating broad validation. Its Swedish translation failure also appears on [main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39163574553/job/117782015543); its non-required Responses fixture timeout is reported separately with unresolved main attribution. Neither is claimed green. The post-merge baseline runtime build passed, but the harness timed out while creating its synthetic account, before any Gateway workload. Its fixture processes and scratch have been removed. This setup failure supplies no compaction or warm-turn measurement; three alternating harness-v3 pairs remain incomplete. The source-derived estimate is 14 fewer SQL statements and 5 fewer requests per manual compaction: three discarded admission SELECTs/requests and approximately eleven display-read/backfill statements across two requests. This is not a measured result or latency claim.

PostgreSQL review approved exact head `c152b60ec041aed42acf05cfc2701f3856b62bca`: the wider append-state SELECT and display carry-over are engine-neutral, and writable admission uses the existing execution owner. Dropping the separate `onRegistryChange` forwarding loses no registry update: this store reader supplies `registry.assertAdmissionCurrent` as that callback, and its captured `assertCurrent` already invokes the same admission check while retaining the selected reader/continuation. Database preparation still owns registration publication; corpus results still pass the reader’s final authority check. No update, Doctor, migration, plugin-loading, or service-lifecycle code changes, so the published-driver update cell does not apply.

prs.title: perf(control-ui): load older history in 2 MiB pages
prs.body:
Related: #176385

## What Problem This Solves

Reaching the beginning of a long conversation requires too many small older-history requests and transcript prepends.

## User Impact

Older history loads in 2 MiB pages instead of 1 MiB. In the measured long histories, traversal takes 9 rather than 17 pages (normal) and 10 rather than 19 (tool-heavy), with total time falling from 6.07 to 3.74 seconds and 6.55 to 4.25 seconds. The accepted tradeoff is a higher median worst arrival frame: 195 → 213 ms and 142 → 171 ms. No migration or user action is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Double the byte budget at the existing history request owner, shared by direct older-page reads and staged prefetch. Keep the 1000-message limit: it does not bind at 2 MiB. Keep the startup budget and one automatic viewport-fill policy unchanged. The 2 MiB setting remains below the server's 6 MiB cap.

The original approximately 120 ms arrival-frame target was invalid because even the 1 MiB baseline exceeds it. The coordinator accepted the 35–38% traversal improvement and +18.6/+29.3 ms worst-arrival tradeoff. 5 MiB is deliberately excluded: larger pages carry more per-arrival work and the message limit can remove their benefit. No new scheduling, caching, configuration, or transport machinery is added.

## Evidence

The campaign began with a signed-in reload of a dashboard deep link showing 14 visual states over about 15 seconds. This change addresses deliberate backscroll after reload, not the already-separated startup path. All fixtures and captures used here are synthetic.

### Curve

Times are milliseconds, shown as median [Q1, Q3] across seven runs. Arrival is each run's worst completed arrival frame. Fill is each run's median per-page fill. Byte totals cover history responses only.

| History | Budget (MiB) | Pages | Total traversal ms | Worst arrival frame ms | Fill/page ms | Largest raw page MiB | Total raw / deflate estimate MiB |

| normal | 2 | 9 | 3737.0 [3723.8, 3754.3] | 213.3 [205.2, 214.5] | 185.7 [180.4, 189.4] | 2.001 | 16.303 / 2.725 |

| normal | 5 | 5 | 2585.8 [2563.8, 2610.3] | 223.9 [217.5, 228.9] | 205.4 [193.5, 209.4] | 4.057 | 16.295 / 2.721 |
| tool-heavy | 1 | 19 | 6550.1 [6490.3, 6585.2] | 141.7 [139.3, 142.7] | 135.5 [132.8, 140.2] | 1.002 | 18.572 / 3.086 |
| tool-heavy | 2 | 10 | 4247.7 [4242.6, 4282.6] | 171.0 [163.8, 173.9] | 160.3 [155.1, 162.5] | 2.002 | 18.555 / 3.074 |
| tool-heavy | 3 | 7 | 3451.4 [3339.4, 3508.5] | 174.4 [168.9, 200.8] | 167.7 [165.2, 169.2] | 2.981 | 18.549 / 3.068 |

The tool-heavy 3 and 5 MiB requests return the same pages: the 1,000-message cap binds at about 2.981 MiB. Normal 5 MiB requests bind at about 4.057 MiB. Response envelopes can slightly exceed the message-only budget.

### Paired deltas against 1 MiB

Candidate minus baseline, in round order. All values are milliseconds. No slow sample was discarded.

<details>
<summary>Measurement method, reload controls, and attribution</summary>

### Environment and method

AWS Crabbox `cbx_4964b2ff9098`, fixed `c7a.4xlarge`, 16 vCPUs (AMD EPYC 9R14), 30 GiB RAM. Node v24.19.0, pnpm v12.11.1, and the repository Playwright Chromium build (Chrome for Testing 156.0.8078.4). One instance and one boot ID served the complete comparison. Pre-run load averages ranged from 0.52 to 2.47. Setup, UI build, and initial attribution succeeded in [run_ea1047a451d2147bc40f4b0708f9e31e](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_ea1047a451d2147bc40f4b0708f9e31e). The curve continued through the sanctioned SSH transport on that retained lease.

The production-bundle Team-scale benchmark retained its canonical shell, Online roster, plugin inventory, and common 240-message tail. The older prefix contains either 4,000 plain-text messages (1,000-character questions and 7,200-character answers) or 6,200 messages in 100 tool-heavy turns (30 call/result pairs per turn, collapsed activity). Full histories contain 4,240 and 6,440 messages respectively. These are long synthetic stress cases, not copies of a private conversation.

Seven rounds per history shape covered 1/2/3/5 MiB, reversing order on even rounds: **56 unprofiled browser runs**. All use the same bundle and source, Chromium, 35 ms synthetic inbound latency, and 4 ms minimum reply spacing. The benchmark changes only outgoing older-history `maxBytes` after the reload measurement. The server fixture honors that budget and the unchanged 1,000-message limit. Startup requests remain untouched.

Each measured page goes through the native history owner with staging disabled (`loadOlderMessages(false)`) to isolate one request and one prepend. The driver moves to older content between pages and reaches the beginning. It validates progress, exactly one history response per step, and a visible transcript viewport. This is a controlled page-through experiment; it does not measure continuous-wheel prefetch effectiveness or a real Gateway network.

Page fill is response arrival to the visible-viewport receipt after two paint opportunities. LoAF records are drained after the phase. Arrival-frame statistics include completed frames after response arrival and before that page's filled receipt; the next scroll can begin in the same task as the receipt, so its later-ending frame is attributed to the overall traversal instead. The whole-traversal maximum includes every scroll and the final movement to the beginning. Raw data retains the timestamps and the original overinclusive prototype field; `analyze.py` reconstructs the completed-arrival metric. Frames below the browser's 50 ms LoAF threshold are conservatively reported as at most 50 ms.

Bytes below are actual history response JSON bytes. Compression is a separate level-1, fresh-context permessage-deflate estimate, excluding WebSocket/TLS overhead; the mock transport does not negotiate compression. Estimates run outside the measured interval. Profiled setup runs and the two superseded boundary-calibration attempts are excluded from the curve.

### Reload control

All 56 reloads issue **zero boot `chat.history` calls** and one unchanged **38,763-byte `chat.startup` response**. This synthetic response does not model the live retained-receipt fast path. No reload timing metric regresses under the campaign's non-overlapping-IQR or ≥6/7 paired-sign-plus-size rule. The occasional slow paints remain in the data. Because the budget override activates after reload, these are unchanged-code controls, not a shipped-candidate reload proof.

### Attribution and limits

Source-mapped `--cpu-profile` captures execute `requestOlderChatHistoryPage`, `performOlderMessagesLoad`, the pane projection, and the real transcript render path. On the 1 MiB diagnostic runs, Solid flush contains 65.4% of sampled normal-history work and 62.1% of tool-heavy work. `maxTranscriptScrollOffset` accounts for 19.4% and 15.5% self time; its principal chain is `syncHistoryObserver` → `isMaintenanceScroll` → transcript geometry. The supplied live source-mapped frame places the same geometry function at 12.3% of sampled busy time. This demonstrates the relevant hot path at a comparable share, while the synthetic long histories and controlled scroll pattern limit extrapolation to a particular live conversation.

The immediate history-apply function accounts for only 0.9–1.5% inclusive time in those diagnostic runs. The evidence points to render/layout work, not a large synchronous history-apply loop. It does not prove that a slicing change at the request owner would remove that cost, and no scheduling, caching, or transport workaround was added. Remaining rendering cost is not claimed to be inherent.

The separate 2 MiB `--cpu-profile-compare` captures preserve that attribution: Solid flush contains 58.1% (normal) and 54.8% (tool-heavy), direct history application 1.0% and 1.4%, and transcript geometry 15.4% and 12.8%. Median synchronous message dispatch is approximately 11.0 and 10.2 ms. These profiles are diagnostic, not samples in the timing table.

</details>

Final head: `e7b1e7e8d8bea1dfe40c71dace29f3b39a726e2d`. Autoreview is clean through P2, including the follow-up correction to the real-Gateway request-budget assertion.

The native-owner budget regression failed with the original 1 MiB value (expected 2097152, received 1048576), then passed with 2 MiB. All 74 focused unit tests pass on the final head. Five files cover the owner, one automatic viewport fill, startup/history, reply navigation, and scroll-maintenance intent.

Final-head AWS proof on `cbx_887ccab15d09`, `c7a.4xlarge`:

|---|---|---:|

Unit commands use `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <file> --maxWorkers=1`; native E2E adds `run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts`. The native tests preserve every-frame anchoring, reach the first message, exhaust paging, and protect cold/warm reload behavior. The real-Gateway test checks actual response budgets and no older-page reads during its long-session reload. Browser layout and real-Gateway setup require the longer E2E wall times; no new fixture boots were added.

The **full UI E2E suite completed on the final head** in AWS `cbx_794664ca5450`, fixed `c7a.4xlarge`: [full-suite run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_07c7758c0ca0b57f1dee2472116a55d6). Original result: **824 files passed, 6 failed, 3 skipped** (833); **3,583 tests passed, 4 failed, 7 skipped** (3,594), **6,182 seconds wall time**. prs.title: fix(ui): keep plugin settings views through reconnects
prs.body:
Related: #174925, #174045, #174046

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Memory overview, Memory search results, the typed query, opened memory files, and plugin settings drafts are wiped when the Gateway connection briefly drops, restarts, or republishes plugin capabilities for the same client and account.

## User Impact

User impact: plugin Settings panels (Memory overview and Memory search today) stay open through a temporary Gateway disconnect or restart; search waits for the connection and keeps earlier results. Switching account, client, credentials, or access, or a connect rejection, still starts a fresh panel.

## Why This Change Was Made

Since Memory search moved into the memory-core plugin, the plugin Settings host tied each mounted view's lifetime to `connected` and `connectionEpoch`, so every transport transition disposed and remounted the view. This follows the offline-first series (#174022, #174043, #174044, #174045, #174046, #174059): retain presentation through same-identity transport loss, reset on identity change.

The host now ends a view only on client replacement, Gateway presentation scope change (credentials, recovery scope, retired offline recovery, user), connect rejection (hello cleared), operator read-access loss, or an agent, engine, route, or advertised method-catalog change. `connected`, `connectionEpoch`, and engine availability reach the mounted view through `update(snapshot)` so plugins can disable writes offline. `context.request` still requires a connected client with operator access before dispatch, and now rejects a reply to a request sent in an earlier `connectionEpoch`, so a retained view never applies a previous transport's response.

In memory-core's Memories view, reopening a file whose read failed (for example, interrupted by the drop) retries it, and the search Retry button is disabled while offline. The Overview controller already reloads on `connected`/`connectionEpoch` changes through `update()`.

Docs: `docs/web/control-ui/offline-and-reconnect.md` and the Settings presentation contract in `docs/plugins/feature-plugins.md`.

## Evidence

- Host boundary (`control-ui-settings-view.solid.test.tsx`): disposal after client replacement, recovery-scope change, retired offline recovery, and connect rejection; existing agent/engine/route/runtime retirement still passes.
- Real WebSocket transport (`control-ui-settings-view.transport.node.test.tsx`): a reply held across a same-client reconnect rejects while the view stays alive and a later request dispatches. Agent, runtime, method-catalog, account/recovery-scope reassignment, and operator-read revocation each abort the retained view; its held reply rejects and a later call from the retained callback never reaches the server (checked against the server's frame ledger after an acknowledged barrier request).
- Page integration (`memory-page.test.ts`): the mounted view survives disconnect/reconnect with advancing epoch and `connected` updates, then retires on client replacement; plugin publication and Gateway boot change keep the view but reject earlier replies; client, method-catalog, and agent changes still retire synchronously.
- Memory search (`memories.test.tsx`): results and query survive a reconnect without a new search, an interrupted file read retries on reopen, and Retry is disabled offline.
- Local: focused Vitest for the files above plus memory-core overview/controller, all green; `tsgo:ui`, ui-other/ui-pages test tsconfigs, and the extensions test tsconfig clean; type-aware oxlint clean on touched core files. Not visual: no layout or styling change beyond the existing disabled-button state.

prs.title: fix(agents): pin legacy default agent workspace on load to prevent silent per-agent move
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A `default: true` agent with **no explicit `workspace`** (inheriting `agents.defaults.workspace`) silently changes its resolved workspace from `<workspace>` to `<workspace>/<agentId>` on upgrade. The new per-agent directory is scaffolded with a blank default identity, and the agent's `memory/` and `outputs/` move to the empty subdir — a silent identity + memory reset, with no error or prompt. Fixes #127802.

## Root Cause

`resolveAgentWorkspaceDir` returns `agents.defaults.workspace` for the legacy default agent only when `tryResolveInheritedWorkspaceAgentId` identifies it. That relies on `getRetainedLegacyDefaultAgentId` — a process-local `WeakMap` keyed by the config object, seeded during the roster migration that strips `default: true`. Across config re-materialization on the read/load path, the config object resolved against is not the one the retention was seeded on, so the retention is lost, `inheritedWorkspaceAgentId` is `undefined`, and resolution falls through to `path.join(defaults.workspace, agentId)` → `<workspace>/<agentId>`.

The write path (`io.write.ts`) already pins the workspace via `materializeWorkspace: true`, but a config that is never rewritten after upgrade (e.g. a read-only mounted config) never receives that pin — so the read path must not depend on the fragile in-process retention.

## Fix

`migratePersistedImplicitMainRoster` now defaults `materializeWorkspace` to `true` when it processes a legacy default agent (callers can still pass `false`). Retiring the `default: true` marker therefore also pins the legacy default agent's workspace into the config **data** on every read path (load, snapshot, validation) — mirroring the write path — so resolution stays correct regardless of `WeakMap` object identity. The pin only applies to a legacy default agent that has no explicit `workspace` (an agent with an explicit workspace is untouched), and it resolves to `agents.defaults.workspace` (its historical value), so behavior is preserved rather than changed. No on-disk config is rewritten on read.

## Evidence

Added a regression test in `legacy.roster.test.ts`: loading a config with `main: { default: true }`, a sibling agent with an explicit `workspace`, and `agents.defaults.workspace` set now yields `entries.main.workspace === defaults.workspace` (previously `main.workspace` was absent, which produced the `<workspace>/main` fallback). Confirmed the failing behavior on latest `main` (`resolveAgentWorkspaceDir` and its `// Read-time migration removes default:true before write-time workspace pinning can run.` comment are unchanged).

prs.title: fix: wait for offline maintenance during Gateway startup
prs.body:
Related: #175730

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway startup exits while a live offline-maintenance process holds shared state, causing service restart churn instead of waiting for maintenance to finish.

## User Impact

Startup, including after an update or service restart, uses its existing five-minute admission budget for offline maintenance and reports the current holder's PID/role every 30 seconds, followed by admission or failure. If the budget expires, the operator can identify the holder and let it finish before retrying. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The earlier bootstrap snapshot admitted only `StateDatabaseAdmissionPendingError` into its retry loop. A live offline owner raises `StateDatabaseOfflineMaintenanceError`, so startup exited before reaching the run loop's existing ownership wait. Both now use the same acquisition-only retry; admitted discovery and cleanup still execute once. Cancellation, exact database matching, the live maintenance fence, lock formats, and independent update-driver custody are preserved. The new start never kills the maintenance owner.

Current main already bounds launcher-dependent CLI maintenance after parent death (#174268) and includes holder diagnostics (#176131). Source inspection found no separate shutdown maintenance subprocess to reparent; this change addresses early-startup contention. The broader report’s alleged shutdown-maintenance producer and alert behavior remain unverified and are not claimed fixed by this PR.

The wait retains the selected snapshot path/environment and fixed deadline. Each attempt rechecks current host admission, captures identity only after admission, and checks cancellation before acquisition and after the await. Progress messages use the current refusal, so a successor holder is reported rather than treated as captured authority. No detached work is added.

Simplification kept the existing owner, retry helper, cancellation, and test tables. Production is +35/-4 (net +31), tests +67/-28 (net +39), docs +2/-0. The production growth supplies bounded progress and terminal diagnostics; deleting unrelated lifecycle safeguards to offset it would broaden this fix.

## Evidence

[ClawSweeper re-review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176548#issuecomment-6255912143) on the final head: ready for maintainer review, no findings or remaining author work. Its earlier merge-conflict and issue-scope requests are resolved; live-proof suggestions remain optional under the stated policy.

Current head: `bfb688029f7179758fd1fa4164c7a49cae2784cb`, after merging current main and preserving its snapshot-family work. [Exact-head CI run 39172601713](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39172601713) completed: 62 successful jobs, 26 skipped, and two failed jobs—the confirmed inherited unsafe-history test shard and its aggregate CI gate. All PostgreSQL, typecheck, and lint lanes passed; no failure caused by this patch was identified. The prior-head failures below are kept separate from current-head evidence.

- Deterministic regressions in `openclaw-state-db-readonly.snapshot-admission.test.ts`: `waits for offline custody before admitting one discovery snapshot`; retained schema-custody coverage; refusal cases for unclassified errors, another database, default no-wait, exhausted budget, cancellation, and shutdown. They also check changing holder diagnostics and exactly one snapshot/callback/cleanup.
- Changed-file oxfmt and source-backed core oxlint: passed (two TypeScript files; formatting also covered the docs change). Independent source review: no actionable P0–P2 findings. Prescribed isolated Codex branch autoreview: scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings; assessment only, no tests run. prs.title: fix(codex): steer busy sessions and unblock thread handoffs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Messages and peer results sent to a busy agent can wait behind the work that needs them, while an exact-thread handoff can wait indefinitely for a Codex process retained by another session. This routes busy peer input through the existing active queue, preserves its original source identity across recovery, and waits for the retired thread rather than requiring its entire process to exit.

## User Impact

A busy recipient accepts ordinary messages and explicit followup into its active input queue and returns admission only. An idle recipient starts a turn and can return a correlated completion. Self-send, paused-child resume, provenance/display, generation checks, and native writer locking retain their existing owners. Accepted input stays in receiver custody; RPC acknowledgment is not transcript-consumption proof, and confirmation waits settle within their existing request budget.

Two related delivery failures are also repaired: a captured receiver that finishes before admission can retain the ordinary follow-up path after source revalidation, and fresh native child input uses internal completion rather than requiring the child to have a messaging tool.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the recipient’s active queue for dependency input, preserve the original source identity during recovery, and release only the exact retired native thread before handoff. Known receiver settlement before admission must remain distinct from an authority refusal; native child follow-ups must retain their existing internal completion owner.

## Behavior decision

The [review asks whether busy explicit followup should return active-queue admission instead of a separate completion](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174967#issuecomment-6228365441). I recommend the busy/idle distinction because dependency input must be available to the work that needs it. The [earlier owner decision](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160842#issuecomment-5882083686) expressly preserved separate-turn followup; this proposal deliberately changes that contract.

Codex supplies a concrete reference, rather than just a naming analogy. Its [followup_task handler](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/83086188ae0614bd882818ff1aa23f3194962012/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/multi_agents_v2/followup_task.rs#L42) selects TriggerTurn. The [delivery-mode contract](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/83086188ae0614bd882818ff1aa23f3194962012/codex-rs/core/src/agent/types.rs#L59) means active-turn delivery or starting work when idle, through the [shared messaging owner](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/83086188ae0614bd882818ff1aa23f3194962012/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/multi_agents_v2/message_tool.rs#L41).

This PR follows that distinction: [busy delivery](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/441b87882afcd725acff2e3137d50fa3fca64b8e/src/agents/tools/sessions-send-tool.delivery.ts#L217) returns admission, preserving receiver custody and uncertainty; idle delivery retains a new turn and correlated completion. Consumption still waits for supported checkpoints, including tool completion. Admission promises neither consumption nor a separate reply. The compatibility cost is real: callers using busy followup specifically to obtain a separate correlated completion lose that behavior. The requested owner decision is whether dependency-delivery liveness justifies that change; Codex precedent and the supplied runtime captures support it but do not confer approval.

## Evidence

### Current revision: conflict resolution against current main

Head `441b87882afcd725acff2e3137d50fa3fca64b8e` merges prior head `62078dfa6ee15ae944ab00c70f6567d363508d1e` with pinned main `89207ad525fc581f59eaa6ed8c999474cb78b376`; tree `5afdf1c01ac08155420489b2fc69512da32445d1`. The three conflicts were generated prompt snapshots, regenerated exclusively with the canonical generator. All eight snapshots verify current.

**115 focused tests pass** across native steering, embedded steering, queue authority, directed send policy, tool guidance, and snapshot generation. Of the 24 PR-owned source/test files, 23 are byte-identical to the prior reviewed revision. The remaining file only incorporates main's independent `session_status capabilities=true` guidance; the PR-owned send behavior is unchanged. Formatting and diff checks pass. Prior independent P0–P2 review and native/upgrade evidence retain their stated scope for the unchanged behavior; exact-head CI now passes (175 reported checks, no failed or pending checks).

The prior revision already consumed upstream HTTP teardown repair #175846. This merge adds no new delivery policy. The explicit busy-`followup` decision below still requires maintainer approval. No operator Gateway was changed for these integration checks.

### Earlier integrated-main validation

The local candidate merges PR head `e56ea81b6caf04fd12f08e981fb412d144632fee` with main `feeafd6b1e79ff4b8791ed6aa3096df4c47a6dae`. Production changes merged without conflicts; three prompt snapshots were regenerated with the canonical generator. The frozen candidate tree is `1ab9f1112ac46e20828da80d97d01a25f2141a11`.

All runtime evidence below uses synthetic messages and fresh isolated state. No operator Gateway, user conversation, or production workspace was used. The Gateway cases use its authenticated HTTP `sessions_send` route, enabled only in the task fixture; receiving turns use the real native Codex 0.163.0 process and provider.

- **Busy followup:** while the recipient was executing a bounded checkpoint command, explicit `followup` returned `accepted` / `steered`. Its actual final model reply consumed the marker. The assertion excludes the attributed peer transcript row.
- **Returned peer result:** an actual idle worker produced its result; the busy requester received one attributed result row and subsequently included the marker in its actual final reply. The requester's original prompt did not contain the result marker. Its native work continued after result admission.
- **Reset after preparation:** a test-only module-load barrier pauses the real `runAgentStep` immediately after `prepareSessionDeliveryGeneration` returns. Canonical `sessions.reset` runs before the original code resumes. Delivery rejects because the original session changed. A transparent native stdio observer records zero result-marker frames to the original native thread; a read-only check of the original transcript records zero marker rows. No production test hook or guard bypass was added.
- **Native handoff:** real old and successor app-server processes use the same isolated native home. The actual release owner observes the old client's exact `thread/closed`; the successor resumes that thread while the old process still serves a real retained idle sibling. Native persistence locking remains authoritative.
- **Stable upgrade:** official OpenClaw 2026.10.4 and its own CLI write/read a synthetic session. After stopping that Gateway, the candidate's canonical `doctor --fix --non-interactive` migration succeeds, creates pre-migration backups, and the candidate preserves the session ID, transcript count, and marker. Direct startup correctly refuses the older schema until Doctor runs. This PR introduces no additional schema.

Focused owner tests: **131 passed across three shards**. Canonical runtime build, generated prompt check, formatting of all 23 changed files, and diff checks pass. A fresh frozen P2 review reports no findings. Current-main core type checking was stopped through its cleanup owner after an extended active compile and remains for PR CI. Scoped lint reports only two existing file-length violations that this patch increases: `sessions-send-tool.ts` 706→707 and `run-attempt-dispatch.ts` 710→721 (limit 700); these are disclosed rather than suppressed.

### Additional delivery-owner repairs on `3071a5f`

These eight-file changes build on the published merge head `3071a5f47f4a4b15427ca5aa1b0ef80834d6ab41`; the earlier runtime/upgrade/handoff evidence above remains evidence for its stated revision.

- **Receiver ends before admission:** the captured embedded target can finish or be replaced while an input waits in its FIFO. Known target loss now uses the existing target-unavailable classification. The source is revalidated before ordinary follow-up fallback; a revoked caller or a live receiver's authority refusal remains an error. Explicit `steer` still refuses an unavailable target. Accepted or unconfirmed input keeps its existing non-replayable custody.
- **Native child input:** fresh `sessions_send` input to a classified native subagent uses `automatic` internal completion. The existing task/one-way completion owner still returns the result; the request does not grant a message tool. Ordinary peer and canonical ACP targets retain `message_tool_only`. Access to another parent's child remains forbidden.

Synthetic owner proof on this public base passed in separate focused runs: **35 embedded-queue tests** (including RED→GREEN FIFO receiver settlement/replacement and caller/receiver revocation controls), **20 tool-policy tests** (including owned child, forbidden unowned child, ordinary peer, and persisted canonical ACP metadata), and **one actual Codex attempt** that resumes a saved message-less child thread and captures its visible internal final. The Codex transport is controlled in that last test; it is not an external-provider proof. Owning `agents-other`/`agents-tools` type graphs and the focused new Codex test type graph pass; typed plugin lint, formatting, and diff checks pass. Fresh P2 reviews of the changed owners report no findings.

An additional **two-case isolated test on the matching local candidate** exercises its preserved message-tool availability guard: `automatic` resumes the exact saved child and captures the final with an empty message-tool catalog, while `message_tool_only` fails with the exact availability error before `turn/start`. That additional guard is absent from this public base; this does not claim that the public test exercised it. No operator conversation, protected source, or production Gateway was used for these tests.

Scoped typed core lint passes without changing or suppressing any rule. The ownership-lookup failure formatting and logging moved unchanged to the existing send helper; the producer retains its lookup classification and all authority decisions. This keeps the native-child conditional below the 700-line limit. The final layout also passes the 20 tool-policy cases again, two separately filtered existing lookup-error regressions, and the owning agents-tools type graph. The existing `run-attempt-dispatch.ts` 710→721 disclosure above is unchanged by these additional repairs. Broader current-head checks remain for PR CI.

### Maintainer decision still requested

This deliberately changes explicit `followup` for a busy recipient to admission into that recipient's active input queue, with an admission-only receipt. An idle recipient still gets a separate turn and can return a correlated completion. The earlier owner decision in #160842 preserved explicit followup as a separate-turn escape hatch; this proposal asks to replace that behavior, and does not claim approval has already been granted.

Codex 0.163.0 uses `MessageDeliveryMode::TriggerTurn` for `followup_task`: an active session drains its mailbox, while an idle session may start a turn. Matching that busy/idle distinction prevents a dependency result from waiting behind the work that needs it. The motivating reports included messages waiting tens of minutes or hours; that history supports this change, without claiming every reported hang had the same cause. Input is consumed at supported execution checkpoints, not by forcibly interrupting an arbitrary blocking tool.

Security review should assess the complete preparation-to-effect chain and the intentional busy-followup contract. The runtime evidence strengthens that assessment; it does not substitute for the maintainer's product/security decision.

CI caught that the new saved-subsession regression was absent from the full-suite database-worker inventory. The existing manifest now registers it. prs.title: fix(codex): preserve native catalog and completion continuity
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Caller-dependent tool declarations and conversation metadata can change a Codex thread’s creation policy while native work still owns it. A valid reply then tries to replace or resume the busy thread and fails with “claimed by active work.”

Producers supply stable declarations; the existing native binding retains the catalog Codex actually accepted while work protects the thread. Genuine additions publish through the existing idle replacement/history handoff. Current executors, permissions and invocation authority still decide every call; accepted declarations never grant execution.

Related completion handoffs can also stall when terminal children keep the parent execution pin, plugin dispatch omits result context, or a harmless busy refusal retires the shared client. This revision repairs those existing owners and retains current native input admission, so pending results can continue without weakening active-work or permission guards.

## User Impact

Owner replies can continue on a protected thread. New tools wait until idle publication, and an implementation whose final prepared schema or description differs from the accepted declaration stays unavailable until then. Both active and fallback executors are prepared before comparison, including in-place schema mutations.

Producer-annotated conversation metadata travels as a complete current-turn snapshot rather than immutable policy. Exact range validation preserves configured policy, execution hints and later suffixes; invalid annotations fail closed. The existing parent-local inference relay supplies the current snapshot on every request. Nonrelay connections use the existing developer handoff before turns and after compaction, avoiding native additional-context deduplication.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep each responsibility with its existing owner: core producers own declarations, the native binding owns acceptance/publication, current tool preparation owns executable definitions, and conversation producers identify transient context. There is no additional catalog manager, pending queue or execution-authority store. This coherent stage prevents the same busy-thread replacement failure across declaration and conversation-context changes.

## Maintainer decision requested

Approve optional `hostCapabilities.readCoreToolDeclarations(tools)` and the existing binding’s accepted-catalog receipt, including deferring genuinely new declarations until native work is idle. The method is optional for existing harness consumers and is used for registration, not execution authority. Unknown remote catalogs remain preserved with an actionable refusal rather than guessed declarations. SDK/publication-policy acceptance is still required; no approving owner decision is claimed.

## Compatibility

No SQL schema migration or configuration option is added. Validated catalog receipt versions 1, 2 and 3 remain readable without rewriting existing receipts. Missing older receipts use the existing native read owner; corrupt/incompatible receipts preserve the thread. Native-owned supervision catalogs and current permission/authority guards remain authoritative. Existing receipt/fingerprint guards are retained at both admission and writer reuse.

**Nonrelay compaction limit:** native continuation may run before the host’s postcompaction callback. The developer handoff restores subsequent requests; it cannot guarantee that immediate continuation sees the latest snapshot. The relay path avoids this gap by supplying the complete current snapshot per request. The native captures below now exercise both modes and directly observe that nonrelay gap and later restoration. They do not remove the immediate-continuation limitation.

## Behavior decision

The [review's SDK/publication question](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174900#issuecomment-6227772583) has two separable decisions. I recommend the data-only SDK reader and binding-owned accepted catalog. The [reader](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/22f8ce7ca9e273a0b3d7a1fdca65e2c2bf364d40/src/agents/harness/host-tool-declarations.ts#L68) accepts only the exact surface built by that admitted host, checks its lifetime, and returns cloned declarations without executors. Core remains the declaration owner; the native binding remains the owner of what Codex accepted.

This preserves the native ownership established by [#134660](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f5f44faeca4e68b178712152e059436f98888e50). [Protected selection](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/22f8ce7ca9e273a0b3d7a1fdca65e2c2bf364d40/extensions/codex/src/app-server/protected-thread-tool-catalog.ts#L19) retains that catalog while native work protects it. Current executors still enforce permissions and declaration compatibility; catalog receipts grant no execution authority. Changed declarations can publish when the existing idle owner permits it.

The nonrelay context question needs a different answer: do not treat the observed immediate post-compaction gap as solved. [The asynchronous handoff](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/22f8ce7ca9e273a0b3d7a1fdca65e2c2bf364d40/extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-compaction.ts#L53) can follow native continuation. I recommend deferring that cutover unless immediate context delivery is repaired or an area owner explicitly accepts the gap. Neither SDK acceptance nor passing adapter tests resolves that separate limitation.

## Evidence

### Earlier test consolidation (66cd068f48ef)

Revision `66cd068f48ef04e13c45afb7aa3f38a857f16562` removes only the weaker 53-line duplicate executor matrix. The stronger 10-case `review-fix-catalog.test.ts` suite remains byte-identical and owns active/fallback schema and description rejection with arguments valid under both schemas, unchanged-definition execution, and receipt controls. The original two-file baseline passed 16/16 cases; the retained owner passes 10/10. Formatting, whitespace checks, and a fresh independent P0–P2 deletion review pass. Production is byte-identical to `b00a6ee430a1ad444f2f1355bd864a594773b2c0`, so its qualified native/build evidence below is reused; it is not a newly executed native trace. This paragraph records that test-only revision; current integration proof follows below.

### Fresh native lifecycle qualification with a separate transport prerequisite

The exact public candidate `22f8ce7ca9e273a0b3d7a1fdca65e2c2bf364d40` was built and booted with official native **0.162.0**. A real child exposed an independent inference-HTTP defect: metadata, retained source and model admission succeeded, but saving its assignment inherited the listener's already closed startup binding lease and became an owner-denied 403. Current upstream main reproduces the same HTTP failure without this PR's catalog changes. The narrow transport repair is now #176311; no lease or permission guard was weakened.

For the lifecycle check, a clean integration build `93fd3c1348dbfb162b93578d9ec7ab32945ea826` combines this PR's exact catalog code with transport commit `bf58bfa2429ac65d7ce904c0dd43585f1a82ba51`. The real native child then reaches the local scripted provider and records a successful final. Its internal completion reaches the creating conversation and produces another actual native final; a fresh authenticated owner return produces its exact expected final. The physical OpenClaw session and native client survive. A separate protected-policy probe refuses before any additional provider I/O and preserves that healthy client.

This does **not** prove uninterrupted native-thread identity. After the child terminates, owner and System turns legitimately offer different `message` and `skill_workshop` schemas. Exact native declaration comparisons and debug lifecycle records show two permitted idle catalog rotations; the owner's original catalog is restored exactly. The collectors retain their failed, overstrict same-thread assertion. Independent native-journal and authenticated RPC readbacks qualify the actual child, completion and owner-return outcomes; the failed collector is not relabeled passing.

All inputs are synthetic, provider responses are locally scripted, and no observer or authority hooks are installed. Both task Gateways, proxies, state directories and TLS private keys were cleaned up. This is combined-build evidence with the separately published transport prerequisite, not a successful standalone `22f8ce7ca9e` lifecycle capture. Protected legacy **receiptless** catalog recovery remains unexercised by this native run; the exact-head stable-upgrade proof below is separate. SDK/publication-policy approval and the documented nonrelay immediate-compaction limitation remain open.


### Fresh exact-head stable upgrade proof

Exact current head `22f8ce7ca9e273a0b3d7a1fdca65e2c2bf364d40` was built in 89.1 seconds and exercised against data written by the latest official stable release, **2026.10.4**. The stable host and its separately installed official stable Codex plugin created an actual synthetic native conversation and assistant final using native **0.160.0**. After the stable Gateway stopped, the candidate's supported `doctor --fix --non-interactive` migrated that same isolated state from state schema **20→27** and agent schema **24→31**. The exact candidate then started and native **0.162.0** produced a fresh actual assistant final in the same physical session.

The original stable assistant final, message content/order, and every prior projected message field were preserved. The only newly exposed projection field is `usage.contextUsage`: source inspection confirms the old sanitizer omitted it while the candidate normalizes/preserves it. Full history projection is therefore explicitly not called byte-identical. The stable-written binding genuinely lacked a managed catalog receipt; after the successful new turn the candidate persisted version 3. The native thread safely rotated across differing release runtimes/declarations. This proves existing stable-written data loads and continues; it does not prove protected receiptless catalog recovery or same-native-thread continuity across the upgrade.

All owner identities, credentials and provider responses were synthetic; the provider wire was scripted locally while actual Gateways, native app servers, migration and persistence owners ran unchanged. No operator state or copied credentials were used. Both task Gateways, proxy, workspace/state and TLS private key were cleaned up. The preceding registry-TLS fixture failure remains separate failed setup evidence.

prs.title: test(ui): tolerate WebKit subpixel drift in menu shortcut alignment
prs.body:
Related: #174044

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the required `checks-ui (1/3)` WebKit step fails intermittently in `menu-shortcut-alignment.browser.test.tsx` when WebKit reports shortcut hint bounds about 0.03px apart (e.g. right 220.304 vs 220.274, width 37.52 vs 37.55), blocking unrelated Control UI PRs.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Control UI PRs stop failing on this WebKit flake, and PRs that touch Solid menu code or its WebKit tests now run the WebKit browser step.

## Why This Change Was Made

WebKit can keep subpixel transform rounding from the menu's opening scale. The check had already been loosened to `toBeCloseTo(x, 3)`, but that still only allows 0.0005px. The test now compares each hint's right edge and width before and after `side-panel.css` loads with an explicit 0.5px absolute tolerance. A real layout shift from the panel stylesheet moves hints by whole pixels and still fails. The row-alignment, check-glyph, and mobile-hidden assertions are unchanged.

While proving this, CI skipped the WebKit step for this PR. The WebKit project runs `src/components/solid/*.browser.test.tsx`, but the CI selection owners didn't include Solid menu files. Adding `ui/src/components/solid/{menu*.{ts,tsx},overlay.css}` (same pattern as the existing `solid/session-hovercard*` entry) means edits to the Solid menu, its stylesheet (which owns the `.shortcut-kbd` alignment rules), or its WebKit tests run WebKit. It reuses the first UI row and adds no runner.

## Evidence

- `menu-shortcut-alignment.browser.test.tsx` passes locally in Chromium, and passes 3/3 runs in WebKit (`OPENCLAW_UI_WEBKIT=1 pnpm --dir ui test --project=webkit`). The 0.03px drift does not reproduce on macOS, so this PR's WebKit step in `checks-ui (1/3)` is the CI proof.
- `test/scripts/ci-webkit-selection.test.ts`: 20/20 pass. The new selection rows (`solid/menu.tsx`, `solid/menu-shortcut-alignment.browser.test.tsx`, `solid/overlay.css`) would fail on the base owners list.
- On the earlier head, the WebKit step ran in `checks-ui (1/3)` and passed.
- That run's only red (`ci-test-runtime-trial` FRV digest) also failed on clean main `993ec298`: #175107 changed the FRV Docker plan without refreshing the pinned digest. Fixed directly on main in 22384b67802, and this branch is rebased onto it.

## What Problem This Solves

Markdown tooltip and table listeners are not consistently retired with their content owner.

## User Impact

File-path copying, table scrolling, expanded tables, keyboard dismissal and linked-session navigation keep their existing behavior. Content cleanup now explicitly retires the associated event handlers.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing `listen` helper supplies teardown for tooltip clicks and table-dialog events. Table scrolling uses one passive capture listener per existing table owner instead of permanent listeners on each table viewport. The existing owner map selects the nearest registered owner when a message and its transcript both own enhancements.

The change adds 31 production lines for explicit teardown and capture delegation. It introduces no per-node registry or state owner. Modal autofocus, delayed link-dismiss routing, lazy loading and Mermaid resource ownership are preserved.

prs.title: refactor(ui): tie widget work to owner publication
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Widget owners publish synchronous state and own completion receipts, but their Solid shells separately watch revisions to schedule committed-DOM work. Markdown image lifetimes and lobster input bursts also have a clearer owner than a rendering effect.

## User Impact

Pending browser/terminal work retires with its existing completion receipt across reconnect and context replacement. Lobster reactions consume the complete mode/outcome setter burst. Markdown image requests remain with an unchanged document and retire when it is replaced. Existing host tags, classes, selectors, focus behavior, lazy boundaries, and markdown trust rules are preserved; no visual change is intended.

## Why This Change Was Made

Browser and terminal publication now schedule their committed-DOM work with Solid 2 `onSettled`, removing renderer callbacks and revision-watching effects. A keyed markdown document owns sanitized DOM and image cleanup; its tracked parsing memo still responds to lazy highlighter readiness. The lobster bridge coalesces native setters into one settled owner update. No dependency, configuration, renderer, or shared abstraction is added.

Main independently converted deferred reader sections to the shared intersection primitive in #176449. The merge keeps that exact implementation and retains this PR's viewport lifecycle regression. Four effects remain in this PR's before/after scope and all four disappear.

| Check | Result |

prs.title: fix: reuse the UI build cache without an explicit root
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated UI bundling when `pnpm ui:build` or the UI step of `pnpm build` runs without `BUILD_ALL_CACHE_ROOT`.

## User Impact

Unchanged UI builds reuse the default content cache. Explicit cache roots and `OPENCLAW_BUILD_CACHE=0` keep their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The UI launcher required an explicit cache root before enabling caching, although the cache owner already resolves the default root. Remove that redundant prerequisite and let the existing owner decide the root. Extend the existing launcher/cache regression to cover default and explicit roots, including invalidation and prerequisite failures. Synthetic launcher fixtures explicitly opt out of caching.

The simplify pass retained one production-condition deletion and the existing test fixture; no new cache policy, dependency, or timeout budget. Diff: production +1/-4, tests +3/-2 (including formatting).

## Evidence

Two consecutive real `pnpm ui:build` runs on macOS with 32 logical CPUs, measured with `/usr/bin/time -l` and `uptime`:

| Run | Wall time | Peak RSS | 1-minute load, start → end |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Uncached | 274.12 s | 3,235,676,160 B (3.24 GB) | 99.78 → 141.55 |
| Cached | 168.40 s | 399,294,464 B (399 MB) | 127.55 → 143.29 |

The second run logged `Control UI build: reused content cache; refreshed release identity`, skipped Vite/precompression, and passed the sidecar and performance validators. All **2,403 output files were byte-identical**, including dotfiles and compressed assets. SHA-256 of the sorted relative-path → file-SHA-256 manifest: `66b820566ef74398539291984a2068e2920d60a1de01bfa667db3c20abe17bf3`.

Both runs used this command, with the default cache root and a fixed release identity so timestamp refreshes do not change the comparison:

```sh
/usr/bin/time -l env -u BUILD_ALL_CACHE_ROOT -u OPENCLAW_BUILD_CACHE \
  OPENCLAW_BUILD_TIMESTAMP=2026-10-18T23:00:00.000Z \
  GIT_COMMIT=c8c8e886daae866027b976d606e83a8ceb6c114c pnpm ui:build
```

Regression and checks:

- Baseline `c8c8e886daae` (then `origin/main`): the default-root case failed because the second invocation reran the bundler; explicit-root reuse passed. Command: `pnpm test test/scripts/ui.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --testNamePattern 'checks source prerequisites'` (368.24 s wall; load 123.22 → 101.96).
- Fixed focused run: **2 passed**, 95.54 s wall, load 85.58 → 104.30.
- Full touched-file run: **17 passed, 2 subprocess timeouts**, 143.01 s wall, load 145.98 → 145.02, with 172.70 observed during execution. Both cache cases hit the existing 10-second `spawnSync` budget.
- One permitted focused retry: **default root passed; explicit root timed out**, 67.00 s wall, load 130.53 → 125.18. The explicit-root case had passed on both the baseline and the earlier fixed run. No budgets or assertions were weakened; the local timeouts are disclosed and PR CI supplies the broad proof on unloaded runners.
- Targeted oxfmt check and oxlint passed for both touched files. Lint configs: `config/tsconfig/oxlint.scripts.json` and `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.json`.
- `git diff --check`, pr-simplify, and isolated autoreview passed; autoreview was scoped-clean at P0–P2.

The subprocess regression exercises the real launcher/cache boundary; the full file also covers publication, validation, and process lifetime behavior. Local test time is reported above; CI seconds are pending.

Board and desktop renderers duplicate lifecycle responsibilities that belong to their existing owners or the shared observer primitive.

Board tabs keep the selected tab visible after their strip disappears and returns. Failed board frames retry on resolver or in-place revision changes without remounting healthy iframes.

Board documents read plain host inputs and retire their provider at the component lifetime. Tab measurement uses the shared ResizeObserver helper. prs.title: perf(gateway): skip no-op startup config rereads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway startup rereads and revalidates its prepared config when enabled shell environment fallback imports no values, while startup traces obscure environment-selection work and external plugin acquisition waits.

## User Impact

Startup skips that redundant config read. Opt-in startup traces now identify environment-selector imports, trusted dotenv loading, config read/validation/recovery, and external plugin source acquisition. Readiness, admission, plugin registration order, and config-over-shell precedence stay intact; no migration or operator action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing prepared snapshot when the shell fallback delta is empty. A nonempty delta still rereads config with lower-precedence shell values. The selector's separate guarded reads around bootstrap are intentional and remain intact.

The existing trace owners carry the new subspans. `modulePreparationMs` is part of plugin `loadMs`, not an additional duration to sum. Registration remains sequential because it mutates and publishes one plugin registry.

Production LOC is +20 (+50/-30); the requested timing breakdown accounts for the growth, while the config-reuse fix adds no lines. There is no new cache, config option, scheduling layer, or alternate loader path.

## Evidence

- Regression reproduced on unchanged production code: no-op shell fallback read the full startup config twice instead of once. Focused CLI proof: 5 selected cases passed across `run.option-collisions.test.ts` and `pre-bootstrap.process.test.ts`. The final parameterized no-op/applied-value cases also passed (2/2), preserving config precedence and startup ordering; artifact preservation with/without backups was unchanged by that test refactor.
- `loader.async-preparation.test.ts`: all 4 tests passed, including acquisition timing and failure isolation.
- Changed-file formatting and core lint passed; `git diff --check` passed. Broad gates run in PR CI. No Testbox/Crabbox lease was used.
- Benchmark builds use the repository's `sourcePerformance` build target on an isolated Linux sandbox. Real Gateway processes must emit the ready log and return HTTP 200 from `/readyz`.
- Four concurrent A/B pairs ran under the exclusive benchmark lock. Each Gateway had 16 CPUs, separate state and ports, identical synthetic fixtures, and a common start barrier. CPU halves were swapped after each pair. Node compile cache was disabled on both sides.

| Pair | A CPU half | Baseline A | Patched B | Paired B − A | Mean observed CPU busy |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 96–111 | 8,792 ms | 8,648 ms | −144 ms | 13.4% |
| 2 | 112–127 | 8,963 ms | 9,094 ms | +131 ms | 26.9% |
| 3 | 96–111 | 10,885 ms | 10,869 ms | −16 ms | 31.1% |
| 4 | 112–127 | 8,427 ms | 8,515 ms | +88 ms | 20.6% |

The paired mean is **+14.7 ms**, median **+35.9 ms**, range **−144 to +131 ms**. This is a neutral result within observed variation, not a speedup claim. The change removes a proven redundant read and supplies the requested diagnostics without a demonstrated readiness regression. Start skew was 0/0/2/0 ms. All eight processes emitted the real ready log, returned `/readyz` HTTP 200 with `ready: true`, and exited cleanly. CPU context comes from per-pair `mpstat -P 96-127`, including benchmark and background activity; it is not used to reject pairs.

The first patched trace separates a 155 ms config-module import inside the 191 ms selector and 149–171 ms acquisitions for each of four external plugins inside the 1,037 ms post-bind phase. The redundant final config read is only a few milliseconds in this fixture. These timings identify future investigation targets; this PR does not change registry publication or readiness ordering.

The synthetic fixture contains 5,000 sessions, 6,000 retained runs, 200 approvals, 100 cron jobs, and 12 real synthetic project worktrees. It selects bundled `github`, `workboard`, `prometheus`, and `openai` plus four synthetic external plugins; seven runtime plugins load. It does not reproduce the production plugin set exactly. Channels/provider transports are disabled and no external account is configured. The fixture's database is about 236 MB; it is not a production database-size benchmark. Node compile cache is disabled equally for A and B; fixtures and builds live on tmpfs to avoid shared-disk interference.

Independent Codex autoreview: scoped-clean through P2; no actionable findings.

## CI attribution

The exact-head [PR CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39174608526) has five failed test jobs matching the same cases and signatures in [scheduled main CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39172446197) at `4812f059427b2db240fbefd3af4411c9d701538a`:

| Failed cases | PR job | Matching main job |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chat history backing-session ID | [small-13-1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39174608526/job/117814971498) | [small-24](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39172446197/job/117808338826) |
| Chat policy verbose-level persistence | [large-16-2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39174608526/job/117814971585) | [large-13](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39172446197/job/117808338880) |
| Restart-safe chat abort; recovery source revocation | [small-14-1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39174608526/job/117814971422) | [small-17](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39172446197/job/117808338765) |
| Update status with unsafe SQLite history, both JSON modes | [small-25](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39174608526/job/117814971382) | [small-9](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39172446197/job/117808338666) |
| Session-row-delta capable/legacy parity timeout and subsequent worker stall | [small-1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39174608526/job/117814971594) | [small-1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39172446197/job/117808338766) |

The chat cases share the same `ws:chat.send` assertion; recovery reports the same active native borrowers; update status reports the same missing expected throw. The row-delta case has the same 120-second test timeout followed by the same 300-second no-output watchdog and unreleased worker-resource failure. The named failing inputs are blob-identical between scheduled main, the PR's actual CI base `b658f4a71a67b766026cf2269fec88ec64cc4f5b`, and tested merge `8cbd4ca6ac87f1a07cc508bb48b5824ee7f23a1f`. These are inherited failures, not passing test coverage. No CI rerun was requested.

The completed run has 83 successful jobs, 25 skipped jobs, and six failed jobs including the downstream aggregate. ## What Problem This Solves

Fixes oversized standalone launcher-bootstrap artifacts that cause the worker bundle scanner to exhaust its heap during Node bundle qualification.

## User Impact

Managed Node launcher selection retains the existing profile, environment, state/version, stdin, and security behavior while avoiding the CLI command implementation graph. No configuration, dependency, scanner, retention, or attestation changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Profile parsing reached command descriptor records containing lazy registration callbacks. The standalone producer followed those callbacks into CLI, agent, and Gateway implementations. One bootstrap-safe metadata catalog now owns command names and help/parsing facts; an exhaustive typed registration map consumes it. Alias callback identity and machine-output callbacks are preserved. The registrar-stubbing test helper is removed so tests exercise the real graph.

## Evidence

Qualified against explicit local main `993ec298df4ee9e5a761553500c623f3c38feab6`, with an independent frozen pnpm install and Node 24.17.0 on Darwin arm64. The only conflict was resolved by retaining main's daemon imports and all newer test cases. `pnpm-lock.yaml` is unchanged.

Canonical standalone tsdown configuration, fresh output directories, no minification/externalization/config changes:

| Artifact | Base | Fixed |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `node-host-launcher-bootstrap.js` bytes | 62,117,225 | 61,075 |
| Emitted modules in bootstrap | 11,918 | 47 |
| Dynamic imports in bootstrap | 27 | 0 |
| Agent/Gateway/TUI/cron implementation modules | 4,319 | 0 |
| 64 KiB regression gate | Fails | Passes |

Reduction: **99.90%**. Base additionally emitted a 4,948-byte command-execution-startup chunk; fixed output contains only the bootstrap file. Both builds used the same checkout-owned pinned dependencies, with the base source frozen from the exact base commit. The original incident's separate G13 artifact was 61,546,806 bytes; that incident artifact is not this main-base measurement.

SHA-256:

- Base bootstrap: `56946ef3aeb465dba033301924b20f42ec29edcb9ef348f553258464851d407b`

prs.title: fix(feishu): retry once on token-invalid errors 99991663/99991664 with cache invalidation (fixes #97287)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #97287.

When the cached `tenant_access_token` becomes invalid (e.g. clock drift, server-side revocation, or Feishu token expiry), the plugin cannot send messages. Error code `99991663 Invalid access token` is returned, but the plugin does not automatically refresh the token and retry. Users must manually restart the gateway to recover.

## Changes Made

- `extensions/feishu/src/comment-shared.ts`: Added `addFeishuTokenCacheClearer` / `clearFeishuTokenCaches`. `getFeishuTokenInvalidCode` detects 99991663/99991664. `requestFeishuApi` retries once on token-invalid (`retriedTokenInvalid` flag, independent of rate-limit budget). Fulfilled token-invalid bodies handled.
- `extensions/feishu/src/client.ts`: `createFeishuClient` creates a plugin-owned `Lark.Cache` via `buildSdkTokenCache()`. `clearClientCache` expires `CTenantAccessToken` in the private cache by appId namespace.
- `extensions/feishu/src/send.ts`: getter pattern — `opts.getClient()` inside request closure, ensures fresh client after cache clear.
- `extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.ts`: `clearFeishuTokenCache` registered. CardKit create retry on 99991663/99991664. Guarded-fetch release on non-JSON response.
- `extensions/feishu/src/client.test.ts`: NEW — client cache isolation tests.
- `extensions/feishu/src/send.retry.test.ts`: NEW — token-invalid + rate-limit retry sequence tests.
- `extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.test.ts`: NEW/UPDATED — card streaming tests including retry and guarded-fetch release.
- `extensions/feishu/src/token-retry-proof.test.ts`: NEW — end-to-end recovery proof tests (99991663/99991664 detection, cache clearing, getter pattern).

## Evidence

### 1. Production requestFeishuApi auto-retry on real 99991663 (7/7 passed)

Loads the ACTUAL `comment-shared.ts` module via `tsx` and exercises `requestFeishuApi` with a real 99991663 error. The production code automatically detects the token-invalid code, clears caches, and retries — all through the same code path that ships in the plugin.

```
 PRODUCTION requestFeishuApi AUTO-RETRY PROOF — PR #97295
 Host: LIN-66D8BD4EA2C
 Time: 2026-07-08T06:01:43Z
 Commit: 83830f71ec

─── 1. Real Feishu API: get token ───
  ✅ GET TOKEN: code=0
  ✅ BOT INFO:  code=0

─── 2. requestFeishuApi auto-retry on 99991663 ───
  ✅ Real API returns 99991663 with tampered token
  ✅ requestFeishuApi called 2x (1st=99991663, 2nd=success)
  ✅ Cache clear callback invoked (via addFeishuTokenCacheClearer)
  ✅ Recovered: result.code=0

─── 3. Cache isolation proof ───
  ✅ Fresh client after cache clear (different instance)

  RESULTS: 7/7 passed

  Production module exercised:
    extensions/feishu/src/comment-shared.ts
      → requestFeishuApi() — auto-retry on 99991663
      → getFeishuTokenInvalidCode() — detects 99991663/99991664
      → addFeishuTokenCacheClearer() — registers cache clearers
    extensions/feishu/src/client.ts
      → createFeishuClient() — builds SDK client
      → clearClientCache() — evicts CTenantAccessToken by namespace
```

### 2. Retry path steps (production code flow)

```
send() → 99991663 thrown
  → getFeishuTokenInvalidCode() detects 99991663
  → clearFeishuTokenCaches() → addFeishuTokenCacheClearer callbacks
  → clearClientCache() evicts CTenantAccessToken
  → retriedTokenInvalid = true (prevents infinite retry loop)
  → requestFeishuApi() RETRIES → SDK/fetch gets fresh token
  → send succeeds → code=0
```

### 3. Unit tests (113/113 passed)

```
 Test Files  5 passed (5)
 Tests       113 passed (113)
```

**Cache storage model**: All token caches are in-memory (Map + Lark.Cache), not persisted. No migration needed.

(Proof scripts run locally and deleted — not committed.)

- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
