prs.title: fix(auto-reply): hide recovered failed tool progress
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Failed tool progress could be treated as visible before transport delivery had actually settled. A cancelled send or a failure before delivery could therefore suppress the no-visible-reply fallback and leave the user with no reliable outcome.

OpenClaw's shipped verbose contract remains unchanged:

- `/verbose off` hides ordinary process/tool summaries.
- `/verbose on` and `/verbose full` keep ordinary tool failure summaries visible.
- Only the existing canonical recoverable category may be hidden after a clean recovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

This branch was rewritten onto current `main` rather than preserving the earlier buffering implementation. The original author commits `1daef420425`, `b651fa67f88`, and `47f3a92a5b2` established the problem and initial repair direction, but their broad regular-verbose buffering conflicted with the shipped verbose contract and with current main's prepared runtime configuration, durable tool-result routing, terminal outcomes, and settled-delivery ledger.

The current patch keeps Alex Tang's original authorship and issue ownership while replacing those commits with a narrow latest-main implementation:

- Queued visibility is recorded from settled delivery outcomes rather than queue admission.
- `cancelled` and `failed-before-deliver` remain invisible and preserve fallback eligibility.
- `failed-deliver` is conservatively visible because transport delivery started and may already have displayed partial content; this prevents a duplicate fallback.
- Direct routed sends continue to use their authoritative `delivered` result.
- Follow-up delivery propagates the existing routed/callback settlement result instead of inferring visibility from callback completion.
- Legacy callbacks returning `void` retain their established visible-success behavior; explicit `false` and rejected callbacks remain invisible.

## User Impact

Users still see ordinary failures according to their verbose setting. When delivery is cancelled or fails before reaching the transport, OpenClaw now retains or triggers the no-visible-reply fallback instead of incorrectly assuming queue admission was visible. Confirmed delivery and delivery that fails after transport delivery starts do not produce a duplicate fallback.

## Evidence

Exact candidate: `9ab2b365e2c532d65952f93628c745ad426a90e7`

The exact-head follow-up also fixes a callback-settlement bug found during review. Three
multi-payload paths used `visibleDelivery ||= await ...`; once an earlier callback was
visible, JavaScript short-circuiting skipped later dispatcher, same-channel recovery, or
cross-channel diagnostic callbacks entirely. Every callback is now awaited and settled
before its visibility is aggregated.

Controlled-transport runtime proof used the real OpenClaw dispatcher, settled-delivery ledger, finalization gate, follow-up delivery path, and pending-final restart custody. Provider/model execution and transport outcomes were deterministic and locally controlled. This was **not** a live Telegram or authenticated channel test.

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.progress.test-utils.ts \
  src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.reply-dispatch.test.ts \
  src/auto-reply/reply/before-deliver.test.ts \
  src/auto-reply/reply/followup-turn-execution.test.ts
```

Result: 4 files, 439 tests passed.

| Controlled outcome | Observed behavior |
|---|---|
| Confirmed source delivery | Exactly one source send; no fallback |
| Cancelled final | Exactly one fallback delivery |
| Failed before delivery | One original attempt, then one fallback |
| Failed after delivery starts | One original attempt; no duplicate fallback |
| Follow-up callback `false` | Invisible; fallback remains eligible |
| Follow-up callback rejection | Invisible; presentation failure propagates |
| Follow-up callback `true` | Visible; duplicate warning/fallback suppressed |
| Legacy follow-up callback `void` | Visible, preserving the existing callback contract |
| Restart/durable pending-final recovery | Delivered custody is not sent twice; failed custody remains recoverable |

Additional validation:

- Multi-payload regressions cover `true` followed by `false`, legacy `void`, and rejection:
  dispatcher callbacks were observed 3/3 times, same-channel recovery 2/2 times, and the
  cross-channel payload plus diagnostic 2/2 times. Later rejection still propagates.
- Focused exact-head owner matrix: 4 files, 97 tests passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`: passed.
- `pnpm check:test-types`: core, extensions, and root test types passed.
- `pnpm lint:core`: all shards passed.
- Formatting and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Codex exact-commit autoreview: clean, no actionable findings.
- Independent Claude exact-commit review: clean, no actionable findings (`0.98`).
- Both review bundles passed TruffleHog scanning.

Latest review repair delta: production `+13/-13` (net `0`) | tests `+117/-2`
(net `+115`).

## Proof Limitations

- No live Telegram proof was run. Channel adapters are unchanged.
- AWS/Crabbox authenticated live proof remains unavailable because the required AWS
  credential/proof tooling is not available in this environment. The controlled-transport
  runtime matrix above is the evidence for this exact head and must not be interpreted as
  live-channel proof.
### Exact-head approved mock-gateway proof (`5be414c2784`)

Ran the repo-owned QA scenario through the real ephemeral Gateway child and qa-channel transport boundary with the mock-openai provider and an isolated OpenClaw state directory:

```bash
OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-pr-97135-qa-20260822 \
OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/openclaw-pr-97135-qa-20260822/openclaw.json \
pnpm openclaw qa suite \
  --scenario qa-channel-failed-tool-terminal-finalization \
  --provider-mode mock-openai \
  --output-dir .artifacts/qa-e2e/pr-97135-settled-delivery
```

Result:

```text
Passed: 1
Failed: 0
Skipped: 0
QA channel final reply after a failed terminal tool: pass
The requested file could not be read: ENOENT. QA-FAILED-TOOL-FINALIZED-OK; calls=1 failed=1 finalizations=1
```

Harness: `qa-channel + qa-lab bus + real gateway child + mock-openai provider`. This proves one failed terminal tool is not replayed and produces exactly one visible final reply through the approved mock-gateway lane. It is not an authenticated live Telegram run.

prs.title: fix(sessions): report archive cleanup in sessions cleanup
prs.body:
Fixes #75658

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators running `openclaw sessions cleanup --dry-run` could not preview expired `.deleted.*` and `.reset.*` transcript archives, and apply output did not report the physical archive files it removed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Cleanup uses the configured archive-retention rules for preview and apply reporting. Physical archive retention is owned by the canonical config/session lifecycle module shared by SQLite cleanup and Gateway callers, without a config-to-Gateway runtime bridge or a new session-accessor debt exemption.

Logical ownership remains separate from physical directory identity. A selected agent cannot remove archives from a directory shared by another configured agent, including a symlink alias; `--all-agents` can clean that physical directory once.

Successful retention deletion clears reset-archive discovery state before notifying transcript subscribers. Dry-run stays non-mutating: archive-directory identity checks use a read-only matcher and never create missing-path alias probes.

## User Impact

Users can see deleted/reset transcript archive cleanup in dry-run and apply summaries. Shared directories stay protected during agent-scoped cleanup, while all-agent cleanup deduplicates physical work and reports the result.

## Current Head

- Head: `add96cdb4c807a6d3e5c6b60ffc352b5292733ca`.
- Rebased onto upstream `main` `165a2e9ede696adbc84313bbb731ee89c1ef53d2`.
- Author and committer: `Sami Rusani <samgithub@pm.me>`.

## Evidence

- Rebase resolution retained current-main compatibility-owner logic and the PR's configured-owner archive coordinator. The resulting change has no conflict markers and `git diff --check` passed.
- Focused archive/config/lifecycle tests: 131 passed across 4 files.
- Command rendering tests: 13 passed.
- Gateway archive tests: 45 passed across 3 files.
- Session-accessor boundary guard and changed-file formatting check passed.
- `pnpm dev` rebuilt the CLI and bundled plugin assets before the isolated CLI proof.
- Changed-file lint was queued behind a separate repository validation lock; exact-head hosted CI remains required before merge.

## CLI Proof

Disposable isolated fixture with two logical agents sharing one archive directory, one expired `.deleted` archive, and one fresh `.reset` archive:

- selected-agent dry-run: reports `shared-directory-requires-all-agents` and preserves the directory;
- all-agent dry-run: scans 2 archives and reports 1 eligible deletion;
- explicit offline apply: scans 2, removes the expired archive, and leaves the fresh archive present.

No external service, credentials, or user data was used.

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted: yes. Codex was used to inspect contributor rules and review feedback, rebase the patch, resolve current-main integration conflicts, run focused validation, and produce the isolated CLI proof. No agent transcript is attached.

prs.title: refactor(ui): scope chat media reads to keyed lifetimes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Attachment previews kept request setup, cancellation and cleanup in component effects. Model each source as a keyed Solid lifetime while preserving same-attachment refresh behavior.

## Changes

Pasted text, PDF and text attachment reads start in `onSettled` under synchronous keyed children. Replacing a source disposes its request immediately; presentation stays outside that child so a renewed ticket does not discard an unchanged PDF reader or text preview. HTML registration follows its active child lifetime. SVG gives each source its own renderer and retained lightbox Blob release closure.

The old effect implementations are removed. Existing size limits, stale-result checks, cancellation, tags, classes and lazy boundaries remain. No intended visual change; markup and styles are unchanged.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Current conflict-resolution proof | 33 text-attachment unit tests and 6 Chromium retention tests pass; one run each, one worker |
| Reused unaffected proof | PDF, SVG and pasted-text behavior remains covered by the prior focused proof; those source changes are unchanged by the merge |
| UI typecheck / four-file UI lint / formatting | Pass on the resolved source |
| Independent review | Fresh full-context P0–P2 scoped clean on the resolved source |
| Prior same-machine production builds / strict performance | Both builds pass. Startup 336,633 B gzip / 7 JS requests; CSS 38,500 B / 1 request. Chat 1,494,597→1,494,624 B (+27 B); new-session 1,046,885→1,046,931 B (+46 B). Both sides exceeded the 1,490,000 B chat ceiling. These are historical pre-merge measurements, not replacement-head evidence. |
| Replacement-head performance / broad CI | Pass: exact-head CI39174793947 completed successfully, including performance and every UI unit, Control UI E2E, browser-extension and real-Gateway shard. Startup 337,311 B gzip / 7 JS requests; CSS 38,500 B / one request. Chat 1,487,690 → 1,487,762 B (+72 B); New Session 1,048,067 → 1,048,102 B (+35 B). The strict base/head performance job passes. |
| Final production Knip | Final scan reports only the same two unused core reply-admission files; both files and Knip config are unchanged from merged main. No unused UI findings |

The merge retains main's identity-derived source toggle and clear policy, together with keyed request cancellation, retained readers and conditional HTML registration. The reviewed source tree is unchanged by the merge commit.

| Pattern across four production files against merged main | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `createEffect` | 4 | 0 |
| `createRenderEffect` | 0 | 0 |
| `untrack` | 0 | 0 |
| Direct listeners | 0 | 0 |
| DOM queries | 0 | 0 |
| Owner escapes | 0 | 0 |
| LOC | 855 | 882 |

The 27-line growth makes the request/render lifetimes explicit. No new abstraction, dependency or state owner. This batch has no surviving target patterns. Merged main: `1cc1efe021d83b670b545308d5cc65f7ab409292`; replacement head: `683d856e659f056b49be221ed5e946bab939cf4f`.

Prior CI [39168645916](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39168645916) passed all UI unit and Control UI E2E shards on the superseded head; its inherited-failure admission evidence is retired. The replacement run completed successfully; the prior failure attribution is no longer needed.

The automated LOC-only finding is declined under this wave's explicit allowance for correctness growth. The local lifetimes separate cancellable requests from retained viewers while preserving ticket refresh and immediate cancellation; no new shared loader abstraction is introduced.

Full exact-head CI [39174793947](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39174793947) completed successfully on `683d856e659f056b49be221ed5e946bab939cf4f`, including all UI shards selected by `ci:full`.

prs.title: fix(gateway): replace blocking sync I/O with async in auth/credential paths (fixes #78805)
prs.body:
## Problem
Gateway auth and credential paths used blocking synchronous I/O (execSync), which blocks the Node.js event loop during authentication operations.

## Root Cause
macOS Keychain access and other credential sources were called via `execSync` in auth-profile resolution paths.

## Fix
Replaced blocking `execSync` calls with async `execAsync` equivalents in the auth-storage credential paths.

Fixes #78805

## Real Behavior Proof

### Test Results (vitest 4.1.9, Node 22.22.0) — rebased onto origin/main (bdf388602)

```
 ✓ |agents-core| src/agents/sessions/auth-storage.test.ts (3 tests | 3 passed)
```

All 3 auth-storage tests pass: storage/retrieval, credential persistence, async I/O resolution paths.

prs.title: fix(agents): agent runs hang when a provider auth step never returns
prs.body:
Related: #141477, #143588

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an agent run hangs with no timeout when a provider's runtime auth exchange (`prepareRuntimeAuth`) or a credential lookup never returns. A stuck scheduled refresh makes every later auth-error refresh in that run wait on it, and later turns for the session queue behind the run.

## User Impact

User impact: a hung auth step now fails after 700 seconds with a named error, `Runtime auth exchange for <provider> timed out after 700000ms` or `Credential resolution for <provider> timed out after 700000ms`. The run then moves to the next auth profile or the configured fallback model, or fails with that error, instead of hanging. A scheduled refresh retries after 60 seconds as before. Normal auth is unchanged, and an OAuth refresh stall still reports the OAuth owner's own 120-second timeout first.

## Why This Change Was Made

The embedded-run auth controller awaited the provider exchange hook and credential resolution with no bound. This wraps both in the existing `withTimeout` (`infra/fs-safe`). It only stops the caller waiting: the hook and any OAuth refresh owner keep running. The controller writes runtime state only after these awaits return, so a result that arrives after the deadline is dropped and no generation fence is needed.

`RUNTIME_AUTH_HARD_TIMEOUT_MS` (700 s) sits with the other runtime-auth timers in `run/helpers.ts`. Credential resolution can make two OAuth manager attempts (the profile, then its legacy-default fallback), each up to 20 lock retries of at most 10 s plus the owner's 120 s observation deadline: 320 s. Two of those plus a minute is 700 s.

Earlier revisions also reworked OAuth refresh ownership and promoted native Codex logins into SQLite. Main now owns both decisions (#141477 durable refresh fences; #143588 and #114397 keep native Codex homes verified, never logged into), so this PR no longer touches them. Details: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/93952#issuecomment-5791578011

## Evidence

Head `e282c0c20c1`, which merges `main` `6b2afbfe981`, on an M4 Pro:

- `auth-controller.deadline.test.ts`, 5 tests, all pass. With `auth-controller.ts` reverted to main, the cold-start exchange, refresh-waiter and credential-resolution tests fail because nothing settles at the limit (3 failed, 2 passed).
- The OAuth test drives a real OAuth manager and SQLite store with a hung provider refresh. The owner's 120 s deadline releases the run first and the row stays a pending fence; the rotated credential then settles durably and the next run adopts it with one provider refresh. It joins that settlement through an `AsyncWorkScope`; with the drain removed the row assertion fails.
- The file runs in the forked database cohort (`test/vitest/vitest.database-worker-core-paths.mjs`), because OAuth persistence on main needs the host SQLite broker. Without the entry the OAuth test times out at 120000 ms.
- `auth-controller.test.ts`: 23 passed. `test/scripts/database-worker-registry.test.ts`: 12 passed.
- `check:changed --base 6b2afbfe981` passes every gate, including core and core-test typecheck, oxlint, format, the dead-export scan and import cycles.
- Test cost: `pnpm test src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-controller.deadline.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, 5 tests, 8.7 s Vitest duration, 16.9 s wall.

Not covered: a live Gateway run against a real hung provider hook, and the other `prepareProviderRuntimeAuth` callers (follow-up).

prs.title: perf(sessions): bound cached rows and omit unused patch results
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Long-lived session stores retain obsolete JSON in unused prepared-query shapes, and bookkeeping patches serialize and deserialize a full entry even when their callers discard it.

## User Impact

Session bookkeeping retains less stale data and avoids unnecessary result transfer. Entry-returning APIs, commit observers, final authority checks, publication, and durable settlement keep their existing contracts. No schema, stored format, configuration, or retention-policy changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Exact-row queries now share one retained payload per connection, with a 1 MiB conservative string-storage bound. A query miss clears the previous payload, including when another projection observes a new admission revision. Oversized rows remain readable; compiled queries remain cached. Alternating projections may execute another SELECT, while immediate same-shape/key/revision reads still reuse the row.

Internal fixed operations accept `result: "none"`. Six discard-only call sites opt in. The worker omits the separate result entry while retaining required publication facts. Observers still receive entries, and omitted results still require the final live-authority grant.

## Evidence

An isolated query-owner heap probe warmed four projections of a synthetic entry (512 KiB skills prompt plus 600 baseline records), replaced it with a small entry, and read only the list projection. Baseline retained three skills JSON strings and three baseline JSON strings (1,946,016 V8 string self bytes). The change retained none. This is a stress reproduction of stale retention, not an estimate of typical entry size or proof of the complete long-uptime production heap trend.

Four concurrent A/B pairs on an isolated 128-core Linux host used two separate 16-core sets under an exclusive lock, swapping assignments between pairs. Each side had an independent synthetic fixture: 5,000 sessions, 6,000 retained runs, 200 approvals, 100 cron records, 12 projects, and 8 MiB transcript text. The 128 hot entries also had 18,000-character skills prompts. Each mode ran 4 × 1,024 operations per side per pair; main allocation used V8 sampling at 32 KiB intervals, including collected objects.

| Per-patch metric | Baseline | Change | Mean paired B−A |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Changed patch: deserialize bytes |49,546|26,965|−22,581 (−45.6%)|
| Changed patch: total main allocation bytes |320,355|300,114|−20,241 (−6.3%)|
| No-op patch: deserialize bytes |22,494|463|−22,031 (−97.9%)|
| No-op patch: total main allocation bytes |263,941|241,108|−22,833 (−8.7%)|

Changed-patch batch differences were −29.8/−9.6/−15.5/−28.8 ms per 1,024 operations (mean −1.1%; treated as neutral). No-op differences were −48.4/−41.7/−22.9/−41.8 ms (mean −3.9%). Required publication data remains on changed writes. Sampled core utilization ranged 11.8–30.1%; it is context, not a run-validity gate. Dirty pages stayed below 380 MiB at pair boundaries.

Worker post-GC old-space remained roughly 97.0–97.4 MiB in both variants over these fixed-cardinality patch runs. In the earlier patch-only worker snapshots, warm→final node self bytes grew 1.59 MiB, of which 92.5% was V8 code; string growth was 3.5 KiB and stopped after the first round. Statement-cache owners and admission-map backing sizes stayed constant. This is node self-size accounting, not a dominator/retained-size estimate, and those snapshots did not exercise hydrated actors. These runs use the real storage APIs and SQLite workers through the source loader, without a Gateway/model roundtrip; they establish transfer/cache behavior, not production-wide memory savings.

Production LOC delta: +61; test LOC delta: +123. Production growth is necessary to enforce the byte bound and preserve type-safe entry/void return contracts and observer semantics; the change replaces per-shape retained payloads rather than adding a second result cache. Four existing read helpers move to the existing exact-read module with unchanged reexports to keep the entry facade within its size limit. No new modules, public API symbols, or test files.

The three new regression cases fail on the original worker/query implementations: oversized rows remain cached, and the no-result patch transfers 94,485 bytes against a <1,024-byte assertion. Final focused validation passed all 53 tests across the two owner files, SDK async reads, pending-final behavior, and both import/source-closure files. Changed-file format and lint pass, as does the export-name collision guard. Independent Codex review of the final diff plus owner-source context is scoped-clean for P0–P2. PR CI owns the broad gates; no Testbox lease was allocated.

## CI failure attribution

[CI run 39175111356](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39175111356), exact head `75010c421a5a973d8a3e0d39eee71c65cb52a890`, reports one failure in `checks-node-changed-compact-small-3`: `src/agents/code-mode.bridge.lifecycle.test.ts`, “settles an abort-ignoring subscribed tool exactly once after snapshot expiry,” line 967 (`activeCount`: expected 0, received 1). The automatic classifier says “unknown / no matching job on main”; independent attribution reproduced the identical failure on the unchanged baseline.

Command on each source: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/code-mode.bridge.lifecycle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, isolated Linux state and repository-pinned Bun 1.4.4. Baseline `50bb09d7ba13a37c8982b91afb3fcd52e13b09ae`: **17 passed / 1 failed**, 17.88 s. PR head: **17 passed / 1 failed**, 20.24 s. Both first attempts failed identically; no retry or CI rerun was used. Nine inspected test/harness/lifecycle/runtime files have identical SHA-256 hashes across baseline, PR head, and CI's main parent `1c07fdeaf230fdf542059641fbe2d1ecae6d1590`. CI tested merge `e8531da2468b77ef5dc7ae9fdb00bf06cdd1ad24`.

The unchanged test uses an in-memory session manager. Tool-registry cleanup precedes an awaited hook-runner load and item-end emission; the assertion waits for the first registry, then immediately checks the separately settling lifecycle counter. This is outside the changed SQLite path. The completed run has 62 successful jobs, 25 intentional skips, and two failures: this test shard and its aggregate CI gate. All three PostgreSQL conformance partitions passed. The inherited failure and red aggregate result remain recorded; no CI rerun was requested.

## Actor heap follow-through

Two additional concurrent A/B pairs, with swapped 16-core assignments, each acquired/read/released 8,128 actors: warm 128, visit all 5,000 sessions, then repeat one 1,000-session cohort three times. All four sides kept the same worker alive. Repeated-cohort old-space growth was 10,416/10,160 bytes in pair 1 (baseline/change), and 7,856/10,936 bytes in pair 2; paired differences −256/+3,080 bytes are neutral. Final old-space was 105.90–105.96 MiB, approximately 2.72 MiB below the hot-entry warm point on every side. These source-loader heap levels are not production absolute-heap estimates.

Warm/final snapshots kept 129 actor-state/transcript shape matches, 128 raw session rows, stable statement counts, and unchanged pending-state map storage on all four sides. The sweep did grow admission scope metadata from 256 to 10,000 records, then held steady across the fixed cohorts. Measured Int32Array/SharedArrayBuffer wrappers plus the direct scope-table growth totaled 2,400,768 bytes for 4,872 newly visited sessions (~493 bytes each), excluding scope objects, keys, and transitive/backing storage. These are cross-worker revision and retirement facts, not disposable row payloads; safe lifecycle reclamation is a separate follow-up in `sqlite-database-write-receipts.ts`. No arbitrary eviction was added.

The change fixes demonstrated stale row retention and unnecessary result transfer. It does **not** establish the cause of the entire reported long-uptime heap increase. Native memory, broader churn/concurrency, and admission metadata over much larger distinct-session inventories remain unproven.

prs.title: fix(runtime): accept Node 27 and its prereleases
prs.body:
Fixes #136429

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw updates fail in preinstall for users running Node 27 HEAD or nightly builds, even though the numeric engine range already allows newer Node majors.

## User Impact

Users can keep Node 27 development builds for installation, updates, CLI commands, and the Gateway. Node 26 remains the recommended default. Prereleases on Node 24 and 26 remain rejected, and every admitted runtime still passes the existing SQLite safety checks.

## Why This Change Was Made

The zero-dependency version owner rejected every prerelease suffix before checking the engine range. It now validates complete SemVer labels and compares the numeric core for prereleases above the highest supported floor. The generated worker check and the three standalone installer mirrors follow the same rule. The shared label corpus covers release, HEAD, nightly, RC/build metadata, supported-line prereleases, and malformed labels. The Node compatibility docs describe the development-build policy.

Two encountered test-harness defects are repaired without changing runtime behavior. The touched runtime suite had an incomplete worker mock: importing the entrypoint loaded the full worker agent graph during an admission test. That hit a 120-second timeout and let its late completion contaminate the next test. The fixture now isolates that unused runtime while retaining the real admission check and worker-entry assertions. The launcher cache-pruning test could lose its filesystem notification during a synchronous subprocess even though pruning had completed. It now waits for the persisted completion marker through its existing bounded helper, retaining the deletion and timestamp assertions.

## Evidence

All runtime commands used isolated HOME/OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR under this lane. Node 27 runs used the official nightly on PATH; no global runtime or operator Gateway was changed.

- Official `v27.0.0-nightly20261018f88a1d25e9` macOS arm64 and Linux x64 archives downloaded and matched the published SHA-256 sums. Runtime execution below is macOS arm64.
- `process.versions`: Node `27.0.0-nightly20261018f88a1d25e9`, SQLite `3.54.0`, V8 `15.6.75.13-node.9`. The loaded SQLite reports `3.54.0` and passes TEXT/BLOB/JSON NUL round trips.
- The real preinstall entrypoint rejected this nightly on the original parser and exits 0 with the fix. The new HEAD/nightly/RC unit cases fail on the original parser.
- `pnpm build` on Node 27 passed in 26m47s, including runtime, declarations, SDK exports, and UI. The longest phases were package declarations (8m17s) and unified declarations (7m57s).
- Node 27: runtime guard, Kysely sync, state database, and Git-update Node preflight: 4 files / 186 tests passed. Package lifecycle enforcement: 45 tests passed.
- Same-runtime fixture proof: the original Bun run took 225.97s and timed out in worker admission; with the fixture fix, all 90 tests pass in 8.74s total (about 2.6s test time). Node 27 passes the runtime suite in about 3.2s test time.
- Three independent Codex review passes found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Focused typechecks and typed lint, formatting, shell syntax, import-cycle check, and diff whitespace check pass. The full `check:changed` SQLite inventory was omitted under the local gate budget. An over-broad lint configuration initially timed out preparing plugin declarations; the correct root-test lint configuration passed.
- Full launcher suite on Node 27: 133 passed / 2 Bun-only cases skipped. The cache-pruning test timed out at 120 seconds on both Node 24 and Node 27 before repair; afterward its focused Node 27 run passed in 262 ms.
- `node scripts/run-node.mjs --version` on Node 27 reports OpenClaw successfully. An isolated built Gateway returned readiness 200, `sessions.list` succeeded (5.11s), `doctor --non-interactive --no-workspace-suggestions` completed (57.16s), and `update --channel stable --dry-run --json --no-restart` completed (23.95s). The package preview resolved `openclaw@2026.10.5` and retained the expected schema-downgrade warning: checkout schema 28 versus published stable schema 20. The owned Gateway shut down with exit 0.

- Cross-consumer run: 1029 tests passed, 53 platform/runtime cases skipped, and one existing slow worker-upgrade scenario timed out. The private Node provisioning live test passed through real installation, lease release, and reuse in 117.3s. Shell/standalone installers, daemon runtime selection, worker bootstrap, SQLite, and update lifecycle consumers passed. The default CLI shard initially excluded the live file; rerunning with the dedicated live configuration passed.
- Known unresolved integration timeout: `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/paired-node-worker-upgrade-wire.e2e.test.ts` hit the same 360s test deadline on both Node 27 and Node 24. Node 27 file time: 676.09s (55% test, 42% transform); Node 24: 516.45s (72% test, 25% transform). The fixture copies the complete built runtime, initializes auth, runs real repair/doctor/config convergence, starts a Gateway, and exercises a worker rebuild/restart. Repair alone took 136s on Node 27 and 206s on Node 24. This expensive fixture needs a separate performance repair; no timeout, retry, or assertion was weakened. The passing live smoke above is separate evidence and does not claim that this worker-upgrade scenario completed.

Linux execution was not run: no immediately available lane-owned Crabbox capacity was established, and no lease was created. The Windows mirror shares the contract corpus; 47 PowerShell release cases and 4 PowerShell execution cases were skipped because no PowerShell runtime is installed. Two additional launcher cases require Bun on PATH.

Production delta: +22/-7 lines. Test/helper delta: +50/-13 lines. Documentation delta: +38/-24 lines. No new owner, dependency, configuration option, or schema.

prs.title: feat: add session stream mode command
prs.body:
Implements the session-scoped streaming control discussed in #74077 (closed automatically for inactivity).

Related: #80989

> AI-assisted with OpenAI Codex; the resulting code and tests were reviewed and validated locally.

## What Problem This Solves

Preview streaming is configured globally per channel, so users cannot switch one active chat between off, partial, block, and progress behavior without editing config. This adds a session-scoped control that preserves channel configuration as the fallback.

## User-Facing Behavior

Authorized Telegram, Discord, and Slack users can run:

```text
/stream status
/stream off
/stream partial
/stream block
/stream progress
/stream default
```

`/streaming` is an alias. Text commands also accept `final` as a compatibility alias for canonical `off`.

The selected mode is persisted only for the current session. `/stream default` removes the override and reports the inherited channel mode. `off` disables previews without suppressing normal final delivery or an inherited block-delivery fallback.

## Implementation

- Adds optional `SessionEntry.streamingMode` state and preserves it across the same lifecycle boundaries as adjacent session preferences.
- Lets supporting channel plugins declare their inherited streaming mode and resolve account config without core assuming a plugin-specific config shape.
- Applies the session override before Telegram, Discord, and Slack account configuration in both preview selection and block arbitration.
- Capability-gates native command registration. ClickClack and other non-participating plugins do not advertise `/stream`; unsupported text invocation returns a clear response and does not persist state.
- Uses conflict-aware session persistence with `touchedFields: ["streamingMode"]` so a concurrent lifecycle change returns the standard retry response instead of acknowledging a lost write.

## Maintainer Decision Requested

This PR intentionally introduces one optional public channel-plugin contract: `plugin.streaming.sessionModeDefault` plus `resolveSessionMode({ account, sessionMode })`.

The contract keeps defaults and account-shape knowledge inside each channel plugin and makes native registration capability-aware. Please confirm whether this is the preferred long-term opt-in boundary for session-scoped streaming controls. The feature should not merge without that API sponsorship.

## Evidence

Exact candidate head: `7b98d15970f59dd3441bf4de782f67880f9c38da`  
Feature base: `d09401295626bebd53aa84492b91e7909e22487f`

- Production-focused matrix on the immediately preceding, production-identical head `9f8a86c87baf7a1528a85f6ac2638e0ec2b5c4d2`: 16 files / 699 assertions passed, covering command selection/persistence, lifecycle carry-forward, capability gating, stream/block resolution, and Telegram/Discord/Slack preview plus final-delivery behavior. A diff-caused duplicate Slack stream-mode mock was reproduced at 205/207 and repaired to 207/207.
- Exact-head boundary repair: the prior hosted `check-additional-boundaries` correctly found that a new standalone Gateway test root raised `gateway-root` from 720 to 721. That regression assertion now lives in the existing `sessions.recover` production-path test; the standalone root is removed. The exact-head recovery file passes 29/29, the repository boundary guard passes at the 720-root cap, and formatting/type-aware Oxlint/`git diff --check` pass.
- Clean merge simulation against live `openclaw/main` `89a1abd12ff92d78e0a5d2cf22641968dce828ea`: passed (tree `23fbae78977fb69774005b763f246b9b21dcdbdb`), with no paths changed on both sides since the feature base.
- Current repair gates: lower-level exact build, 49-file current-format check, direct type-aware Oxlint, `git diff --check`, and docs format/MDX/internal-link/config-example/glossary checks pass. Full wrapper `check:changed` remains delegated to hosted clean-install CI because local shared dependencies were intentionally not reconciled.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Audio and video players used reactive effects to notice native host input changes. Old preparation and playback therefore remained active until a Solid flush, and each player maintained a reactive source snapshot solely to synchronize its browser media resource.

Move that synchronization to the existing native bridge input boundary. Identity and authorization changes cancel old preparation and pause playback immediately; one queued synchronization reads the complete set of host inputs after related property assignments. `ChatMediaSourceOwner` remains the sole playback owner, preserving renewed-ticket handoff, retained media nodes, waveform Blob reuse, viewport admission, and browser user activation. Audio metadata changes retain the existing bounded waveform admission policy.

prs.title: refactor(gateway): simplify startup plugin publication ownership
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway plugin startup and reload maintain a second claim/reservation protocol
and an artificial startup service handle around owners that already serialize
reloads and settle real service work.

## User Impact

Normal startup, plugin reload, readiness reporting, and shutdown retain their
existing paths. A config-file edit overlapping deferred startup can now receive
late startup facts; another reload or restart repairs that recoverable overlap.
Security checks, admitted writes, and actual service cleanup are not relaxed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the private claim/reservation/wait/publication protocol and publish the
existing actual service handle directly. Keep the existing reload queue, closing
and effect checks, startup producer joins, physical service settlement, bounded
recovery, discovery FIFO and acquired-handle cleanup, and failure diagnostics.
There is no replacement epoch, barrier, mutex, cache, or startup-readiness wait.

This is one startup/publication AREA recovered from a previously parked wide
cleanup, not the wider family's proof. It changes 21 files, including the
orphaned model helper predicate and its claim-only tests: production +158/-388,
230 net lines removed; tests/support +78/-549, 471 net lines removed. The
independent final-drain and startup-metric cuts are excluded. Existing internal
module/factory/kernel names stay to avoid an unrelated migration.

No public config, schema, protocol, SDK, dependency, permission, retention or
durability change. Installed update formats and migration paths are unchanged;
startup still lazily loads the same service owner and retains cleanup failures.
Phase E standalone session memory, its factory/registry/expiry/federation, and
its tests remain untouched. The shared resumeMemory path changes only its
generic handle-publication invocation, not memory behavior.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Startup reservation/winner gating originated in #126627's deterministic
  internal fixture, not a cited human actual-use incident. Today's file watcher
  can really overlap deferred startup: already-admitted startup may publish old
  registry/model/transcript-selection facts after reload. A later reload
  or restart repairs it. Closing, live credentials, invoker/source/config and
  capability checks remain; startup readiness is not delayed by a new barrier.
- Discovery no longer waits outside its FIFO for claim settlement. The same
  synthetic reservation provenance does not justify that replay protocol. A
  mode-only update may briefly advertise the prior registry before the following
  registry update retires it through normal FIFO and acquired-handle cleanup.
- The artificial startup service handle and its pending-owner/timeout forwarding
  originated in #124309 and #145816's scanner/reentrant/import and controlled
  contention probes, not a cited human import-custody incident. There is now one
  actual service handle, published synchronously before service startup yields.
  Close or reload during lazy import refuses start at the existing final effect
  check. Reload consumes any already-published handle when stopping services;
  ordinary shutdown still joins the startup producer and actual cleanup.
- A second unsupported direct internal reload no longer gets a reservation's
  special rejection/status fence. Normal callers remain serialized by their
  existing owner. We do not add another scheduler for that unsupported call.

Peter's actual production cleanup/readiness incident in #150953 is distinct:
paused-channel release, admitted-write settlement, unavailable/sibling failure
diagnostics, captured-code rollback and bounded recovery all remain.

## Evidence

Current rebased head bae635b79e4ea83a8834ad4fa0a18b2edaec2051 passes hosted
CI run 39166554916, including openclaw/ci-gate, changed runtime/boundary suites,
production/test types, lint, architecture, baseline ratchets and security.
All head check runs were enumerated; there is no failing job. The older cancelled
context-and-evidence job has a successful same-head successor, not missing suite
proof. No run was rerun or branch updated to chase green. Earlier local failures
and the interrupted post-rebase attempt remain accurately recorded below.

Conflict-only rebase qualification is against cd7ebe9, preserving #175989's
module-boundary mocks/restorers, post-ready cleanup, closing predicate and
behavioral coverage. Only the removed winning-claim mechanism test disappears.
Fresh independent P0-P2 review of the complete rebased 21-file diff is
scoped-clean; all 237 captured source/context files verify unchanged. Targeted
nine-root types pass in 18.28 seconds and official lint of the two conflicted
test/support files passes in 174.80 seconds. No production import edge is added;
broad cycle/graph proof remains hosted CI under the campaign's local budget.
The mandatory suppression audit passes all 14 cases (51.43 seconds configuration,
90.96 seconds isolated wrapper). The interrupted focused wrapper settled with
SIGINT in 868.38 seconds; its owned children were joined before the audit.

The rebased focused recovery/startup/transcript attempt was intentionally
interrupted after more than thirteen minutes of preparation with no assertion
or aggregate verdict. Its worker compiler prepared 16,745 inputs successfully,
but this is not passing test coverage or a load-only attribution. The same
selected behavior passed before the rebase as recorded below; that historical
result does not substitute for current-head CI. No source, assertion, deadline,
retry or skip was changed to address this incomplete run.

Hosted review identified a real cleanup loss: deferred startup could publish a
service handle during reload preparation after reload had captured null. The
repair reads the current handle at the stop effect and uses the existing final
startup predicate to refuse service startup during active or failed reload.
No claim, reservation, epoch, barrier, retry, or second service owner is added.
The regression invokes actual service startup during preparation and checks
changed-service cleanup, retained-sibling continuity, and final cleanup. It
failed before the repair (stop count zero instead of one), then passed with
the repair. Focused recovery/startup proof passed 24 selected cases, including
close/reload refusal during lazy import, in 167.01 seconds wall time (136.86
seconds Vitest configuration duration). Fresh independent P0-P2 review of the
repair completed scoped-clean; the transcript fixture's callback migration is
mechanical. These results do not resolve the earlier local failures below.
The final transcript-fixture consumer run passed all five selected capture/
replace/remove/disable/rollback cases (105.23 seconds configuration duration).
Repair qualification also passes targeted nine-root types (38.94 seconds),
official six-file type-aware lint (64.81 seconds), six-file formatting, and the
mandatory 14-case suppression audit (10.08 seconds configuration duration).

Fresh independent P0-P2 review completed scoped-clean across two passes, with
27 intact selected owner/test contexts. The complete 21-file diff and all 236
captured source/context files verified unchanged before and after review.
After the mixed serial replay, a fresh independent P0-P2 review reassessed the
complete unchanged diff with the exact failure results and 16 intact critical
fixture, observer, prewarm, root-admission and service contexts. It completed
scoped-clean in one pass while explicitly leaving causality unresolved; this
static review is not runtime acceptance or an inherited-CI exception.
Formatting and whitespace checks pass. No new production import edge is added;
the lazy services import only moves within its existing owner.

Focused isolated proof covered all seven selected roots. The tooling benchmark
root passed all 12 cases (12ms test time, 247.18 seconds configuration wall time).
Discovery passed 27 cases, startup-early 15, model startup five, and reload-status
one; recovery passed 102 cases with the two original indexing failures below.
The initial Gateway run was interrupted after four failures. One serial replay
then ran those same four cases, candidate followed by exact authored base
7aab596ad005c15824143c482e9d6da732c6f102, with original deadlines and one worker:

| Retained case | Candidate | Exact base |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Indexing checkpoint recovery | FAIL: expected reloading, observed recovering; 34,851ms | PASS; 27,437ms |
| Indexing restart recovery | PASS; 10,228ms | PASS; 15,089ms |
| Startup-gated methods | FAIL: original 120,000ms deadline; 120,914ms | PASS; 18,085ms |
| Main-session restoration, failure false | FAIL: original 120,000ms deadline; 122,147ms | PASS; 20ms |

Candidate configuration wall time was 1,458.34 seconds; exact base was 994.80
seconds. This pair does not establish inherited failures or a load-only cause.
The passing restart replay does not repair its original failure. The indexing
helper and complete startup-gated-method case remain byte-identical to base;
no deadline, retry, skip declaration or assertion was changed.

Earlier #175706 recorded these indexing phase failures on its exact 7836689
base. That helper, reload owner and generation owner are byte-identical between
that historical base and this authored base. This is historical intermittent
baseline evidence, not attribution of the current candidate or a CI waiver.
The candidate's contribution to the checkpoint mismatch and startup timeouts
remains unresolved. Remaining interrupted keeper coverage completed with 65
passes, three failures and ten cases selected out. Restoration-failure true
timed out at 120,027ms and independent-sidecar recovery at 124,061ms, both against
their original 120,000ms deadlines. Forward-wall-clock ACP readiness failed its
one-call assertion (zero observed); backward-wall-clock passed. Those three
cases were not selected by the completed four-case serial comparison and are
not attributed. Runner wall time was 627.14s (589.58s configuration), wrapper
669.01s. Targeted nine-root types pass (14.46s); official-core touched-file
type-aware lint passes (120.56s). The mandatory suppression audit passes all 14
cases (41.01s runner, 51.51s isolated wrapper). The complete reviewed diff and
236 captured inputs were unchanged for the original review. Original-head
e09d68e CI39093759182 completed successfully, including openclaw/ci-gate.
The substantive cleanup repair requires fresh exact-head hosted CI after push;
the original green run is not new-head proof.
Historical wider-family results are not current acceptance.
No live operator Gateway, device, deployment or real state is exercised.

prs.title: refactor(sqlite): trust schema and worker lifecycle owners
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

SQLite infra repeats decisions already owned by its schema lifecycle, worker broker, input admission, and retained-task pool. Remove seven redundant checks/fallbacks while preserving actual schema, authority, cancellation, input-custody, and shutdown boundaries.

## Design and impact

- Additive schema ensure keeps its initial admitted-catalog check and existing transaction/refresh owner. It stops checking presence again inside installation. If a sibling installs during synchronous writer acquisition, the already-idempotent additive DDL may execute again and invalidate schema/integrity admissions; ordinary warm ensures still skip it. All 27 callers use additive `IF NOT EXISTS` DDL.
- Index repair validates canonical identifiers before forming the repair set, then uses that validation through DROP/CREATE. Remove the second identical name check after DROP.
- Schema issue descriptions use the closed issue-code union and exhaustive description map without a runtime own-property check.
- Input handoff checks retained membership and owner shutdown once. Rejection still releases custody; successful handoff still releases immediately before synchronous enqueue. The existing test now waits for shutdown without manually releasing the rejected preparation.
- Unscoped client execution uses the sealed flag; close sets it synchronously before retaining its promise, and a failed close never unseals it.
- Actor reuse consumes the broker's synchronous failed-slot decision. Backend and state-context matching, post-await checks, and dispatch admission remain.
- Snapshot staging uses the retained task returned by its concrete retained-transport pool. The pool already handles supported startup failures; remove the fabricated failed task with a no-op release. Unexpected internal startup exceptions propagate directly instead of being converted into a pretend task.

No SQL text, schema, transaction policy, commit ordering, grants, identity comparisons, or public API changes. Broker bookkeeping is shared by PostgreSQL-backed state workers; the native schema ensurer still refuses PostgreSQL. The removed schema-presence call normally repeats admitted-catalog validation and set membership, without SQL; transaction acquisition still owns its catalog refresh. No statement/request reduction is claimed for these removals. No speculative fallback or replacement state was added. Delta against the merge base: production -26 lines, tests -2, total -28 (+17/-45).

## Evidence

Changed-file formatting, type-aware oxlint, and `git diff --check` pass. Existing schema rollback/re-ensure, index repair, failed-actor reopen, retained staging, and client shutdown tests cover the affected owners. The changed input-handoff test now proves that refusal itself releases custody. PR CI supplies the owner tests and static gates.

Independent Codex autoreview of the production changes completed scoped-clean through P2, with no actionable findings. A second and final review found no P0/P1 defects in the type-only Knip cleanup: delete the now-unused infra type re-export and import the test type from its owning package. Reviewers do not supply test proof; CI supplies that evidence.

The production revision e583df9249803ca3b12d0c8581a69ce36ccd46dd passed ordinary CI [39169975401](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39169975401), including all three PostgreSQL conformance shards, owner tests, types, lint, contracts, architecture and ratchets. The [published-driver update](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39170004180/job/117806558767) also passed on that runtime-identical revision. The first type-only cleanup exposed one missed test import in `openclaw-state-db-readonly.error-mapping.test.ts`; the final correction imports that type directly from its owning package. The previously failing state/logging typecheck now passes locally through the native compiler runner. Final-head CI [39174840836](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39174840836) completed successfully: 53 passing jobs, no failures, including the repaired [typecheck](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39174840836/job/117816477908), all three PostgreSQL conformance shards, owner tests, lint, architecture and ratchets. PostgreSQL owner acknowledgment is recorded for exact head 639a5a96490dc5a1998976fe001324abaeaee8fc. The supplemental main-tier run had unrelated failures and is not represented as an overall pass.

The initial local baseline was excluded because its installed process helper did not match the unchanged lockfile. After task-local dependency reconciliation, the corrected native build completed bundling but stalled in plugin-artifact filesystem renames before the workload (1,757/1,757 sampled frames in `__rename`). prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated native TypeScript work when a local Vitest invocation already has valid cached worker outputs.

## User Impact

Node Vitest runs reuse retained workers without opening a native TypeScript project, parsing its config, or rediscovering compiler imports. Cold misses still discover and compile normally. Existing entries rebuild once because the cache signature changes. Bun's existing cache policy is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The compiler discovered its import closure before attempting restoration, and the cache signature separately reparsed TypeScript configuration. Restoration now runs first, using the existing manifest verifier to rehash the recorded compiler/source/config inputs. The snapshot owner supplies a native-free signature covering the toolchain, resolution namespace, runtime arguments, and absolute output slot. Cold compilation records inherited config files alongside compiler inputs, so transitive edits still invalidate.

The simplify pass kept the existing cache and snapshot owners and removed the duplicate compiler-input inventory from cache metadata. Net change: 13 production lines and 25 test lines; the added configuration capture and work-count assertions protect invalidation and the hot-path contract.

## Evidence

The cache regression is red on `c8c8e886daae` (the origin/main base): 23 passed, 1 failed because a warm restoration read native TypeScript config once. With the fix, the cache and snapshot-owner suites pass: **41 tests** (`pnpm test test/scripts/vitest-worker-cache.test.ts test/scripts/compiler-input-snapshot.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, Node mode; 68.19 seconds wall). Real native project-open counts are **miss 1 → unchanged hit 0 → recorded transitive edit 1**, with updated executable output. Warm native config reads are also zero. Extended-config, compiler-source, resolution, output corruption, and unrelated-source reuse checks pass. CI timing is pending.

prs.title: fix(feishu): stop inbound mentions from cascading into replies
prs.body:
Closes #121921

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Feishu group replies would automatically mention every non-bot participant mentioned in the inbound message, even when the agent's reply did not request those mentions. Error and fallback replies could therefore wake multiple bots and create an unintended cascade.

## Why This Change Was Made

Inbound mention targets remain available as agent context, but they are no longer passed into the reply dispatcher or automatically attached to generated replies. Explicit outbound mentions, native Feishu `at` rendering, and bot-authored required mentions (`requiredMentionTargets`) remain unchanged.

This restores the boundary introduced by #71396 without reverting the native mention-rendering improvements from #93522.

## User Impact

Feishu users and multi-agent groups no longer receive unrequested `@` notifications from ordinary, error, fallback, card, streaming, block, or chunked replies. Agents can still explicitly mention users when the outbound content or message-tool request asks for it.

## Evidence

- Regression coverage verifies non-streaming final/error replies, static cards, streaming card closes, and independent block/chunk delivery do not inherit inbound mention targets.
- Existing coverage verifies `requiredMentionTargets` still reaches every required text chunk and static card reply.
- Focused Feishu tests pass:
  - `reply-dispatcher.test.ts`: **124/124**
  - `bot.test.ts` + `send.test.ts`: **131/131**
  - Total: **255/255**
- `oxfmt --check` passes for all 3 changed files.

prs.title: fix(agent-core): bound runaway loops with turn/error-batch/idle-repeat guards (#120962)
prs.body: Closes #120962 [AI-assisted] ## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where a worker agent could enter an unbounded retry loop inside the native runLoop: an external service returning HTTP 429 (masked inside a "successful" tool output) drove 219 assistant turns / 177 tool calls / ~15M tokens over 6h42m, stopped only by the global `stuckSessionAbortMs` timeout rather than by any active guardrail. ## Why This Change Was Made Adds three opt-in hard cutoffs to the agent-core runLoop, each activating independently when set to a positive integer in `tools.loopDetection`: - **`turnLimit`** — max assistant turns per run; ends gracefully with a terminal message instead of another provider request. - **`maxConsecutiveErrorBatches`** — max consecutive all-error tool batches; any success resets the streak. - **`maxIdleRepeatCalls`** — max consecutive identical tool calls (same name + args); catches errors hidden inside successful output. Steering-skipped calls are excluded. `enabled: true` alone does not engage hard cutoffs (preserves upgrade contract). `enabled: false` disables both layers. Resolved config propagates through sessions, compaction, and worker launch descriptors. The launcher fences guard-enabled turns on worker bundles lacking the `worker-loop-guard-v1` capability; configless and `enabled:false` turns are unaffected. ## User Impact Operators who want the guardrails set at least one guard key (e.g. `turnLimit: 200`) in a `tools.loopDetection` block. Existing configurations gain no new hard termination behavior unless a guard key is explicitly set. Public package consumers see no change unless they opt in. ## Evidence **Focused tests (all pass):** - `packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.guard.test.ts` — 23 tests: maxTurns, error-batch, idle-repeat, steering-skip exclusion (sequential + parallel), steering requeue - `src/agents/sessions/agent-session-loop-guard-transport.test.ts` — real `AgentSession` through local HTTP/SSE transport, 3 repeated calls → graceful termination, no 4th request - `src/agents/tool-loop-detection-config.test.ts` — 9 tests: per-key activation, `enabled:false` kill switch, per-agent cascade - `src/gateway/worker-environments/worker-turn-launcher.loop-guard.test.ts` — 6 tests: launcher fence, serialization, guard-off compatibility - `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/worker-admission.test.ts` — 25 tests: loop-guard capability in worker protocol features

prs.title: refactor(ui): bind browser dashboards to Solid lifetimes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The browser dashboard widget still reconciles request identity through a rendering effect, and development Gateway selection still scans Vite's injected script element.

## User Impact

No intended appearance or behavior change. Hiding a browser dashboard preserves its live tab; replacing its widget, connection, or authorization retires pending results. Development servers continue to choose the local Gateway by default, while bundled builds and remote ingress use their serving Gateway.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keyed Solid ownership now retires the dashboard request state. Activation and completed requests perform their own follow-up work, removing the generation counter, copied identity, and effect feedback loop while retaining the synchronous pending latch. Vite publishes whether it is serving the UI, so settings no longer infer that fact from DOM content or `NODE_ENV`.

The simplify pass retained the existing Gateway owner, browser request contract, registered tag, and rendering markup. The small production increase represents the explicit lifetime boundary; the Vite configuration owns a shared defines function for its two source-server callers, with no new dependency.

## Evidence

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm tsgo:ui` | Pass |
| Changed browser/settings/dev-Gateway test files | 50 cases passed: 30 settings, 12 browser, 8 dev-Gateway |
| Targeted lint, formatting, line-cap ratchet | Pass |
| Production Knip | Same failure on exact merge base and head; output is byte-identical (2 backend unused files, 20 export groups, 7 type groups). No changed UI findings. |
| Independent review through P2 | Pass: no actionable findings |
| CI run [39172197442](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39172197442) | Only reported failure is inherited chat-boot budget breach: base 1,490,230 B → head 1,490,253 B (+23 B), both above the 1,490,000 B cap. CI startup is 337,238 B and within budget. |
| Base/head `pnpm ui:build` and strict performance | Pass |
| Startup JavaScript gzip | 336,805 B → 336,770 B (−35 B) |
| Startup CSS requests | 1 → 1 |

Performance uses the same machine and base `95c7b0d4cdabc4b88be631e38f38e4885e4f99fd`. This is a nonvisual ownership refactor; browser behavior assertions cover the existing rendered controls, retirement of widget/client/auth scopes, hiding/resuming, and reopening after an inspection finds no live tab. The first multi-file run passed all 30 settings cases before the test wrapper timed out waiting for a concurrently held artifact lock. The two unfinished files then passed serially with no competing artifact owner. No local E2E suite was run; `ci:full` supplies broad proof.

| Checklist pattern in touched production files | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Controller/lifecycle pattern | 0 | 0 |
| `createEffect` | 1 | 0 |
| `createRenderEffect` | 0 | 0 |
| `untrack` | 0 | 0 |
| `addEventListener` | 0 | 0 |
| `querySelector(All)` | 1 | 0 |
| Hand-built class strings | 0 | 0 |
| `flush` | 0 | 0 |
| Captured Solid owner | 0 | 0 |

Measured production scope: browser widget, settings, dev-Gateway globals, and Vite config. No survivors. Production LOC: 1,850 → 1,865 (+15); test LOC: 1,289 → 1,368 (+79). The source E2E harness shrinks by one line through the shared defines function.

prs.title: perf(sessions): streamline transcript identity replacement
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Transcript replacement executes duplicate identity cleanup and reads owners for idempotency keys that have no replacement candidate.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible behavior change. Replacing or clearing a transcript performs less database work while preserving export order, search, retry ownership and cold-transcript behavior. No schema migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both supported database schemas already cascade event deletions to their identity rows. Full and suffix replacement now use that existing owner relationship instead of issuing a second DELETE. Suffix replacement iterates the planner’s replacement map directly and uses one conditional UPDATE per candidate instead of a SELECT followed by an UPDATE.

The UPDATE keeps a NOT EXISTS ownership predicate: earlier inserts in the same transaction may already have claimed the key. This checks the current row at the write itself. Opaque payload staging creates raw event rows without identity rows, so its excluded temporary sequence range does not leave identities behind. The admitted database’s existing foreign-key enforcement is the operating contract; no schema or freshness probe is added.

Transaction boundaries, write admission, retained-event order, cursor rotation, cold-data refusal and search/projection updates remain unchanged. Production code is reduced by 17 lines (+20/−37); test changes are +60/−15 lines.

## Evidence

The existing full-clear and suffix ownership cases now assert durable identity cleanup/order and count executed redundant DELETEs and owner reads. A suffix case also proves that a key claimed by an earlier insert is not reassigned. No test-only production seam was added.

Source-level expected savings: one SQL statement per full or suffix replacement, plus one statement for each removed key without a replacement candidate or each candidate that needs promotion; worker request counts are unchanged. These are estimates, not workload measurements. Workload savings are estimated, unmeasured. Per-PR workload runs are deferred after the local filesystem stall; a combined census will provide operation-level measurement.

Independent Codex review found no actionable P0–P2 production issue across two rounds. Two test-only fixture corrections were needed: the new case must preserve the bounded replacement length, and its expected owner rows must follow the reader's existing ORDER BY event_id. All 32 transcript-store tests now pass on final head 3f92e0b in CI run 39172711573 (job 117809432693). The final run passes all required checks, including all three PostgreSQL conformance shards, changed tests, formatting/lint, source contracts, types, Madge and ratchets. The aggregate openclaw/ci-gate is green. No production change was needed for either fixture correction.

The completed supplemental Knip scan reports 59 production / 38 full-tree / 0 script exports. Every finding has matching scheduled-main evidence in runs 39168070659 and 39172446197 (jobs 117795291143 and 117808338097). The newer main run confirms the cron-test export; a clean merge-tree comparison preserves main’s subsequent cron-helper and script-entrypoint cleanup. There are no new findings attributable to this PR. The supplemental Swedish translation failure also matches main. The PostgreSQL review approval covers final head 3f92e0b.

The focused baseline/fix replay is complete on Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m58mn473stktnp1f03jf6mr6` ([run 39175598378](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39175598378)). With the final tests unchanged, reversing only the two production-file changes produces exactly six assertion failures at the redundant DELETE/owner-read counts. Restoring the reviewed production bytes produces six passes. The runner used one fresh frozen install and Node 24.19.0; it verified source restoration, unchanged dependency inputs and no remaining test processes. The delegated command exited 0; subsequent lease cleanup may mark its hosting workflow cancelled. The full 32-case final-head CI result above remains the broader owner proof.

The first local baseline attempt stalled in filesystem setup before assertions and was stopped; it provides no product verdict. The later disk-clearance wait was stopped after approximately 56 minutes. Optional workload preparation was retired under the combined-census policy. Workload comparisons remain unrun, and no workload or latency saving is claimed.

prs.title: refactor(agents): simplify owned MCP and reaction state
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

MCP catalog/session bookkeeping and serialized status reactions repeat checks or copy state whose lifecycle is already controlled by their owner.

## User Impact

Catalog sharing, transport recovery, lease accounting, and status-reaction behavior keep their existing contracts while doing less bookkeeping.

## Why This Change Was Made

Catalog loaders have one producer and join its pending promise, so the producer can clear its slot directly. Runtime disposal prevents a successor load. Session retirement synchronously clears the current session before awaiting cleanup, making the current-but-retiring branch unreachable. Lease release already has an idempotent closure, so each release decrements once without a zero floor.

Status-reaction entry points check immutable enablement before queueing work. The queue owns every mutation of the active-reaction set, so cleanup can iterate that set directly, and extra-reaction detection can use set size/membership without copying and scanning an array. The cleanup helper owns the optional adapter check.

The patch is net -11 production lines and removes two array allocations. No additional behavioral edge is accepted. Transport and execution authority checks, disposal checks, catalog invalidation semantics, and terminal-hold cancellation remain. No SQL, worker requests, exports, schemas, or public contracts change.

## Evidence

Exact-head [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39171963743) passed all 41 selected checks, including 75 tests across MCP runtime (58), status reactions (12), and Slack reaction lifecycle (5). Types, type-aware lint, source contracts/export collisions, Madge (zero cycles), and database ratchets passed. T1 remained 180 → 180 live calls and 10 → 10 compatibility calls. Local formatting, lint, and diff checks also passed. Independent Codex review through P2 is scoped-clean after the final pass inspected the complete lifecycle modules and tests; GitHub Codex review completed without findings.

The separate [canonical Knip job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39172166120/job/117807557072) completed with no new export findings: 59 production findings, 37 full-tree findings, and zero script findings. All production findings and 36 full-tree findings match [scheduled main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39172446197/job/117808338097). The remaining full-tree finding, `src/cron/service.test-harness.ts: createCronServiceStateWithJobs`, also appears in [earlier scheduled main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39163574553/job/117782017361) and was subsequently removed there. None concerns a changed file.

Existing tests cover concurrent catalog sharing, cancellation, retirement during discovery, refresh/recovery, lease reuse, disabled reactions, serialized cleanup, and terminal-hold cancellation. No read or write class is removed. No provider-request shape changes.

SQL/request/MAIN delta is **estimated 0/0/0, unmeasured**. The exact-base v3 workload passed all 14 turns, including ten warm turns, spawn, cron, compaction, restart, and child cleanup. Baseline warm medians [min–max] were 57 [57–58] SQL, 16 [16–17] worker requests, and 0 [0–0] MAIN. This is baseline evidence only. Candidate Testbox allocation was queued without an assigned host and was stopped before any candidate workload; paired counts defer to the combined campaign census under the wave-28 measurement policy. No latency or measured SQL saving is claimed.

The baseline ran on Blacksmith Testbox with Node 24.19.0, SQLite 3.53.3, and the exact locked `@openclaw/proc-safe` 0.4.1; the requested 16-class profile supplied four CPUs and about 16 GB RAM. Its full source tree was verified against the base despite the wrapper using a transport carrier commit. Earlier setup attempts failed before measurement on an incorrect carrier-HEAD assertion and slow local source preparation. The successful harness exited zero; the native CLI then exited two from a shell-trailer syntax error, so that CLI exit is not represented as success. Independent workload and cleanup receipts establish the baseline result.
