releases.body:
## 2026.10.5

### Highlights

- **Updates finish and recover on their own:** `openclaw update` completes across devices, filesystems, pnpm 12, Windows elevation, and macOS login shells, settles stale handoff leases and package-activation journals instead of stranding the install, keeps busy or unhealthy Gateways from blocking the update, and `--no-restart` package updates now report success honestly. (#164769, #165863, #166695, #167302, #169410, #170046, #172196, #172640, #173358, #173409, #174649, #171015) Thanks @shanselman, @patrickschiller, @RomneyDa, @SergeiAug, @giulianoaccorsi, @mwbroxson, and @Bamorem.
- **Restart-safe conversations:** interrupted turns, first messages during worktree preparation, subagent work, and deferred tasks resume after a Gateway restart, and user input and committed session data survive restarts, concurrent writes, and failed publications. (#165333, #166042, #165184, #168650, #169144, #170161, #170223, #165502, #167570, #166010, #167662) Thanks @DonnieFi, @jjjhenriksen, and @RomneyDa.
- **Faster, lighter Gateway:** session, transcript, history, and metadata reads move onto worker threads with far less SQLite work per turn, startup maintenance runs after readiness, and Gateway startup and memory search workers use less memory, back in the 2026.10.4 range. (#164744, #165470, #165614, #166587, #167194, #164779, #165028, #166041, #167278, #165993, #174718, #172392) Thanks @obviyus, @RomneyDa, @DonnieFi, and @jjjhenriksen.
- **Reliable turns and subagents:** turns recover from stalled streams, reused tool-call IDs, expired ChatGPT websockets, and malformed OpenAI or Google streams, incomplete turns end with a visible notice, and subagent results keep returning through restarts. (#165983, #167013, #165212, #167972, #166846, #168400, #173404, #173612) Thanks @cestercian, @Irish-Joseph, @rmyers64, @sszyh2026, and @RomneyDa.
- **X channel:** answer X (Twitter) mentions through a new channel plugin with streaming, guest mode for repository questions, and enforced API cost limits. (#165138, #165337, #165354, #165351)
- **Voice calls:** voice calls gain per-call briefs, call reports, live steering, callbacks, and voicemail detection. (#165716) Thanks @mbelinky and @jacobtomlinson.
- **Smarter model pickers and new models:** pickers lead with each provider's recommended models, show newly listed Claude, ChatGPT, and Ollama models without waiting for an OpenClaw release, and Google adds Gemini 4 Argon and Gemini 3.8 Flash. (#167370, #166737, #167658, #167387, #167463, #171852, #172339) Thanks @obviyus.
- **ClawHub in the Gateway:** browse and search ClawHub plugins and skills from the Gateway, and plugins automatically pick the newest official release your OpenClaw supports. (#163459, #167485, #166588) Thanks @jacobtomlinson and @charlesBerg-ux.

### Changes

- **Tool approval hooks:** ordinary hooks can no longer rewrite trusted-inline-approved tool arguments without another approval, and transforming plugins must request separate approval for their final arguments or the call is blocked; see `docs/plugins/hooks/tool-policy.md` for migration. (#142700) Thanks @giodl73-repo and @giodl73.
- **Sessions:** allow directed sends to a session without granting transcript access. (#164444)
- **Worker-local inference:** add a native worker inference runtime with Gateway dispatch, client placement, required worker policy and destination checks before local inference, and clear setup-failure explanations. (#158902, #163645, #163646, #163647, #166611, #166613, #165960) Thanks @RomneyDa.
- **Device joins:** the CLI and Control UI join command now installs a background node service that can host agent sessions (`--service --session-host`), with a command-only service alternative, and already-paired devices get a working command to enable session hosting. (#168623) Thanks @obviyus.
- **Public threads:** open public threads at their regular links. (#166049)
- **Subagent progress:** count running subagents on the working line, name launched subagents in the operations group, and continue a resumed answer in the block that handed off. (#165477, #165725, #165542) Thanks @shakkernerd.
- **X channel:** add the X (Twitter) mentions channel plugin with Activity API streaming and backfill, repository-question guest mode with hidden same-agent helpers, GitHub-verified repository writers, and daily and monthly X API cost limits. (#165138, #165337, #165376, #165354, #165543, #168071, #165351) Thanks @obviyus.
- **Automation repair:** let a failing automation's owner conversation repair it before alerting, give a second repair turn when the error changes, and post a clear warning when a repair turn times out. (#161007, #162702, #162772) Thanks @obviyus.
- **Channel progress:** show useful Telegram and Discord progress by default, add per-tool glyphs to Discord progress drafts, restore per-tool emoji on Telegram tool rows, and hide routine Slack reaction rows. (#166861, #168032, #167392, #166880) Thanks @obviyus, @keshavbotagent, and @notmnp.
- **Skills:** keep learned skills focused on repeatable procedures rather than facts or codebase knowledge, and keep longer legacy Workshop skills manageable. (#167404, #167639) Thanks @obviyus.
- **Memory:** explain why trigger recall is skipped and why embedding responses are rejected, and report managed Ollama and LM Studio embedding readiness. (#164409, #168035, #156483) Thanks @Ayushdevo, @wangmiao0668000666, and @obviyus.
- **Models and catalogs:** show each provider's recommended models first in pickers, publish curated per-provider recommendations in catalog v2, lead NVIDIA recommendations with its featured models, and apply downloaded catalogs without a Gateway restart. (#167370, #166737, #167989, #158000) Thanks @obviyus.
- **Google:** add Gemini 4 Argon and Gemini 3.8 Flash, and make Gemini 4 Argon the default Google model. (#171852, #172339)
- **Anthropic and Claude CLI:** show newly listed Claude models without waiting for an OpenClaw release, list each Claude CLI model once, and keep logged-out Claude CLI models listed with a login reason. (#167658, #166311, #166338, #167942) Thanks @obviyus.
- **OpenAI:** support custom realtime voice endpoints, show account chat models missing from the manifest, surface new ChatGPT-login models without a release, and stop offering ChatGPT-only or bundled-Codex-rejected models that would fail. (#165632, #162563, #167387, #167633, #167975) Thanks @jacobtomlinson, @obviyus, and @RomneyDa.
- **Codex runtime compatibility:** plugin admission rejects official Codex runtimes below 2026.9.7 with update and repair guidance, and incompatible plugins stay inspectable without being imported. (#168930, #168748, #168749, #168977) Thanks @ezimerman and @RomneyDa.
- **Context limits:** status shows corrected context limits after model discovery, and llama.cpp keeps live router model limits and tools on refresh. (#165991, #168309) Thanks @snotty, @saju01, and @RomneyDa.
- **Tool rows and subagent progress:** show Tool Search calls in native tool rows with shared tool icons across clients, show the subagent wait in place without handoff markers, and guide users after HTTP 400 prompt-size rejections. (#165095, #165378, #159712) Thanks @shakkernerd, @sunlit-deng, and @RomneyDa.
- **Voice calls:** add per-call briefs, call reports, live steering, callbacks, and voicemail detection to voice calls. (#165716) Thanks @mbelinky and @jacobtomlinson.
- **Control UI subagents:** show when a chat is waiting on subagents, open the Subagents panel from the chat's subagent count and names, and surface child failures and attention in the parent chat. (#164190, #166142, #166224, #166312, #166347) Thanks @shakkernerd and @vincentkoc.
- **Control UI customization:** let themes customize Control UI branding, use agent avatars or unlocked Lobsterdex icons for browser tabs, choose favicon shapes, and add seven Lobsterdex character variants. (#168027, #165201, #166325, #167809, #159815) Thanks @vyctorbrzezowski, @jacobtomlinson, and @hannesrudolph.
- **Terminal:** add configurable terminal fonts with built-in Nerd Font icons. (#166180) Thanks @jacobtomlinson.
- **Control UI navigation:** copy file paths from chat tooltips, pin agents directly from the switcher, make agent menus easier to scan, let users hide a session's branch PR row, and simplify optional question cards. (#164431, #165640, #165641, #166366, #168040, #150587) Thanks @jjjhenriksen, @vyctorbrzezowski, and @RomneyDa.
- **Skill Workshop:** show each skill with its changes, files, and history in one view. (#167440) Thanks @obviyus.
- **iOS:** connect the Gateway through native Cloudflare Access with app-owned browser and profile admission. (#147244, #147238) Thanks @vincentkoc, @Solvely-Colin, @Patrick-Erichsen, and @RomneyDa.
- **ClawHub:** browse and search ClawHub plugins and skills through the Gateway. (#163459) Thanks @jacobtomlinson.
- **Plugins:** let plugin tools deliver their finished reply without a second model turn, allow every loaded plugin its own queue modes, and select plugin-owned self-hosted executors. (#164558, #165965, #161609) Thanks @mbelinky and @sjf-oa.
- **Plugins:** pick the newest official plugin release the running OpenClaw supports and keep a working plugin when its matching release is unavailable. (#167485, #166588) Thanks @charlesBerg-ux.
- **Workboard:** pin, unpin, and delete boards from the sidebar, keep card notes selectable with a roomier notes editor, and keep column edits on rename. (#165020, #166625, #167348) Thanks @rogeriochaves, @llmsommelier, and @obviyus.
- **GitHub:** support asynchronous PR merges and compact the Publish PR card. (#163579, #165219) Thanks @vincentkoc.
- **Session performance:** serve per-turn session projections, entry reads, authority checks, compaction reads, and first-turn headers from worker threads to keep the Gateway main thread responsive. (#164779, #165028, #165205, #165406, #165401, #165581, #165819, #165027, #165367, #164747, #164989, #165073)
- **Session list and search performance:** stop Control UI list refresh bursts, bound list materialization, scope and prefilter transcript search, speed up cold suggestion lists, and retain previews across metadata edits. (#162280, #164764, #165080, #165089, #165570, #165150, #165834, #165096, #165932, #166635, #165887, #167909) Thanks @RomneyDa.
- **Turn database performance:** reduce SQLite statements, worker requests, and redundant reads per chat turn, batch snapshot and metadata queries, and reuse admitted schema and reader facts. (#164490, #166041, #166053, #166054, #166074, #166102, #166541, #166503, #166519, #166698, #167278, #167686, #167685, #167690, #167932, #167046, #166966, #166925, #167291, #166703, #167029, #165360, #165193)
- **State database performance:** speed up cold agent database admission and crash recovery, reuse integrity checks on clean restarts, stop reopening executors when switching agents, and release leases promptly during shutdown. (#164846, #165070, #165186, #165293, #165680, #166112, #165993, #167001, #168008, #164788, #164962, #165085, #165910, #166822) Thanks @RomneyDa.
- **Maintenance and history performance:** lighten idle and manual maintenance, lifecycle cleanup, archive, reset, and trajectory retention work, and speed history reads with nested tool activity. (#164851, #164755, #164938, #165081, #165082, #165254, #165090, #165074, #165274, #165678, #167268, #167070, #167549, #167643, #168013, #167449, #165221, #165181, #165093, #165086, #165111, #165377, #165495, #165909, #166069, #166631, #166778, #166804, #167434, #167915, #167959) Thanks @Patrick-Erichsen, @obviyus, and @DonnieFi.
- **Agent performance:** reduce retained heap, per-turn prompt allocations, transcript reads, and main-thread SQLite work during runs, preserve prompt cache across instruction refreshes and image cleanup, and reuse verified history images across turns. (#167454, #167922, #167682, #167547, #167698, #167613, #167355, #165142, #165404, #167282, #164685, #165012, #165410, #165370, #165552) Thanks @RomneyDa and @DonnieFi.
- **Model catalog performance:** speed up multi-provider catalog refreshes, avoid discovery on cold account reads and unrequested plugin catalogs, retain account catalogs during refresh, and reduce catalog worker heap. (#167101, #167334, #167359, #167009, #167008, #166007, #166434, #165911, #165708, #165547, #165034, #165491, #166602) Thanks @vincentkoc, @obviyus, and @xialonglee.
- **Subagent and ACP performance:** reduce startup registry restore latency, move bulk registry work off the Gateway thread, batch registry cohorts, and avoid full-session scans when resuming ACP sessions. (#165942, #165684, #165098, #167684, #167010, #167372, #165550, #167086) Thanks @RomneyDa.
- **Update performance:** updates stop rehashing unchanged runtime files while retaining the running updater and publishing the candidate, reducing update I/O. (#168958)

### Fixes

- **Gateway memory:** Gateway startup memory is back in the 2026.10.4 range: on a cold start, memory indexes open on the first search or turn that needs them instead of all at once after readiness, catalog, SQLite broker, and transcript worker heaps are capped, and memory search workers used by `openclaw agent` and memory recall retain less memory. (#174718, #172392) Thanks @RomneyDa, @xialonglee, @DonnieFi, @jjjhenriksen, and @jacobtomlinson.
- **Session data safety:** preserve user input and committed facts through restart recovery and failed publication, keep accepted locked appends settled before releasing the writer, and fence cross-store worker commits. (#165502, #167570, #165894, #168018, #168029)
- **Security boundaries:** fail closed when the process census cannot prove a temp root is unused, reject incompatible worker prompt contexts before launch, keep browser pairing credentials out of opener process arguments, expand `file:` SQLite targets before the exec live-state guard checks them, require approval before setup diagnostics repair state, run plugin `before_tool_call` hooks under `openclaw agent exec`, and reject oversized local workspace document saves. (#165079, #166268, #170289, #170253, #171960, #159333, #171938) Thanks @Dhotei, @vincentkoc, @obviyus, @eleqtrizit, @joseairosa, and @RomneyDa.

issues.title: Matrix: "listen" group policy — observe the room, reply only on mention
issues.body:
## Problem

Under Matrix's `mention` policy, messages that fail the policy check are dropped outright in `_on_message` (`nanobot/channels/matrix/runtime.py`) — the bot never ingests them. So in a busy group, when someone finally @mentions the bot, it has no knowledge of the conversation that happened since its last reply. Under `open` it replies to everything. There is no way to get "aware but quiet": read the room, respond only when addressed.

## Request

Add a third group policy value, **`"listen"`** (usable as the channel-wide `groupPolicy` and, with #6286 / PR #6287, per-room via `groupPolicyOverrides`):

- Every message from an allowed sender in a listen room is ingested.
- The bot replies only when mentioned (same `m.mentions` / `allowRoomMentions` semantics as `"mention"`).
- When a mention-triggered turn fires, the recently heard room chatter is attached as context for that turn, so the reply reflects the intervening conversation.

## Proposed v1 (channel-contained, no agent-core changes)

- A bounded per-room transcript buffer (oldest-dropped, hard caps on entries and characters) is filled at ingest time for unmentioned messages.
- On a mention-triggered turn the buffer is attached via the **existing trusted channel seam** `_runtime_context_blocks` (`nanobot/runtime_context.py`, `RUNTIME_CONTEXT_INPUT_META`) — blocks are appended to the turn's user content and persisted with a display-time-removal marker, and the buffer is cleared once consumed.
- No LLM cost for unheard messages; bounded memory; delimiters and caps per the `RuntimeContextBlock` docstring's "bound and delimit content obtained from untrusted sources" requirement.

## Future option (separate discussion if there's interest)

Fully persisting unheard room chatter into the session transcript *without* an agent turn would need an append-only admission path in the loop — today every non-user inbound becomes a `TurnKind.SYSTEM` turn, which runs the LLM. That interacts with auto-compaction/token burn, so it needs maintainer design review; v1 above needs none.

issues.title: Agnes AI (custom provider) double-encodes nested-object tool arguments as JSON strings
issues.body:
### Bug Description

When using Agnes AI (`apihub.agnes-ai.com/v1`, model `agnes-2.5-flash`, via `providers.custom`) as the model provider, any MCP tool call with a **nested-object parameter** fails with:

```
MCP error -32602: Input validation error: Invalid arguments for tool obsidian_get_note: Invalid input: expected object, received string at target
```

Root cause, confirmed by inspecting the raw session log (`workspace/sessions/*.jsonl`): Agnes emits the nested object as a **JSON-text string** instead of a real nested object. For example, calling `obsidian_get_note` (from `cyanheads/obsidian-mcp-server` via an MCP bridge), the actual `tool_calls[0].function.arguments` Agnes returned was:

```json
{"format": "content", "target": "{\"type\": \"path\", \"path\": \"Projects/nanobot.md\"}"}
```

`target` should be a real object (`{"type": "path", "path": "..."}`), but it arrives double-JSON-encoded as a string. The MCP server correctly rejects this per its schema.

This reproduces on **every** call to any tool with a nested-object parameter, 40+ consecutive attempts. Flat-parameter tools (e.g. `obsidian_list_notes`) succeed every time on the same connection — so this is isolated specifically to nested-object schema parameters, not a general MCP/transport failure.

**Isolated to Agnes, not a general nanobot bug:** I tested the identical call against two OpenRouter free-tier models to rule out nanobot's own tool-calling/dispatch layer:
- `openai/gpt-oss-20b:free` — different failure: the provider rejected the tool's schema outright (`"auto tool schema uses unsupported assertions or reserved metadata"`, likely the `oneOf` union on `target`).
- `nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free` — **worked correctly**. Raw log shows a genuine nested object: `{"target": {"type": "path", "path": "Projects/nanobot.md"}, "format": "content"}`, and the tool call succeeded with real content returned (verified against the file on disk).

This suggests nanobot correctly relays whatever the model emits — Agnes's function-calling output is what's malformed for nested-object schemas. Filing this as a bug against nanobot anyway since (a) it may be reproducible with other/related providers with similar function-calling limitations, and (b) a defensive repair on nanobot's side (similar to the fix already shipped for #1487's malformed-argument replay path) could make nanobot more robust against providers with this class of limitation, the same way #1487 already handles malformed `function.arguments` on history replay. Filing primarily as documentation for other Agnes AI users who hit the same wall, and to let the maintainers decide whether a defensive fix belongs here or is out of scope (upstream/Agnes-side only).

Related but distinct issues I checked first: #1487 (fixed a different code path — repairing malformed arguments on **history replay**, not the original construction) and #4864 (a different tool entirely — wrong tool name / XML-style call format confusion, unrelated to nested-object serialization).

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure nanobot with Agnes AI as the provider (`providers.custom` pointed at `apihub.agnes-ai.com/v1`, model `agnes-2.5-flash`) and any MCP server exposing a tool with a nested-object parameter (reproduced with `cyanheads/obsidian-mcp-server`'s `obsidian_get_note`, which takes `target: {type, path}` via a `oneOf` union).
2. Send a message forcing the model to call that tool, e.g.:
   ```
   nanobot agent -m "You MUST use ONLY the obsidian_get_note MCP tool to read the note at path 'some/note.md'. Do NOT use the file tool. If the tool call fails, report the EXACT error message verbatim and stop."
   ```
3. See error: `Invalid input: expected object, received string at target` on every attempt.

### Expected Behavior

The tool call should succeed with a genuine nested-object argument, as it does when using `nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free` via OpenRouter against the identical MCP server/tool/prompt.

### Relevant Logs

Malformed call (Agnes), from `workspace/sessions/<session>.jsonl`:
```json
{"role": "assistant", "content": "", "tool_calls": [{"id": "call_ed85de2e7e0b4008b8c28feb", "type": "function", "function": {"name": "mcp_obsidian_obsidian_get_note", "arguments": "{\"format\": \"content\", \"target\": \"{\\\"type\\\": \\\"path\\\", \\\"path\\\": \\\"Projects/nanobot.md\\\"}\"}"}}]}
```
```
MCP error -32602: Input validation error: Invalid arguments for tool obsidian_get_note: Invalid input: expected object, received string at target
```

Working call (OpenRouter/nemotron), same tool/prompt:
```json
{"role": "assistant", "content": "", "tool_calls": [{"id": "chatcmpl-tool-af190a63b0bff2d4", "type": "function", "function": {"name": "mcp_obsidian_obsidian_get_note", "arguments": "{\"target\": {\"type\": \"path\", \"path\": \"Projects/nanobot.md\"}, \"format\": \"content\"}"}}]}
```

### nanobot Version

0.3.0 (latest release, confirmed via `nanobot --version` and `pip index versions nanobot-ai`)

### Python Version

Other — 3.14.6 (`C:\Python314`) on PATH; nanobot itself installed as a standalone pipx-style binary, exact bundled interpreter version not independently confirmed.

### Operating System

Windows

### Channel / Platform

Other — reproduced via direct CLI (`nanobot agent -m "..."`), not through a chat channel.

### LLM Provider

Other — Agnes AI (`apihub.agnes-ai.com/v1`, model `agnes-2.5-flash`), configured via `providers.custom` (not a named provider preset).

### Configuration (Optional)

```json
{
  "providers": {
    "custom": {
      "apiBase": "https://apihub.agnes-ai.com/v1",
      "apiType": "auto"
    }
  },
  "modelPresets": {
    "agnes": {
      "provider": "custom",
      "model": "agnes-2.5-flash",
      "maxTokens": 4096,
      "contextWindowTokens": 65536,
      "temperature": 0.1
    }
  },
  "tools": {
    "mcpServers": {
      "obsidian": {
        "command": "jmunch-mcp",
        "args": ["--config", "obsidian.toml"]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Additional Context

Worked around locally by switching the default model preset to `nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free` via OpenRouter, with `agnes` kept as a `fallbackModels` entry rather than removed. This isn't a request to fix Agnes's own model behavior (out of nanobot's control) — filing so other Agnes users searching for this exact error message find it, and so maintainers can decide whether a defensive argument-repair (parallel to the #1487 fix, but for initial construction rather than history replay) is worth adding.

issues.title: Cron completion consumes schedules changed during execution
issues.body:
Rescheduling a running cron job can lose the next occurrence when the current run finishes. If the replacement is a one-shot schedule, completion disables or deletes it; if it is a recurring schedule, completion recalculates its deadline from the finish time.

Reproduced on main at `6ff96f2a8f10bfef7f4e7ec519531b367d75eca6` (nanobot 0.3.5, Python 3.12.2, Windows). No model or channel connection is needed:

```python
import asyncio
import time
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

from nanobot.cron.service import CronService
from nanobot.cron.types import CronSchedule


async def main():
    with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
        async def execute(job):
            service.update_job(
                job.id,
                schedule=CronSchedule(kind="at", at_ms=int(time.time() * 1000) + 120_000),
            )

        service = CronService(Path(directory) / "cron" / "jobs.json", on_job=execute)
        job = service.add_job(
            name="Report",
            schedule=CronSchedule(kind="at", at_ms=int(time.time() * 1000) + 60_000),
            message="Summarize the latest figures",
            session_key="websocket:report",
            origin_channel="websocket",
            origin_chat_id="report",
            delete_after_run=True,
        )
        await service.run_job(job.id)
        print(service.get_job(job.id))


asyncio.run(main())
```

Actual: `None`. Expected: the job remains enabled with its newly scheduled occurrence. The same happens when another coroutine edits the job while its callback is awaiting.

The completion step needs to advance only the schedule that started that run. I have a small fix and regression coverage for both one-shot and recurring replacements.

issues.title: Telegram: classify remote media URLs with query strings by path extension
issues.body:
## Problem

The Telegram channel determines media type from the full remote URL string. For a valid image URL such as `https://cards.scryfall.io/.../card.jpg?width=672`, the inferred extension becomes `jpg?width=672`, so the channel treats it as a document.

As a result, consecutive remote images are sent as separate documents rather than a photo album.

## Expected behavior

Determine the extension from the URL path, ignoring its query string and fragment. The example above should be classified as a photo and be eligible for `sendMediaGroup`.

## Reproduction

Send an outbound Telegram message with several `.jpg` or `.png` URLs that contain query parameters. The debug log reports `type=document remote=True`; Telegram receives separate file attachments.

## Scope

This is distinct from #6121, which adds album delivery for media already classified as photos or videos.

prs.title: fix(docker): make first-run Compose services usable
prs.body:
## Description

Fixes #6165.

The issue reports that a fresh `git clone && docker compose up` produces a nanobot that is unreachable on every published port, with `nanobot-api` crash-looping. Confirmed at the code level and reproduced end-to-end against the committed compose file:

- `entrypoint.sh` only bootstraps `config.json` when `RENDER=true`, so a local `docker compose up` starts with no config at all.
- The resulting default binds are container-local: `GatewayConfig.host` and the WebSocket channel's `host` both default to `127.0.0.1` (`nanobot/config/schema.py`, `nanobot/channels/websocket/runtime.py`), so the ports the compose file publishes (`8765`, `127.0.0.1:18790`) can never reach them — `curl` gets `Connection reset by peer`, matching the issue.
- `nanobot-api` is started with `serve --host 0.0.0.0` but no `api_key`, so the non-loopback auth guard rejects the host and the process exits (1) into the compose `restart: unless-stopped` loop — the "constantly exiting and restarting" container from the issue.

Reproduction log (before this change): gateway healthy but `WebSocket server listening on ws://127.0.0.1:8765/`; `curl` 8765/18790 → exit 56 (reset); api restart loop with `Error: host 0.0.0.0 is available beyond this device but api_key is not set.`

### Change

- Default Compose startup keeps both the gateway and OpenAI-compatible API running. `serve` reuses the existing unconfigured-provider runtime when provider/model setup is incomplete. Authenticated chat-completion requests return HTTP 503 with `configuration_error` before executing a turn, for both regular and streaming requests. Health and model-discovery endpoints remain available; API authentication requirements are preserved. Restart the API after configuring a model to load those settings, as with other configuration changes.
- First-boot Docker configuration uses Python models, JSON serialization, secure random credentials, and atomic `save_config`. A shared file lock serializes initialization when both services start. The entrypoint drops to UID 1000 before initialization, matching bind-mount ownership and the Compose capability boundary. Existing configurations and credentials are preserved.
- Only gateway/API startup triggers Docker initialization. CLI commands, including first-time non-interactive `onboard`, retain their original behavior without an extra overwrite prompt.
- `NANOBOT_WEB_TOKEN` and `NANOBOT_API_KEY` can supply first-boot credentials; generated credentials are printed by whichever service initializes the config. Deployment documentation uses combined Compose logs, leads with startup and WebUI model setup, and documents API setup errors. The image includes `curl`; Render retains its template/environment-reference flow.
- Docker CI checks the actual service lifecycle, credentials, API setup errors, container recreation, read-only mounts, and the legacy onboarding command. Test fixture writes use the container runtime UID so the smoke test also works for non-root CI runners.

### Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix

### Related Issue

- Fixes #6165

### Testing

- Windows: CLI, onboarding, OpenAI API, streaming, attachments, and Docker initializer regressions — 859 passed, 28 platform-dependent tests skipped.
- Ruff, touched-file strict BasedPyright with the test interpreter, Python import boundaries, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Ubuntu 22.04 under WSL: complete Dockerfile build, including compiled WebUI and default WhatsApp dependencies. The Docker smoke test also passed as a non-root host user (UID 1001).
- Generated and special-character credentials: both default services start; WebUI login accepts the persisted credential and rejects incorrect passwords; API health remains available before model setup; authenticated regular and streaming model requests return HTTP 503 with a setup error. Exactly one service initializes the shared config.
- First-time `docker compose run --rm --no-deps -T nanobot-cli onboard` succeeds without an overwrite prompt. Container recreation preserves provider settings and credentials despite changed environment values. Restarting the configured API enables authenticated model discovery.
- A read-only config mount exits with code 1, writes no config, and prints no successful login message. Test containers and networks are cleaned up.
- Authentication and API behavior were verified through real HTTP endpoints. No real model requests or browser interaction were exercised. 

- Windows config checks explicitly read and write UTF-8. The native handoff test keeps its ACL/readability/cleanup assertions with a 45-second PowerShell/C# cold-start budget.
- Remote CI: all 9 checks passed for `dfe3199d0`, including Windows Python 3.14: [Test Suite](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/38373244018).

prs.title: fix(session): prevent consumed follow-ups from replaying after restart
prs.body:
## Why

A follow-up can enter the durable pending journal after the active turn's detached draft was created. Acknowledging it only on that old draft leaves the canonical journal unchanged even after its input and answer are committed, so recovery can execute the input again after restart. This also creates disagreement between the chat body and My messages when the replay has no new user transcript event.

Related: [NAN-273](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-273)

## What changed

- Make consumed follow-up IDs an explicit draft command applied by the Session owner against the latest journal, in the same SQLite transaction as history. Preserve unconsumed arrivals and retain the command for retry after rollback.
- Preserve each input's admission ID and timestamp through journaling, recovery, injection, and history persistence, independently of the execution consuming it.
- Keep normal restored thread rows and My messages on the same stable projection IDs, original timestamps, anchors, and cursors. Include canonical recovery data in response validators, preserve intentional identical-text inputs, and leave unknown timestamps unset.
- Remove compatibility for anomalous historical data produced by this bug: no answer-turn-ID inference, cross-history replay deduplication/suppression, additional logical input identity wire fields, or logical fork-offset rewriting.

### Sequence: before the fix

`F1` arrives after the detached draft was created. Saving its history does not acknowledge the latest canonical journal because the old draft never contained `F1`.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant L as AgentLoop
    participant D as Detached turn draft
    participant O as SessionState owner
    participant S as SQLite history + journal
    participant R as Restart recovery

    O->>D: Create draft and baseline, neither contains F1
    L->>O: queue_followup(F1)
    O->>S: Commit pending journal = [F1]
    O-->>L: Durable follow-up ID F1
    L->>L: Inject F1 at the next model boundary
    L->>D: _save_turn adds F1 input and answer
    L->>D: Acknowledge F1 on the old draft
    Note over D: No matching journal entry, acknowledgement is a no-op
    L->>O: finish_turn(draft)
    Note over D,O: Unchanged pending metadata yields no removal command
    O->>S: Commit history, canonical pending still contains F1
    Note over L,R: Gateway restarts after normal completion
    R->>S: Read durable pending follow-ups
    S-->>R: F1
    R->>L: Publish F1 to the inbound bus again
    Note over L: Input executes again despite its committed answer
```

### Sequence: after the fix

The draft carries an explicit consumed-ID command. The owner applies it to the latest journal inside the history transaction, a later, unconsumed `F2` survives. Input IDs and admission times travel with the saved user rows, independently of execution IDs.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant L as AgentLoop
    participant D as Detached turn draft
    participant O as SessionState owner
    participant S as SQLite history + journal
    participant R as Restart recovery

    O->>D: Create draft and baseline, neither contains F1
    L->>O: queue_followup(F1)
    O->>S: Commit F1 with input ID and admission time
    O-->>L: Durable follow-up ID F1
    L->>L: Inject F1 at the next model boundary
    L->>D: _save_turn adds F1 input and answer
    L->>D: Set consumed_followup_ids = {F1}
    L->>O: queue_followup(F2) after that model boundary
    O->>S: Commit pending journal = [F1, F2]
    Note over D,S: F2 is durable but has not been consumed
    L->>O: finish_turn(draft)
    rect rgb(240, 245, 250)
        Note over O,S: One existing SQLite write transaction
        O->>S: BEGIN, load latest canonical session
        O->>O: Merge history and acknowledge exactly F1
        O->>S: Write history and pending journal
        alt Transaction commits
            O->>S: COMMIT
            O->>O: Publish committed state
            O->>D: Refresh draft from committed state
            Note over D,S: History contains F1, pending journal contains only F2
        else Write fails
            O->>S: ROLLBACK
            Note over D,S: No partial history or acknowledgement, draft retains F1 command for retry
        end
    end
    opt Gateway restarts after successful commit
        R->>S: Read durable pending follow-ups
        S-->>R: F2 only
        R->>L: Publish F2, do not replay F1
    end
```

The rollback branch leaves genuinely uncommitted inputs recoverable. For normal restored inputs, thread backfill and My messages share stable projection IDs, original times, and navigation anchors; independent same-text sends remain separate.

## Scope

Prevent new consumed-follow-up replay while preserving genuinely uncommitted input recovery and normal WebUI replay/navigation. Per the user's clarified requirement, compatibility or repair for anomalous historical data created while this bug existed is explicitly out of scope, superseding the original historical-data compatibility criterion in NAN-273. Existing stored records are left untouched; no production journal clearing, duplicate suppression, or historical migration is included. The separate stale browser queue issue, NAN-275, is unchanged.

## Tradeoffs

The owner acknowledges exact consumed IDs instead of clearing the journal or inferring consumption from a stale metadata diff. Normal missing-transcript recovery remains supported, but this PR no longer attempts to identify or reconcile old erroneous replays. Raw-transcript fork offsets retain their existing meaning; missing-transcript fork-boundary behavior is not expanded by this fix.

## Blast Radius

Affects WebSocket follow-up persistence/recovery and normal WebUI thread projection/navigation. The existing HTTP/event payload shape and protocol floor are retained; the proposed `inputId` / `input_id` additions have been removed. Ordinary complete thread pages retain bounded chunk reads without loading canonical history. Conditional responses for recovered pages include the canonical snapshot used for display.

## Verification

Reverified on Windows AMD64 / Python 3.14.6 after narrowing the scope, pinned to published head `1fd31f7e0747d9c02a21b3d8d0ec66687959b068`. Source fingerprints, logs and synthetic screenshots are retained outside tracked source.

| Check | Actual result |
| --- | --- |
| `python -m pytest tests/session tests/agent -q --tb=short` | 2123 passed, 4 skipped |

## Why

The sidebar settings gear looks unstable during hover rotation. Its custom outline, introduced in #6074, is asymmetric about the hub. The first version of this PR corrected that geometry, but user preview feedback showed that this alone did not resolve the perceived wobble.

A follow-up controlled browser comparison found that the active outer-SVG transform also changes the rasterized appearance of the tiny circular hub even when its computed center stays fixed. A fixed geometric center therefore did not establish visual acceptance.

## What changed

- Shorten the two vertical outline segments from `2.4` to `1.8` to restore symmetry about `(12, 12)`.
- Apply the hover transform only to the gear outline path, around the SVG viewBox center. Leave the outer SVG and circular hub untransformed.
- Add real-browser regressions for outline symmetry and for hover entry/exit that actually rotates the outline without changing the hub's screen matrix.

## Scope / blast radius

The shared SettingsIcon and its settings-specific hover CSS. Preserve the circular hub, size, stroke, accessible labels, button layout, 90° rotation, 300 ms duration, easing, hover/disabled guards and reduced-motion behavior. Other icons, gateway behavior and configuration are unchanged.

## Verification at `8edba68ac0172d9fc528107fefe120d0e1731ef9`

- **RED → GREEN:** the original outline has maximum symmetry error `0.860614`; the corrected outline has error `0.00000582`. The new hub-transform regression also fails against the first PR version and passes with the path-only hover correction.

- **PASS:** `bun run test -- src/tests/app-layout.test.tsx src/tests/sidebar-selection-highlight.test.tsx src/tests/settings-sidebar.test.tsx` — 111/111.

prs.title: fix(providers): keep parallel tool calls apart when the stream omits index
prs.body:
Gemini's OpenAI-compatible API streams parallel tool calls without `tool_calls[].index`: each call arrives whole (id, name and arguments) in its own chunk, and the turn ends with `finish_reason: "stop"`. `_parse_chunks` falls back to the call's position inside its chunk when `index` is missing. That's 0 for every one of these chunks, so all the calls of a turn land in one buffer: the id and name of the last call win, and the arguments are concatenated.

Replaying a captured `gemini-3.5-flash` stream with two parallel `get_weather` calls through the `openai` client and `_parse_chunks`:

```
before: call_4234487 get_weather '{"city":"Paris"}{"city":"Tokyo"}'
after:  call_4234484 get_weather {'city': 'Paris'}
        call_4234487 get_weather {'city': 'Tokyo'}
```

### Change

A delta without `index` now starts a new call when it carries an id different from the current call's id, or a name on an id-less call that already has one. Anything else is appended to the current call, so providers that stream unindexed argument fragments keep working. Deltas that do carry `index` are handled as before.

### Tests

- `test_parse_chunks_keeps_parallel_calls_without_index_apart`: the two-call Gemini shape from the capture (thought signature shortened). It fails on `main` and passes with the fix.
- `test_parse_chunks_appends_unindexed_fragments_to_the_last_call`: id-less argument fragments still join the current call.
- `tests/providers` plus `tests/agent/test_gemini_thought_signature.py`: 1464 passed.
- `ruff check nanobot/`: clean.

This change was made with Claude Code; the tests above were run on the branch to check it.

prs.title: feat(matrix): add "listen" group policy (observe room, reply on mention)
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds a third Matrix group policy value — **`"listen"`** — for rooms where the bot should read the whole conversation but reply only when mentioned (#6288).

Under `mention`, messages that fail the policy check are dropped outright (`_on_message`), so the bot has no knowledge of the conversation when it's finally mentioned. Under `open` it replies to everything. `listen` closes that gap:

- Every message from an **allowed sender** in a listen room is ingested into a bounded per-room buffer.
- The bot replies **only when mentioned** — same `m.mentions` / `allowRoomMentions` semantics as `mention`.
- On a mention-triggered turn, the buffered chatter rides along as **trusted runtime context** so the answer reflects the intervening conversation.

## How context is attached

Uses the existing trusted channel seam `RUNTIME_CONTEXT_INPUT_META` (`nanobot/runtime_context.py`) — this is the first channel producer of `_runtime_context_blocks`, whose docstring describes exactly this: *"trusted, channel-produced context blocks"* read from inbound metadata. Blocks are appended to the turn's user content and persisted with a display-time-removal marker, so the LLM retains the context in subsequent turns while users never see the injected block as chat output.

Bounds per the `RuntimeContextBlock` docstring's requirement ("callers must bound and delimit content obtained from untrusted sources"): 30 messages / 6,000 chars per room, 500 chars per line, header-delimited block, buffer cleared once consumed. No LLM calls for unheard messages; no agent-core changes.

## Behavior details

- Deny-listed senders are never buffered.
- Direct rooms (≤2 members) bypass the policy entirely, as today.
- Media messages buffer a caption or `[attachment]` note — downloads/transcription are not triggered for unheard messages.
- Composes with per-room `groupPolicyOverrides` from #6287 once that lands (a trivial rebase in `_should_process_message`).

## Fixes #6288

## Tests

Seven new tests in `nanobot/channels/matrix/tests/test_matrix_channel.py`:

1. `"listen"` accepted via attribute and camelCase config; unknown policy values still rejected.
2. Buffer bounds: oldest-dropped at 30 entries, 6,000-char budget, 500-char line truncation.
3. Unmentioned messages buffered with no reply/typing; the next mention triggers one turn carrying a bounded `matrix_room_transcript` block containing the buffered line; buffer cleared (subsequent mention carries no block).
4. Denied senders neither replied to nor buffered.
5. Direct rooms unaffected (no buffering, normal DM path).
6. `open` policy rooms never buffer (regression guard).
7. Media captions buffered as notes.

Verified locally: 127 matrix-channel tests pass, 152 channel-contract tests pass, `ruff check nanobot tests` clean, import-boundary check passes, `basedpyright` clean (0 errors) on touched files. WebUI locale copy added for all 10 languages (en, es, fr, id, ja, ko, pt-BR, vi, zh-CN, zh-TW).

> Note: this branch is based on current `main` without #6287. If #6287 merges first, expect small conflicts in `_should_process_message` (adjacent lines) and the docs table — happy to rebase.

prs.title: feat(channels): add Sendblue iMessage and SMS transport
prs.body:
Adds a native Sendblue channel so a user can text a nanobot agent over iMessage/SMS and receive its answer on the same phone. The setup guide covers a fresh free account, the required human phone/contact verification, model prerequisites, secret configuration, and receive-webhook registration.

The adapter uses the existing channel package, setup manifest, manager, and message bus. It checks the webhook secret, receiving line, and sender before admitting a direct message. It suppresses duplicate callbacks within a bounded in-memory window and avoids automatically repeating a send after an ambiguous POST outcome.

### Scope

- Direct-message text; incoming attachments produce an explicit unsupported-attachment notice. Groups and delivery-status callbacks are ignored.
- Sender allowlist required; `*` is an explicit opt-in.
- Deduplication covers the last 4096 accepted handles in one process. There is no durable inbox or exactly-once guarantee.
- Secrets use the existing configuration/environment mechanism. There are no new runtime dependencies.
- Manual setup guide; no dedicated WebUI panel in this proposal.

### Validation

Head: `535e6cb4998ade439a839345f545fb59cb4bcfc0`

prs.body:

prs.title: fix(cron): keep pending interval runs across gateway restarts
prs.body:
## Problem

`every` jobs lose their pending run whenever the gateway restarts:

- `CronService._recompute_next_runs()` (called from `start()`) recomputes every enabled job from `now`, which for an `every` schedule means `now + every_ms`.
- `register_system_job()` (called on every gateway boot for Dream and heartbeat) also rebuilds the job state from `now`.

So each restart pushes an interval job back by a full interval. With the default Dream schedule (`every` 2h), a gateway that is restarted more often than every two hours never runs Dream at all; the same happens to the heartbeat and to user `every` jobs with long intervals.

Reproduction on current `main` (Dream registered as on boot, restart at +90 min and +180 min):

```
boot@0   next at +120 min
boot@90  next at +210 min   # expected +120
boot@180 next at +300 min
```

## Fix

Add `_resume_next_run()`: for `every` schedules, keep a persisted `next_run_at_ms` when it is still in the future and no more than one interval away; otherwise fall back to `_compute_next_run()` as before. It is used in `_recompute_next_runs()` and in `register_system_job()` (only when the stored system job is enabled and has the same schedule, so a changed interval is still computed from now).

Unchanged behavior: `cron` and `at` schedules, and overdue `every` runs (still `now + every_ms`, no catch-up firing).

## Tests

- `test_restart_keeps_pending_every_job_run`: a bound 24h job restarted after 23h keeps its original next run.
- `test_reregistering_system_job_keeps_pending_every_run`: re-registering Dream on boot keeps the pending run; changing the interval recomputes it.

Both fail on `main` and pass with this change.

## Validation

- `pytest tests/cron`: 160 passed
- full `pytest`: 8758 passed, 14 failed; the same 14 (`tests/webui/test_remote_*`, `tests/webui/test_ssh_config.py`, `tests/channels/test_channel_setup.py`) also fail on unmodified `main` in my environment (no SSH / optional channel deps)
- `ruff check nanobot tests conftest.py`: clean
- `basedpyright` on the changed files: 0 errors

AI-assisted: an AI coding agent helped trace the issue and draft the patch and tests; the change was reviewed and verified locally with the commands above.

prs.title: fix(mcp): discover all resource and prompt pages
prs.body:
MCP servers can paginate their resource and prompt catalogs, but `connect_mcp_servers()` currently requests each catalog only once. Resources and prompts after the first page never reach the agent's tool registry. Tool pagination was addressed in #5916; this change covers the two remaining supported catalogs.

Follow each catalog's `nextCursor` before registering its wrappers. Empty pages and empty-string cursors are supported, and repeated cursors stop discovery. If a later page fails, that catalog is left unregistered while existing tools and the other catalog remain available. The existing `enabledTools` restriction still skips resource and prompt discovery entirely.

Validation:

- All six new regression scenarios failed on the original implementation.
- MCP test module: `120 passed`.
- `uv run --no-sync pytest tests/tools tests/agent/test_mcp_connection.py tests/agent/test_mcp_reconnect_crash.py tests/agent/test_mcp_transient_retry.py -q`: `1144 passed, 66 skipped` on Windows / Python 3.13.
- Ruff, strict BasedPyright for the production module, and `git diff --check` passed.
- A separate offline protocol check used MCP SDK 1.30.0's real `Server` and `ClientSession` over in-memory streams. It verified three-page discovery, invoking a later-page resource and prompt through `ToolRegistry.execute()`, and skipping both catalogs under a tool allowlist. Only the stdio transport factory was replaced.

prs.title: fix(mcp): prevent credential leakage in discovery error logs
prs.body:
When `resources/list` or `prompts/list` fails, the discovery handlers log the raw exception at DEBUG. HTTPX status errors include the request URL, which can contain userinfo, path credentials, and query signatures; MCP errors can also include arbitrary server-provided secrets. These handlers are not covered by the URL redaction added in #4584.

Log the exception type instead of its message in both handlers. Diagnostics retain the server name, discovery stage, and error category. Discovery still continues so tools and the other catalog can be registered after a failure.

The regression test covers HTTPX-generated status errors and MCP RPC errors in both catalogs, checks the rendered DEBUG output for fake secrets, and verifies that the connection and other capabilities survive. All four cases failed against the unchanged base and pass with this patch.

prs.title: fix: use JSON equality for enum validation
prs.body:
Tool argument validation uses Python membership for `enum`, so `True` is accepted by `{"enum": [1]}`, and `0` is accepted by `{"enum": [false]}`. The same problem occurs inside array and object enum values. JSON Schema treats booleans and numbers as distinct types.

This replaces enum membership with a recursive JSON value comparison. It still accepts numerically equal values such as `1` and `1.0`, and compares objects independently of key order.

The regression test goes through `ToolRegistry.execute` and checks that rejected arguments never reach the tool implementation.

### Validation

```bash
python -m pytest tests/tools/test_tool_validation.py -q -k 'not test_exec_guard_allows_public_urls'
ruff check nanobot/agent/tools/base.py tests/tools/test_tool_validation.py
```

109 tests passed; 3 public URL cases were deselected because they require network/DNS access. BasedPyright also reported no errors or warnings for `nanobot/agent/tools/base.py`.

Related: #5965 changes null validation in the same file. This patch only changes enum equality.

prs.title: fix(tools): accept integral JSON numbers for integer parameters
prs.body:
## Problem

A model can return `{"query":"hello","count":3.0}` for a tool whose `count` parameter has an integer schema. [JSON Schema treats numbers with no fractional part as integers](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/reference/numeric#integer), but Python decodes `3.0` as a float. Nanobot rejects the call with `count should be integer` before the tool can run.

The same mismatch affects nullable integer fields and unions such as `["integer", "string"]`.

## Fix

Use one integer predicate for validation and union matching. When an integral float matches an integer parameter, convert it to a Python `int` before execution so tools can safely use it for counts, ranges, or indexes. Fractional values, booleans, and non-finite numbers remain invalid integers.

## Tests

Added three schema cases and a registry execution regression. All four fail on the base revision; the registry now executes the call with `count=3`.

- Full tool-validation suite: **144 passed**.
- Existing fraction, boolean, range, and union checks pass.
- Ruff, BasedPyright on the changed implementation, import-boundary checks, and `git diff --check`: passed.

prs.title: fix(providers): preserve the first SSE event with a leading UTF-8 BOM
prs.body:
A Responses API SSE stream starting with a UTF-8 BOM silently loses its first `data:` event. For example, deltas `Hello ` and `world` produce only `world`, including in the content callback.

Strip exactly one BOM from the first decoded line in `iter_sse`, as required by the [SSE decoding rules](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/server-sent-events.html#interpreting-an-event-stream). Preserve U+FEFF inside response text. The regression uses a real HTTPX response containing UTF-8 bytes and covers both BOM-prefixed and ordinary streams.

Validation:

- Responses parsing, terminal-stream, Codex and xAI provider tests: 213 passed.
- Ruff for `nanobot/` and the changed test file: passed.
- BasedPyright for both changed files: 0 errors, 0 warnings.

Legacy JSONL files written with `ensure_ascii=False` can contain U+0085, U+2028, and U+2029 inside JSON strings. Python's `splitlines()` treats these characters as record boundaries, causing valid sessions to fail migration.

prs.title: fix(deepseek): align model capabilities with the official API
prs.body:
## Why

DeepSeek serves both legacy Flash names through the current multimodal `deepseek-flash`, but nanobot silently removes images for `deepseek-v4-flash`. Model discovery also discards official capability metadata and suggests generic reasoning levels. Keep immutable compatibility facts in the existing provider model registry and normalize advisory discovery metadata at the settings boundary.

## What changed

- Resolve Flash aliases through shared model metadata and preserve image input on Chat Completions and Responses; Pro remains text-only. Keep wire model IDs and existing official/proxy API routing unchanged.
- Validate catalog output limits, modalities and supported/default thinking levels, with known-model fallback. Preserve the explicit `none` control even when the live catalog lists only enabled thinking levels; distinguish it from provider-default and keep custom strings usable.
- Extend the settings DTO with optional fields, reuse the existing picker without frontend provider branches, and document naming, budgets and deferred search support.

## Scope

Tracks [NAN-271](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-271). This PR was initially published as **Draft** at `b0eb7608517`; bounded real-key verification subsequently passed on `2ecebac8a96fd96ea94c47898e9984a2baac5844` before requesting Ready for review.

Does not enable standalone DeepSeek Search/Fetch, Pro hosted search, Anthropic Messages or Files; does not migrate cross-provider reasoning configuration. Does not rewrite users' model IDs or change existing preset budgets, API routing, credentials or services. Catalog output limits remain advisory; existing new-preset context initialization is unchanged.

## Tradeoffs

Runtime image policy uses the immutable provider record, not online discovery or a new network/cache service. Valid online metadata takes precedence over static fallback, with a known explicit off control separate from enabled thinking strengths. Raw `api_capabilities` is not forwarded: its Messages behavior has no adapter consumer here.

The suspected Responses reasoning-history incompatibility did not reproduce: a real Chat-history reconstruction containing `output_text` reasoning parts returned HTTP 200 and the expected synthetic token. The shared OpenAI converter therefore remains unchanged; this single successful case is not a guarantee about every future endpoint or payload.

## Blast Radius

DeepSeek message sanitization and additive model catalog fields. Unknown/custom models retain manual values and do not inherit DeepSeek model facts. The existing picker tolerates hosts without the new fields; older clients can ignore the optional additions. Other providers' request conversion and third-party naming/routing are unchanged.

## Verification

- Documentation-only follow-up `6736f5f0e` reorganizes `docs/providers.md`: DeepSeek has its own section, Muse guidance is under OpenCode, and general preset guidance is shared. All 21 JSON examples and 22 local links/anchors passed checks; documented API defaults were checked against the provider registry. Runtime/frontend/test sources are unchanged from `2ecebac8a96f`, so existing code verification is carried forward without new live API calls.
- Relevant provider/settings suite: **1624 passed** (`PYTHONPATH=tests .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/providers tests/webui/test_settings_routes.py tests/webui/test_settings_models.py tests/webui/test_settings_api.py -q --disable-warnings`). Legacy-alias regression demonstrated before the fix; updated the existing text-only image test to use nonvisual Pro instead of the now-visual Flash alias.
- Model-settings frontend suite: **75 passed** (`PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:$PATH /home/cyr/.bun/bin/bun run test src/tests/settings-models.test.tsx --reporter verbose`, in `webui/`).
- Full repository Ruff and BasedPyright: passed, 0 type errors/warnings. Python import boundaries: passed. `bun run check:imports`, `bun run test:imports`: passed (37 tests, one Windows-only case skipped on Linux). `bun run lint` and `bun run build`: passed; build retains the bundle-size warning.
- Isolated gateway + Chromium, synthetic local catalog: `max`, `none`, Default and a custom effort each saved and survived reload; no browser runtime/console errors. Catalog fields reached the existing picker. Owned gateway, fixture server, browser and ports were cleaned up. This browser check is not a real model call.
- **Real DeepSeek official API**, locally configured credential loaded only in-process: **14/14 HTTP 200 requests and 26 checks passed on code head `2ecebac8a96fd96ea94c47898e9984a2baac5844`**, plus one earlier successful `/models` discovery request (15 total, within a 16-request budget). The initial discovery exposed that live `supported_levels` omits `none`; a failing regression and the final normalization correction cover that observation.
  - Authenticated `/v1/models`: real max output, modalities, enabled levels/default retained; explicit off control preserved.
  - Chat Completions and Responses basic calls with `none`: expected marker returned, no thinking content.
  - Canonical Flash and both legacy aliases × both APIs: in-memory blue PNG retained on the wire and correctly identified (6 calls).
  - Both APIs: low-effort streaming function call, reasoning deltas, synthetic tool result and final answer; Responses continued from raw provider state (4 calls).
  - Chat-history reasoning reconstructed into Responses without saved Responses state: expected token returned.
- Only synthetic prompts/image/tool results were sent; no user chats/files. Each model call capped at 1024 output tokens, SDK retries disabled. Reported aggregate usage: 3054 input / 137 output tokens, including 765 cache-read input tokens; billing was not queried. No keys, headers or raw configuration were committed or published.

Local evidence (not committed) is retained under `.nanobot-workflows/runs/deepseek-nan271-20261018/` in the agent workspace, including exact-head live JSON, first discovery, red/green logs and browser evidence. Python checks were rerun after the final normalization correction; unchanged frontend/build/browser evidence is carried forward because its source and DTO contract are unchanged. Remote CI on the current head is still queued/in progress, not reported as passed. Live coverage is Linux/Python 3.12 with OpenAI SDK 3.33.0 against official Flash; Pro image policy and proxy routing have offline regression coverage, not live third-party/proxy validation.

prs.title: fix(napcat): keep a message whose image declares a non-numeric file_size
prs.body:
## What

`_download_image` rejects an image upfront when Napcat declares a size above `max_image_bytes`:

```python
try:
    declared_size = int(info["file_size"])
    if declared_size > max_bytes:
        ...
        return None
except (TypeError, KeyError):
    pass
```

`_parse_segments` already documents that Napcat sends `file_size` as a string ("bytes, sometimes a string", `runtime.py:331-333`). A string that is not a number — `""`, `"unknown"`, `"12KB"` — makes `int()` raise `ValueError`, and that is the one exception this guard does not catch.

## Why it matters

The `ValueError` escapes `_download_image` into its caller `_on_message` (`runtime.py:254-256`), which has no surrounding `try`, so the loop aborts **before** `_handle_message` runs. The whole inbound message is dropped — the image *and* the text the user sent with it — and the only trace is a `napcat: message handler failed: ...` warning from the background-task callback.

Skipping the upfront check is also what the code already intends for a size it cannot read: the check is only an optimization, and the streamed download below still caps the body at `max_image_bytes` and returns `None` when it is exceeded, so nothing unbounded reaches disk. The new branch logs the unusable declaration instead of swallowing it silently.

## Tests

Two regression tests in `nanobot/channels/napcat/tests/test_napcat_channel.py`:

- `test_download_image_ignores_unparsable_declared_size` — declared sizes `""`, `"unknown"`, `"12KB"` now download the image instead of raising.
- `test_message_with_unparsable_image_size_still_routes` — a private message carrying text plus such an image still reaches the bus with its text and its media path.

Before the fix both fail on `origin/main`:

```
E   ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: ''
    nanobot/channels/napcat/runtime.py:536: ValueError
2 failed, 7 passed in 4.66s
```

After it:

```
$ pytest nanobot/channels/napcat -q
9 passed in 1.40s
$ ruff check nanobot tests conftest.py
All checks passed!
```

`basedpyright nanobot/channels/napcat` reports the same unknown-type class as pristine `main` (69 errors before, 70 after — the extra one is the new `logger.warning` call, a class every existing log line in this file already belongs to locally).

prs.title: fix(telegram): render tilde and longer code fences as code
prs.body:
## Problem `_markdown_to_telegram_html` protects code blocks from the Markdown-to-HTML steps with ```` r'```(?:[^\n]*\n)?([\s\S]*?)```' ````. That pattern only knows backtick fences and closes a block at the first ``` it meets: - **`~~~` fences** aren't protected, so the code is formatted as prose: `~~~python / # setup / def __init__(self): pass / ~~~` renders as `setup` and `def init(self)`. - **A longer fence around a ``` example** (common when the model explains Markdown or shows a fenced snippet) closes on the inner ```. The output is an empty `
`, then the example leaks out as re-formatted text, and a stray backtick is left behind:
  `Example:\n
python\nx = a * b * c\n
**not bold in code**\n
`\nAfter bold`

`_telegram_command_text` in the same module already treats both ``` and `~~~` as fences.

## Fix

- New `_replace_fenced_code(text, replace)` helper. It first replaces fenced blocks line by line: a block opens on a ``` or `~~~` line (a backtick fence's info string can't contain a backtick) and closes on a line holding only a run of the same character that is at least as long.
- Whatever is left, meaning one-line ```` ```code``` ```` and unclosed fences, goes through the existing regex. Output for those inputs and for ordinary ``` blocks is byte-for-byte unchanged.
- `_markdown_to_telegram_html` and the streaming preview `_strip_md_block` both use the helper.

## Tests

prs.title: fix(webui): make full chat navigation scrollable and efficient
prs.body:
## Summary

The message rail currently grows only when older chat pages load. Long rails can exceed the viewport, and users cannot select prompts that have not loaded yet.

This change gives the rail a complete prompt directory, independent scrolling, and fading edges. Long and short rails stay centered against the complete chat frame, including the shared composer. Clicking a prompt loads the nearby history page instead of every preceding answer.

## Implementation

- Build bounded prompt summaries from the existing WebUI display transcript. Cache summaries by segment identity. Do not change SQLite, agent context, configuration, or chat storage.
- Reuse the transcript reader for forward and backward cursor pages. Keep at most three navigation pages. Keep the canonical live conversation separate, and provide a return-to-latest action.
- Window both the rail and the searchable message navigator. Preserve Markdown previews, keyboard navigation, and reduced-motion behavior.
- Revalidate unchanged directories with HTTP 304. When a previous snapshot is cached, transfer only the changed suffix. Send a complete directory after cache eviction or restart. Cache keys include the instance data path.
- Keep the current page on a failed read. Cancel superseded requests, reject stale jump targets, and hydrate deferred activity details in the correct browsing window. Return to the live conversation when selecting a new prompt that has not yet acquired a saved cursor.
- Avoid rebuilding the complete directory or its position observers for each streamed answer token.
- Cancel an in-flight history read when the user selects an already-rendered prompt or returns to the latest messages. A late response cannot replace the newer selection.

## Compatibility

WebUI protocol 1 and `webui.core.v1` remain unchanged. The new read path uses optional capability `webui.prompt-navigation.v1`. Older compatible hosts keep navigation within loaded messages; older clients keep the existing latest/before reads. Authentication still runs before conditional responses.

No data migration, new persistent index, dependency, installer, or startup requirement is added. The update and recovery paths are unchanged. Navigation caches are derived and memory-only; they do not replace either session storage or display transcripts.

## Verification

- Rebased onto `main` at `5f6e8a6baab8487ff5249993cb54a2c05bf0f587`. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39113793736) passed for `b1e898155d369e2a3e9c3d8c7018569e877aa7d9`: seven successful jobs, including Linux, Windows, WebUI and Docker, with one conditional matrix placeholder skipped.
- After rebase, 361 focused frontend tests and 65 backend prompt-index, transcript and client-contract tests passed. After the final cancellation fix, the affected hook/viewport suites passed 76 tests, including two new regressions. The two regressions fail without the fix: a delayed request replaces the later local selection in both live and historical views.
- All four real-browser regression tests passed after the final repair. Geometry assertions use the real workbench and its portalled composer. They cover long and short rails, a taller composer in a shorter window, and narrow-to-wide resizing.
- Full ESLint, production TypeScript/build, affected-file Ruff, Python/client import boundaries and `git diff --check` passed locally. Exact-head CI also passed strict BasedPyright, the full configured suites, and the browser regression job.
- Tests cover a complete 2,000-prompt rail, virtualized controls, centering, independent scroll, unloaded-message jumps, bounded forward/backward browsing, retry, rapid switches, old-host fallback, deferred trace details, directory truncation/replacement, and cache eviction.
- The browser performance harness also used the production components and a real authenticated local HTTP handler with 10,000 synthetic conversation rounds. No personal configuration or chats were used. It does not exercise a model or an installed release package.

## Local performance evidence

Comparison is against the first implementation of this fix (`affe68db1`), not against an equivalent complete-directory feature on `main`, which did not have one. Measurements used macOS ARM64, Python 3.11.4, and headless Chrome. Backend source data was about 55 MiB; the OS filesystem cache was warm.

| Measurement | First implementation | Optimized |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Uncached summary build, median / P95 (7 runs) | 271 / 335 ms | 136 / 158 ms |
| One new round, uncompressed directory JSON | 4,166,649 bytes | 503 bytes |
| Revalidation, browser click-to-response P95 (30 operations) | 111 ms, HTTP 200 | 59 ms, HTTP 304 |
| Old-message jump, click-to-visible P95 (20 operations) | 179 ms | 102 ms |
| Position observer constructions, 120 simulated token updates | 120 | 1 |
| Prompt geometry reads during those updates | 3,510 | 300 |
| Sampled browser JS heap high-water mark | 98 MiB | 53 MiB |

The optimized browser run recorded no tasks over 50 ms during those jumps or simulated token updates. These are local development-harness observations, not latency or memory guarantees for every browser and conversation. The first uncached visit still reads transcript segments. The build retains the existing large-chunk advisory.

## Documentation and release

`docs/webui.md` describes the navigation behavior and cache boundaries. Include the user-facing improvement in the release notes when this change ships; do not advertise it as released before then. No release or running-gateway restart is part of this change.

prs.title: fix(documents): preserve complete PDF pages across reads
prs.body:
When a PDF read reaches the character limit midway through a page, `read_file` currently suggests continuing from the next page. Following that instruction loses the rest of the partially returned page. In a 16-page test PDF with the default 128,000-character limit, the first read stops midway through page 10 but says to continue with pages 11–16.

Stop before adding a page that does not fit after the pages already collected. The next read then starts at that page and can return it in full. The same fixture now returns complete pages 1–9, followed by pages 10–16; all 16 page-end markers are present.

A first non-empty page that exceeds the limit by itself retains the bounded, truncated result. Mark that case explicitly in the extraction result and tell the caller that the rest of that page is not shown. Subsequent pages remain accessible without repeatedly suggesting the oversized page. File-size, page-count, and PDF content-stream limits are unchanged.

Add real-PDF regression coverage for character limits reached on a final or intermediate page, and for an oversized page followed by a readable page. All three cases fail before the fix and pass afterward.

Validation (Python 3.12):
- 215 tests passed across `tests/tools/test_search_tools.py`, `tests/tools/test_read_enhancements.py`, `tests/tools/test_filesystem_tools.py`, `tests/test_document_parsing.py`, and `tests/test_context_documents.py`, using a temporary config path.
- Repeated the original 16-page reproduction with the default character limit; following the continuation returned every page-end marker exactly once.
- Ruff passed for all three changed files; BasedPyright passed for the two production modules.
- `git diff --check` passed.

prs.title: fix: preserve XLSX grep cell locators with literal tabs
prs.body:
When an XLSX cell contains a literal tab, `grep` counts it as a cell separator and reports the wrong Excel column. A match in B1 can be labeled C1; a match later within A1 can be labeled B1.

Record actual cell start offsets during XLSX extraction and use those offsets for match locators. Preserve the extracted text, empty-cell positions, and the existing fallback for other document sources. Five tests exercise real workbooks through the grep tool, including tabs within the matched cell and empty leading cells.

Validation on base `db804ef` and candidate `95a85af`:

- Three new regression cases fail on the baseline; two controls pass. All five pass with the fix on Linux Python 3.11/3.14 and Windows Python 3.14.
- Full Python suites preserve all original outcomes: Linux 9,433 original cases plus five new cases (53 unchanged skips); Windows 9,378 original cases plus five new cases (113 unchanged skips). Separate CLI and Windows process suites also pass, with their original skip outcomes preserved.
- Ruff, strict type checking, import boundaries, dependency consistency, and the canonical Docker build/compose/permissions checks pass. Linux coverage is 85.65%.

[Native validation run](https://github.com/rudycelekli/nanobot/actions/runs/38408843497): all ten native jobs pass. The overall workflow is **failed** because its synthetic comparison-control fixture looked for the workflow file beside the helper rather than at `.github/workflows/`. After correcting that separate fixture, 50 evaluator controls pass; two independent reviews also reran the unchanged deployed comparator against all five downloaded baseline/fixed pairs, verifying source identities, artifact hashes, test identities and original outcomes. The original workflow failure is retained, not reported as green.

PRs #6093 (PDF pages) and #6097 (chart-only sheets) also touch the document extractor. This fix addresses a different locator bug; both current heads merge cleanly with this candidate. No validation harness files are included in this PR.

prs.title: fix(web): handle case-insensitive image media types
prs.body:
When a server returns `Content-Type: Image/PNG`, `web_fetch` misses its image checks and returns decoded image bytes as raw text. HTTP media type names are case-insensitive ([RFC 9110 §8.3.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-8.3.1)).

Normalize the type/subtype for image handling in both the streaming and local extraction paths, while retaining parameter values. One parameterized regression checks native image blocks and the original bytes for lowercase and mixed-case headers, including opaque parameter preservation. It covers direct streaming and the supported connection-error-to-GET fallback using HTTPX MockTransport.

Validation:

- Before the fix: 4 regression cases failed; the 2 lowercase controls passed.
- After the fix: all 6 regression cases passed.
- WebFetch security, Jina privacy, and URL sanitization tests: 64 passed.
- Ruff on both changed files and `git diff --check`: passed.
