prs.title: feat(tools): add DeepSeek Search as a web_search provider
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds DeepSeek as a new `web_search` provider backed by the standalone DeepSeek Search API (`POST https://api.deepseek.com/v1/tools/search`).

This is a search-only backend. It is unrelated to the DeepSeek LLM provider and never injects a `web_search` tool into chat completion requests. It follows the provider layout established by AnySearch (#5607) and Bocha (#4182).

## Motivation

DeepSeek's Search API is a first-party, AI-oriented search endpoint with model-readable summaries (`summary`), relevance/authority scores, and support for search operators (`site:`, `lang:`, `after:`, `before:`, quoted phrases). Users already holding a DeepSeek key can now use it for `web_search` without adding another vendor.

Because the API bills per successful request (¥5 / 1,000 requests) and returns summaries written for models to read, it is a good fit for agent workflows; requests that fail or return no results are not billed.

## Changes

- `nanobot/agent/tools/web.py`
  - Add `_DEEPSEEK_SEARCH_API_URL`, `_DEEPSEEK_MAX_QUERY_CHARS` (128), `_DEEPSEEK_MAX_RESULTS` (50), `_DEEPSEEK_MAX_SUMMARY_CHARS` (500), `_DEEPSEEK_ERROR_DETAIL_MAX_CHARS`, and `_DEEPSEEK_RETRY_DELAY_S`.
  - Register `{"name": "deepseek", "label": "DeepSeek", "credential": "api_key"}` in `SEARCH_PROVIDER_OPTIONS`, which drives both the CLI wizard and the WebUI settings list.
  - Resolve the key in `_effective_provider()` and dispatch in `execute()`.
  - Add `_search_deepseek()` plus four module-level helpers: `_normalize_deepseek_query()`, `_deepseek_is_retryable()`, `_deepseek_text()`, and `_deepseek_error_detail()`.
- `tests/tools/test_web_search_tool.py`
  - Add `deepseek` to the keyed-provider concurrency parametrization.
  - Add one provider-option registration test plus 23 behavioral tests, parametrized into 35 collected cases.
- `tests/webui/test_settings_api.py`
  - Add WebUI registration tests: accepting `deepseek` with a key, and requiring a key when none is supplied.
- `docs/configuration.md`
  - Add a DeepSeek section: config example, pricing, QPS, retry and query limits, search syntax, the summary cap, and the distinction from model-hosted search.
  - Add `deepseek` to the `tools.web.search` provider table.
- `webui/src/tests/provider-brand.test.ts`
  - Assert the existing bundled DeepSeek brand asset is reused for the search provider (no new frontend code required).

### Implementation notes

- **Query normalization** trims surrounding whitespace and truncates to 128 Unicode code points (not bytes), so CJK and emoji queries never produce a request that fails with HTTP 400. Whitespace-only queries are rejected locally without a network call.
- **`count`** is clamped to the API's 1–50 window inside the provider. The tool-level `execute()` path caps at 10 for every provider (and the tool schema advertises the same bound), so the wider API range only matters if the tool-level limit is raised later.
- **Results** use `summary`, falling back to `snippet`; each result's text is capped at 500 characters before `date` is prefixed. The cap was added after testing the live API: real `summary` values reach ~4,500 characters (the docs say 600–800), and ten uncapped results cost ~35,700 characters (~10k tokens) per call. With the cap the same call returns ~6,400 characters (~1.8k tokens). `need_content` is always `false` so page bodies never enter the model's context.
- **Errors**: 401 and 402 get actionable messages (402 points at top-up); 408/429/5xx are retried once after 1.0 s, matching the Brave provider; other 4xx are not retried and surface `error.message`, tag-stripped because the upstream body is untrusted. Timeouts and transport failures return a distinct message; unexpected transport errors report the exception type only, with the detail logged only when tool log content is allowed.
- **Secret hygiene**: the key only appears in the `Authorization` header. It is never logged, and error text is built from the status code and the response's `error.message` only.

## Testing

Targeted suite:

```
$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tools/test_web_search_tool.py -q --no-header
86 passed in 1.60s
```

WebUI settings suite:

```
$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/webui/test_settings_api.py -q --no-header
124 passed in 1.43s
```

Lint and types (as configured in `pyproject.toml` and CI):

```
$ .venv/bin/ruff check nanobot/agent/tools/web.py tests/tools/test_web_search_tool.py tests/webui/test_settings_api.py
All checks passed!

$ .venv/bin/basedpyright nanobot/agent/tools/web.py
0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes
```

Frontend test for the brand reuse:

```
$ cd webui && bun run test -- provider-brand
✓ src/tests/provider-brand.test.ts (22 tests)
```

Project-wide type check (same command CI runs, after `install_channel_dependencies --all-channels`):

```
$ .venv/bin/basedpyright
0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes
```

Full Python suite:

```
$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q --no-header
18 failed, 9983 passed, 15 skipped, 3 warnings in 356.67s
```

All 18 failures are environment-specific and unrelated to this change: 17 in
`tests/tools/test_seatbelt_native.py` (the macOS sandbox launcher) and 1 in
`tests/test_benchmark_session_storage.py` (a timing benchmark). CI on the PR is
the authoritative run.

Frontend tests were run on Node v26 with
`NODE_OPTIONS=--no-experimental-webstorage`, because that Node version exposes
an experimental global `localStorage` that the current vitest setup does not
expect. The flag only affects the test environment; no frontend source changed.

Covered cases in `tests/tools/test_web_search_tool.py`:

1. Success — asserts URL, headers, and body (`query`, `count`, `need_content: false`), and formatting.
2. `summary` preferred over `snippet`; `snippet` fallback when `summary` is empty; whitespace-only `summary` falls back to `snippet`; fields are stripped; `date: null` tolerated.
3. Empty results return the shared "No results for" text, not an error.
4. Env-var key (`DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`); missing key in both places falls back to DuckDuckGo.
5. 128-character truncation for CJK and astral-plane emoji; surrounding whitespace stripped; blank query rejected without a request.
6. `count` clamping (0→1, 100→50) at the provider boundary, and the tool-level 10 cap.
7. 401/402/403 do not retry and return the expected messages.
8. 408/429/500/503 retry once and succeed; 408/429/500 exhaust the retry budget and fail cleanly.
9. Timeout returns an actionable error; unexpected transport errors report the exception type without internal detail.
10. Malformed result entries are skipped without crashing; non-JSON 200 bodies are reported; oversized summaries are capped.
11. Error text never contains the API key, and relayed upstream messages are stripped of markup.
12. WebUI accepts `deepseek` with a key and rejects it without one.

Tests use `monkeypatch` on `httpx.AsyncClient.post` and never reach the network. Retry tests also stub `asyncio.sleep` so the suite stays fast.

## Live API verification

The implementation was exercised against the real endpoint with a valid key:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Success path, Chinese query | 200; `summary`, `snippet`, and `date` parsed correctly |
| Search syntax passthrough (`site:`, `lang:`, `after:`) | 200; results restricted as requested |
| 200-character CJK and 150-emoji queries through the tool | 200 — local truncation prevents the 400 the API returns above 128 characters |
| Raw 200-character query sent directly | 400 `'query' must be at most 128 characters` (confirms truncation is required) |
| `count=100` at the provider boundary | clamped to 50; raw `count=51` returns 400 |
| Blank query | rejected locally, no request sent |
| Invalid key | 401 message; the key is absent from the output |
| Burst of 20 requests | 14 × 429 (`Your current QPS: 5`), confirming the documented limit |
| Tool call during a real 429 | retried after ~1.0 s and recovered |
| `date: null` | present in real results; rendered without error |
| Ten results, before/after the summary cap | ~35,700 chars (~10k tokens) → ~6,400 chars (~1.8k tokens) |

This testing found and fixed four issues that unit tests could not: unbounded
summary size, a whitespace-only summary hiding the snippet, unstripped markup
in relayed error messages, and raw transport-error detail in the tool result.

## Scope / Non-goals

- **No Fetch.** `POST /v1/tools/fetch` is out of scope and will be a separate PR.
- **No LLM provider changes.** `nanobot/providers/`, the DeepSeek model registry, and model request assembly are untouched. No provider-hosted `web_search` tool is injected.
- **No interaction with #6283.** That PR explicitly does not enable standalone DeepSeek Search/Fetch; this PR adds the search backend only. None of its files (`docs/providers.md`, `nanobot/providers/openai_compat_provider.py`, `nanobot/providers/registry.py`, `nanobot/webui/settings_models.py`, `webui/src/lib/types.ts`, and its tests) are modified here.
- **`ori_question` and `localization`** are not sent; they are optional and not needed for a generic search tool.
- **No new dependency.** Uses the existing `httpx` client and the existing provider patterns.

## Open questions

1. **Is the shared `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` environment variable acceptable?** Search reads `tools.web.search.apiKey` first, then `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, and falls back to DuckDuckGo when neither is set — consistent with Brave, Tavily, and Bocha. That env var is also what the DeepSeek LLM provider declares in `nanobot/providers/registry.py`, so a user who already set it for models gets search without extra setup. We deliberately do **not** read `providers.deepseek.apiKey` from config: that would couple two independently billed services. Maintainers may prefer that search require an explicit key so search spend is always a deliberate choice.
2. **When should Fetch follow?** The Fetch endpoint shares auth, billing, and QPS characteristics and could reuse the same helpers. It maps naturally onto `web_fetch`, so it deserves its own design discussion rather than being folded in here.
3. **Should the tool-level `count` cap be raised?** The API supports up to 50, but `execute()` caps every provider at 10. Left unchanged to avoid changing behavior for all providers.

## Checklist

- [x] `git diff --check 74942bd1 d232f43e` passes
- [x] Changed Python files pass `ruff` (E, F, I, N, W)
- [x] `basedpyright` strict passes project-wide
- [x] Targeted tests pass
- [x] Full test suite run locally; remaining failures are pre-existing and unrelated
- [x] Frontend tests for the touched area pass
- [x] Verified against the live API, including 401 and 429 paths
- [x] Docs updated (`docs/configuration.md`)
- [x] No secrets, keys, or `.env` content added
- [x] No unrelated files, debug code, or formatting noise
- [x] No breaking changes; `deepseek` is additive and opt-in

prs.title: fix(media): keep Unicode upload names within the filesystem byte limit
prs.body:
## Problem

Document uploads can fail with `OSError: [Errno 36] File name too long` when the original name contains CJK characters or emoji. `media_destination` limits the stem to 80 characters, but filesystem component limits are measured in bytes on Linux.

For example, an 80-character CJK stem plus `.pdf` uses 244 UTF-8 bytes. The 12-character upload ID and underscore increase the saved name to 257 bytes. The same helper chooses names for data-URL attachments and binary WebUI uploads.

## Fix

Keep the existing character limit, then fit the stem into the byte budget left by the ID, separator, and MIME-derived extension. Drop an incomplete final UTF-8 sequence when truncation is needed. Names that already fit retain their current layout.

## Tests

Added real file-write regressions for CJK and emoji document names. Both fail on the base revision with `ENAMETOOLONG` and pass with this change. The tests also check the extension, saved content, and valid Unicode name.

- Media decoding and binary attachment-store suites: **38 passed**.
- Ruff on both changed files: passed.
- BasedPyright on `media_decode.py`: passed.
- Import-boundary checks: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

prs.body:
## Summary

Adds `whatsapp_agent`, an opt-in channel that connects nanobot to the [WhatsApp Agent Platform](https://faq.whatsapp.com/1050934623978152) API. nanobot is an independent third-party project, not a WhatsApp product. The existing `whatsapp` linked-device channel is unchanged.

| | `whatsapp_agent` | `whatsapp` |
|---|---|---|
| Connection | Agent API token; long polling | Linked device via Neonize and QR pairing |
| Reach | The agent's creator only | Chats and groups the linked device can access |
| Groups | Not supported | Supported |
| Agent chat encryption | Not end-to-end encrypted | WhatsApp linked-device transport |
| Availability | Limited by country and account | Where linked devices are available |

Messages are processed by nanobot and the configured model provider. The setup form shows this privacy notice before credentials are entered, in all ten supported languages. The guide links to the [third-party agent terms](https://www.whatsapp.com/legal/third-party-agents-terms) and distinguishes channel access from nanobot tool permissions.

## Behavior

- Authenticated long polling with an atomic cursor, deduplication window, creator identifier, and restart recovery. Tokens are not stored in the cursor file.
- On first start, save a timestamp boundary and poll from `offset=0`. Discard older or undated retained messages. This avoids skipping new messages after an empty poll. Accurate host time is required; see the guide for the one-second boundary and backlog latency.
- Record message IDs before dispatch and accept the server cursor after processing the batch. A crash between recording and dispatch can lose a message; this is not exactly-once delivery. State-write failure stops the channel.
- Split text at 4096 characters. Resume ordinary in-memory retries after acknowledged parts. Ambiguous send failures are not retried unless the operator opts in.
- Keep wholly unsent scheduled results pending when the channel is disconnected or has not learned the creator identifier. Partial scheduled sends remain unknown and are not automatically replayed.
- Support read receipts, typing, inbound/outbound media, MIME and size checks, digest verification, and existing voice-transcription configuration. Media URLs use the shared URL-target guard. Redirects are disabled.
- Keep progress and tool-hint traffic off by default. Permit one poller per token. Token rotation resets channel cursor state.
- Use existing channel discovery, settings, and secret handling. No new optional Python dependencies, shared agent-loop changes, or migration of existing linked-device data.

## Closeout verification

Rebased onto `main` at `74942bd1904b197a3144a4a757326fc04610c9e4`. Original contributor commits are retained. Fixed the Python configuration-base import, relocated WebUI catalog import, and generated channel-gallery fixture for the current main branch.

- 288 focused Python tests passed: channel package, discovery/setup, manager concurrency, and scheduled delivery. Pre-fix regressions reproduced the unsent scheduled-result loss; tests also cover reconnect and partial-send safety.
- Ruff, strict channel BasedPyright, Python/client import-boundary checks, and generated-fixture consistency passed.
- 71 focused WebUI tests passed. Production TypeScript/Vite build and ESLint passed.
- Real Chromium rendering of the production setup component with generated fixtures passed at 1280px and 390px, light/dark, with Advanced expand/collapse and a rejected-credential state. The privacy notice remains visible before credential entry. This is fixture-backed UI verification, not live account E2E.

The [current-head CI matrix](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39102619401) passed at `bd77c86997871150f073df4d39f06519b14c4deb`, including Python 3.11/3.14, Windows, WebUI, and Docker. The first Python 3.14 run hit an unrelated, unchanged Docker smoke assertion; the failed job passed on its single rerun without code changes. Local focused checks and CI do not certify live platform availability or all media flows. Existing installations retain their channel/configuration contracts; release artifact acceptance remains separate.

## Earlier live verification reported by the contributor

The contributor reported a real API round trip: authentication, inbound text, cursor persistence, replay deduplication, outbound text, and a delivered receipt. That verification was not repeated during closeout. Live attachment upload/download, digest verification, and transcription remain unverified end-to-end.

The contributor also observed a non-creator destination returning HTTP 500/code 2 rather than the documented 403/131005, and an over-length text returning HTTP 400/code 100 with `body` as the message. The adapter retains conservative ambiguous-send handling and does not classify that text-length error as a bad token.

See the [channel guide](https://github.com/CarmeloCampos/nanobot/blob/feat/whatsapp-agent-platform/docs/guides/whatsapp-agent-platform.md) in this PR for setup, limits, and troubleshooting.

issues.title: [Bug]: use_real_profile fails on AppArmor-restricted userns hosts: sandbox bypass not applied to the real-profile daemon env
issues.body:
### Bug Description
With `browser.use_real_profile: true` on a host where `kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns = 1` (Ubuntu 23.10+/26.04), the real-profile lane fails with:

`browser.use_real_profile is on, but the real-profile browser started without exposing a devtools endpoint. Retry, or turn the toggle off.`

### Root cause
`_apply_chromium_sandbox_args()` (the `--no-sandbox,--disable-dev-shm-usage` auto-injection) is only called from the normal command path (`tools/browser_tool_session.py` ~L757) and the Lightpanda fallback. The real-profile lane builds its daemon env via `_real_profile_daemon_env()` -> `_agent_browser_command_env()`, which never applies it. Hermes' own Chrome launch on the profile copy succeeds and `agent-browser --cdp <port> open about:blank` succeeds, but the next daemon command (`get cdp-url`) dies with Chromium's "No usable sandbox!" error. `_agent_browser_get_cdp()` swallows that, returns None, and `_attach_agent_browser_to_real_profile()` reports "without exposing a devtools endpoint".

### Reproduction
1. Ubuntu with `sysctl kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns` = 1, Chrome as the default browser, `browser.use_real_profile: true`, `AGENT_BROWSER_ARGS` unset.
2. Call `browser_navigate` (or `tools.browser_tool_real_profile._real_profile_cdp()`).
3. Fails as above. Running the same steps by hand with the daemon env, `open about:blank` returns 0, `get cdp-url` returns 1 with "No usable sandbox".

### Verification of the cause
Same flow, only change: add `AGENT_BROWSER_ARGS=--no-sandbox,--disable-dev-shm-usage` to the daemon env. `get cdp-url` returns the ws URL, navigation works, `get title` works, and `browser_navigate`/`browser_snapshot` return `used_real_profile: true`.

### Proposed Fix
Call `_apply_chromium_sandbox_args(env)` in `_real_profile_daemon_env()` (or inside `_agent_browser_command_env`). Optionally surface the daemon's stderr in the "no devtools endpoint" error instead of discarding it, so the sandbox message is visible.

### Environment
Hermes Agent v0.22.0 (2026.9.24), git install e06df9c2ea; agent-browser 0.39.1 (also reproduced the daemon-side failure on 0.26.0); Ubuntu 26.04, Python 3.14.7; Google Chrome via /usr/bin/google-chrome.

issues.title: [Feature]: let browser.use_real_profile name its browser instead of requiring a Chromium OS default
issues.body:
### Summary
Real-profile browsing picks its browser only from the OS default (`xdg-settings get default-web-browser` on Linux via `detect_default_chromium()`). There is no config key or env var to name the browser, and `browser.real_profile_pin` only selects a profile directory inside it.

### Impact
Users who deliberately keep a non-Chromium default (e.g. Firefox for daily use) and have a Chrome/Edge/Brave dedicated to the agent cannot use `browser.use_real_profile`: every `browser_*` call fails with "your default browser is not a supported Chromium browser". The only workaround is changing the system-wide default, which also changes where links from every other app open.

### Proposed
Add e.g. `browser.real_profile_browser: chrome|edge|brave|chromium` (and/or `HERMES_REAL_PROFILE_BROWSER`) that overrides `detect_default_chromium()`; keep today's behaviour when unset. The existing fail-closed checks (pre-release channels, unsupported browsers) can stay as they are.

### Environment
Hermes Agent v0.22.0 (2026.9.24), git install e06df9c2ea; Ubuntu 26.04; default browser `firefox_firefox.desktop`, `google-chrome` and `microsoft-edge` installed.

Related: a separate bug report for the AppArmor sandbox failure in the same lane.

issues.title: [Bug]: User message racing a running cron fire dies as opaque 'The admitted turn failed.' card; diagnostics stamp copy-time so stale failures look live
issues.body:
**Summary**

While a cron job is executing on a desktop chat session, any message typed into that chat is rejected with the raw internal `admission_conflict` error, surfaced to the user only as an opaque red card: *"The admitted turn failed."* The card is made worse by `formatErrorDiagnostics` stamping `time:` with `new Date().toISOString()` — the moment the card is copied/rendered, not when the turn failed — so reopening the old chat hours later makes a stale failure look like a brand-new incident.

**Environment**

- Backend: `v0.22.1+canary.20261015T070051Z-161-gacc3cada0d` (macOS 26.5.2, Apple Silicon, local llama.cpp provider)
- Platform: desktop (local operator)

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Have a cron job whose result delivers into a desktop chat, and get it firing (a run taking several minutes helps; `deliver: origin`).
2. While the run is in flight, type a message into that same chat (e.g. "run this again now").
3. Observe: the message is refused with a red error card "The admitted turn failed." and nothing else.
4. Hours later, reopen that chat / copy the error details again — a fresh card appears with `time:` = now.

**Actual behaviour**

- Both messages typed during/just after the cron run were rejected. From `state.db` `session_admissions`:
  - admission `29432b26…` payload text `"run this again now"` → `outcome=failed`
  - admission `e4445bc0…` payload text `"where are my results"` → `outcome=failed` (arrived at 10:17:15, the exact second the run completed at 10:17:16)
- Gateway log (`gateway.error.log`), both times:

```
ERROR gateway.session_authority: Admitted turn e4445bc0ff5a4c52b17917ebbe930154 failed
  File "gateway/session_authority.py", line 901, in _execute_claimed
    return await execute_finite_admission(self, ref, row), 'completed'
  ...
  File "gateway/session_cron.py", line 231, in execute
    raise RuntimeStoreError('admission_conflict')
hermes_state_runtime.RuntimeStoreError: admission_conflict
```

- `session_authority._execute_claimed` swallows it into the generic string: `_execute_claimed` → `return 'The admitted turn failed.', 'failed'`.
- The card had **no structured error surface** (no `layer:` / `code:` lines in the diagnostics blob — only time/model/error), so the desktop shows zero recovery affordance.
- Meanwhile the cron job itself **completed fine and delivered its result** (`cron/executions.db`: `status=completed`, `last_status=ok`). So the user is told "failed" about a system that worked, with no hint that only their interjected message was dropped — and, confusingly, the 09:58 attempt also logged a `failed` execution row `Fire claim was not acquired` (that dedupe is correct; the surfacing is not).

**Timestamp bug detail** (`apps/desktop/src/lib/error-surface.ts`, `formatErrorDiagnostics`, ~line 319):

```ts
`time: ${new Date().toISOString()}`,
```

This stamps copy/render time. My real failures were 09:58:44 and 10:17:15 NZDT; I copied the details at 14:58:44 NZDT and the blob read `time: 2026-10-19T01:58:44.535Z` — indistinguishable from a fresh incident. The descriptor comment right above it even says "captured when the turn failed" for provider/model; the time should come from the same place (or the failed turn's `updated_at`).

**Expected behaviour**

1. A user message that races a cron-owned session should get a plain-words card, e.g. "A scheduled job is running in this session; your message couldn't be delivered — retry after it finishes", not the catch-all string.
2. `admission_conflict` should carry a structured error surface (`layer: gateway`, `code: admission_conflict`, `retryable: true`) so the card can offer Retry.
3. Error diagnostics `time:` must be the turn's failure timestamp, not copy time.

**Notes / related**

Similar `admission_conflict` surfacing issues exist (#140845 Telegram edit, #139835 legacy API sessions, #141153 delegation requeue loop), but none cover the desktop-chat-during-cron-fire path or the copy-time timestamp. Happy to add any local traces.

issues.body:
On v0.22.2 (`d923a5eb`), when a provider returns a non-retryable error (observed with HTTP 400), Hermes writes the full request including the prompt to `sessions/request_dump_*.json`, also with `logging.level: WARNING` (`hermes_logging.py:344-376, 957-980`, `agent/turn_context.py:1092-1107`, `agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py:1560-1603`). The API key in the dump is shortened, the prompt is not.

For deployments that keep prompts only in `state.db` under a retention policy, these dumps are an extra copy outside that policy. Suggestion: a config switch (e.g. `logging.request_dumps: false`) or tying the dumps to `DEBUG`, plus applying `sessions.retention_days` to them.

Happy to test a change against the release.

issues.title: `delegate_task` ignores model pin — manifest always shows `model: null, provider: null`

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: tool/delegate
labels.description: Subagent delegation

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low — cosmetic, nice to have

issues.body:
## Summary

When a parent dispatch specifies a target model in the subagent's `context` string (or asks for one to be pinned via `delegation.model`/`delegation.provider`), the resulting subagent runs on the **default** model rather than the requested one. Both the subagent and the parent learn about this only by reading the live transcript manifest after the run completes — there's no warning at dispatch time and no error returned.

## Reproduction

1. Dispatch a subagent via `delegate_task` with a goal/context string that names a target model (e.g., "pin the running model to `kimi-coding/kimi-k3`, subscription direct path").
2. Wait for completion.
3. Read `/Users/nathan/.hermes/cache/delegation/live/<delegation_id>/manifest.json`.

The manifest shows:

```json
{
  "delegation_id": "deleg_xxxxx",
  "started": "2026-09-26 ...",
  "task_count": 1,
  "model": null,
  "provider": null,
  ...
}
```

`model` and `provider` are both `null` even though the brief explicitly named a target model.

## Expected

Either:
- The subagent runs on the requested model and the manifest records `model: "kimi-coding/kimi-k3"`, `provider: "kimi-coding"`.
- OR `delegate_task` returns a warning at dispatch time: "Model pin not honored in this Hermes version; subagent will run on the default model. Set `delegation.model` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml` to change the default."

## Actual

The subagent runs on the default model. The parent sees `status=completed` and only learns about the model mismatch by manually inspecting the manifest after the fact. The subagent itself cannot know what model it ran on.

## Impact

- Review tasks that require a specific model's perspective (e.g., "review this spec as if you were Claude", or "route through kimi-k3") silently run on the wrong model. The output is uncalibrated for the operator's intent.
- Cost attribution is wrong — the manifest is the only place to record what was actually billed, and it's `null`.
- Audit trails for "which model produced this decision" lose their load-bearing provenance.

## Reproduction environment

- Hermes version: current (Mac mini M4, macOS 26.6.2)
- Reproduced twice in one session on 2026-09-26: delegations `deleg_5958ba21` and `deleg_f631b9c3`. Both briefs asked for `kimi-coding/kimi-k3`. Both manifests showed `model: null, provider: null`.
- The `mcp__jev__*` tools correctly routed to `jev-latest` independently (so Jev calls work; the issue is specifically the LLM-call path for the subagent's reasoning).

## Workaround

Set `delegation.model` / `delegation.provider` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml` to change the default model that all subagents run on. There's no per-dispatch pin working as of this report.

## Suggested fix (one of)

1. **Honor a `model` parameter in `delegate_task`'s `tasks[]` entries.** Pass `model: "kimi-coding/kimi-k3"` per-task; populate the manifest from that.
2. **Warn at dispatch time** if the brief references a model but no pin was honored. Don't silently degrade.
3. **Document the limitation** in `delegate_task`'s tool description so callers stop expecting per-dispatch pins.

## Severity

Medium. The subagent's output is still produced and often useful, but the operator's stated intent ("run on model X") is silently violated. For QA-review and audit tasks specifically, this is a correctness bug — the operator gets a verdict attributed to an unknown model.

prs.title: fix(estimates): keep main's ~ context marker after Ctrl+C and price cold no-op /compress like main
prs.body:
Package 12, lane 2: context and token estimates (#141321).

- T4: after Ctrl+C during a turn's first request, the classic CLI status bar keeps main's `~` estimate. An interrupted turn's own `api_calls` counts the attempt that was cut off, so the stand-in now falls back to the gateway's per-response cumulative count. Refs #134889 (T4)
- T15: on a cold session, a no-op `/compress` prices messages plus the stored system prompt and tools[] pin, the same estimator main used with a resident agent, instead of the messages alone. Refs #134889 (T15)

Design choices:
- T4 reads gateway data only. There's no new client state and the gateway's numbers don't change.
- T15 lives on the gateway, so every client shows the same figure. The session row's prompt and tools pin are what the next agent restores and sends.

Still needs live retest:
- T4: Ctrl+C during the first request in `hermes` should show `~N/…` in the status bar.
- T15: `/compress` on a 2-message session with the agent evicted should give about the same figure as with the agent resident.

Refs #141321

prs.title: fix(usage): ignore model-only cooldowns for Codex quota reads
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes missing OpenAI Codex account quota when native credential resolution fails and the fallback pool contains a valid credential benched for an unrelated model.

The fallback currently calls model-less `pool.select()`, which deliberately excludes any credential with an active model cooldown. A year-long model-entitlement bench can therefore suppress account usage even though the same token can read `/wham/usage`.

## Changes made

- Add `select_for_usage()` for account-scoped metadata selection. It bypasses model cooldowns only; credential-wide dead/exhausted checks and OAuth refresh rules remain in force.
- Use it in the final Codex quota credential fallback, preserving explicit credential and native-resolver precedence and each credential's route URL.
- Do not acquire an inference lease, rotate credentials, increment request counters, clear model cooldowns, or change inference selection.
- Add regressions for quota recovery, blocked credentials, successful/failed refresh, and unchanged inference state. Include a persisted pool row and real loopback HTTP usage endpoint.

## Verification

Tested on Linux using the canonical isolated runner:

```sh
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_credential_pool*.py tests/agent/test_account_usage*.py tests/agent/test_anthropic_model_cooldowns.py tests/agent/test_codex_model_entitlement_rotation.py tests/agent/test_codex_usage_model_cooldowns.py tests/hermes_cli/test_auth_codex_provider.py tests/hermes_cli/test_auth_codex_quota_probe.py tests/hermes_cli/test_codex_credential_host_binding.py tests/e2e/core/providers/test_openai_codex_pool.py -j 6
python scripts/check
```

- 268 tests passed across 34 files, with one existing expected failure concerning independent-login quarantine (#120741); all 12 blocking repository checks passed.
- Independent review accepted exact commit `4a852b7c68f062577c71440a5c51dc054edd7cea` with no findings, repeated the relevant suite and checks, and passed seven additional selection/refresh/native-fallback controls.
- On the unchanged base, the new stored-row/HTTP regression returns no snapshot; it passes with this fix. The new selector tests also fail on the base and pass on the candidate.
- The full repository test suite and other operating systems were not run.
- Tests use synthetic credentials and isolated homes; no production credentials, configuration, or routing were changed.

The broader tests were run from a standalone checkout outside the installed Hermes home: the existing home-I/O guard rejects ancestor Git/PM metadata probes from checkouts nested inside that home. The same guard failure was reproduced on the unchanged base; neither product code nor the guard was changed to bypass it.

## Checklist

- [x] Focused bug fix with regression coverage
- [x] Searched existing PRs for overlapping quota/cooldown fixes
- [x] Conventional commit
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes
- [x] Relevant tests pass
- [ ] Full repository suite

prs.title: refactor(gateway): rename session_contract.Principal to SessionActor
prs.body:
## What

Renames `gateway.session_contract.Principal` to `SessionActor`. The change is mechanical: a whole-word rename in every module that imports the type from `gateway.session_contract`, with no alias kept.

## Why

`Principal(subject, profile_id, capabilities, transport_id)` describes **whoever acts on a canonical session**. That covers an attached CLI, TUI, Desktop or ACP viewer, the API server, the messaging control path, cron and automation. Most call sites already name the variable `actor` (`actor = Principal('api', ...)`), and several instances are not clients of any person (`'api'`, `'messaging-control'`, `'durable-room-owner'`).

Hosted multi-tenant Hermes needs "principal" for a different concept: a member of a tenant. gateway-gateway already uses the word that way (Tenant ⊃ Membership(Principal) ⊃ Agent). A hosted turn can involve both concepts at once: a tenant member speaking through a relay connection that is itself a session actor. This rename lets both repos use one vocabulary before the tenant-scoped type is introduced, and avoids two unrelated types sharing one name.

`SessionActor` was chosen over `ClientPrincipal` (it keeps "principal" for two meanings) and over `Actor` (`tools/connectors/contract.py` already defines an unrelated `Actor` enum). The name has zero prior hits on `main`.

## Scope

- 102 files (13 source, 89 tests), +284/−284. No behaviour change.
- Untouched on purpose: Windows Task Scheduler XML `<Principal>` in `hermes_cli/gateway_windows.py` and `hermes_cli/gateway_runtime_service_identity.py`. That is a different "principal".
- No docs or `AGENTS.md` referenced the type by name.

## Verification

- `scripts/run_tests.sh` over the 89 changed test files: **466 passed, 0 failed** (5 macOS-only skips on Linux).
- `python scripts/check`: 12 checks ok; code-health ratchet 0 blocking, 0 advisory.
- Every changed file compiles.

## Infographic

![session-actor](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aaef4ee/18MVBZ8SY4Q0SiO8lbOG3_LBpFsuF1.png)

prs.title: Catalog: REA crash triage works on stripped binaries
prs.body:
Catalog installs of the official REA plugin get the updated crash-triage skill: it now works on stripped release binaries, not only ones with symbols or source.

- It checks the binary's build ID against the crash dump and stops on a mismatch instead of reporting wrong addresses.
- It names functions from the unwind tables (`sub_11d4+0x1f`, labelled as derived) and walks back from the crash to the caller that produced the bad value, by disassembly and the dump's memory, without running the program.

`plugin-catalog/rea.yaml`: `sha:` and the image URL move from `6dacaad` to `dc3b3b0`, the merge of NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins#109 (@mingleiw). The only change in `rea/` between the two pins is that PR (skill text, README, `core_mappings.py`; standard library only, no new tools or `mcp.json` change). Install scanner at the new pin: `safe` (the two known `.env` prose mentions). Still on REA 6.4.0; the 6.7.0 update is NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins#111.

prs.title: fix(gateway,tui): name the restart on interrupted turns and the backend on !cmd refusals; confirm TUI-14/T22
prs.body:
Package 12 lane 11: confirm the decided rows. Behaviour is unchanged; only the named messages and docs change.

- F1: the default stays `agent.restart_drain_timeout: 0` (pinned). A turn a restart/stop interrupts still settles interrupted and is never replayed, and its `message.complete.warning` now says "Gateway restarting: this turn was interrupted and will not be run again…". Ink and Desktop already render `warning`; `hermes chat` prints it for interrupted turns. The key is documented under Configuration → Gateway Restart Drain, with the systemd `TimeoutStopSec` caveat, and the wrong env-var default (900) is fixed. Refs #134889 (F1)
- TUI-14: out of date. Ink and Desktop send `/browser` as `browser.manage`. Added a Desktop test for connect/disconnect; Ink was already pinned (`createSlashHandler.test.ts:690`). Refs #134889 (TUI-14)
- TUI-16: the refusal stays. The `!cmd` refusal on a Docker/SSH session now names the backend and says to ask the agent (owner `field/detail`, plus Ink copy in all TUI packs). Local sessions still run. Refs #134889 (TUI-16)
- T22: `LOCAL` stays. A test shows that API-created sessions are `LOCAL` from local and remote connections alike; the connection mode (`native_owner` → `client_env_remote`) is what differs. `created_source` is untouched. Refs #134889 (T22)

Refs #141321

Design choices:
- The F1 notice reuses the existing `message.complete.warning` field: no new event or field, and no Ink/Desktop code. It fires only once stop() has begun, so a user Stop during the after-turn wait is not mislabelled.
- The TUI-16 backend name rides the existing refusal `detail` slot, so there's no contract change, and older gateways still get the "ask the agent" wording.
- T22 gap (not built): no wire field exposes a stored session's origin connection mode. If a surface needs it, expose `client_env_remote` on the session info rather than renaming the platform.

Still needs a live retest:
- `hermes gateway restart` mid-turn: the Ink warning line, the Desktop toast, and the `hermes chat` stderr line.
- Ink `!ls` on a docker-backend profile shows the new sentence.

prs.title: feat(telegram): opt-in dm_topic_auto_transfer opens a fresh topic for root-DM messages
prs.body:
Adds an opt-in Telegram `/topic`-mode key, `dm_topic_auto_transfer` (off by default). With it on, a message typed in the root DM opens a new session in a freshly created topic, and the reply lands there. If creating the topic fails, the message falls back to the default lobby recovery. With the key unset, nothing changes: the v0.22 lobby recovery stays the default (#136567).

- MSG-15: Refs #139136, Refs #134889 (MSG-15), Refs #141321
  - Salvages #139188 by @KoNit-K (cherry-picked, authorship kept).
  - Fix on top: the transfer now runs at Telegram adapter ingress, before session keying. Run from the runner, the real adapter answered root-DM messages with the lobby reminder and never created a topic.

Design choices
- Off by default. The key is read from `platforms.telegram.extra` (top-level `telegram:` YAML is bridged too).
- If topic creation fails, the message goes to the last bound topic.
- Root-DM commands, internal wakes and routed events are never moved.
- The first reply in the new topic carries no reply anchor (the root message lives outside the topic).
- The hook lives in the Telegram plugin (`telegram_topic_transfer.py`), not in `gateway/platforms/base.py`.
- Documented in the Telegram docs: "Messages sent in the root DM".

Tests: `tests/gateway/test_telegram_dm_topic_auto_transfer.py` drives the real TelegramAdapter into the real runner with a fake Bot API. The opt-in and fallback tests fail on main; the default lobby-recovery test passes on both.

Still needs live retest
- Real bot with Threaded Mode, `/topic` on and `dm_topic_auto_transfer: true`: a root-DM message creates a topic, and the reply appears inside it.
- A client that delivers root messages thread-less.
- The fallback when Threaded Mode is disabled.

prs.body:
Desktop model picks to user-defined `providers.<slug>` endpoints (Package 12, lane 9)

- MP-13: a Desktop model pick to a `providers.<slug>` endpoint added after the session was created no longer fails `model_resolution_failed`. Refs #139740, Refs #134889 (MP-13), Refs #141321

Design choices
- A pick is an explicit user action, so it resolves against the owning profile's CURRENT `providers:` entries (as CLI/TUI `/model` do). The current entry wins over one the session froze earlier.
- Only that one entry plus `model.key_env` (the pointer) is frozen into the session. Its key value stays in the private secret store, never the receipt.

It checks that the next turn reaches that loopback with its key, that a second profile with the same slug is never contacted, that the frozen config is otherwise unchanged, and that the key value is absent from state.db.
- Live: native Electron on its own display and gateway, a loopback endpoint added after the session existed, then a pick in the Desktop model picker. The next turn reached the loopback (frames, stub log and screenshot in the lane evidence).

Still needs live retest
- A real remote OpenAI-compatible endpoint (the reporter's setup, macOS).
- A multiplexed gateway where the session's owner is a secondary profile.

prs.title: fix(acp): restore Accept Edits / Don't Ask as a gateway-owned per-session edit policy
prs.body:
Restore ACP Accept Edits / Don't Ask as a per-session edit-approval policy owned by the gateway.

- ACP-7: Refs #134889 (ACP-7), Refs #141321. `hermes acp` showed only Default, and `set_session_mode` / `set_config_option` refused the other two modes with `acp_edit_policy_mutation_unavailable`.

Design choices
- `edit_approval_policy` (`ask` / `workspace_session` / `session`, default `ask`) is a plain-data field on the session's frozen LocalSessionPolicy. It is written by a new `session.mutate` operation, `edit_policy` (`{policy}`), which is revision- and generation-fenced like `reasoning`/`workspace` and works on idle sessions only. It is stored in the session receipt, so it survives an owner restart. Only ACP sessions accept it.
- It is enforced in the owner's existing editor edit guard, using main's `should_auto_approve_edit`. Sensitive paths (`.env`, `.git`, `.ssh`, keys) always ask.
- `session.info` reports it, so every attached surface sees the same policy. The ACP adapter advertises all three modes, maps both ACP verbs onto the mutation, and turns another surface's change into `current_mode_update`.
- Backward compatible:
  - A receipt minted by main restores as `ask`.
  - `policy_identity` ignores the field while it is `ask`, so existing credential references still match.
  - `session.create`'s `editor.edit_approval_policy` is unchanged and still accepts only `ask`.
- Changing the policy does not evict the cached agent, because the policy is read on each edit.
- WS contract: `edit_approval_policy` is added to the session info result models, and the generated artifacts are regenerated.

Still needs live retest
- A real editor (Zed): pick Accept Edits, then confirm a workspace edit runs without a prompt and a `.env` edit still prompts.

prs.title: fix(gateway): replay waiting prompts after a legacy reconnect (salvage #140456)
prs.body:
Desktop in URL, Cloud or SSH mode: replay a waiting approval or clarify prompt after a reconnect.

- DB-7 (Refs #134889, Refs #140455, Refs #141321): standalone `hermes serve` refused `session.events.since` with `replay_epoch: Extra inputs are not permitted`, so the reconnect replay never ran and a waiting prompt was lost. This salvages #140456 by @dokterdok with authorship kept: the code is unchanged, and the commit's `Fixes #140455` became `Refs #140455` because the remote-mode live retest is still to do. Tests are added on top.

Design choices
- The client sends `replay_epoch` only when it is the session's own epoch. It no longer falls back to the process epoch from gateway.ready.
- The legacy `session.events.since` contract accepts `replay_epoch` as optional and ignores it, so shipped clients still replay. Every other unknown key is still refused.
- Backend-restart detection is unchanged: the client compares the answer's `epoch` with the gateway.ready epoch.
- No new `hermes serve` feature.

Tests
- Red on main, green here: Python contract and dispatch tests, plus shared vitest for the legacy reconnect, including restart detection.
- `gen_gateway_contracts.py --check` passes.

Still needs a live retest
- Desktop in remote mode against a standalone `hermes serve`: leave an approval or clarify waiting, reconnect, and check the prompt reappears. Also restart serve while disconnected and check the resync.

prs.title: fix(gateway): lost automation turns settle; discard on every surface; classic /browser via browser.manage; pause holds interactive turns
prs.body:
Package 12 lane 5 (#141321): three decided rows from #134889. One commit per row (GW-10 has three).

## GW-10: lost turns after a restart
- **Automation deliveries** (principal `cron-owner` or `automation:*`, a `local_automation_v1` payload, or a native envelope with an `automation` block) that a restart fences `unknown` now settle as terminal `interrupted`.
  - They go through the existing `resolve_unknown_session_input` (Discard's fenced transition), with a `failed_turn` notice committed in the same transaction. Nothing is replayed, and the FIFO moves on.
  - Hooked at boot recovery (before any drain) and in the drain when it claims an `unknown` head.
- **A person's lost turn still pauses.** Every surface now says why and offers discard in place:
  - Messaging: the pause notice explains and offers `/discard`, a new gateway-only command. On Slack it is `/hermes discard`, because of the 50-command cap. Strings are in all 17 locales.
  - TUI: the lost row reads `[paused: lost in restart · ↑ select, Ctrl+X discard]`.
  - ACP: `/discard <id>` in the editor, salvaged from #139541 by @KoNit-K (`cherry-pick -x`, author kept), resolved against main's newer `ROUTES` table and pre-prompt refresh.
  - Desktop: unchanged; it already had the "Turn lost during restart / Discard" card.
- **Live (Desktop, isolated display, fake HOME, loopback model):** killed the gateway mid-turn, and the restart fenced the turn `unknown`. The queue showed "Turn lost during restart / Discard". Discard settled it as interrupted with no replay, and the queued follow-up then ran exactly once.

## CLI-9: classic CLI `/browser`
- With a gateway session, classic `/browser` sends `browser.manage`, the verb Ink and Desktop use. The browser tools run in the gateway, so changing the CLI process's `BROWSER_CDP_URL` did nothing.
- `connect` and `disconnect` are refused client-side against a remote gateway (Desktop's rule).
- The gateway (`ws_legacy_fallback`) runs connect/disconnect when it serves one profile and refuses them by name when it serves several. The browser connection and the reap of open browsers are process-wide, so per-profile scoping isn't possible without a per-profile browser, which is out of scope.
- A test shows a browser connected from one profile never reaches another profile's sessions.
- The gateway `/browser` helpers moved to `hermes_cli/cli_browser_gateway.py` (file-length cap).

## GW-1: `hermes pause` holds every gateway turn
- A live probe (real gateway, WS API, loopback model):
  - a turn already running when the pause lands finishes;
  - a new interactive turn gets exactly `estop.paused_reply()` (the reason plus "run `hermes resume`"), with no model call;
  - after `hermes resume` the next turn runs.
- `hermes pause --help`, its confirmation output and `website/docs/reference/cli-commands.md` now say interactive CLI, TUI and Desktop turns are held too.

## Tests
- **Red on main:** the 3 new test files fail 10 of 14. The 4 that pass are controls: a person's turn still pauses, the single-profile browser path, and a running turn finishes under pause.
- **Green:** 829 tests across 11 files, including the full ACP suite, the `/browser` tests and the parity docs. `ruff` and `scripts/check` (12) are clean.
- **Still needs a live retest:** `/discard` on a real messaging platform, a multiplexed Bot Chat behind a lost cron delivery, and `/browser` on a real multi-profile gateway.

Refs #134889 (GW-1, GW-10, CLI-9). Refs #141321. Supersedes #139541.

prs.title: fix(worker): persist activity and aux usage off Relay's event loop (KB-2)
prs.body:
Managed workers no longer reach the synchronous persistence RPC from Relay's event loop.

- KB-2 (Refs #139029, Refs #134889 (KB-2), Refs #141321): Relay runs provider and tool callbacks synchronously on its private loop. Three writers called `worker.persist` on that loop:
  - `_touch_activity` (non-streaming wait notice, concurrent tool start)
  - the label clear at turn end
  - sync aux-usage accounting

  The #139472 guard refused the call, and the failure stuck for the rest of the turn. These writers now go through `call_off_event_loop`, which hops to a worker thread only when a loop is running. The guard is unchanged.

Design: fixed at the best-effort writers, not in WorkerRPC, so the guard still catches and names any other on-loop caller. Tests drive the real Relay pipeline, store and guard; only the owner socket is replaced.

Not in scope: the run-budget "dies early" reports on #139029 (profile `run_budget_seconds`/`max_turns`) and the sticky store failure (#140128).

Still needs live retest:
- a kanban managed worker on a Relay-managed profile with long tool calls and a non-streaming provider. Expect no `synchronous_rpc_on_event_loop` in errors.log, and the run should not be recorded `crashed`.

prs.title: fix(desktop): T11: run refused Desktop slash commands on gateway verbs, write /save files on the Electron side
prs.body:
Desktop slash commands the shared gateway refused, or Desktop didn't offer, now run on gateway verbs or give a named refusal. Files are written on the Electron side, because the gateway may be remote.

- /rollback, /agents (/tasks), /config, /history: Desktop actions on existing owner verbs (rollback.*, subagent.list + process.list, config.get key=full, the session.resume snapshot). Refs #134889 (T11)
- /save: new `session.export` verb returns the rendered json|md|html (optional redact); Electron's main process writes it after a native save dialog. `session.save` is unchanged; an older gateway falls back to it. Refs #134889 (T11)
- /export, /import: the existing profile-share dialogs on a local gateway; named refusal (`hermes profile export|import` on the host) on a remote one. Refs #134889 (T11)
- /timestamps (/ts), /palette: client display toggles (UI state, not session state). Refs #134889 (T11)
- /worktree, /snapshot: named terminal refusals (both act on the gateway host's cwd/state). Refs #134889 (T11)

Refs #141321

Design choices
- The gateway never writes the client's file: `session.export` returns `{format, filename, content}`. Electron takes only a bare file name from the renderer, and the user picks the directory.
- /agents reads this chat's subagents and processes, not the process-global delegation.status.
- /config shows the owner's presentation-only projection (no provider, MCP or secret config).
- No bytes-over-WS profile export/import. Archive transfer through the gateway is a new capability, so remote /export and /import refuse by name for now.
- The save-dialog IPC moved into electron/save-text-file.ts, so main.ts shrinks.

Still needs live retest
- /save, /export, /import against a remote gateway
- macOS and Windows save dialogs
- /rollback restore and diff with real checkpoints
- /agents with a running subagent


**Shared commit:** `feat(gateway): session.export …` is the same patch on this PR and the Ink PR (T10), so they merge in either order.

**Follow-up decision:** remote `/export` and `/import` would need profile archives sent through the gateway. That's a new capability bigger than this row, so on a remote gateway they refuse by name and point to `hermes profile export|import` on that host.

prs.title: fix(tui): serve Ink /voice, /reload-mcp, /config, /save, /timestamps from the gateway; name the rest
prs.body:
Ink commands that the shared gateway still refused, or that still ran on the pre-gateway sidecar, now get a gateway handler or a named refusal. Ink half of lane 1 in package 12.

- `/voice on|off|status` runs the owner's per-session `/voice` handler (`slash.exec`) and mirrors it through a new `config.get key=voice`. Push-to-talk (`voice.record`) gates on that mode, not the owner process's `HERMES_VOICE`. Refs #134889 (T9)
- `/reload-mcp` uses the owner's session-scoped `reload.mcp`. `/config` pages `config.get key=full`. Refs #134889 (T10)
- New owner verb `session.export {format, redact}` returns the rendered `/save` transcript and writes nothing; Ink's `/save [json|md|html] [filename] [redact]` writes the file locally. Refs #134889 (T10)
- `/timestamps` (`/ts`) writes `display.timestamps` through `config.set`. Refs #134889 (T10)
- `/export /import /snapshot /handoff /hatch /worktree /palette` stay `unsupported_command`, but the refusal now carries what to use instead (`data.detail`), and Ink prints it. Refs #134889 (T10)

Refs #141321

Design choices
- The gateway returns the data and the client writes the file: one verb (`session.export`) serves both local Ink and remote Desktop, whose Electron-side write can reuse it. `session.save` is kept for shipped clients.
- Profile archives, state snapshots, `/handoff`, `/hatch` and `/worktree` act on the gateway host's disk, terminal or git checkout, or need more than a small handler. They get a named refusal that points at `hermes profile export|import`, `hermes backup --quick`, `hermes -w`, or the classic CLI. The wire reason is unchanged, so shipped clients still work.
- `/voice tts` stays refused (CMD-2), so a local session's TTS is always off. Ink sets speech output off on every `/voice`.
- On the shared gateway `/reload-mcp always` confirms once: the owner verb has no persistent opt-out.
- `/subscription`, `/topup` and the `/skills` hub are left as they are. On canonical Ink they already run in the owner process, through the grant-checked, profile-bound legacy fallback (`ws_legacy_fallback.dispatch_legacy`), with no session state or second writer. Moving them onto the authority handler table would be a mechanical follow-up with no behaviour change.

Still needs live retest
- canonical Ink: `/voice on`, then real-microphone push-to-talk
- `/reload-mcp` against a real MCP server
- `/save md out.md` writing into the cwd
- `/timestamps` repainting the transcript


**Not moved: `/subscription`, `/topup` and the `/skills` hub.** On the shared gateway these don't reach a client-side sidecar. They reach the existing handlers inside the gateway process, which check the connection's grant and are bound to its profile. They hold no session state and write nothing a session owns, so re-registering them as gateway handlers would move billing calls (`subscription.change`, `billing.charge`) with no behaviour change. T10's "off the old sidecar" is met for these three.

**Shared commit:** `feat(gateway): session.export …` is the same patch on this PR and the Desktop PR (T11), so they merge in either order. Desktop writes the file through Electron; Ink writes it locally.

prs.title: feat(webapp): serve Desktop renderer in browsers
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds `hermes webapp`, an authenticated browser-hosted mode for the **actual Hermes Desktop renderer**. This is not the Web Dashboard: it serves the chat-first Desktop workspace and installs a browser implementation of `window.hermesDesktop` backed by the host running Hermes.

The implementation keeps the existing authority boundaries instead of cloning Desktop UI or adding a parallel backend:

- the renderer is built separately to `apps/desktop/dist-webapp` from the pinned repository workspace;
- the existing FastAPI authentication/session-token and one-time WebSocket-ticket controls gate the surface;
- host files, Git, previews, uploads, profiles, terminal, gateway, and Bot routing reuse existing profile-scoped APIs;
- native-only Electron capabilities are absent or fail explicitly rather than being falsely emulated;
- non-loopback binds remain fail-closed behind configured authentication.

### Lineage and overlap

- Browser bridge/build lineage is carried forward from @adybag14-cyber's #85604; the arbitrary-shell design that originally blocked that PR is not reused.
- The explicit `hermes webapp` product boundary is carried forward from @seagpt's #61171.

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/webapp.py`, CLI parser/lifecycle code, and docs: add `hermes webapp`, isolated renderer builds, process identity, `--status`/`--stop`, and loopback-by-default launch behavior.
- `apps/desktop/src/lib/browser-desktop-bridge*.ts`: implement the browser preload contract for authenticated REST/gateway calls, uploads, files, Git, previews, clipboard, microphone, profiles, and Bot registry routes.
- `hermes_cli/web_server_chat.py`, `hermes_cli/web_host_terminal.py`, and the `chat_ws`, `files`, and `uploads` routers: add authenticated Webapp routing, profile-scoped upload staging, and host-terminal setup through the topical owners. The shared `/api/pty` transport remains in the chat router.
- Desktop preview/files/layout/terminal surfaces: website links open in a separate browser tab by default in Webapp; Electron retains its embedded browser with local or remote gateways. Explicit URL previews retain the sandboxed iframe and **Open in browser** recovery action. Other browser adaptations include deliberate native-only degradation, configured-layout persistence, and refresh-safe terminal history.
- Webapp downloads and media: implement the browser save bridge using authenticated download URLs and a HEAD check before handing off to the browser. Audio/video use authenticated HTTP streams with Range support. URLs retain the active profile and proxy base path; Electron keeps its native save dialog and media protocol. Existing managed-file access rules and size limits still apply.
- Profile lifecycle: persist a fresh incarnation per create/import, preserve it across rename, carry it through sessions/workers, and use the same cross-process lifecycle lease for legacy marker backfill, `SessionDB` pathname binding/schema initialization, and attachment writes so delete/recreate cannot cross a checked generation boundary. Partial-delete retries durably recover the token. Publication and retirement coordination lives in `hermes_cli/profile_lifecycle.py`; gateway retirement/fence policy lives in `tui_gateway/profile_lifecycle.py`.
- Upload and attachment handling: reuse the incoming upload spool, check its actual length, and carry captured installation/profile/incarnation ownership through browser picks, drops, edits, drafts, and retries. Already-staged files attach through the owning backend and retain the copy into the container-visible attachment cache.
- Clipboard publication: extract native clipboard images outside lifecycle/session locks, then validate the captured session and profile generation before publishing the image.
- Session display and recovery: derive human/runtime provenance from the backend's canonical classifier and carry it through REST/RPC hydration and reconciliation. Runtime journal boundaries preserve partial replies, tool/reasoning structure, human corrections, and stream ownership across reloads and reused stream IDs; completed replies retire the journal tail. Older gateways retain the existing fallback, with durable row IDs compared before text normalization.
- Detached turn continuity: a brief browser disconnect retains the running session and worker for a bounded reconnect grace period. Resume, activation, and prompt submission check profile generation and disconnect ownership before reattaching.
- Shared policy: use one typed Git REST mapping, the existing upload-generation resolver and desktop control-plane process classifier, an explicit staging destination for private profile initialization, and shared attachment response/error helpers. Profile checks access their lifecycle owner directly.
- Config revision: `GET /api/config?with_revision=true` answers `{config, revision}` and `PUT /api/config` answers `{ok, revision}`, so the renderer can order racing appearance reads and saves. The revision is `config.yaml`'s mtime in microseconds. The shared config writer (`atomic_roundtrip_yaml_save`, through `save_config` and `atomic_config_write`/`atomic_config_replace`) stamps each write at least 1 µs past the file it replaces and returns the published mtime, so a later write never ties or goes backwards unless the filesystem's timestamps are too coarse to keep the stamp or it refuses `utime`. A bare `GET` is unchanged.
- Tests and smoke coverage: add browser bridge, uploads, Webapp command/lifecycle, same-name recreation ABA, deterministic barriers at attachment write/DB connect/legacy backfill, fail-closed lease-timeout behavior, concurrent cross-process marker publication, named-launch profiles, partial-delete retry, generation-scoped resume, fallback enumeration, real Chromium host-terminal/layout checks, concurrent clipboard extraction, staged-file ownership, canonical display provenance, and runtime journal recovery.

### Recent browser UX and reliability hardening

- Mobile controls: 44px touch targets for message actions, **Copy**/**More** access, native text selection, and a compact tab picker. Tapping outside the sidebar dismisses it without incidentally focusing the composer.
- Keyboard and media focus: keep the composer visible with visual-viewport fallback and a resize hint; preserve native video/audio controls and prevent queued focus retries from stealing focus after media interaction.
- Ticket and file ownership: carry profile incarnation through tickets and retain the checked ownership boundary through leased, pinned file opens. Profile asset/configuration writes and named-profile mirrors preserve the captured incarnation.
- Private launch containment: on macOS, private auto-open falls back to the operator's manual link instead of putting a bearer in process arguments. Launch-ticket redemption fails closed there; authenticated child-window tickets remain separate.
- Session and platform reliability: harden PTY worker/viewer ownership and reconnect/dead-shell cleanup, roll appearance back to confirmed state without overriding newer peer/profile changes, and correct SQLite lock tracking/read-only inspection and Docker runtime fingerprinting.

## How to Test

1. Build the browser renderer:
   ```bash
   hermes webapp --build-only --force-build
   ```
2. Start locally:
   ```bash
   hermes webapp --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9119
   ```
3. Verify Desktop sessions/files/Git/previews/terminal, create and delete a profile, refresh, and confirm the deleted profile remains absent from `/api/profiles`, Bot roster/routes, and the profile filesystem.
4. Click a website link in Webapp: it should open in a separate browser tab without creating a preview pane. In Electron, a normal click should still open its embedded browser, including when connected to a remote gateway.
5. Explicitly choose **Open in app** from a link context menu to use an embedded preview. Sites that reject embedding should retain the **Open in browser** recovery action.
6. Download a file from a chat attachment, play and seek an inline video/audio attachment, and try **Open video file** for an unsupported format. Missing files should show a download error while keeping the chat open.
7. For remote use, configure dashboard authentication first, then launch with an explicit non-loopback bind.
8. At a narrow/mobile viewport, select message text, use **Copy**/**More**, switch tabs, and dismiss the sidebar by tapping outside it. Sidebar dismissal and video/audio controls should not unexpectedly focus the composer. Open and close the software keyboard and check composer visibility; repeat media interaction while a focus retry is pending.
9. Disconnect/reconnect a running session and terminal, switch profiles, and retry after same-name profile recreation. Stale profile/ticket ownership must fail closed. For private macOS launch, follow the manual-link fallback.
10. With a profile whose `terminal.backend` is `ssh`, paste an image into the Webapp composer and send it. In Settings → Sessions, choose a default project folder, reload, and confirm it is kept.

## Security, compatibility, and non-goals

- An authenticated Webapp user has host-level Hermes capabilities, including an interactive shell as the account running Hermes. The docs call this out explicitly; trusted VPN/SSH-tunnel access is preferred and direct internet exposure should use OAuth/OIDC plus HTTPS.
- Browser-selected files are uploaded as bytes into profile-scoped host staging; client filesystem paths are never treated as host paths.
- URL previews use a capability-minimal sandboxed iframe. Electron DevTools/trusted-input automation, native window inspection, global shortcuts, always-on-top/HUD behavior, external-terminal launch, and native updating remain Electron-only.
- No direct or transitive dependency versions changed.
- This does not redesign the Web Dashboard, replace native Desktop, add an unauthenticated shell transport, or claim arbitrary access to a browser client's filesystem.

prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Anthropic 1.7.0 is now available to the optional native provider instead of the pinned 0.87.0 release. Anthropic 1.x validates that injected timeout and HTTP client objects come from its `httpx2` dependency; Hermes previously supplied objects from its separate `httpx` dependency, so normal and Entra bearer client construction raised `TypeError` before a request could be made. This change constructs only the Anthropic-bound timeout and bearer-hook client with `httpx2`, while retaining the existing bearer-header hook, proxy normalization, timeout values, and retry behavior.

- `agent/anthropic_adapter.py` — build SDK timeout values with `httpx2.Timeout` so normal Anthropic clients meet the 1.x constructor contract.
- `agent/azure_identity_adapter.py` — build the Entra request-hook client with `httpx2.Client` while preserving token refresh and authorization-header replacement.
- `tests/agent/test_anthropic_client_auth.py` — cover successful standard and bearer-hook client construction against Anthropic 1.7.0.

prs.title: Image and video generation no longer exhaust the Nous gateway's rate limit by polling FAL every 0.1 s
prs.body:
Image and video generation through the Nous tool gateway now poll the FAL queue every 2 s instead of every 0.1 s. One image used to spend the whole 200-requests-per-minute gateway budget by itself, so a second concurrent job got 429s.

**Root cause:** `fal_client` 0.13.1 `SyncRequestHandle.get()` runs `iter_events()` at its default `interval=0.1`. That is a status GET every ~0.3 s once you add the round trip, and all of them count against the gateway's fixed one-minute window of 200 requests.

## Changes
- `tools/fal_common.py`: `wait_fal_queue_result(handle)` drains `handle.iter_events(interval=FAL_QUEUE_POLL_SECONDS)` (2 s), then calls `handle.get()`. Its first status check sees `Completed` and goes straight to the result GET. It uses only public SDK API (no monkeypatching) and keeps the SDK's own 429/5xx retry on every call.
- `tools/image_generation_tool.py`: the interrupt-aware `_wait_fal_result` worker calls the helper. The interrupt polling on the caller thread is unchanged, so an interrupt still abandons the job within 0.5 s.
- `plugins/video_gen/fal/__init__.py`: both blocking `.get()` waits (generation and the SeedVR upscale) use the helper. Video jobs run for minutes, so at 0.1 s they cost hundreds of polls each.
- Tests: one invariant test, `test_image_wait_polls_queue_status_at_gateway_cadence`. It drives the real SDK handle over an `httpx.MockTransport` and asserts the poll sleeps equal `FAL_QUEUE_POLL_SECONDS`. It fails on main. Test fakes that only had `get()` gain an empty `iter_events()`, and two touched test files get `encoding="utf-8"` (windows-footguns). No existing assertion changed.

**Why 2 s:** a poll cycle is 2 s plus RTT, about 25 requests/min per running job, so 8 jobs fit in the 200/min window where 1 did before. The added latency is at most one interval (2 s), about 1 s on average. In an earlier 3-worker run that forced the interval to 2 s, throughput went from ~1.75 to 6.3 images/min and the 429s dropped from many to zero.

## Live probe (real gateway, real `image_generate_tool`, `openai/gpt-image-2.5/flare/text-to-image`)
This counts every `httpx.Client.send` in-process. Requests pass through unmodified. One image per leg on `fal-queue-gateway.nousresearch.com`.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| wall clock | 12.1 s | 12.5 s |
| requests total | **42** | **9** |
| submit / status / result | 1 / 40 / 1 | 1 / 7 / 1 |
| request rate during the job | ~208 /min | ~43 /min |
| 429s | 0 | 0 |

An earlier 35.5 s gpt-image-2.5 run on main measured 75 requests, 17 of them silently retried 429s.

**Not live-probed:** FAL video generation (cost). It goes through the same helper, and the unit suite covers both video call sites.

## Validation
- `scripts/run_tests.sh` over the 35 test files that reference the image/video/FAL modules: 457 passed, 0 failed.
- `tests/tools/test_fal_sdk.py` (needs `fal_client`): 38 passed. The new test fails on main.
- `scripts/check --only health`: 0 blocking, 0 advisory.

## Infographic
![image-poll-interval](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aaef477/Njwfnb5qRqd6x5NKR5SOs_BKiyXpeJ.png)

The classic prompt_toolkit terminal composer can now use more than its fixed eight visible rows through `display.composer_max_lines` in `config.yaml`.

prs.body:
## Summary

`onebot-platform` is a community **platform plugin**: a QQ bot via the OneBot 11 protocol. It connects Hermes to the user's own self-hosted NapCat, Lagrange, LLOneBot or go-cqhttp deployment over WebSocket — the plugin hosts a reverse-WS server inside the Hermes gateway, or dials an existing forward-WS endpoint — and registers the `qq` toolset for DM and group chats with admin allowlists, group mention gating, per-member soft limits, and cron/notification delivery to a configured home channel. Inbound images are downloaded (and Pillow-downscaled) for the vision tool; long replies are split at sentence boundaries or rendered locally into a text image with fonttools/Pillow.

Tools: `qq_send_image`, `qq_send_voice`, `qq_send_video`, `qq_send_file`, `qq_send_forward`, `qq_napcat_api`, `qq_group_history`.

## Admission checklist

- **Rule 1 / Rule 5 — owner submission:** I am the owner of the plugin repository.
- **Rule 2 — exact pin:** full 40-character SHA `623ce54b48b2ae2dfb3028cab1a6ed435ac6aa29`.
- **Rule 3 — no self-updating code:** the plugin fetches and replaces nothing; updates land as SHA-bump PRs here.
- **Rule 6 — capabilities match reality:** `capabilities:` mirrors what the plugin registers at the pinned commit — 7 tools, no hooks, no middleware, no required env (every `ONEBOT_*` variable is optional, with config fallbacks). Confirmed by `hermes plugins validate` below.
- **Rule 7 — install scanner:** `security scan — safe`; no `dangerous` findings. prs.title: fix(cron): record preloaded cron skills in skill_view dedup cache
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Skills listed in a cron job's `skills:` are loaded into the prompt before the agent starts, via a raw `skill_view()` call. That preload never reached the skill_view dedup cache. If the agent then called `skill_view` on the same skill, which it often does when the prompt tells it to follow the skill, it got the whole SKILL.md a second time instead of the short "unchanged" stub.

On one daily digest job with three preloaded skills, this re-sent about 83k chars per run. That content then stayed in context for every later turn.

This PR records each successfully preloaded skill in the dedup cache, under the same task id the agent's tools run with:
- A repeat bare `skill_view(name)` of an unchanged skill now returns the stub.
- A changed skill, a `file_path` view, or a different run still returns full content, as before.

## Related Issue

No existing issue. Related open PRs that touch the same functions:
- NousResearch/hermes-agent#119086 adds a `bound_skills_out` kwarg to `_load_cron_skill_parts` / `_build_job_prompt`.
- NousResearch/hermes-agent#128700 adds a `session_id` kwarg to the dedup helpers.

Whichever merges second will need a small rebase.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `cron/scheduler.py`:
  - `run_job` now resolves `execution_id` before building the prompt, rather than only inside `_CronRunScope`. The fallback order is unchanged: argument, then `job["execution_id"]`, then a new uuid.
  - It passes `cron:{job_id}:{execution_id}` through `_prepare_job_prompt` to `_build_job_prompt`. The scope receives the same resolved id, so the prompt and the agent's tools share one task id.
  - File length is unchanged.
- `cron/scheduler_prompt.py`:
  - `_build_job_prompt` and `_load_cron_skill_parts` take an optional `run_task_id`.
  - After a skill loads successfully, it is recorded with `_record_skill_view(run_task_id, name, None, payload)`.
  - Without `run_task_id`, nothing is recorded, as today.
  - Bundle members are not recorded; that is left for a follow-up.
- `tests/cron/test_cron_preloaded_skill_dedup.py` (new):
  - The preload, then a `skill_view` in the same run, returns the dedup stub; another run id and a `file_path` view return full content.
  - `run_job` builds the prompt under the same task id that `run_conversation` receives.

Prompt caching is unaffected. The prompt text is identical; only the later tool result is shorter.

## How to Test

```bash
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/cron/test_cron_preloaded_skill_dedup.py -v
```

Both new tests fail on `main`: `_build_job_prompt()` rejects `run_task_id`, and `run_job` builds the prompt with no task id. Both pass with this change.

```bash
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/cron tests/tools/test_skill_view_dedup.py tests/tools/test_skills_tool.py
```

```bash
python scripts/check
```

`website/docs/reference/cli-commands.md` documents only 6 of the 12 flags `hermes update` actually accepts:

The prose guide already documents these flags, so the reference page is the one stale surface. Rewriting the guide would duplicate content; a "see also" pointer alone would leave the canonical flag table incomplete for anyone using the reference as the authoritative CLI surface.

The subcommands are fully implemented and user-facing (pinning is a documented Desktop feature; import is the advertised path for migrating from Claude Code/Codex per its parser description). Leaving them out of the reference forces users to discover them via `--help`. There is no prose page that documents them, so the reference table is the right (and only) place.
