prs.title: fix(agent): re-fold the active /goal and its contract at the compaction boundary
prs.body:
## Problem

`/goal` state lives in `state_meta`, not in the transcript. The model sees it only as a user message — the kickoff, and the `[Continuing toward your standing goal]` prompt queued between turns. The todo list, by contrast, is re-folded into the transcript at **every** compaction boundary (`_fold_todo_snapshot`).

So whether the goal and its completion contract survive a compaction depends on where the goal text happens to sit when the cut lands:

- **Active turn opened by a goal prompt:** survives (the active request is kept in the tail).
- **Active turn opened by something else** (a real user interjection, a busy-steer, a `/heartbeat` tick, a `/loop` tick while the goal is parked): after a mid-turn compaction the goal and contract exist only inside the summary's **lossy free-text `## Goal` section**. `agent/context_compressor.py` writes that slot as model-authored prose ("What the user is trying to accomplish overall"), so **Verification, Constraints and Stop condition are routinely paraphrased or dropped** for the rest of the turn — exactly the fields the judge later enforces. Losing them lets the agent drift from the contract that decides continuation.
- **Gateway hygiene compaction** (in place, between turns, before the next message is appended): if that next message is not a goal continuation, the turn starts from a summary where the goal is free text only.
- **Third-party context engines:** any engine that does not reproduce the built-in active-request anchor drops the goal.

Reported as #133643.

## Fix

Give `/goal` the todo list's own machinery.

- `hermes_cli/goals.py`: factor the goal+contract body out of `GoalManager.next_continuation_prompt` into a shared `_goal_body_block()`, so the continuation prompt and the preserved block render the same contract fields from one place. Add `render_preserved_goal_block()` (active + not parked only) under a distinct, non-imperative header `[Your standing /goal was preserved across context compression]`, and `goal_is_parked()`.
- `agent/conversation_compression_goal_fold.py` (new topical sibling, kept out of the `conversation_compression` facade to respect its line cap): `fold_goal_snapshot()` mirrors `_fold_todo_snapshot` — strips any earlier preserved goal block (refresh, never stack), folds the live active-goal block into the trailing user row the todo fold already produced (so two synthetic user rows never sit adjacent), and appends a flagged row only when the tail is not a user row.
- `agent/conversation_compression.py`: the compaction commit boundary now calls `fold_state_snapshots()` (todo fold + goal fold) instead of the bare todo fold; the goal row is registered as synthetic (`_goal_snapshot_synthetic` flag + header prefix) so provenance/scaffolding classification (#69292) is unchanged and the row is never treated as human intent.
- Folds **nothing** for a goal the judge marked done, a paused/cleared goal, or a parked (waiting) goal — no resurrection (#34197). Skipped on a continuation-opened turn, where the goal is already verbatim in the request.

Carve-out respected: `next_continuation_prompt` output is byte-for-byte unchanged (only refactored through `_goal_body_block`).

## Why not a whole new mechanism

The todo list already solves exactly this ("state that lives outside the transcript but must survive compaction"); the goal is the one remaining such state. Reusing the fold keeps one code path and one set of provenance flags.

## Validation

- `tests/agent/test_goal_snapshot_fold.py` (new, 11 tests): contract carried verbatim; refresh-not-stack across two boundaries; merge into a trailing real user row (provenance stays real); done/paused/cleared/parked fold nothing; no duplicate on a continuation turn; an unavailable store preserves the pending snapshot; header literal stays in sync; and an **end-to-end** run through `compress_context` asserting the active goal + contract survives a compaction exactly once.
- Regression: `tests/hermes_cli/test_goals.py`, `tests/tui_gateway/test_goal_command.py`, `tests/gateway/test_goal_status_notice.py`, `tests/gateway/test_goal_resume_restart.py`, `tests/agent/test_context_compressor_zero_user_provenance.py`, `tests/agent/test_compression_rotation_state.py`, `tests/agent/test_skill_todo_retention_parity.py`, `tests/agent/test_in_place_compaction.py`, `tests/agent/test_compression_boundary.py`, `tests/agent/test_salvage_grown_transcript.py` — **all pass** (≈230 tests).
- `scripts/run_tests.sh` (per-file isolation, CI parity); `python scripts/check` → 11 checks, ok (ruff + code-health ratchet clean; the new module keeps `conversation_compression.py` at its line cap).

prs.body:
## Problem

The CLI reference's **Top-level commands** table is the index readers use to discover
commands, but five commands that `hermes --help` lists are missing from it:
`worktree`, `browser`, `verify`, `monitoring` and `vault`. Of those, `hermes verify`
had **no documentation anywhere** in `website/docs`, so its phases, flags and exit
codes were undiscoverable.

Reproduction:

```bash
$ hermes --help | grep -E 'browser|monitoring|vault|verify|worktree'
    browser             Real-profile browsing helpers (close a browser locking ...
    monitoring          Inspect gateway monitoring (health & diagnostics export)
    vault               Manage the local encrypted autofill vault (add/list/rm ...
    verify              Detect a project's run recipe and smoke-test it
    worktree            Audit and reclaim accumulated git worktrees and merged branches

$ grep -n 'hermes verify' website/docs/reference/cli-commands.md
(no match)
```

The same table also carried one garbled row: the `pause` / `resume` entry read
"no new cron fires (…), kanban dispatch or gateway turns start until resumed",
which says the opposite of what the command does.

## The fix

- Add the five missing rows to the Top-level commands table. Four have topical pages
  (`cli.md#worktree-cleanup`, `features/browser.md`, `developer-guide/gateway-monitoring.md`,
  `features/credential-vault.md`), so the rows link to them rather than duplicating them.
- Add a full `## hermes verify` section: what it detects, the phase order
  (bootstrap → build → test → start → readiness → teardown), every flag, the exit
  codes, and examples.
- Repair the `pause` / `resume` row (`neither kanban dispatch nor new gateway turns
  start until resumed`) and note `hermes pause --reason <text>`.

## Why not another approach

No new page was needed: the four non-`verify` commands already have authoritative
topical pages, and the reference page's job is the command index. `verify` is the
only one with no page anywhere, so it gets the section.

## Validation

```bash
$ hermes verify --help        # every flag row matches the parser
$ hermes verify /tmp/verifydemo --detect-only   # -> {"source":"detected","recipe":{...}}, exit 0
$ hermes verify /tmp/emptyproj                  # -> "No recognizable project found", exit 1
$ hermes verify /tmp/does-not-exist-xyz         # -> "error: not a directory", exit 2
$ python3 website/scripts/check_doc_links.py    # -> OK: no route-style links ... (CI docs-site check)
```

Exit codes `0` / `1` / `2` documented in the new section were reproduced with the
three commands above. `check_doc_links.py` is the same script the `Docs Site Checks`
workflow runs.

prs.title: fix(agent): stop server fingerprinting after a read timeout (#126567)
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

A custom OpenAI-compatible gateway may accept a connection but never answer paths it does not route. The server-type fingerprinting waterfall currently treats a read timeout as a failure of just that path, so it waits through later probes too. This stops after the first read timeout and keeps the negative result in the existing short-lived in-memory cache. It does not mark the reachable host blackholed or persist the negative verdict to disk. Connect timeouts retain their existing blackhole behavior, and quick 404s still allow the next probe.

## Related Issue

Fixes #126567

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `agent/model_metadata.py`: leave the fingerprint waterfall on `httpx.ReadTimeout`, without recording a TCP-connect blackhole.
- `tests/agent/test_endpoint_blackhole.py`: use an HTTPX mock transport to prove that a read timeout makes one request per negative-cache lifetime, does not persist the verdict or blackhole the host, and that 404s still reach all five paths.

## How to Test

1. Run `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_endpoint_blackhole.py tests/agent/test_probe_cache_followups.py -q` with a test interpreter available at that path. On this Linux checkout: 29 passed.
2. The new read-timeout test fails on unchanged main: four probe paths are attempted instead of one. It passes with the patch. The 404 control still observes all five paths.
3. Run `ruff check agent/model_metadata.py tests/agent/test_endpoint_blackhole.py` and `git diff --check`. Both passed. No live corporate gateway was available for an end-to-end timing measurement.

## Checklist

- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)

prs.title: fix(doctor): state.db repair hints order "stop the profile's gateway" before --fix (#110054)
prs.body:
Item 3 of #110054 removed the bare `run 'hermes doctor --fix'` from the large-WAL warning while a live writer holds state.db (landed as #113055). Three more doctor state.db hints still print it:

- FTS repair hint — `state.db FTS write corruption — run 'hermes doctor --fix' (or 'hermes sessions repair') to rebuild the FTS index`
- malformed-schema hint — `state.db schema malformed — run 'hermes doctor --fix' (or 'hermes sessions repair') to recover hidden sessions`
- the >1 GB write-health probe skip info line — `… (run 'hermes doctor --fix' to probe it)`, printed from inside the branch that already *knows* a live writer may hold the store

**Problem / reproduction** (Linux, any checkout). Hold `state.db` from a second process (Desktop or `hermes gateway`), then run `hermes doctor` (no `--fix`) on a store that fails the write-health probe. The hint is printed with no holder qualifier, so the user follows it into `hermes doctor --fix` while the writer is live — the second-writer nudge #110054 documents — and the repair path refuses outright:

```
state.db repair skipped: a live writer still holds state.db; skipped schema surgery to avoid tearing
b-tree pages under a concurrent writer. Stop the gateway (hermes gateway stop) and retry.
```

So the user is told to run a command that cannot succeed, and is not told what to stop first.

**Fix.** The two repair hints gain a held form, selected by the same wrapper the WAL path already uses (`hermes_state_repair._live_writer_holds_db` — foreign-holder scan first, fails closed), worded like the WAL `_SKIP` line: *"cannot prove state.db is quiet (stop the profile's gateway first, then run …)"*. An unprovable store is never asserted as a live writer (gate C1's honest disjunction); a holder scan that raises is treated as held. The probe-skip info line orders "stop" first. `--fix` semantics, and the hint for a provably quiet store, are unchanged. No new scan, no new surface, no new dependency.

**Validation**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `tests/hermes_cli/test_doctor_repair_hint_holder_guard.py` on `origin/main` (production file reverted) | 4 failed, 1 passed |
| Same file on this branch | 5 passed |
| Sibling suites: `test_doctor.py`, `test_doctor_wal_checkpoint_guard.py`, `test_doctor_wal_holder_guard.py`, `test_observational_sessiondb_modes.py`, `test_state_db_repair_non_destructive.py` + this file | 102 passed, 8 skipped |

Tests: held → the hint orders "stop the profile's gateway" before `hermes doctor --fix` and says "cannot prove state.db is quiet"; provably quiet → today's hint, byte for byte; holder scan raising → the held hint (fail closed); held + >1 GB → the probe-skip line orders stop first.

Refs #110054 (item 3's rule, remaining surfaces), #113055, #110914. No open PR touches these hints — #123511 is about repair *admission*, not the hint text.

prs.title: fix(gateway): explain read-only cron session failures
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Messages submitted to a cron-owned session currently become an opaque "The admitted turn failed" card. That session retains its frozen scheduled request after the run ends, so retrying an ordinary message there cannot work.

Return a specific, non-retryable `cron_session_read_only` error instead. Desktop explains the scheduled-session restriction and offers Start new session. The original payload, request and principal checks stay intact; no message is replayed automatically.

Copied diagnostics use the gateway's recorded failure time when available. They omit `time:` when no honest failure timestamp reaches the card, rather than stamping the time of copying or the start of a long turn.

## Related Issue

Fixes #141348

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Changes Made

- Carry the optional terminal timestamp through the generated gateway contract and Desktop message metadata.

prs.title: feat(tui_gateway): idempotent prompt.submit via client_turn_id, plus turn.status
prs.body:
## What

A client can now make a chat turn retry-safe. `prompt.submit` accepts an optional `client_turn_id` — an opaque id minted by the client — and a second submit carrying the same id and the same text answers the *stored* ack of the turn that already exists instead of starting a second agent run. A new `turn.status` RPC reports what the server knows about an id.

This closes the last hole in the "the socket dropped while my message was being sent" case. Today a client that cannot tell whether its submit landed has two options: resend and risk a duplicate turn, or stay silent and risk losing it. The transcript is the only arbiter, and reading a 25k-message transcript to answer "did my turn start" is both expensive and racy.

## Contract

`prompt.submit` request params gain `client_turn_id` (optional, 1..180 chars; absent = today's behaviour, byte-identical ack).

`prompt.submit` result, at the top level:

```json
{"accepted": true,
 "client_turn_id": "<echo>",
 "server_turn_id": "<non-empty>",
 "state": "accepted" | "running" | "terminal",
 "duplicate": false,
 "idempotent": true,
 "replayed": false}
```

`duplicate` is the compatibility field and always equals `replayed`. `outcome` (`succeeded` / `failed` / `cancelled`) rides beside `state` when the state is `terminal`, because the ack path has no other way to say "already finished, badly".

`turn.status`: `{"session_id", "client_turn_id"}` → `{"known": true, "client_turn_id", "server_turn_id", "state"}` or `{"known": false, "client_turn_id"}`. The echo is present in both cases: a client matches it before trusting any answer. `turn.status` reports all five turn states (`accepted`/`running`/`terminal`/`failed`/`cancelled`) while the ack accepts three — status is a report, the ack is a commitment.

`/v1/capabilities` gains the feature `turn_idempotency_v1` so a client can detect the surface instead of version-sniffing.

## Semantics

- Key: `(profile home, runtime session id, client_turn_id)`. Same key + same text = one run, replayed. Same key + different text is not a retry (the client reused an id): it runs, under a fresh server turn id.
- State is recorded by the turn, never by the request: `accepted` when the submit is admitted, `running` when the agent actually starts, `terminal` + that run's own outcome in the turn loop's `finally`. A replay of a finished turn therefore reports what happened, not what was asked.
- Every exit that never reaches the loop (refused slot, admission failure, persist failure, dispatch refusal) ends the turn as `terminal`/`failed`, so an id is never left `accepted` by a turn that died before it started.
- The registry is per-process and in-memory, like `_IdempotencyCache` in `gateway/platforms/api_server.py`: 1000 entries, one hour after the last transition, evicted oldest-first. A backend restart loses it and the client falls back to its own transcript check.

Two deliberate bounds, both only costing a stale report and neither able to run a turn twice: a turn dispatched to an isolated compute host cannot be observed finishing from this process and stays `accepted` until the TTL, and a steer/redirect whose live turn ends in the gap between the redirect ack and the join stays `running` until the TTL.

## Wire generation

`tui_gateway/contracts/prompt_voice.py` carries the new params/result models and the `turn.status` pair; `apps/shared/src/gateway-contract.generated.ts` and `gateway-contract.openrpc.json` are regenerated, so `tests/tui_gateway/contracts/test_generated.py` is green.

## Tests

- `tests/tui_gateway/test_turn_identity.py` — **19 passed**: first submit acks with `duplicate=false`/`replayed=false`; an identical retry runs the agent once and replays the same `server_turn_id` with `replayed=true`; a mid-flight retry reports `running`; the same id with different text runs again; a legacy submit is byte-identical and resolves none of the helpers; an over-long or non-string id is `4001`; a finished failed turn replays as `terminal` + `outcome: failed`; `turn.status` echoes on both known and unknown; the id is scoped per profile home; the registry expires and evicts.
- `tests/gateway/test_api_capabilities_turn_idempotency.py` — **1 passed** (the flag is declared).
- `tests/tui_gateway/contracts` — **5 passed** (generated wire is current).

`tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_server.py`: **656 passed, 4 failed** — and the same 4 fail on `origin/main` in the same environment (verified side by side in two worktrees), so they are pre-existing on this host rather than caused by this branch.

`scripts/check` (the repo's ruff/uv-pinned lint gate) and `tsc` on the regenerated TypeScript both need a dev environment this machine does not have; CI is authoritative for both. `py_compile` is clean on every touched Python file.

prs.title: feat(a2a): reachable behind a reverse proxy and on IPv6-only private networks
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Lets the A2A plugin run behind a reverse proxy and on IPv6-only private networks, safely.

- **IPv6 bind.** `ThreadingHTTPServer` is IPv4-only, so `A2A_HOST=::` failed to bind and the plugin could not be reached on IPv6-only private networks (for example Fly's 6PN). An IPv6 host now binds dual-stack.
- **No-token mode never trusts a proxied request.** Without a token the plugin binds loopback and trusts every caller as local. A reverse proxy on the same host would make every remote caller look local, so a request carrying `X-Forwarded-For`, `Forwarded` or `X-Real-IP` is now refused (401) in that mode, and an unauthenticated `GET /` behind a proxy no longer lists the served agents. Token mode is unchanged. This is §3.2 hardening (exposure through a proxy is an operator decision under §2.5).
- **Card URL behind a path prefix.** The card already honours `X-Forwarded-Host`/`X-Forwarded-Proto`; it now also honours `X-Forwarded-Prefix`, so a proxy serving the plugin at `https://host/a2a/` advertises a URL peers can call back.

Hermes Cloud will route `https://<agent>.agents.nousresearch.com/a2a/` to each agent's plugin (hermes-agent-router), so hosted agents on different backends can call each other with the plugin's own tokens as the gate.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `plugins/platforms/a2a/adapter.py`: dual-stack server class for IPv6 hosts; one `_authenticate()` that passes "forwarded" to the security context; `X-Forwarded-Prefix` in the request public URL.

prs.title: feat(skills): PR comments, reviews and CI now follow back into the agent's chat (inspired by Amp)
prs.body:
After the agent opens a pull request, new comments, reviews and the CI verdict now come back into the same conversation on their own, with no new tool and no webhook to expose.

## Infographic

![Follow a PR back into the chat](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aaef44a/WGLr9Sg0zm8TWB0F6qyqL_EwpXlDBP.png)

## Inspired by Amp

Source: [You've Got Comments](https://ampcode.com/news/github-listeners) (2026-10-12) + [docs/github § GitHub Webhooks](https://ampcode.com/docs/github#github-webhooks).

**Their mechanism:** when Amp opens a PR, the agent subscribes to the PR's comments, reviews and the CI for its latest commit. Amp receives the events through its GitHub App webhooks and continues the thread that opened the PR. Subscriptions carry no custom instructions and grant no permission to push or to follow instructions posted in comments.

**Our adaptation:** Hermes already wakes a session when a background terminal job started with `notify=true` exits, on every surface (CLI, TUI, Desktop, messaging gateway). `skills/software-development/github/scripts/follow_pr.py` is a `gh`-based follower that blocks until the PR has something new, prints one digest and exits, so that existing wake carries the event into the conversation that opened the PR. The `github` skill's PR workflow now tells the agent to start it after `gh pr create` and to start it again after each batch.

| | Amp | Hermes (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| Transport | GitHub App webhooks, hosted ingress | `gh` polling from the user's own machine; no public endpoint, no app install |
| Events | comments, reviews, inline comments, head CI, merge queue | comments, reviews, inline comments, head-commit CI verdict (once per head, failed check names), merge/close |
| Delivery | continues the subscribed thread | the `notify=true` completion wake continues the session that started it |
| Self-echo | n/a (server side) | the agent's own `gh` login is skipped, so its replies never wake it |
| Trust | comment text never grants permission | same rule, stated in the skill |
| Spawn a new session per new issue/PR | yes (orb spawner) | not ported; `hermes webhook subscribe` + the `watchers` skill already cover new-item fan-out |

Footprint: zero schema or system-prompt growth (one script, one skill routing row, one reference section).

## Changes

- `skills/software-development/github/scripts/follow_pr.py`: the follower. The first run treats existing comments and reviews as history; an already-finished CI verdict is reported. State lives in `$HERMES_HOME/watcher-state/pr-<repo>-<n>.json`. A short settle window batches a review together with its inline comments. Exit 0 = events, 3 = quiet window elapsed (`--hours`, default 24), 2 = `gh` kept failing.
- `references/pr-workflow.md` § Follow a PR, plus a routing row in `SKILL.md`.
- `tests/skills/test_github_follow_pr.py`: 2 invariants. CI is reported only once settled and once per head. Own comments and baselined history never wake.

## Validation

**Live (real GitHub, our PR #136951):**
- First run: `## [ci] passed on dfe91c99cd`, exit 0, with 8 existing comments and reviews baselined.
- Second run of the same command: `no new events`, exit 3. Nothing replayed.
- After one review key was removed from the state file: `## [review] @greptile-apps COMMENTED`, exit 0.
- On a fork PR with no checks yet (#137411), the follower keeps waiting and reports nothing, as intended.

**Local checks:** `scripts/run_tests.sh` over the new test plus the skill doc and authoring contracts: 1516 passed, 0 failed. ruff, windows-footguns, the no-tmp check and `scripts/check --only health` are all clean.

**Not covered:** an end-to-end wake through a live gateway chat. The follower only relies on the existing `notify=true` completion path, which this PR does not change.

prs.title: fix(worktree): a merged PR only vouches for the commits it carried
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`_worktree_branch_pr_merged` treats **any** merged PR whose head branch has the same *name* as proof that a worktree holds no unmerged work:

```python
["gh", "pr", "list", "--head", branch, "--state", "merged", "--json", "number", "--limit", "1"]
merged = isinstance(prs, list) and bool(prs)
```

A branch name is not an identity. When a branch is reused after its PR merged (a follow-up card continuing on the same branch, a fix pushed after a squash-merge, a recycled `hermes/<name>`), the worktree carries new local commits that the merged PR never saw. `_prune_stale_worktrees` consults this helper precisely *because* those commits are unpushed and not patch-equivalent upstream, so a false `True` here reaps the only copy of that work.

This PR makes the escape hatch prove what it claims: a merged PR only vouches for the commits it carried. The local tip must equal a merged PR's `headRefOid`, or be an ancestor of it (the PR received extra review commits the worktree never pulled — everything local still went in). Ancestry is checked with `git merge-base --is-ancestor` against the local object database, so a head we never fetched reads as "not proven" and preserves the tree.

## Related Issue

No separate issue. Related: #118238 reclaims done-card worktrees in `kanban gc` and applies the same `headRefOid` rule in its own module; this PR fixes the existing helper in `worktree_ops.py` that the CLI pruner uses today, independently of that work.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/worktree_ops.py`
  - `_worktree_branch_pr_merged` requests `number,headRefOid` and returns `True` only if some merged PR's head is the local tip or a descendant of it.
  - New `_tip_in_merged_head` helper; fails safe on a missing/non-string `headRefOid` or an unfetched head object.
  - The `rev-parse HEAD` it already ran for the cache key is now computed once and reused for the check. Caching semantics are unchanged (only `True` is memoized, on `(branch, head_sha)`).
  - `--limit 1` becomes `--limit 100`: with several merged PRs on a reused name, the newest is not necessarily the one that carried this tip. More than 100 merged PRs on one head name falls through to "not proven" (preserve), never to a removal.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_worktree.py` (`TestPrMergedEscapeHatch`)
  - Existing positive tests now stub a `gh` answer carrying the worktree's real `headRefOid`.
  - New: reused branch with commits after the merge is **not** merged and is preserved by `_prune_stale_worktrees`; tip behind the merged head **is** merged; unfetched head fails safe; merged PR without `headRefOid` fails safe.

## How to Test

```
pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_worktree.py -q -k TestPrMergedEscapeHatch
```

prs.title: fix(desktop): preserve durable mid-turn prompt order
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

When Desktop reattaches a tool-heavy turn, it can append already-persisted user prompts below that turn's final answer even though the stored transcript is correctly ordered. The latest-user-run matcher stops at persisted tool rounds, so it mistakes the starting prompt and earlier corrections for missing messages.

Collect the current turn's user run across persisted tool rounds as well as live assistant segments. Crossing a persisted tool round requires its timestamp to fall within the current turn; this keeps an older completed tool-bearing reply from swallowing a newly repeated prompt.

## Related Issue

Fixes #141351

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- Extract the user-run traversal into `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-session-actions/inflight-user-run.ts` and use it from `appendLiveSessionProjection` in `utils.ts`.
- Recognize `durableComplete: false` tool rounds only when their timestamps prove they belong to the active turn. Completed replies and older or unproven durable rounds still bound the scan.
- Add `durable-user-order.test.ts` using the real transcript hydrator and reconciliation helpers. Cover both streaming flags, snapshots with plain corrections or only the steer correction, and repeated prompts after plain or tool-bearing prior replies.

## How to Test

1. On `main` at `67481b6f37615e58f1434ba6a1528e4c6e9b754c`, apply only the new regression file. Hydrate correctly ordered user rows 90/100/145/151, intervening tool rounds, and final answer 274 with `toChatMessages`.
2. Replay an in-flight activation snapshot without correction offsets. The committed final row makes `reconcilePersistedLiveTurn` return `null`, selecting the projection fallback. On the base, user prompts are projected again after answer 274. With the fix, the durable transcript retains its order and each user row appears once.
3. Run the regression and neighboring session, prompt, stream, and chat-message suites; run Desktop typechecking, ESLint on the touched files, and the required repository checks.

Reproduced on `main` at `67481b6f37`; the branch is rebased onto `7fdaad5da098`, whose Desktop sources are unchanged. Tested on Ubuntu 22.04.5 (Linux x86_64), Node.js 24.14.0, Vitest 4.1.11:

prs.title: fix(kanban): resolve a new card's board from the store it lands in
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`create_task()` decided where a new card belonged by asking the session which board was current, while the row itself went to whichever store the connection opened. Those two disagree whenever `HERMES_KANBAN_DB` is set, because the pin outranks the board slug (`hermes_cli/kanban_db.py:473-493`). The row could then land in one board's store stamped with another board's project, `workspace_kind=worktree`, and a `branch_name` resolving under that other board's repository, so a worker claiming the card would build and push in the wrong repo. That is the normal environment for a dispatcher-spawned worker, since the dispatcher injects the pin into every worker.

I hit this while filing cards onto another board from a session: the row landed in the pinned store and came out owned by the board the session sat on instead.

The store is the only reliable answer to which board a row is about to land in, so this makes the store the authority:

- `board_for_db_path()` (`:496`) is the inverse of `kanban_db_path()`: root store -> `default`, `<boards_root>/<slug>/kanban.db` -> `<slug>`, anything else -> no board identity.
- `_board_for_connection()` (`:523`) reads that back off the connection (`PRAGMA database_list`) and prefers it over the board the caller declared.
- `create_task()` (`:1313`) resolves the board that way before deriving any column, so the row's project follows the store it lands in.

Preferring the store over the declared board is deliberate: when the pin is set, the declared board is exactly the value `_board_path()` just discarded, and trusting it is what produced the bug. A store with no board identity (a copy, a relative path, `:memory:`) does not guess; it falls back to the declared board and behaves as before. An explicit `workspace_kind` or `project_id` still wins.

## Related Issue

Fixes #109435

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/kanban_db.py`: added `board_for_db_path()` and `_board_for_connection()`; `create_task()` now resolves the board from the connection's store before deriving board-derived columns.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_board_project.py`: two behaviour tests, red on main and green with the change.

118 insertions across those two files, nothing else touched.

## How to Test

1. `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_board_project.py -q` -> `7 passed`. With the source change stashed, the two new tests fail: `test_create_task_uses_the_store_board_not_the_session_board` and `test_create_task_inherits_from_the_store_board`.
2. The repro from #109435, run against a hermetic `HERMES_HOME`, three creates in one pass: pin at the root store with the session on the project-scoped board, the same with `--workspace scratch`, and the inverse (pin at the scoped store, session on `default`). On main the first row comes out `<project>|worktree|scoped/<id>` and the inverse row loses the project; here the first is `None|scratch|` and the inverse row inherits the scoped project and its worktree.
3. `pytest tests/hermes_cli -q`, same tree both ways: 27 failed / 307 passed with the change, 29 failed / 305 passed without it. Apart from the two tests above the failure sets are identical, so nothing else regressed. Those 27 fail on a clean checkout too (they are tied to this machine's paths and notification setup).

prs.title: fix(kanban): fail the delegate-child write fence closed when the delegation context is un-evaluable
prs.body:
The delegate-child write fence computes its verdict from `agent.delegation_context`, but
`tools.kanban_tools._delegation_ctx` returned its `default` (`False` == "not a delegate
child") out of a bare `except Exception`. A process that could not evaluate
`agent.delegation_context` therefore had the fence's own verdict computed as **allow**, and
only the board-connection layer stopped the write — reporting an error that misattributes
the cause.

Reproduction, measured on current `main`: with `agent.delegation_context` made
unimportable, a delegate child's board write passes the fence and is refused later at
`hermes_cli/kanban_db_connect.py` with `ModuleNotFoundError: import of
agent.delegation_context halted`. The write is still blocked, but by a guard further down
and with an error that points at the wrong cause.

### The fix

- `_delegation_ctx_or_none()` reports "un-evaluable" distinctly, and the write fence
  **refuses** on it for every caller instead of assuming, logging a `WARNING` that names the
  real cause.
- No env-bit escape: the `owned = os.environ.get("HERMES_KANBAN_TASK")` allow-branch is
  removed, so the only outcome that permits a board write is a definite "not a delegate
  child" (`verdict is False`). An un-evaluable context refuses even for a dispatcher-owned
  worker, because the escape bought no reachable write: every board write goes through
  `kanban_db_connect.connect()`, which imports the same `agent.delegation_context` module
  unwrapped and dies one step later with an opaque `ImportError` anyway. Reading "unknown"
  as "allow" on an identity gate is the silently-disabled gate this guard exists to remove.
- Read-only / visibility gates keep their previous defaults — `_delegation_ctx(...,
  default)` stays fail-open because it is hints/visibility only; only the write fence
  changes behaviour.

### Tests

`tests/tools/test_delegate_kanban_isolation.py` gains three tests (`+116/-0`; the file holds
10):

- `test_unavailable_delegation_context_direct_fence_refuses_an_owned_worker` — the
  direct-fence assertion from the review: `agent.delegation_context` unimportable,
  `HERMES_KANBAN_TASK` present, `_reject_delegated_child_mutation` called directly, so a
  pass cannot come from `kanban_db_connect.connect()`'s later import failure;
- `test_unavailable_delegation_context_cannot_mutate_the_board` — the **invariant**: neither
  an owned nor an unowned caller moves board state (task status, run status and comments read
  straight from the board file);
- `test_unavailable_delegation_context_fence_refuses_when_the_process_owns_no_task` — the
  un-evaluable branch refuses here, with the audit line (`un-evaluable`) captured.

Run at `d77213b0c7` — `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_delegate_kanban_isolation.py`,
receipt `evidence/t_f1f2beab/pytest_settree.txt`: **10 collected → 8 passed, 2 failed**. Both
failures are the pre-existing `home_io_guard` environment artifact ("TEST BUG: file I/O
against the REAL hermes home"), reproduced identically on a control tree carrying the branch
WITHOUT this change → **0 regressions from this change**. Negative control: with the
`owned = os.environ.get("HERMES_KANBAN_TASK")` allow-branch restored, the direct fence test
fails with `DID NOT RAISE _Reject`.

At this head `tools/kanban_tools.py` is byte-identical to the revision measured above; the
test file has since taken upstream linter-only edits to its pre-existing tests (still 10
