prs.title: fix(agent-runner): refuse reactions to notes the host wrote
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Stops `add_reaction` from queuing a reaction to a note the host wrote, which no platform can accept.

- **Problem**: the host writes notes into a session as messages from `system` (approval results, restart wake messages, self-mod confirmations, `create_agent` notices). The agent sees each with a numeric id like any other message, so `add_reaction` accepted one, answered "Reaction queued", and delivery asked the channel to react to the note's host id. The platform rejects it (on Google Chat: 404, retried until the delivery fails permanently), while the agent believes it reacted.
- **Fix**: `add_reaction` refuses a message whose content has `senderId: 'system'`, with a reason the agent can act on, and queues nothing. Reactions to messages people posted are unchanged.
- **Out of scope**: the agent-group suffix on inbound target ids (#3970, issue #3153), and emoji names (#2627, #3553). Both are separate problems in the same tool.

## Related work

No issue. Related but distinct: #3970 / #3153 (target id suffix). Even with that fixed, a host note's id is not a platform message id.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `bun test src/mcp-tools/core.test.ts`: 10 pass. Two new tests: a reaction to a posted message still queues; a reaction to a host note is refused and writes no outbound row.
- With the new check disabled, the refusal test fails (1 fail), so the test pins the fix.
- `bun test` (agent-runner): 616 tests, 0 fail.

prs.title: fix(whatsapp): keep every pending question answerable in a chat
prs.body:
<!-- contributing-guide: v1 -->
## Type of Change

- [ ] **Feature skill** - adds a channel or integration (source code changes + SKILL.md)
- [ ] **Utility skill** - adds a standalone tool (code files in `.claude/skills/<name>/`, no source changes)
- [ ] **Operational/container skill** - adds a workflow or agent skill (SKILL.md only, no source changes)
- [x] **Fix** - bug fix or security fix to source code
- [ ] **Simplification** - reduces or simplifies source code
- [ ] **Documentation** - docs, README, or CONTRIBUTING changes only

## Description

A second `ask_question` card delivered to a WhatsApp chat silently disables the
first one. The earlier card stays on screen, its slash commands stop working,
and its approval row is left pending with nothing to clear it.

`pendingQuestions` is keyed by chat and holds one entry:

```ts
const pendingQuestions = new Map<string, { questionId: string; options: NormalizedOption[] }>();
...
pendingQuestions.set(platformId, { questionId, options });   // deliver — overwrites
...
const pending = pendingQuestions.get(chatJid);               // inbound — newest only
```

So the inbound side can only ever see the most recent question in a chat. A
reply aimed at the earlier card matches nothing and is forwarded to the agent as
plain text — or, if the two cards share an option label, is silently counted as
an answer to the newer question.

Nothing recovers the abandoned row: `pending_approvals.expires_at` exists in the
schema, but nothing outside its migration reads or writes it.

### Observed

Three cards sent to one DM; only the last could be answered. The other two
stayed on screen with unresponsive commands and their rows stayed pending.

### Fix

Hold a list per chat. On delivery the question is appended; on reply,
`matchPendingQuestion` scans newest first and returns the array index, so only
the question that was answered is removed and the rest stay answerable. The key
is deleted once its list empties.

```ts
export function matchPendingQuestion(
  pendings: PendingQuestion[],
  content: string,
): { index: number; pending: PendingQuestion; option: NormalizedOption } | undefined
```

**On ambiguity.** Two cards live in the same chat can offer the same option
label — two approvals both rendering `/reject` — and a WhatsApp reply is plain
text with nothing tying it to the card it came from. That ambiguity is not
resolvable, so newest wins: it is the card the user was just shown.

**On bounds.** `PENDING_QUESTIONS_MAX` bounds how many *chats* hold a question;
because the map was keyed by chat, it never bounded questions *within* one. A
list per chat needs its own bound, since an entry whose question was resolved
elsewhere is never cleared — hence `PENDING_QUESTIONS_PER_CHAT_MAX`.

### How it was tested

Matching is extracted as an exported pure helper and unit-tested (7 cases:
earlier question still answerable, newest-wins on a shared label, index reported
so siblings survive, no match, empty list, case/whitespace, multi-word label).
This matches how the other pure helpers in this file are covered — the map
itself lives in the adapter setup closure and is not reachable from tests.

Full host suite run against this branch and against the unmodified base: same 16
failing files / 20 failing tests either way (the `channels` branch does not
currently typecheck or fully pass on its own), with the 7 new tests as the only
difference in the pass count.

Note: `src/channels/imessage.ts` has the same one-entry-per-chat shape and looks
to have the same bug. Left out deliberately to keep this PR to one thing.

prs.title: fix(whatsapp): ignore @newsletter JIDs at the inbound boundary
prs.body:
<!-- contributing-guide: v1 -->
## Type of Change

- [ ] **Feature skill** - adds a channel or integration (source code changes + SKILL.md)
- [ ] **Utility skill** - adds a standalone tool (code files in `.claude/skills/<name>/`, no source changes)
- [ ] **Operational/container skill** - adds a workflow or agent skill (SKILL.md only, no source changes)
- [x] **Fix** - bug fix or security fix to source code
- [ ] **Simplification** - reduces or simplifies source code
- [ ] **Documentation** - docs, README, or CONTRIBUTING changes only

## Description

WhatsApp Channel (newsletter) broadcasts are routed as direct messages, so each
one opens a channel-approval card that can never be resolved usefully.

`messages.upsert` drops `status@broadcast` but nothing else:

```ts
if (!rawJid || rawJid === 'status@broadcast') continue;
```

A WhatsApp Channel delivers on the same stream with a JID ending in
`@newsletter`. That is neither `@g.us` nor `@s.whatsapp.net`, so `isGroup` is
false a few lines down and the router takes the broadcast for a fresh DM: a
`messaging_groups` row is created and `buildQuestionText` renders
"<id> sent your bot a DM on whatsapp". Channels are read-only, so the bot can
never act on one — and since a channel keeps publishing, the cards keep coming.

### Observed

A newly provisioned Singapore number auto-followed three local channels. In
16 hours that produced 6 `messaging_groups` rows and 3 stuck
`pending_channel_approvals`, from The Straits Times, Zaobao and WhatsApp's own
announcements channel. Sample of what arrived as a "DM":

```
platform_id : 120363144038483540@newsletter
content     : "*Polls that keep up with the group chat* ... blog.whatsapp.com/..."
question    : "120363144038483540 sent your bot a DM on whatsapp."
```

Unfollowing the channels on the phone stops the inflow, but that is a
per-install workaround for something the adapter can decide on its own.

### Fix

Extract the boundary predicate and add the `@newsletter` suffix:

```ts
export function isIgnorableChatJid(jid: string): boolean {
  return jid === 'status@broadcast' || jid.endsWith('@newsletter');
}
```

`!rawJid` stays ahead of the call so the existing narrowing to `string` is
unchanged. The predicate is exported and unit-tested, matching how the other
pure helpers in this file are covered (`isBotMentionedInGroup`,
`computeWhatsappDefaults`, …).

Tests cover both ignored suffixes, that group and DM JIDs still route, and that
a JID merely containing the word "newsletter" is not ignored.

No behaviour change for any JID that reaches the router today.

prs.title: fix(add-dashboard): read transcripts without loading whole files
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Keeps the `/add-dashboard` pusher working when an agent's transcript gets large.

- **Problem**: the pusher reads transcripts with `fs.readFileSync(…, 'utf-8')`. Past ~512 MB (Node's maximum string length) that throws `Cannot create a string longer than 0x1fffffe8 characters`. `collectContextWindows` doesn't catch it and `collectSnapshot` uses `Promise.all`, so the whole snapshot fails: the dashboard stops updating and the error is logged every minute. `scanJsonlTokens` catches it and silently drops the file from token totals.
- **Why a normal install hits it**: the agent-runner rotates transcripts at 12 MB, but only when a container starts. A busy agent's container is never idle long enough to be restarted. We saw one container run ~9.5 h on a single long task, with image tool results, and its transcript reached 540 MB.
- **Also below the limit**: every 60 s the pusher re-read every transcript of every agent from byte 0. That costs CPU and memory in proportion to the whole history.
- **Fix**: files are never read whole any more.
  - Context window: read the transcript's last 256 KB, doubling the window until a usage line is found.
  - Token totals: a per-file cache of `{ inode, offset, entries }`. Each snapshot reads only the appended bytes, in 1 MB chunks, and holds a half-written last line until it is complete. A file that shrank or was replaced is read again; files that disappear are dropped from the cache.
  - Log backfill: read the last 512 KB of `nanoclaw.log` for the 200 lines.
  - A transcript that vanishes between the directory walk and the read (e.g. rotated away) is skipped, not the whole snapshot.
- **Same output**: on a 100 MB transcript the snapshot's `context_windows` and `tokens` are identical before and after.
- **Trade-off**: the token entries now stay in memory between snapshots (one small object per assistant call) instead of being rebuilt every minute.
- **Out of scope**: which transcript counts as "live" (the newest `.jsonl`, which can be a subagent's), and when the agent-runner rotates transcripts.

<details>
<summary>Before / after numbers</summary>

A fake data dir with one transcript of 200 KB tool-result lines plus an assistant usage line after each. One snapshot through `startDashboard()` (vitest), peak RSS from `/usr/bin/time -v`.

| Transcript | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 100 MB | snapshot in 626 ms, peak RSS 456 MB | 234 ms, 155 MB, identical snapshot |
| 600 MB | **no snapshot** (error at start and again at 60 s), peak RSS 1.17 GB | 1.06 s, 158 MB; totals correct (3,139 requests) |

Later snapshots read only the bytes appended since the previous one.
</details>

## Related work

No issue: this is a self-contained fix inside `.claude/skills/add-dashboard/resources/`, with its tests. #3417 also edits `dashboard-pusher.ts` (shutdown wiring, SQL, docs); its hunks don't overlap these lines.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- New tests in `dashboard-pusher.test.ts`, driven through `startDashboard()` like the existing one:
  - `finds the last usage line behind a long tail, without reading the transcript whole`
  - `reads only appended bytes, and counts a half-written line once it is complete`
  - `starts over when a transcript is replaced by a smaller one`
  - `still posts the snapshot when a transcript vanishes mid-read`
- Same tests on the old pusher -> 3 of the 4 fail (the "replaced" test guards the new cache, so it passes on both).
- Fresh clone, skill applied per `SKILL.md` steps 1–3 -> `pnpm run build` OK -> `pnpm exec vitest run src/dashboard-pusher.test.ts src/dashboard-wiring.test.ts` -> 7 passed.
- Same clone: `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` -> OK; `prettier --check` on the changed files -> OK.

prs.title: fix(router): send the command-gate denial without writing outbound.db
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Stops the command-gate's "Permission denied" reply from writing into a running session's `outbound.db`.

- **Problem**: `outbound.db` is the container's file: the agent-runner writes every reply, receipt and tool-state update there. The command-gate denial in `src/router.ts` also wrote it from the host, via `writeOutboundDirect`, while the container could be writing. Docker Desktop's file share does not carry SQLite locks between host and container, so both writers proceed at once. In a reproduction, host writes that were reported as committed went missing, and `PRAGMA integrity_check` reported a damaged index. The user never sees their "Permission denied".
- **Fix**: the router sends the denial straight through the delivery adapter (`getDeliveryAdapter().deliver(...)`), the same way approval cards and sender-approval cards are already sent, on the chat's own adapter instance. A failed send is logged and never fails inbound routing. 3 production files, +29 / −14.
- **Kept**: `writeOutboundDirect` stays exported, because `docs/agent-mailbox-seam-migration.md` names it for customized installs. Removing it would be a breaking change. Its doc comment now says it is only safe while no container is running.
- **Out of scope**:
  - Orphan-claim cleanup in `reconcile-session.ts` also writes `outbound.db`, right after killing a stuck container. That container is already silent, so the overlap is narrow and has not been demonstrated.
  - The `writeDirect` mailbox method is unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Trade-off of the direct send</summary>

The denial no longer goes through the delivery loop. So it loses the loop's persisted retries (3 attempts), the delivered record, and the cross-session echo. This matches how approval cards are delivered today. A rejected slash command can simply be re-sent.

</details>

## Related work

No issue filed. Same root cause (SQLite locks not shared across Docker Desktop's file share) as #4118, which handles the container's reads of `inbound.db`. The two PRs are independent.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`

- [ ] `kind/cleanup`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/router-command-gate-deny.test.ts` → 2 pass. These drive a non-admin `/clear` through the real `routeInbound`:
  - The adapter receives the exact denial on instance `testchat`.
  - Every session `outbound.db` has 0 `messages_out` rows.

prs.title: fix(agent-runner): retry inbound.db reads caught mid host write
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Stops a brief `inbound.db` read error from aborting an agent turn on Docker Desktop.

- **Problem**: Docker Desktop's file share does not carry the host's SQLite locks into the container. A read-only read of `inbound.db` can land in the middle of a host write and fail with `SQLITE_READONLY_ROLLBACK` (the host's live journal looks like one that needs rollback) or `SQLITE_CORRUPT` (a torn page). Between turns the next poll absorbs it. Inside a turn it reaches `processQuery`'s catch: every open route, users and peer agents alike, gets "The agent run failed. Check the logs for details.", and the batch is acked completed without redelivery. It was seen in a busy multi-agent Slack channel, on the agent that hears the most traffic. The likeliest trigger is the `messages_in` seq read inside `sqliteWriteMessageOut`, which runs on every send.
- **Fix**: every container read of `inbound.db` goes through `readInbound(read)` in `container/agent-runner/src/mailbox/sqlite/connection.ts`. It opens a fresh read-only connection and retries those two codes for up to 1 second, then throws. Any other error throws at once. The long-lived inbound connection is removed. `getInboundDb()` now only serves tests: provider test files already installed from older payloads import it, which CI's `pre-contract-providers` job checks. In test mode `readInbound` reads the in-memory DB only for the default path, so an explicit path always reads that file. `Query error` now logs the stack, so the next mid-turn failure names its call site.
- **Lock held during a retry**: `sqliteWriteMessageOut` calls `readInbound` inside `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` on `outbound.db`, so a retry can hold the container's RESERVED lock up to 1 s longer. The host never waits on it:
  - The host's outbound reader is read-only, and in rollback-journal mode RESERVED does not block readers.
  - The host has two outbound writers: the command-gate denial (`router.ts` → `writeOutboundDirect`) and orphan-claim cleanup (`reconcile-session.ts`). They can only wait where host and container share locks. On native Linux they do, but there the retry never fires: the reader sees the host's lock, so no journal looks hot. On Docker Desktop the retry can fire, but locks don't cross the file share, so nothing waits.
  - Inside the container the sleep pauses the event loop, so the heartbeat file touch slips by at most 1 s, against the sweep's default 60 s `CLAIM_STUCK_MS`.
- **Exact error code**: on Linux Bun (the agent image's 1.4.0, and CI), `bun:sqlite` throws `code: 'SQLITE_READONLY_ROLLBACK'` (`errno` 776) for a hot journal, not the base `SQLITE_READONLY`. A new test builds a real hot journal (a writer killed mid-transaction) and asserts that code and that it was retried. It skips where the runtime's SQLite reads past a hot journal: Bun on macOS uses the system SQLite.
- **Production lines**: +113 / −118. Most of that is the 13 call sites in `operations.ts` and `index.ts` moving to the helper.
- **Out of scope**: the host's read-only reads of `outbound.db` have the same exposure in reverse. Nothing has failed there yet, so it is not changed here. The host's command-gate write into `outbound.db` is handled separately in #4119.

<details>
<summary>Why not a setting instead</summary>

| Alternative | Measured result |
|---|---|
| Host `journal_mode=MEMORY` (no journal file) | The rollback error goes away, but reads return inconsistent data with no error, and `SQLITE_CORRUPT` rises about 10× |
| Read-write container connection | The container can take `EXCLUSIVE` while the host holds it, so it would roll back the host's live write |
| WAL | Already ruled out: `-shm` mmap is not coherent across virtiofs (see `connection.ts` header) |

</details>

## Related work

No issue filed. Reproduced locally (below); the change is confined to the agent-runner's read path.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `cd container/agent-runner && bun test src/mailbox/sqlite/read-inbound.test.ts`:
  - Linux, in the agent image (Bun 1.4.0): 6 pass.
  - macOS: 5 pass, 1 skip (the real hot-journal test).
  - Linux, with `SQLITE_READONLY_ROLLBACK` removed from `MID_WRITE_ERRORS`: 3 fail, including the real hot-journal test.
  - With the set emptied: the two synthetic retry tests and the deadline test fail.
- `cd container/agent-runner && bun test` → 610 pass, 4 skip, 0 fail (macOS; the extra skip is the hot-journal test). `bun run typecheck` and `pnpm exec tsc -p container/agent-runner/tsconfig.json --noEmit` are clean.
- Same suite on Linux in the agent image (Bun 1.4.0): 613 tests, 610 pass, 3 skip, 0 fail.
- `pnpm exec tsx scripts/test-registry-skills.ts --pre-contract-providers` at this head → `PASS: new core with pre-contract provider payloads`. As a control, at a head that removed `getInboundDb()` it fails with `SyntaxError: Export named 'getInboundDb' not found`, matching CI.
- Lock visibility: the host held `BEGIN EXCLUSIVE` on a bind-mounted DB. The container (Bun 1.4.0, SQLite 3.53.2, Docker Desktop 29.8.2, macOS) still took `BEGIN EXCLUSIVE` with `busy_timeout=0`. A second host process got `SQLITE_BUSY`.
- Side by side, same host writer: a better-sqlite3 open → insert → close loop with `journal_mode=DELETE`, as in `src/mailbox/sqlite/session-db.ts`, at 20 writes/s for 3 minutes. Two container readers in the agent image polled every 500 ms:
  - Old read pattern: 20 failures in 686 reads.
  - Patched `readInbound` (real module, mounted): 0 in 352. Slowest read 31 ms.

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

A template create no longer fails when a group that has never run already holds the folder name.

- **Problem**: `createAgentFromTemplate` picked the folder by checking disk only. A group created by setup or a v1 migration gets its row before its folder, which first spawn makes. `agent_groups.folder` is UNIQUE, so a template create with the same name threw `UNIQUE constraint failed: agent_groups.folder`. Nothing partial was written.
- **Fix**: also check the row, using `groupFolderExistsOnDisk` for disk like the plain `create_agent` path and channel approval. A hit takes the existing random suffix.
- **Also**: the suffixed folder is validated. A long name that collided used to get a folder over the 63-character limit, so the group was created but could never spawn. It now fails before anything is written.
- **Reach**: every template create: `create_agent` from chat, `ncl groups create --template`, and setup's template step.

prs.body:
## Summary Setup's template library picker lists the library from its `index.json` instead of scanning for `plugin.json` files. - **Before**: picking "the public template library" shallow-cloned `nanocoai/nanoclaw-templates`, scanned the clone for `plugin.json`, and showed only folder names (`sdr`, `analyst`). - **Now**: the same single clone; the list comes from its `index.json` (kept in sync by that repo's CI), each entry shows its description, and the pick is copied out of the clone through `ensureTemplateLocal`, the path `create_agent` uses. - **Why still git, not a fetch of `index.json`**: setup's Node `fetch` ignores `HTTPS_PROXY`, git does not, so behind a proxy the picker keeps working. - **Unchanged**: local templates are still found by scanning `templates/`; an existing local copy is kept; failures warn and return to the menu as before. - **Removed**: `copyTemplate` in `src/templates/library.ts` has no caller left; forks use `ensureTemplateLocal`. ```mermaid --- config: look: neo --- flowchart LR subgraph before["Before"] direction TB b1["git clone
nanoclaw-templates"] -->|"scan for plugin.json"| b2["picker
folder names only: sdr, analyst"] b2 -->|"copy the pick"| b3["templates/"] end subgraph after["After"] direction TB a1["git clone
same single clone"] -->|"read index.json"| a2["picker
name + description"] a2 -->|"ensureTemplateLocal
from the same clone"| a3["templates/"] end before ~~~ after classDef same fill:#f6f8fa,stroke:#8c959f,stroke-width:1px,color:#1f2328 classDef new fill:#dafbe1,stroke:#1a7f37,stroke-width:1px,color:#1f2328 class b1,b2,b3,a1,a3 same class a2 new style before fill:none,stroke:#8c959f,stroke-dasharray:4 4,color:#57606a style after fill:none,stroke:#8c959f,stroke-dasharray:4 4,color:#57606a linkStyle 0,1,2,3 stroke:#8c959f,stroke-width:1px ``` ## Related work Stacked on #4112, which adds `src/templates/library.ts`. Merge that first. ## Change kind - [ ] `kind/bug` - [x] `kind/feature` - [ ] `kind/documentation` - [ ] `kind/cleanup` - [ ] `kind/hardening` ## Validation - `pnpm exec vitest run` -> 284 files, 3587 passed, 15 skipped (on this branch's tip) - `readTemplateIndex` and `ensureTemplateLocal` (with a reused clone) are covered by `src/templates/library.test.ts` - The picker's sequence minus the prompt, against the real library: one clone, 6 templates listed in 0.8 s, `sales/sdr` copied in 4 ms, clone removed; with `HTTPS_PROXY` at a dead proxy the clone fails, so the proxy is honored - `setup/` is not in CI's typecheck; a scratch `tsc` over `setup/auto.ts` shows the same 26 existing errors on `main`, #4112 and this branch, none new - The interactive wizard (`bash nanoclaw.sh`) run by hand on a local install: the library picker installed `sales/sdr` - [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not) ## User and release impact - [ ] No user-visible behavior change - [ ] User-visible change — release note below - [x] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback ```release-note Setup's template library list now shows what each template does. Breaking for forks that point setup at their own template library or call `copyTemplate`: - Detect: choosing the template library in setup stops with "Could not load the template library." followed by "The template library has no index.json" or "The template library index has a format this NanoClaw does not read"; fork code calling `copyTemplate` from `src/templates/library.ts` stops compiling. - Why: setup lists the library from its `index.json` instead of scanning the clone for `plugin.json` files, and copies the pick with `ensureTemplateLocal`, the path `create_agent` uses. - Fix: add an `index.json` at the library's root in the same shape as `nanocoai/nanoclaw-templates`: `{ "schema": 1, "categories": { "": [{ "ref": "", "name": "...", "description": "..." }] } }`; call `ensureTemplateLocal` instead of `copyTemplate`. - Rollback: revert this release. ``` ## Security and trust boundaries None new: the same single clone of the same repo as before. ## AI assistance - [x] AI tools or agents helped produce this change - [x] A human has reviewed this PR and stands behind every change

prs.title: feat: create agents from templates in chat
prs.body:
## Summary Lets an agent create another agent from a template, from this machine or the public library, instead of writing the persona by hand. - **Before**: `create_agent({ name, instructions })` only made a blank agent; templates were reachable only from a terminal (`ncl groups create --template`) or setup. - **Now**: `create_agent({ name, template: "sales/sdr" })`, plus `ncl templates list` (this machine, no network) and `ncl templates list --registry` (the public library's `index.json`) so the agent can offer one. - **Fetch**: a template not on this machine is shallow-cloned from `nanocoai/nanoclaw-templates` into `templates/` after the permission check and before any DB write. A local copy always wins. - **Approval**: same `agents.create` rule as today (`cli_scope: global` creates directly, anything else waits for an admin). The hold stores the template, the grant is bound to it, and the card says whether approving downloads it. - **Provider**: the child runs on its creator's provider, like a plain create. - **Slack**: the `slack-agent-flow` wrapper keeps the template through its own hold, names it in the success text, seeds the bot's avatar from the template's description and reports the ref to the provisioning service. - **Library content is data**: the clone runs with `core.symlinks=false` and Git LFS skipped; every copy goes through the hardened plugin copier with a real-path check, and a fetched template must parse before it becomes the local copy. - **Delivery stays responsive**: `ncl templates list --registry` runs inside the host's delivery loop, so the index (or its failure) is memoized for five minutes. - **Moved**: the library code setup used (`cloneRegistry`, `listTemplatesFromDir`, `copyTemplate`) moves from `setup/templates.ts` to `src/templates/library.ts`, so setup and agents share one copy. Setup behaves the same. - **Breaking for forks**: see the release note. ```mermaid --- config: look: neo --- flowchart LR subgraph before["Before"] direction TB b1["agent
writes the persona by hand"] -->|"create_agent
name, instructions"| b2["blank agent
no skills, no MCP servers"] end subgraph after["After"] direction TB a0["agent
ncl templates list
local or --registry"] -->|"user picks sales/sdr
create_agent name, template"| a1{"agents.create
same rule as today"} a1 -->|"group scope: hold"| a2["admin card
names the template
grant bound to it"] a1 -->|"global scope"| a3 a2 -->|"approve"| a3["template local?
else clone into templates/"] a3 -->|"fails"| a5["nothing created"] a3 -->|"stamp"| a4["new agent from the template
parent's provider, wired both ways"] end before ~~~ after classDef same fill:#f6f8fa,stroke:#8c959f,stroke-width:1px,color:#1f2328 classDef new fill:#dafbe1,stroke:#1a7f37,stroke-width:1px,color:#1f2328 classDef gate fill:#fff8c5,stroke:#9a6700,stroke-width:1px,color:#1f2328 classDef stop fill:#ffebe9,stroke:#cf222e,stroke-width:1px,color:#1f2328 class b1,b2,a0 same class a3,a4 new class a1,a2 gate class a5 stop style before fill:none,stroke:#8c959f,stroke-dasharray:4 4,color:#57606a style after fill:none,stroke:#8c959f,stroke-dasharray:4 4,color:#57606a linkStyle 0,1,2,3,4,5,6 stroke:#8c959f,stroke-width:1px ``` ## Related work Replaces nanocoai/nanoclaw#3396 and nanocoai/nanoclaw#3428 (closed as stale). The Slack half no longer needs its own PR on `channels`: `slack-agent-flow` lives on `main` now. ## Change kind - [ ] `kind/bug` - [x] `kind/feature` - [ ] `kind/documentation` - [ ] `kind/cleanup` - [ ] `kind/hardening` ## Validation - `pnpm exec vitest run` -> 284 files, 3587 passed, 15 skipped (on the stacked tip) - `cd container/agent-runner && bun run test` -> 603 passed, 3 skipped - `tsc --noEmit` (host and container), `pnpm run format:check` -> clean - New tests: `src/templates/registry.test.ts`, `src/cli/resources/templates.test.ts`, the template cases in `src/modules/agent-to-agent/create-agent.test.ts`, `container/agent-runner/src/mcp-tools/agents.test.ts` - Slack: `slack-agent-flow` applied to a scratch tree, `vitest run src/modules/slack-agent-flow` -> 72 passed, including two new template cases (`provision.congruence.test.ts` needs the provisioning module from another branch and was left out) - Real network, real host code (container start stubbed): a group-scoped agent listed the 6 library templates (0.2 s); a trusted agent created an agent from `sales/sdr` it did not have (clone + stamp, 0.9 s), on its parent's provider; a second create used the local copy (9 ms); `sales/nope` created nothing - Hardening: a library template with a symlink, a symlinked parent folder, a manifest read through a symlink, a template that does not parse, and a burst of `--registry` calls against a blocked network each have a test (`src/templates/library.test.ts`, `src/cli/resources/templates.test.ts`) - Real network again after the hardening: same create from `sales/sdr`, clone with `core.symlinks=false` and LFS skipped, library commit logged - Merge #4112 and #4113 together: at #4112 alone, setup's picker still copies straight into `templates/`; #4113 moves it onto the staged path - Not run: the full chat journey in a running install (agent in a container, Slack bot provisioning) - [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not) ## User and release impact - [ ] No user-visible behavior change - [ ] User-visible change — release note below - [x] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback ```release-note Agents can create other agents from templates: ask for one in chat, pick from `ncl templates list` or the public library, and the agent builds it. Breaking for forks and hand-made templates: - Detect: a new folder under `templates/` no longer shows in `git status`; fork code importing `cloneRegistry`, `listTemplatesFromDir`, `copyTemplate` or `DEFAULT_TEMPLATES_SOURCE` from `setup/templates.ts` stops compiling; a fork that edits the `GROUP_SCOPE_RESOURCES` line or the stamper's `ensureContainerConfig` line no longer matches. - Why: templates fetched by setup or `create_agent` are install state and must not block `/update-nanoclaw`; the library code is shared by setup and agents in `src/templates/library.ts`, and `cloneRegistry` is async because the host runs it. - Fix: keep a hand-made template in git with `git add -f templates/`; import `cloneRegistry`, `listTemplatesFromDir` and `copyTemplate` from `src/templates/library.ts` and `await cloneRegistry()`; `DEFAULT_TEMPLATES_SOURCE` is gone: the library's address is now the `LIBRARY_REPO` constant in `src/templates/library.ts`, so a fork that changed it makes the same edit there; re-anchor fork edits on the new lines. - Rollback: revert this release; templates already in `templates/` stay in place, but `templates/` is no longer ignored, so fetched ones show as untracked in `git status`: delete them, or `git add` the ones to keep. ``` ## Security and trust boundaries - The ref comes from the container (untrusted). The precheck accepts only plain `/`-separated segments, so it cannot leave the templates directory; nothing is read or fetched before that check and the permission decision. - The library URL is fixed; nothing the agent typed is sent anywhere. - No new permission: a template create is still `agents.create`. The grant now covers name and template, so an approval for a plain create (or another template) never runs a templated one. - A trusted (`cli_scope: global`) agent can pull a library template without an admin, the same trust setup has for the operator. - `ncl templates list` is read-only and added to the `cli_scope: group` allow-list; its library index is memoized, so repeated calls cannot stall delivery. - Library content never reaches outside the clone: no symlinks on checkout, no Git LFS, copies only through `copyPluginDir` after a real-path check, and listings never read a manifest through a symlink. ## Skill delivery - [ ] Not a skill - [x] Skill: apply/remove footprint and fresh-clone verification are described above ## AI assistance - [x] AI tools or agents helped produce this change - [x] A human has reviewed this PR and stands behind every change

prs.title: fix(cross-session-context): the agent's own replies from other threads read as "you"
prs.body:
## What and why In a DM or channel where each thread has its own session, the agent's reply in one thread is copied into its other live threads as context. The copy was signed with the agent group's name, so in thread B the agent saw `sender="Pixel"` and took its own earlier reply for a second agent's. History rows already show the agent's own posts as `sender="you"`, through a `self` flag that backfill writes. The copies now carry the same flag. ## How it works ```mermaid --- config: look: neo --- flowchart LR subgraph before["Before"] direction TB b1["Thread A
Pixel replies to Alex"] b2["fanOutbound
copy: sender Pixel"] b3["formatEchoMessage
sender=#quot;Pixel#quot;"] b4["Pixel in thread B
another agent said this"] b1 -->|delivered| b2 -->|"writes to thread B"| b3 -->|renders| b4 end subgraph after["After"] direction TB a1["Thread A
Pixel replies to Alex"] a2["fanOutbound
copy: sender Pixel
+ self: true"] a3["formatEchoMessage
self → sender=#quot;you#quot;"] a4["Pixel in thread B
I said this in another thread"] a1 -->|delivered| a2 -->|"writes to thread B"| a3 -->|renders| a4 end before ~~~ after classDef req fill:#ddf4ff,stroke:#54aeff,color:#0a3069 classDef step fill:#f6f8fa,stroke:#8c959f,color:#24292f classDef bad fill:#ffebe9,stroke:#ff8182,color:#82071e classDef good fill:#dafbe1,stroke:#4ac26b,color:#116329 classDef new fill:#fff8c5,stroke:#d4a72c,color:#4d2d00 class b1,a1 req class b2,b3 step class b4 bad class a2,a3 new class a4 good style before fill:none,stroke:#8c959f,stroke-dasharray:4 4,color:#57606a style after fill:none,stroke:#8c959f,stroke-dasharray:4 4,color:#57606a linkStyle default stroke:#8c959f ``` - `fanOutbound` copies the agent's own delivered messages, and now passes `self: true`. `fanEcho` writes the flag into the copy. Copies of people's messages never carry it. - `formatEchoMessage` uses one rule for history rows and copies: a row with `self` renders `sender="you"`. The history branch's own copy of that rule is removed. - The system prompt said a copy's `from` tells the agent which kind it is. For a reply from a sibling thread it doesn't (`from="another conversation in #pixel-room room"`), so the sentence now says `sender="you"` marks the agent's own. - Copies the agent posts into a conversation from a scheduled task, or from another conversation, get `sender="you"` too. Their labels already say "posted by your scheduled task" and "posted by you from another conversation". ## Tested - Real host and runner code against the same mailbox file, locally: `fanInboundMessage` and `fanOutboundMessage` wrote into thread B's `inbound.db` for a channel with two thread sessions, and the runner's `formatMessages` read that file. - On `main`: `Here is the summary: launch moved to Tuesday.`. - On this branch: the same line with `sender="you"`. The person's message keeps `sender="Alex"`. - `fan.test.ts`: the agent's outbound copy carries `self: true` and a person's copy does not. - `cross-session-echo.test.ts`: a copy from a sibling thread with `self` renders `sender="you"`, and a history row with `self` still does. - `destinations.test.ts`: the reading section names `sender="you"`. - Each test fails when its change is reverted. Dropping the moved rule fails both formatter tests. Writing `self` on every copy fails the person's-copy test. - `pnpm run format:check`, `tsc` for host and runner, and `bun run test` (603 pass) all pass. `vitest run`: 3544 pass. 5 tests in `scripts/update/` timed out at 5 s in the parallel run; on their own they pass (45/45), and they touch none of these files. - Reviewed by a second agent. ## Not done - Not run in a live Slack workspace. ## AI assistance - [x] AI tools or agents helped produce this change - [x] A human has reviewed this PR and stands behind every change

prs.title: feat: add Sendblue iMessage and SMS extension
prs.body:
## Summary

- Add a bundled Sendblue extension for direct iMessage/SMS: phone pairing, authenticated receive webhooks, terminal replies, and stored DM targets through the existing host lifecycle and conversation path.
- Keep both Sendblue API credentials in host custody. Add declarative, bounded additional credential headers to channel egress; reject adapter-supplied credential headers and fail closed before network I/O when a required secret is missing.
- Document fresh free-account verification, model setup, encrypted configuration, HTTPS webhook registration, phone pairing, a two-turn handset smoke test, and removal. Text only; groups and media downloads are excluded. Ambiguous non-idempotent sends are not automatically replayed.

## Change Type

- [x] New feature
- [x] Documentation
- [x] Security
- [x] Dependencies (new workspace package; existing tracing/tracing-test dependencies reused)

## Linked Issue

Feature proposal: #8130. **Maintainer approval is pending** for the first-party extension and generic multi-header credential contract; this link does not claim an approved feature issue.

## Validation

The local integration uses the real production host, encrypted credentials, phone pairing, ingress, durable turn/delivery path, and model decorators, with a scripted model SDK and recording vendor transport. **No live Sendblue account, carrier, handset, or paid model was exercised.**

- [x] Full-workspace Clippy with all targets/features and warnings denied
- [ ] Manual handset/browser testing
- [ ] `pr-shepherd` / independent human review

See the test evidence below for commands and results. These unchecked items are not claimed complete.

## Test Strategy

User behavior: after verifying a free Sendblue account, configuring the extension, and pairing an allowed phone, a text reaches the normal agent path and its final answer returns to that phone.

Risk areas:
- [x] Side effect
- [x] Security or permissions
- [x] External provider
- [x] Cross-component behavior
- [ ] Model behavior (no tool-choice change)
- [ ] Browser (existing generic configuration UI)
- [ ] Persistence (existing host stores; no schema change)

Tests added or updated:
- Unit or contract: additional header validation/projection, host-owned header rejection, missing-secret fail-closed behavior, actual host header injection; shared channel conformance; sender/line/event admission; Unicode splitting; rejected/ambiguous acceptance; partial-reply checkpoint recovery without duplicate POSTs.
- Reborn integration: `sendblue_phone_pairing_and_text_reply_use_the_production_host` in the existing extension-delivery harness. Asserts phone binding, bad-secret rejection, normal turn/reply, both wire credentials, no raw credential values in the model transcript, and replay suppression.
- Recorded fixture: not applicable; deterministic SDK-seam script covers transport behavior, not model tool selection.
- Browser E2E: not run; no frontend implementation changes. The generic form still needs a manual setup pass.
- Backend or runtime: production assembly with LibSQL. PostgreSQL was not exercised; no database implementation/query/schema changes.
- Live canary: not run; the README includes the required two-turn handset procedure.

What the tests prove: local admission, pairing, orchestration, credential mediation, provider request shape, and conservative recovery. Provider acceptance is not delivery to a handset. A crash between provider acceptance and host checkpoint persistence can still leave an uncertain outcome.

Current head: `fe0bd7e7ed5ed9f8b999bc43f831642977210dca`. Review follow-up to `e6f8d975386e713256c7d603c05393aa1a0a3955`:

- A package-owned `sendblue_surfaces()` constructor now supplies native activation, host assembly and the test harness.
- Provider `QUEUED` returns an ambiguous outcome: the host stores it as unknown, stops subsequent chunks, and does not automatically replay it. `SENT`/`DELIVERED`/`READ` retain the existing successful outcome.
- Malformed and unsupported checkpoints fail closed with distinct safe reasons. Debug diagnostics retain the JSON error category/location or unsupported version, without logging checkpoint content or serde's potentially sensitive Display string.
- New queued/checkpoint regressions failed against the old behavior before the fix. Existing successful delivery fixtures now use `SENT`; a dedicated `QUEUED` regression verifies the corrected contract.

Validation at this head:

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `scripts/pre-commit-safety.sh` — passed.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` — passed (local macOS rust-objcopy/linker warnings were emitted by a build script).
- `cargo test -p ironclaw_sendblue_extension --test channel_conformance` — **7 passed**. Includes queued partial replies, replay suppression, invalid checkpoint versions and syntax/type failures with captured logs proving the private payload is absent.
- `RUST_MIN_STACK=8388608 cargo test -p ironclaw_integration_tests --test reborn_integration_extension_delivery sendblue_phone_pairing_and_text_reply_use_the_production_host` — **1 passed**. Real production host and LibSQL, scripted model/vendor; durable queued state stays unknown and duplicate callbacks issue no second POST. The stack setting matches the repository's integration coverage policy. macOS emitted linker warnings; the test completed.
- `cargo test -p ironclaw --bin ironclaw runtime::native_extensions::tests` — **4 passed**.
- `cargo test -p ironclaw_architecture_tests --no-fail-fast` — **323 passed, 0 failed** across the complete suite.

Earlier implementation checks at `fbf284285c40946a1158de2ee45373a48f3e26a4`: extension/contracts unit and integration tests **197 passed**; host egress **25 passed**; registry and product ingestion **72 passed**. These broader contract results are historical, not reruns at the current head. The current follow-up changes the Sendblue adapter, shared registration constructor and tests, not the generic credential contract.

The new multi-header contract test was first run red against the old schema (`unknown field header_credentials`).

## Security Impact

Adds a 64 KiB shared-secret webhook and egress restricted to HTTPS `api.sendblue.com/api/send-message`. Empty sender allowlists deny all; wildcard is explicit and still requires host phone pairing. The adapter receives secret handles, never raw secrets. Additional header declarations are limited to eight, must reference declared secret admin fields, cannot collide with primary/transport headers, and are injected only alongside the requested primary credential. No arbitrary media URL is fetched. Existing model permission and approval paths remain in control.

## Reborn Trust-Boundary Checklist

- [x] Public policy types: declarative `ChannelHeaderCredentialDescriptor` is validated by the contract/registry and resolved by host policy; the adapter cannot construct injected wire credentials.
- [x] Inbound text reaches prompts through the existing normalized message/product/turn path.
- [x] No new hash-based authority or authenticity mechanism; webhook authentication uses the host shared-secret verifier.
- [x] No new status/error enum variants; existing delivery outcomes remain terminal on ambiguous sends.
- [x] `header_credentials` defaults empty, preserving old manifests; missing declared values block transport.
- [x] Webhook/request/response/handle/header/checkpoint bounds are explicit; provider-reference evidence is capped to fit the checkpoint.
- [x] Stable unauthorized/permanent/ambiguous outcomes; no implicit resend after uncertain acceptance.
- [x] First-party native adapter still uses host-restricted egress and existing trust activation.

## Database Impact

None: no migrations, schema changes, SQL, or backend-specific storage code. Existing host persistence owns identity, conversation, replay protection, and delivery state.

## Blast Radius

New package, package inventory, and shipping binary registration; shared channel contracts/registry/egress add optional additional credential headers. Old manifests retain their previous shape. The CLI dependency inventory explicitly adds this concrete package because the binary owns native extension bindings; generic composition remains vendor-neutral. The extension-specificity gate also lists Sendblue alongside Slack and Telegram as concrete extension code; the generic-code vendor allowlist is unchanged.

The cross-crate asset include inventory grows **17 → 18** for the package-owned manifest embed, following the existing bundled package pattern. This deliberately records one more instance of the existing asset-ownership debt tracked by #7093; it does not claim to resolve that debt or relax the include scanner generally.

## Rollback Plan

Deactivate/uninstall Sendblue, remove only this deployment's Sendblue webhook and public route, and clear its admin credentials if no longer needed. Revert this commit to remove the package and optional credential extension. No migration rollback or history deletion is required.

## Review Follow-Through

Ready for maintainer review. Approval of proposal #8130, independent review of the generic credential extension and asset inventory amendment, and live account/browser/handset proof remain outstanding. The integration is text-only; outbound provider status is acceptance evidence, not carrier delivery evidence.

**Review track**: C (security/runtime)

Updates `tower-http` from 0.7.0 to 0.7.1
Release notes

Sourced from tower-http's releases.

tower-http-0.7.1

Added

  • fs: add ServeDir::redirect_to_trailing_slash() to serve directory indexes directly instead of first redirecting to the trailing-slash path. The redirect remains the default (#728)
  • fs: add ignore_multi_range_requests() to ServeDir and ServeFile, serving the full representation when a request asks for multiple byte ranges. The existing 416 Range Not Satisfiable response remains the default (#727)
  • request-id: the constructors and accessors on the request-id layers, services, and RequestId are now const fn, so they can be used in const context (#716)

Changed

  • fs: the minimum http-range-header requirement is now 0.4.2 (#661)

Fixed

  • behavioral change: fs: make ServeDir::try_call propagate expected filesystem I/O errors when no fallback is configured, as documented, instead of converting them to 404 Not Found responses (#718)
  • decompression: don't end the body when a data frame with no remaining bytes arrives after the decompressor reports end-of-stream. Trailers following such a frame were dropped and could not be recovered (#722)
  • decompression: return a body error when a data frame with remaining bytes arrives after the decompressor reports end-of-stream, rather than silently truncating. This regressed in 0.7.0 (#712)
  • fs: multipart range requests are now rejected before range validation, so they consistently return 416 Range Not Satisfiable with a Cannot serve multipart range requests body instead of a generic unsatisfiable-range response (#661)
  • fs: range error responses no longer carry representation headers such as Content-Type and Content-Encoding (#727)
  • set-header: SetMultipleResponseHeadersLayer and SetMultipleResponseHeader are now Clone regardless of the response body type, matching the fix applied to the request-side types in 0.7.0 (#714)

Updates `quick-xml` from 0.41.0 to 0.42.0
Release notes

Sourced from quick-xml's releases.

v0.42.0 - String Ergonomics

What's Changed

0.42.0 -- 2026-08-22

This is a large release. The primary change is an ergonomic improvement across the entire API - quick_xml now makes use of &str and String types where possible instead of &[u8] and Vec<u8>. This requires significant refactoring of downstream code, but should result in a net simplification as well as potential performance improvements, and opens up additional opportunities in future releases.

The MSRV has been raised to 1.86. We now use Rust 2024 Edition.

Breaking Changes

  • #963: Reader now validates that input is valid UTF-8 when constructing events. Non-UTF-8 input passed to Reader::from_reader() without DecodingReader will now produce Error::Encoding instead of silently passing through invalid bytes. Use DecodingReader to transcode non-UTF-8 sources.
  • #963: Name types (QName, LocalName, Prefix, Namespace, PrefixDeclaration) now wrap &str instead of &[u8]. into_inner() returns &str, and AsRef<str> is implemented (AsRef<[u8]> has been removed). ResolveResult::Unknown now contains String instead of Vec<u8>, and NamespaceError variants contain String instead of Vec<u8>.
  • #963: Removed the decoder: Decoder field from event types (BytesStart, BytesText, BytesCData, BytesRef) and Attributes. The decoder() method is no longer available on these types. Decode methods on events now always assume UTF-8 input. Error::missed_end() no longer takes a Decoder parameter.
  • #963: Event types (BytesStart, BytesEnd, BytesText, BytesCData, BytesPI, BytesRef) now store Cow<str> internally instead of Cow<[u8]>. into_inner() on BytesText, BytesCData, BytesPI, and BytesRef now returns Cow<str>. BytesStart::set_name() now takes &str instead of &[u8].
  • #963: All event types and the Event enum now implement Deref<Target = str> instead of Deref<Target = [u8]>. Explicit AsRef<str> impls are provided to avoid ambiguity.
  • #963: Removed decode() methods from BytesText, BytesCData, and BytesRef. Content is already available as &str via Deref. The xml10_content(), xml11_content(), xml_content(), and html_content() methods now return Cow<str> directly instead of Result<Cow<str>, EncodingError>.

Updates `tower-http` from 0.7.0 to 0.7.1
Release notes

Sourced from tower-http's releases.

tower-http-0.7.1

Added

  • fs: add ServeDir::redirect_to_trailing_slash() to serve directory indexes directly instead of first redirecting to the trailing-slash path. The redirect remains the default (#728)
  • fs: add ignore_multi_range_requests() to ServeDir and ServeFile, serving the full representation when a request asks for multiple byte ranges. The existing 416 Range Not Satisfiable response remains the default (#727)
  • request-id: the constructors and accessors on the request-id layers, services, and RequestId are now const fn, so they can be used in const context (#716)

Changed

  • fs: the minimum http-range-header requirement is now 0.4.2 (#661)

Fixed

  • behavioral change: fs: make ServeDir::try_call propagate expected filesystem I/O errors when no fallback is configured, as documented, instead of converting them to 404 Not Found responses (#718)
  • decompression: don't end the body when a data frame with no remaining bytes arrives after the decompressor reports end-of-stream. Trailers following such a frame were dropped and could not be recovered (#722)
  • decompression: return a body error when a data frame with remaining bytes arrives after the decompressor reports end-of-stream, rather than silently truncating. This regressed in 0.7.0 (#712)
  • fs: multipart range requests are now rejected before range validation, so they consistently return 416 Range Not Satisfiable with a Cannot serve multipart range requests body instead of a generic unsatisfiable-range response (#661)
  • fs: range error responses no longer carry representation headers such as Content-Type and Content-Encoding (#727)
  • set-header: SetMultipleResponseHeadersLayer and SetMultipleResponseHeader are now Clone regardless of the response body type, matching the fix applied to the request-side types in 0.7.0 (#714)

  • feat(request-id): Allow request-id constructor in const context by @​tottoto in tower-rs/tower-http#716
  • fs: Avoid unnecessary conversions between SystemTime and HttpDate by @​tottoto in tower-rs/tower-http#717
  • fs: Use HeaderValue::is_empty to check for empty values by @​tottoto in tower-rs/tower-http#720

prs.title: feat(openclaw): keep user overrides in openclaw.user.json across config syncs
prs.body:
## Summary
LobsterAI regenerates `openclaw.json` on every config sync, so users who hand-edit it (e.g. to enable enhancement plugins or tweak OpenClaw options) lose their changes on restart. Instead of a "protection" switch that freezes the file — which would stop model, IM, MCP, skill and agent changes from reaching the gateway and can break startup when ports or plugin paths change — this adds a persistent user override layer: `openclaw.user.json` next to `openclaw.json` is merged on top of every rendered config.

Merge order: LobsterAI-generated config → user overrides → enterprise config (enterprise still wins).

## Related Issue
User feedback: manual `openclaw.json` edits are reset after restart; request for a protection toggle.

## Changes Made
- **Override layer** (`src/main/libs/openclawUserConfigOverlay.ts`): JSON5 file (comments, trailing commas), JSON Merge Patch semantics (objects merge, arrays replace, `null` removes). `plugins.allow` / `plugins.load.paths` are unioned so users can't drop bundled plugins; `plugins.allow` stays sorted so repeated syncs are stable.
- **Protected paths** are ignored and reported: `gateway.auth/mode/port`, `meta`, `agents.defaults.sessionStore`, `plugins.installs`, `plugins.slots.memory`, LobsterAI-internal plugin entries, and `$include` anywhere.
- **Removal works**: the renderer copies existing `gateway`, `plugins.entries` and unknown top-level keys back from the file, so a deleted override would otherwise linger. The paths each sync applied are recorded (kv) and reverted from the base before the next render, only where the value is still what was applied. `createOpenClawConfigTarget` gains an optional merge base / extra owned sections; `baseRaw` stays the real file so the rebase propagates removals.
- **Fail-safe**: a syntax error keeps the last valid overrides. If OpenClaw rejects the config (`config.apply` → `Rejected`, or startup "Invalid config"), overrides are suspended and the config is retried without them (the gateway is restarted once on startup failure); if it still fails, overrides are restored and not blamed again. Quick Repair also suspends overrides until the user applies them again.
- **Settings card** in Agent Engine → 运行维护: enable toggle, state (missing / active / parse error / suspended / disabled), overridden and ignored paths, OpenClaw's rejection detail, Open File / Show in Folder / Apply. zh + en strings.
- **IPC**: `openclaw:userConfig:*` (constants in `src/shared/openclawUserConfig/constants.ts`), handlers in `src/main/ipcHandlers/openclawUserConfig/handlers.ts`, exposed as `window.electron.openclaw.userConfig`.
- `json5` added as a runtime dependency (was dev-only transitively). It's imported as `json5/lib/parse` because the package's ESM entry has only a default export, which broke the Vite-bundled main process with a named import.

## Type of Change
- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Code refactoring
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Performance improvement
- [ ] Other (please describe):

## Testing
- [x] Tested locally
- [x] Added new tests
- [x] Updated existing tests
- [x] Manual testing performed

- `npm test`: 689 files / 7439 tests pass. New: `openclawUserConfigOverlay.test.ts` (19), two `OpenClawConfigSync` runtime tests through the real renderer (apply → steady state reports `changed: false` → removal → steady again; minimal no-model path), one `openclawConfigTarget` test.
- ESLint (CI command) clean on all touched files; `tsc --noEmit` for renderer and `electron-tsconfig.json` pass; `compile:electron` passes.
- End-to-end in `electron:dev` on an isolated profile (`LOBSTERAI_DEV_USER_DATA_DIR`), driven via CDP, both logged out and logged in (lobsterai-server provider): template creation, apply, survives restart, coexists with a managed setting change in the same `agents` section, removal across `agents` / `plugins.entries` / `gateway`, protected paths ignored, syntax error keeps last valid overrides, invalid key rejected while running (engine stays up), invalid key at cold start (gateway auto-restarts without overrides), toggle off/on, Quick Repair suspend + reapply, file deletion.

## Screenshots (if applicable)
Not attached. The card was checked in the dev app (dark theme) in active, ignored-paths, parse-error and suspended states.

## Checklist
- [x] My code follows the project's style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my code
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

## Electron-Specific Changes
- [x] Changes to main process (src/main/)
- [x] Changes to preload script (src/main/preload.ts)
- [x] Changes to IPC communication
- [ ] Changes to window management
- [ ] None

**OpenClaw config / restart behavior:** with no `openclaw.user.json` (the default), the rendered config is unchanged. With overrides, they become part of the target `OpenClawConfigSync` renders, so the existing change detection, `config.apply` delivery and restart decisions apply to them. New automatic restart: only after a gateway startup failure caused by the overrides (one attempt without them).

## Additional Notes
- This branch was cut from `release/2026.10.19`, so against `main` the diff also shows the two commits of #2892 (kit catalog recovery) that are not on `main` yet. The override feature itself is commit `ad8a3009`.
- Suspension is all-or-nothing: one invalid key withholds the whole file until it changes or the user clicks Apply Again; the card lists the paths and OpenClaw's error.
- Local dev note: a runtime built before the 2026-10-16 preset context-window patches rejects LobsterAI's own config after login (`contextWindowDefault` unrecognized). That's unrelated to this PR; `npm run openclaw:runtime:host` fixes it.

prs.title: feat(providers): support OpenAI Responses and Gemini formats for custom providers
prs.body:
## Summary

Custom model providers can now use the **OpenAI Responses** and native **Gemini (generateContent)** API formats, on top of OpenAI Chat Completions and Anthropic. Both reuse OpenClaw's native transports instead of adding LobsterAI-side protocol code.

- **Settings UI:** the API format radio buttons become one dropdown. Custom providers list OpenAI Chat Completions, Anthropic, OpenAI Responses and Gemini; built-in providers keep Chat Completions and Anthropic only.
- **Storage:** Responses is a sub-mode, `ProviderConfig.openaiApiMode`, stored next to `apiFormat: 'openai'`. Older builds therefore fall back to Chat Completions. Gemini is stored as `apiFormat: 'gemini'` on custom providers only.
- **OpenClaw config sync:** Responses mode maps to the `openai-responses` transport (a pasted `/responses` suffix is stripped). Custom Gemini maps to `google-generative-ai`, with a versioned base URL that keeps relay path prefixes and adds `/v1beta` when no version is given.
- **Other callers follow the same choice:** the connection test (native `generateContent` probe for Gemini) and provider export/import, plus the compat proxy, legacy chat path and native Gemini clients for titles and quick answers.

### Why built-in providers don't get Responses yet

Several OpenClaw provider plugins are tuned for Chat Completions:

- The DeepSeek V4 and Xiaomi MiMo thinking wrappers inject Chat Completions fields regardless of transport. This is still true upstream in v2026.10.4.
- Moonshot's Kimi K3 runtime profile requires Chat Completions.
- Volcengine Ark rejects unknown Responses fields.

So the option is limited to custom providers for now.

## Electron-specific behavior

- **OpenClaw config:** changes only for custom providers set to Responses or Gemini. The gateway picks the new transport up through the normal config sync.
- **Provider export:** writes `openaiApiMode` only when it is Responses, so default exports stay importable by older builds with the strict schema.
- **Renderer config normalization:** keeps `apiFormat: 'gemini'` on custom providers. It used to coerce unknown formats to Anthropic.

## Testing

- `npm test`, CI eslint on touched files, `npm run compile:electron` and `npm run build` pass.
- Not yet checked in `npm run electron:dev`: the new dropdown, a Responses or Gemini custom provider (connection test and chat), and that built-in providers show only two options. No screenshots yet.

prs.title: refactor(cowork): remove the OpenAI compatibility proxy
prs.body:
> Stacked on netease-youdao/LobsterAI#2897. Review that one first; once it merges, I'll change this PR's base to `release/2026.10.19`.

## Summary

Removes the Claude Agent SDK-era **OpenAI compatibility proxy** (`coworkOpenAICompatProxy.ts` and `coworkFormatTransform.ts`, about 3500 lines). It translated Anthropic `/v1/messages` to OpenAI Chat Completions or Responses. The agent runtime is OpenClaw now, so only two live users were left, and both get a smaller replacement. Design doc: `specs/refactors/remove-cowork-compat-proxy/2026-10-17-remove-cowork-compat-proxy-design.md`.

Commits, in order:

1. **Delete dead code:** `getEnhancedEnv`, the model probe, `get-api-config` / `save-api-config` IPC and `api-config.json`, the Claude SDK telemetry and count-tokens routes, and the unused passthrough route.
2. **`copilotLoopbackProxy.ts`:** the Copilot passthrough that OpenClaw's `lobsterai-copilot` provider uses, moved out unchanged. It keeps the same path, port key, `LOBSTER_PROXY_TOKEN` auth and 401/403 refresh-and-retry, so `openclaw.json` does not change and no gateway restart follows the upgrade.
3. **`oneShotModelClient.ts`:** sessionless streamed text calls. It resolves the model through the same `buildProviderSelection()` that renders `openclaw.json`, so its transport and endpoint always match the agent runtime. It supports Anthropic, Chat Completions, Responses and Gemini, and the loopback token routes server models and Copilot like OpenClaw does.
4. **Callers moved off the proxy:**
   - Desktop companion quick answers use the one-shot client.
   - `check-api-config` uses the raw config. An OpenAI-format model is no longer reported as "no model" when the proxy fails to start, and the response no longer carries API keys to the renderer.
5. **Delete the proxy and what only it used:** `resolveCurrentApiConfig`, the server token refresher and `setCoworkProxySessionId`.
6. **IM cleanup:**
   - Removed the dead `IMChatHandler`, the scheduled-task LLM detector, the `processMessage` path of `IMCoworkHandler`, and helpers and i18n keys only those used.
   - Removed the unused `skillsEnabled` and `systemPrompt` IM settings.
   - Per-message IM logs moved to debug.

Net change: about 7000 lines removed.

## Electron-specific behavior

- **Startup:** the compat proxy no longer starts. The Copilot loopback proxy starts in its place, before the first config sync, on the same remembered port.
- **Quick answers:**
  - They now call the upstream directly, or go through the token proxy or the Copilot passthrough, like OpenClaw does.
  - Responses-mode and custom Gemini providers now work.
  - ChatGPT OAuth and other OAuth providers whose credential isn't in the rendered config now show an explicit "not supported" message. They didn't work through the proxy either.
- **`check-api-config` IPC:** returns `{ hasConfig, error }`.
- **IM plugin approvals:** the 60 s auto-deny for channel plugin approvals is kept unchanged.

## Testing

- `npm test` passes. One known-flaky watcher test fails occasionally and passes on rerun.
- CI eslint on touched files, `npm run compile:electron` and `npm run build` pass, and the legacy IM `node:test` suites pass.
- New unit tests cover the Copilot proxy (auth, host check, retry, streaming), the one-shot client (four transports, token placeholders, unsupported routes), the new SSE readers and quick answer integration.
- Not yet checked in `npm run electron:dev`:
  - Copilot chat across a token refresh, with no gateway restart and an unchanged `openclaw.json`
  - quick answers on Anthropic, Chat Completions, Responses, Gemini, server and Copilot models
  - an IM channel round trip with reminder relay

prs.title: fix(openclaw): bound disk usage of repair backups and runtime caches
prs.body:
## Summary

A long-running install reached ~17G under `~/Library/Application Support/LobsterAI`. Most of it came from OpenClaw data that only grows and is never cleaned up. End users hit the same sources, so this PR bounds each one from the LobsterAI side, without an OpenClaw patch.

| Source | Observed | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `openclaw/repair-backups` | 8.2G (2 runs) | Snapshots skip regenerable caches. At most 2 runs are kept, none older than 14 days; the current run is always kept. Pruning runs after each repair and in the background cleanup, and caches are stripped from retained older runs. |
| `state/.compile-cache` | 1.0G | Subdirectories left by other Node/Electron versions are removed. |
| Agent browser caches | 1.6G + 0.9G (`~/Library/Caches`) | The HTTP cache is capped via `--disk-cache-size` in `browser.extraArgs`. Once a day, if no Chrome holds the profile and its caches exceed 512 MiB, `Cache`, `Code Cache`, `GPUCache` and `Service Worker` are cleared. Cookies, Local Storage, IndexedDB and Login Data are never touched. |
| `agents/*/sessions/sessions.json.*.tmp` | 249M | Orphaned files older than 7 days are removed, matching OpenClaw's own temp file name pattern. |
| `*.jsonl.deleted.*` / `*.reset.*` archives | 50M | `session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetention` is set to `30d`, so OpenClaw expires both the files and their `session_transcript_archives` rows. |
| `agents/*/session-sqlite-import-archive` | ~1G | Removed 14 days after the last clean session→SQLite migration. Archives are kept while the newest migration run is in flight, failed or unreadable, since `doctor --session-sqlite recover` may need them. LobsterAI itself only runs `import`. |

### Cleanup timing and pacing

All cleanups live in `openclawStartupDiskCleanup.ts`. A first pass after an upgrade can delete several hundred thousand files; on the reporter's machine the old snapshots' compile caches alone held ~266k. To keep that off low-end machines' disks:

- **Deferred:** a pass starts 60s after the gateway reports `running`. Gateway restarts inside the window share one pending pass, and timers are `unref`'d.
- **Paced:** `openclawDiskCleanupThrottle.ts` runs deletions in 20ms work slices with 80ms rests (about 20% duty cycle). Steps run one at a time, cheapest per byte first: session temps, import archives, browser caches, repair backups, compile cache.
- **Bounded:** each pass stops after 5 minutes of wall time. A stopped pass retries after 30 minutes and on the next app start.
- **Battery:** the pass is skipped on battery power (`powerMonitor.isOnBatteryPower()`), and a running pass stops at its next rest once the laptop switches to battery.
- **Resumable:** every step is idempotent. Repair backup runs and import archives are renamed aside (`.lobsterai-stale-*`) before deletion, so a partly removed one is finished later and is never mistaken for an in-progress repair or a recently modified archive. The post-repair prune is paced the same way.

Measured on an M1 with 100k small files: unpaced deletion ran at ~9.7k files/s using a full core; paced deletion runs at ~1.1k files/s using ~0.2 of a core, with main-process event-loop lag ≤ 8ms. One pass can therefore delete roughly 330k files there; slower disks take more passes.

Every step is best-effort, logs its own failures, and never follows symlinks or Windows junctions. A repair backup run modified in the last hour is never touched.

## Behavior changes to note

- **OpenClaw config:** `openclaw.json` gains `--disk-cache-size` in `browser.extraArgs` and `session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetention: "30d"`. The first config sync after an upgrade may restart the gateway once.
- **History:** LobsterAI's visible chat history is in `lobsterai.sqlite` and is unaffected. `chat.history` reads only the current transcript generation, never the `.deleted`/`.reset` archives.
- **Repair helper:** the snapshot exclusions take effect once the bundled `openclaw-gateway-repair.mjs` is rebuilt, which happens in the normal runtime build.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run src/main/libs/openclaw src/main/openclawSessionPolicy src/main/libs/removeTreeNoFollow`: 1226 passed
- [x] `npx eslint --ext ts,tsx --report-unused-disable-directives --max-warnings 0` on touched files
- [x] `npm run compile:electron`
- [ ] Manual check with `npm run electron:dev` on an existing profile: about 60s after the gateway is running (on AC power), the cleanup log lines appear, the agent browser keeps its logins, and one-click repair succeeds with a slimmer snapshot

prs.title: feat(desktop): add custom and animated GIF companion skins, screenshot tools and follow-ups
prs.body:
## Summary
Add portable desktop customization and interaction improvements while preserving LobsterAI's built-in skins and branding.

- **Custom companion skins:** upload PNG/JPEG/WebP or animated GIF, preview, save multiple named skins, switch, rename/delete, and restore the default. Static images support scale/position adjustments and normalize to 512×512 PNG. GIFs retain their original frames, timing, transparency, loop metadata and aspect ratio in previews and on the desktop; static crop controls are hidden for GIFs.
- **Cowork follow-up suggestions:** show one contextual suggestion after a completed reply. Tab inserts an editable draft and Escape dismisses it; it never auto-sends. Requests use existing model configuration, a 10-second timeout, scoped caching and stale-response protection.
- **Screenshot tools:** adjust the region, annotate shapes/arrows/pen/mosaic/text, undo, copy, save, ask LobsterAI, extract text or translate. Independent Cowork tasks preserve the unsent composer draft and provide retry after failure.

## Electron-specific behavior
- Custom images stay in the local profile under content-hash filenames. Static formats accept uploads up to 5 MB; GIFs up to 2 MB, with each dimension between 128 and 2048 pixels. Validate GIF structure, frame bounds, byte limits, file ownership and content hash before restoration. Preserve GIF bytes instead of flattening through canvas or Electron nativeImage.
- Keep sandboxing and main-frame/sender checks; only the main settings window can mutate skins. Existing PNG profiles remain compatible. The desktop image element stays mounted across task mood changes.
- Keep per-display screenshot capture and explicit crop approval. Add preload bridges for local skin management, isolated screenshot tasks and suggestions.
- No server API, database migration, bundled runtime change, billing or private cloud image-generation dependency.

## Validation
- GIF follow-up: **166 tests passed across 5 files**, covering local persistence/restoration/deletion, malformed and oversized GIFs, forged types, symlinks, unchanged animation bytes, editor behavior, stable desktop image mounting and companion manager regressions.
- Renderer TypeScript (`tsc --noEmit`), Electron compilation, production build and changed-file ESLint (zero warnings): passed. `git diff --check`: passed.
- Windows Electron 43.5.0 component smoke: real upload decoding, animated editor preview, original-byte apply callback and desktop character playback passed. Captured two distinct rendered animation frames. The fixture mounts the actual editor and character components; it does not exercise the full app IPC/window lifecycle.
- Earlier base contribution: 241 focused tests passed, 1 macOS-only test skipped, plus renderer/main type checks, lint and production build.

## Screenshot
Actual Electron component smoke using a generated two-frame fixture:

![Custom GIF preview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alison-xx/LobsterAI/feat/companion-customization-cowork-suggestions/specs/features/desktop-companion/custom-gif-preview.png)

## Remaining manual coverage
Full-app native file-picker/IPC roundtrip, restart across actual profile sessions, multi-monitor/DPI behavior, OS clipboard/save dialogs, and live-model OCR/translation/suggestions still need manual desktop acceptance. The component smoke and automated tests do not claim that coverage.
