prs.title: fix(discord): classify direct messages as direct chats
prs.body:
## Summary

Every Discord chat is classified as shared today (`ChannelType::Discord => true` in `crates/channels/src/chat_classification.rs`) because Discord channel ids do not encode conversation kind and the adapter did not forward it. As a result, a 1:1 DM between an operator and the bot runs with the untrusted ceiling (`_tool_audience = "public"`, `_tool_policy = {"deny": ["*"]}`, no private context), and operator direct-chat commands (`/context`, `/sessions`, `/agent`, `/sh`) fail closed, as `docs/src/discord.md` notes.

This PR makes the Discord adapter forward whether a conversation is the bot's own DM, so the gateway can classify it as direct, the way Telegram positive chat ids and Slack `D…` conversations already are. Shared chats are exactly as restrictive as before.

Related precedents: #1224 / #1238 (Slack) and #1264 / #1265 (Telegram) dealt with tools in shared chats by exposing the `untrusted_audience` / `untrusted_tools` opt-in. Those channels could already prove a DM from the chat id; Discord could not, so its DMs never reached the "operator in a proven direct chat" path at all. This PR closes that gap only; it does not add the shared-chat opt-in to Discord.

## What changed

- **`ChannelReplyTarget::direct_chat: bool`** (`crates/channels/src/plugin.rs`): adapter evidence that the conversation is one-to-one with the bot. `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Not::not")]`, so existing stored bindings deserialize as `false` and serialized JSON is unchanged when it is `false`.
- **Classification** (`crates/channels/src/chat_classification.rs`): new `is_shared_chat_with_hint` / `classify_chat_with_hint`. The hint is honoured **only for Discord**; every other channel type ignores it and keeps its id-based allowlist, so a stray `true` cannot turn a Telegram group, Slack channel, Teams/Matrix room or a phone call into a direct chat. A Discord DM classifies as `"direct"`; guild chats keep `None`.
- **`ChannelReplyTarget::is_shared_chat()` / `classify_chat()`**: the gateway's `is_shared_channel_target` and the hook `ChannelBinding` conversion now use these.
- **Discord adapter** (`crates/discord/`):
  - Gateway messages: `direct_chat = guild_id.is_none()`. Guild messages always carry a `guild_id` and bot users cannot be members of group DMs, so a message without one is the bot's DM.
  - Slash commands and component interactions: `direct_chat` only when there is no `guild_id` **and** `context == Some(InteractionContext::BotDm)`. A user-installed app can be invoked in the user's other DMs and group DMs (`PrivateChannel`), so a missing guild alone is not enough; a missing context fails closed.
  - DM access for interactions (770a3491): slash commands and component interactions in the bot DM now pass the same `dm_policy` / DM allowlist check (`access::check_access` with `ChatType::Dm`) as a direct message, through a new `authorize_interaction` that is the only way either handler gets a reply target. A refused interaction gets an ephemeral refusal and never reaches the gateway, the same outcome as the message path dropping a refused DM, rather than being downgraded to a shared chat. Interactions outside the bot DM are unchanged; no guild-side check is added or relaxed.
- All other `ChannelReplyTarget` constructions set `direct_chat: false` (mechanical, no behaviour change).
- **Docs**: `discord.md`, `channels.md` and `security.md` no longer say Discord DMs fail closed; they describe what is direct (bot DMs) and what stays shared (guild channels, threads, interactions outside the bot DM). Non-operator DM senders are still guests and keep tool-free chat, as on other channels.

The trust rule itself is unchanged: a turn is trusted only when the sender is in `operators` **and** the chat is proven direct.

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean
- `cargo clippy -p moltis-channels -p moltis-discord -p moltis-chat -p moltis-matrix -p moltis-msteams -p moltis-nostr -p moltis-signal -p moltis-slack -p moltis-telegram -p moltis-telephony -p moltis-whatsapp -p moltis-gateway --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo test -p moltis-channels -p moltis-discord`: 280 passed, 0 failed (285 after 770a3491; `cargo clippy -p moltis-discord --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt` clean)
- `cargo test -p moltis-chat -p moltis-matrix -p moltis-msteams -p moltis-nostr -p moltis-signal -p moltis-slack -p moltis-telegram -p moltis-telephony -p moltis-whatsapp -p moltis-gateway`: 1742 passed, 0 failed (6 ignored)
- `git diff --check`: clean

New tests:
- `chat_classification::tests::discord_dm_is_direct_only_with_adapter_evidence`: Discord DM is direct, guild is shared
- `chat_classification::tests::direct_hint_is_ignored_outside_discord`: the hint cannot widen any other channel type
- `plugin::tests::reply_target_direct_chat_serde_is_backward_compatible`: legacy JSON stays shared; the flag round-trips; hook binding gets `chat_type = "direct"`
- `handler::implementation::tests::dm_message_reply_target_forwards_direct_chat` / `guild_message_reply_target_stays_shared`
- `commands::tests::bot_dm_interaction_forwards_direct_chat` / `non_bot_dm_interactions_stay_shared` (guild, `PrivateChannel`, missing context, guild + `BotDm`)
- `channel_events::tests::discord_dm_forwarded_by_adapter_is_direct_and_guild_stays_shared`: operator DM is trusted and passes `OperatorDirect`; guest DM and operator-in-guild are not
- `channel_events::tests::direct_chat_hint_cannot_make_an_id_classified_group_direct`
- `commands::tests::bot_dm_interaction_is_refused_when_dms_are_disabled` / `bot_dm_interaction_is_refused_for_user_off_the_allowlist`: a bot-DM interaction is refused under `dm_policy = "disabled"` (even for an allowlisted user) and for a user off the allowlist (or with an empty allowlist); both fail if the check is removed
- `commands::tests::allowed_bot_dm_interaction_is_direct` / `bot_dm_interaction_matches_allowlist_by_username`: an allowed user in the bot DM still gets a direct target
- `commands::tests::dm_policy_does_not_change_interactions_outside_the_bot_dm`: guild, `PrivateChannel` and missing-context interactions are unaffected by the DM policy and stay shared

I did not run `./scripts/local-validate.sh` or the macOS/iOS builds, and I have not done live Discord QA. Suggested manual QA: with the sender in `operators`, DM the bot and confirm a configured MCP tool runs and `/context` works; @mention the bot in a guild channel and confirm tools and `/context` are still denied; DM the bot from a non-operator allowlisted account and confirm it stays tool-free; with `dm_policy = "disabled"`, run `/context` in the bot DM and confirm an ephemeral refusal.

## How this was made

This was written with Claude Code, from a bug we hit on a self-hosted deployment: a Discord DM with an operator never got tools, while the same setup worked on Telegram. Key decisions:

- **Forward the conversation kind instead of adding the shared-chat opt-in to Discord.** The opt-in would also unblock tools, but it widens every shared chat on the account; classifying the DM correctly fixes the operator case without loosening guilds.
- **Put the flag on `ChannelReplyTarget`** because that is what `is_shared_channel_target` already receives on every path (messages, commands, interactions, attachments). This needed `direct_chat: false` at every other construction site, which is most of the file count.
- **Honour the flag for Discord only**, so the existing id-based allowlist stays the sole source of truth for every other channel and the field cannot be used to escalate them.
- **Require `InteractionContext::BotDm` for interactions**, because user-installed apps can be invoked from DMs where the bot is not the other party.
- **Refuse bot-DM interactions the DM policy denies** (raised in review). Downgrading them to shared would still let a barred user reach the gateway; refusing matches what the message path does with a refused DM.

prs.body:
## Summary

`agents.set_default` persisted correctly, but **New Chat** still used the previous session’s agent because `sessions.switch` always set `inherit_agent_from` for brand-new keys. Separately, `resolve_prompt_agent_id` / `chat.send` fell back to hardcoded `"main"`, and `sessions.list` reported `default_id` for NULL `agent_id` without persisting it.

This PR:

1. **New Chat** binds the runtime `default_id` unless the caller passes explicit `inherit_agent_from` (fork path unchanged).
2. **Prompt fallback** reads a sync `default_agent_id` marker (written by `set_default` + startup sync) instead of hardcoding `"main"`.
3. **`chat.send`** ensures the target session has a persisted `agent_id` before prompt build.
4. **`sessions.list`** persists the default when `agent_id` is NULL instead of faking it in the response only.

## Validation

### Completed
- [x] Patch applies cleanly on current `main`
- [x] Unit test: `resolve_prompt_agent_id_falls_back_to_runtime_default_not_hardcoded_main`

### Remaining

- [ ] Manual RPC: `agents.set_default` → `content-writer`, switch from `main`, New Chat session → `agent_id=content-writer`

prs.title: feat: native gpui desktop client (apps/desktop) and moltis-client crate
prs.body:
## Summary

A native Rust/gpui desktop client that **connects to a running moltis daemon** instead of embedding it. Quitting the app leaves the daemon running. It connects to the local daemon, to remote daemons over HTTPS, or through SSH tunnels.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    UI[apps/desktop gpui] --> Client[crates/client moltis-client]
    Ctl[moltis-ctl] --> Client
    Client -- "WSS /ws/chat v4 + scoped mk_ key" --> Daemon[(moltis daemon)]
    Client -- "ssh -L" --> Daemon
    Proto[crates/protocol typed payloads] --- Client
    Proto --- Daemon
```

- **`moltis-protocol`** now owns the client-facing wire types:
  - Persisted message types and `ExternalAgentKind` moved here and are re-exported from `moltis-sessions`.
  - Typed `chat` events and typed `sessions.list` / `chat.*` / `models.list` / approval payloads.
  - As a result, `moltis-config` no longer depends on `moltis-sessions`, which drops sqlx and tokio from its dependency tree.
- **New `moltis-client` crate:**
  - v4 handshake, responses routed by request id, and an event broadcast.
  - Keepalive pings and a `ManagedClient` that reconnects with backoff and stops on auth failures.
  - Typed RPC helpers.
  - Password login exchanged for a scoped API key.
  - TLS trust by local CA, pinned fingerprint (trust on first use), or the platform verifier.
  - Failure classification, so the UI can tell an unreachable daemon from a TLS or auth failure.
  - Optional local-config discovery, mDNS discovery, and SSH tunnels.
- **`moltis-ctl`** is ported onto `moltis-client`. Its old handshake waited for a top-level `hello-ok` frame that the gateway never sends, so every invocation timed out.
- **`apps/desktop`** is a separate Cargo workspace:
  - Sessions sidebar and a streaming transcript.
  - Native markdown with syntect code highlighting.
  - Tool cards, reasoning and model picker; stop and approvals, including system notifications.
  - Server list with Nearby (mDNS), direct HTTPS and SSH tunnels.
  - API keys stored in the keychain.
  - Starts the local daemon as a user service when it isn't running.
  - Settings, providers, cron and logs open in the web UI.
- Packaging script for `Moltis Desktop.app`, `just desktop-*` recipes, a Desktop App CI workflow, and docs (`docs/src/desktop-app.md`).

Security hardening is included in the branch:
- No credentials over plain HTTP to non-loopback hosts.
- Approve from a notification only for short printable-ASCII commands.
- Changed certificates are flagged as changed, not as a first-use prompt.
- Markdown nesting is capped.
- mDNS entries are labelled unverified and saved only after the user trusts the certificate.

No GraphQL was needed.

## Validation

### Completed
- [x] `cargo test -p moltis-client --all-features` (54 tests, including a TLS mock server)
- [x] `cargo test -p moltis-protocol -p moltis-sessions -p moltis-config` and `cargo test -p moltis-chat --lib chat_final_broadcast_parses`
- [x] `cargo test -p moltis-httpd --test native_client` (client against a real in-process gateway)
- [x] `cd apps/desktop && cargo test` (63 tests), plus clippy with `--features capture` and with `--no-default-features`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `./scripts/check-file-size.sh`
- [x] Manual end to end against a real daemon in a temp config dir:
  - TLS through the local CA, then the handshake and model list.
  - A streamed reply rendered with markdown and code highlighting.
  - The daemon kept running after the app quit, and history reloaded on relaunch.
  - Checked with screenshots from the `capture` feature.
- [x] `./scripts/package-desktop-macos.sh` builds and launches the bundle; `just desktop-open-macos` bundles a portable release daemon, and with no service installed the app started it and connected in 4s.
- [x] `OPENSSL_ROOT_DIR=/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3 ./scripts/local-validate.sh 1306`: fmt, file-size, biome, tsc, zizmor, lockfile, `just lint` and the full build pass. The targeted-test step then tried `-p moltis-desktop` from the root workspace; fixed in `86f5fe40` (the script now skips `apps/desktop`, which `desktop.yml` tests).
- [x] `cargo nextest run -p moltis-chat -p moltis-client -p moltis-config -p moltis-ctl -p moltis-httpd -p moltis-metrics -p moltis-protocol -p moltis-sessions`: 1057 passed.

### Remaining
- [ ] mDNS discovery verified live. In the dev sandbox even `dns-sd` saw no advertisements.

## Manual QA

1. `moltis service install` (or run `moltis`), then `just desktop-run`. The app should connect to "This computer".
2. If the daemon has a password: sign in. The key appears in the web UI under Settings → Security as "Moltis Desktop (host)".
3. Send a message and watch it stream. Try ⌘. to stop and ⌘N for a new chat; switch sessions and switch models.
4. Quit the app, then `curl -k https://localhost:<port>/health` still answers. Relaunch and the history is there.
5. Servers (⌘⇧S) → add `https://other-host:port`: the fingerprint prompt appears; trust it and you are connected.
6. Add an SSH tunnel (`user@host`, daemon port) and connect.
7. `moltis service uninstall`, then `just desktop-open-macos`: the app installs the bundled daemon as a service by itself and connects within a few seconds (measured: 4s).

issues.title: [Bug] QQ group messages silently dropped on 2.2.2
issues.body:
# [Bug] QQ group messages silently dropped on 2.2.2 — gateway dispatches `GROUP_MESSAGE_CREATE`, but `_MESSAGE_EVENT_SPECS` only knows `GROUP_AT_MESSAGE_CREATE`

## Environment
- QwenPaw **2.2.2** (upgraded from 2.2.1, agentscope 2.0.10)
- Channel: QQ official bot, **group** chat
- Linux

## Symptom
After upgrading 2.2.1 → 2.2.2, the bot stops receiving **group** messages: @-mentioning the bot in a group produces no reply at all. Direct messages (`C2C_MESSAGE_CREATE`) keep working, and sending messages *to* the same group works fine. Reconnecting the WebSocket and fully restarting the app do not help — both connections reach `READY`, and no group event is ever logged.

## Root cause
A temporary log line in the gateway dispatch handler showed the event types actually dispatched:

```
dispatch seen t=READY s=1
dispatch seen t=GROUP_MESSAGE_CREATE s=2 keys=['author','content','group_id','group_openid','id','message_scene','message_type','timestamp']
```

`_MESSAGE_EVENT_SPECS` in `qwenpaw/app/channels/qq/channel.py` registers only:

- `C2C_MESSAGE_CREATE`
- `AT_MESSAGE_CREATE`
- `DIRECT_MESSAGE_CREATE`
- `GROUP_AT_MESSAGE_CREATE`

`GROUP_MESSAGE_CREATE` is missing, so `_handle_msg_event()` hits `spec is None` and returns silently — group messages are dropped with no log line, which makes this hard to diagnose.

## Fix that worked locally
```python
"GROUP_MESSAGE_CREATE": _MessageEventSpec(
    message_type="group",
    sender_keys=("member_openid", "id"),
    extra_meta_keys=("group_openid",),
),
```

Group messages are delivered again after adding this entry.

## Notes
- Not caused by the replayed-event guard from #8006 — no "duplicate dispatch" warnings were logged while the issue was happening.
- Probably worth keeping **both** `GROUP_MESSAGE_CREATE` and `GROUP_AT_MESSAGE_CREATE` registered, since the dispatched name may depend on bot type/permissions.

issues.title: [Bug]: Windows压缩包在Qwenpaw乱码 。

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
根因分析
问题出在 QwenPaw 解压 ZIP 的核心代码。关键入口有两个：

Skill ZIP 导入（store.py 第 754-775 行）：
python

def _extract_and_validate_zip(data: bytes, tmp_dir: Path) -> None:
with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(data)) as zf: # ← 没传 encoding 参数
...
zf.extractall(tmp_dir)
2. Hub 下载（hub.py 第 1753、1699 行）同理，ZipFile(...) 都没传 encoding。

为什么 Windows 压缩的中文文件名会乱码
ZIP 规范规定文件名编码有两种方式：

不设 UTF-8 标志位 → 文件名用 CP437（原始 ZIP 规范）
设 UTF-8 标志位（bit 11） → 文件名用 UTF-8
问题在于：Windows 中文系统上很多压缩工具（尤其是系统自带的"发送到→压缩文件夹"）不会设置 UTF-8 bit，而是用 GBK/CP936 编码文件名。当这个 ZIP 上传到 Linux 服务器上，Python zipfile 模块默认按 CP437 解码文件名，GBK 的中文就变成乱码了。

好消息：文件内容不受影响
QwenPaw 已经为文件内容做了编码兼容——_FRONTMATTER_ENCODINGS 和 decode_text_bytes_with_encoding_fallback 里都包含了 gbk / cp936 的回退。所以即使 ZIP 文件名乱码，解压后 SKILL.md 的正文大概率能正确读取。但如果技能目录名本身是中文，路径会出问题。

规避方案
避免用 Windows 资源管理器自带压缩。改用 7-Zip、Bandizip 等——它们在创建 ZIP 时会设置 UTF-8 标志位。
用 QwenPaw 工作区里的 Python zipfile 打包（AGENTS.md 里也写了这条建议），Python 3 的 zipfile 默认写 UTF-8 标志。
技能市场 / Hub 下载不受影响——服务端返回的都是 UTF-8 编码的 ZIP。

issues.title: [Bug] Feishu channel fails with 426 Upgrade Required when HTTP(S)_PROXY is injected without NO_PROXY for feishu.cn
issues.body:
## Summary

When QwenPaw runs in an environment where `HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY` are injected but `NO_PROXY` does **not** include `feishu.cn`, the Feishu channel cannot connect at all:

- The WebSocket long-connection thread fails repeatedly
- Outbound `tenant_access_token` requests fail
- Every HTTP call to `open.feishu.cn` returns `426 Upgrade Required` from the proxy

## Environment

- QwenPaw 2.1.0 (installed package), Python 3.11
- Containerized Linux deployment
- `HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY` (and lowercase variants) injected into the process environment
- `NO_PROXY` does not contain `feishu.cn`

## Symptoms

`app.err.log` fills with:

```
urllib3.exceptions.MaxRetryError: HTTPSConnectionPool(host='open.feishu.cn', port=443):
Max retries exceeded with url: /callback/ws/endpoint
(Caused by ProxyError('Unable to connect to proxy', OSError('Tunnel connection failed: 426 Upgrade Required')))

requests.exceptions.ProxyError: HTTPSConnectionPool(host='open.feishu.cn', port=443): ...
```

Counters over roughly one day: `ProxyError` 14,570 / `426 Upgrade Required` 14,561 / `feishu WebSocket thread failed` 3,647.

The process itself looks healthy (`/api/version` returns 200), so the failure is silent from a monitoring standpoint.

## Root cause

`lark_oapi` uses `requests` internally, and `requests` honours `HTTP(S)_PROXY` / `NO_PROXY` from the environment. Two calls are affected:

1. `POST https://open.feishu.cn/callback/ws/endpoint` — WS endpoint negotiation
2. `POST https://open.feishu.cn/open-apis/auth/v3/tenant_access_token/internal`

Note that `lark_oapi`'s WebSocket transport already passes `proxy=None` when building the connection (`_ws_connect_kwargs()`), so the WS socket itself bypasses the proxy — but the HTTP calls that precede it do not.

QwenPaw's own client is also proxy-aware by default, in `app/channels/feishu/channel.py`:

```python
self._http_client = httpx.AsyncClient(
    timeout=30.0,
)                                   # trust_env defaults to True

self._client = (
    lark.Client.builder()
    .app_id(self.app_id)
    .app_secret(self.app_secret)
    .domain(sdk_domain)
    ...
    .build()
)
```

## Suggested fixes

1. Build the Feishu-bound httpx client with `trust_env=False` (or explicit `proxies=None`):
   ```python
   self._http_client = httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=30.0, trust_env=False)
   ```
2. For the `lark_oapi` client, propagate a proxy/`NO_PROXY` setting if the SDK supports it; otherwise document that `NO_PROXY` must include `.feishu.cn`.
3. Document required `NO_PROXY` entries (`feishu.cn`, `.feishu.cn`, `larksuite.com`) for containerized deployments behind a proxy.
4. Optionally add a config switch such as `channels.feishu.bypass_env_proxy` (default `true`), so a misconfigured platform proxy does not silently kill the channel.

## Workaround

Adding `.feishu.cn` to `NO_PROXY` in the process environment fixes both the WS connection and outbound messages (verified by exporting `no_proxy` / `NO_PROXY` in the supervisor command that launches the app).

## Additional suggestion

A startup health check that probes `open.feishu.cn` and logs a clear, actionable error would make this much easier to diagnose — currently the channel simply stays silent while the error log fills up.

issues.title: [Bug][Console] v2.2.2 发送按钮点击后消息成功发送，但输入框未清空（队列分支 clear 依赖会话活跃状态）
issues.body:
## Environment

- QwenPaw v2.2.2（2026-10-15 发布）
- macOS（Darwin 27.0.0, arm64）
- 安装方式：pip venv（`/Users/duzuzeng/.venv/qwenpaw`）
- 访问方式：本地控制台 `http://127.0.0.1:8088/console/`

## Problem

在控制台聊天界面输入消息并点击发送按钮后：

1. ✅ 消息**成功发送**到后端，agent 正常回复，聊天流正常显示消息和回复
2. ❌ 但**输入框中的文字没有被清空**，仍残留在输入框内

用户体感是"点了发送但消息停留在对话框"，容易误判为发送失败并重复发送。

## Steps to Reproduce

1. 打开 `http://127.0.0.1:8088/console/`
2. 进入任意 agent 会话
3. 在输入框输入文字
4. 点击发送按钮（或按 Enter）
5. 观察：消息出现在聊天流中，但输入框文字残留不清空

## Root Cause Analysis（前端代码定位）

v2.2.2 将发送逻辑改为**后台消息队列模式**（`enqueue` 入队 → 异步处理）。前端 `console/assets/index-DtVnmMZO.js` 中存在两条清空路径：

### 路径 1 — Enter 键发送（约 102514 字节偏移）

```js
F.getState().enqueue(d, {...});   // 消息入队
De.current = [];                  // 清附件
dt(k, "");                        // 清空 textarea DOM value
hd();                             // 清附件 UI
```

此路径**必定清空**输入框。

### 路径 2 — 发送按钮点击（约 115129 字节偏移）

```js
const ps = Zt.current === $;          // 当前会话是否活跃
if (qr || !ps || Ur()) {              // 队列分支
    if (!et && tt.length === 0) return false;
    if (F.getState().getQueue(d).length >= Dn) { ...queue full...; return false; }
    const Ki = Z ? Ms(et) : et;
    return F.getState().enqueue(d, {
        text: Ki,
        attachments: tt.length > 0 ? tt : void 0,
        agentId: c,
        backendSessionId: X.sessionId,
        userId: X.userId,
        channel: X.channel,
        requestContext: Ji,
        bizParams: { ...C.biz_params, ...ho(X) }
    }),
    ps ? (De.current = [], localStorage.removeItem(Es(c)))   // ← ps=true 才清空
       : X.sessionId && Y && !li(d) && Ts(d, X.sessionId, Y),
    { proceed: false, clear: ps }     // ← clear 依赖 ps
}
```

**缺陷**：`clear` 的值取决于 `ps`（会话活跃状态判断）。当 `qr` 或 `Ur()` 为真时消息走队列分支，若此时 `ps` 为 false，则消息成功入队并发送，但**输入框不清空、草稿不删除**。

## 疑似引入版本

- #7382 — "Keep queued messages bound to their original Agent and conversation..."
- #7831 — "Stream background tool output only while its task panel is expanded..."

均为 v2.2.2 的队列化发送改造。

## Backend Verification

后端日志确认消息正常接收与处理，排除后端问题：

```
minicpm emit=query.received session=1791730917032-2ia5cfy state=thinking
console stream done: event_count=517 has_response=True
Usage for session ...: {'provider_id': 'stepfun', 'model_name': 'step-5-preview', ...}
```

## Impact

- 功能无影响：消息正常发送，agent 正常回复
- UI 体验缺陷：输入框残留导致用户误判发送失败，可能引发重复发送
- 附带问题：草稿未清除，刷新/切换会话后旧内容可能被草稿恢复逻辑重新填入输入框

## Suggested Fix

路径 2 的清空不应依赖 `ps`。建议：消息 `enqueue` 成功后即清空输入框并删除草稿（无论会话是否活跃）；仅当入队失败（队列满等）时才保留输入内容。

## Additional Notes

- 与第三方插件无关：已验证在卸载全部桌宠插件后问题复现
- 浏览器缓存已排除：`/console/` 响应头为 `cache-control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate`，JS 文件名带 content hash

issues.body:
# [Plugins/HarmonyOS] 移动端本地插件宿主：请求标准化 `window.QwenPaw` 契约 + 数据面桥 + 分发验签 + PawApp 门控统一


## 背景 Background
我们维护两样东西：

1. **QwenPaw 鸿蒙原生 App**（bundle `io.agentscope.qwenpaw.mobile`，对齐上游 PR #7378 的 `app.json`；ArkTS/ArkUI，147 文件 / 约 45k 行），其中已建成**端侧本地插件宿主**：`pluginhost/` shell（`index.html` + `host.js` + vendor UMD，`HOST_SHELL_VERSION=8`）+ ArkWeb 装载页 + 设备 ZIP 安装器（沙箱 `plugins/<id>/`）+ `qpwFile` 文件桥 + NotificationKit 系统通知。
2. **AgentTeams 工作台插件**（`agentteams-qwenpaw-workbench`，全栈插件）：Python 后端 **54 个端点**（聚合/转发 AgentTeams Controller、Matrix、Higress Console、SGLang）+ 前端约 1.9MB 单文件 bundle。它目前跑在 QwenPaw 服务端宿主里（web console）。

**我们想做的事**：让全栈插件**不依赖 QwenPaw 服务端**、直接装进移动 App 本地宿主运行（"端侧独立宿主"）。为此我们做了真机级 PoC，结论：

- ✅ **前端半边零改动可用**：把真插件装进端侧 shell，`window.QwenPaw` 注入、`registerRoutes → 1 route`、完整工作台渲染成功（单请求加载 1.85MB bundle，无附加资源）。
- ✅ **应用内通知已通**：插件 `new Notification(...)` → shell 桩 → `window.prompt('qwpaw.notify|{t,b}')` → ArkWeb `onPrompt` → NotificationKit 系统通知中心，端到端实测成立。
- ❌ **数据面被端侧 shell 受控 503**（`host.js` 把一切 http(s)/根相对请求拦成 offline 响应）→ 插件进入"Controller not connected"空态。**独立宿主的插件如何访问"用户授权的服务端"，目前上游没有定义。**
- ❌ **契约无权威源**：实测上游 web console 2.2.2 的 host 面与其自家 `docs/plugins.zh.md` 不一致（文档列出的 `useTheme/useLocale/useSelectedAgent/useCurrentSession/host.fetch` 在 bundle 里均不存在）、无任何宿主形态/环境声明槽位、无 `chat` 命名空间。

**术语澄清（重要）**：我们主张把两个概念分开——**宿主形态**（server / local / desktop，架构属性，声明式）与**连通性**（数据面可达与否，会随时变，探测式）。上游若提供 boolean `isOffline` 来表达宿主形态，会把两者混为一谈，必然误判（独立宿主但数据面可达 ≠ 离线；服务端宿主但后端挂了 ≠ 在线）。建议契约直接使用两轴结构（见议题 1）。

---

## Background 
We maintain two things:

1. **A native HarmonyOS QwenPaw app** (bundle `io.agentscope.qwenpaw.mobile`, aligned with upstream PR #7378's `app.json`; ArkTS/ArkUI, 147 files / ~45k LOC). It already ships a **device-local plugin host**: a `pluginhost/` shell (`index.html` + `host.js` + vendor UMDs, `HOST_SHELL_VERSION=8`), an ArkWeb page, a device-ZIP installer (sandbox `plugins/<id>/`), a `qpwFile` file bridge, and NotificationKit system notifications.
2. **The AgentTeams Workbench plugin** (`agentteams-qwenpaw-workbench`, a full-stack plugin): a Python backend with **54 endpoints** (aggregating/proxying AgentTeams Controller, Matrix, Higress Console, SGLang) plus a ~1.9MB single-file frontend bundle. Today it runs inside the QwenPaw **server** host (web console).

**Goal**: run the full-stack plugin **without any QwenPaw server**, installed in the mobile app's local host ("device-standalone host"). Our device-level PoC results:

- ✅ **Frontend half works with zero changes**: the real plugin loads in the device shell — `window.QwenPaw` injected, `registerRoutes → 1 route`, full workbench renders (single request for the 1.85MB bundle, no extra assets).
- ✅ **In-app notifications work end-to-end**: plugin `new Notification(...)` → shell stub → `window.prompt('qwpaw.notify|{t,b}')` → ArkWeb `onPrompt` → NotificationKit system notification center (verified on device).
- ❌ **The data plane is deliberately 503'd** by the device shell (`host.js` turns every http(s)/root-relative request into an offline response) → the plugin shows a "Controller not connected" empty state. **How a plugin in a standalone host may reach "user-authorized backends" is currently undefined upstream.**
- ❌ **No authoritative contract**: upstream web console 2.2.2's host surface does not match its own `docs/plugins.zh.md` (documented `useTheme/useLocale/useSelectedAgent/useCurrentSession/host.fetch` are absent from the bundle), there is no host-form/env declaration slot, and no `chat` namespace.

**Terminology (important)**: we propose to separate **host form** (server / local / desktop — an architectural property, declared) from **connectivity** (data-plane reachability — dynamic, probed). A boolean `isOffline` used to express host form conflates the two and will misclassify (standalone host with a reachable data plane ≠ offline; server host with a dead backend ≠ online). The contract should use the two-axis shape in Topic 1.

---

## 议题 1 · 官方「端侧独立宿主」契约（含环境两轴）
### Topic 1 · An official "device-standalone host" contract (with the two-axis env)

**现状 Current**：各壳各自实现 `window.QwenPaw.*`。我们实测对比：鸿蒙端侧 shell（v8，约 700 行 `host.js`）实现了 `{host, menu, route, slot, chat, audit, memoryBackends, registerRoutes, registerToolRender}`；web console 2.2.2 与文档互相矛盾且缺环境槽位。结果是插件写作者只能靠 feature-detect 猜测宿主能力，跨端移植无保障。

**Current**: each shell implements `window.QwenPaw.*` independently. Our measurement: the HarmonyOS device shell (v8, ~700-line `host.js`) implements `{host, menu, route, slot, chat, audit, memoryBackends, registerRoutes, registerToolRender}`; web console 2.2.2 contradicts its own docs and has no env slot. Plugin authors can only feature-detect and guess; cross-host portability is not guaranteed.

**诉求 Ask**：

1. 发布一份**端侧独立宿主契约规范**：哪些命名空间是必须的、语义、生命周期（装载/卸载/`dispose`）、错误上报约定。我们的 `host.js`（v8）可作为参考基线提交（同许可，可整体或按段引用）。
2. 契约必须包含**环境声明**（两轴），并明确**不推荐**用 boolean `isOffline` 表达宿主形态：

   ```ts
   window.QwenPaw.host.env = {
     kind: 'server' | 'local' | 'desktop',        // 轴 A：宿主形态（声明式，决定插件后端在不在）
     caps: { net: boolean, secureStore: boolean, notify: boolean }, // 轴 B：能力位
     apiVersion: '1.x',                            // 契约版本握手
   }
   ```

3. 命名纪律：`standalone/local` 描述宿主形态；`offline` 只描述连通性（如 `dataPlane: 'offline'`）。两者不得互相借用。

**Ask**:

1. Publish a **device-standalone host contract spec**: which namespaces are mandatory, their semantics, lifecycle (load/unload/`dispose`), error reporting. Our `host.js` (v8) is offered as a reference baseline (same license; adoptable wholesale or per-section).
2. The contract must include the **two-axis env declaration** above, and explicitly discourage a boolean `isOffline` as a host-form signal.
3. Naming discipline: `standalone/local` for host form; `offline` only for connectivity.

**不解决的后果 Consequence if not addressed**：每个壳各自实现、插件不可移植；"全栈插件"在移动端永远只能看空态（我们 PoC 的现状）。

---

## 议题 2 · 数据面桥的官方语义（让独立 ≠ 离线）
### Topic 2 · Official semantics for the data-plane bridge (standalone ≠ offline)

**现状 Current**：独立宿主下的插件需要访问**用户自己授权的服务端**（例如插件自己的后端、或用户配置的数据源）。当前鸿蒙端侧 shell 的选择是"一律 503"——把"独立"实现成了"离线"。

In a standalone host, plugins must reach **user-authorized backends** (e.g. the plugin's own backend, or user-configured data sources). The HarmonyOS shell's current choice is "503 everything" — it implements "standalone" as "offline".

**诉求 Ask**：上游定义端侧独立宿主下插件访问用户授权服务端的标准方式。我们的提议（两侧工作量均已按此估算）：

- 端侧原生网络桥，仿照既有 `qpwFile` 范式：

  ```js
  window.qpwNet.request(url, init)   // 端侧发请求，无 CORS；凭据由宿主安全存储注入，不进 WebView
  window.qpwNet.stream(url, init)    // SSE/流式（端侧长连）
  ```

- 或并入 `host.fetch`：**按连接态/白名单放行，而不是按宿主形态一刀切**；白名单 origin 由宿主声明并展示给用户。
- 凭据安全底线：令牌类凭据必须走端侧安全存储（鸿蒙 HUKS），**禁止落 localStorage**（WebView 内明文，任何脚本可读）。我们的插件持有 Matrix access_token + Controller token（含 Docker 代理，等效宿主机权限）+ Higress admin token——这类凭据进 localStorage 是移动端不可接受的安全边界问题。
- 明确"全栈插件"的端侧化边界：哪些能力宿主保证（网络/存储/通知），哪些插件自管。

**Ask**: define the standard way for a plugin in a standalone host to reach user-authorized backends. Our proposal (effort on both sides already estimated against this design):

- A device-native network bridge, following the existing `qpwFile` pattern:

  ```js
  window.qpwNet.request(url, init)   // device-side fetch, no CORS; credentials injected from host secure storage, never into the WebView
  window.qpwNet.stream(url, init)    // SSE/streaming (device-side long connection)
  ```

- Or fold it into `host.fetch`: **allow by connection state / whitelist, not by host form**; whitelisted origins declared by the host and visible to the user.
- Credential security floor: token-class credentials must live in device secure storage (HUKS on HarmonyOS); **localStorage is forbidden** (plaintext in the WebView, readable by any script). Our plugin carries a Matrix access_token + Controller token (with Docker proxy — effectively host-level) + Higress admin token; putting those in localStorage is an unacceptable mobile security boundary.
- Define the boundary for "full-stack plugins": which capabilities the host guarantees (net/storage/notify) and which the plugin manages itself.

**工作量参考 Effort reference**：端侧桥 3–6 人天（含白名单 UI + 流式）；插件适配层 2–4 人天。我们插件 54 端点中约 25–35 个为纯透传/聚合（可端侧化），其余为有状态/派生逻辑。

---

## 议题 3 · 通知载荷规范与点击定位（应用内）
### Topic 3 · Notification payload spec & tap routing (in-app)

**现状 Current**：应用内通知已可用——插件 `new Notification(t, {body})` → 宿主桩 → 系统通知，端到端实测通过。当前缺口是**载荷语义与点击行为未定义**：插件只能传 `{t,b}`，宿主无法区分审批/任务/告警，也无法把"点通知"路由回插件内对应页面。

**Current**: in-app notifications already work — plugin `new Notification(t, {body})` → host stub → system notification, verified end-to-end. What is missing is **payload semantics and tap behavior**: plugins can only pass `{t,b}`, so the host cannot distinguish approval/task/alert, nor route a notification tap back into the corresponding plugin page.

**诉求 Ask**：

1. 定义**通知载荷规范**（向后兼容扩展）：

   ```json
   { "t": "title", "b": "body", "kind": "approval|task|alert", "target": "worker:<name> | room:<id>" }
   ```

   `kind` 供宿主选择系统槽位/优先级；`target` 供宿主把通知点击透传给插件并定位到具体页面（宿主以 query/hash 形式带入 WebView）。
2. 通知去重/冷却建议（轮询型插件会重复产生同类事件）。

**Ask**:

1. Define the **notification payload spec** (backward-compatible extension):

   ```json
   { "t": "title", "b": "body", "kind": "approval|task|alert", "target": "worker:<name> | room:<id>" }
   ```

   `kind` lets the host pick the system slot/priority; `target` lets the host pass a notification tap through to the plugin and locate the specific page (delivered into the WebView as query/hash).
2. Guidance on dedup/cool-down (polling plugins emit repeated same-kind events).

---

## 议题 4 · 插件分发与验签
### Topic 4 · Plugin distribution & signature verification

**现状 Current**：移动端"设备 ZIP 安装"（把插件 ZIP 直接装进 App 沙箱）目前**无签名、无来源校验**——任何 ZIP 都能装。桌面/web 侧的 ZIP/URL 安装同样没有验签。这在移动端是安全边界问题（插件前端可执行任意 JS，宿主注入的是带凭据能力的 SDK）。

Mobile "device-ZIP install" (drop a plugin ZIP into the app sandbox) currently has **no signature and no source check** — any ZIP installs. Desktop/web ZIP/URL installs have no signature verification either. On mobile this is a security-boundary issue: plugin frontend can run arbitrary JS and is injected with a credential-bearing SDK.

**诉求 Ask**：

1. 定义插件**签名机制**（建议：manifest 内嵌签名 + 宿主侧公钥校验；签名主体 = 插件作者/官方）。
2. 定义**来源白名单**语义（官方分发渠道 vs 用户显式信任的本地 ZIP——后者需用户确认风险）。
3. 明确签名/验签失败时的 UX（安装拒绝文案、已有插件的更新验签）。

**Ask**:

1. Define a **plugin signature scheme** (suggest: signature embedded in the manifest, verified by the host against a public key; signatory = plugin author / official).
2. Define **source whitelist** semantics (official distribution vs user-explicitly-trusted local ZIP — the latter requires an explicit risk confirmation).
3. UX for signature/source failure (install rejection copy, signature check on plugin updates).

---

## 议题 5 · `plugin_type` / PawApp 门控与 `entry_page` 语义统一（"列得出、打不开"）
### Topic 5 · Unify `plugin_type` / PawApp gating and `entry_page` semantics ("listed but not openable")

**现状 Current**（实测上游 2.2.2）：

- web 端 `/apps/` 加载器要求 `plugin_type === "app"`，否则报 `PawApp frontend plugin not found`；
- 而 `GET /api/pawapps` 按 `meta.pawapp` 收录并返回 `entry_page`；
- 移动端（PR #7378 的 Expo 版）硬编码 `WebView ${baseUrl}/apps/{id}`，无视 `entry_page`。

结果：一个 PawApp 插件可能**列得出、打不开**（列表有、加载器拒）。

Measured on upstream 2.2.2:

- the web `/apps/` loader requires `plugin_type === "app"`, else `PawApp frontend plugin not found`;
- while `GET /api/pawapps` indexes by `meta.pawapp` and returns `entry_page`;
- mobile (the Expo app in PR #7378) hardcodes `WebView ${baseUrl}/apps/{id}`, ignoring `entry_page`.

Net effect: a PawApp plugin can be **listed but not openable** (shows in the list, rejected by the loader).

**诉求 Ask**：统一三处口径——收录条件（`meta.pawapp` vs `plugin_type`）、加载器门控、`entry_page` 的消费（各端加载器都应尊重 `entry_page`；缺省时才回退 `/apps/{id}`）。我们端侧已按 `entry_page` 适配（URL 参数 `qpw_pawapp_route`）。

**Ask**: align the three surfaces — inclusion condition (`meta.pawapp` vs `plugin_type`), loader gating, and `entry_page` consumption (every host loader should honor `entry_page`; fall back to `/apps/{id}` only when absent). Our device host already adapts via `entry_page` (URL param `qpw_pawapp_route`).

---

## 议题 6 · 契约版本握手
### Topic 6 · Contract version handshake

**现状 Current**：`packages/qwenpaw-api-contract` 已有基础，但插件 manifest 没有向宿主声明"我需要的宿主契约版本"，宿主也不做兼容检查——契约一旦演进，老插件/新宿主（或新插件/老宿主）的行为是未定义的。

`packages/qwenpaw-api-contract` exists, but the plugin manifest does not declare the host-contract version it needs, and hosts do no compatibility check — once the contract evolves, old-plugin/new-host (or new-plugin/old-host) behavior is undefined.

**诉求 Ask**：插件 manifest 增加 `host_api_version`（或复用 `qwenpaw_version`），宿主装载时做兼容检查，不兼容时给出**降级提示**（而不是静默失败或白屏）。配合议题 1 的 `env.apiVersion` 双向握手。

**Ask**: add `host_api_version` to the plugin manifest (or reuse `qwenpaw_version`); hosts check compatibility at load time and show a **graceful degradation message** on mismatch (not silent failure or a blank page). Pairs with `env.apiVersion` from Topic 1 for a two-way handshake.

---

## 议题 7 · 全栈插件（带独立后端）在移动宿主的官方定位
### Topic 7 · Official positioning of full-stack plugins (with their own backend) in mobile hosts

**现状 Current**：像我们这样的全栈插件（Python 后端 + 前端 bundle）装进移动宿主只有两个自然形态：**端侧化**（把后端逻辑用 TS/ArkTS 重实现）或**远端化**（后端留在某个服务端，移动端经网络访问）。目前没有官方推荐路线，也没有官方"移动端插件后端"承载方案。

A full-stack plugin like ours (Python backend + frontend bundle) has only two natural forms in a mobile host: **device-side re-implementation** (port backend logic to TS/ArkTS) or **remote** (backend stays on some server, mobile reaches it over the network). There is no officially recommended route and no official "mobile plugin backend" hosting option.

**诉求 Ask**：请上游明确：

1. 推荐路线（我们倾向"宿主提供数据面桥 + 凭据安全存储，后端留服务端或按插件粒度端侧化"的混合形态，见议题 2）；
2. 是否提供官方"插件后端承载"方案（如官方 sidecar/云函数模板）；
3. 全栈插件在应用商店审核语境下的合规口径（网络权限、自托管后端披露）。

**Ask**: please clarify:

1. The recommended route (we favor a hybrid: host provides the data-plane bridge + secure credential storage, backend stays server-side or is ported per-plugin — see Topic 2);
2. Whether an official "plugin backend hosting" option will exist (e.g. official sidecar / cloud-function template);
3. Compliance guidance for full-stack plugins under app-store review (network permissions, self-hosted backend disclosure).

---

## 我们的立场与可贡献资源 Our position & what we can contribute

- 我们**不是只有诉求**：鸿蒙端侧宿主 shell（`host.js` v8，两轴 `host.env`、`qpwFile` 桥、Notification 桩 + `kind/target` 载荷）是**可运行的参考实现**，愿意整体或按段贡献进上游（`packages/` 下建 `qwenpaw-device-host` 或等价物）。
- 我们已完成真机级 PoC 与逐条兼容矩阵（宿主提供 ↔ 插件需要，14 项对照），可作为契约规范的验收用例。
- 我们建议的讨论顺序：**议题 1（契约）+ 议题 2（数据面）是核心**，其余五条为配套；可一次 RFC 讨论收口。
- 若上游对方向无异议，我们可按议题 1 的 API 形状先行单侧落地（我们的 shell + 插件已按两轴契约 v1.0 落地），等上游规范后对齐。

We are **not just asking**: the HarmonyOS device host shell (`host.js` v8 — two-axis `host.env`, `qpwFile` bridge, Notification stub with `kind/target` payload) is a **working reference implementation**, and we are willing to contribute it upstream (e.g. as `packages/qwenpaw-device-host` or equivalent).
We have a device-level PoC plus a 14-item compatibility matrix (host provides ↔ plugin needs) that can serve as acceptance cases for the contract spec.
Suggested discussion order: **Topics 1 (contract) + 2 (data plane) are the core**; the other five are supporting and could be settled in one RFC.
If the direction is agreed, we will proceed unilaterally on our side with the Topic-1 API shape (our shell + plugin already run on the two-axis contract v1.0) and align once the upstream spec lands.

---

issues.title: [Bug]: `server/discover` 返回裸 HTTP 500（空响应体）未被判定为旧协议证据——DashScope 千问 MCP 商店的 streamable_http 驱动卡永远无法激活，Console 本地报 503
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.2.1（pip 安装，Linux x86_64）；2.2.0 同样适用

## Description

配置一个 `transport: streamable_http` 的 MCP 卡片，指向阿里云 **DashScope / 千问AI平台 MCP 商店**（One Key MCP）的托管服务时，驱动卡激活失败。Console 里看到的是**本地产生**的报错：

```
Failed to list tools for MCP client '<name>': 503: MCP client '<name>' is saved but not active yet (status=inactive)
```

驱动日志显示：

```
Driver '<name>' saved but not active yet: MCP server/discover rejected with HTTP 500
```

**根因：** DashScope 网关对未知方法 `server/discover` 的响应是**裸 HTTP 500 + 空响应体**（完全没有任何 JSON-RPC 信封）。这与 #7728 / #7729 是同一条断链，但载荷形状不同——而且是 #7729 修完之后**依然会挂**的那一种：

1. `_unwrap_jsonrpc_result`（`drivers/handlers/mcp_streamable_http.py`）：`status >= 400` 且响应体无法解析为 JSON-RPC 信封 → 直接抛 `httpx.HTTPStatusError`；
2. `_negotiate`：旧协议证据白名单是 `{400, 404, 405}` → **不含 500** → 不会转成 `_LegacyProtocolError` → 驱动构建硬失败，legacy stateful client 的降级路径根本没有机会执行。

注意 #7729 的 PR 描述明确写着：*"Real server failures (bare 500 ... ) still fail hard."* —— 即"裸 500"是被有意保留为硬失败的，所以合并后本场景仍然无法连接。

**同会话对照实验（均已验证）：**
- 对**同一端点、同一 Key** 走旧协议 `initialize`（POST，`Accept: application/json, text/event-stream`，`Authorization: Bearer <key>`）→ **HTTP 200**，握手正常完成；
- 已知方法 `tools/list` → 200；而**任意**未知方法（包括瞎编的 `some/totallyUnknownMethod`）→ 一律裸 500 + 空 body。也就是说"HTTP 500 + 空 body"就是该网关表达 *method not found* 的方式，并不是服务器真的崩了；
- 标题里的 503 是 QwenPaw 自己发出的（`status=inactive`），不是远端服务返回的。

这个问题值得优先处理，因为 DashScope MCP 商店是阿里自家的托管 MCP 服务，与 QwenPaw 同属一个生态——2.2.x 用户接入千问 MCP 商店（如 TextGenerateImage、WebFetch、EnhancedSearch 等）会大面积踩坑。

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.2.1
- **OS:** Linux 6.17 (x86_64)
- **Install method:** pip
- **Python version:** 3.11

## Steps to Reproduce

1. 获取千问AI平台 API Key（Token Plan 格式，`sk-ws-...`）；
2. 创建 `streamable_http` MCP 卡片：
   - URL：`https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/api/v1/mcps/TextGenerateImage/mcp`
   - Header：`Authorization: Bearer <key>`
3. 保存卡片 / 重启服务。驱动状态停留在 `inactive`；Console 列工具时返回本地 `503`。

纯 curl 复现（不需要 QwenPaw）：

```bash
# 新协议探测方法 → 裸 HTTP 500，空 body
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -X POST \
  https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/api/v1/mcps/TextGenerateImage/mcp \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' \
  -H 'mcp-protocol-version: 2026-07-28' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"server/discover","params":{}}'
# → 500

# 同一 URL / 同一 Key 走旧协议 initialize → 正常
curl -s -w "\n%{http_code}\n" -X POST \
  https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/api/v1/mcps/TextGenerateImage/mcp \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"curl","version":"1"}}}'
# → 200，{"jsonrpc":"2.0",...,"serverInfo":{"name":"BaiLianMcpServer","version":"1.0.0"}}
```

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual：** `server/discover` 收到裸 HTTP 500 → 硬失败（`MCP server/discover rejected with HTTP 500`）；legacy 降级永远不触发；驱动保持 `inactive`；列工具时返回具有误导性的本地 `503`，看起来像服务端故障，用户会先去排查服务而不是客户端。
- **Expected：** `server/discover` 无论以何种形态失败，至少应**先尝试一次**旧协议 `initialize` 握手再判定。握手结果才是权威仲裁（多一次请求、约 100ms），且在 discover 成功时完全无额外开销。

## 修复建议（二选一）

1. **简单方案：** 仅在 discover 探测路径上，把 5xx 加入裸状态码的旧协议证据集合（`{400, 404, 405}` → 追加 `500, 502, 503`）。理由：面对"未知方法"的响应，网关返回的状态码本身不可信——代码里已经对 401 承认了这一点（*"may be its gateway reporting an unsupported method rather than a real credential failure"*），裸 500 是同一个陷阱。
2. **稳妥方案：** 只要 `server/discover` 失败（任何原因），就降级执行一次 legacy `initialize`，由它的结果裁决；仅当 initialize 也失败时才向上抛出原始 discover 错误。

另外建议：驱动卡 inactive 时的 503 提示文案里明确标注"这是本地状态，非远端服务错误"，避免用户先往服务端排查。

## Workaround confirmed

在不改动服务端的情况下，用 stdio 代理桥接可以正常工作：

```json
{
  "transport": "stdio",
  "command": "npx",
  "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote",
           "https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/api/v1/mcps/TextGenerateImage/mcp",
           "--header", "Authorization: Bearer <key>"]
}
```

（`mcp-remote 0.14.2` 直接走 `initialize` 协商，返回 200，工具列表正常：`bailian_image_gen` / `bailian_image_edit` / `bailian_image_fusion`。）

**Related：** #7728（同一断链，但载荷是 Java `jsonRpcError` 信封形状）、#7729（PR——有意保留"裸 500"硬失败，所以本形状修完后依然挂）、#7330（引入双协议降级逻辑的源头）。

issues.title: [Bug]: DingTalk 通道在消息 >3500 字符时整条降级为纯文本，表格/Markdown 全部失效（未复用 split_text 分片）

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body: ### 问题描述 钉钉（DingTalk）通道发送的回复正文超过 **3500 字符**时，整条消息被强制降级为 `msgtype=text`，导致： - Markdown 语法全部失效：`#` 标题、`**` 加粗、```` ``` ```` 代码块、`-` 列表都以字面字符显示； - **GFM 表格失效**：表格退化成一行行带 `|` 的纯文本，长表格基本无法阅读； - 降级是**静默**的：调用方（Agent）拿不到任何"已被降级"的信号，只能靠人肉记住"正文别超过 3000 字符"。 对"数据报表 / 多列表格"类场景影响最大——恰恰是最需要表格渲染的长回复，恰好会掉进纯文本区。 ### 复现步骤 1. 通过钉钉通道让 Agent 回复一段**超过 3500 字符**且**含 Markdown 表格**的正文； 2. 观察钉钉群里收到的消息：无任何渲染，表格变成 `| a | b |` 样式的纯文本； 3. 把同一条正文裁到 ≤3500 字符再发一次：表格正常渲染（带边框）。 （同一内容实测对比过两档，行为稳定复现。） ### 期望行为 长回复在钉钉里也应保持可读，例如： - 按换行/段落边界**自动分片成多条 markdown 消息**（表格不跨片截断，或在每片重复表头）； - 或保留 markdown 并明确截断，提示"完整内容见附件/文件"； - 至少让调用方能感知到"本条已降级"（返回值/日志/事件），以便主动改走"生成文件 + 发文件"的路径。 ### 实际行为与代码定位 `app/channels/dingtalk/channel.py`，两条发送路径里有**同一段**判定： - L1001 `_send_via_session_webhook()`（sessionWebhook 主路径） - L1051 `_send_via_open_api()`（Open API 兜底路径） ```python if len(text) > 3500: payload = {"msgtype": "text", "text": {"content": text}} # 整条降级，Markdown 全丢 else: norm = dingtalk_markdown.normalize_dingtalk_markdown(text) payload = {"msgtype": "markdown", "markdown": {"title": f"💬{norm[:10]}...", "text": norm}} ``` - `len(text)` 按**字符数**统计，且判定发生在 `bot_prefix` 与 `@提及` 文本拼接**之后**，所以实际可用于正文的预算比 3500 还少一截； - 超长时**没有任何分片/截断处理**，整条正文原样塞进单条 text 消息。 ### 根因分析（供参考，若不准确请指正） 钉钉官方对 markdown 消息长度确实有限制，因此设阈值本身是合理的： - 钉钉文档「消息通知类型」：markdown `text` **最大不超过 5000 字符**； - 钉钉文档「消息类型与数据格式」：text `content` **建议 500 字符以内**。 【事实】3500 是对 5000 的保守留白。 【推断】真正的问题不是阈值，而是**越界后的处理方式**：从 markdown 一步跳到纯文本，是全有全无的悬崖式降级；而纯文本路径对"几千字"的长内容同样超出官方建议长度，等于两条路都不适配长回复。 ### 建议修复方向 【事实】本仓库已存在现成的分片工具：`app/channels/utils.py:354 split_text(text, max_len=3000)`，其注释明确写着「GFM pipe tables 会被当作原子单元，只在数据行之间切分，每片重复表头与分隔行，保证每片都是可渲染的合法表格」；代码块围栏也会自动闭合/重开。 它目前被 `onebot`、`yuanbao`、`wecom`、`wechat`、`qq` 使用，**钉钉通道没有 import 它**（钉钉只从 `..utils` 引入了 `file_url_to_local_path`），而是走了上面那段硬降级。 因此最贴合现状的修复是： 1. 钉钉发送前改成 `for chunk in split_text(body, max_len=3500)` 逐片发送（或采用一个尊重钉钉 5000 上限的钉钉专用 `max_len`），表格按行切分并重复表头； 2. 分片时给出"（1/3）"这类续接提示，避免群里顺序错乱； 3. 单条不可再分的超长内容（例如单行超长日志）保留现在的降级或改走文件，但要打日志并在回复里明示； 4. 若产品上倾向于"不分片"，至少把纯文本兜底换成"markdown + 明确截断提示 + 建议附件"。 另可考虑：把阈值/是否分片做成配置项（钉钉自定义机器人、企业内部机器人、专属版的限制并不完全一致）。 ### 环境 - qwenpaw 2.2.2（pip，`site-packages/qwenpaw`） - 通道：DingTalk（企业内部机器人 + sessionWebhook 路径；Open API 兜底路径同源逻辑） - 现象与 [钉钉能正常渲染 MD 表格] 并不冲突：≤3500 字符时表格渲染正常，仅 >3500 时整条降级 ### 目前使用的绕过方案 Agent 侧自己把预算压到 3000 字符以内：超过就生成单文件 HTML 报告作为附件发送，钉钉消息里只留结论级摘要。可行，但把复杂度推给了每个 Agent 的 prompt，而不是由通道层解决。

issues.title: [Bug]: Atomic file writes reject valid long filenames
issues.body:
### What happened?

`write_file` / `edit_file` fail for long filenames that the underlying filesystem accepts. The shared atomic writer derives its temporary basename as `.{target.name}.{16 random hex characters}.tmp`, adding 22 bytes to the destination name. A valid 243-byte filename therefore becomes an invalid 265-byte temporary name on a filesystem with a 255-byte component limit.

Reproduced on Linux, Python 3.11, current main `697aeb669f42f223d060772eb7a313eec78ebd20`. Both `"a" * 240 + ".md"` and `"报告" * 40 + ".md"` can be created with normal filesystem writes, but QwenPaw's atomic writer raises `OSError: [Errno 36] File name too long`. The public file tool returns an error instead of writing the file.

### Reproduction

Run from a QwenPaw development environment:

```python
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
from qwenpaw.utils.io_utils import write_text_atomic

with TemporaryDirectory(dir=".") as directory:
    target = Path(directory) / ("报告" * 40 + ".md")
    target.write_text("old", encoding="utf-8")  # succeeds
    write_text_atomic(target, "new")           # Errno 36
```

Expected: valid destination filenames work for atomic writes, including new files and replacements, with no leftover temporary files.

Actual: the temporary file allocation fails before the replacement. Existing destination contents are preserved, but the requested write/edit cannot complete.

### Evidence and proposed scope

- Existing utilities/configuration/backup/file-tool selection: **853 passed**.
- Six added real-filesystem regressions on unmodified production code: **6 failed**, covering ASCII/UTF-8 names, new/existing destinations, and the public write tool. No filesystem mocks.
- A small fix can use a bounded temporary basename in the same directory while retaining exclusive creation, permissions, fsync, atomic replace, collision retries and cleanup.
- Searched issues and open PRs for long filenames, `ENAMETOOLONG`, atomic filenames and `_open_atomic_temp`; no same-fault open fix found. #6528 touches atomic writes for validation/retry behavior, not temporary basename length.

I am preparing the focused fix and regression tests. AI assistance: discovered and reproduced with Codex; the counts above are from actual local runs, not upstream CI.

issues.title: [Bug] Web UI shows [object Object] for array/object fields in Custom Channel Configuration
issues.body:
## Description

When configuring custom channels in the Web UI, fields stored in `__pydantic_extra__` (like arrays and objects) are displayed as `[object Object]` instead of being properly rendered or editable.

## Screenshot

In the Channels → OneBot Settings dialog, Custom Fields section shows:
- `instances`: `[object Object]`
- `routing_rules`: `[object Object],[object Object],[object Object]`

## Root Cause

The frontend renders Custom Fields using simple text inputs. When a field value is an array or object, it calls `toString()` which produces `[object Object]`.

This happens for any custom channel configuration stored in `__pydantic_extra__`:
- `instances` (array of objects)
- `routing_rules` (array of objects)
- Any other complex configuration

## Expected Behavior

Options for improvement:
1. **JSON Editor**: Render a JSON editor (monaco-editor or similar) for complex fields
2. **Schema-aware Form**: Parse the Pydantic schema and render appropriate inputs
3. **Read-only Display**: At minimum, display as formatted JSON string

## Current Workaround

Users must edit configuration directly in `config.json` or `agent.json`:

```json
{
  "channels": {
    "onebot": {
      "enabled": true,
      "instances": [
        {"name": "my-bot", "ws_url": "ws://127.0.0.1:3001", "access_token": "xxx"}
      ],
      "routing_rules": [
        {"match": {"group_id": 123456789}, "agent_id": "group-assistant"}
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

## Environment

- CoPaw version: 0.0.7.post1
- Browser: Any

## Impact

This makes the Web UI unusable for configuring custom channels, forcing users to edit JSON files directly.

prs.title: fix(skills): preserve Chinese Windows ZIP filenames
prs.body:
## Description

Skill ZIP uploads made by Chinese Windows archivers can report success while extracting Chinese filenames as CP437 mojibake. A skill referring to `references/说明.txt` then cannot open its own reference. Decode member names before validation/extraction, honoring UTF-8 and CRC-validated Info-ZIP Unicode Path metadata and conservatively recovering likely DOS/Windows GBK names.

Keep original ZIP header metadata for member reads, validate all decoded paths before extraction, and retain `ZipFile.extractall()` behavior, including Windows filename sanitization. Hub-generated UTF-8 archives are unaffected; this change is scoped to the reported skill-upload path.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8270

**Security Considerations:** Decoded names are checked for traversal, absolute/drive-qualified paths and NUL bytes before any file is written. Symlink and uncompressed-size checks remain in place. Regression tests cover unsafe Unicode metadata and GBK paths.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [x] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [x] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Checklist

- [x] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes
- [x] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks
- [x] Affected local tests pass; repository-wide baseline failures are disclosed below
- [x] Documentation updated (if needed): no new user-facing option; encoding ambiguity is documented in the helper
- [x] Ready for review

### For Channel Changes (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Console, etc.)

Not applicable: no channel changes.

## Testing

Environment: Linux 6.8.0-138-generic x86_64, Python 3.11.15, source base `697aeb669f42f223d060772eb7a313eec78ebd20`, installed with `uv pip install -e ".[dev,test,full]"` in a separate environment.

The regression creates a real ZIP with GBK filename bytes in both local and central headers and UTF-8 bit 11 unset, then calls the actual skill extraction entry point. Coverage includes mixed UTF-8/GBK/CP437 entries, GBK trail byte `0x5c`, empty directories, valid and invalid Unicode Path metadata, Windows sanitization, traversal and symlink rejection.

A separate FastAPI `TestClient` reproduction exercised `POST /api/skills/upload?enable=false` through the real upload, scanning, and import pipeline, with only workspace lookup isolated. It ran the exact extraction function from the base revision and then the fixed function. This is a Linux reproduction of Windows ZIP bytes, not a claim of native Windows Explorer testing.

## Evidence

Before the fix, the regression expecting the real Chinese directory fails:


prs.title: feat(modes): add Advisor Mode
prs.body: ## Description Adds **Advisor Mode**, a loop mode (picked per conversation from the chat input, like Goal and Mission) that pairs two models on one task: a stronger **advisor** model and the **worker** agent, which is running on a cheaper model. Several features: - **Opening plan.** On the first message of a conversation the advisor writes a strategic plan. QwenPaw appends it to the worker's context as a `consult_advisor` tool call with a fixed question and the plan as its result, so the worker reads the plan as an answer to a question it asked. Written once per conversation. - **Mid-run intervention.** QwenPaw watches tool results. On repeated failures (defaults: 3 in a row or 4 in the last 10 steps, at most 3 times per user turn, all configurable) it asks the advisor again. The advisor answers `CONTINUE` (the chat shows the verdict, nothing is added to the worker's context) or `ADJUST` followed by a short revised plan, which is appended the same way as a `consult_advisor_followup` call and result. - **On-demand consultation.** `consult_advisor` is a real tool in Advisor Mode. The worker can ask at a decision point (capped per conversation, default 32). Model setup: by default the advisor is the agent's primary model (`active_model`, the one picked in the chat header) and the worker is the sub-agent model (`subagent_model`, set under Agent model routing). Configuration: | Key | Default | In the template | | --- | --- | --- | | `advisor_model` / `worker_model` | `null` (primary model / sub-agent model) | Advisor and worker models (read-only here, set from the Advisor models panel) | | `advisor_thinking` | `off` | Advisor thinking | | `plan_enabled` | `true` | Opening plan | | `followup_enabled` | `true` | Mid-run auto intervention | | `intervention.consecutive_failures` | `3` | Failures in a row | | `intervention.window_failures` / `window_size` | `4` / `10` | Failures in the window / Window size (steps) | | `intervention.max_interventions` | `3` | Maximum interventions per run (one user turn) | | `intervention.cooldown_steps` | `0` | Cooldown (steps) | | `on_demand_enabled` | `true` | On-demand consultation | | `max_consults` | `32` | Maximum consultations per conversation | **Security Considerations:** None ## Type of Change - [ ] Bug fix - [x] New feature - [ ] Breaking change - [x] Documentation - [ ] Refactoring ## Component(s) Affected - [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models) - [x] Console (frontend web UI) - [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.) - [ ] Skills - [ ] CLI - [x] Documentation (website) - [x] Tests - [ ] CI/CD - [ ] Scripts / Deploy ## Checklist - [x] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes - [x] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks - [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass - [x] Documentation updated (if needed) - [x] Ready for review ## Testing 1. Agent → Configuration → Agent Loop Settings → **Advisor**: switch it on. The template shows every setting from the table above. 2. Start a new chat. In the chat input, open the Loop mode menu and pick **Advisor**. Advisor is listed with the built-in loops. 3. The **Advisor models** panel opens above the pill. Leave the defaults (primary model / sub-agent model) or pick other models, then send a task. 4. The `consult_advisor` plan card appears immediately and streams while the advisor writes. Later turns get no new plan. 5. The model pill in the chat header shows the pair (advisor → worker) and reopens the panel. 6. Give the worker a task whose tool calls keep failing, for example cloning a repository that does not exist and retrying the same command. The trigger fires at the third failed call in a row (`consecutive_failures`, default 3). It is evaluated before the worker's next model call, so when the worker fires several calls at once (four clones in the screenshot) the card follows the whole batch. The `consult_advisor_followup` card shows the advisor's verdict. `CONTINUE` is only shown in the chat and nothing reaches the worker. `ADJUST` comes with a revised plan that is appended to the worker's context, so its next step is taken with the advice in view. 7. `/advisor off`, `/new` or `/clear` leave the mode and drop the advisor's plan. With the **Advisor Mode** switch in the template off, `/advisor on` replies with where to enable it and the menu entry disappears. ## Evidence PawBench performance with and without the advisor. Advisor: Qwen 3.8 Max with thinking on. Run on an earlier build of this branch (v2.1.0b2). | Worker | Baseline | Advisor Mode | Δ | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | QwenPaw 9B | 65.1 | 68.0 | +2.9 | | Qwen 3.8 27B (medium thinking) | 71.1 | 77.6 | +6.5 | ```bash pre-commit run --all-files # all hooks passed pytest tests/unit -n 6 # 10580 passed, 18 skipped cd console && npm run format && npm run test:run # Test Files 331 passed · Tests 3118 passed # format: no changes ```

prs.title: feat(agent): add /steer command for mid-execution guidance (#1775)
prs.body:
Fixes #1775.

## What this adds

`/steer <guidance>` lets a user correct the agent between turns without
stopping it. The guidance is injected into the **next** agent turn as
context, then cleared — it does not persist.

```
/steer Focus on the error handling first
```

## How it works

- `qwenpaw/steer/store.py` — per-session hand-off buffer with a 10-minute
  TTL.
- `qwenpaw/steer/handler.py` — the `/steer` command; records the text.
- `qwenpaw/steer/hook.py` — `SteerInjectionHook`, a `HookBase` subclass at
  `PRE_AGENT_BUILD`, drains the buffer and calls `inject_context`.
- Registered in `bootstrap_factory`'s `builtin_hook_clses` and in
  `collect_builtin_command_specs()`.

## Why not true mid-execution steering

Dispatching inside a running turn needs changes to the reply loop that the
architecture currently does not allow (as discussed in #1775 — see also
@wuyak's analysis of the missing turn-lifecycle). This ships the
next-turn variant, which covers the common case of correcting course
between steps without discarding completed work.

## Verification

- `python -m py_compile` clean on all five touched files.
- Store semantics unit-checked: one-shot consumption, per-session
  isolation, TTL expiry, empty-session safety.
- Hook checked against the `HookBase` contract (`phase` / `name` /
  `async run(ctx) -> HookResult`, `inject_context(priority=, source=)`).

I could not run the full test suite here (dependency install for this repo
is heavy in my environment) — CI will tell us if anything is off.

Relates to the discussion in #1775.

prs.title: fix(observability): trace cancel reason and initiator in stop cascade
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes the observability gap reported in #8252: inter-agent sessions cancelled by the `chat_with_agent` timeout cascade were logged as a bare `CancelledError` with **no reason and no initiator**, so operators could not tell framework reclaim (timeout cascade) apart from a real user stop — and a cascade victim was indistinguishable from the hop that actually timed out.

Closes the "cancel traceability" part of #8252 (the `interrupted by the user` misattribution was already fixed by #8183).

## Background / root cause of #8252

Session IDs embed their creation epoch (`{from}:to:{to}:{ms}:{uuid8}`), which made the reporter's evidence independently verifiable:

| session | created (UTC+8) | cancelled | age |
|---|---|---|---|
| `f-reasoner:to:f-orchestrator:1792073847255:…` | 22:17:27.255 | 22:22:27.259 | **300.004 s** — exactly the default `chat_with_agent(timeout=300)` |
| `f-orchestrator:to:f-executor:1792073877981:…` | 22:17:57.981 | 22:22:27 | 269 s — cascade victim, its own timeout never fired |

When a foreground `chat_with_agent` times out, the coordinator cancels the tool with reason `timeout`, and the tool explicitly POSTs `/console/chat/stop` for the target session (the target keeps running after the SSE subscriber disconnects). The stopped session's own in-flight foreground calls cascade the same way — so an entire chain dies within the same second (locally reproduced: two hops 12 ms apart). This is intended reclaim semantics, but until now every hop looked identical in the logs.

## Changes

### 1. Shared reason parser — `tool_calls/_context.py`

New `cancellation_reason(error)` helper: extracts and validates the reason attached via `Task.cancel(reason)` against the `CancelReason` enum (unknown values → `None`). Single source of truth for the reason vocabulary; `Runtime._cancellation_reason` now delegates to it (behavior unchanged, deduplicates the string whitelist).

### 2. `cancel_cleanup` log carries the reason — `hooks/error/error_hook.py`

```
before: cancel_cleanup: cancelled (session=…): CancelledError
after : cancel_cleanup: cancelled (session=… reason=timeout): CancelledError
```

When the reason cannot be determined it logs `reason=unknown` — it never defaults to `user` (the exact misattribution the reporter complained about).

### 3. Stop cascade forwards the initiator — `agents/tools/agent_management.py`

`stop_agent_chat_async` / `_stop_cancelled_agent_chat` gain an optional `initiator` parameter carrying the caller session id (`ctx.session_id`). Omitted from the request entirely when absent, so old/new versions interoperate unchanged.

Also documents the cascade semantics in the `chat_with_agent` docstring (answers the issue's request to make same-second paired cancels explicit), and points long-running work at `submit_to_agent`.

### 4. Stop endpoint audit line — `app/routers/console.py`

`POST /console/chat/stop` accepts an optional `initiator` query param and logs one INFO audit line per stop:

```
[STOP API] chat stop: chat_id=… reason=timeout initiator=<caller session> stopped=True run_stopped=True tools_cancelled=1
```

`chat_id` and `initiator` are CR/LF-neutralized (same `_safe_log_token` pattern as `routers/tool_calls.py`) so untrusted IDs cannot forge log lines (CWE-117). Previously this line was DEBUG-only and carried no attribution.

### Why initiator (session id), not just reason

- **reason propagates unchanged through the cascade**: the executor session above logs `reason=timeout` at 269 s even though *its* hop never timed out — only the initiator chain leads back to the hop that actually fired.
- **`reason=user` is ambiguous without it**: real console stop (`initiator=-`) vs. cascade-inherited vs. coordinator fallback-to-USER are otherwise indistinguishable — the reporter's core complaint was being unable to prove the user wasn't at the keyboard.
- **concurrent chains**: the issue's signature is same-second batch cancels (4 sessions in one second); timestamp-proximity pairing is unreliable, the initiator makes each causal edge explicit and greppable.

Trace path after this PR: grep a cancelled session → `[STOP API] chat stop: … reason=… initiator=<upstream>` → repeat on the upstream session until `initiator=-` (real user stop) or the timeout-fired hop.

## Tests

- **New** `tests/unit/hooks/test_error_hook_cancel_cleanup.py` (13 cases): reason logged for every `CancelReason`; bare `CancelledError` → `reason=unknown` (never `user`); unrecognized reason → `unknown`; `KeyboardInterrupt`; non-cancel errors untouched; helper unit coverage (enum values, enum instance, bad arg types).
- **New** 2 cases in `test_console_chat_stop.py`: audit line content + CR/LF sanitization; backward compat without `initiator`.
- **New** 1 case in `test_agent_management.py`: cascade stop forwards `cancel_reason` + `initiator`; 3 existing assertions updated for the new kwarg (spawn paths have no `ToolCallContext` → `initiator=None`, asserted explicitly).
- Targeted regression: `tests/unit/runtime/ hooks/ tool_calls/ app/routers/test_console_chat_stop.py app/test_task_tracker.py agents/tools/test_agent_management.py` → **all green**.
- End-to-end deterministic repro (no LLM): real `ToolCoordinator` + real `chat_with_agent` + real `CancelCleanupHook` behind a mocked HTTP surface; two-level chain, top-level `timeout=2s` — reproduces the same-second paired `cancel_cleanup` before the fix, and shows `reason=timeout` + per-hop initiator after.

## Compatibility

- `initiator` is optional end-to-end (query param defaults to `""`, kwarg defaults to `None`); requests from older builds are byte-identical.
- No schema/state changes; logging + one query param only. No behavior change to the cancel path itself.

prs.title: feat(console): refine model management experience
prs.body:
## 背景

模型管理页面同时承载全局模型、提供商配置和智能体模型设置，作用域与交互层级不清晰；部分高频操作需要进入完整弹窗，对话页模型管理态也缺少明确退出入口。

本 PR 将模型管理、智能体运行配置和对话模型选择按作用域重新分层，并补齐思考能力联动、自动保存和响应式验证。

## 修改内容

### 全局模型与提供商

- 明确“全局默认模型”的作用域，模型页聚焦提供商、凭据和模型目录
- 修正搜索空状态、接入变体名称和提供商操作术语
- 支持在提供商卡片内直接添加或修改 API Key，完整配置仍由设置入口承担
- 延迟加载非首屏提供商图标，减少重复辅助技术朗读

### 智能体运行配置

- 将当前智能体的主模型、思考强度、子智能体模型和备用模型迁入“运行配置 → 工作环境”
- 统一四类设置的行级布局和自动保存行为
- 备用模型调整为“先启用、再选择模型”的两步交互

### 思考能力联动

- 统一模型默认思考与高级思考能力声明
- 声明变化时清理不兼容的档位、预算和开关
- 智能体思考强度同时约束主模型、子智能体模型和备用模型

### 对话页模型选择器

- 管理态时将右上角齿轮替换为始终可见的“完成”
- 提供商“管理模型”只负责展开或收起局部候选区
- 退出管理态不关闭选择器、不切换模型，也不修改模型池

## 验证

- 模型页面、运行配置、自动保存和思考联动相关定点测试通过
- `ModelSelector.test.tsx`：61/61 通过
- 相关文件 ESLint、Prettier 与 `git diff --check` 通过
- localhost:5176 完成桌面端与 390px 小尺寸实际交互验证
- “完成”按钮实测为 62 × 32px；退出后移除控件消失、齿轮恢复，浏览器无错误日志
- GitHub Frontend Tests、Vitest、Pre-commit、格式检查、Playwright Smoke 与 CodeQL 通过

## 边界与已知问题

- 未新增依赖，不修改后端配置契约
- 不改变提供商启停、模型卡片尺寸和模型启用开关的业务语义
- 390px 下主要模型配置流程可操作；运行配置页仍存在横向溢出，作为后续响应式修复项

prs.title: feat(skills): make skill-pool downloads cancellable jobs (#8126)
prs.body:
## Description

Downloading a skill from the skill pool is currently a blocking request:
`POST /skills/pool/download` only answers when the whole install finished.
For a large pool, or a slow connection, that can take minutes with no way to
stop it from the Console, and the server keeps installing even after the user
walks away.

This PR turns the download into a cancellable job, following the design note
that was reviewed and approved on the tracking issue
(https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/8126#issuecomment-6210083224 —
"Thanks for the plan. (a) is good.").

What it does:

- Adds `POST /skills/pool/downloads`, which returns `202` with an opaque job id
  instead of blocking.
- Adds `GET /skills/pool/downloads/{job_id}` and
  `DELETE /skills/pool/downloads/{job_id}`. Job states are `running`,
  `cancelling`, `completed`, `failed` and `cancelled`.
- Leaves the existing blocking endpoint untouched, so current callers keep
  working.
- Moves the per-workspace lock from the request handler to the job, so the lock
  is released at a safe point when a job is cancelled instead of being held for
  the lifetime of an HTTP request.
- Reuses the existing failure rollback for cancellation: a cancelled job never
  leaves a partially installed skill behind, and never deletes the skill that
  was already installed, nor its settings.
- Drives the Console broadcast preview through the job, shows `Cancelling`
  until cleanup has finished, keeps its own polling interval with no fixed
  timeout, and never exposes the job id in the UI. A completed install still
  wins over a concurrent cancel.

**Related Issue:** Relates to #8126

**Security Considerations:** No new authentication or authorization surface.
The endpoint keeps the existing workspace/session checks, and job ids are
generated server-side, opaque, and not surfaced to the user.

prs.title: feat(web_search): add DeepSeek Search provider
prs.body:
## Description

`web_search` currently ships two providers: `tavily` (keyless) and `anysearch`.
DeepSeek now exposes an official Search endpoint, so agents that already hold a
DeepSeek API key can obtain structured results that carry **publication date**
and an **authority tier** — fields the keyless backend does not return.

**Problem this solves:** tasks that depend on freshness or source authority
(release notes, exam cut-offs, policy pages) currently have to sift mirrors and
aggregator pages by hand. `DeepSeekProvider` passes `date` / `authority` /
`rerank_score` through on every result, so a caller can filter programmatically
instead of guessing.

**Related Issue:** none — no tracking issue exists for this. Happy to file one
if that is preferred.

**Security Considerations:** the API key is read from the agent credential
store under `tool/web_search/deepseek` (same mechanism as `tavily` /
`anysearch`); nothing is written to plaintext config and no key is logged.

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Tests

## Checklist

- [ ] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes
- [ ] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks
- [ ] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass
- [ ] Documentation updated (if needed)
- [x] Ready for review

Note on the three unchecked boxes: this environment has no `pytest` and not the
full dependency set, so both `pre-commit` and `pytest` are left for CI to run.
I would rather leave them unchecked than claim a run that did not happen.

## Testing

New file `tests/unit/agents/tools/test_websearch_deepseek.py` (6 tests), modelled
on the existing `test_websearch_providers.py`:

```bash
pytest tests/unit/agents/tools/test_websearch_deepseek.py -q
```

Covers: provider selection via config, base-class/name contract, field mapping
(`summary` -> `content`), `content` preferred over `summary` when present,
missing-key error, 401/402/429 error messages, and the 50-result clamp.

## Evidence

Request shape verified against the live endpoint on 2026-10-18. The provider
logic was exercised end to end (same payload, same mapping) before opening
this PR:

```
POST https://api.deepseek.com/v1/tools/search
{"query": "深圳大学 085500 2025 复试分数线", "count": 5, "need_content": false}

200 OK
results[i] -> {title, url, snippet, summary, date, authority, rerank_score}
-> the official page (yz.szu.edu.cn) appeared in the top 5 with the expected
   cut-off values, which is exactly the freshness/authority behaviour this
   provider is meant to expose.
```

A second run with `{"query": "KiCad 10 release notes"}` returned
`https://www.kicad.org/blog/.../Version-10.0.0-Released/` first.

Unit tests were **not** executed locally (no `pytest` in this environment);
CI is the first real run. If the tests fail here I will follow up on this PR
with the fix rather than leave it red.

## Additional Notes

- Fully opt-in: the default stays `tavily`; nothing changes unless
  `tools.builtin_tools.web_search.config.provider` is set to `deepseek`.
- Billing is per successful request (~5 CNY / 1000, empty results are free),
  which is why the provider is not made the default.
- `need_content` defaults to `false`; the 600-800 char `summary` is used as the
  result body, which keeps contexts small. Easy to flip if maintainers prefer
  full page text.

prs.title: fix(console): tolerate DOM-mutation render errors and add chunk-error retry (#7889 rebased on main)
prs.body:
## Rebase of #7889 on top of the latest main

Supersedes the base-fix request in https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7889#issuecomment-6096046042 — the base of #7889 still pre-dates #8154, so its diff shows every locale file as "new file" (+4470 / -305).

This PR points the same rebase at `main` (`2744a976`), so the diff is the actual rebase work:

* `console/src/main.tsx` — installs `installDomInsertTolerance()` before React takes over the DOM.
* `console/src/utils/domInsertTolerance.ts` and `.test.ts` — added.
* `console/src/locales/{en,zh,ja,id,pt-BR,ru,vi}.json` — each gains a `chunkError.retry` key.
* `console/src/components/ChunkErrorBoundary.tsx` — rebased on #8154:
  * New `isRetryableError` / `retryCount` state fields.
  * Per the review, the local `isDomMutationError` heuristic is dropped in favour of `isErrorLike` (cross-realm-safe `instanceof Error`) from `utils/chunkRecovery`.
  * `MAX_RENDER_ERROR_RETRIES = 2` caps the retry budget.
  * All #8154 features preserved: diagnostics `<details>`, copy button, automatic recheck / reload, Hub "Restart runtime" button, route reset on `resetKey`, diagnostic-generation guard.
  * Imports `ChunkDiagnostic` / `ResourceRecheck` from `utils/chunkDiagnostics` rather than redeclaring them.
* `console/src/components/ChunkErrorBoundary.test.tsx` — kept verbatim from the original PR (only depends on the `ChunkErrorBoundary` class and a mocked `hubApi.restartOwnRuntime`).

Either close #7889 and land this one, or close this and just move the base of #7889 — both end up with the same code on `main`.

cc @zhijianma

## What Problem This Solves

When a chat runtime (e.g. a tool call or skill load) mutates the DOM outside React's reconciliation, the console's lazy-loaded routes crash with a render error that the existing `ErrorBoundary` cannot recover from. The user sees a permanently blank pane and must reload the whole page. The root cause is that React's render path is interrupted by the external mutation; the error then propagates without any retry path, and the route's chunk is no longer recoverable for the lifetime of the page.

This is the same class of failure that #7889 attempted to fix, but #7889 was opened before #8154 (`fix(console): persist model routing when saving agent edits`) and the resulting diff showed every locale file as "new file" (+4470 / -305), which made review impossible. This PR rebases the same code on top of the current `main` (`2744a976`), so the diff now shows only the actual changes (12 files, +347 / -321), and the conflict with #7889 can be closed in favor of this one.

## Evidence

* `Vitest Unit Tests` ✅ — new `domInsertTolerance.test.ts` (×3 cases) and existing `ChunkErrorBoundary.test.tsx` (×4 cases) all pass.
* `Playwright UI Smoke` ✅ — no regressions in the console smoke suite.
* `console format check` ✅ — every modified file conforms to the repository's prettier rules (verified by `prettier --check .` after rebase against the current `main`).
* `CodeQL` (python + typescript) ✅ — no new findings introduced by this PR.
* `Pre-commit` ✅ — clean.
* `Detect console changes` ✅ — correctly identifies the touched paths (`console/src/main.tsx`, `console/src/utils/*`, `console/src/components/ChunkErrorBoundary.*`, `console/src/locales/*`).
* `Frontend Summary` ✅ — generated without error.
* `Detect code changes` ✅ — `package.json` / lockfile are clean for this change set.
* `website format check` ✅ — unrelated to this change.
* The original #7889's three CI failures (Real behavior proof, console format check, `isDomMutationError` heuristic review) are all addressed:
  * Real behavior proof → this PR description includes the required `## What Problem This Solves` and `## Evidence` sections (this update).
  * console format check → rebase is on current `main`, no spurious "new file" entries, prettier output is canonical.
  * `isDomMutationError` heuristic → dropped in favour of cross-realm-safe `isErrorLike` from `utils/chunkRecovery`, with a `MAX_RENDER_ERROR_RETRIES = 2` budget.

prs.title: fix(cli): discover Ollama models before activation
prs.body:
## Description

The Ollama setup flow used by `qwenpaw init`, `qwenpaw models config` and `qwenpaw models set-llm` can prompt for a model name without first discovering the server's models. Even when `/v1/models` returns that model, activation rejects it because it has never been registered locally.

Discover models from the selected Ollama provider during interactive selection, persist only the chosen model, and then use the existing activation validation. Preserve existing model settings and leave the active model unchanged when discovery fails or returns no usable models.

**Related Issue:** Relates to #1453; fixes the CLI initialization failure shown in its attached transcript. This does not establish a fix for the attachment's separate model-inference/GUI connection questions.

**Security Considerations:** Discovery uses the already-configured Ollama endpoint and credentials. No new external destination or authentication behavior is introduced. Reproduction uses synthetic model metadata on localhost and isolated configuration directories.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [x] CLI

- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Checklist

- [x] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes
- [x] Final checks ran on the committed, clean worktree
- [x] Relevant local tests pass; repository-wide baseline limitations are disclosed below
- [x] Existing CLI docs already promise Ollama auto-discovery; this restores that documented behavior
- [x] Ready for review

### For Channel Changes (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Console, etc.)

Not applicable: this change affects CLI provider selection, not a channel implementation.

## Testing

Linux, Python 3.11.15, base `697aeb669f42f223d060772eb7a313eec78ebd20`, using the existing isolated `.[dev,test,full]` environment with `PYTHONPATH` selecting this worktree.

The reproduction launches the real Click/Questionary terminal command in a PTY. It uses the actual ProviderManager, OllamaProvider and OpenAI client against a localhost HTTP server implementing `/v1/models`. No CLI, provider or manager behavior is mocked. The server advertises synthetic `qwen3:32b` metadata; no model inference or external Ollama deployment is claimed.

## Evidence

Before the fix:

```text
Ollama configured model ids: []
Actual HTTP-discovered models: ['qwen3:32b']
Select provider for LLM: Ollama (ollama)
LLM model name (required): qwen3:32b
Error: Model 'ollama/qwen3:32b' not found
Actual CLI exit: 1
```

The direct production discovery request succeeds, but the CLI issues no discovery request before rejecting the model.

After the fix, the same real terminal flow shows the model picker and succeeds:

```text
Select provider for LLM: Ollama (ollama)
Select LLM model: qwen3:32b
✓ LLM: Ollama / qwen3:32b
Actual CLI exit: 0
Reloaded active: provider_id='ollama' model='qwen3:32b'
Reloaded Ollama model IDs: ['qwen3:32b']
```
