issues.body:
## Problem

`zeptoclaw serve` (`src/cli/serve.rs`) exposes `POST /v1/chat/completions` and `GET /v1/models` with no authentication at all. The module doc says so: "No panel UI, no auth middleware — intended for local or trusted-network use."

The default bind is `127.0.0.1`, but nothing stops `--bind 0.0.0.0`. Once bound off-loopback, anyone who can reach the port can:

- spend the operator's provider credits: the route is a pass-through to the configured provider chain, using the operator's API keys
- pick any model the provider accepts, with any `max_tokens`, at any rate (no rate limiting)
- enumerate configured models via `/v1/models`

Nothing warns at startup when it binds to a non-loopback address without auth.

For comparison, the panel server (`src/api/server.rs`) mounts the same `/v1/*` routes behind `auth_middleware`, which requires a Bearer token and skips only CSRF for `/v1/`. That router also applies a 1 MiB `DefaultBodyLimit`, which `serve` lacks. So the gap is specific to the standalone `serve` command.

Minor: the comment in `server.rs` ("auth skipped by auth_middleware for /v1/ prefix") is stale. Only CSRF is skipped; the middleware regression test confirms `/v1/` requires Bearer auth.

## Proposal

1. Add an optional bearer token: `--api-key` / `ZEPTOCLAW_SERVE_API_KEY`, checked with a constant-time comparison on every `/v1/*` request (`401` + `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` otherwise). OpenAI clients already send `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.
2. Fail closed off-loopback: refuse to start when `--bind` is not a loopback address and no key is set, unless the operator passes an explicit `--insecure-no-auth`.
3. Apply the same 1 MiB `DefaultBodyLimit` the panel router uses (shared constant).
4. Optionally reuse `SlidingWindowRateLimiter` per peer IP, as panel login does.
5. Fix the stale comment in `server.rs`.

## Acceptance

- Tests: no key + loopback serves as today; key set → missing/wrong token is 401, correct token is 200; non-loopback bind without key and without `--insecure-no-auth` errors at startup.
- `docs/claude/commands.md` and CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md describe the new flags.

issues.body:
## Problem

Since #710 enabled Anthropic prompt caching, Claude responses report three input counters:

- `input_tokens`: only the uncached tail of the prompt
- `cache_read_input_tokens`: prefix served from cache (billed ~0.1x)
- `cache_creation_input_tokens`: prefix written to cache (billed ~1.25x for 5-min TTL)

`src/providers/claude.rs` deserializes all three, but only logs the cache fields (`log_cache_usage`). It builds `Usage::new(input_tokens, output_tokens)` in both `chat` and `chat_stream`, so cache tokens are dropped before they reach:

- `TokenBudget::record` (`src/agent/budget.rs`), so the token budget undercounts, often by most of the prompt on long sessions
- `CostTracker` / `estimate_cost` (`src/utils/cost.rs`), so cost is wrong in both directions: cache writes are underbilled, and the cache-read discount is never modelled
- telemetry / metrics, which report the same partial counts

## Proposal

1. Add optional `cache_read_tokens` / `cache_creation_tokens` to `providers::Usage` (default 0; OpenAI's `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` can map into `cache_read_tokens` later).
2. Populate them in the Claude non-streaming and SSE paths.
3. Token budget: count total prompt tokens (`input + cache_read + cache_creation`) so the limit reflects real context size.
4. Cost: add optional `cache_read_cost_per_million` / `cache_write_cost_per_million` to `ModelPricing`, defaulting to 0.1x / 1.25x input price when unset.
5. Surface the cache hit ratio in telemetry.

## Acceptance

- Unit tests: a Claude response with cache counters yields the right `Usage`, budget totals and cost.
- Existing providers without cache fields behave exactly as before.

Follow-up to #661 / #710.

prs.title: fix(serve): require an API key for the OpenAI-compatible serve API
prs.body:
## Summary

- `zeptoclaw serve` exposed `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/models` with no authentication. A non-loopback `--bind` let anyone reaching the port spend the operator's provider credits with any model at any rate. With `ZEPTOCLAW_SERVE_API_KEY` or `--api-key` set, every `/v1/*` request now needs `Authorization: Bearer <key>`: constant-time compare, and an OpenAI-style `401` with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` otherwise. Blank keys count as unset.
- Fail closed off-loopback: without a key, `serve` refuses to start on a non-loopback bind unless `--insecure-no-auth` is passed, and logs a warning when it is. The default `127.0.0.1` bind with no key behaves exactly as before.
- Applies the panel's 1 MiB body limit, now a shared `api::server::API_BODY_LIMIT_BYTES`. The router and bind guard live in the new `api::serve` module, so they are unit-tested; `cli/serve.rs` is a thin wrapper. The key is read from the env by hand, because clap's `env` feature isn't enabled and adding it isn't worth the binary size.
- Fixes the stale `server.rs` comment: the panel's own `/v1/*` routes already require its Bearer token and skip only CSRF.
- Separate commit: fixes `tests/e2e.rs`, which stopped compiling after #712 added fields to `Usage`. The lib-only checklist doesn't build integration tests, so it slipped through.

Not included: per-IP rate limiting (optional in the issue); can follow if wanted.

## Related Issue

Closes #713

- [x] I added or updated tests for my changes
- [x] New constants/limits are shared (not duplicated across files)
- [x] No new dependencies unless necessary (we target ~6 MB binary)

## Security Considerations

- Untrusted input: the `Authorization` header is compared in constant time (`api::auth::constant_time_eq`, `subtle`). Bodies are capped at 1 MiB.
- Network listener: auth is on whenever a key is set. An unauthenticated non-loopback listener now requires an explicit `--insecure-no-auth`. `localhost`, `127.0.0.0/8` and `::1` / `[::1]` count as loopback; hostnames and anything unparsable count as non-loopback (fail closed).
- Secrets: the key is never logged. The `--api-key` help text recommends the env var, since flags are visible in `ps`.

- `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` and `cargo clippy --features panel -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo fmt -- --check` clean

Not caused by this PR.

  - key resolution (flag over env, blank ignored)
  - no key → 200
  - missing / wrong / non-Bearer tokens → 401 with `WWW-Authenticate`

### Summary

Give empty Config sections a clear Add action and explain the next required setup steps.

### Problem statement

Empty TTS alias and model-route lists show only `[+ Add]` and `?=help`. They do not explain whether the section is optional, simply unconfigured, or incomplete. The alias-name form does not show what the operator will need to configure next.

Observed in a real 120-column by 40-row ZeroCode Config session at `625285ce43a27ed06711113347b0e5aea2f5d4c9`, using a daemon reporting v0.8.5. This is a follow-up to #11460; its provider-rename and navigation scope remains separate.

### Proposed solution

Show a concise section-specific empty state and discoverable Add action. Explain which fields are required after creating an entry and guide the operator to them using canonical schema metadata.

### Non-goals / out of scope

The small mouse activation repair for `[+ Add]` stays in #11460. This issue concerns explanation and setup guidance. It does not redesign Quickstart or change creation/persistence semantics.

### Alternatives considered

Relying on the help overlay still requires the operator to infer whether anything is missing and which fields are needed.

### Acceptance criteria

- Empty provider and route lists explain their current state and how to add an entry.
- Optional sections are not presented as required failures.
- Required-field guidance comes from the existing schema/validation contract.
- The alias form explains what creation will do and what remains to configure.
- Cancelling setup leaves the configuration unchanged.

### Architecture impact

ZeroCode Config empty-list/create rendering, locale strings, and existing schema/validation metadata. Related prior scope: #7117.

### Risk and rollback

Incorrect guidance could imply an optional section is mandatory or an incomplete entry is ready. Use existing readiness/validation facts and verify both optional and required examples. Rollback removes the guidance only.

### Expected routing

Ordinary feature triage

### Next decision surface

Ordinary issue triage should select a bounded Config UI implementation slice.

### Breaking change?

No

### Affected component

runtime/daemon

### Severity

S2 - degraded behavior

### Current behavior

I do not see a budget warning in ZeroCode despite having `cost.warn_at_percent` configured. Source inspection at `c9b08abddc5115dc864a9c5f5609780f95416811` identifies a concrete gap: `CostTracker::check_budget` returns `BudgetCheck::Warning` when recorded spend reaches the configured percentage, but `enforce_tool_loop_budget` handles only `BudgetCheck::Exceeded`. The warning result falls through without being surfaced.

Sources: [threshold calculation](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/c9b08abddc5115dc864a9c5f5609780f95416811/crates/zeroclaw-config/src/cost/tracker.rs#L136) and [runtime consumer](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/c9b08abddc5115dc864a9c5f5609780f95416811/crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/agent/turn/provider_call.rs#L119).

The running binary's exact revision and a live threshold crossing have not been established. This report does not claim that cost accounting or hard-limit enforcement is broken.

### Expected behavior

When a configured daily or monthly warning threshold is reached, surface a non-blocking operator-visible warning, including in ZeroCode. Identify the period, recorded spend, and limit. Avoid repeating the warning on every provider call. Preserve hard-limit enforcement and conversation contents.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
# Deterministic regression scenario to implement; not executed for this report:
# 1. Enable cost tracking with daily_limit_usd=10, monthly_limit_usd=100,
#    and warn_at_percent=80 in an isolated configuration.
# 2. Seed recorded usage of $8 for the current day, below the hard limit.
# 3. Confirm check_budget(0.0) returns BudgetCheck::Warning.
# 4. Exercise the production pre-provider budget check and observe that
#    the warning is ignored instead of delivered to the operator.
# Repeat with monthly usage at its warning threshold and daily usage below it.
```

### Impact

Users cannot rely on the advertised early-warning setting to notice approaching spend limits. This is separate from missing pricing or zero-cost accounting reports such as #9816: even a correctly calculated Warning is ignored by this runtime consumer.

### Logs / stack traces

_No response; source inspection rather than a captured runtime trace._

### ZeroClaw version

Source inspected: `c9b08abddc5115dc864a9c5f5609780f95416811`. Running binary revision unverified.

### Rust version

_Not collected; no build or test run for this report._

### Operating system

Observed through ZeroCode on macOS; the inspected warning-consumer path is not OS-specific.

Unknown

issues.body:
## Summary

ZeroCode Dashboard should expose the active runtime context.

## Problem statement

ZeroCode can connect to different daemon/config roots, workspaces, agents, runtime profiles, and session states. Today the Dashboard does not make that context clear enough, so users have to infer it indirectly from downstream panes or error messages.

This is especially confusing when a temporary/minimal config, test daemon, or non-default workspace is active. The app does not give the user a persistent top-level answer to questions like:

- Which config am I looking at?
- Which daemon am I connected to?
- Are my TUI and daemon versions matched?
- What workspace/CWD will Chat or Code use?
- Which agent/model/runtime profile is currently selected?
- Is a session running, paused, queued, waiting for approval, or unhealthy?

## Proposed solution

Make the ZeroCode Dashboard the compact orientation surface for active runtime context.

Useful fields include:

- active config directory and config file, with temporary/local configs clearly labeled
- TUI version and daemon version, with a clear mismatch warning
- daemon endpoint, PID, and uptime
- current Chat and Code workspace/CWD
- selected agent, model provider/model, and runtime profile
- important runtime limits such as tool iteration/action/context limits when available
- active session and queue state, including paused, cancelled, waiting-for-approval, or turn-running states
- compact health/Doctor rollup with a route to the full Doctor pane

The Dashboard should stay glanceable. It should orient the user and link to detailed panes rather than becoming a second Config or Doctor screen.

## Non-goals / out of scope

- Do not add synthetic Doctor checks just to make the Doctor list longer.
- Do not change config selection behavior.
- Do not turn Dashboard into a full config editor or full diagnostics table.
- Do not expose secrets or environment-derived credential values.

## Alternatives considered

Relying on downstream panes, logs, or error messages leaves users to reconstruct context after something looks wrong. Runtime context is global app context, so it belongs on the Dashboard.

## Acceptance criteria

Minimum first pass:

- Dashboard shows the active config directory for the connected daemon/session.
- Dashboard shows TUI and daemon versions, with a clear mismatch warning.
- Dashboard shows the daemon endpoint or local IPC target in a compact form.
- Temporary/local config roots are visually distinguishable or clearly labeled.
- The display avoids leaking sensitive values and does not include unrelated local environment details.

Complete orientation surface:

- Dashboard shows current Chat and Code workspace/CWD when available.
- Dashboard shows selected agent, provider/model, and runtime profile.
- Dashboard shows active session and queue state.
- Dashboard shows a compact health rollup with a route to details.
- Users should not need to open Config, Logs, or another pane just to understand which runtime context ZeroCode is currently operating against.

## Architecture impact

ZeroCode Dashboard and the existing daemon/config/status RPC surfaces. If the Dashboard does not already receive a field, the daemon should expose it through an existing status/config-status style response rather than duplicating config or runtime state in the TUI.

## Risk and rollback

Risk is low to medium depending on how much data must be added to RPC responses. The intended change is display-only and should resolve values from canonical daemon/config/session state. Rollback is to remove the Dashboard fields.

## Expected routing

Ordinary feature triage.

## Next decision surface

Ordinary ZeroCode/dashboard UX triage is enough.

## Breaking change?

No

## Data hygiene checks

- [x] I removed personal/sensitive data from examples, payloads, and logs.
- [x] I used neutral, project-focused wording and placeholders.

prs.title: feat(a2a): extract A2A protocol core into a dedicated zeroclaw-a2a crate
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Extract the A2A protocol core out of `zeroclaw-api` / `zeroclaw-tools` / `zeroclaw-gateway` into a single `zeroclaw-a2a` crate, so the wire model, outbound client, and inbound protocol handling have one ownership home instead of four, and the protocol layer doesn't depend on any host config module.
  - Follow the official `a2a-rs` layering: the crate defines `A2aExecutor` / `AgentCardProducer` / `A2aPeerSource` as host-implemented seams and keeps its own config types, letting hosts adapt + inject.
  - Wire moves from `zeroclaw_api::a2a_wire` to `zeroclaw_a2a::wire`; `api` stops re-exporting it.
  - Hosts adapt through `A2aPeerSourceHost` (implements the protocol-layer `A2aPeerSource` over the host's **live** config handle) and the standalone `a2a_router` defaults closed to task operations.
- **Scope boundary:** Organization-only extraction — no new A2A protocol capability, no config-field change. Streaming and inbound task management are explicitly out of scope. The extraction preserves the pre-existing live/lazy host behavior (see below); it does **not** intentionally change runtime behavior.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw-api` loses its `a2a_wire` module (import sites moved); consumers of `zeroclaw-tools` / `zeroclaw-gateway` / `zeroclaw-runtime` see no tool, route, or behavior change.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #3566; Implements (RFC) #11254

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw's A2A support previously lived in four crates, split by hosting crate rather than by protocol: the wire model in `zeroclaw-api`, the outbound client in `zeroclaw-tools`, and the inbound surface in `zeroclaw-gateway`. That made every A2A extension thread re-export paths across multiple manifests. This PR consolidates the A2A protocol core into one `zeroclaw-a2a` crate whose layout mirrors the official a2a-rs SDK, and keeps host-coupled glue (the 4 `a2a_*` tools, gateway card building + auth) in the host crates, adapted through `A2aExecutor` / `AgentCardProducer` / `A2aPeerSource`.

### Live configuration ownership (review follow-up)

The first revision of this PR snapshotted peers, decrypted tokens, and proxy policy at client-construction time. That regressed the behavior the pre-extraction client had via its live config handle: removing a peer, rotating a token, tightening private-host policy, or changing the proxy no longer took effect on a retained agent, and one peer with a corrupt credential disabled all four tools.

This revision restores live/lazy semantics through a single host-implemented seam, `A2aPeerSource`, consulted on **every** call:

- `peers()` returns the current peers with **raw** (undecrypted) token fields — no snapshot.
- `resolve_token()` decrypts **lazily**, for the resolved peer only — one broken credential can no longer disable the whole tool set.
- `proxy_policy()` is resolved per call, including the `tool.a2a` service-scope check, so a proxy scoped to another service (or disabled while its URL is configured) does not block A2A.
- `settings()` reads card-cache TTL / response cap / SSRF allowlists live.

The protocol crate depends on none of the host's config modules (it holds an `Arc<dyn A2aPeerSource>`), preserving the RFC's config boundary while keeping resolution host-owned and current-at-use.

## Testing (required)

### How I tested

- `cargo +1.98.0 clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean, no warnings.
- `cargo +1.98.0 doc --no-deps --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop` (Rustdoc warnings gate) — clean.
- `cargo test -p zeroclaw-a2a` → `94 passed; 0 failed`
- `cargo test -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib a2a` → `34 passed; 0 failed`
- `cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib a2a_client` → `36 passed; 0 failed` (2 ignored = cross-harness external-peer tests)
- `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib a2a` → passed

The A2A conformance/security tests moved with the code. Previously dropped tests were restored except for `e2e_get_task_refuses_unmatched_task_id`, whose production guard remains intact. New boundary tests were added for the host adapter: lazy token decryption (encrypted / missing-dir / literal), disabled and other-service proxy scopes, live config reload (a removed peer disappears, settings follow), and the standalone catalog's `catalog` interface marker.

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — organization-only extraction; behavior matches the pre-extraction client.
- **Commands run and tail output:**
  ```
  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-a2a --lib
  test result: ok. 94 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored
  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib a2a
  test result: ok. 34 passed; 0 failed
  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib a2a_client
  test result: ok. 36 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored
  ```
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The host source reads live config per call (verified by a reload test: publishing a config with a peer added/removed is reflected immediately); proxy policy honors the `tool.a2a` service scope; a standalone `a2a_router` rejects task injection without a configured admission check; the standalone catalog emits the `catalog` interface marker so a single published alias is not mistaken for a single agent by `select_interface`.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A (no user-visible interface change)

### CI note

The current required checks, including `Security`, pass for head `8ceca7ca1dedbcb330eed7147ccd3e64bda67e0c`. [Quality Gate run 38840628685](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38840628685) tested its merge with the recorded base.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No**
- New external network calls? **No**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No behavior change.** Peer-token decryption stays host-owned (`A2aPeerSourceHost`, via the canonical `SecretStore`) and is now performed lazily per resolved peer; the protocol layer only applies `${VAR}` interpolation to the plaintext it is handed.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No**

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Runtime, protocol and configuration behavior is preserved; Rust source compatibility changes.** Replace `zeroclaw_api::a2a_wire` imports with `zeroclaw_a2a::wire`. `A2aHttpClient::new` now accepts an `Arc<dyn A2aPeerSource>`, timeout and route cache instead of the previous host configuration, directory and encryption arguments; ZeroClaw host code uses `A2aPeerSourceHost::build_a2a_client`.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No**
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No**

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

`git revert <sha>` is the plan. Organization-only extraction with no data/config surface; reverting the merge restores the prior layout.

## Supersede Attribution

N/A (no `Supersedes #` used).

prs.title: fix(providers): recognize snake_case context-window overflow codes
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** `is_context_window_exceeded` matches a list of phrases
  against the provider's error text. A local OpenAI-compatible server reports
  overflow as a snake_case `code` — `{"code":"context_length_exceeded", ...}` —
  instead of prose, and the existing entry `"context length exceeded"` only
  matches with a space, so the predicate returned `false`. That skipped the
  trim-and-retry recovery and left the user with the generic "the selected model
  provider rejected the request" text. This adds the one missing spelling, plus a
  regression test built from the real 400 body.
- **Scope boundary:** No change to trimming, token budgets, retries, refusal
  timing, or user-facing strings. `zeroclaw-channels` now delegates to this
  predicate, so no second list is touched.
- **Blast radius:** Narrow. The predicate only turns `true` for error text
  containing `context_length_exceeded`, which no other path in the workspace
  produces.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10329 (closed by #10416, which made the detector
  walk the error cause chain; this completes it for snake_case codes).

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw decides "the conversation no longer fits the model's memory" by matching
phrases in the provider's error text. When it recognises overflow it drops the
oldest whole turns and retries, and it tells the user to shorten rather than
blaming the provider configuration. One local server words the same condition as
a JSON field name — `context_length_exceeded` — which the list did not contain,
so a conversation a few dozen tokens over the window failed outright. This PR
adds that spelling.

## Testing (required)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A` — the trigger is a provider-specific error
  body that no public endpoint returns; the boundary is unit-tested.

### How I tested

```sh
cargo test -p zeroclaw-providers is_context_window_exceeded
# cargo test: 3 passed, 2024 filtered out (3 suites, 0.00s)
cargo fmt --all -- --check
# exit 0
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-providers --all-targets -- -D warnings
# cargo clippy: No issues found
```

A/B against a local mock provider replaying the captured 400 body: on `master`
the second turn ends with `Error: The selected model provider rejected the
request…` and nothing is trimmed; on this branch the runtime drops the oldest
whole turn (`messages=4` → `messages=2` in the mock's request log) and the retry
answers.

Not verified: a live overflow against the real server (needs a multi-minute
prefill on a memory-tight machine), and a live channel turn; the channel path
inherits this predicate.

- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A` — no rendered interface change.
- **Tested revision, interface:** `5cf71e6`, surface `cli`.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** the full workspace suite, and
  the local `pre-push` hook that chains it (workspace tests, firmware protocol
  gate, parallel runtime gate), skipped with `git push --no-verify`; CI covers
  them.
- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `CI Required Gate` on 5cf71e61e223230b09d9093420518f56a367090a covers the changed surface: the `zeroclaw-providers` suite runs `is_context_window_exceeded` with the new regression case, and the gate's lint leg runs `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy` over the touched crate.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** the required gate never talks to a live OpenAI-compatible server, so the trigger is proven only at the unit boundary (the mock-provider A/B above); a live overflow against the real server was not verified.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

All `No`: no new permissions or file system scope, no new network calls, no
secrets handling change, no PII, no model-visible text change.

## Compatibility (required)

Backward compatible `Yes`. No config/env/CLI surface change. No MSRV change.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** revert the squash commit that adds the hint and its regression test — `git log --oneline --grep '#11659'`, then `git revert <that sha>`; no data or schema migration is involved.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `None` — the hint always applies, so reverting the commit is the only switch.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** overflow `400`s carrying `context_length_exceeded` stop reaching trim-and-retry and surface as `The selected model provider rejected the request.`; a false positive shows up as unexpected `Context window exceeded, attempting in-loop recovery` warnings in the log.

prs.title: feat(channels): add configurable XMPP/Prosody channel with optional OMEMO
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- Add a first-class, opt-in `channel-xmpp` adapter for direct XMPP conversations, including Prosody. Inbound messages and replies use the existing channel supervisor and agent runtime, rather than an HTTP bridge or a separate agent loop.
- Expose account JID, server, port, Direct TLS or mandatory STARTTLS, masked password, resource, limits, interpreter and optional OMEMO settings through the schema-driven WebUI. The channel page's **Allowed users** tab creates alias-scoped canonical authorization policies and edits allowed/blocked users without a second allowlist.
- Require verified TLS in both transport modes. Optional OMEMO requires manually pinned device fingerprints, persists identity/ratchet state per alias and never downgrades to plaintext.
- **Scope boundary:** direct one-to-one text; no MUC, attachments, MAM, carbons or OMEMO v2. No deployment-specific hosts, ports, accounts, credentials or server provisioning.
- **Blast radius:** additive configuration/attribution metadata, feature-gated channel registration/runtime wiring, and one WebUI tab scoped to XMPP aliases. Existing listeners and the shared agent loop are unchanged.

Closes #9814

### What this does, simply

Operators who already have an XMPP server can bind a ZeroClaw agent to an account and converse with it from authorized accounts. Server address and JID domain are independent: the former selects the TCP destination and the latter remains the TLS service identity. Both STARTTLS and Direct TLS are selectable, and changing protocol does not silently change the configured port.

The Rust adapter owns the normal `Channel` lifecycle and authorization. An embedded, isolated Python transport worker uses Slixmpp for XMPP and an optional slixmpp-omemo backend for legacy OMEMO. It does not call the gateway or run models/tools. Python dependencies must be installed explicitly; Cargo does not install them. Missing dependencies fail closed.

The optional **slixmpp-omemo backend is AGPL-3.0-only**. It is not vendored. This dependency/license tradeoff is explicit in the installation guide and requirements file; TLS-only operation needs only MIT-licensed Slixmpp.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=web`; messaging `channel=xmpp`.
- **Setup / preconditions:** build with `channel-xmpp`, install the documented Python requirements in a dedicated venv, and use disposable XMPP accounts with a trusted server certificate. For OMEMO, enable server PEP/pubsub and verify device fingerprints out of band.
- **Steps to run:** follow `docs/book/src/channels/xmpp.md`; create an XMPP alias in Config, enter the connection fields, authorize bare JIDs under Allowed users, bind the channel to an enabled agent, enable the listener and reload. Send a direct message from an authorized account and compare with an unauthorized account. Repeat with STARTTLS and Direct TLS. Enable OMEMO and verify that unencrypted/untrusted traffic is refused.

### How I tested

Passed on the independent `master` base, including an isolated no-default-features channel build. Registry tests (2) and the channel-migration inventory regression (1) also passed.

- Python helper unit tests: 2 passed. New guide Markdown lint: 0 errors. Frontend TypeScript and Vite production build passed on the independent source, and the final Chrome fixture run includes creating an initially empty authorization policy. Focused Clippy passed with `-D warnings`.

The final head reruns the required suite and adds an isolated XMPP feature test lane. No claim is made that every final-head CI job has finished.

- **Visual interface evidence:** Screenshot.

Only the authorization fields are edited by that scoped form. No page JavaScript errors or mobile page overflow in the fixture run.

A clean generated-contract check relies on CI because the local Windows generator cache contained missing build-script artifacts. The first CI run identified the migration inventory, expanded all-feature installer lists and one Clippy expression; all three are addressed in the final update.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

prs.title: fix(security): split POSIX commands at substitution and subshell boundaries
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - The shell command scanner split segments only at `;`, newlines, `|`, `||`, and `&&`, and split words only at whitespace. The closing `)` of `$(...)`, `<(...)`, `>(...)`, or a subshell, and the closing backtick of `` `...` ``, stayed glued to the last inner word. `x=$(cmd 2>/dev/null)` therefore produced the redirect target `/dev/null)`. That is not the null device, so with the default forbidden `/dev` the shell tool refused it: `Path blocked by security policy: /dev/null)`. #11469's exact null-device matching is correct and unchanged; the bad token came from the tokenizer.
  - Under the POSIX dialect, `split_unquoted_segments` now treats command substitution, process substitution, backticks, and subshells as segment boundaries, tracked on a frame stack so nesting and substitution inside double quotes work. The inner command becomes its own segment, and the enclosing word keeps a `$()`-style placeholder.
  - Every character other than those delimiters still lands in exactly one segment (heredoc bodies aside), including for unbalanced input. An unterminated `$(` still flushes the command around it, and a stray `)` (for example a `case` pattern terminator) is a boundary. A misparse can over-split but cannot drop text from the scan.
  - `<<` inside `$((...))` is a shift, not a heredoc. Previously `echo $((8<<1))` opened a heredoc that hid the following lines from the scan, though bash runs them. A command substitution nested inside arithmetic is ordinary shell syntax again, so its heredocs are recognized.
  - A substitution closes only at the `)` bash treats as its closer. A `case` pattern terminator, a `)` inside `${...}`, or a `)` inside a `#` comment no longer ends `$(...)` early. Closing early would restore the enclosing quote state and hide the rest of the inner command inside one quoted argument. Comment text is not syntax until the newline, so an apostrophe in a comment no longer opens a quote that hides the next line (separators inside comments still split, conservatively). This addresses review feedback in 4935b7a82.
  - The strict allowlist keeps rejecting unquoted POSIX grouping parentheses, so `(git status)` is not newly accepted as `git status` as a side effect of the split. Escaped and quoted parentheses (`find . \( ... \)`, `grep -E '(a|b)'`) are still allowed.
- **Scope boundary:** Does not change null-device classification (`is_null_device`, `is_safe_device_redirect_target`), the safe-redirect regexes, forbidden-path defaults, allowlists, or sandbox grants. `cmd.exe` and PowerShell splitting are unchanged. Not addressed here: `$(...)` inside an unquoted-delimiter heredoc body (bash runs it; the scanner still skips heredoc bodies by design), and `cmd.exe` parenthesized blocks.
- **Blast radius:** Every consumer of `split_unquoted_segments` under the POSIX dialect: the workspace path scan (`forbidden_path_argument*`) used by the shell, skill shell, and cron paths; `command_risk_level`; `is_command_allowed`; and `is_command_explicitly_allowed`.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11469. Related #11823, Related #11824 (follow-ups for the scope this PR leaves out), Related #11825 (`zeroclaw-tools` test flake seen while validating).

### What this does, simply

Before running a shell command, ZeroClaw splits it into the individual commands it contains and checks each file path it mentions. That splitter didn't understand `$(...)`, backticks, or `(...)`, which are how shells run one command inside another. So in `x=$(ls 2>/dev/null)` it read the redirect target as `/dev/null)`, including the closing paren, and refused it as a forbidden path, even though #11469 made `/dev/null` always allowed. This was easy to hit, because `$(something 2>/dev/null)` is a very common shell idiom.

This PR teaches the splitter where those inner commands start and end. The inner command is checked on its own, so `2>/dev/null` inside it works again. As a side effect, commands hidden inside `$(...)` are now actually checked: a forbidden path inside `"$(...)"` is blocked, and `x=$(rm -rf ./build)` is rated high risk instead of low. Commands that the strict allowlist rejected before are still rejected.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** the `shell` tool, through any surface (`cli`, `tui`, or `web`)
- **Setup / preconditions:** Unix host, default `forbidden_paths` (includes `/dev`), `allowed_commands = ["*"]`, `block_high_risk_commands = false`
- **Steps to run:** Ask the agent to run each of these with the shell tool: `x=$(echo a 2>/dev/null); echo "$x"`, then `(echo a 2>/dev/null)`, then ``echo "`echo a 2>/dev/null`"``
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Each command runs and prints `a`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Each is refused with `Path blocked by security policy: /dev/null)` (or ``/dev/null` `` for the backtick form).

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** CI Required Gate (format, lint, Linux workspace tests, MSRV, Windows/macOS compile checks). The change is in `zeroclaw-config` policy parsing, plus one runtime shell-tool test.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None specific. The behavior change is gated to `ShellDialect::Posix`, and a new test pins `cmd.exe` splitting as unchanged.
- **Commands run and tail output:** On `4935b7a82` (base `cdefa0d0a`), with the CI toolchain `1.98.0`:

```sh
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
FMT_OK

$ cargo +1.98.0 clippy -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 1m 22s

$ cargo +1.98.0 test -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib
test result: ok. 1799 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
test result: ok. 5777 passed; 0 failed; 8 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out

# New end-to-end test against master's policy.rs (fix removed):
test tools::shell::tests::shell_allows_null_redirects_inside_posix_substitutions ... FAILED
x=$(echo zc-subst 2>/dev/null); echo "$x" must run, got: ToolResult { success: false, ..., error: Some("Path blocked by security policy: /dev/null)") }

# New policy tests against the unmodified tokenizer:
posix_segments_split_at_substitution_boundaries ... FAILED   left: ["x=$(echo a)"]
command_risk_level_sees_commands_inside_posix_substitutions ... FAILED   left: Low  right: High
forbidden_path_argument_allows_safe_devices_inside_posix_substitutions ... FAILED   left: Some("/dev/null)")
forbidden_path_argument_scans_inside_posix_substitutions ... FAILED   left: Some("/dev/nullx)")  right: Some("/dev/nullx")
```

- **Tests added or changed:**
  - `posix_segments_split_at_substitution_boundaries`: segment output for `$(...)`, `"$(...)"`, backticks, subshells, `<(...)`/`>(...)`, nesting, `$((...))`, unterminated and unbalanced input, quoted and escaped literals, and quotes inside a substitution.
  - `forbidden_path_argument_allows_safe_devices_inside_posix_substitutions`: 18 forms with `/dev/null` redirects inside substitutions, subshells, backticks, and process substitution, all allowed.
  - `forbidden_path_argument_scans_inside_posix_substitutions`: lookalikes (`/dev/nullx`, `/dev/null/../../etc/passwd`) and forbidden paths inside substitutions stay blocked and are reported without the closing `)`. This includes the double-quoted form, `case` bodies (quoted, unquoted, `(x)` patterns, after `then`, with a subshell in the body), `)` inside `${...}` and inside comments, a nested substitution in `${x:-...}`, a stray `)`, and the arithmetic-heredoc case.
  - `command_risk_level_sees_commands_inside_posix_substitutions`: `rm -rf` inside `$(...)`, `"$(...)"`, backticks, subshells, and `<(...)` is High; `x=$(git rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null)` stays Low.
  - `strict_allowlist_still_rejects_posix_grouping_and_substitution`: the default strict policy still rejects `(git status)` and similar, and still allows escaped and quoted parentheses. Passes on both `master` and this branch.
  - `windows_cmd_does_not_split_posix_substitution_syntax`: `cmd.exe` splitting is unchanged.
  - `tools::shell::tests::shell_allows_null_redirects_inside_posix_substitutions`: the reported scenario end to end through `RateLimitedTool<ShellTool>` with the default forbidden `/dev`. A forbidden path inside `$(...)` is still refused and named without the `)`.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Reproduced the original refusal in a live session on a binary that includes #11469. Checked the test fixtures against real `bash` (and `sh`, which is bash on the test host): a quote inside `"$(...)"`; a backtick inside double quotes running a command; `\$\(a\)` being literal while `\$(a\)` is a syntax error; `case` bodies running; and the line after `$((8<<1))` running, not being swallowed as a heredoc. Not verified: Windows execution (`cmd.exe` behavior is unchanged by construction and pinned by a unit test), and dash as `/bin/sh` (no POSIX-only constructs that dash treats differently are interpreted beyond what the tests cover).
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. No user-visible interface state changed beyond the tool result shown above.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `4935b7a82`, `shell` tool via unit test `tools::shell::tests::shell_allows_null_redirects_inside_posix_substitutions`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** See the command output above.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** `x=$(echo zc-subst 2>/dev/null); echo "$x"` returns success with output `zc-subst`. On `master` it is refused with `Path blocked by security policy: /dev/null)`.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:**
  - Workspace-wide `cargo test` was not run. The diff is confined to `zeroclaw-config` and one `zeroclaw-runtime` test, and the only other crate calling these policy APIs is `zeroclaw-tools`.
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib` passed (2092 passed with `--test-threads=1`) on the pre-rebase base `329e66f76`, not re-run after the rebase. In parallel it fails intermittently, in a different test on each run (`coding_agent_budget_tests::coding_agent_wrappers_charge_one_action_each`, `browser::tests::computer_use_dispatch_fails_closed_on_malformed_screenshot_response`), because a `codex_cli.rs` test sets the process-wide `PATH` to an empty directory. That is unrelated to this change.
  - Clippy on a newer local toolchain (`1.99.0`) reports `needless_borrows_for_generic_args` and `fetch_update` deprecations in untouched files (`zeroclaw-providers/src/lib.rs`, `zeroclaw-runtime/src/rpc/upload.rs`, `rpc/dispatch.rs`, `agent/turn/stream_guard.rs`). These are left to a separate PR; the CI toolchain `1.98.0` is clean.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? (`Yes`)
- New external network calls? (`No`)
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? (`No`)
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? (`No`)
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? (`No`)
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation:
  - **Widened:** the workspace path scan now accepts the existing safe-device redirect targets (exact `/dev/null`, `/dev/stdout`, `/dev/stderr`, `/dev/zero`) when they appear inside a substitution or subshell. Before, those targets were refused only because a trailing `)` or backtick made them unrecognizable. No new device, path, or command is allowed, and lookalikes stay blocked (tested).
  - **Tightened:** commands inside `$(...)`, `"$(...)"`, backticks, `<(...)`, `>(...)`, and subshells are now scanned and risk-classified as their own commands. A forbidden path inside a double-quoted substitution, previously unscanned, is blocked. A high-risk command inside a substitution now makes the whole command High, so under Supervised autonomy it requires approval.
  - **Strict allowlist:** unchanged. A new guard keeps rejecting unquoted POSIX `(`/`)`, so the split does not turn `(git status)` into an accepted `git status`. `$(`, `<(`, `>(`, and backticks were already rejected in strict mode.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? (`No`)
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? (`No`)
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A. Behavioral note: with `allowed_commands = ["*"]`, `block_high_risk_commands = false`, and Supervised autonomy, a command that hides a high-risk command inside a substitution now asks for approval.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert` the squash commit. There is no config, data, or migration state to unwind.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** (a) a shell command containing `$(... 2>/dev/null)`, `(...)`, or backticks refused with `Path blocked by security policy: /dev/null)` (regression of this fix); (b) a POSIX command using substitution or grouping that was accepted before and is now refused, or rated higher risk than expected (over-splitting); (c) a strict-allowlist policy accepting `(cmd)` grouping (guard regression).

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A. This PR does not supersede another.

prs.title: fix(tunnel): supervise and verify the tailscale gateway serve process
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - The gateway's `tailscale serve|funnel --https=443` child was spawned in `TailscaleTunnel::start()` and never waited for. When it exited (port 443 still held by another foreground session, or a lost serve-config etag race with the `--tcp` forwarders started right after it), it stayed `<defunct>` for the life of the daemon. `health_check` still reported it alive because `tokio::process::Child::id()` stays `Some` until the child is polled to completion, and `start()` had already advertised a URL that nothing served.
  - The gateway serve process is now owned by the same watcher the TCP forwarders already use (`TcpForwarder` generalised to `ServeProcess`). An exit is reaped and logged with its stderr, stop or drop kills and reaps it, and `health_check` reflects the real state.
  - `start()` returns the URL only once `tailscale serve status --json` shows a new foreground session proxying `443` to `http://127.0.0.1:<local_port>`. Otherwise it fails with the process's stderr, and the gateway's existing `Err` path falls back to local-only.
  - `listener already exists for port N` (observed on Tailscale 1.104.1) is now retryable alongside the existing etag-conflict case, bounded to five attempts (about 2.5s of linear backoff). A previous generation's session being torn down across a reload is waited out; a holder that stays is reported, not spun on.
  - Serve stdout (an unread banner) is discarded instead of piped, so it can never fill a pipe and block the process.
- **Scope boundary:** No other tunnel provider, no change to the `Tunnel` trait or the gateway crate, no automatic respawn of an exited serve process, and no public exposure change (WSS/enrollment stay tailnet-only). Serve processes orphaned by a daemon that dies without running destructors (crash, SIGKILL) are **not** addressed here: they keep holding the port, and with this PR the next start reports that clearly instead of going defunct. A parent-death signal needs a dedicated spawner thread (Linux `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` is per forking thread, and tokio's `block_in_place` can retire such a thread), so it is left for a separate change.
- **Blast radius:** Tailscale tunnel users only. Behaviour change: if 443 cannot be published, `start()` now fails, so the gateway takes its existing "Tunnel failed to start, falling back to local-only" path and does not go on to publish WSS/enrollment via `publish_tcp_services`. Before, those were published next to a dead 443 proxy. Gateway startup may also wait up to about 2.5s (retries) or 5s (apply timeout) per serve process when tailscaled is slow or the port is held.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11530, Related #11531

### What this does, simply

With the Tailscale tunnel, ZeroClaw starts a `tailscale serve` process to put the gateway on the tailnet at `https://<node>`. If that process failed right away, for example because the port was still in use, ZeroClaw never noticed. The dead process lingered as a "defunct" entry in `ps`, health checks said all was well, and the startup output printed a URL that didn't work. This PR has ZeroClaw watch that process the same way it already watches the WSS/enrollment forwarders. It confirms that Tailscale is actually serving the gateway before printing the URL, waits briefly for a port that is still being released, cleans up the process if it exits, and logs why. It does not restart a process that dies later, and it does not yet clean up serve processes left behind by a daemon that crashed.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `Yes`
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` (`zeroclaw daemon` with `[tunnel] tunnel_provider = "tailscale"`)
- **Setup / preconditions:** Linux node logged into a tailnet (`tailscale up`), serve permitted for the operator (`tailscale set --operator=$USER`), `[tunnel] tunnel_provider = "tailscale"`.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. In another terminal, hold the gateway port: `tailscale serve --https=443 8080` (leave it running).
  2. Start `zeroclaw daemon`.
  3. `ps -eo pid,stat,cmd | grep 'tailscale serve'`
  4. Stop the holder from step 1 and restart the daemon.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Step 2 prints `Tunnel failed to start: tailscale serve --https=443 <port> did not publish the gateway: exited (exit status: 1) after 5 attempt(s): ... listener already exists for port 443` and falls back to local-only. Step 3 shows no `<defunct>` entry. After step 4, `Tunnel active: https://<node>` and `tailscale serve status` shows the gateway proxy.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Step 2 prints `Tunnel active: https://<node>` even though nothing serves it, and step 3 shows `tailscale serve --https=443 <port> <defunct>` for as long as the daemon runs.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The CI `Clippy` job (`scripts/ci/run_clippy.sh --scope workspace`, Rust 1.98.0, `--features ci-all`, `-D warnings`) and the test jobs cover the changed Rust file. I ran the same clippy script locally on this head as well (below).
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No CI job runs a real `tailscaled`. tailscaled's behaviour is pinned by the manual check below, and the tests use `sh` stand-ins for the process plus status JSON captured from a live 1.104.1 node.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```sh
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
# clean (no diff)

$ RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.98.0 RUNNER_TEMP=$PWD/target/ci-tmp \
    bash scripts/ci/run_clippy.sh --scope workspace --summary-title "Lint diagnostics" --log-name cargo-clippy.log
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 3m 20s
# exit 0; 0 warning/error lines in cargo-clippy.log

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib tunnel::
test tunnel::tailscale::tests::gateway_serve_exit_is_reaped_not_left_defunct ... ok
test tunnel::tailscale::tests::dropping_the_tunnel_kills_and_reaps_its_gateway_serve ... ok
test tunnel::tailscale::tests::gateway_sessions_match_only_an_https_proxy_to_the_local_port ... ok
test tunnel::tailscale::tests::held_port_is_retryable_but_other_failures_are_not ... ok
test tunnel::tailscale::tests::start_forwarder_waits_out_a_port_that_is_being_released ... ok
test tunnel::tailscale::tests::start_forwarder_reports_a_port_that_stays_held ... ok
test result: ok. 126 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5586 filtered out; finished in 0.33s
```

prs.title: fix(anthropic): classify incomplete terminal responses
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Treat incomplete Anthropic responses and semantic-empty terminals as typed failures, not successful blank or partial answers. Validate buffered envelopes and SSE framing, terminal reasons, content-block lifecycles, and execution-bearing tool input.
  - Preserve the first incomplete cause, observed usage, and opaque reasoning state through provider parsing and downstream consumers. Valid signed/redacted reasoning remains available for later provider reuse without becoming final display text.
  - Carry typed recovery and chargeability policy through Reliable and the runtime. The changed typed-terminal paths reject replay after immutable output, client-tool activity, provider-executed work, or cancellation; retain the documented pre-send connection, exact image-replacement, and sole-candidate exceptions.
  - Bind final failure and serving-provider identity to the same physical attempt. Reconcile terminal usage field by field, account rejected work once, and attribute successful fallback to its actual serving route. Preserve combined usage for direct unscoped structured calls, while scoped runtime calls retain accepted and rejected usage separately. Derive missing accepted-summary input estimates from the finalized sanitized request, floored at known cached input; estimates remain display-only.
  - Deliver localized terminal failures through CLI, ordinary turn/RPC, SOP, and delegation. Settle completed rejected-attempt usage when provider-backed work is cancelled, times out, or its future is dropped; controlled summary exits flush the existing usage-event projection before returning. Isolate the real peer-execution cost regression in an exact subprocess and wait for its durable terminal task before asserting accounting.
- **Scope boundary:** No OAuth/authentication, credentials, provider-default, gateway/config-schema, deployment, Matrix-adapter, telemetry-schema, or generic response-metadata changes. No paid/live provider calls. OpenAI-compatible output-limit classification remains a separate slice. The SOP accounting change is a narrow fix for usage lost at cancellation/timeout; broader SOP lifecycle architecture is deferred rather than folded into this PR. The peer-test correction does not change production cost-tracker policy.
- **Blast radius:** Provider API/parsers; Reliable/Router recovery and attribution; ordinary runtime turn, history, accounting, RPC, SOP and delegate delivery; direct CLI error output; external Rust consumers of changed public error types.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #9421. https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/9421

### What this does, simply

A provider can finish an HTTP request without finishing the answer: it may exhaust its output/context budget, pause, refuse, return malformed tool data, or return no usable answer. Those outcomes should not be reported as success. This PR preserves their cause and usage all the way to the caller and restricts recovery of these typed outcomes so an already visible answer or tool operation is not silently repeated. Any text already streamed remains visible as partial output; the turn still ends as incomplete, not as an accepted final answer. An unchanged generic outer context-overflow recovery path can still restart after visible output when it recognizes an overflow diagnostic; that pre-existing limitation needs a separately scoped follow-up and is not claimed fixed here.

Merged #11625 records the original bounded runtime holding-crate exception. The additional production accounting changes in `src/agent/turn/mod.rs` still require the separate Core-approved scope record proposed in #11816 to land before #9447 merges. A pending proposal, green CI, or earlier approval does not grant that additional scope or establish merge readiness.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A - deterministic buffered/SSE, recovery, accounting, and production-CLI fixtures cover the contract without credentials or paid/live requests.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Fresh [Quality Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39175086109) succeeded for `4b0f181594d1f6de8224be3a91598373db7a3631`, including `CI Required Gate`, Security, Test, Lint, MSRV, the repeated parallel-runtime gate, required Windows checks, platform/feature checks, and documentation checks. Code Analysis/Semgrep and Greptile also succeeded on this head. Greptile's edited summary explicitly names this commit, reports 5/5, and establishes no new actionable issue; that advisory result is not Core approval. All reported current-head checks are terminal, with no failures or pending checks. The previous-head Security failure is not carried forward as a current failure.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Ten conditional skips are expected and nonblocking: master-only debounce, non-PR benchmarks, label-gated advisory Windows selection/execution, path-gated Relay smoke, targeted Windows Clippy, Nix eval/hash, package preflight, and unselected Windows recovery. Selected required Windows root/service checks passed independently. No live Anthropic or Matrix/ZeroCode smoke, external downstream-crate build, local Windows execution, or full-workspace local test run. Ignored tests and conditional skips are not executed coverage. Provider tests below use one thread; that is not proof of parallel provider reliability. Fresh hosted tests supply their own exact-head coverage, not proof of unexecuted cases.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Rust 1.98.1; isolated output with incremental compilation and debug information disabled. The final staged source was validated before being committed unchanged as `4b0f181594d1f6de8224be3a91598373db7a3631`, integrating official `master` at `8faf3a89f66e4c2f29b3c7da3d437d927a795363`. Earlier failures remain historical evidence, not rewritten as successes. The peer fixture's former process-global tracker interference was diagnosed with a source-backed replacement probe and corrected using subprocess isolation plus terminal-task waiting, without weakening its one-request, recipient-attribution, shared-budget, or admission-lifetime assertions. Six summary interruption/event-sink regressions failed four cases before the usage-projection repair and passed all six afterward. The inherited release-fixture formatting failure is corrected by the merged upstream change, not an unrelated local edit. The existing macOS compact-unwind linker warning persists; linking and tests succeeded. The docs gate reports an existing duplicate heading outside changed lines as nonblocking.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** No live manual session. Local automated fixtures exercise buffered/SSE terminals, opaque continuation reuse, replay restrictions, every-exit usage settlement, serving-provider identity, summary cancellation/timeout with open/full/closed event sinks, and the real peer execute-to-durable-terminal boundary. Generic outer context-overflow recovery remains outside this PR.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact final-interface output for the semantic-only CLI change; no presentation-sensitive redesign is claimed.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Source committed unchanged as `4b0f181594d1f6de8224be3a91598373db7a3631`; `surface=cli`; production `zeroclaw agent`, one-shot and piped interactive modes, `locale=en`, logging disabled; `tests/component/direct_cli_terminal_completion.rs`. No terminal-width claim is made.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** The one-shot output-limit fixture observes empty stdout, exit status 1 and stderr `Error: The provider reached its output token limit before completing the response.\n`. Interactive mode retains streamed partial text and emits the localized error with one provider request. The production component suite checks all five terminal reasons and the image-recovery control.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Submit a prompt to deterministic incomplete buffered/SSE responses. One-shot fails; interactive mode reports failure and remains usable. Incomplete output is not accepted or replayed. Image recovery and the subsequent text-only turn retain request image counts `[1, 0, 0]`.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Live/provider credentials and local Windows execution were outside validation. Four provider tests require authenticated Grok CLI; parser/runtime/channel ignores remain unexecuted. External HTTP link verification requires unavailable `lychee`; scanner tests passed and there are no added links. Full-workspace local validation was not run; no ignored or skipped case is claimed executed.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No. Recovery uses existing configured provider calls and is more constrained by typed terminal state.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes. Provider-controlled signed/redacted reasoning continuation data is newly retained and reconstructed for later Anthropic requests; this does not add human-authored prompt text or a credential/permission surface.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Opaque provider continuation data crosses the later-request boundary and must not become displayed text or executable client-tool input. Structural validation, typed block reconstruction, opaque retention outside final display, and preservation/rejection fixtures constrain its reuse to provider continuation state; raw diagnostics remain separate from localized user delivery.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? No for Rust consumers of the changed Experimental APIs and for callers that previously accepted incomplete output as success.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes for CLI terminal-error semantics; no public flags, configuration keys, environment variables, or defaults are added or changed.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: Add exhaustive match arms for the new `StreamError::TerminalCompletion` and `StreamError::SemanticEmpty` variants. Include `provider_executed_tool_activity` when constructing `ModelRefusalError`: set it from actual provider-executed work, using `true` when replay could duplicate that work and `false` when none occurred. Use the new typed terminal/semantic-empty error helpers rather than diagnostic-string matching, and handle incomplete turns as failures. Accounted/scoped calls keep rejected usage separate from accepted context; direct unscoped structured Reliable calls retain legacy combined totals, including billable typed failures and cache-write counters. `ThinkingDelta`, `ReasoningFinalized`, and `ModelRefusal` already exist in the base and are not additions made by this PR. Provider implementations should return typed terminal/semantic-empty errors with known usage rather than emit `Final` for incomplete output. Direct string consumers must account for stripped trailing `<eom>`/`<|eom|>` markers and hidden `<think>` content; marker/think-only output is now a semantic-empty failure. Use the canonical normalizer in `zeroclaw-api` (re-exported by `zeroclaw-tool-call-parser`) instead of maintaining a separate vocabulary. Existing users need no config migration; CLI callers must honor error status/output rather than treating HTTP completion as answer success.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** After merge, revert the merge/squash commit that GitHub records for #9447: `git revert <squash-sha>` or `git revert -m 1 <merge-sha>`, as appropriate to the actual merge method. Before merge, abandon the unmerged proposal or revert its owned functional commits on the feature branch while preserving upstream integration; do not revert one historical repair as if it represented the complete change.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Unexpected localized incomplete-terminal errors, lost/duplicated rejected usage, wrong serving-provider attribution, or repeated work after visible/tool output. A summary context estimate smaller than its cached subset or describing stale history indicates an estimate-projection regression; estimates must remain labelled and non-billable. Typed diagnostics distinguish output/context limits, paused turns, refusals, invalid terminal state, and semantic-empty output without relying on payload logging.

prs.title: feat(config): control OpenRouter balance reporting in web settings
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Add per-alias `credit_balance_enabled` in the OpenRouter Connection tab. Reporting requires explicit opt-in and defaults to disabled.
  - Keep the Management API Key in the same schema-driven form. Saved secrets show a constant `********` indicator; Change starts an empty password input rather than retrieving the stored key.
  - Gate credit requests on the current typed config. Disabling reporting retains both credentials and does not disable inference.
  - Honor the configured `model_provider.openrouter` proxy with the existing five-second timeout, and identify the selected provider alias on the balance card.
  - Add config/API persistence and privacy tests, a secret-field interaction test, documentation, and full-dashboard screenshots.
- **Scope boundary:** This is the settings follow-up to the balance endpoint/card. It does not add spend accounting, change model routing, or deploy a release. The shared secret renderer now consistently shows a fixed mask for all populated secret fields.
- **Blast radius:** OpenRouter config/introspection, authenticated credits selection, and the shared web secret renderer. Other Rust changes only update test literals for the added config field.
- **Linked issue(s):** Depends on #11845. This stacked branch retains that PR's implementation until the prerequisite lands. The incremental settings change is commit [622a477b4](https://github.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/commit/622a477b4482d091039953a7cfab770fa7afc52e).

### What this does, simply

Operators can open Config → Model providers → OpenRouter → their alias → Connection, enter a separate Management API Key, and turn the balance card on or off. A previously saved key appears as eight asterisks, independent of its actual length. Changing it edits a new value; the browser never receives the saved credential. Turning reporting off keeps the key available for later use and leaves model inference working.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface: web`.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Build the branch and its web assets; configure an OpenRouter alias used by an enabled agent. Use a disposable configuration and separate inference/Management API credentials for live verification.
- **Steps to run:** Open that alias's Connection tab. Set the Management API Key, enable reporting, save, and reload. Select Change, confirm the input starts empty, replace the key, save, and reload. Disable reporting, save, reload, and inspect the dashboard.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The key is masked after saving, the toggle persists, disabled reporting omits the card/returns 204 without a credits request, and both credentials remain configured. With reporting enabled and valid credentials, the existing balance card can appear.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Master has no balance feature. The direct comparison against prerequisite #11845 is automatic reporting with no explicit toggle and a saved-secret Change button without an asterisk indicator.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The initial settings head `622a477b4` completed all 47 checks successfully. The follow-up review fixes add proxy and account-alias tests; checks on their new head are pending and not claimed as passing. Prerequisite #11845 completed 47 checks successfully; those are baseline evidence, not validation of this settings commit.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Local Windows builds emit pre-existing warnings for unused `resolved_launcher`, `resolved_shell`, `SERVICE_STOP_TIMEOUT`, and `replace_parent`, plus a localized MSVC import-library notice. The affected production lines match upstream master; no suppressions or unrelated fixes were added. Strict Linux lint remains a CI responsibility.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

  ```text
  cargo fmt --all -- --check
  # exit 0
  git diff --check 44e60879
  # exit 0
  cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway openrouter --lib
  # 5 passed; 0 failed (includes configured-service proxy and selected-account tests)
  cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config openrouter_ --lib
  # 2 passed; 0 failed
  web spec-dump --out <temporary-output>
  node node_modules/openapi-typescript/bin/cli.js <temporary-output>/openapi.json -o src/lib/api-generated.ts
  # Canonical compiled spec + TypeScript generation; exit 0
  node node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc -b
  # exit 0
  npm run test:permissions
  # exit 0; includes SecretField interaction test
  ```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Visible Chrome exercised the full local dashboard: enable/save/reload; replace a management-key fixture from an empty password input; save/reload to a fixed mask; disable/save/reload while retaining the credential. The gateway test independently exercises the native config list/PATCH handlers, verifies that no secret value is returned, confirms persistence with an encrypted key on disk, and confirms plaintext remains only in the server's live config. The credits resolver tests cover opt-out, re-enable, and matching the selected provider alias to its management key with two accounts. A local TCP proxy test receives the HTTPS CONNECT request for a fictional host, proving that the credits client uses the configured service proxy without contacting OpenRouter. No live OpenRouter call or production config change was made for this follow-up.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Screenshots of the actual full Vite-served dashboard with stateful local API fixtures, not component-only previews. Browser fixtures verify UI rendering/PATCH transitions; they are not presented as an end-to-end live backend test.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Settings source in `622a477b4`; proxy/account fixes in `65f064f5c` and attribution-test correction in `f54944d37`. Final head `8e9b74e73506d0bc6c2168bc553f645138365b48`. Chrome, English locale, desktop 1440 x 1000 and mobile 390 x 844. Captures and provenance are under `.pr-evidence/openrouter-settings*`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** [Desktop](https://github.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/blob/622a477b4482d091039953a7cfab770fa7afc52e/.pr-evidence/openrouter-settings-desktop.png), [mobile](https://github.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/blob/622a477b4482d091039953a7cfab770fa7afc52e/.pr-evidence/openrouter-settings-mobile.png), [provenance](https://github.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/blob/622a477b4482d091039953a7cfab770fa7afc52e/.pr-evidence/openrouter-settings.md).
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Reporting persisted through false → true → false; credential replacement returned to the saved mask after reload. No page errors or horizontal document overflow at either viewport.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Local strict Windows Clippy is not claimed because the baseline Windows warnings above already block warning-denied checks. Required Linux CI covers that gate. Tests did not contact OpenRouter or use real credentials.

The follow-up also adds an account label to the card. Full-dashboard fixture captures: [account desktop](https://github.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/blob/8e9b74e73506d0bc6c2168bc553f645138365b48/.pr-evidence/openrouter-account-desktop.png), [account mobile](https://github.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/blob/8e9b74e73506d0bc6c2168bc553f645138365b48/.pr-evidence/openrouter-account-mobile.png). The running Vite app used an exact copy of this branch's web sources with local fixtures; source files were not altered to make the capture. Motion was reduced for stable captures. Provenance is documented alongside the images. The new response field is `provider_alias`; no credential is returned. The first follow-up lint caught a direct task spawn in the proxy test; it was replaced with the repository attribution-preserving spawn macro in `f54944d37`. Fresh CI is requested for the final head.
