prs.title: test(runtime): tolerate concurrent writers when checking persisted trace correlation
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `agent::loop_::tests::concurrent_session_scopes_correlate_provider_traces_in_logs` parsed every line of the persisted runtime trace with `expect("valid trace JSON")`. The trace file is process-wide, and `flush_for_test` only drains the records queued before it, so under the parallel gate another test's in-flight record can sit on the tail as a partial line. The writer serializes each record through an 8 KiB `BufWriter`, so a record longer than that reaches disk in several syscalls, which is how a reader observes a line cut mid-string.
  - The test now keeps the lines that parse and lets `assert_correlations` select its own records by trace id, the same way the broadcast check already does and the same pattern the log crate's own persisted-sink tests use. The file is read as bytes and parsed with `from_slice`, so a tail cut inside a multi-byte character cannot fail `read_to_string` for the same reason.
  - After the flush the test appends a deliberately partial foreign record (cut inside a string value and inside a multi-byte character), so every run exercises the tolerance instead of depending on scheduling. Restoring the strict read fails deterministically with the exact CI message.
- **Scope boundary:** test-only. No change to `zeroclaw-log`, the writer, the flush protocol, or the correlation assertions (both iterations of both sessions must still emit `llm_request` and `llm_response` under the right `session_key`, in both the broadcast and the persisted sink).
- **Blast radius:** one runtime unit test. The `Parallel Runtime Test` job (`scripts/ci/parallel_runtime_test_gate.sh`) stops failing on this test's torn-tail read.
- **Linked issue(s):** none filed. Observed in Quality Gate runs 38309731852 (PR 11309) and 38306946639 (feat/firecrawl-web-search) on 2026-10-12, `Repeat parallel runtime tests` step:

  ```
  thread 'agent::loop_::tests::concurrent_session_scopes_correlate_provider_traces_in_logs' panicked at crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/agent/loop_.rs:20547:52:
  valid trace JSON: Error("EOF while parsing a string", line: 1, column: 360)
  ```

### What this does, simply

The runtime writes one JSON record per line to a trace file, and this test checks that two interleaved conversations each keep their own trace id and session key in that file. The file is shared by every test in the process, so while this test reads it, some other test may be halfway through writing a record. The old code treated any unparseable line as a failure, even one that belonged to a different test and was simply not finished yet. The test now only requires its own records to be present and correct, and it plants an unfinished foreign record on purpose so the case is covered on every run rather than only when the scheduler happens to produce it.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A`: test-only change; the A/B below is reproducible from the commands in `How I tested`.

### How I tested

Local: macOS arm64 (18 cores), rustc 1.97.1, fresh target dir for this worktree.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Test` runs the changed test; `Parallel Runtime Test` repeats the runtime lib suite at 16 threads three times, which is the surface this change targets.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None beyond the statistical nature of the original flake; the planted partial record makes the tolerance deterministic.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

Fixed test, single run and 40 repeats straight from the test binary:

```sh
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- agent::loop_::tests::concurrent_session_scopes_correlate_provider_traces_in_logs --exact
# test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5718 filtered out
# 40 consecutive invocations of the built test binary with --exact: pass=40 fail=0
```

A/B with master's strict read restored (`read_to_string` + `from_str(...).expect("valid trace JSON")`) while keeping the planted partial record:

```
# ASCII-only partial tail (the CI shape):
thread 'agent::loop_::tests::concurrent_session_scopes_correlate_provider_traces_in_logs' panicked at crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/agent/loop_.rs:20565:52:
valid trace JSON: Error("EOF while parsing a string", line: 1, column: 59)
test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5718 filtered out
# partial tail cut inside a multi-byte character:
thread 'agent::loop_::tests::concurrent_session_scopes_correlate_provider_traces_in_logs' panicked at crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/agent/loop_.rs:20563:62:
read runtime trace: Error { kind: InvalidData, message: "stream did not contain valid UTF-8" }
test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5718 filtered out
```

Runtime lib suite the way the gate runs it (`--test-threads=16`), three times:

```sh
for run in 1 2 3; do cargo test --locked --quiet -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- --test-threads=16; done
# run 1: test result: FAILED. 5709 passed; 2 failed; 8 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 35.49s
#   failed: rpc::dispatch::tests::new_session_methods_are_denied_without_their_grants, tools::send_message_to_peer::tests::peer_turn_cost_scope_through_execute_boundary_attributes_recipient_and_shares_budget
#   concurrent_session_scopes_correlate_provider_traces_in_logs: passed
# run 2: test result: FAILED. 5710 passed; 1 failed; 8 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 35.55s
#   failed: rpc::dispatch::tests::new_session_methods_are_denied_without_their_grants
#   concurrent_session_scopes_correlate_provider_traces_in_logs: passed
# run 3: test result: FAILED. 5710 passed; 1 failed; 8 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 36.11s
#   failed: rpc::dispatch::tests::new_session_methods_are_denied_without_their_grants
#   concurrent_session_scopes_correlate_provider_traces_in_logs: passed
```

The two failures above are pre-existing and unrelated to this change: `rpc::dispatch::tests::new_session_methods_are_denied_without_their_grants` fails 3/3 even when run alone on macOS (temp workspace under `/var/folders`; fixture fix in #11630), and `tools::send_message_to_peer::tests::peer_turn_cost_scope_through_execute_boundary_attributes_recipient_and_shares_budget` is the shared cost-tracker parallel flake (passes 3/3 alone; fix in #11350). Neither touches the log sink.

Gates:

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                      # clean
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings   # clean, exit 0
python3 scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.py <list>               # Comment hygiene gate passed.
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** That the test's own records cannot be the partial ones: `record_event` enqueues synchronously via `try_send`, the worker is FIFO, and `flush_for_test` acks only after the records queued before it are written, so the planted record (and any concurrent writer's tail) always sits behind this test's complete records. Not verified: the original torn read on a shared file under CI load, which is statistical by nature; the planted record stands in for it.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A`
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `N/A` (no user-visible interface state changed)
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** `N/A`
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** `N/A`
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `zeroclaw-channels` half of the gate script not run locally; the change does not touch that crate.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? `No`
- New external network calls? `No`
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? `No`
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? `No`
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? `No`

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? `Yes`
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? `No`
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? `No`

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low-risk, test-only: `git revert <sha>`.

prs.title: feat(sessions): add persistent session prompt attachments
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Adds an opt-in SQLite collection of four bounded prompts owned by one durable Chat session. Restart preserves them; whole-session reset, deletion and TTL cleanup remove them transactionally with their owner. Legacy prompt binding schema and ownership reconciliation migrate in one immediate transaction, including rollback on failure.
  - Adds current-session `session_prompt_list`, `session_prompt_set` and `session_prompt_delete`. Mutations require exact one-time approval by default. Global/per-risk-profile `session_prompt_approval = "disabled"` is an explicit operator choice. The tools are direct-only, not skill aliases, pipeline children or inherited auxiliary capabilities.
  - Injects a deterministic next-primary-turn section after immutable host context. Provider context, explicit list and dedicated approval previews retain content; ordinary events, progress and retained/export history mask it without rewriting provider working history. Modifying LLM hooks are skipped for private requests rather than receiving a masked mutable copy. Independent child transcripts do not inherit attachment-bearing parent prompt scope; same-agent SOP continuation retains its existing primary transcript without prompt-tool capability.
  - Binds primary work to the admitted durable incarnation. Chat deletion now coordinates RPC and gateway work: cancel the captured generation, serialize deletion, commit durable alias removal atomically in SQLite, and invalidate the gateway generation only after commit. SQLite rollback preserves the durable owner and leaves an idle WebSocket usable; already-cancelled work cannot be restored. Non-transactional backends delete aliases sequentially and can partially delete them before reporting an error. Gateway cancellation binds the exact admitted queue key and generation, preventing deletion of an underscore session from cancelling a distinct dotted WebSocket session.
  - Merges official master through `8faf3a89f66e` without rebasing, preserving its dispatch/model-switch, optional built-in selection, native-name ownership, cost notices and ZeroCode live updates. Prompt tools compose `[tools].optional` with existing Chat/persistence/SQLite prerequisites; their names remain reserved against plugins and ordinary/prepared skills even when disabled. Prompt schemas stay out of registry-lived discovery. The complete diff also contains the documented parser/export, exact-preview, adapter, WhatsApp CI and Dashboard Kill repairs. Host-only tool-mode framing preserves approved attachment text, including literal framing phrases, through later turns and request reconstruction.
- **Scope boundary:** Channel and gateway-RPC Chat sessions, including Web and ZeroCode Chat. No ACP prompt support, JSONL prompt support, cron/SOP/delegate/subagent/one-shot/auxiliary capability, arbitrary-session management, REST collection management or new slash commands. Ordinary ACP lifecycle handling remains isolated from Chat aliases. No deployment, WIT/WASM ABI change, new lockfile package or workflow-permission expansion. `zeroclaw-infra` adds a direct dependency on the already-locked `tokio-util`.
- **Blast radius:** 117 files, `+20,203/-1,536` against official `8faf3a89f66e4c2f29b3c7da3d437d927a795363` at `1afbd5791b9c51fbf322367e1ae7f81db7920bb2`: storage/lifecycle, daemon coordination, approvals/redaction, channels/RPC, configuration/localization, Web/ZeroCode and prompt budgeting. Private-request hook exclusion affects programmatic hook transforms, cancellation and model selection.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #9998, the accepted contract; Related #10405, the Chat/ACP tracker. ACP remains a separate follow-up. Related #10412 is parallel session-contract work, not a dependency or supersession.
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/9998
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/10405
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/10412

### What this does, simply

A chat can keep a small reminder attached to itself rather than relying on remaining conversation history. A later primary turn receives it after restart, but another session and auxiliary workers do not. Successful whole-session reset starts without the attachments. The feature is off by default.

Operators normally approve the exact proposed mutation once. Unsupported confirmation surfaces refuse it; ordinary approvals still work. Prompt text grants no permissions and cannot override immutable safety/host instructions. If the complete collection and required tool-protocol framing cannot fit, provider dispatch fails instead of silently dropping content.

There are at most four attachments, each at most 2 KiB and 8 KiB collectively. Symbolic IDs follow `[a-z][a-z0-9_.-]{0,63}`. Changes take effect on the next top-level turn, not during the already-running turn.

The deletion fix prevents an open WebSocket from recreating a session that RPC just deleted. A same-ID successor is a new owner, not permission for the old connection or queued work to continue. Deleting `team_alpha` does not cancel an unrelated active `team.alpha` WebSocket queue; HTTP/SSE still uses its actual normalized queue and raw abort ID.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, on disposable sessions.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface: web` and `surface: tui` (ZeroCode Chat/Dashboard); messaging channels `matrix`, `slack`, `telegram`, `signal`, plus CLI confirmation. Other adapters have negative strict-capability coverage, not enabled-feature claims.
- **Setup / preconditions:** SQLite Chat persistence, `[channels].session_prompts_enabled = true`, global `session_prompt_approval = "required"`, matching clients. Default full tool selection includes the tools; a minimal configuration must name `session_prompt_list`, `session_prompt_set` and `session_prompt_delete` in `[tools].optional`, then reload. Selection grants no execution permission and does not gate injection of stored attachments into an enabled primary Chat turn. WebSocket Chat additionally requires `[gateway].session_persistence = true`; restart after enabling that prerequisite. Matrix-only configurations need not enable gateway persistence.
- **Steps to run:** Ask the agent to set `{"id":"task","content":"Keep this chat focused on the synthetic inventory task."}`; inspect the literal preview and approve once. List the collection, send another turn, restart and ask again. Check another session, then reset the original and list again. Inspect and reject a 2 KiB synthetic proposal after scrolling to its end. Separately keep a WebSocket open, delete its Chat session through RPC and try another prompt through that old connection; reconnect to create or use the intended successor.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Next-turn injection and restart persistence are current-session-only; successful reset clears the collection. Strict approval has one-time allow/reject, no Always, and rejection changes nothing. After committed deletion the old WebSocket reports `SESSION_NOT_FOUND`; it cannot recreate or adopt the successor. Durable deletion failure is reported without claiming success and preserves the durable state.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The prompt collection/configuration/tools do not exist. The independent RPC/gateway deletion paths can leave an open gateway connection able to recreate deleted durable Chat state.

### How I tested

Current candidate `1afbd5791b9c51fbf322367e1ae7f81db7920bb2` normally merges official master
`8faf3a89f66e4c2f29b3c7da3d437d927a795363` after published head `9e90a944f5e2`
(the earlier `c47322131334` merge). No rebase or force push. Source tree:
`051430426e994b2ad1be7fe24823815bdcbe7570`. Full base-relative diff SHA-256:
`db1556747bc7a0121207dff86bffee680d555b9031037534b82f316740d46373`.
The two latest conflict
resolutions retain the separate Dashboard Kill and upstream Overview-scroll
tests, plus both private-export redaction and budget-warning imports.
Upstream focused-context, setup-guidance and repaint behavior is preserved.
The following host-only anchor repair fixes Greptile's P1: previously an
attachment quoting a tool-framing phrase could be changed before dispatch.
All three new regressions failed before the repair and pass afterwards,
including captured provider requests in native/text and buffered/streamed
modes over two top-level turns. The repair does not change storage or approval.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Exact-head CI at
  `1afbd5791b9c` is terminal: 51 passed, five expected conditional skips,
  no failures; `CI Required Gate` passed. Workspace, platform, plugin,
  Web, Docs and channel-feature lanes passed. All three new anchor regressions
  passed in the workspace run; repeated runtime/channel suites passed three

  The two bounded inherited-stdio fixtures are unchanged from master; their

https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11473

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes.** Opt-in durable metadata and current-session tools. Admission/transactional ownership checks prevent stale or cross-session mutations.
- New external network calls? **No.** Approval previews use existing transports without marker expansion/upload. Matrix clients may independently fetch URL previews; disable those in the reviewing client when appropriate.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No.**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes.** Opaque bounded text intentionally enters the system prompt, beneath immutable host/safety authority.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Exact default-required single-use approval, current-session incarnation ownership, direct-only dispatch, complete prompt-budget checks and output masking contain the risk. `disabled` relaxes additional content-bound confirmation, not ordinary authorization, and can permit auto-approved writes without operator preview. Hooks cannot read sensitive bodies/results. Content hashes can permit low-entropy guessing; masking is not secrecy. Sensitive text-mode exchanges omit unrepresentable media declarations; ordinary rounds/native carriers retain upstream behavior. Previously stored opaque transcripts are not retroactively scrubbed.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **No for Rust source APIs; additive/defaulted wire and configuration fields.** Feature-off users retain ordinary session operations but are affected by the explicit lifecycle, retention, reserved-name and native-prompt changes below.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes.** `[channels].session_prompts_enabled` defaults to `false`; global/per-risk-profile `session_prompt_approval` accepts `required`/`disabled`, global default `required`, profile default inheritance. SQLite only; enabled JSONL is rejected. When session prompts are enabled, WebSocket Chat needs gateway persistence or fails with `SESSION_PROMPT_LOAD_FAILED` before dispatch.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.**
- **If backward compatibility is No or either surface/floor question is Yes: exact upgrade steps for existing users:** Back up SQLite, rebuild out-of-tree Rust consumers, match Web/ZeroCode clients to the daemon and restart after enabling persistence. Existing WebSockets need reconnect after policy changes; channels need restart. RPC resolves current policy at primary-turn entry. Add `Config.session_prompt_approval = Required`, `ChannelsConfig.session_prompts_enabled = false`, and `RiskProfileConfig.session_prompt_approval = None` to struct literals to preserve defaults.

**Rust integration migrations:**

- Add `ChannelApprovalRequest.strict_session_prompt_approval`, approval `allow_always`, and `SessionIdParams.chat_mode` (defaulted/optional on wire). Old Always responses fail closed without consuming strict requests. Unsupported/WASM adapters decline strict requests; ordinary approval remains available and WIT/WASM ABI is unchanged.
- ZeroCode Rust consumers constructing `SessionUpdate::ApprovalRequest` must supply `allow_always`; missing wire fields default to `true` for older ordinary producers. `RpcClient::session_kill` now returns `SessionKillResult { session_id, killed }`, not an untyped JSON value; callers must inspect `killed` before reporting an ended session. The channel prompt-building compatibility helpers are now test-only, but were already crate-private on master and create no external Rust migration.
- Add `TurnAttribution.session_id: Option<String>` for caller-visible identity separately from durable `session_key`. `rpc::turn::execute_turn` takes `session_prompts: Option<SessionPromptAdmission>` after `cost_context`; capture `{ backend, owner }` at primary Chat admission, never resolve a fresh owner after asynchronous preparation. Excluded execution uses `None`.
- Migrate queue `generation` use to `transcript_generation` or the separate async lifecycle-generation/lease APIs. `GatewayStarter` and gateway supervision constructors receive the shared coordination capability; `RpcContext` requires `gateway_sessions`. Share it across restart within a daemon generation, create a fresh coordination scope on reload, and do not share Chat coordination with ACP.
- `AppState.cancel_tokens` changes from upstream `Arc<Mutex<HashMap<String, Arc<CancellationToken>>>>` to `Arc<Mutex<GatewayCancellationRegistry>>`. Direct constructors use the registry instead of a plain map; entries are `GatewayCancellationEntry { session_key, generation, token }`. Registration and deletion helpers carry the actual admitted queue key and lifecycle generation, not a queue reconstructed from a normalized abort ID. Wire/configuration/SQLite formats are unchanged by this correction. Do not invent generations outside the lifecycle.
- `SessionStore::insert_admitted` is removed. Use `insert_admitted_if_absent` with the matching session permit held through restoration; handle an existing successor without replacement. `insert` acquires admission itself and must not be called while holding that permit. `insert_for_prompt` requires matching cancellation registration. `SessionStore::register_cancel_token` is test-only/crate-private; external code must use RPC lifecycle rather than directly maintaining that registry. The separate public infra gateway registration helper remains the admission path for gateway tokens; do not bypass its latch/replacement checks with raw map insertion.
- Gateway `PendingApprovals` maps IDs to public `PendingApproval` entries with crate-private fields. Construct it with `new_pending_approvals()` and pass it to `WsApprovalChannel::new`; external manual insertion/resolution must be retired or replaced by a separately designed adapter API. `ApprovalPendingMap::register` now requires `strict_session_prompt_approval: bool`; its old `insert` helper is test-only. Use `insert_with_policy(..., false)` for ordinary approvals and explicit strict metadata for prompt mutations.
- Implement durable owner/reset/prompt operations for any `SessionBackend` supporting attachments. Unsupported key-set owned deletion fails closed. The default whole-reset implementation only clears messages and is insufficient for prompt support.

**Observable changes, including with attachments disabled:**

- `sessions_reset` invokes whole-session reset, clearing attachments and rotating incarnation atomically in SQLite. Its "already empty" wording still counts removed messages, not attachment removal. Message-only clear preserves attachments.
- Durable `/new` deletion failure keeps existing history and reports `channel-runtime-new-session-failed` instead of claiming success. Without a durable backend, ordinary ephemeral behavior remains.
- Chat RPC deletion attempts `<id>`, `rpc_<id>` and `gw_<id>` aliases, even without metadata, and coordinates live gateway cancellation/invalidation. Alias deletion is atomic in SQLite; non-transactional backends delete aliases sequentially and can partially delete them on failure. Unscoped callers no longer condition durable deletion on the live record's owner (master did). ACP deletion stays in its own recorded domain. Scoped callers return `FORBIDDEN` and retain live state when principal-bound durable deletion cannot be proved, including JSONL/unavailable backend. Queue admission can report `SESSION_BUSY`; old deleted WebSockets report `SESSION_NOT_FOUND` and must reconnect. Already-cancelled work is not resumed on rollback. Gateway deletion cancels only entries bound to the deleted queue and generation; a distinct dotted WebSocket queue survives an underscore-session deletion. RPC Kill captures the queue generation before waiting and prevents prompts queued behind that killed generation from entering the provider; it does not cancel a same-ID successor.
- Current-session views, strict previews, turn spans and delegate forensic principal identity use the canonical storage key. Public RPC/cost/OpenCode/shell identity remains separate; `ZEROCLAW_SESSION_ID` prefers caller-visible identity. ACP identity is unchanged.
- The three session-prompt tool names are reserved for plugins/skills even when disabled, including prepared-skill registration. Rename conflicts. They also follow master's built-in selection: default full includes eligible prompt tools; minimal requires their explicit names in `[tools].optional` and a reload. This selection changes availability, not authorization or injection of already-stored prompts into an enabled primary Chat turn. Deferred MCP tools must use full `server__tool` names rather than conflicting bare suffixes. Indirect `unfiltered_tool_arcs` excludes prompt tools; use canonical direct calls.
- Native tool framing changes from 42 to 36 characters ("Use tools when this request needs it") for exact budget substitution, including feature-off turns. Native prompt fingerprints consequently change. Complete native/XML prompt framing is paired; nonempty attachment overflow fails closed without truncating host context.
- Strict mutation previews visibly encode Unicode 17 format/default-ignorable characters, including legitimate joiners and variation selectors. This can change how joined text and emoji look in the preview; stored text, content hashes and provider context keep the original bytes. This is display encoding, not a new restriction on valid prompt text.
- Channel retention preserves upstream selection after the last user-role row, including synthetic text-tool results. Text-protocol call/result exchanges are omitted from retained history; native-tool retention remains unchanged. Privacy projection scans the complete exchange before selection so host-marked results can identify sensitive calls. Provider working history is unchanged.
- Export recovery separately recognizes malformed JSON/XML/MiniMax prompt-tool material before ordinary diagnostic output; shared streamed detection retains master's name-based behavior. Recovery is best-effort, not approval or execution. Unrepresentable text media carriers are omitted only for marked sensitive rounds; ordinary media behavior remains upstream.
- Programmatic `HookHandler::before_llm_call` is skipped when the request or active scope carries private session-prompt content, including max-iteration summaries. Its transforms, cancellation and model selection do not apply to these requests; ordinary requests retain them. The classifier is deliberately conservative: parseable `session_prompt_*` envelopes can skip the hook even with the feature disabled. The feature guide documents this caveat; the short API rustdoc does not enumerate it. Observational input masking remains separate, and provider working history is never replaced with a masked hook projection.
- With single-tool rounds enabled, the host instruction is inserted before the private Session Prompts suffix. Diagnostic exports retain that instruction, and host protocol replacement leaves opaque attachment bytes unchanged. Trim reconstruction preserves the canonical host prompt before reapplying the transient instruction. Ordinary no-attachment and no-system behavior is preserved.
- Independent child transcripts withhold attachment-bearing parent protocol scope, while same-agent inline SOP continues the primary transcript without attachment tools. Ordinary non-attachment child protocol inheritance is pre-existing and intentionally unchanged by this repair; this is not general child-context isolation.

The additive incarnation migration adopts valid unbound legacy attachments and removes mismatches/orphans. Historical legacy ownership cannot be proved retroactively; reset questionable old sessions. Feature-off does not delete stored attachments or scrub old histories. Downgrading and clearing history with an older binary can leave attachments that reappear after re-upgrade; reset affected sessions before downgrade and retain the backup.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Reset/delete affected sessions with this version first when stored attachments must be removed; back up SQLite and restore the previous known-good binary/client pair. Reverting this feature restores previous source behavior but does not retroactively clean stored data. Keep the backup for migration recovery.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** Set `[channels].session_prompts_enabled = false` and restart. This stops injection/tools, not attachment persistence, redaction of previously marked history or the feature-off lifecycle/retention changes described above. Reset/delete is required to remove attachments.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `SESSION_PROMPT_LOAD_FAILED`, `SESSION_NOT_FOUND`, `SESSION_BUSY`, `FORBIDDEN`, `channel-runtime-new-session-failed`, strict-preview refusal or prompt-budget errors before provider dispatch. Modifying-hook callbacks not firing for classified private requests is intentional; deployments relying on hook transforms/cancellation/model selection must account for this exclusion and conservative feature-off cases. Inspect lifecycle/approval metadata without dumping prompt bodies. An idle old WebSocket refusing after committed deletion is expected behavior, not a reason to bypass the owner fence.

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Adds an optional, encrypted OpenRouter management API key, separate from the inference API key.
  - Adds an authenticated gateway endpoint that retrieves OpenRouter credit totals without exposing the management credential or upstream response to the browser.
  - Shows an OpenRouter balance card in the web dashboard only when an enabled agent uses OpenRouter and the integration is configured and reachable.
  - Adds English and Portuguese UI strings and documents the optional configuration.
- **Scope boundary:** This does not change inference routing, model selection, billing, or other providers. It does not expose the management key to the dashboard.
- **Blast radius:** OpenRouter provider configuration, the authenticated web API, and the dashboard overview. Existing installations without `management_api_key` retain their current behavior and do not show the card.
- **Linked issue(s):** Supersedes #11231. Related #11204; this account-balance card does not repair per-request spend accounting.

### What this does, simply

OpenRouter users could configure inference but could not see their remaining credits in ZeroClaw. This change introduces a distinct management credential for the OpenRouter credits API, keeps that credential encrypted and server-side, and conditionally displays the returned credit balance on the dashboard. If OpenRouter is not actively configured, the management key is absent, or the request fails, the endpoint returns no content and the dashboard card stays hidden.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface: web`.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Configure an enabled OpenRouter agent, its inference API key, and a separate `management_api_key`; start the gateway and pair the dashboard.
- **Steps to run:** Open the overview. On a test installation, repeat with the management key missing or invalid and with the OpenRouter agent disabled.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Credit totals appear only for an active, configured, reachable integration. Missing/inactive/unavailable integrations return `204` and hide the card. Unauthenticated requests return `401`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** No account-credit endpoint or balance card.

### How I tested

Refreshed against master `8faf3a89f`. Repaired the four findings in the original review: deterministic `sort_by_key` and direct struct initialization in the credits tests. No lint-suppression attributes were added.

- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check
# exit 0

git diff --check upstream/master
# exit 0

npm ci --no-audit --no-fund
# added 226 packages; exit 0
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The Linux workspace Lint and Web Permission Tests checks passed on head `44e60879fd57f6f9bf693528e481de6e878244e0`. Other platform/runtime checks are still running; pending checks are not claimed as passing.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Strict local Windows Clippy was attempted, both with and without dependency linting. Files identical to master block it with Windows-only diagnostics: `resolved_launcher`, `resolved_shell`, the nested conditional in `windows_key_file.rs`, and `replace_parent` in `api_config.rs`. The Windows linker also emits a localized import-library notice. These platform limitations are disclosed, not suppressed or bundled as unrelated fixes. The focused gateway credits tests passed: `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway openrouter_credits --lib` (2 passed, 0 failed). The credential-encryption test also passed: `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config openrouter_management_key_encrypts_and_decrypts --lib` (1 passed, 0 failed).
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The running authenticated dashboard renders the balance card; reload retains authentication; authenticated credits return numeric totals; unauthenticated access returns `401`. We continue using the integration successfully in our own deployment.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Real browser screenshots with financial text lines masked before writing the PNGs; no generated illustrations or isolated component mocks.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** The renderer introduced in `0f965eee` is unchanged by this refresh and lint repair. Captures were taken on 2026-10-18 in visible Chrome at 1440 x 1000 and 390 x 844. The deployment reports gateway 0.8.6 and uses a compatibility adapter for its credits route. These screenshots prove the UI and deployed use, not this head's native Rust handler. Details are in the provenance note.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:**
  - [Desktop screenshot](https://github.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/blob/44e60879fd57f6f9bf693528e481de6e878244e0/.pr-evidence/pr-11231-openrouter-balance-desktop.png)
  - [Mobile screenshot](https://github.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/blob/44e60879fd57f6f9bf693528e481de6e878244e0/.pr-evidence/pr-11231-openrouter-balance-mobile.png)
  - [Capture provenance and limits](https://github.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/blob/44e60879fd57f6f9bf693528e481de6e878244e0/.pr-evidence/pr-11231-openrouter-balance.md)
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Opened the overview, verified the visible card, refreshed, and scrolled to it at mobile width. No JavaScript page errors or horizontal document overflow were observed.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** A full local Linux workspace gate is not claimed; this workstation hits the baseline Windows diagnostics above. Required Linux CI remains the full gate. A new local web build is not claimed; the required web typecheck covers the refreshed schema and TypeScript contract.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No**
- New external network calls? **Yes**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **Yes**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No**
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: The gateway makes a fixed-host HTTPS request to OpenRouter's credits API with a short timeout. The distinct management key uses the existing encrypted configuration path, is never returned to the browser, and upstream bodies are not logged. The endpoint is protected by the gateway bearer authentication and returns only normalized numeric totals.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes**
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes**
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No**
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: Existing users need no action. To enable the optional card, add `management_api_key` to the relevant OpenRouter provider entry; omitting it preserves existing behavior.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Remove `management_api_key` to disable the integration; existing inference credentials are unaffected. Revert the balance feature if rollback is needed. No database migration is introduced.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

- Superseded PRs + authors: #11231 by @CastelloBrancoTecnologia.
- Scope materially carried forward: The original optional encrypted management credential, authenticated credits endpoint, dashboard card, localization, documentation, and tests.
- Co-authored-by trailers added for incorporated contributors? No.
- If No, why: This is the same author's branch and implementation; the original commit remains in the branch history. No other contributor's implementation was incorporated by this refresh.

prs.title: fix(zerocode): render live session updates promptly under load
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - The app event loop drained the notification broadcast only once per frame and otherwise blocked in `event::poll` for up to the 200 ms idle `TICK`, so streamed `session/update`s rendered late. The input wait is now split into 16 ms slices (`poll_input_or_transport`). It returns early when either chat pane reports pending transport events (`has_pending_transport_events`: notification broadcast, prompt completions, resync and reattach results). Input is always polled for one slice first, so redraws stay at about 60 fps or less while streaming.
  - Every `ToolResult` called `mark_dirty_full()`, which re-renders up to 1000 entries (markdown parse and wrap) per result. With large transcripts and tool-heavy turns, those slow frames are what let the broadcast overflow. A result on the tail entry now uses `mark_dirty_tail`. `rebuild_lines` already falls back to a full rebuild when the mutated entry is not the cached tail (parallel tool calls), so the cache never goes stale.
  - `NOTIFICATION_CHANNEL_CAPACITY` goes from 1024 to 4096 as headroom for draw stalls (resize storms, full rebuilds, descheduling).
  - Why it matters: after #10801, a `Lagged` broadcast no longer cancels turns. It still reloads every tracked session's durable transcript with the live stream gated, and with large transcripts that shows up as multi-second stalls in live updates whenever several sessions or tool calls are active. This PR makes that lag much rarer.
- **Scope boundary:** Does not change the `Lagged` recovery path (`begin_notification_resync` / `Reattach` from #10801), the daemon, or the wire protocol. Does not move broadcast draining onto a dedicated task. #10785 also suggests that, but it needs the synchronous `push_notification_for_test` → `drain_notifications` tests reworked, so it is left for a follow-up.
- **Blast radius:** zerocode TUI only. Affects the app event loop's input wait (redraw cadence for every pane), chat/ACP transcript caching for tool results, and the per-connection notification buffer size, which also backs the Logs pane subscriber.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10785 (follow-up to #10801; addresses its "drain more promptly / raise the capacity" item but not the off-draw-loop drain).
- **Labels:** (path and size labelers to apply; maintainer to set `risk:*`)

### What this does, simply

When several agent sessions are streaming in zerocode, or a turn makes many tool calls, the screen can stop updating for seconds and then jump ahead. Three things caused this. Zerocode only checked for new updates about five times a second. Each tool result made it re-render the whole visible transcript. If too many updates piled up between checks, the buffer overflowed and zerocode reloaded every session from scratch, showing nothing new until the reload finished. With this change, zerocode wakes up as soon as updates arrive (at most about 60 redraws a second), re-renders only the tool card that changed, and has a four-times-larger buffer. Overflows are much rarer, so live output keeps flowing. If an overflow still happens, the recovery behaves exactly as before.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface`: `tui` (zerocode Code/Chat panes, agent sidebar)
- **Setup / preconditions:** A daemon with an agent on a chatty model that runs tool loops. Open 3 or more Code (ACP) sessions in one zerocode instance.
- **Steps to run:** Start a long tool-heavy turn in each session. Watch the focused transcript and the sidebar status dots. Optionally stress the draw loop by resizing the terminal repeatedly, or by `kill -STOP <zerocode pid>` for about 1 s then `kill -CONT`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Streamed text and tool cards appear smoothly with no visible 200 ms batching. The "Live updates were missed, so the durable transcript was reloaded" notice is rare and only shows up after long stalls.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Output arrives in visible 200 ms batches. With several busy sessions, the reload notice appears repeatedly and the live stream freezes for each reload.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The required Rust lint and test jobs cover `apps/zerocode` (fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo test` for the zerocode bin target, where the chat and app tests live). Pending on this head; not yet used as evidence.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** CI does not exercise a live daemon with concurrent streaming sessions, so the latency improvement is not proven end-to-end by CI (see the manual verification note below).
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```sh
cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode
# test result: ok. 1396 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 5.75s

cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode -- tool_result_rerenders input_wait_returns_early notifications_route_to_background
# test chat::tests::notifications_route_to_background_sessions ... ok
# test chat::tests::tool_result_rerenders_only_the_tail_card_and_matches_full_rebuild ... ok
# test app::tests::input_wait_returns_early_for_pending_transport_events ... ok
# test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1395 filtered out

cargo clippy -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings
# Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 45.68s   (no warnings)

cargo fmt -p zerocode -- --check
# (clean)
```

  New and extended tests:
  - `input_wait_returns_early_for_pending_transport_events`: pending transport ends the wait after exactly one slice; input wins in the same slice; when idle, the wait slices up to the full timeout and never polls past a slice.
  - `tool_result_rerenders_only_the_tail_card_and_matches_full_rebuild`: a tail `ToolResult` sets `TailChanged`, and the incremental output equals a forced full rebuild; a non-tail result (parallel calls) also equals a full rebuild.
  - `notifications_route_to_background_sessions`: now also asserts `has_pending_transport_events()` is true with a queued notification and false after draining.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Code-path review: `has_pending_transport_events` uses only non-consuming `is_empty()` checks; every pane `tick()` reached by the extra early-wake iterations (dashboard, logs, quickstart, SOP, chrome status) is already rate-limited, so faster wakes do not add RPC traffic. **Not verified:** a live multi-session run against a daemon. The reviewer A/B steps above are the intended end-to-end check.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. No layout, styling, or wrapping change: transcript output is unchanged (the tail re-render produces lines identical to a full rebuild), and only redraw timing changes. The equality assertion is helper-level, not final-interface evidence.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `265465ddc`, zerocode bin unit tests, Linux x86_64, rustc 1.98.1.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A (see above)
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** See the test descriptions above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full-workspace `cargo test` and `clippy` were not run locally: the change is confined to `apps/zerocode` and the required CI covers the workspace.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert 265465ddc` (single commit, zerocode only)
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Higher zerocode CPU while sessions stream (expected up to about 60 redraws/s; sustained CPU when idle would be a regression). A tool card not showing its result until the next full redraw would indicate the tail-path fallback misbehaving. The "Live updates were missed…" notice (`zc-chat-resync-*`) appearing as often as before would mean the lag is not reduced.

prs.title: feat(tools): add opt-in subprocess memory watchdog
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Add `runtime_profiles.<alias>.shell_max_memory_mb`, measured in MiB and disabled by default, for native shell and skill subprocesses.
  - Sample the command's resident memory plus its visible descendants. Stop the owned command group or Windows Job Object when a sample exceeds the threshold, and return a failed `ToolResult` with the threshold and observed memory.
  - Share the existing capped-output execution path between shell and skill tools. Stop the command on monitoring failure, preserve capped partial output with truncation markers, and bound cleanup waiting after timeout or failure.
  - Check zero RSS readings through the operating system's process API. Accept a confirmed zero for the same observed process identity and skip descendants confirmed to have exited after the snapshot. Unreadable live processes and incomplete responses remain monitoring errors.
  - Carry the threshold through the existing runtime-profile policy. Explicit child policies cannot raise or disable a finite parent threshold.
- **Scope boundary:** No `RLIMIT_AS`, default memory cap, hard allocation ceiling, cgroup implementation, or guarantee against host OOM. Detached or reparented processes can escape sampling. Docker keeps its existing container memory controls.
- **Blast radius:** Native shell and skill execution, runtime-profile policy construction, explicit child-policy validation, and Windows process ownership. Existing tool admission, environment filtering, and sandbox authorization remain in place.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #6916. The original strict OOM-prevention requirements remain open. #7937 introduced the earlier implementation, which #8417 reverted; this PR uses resident-memory sampling instead of restoring it.
- **Runtime placement:** The bounded native shell/skill RSS scope was approved by @tidux and recorded in merged #11436. Merged #11697 widens its catalogue coverage to all five locale files used here.

### What this does, simply

The shell and skill tools let an agent run programs on your machine. Their timeout and output cap limit how long a command runs and how much text ZeroClaw stores, but they do not limit the memory used by the program itself.

This adds an optional watcher. You choose a memory threshold in the agent's runtime profile. While its command runs, ZeroClaw samples the physical memory used by that command and its visible children. If the total crosses the threshold, ZeroClaw stops the owned command group and tells the agent why it failed. A zero reading is checked directly with the operating system so an unavailable measurement is not mistaken for no memory use. A child that exits between the snapshot and that check no longer causes an otherwise healthy command to be stopped. If output was capped before a command failed, its partial output says it was truncated.

The watcher is off unless configured. It reacts after observing memory use, so a command can exceed the threshold between samples. It does not reserve memory, impose a kernel allocation ceiling, or guarantee that an out-of-memory event cannot happen. Virtual-address reservations alone do not count, avoiding the earlier virtual-memory-limit approach.

### Scope and maintenance tradeoff

Both tool entry points need the same child ownership, bounded output capture, timeout, and memory-failure handling. Sharing the existing shell runner avoids implementing those lifecycles twice. The new sampler uses the existing `sysinfo` dependency; Windows containment and failed-spawn cleanup reuse the existing `process-wrap` dependency and service guard.

The essential new work is per-command process ancestry and RSS sampling, plus platform-specific ownership on Windows. Three small native readers resolve zero readings without adding another process cache or dependency. They compare the returned process identity at the existing whole-second precision; this does not eliminate every descendant PID-reuse race. There is no global process cache, new dependency, polling scheduler, or sandbox backend. Sampling runs about every 100 ms plus observation time. Its metadata work scales with host process count and concurrent monitored commands; disabled monitoring starts no sampler. Shared resident pages may count more than once.

Monitoring follows the root command's lifetime. On Windows, dropping the enabled command's owner explicitly terminates its Job Object before closing the handle, stopping remaining job descendants even after root completion. Non-native runtimes, Docker sandboxes, and unsupported operating systems reject an enabled watchdog before spawning; Docker deployments should use their existing container memory limits.

The bounded runtime placement exception is recorded by merged #11436.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. Focused tests spawn real subprocesses and exercise resident allocation, descendant aggregation, virtual reservation, and tool-result conversion without requiring a provider or changing a live agent's configuration.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [Required CI](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38010558146) passes on `73db3b5cae818a5d45d9f5676f69643d8ee48007`, including Linux Test, Parallel Runtime Test, Lint, Format, Windows compilation and task-owner recovery. The same head ran in [hosted macOS](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39163181716/job/117780719339) and [hosted Windows](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39163181716/job/117780719366) jobs. All 12 macOS and 11 Windows subprocess-memory tests passed, including `descendant_departure_after_snapshot_is_not_a_monitor_failure` and `failed_native_read_does_not_accept_sysinfo_zero` on both platforms, the complete native-record check on macOS, and `root_exit_closes_owned_job_descendants` on Windows. Both platforms also pass the resident-memory tool diagnostic, shell/skill container rejection and policy non-escalation tests. macOS passes terminal detachment, timeout/cancellation descendant cleanup and all three truncation tests. Both hosted jobs ran `cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-fail-fast`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The new departure regression has now executed on both macOS and Windows at the current head. The full platform suites remain red: macOS ran 19,490 tests with 19,484 passed, six failed and 39 skipped; Windows ran 19,043 tests with 19,034 passed, nine failed and 36 skipped. The six macOS failures exactly match the [earlier macOS run](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38000741090/job/114058025862), covering Telegram prompt timing, a filesystem spelling fixture, Hailo-Ollama and Serply connection classification, RPC session-method grants and Tailscale probe timing. No clean-master macOS execution baseline was run. The nine Windows failures exactly match both the [earlier Windows run](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38000741090/job/114058025868) and the [clean-master Windows run](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/37880263821/job/113658218149). The previously identified fixes in #11361, #11362, #11363, #11365, #11366 and #11630 remain separate from this branch.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

The integrated head `73db3b5cae818a5d45d9f5676f69643d8ee48007` passes the focused macOS watchdog, terminal-detachment and descendant-cleanup checks:

```text
cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -E 'test(tools::subprocess_memory::tests) | test(shell_child_cannot_open_owners_controlling_terminal) | test(shell_reaps_descendants_after_timeout_or_cancellation)' --test-threads=1
Summary: 14 tests run, 14 passed.

cargo fmt --all -- --check
Passed.

bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
Comment hygiene gate passed.

git diff --check
Passed.
```

The departure repair at `a42774653cd4f1458707854863228f3e5d6594ef` passes the focused macOS watchdog suite, formatting, diff integrity and comment hygiene:

```text
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib tools::subprocess_memory::tests -- --test-threads=1
12 passed; 0 failed on macOS, including descendant departure and live read-failure controls.

cargo fmt --all
Passed.
```

The following results are from earlier implementation and repair candidates:

```text
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib tools::subprocess_memory::tests -- --test-threads=1
11 passed; 0 failed on the repaired candidate.

cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib tools::shell::tests::shell_marks
3 passed; 0 failed, including capped stdout/stderr on timeout.

cargo fmt --all
Passed on the repaired candidate.

Earlier implementation validation:
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config --lib -- from_profiles_ ensure_no_escalation_
27 passed; 0 failed.

cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- tools::subprocess_memory:: tools::shell::tests:: tools::skill_tool::tests::
110 passed; 0 failed; completed in 2.86 seconds after compilation.

cargo fmt -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime
Passed.

bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
Comment hygiene gate passed.

git diff --check
Passed.
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Source comparison confirms that shell and skill tools use the same runner, enabled monitoring is rejected before unsupported execution, and bounded delegates retain their parent-owned tool policy. No real-account or live-agent exercise was needed for the subprocess contract.
- **Build warning:** The macOS linker reported that the debug test executable's `__eh_frame` section exceeds its 16 MiB compact-unwind encoding limit. All selected tests completed. Existing clean-master validation also records this linker warning; no new source warning was reported.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. This changes subprocess enforcement rather than visual presentation. The shell regression observes the returned failed tool result and memory diagnostic.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** The commits in this PR; native subprocess execution and `ToolResult`, exercised by `tools::subprocess_memory::tests`, `tools::shell::tests`, `tools::skill_tool::tests`, and the config policy tests.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** `shell_memory_failure_surfaces_resident_cause` checks that the failed tool result identifies the resident-memory threshold.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** The process fixtures distinguish touched resident pages from a large untouched virtual reservation, aggregate two descendants, and preserve completion when monitoring is disabled or memory stays below the threshold. Focused regressions distinguish successful zero measurements from failed reads and identity changes, and confirm truncation markers on both captured streams after a timeout. The departure regression discovers a live child, deliberately kills and reaps it before the native fallback, and confirms that sampling continues; its live-process read-denial control remains an error. The integrated master regressions confirm the child cannot open its owner's controlling terminal and descendants stop after timeout or cancellation. Policy tests parse the setting and reject child escalation.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No duplicate local full-workspace run. Hosted macOS and Windows execution now covers the changed native process paths on the current head, alongside the focused local macOS checks and required Linux CI. The remaining full-platform failures are recorded above.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes. Memory failure adds a localized diagnostic to the existing tool result. Its threshold and RSS values are numeric, and it grants no authority. Existing command output remains untrusted and capped.
- **Risk and mitigation:** A configured watchdog can stop a legitimate memory-heavy command. Shared pages can inflate the total, and polling can miss short spikes. Only owned process groups or Job Objects are signaled; sampled descendant PIDs are never termination targets. Samples remain in memory for the invocation and are not persisted.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for existing configuration. The new setting defaults to `0`. Sharing the shell runner also bounds skill output during collection and applies owned-process cleanup on skill timeout or cancellation.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes. Adds `runtime_profiles.<alias>.shell_max_memory_mb`.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- **Upgrade steps:** None for existing users. To opt in, set `shell_max_memory_mb` in the runtime profile selected by the agent. Use `0` to disable it. For Docker runtime limits, use `runtime.docker.memory_limit_mb` instead of this native watchdog.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Set the selected runtime profile's `shell_max_memory_mb` to `0` and recreate the affected agent/session. Revert the merge commit to remove the implementation and shared skill-runner change entirely.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `runtime_profiles.<alias>.shell_max_memory_mb = 0` disables sampling.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Failed tool results containing `resident-memory threshold`, `resident-memory monitoring failed`, or the unsupported-native-runtime diagnostic. Legitimate commands terminating early indicate a threshold that is too low or a monitoring failure.

## Supersede Attribution

N/A. This does not supersede an open PR or incorporate contributor code from the reverted implementation.

prs.body: ## Summary - **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions) - **What changed and why:** - `CostTracker::check_budget` returns `BudgetCheck::Warning` once recorded spend reaches `cost.warn_at_percent` of the daily or monthly limit, but `enforce_tool_loop_budget` only handled `Exceeded`. The warning was dropped, so the first sign of a limit was a failed turn. - The main tool loop now calls `announce_budget_warning` before the hard-limit gate. It sends a new `TurnEvent::BudgetWarning { current_usd, limit_usd, period }` at most once per turn. It never blocks the turn: an exceeded limit is still `enforce_tool_loop_budget`'s stop, and a full or closed event channel just drops the notice. - The RPC surface forwards the event as a `budget_warning` `session/update` (`SessionUpdateEvent::BudgetWarning`, `period` is `"day"` or `"month"`). - ZeroCode parses it and shows a system notice: "Cost warning: $8.25 of the $10.00 daily limit spent (82%). Turns stop at the limit." The daemon repeats the event on every turn while spend stays over the line. The client shows it once per period and limit per session, so it reappears only when the limit changes or the other period crosses its own threshold. - **Scope boundary:** no notice for a turn that stops at the hard limit (that is still the failed-turn message, and #11589 covers the override prompt). ACP (`acp_server.rs`) and the web gateway (`ws.rs`) ignore the new event; their `_ =>` arms already drop unknown variants. Only the English locale gets the new strings; the other locales fall back to English. `cost.enforcement.mode` stays unread. - **Blast radius:** a new `#[non_exhaustive]` `TurnEvent` variant. Every existing match has a wildcard arm (workspace `check --all-targets` passes). One extra `check_budget(0.0)` per provider call, which is the same ledger read `enforce_tool_loop_budget` already does. - **Linked issue(s):** Closes #10950. Related #11585, #11589. ### What this does, simply ZeroClaw can be told to warn you when you have spent, say, 80% of your daily AI budget. The code that works out "you are at 80%" already existed, but nothing passed the result on, so you never saw a warning. You only found out when a turn failed at 100%. This PR passes the warning through to ZeroCode, which shows it once as a line in the chat. Nothing is blocked and no setting changes. ## Testing (required) ### How you can test (when useful) - **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes - **Interface(s) exercised:** `tui` (ZeroCode) - **Setup / preconditions:** an isolated config with `[cost] enabled = true`, a small `daily_limit_usd` (for example `0.50`) and the default `warn_at_percent = 80`, on a priced model. - **Steps to run:** chat until recorded spend passes 80% of the limit, then send one more message. - **Expected on this branch (after):** a "Cost warning: $… of the $0.50 daily limit spent (…%)" system line appears once, before the reply. Later turns don't repeat it. - **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** no warning. The first visible sign is "Budget exceeded: … Cannot make further API calls until the budget resets." when the limit is hit. ### How I tested - **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the Rust test and clippy jobs cover all three crates touched. - **Conflict refresh validation:** Head `42170990c043461acf72e8ebe5977160095c9cf0` integrates master `cdefa0d0a6bf95bb9c7fe90e174b948af3a76166`, preserving its seeded request usage alongside the once-per-turn warning latch. Formatting and scoped comment hygiene passed. The resolved file and the eight-file PR diff pass whitespace checks; the full merge check only flags unchanged vendored Markdown inherited from master. Comparison with Git's automatic merge confirms only the one approved conflict block differs. [Fresh Quality Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39035246444) passed Format, `Check (default features, all targets)` and Lint on this exact head, including Clippy and the Rustdoc warnings gate; other CI jobs are still running. No local Cargo or new terminal interaction was run for this mechanical refresh. Prior-head test results below remain historical. - **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none for the logic. The live crossing in ZeroCode is being dogfooded (below). - **Commands run and tail output** (run on a Mac mini through our cargo wrapper, at 5f66713d5a9d): - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- budget_warning spend_past_the_warning spend_below_the_threshold` → `test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed` - `cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode -- budget_warning` → `test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed` - Each test fails with its fix removed: with `announce_budget_warning` made a no-op and the dispatch arm returning `None`, 2 of the 3 runtime tests fail; with the client dedupe disabled, `budget_warning_shows_one_notice_per_period_and_limit` fails. - `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` → `Finished`, no warnings - `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` → `Finished` - Wider runs: `zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- agent::turn rpc::dispatch agent::cost` gives 938 passed, 1 failed; `zerocode --bin zerocode` gives 1447 passed, 1 failed. The two failures (`new_session_methods_are_denied_without_their_grants`, `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint`) also fail on master on this machine. - `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on the changed files is clean. - **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Tested with $40 budget. Warning appeared at $33.73. - **Visual interface evidence:** - **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** 5f66713d5a9d, ZeroCode chat state (`chat::tests::budget_warning_*`). - **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** above - **Action or changed state and observed result:** see the tests above. - **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** a full `cargo test --workspace` was skipped; CI runs it. ## Security & Privacy Impact (required) - New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No - New external network calls? No - Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No - PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No - Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. The notice is client-side chat state and never enters model history. - If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A ## Compatibility (required) - Backward compatible? Yes. Older clients ignore an unknown `session/update` type. Older daemons never send it. - Config / env / CLI surface changed? No. `warn_at_percent` now does what its docs say. - Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No ## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs) - **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert 5f66713d5a9d` - **Feature flags or config toggles:** `cost.warn_at_percent = 100` makes a warning coincide with the limit, which in effect turns it off. - **Observable failure symptoms:** repeated cost-warning lines in ZeroCode, or none at all. Grep the runtime trace for `cost warning threshold reached`.

prs.title: feat(zerocode): show focused runtime context
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** Show the focused Code and Chat agent, live provider/model, client queue, and configured runtime profile in Dashboard Overview, plus a Sessions row with each agent's open sessions in this window counted by state (blocked, working, idle, done). Add the client version beside the daemon version and summarize existing component health with a pointer to the Health tab.
- **Scope boundary:** Profiles describe the daemon's current configuration, not a running session's retained profile generation or limits. This does not change config selection, agent execution, queue behavior, diagnostics checks, or the existing connection-time version mismatch rejection.
- **Blast radius:** ZeroCode's focused-session projection and Overview rendering, its existing status caches, five built-in Fluent catalogues, and an additive optional field in the existing `agents/status` response.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #8383

### What this does, simply

ZeroCode can keep separate Code and Chat sessions open. They can use different agents, models, and workspaces. Dashboard already identifies the daemon, config, endpoint, and working directories, but users still had to open other panes to see which session choices were active or whether work was running or queued. The focused session's own state was not enough: it read idle while another session of the same agent was working.

This PR puts that information together in Overview. Matching Code and Chat values share a clearly labeled row; different values stay separate. Each context also shows its agent's configured runtime profile. This is configuration information, not a measurement of the profile or limits applied inside a running turn. An unavailable profile stays unavailable rather than showing a guessed default.

Overview also shows both program versions and a short health summary with a route to details. Unknown or starting components do not count as healthy. Failed polling clears old profile or health evidence instead of continuing to show it as current. These are orientation changes, not new controls over the daemon or its sessions.

### Scope and maintenance tradeoff

The client reuses its focused-session accessors, existing agent polling, health snapshot, and Fluent catalogues. The daemon adds one optional configured-profile field to `agents/status` because that value belongs to daemon config, not a second client-side config reader. Older responses without the field remain readable. No new RPC method, dependency, configuration key, or profile registry is introduced. The runtime part is covered by the holding-crate exception row for the configured runtime-profile status projection in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md`, [approved in #11732](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11732#pullrequestreview-5549713890).

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=tui`
- **Setup / preconditions:** Use a matching ZeroCode/daemon build and existing Code or Chat sessions. For a visible profile value, use an agent that already references a valid runtime profile. Focus different agents or model overrides in the two panes to inspect separate contexts; matching contexts should combine.
- **Steps to run:** Launch `zerocode`, open Dashboard, then Overview at an 80-column terminal width. Inspect the context, profile, version, and health rows. Open the Health tab for details. Queue a follow-up during a running turn to inspect the client-queue continuation. Repeat the same navigation on `master`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Code and Chat retain their own context labels and choices. Each displays a configured profile or unavailable. Both versions appear. Health counts distinguish healthy, unhealthy, and unconfirmed components. A nonempty client queue shows its count and pause marker on a short continuation; long identifiers retain existing clipping behavior.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Overview has daemon/config/endpoint/workspace orientation but lacks the focused Code/Chat context and configured profile, explicit client version, and component health rollup.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38515376567/job/115695728018) passed on exact head `196500bf9d7`. Format, Lint, Test, Parallel Runtime Test, Security, Zerocode RPC Boundary, MSRV, the Linux build, and macOS/Windows checks passed. The aggregate compilation and runtime suites validate the final fixture form with current master's live-config handle.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None beyond the visual check below.
- **Commands run and tail output:** These local results cover completion `3d532fa7c8e`. The subsequent change only reconstructs the valid and missing-profile runtime fixtures, which the final-head hosted tests validate. The ZeroCode source and its 19-test result are unchanged.

  ```text
  cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode -- runtime_context overview_status_lines health_rollup runtime_profile_tests argument_messages_format_in_all_builtin_catalogues chrome_status_failed_health_refresh
  test result: ok. 19 passed; 0 failed; 1411 filtered out

  cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib agents_status_runtime_profile
  test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 5466 filtered out

  cargo fmt --all -- --check
  exit 0
  ```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Source comparison confirms pane-local session ownership, canonical configured-profile resolution, legacy response compatibility, and reuse of the existing version-mismatch rejection. I have been running the Dashboard Overview in daily use since 2026-10-15 in the [experiment build](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/experiment/zerocode-builds/20261015T062922Z-af67956b5e9d), which carries this PR's commits.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Screenshot.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Local completion evidence at `3d532fa7c8e`; final runtime fixture repair and aggregate CI at `196500bf9d7`. Dashboard Overview captured from the [experiment build](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/experiment/zerocode-builds/20261015T062922Z-af67956b5e9d), which contains this PR's commits. The Sessions row (one line per agent with how many of this window's sessions are blocked, working, idle or done) is `0c663e380564` on this branch, the same change the build carries.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** [Dashboard Overview screenshot](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11513#issuecomment-6231978407)

### Visual evidence

The [Dashboard Overview screenshot](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11513#issuecomment-6231978407) shows the complete status box: daemon and client versions, the focused context with its configured runtime profile, and the health summary.

- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Automated tests cover combined, single-pane, and split context composition; profile matching and unavailable values; legacy payloads; health classification and failed-refresh invalidation; and all built-in catalogue interpolation. A queue-width assertion protects its count and pause marker. These checks do not establish final terminal clipping or glanceability.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** None.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A. The additive response exposes only the configured profile alias to the existing status client, not profile contents or credentials.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. The optional response field can be absent in older payloads. Existing clients ignore the additive field.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No new settings or arguments. Dashboard display changes as described above.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: N/A. No migration is required; existing client/daemon version-matching rules still apply.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the PR's squash commit. On the unmerged branch, revert `196500bf9d7`, then `3d532fa7c8e`, then `2324f987f8`.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Overview mislabels Code/Chat context, shows a stale configured profile or healthy snapshot after failed polling, or clips the status box or queue marker at ordinary terminal sizes.
