prs.title: fix(tools): expose scenario routing requirements
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Advertise `hint`, `model_provider`, and `model` as required nonblank strings when `model_routing_config` selects `upsert_scenario`. Put the guarded `if` and `then` directly on the object schema, without a top-level composition wrapper. Require an explicit action in the condition so an omitted action still defaults to `get`.
  - Share that field list with validation and report all missing, non-string, or blank required fields in one localized error, before reading or changing configuration.
  - Preserve whole-object argument recovery for schemas with `if`, `then`, or `else`. Decode one JSON-stringified value matching an explicit object/array type, then stop before conditional child traversal. Keep the existing reference, composition, tuple-array, ambiguous-type, malformed-input, shape and depth safeguards.
- **Scope boundary:** Other action contracts, optional-field parsing, persistence, permissions, provider implementations, and repetitive-tool recovery are unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** Consumers of this tool's parameter schema and scenario-validation feedback, plus native and text-fallback argument recovery for explicitly typed conditional schemas. The flat argument object and tool registration remain unchanged.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11708.
- **Runtime placement:** The bounded #11371/#11479 scope amendment is proposed separately in the existing exception batch #11697. It covers only explicit outer object/array decoding for conditional schemas and its focused regressions. Explicit Core Team approval must be recorded before merge; the existing #11436 approval covers only the original scope. This implementation PR does not change ADR-016 or the exception table.

### What this does, simply

Agents use this tool to choose which model handles a kind of request. Previously, its published instructions did not say which fields a scenario update required. If a model left several fields out, the tool reported only the first problem, leaving the model to discover the others over successive retries.

This change publishes the complete required set for scenario updates and returns every invalid required field together. The model receives enough information to correct the call in one retry. This does not guarantee that a model follows the instructions or chooses the right tool, and it does not turn model routing into a network-permission control.

Some models return the entire argument object as a JSON string. The new conditional schema initially prevented ZeroClaw from decoding it, so a requested scenario update could become a successful read without saving anything. The response parser now restores the declared outer object before dispatch. It leaves conditional child values to the tool's normal validation.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The focused suite exercises the actual tool dispatch, configuration bytes, schema cleaner, and prompt serializer deterministically; interactive model tool choice is nondeterministic.

### How I tested

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
# Passed.

cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-tools --lib model_routing_config
# test result: ok. 16 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured;
# 2071 filtered out; finished in 0.27s

cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib argument_preservation_tests
# test result: ok. 8 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured;
# 5718 filtered out; finished in 0.08s

bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
# Comment hygiene gate passed.

git diff --check
# Passed.

```

- **Coverage:** Tests check complete correction feedback for missing, wrong-type, and blank strings, byte-identical configuration after invalid calls, argument errors before config-read errors, preserved read-only admission, implicit `get`, partial `set_default`, valid scenario persistence, and dotted-provider agent calls without `model`. They also check that raw, OpenAI-cleaned, and Anthropic-cleaned schemas preserve the guarded requirements without root composition keywords, and that the complete schema reaches the text-tool prompt.
- **Recovery coverage:** The real routing tool's schema enters `interpret_chat_response` through native and extra-encoded text-fallback calls. Both retain `upsert_scenario` and save the expected route to a temporary configuration file. A separate control proves that conditional object/array schemas decode only their outer type and leave child strings untouched. Existing controls cover free text, references, composition, ambiguous types, tuple arrays, invalid input, type mismatches and depth limits.
- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The workspace Test job covers the tool and runtime library tests; Lint and Format cover the changed Rust code. [Required CI passes](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38505495932) at recovery commit `b92d5f20957b15c85264aa7fde3c41e1f016a79f`, including Test, Lint, Format and CI Required Gate. Head `d42af917707b76cd8dd1610529b1e83529f5193b` restores the original exception documentation after relocating the proposal to #11697; its complete tree matches the tested recovery commit. Fresh CI is pending.
- **Known coverage gap:** A live local-model conversation and vendor endpoint acceptance have not been tested. The tests establish contract visibility and validation behavior, not universal backend acceptance or a measured reduction in model retries.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The generated English catalogue matches the canonical catalogue plus the renderer's provenance header. No provider server or agent configuration was changed for testing.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. No layout, styling, or rendering behavior changes; the changed error is a tool result returned to the model.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Tool tests ran at `48253684a5cb589a3ff158a9c4747011f06ec6f9`. The runtime argument-preservation suite ran on the patch committed as `b92d5f20957b15c85264aa7fde3c41e1f016a79f`, with source identity checked afterward. Evidence is in the owning module tests and the output above. The macOS linker warned that the test harness's unwind section exceeds the compact-unwind table limit; compilation and all selected tests completed successfully.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** An incomplete `upsert_scenario` call returns one error naming all invalid required strings and leaves saved configuration unchanged. JSON-stringified valid calls preserve their selected action and save the route rather than silently reading configuration.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full local workspace tests and Clippy were not repeated; the focused suite covers this bounded repair, with broader coverage left to hosted CI.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes. The tool's schema descriptions and validation feedback change. The new error contains fixed field names, never argument values, and existing write admission remains in place.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. Existing valid calls retain their behavior. Invalid scenario calls receive complete feedback instead of the first-field error.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No. Tool argument metadata, invalid-call feedback and conditional-schema argument recovery change; there are no new operator settings.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps: None. Omitted-action reads, partial default updates, and dotted-provider agent updates keep their existing contracts.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this PR's commits and rebuild or reinstall the previous binary. No configuration migration is needed.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Valid routing calls unexpectedly fail or become reads without saving a route, omitted-action reads require scenario fields, or invalid calls return a missing-localization-key error instead of the complete correction.

## Supersede Attribution

N/A. This PR does not supersede another contribution.

prs.title: fix(runtime): keep personality files stable per session so edits don't bust the prompt cache
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `Agent` renders the `## Project Context` block (the personality files: `AGENTS.md`, `SOUL.md`, `TOOLS.md`, `IDENTITY.md`, `USER.md`, `HEARTBEAT.md`, `BOOTSTRAP.md`, `MEMORY.md` when injected) once, on its first system-prompt build, and reuses that text every turn. Before this, `IdentitySection` re-read the files on every turn's rebuild. The system prompt heads the provider's cached prefix, so any edit to one of those files made the next request of every live session of that agent miss the prompt cache for the whole conversation (#11696).
  - New `PromptContext::identity_snapshot` carries the pre-rendered text. `prompt::render_identity_section` is the shared renderer, and `None` keeps today's read-now behavior for other builders.
  - New `Agent::reload_personality` re-reads the files on purpose and rebuilds the system prompt. It's exposed as `session/reload_context` (RPC, `sessions:update` grant, owner-only, refused with `SESSION_BUSY` while a turn holds the agent) and as the ZeroCode `/reload-context` command. ZeroCode says whether anything changed and that the next request will be uncached.
- **Scope boundary:** this doesn't touch the CLI `loop_::run` path or the channel orchestrator (the channel path already builds once). It also doesn't touch the `tool_search` deferred-tools section, which still changes the prompt when a tool is activated (noted in #11696). No config switch.
- **Blast radius:** long-lived `Agent` sessions (ZeroCode/ACP, gateway WS). **Behavior change:** an agent that edits its own rules mid-session no longer sees the new text in its system prompt on the next turn. It already has the edit in its conversation context, and other live sessions get it on `/reload-context` or in a new session.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11696. Related #8321.
- **Holding-crate exception:** the `zeroclaw-runtime` changes are covered by the pending personality-snapshot row in #11697 (ADR-016), which has to merge first.

### What this does, simply

Each agent has a few notes files that are pasted into the start of every conversation. ZeroClaw re-read those files before every turn. If anything in them changed, even one line, the provider couldn't reuse its cached copy of the conversation, and the next request was billed at full price. That happened for every open session of that agent, not just the one that edited the file. With long sessions this cost about $1–2 per session per edit.

Now a session reads the notes once and keeps that copy. New sessions see edits right away. An open session picks them up when you type `/reload-context`, and that costs exactly one full-price request, which you choose to pay.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface` = `tui` (ZeroCode Code pane over RPC)
- **Setup / preconditions:** a provider that reports cached input tokens. Two ZeroCode sessions of the same agent, each a few turns in.
- **Steps to run:** append a line to the agent's workspace `AGENTS.md`. Send one message in each session. Check `cached_input_tokens` in the cost ledger. Then run `/reload-context` in one session and send one more message.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the first request after the edit stays cached in both sessions. `/reload-context` shows "Context reloaded…", and only that session's next request is uncached. A second `/reload-context` says "Context unchanged".
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the first request after the edit is uncached (`cached_input_tokens` null/0) in both sessions.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the Rust test/clippy jobs for `zeroclaw-runtime` and `zerocode`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none known.
- **Commands run and tail output** (through the remote cargo wrapper, at the head `f0fd4f895a78`):
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- personality_edit_mid_session session_reload_context new_session_methods_are_classified remote_dispatch_rejects_every_foreign build_system_prompt_omits_memory_md method_all_no_duplicates method_from_wire_roundtrip agent::prompt::` → `test result: ok. 35 passed; 0 failed`
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- agent:: rpc::dispatch tools::delegate` → `2149 passed; 1 failed`. The failure is `new_session_methods_are_denied_without_their_grants`, which fails the same way on the base `f12da7462a0f` in a clean detached worktree (`0 passed; 1 failed`). It isn't caused by this change.
  - `cargo test -p zerocode -- input_bar chat::tests::old_daemon reload` → `160 passed; 0 failed`
  - `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` → clean. `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` → clean. `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on the changed files → clean.
- **Regression guard:** `personality_edit_mid_session_keeps_system_prompt_byte_stable` runs two streamed turns with an `AGENTS.md` edit between them and asserts the provider-visible system prompts are byte-identical. It then checks that `reload_personality` reports the change and that turn 3 carries the new text. With the snapshot disabled (render every turn) it fails: `assertion left == right failed: a mid-session AGENTS.md edit must not change the cached system prompt`.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** I'm verifying this in the experiment build. I didn't run a live provider cache check on master.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. The only UI change is one localized info line from a new slash command, and I'm verifying it in the experiment build.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `f0fd4f895a78`, unit and RPC handler tests.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A (see above).
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** see the regression guard.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** no full `cargo test --workspace`. The changed surface is covered by the runtime and zerocode runs above.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. The new RPC re-reads the same workspace files the prompt already read, for the session's own agent, and needs `sessions:update` plus session ownership like `session/rename`.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Embed a `zeroclaw-docs` skill that directs agents to the installed binary, configuration schema, active tools, and matching documentation instead of relying on model memory.
  - Add built-in skills at the lowest precedence without copying files into agent workspaces. Same-name workspace, community, and assigned-bundle skills still win. Plugin skills use qualified names.
  - Load the built-in instructions on demand in both Full and Compact prompt modes when `read_skill` is callable. Inline them when the provider or tool policy makes that loader unavailable, and refresh cached channel prompts when availability changes.
  - Expose the additive `built-in` origin through the effective-skills API, RPC, and dashboard client type. Existing operator skills retain their configured prompt behavior.
- **Scope boundary:** No new configuration keys, documentation mirror, fetch/cache helper, permission bypass, or live capability-readiness registry. The embedded instructions do not themselves make network calls or establish which capabilities are currently ready.
- **Blast radius:** Agents gain one lowest-precedence skill. The existing `read_skill` tool can also register in Full mode while an effective built-in requires on-demand loading. Runtime and channel prompts, skill reads, and effective-skill origin consumers are affected.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #1948. Related #8367. The live capability-readiness scope of #8367 remains independent.

### What this does, simply

An agent helping you configure or diagnose ZeroClaw needs to know what your installed version actually supports. Its remembered documentation can describe another version, and a feature being documented does not mean the current agent has permission to use it.

This PR gives every agent a small built-in guide for finding the right sources before answering or acting. The guide comes with the binary, so you do not need to install or maintain a workspace copy. Your own skill with the same name takes precedence.

Normally the agent sees a short description and reads the full guide only when needed. If its provider or tool policy prevents that read, ZeroClaw includes the guide directly in the prompt instead. Switching providers cannot leave a cached prompt telling the agent to call a loader it no longer has. The guide remains instructions, not a new permission or an automatic check of live readiness.

### Scope and maintenance tradeoff

This is one embedded guide plus support in the existing skill resolver, prompt renderer, tool factory, and origin converters. The thirteen-file scope connects those existing consumers and tests; it does not introduce a second registry or a documentation service. Adding only the file would leave agents unable to discover or read it, and registering only the loader would leave unusable guidance when tools become unavailable. Future binary releases maintain the guide alongside the code. Live capability readiness remains separate.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. Focused tests exercise the built-in reads, override precedence, API conversion, and real channel provider-transition path directly.

The effective-skills converter test covers the API origin contract. This repair did not rerun an interactive dashboard smoke or local web build.

prs.title: feat(zerocode): show message times in the transcript
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The ZeroCode transcript never showed when anything happened. When an automated prompt, a refused queued message and a long tool call overlap in one session, there was no way to tell the order or the durations from the screen. A time on every message proved to be too much (an earlier revision of this PR did that). The transcript now shows time context in two places only:
    - a dim, centered divider (`── Today 01:00 ──`, `── Yesterday 22:20 ──`, or a date) before a prompt that starts the transcript, comes 15 minutes or more after the previous activity, or starts a new day. A quick back-and-forth gets no dividers.
    - a dim footer (`─── 01:00 → 01:31 · 31m 40s`) under a turn that ran for a minute or more. Short turns get none.
  - `session/messages` entries gain an optional `created_at` (RFC 3339) wherever the store has one: ACP full loads, ACP cursor pages, and the Chat backend via `load_with_timestamps`. It is skipped when absent and `#[serde(default)]` on the client, so either side can be older.
  - **Store fix underneath.** Checkpointed ACP turns write all their visible rows at finalization with one timestamp, so a turn's prompt read as the time the turn **ended**. A divider or footer built on that would be wrong by the whole length of the turn. The checkpoint row now records `started_at` (a nullable column, added on upgrade), and finalization and crash recovery stamp the turn's prompt row with it. The other rows of the turn keep the finalization time, which is the turn's end: exactly what the footer needs.
  - Live turns: entries are stamped on receipt, and the footer is placed when the turn settles. A later terminal frame for the same turn does not move it. A history load taken mid-turn hands the footer to the live settle.
  - A reloaded turn that ends in a recovery marker gets no footer, because recovery stamps its rows when it runs, which can be hours after the turn stopped.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - Individual tool calls and replies in ACP history still share the turn's finish time. Giving each its own time would need a time on every checkpoint journal event; it isn't needed for dividers and footers.
  - No toggle. The only existing display toggle is thoughts; a timestamp toggle would need a new action, keybinding and help text.
  - The Chat-backend path (gateway SQLite) is affected by #11420, which rewrites every row's `created_at` on each turn. This PR passes through what that store holds.
- **Blast radius:** the ACP store's write path for checkpointed turns (only the prompt row's `created_at`) and one additive column on `acp_turn_checkpoints`; the `session/messages` wire shape (additive, optional); ZeroCode transcript layout (divider and footer rows drawn outside each entry's line range, with the tail re-render accounting for them).
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11620. Related #11420.
- **Holding-crate exception:** the `zeroclaw-runtime` part (`created_at` on `session/messages`, confined to `handle_session_messages` and the entry builder) is covered by the row added in #11697 (merged).

### What this does, simply

ZeroCode now shows a small grey date-and-time line when you come back to a conversation after a break or on a new day, and a small grey line under any turn that took more than a minute, saying when it started, when it finished and how long it took. Quick exchanges look exactly as before. Under the hood, the daemon's database used to record every message of a turn as happening when the turn finished; this PR records when the prompt was sent, so those lines are right after a reload too.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `tui` (ZeroCode over the daemon socket)
- **Setup / preconditions:** a daemon and ZeroCode built from this branch; any agent.
- **Steps to run:** send a prompt that runs a tool and takes over a minute. Then send a quick follow-up. Wait 15 minutes (or reload a session from yesterday) and send another. Switch away from the session and back to force a `session/messages` reload.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** a `── Today HH:MM ──` divider above the first prompt; a `─── start → end · duration` footer under the long turn; nothing around the quick follow-up; a new divider after the gap. The same marks after the reload. A session from an older daemon shows no marks rather than wrong ones.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** no times anywhere.

### How I tested

All builds and tests ran through `scripts/zc-cargo` on the remote build host.

- `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on the touched files: clean.
- `zc-cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-infra -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
Results below are for head `c57119d62da9` (rebased on `master` 2026-10-17) unless marked.

- `zc-cargo test -p zerocode`: `test result: FAILED. 1537 passed; 1 failed; 2 ignored`. The one failure, `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint`, fails the same way on unmodified `master` on the same host.
- `zc-cargo test -p zeroclaw-infra acp_session_store`: `test result: ok. 88 passed; 0 failed`.
- `zc-cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib rpc::`: `test result: ok. 850 passed; 0 failed`.
- `zc-cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib`: `5627 passed; 4 failed` at the earlier head. The 4 (`relay::local_dial_tests` x2, `new_session_methods_are_denied_without_their_grants`, `peer_turn_cost_scope_through_execute_boundary_attributes_recipient_and_shares_budget`) fail the same way on unmodified `master` on the same host. The runtime diff is unchanged since.

Each new test fails with its fix reverted and passes with it restored:

- Store: `finalized_turn_prompt_keeps_turn_start_time_and_reply_keeps_finalization_time`, `recovered_turn_prompt_keeps_turn_start_time` (fail when the prompt keeps the finalization time); `turn_checkpoint_start_column_is_added_to_an_existing_database` (fails without the migration).
- RPC: `conversation_message_entries_carry_each_source_message_time` (fails when the projection drops times).
- Rules (`chat::entry_time`): `dividers_mark_the_first_prompt_gaps_and_day_changes_only` (fails when every prompt divides), `a_day_change_divides_even_after_a_short_gap` (fails without the day check), `footers_follow_finished_turns_of_a_minute_or_more` (fails without the one-minute floor), plus label and parsing tests.
- Transcript: `transcript_shows_gap_dividers_and_long_turn_footers_not_message_times` and `a_live_turn_gets_its_footer_when_it_settles` (fail when the layout drops the footer row, when a settle doesn't invalidate the tail, or when a later frame may move the end); `a_history_load_taken_mid_turn_hands_the_footer_to_the_live_settle` (fails when a moved footer doesn't force a full rebuild); `a_footer_on_a_divided_entry_keeps_one_divider` (fails when the tail re-render ignores the divider row); `a_recovered_turn_gets_no_footer_from_its_recovery_time`.

`rpc::dispatch::tests::cursor_pages_equal_legacy_projection_for_valid_tool_groups` was updated: cursor pages now carry times, so its full-load reference uses the timed projection.

- **CI checks relied on:** the Rust lanes for the three crates.
- **Known CI coverage gap:** no end-to-end daemon+TUI run in CI for this.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The divider and footer rows were checked in a live ZeroCode pane against a scratch daemon (seeded history plus a live turn), by reading the terminal's text.
- **Visual interface evidence:** I'm verifying this in the experiment build.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** none.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. Times are display-only and never reach the model.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. The new wire field is optional both ways. The new column is nullable and added on open; an older binary ignores it (its inserts name their columns). A checkpoint begun by an older binary has no start time, and its prompt keeps the finalization time as before.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert` the PR's commits. The added `acp_turn_checkpoints.started_at` column is harmless to the reverted code and needs no down-migration.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** no dividers or footers (old daemon or missing `created_at`), or a footer whose start is later than expected (start time not recorded).

prs.title: feat(zerocode): steer the running turn when you send a message mid-turn
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - #11132 added `session/steer` to the daemon, but zerocode never calls it. A message typed while a turn is running still waits in the client queue until the turn ends. Submit now offers that message to the running turn first.
  - Only plain text with nothing already queued is steered. `session/steer` carries no attachments, and steering past queued messages would reorder what the user sent. It is also skipped while the turn is cancelling or waiting on an approval.
  - When the daemon accepts it, the message is added to the transcript after any text already streamed, and no new client turn starts. The running turn's own `TurnComplete` still settles it.
  - When the daemon doesn't accept it, the message goes into the queue exactly as before. That covers the turn having just ended, a full steering queue, or a daemon without the method. Nothing typed is lost.
- **Scope boundary:** No daemon change. No steering for attachments, queued messages, or the existing Inject action (which cancels the turn). No new key binding or setting. On older daemons the behavior is unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** zerocode's Submit path while a turn is in flight (`chat.rs`) and one new client method (`client.rs`). Idle Submit is untouched.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11132, Related #9487

### What this does, simply

When the agent is in the middle of a long turn and you think of something it should know, you can now just type it and press Enter. The agent picks it up at its next step, within the same turn. Before, the message waited until the whole turn finished and then started a new one.

If the agent can't take it right then (for example, the turn finished a moment earlier), the message is queued the same way it always was.

The agent reads steered messages between steps. It won't interrupt a single long tool call, such as a build, until that call returns.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface`: `tui`
- **Setup / preconditions:** A daemon from current `master` (it has `session/steer`), and zerocode from this branch.
- **Steps to run:** Start a prompt that runs several tool calls (for example "list the files in this repo one directory at a time"). While it is working, type "also count them" and press Enter.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Your message appears in the transcript right away, under the text streamed so far. The queue stays empty. The same turn continues and addresses it, and there is one `TurnComplete`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The message sits in the queue panel until the turn ends, then runs as a separate turn.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `CI Required Gate` (fmt, clippy, workspace tests) covers `apps/zerocode`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No end-to-end test against a live daemon.
- **Commands run and tail output:** All via the remote cargo wrapper.
  - `cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode -- steer` → `test result: ok. 4 passed; 0 failed`. The four tests: the wire shape of `session/steer` (`content` in, `accepted` out); when steering is offered (running turn, plain text, empty queue, not cancelling); that a steered message starts no client turn and lands after streamed text; and the real key path, where Enter during a running turn sends `session/steer`, and an error reply falls back to the queue without showing the message as sent.
  - Mutation check: with steering disabled in the Submit handler, the key-path test fails (`FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed`).
  - `cargo test -p zerocode` → `1424 passed; 1 failed`. The one failure, `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint`, fails the same way on unmodified `master` `05f9fe95d4`.
  - `cargo clippy -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` → exit 0.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Ran it live on the experiment build [`20261015T062922Z-af67956b5e9d`](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/experiment/zerocode-builds/20261015T062922Z-af67956b5e9d), which carries this change and #11725 (dogfood base [`20261008T194402Z-0341618f9d69`](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/dogfood/zerocode-builds/20261008T194402Z-0341618f9d69)). I started a multi-step turn ("list the files in this repo one directory at a time"), then sent "also count them" while tools were running. The message appeared in the transcript right away, no new turn started, and the agent acted on it at its next tool step within the same turn.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Screenshot of the live run: https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11621#issuecomment-6232681990
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** unit tests, clippy, rustfmt and the comment hygiene gate on head `aa751b0df2e1` (rebased onto master `4e82ce46e9`); live TUI run on the experiment build above.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** See the screenshot comment linked above.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** See the tests above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** None.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. The user's own text reaches the model through the daemon's existing `session/steer` admission.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. Against a daemon without `session/steer`, the call errors and the message is queued as before.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

prs.title: feat(runtime): let the operator override an exceeded cost limit
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - `cost.allow_override` was documented but read by nothing, so an exceeded shared limit always failed the turn and the only way on was a daemon restart. With it on, the main tool loop now pauses before a provider call that would exceed the shared daily or monthly limit and asks through the turn's approval channel (`tool_name = cost_limit_override`, exported as `COST_LIMIT_OVERRIDE_APPROVAL`). Deny, no answer within 10 minutes, or a channel that cannot ask stops the turn exactly as before.
  - Approval calls `CostTracker::grant_override`, which records the override for the current UTC day or month on state shared by every derived tracker, so one answer covers every session and delegation of the daemon. `check_budget` skips that limit (and its warning) while the stored period matches, so it expires on its own at rollover. Per-hop and per-agent ceilings still bind, and `grant_override` refuses when `allow_override` is off.
  - The grant is written to `state/cost-overrides.json` beside the ledger (temp file plus rename, best effort) and loaded when the tracker starts, so a daemon restart keeps it until rollover. An unreadable file means no override, and a stored grant is ignored while `allow_override` is off.
  - A turn waiting on its own prompt also watches for a grant from another session (a `watch` channel on the tracker). When one arrives it drops its request and continues. `RpcApprovalChannel` sends a new `session/update` type, `approval_withdrawn` (`request_id`), for any approval that ends without an answer from its client, and ZeroCode takes that prompt down. Before this, approving in one session left the same prompt up in the other, and that turn stopped at the 10-minute timeout although the limit was already lifted.
  - `RpcApprovalChannel` and `AskUserApprovalBridge` now implement `request_approval_attributed_with_timeout`. The trait default wrapped `request_approval_attributed`, whose own 120 s deadline fired first, so the 10-minute wait would have been cut short.
  - ZeroCode renders a `cost_limit_override` approval as a centred, bold red notice with Override and Stop buttons instead of the tool card. Only Override or Stop (key or click) closes it.
- **Scope boundary:** no warning at `warn_at_percent` (#10950) and no notice for a turn that stops with no override possible; both need a daemon-to-client budget event this PR does not add. `cost.enforcement.mode` stays unread. Applying `config/set` limit changes to the live tracker is #11587.
- **Blast radius:** turns that hit a shared limit with `allow_override = true` now wait for an answer instead of failing, on any channel that answers approvals (ZeroCode, ACP, Telegram inline buttons). The approval bridge's timeout plumbing is used only by callers that pass a budget; tool approvals are unchanged.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11585
- **Labels:** (set after open)

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw can stop the agent when spending passes a daily or monthly limit. There was a setting meant to let you go past the limit, but nothing used it: once the limit tripped, every message failed, and the only way to continue was to raise the limit and restart, which closes every open session.

Now, with that setting on, the agent pauses when it reaches the limit and ZeroCode shows a red box asking whether to keep going. Say yes and the same task carries on, and the limit stays lifted until the day (or month) ends, even if the app or daemon restarts. If several sessions were waiting at the limit, one yes lets all of them continue. Say no, or leave it for ten minutes, and the task stops as it does today. Chat apps that cannot show the question, and scheduled jobs, still stop at the limit.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface` `tui` (ZeroCode Code tab over RPC)
- **Setup / preconditions:** `[cost] enabled = true`, `allow_override = true`, `daily_limit_usd` just above today's recorded spend.
- **Steps to run:** in ZeroCode, run a prompt that makes a few model calls until spend passes the limit. When the red notice appears, click Override. Then open a second session and send a prompt. Separately: get two sessions waiting on the notice at once and Override in one; and restart the daemon after an Override and send a prompt.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the first turn pauses on the red notice and continues after Override; the second session is not asked again; with two waiting, the other notice closes and its turn continues; after a restart nobody is asked again that day. With Stop instead, the turn ends with the budget error.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the turn fails with `Budget exceeded: ... Cannot make further API calls until the budget resets.`, there is no prompt, and every later turn fails until a restart.

### How I tested

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check   # rustfmt --edition 2024 on the changed files
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib cost::tracker
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib budget_override
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib approval_
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- budget_override_tests rpc::approval_channel
cargo test -p zerocode --bins -- approval parse_approval cost_limit
cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode cost_limit
cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode approval
scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Rust test and clippy jobs for the four crates; Docs Style for `docs/book/src/ops/cost-tracking.md`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** no end-to-end test drives a real provider turn into the gate; the gate tests call it under a scoped tracker with a scripted channel.
- **Commands run and tail output:** on `225c52bb636f` (rebased on master `f12da7462a0f`): clippy `-D warnings` clean on the four crates; `cost::tracker` 50 passed; runtime `budget_override_tests rpc::approval_channel` 17 passed; zerocode `approval parse_approval cost_limit` 13 passed; comment hygiene gate passed. With each fix disabled, `override_survives_a_restart_and_stops_counting_when_disallowed` and `approval_in_another_session_releases_a_waiting_prompt` fail. Earlier run at `58a7050d`: clippy `Finished`, no warnings. `cost::tracker` 47 passed, `budget_override` 3 passed, `approval_` 106 passed, zerocode `cost_limit` 2 passed, zerocode `approval` 9 passed, docs gate 0 errors.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Coverage: tracker override (day lifts, rollover expiry, derived trackers share it, per-hop and per-agent ceilings still bind, day does not lift month, refused when not allowed); gate (approve continues and does not ask twice, deny and runtime timeout stop, no prompt without `allow_override` or a channel); RPC channel honours a 600 s budget through `dyn Channel`; ZeroCode notice render and button clicks; restart persistence, unreadable file, cross-session release, `approval_withdrawn` sent only for unanswered prompts and cleared only for the matching id. I ran the override live in the experiment build; the two follow-up bugs above came from that run.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact final-interface output pending; the render test asserts the title, summary, both buttons and the red button fill through `render_with_plan_placement` at 100x30.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `225c52bb636f` on master `f12da7462a0f`; tests on a remote macOS arm64 builder. Live: experiment build https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/experiment/zerocode-builds/20261013T015950Z-b89c9e407c42 (commit https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/commit/b89c9e407c4279bbfb05f9d0e0cdec7e34b6e561).
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** to be added from the dogfood smoke before Ready.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** full crate suites not run locally; CI runs them.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No (one new file, `state/cost-overrides.json`, in the existing cost state directory)
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A. The override is off by default and only an operator answer grants it; a runtime timeout or unreachable client does not.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. With `allow_override = false` (the default) behaviour is unchanged.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No new keys; one new RPC `session/update` type, `approval_withdrawn`, which older clients ignore; `allow_override` now does what its docs say, and the docs are corrected.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert 225c52bb636f 0c7a8844d260 312ffc65d3ae` (newest first).
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `cost.allow_override = false` restores the hard stop without a revert.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** turns stuck waiting at the limit; grep the runtime trace for `cost limit overridden by the operator` and `cost limit override prompt failed`.

prs.title: feat(zerocode): make Config save and cancel predictable
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Honor the resolved Save action in scalar and choice editors as well as multiline editors. Preserve Enter-to-save for scalar/choice and Enter-to-newline for multiline input.
  - Show resolved Save/Cancel controls and pending-edit state. Ask Stay/Discard before navigation replaces a changed draft; allow navigation that parks it.
  - Preserve personality content after Save and retain failed-write drafts for retry. Explain automatic import/save before launching the external personality or Skills editor, including when applying a personality template.
  - Route connection paste and remapped editor actions to the visible local editor. Persist connection candidates before replacing the in-memory saved value.
- **Scope boundary:** No persisted schema, RPC method, default shortcut, modifier migration, global navigation redesign, secret-handling change or Delete/Reset confirmation change.
- **Blast radius:** ZeroCode Config key, paste and mouse dispatch; personality/Skills editing; local connection draft writes. Existing persistence owners remain unchanged.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11486. Builds on #11460 (merged).
- **Labels:** `enhancement`, `risk:medium`, `size:XL`, `zerocode`, `docs`.

### What this does, simply

ZeroCode Config lets you change daemon settings, personality files, Skills and the client's connection settings. Before this change, each editor had different save and cancel conventions. Moving away could lose typed work, and saving a personality file could clear the content of the still-open editor.

This PR makes the existing Save and Cancel actions visible and consistent. Enter still saves a single value, but still adds a newline when you are editing several lines. A changed draft shows that edits are pending. If navigation would throw it away, Config asks whether to stay or discard it. Switching to a pane that keeps the draft does not ask.

Saving a personality file leaves its content open. A failed save keeps your work so you can retry. External editors still import and save changed content after a successful exit, but Config explains that behavior before launch and lets you cancel there. When applying a personality template, it compares the edited result with the current file, or an empty baseline if the file does not exist. Config continues using the same files and daemon persistence calls.

### Scope and maintenance tradeoff

Four files, 1191 additions and 246 deletions against current `master`. The change stays inside the existing Config editor, ZeroCode connection pane, locale file and Config docs.

The interaction policy must cover keyboard, paste and mouse entry into the existing scalar, choice, multiline and composite editors. A footer-only change would still allow silent draft loss and the personality repeat-Save defect. The change keeps one Config owner, adds an original field snapshot where none existed, and derives pending state from existing draft baselines. It does not introduce a second configuration model or replace the editor. Much of the added code exercises real handler dispatch and existing persistence boundaries; future Config navigation should preserve this same departure policy.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, for the visible controls and modal layout.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=tui`, ZeroCode Config.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Use an existing non-sensitive agent and a matching-version daemon. Build ZeroCode from this head with `cargo build --locked -p zerocode --bin zerocode`, then launch `target/debug/zerocode --config-dir <your-existing-config-directory>` using your existing connection setup. An explicitly configured Cargo target changes the binary's location.
- **Steps to run:** Open Config, edit an ordinary scalar or choice and change its value without saving. Click an earlier breadcrumb or another daemon section. Cancel the dialog to keep editing, then use Save. Open an existing personality file, edit it inline, save twice, and confirm its text remains present. Return to the file list and invoke its existing external-editor action, then cancel the prelaunch dialog. Repeat that prelaunch check for an existing Skill if available.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The footer names the resolved Save/Cancel keys and pending state. Destructive navigation offers Stay/Discard without saving. Save retains personality content and failed writes remain editable. The external-editor dialog explains import/save after successful exit.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Scalar/choice editors use only Enter to save; draft loss on navigation is not deliberate; personality list refresh can clear the retained editor; no external-editor prelaunch explanation appears. Breadcrumb navigation itself came from #11460 and is already on `master`.

### How I tested

```text
# on 60f89750470d (master 4e82ce46e9c6 merged in)
cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode
test result: 1536 passed; 1 failed; 2 ignored
  failing: connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint
  (fails identically on plain master 4e82ce46e9c6; unrelated to this change)

cargo clippy -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings
passed

rustfmt --edition 2024 --check (changed files)
passed

bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
Comment hygiene gate passed.

git diff --check origin/master HEAD
passed
```

The suite exercises production Config handlers with scripted RPC responses. New cases check scalar/choice/array Save payloads under a remapped key, no writes on Cancel/Discard, filtered-choice cancellation, personality content after repeated Save, failed external personality import followed by inline retry, and keyboard/mouse departures. App-level connection cases verify paste reaches the visible editor, Save/Cancel remapped to Tab outrank section navigation, and a parked daemon draft stays untouched. Local connection tests use temporary real config files to check failure retention, successful retry and cancellation without a write. Existing Skills and breadcrumb-navigation tests also pass; Skills retention and payload compatibility were additionally source-reviewed rather than claimed as a new dedicated failure matrix.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Quality Gate passed on `efc9cfdb566c`; the run for `60f89750470d` (Greptile fixes) is in progress. Workspace Test and Lint provide broader compilation, test and lint coverage; Format and Zerocode RPC Boundary cover formatting and Config RPC isolation. Applicable cross-platform and MSRV checks also passed.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** CI and scripted handlers do not supply a human-operated TUI layout check.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Source and dispatch review plus the automated tests above. I also ran the Config flows by hand on experiment build [20261015T062922Z-af67956b5e9d](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/experiment/zerocode-builds/20261015T062922Z-af67956b5e9d): a changed scalar draft followed by navigation, and the external-editor prelaunch dialog.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Two frames in [this comment](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11511#issuecomment-6232646371): the Stay/Discard dialog over a changed scalar draft, and the external-editor prelaunch explanation.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Automated evidence is for `60f89750470df86bc251e179530f7d2b13c0b7a5`; ZeroCode Config, English. The frames were captured on experiment build [20261015T062922Z-af67956b5e9d](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/experiment/zerocode-builds/20261015T062922Z-af67956b5e9d) (dogfood base `0341618f9d69`), which carries this PR's Config draft changes. It is not this exact head.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Scripted Save sends the expected persistence payload, Cancel/Discard send no write, personality Save preserves content across refresh, and failed connection Save keeps its draft until retry succeeds.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full local workspace tests and broad Clippy are delegated to current-head CI; the focused binary suite directly checks the edited dispatch paths without repeating that broader coverage.

### Visual evidence

Frames: see [this comment](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11511#issuecomment-6232646371).

Use this revision in a real 120-column by 40-row English terminal. The first frame should retain the editor's Save/Cancel/pending footer around the discard dialog. The second should show the explanation that a successful external-editor exit imports and saves changed content, with its launch and cancel actions. Expected visible result: readable explanation and controls without overlap or clipping. Observed result: readable dialog and controls, with no overlap or clipping. These frames check presentation; the handler and file tests establish save/cancel transitions.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.
- Risk and mitigation: The local connection candidate uses the existing config writer. External editors and daemon writes retain their existing access and persistence boundaries.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. Existing defaults are retained and scalar/choice Enter remains a Save alias.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No schema, environment or CLI option changes. Config TUI interaction changes as described above.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps: None. Existing keybindings continue to resolve through the current action registry.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the squash commit. It contains only this change; the navigation work from #11460 is already on `master` separately.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None; no new persisted controls.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Save does not persist the selected value, Cancel unexpectedly writes, navigation discards a changed draft without asking, or a saved personality editor becomes empty. Check the Config footer's localized save failure and pending status, then reopen the value to verify persistence.

## Supersede Attribution

N/A. No PR is superseded.

prs.title: feat(zerocode): confirm config deletion and reset
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Require target confirmation before deleting a Config alias or Costs resource, or resetting a configured field.
  - Keep deletion refusals, cleanup warnings and refresh failures in a scrollable result panel until dismissed. A completed or uncertain mutation cannot be retried by dismissing its result.
  - Name the actions Delete and Reset in Help and rebinding while preserving existing stored binding identifiers.
  - Show the resolved Delete shortcut in the footer for an existing alias or Costs entry, so deletion is discoverable without opening Help.
- **Scope boundary:** ZeroCode only. No new cascade rules, daemon mutation semantics, undo storage or secret-value display.
- **Blast radius:** Config input routing, client response handling and Config action labels. Skills archival and local keybinding override clearing retain their behavior.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11487. Related #11172 for the optional daemon deletion preview.

### What this does, simply

ZeroCode's Config editor can remove aliases and restore fields to their default behavior. Previously, pressing the deletion or reset key sent the change immediately. The daemon could reject an unsafe deletion, but it could not tell whether a valid deletion was accidental.

This PR shows the selected target first. You can confirm or cancel; moving the underlying selection cannot change the captured target. After confirmation, the result stays readable, including warnings when cleanup was incomplete or the list could not be refreshed.

When the daemon supports `config/delete-plan`, the confirmation shows its blockers and references that would be removed. Older daemons show an explicit unavailable-preview notice. The daemon still makes the final authorization and deletion decision.

### Scope and maintenance tradeoff

Delete and Reset share one Config dialog: either a confirmation with a captured target, or a result that cannot send a mutation. The outer input loop gives it priority over pane navigation and paste. Typed client responses preserve the daemon's applied flag and optional warnings; no second cascade planner is introduced. The larger diff includes request-recording regressions for destructive input and failure paths, plus existing action consumers that follow the renamed Rust variants.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, for the running TUI's presentation.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=tui`, ZeroCode Config.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Use a disposable Config alias or Costs entry, or a non-secret field whose reset is safe. Use a ZeroCode binary built from this PR with an existing daemon connection.
- **Steps to run:** Open Config and focus an existing alias or Costs entry. Check that the footer shows the resolved Delete binding (`x` by default), then press it. Check the displayed target and cancel with Esc. Reopen confirmation and confirm only a disposable target. For a field, use the resolved Reset binding (`d` by default). The Delete hint should disappear on the Add row or when Delete is unbound.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Opening and cancellation do not change configuration. Confirmation applies one change to the displayed target. The result remains visible until dismissed; long text can be scrolled.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The same Delete or Reset key sends the mutation immediately, without a target-confirmation step.

### How I tested

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check
passed

cargo test --offline --locked -p zerocode --bin zerocode config -- --test-threads=8
159 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 1311 filtered out

bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
passed
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Required CI passed after integrating master; it is running again on `f1801c1bbb0db7627f596f2f23205055bcf0e29f`, which fixes the two review findings (result kept across reconnect, scroll clamped). Workspace Test includes ZeroCode, while Lint checks the changed Rust code. The focused Config command above passed on this revision.
- **Known CI coverage gap:** CI does not show the dialog in a running terminal.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Source and response-contract comparison. Recorded outbound requests exercise the real Config handlers and client: open/cancel/mouse/paste/repeat, captured alias and Costs targets, reset tab/cursor preservation, blocked and unavailable previews, preview failure and committed refresh failure. The footer regression covers custom and unbound Delete shortcuts, independent alias/Costs selection, and Add/filter/pane suppression. Master integration preserves SecretMap container refusal and Config RPC-timeout handling; their focused tests passed alongside confirmation. Existing Config editing tests also passed. No live configuration was deleted for this verification.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Screenshots from a running ZeroCode build, linked under Visual evidence below.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Automated confirmation sent one mutation for the captured target; cancellation sent none. Refresh failure retained the committed result and warning without retrying.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Broader local workspace tests and Clippy are delegated to required published-head CI.

### Visual evidence

I checked this in the experiment build https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/experiment/zerocode-builds/20261017T101556Z-237438642a40 (commit https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/commit/237438642a40bb77a39a6b6a1cdef97e362778a1, dogfood base https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/dogfood/zerocode-builds/20261008T194402Z-0341618f9d69), which carries this change.

Screenshots of the Delete shortcut in a provider alias footer and of the deletion dialog: https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11510#issuecomment-6233163044

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No; the optional read-only preview uses the existing daemon RPC connection.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No. Confirmation displays paths and aliases, not field values or the planner's raw reference values.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No; fixtures use neutral names.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for stored configuration and daemon mutation contracts. Delete and Reset now require confirmation.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No. Help and rebinding labels change; stored `config_tab.toggle_secret` and `config_tab.delete_row` identifiers remain valid.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps: No configuration migration. Costs deletion uses Delete (`x` by default); the old redundant Reset (`d`) deletion shortcut is removed. Existing custom Delete bindings still resolve through the preserved identifier. Only `METHOD_NOT_FOUND` permits the unavailable-preview path; other preview failures are shown instead of enabling confirmation.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this PR's commit and use the prior ZeroCode binary. This restores immediate Delete/Reset behavior; it does not undo changes already confirmed.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. Existing keybinding overrides continue to apply.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Confirmation does not open, displays a wrong target, disappears instead of preserving an error, or a confirmed mutation reports a refresh failure. The daemon's authorization and deletion safeguards remain unchanged.

prs.title: fix(agent): bound repeated tool failures and preserve completed work
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Resolve existing root pacing policy for configured Agent turns instead of forcing loop detection off.
  - Give repeated identical successful results one advisory. Contain repeated identical completed failures with a correction, one final retry, and a recoverable stop that retains completed results.
  - Use the executed tool's canonical identity so short/full aliases cannot bypass the retry budget. Keep approvals, exclusions and cancellation outside executed-failure evidence.
- **Scope boundary:** No blanket duplicate suppression, successful-polling hard stop, permanent blacklist, model setting, context/iteration-limit change, new config key or public API shape change. Standalone builders without full/live config and legacy channel detection keep their behavior.
- **Blast radius:** Both configured Agent APIs and their ACP consumers. Shared tool resolution and history closeout require coverage across sequential/parallel batches, aliases, hooks and cancellation.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11484.
- **Runtime placement:** The bounded recovery scope is covered by the approved exception merged in #11436.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw runs the model's requested tools and sends their results back so it can decide what to do next. A model can keep requesting the same action even after it gets the same error. Configured Agent turns previously forced the repetitive-tool safeguards off, so that cycle could continue until the general iteration limit.

After three identical completed failures by default, the next model request now receives a correction. The model can change approach or make one final identical retry. If that retry fails identically and nothing else in the round makes progress, ZeroClaw ends the turn with an explanation and keeps every completed result. Extra identical requests in that recovery batch get paired skipped results instead of more executions. A new user turn can retry normally.

An unchanged successful result is not proof of a stuck turn. Successful polling gets at most one reminder and can continue; changing results and successful recovery can continue too. This is a runtime retry policy, not a claim that a network error is permanent or that every model loop can be recognized.

### Scope and maintenance tradeoff

The larger diff is one connected repair. Actual-dispatch provenance, recovery admission and transcript-preserving closeout must agree. Simply enabling the old arguments/names-only detector would stop productive polling and can discard the final completed round. The focused test module supplies deterministic Agent-boundary coverage; the runtime reuses the existing policy, executor and shared turn engine rather than adding another orchestration layer.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. Whether a particular model repeats a call is nondeterministic; the focused tests deliberately repeat after correction through the production Agent APIs.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The [Quality Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39020947601) passed at `6e7508873e3f0108efdd44173b67a689c643efaa`, including workspace tests, Lint, Format, Landlock, PostgreSQL memory and channel suites. That head merges current master (`bec5a3f04c0b744038ed6114da3ada7df4f6279d`) and updates two recovery/steering tests: mid-turn steering now yields the tool loop after a round (#11725), so each test queues its steering message at the round it exercises. The guarded behavior is unchanged: queued steering cannot restart an exhausted turn, and reentry keeps the advisory and the spent recovery budget.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** A live Woof/MLX-LM turn and complete ZeroCode UI replay were not captured. The deterministic tests reach both Agent APIs, including the streamed entry point used by ACP.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

The result below was obtained at `6e7508873e3f0108efdd44173b67a689c643efaa`. Formatting, Clippy with `-D warnings` and comment hygiene were rerun at the same head. Catalogue checks confirmed unique IDs and retention of all four recovery messages and the incoming HTTP-timeout message.

```text
cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -E 'test(agent::safety_net) | test(agent::tool_execution) | test(steering) | test(tree_budget_final_completion) | test(single_tool)'
Summary: 118 tests run: 118 passed, 5682 skipped

cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings
Finished

cargo fmt --all -- --check
Passed

bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
Comment hygiene gate passed.
```

The macOS debug test harness emits a linker warning because its `__eh_frame` section exceeds the 16 MiB compact-unwind offset limit. Section inspection confirms that cause. Linking and all selected tests completed successfully; this is not production-build performance evidence.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Inspected canonical policy ownership, the two Agent callers, private loop compatibility, actual completion provenance, alias resolution, paired skipped results, hook abandonment and append-before-stop ordering. Successful polling, final-attempt recovery, changed arguments, useful work in the same batch, ignored aliases, live-policy refresh and queued steering are exercised by automated Agent tests.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A for presentation. This PR changes runtime enforcement, not a renderer or layout; responses and `TurnEvent::Chunk` supply the relevant automated boundary evidence.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** This PR's candidate source, streamed and non-streamed Agent APIs; `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/agent/safety_net_loop_recovery.rs` plus existing safety-net and executor tests.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** `repeated_failures_close_both_agent_apis_after_correction_and_preserve_pairs` checks the full correction in the next outgoing system prompt, four actual executions, preserved result IDs and the localized terminal response. Streaming cases also check matching call/result IDs and the terminal chunk.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** A scripted provider disregards the correction and repeats the failure. The turn completes recoverably after its final retry rather than requesting another summary/model round. Sequential/parallel recovery batches execute only one matching retry and pair the extra calls with skipped results.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Local workspace-wide tests and Clippy are delegated to fresh required CI instead of duplicating that breadth. No interactive model/UI smoke was run.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No. The guard limits existing repeated dispatches.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No. Existing executor egress scrubbing is retained.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No. Fixtures use synthetic tool names and arguments.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes. Runtime-owned localized correction and stop messages are model-visible. They interpolate no tool arguments, remote error bodies or credentials; evidence retains hashes only. Existing tool output remains subject to the same security and approval policy.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for public API/config shape, standalone defaults and legacy detector behavior. Configured Agent turns intentionally begin honoring the existing enabled pacing policy.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No new fields or commands. Existing `pacing.loop_detection_enabled`, `loop_detection_max_repeats` and `loop_ignore_tools` govern the Agent guard. The legacy elapsed-output setting does not delay this failure recovery.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps for existing users: No migration. Configured turns use the existing policy; opt out with `pacing.loop_detection_enabled = false` when needed. Canonical ignore entries cover short aliases of the executed tool.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this PR's commits, or disable `pacing.loop_detection_enabled` in the supported config editor and begin a new turn after configuration reload.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** Existing `pacing.loop_detection_enabled`; existing repeat threshold and canonical `loop_ignore_tools` entries remain available.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** A useful retry is stopped unexpectedly, recovery skips lack paired result IDs, or the user sees a recovery-exhaustion message despite changed completed work. The Agent-boundary tests cover these contracts. A finite retry budget can stop before a later transient network recovery; retrying in a new turn is the recovery path.

prs.title: feat(zerocode): expose settings actions and filter keybindings
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:** Client settings now show contextual action hints using the effective keymap. Keybindings can be searched by action name, action identifier, or effective key without executing settings actions while typing.
- **Scope boundary:** Existing settings writes, preset application, and modified global shortcuts keep their existing behavior. Effective-key collision handling and Shift+Tab normalization remain separate work.
- **Blast radius:** The ZeroCode client settings pane, its Config footer and input routing, and its English Fluent catalogue. No daemon, RPC, configuration schema, or dependency changes.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11492.

### What this does, simply

ZeroCode's Config screen lets you change client preferences such as themes, keybindings, and connection settings. Several pages previously left their action hints blank, and some instructions named Enter or Esc even when those keys had been overridden. Finding an action to rebind also required scrolling through the whole list.

The footer now identifies the current client-settings page and active pane and shows the controls that can actually reach it. The Keybindings page adds a search field. Typing edits the query; confirming it lets you browse the matching actions, and a separate activation starts rebinding. Searching, clearing, and cancelling do not save a binding. Rebind and reset still operate on the action displayed in the selected row.

### Scope and maintenance tradeoff

The change reuses the existing action registry, resolved bindings, search controls, Config footer, and locale loader. The full binding list remains authoritative; search derives visible row indices from it. Config and global routing yield ordinary query text so characters cannot accidentally reset a binding or switch sections. Modified global shortcuts retain their established priority, and hints omit local keys those shortcuts intercept.

The source and catalogue changes are accompanied by tests at the pane, Config, and global input boundaries. No new persistence owner, API, registry, or dependency is introduced.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, for actual terminal presentation and focus.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=tui`, ZeroCode Config client settings.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Build this revision and use your existing compatible daemon, client profile, and keybindings. No additional feature settings are needed.
- **Steps to run:** Open Config, switch the outer section to ZeroCode, and select Keybindings. Open detail, start search with the resolved search key, and enter an action name such as `clear input` or a key such as `Ctrl+z`. Confirm the query, select a result, and activate it. Cancel capture, clear the filter, and return to the section list. Inspect the other settings pages and Connection editing. Use the same steps on `master` for comparison.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Contextual controls reflect your effective bindings. The filter narrows the actions; query confirmation does not start capture. Capture/reset target the displayed action. Clearing preserves useful selection. Mouse or keyboard departure stops query editing while retaining its text.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Keybindings has no filter; client-settings footers generally lack contextual controls, and some titles/editor instructions use fixed keys.

### How I tested

The original implementation was validated on `c75f24e832eb1437b6614bbaeddd2d537814d7e1`:

- `cargo test --locked -p zerocode --bin zerocode`: 1,431 passed, 0 failed, 2 existing ignored tests. This includes filtering, correct capture/reset targets, empty results, cancellation, repeated search selection, typing without config writes, mouse list/query geometry, paste isolation, effective hints, locale fallback, and narrow footer rendering.
- `cargo clippy --locked -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- Touched-file rustfmt, `git diff --check`, comment hygiene, and the ZeroCode RPC-only dependency gate passed.
- The [Quality Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/37142730934) passed on `c75f24e832eb1437b6614bbaeddd2d537814d7e1`, including workspace nextest, lint, cross-platform checks, and the ZeroCode RPC boundary. All applicable checks passed; conditional checks were skipped. Production terminal visual evidence remains pending; automated renderer assertions do not establish actual terminal clipping or appearance.

Subsequent updates preserve those behaviors and correct effective hints during Connection text editing. Three existing standalone settings tests passed for that correction. The existing `keymap::guard::tests::no_hardcoded_chords_in_handlers` test passes after documenting the printable-editor-input classification; that annotation changes no runtime behavior.

CI on the current head `ad847fb32fbf6b9104b09079daeb24e0acf4f013`: [Quality Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/37826288701) passed, including the Test job, lint, cross-platform checks and RPC boundary. Workspace nextest passed 19,371 tests with 39 skipped; the keymap guard passed in both ZeroCode test targets. The hardware-feature suite passed 189 tests with 1 skipped. All applicable checks succeeded; conditional checks were skipped.

Rebased onto `master` at `4e82ce46e9c6` (head `0723ca1a67b1`). The rebase needed one adaptation: master added a layout row to the Config view, so the client-settings footer now renders into the last row. `config_manager::tests::client_binding_query_owns_printable_outer_keys_and_paste` caught the misplaced footer before the fix. On the new head, `cargo clippy --locked -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed and `cargo test --locked -p zerocode --bin zerocode` passed 1,535 tests. The one failure, `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint`, also fails on `master` on my test machine and is unrelated. Touched-file rustfmt, `git diff --check` and comment hygiene passed.

### Visual evidence

I dogfooded this in ZeroCode on experiment build [`20261015T062922Z-af67956b5e9d`](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/experiment/zerocode-builds/20261015T062922Z-af67956b5e9d) ([commit](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/commit/af67956b5e9d); dogfood base [`0341618f9d69`](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/commit/0341618f9d69e31bf38300d134ba86e98491d49d)), which already carries this change. Screenshot: https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11505#issuecomment-6232477525

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions / trust boundaries? No.
- Secrets / sensitive data handling changed? No. Connection-setting persistence is unchanged.
- Network / filesystem access changed? No. Filtering is transient; existing explicit settings actions retain their write paths.
- Any real identities, secrets, tokens, credentials, personal emails, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps: None. New client strings use the existing English fallback until translated catalogues include them.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** After merge, run `git revert <merge-commit>` for this PR's merge commit.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Query text invokes a shortcut, capture/reset targets a different action, or a footer advertises a key intercepted by another control. Existing configuration remains readable after reverting the UI change.
