prs.title: feat(zerocode): add multi-select editors for alias-reference arrays
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Offer searchable multi-select editing for Config arrays that reference existing names, using the same schema metadata and alias lookup as scalar references.
  - Keep changes local until Ctrl+S. Preserve the existing order and unresolved entries, append newly selected names, and send an array when saving, including an empty array.
  - Read the daemon's TOML array display correctly so quotes, backslashes, and untouched text fallback entries survive a save.
- **Scope boundary:** Ordinary text arrays and structured JSON editing retain their current editors. Alias rename, MCP grants, config serialization, and provider fallback execution are unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** Generated Config field metadata, reference-name lookup, and ZeroCode Config field editors. Five arrays receive reference metadata: agent `skill_bundles`, `knowledge_bundles` and `mcp_bundles`, and MCP bundle `servers` and `exclude`. Provider `fallback_models` and channel-reference arrays keep the text editor; they can be added later with the same `#[alias_source]` attribute.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11485. Related #8062 and #7468 remain separate.
- **Labels:** `enhancement`, `risk:medium`, `size:L`, `config`, `zerocode`.

### What this does, simply

ZeroCode's Config tab lets you choose the bundles an agent uses. Several settings take a list of existing names, but the editor previously asked you to type each name on a separate line.

This PR lists those names with selection boxes. Search with `/`, toggle a name with Enter or a double-click, and save the staged list with Ctrl+S. Escape cancels the edit; while searching, the first Escape clears the search.

Opening the editor keeps every saved entry, including names that no longer appear in the available choices. Existing entries keep their order. New choices are appended. Fields without reference metadata, or without available lookup results, keep text editing.

### Scope and maintenance tradeoff

The schema remains the owner of reference metadata, and the existing alias lookup RPC supplies choices. MCP server names use the existing lookup of server `name` keys. The editor adds one ordered staging list; it does not maintain another catalogue of valid aliases. Tests exercise both generated metadata and input handlers with RPC save/readback. The added wire enum variant follows the existing requirement that the daemon and ZeroCode come from the same build.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. A real Config session provides useful visual confirmation of the selection boxes and help.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=tui`, ZeroCode Config.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Run a daemon and ZeroCode built from the same checkout. Use an existing agent and at least two skill bundles (`[skill_bundles.<alias>]`; with `directory` unset, each resolves to `<install>/shared/skills/<alias>/`). With none configured, the field falls back to the text editor with "None configured yet. Enter manually." No provider request is required.
- **Steps to run:** In Config, open Agents, select the agent, open Bundles, and edit `skill_bundles`. Search with `/`, use Enter to toggle a name, clear the search with Escape, then cancel with Escape. Reopen, toggle a name, save with Ctrl+S, and reopen to check the saved selection. Repeat with `knowledge_bundles` or `mcp_bundles`. For MCP bundles, edit `servers` or `exclude` using existing server names.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Reference arrays show available names with checked/unchecked boxes. Toggles remain staged until Ctrl+S. Cancellation leaves the saved list unchanged. An empty selection saves an empty list with the field's existing meaning.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The same arrays open a one-entry-per-line text editor, requiring you to type valid identifiers.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [Required CI passed](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/37142265772/job/111260581062) on the pre-rebase head `280fc9ca851147e21a0976ca3c399e053e08bdfb`; CI is rerunning on the current head `aa8a7dfd5acfb42af178a67f51edf2fb544d1589`. Workspace tests, formatting, lint, schema/build checks, Windows compilation, and the ZeroCode RPC dependency boundary supply the broader coverage.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** CI cannot provide direct visual evidence from a real interactive Config session.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo test --locked -p zerocode --bin zerocode config_manager::tests -- --test-threads=8
64 passed; 0 failed
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config --lib alias_metadata_tests
3 passed; 0 failed
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-macros --lib alias_source
2 passed; 0 failed
cargo test --locked -p zerocode --bin zerocode mcp_servers_alias_source_round_trips
1 passed; 0 failed
cargo fmt --all -- --check
Passed
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
Comment hygiene gate passed.
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Source tracing confirmed that keyboard and mouse selection use the same staging handler and that MCP names use the canonical resolver. Automated input/RPC tests cover filtered toggles, ordered and unresolved selections, cancellation without a write, empty saves, scalar selection, lookup failure/empty-result text fallback, TOML quote/backslash handling, and reopening after TOML-string readback. I also ran the picker in a real ZeroCode Config session: two skill bundles listed with selection boxes on the agent's `skill_bundles` field, and `/` search narrowed the list.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Two screenshots in [this comment](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11502#issuecomment-6232005804): the `skill_bundles` picker with bundles listed, and a search.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Automated tests used the current head `aa8a7dfd5acfb42af178a67f51edf2fb544d1589`, ZeroCode Config input/RPC boundary. The screenshots come from my experiment build [`experiment/zerocode-builds/20261015T062922Z-af67956b5e9d`](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/experiment/zerocode-builds/20261015T062922Z-af67956b5e9d) (commit [`af67956b5e9d`](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/commit/af67956b5e9d1b9a9f0521dab4a1f48c999d6e71)), which carries this PR's changes in its dogfood base [`0341618f9d69`](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/commit/0341618f9d69e31bf38300d134ba86e98491d49d), plus a one-line fixup adapting the save path to a newer `config/set` return value. That fixup is now part of this PR after the rebase onto master.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** See Visual evidence below.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Handler tests stage filtered additions without `config/set`, save one JSON array followed by one readback, preserve original order/unknown entries, and send no write on cancellation.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full local workspace validation is delegated to required CI.

### Visual evidence

Screenshots are in [this comment](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11502#issuecomment-6232005804): (1) Agents, agent, `skill_bundles` showing the configured bundles with selection boxes and the toggle/save/cancel help; (2) the same list narrowed by `/` search. They check presentation; the RPC tests above establish save, cancel and ordering behavior.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No. The existing daemon RPC supplies choices and saves.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for saved configuration. The existing matched daemon/ZeroCode version requirement remains in effect.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes. Reference arrays have a multi-select Config editor, and field metadata includes array alias sources and `mcp_servers`.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Exact upgrade steps for existing users: Rebuild and restart the daemon and ZeroCode from the same checkout, as required by the current wire protocol. No config migration is needed. Missing metadata or failed/empty lookup results use the text editor.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the editor commit, then the metadata commit, and rebuild both binaries: `git revert --no-edit aa8a7dfd5acf 2198666216cb 779bc969bb`.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. The text editor remains the fallback for unsupported arrays and failed/empty lookup results.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Incorrect checked names, lost references or changed priority after save/reopen, a write after cancellation, or an array editor sending a scalar value. Check the saved field and Config RPC payload.

## Supersede Attribution

N/A. This PR does not supersede another contribution.

prs.title: feat(zerocode): show readable Config labels and full field details
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Config field rows use readable labels and bounded value previews so long arrays do not consume the visible row.
  - The selected field's Help view starts with its exact path, complete description, and current masked value. It follows the selected row on regular field tabs, including filtered results.
  - Shared help prose uses the existing Unicode-aware text wrapper so long paths and array items wrap and remain reachable by scrolling.
- **Scope boundary:** Presentation and field help only; configuration keys, defaults, validation, registry, and save behavior are unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** ZeroCode Config rendering, prose wrapping in the shared Help overlay, and Config documentation.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11489. Related #9363 for localization completeness and #8062 for structured JSON editing.
- **Labels:** `enhancement`, `risk:medium`, `size:M`, `zerocode`, `docs`.

### What this does, simply

Config currently shows raw setting names and clips descriptions into a small fixed area. This PR makes the rows easier to scan and lets you open Help to read the full setting information, including its exact configuration path and long value. Secrets stay hidden. Unset values and environment overrides remain distinguishable; unit and default explanations come from the schema description, without inferring how a current value was configured.

### Scope and maintenance tradeoff

The change reuses the existing Config descriptors, Fluent catalogue, Help overlay, and text-input wrapping. It adds no metadata registry, RPC method, dependency, or persisted state. One-line rows preserve existing list and mouse geometry. The inline Enter-to-edit hint is removed to leave room for the label and preview; the existing edit binding remains available. The supporting shared-help change is needed because whitespace-only wrapping permanently clipped long unbroken paths and values.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=tui`, ZeroCode Config and Help.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Connect ZeroCode to your existing daemon. Use an existing agent with a precheck timeout or a risk profile with a long command/path list; no configuration change is needed.
- **Steps to run:** Open Config and select a field with a long value (for example a risk profile's command list). Inspect its label and preview, then press `?` (or Ctrl+G) to open Help and scroll through the complete path, description, and value. Close Help, open the filter, type part of a setting path, move to a match with the arrow keys, and press Ctrl+G; while the filter box is focused, `?` is typed into the filter and Enter opens the editor. Help should describe the highlighted match. Repeat on a secret field. Run the same steps on `master` to compare. The filter matches setting paths, not values.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Readable labels, an ellipsis on clipped previews, the highlighted field's exact path and full description/value accessible through scrolling, and hidden secret contents.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Raw path labels, clipped long row values, and descriptions limited to one or two rows. Field information is absent from Help; long unbroken help prose can be clipped.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Required CI on head `e586ce2821d9716af5a8deb8d31f620b944a031c` (rebased onto master 2026-10-17 as `30e1a68770f9eab6e4e4a4eec8b934b2a9feb90c`, plus the Greptile fix); the earlier [Quality Gate run](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/37141751014) passed on the pre-rebase head `fc265b5148f56cbb5c853f5bdf85504e82d538f0`. Focused local tests exercise Config selection and Help rendering.
- **Known CI coverage gap:** CI does not render a real terminal; that was checked by hand in a running ZeroCode (Visual evidence below).
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo test --locked -p zerocode config_manager::tests
28 passed; 0 failed
cargo test --locked -p zerocode help_
3 library tests and 24 binary tests passed; 0 failed
cargo build --locked -p zerocode
Finished dev profile successfully
cargo fmt --all
Passed
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
Comment hygiene gate passed.
git diff --check
```

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **Current base/head:** `a7ec85708a68d100546f8d1aa53317a1bffa16da` / `b75a48705c6f294eb50618df01b2bf7e4b3ff4b2`
- **What changed and why:** `connection_establishment_failure_does_not_quarantine_endpoint` previously targeted a bound-but-not-listening ephemeral socket. Linux refuses that connect immediately, but macOS can leave it pending until timeout, causing a different error and quarantining the endpoint. The test now targets `http://127.0.0.1:1`, which is refused immediately on both platforms, and asserts the second request also returns the exact redacted connection-failure error without quarantine.
- **Credit:** This adopts the faster port-1 approach proposed by @IftekharUddin in #11321, with the stronger repeated-request assertions requested by @Audacity88. This PR keeps the original contribution; the two overlapping fixes should not both merge.
- **Scope boundary:** Test-only. No provider or runtime code changes.
- **Blast radius:** One test in `crates/zeroclaw-providers/tests/hailo_ollama.rs`.
- **Linked issue(s):** None.
- **Labels:** `risk:low`, `size:XS`, `type:test`

### What this does, simply

Port 1 is below the ephemeral range, so a parallel fixture cannot be assigned that port. With no listener on loopback port 1, Linux and macOS refuse the connection immediately; this avoids the platform-specific pending-connect behavior and the 10-second waits. The explicit trade-off is that the test assumes no service on the host is listening on port 1.

prs.title: feat(channels): Gemini speech-to-speech broker channel (PR1: daemon-side core)
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:** PR1 of the accepted Gemini speech-to-speech broker
  RFC (#8780, tracker #10406). Adds a feature-gated `speech_to_speech` channel
  where a realtime voice model (Gemini Live) owns the caller audio and reaches
  the ZeroClaw agent through exactly one bridge function, `consult_agent`
  (+ `end_session`) — the voice model never sees tools; only the agent does.
  Vendors a small MIT `gemini-live` crate for the wire protocol. Adds config
  surface (`channels.speech_to_speech.<alias>`), broker-persona resolution
  confined to the agent workspace, consult-history binding, and a startup
  retention/cost privacy warning.
- **Scope boundary:** No audio-frame transport (mic in / speaker out) yet — the
  channel ships its session engine and config surface and stays inert (parks
  until cancelled) until the transport lands in a follow-up PR. No changes to
  existing channels, the tool pipeline, or provider wiring.
- **Blast radius:** Off by default (`channel-speech-to-speech` cargo feature).
  When the feature is off, nothing compiles in. Touches `zeroclaw-channels`,
  `zeroclaw-config` (new optional section + one warning), `zeroclaw-api`
  (`ChannelKind::SpeechToSpeech`), and adds the vendored `gemini-live` crate.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #8780, Related #10406.

### What this does, simply

A phone call is answered by a voice model, not by the agent. It chats with the
caller and, whenever something needs the agent, passes the question through one
bridge function and speaks the answer back in its own words. The agent's tools
stay out of the voice model's reach entirely.


- **Review rounds addressed (refreshed onto current master).** The branch was
  re-applied on top of master; the conflicts were content conflicts
  (workspace members, the config warning collector, the generated feature
  lists) and were resolved keeping master's side plus this branch's addition.
  The blocking findings are answered as follows.
  - *Control messages lost on reconnect.* Every `ClientText` and
    `ToolResponse` now carries a receipt the transport driver resolves to
    `Written`, `Discarded` or `Failed`: written once the transport accepts the
    frame, discarded when the command is dropped in the backoff window, failed
    when the transport refuses the write. Commands queued during reconnect and
    setup stay queued and are written after the reopen, so nothing is replayed
    twice. `Channel::send` waits for that verdict (bounded) and reports a lost
    reply as a delivery failure instead of a silent success; no backlog is
    re-sent behind the caller's back, and an older turn completion no longer
    retires a newer reply because there is no shared pending list to clear.
    A tool acknowledgement has no caller to answer, so a discarded or refused
    one is logged with its call id and listed again when the call ends.
    Exactly-once across a broken connection is not attempted.
  - *A timed-out reply written late.* The queued command and its receipt now
    share one claim. When `send()` runs out of time it expires the receipt:
    a reply the driver has not started writing is withdrawn (the driver skips
    it when it reaches it), so a reply reported undelivered is never spoken
    after the agent has answered again; a write already in progress cannot be
    withdrawn and is reported as undecided, not as a confirmed failure.
    Teardown gives the acknowledgements still undecided the same budget before
    counting any of them lost: the session handle is released so the driver
    drains, the verdicts are awaited up to the deadline, and only an
    acknowledgement the driver never started is reported as unanswered.
  - *History and delayed replies.* Every attached call mints its own identity
    and carries it in `sender` and `reply_target`, so two calls on one alias no
    longer share a conversation history. The orchestrator echoes that address
    back as `SendMessage::recipient`, and a reply naming a call that has ended
    is dropped with a log instead of being spoken to whoever is on the line.
  - *Staged outbound surfaces.* Both spellings are declared in the one-shot and
    announcement intentional-unsupported dispositions, so the feature-enabled
    registration guards pass without new outbound functionality.
  - *SOP identity.* `ChannelKind::VoiceBroker` is renamed to `SpeechToSpeech`,
    so configuration, inbound topics (`speech_to_speech/<alias>`), attribution
    and discovery all use one token; the sender label follows the same name. A
    configured alias now appears in the trigger projection with its setup path,
    covered by a new registry test.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A` — the channel has no audio transport
  yet, so there is no end-to-end caller flow to exercise; behavior is covered
  by unit tests on setup assembly, the security tool-set invariant, persona
  confinement, history binding, and the parked-listen contract.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** On `00bad6402b1e6e209862ba37b7d05d0f5fa7cefc`, the required CI run is linked from the checks tab; the `Test` job compiles the feature-enabled channel and runs its tests, and `Lint` runs clippy with `-D warnings` over the workspace, which is what caught the dead test helper in the previous iteration. Before pushing, the same head passed a fork-side Linux run of fmt, `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` with `-D warnings`, clippy, and the `gemini-live` and `zeroclaw-channels` lib tests with `channel-speech-to-speech` enabled: https://github.com/metalmon/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39140694835. That run's one failure is `openai::tool_round_policy_tests::native_tool_round_flags_reach_stream_and_chat_wires_without_changing_defaults` in `zeroclaw-providers`, a local-mock HTTP test on a file this branch does not touch, which fails on that runner on every current head; the `gemini-live`, feature-enabled `speech_to_speech` and full `zeroclaw-channels` suites pass there. The branch sits on master at `dc8c850891`; the master head `c473221313` fails `cargo fmt --check` on `tests/architecture/release_workflow.rs`, which is not from this branch. `Security` is green on this head. The `Source Image Build` jobs fail on every current PR, including this one: the Dockerfile prefetch stage does not stage the `sign_manifest` example that master added to `zeroclaw-plugins`, so cargo refuses the manifest before any source from this branch is involved; an upstream fix is open.

- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No live audio round trip was run; audio transport remains deferred. The lifecycle follow-ups the last round listed as nonblocking (an awaited queue send delaying `stop()`, cancellation of `run_session` skipping detachment, `goAway` after a successful connection counting toward the reconnect budget) are not addressed here and are carried into the audio-transport PR.

- **Commands run and tail output:**

```sh
cargo test -p gemini-live                                   # 45 passed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --features channel-speech-to-speech --lib speech_to_speech
```

- **Tests added for this round:**
  - `an_expired_control_is_never_written_and_an_in_flight_one_says_so`
    (`gemini-live`) — with the transport stalled on one write, expiring the
    queued control reports `Unwritten` and the driver skips it once the stall
    lifts, while expiring the stalled one reports `InFlight`; `FakeTransport`
    gained `stall_writes_after` so a hanging write is actually exercised.
  - `a_reply_that_expires_during_the_reconnect_is_never_written_after_the_reopen`
    — the gated reconnect outlasts `CONTROL_ACK_TIMEOUT`; `send()` reports the
    reply undelivered, and after the reopen the reply never reaches the new
    connection.
  - `a_reply_whose_write_is_still_in_progress_is_reported_as_unknown_not_lost`
    — a write the transport has taken and not completed is reported as
    undecided, not withdrawn.
  - `model_end_session_closes` now asserts the final acknowledgement is on the
    wire before `run_session` returns, which is the bounded teardown settle.
  - `a_written_control_reports_written_and_a_refused_one_reports_failed`
    (`gemini-live`, previous round) — the receipt resolves to `Written` when the transport
    accepts the frame and to `Failed` when it refuses it; `FakeTransport`
    gained `fail_writes_after` so a refused write is actually exercised rather
    than ending through the idle timeout.
  - `a_reply_enqueued_while_the_driver_reconnects_is_written_once_after_the_reopen`
    — a reply queued during connect/setup reaches the reopened connection
    exactly once; a control dropped in the backoff window reports `Discarded`
    and is not replayed.
  - `an_earlier_turn_completion_does_not_cancel_a_newer_reply` — a buffered
    `TurnComplete` from the previous turn does not affect a reply queued after
    it.
  - `a_reply_the_provider_refuses_is_reported_as_a_failure` — `send()` returns
    an error naming the refusal instead of `Ok`.
  - `an_acknowledgement_that_is_never_written_is_reported_with_its_call_id` —
    a tool acknowledgement discarded with the dead connection shows up in the
    call's unanswered-tool-call report under its id.
  - `a_reply_for_an_ended_call_is_not_spoken_into_the_next_one` and
    `speech_to_speech_alias_projects_under_its_ingress_identity` carry over
    from the previous round.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The setup builder emits exactly `{consult_agent, end_session}` in `setup.tools[]` (security invariant test); the broker persona path is resolved relative to and confined to the agent workspace and never falls back to `AGENTS.md`; `listen()` parks until cancelled rather than returning `Ok(())` immediately; the configured `model` id is threaded onto the wire via `SetupConfig.model_id_override` without the crate guessing api-version compatibility (Gemini rejects an incompatible combo itself). Reconnect: a `sessionResumptionUpdate` with `resumable: false` now clears the stored handle so a stale handle is never replayed; the crate discards commands during backoff and emits `SessionOpened { is_reconnect, resumed }`. Not verified: live audio round-trip (no transport yet).
- **Visual interface changed?** `N/A`.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes** — reads a
  broker persona file, resolved relative to and hard-confined within the agent
  workspace (path canonicalized and checked to stay under the workspace root);
  it never reads `AGENTS.md` or escapes the workspace.
- New external network calls? **Yes** — the session API opens a connection to a fixed `wss://` Gemini Live endpoint. The configured channel listener remains inert in this slice, so enabling an alias does not yet open that session. The separately exported raw `connect_ws` helper accepts a supplied URL and does not enforce `wss://` on its direct, no-proxy branch.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **Yes** — adds a channel-local `api_key: Option<String>` field marked `#[secret]` and `x-secret`. This slice does not yet wire that key into a live session; production credential resolution is deferred with the listener integration. It does not currently resolve an existing Gemini provider profile.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs?
  **No**.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes,
  bounded** — the voice model can only reach the agent through `consult_agent`;
  it never receives tool schemas or results, so a compromised/confused voice
  turn cannot invoke tools. Caller audio flows to the provider; a startup
  warning (`speech_to_speech_provider_retention`) discloses provider retention
  and that enabled transcription is billed as text tokens on top of audio.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes** — new optional config section; absent config and
  the default build are unaffected (feature off by default).
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes** — adds
  `[channels.speech_to_speech.<alias>]` (all fields optional with defaults).
  No env or CLI changes.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No** — vendored crate is edition 2021;
  workspace crates stay edition 2024 on the existing floor.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <merge-sha>`; or simply build
  without `--features channel-speech-to-speech` — the channel is off by default.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `channel-speech-to-speech` cargo feature
  (off by default); per-alias `enabled = false`.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** startup warning
  `speech_to_speech_provider_retention` per enabled alias; a live session logs a
  `wss://` connect. With the feature off, no code path is reachable.

prs.title: feat(tools): add agy_cli coding-CLI tool for Antigravity CLI
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Google has moved terminal Gemini use from Gemini CLI to Antigravity CLI (`agy`), and Gemini CLI has stopped serving most accounts (Google Developers Blog, June 2026). ZeroClaw can delegate coding tasks to Codex, Claude Code, Gemini CLI and OpenCode, but not to `agy`.
  - Adds `agy_cli`, a peer of `codex_cli` / `claude_code` / `gemini_cli` / `opencode_cli`. It is built on the shared coding-CLI executor, so it inherits the same authorization, working-directory validation, timeout, output bounding and runtime-executor routing.
  - Headless `agy` exits 0 and reports `status: SUCCESS` even when it auto-denies a tool permission, so the exit code alone would report a blocked task as a success. `agy_cli` requests JSON output and decides success from it. A run succeeds only when the process exits 0, `status` is `SUCCESS`, and `denied_actions` is empty. Non-JSON or status-less output fails closed.
  - Tool-owned flags are attached (`--print=<prompt>`, `--model=<id>`, `--print-timeout=<n>s`) and placed after operator `extra_args`. A model-supplied prompt that starts with `-` cannot be parsed as a flag, and the tool's own settings take precedence over operator arguments.
- **Scope boundary:** `gemini_cli` is not changed or deprecated here. There is no `agy` model provider. The shared coding-CLI executor is unchanged apart from recognising the new tool name in the env-boundary helper. The sandbox and permission defaults of `agy` itself are left to the operator's agy settings.
- **Blast radius:** Opt-in only. The new `[agy_cli]` section defaults to `enabled = false`, and nothing changes for existing configs. Shared test fixtures changed in two places: the budget-test fake now returns agy-shaped JSON, which the other adapters pass through unchanged, and the runtime routing test now expects `agy_cli` to fail closed on its plain-text probe.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11075. Related #4879, whose closing comment suggested Antigravity CLI support as the follow-up. Related #10381 (merged): `agy_cli` builds its command through the shared `CodingCliCommand`/`CodingCliExecutor` path, so it inherits that PR's host-launcher resolution before the workspace working directory is applied.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw agents can hand a coding task to an external coding CLI. Google has replaced Gemini CLI with a new tool called Antigravity CLI (`agy`), so Gemini users had no supported way to do that. This PR adds an `agy_cli` tool that works like the existing Codex and Claude Code tools. It stays off until you turn it on in config.

The main difference from the other CLIs is how failure is detected. When `agy` runs without a terminal and wants to do something that needs permission, such as running a shell command, it refuses automatically but still exits successfully. `agy_cli` reads agy's JSON result, reports those refusals as a failure, and tells the user how to allow the action in agy's own settings.

ZeroClaw checks that the requested working directory is inside the workspace, but it does not sandbox what `agy` does once it is running. That is governed by agy's own permission settings. The docs section added in `tools/overview.md` states this plainly.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The behaviour is covered by unit tests with fixtures copied from real agy 1.2.9 output. Manual testing needs an authenticated `agy` install, which most reviewers will not have.

### How I tested

- **Revision (2026-10-11):** one commit, which supersedes `76275ecf6`. It was authored and validated at `34d7aea0825a1e7cd7701135e4dc3f341271a56b` on master `0f8fb9d372a5cf850e87f9464c7f5c216a717fee`. **Rebase note (2026-10-11):** the then-current head `6239f29f26fcbe1e6b520016cb98b9eade20f329` was a base-only rebase of that commit onto master `d03325172eb6c64272f01042b60fd7f66d74c711` with GitHub's update-branch (`git range-diff` shows the commit identical; the local validation and review below were recorded on `34d7aea08`). **Rebase note (2026-10-14):** the then-current head `dc09ad4048d50e3960e9d8c44132a8fec3b4b1cd` was a base-only rebase of `6239f29f2` onto master `329e66f76` with GitHub's update-branch. ## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes**
- New external network calls? **Yes**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes**
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation:
  - Permissions and network: when enabled, `agy_cli` launches `agy`, which acts on files and calls Google's services under its own permission model, like the existing coding-CLI tools. The tool is disabled by default and gated by the same security policy, autonomy level and rate limiting as its peers, and the working directory is canonicalized and must stay inside the workspace. Operator `extra_args` that widen agy's permissions (`--dangerously-skip-permissions`, `--add-dir`) produce a non-blocking config-validation warning that does not echo the values.
  - Prompt injection: agy's response is returned to the model as tool output, the same as for the other coding CLIs. Output is bounded by `max_output_bytes`.
  - Containment limit, stated in the docs: ZeroClaw validates only the starting directory. What `agy` touches after launch is governed by agy's own settings.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes**
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes.** New optional `[agy_cli]` config section, disabled by default. Existing configs are unaffected.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No**
- Upgrade steps: none required. To use the tool, add `[agy_cli]` with `enabled = true` and have an authenticated `agy` on `PATH`.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Medium risk and opt-in: `git revert <sha>`. The `[agy_cli] enabled = false` setting, which is the default, also disables it at runtime.

prs.title: build(container): publish a dist-broad image variant with the full channel set
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:** The standard release container images are built from the `dist` selection, which carries only a subset of the bundled channels, so a configured `[channels.slack.<alias>]` never starts in them. Adding Slack to `dist` would push the standard-distribution **release binary** over the release size cap (measured: +366,592 bytes, taking x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu from 310 KiB under the 64 MiB cap to 47 KiB over it). This PR leaves `dist` untouched and instead publishes the already-defined broad selection as a fifth image variant: `ghcr.io/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw:dist-broad`.
- **Scope boundary:** No feature-registry change, no change to `dist`, the release binaries, the Cargo `default` set, or the installer menus. The new tag uses one `TagSpec` row and its generated output, plus profile forwarding through `docker-publish.yml` and the shared `Dockerfile`. Only `dist-broad` selects thin LTO with one codegen unit, after fat LTO exceeded the arm64 runner memory limit. Existing tag settings remain unchanged. The weekly Trivy matrix is deliberately **not** extended (see Blast radius).
- **Blast radius:** `docker-publish.yml` iterates every `[[tags]]` entry in `dev/ci/docker-tags.toml`, so the new stem is built, signed, and pushed on every release alongside the existing four. `release-stable-manual.yml` calls that workflow synchronously, so release time and artifact count grow by one image per release. `Selection::DistBroad`'s doc comment changes because publishing it is the "stable broad artifact lifecycle" the old comment was waiting for; `Selection::menu()` still excludes it from installer menus. The weekly `trivy-scheduled.yml` scan is intentionally **not** extended to the new stem: it uses a hand-written subset matrix and hard-fails on a missing image, so it can only be added after the first release actually publishes `dist-broad`.
- **Linked issue(s):** None.

### Why a separate image rather than widening `dist`

Measured with the repository's own tool (`scripts/ci/binary_size_report.sh measure --profile standard-distribution`, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, rustc 1.98.1, `release` profile):

| revision | bytes | MiB | margin to the 64 MiB cap |
|---|---|---|---|
| `master` (329e66f76) | 66,790,896 | 63.70 | +317,968 (+310 KiB) |
| `dist` + `channel-slack` | 67,157,488 | 64.05 | -48,624 (-47 KiB) |

`release-stable-manual.yml` enforces `BINARY_SIZE_HARD_LIMIT: "67108864"` and `check_binary_size.sh` exits 1 above it, so widening `dist` would fail the x86_64 release job. The cap is a **binary** gate only: `check_binary_size.sh` is referenced nowhere else, and the container path has no upper size bound - the `Dockerfile` enforces only a floor (`size < 1000000` bytes is treated as a dummy artifact). A broad image can therefore exceed 64 MiB freely, which is exactly the trade this PR makes: a larger, opt-in image instead of a larger default binary.

Why not just point users at the existing `all-features` tag: it is already published (`all-features`, `all-features-v0.8.5` on GHCR) and does include Slack, but it is built from `Containerfile` and is **amd64-only**, and it is the kitchen sink (`hardware`, `browser-native`, `plugins-wasm*`, `sandbox-*`, `memory-postgres`, `dev-sim`, `probe`). There is no arm64 Slack-capable image today, and the kitchen sink is the wrong shape for "I just need the channels". `dist-broad` is `dist` plus the canonical `channels-full` aggregate - the repo's own definition of "the broad channel set" - and builds multi-arch through `Dockerfile`.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw's standard release container images ship a fixed set of messaging channels. Slack is not in that set, so a Slack bot configured against the published image never comes up. The obvious fix - add Slack to the set - makes the release binary cross the project's 64 MiB size cap, so it fails the release job.

This PR takes the other road. ZeroClaw already has a second, broader feature selection (`dist` plus the canonical `channels-full` aggregate), which it uses for measurement. This PR publishes that selection as its own image tag, `dist-broad`, so anyone who needs Slack, Signal, IRC, Matrix, or another channel in that aggregate can pull a bigger image instead of rebuilding from source. The standard image, the release archives, and the default build are all unchanged; nothing gets heavier unless you ask for it. Nostr and WeChat are excluded from `channels-full` and from this image.

The seven changed files cover the tag generator and its tests, generated matrix, Dockerfile profile arguments, publish-workflow forwarding, two documentation pages, and the broad-selection doc comment. Publishing the image begins the broad container lifecycle; installer menus and binary archives remain unchanged.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `No` additional build requested. The [non-publishing run](https://github.com/wray-lee/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38728678483) built amd64, arm64, and the combined multiarch target successfully. The commands below inspect or reproduce the feature/profile inputs.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** the non-publishing Docker build and `cli` startup/configuration loading through `zeroclaw channels list` inside the amd64 image.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Docker with buildx, the repository Rust toolchain, and `yq`; a checkout of this branch.
- **Steps to run:**

  ```bash
  # 1. The publish workflow's build input for the new tag, straight from the
  #    generated matrix the workflow reads.
  yq -o=json '.tags[] | select(.stem == "dist-broad")' dev/ci/docker-tags.toml

  # 2. Build the same feature set and release profile locally (slow).
  FEATURES="$(cargo run -p xtask --bin generate -- features --selection dist-broad)"
  CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO=thin CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_CODEGEN_UNITS=1 \
    cargo build --release --locked --no-default-features --features "$FEATURES"

  # 3. With a disposable Slack alias configured, check startup/config loading.
  # This lists configured aliases; it does not prove compiled channel support.
  ./target/release/zeroclaw channels list
  ```

- **Expected on this branch (after):** step 1 prints one entry with `stem = "dist-broad"`, `floating_tag = "dist-broad"`, `dockerfile = "Dockerfile"`, `platforms = "linux/amd64,linux/arm64"`, `lto = "thin"`, `codegen_units = 1`, and a `flags` string containing `channel-slack`. Step 3 lists the configured Slack alias. Slack inclusion follows from the generated flag, Cargo forwarding, and successful image compilation, not from alias enumeration.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** there is no `dist-broad` matrix entry. The `dist` feature set omits `channel-slack`; `channels list` can still enumerate a configured Slack alias. The new image tag becomes available when a release publishes it.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Installer Drift` runs `cargo generate installers --check`, which gates the generated `dev/ci/docker-tags.toml`; `Docs Style` covers the documentation; the `check` / `build` legs compile the root crate. Current-head Quality Gate and Docker Image PR Check both pass at `15c3a257a6687b04c938c36d8f4a3b3eb11ec935`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The standard `docker-image-pr.yml` compiles source Dockerfiles with default build args, not the per-tag flags/profile values. The separate non-publishing run covers the broad image at the earlier combined revision described below. Its combined job excludes image export, pushing, and signing, so the measured build duration does not establish total publication time within the 60-minute release-job timeout.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

  ```bash
  cargo run -p xtask --bin generate -- installers --check
  # ok: install-sh in sync
  # ... (21 surfaces)
  # ok: zerocode-themes in sync
  # exit 0

  cargo test --locked -p xtask
  # test result: ok. 236 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out

  cargo fmt --all -- --check
  # exit 0

  cargo run -p xtask --bin generate -- features --selection dist-broad
  # acp-bridge,agent-runtime,channel-acp-server,channel-amqp,channel-bluesky,channel-clawdtalk,
  # channel-dingtalk,channel-discord,channel-email,channel-filesystem,channel-git,channel-imessage,
  # channel-irc,channel-lark,channel-line,channel-linq,channel-matrix,channel-mattermost,
  # channel-mochat,channel-mqtt,channel-nextcloud,channel-notion,channel-qq,channel-reddit,
  # channel-signal,channel-slack,channel-telegram,channel-twitch,channel-twitter,channel-voice-call,
  # channel-webhook,channel-wecom,channel-wecom-ws,channel-whatsapp-cloud,gateway,
  # observability-prometheus,schema-export,whatsapp-web

  cargo check --locked --no-default-features --features "<the list above>"
  # Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s)
  # exit 0
  ```

At the original local validation, `actionlint` was unavailable. The current diff changes workflow YAML to forward the profile arguments, and current-head CI passes. Workspace-wide clippy was not runnable in the original environment either (this container's clippy 1.98.1 flags a pre-existing `clippy::drop_non_drop` in `crates/zeroclaw-channels/src/orchestrator/mod.rs`, untouched by this PR); the changed Rust file is clean under `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings`.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Confirmed against the live registry that `minimal`, `default-features`, `dist`, and `all-features` are the published stems today, and that the `latest` / versioned / `debian` tags come from a *different* job (`release-stable-manual.yml`) that packages the pre-built `dist` release binaries - which is why those images also lack Slack, and why this PR does not change them. Confirmed no upper-bound size gate applies to images, and that the Trivy scheduled scan uses a hand-written subset matrix and fails hard on a missing image (hence the deliberate omission below). The subsequent [build report](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11741#issuecomment-6192011982) records a fat-LTO arm64 memory failure and successful thin-LTO builds. The combined amd64/arm64 build finished in 36m51s, exit 0, at 12,180 MiB peak runner memory. The amd64 job finished in 21m42s and loaded a 155 MB image containing an 84,097,856-byte `zeroclaw` binary. The configured Slack alias appeared in the amd64 startup/config-loading probe.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A` - no rendered or presentation surface changes.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** The original generator, xtask, and feature-set checks above were reported on `feat/publish-broad-image`. The image run used wrapper `7cc7ebda124eeeecdc3ef00eaf13c13e7bb9cac3` over combined implementation `d3b243fe05c2f9213f1a68062e70d786d588c095`, with fork-only profile/size diagnostics. The Dockerfile, tag matrix, generator, feature selection, base-image pins, and publish recipe at that combined revision match reviewed head `15c3a257a6687b04c938c36d8f4a3b3eb11ec935`. Later shared-source/dependency integration has passing current-head source-image CI. The broad build result is carried evidence, not a fresh broad build at the current head.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Original command tails are above; image build output and measurements are in the linked run and report.

prs.title: feat(rpc-client): verify the endpoint's OS account before sending a credential
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`. Stacked on #11186 and contains its commits, because #11186's branch lives on a fork and a PR here cannot target it. Review only the last two commits until #11186 merges: `feat(rpc-client): verify the endpoint's OS account before sending a credential` and the review fix `fix(rpc-client): close the unchecked stream path and gate environment and TUI signatures`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - `RpcClient::connect_local` opened the socket and wrote `initialize`, bearer included, to whatever was listening at the resolved path. A listener can put any pid or version in its handshake reply, so another local user's socket at that path, or a stale `ZEROCLAW_SOCKET`, would receive the credential. The separate gateway will send end-user bearers over this path, so this has to hold before the gateway uses it.
  - When `initialize` carries a credential, the dial now checks with the kernel before writing a byte. A credential here is an `auth_token`, a TUI signature (`tui_sig`, which is replayable), or a non-empty forwarded environment (`env`, which can hold API keys). On Unix, the connected socket's peer uid (`UnixStream::peer_cred`, which is `SO_PEERCRED` on Linux and `getpeereid` on macOS) must equal the expected account. The directory that actually holds the socket, with symlinks resolved, must be owned by that account with no group or other write access. The sticky bit does not count as protection: it stops others from deleting a socket, but not from binding the path first while the daemon is down.
  - The expected account is `ConnectOptions::endpoint_owner`: `EndpointOwner::SameAccount` (default, this process's effective uid) or `EndpointOwner::Uid(n)` for a launcher that runs the core as another account. There is no option that skips the check. A refusal drops the stream with nothing written and returns `ClientError::UntrustedEndpoint`, naming the endpoint and both uids (`refusing to send a credential to core endpoint <path>: served by uid 1002, expected 501`). The pid and version the peer reports stay diagnostics only.
  - **No unchecked path to an OS endpoint.** `connect_local` is the only public constructor that reaches a socket or pipe. `RpcClient::connect_over` now takes the daemon's in-process `DuplexStream` only, the transport its in-process connector hands out, and the generic handshake is private. Before the fix, a caller could open a Unix socket or a named pipe itself and pass it to `connect_over`, which sent the token unverified. That no longer compiles. I kept the name `connect_over` rather than renaming it, so every existing caller that passes the duplex (the gateway seam, and the credential pool in #11277) compiles unchanged.
  - **Windows fails closed.** This PR does not implement the pipe-server SID check (`GetNamedPipeServerProcessId`, then the process token's user SID). On Windows, a credential-bearing `connect_local` (token, TUI signature or forwarded environment) returns `UntrustedEndpoint` with `EndpointRejection::Unsupported`, and the pipe receives nothing. Since `connect_over` no longer accepts a pipe, this holds for every public constructor. I could not run Windows code for this change, and a security check that has never run would be the weak point. The SID check belongs with the core-side pipe DACL work in #11001. Tokenless Windows dials are unchanged.
  - The check runs on every call, so each reconnect re-verifies, and a path that now leads somewhere else is judged again. Dials that present no token, no TUI signature and no environment are not gated (an unsigned TUI id does not count). The daemon still authenticates them by the peer credential it reads on its side, which is how a `[users]` roster member reaches a daemon running as another account.
- **Trust-boundary decision still open:** Jordan has not yet decided whether a separate gateway runs under the same OS account as the core or under its own low-authority account. This PR implements the same-account floor that both options need. On Unix it also accepts the launcher-provided uid that the separate-account option would add. The check does not isolate processes that run as the same account, and cannot: they can read the core's config and tokens directly. With Windows failing closed, a preview built on this PR is Unix-only for anything that sends a credential; that belongs in the OS account trust-boundary decision record.
- **Scope boundary:** No gateway, runtime or daemon changes. The gateway still reaches the core only through the in-process duplex (`connect_over`), where both ends live in one process and there is no other account to verify. The following are not included: the Windows SID check and pipe DACL, child-mode pid pinning (no launcher passes a pid yet), and the no-tokenless-fallback pool.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw-rpc-client` only. `connect_local` has no callers yet. `connect_over`'s only caller outside the crate, the gateway seam, already passes the in-process duplex. The gateway builds `ConnectOptions::default()` and matches `ClientError` with a catch-all, so the new field and variant change nothing there. The crate gains `libc` on Unix, already linked through tokio. The Cargo.lock change adds only that edge and the `tempfile` dev-dependency, with no new crates. The rpc-client dependency ratchet in `tests/architecture/rpc_proto_boundary.rs` now reads `[target.*]` tables too, so the new dependency is checked instead of slipping through, and it allows `libc`.
- **Review follow-ups not in this PR:**
  - A real second-account listener test on Linux CI (the contract's CT-ID-06). The unit tests reach the same refusal by expecting a uid other than the listener's.
  - The Windows pipe-server SID check and the core-side pipe DACL, with #11001.
  - A `risk:*` / security-review label, which is a maintainer call.
  - Restack onto `master` once #11186 merges, so the diff shrinks to these two commits.
  - A hardened-mode launcher that uses socket activation or a root-owned runtime directory would be refused today, as the notes beside the checks say.
- **Linked issue(s):** Part of #11001. Depends on #11186.
- **Labels:** `release:v0.9.0`, `ci:windows` (so the Windows tests run)

### What this does, simply

Before this change, a program that connected to the ZeroClaw daemon's local socket with a login token would hand the token to anything listening at that address. On a shared machine, another user could put their own listener at that address and collect the token. The client now asks the operating system which user account runs the other end, and whether anyone else could have planted the socket. It sends the token only when both answers are right. The same applies to the other secrets a connection can carry: a reconnect signature and forwarded environment variables. This happens on every connection, there is no setting that turns it off, and the client has no other way to talk to a socket. Windows cannot do this check yet, so there the client refuses to send any of these at all. Connections that carry none of them work as before.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The behavior is at the socket boundary and the tests below exercise it with real Unix sockets. Reproducing it by hand needs a second OS account.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `CI Required Gate`: the Linux test job runs the new `zeroclaw-rpc-client` tests with `SO_PEERCRED`, and the Windows `Check` build compiles the Windows dial path as part of the gateway graph.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The two Windows tests (`windows_refuses_a_credential_dial_it_cannot_verify`, which now covers a token, a TUI signature and forwarded environment, and `windows_dials_without_a_token_as_before`) run only in the advisory Windows job. The `ci:windows` label is now applied so that job runs them. CI runs tests with nextest, which skips doctests, so the `compile_fail` doctest on `connect_over` runs only under `cargo test`. Locally I compiled and linted the Windows code on macOS only: a full cross-check of this crate stops in `ring`'s C build, reached through `zeroclaw-config`. So I built `verify.rs` unchanged, plus the Windows dial path and test helpers copied verbatim, in a standalone crate. `cargo check --all-targets` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` for `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` both pass. Those Windows tests have not run anywhere.
- **Commands run and tail output** (macOS arm64, Rust 1.96.1):

  ```text
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-rpc-client
  test client::tests::a_credential_is_never_written_to_an_endpoint_of_another_account ... ok
  test client::tests::a_same_account_endpoint_in_a_private_directory_receives_the_credential ... ok
  test client::tests::a_socket_in_a_directory_other_accounts_can_write_is_refused ... ok
  test client::tests::every_dial_verifies_the_endpoint_again ... ok
  test client::tests::environment_and_tui_signature_dials_are_verified_like_tokens ... ok
  test client::tests::a_dial_that_presents_nothing_reusable_is_not_gated ... ok
  test verify::tests::a_peer_of_another_account_is_refused_and_both_uids_are_named ... ok
  test verify::tests::a_peer_of_the_expected_account_passes ... ok
  test verify::tests::a_directory_of_another_account_is_refused ... ok
  test verify::tests::a_directory_others_can_write_is_refused_even_when_sticky ... ok
  test verify::tests::a_private_or_read_only_shared_directory_passes ... ok
  test verify::tests::the_default_owner_is_this_account ... ok
  test result: ok. 26 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored
  test crates/zeroclaw-rpc-client/src/client.rs - client::RpcClient::connect_over (line 405) - compile fail ... ok
  test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored

  cargo test --test architecture rpc_
  test rpc_proto_boundary::rpc_client_depends_only_on_foundation_crates_and_tokio ... ok
  test result: ok. 5 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 54 filtered out

  cargo fmt --all -- --check                                        EXIT:0
  cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-rpc-client --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings   EXIT:0
  cargo check -p zeroclaw-rpc-client -p zeroclaw-gateway -p zeroclaw --all-targets   EXIT:0
  RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc -p zeroclaw-rpc-client --no-deps   EXIT:0
  scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh                                 Comment hygiene gate passed.
  scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh                                    Summary: 0 error(s)
  scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh                                      OK
  ```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - Each test fails against the mutant it targets:
    - Removing the check entirely fails the other-account, writable-directory and re-verify tests.
    - Dropping only the peer-uid comparison fails the other-account test.
    - Dropping only the directory check fails the writable-directory and re-verify tests.
    - Gating tokenless dials too fails the tokenless test.
    - Exempting sticky directories, as the daemon's own lock-directory rule does, fails both sticky cases.
    - Removing `libc` from the ratchet's allow-list fails `rpc_client_depends_only_on_foundation_crates_and_tokio`, which shows the target-table walk is live.
    - Gating on the token alone, dropping `env`, or dropping `tui_sig` from the credential test each fails `environment_and_tui_signature_dials_are_verified_like_tokens`. Gating on an unsigned TUI id too fails `a_dial_that_presents_nothing_reusable_is_not_gated`.
  - The `compile_fail` doctest fails for the intended reason. Turned into a normal doctest, it stops with `error[E0308]: mismatched types ... expected DuplexStream, found UnixStream`. The same snippet with a `DuplexStream` compiles.
  - "Nothing written" is measured, not inferred. The fake endpoint records every byte it receives until the client closes, and each refusal test asserts it received zero bytes.
  - **Other-account endpoint:** a unit test cannot run a listener as another uid. So the real-socket test expects a uid other than the listener's. That leaves the client in the same position as when it faces another user's socket, and the pure `check_peer_uid` tests cover the comparison itself. The contract's CT-ID-06 test, which uses a real throwaway user on Linux CI, is not part of this PR.
  - **Endpoint replacement:** the test first completes a verified dial. It then swaps the socket path for a symlink to a same-account listener in a world-writable directory. The next dial with the same options is refused and the new listener receives nothing.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** the head of this PR; library tests only.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** see the test list above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:**
  - Workspace-wide `cargo test`: the change is confined to one crate and one architecture test.
  - Linux run of the crate tests: left to the required CI job.
  - Windows execution: not available locally, covered above.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. The client now reads the metadata of the directory holding the socket it already dials.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes. `connect_local` now withholds `auth_token`, a TUI signature and forwarded environment unless the kernel shows that the expected account serves the endpoint. On Windows it always withholds them, since it cannot check yet. A refusal says which check failed and never includes the secret. There is no bypass switch, and no other public constructor reaches an OS endpoint.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: The risk is a false refusal. Examples: a socket in a shared directory such as `ZEROCLAW_SOCKET=/tmp/x.sock`, a core that runs as another account without the launcher passing that uid, a socket in a root-owned directory, a socket that a root supervisor binds and hands over (the kernel reports the account that called `listen()`), or any credential-bearing dial on Windows. Each fails closed with an error that names the reason. The default layout, `<data_dir>/daemon.sock` in a directory the daemon sets to `0700`, passes.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for every current caller. Nothing calls `connect_local` yet, and the new field has a default. `ClientError` gains a variant. The crate is unreleased, and the only match on it outside the crate has a catch-all.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No. `endpoint_owner` is a library option; no config key, env var or flag.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <merge sha>`. This removes the check and restores unverified dials, so revert only together with anything that sends real bearers through `connect_local`.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None, on purpose. The check has no off switch.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** credential-bearing dials fail with `refusing to send a credential to core endpoint <path>: ...`. The text after the colon names the uid, the directory mode, or `this platform cannot verify which account serves a local endpoint yet`.

Existing OIDC, principal-isolation, and ZeroRelay work must integrate with this boundary. WATI is already retired. Feature acceptance and normal review/CI/release holds still apply.

prs.title: fix(build): stop metrics and embedded-web from enabling the gateway
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `observability-prometheus` and `embedded-web` forwarded to `zeroclaw-gateway/<feature>`. That is a strong edge: it also turns the optional gateway dependency on. A build that selected metrics or the embedded dashboard without `gateway` therefore compiled the whole HTTP gateway (axum, hyper server, tower-http, the dashboard build script). Every root use of the gateway is behind `cfg(feature = "gateway")`, so that code was never reachable. Both now forward with `zeroclaw-gateway?/<feature>`, like every other forward into the gateway already does.
  - `zeroclaw-runtime` declared `tower` and `tower-http` as optional dependencies that no feature enables and no runtime code uses. They are removed.
  - A new architecture gate fails when any root feature other than `gateway` enables the gateway crate, either through `dep:` or through a strong sub-feature edge. Headless builds cannot quietly pick the server up again.
- **Scope boundary:** no change to the `gateway` feature, the default feature set, the dist feature sets, or any Rust source outside the new test. This PR does not remove the gateway from any shipped artifact. That is later work in the process split. The existing strong forwards into `zeroclaw-runtime` (`observability-prometheus`, `webauthn`, `plugins-wasm`, `sandbox-*`) are outside this PR's scope; this change only adjusts optional gateway activation.
- **Blast radius:** Cargo feature resolution only.
  - Builds that include `gateway` (default, every dist target, the desktop kernel) resolve exactly as before.
  - Builds without `gateway` that select `observability-prometheus`, `metrics` or `embedded-web` stop compiling `zeroclaw-gateway`. This includes `install.sh --without-gateway`, whose default set carries `observability-prometheus`.
  - `Cargo.lock` loses two unused edges from `zeroclaw-runtime`.
- **Linked issue(s):** Part of #11002
- **Labels:** `dependencies`, `tests`, `size:S`, `release:v0.9.0`

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw's web gateway (dashboard, REST API, webhooks) is an optional part of the binary, switched on by the `gateway` build feature. Two unrelated features, Prometheus metrics and "embed the dashboard files", were wired so that asking for either one also switched the gateway on. Someone building a headless agent with metrics got the full web server compiled in, even though nothing could start it. This PR wires those two features so they only adjust the gateway when it is already included. It also adds a check so no other feature can make the same mistake later. Normal builds, including every release build, are unchanged.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. It is quick and needs no build, only dependency resolution.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** build (`cargo tree`), no runtime surface
- **Setup / preconditions:** a checkout of this branch and of `master`
- **Steps to run:** `cargo tree -p zeroclaw --no-default-features --features observability-prometheus -e normal --prefix none | grep -c '^zeroclaw-gateway '` (repeat with `embedded-web`)
- **Expected on this branch (after):** `0`
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `1`. The gateway is in the graph although `gateway` was not selected.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `CI Required Gate` runs the workspace tests, which include the `architecture` test target with the new gate, plus the lint and build jobs over the changed manifests.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** CI does not build a headless (`--no-default-features`) configuration with metrics. That delta is shown with `cargo tree` below and compiled locally.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                  → exit 0
scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh                          → Comment hygiene gate passed.
cargo check --all-targets -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw    → Finished `dev` profile, exit 0
cargo clippy --no-deps --all-targets -p zeroclaw -- -D warnings          → exit 0
cargo clippy --no-deps -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib --bins -- -D warnings    → exit 0
cargo check -p zeroclaw --no-default-features \
  --features agent-runtime,default-channels,acp-bridge,observability-prometheus,schema-export \
  --lib --bins                                              → Finished `dev` profile, exit 0
  (6 pre-existing dead-code warnings in src/main.rs for gateway-off builds; unchanged by this PR)
rustc --edition 2024 --test tests/architecture/gateway_feature_edges.rs (standalone, see below)
  this branch's Cargo.toml → test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed
```

Gateway present in the resolved graph (`cargo tree -p zeroclaw --no-default-features --features <F> -e normal`, count of `zeroclaw-gateway` nodes):

| `--features` | master | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `observability-prometheus` | 1 | 0 |
| `embedded-web` | 1 | 0 |
| `metrics` | 1 | 0 |
| `agent-runtime,observability-prometheus` | 1 | 0 |
| `gateway,observability-prometheus` | — | 1 |
| `gateway,embedded-web` | — | 1 |

Default and release builds unchanged:
- `cargo tree -p zeroclaw -e features --prefix none --target all` is byte-identical between master and this branch for the default set, for the resolved dist feature list of `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, for `armv7-unknown-linux-gnueabihf` (which excludes Prometheus), and for `--all-features`.
- The per-package resolved features from `cargo metadata` are identical for default and both dist sets.
- With `--all-features`, the only difference is that `zeroclaw-runtime` no longer has the dead implicit `tower`/`tower-http` features.
- The weak edges still apply when the gateway is on. The inverted tree (`-i zeroclaw-gateway -e features`) shows `zeroclaw-gateway feature "observability-prometheus"` for the default build and `zeroclaw-gateway feature "embedded-web"` for `--features gateway,embedded-web`.

Gate proven to fail on master's manifest: compiled the new gate as a standalone test crate (`rustc --edition 2024 --test`, linked against the workspace's `toml` 1.1 rlib) with `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` pointing at this branch's `Cargo.toml`, then at master's. Against master it fails and names exactly the two edges, and it does not flag the intentional `gateway = ["dep:zeroclaw-gateway", ...]` feature:

```text
test gateway_edge_classifies_every_entry_form ... ok
test only_the_gateway_feature_enables_the_gateway_crate ... FAILED
these root features switch on the gateway crate without the `gateway` feature; forward with `zeroclaw-gateway?/<feature>` instead, or select `gateway` explicitly:
  embedded-web = "zeroclaw-gateway/embedded-web"
  observability-prometheus = "zeroclaw-gateway/observability-prometheus"
test result: FAILED. 1 passed; 1 failed
```

The gate's real target (`architecture`) was type-checked by the clippy `--all-targets` run above, and CI runs it in the workspace test job. I did not run `cargo test --test architecture` locally.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The headless feature combination compiles. Every root use of the gateway crate is behind `cfg(feature = "gateway")`, so nothing that could run changes. Not verified: a full release build of any target.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A (no user-visible interface state changed)
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** 78f5bb4000, `cargo tree` / `cargo metadata` / standalone `rustc --test` of the gate
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** the table and tails above
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** see the table
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:**
  - Full `cargo test` for the workspace: the change is manifest-only apart from the new test, and CI runs the full suite.
  - Clippy on the `zeroclaw-runtime` test target: it stops locally on a macOS-only unused import in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/service/mod.rs` that is already on master. This PR changes no runtime source.
  - Clippy without `--no-deps`: on the local toolchain (older than CI's pinned 1.98) it also stops on an existing lint in the untouched `zeroclaw-infra`.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
